label: 'perfect' gold
title: 'perfect' gold
lead:
perfect' gold may refer to:
*'perfect' gold ore
*'perfect' gold bar
*'perfect' necklace
*'perfect' ring

label: 'perfect' gold bar
title: 'perfect' gold bar
lead:
A 'perfect' gold bar is an untradeable gold bar smelted from 'perfect' gold ore. It is used in the Family Crest quest with a ruby and a necklace mould or ring mould to craft a 'perfect' necklace and 'perfect' ring respectively. It can be used as a normal gold bar when crafting any other item of jewellery, creating a normal piece of jewellery, which will not receive the prefix of 'perfect'.

Just like normal gold ore, two 'perfect' gold bars can be smelted at once at the Edgeville furnace if the appropriate tier of Varrock armour is worn.

label: 'perfect' gold ore
title: 'perfect' gold ore
lead:
'Perfect' gold ore is ore mined in the Witchaven Dungeon, found south-east of Ardougne. It requires 40 Mining to mine and can be smelted into a 'perfect' gold bar.

'Perfect' gold ore is the same as regular gold ore. The differences are only seen by Avan from Family Crest quest. He will say that he'll give you his piece of the crest if you make him a necklace and ring made from a 'perfect gold bar' with rubies in them.

label: 'perfect' necklace
title: 'perfect' necklace
lead:
A ' perfect' necklace is a quest item in the Family Crest quest. It is made with a 'perfect' gold bar, ruby, and necklace mould at a furnace, requiring 40 Crafting and yielding 75 Crafting experience. A 'perfect' necklace and 'perfect' ring are given to Avan in exchange for his crest part.

It is possible to mine 'perfect' gold and craft 'perfect' jewellery without speaking to Boot, but he must be spoken to in order to give the jewellery to Avan.

label: 'perfect' ring
title: 'perfect' ring
lead:
A 'perfect' ring is a quest item in the Family Crest quest. It is made with a 'perfect' gold bar, ruby, and ring mould at a furnace, requiring 40 Crafting and yielding 70 Crafting experience. A 'perfect' ring and 'perfect' necklace are given to Avan in exchange for his crest part.

It is possible to mine 'perfect' gold and craft 'perfect' jewellery without speaking to Boot, but he must be spoken to in order to give the jewellery to Avan.
(-) is a suffix used by Chamber of Xeric potions. It denotes the weaker potency of the potion's effects over the regular and (+) variants.
(+) is a suffix used by Chamber of Xeric potions. It denotes the greater potency of the potion's effects over the regular and (-) variants, with the exception of weapon poison(+).

label: (a)
title: (a)
lead: (a) is a suffix typically found on items that have been activated.

label: (attuned)
title: (attuned)
lead: (attuned) is a suffix used exclusively in the Gauntlet, that denotes a piece of equipment as attuned.

label: (b)
title: (b)
lead: (b) is a suffix used to identify blessed items able to cast bloom.

label: (basic)
title: (basic)
lead: (basic) is a suffix used exclusively in the Gauntlet, that denotes a piece of equipment as basic.

label: (beginner)
title: (beginner)
lead: (beginner) is a suffix that denotes items used during beginner Treasure Trails.

label: (bh)
title: (bh)
lead: (bh) is a suffix applied to items earned from playing the Bounty Hunter minigame that can only be used within Bounty Hunter, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, and Soul Wars.

label: (blue)
title: (blue)
lead: (blue) is an uncommon suffix used to denote the colour blue.

label: (broken)
title: (broken)
lead:
(broken) is a suffix applied to items that must be repaired to be usable, though the method of repair varies.

The suffix is added to pieces of Eclipse moon armour, Blue moon armour, and Blood moon armour that have fully degraded. These can be repaired at an armour stand in a Player-owned house or at a repairing NPC such as Bob in Lumbridge. The cost to repair the item depends on where it is repaired and (if repaired at the armour stand) the player's Smithing level.

label: (c)
title: (c)
lead: (c) is a suffix applied to elven equipment that has been corrupted in the Corrupted Gauntlet.

label: (cr)
title: (cr)
lead: (cr) is a suffix applied to dragon equipment to which a Bounty hunter ornament kit has been applied. This equipment is intended to imitate the original appearance of from RuneScape 3.

label: (d)
title: (d)
lead: (d) is a suffix used to identify defensive blackjacks.

label: (dark)
title: (dark)
lead: (dark) is a suffix that denotes that an item is part of the dark mystic robes set.

label: (deadman)
title: (deadman)
lead: (deadman) is a suffix applied to certain equipment to which an annihilation weapon scroll, armageddon weapon scroll, or armageddon cape fabric has been applied to.

label: (dry)
title: (dry)
lead: (dry) is an uncommon suffix used to denote that an item or object is dry.

label: (dusk)
title: (dusk)
lead: (dusk) is a suffix that denotes that an item is part of the dusk mystic robes set.

label: (e)
title: (e)
lead: (e), for enchanted or enhanced, is a suffix applied primarily to enchanted bolts, as well as several pieces of enchanted or enhanced equipment.

label: (easy)
title: (easy)
lead: (easy) is a suffix that denotes an item as easy. Used by Treasure Trails, Temple Trekking, and by antique lamps rewarded from Achievement Diaries.

label: (elite)
title: (elite)
lead: (elite) is a suffix that denotes an item as elite. Used by Treasure Trails and by antique lamps rewarded from Achievement Diaries.

label: (empty)
title: (empty)
lead: (empty) is a suffix that denotes an item as exhausted, used up entirely, or never filled. In the case of nest box (empty), it denotes a nest box that contains empty bird nests.

label: (f)
title: (f)
lead: (f) is a suffix used to denote that a piece of armour is fortified, referring to upgraded rewards from the Tombs of Amascut.

label: (full)
title: (full)
lead: (full) is a suffix used to denote that an item is full to capacity.

label: (g)
title: (g)
lead: (g) is a suffix used to denote that a piece of armour is gilded, or gold trimmed. These items are only obtainable from Treasure Trails.

label: (green)
title: (green)
lead: (green) is an uncommon suffix used to denote the colour green.

label: (h)
title: (h)
lead:
(h) is an uncommon suffix that stands for hint, referring to the poetry scrolls used during the 2023 Pride event containing hints towards the locations of the poets and their love interests.

The suffix may be confused with the suffixes (h1), (h2), (h3), (h4), or (h5), which are a different type of suffix used for heraldic armour.

label: (h1)
title: (h1)
lead: (h1) is a suffix found on heraldic armour sets which denotes the item as part of set 1.

label: (h2)
title: (h2)
lead: (h2) is a suffix found on heraldic armour sets which denotes an item as part of set 2.

label: (h3)
title: (h3)
lead: (h3) is a suffix found on heraldic armour sets which denotes an item as part of set 3.

label: (h4)
title: (h4)
lead: (h4) is a suffix found on heraldic armour sets which denotes an item as part of set 4.

label: (h5)
title: (h5)
lead: (h5) is a suffix found on heraldic armour sets which denotes an item as part of set 5.

label: (hard)
title: (hard)
lead: (hard) is a suffix that denotes an item as hard. Used by Treasure Trails, Temple Trekking, Nightmare Zone, and by antique lamps rewarded from Achievement Diaries.

label: (i)
title: (i)
lead: (i) is a suffix applied to equipment that have been imbued.

label: (inactive)
title: (inactive)
lead: (inactive) is a suffix that denotes an item as inactive, lacking crystal shard charges. It is used exclusively for crystal equipment and the blade of Saeldor. This suffix is functionally similar to (uncharged).

label: (inert)
title: (inert)
lead: (inert) is a suffix used to denote an item is in an uncharged state.

label: (kg)
title: (kg)
lead: (kg) is a suffix used to differentiate the weight of an item in kilograms.

label: (kp)
title: (kp)
lead: (kp), for karambwan paste, is a suffix indicating a weapon has been poisoned with karambwan paste. It can only be applied to spears and hastae (excluding Zamorakian spears and Zamorakian hastae, as well as the Bone spear).

label: (l)
title: (l)
lead:
(l) is a suffix applied to untradeable equipment that has been locked using Trouver parchment and coins via Perdu. In a PvP death, unprotected items with this suffix are prevented from becoming (broken) in the case of level 20 and below Wilderness, or prevented from being converted to coins in the case of above level 20 Wilderness. In either case, the unprotected locked item is sent to the inventory and the locked status is removed. Protected items with this suffix retain the locked status upon PvP death, instead.

Exceptions are the Rune pouch (l) and Divine rune pouch (l), which will always lose the locked status upon PvP death. While the rune pouch is kept in the inventory, runes stored inside the previously locked rune pouch are still lost.

label: (lg)
title: (lg)
lead: (lg), for legs, is a suffix found on Grand Exchange item sets that denotes the particular set as containing platelegs, as opposed to plateskirts which are found in (sk) sets.

label: (light)
title: (light)
lead: (light) is a suffix that denotes that an item is part of the light mystic robes set.

label: (lit)
title: (lit)
lead: (lit) is a suffix applied to fire arrows that have been lit.

label: (m)
title: (m)
lead: (m) is a suffix used to denote an ale as mature, which means having a stronger effect than their non-mature counterparts. Ales contained in calquat kegs may also have the mature suffix, paired with a numerical value relating to the number of servings remaining. Glasses of mature cider and mature wizard mind bombs do not have this suffix, but the kegs do.

label: (master)
title: (master)
lead: (master) is a suffix that denotes items used during master Treasure Trails.

label: (medium)
title: (medium)
lead: (medium) is a suffix that denotes an item as medium. Used by Treasure Trails, Temple Trekking, and by antique lamps rewarded from Achievement Diaries.

label: (numerical)
title: (numerical)
lead: Numerical suffixes are often used to denote quantity or item tier. In terms of quantity, this could refer to the remaining charges of an item such as a black mask, or the remaining contents of a container e.g. the doses of a potion or calquat keg.

label: (nz)
title: (nz)
lead: (nz) is a suffix found on Nightmare Zone variants of items which are used exclusively within the minigame and cannot be taken outside it.

label: (o)
title: (o)
lead: (o) is a suffix used to identify offensive blackjacks.

label: (or)
title: (or)
lead:
(or) is a suffix used to denote certain ornamental equipment. The ornament kits used to create these items are obtainable from various content.

Some ornamental items do not have the (or) suffix in-game, such as the ornamented mystic steam staff. The ornament kits used for these items may be purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing.

label: (p)
title: (p)
lead:
(p) is a suffix indicating a weapon or type of ammunition is poisonous and has been coated in weapon poison.

All metal arrows (including amethyst), normal metal bolts, darts, and throwing knives can have weapon poison applied. Most daggers, spears and hastae may be poisoned as well.

label: (p+)
title: (p+)
lead:
(p+) is a suffix indicating a weapon or type of ammunition is poisonous and has been coated in weapon poison(+).

All metal arrows (including amethyst), normal metal bolts, darts, and throwing knives can have weapon poison(+) applied. Most daggers, spears and hastae may be poisoned as well.

label: (p++)
title: (p++)
lead:
(p++) is a suffix indicating a weapon or type of ammunition is poisonous and has been coated in weapon poison(++).

All metal arrows (including amethyst), normal metal bolts, darts, and throwing knives can have weapon poison(++) applied. Most daggers, spears and hastae may be poisoned as well.

label: (perfected)
title: (perfected)
lead: (perfected) is a suffix used exclusively in the Gauntlet, that denotes a piece of equipment as perfected.

label: (r)
title: (r)
lead:
(r) is an uncommon suffix that can be found on three items.

The (r) on the ring of suffering (r) and (ri) refer to their recoil effect given by charging them with rings of recoil.

label: (red)
title: (red)
lead: (red) is an uncommon suffix used to denote the colour red. Not to be confused with (r).

label: (sk)
title: (sk)
lead: (sk), for skirt, is a suffix found on Grand Exchange item sets that denotes the particular set as containing plateskirts, as opposed to platelegs which are found in (lg) sets.

label: (t)
title: (t)
lead: (t) is a suffix typically used to denote that a piece of armour or weapon is trimmed. These items or the ornament kits used to make them are only obtainable from Treasure Trails. (t) is also used for trimmed skillcapes for players who have achieved skill mastery in more than one skill. It can also appear on trimmed skillcapes that are displayed on cape hangers in a player-owned house Achievement Gallery

label: (tattered)
title: (tattered)
lead: (tattered) is a suffix used by exclusively by kq head (tattered) and stuffed kq head (tattered) to differentiate them from their regular counterparts, as the tattered head is a guaranteed drop from the Kalphite Queen on a player's 256th kill. They cannot be used to create green Slayer helmets.

label: (tier)
title: (tier)
lead: (tier) is a suffix that denotes an item is divided into tiers. This suffix is always accompanied by a numerical value.

label: (u)
title: (u)
lead: (u) is a suffix usually denoting an item as unstrung, with a few exceptions.

label: (uncharged)
title: (uncharged)
lead: (uncharged) is a suffix applied to degradable items that have run out of charges and must be charged again before they can be used with their full effects active; some (empty), (e), and (u) items act similarly to (uncharged) items.

label: (unf)
title: (unf)
lead: (unf), for unfinished or unfeathered, is a suffix applied to unfinished potions and bolts.

label: (w)
title: (w)
lead: (w) is a suffix used to denote that a tree seedling has been watered.

label: (wound)
title: (wound)
lead: (wound) is a suffix found on clockwork toys denoting that they have been wound and may be released.

label: 12 Days of Dragon Sleigher
title: 12 Days of Dragon Sleigher
lead:
12 Days of Dragon Sleigher was a festive dragon-themed clue-seeker event held in the run-up to the launch of Dragon Slayer II, where a clue was released each day on three separate social media channels starting on Christmas Day of 2017 up until the quest's launch on 4 January 2018. The event was announced in the It's Christmas Time update post, alongside the launch of the in-game Christmas event of that year.

Upon solving the riddle posted on one of these channels, the first player to perform the in-game actions hinted at would trigger a "Christmas loot explosion", causing holiday items to spawn in the nearby area for a period of 20 minutes, the total amount of which would scale based on the amount of players present at that time.

The following is a list of updates and events that happened in RuneScape in 1998.

*Andrew Gower and Paul Gower started development of DeviousMUD. This was the first version of RuneScape, this version was never released to the public. It had several rudimentary features that we have today, including Attack (the game may or may not have been PvP at that time), trade, and talk-to, all via a row of buttons at the bottom of the screen.

The following is a list of updates and events that happened in RuneScape in 1999.

*DeviousMUD (also known as MUD client), an early version of RuneScape, is completely rewritten by Andrew Gower and his brothers. Together they would be known as Jagex, standing for JAva Gaming EXperts.
*"Jagex" is first used as a trading name.
*RuneScape begins development.

label: 200 million experience
title: 200 million experience
lead:
200 million experience is the maximum amount of experience that a player can obtain in any one skill. This amount of experience represents a large time investment, with each skill taking hundreds or thousands of hours of efficient playing. At current rates, obtaining 200 million experience in all skills takes approximately 13,000 hours of playing at minimum, using the best methods available.

The first player to achieve 200 million experience in all skills was Lynx Titan on 28 December 2018, approximately six years after Old School RuneScape s release.

label: 2017 PvP Championship
title: 2017 PvP Championship
lead:
The 2017 PvP Championship was an offical Jagex hosted event streamed live on 12 August and 13 August 2017. It was an invitational PvP event made up of three separate brackets, competing for a total prize of $30,000 split across the three competitions.

The 1v1 bracket was made up of 32 players, the 5v5 bracket was made up of 16 teams of 5 players, and the 20v20 bracket was made up of 8 teams of 20 players, for a total of 272 players participating in the tournament. The competition used the ladder format, with the winner of each fight moving on and the loser being eliminated.

label: 3rd Age Druidic robes
title: 3rd Age Druidic robes
lead:
3rd age druidic robes are a set of 3rd age equipment. The robes require level 65 Prayer to wear. Players can obtain 3rd age druid robes equipment through master Treasure Trails; they cannot be bought in stores nor made through the Crafting skill.

Unlike its RuneScape 3 counterpart, the 3rd age druidic wreath does not exist in Old School RuneScape. This is due to the druidic wreath, a reward from midsummer events, already existing.

label: 3rd age equipment
title: 3rd age equipment
lead:
3rd age equipment are a group of members items obtained by completing the highest tiers of Treasure Trails (hard and above). There are four combat sets, plus an axe, a pickaxe, a ring and a cloak.

Lore-wise, they were presumably made during the Third Age of Gielinor. The examine texts reveal that the 3rd age melee armour is made from "magical silver", while the range armour is made from "white dragonhide".

label: 3rd Age mage robes
title: 3rd Age mage robes
lead:
3rd age mage robes are a set of 3rd age equipment, and are the third most powerful non-degradable Magic armour in-game. All 3rd age mage equipment requires level 65 Magic to use with the armour and level 30 Defence to wear. Players can obtain 3rd age mage equipment through the completion of hard, elite, and master tier Treasure Trails.

3rd age mage robes offer higher Magic bonuses compared to infinity and mystic robes but have lower bonuses than those of Ahrim's and ancestral robes. The Magic damage bonus of the 3rd age mage hat, top, and robe is 1% for a total of 3%.

label: 3rd age melee equipment
title: 3rd age melee equipment
lead:
3rd age melee equipment is a set of 3rd age equipment, often considered the rarest melee armour set in the game. 3rd age melee armour requires level 65 Defence to wear, whilst the 3rd age longsword requires 65 Attack to wield. Players can obtain 3rd age melee equipment through the completion of hard, elite and master tier Treasure Trails.

3rd age melee armour offers higher defence bonuses over Bandos armour while lacking the same Strength and Prayer bonuses, though it has lower defence bonuses compared to Justiciar armour. Some players wear 3rd age melee equipment as a display of wealth.

label: 3rd Age ranger kit
title: 3rd Age ranger kit
lead:
3rd age ranger kit is a set of 3rd age equipment, and is the fourth most powerful non-degradable Ranged armour in-game. All 3rd age range equipment requires level 65 Ranged to use with the armour also requiring level 45 Defence to wear. Players can obtain 3rd age range equipment through the completion of hard, elite, and master tier Treasure Trails.

3rd age range armour has similar bonuses to blessed dragonhide armour except with higher magic defence bonuses. It has lower overall bonuses compared to those of Karil's equipment, Armadyl armour and Masori armour whilst also being outdamaged by Elite Void Knight equipment.

50 Defence Build
title: 50 Defence Build
lead: A 50 Defence build or moon pure is an account build characterised by its defence level of 50, allowing them to equip powerful Moons equipment while still being a low enough combat level to attack weaker builds such as one-defence pures and berserkers, even in lower level wilderness. These builds are primarily used in no-honour PKing, but are also a strong option for Bounty Hunter or PvP worlds, where they can use the Eclipse set along with melee and Vengeance.

label: A scruffy note
title: A scruffy note
lead:
A scruffy note is a quest item used only in Plague City. It is obtained from Bravek after the player asks how to cure a hangover, but it is difficult to read.

The note is not required to learn how to make hangover cure and can be dropped at any time. Players may make a hangover cure even before obtaining the note.

label: A small key
title: A small key
lead:
A small key is a quest item used only in the Plague City quest. It is found by searching the barrel on the of the plague house where Elena is being held. The house can only be accessed while holding a warrant that is obtained from Bravek.

It is used to open Elena's cell in the basement of the plague house.

label: A stone bowl
title: A stone bowl
lead:
A stone bowl is a quest item used only in Elemental Workshop I. It is found by searching the boxes north-east of the hatch in the Elemental Workshop.

It is used to make a stone bowl filled with lava from a lava trough. The full stone bowl is then used on the furnace to heat it up.

id: page:a tail of two cats/quick guide
label: A Tail of Two Cats/Quick guide
title: A Tail of Two Cats/Quick guide

label: A used spell
title: A used spell
lead: A used spell is one of the results of using the druidic spell given to the player by Filliman Tarlock during the Nature Spirit quest. When the player uses the druidic spell to cast Bloom, it turns into a used spell. This item must later be used on the grey stone outside of the nature spirit's grotto to progress in the quest.

label: A wooden log
title: A wooden log
lead: A wooden log is an Agility shortcut found west of the Shipyard (Karamja) near a broken gnome glider.

label: A'abla
title: A'abla
lead: A'abla is a nurse, alongside Sabreen, in the Emir's Arena hospital. She heals the player for 20% of their total Hitpoints plus 2, but does not cure poison.

label: Aaron's Archery Appendages.
title: Aaron's Archery Appendages.
lead: Aaron's Archery Appendages is a shop where Aaron the Armour salesman sells low level ranged armour. Aaron also sells the Ranged Cape of Accomplishment. His shop is located in the Ranging Guild, so it can only be accessed by players with at least level 40 Ranged.

label: Abbot Langley
title: Abbot Langley
lead:
Abbot Langley is the head of the Edgeville Monastery in northern Asgarnia. He prevents players with less than 31 Prayer from entering the guild (this cannot be boosted in any way). He can restore 4 + 12% of the player's hitpoints if they are injured.

He can also attach a sigil to a blessed spirit shield for a fee of 1,500,000 coins, as well as remove sigils from them, though this destroys the blessed spirit shield; this is usually done to the arcane spirit shield in order to use the sigil to fortify Elidinis' ward.

label: Ablenkian
title: Ablenkian
lead:
Ablenkian was one of the Dragon riders, a group of beings with a unique talent for taming dragons. Ablenkian served along with his kin in the Zarosian Empire, known for Venator ranking, riding the dragon Hekala.

In the Battle of Carrallanger, he once saved Corveth, a fellow Zarosian, with Hekala as Corveth was being nearly consumed by flames.

label: Abyss (disambiguation)
title: Abyss (disambiguation)
lead: Abyss may refer to:

label: Abyss/Strategies
title: Abyss/Strategies
lead: The Abyss is a location that allows quick access to almost every Runic altar. Before entering the Abyss, players must complete the Enter the Abyss miniquest. Entry to the Abyss is granted by the Mage of Zamorak, who is located in low-level Wilderness north of Edgeville.

label: Abyssal dye
title: Abyssal dye
lead:
Abyssal dye is an item that can be used to recolour pieces of the Raiments of the Eye (excluding the boots), the amulet of the eye, and the lost bag. There are 3 types of abyssal dye:
* Abyssal blue dye
* Abyssal green dye
* Abyssal red dye

label: Abyssal head (disambiguation)
title: Abyssal head (disambiguation)
lead:
Abyssal head may refer to:
*Abyssal head
**Stuffed abyssal head
**Abyssal demon head (mounted)
*Ensouled abyssal head

label: Abyssal Sire/Strategies
title: Abyssal Sire/Strategies
lead:
The Abyssal Sire is a level 350 Slayer boss that can only be killed when assigned Abyssal demons or the Sire itself with the required Slayer level of 85.

It is mainly killed for its unsired drops, which can be used at the Font of Consumption to obtain valuable rewards such as the abyssal dagger, parts of the abyssal bludgeon, or the abyssal orphan pet.

label: Abyssal weapon
title: Abyssal weapon
lead:
Abyssal weapon may refer to:

*Abyssal bludgeon
*Abyssal dagger
*Abyssal whip/tentacle

label: Accept Aid
title: Accept Aid
lead:
Accept Aid is a button under the Settings menu that lets other players cast teleother and a variety of Lunar spells on the targeted player, among other interactions. While in a waiting room for Barbarian Assault, it allows players to receive recruitment requests. It is mostly only useful in members' worlds as there is no situation in which aid can be offered in free-to-play, with the exception of Christmas crackers.

Ironmen can't enable Accept Aid, but can still participate in some group activities such as Barbarian Assault. Group ironmen may engage in most interactions typically requiring the option to be enabled, but only with the members of their group.

label: account
title: account
lead:
, officially titled Account Security.]]
A player's account is their digital profile, which stores information and is represented in-game by the player character. Accounts are accessed by unique log-in credentials, with a password and either a login email or username, depending on when the account was created.

An account holds all the information on the player's in-game activities, including their skills and achievements, the items they possess, and the quests they have done. It also makes the player responsible for anything they have said via the game's chat interface, as well as any actions that breach Old School RuneScapes Code of Conduct.

label: account builds
title: account builds
lead: This article lists the major account builds.

label: Account Management
title: Account Management
lead: The account management tab shows information related to the player's account. It has three tabs: Account, Community and Links.

label: Accuracy
title: Accuracy
lead:
Accuracy may refer to:
*Amulet of accuracy, a reward from Imp Catcher.
*Attack, a skill that increases a player's accuracy with Melee weaponry as it increases.
*Weapon accuracy, the stats on a weapon that determines how likely players are to hit an enemy.
*Chance to hit, the formula that determines how likely players are to hit an enemy with Melee and Ranged.
*Magic accuracy, the formula for Magic that determines how likely players are to hit an enemy with spells.

label: Acheron
title: Acheron
lead:
Acheron is an inhospitably cold landmass somewhere north of the Fremennik Province and the islands of the Northern Ocean.

Freja the Kyattess mentions that the early Fremennik tribes used to trade with the inhabitants of Acheron. The Fremennik share stories of icy winds on Acheron that could freeze hearts to stone, it is described as a terribly vicious place where no living thing can survive.

id: category:locations that do not appear in-game
label: Locations that do not appear in-game
Achey Tree
title: Achey Tree
lead: Achey Trees are uncommon lumber trees that require level 1 Woodcutting to chop, providing 25 Woodcutting experience per set of achey tree logs received. Achey trees are near exclusively cut to obtain achey tree logs, for the purpose of creating Ogre arrows and Brutal arrows. These arrows are required in the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest and optional in the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest.

label: Achey tree logs
title: Achey tree logs
lead:
Achey logs are logs only available to members. They can be obtained at level 1 Woodcutting from Achey trees for 25 experience each. Players can burn these logs at level 1 Firemaking for 40 experience each.

These logs are needed for the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest to make ogre arrows, as well as composite ogre bows for Zogre Flesh Eaters.

label: Achey Tree stump
title: Achey Tree stump
lead: An Achey Tree stump appears when an Achey Tree is cut down. After a period of time between 35.4 - 58.8 seconds the tree will grow back.

label: Achietties
title: Achietties
lead:
Achietties is the guard and chancellor of the Heroes' Guild, between Burthorpe and Taverley, standing outside the guild's front door. She is the starting and finishing point of the Heroes' Quest. After the quest is complete, she allows players to enter the guild. She wears steel armour and a grey headband.

When spoken to outside of the guild, Achietties gives the player information about the Heroes' Quest, including the requirements. She later makes an appearance in Dragon Slayer II.

label: Achievement Diary
title: Achievement Diary
lead:
The Achievement Diaries are sets of challenges exclusive to members that are completed for various rewards and benefits. These diaries consist of 492 tasks across 12 regions in Gielinor, intended to test the player's skills and knowledge about Old School RuneScape.

The tasks of each diary are split into four tiers based on their perceived difficulty: easy, medium, hard, and elite. Easy tasks may simply involve browsing a shop or praying at an altar, whereas the most difficult tasks involve surviving the TzHaar Fight Cave and having completed all quests. The skill requirements for all tasks are also based on these tiers, with levels reaching up to 40 for easy tasks, 65 for medium tasks, 75 for hard tasks, and in the 90s for elite tasks (Ironmen may require even higher levels).

label: Achievement Diary/All achievements
title: Achievement Diary/All achievements
lead:
This page contains a list of all Achievements found in Old School RuneScape. For more details on a specific achievement, click the achievement's difficulty to be taken directly to its location in its respective diary.

If any achievements or requirements are missing, please add them in or report them on the Talk page.

label: Achievement Diary/Rewards
title: Achievement Diary/Rewards
lead: This page lists all Achievement Diary rewards for comparison.

label: Acid
title: Acid
lead:
Acid may refer to:

* Acetic acid
* Great Olm's acidic attacks
* Lizardman shamans' acid spit
* Sulphuric acid
* Vorkath's acid barrage

label: Acidic
title: Acidic
lead:
Acidic may refer to:
* Acidic Araxyte
* Acidic bloodveld
* Acidic miasma

label: Acquisition
title: Acquisition
lead:
Acquisition can refer to one of the following:

* Contract of catalyst acquisition
* Contract of worm acquisition
* Contract of shard acquisition
* Contract of oathplate acquisition
* Contract of harmony acquisition
* Contract of familiar acquisition

label: Activity Adviser
title: Activity Adviser
lead:
The Activity Adviser is an interface that recommends certain activities to players based on their current stats and quests progress. It currently only suggests quests to complete; skills, minigames, and other suggestions are expected to be added at a later date per July 2022's Gielinor Gazette.

The activity adviser's orb button appearance can be toggled in the settings.

label: adamant
title: adamant
lead: Adamant, or Adamantite may refer to:

label: Adamant 2h sword
title: Adamant 2h sword
lead:
The adamant 2h sword is a two-handed sword that requires 30 Attack to wield. As with other two-handed weapons, a shield may not be equipped while wielding one.

Players may smith one at level 84 Smithing with 3 adamantite bars for 187.5 Smithing experience.

id: category:items needed for an emote clue
label: Items needed for an emote clue
Adamant arrow
title: Adamant arrow
lead:
Adamant arrows are stronger than mithril arrows, and can be used by any standard bow of maple or stronger. They can be made at level 60 Fletching by using 15 adamant arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 150 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

They are the best arrows available to free-to-play players.

label: Adamant arrowtips
title: Adamant arrowtips
lead:
Adamant arrowtips are made with an adamant bar requiring 75 Smithing, yielding 62.5 Smithing experience and 15 adamant arrowtips. They are made into adamant arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 60 Fletching, yielding 150 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.

label: adamant axe
title: adamant axe
lead:
An adamant axe is a one-handed axe requiring 30 Attack to wield and 31 Woodcutting to use to cut trees. Making one requires 1 adamant bar and 71 Smithing, yielding 62.5 Smithing experience. As with all axes, it can be used to cut trees even when in the player's inventory.

The success rate for getting a set of logs is approximately 300% that of a bronze axe and 20% better than a mithril axe.

label: Adamant axe head
title: Adamant axe head
lead:
The adamant axe head is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while Woodcutting. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while Mining, but with a pickaxe head and pickaxe handle.

label: Adamant battleaxe
title: Adamant battleaxe
lead:
The adamant battleaxe is a battleaxe that is stronger than a mithril battleaxe, but weaker than a rune battleaxe. Like most adamant weapons, 30 Attack is required in order to wield it.

Players are able to obtain adamant battleaxes via trading with players, monster drops, or purchasing it at Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar (located in Port Sarim). It may also be a reward from a clue scroll. At level 80 Smithing, players can use 3 adamant bars to smith an adamant battleaxe, granting 187.5 experience.

label: Adamant chainbody
title: Adamant chainbody
lead: Adamant chainbody is piece of armour made from adamantite. A player can create an adamant chainbody by using an adamantite bar on an anvil while a hammer and 3 adamantite bars are in the player's inventory. A Smithing level of 81 is required to make an adamant chainbody and doing so will grant the player 187.5 Smithing experience. Level 30 Defence is required to wear an adamant chainbody. It can also be bought from Wayne's Chains in south Falador. One adamant chainbody is required for Song of the Elves.

label: Adamant claws
title: Adamant claws
lead: Adamant claws are a two-handed melee weapon. They can be made with two adamantite bars and a hammer at any anvil granting 125 Smithing experience. They can only be made by players who have completed the Death Plateau quest and have a Smithing level of at least 83. They have an Attack requirement of 30 to wield. They are not a very popular weapon due to the fact they require 2 hands to wield and provide inferior stats to that of the adamant scimitar.

label: Adamant dagger
title: Adamant dagger
lead: The adamant dagger is a dagger made of adamantite. It can be created by using one Adamant bar and a hammer on an anvil at level 70 Smithing, granting 62.5 Smithing experience. As with most daggers, it can be poisoned.

label: Adamant dart
title: Adamant dart
lead:
Adamant darts are Ranged throwing weapons. To wield the player must have at least 30 Ranged. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Adamant darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To make adamant darts, the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least 74 Smithing and 67 Fletching. Each adamant bar will create 10 adamant dart tips and the player will receive 62.5 Smithing experience. When feathers are added the player will receive 10 adamant darts and 15 Fletching experience per adamant dart.

label: Adamant dart tip
title: Adamant dart tip
lead:
Adamant dart tip is an item that can be created at level 74 Smithing. It grants 62.5 Smithing experience upon making and requires one adamantite bar to make 10 adamant dart tips. They can be fletched into adamant darts at level 67 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 150 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must complete the Tourist Trap quest.

label: Adamant dragon/Strategies
title: Adamant dragon/Strategies
lead: After completion of Dragon Slayer II, adamant dragons can be found and fought in the Lithkren Vault. As the second strongest metal dragons, caution should be exercised at all times.

label: Adamant equipment
title: Adamant equipment
lead: Adamant equipment are items made from adamantite metal. Adamant equipment is stronger than mithril equipment, but weaker than rune equipment. Adamant items are green-coloured and are slightly heavier than the same items made of other conventional metals. Adamant armour requires 30 Defence to wield, weapons generally require 30 Attack.

label: Adamant fire arrow
title: Adamant fire arrow
lead:
Adamant fire arrows are adamant arrows wrapped in an oily cloth, which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox. They, along with any other fire arrow, are primarily used to pierce the rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same Ranged Strength as regular adamant arrows.

label: Adamant full helm
title: Adamant full helm
lead: An adamant full helm is a full helmet made out of adamant. It can be worn with at least level 30 in Defence and can be smithed with at least level 77 Smithing using 2 adamantite bars (this grants 125 Smithing experience). These helms are stronger than mithril full helms but weaker than rune full helms.

label: Adamant full helm (g)
title: Adamant full helm (g)
lead: Adamant full helm (g) is a part of adamant gold-trimmed armour and a reward from medium Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Adamant full helm, and requires level 30 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

id: category:items storable in the costume room
label: Items storable in the costume room
Adamant full helm (t)
title: Adamant full helm (t)
lead: Adamant full helm (t) is a part of adamant trimmed armour and a reward from medium Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Adamant full helm, and requires level 30 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: adamant gold-trimmed armour
title: adamant gold-trimmed armour
lead: Adamant gold-trimmed armour is a possible reward from medium Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to adamant armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Adamant helm (disambiguation)
title: Adamant helm (disambiguation)
lead:
Adamant helm may refer to:
*Adamant helm (Shipbuilding)
*Adamant full helm
**Adamant full helm (t)
**Adamant full helm (g)
*Adamant med helm
*Adamant med helm (Mage Training Arena)

*Adamant heraldic helms (Treasure Trails)
**Adamant helm (h1)
**Adamant helm (h2)
**Adamant helm (h3)
**Adamant helm (h4)
**Adamant helm (h5)

label: Adamant heraldic armour
title: Adamant heraldic armour
lead: Adamant heraldic armour are pieces of the adamant armour set that have a heraldic design on them. The heraldic armour set consists of a helm, platebody and shield, which can be only obtained as a reward from medium Treasure Trails. The helms, platebodies and shields are equivalent, in stats, to the adamant full helm, the adamant platebody and adamant kiteshield respectively and requires a Defence level of 30 to equip.

label: Adamant javelin
title: Adamant javelin
lead:
The adamant javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching adamant javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 62 Fletching, granting 150 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.

label: Adamant kiteshield
title: Adamant kiteshield
lead: The Adamant kiteshield is the second-best smithable kiteshield, requiring 30 Defence to wield. A player with 82 Smithing can make the shield by using three adamantite bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 187.5 Smithing experience.

label: Adamant kiteshield (g)
title: Adamant kiteshield (g)
lead: Adamant kiteshield (g) is a part of adamant gold-trimmed armour and a reward from medium Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Adamant kiteshield, except for the ranged attack bonus (-2 rather than -3), and requires level 30 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Adamant kiteshield (t)
title: Adamant kiteshield (t)
lead: Adamant kiteshield (t) is a part of adamant trimmed armour and a reward from medium Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Adamant kiteshield, except for the ranged attack bonus (-2 rather than -3), and requires level 30 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Adamant knife
title: Adamant knife
lead:
The adamant knife is a throwing knife that requires a Ranged level of 30 to wield. It is stronger than a mithril knife but weaker than a rune knife. To create adamant knives, the player must have at least 77 Smithing. Each adamant bar will create 5 adamant knives and give the player 62.5 Smithing experience. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged.

label: Adamant longsword
title: Adamant longsword
lead: The adamant longsword is a longsword that is stronger than the Mithril longsword, but weaker than the Rune longsword. Like all other adamant weapons, it requires 30 Attack to wield. Players can make an adamant longsword with 76 Smithing using 2 adamantite bars, granting 125 experience. It can be bought from the Varrock Swordshop for 3,200 coins.

label: Adamant mace
title: Adamant mace
lead: An adamant mace is a mace that requires level 30 Attack to wield. Players can make an adamant mace with the Smithing skill at level 72 using 1 Adamant bar, giving 62.5 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this mace from Flynn's Mace Market in Falador or the weapons shop in the Warriors' Guild, and is also dropped by Twisted Banshees.

label: Adamant med helm
title: Adamant med helm
lead:
The adamant med helm is a medium helmet made of adamantite. This helm requires 30 Defence to wear. It provides more protection than its mithril counterpart. It can be made at level 73 Smithing using an adamantite bar, granting 62.5 experience.

Though the helmet provides a smaller Defence bonus than that of an adamant full helm, it has a lower penalty to Magic and Ranged attack. This means it is potentially more useful than the full helm to players who are training the Magic skill.

label: Adamant pick head
title: Adamant pick head
lead:
An adamant pick head was obtained as part of a discontinued random event, in which the adamant pickaxe head flew off the handle while the player was mining. To fix it, the player had to collect it off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

If players were not paying attention when this occurred, the head would disappear from the ground or be picked up by another player, requiring them to purchase another.

label: Adamant pickaxe
title: Adamant pickaxe
lead:
The adamant pickaxe is a pickaxe that is stronger than the mithril pickaxe, but weaker than the rune pickaxe. It requires an Attack level of 30 to wield, and a Mining level of 31 to mine with.

The adamant pickaxe mines on a 4-tick cycle, unlike other pickaxes. This allows it to be used for tick manipulation in various places, such as mining shooting stars.

label: Adamant platebody
title: Adamant platebody
lead:
The adamant platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between mithril and rune. It requires 30 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than an adamant chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 88 Smithing can make one by using 5 adamantite bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 312.5 experience.

label: Adamant platebody (g)
title: Adamant platebody (g)
lead: Adamant platebody (g) is a part of adamant gold-trimmed armour and a reward from medium Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Adamant platebody, and requires level 30 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Adamant platebody (t)
title: Adamant platebody (t)
lead: Adamant platebody (t) is a part of adamant trimmed armour and a reward from medium Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Adamant platebody, and requires level 30 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Adamant platelegs
title: Adamant platelegs
lead:
Adamant platelegs are platelegs made of Adamant and, as such, require a Defence level of 30 to wear. These platelegs have the same stats as the Adamant plateskirt, but are 1kg heavier.

Adamant platelegs can be smithed using 3 adamant bars at level 86 Smithing, granting 187.5 experience.

label: Adamant platelegs (g)
title: Adamant platelegs (g)
lead: Adamant platelegs (g) is a part of adamant gold-trimmed armour and a reward from medium Treasure Trails. They have the same stats as regular Adamant platelegs, and require level 30 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Adamant platelegs (t)
title: Adamant platelegs (t)
lead: Adamant platelegs (t) is a part of adamant trimmed armour and a reward from medium Treasure Trails. They have the same stats as regular Adamant platelegs, and require level 30 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Adamant plateskirt
title: Adamant plateskirt
lead:
The Adamant plateskirt is a plateskirt made out of adamant. At least 30 Defence is required to wear it. The plateskirt has the same stats as the Adamant platelegs, but are 1kg lighter.

They can be made at level 86 Smithing using 3 adamantite bars, which grants 187.5 experience.

label: Adamant pure (free-to-play)
title: Adamant pure (free-to-play)
lead:
An adamant pure is a type of medium level free-to-play combat pure account with the Defence skill trained up to 30 level.

At 30 Defence level, adamant pures have access to the adamant armour, as well as the gold decorative boots that are necessary to achieve the highest maximum hits with all free-to-play melee weapons across all Strength and Prayer levels. In fact, 30 is the lowest Defence level that allows to maximize damage with all combat styles in the free-to-play worlds.

label: Adamant scimitar
title: Adamant scimitar
lead:
The adamant scimitar is the fourth strongest scimitar in the game, behind rune, gilded and dragon. Like most adamant weapons, it requires to wield.

Players can make it with using two adamantite bars, earning 125 experience. The scimitar can also be obtained from killing monsters, and is a reward from the quest The Feud.

label: Adamant shield
title: Adamant shield
lead:
Adamant shield may refer to:
*Adamant kiteshield
**Adamant kiteshield (t)
**Adamant kiteshield (g)
*Adamant kiteshield (Mage Training Arena)
*Adamant sq shield

*Adamant heraldic shields (Treasure Trails)
**Adamant shield (h1)
**Adamant shield (h2)
**Adamant shield (h3)
**Adamant shield (h4)
**Adamant shield (h5)

label: Adamant spear
title: Adamant spear
lead: The adamant spear is a two-handed members'-only melee weapon requiring 30 Attack to wield. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create adamant spears with level 75 Smithing This requires 1 adamantite bar and 1 yew log. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the adamant spear can be poisoned. Smithing an adamant spear at the anvil at Otto's Grotto is a requirement for the Kandarin Hard Diary.

label: Adamant sq shield
title: Adamant sq shield
lead: Adamant square shields are the third-strongest square shields, requiring 30 Defence to wield. A player with level 78 Smithing can make the shield by using two adamant bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 125 Smithing experience.

label: Adamant sword
title: Adamant sword
lead:
The adamant sword is the second-strongest sword available to free players, after the rune sword. As with most adamant weapons, level 30 Attack is required to wield it.

Adamant swords can be created at level 74 Smithing. One adamant bar is required to make the sword, and 62.5 Smithing experience is rewarded per sword created.

label: Adamant thrownaxe
title: Adamant thrownaxe
lead: The adamant thrownaxe is the third strongest type of throwing axe, requiring level 30 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by buying them from the Tribal Weapon Salesman in the Ranging Guild.

label: Adamant trimmed armour
title: Adamant trimmed armour
lead: Adamant trimmed armour is a possible reward from medium Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to adamant armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Adamant trophy
title: Adamant trophy
lead:
Adamant trophy may refer to:

* Twisted adamant trophy
* Trailblazer adamant trophy
* Shattered relics adamant trophy
* Trailblazer reloaded adamant trophy
* Raging echoes adamant trophy

label: Adamant warhammer
title: Adamant warhammer
lead:
The adamant warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the mithril warhammer. Unlike other adamant weapons, it requires 30 Strength to wield. They are the fourth-strongest warhammers for all players. Players can make them using the Smithing skill at level 79 using 3 adamantite bars, giving the player 187.5 Smithing experience.

The adamant warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon.

label: Adamantite bar
title: Adamantite bar
lead: Adamantite bars can be smelted with 6 coal and 1 adamantite ore at level 70 Smithing. Smelting the bar grants 37.5 Smithing experience, and any item that is smithed from adamantite bars grants 62.5 Smithing experience per bar, yielding a net of 100 experience.

label: adamantite ore
title: adamantite ore
lead:
Adamantite ore can be mined at level 70 Mining providing 95 Mining experience. After adamantite rocks are mined, it will take four minutes until it reappears. Adamantite ore is used with six coal to smelt adamantite bars. Smelting an adamantite bar gives 37.5 Smithing experience.

Wearing either superior mining gloves or expert mining gloves while mining an adamantite rock makes the rock not deplete upon mining adamantite, allowing you to mine one or two additional ore, respectively, before depleting.

label: adamantite rocks
title: adamantite rocks
lead:
Adamantite rocks are a rock containing adamantite. A player with a Mining level of 70 or higher can mine adamantite ore from adamantite rocks. Each rock grants 95 Mining experience for each ore mined. After being mined, an adamantite rock takes 4 minutes to respawn, or two minutes within the Mining Guild. Players may want to employ a world switch tactic due to the scarcity of available ore.

Wearing superior mining gloves or expert mining gloves makes the rock not deplete upon mining adamantite, allowing you to mine one (with superior gloves) or two (with expert gloves) additional ore before depleting.

label: Address label
title: Address label
lead:
The address label is an item used during Tribal Totem. Players can obtain it by searching the double-stacked crates south-east of the southernmost bank in East Ardougne in the GPDT Depot.

The player must then use the label on the teleport block created by Wizard Cromperty so that it is delivered to Lord Handelmort's Mansion, after which the player can teleport into his house to continue the quest.

label: Admiral Bake
title: Admiral Bake
lead:
Admiral Bake was a famous gnome explorer from the Fourth Age. He was best known for presenting the tortoise Mibbiwocket to King Healthorg the Great shortly after its birth. This tortoise would go on to become the world's oldest tortoise.

Admiral Bake is the correct answer to the Natural history quiz question: "Name the explorer who discovered the world's oldest tortoise."

label: Advanced arena (interface item)
title: Advanced arena (interface item)
lead:
The Advanced arena is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Advanced arena.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Adventure
title: Adventure
lead:
Adventure is a music track that can be unlocked inside Varrock city walls, excluding the Grand Exchange. It also plays in the Phoenix Gang Hideout and in the basement of the Blue Moon Inn. Within this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Garden, Medieval, and Spirit.

In Classic mode, this track plays in Varrock Palace.

label: Adventure Paths
title: Adventure Paths
lead:
Adventure Paths are a task system intended to help new players get on their feet by completing tasks for various low level rewards. Players will only be eligible for Adventure Paths if they've told the Gielinor Guide at the very beginning of Tutorial Island that they are either a new player or are a player that has played in the past, but not recently. In addition, players who choose to play Ironman Mode are not eligible.

The task system currently has two paths available at the same time: the Combat Path, with a total of 15 tasks, and the Gatherer Path, with three tasks (one per skill).

label: Adventurer (disambiguation)
title: Adventurer (disambiguation)
lead: Adventurer may refer to:

label: Adventurer's outfit
title: Adventurer's outfit
lead:
The adventurer's outfit is a cosmetic set of clothing earned from Quest Speedrunning. It consists of a hood, top, trousers, and boots.

The outfit comes in three tiers, each purchased from the Speedrunning Reward Shop using reward points:
* Tier 1 - 200 points
* Tier 2 - 600 points
* Tier 3 - 1,800 points

label: Adventurer's outfit (tier 1)
title: Adventurer's outfit (tier 1)
lead:
The adventurer's outfit (tier 1) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing Quest Speedrunning. It can be purchased for 200 Speedrun Points from the Speedrunning Reward Shop.

The set can be stored in an armour case in a player-owned house.

label: Adventurer's outfit (tier 2)
title: Adventurer's outfit (tier 2)
lead:
The adventurer's outfit (tier 2) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing Quest Speedrunning. It can be purchased for 600 Speedrun Points from the Speedrunning Reward Shop.

The set can be stored in an armour case in a player-owned house.

label: Adventurer's outfit (tier 3)
title: Adventurer's outfit (tier 3)
lead:
The adventurer's outfit (tier 3) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing Quest Speedrunning. It can be purchased for 1,800 Speedrun Points from the Speedrunning Reward Shop. After purchasing the set once, you can claim unlimited sets from the Speedrunning Reward Shop. Each piece of the outfit can be used on a piece of the graceful outfit to change its appearance, removing any existing recolour. Osten in Shayzien can revert your Adventurer's Graceful back to the default appearance for free.

The set can be stored in an armour case in a player-owned house.

label: Adventurers' Camp (Lumbridge Swamp)
title: Adventurers' Camp (Lumbridge Swamp)
lead: The Adventurers' Camp (Lumbridge Swamp) is a small camp located at the threshold between the forest and the swamp between Draynor Village and Lumbridge and north of Father Urhney's house. It has a monk, wizard, archer, and warrior. The monk, wizard, and archer will not talk to the player much, but talking to the warrior will clumsily reveal their intentions to find Zanaris and start the Lost City quest.

label: Adwr Cadarn
title: Adwr Cadarn
lead:
Adwr Cadarn was an elven scout from the Cadarn clan. In the late Fourth Age, he and four other scouts were sent to Tirannwn to uncover the reason for losing contact with the elves there and the gates built to block the Arandar Pass.

The five scouts travelled through the Well of Voyage in the Underground Pass and witnessed the chaos from the siege of Prifddinas. Only Adwr managed to return, and, with tears in his eyes, he gave King Baxtorian and his emergency council the news of clan Iorwerth's betrayal and takeover of the Tower of Voices.

label: Aemad
title: Aemad
lead:
Aemad runs Aemad's Adventuring Supplies. together with Kortan in East Ardougne. His store can be found south of the church and north of the Ardougne Zoo.

His store acts like a general store, even though it sells some unique items, like papyrus and cooked meat, but it does not sell common staples seen in other stores such as bowls.

label: Aemad's Adventuring Supplies.
title: Aemad's Adventuring Supplies.
lead:
Aemad's Adventuring Supplies is a general store in East Ardougne. The store is run by its owner, Aemad, and his assistant, Kortan. Although it does not sell the default items of a typical general store, it sells several items used in quests around RuneScape, notably rope.

Two nearby banks (Ardougne north bank and Ardougne south bank) make this general store useful for buying and banking vials of water. The Ardougne Market is also nearby, making this store handy for selling items stolen from stalls.

label: Aenwyn Iorwerth
title: Aenwyn Iorwerth
lead: Lady Aenwyn Iorwerth was a former leader of the Iorwerth Clan on the elves' homeworld Tarddiad. Aenwyn was leader around the time, where the elves left Tarddiad for Gielinor after they and their goddess Seren were invited to the world by Guthix. Aenwyn was reluctant to leave and in the end decided to stay, however she did not want her clan to remain with her and told Seren to take them with her. Seren respected Aenwyn's choice and her leadership and let her remain, while she guided the rest of Aenwyn's clan with her to Gielinor. Her fate is unknown, but it is assumed she is deceased.

label: Aerial fishing
title: Aerial fishing
lead:
Aerial fishing is a hybrid Fishing and Hunter technique requiring 35 Hunter and 43 Fishing. The aerial fishing technique is used to catch several fish species at Lake Molch.

Hunters can get a cormorant's glove and a cormorant, free of charge, from the fishing expert Alry the Angler at Lake Molch. Both hands must be free for aerial fishing, which means no items may be carried in the weapon, shield, or hands slots. It is possible to use skill boosts to receive a cormorant's glove, which will allow players to catch bluegill even if their level(s) drain back to normal.

label: Afrah
title: Afrah
lead: Afrah is one of the people observing the fights at the Emir's Arena. She can be found at the south-easternmost corner of the walls.

label: Age
title: Age
lead: Age may refer to:

label: Age of Strife
title: Age of Strife
lead:
The Age of Strife was the period in which the kingdom of Great Kourend was ruled over by the mage Xeric, starting only a few days after the death of King Shayzien VII during the Battle of the Concourse late in the 37th decade (1,040 years ago), and lasting for a hundred years in Kourend's timeline, when Xeric was dethroned as a result of Byrne's Revolt in the 47th decade. After killing the rulers of the five cities, Xeric used both the powers of the Dark Altar and his army of lizardmen in order to consolidate his position and exert dominance of the kingdom, marking the beginning of what would be called the Age of Strife.

Xeric's reign left a deep mark on the cultural memory of Kourend, and is recounted as a notoriously brutal one by the citizens of Kourend to the present day, characterised by its authoritarian control over the populace and arbitrary acts of violence. A compilation of testimonies that together bear witness to the Age of Strife can be read in the Chronicles of Xeric.

label: Aggie
title: Aggie
lead:
Aggie is a witch that resides in Draynor Village. She sells dyes if the player provides her with the ingredients. Players can use ingredients directly on Aggie to save going through three parts of dialogue.

If the player insults her, she will take either 5 or 20 coins from them (depending on how many coins are in their inventory). Should the player not have coins, but instead a pot of flour, she will take that instead.

label: Aggressiveness
title: Aggressiveness
lead:
Aggressiveness (or hostility) refers to whether monsters will attack nearby players without being provoked. Aggressive monsters may attack players without being attacked first; some are aggressive based on players' combat levels, and others are aggressive regardless of level such as various bosses and most monsters in the Wilderness. Aggressive monsters can be particularly dangerous in a multi-combat area with multiple monsters. Non-aggressive, or passive, monsters will not attack players unless they are attacked first.

Some monsters, such as chompies and jubblies, will not attack a player even if engaged in combat. Yet, others, most notably dark beasts and bosses, remain hostile no matter how long the player remains in the vicinity.

label: Agility
title: Agility
lead:
Agility is a members-only skill which gives access to various shortcuts around Gielinor. Other benefits of the skill include faster run energy restoration, slower run energy dissipation while running, and the ability to wear weight-saving outfits like the graceful outfit, as well as wield certain tools and weaponry. Note that the passive benefits of faster energy restore and lower run energy drain rate also apply in free-to-play worlds.

label: Agility arena ticket (discontinued)
title: Agility arena ticket (discontinued)
lead:
Agility arena tickets were earned from tagging ticket dispensers within the Brimhaven Agility Arena minigame. Each ticket was rewarded after tagging more than one dispenser in a row. Tickets could then be redeemed for Agility experience and rewards from the Brimhaven Agility Arena Ticket Exchange run by Pirate Jackie the Fruit.

Exchanging larger amounts of tickets for Agility experience offered experience bonuses, up to 33% more per ticket. Wearing Karamja Gloves 2 or higher from completing the medium Karamja Diary when exchanging tickets rewarded 10% more total experience. Completing the elite Karamja Diary rewarded a 10% chance of receiving double tickets when tagging a pillar. The experience rewards increased by 5 per ticket for each Agility level above 40.

label: Agility Level Up!
title: Agility Level Up!
lead: Agility Level Up! is a jingle for levelling Agility.

label: Agility potion
title: Agility potion
lead:
Agility potions are made by mixing toadflax into a vial of water, creating a Toadflax potion (unf), and then adding toad's legs. This requires level 34 Herblore, and grants 80 Herblore experience. Agility potions temporarily raise your Agility by 3.

A 4-dose agility potion is required for Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. Ironmen who want to complete the quest but do not have the Herblore requirement can have an irit leaf cleaned by Zahur in Nardah (for 200 coins), then wait for the Dr Jekyll random event, for which he will trade the irit leaf for a 4-dose agility potion. Alternatively, level 40, 63, 72, and 77 skeletons in Tarn's Lair as well as the level 77 skeletons nearby the entrance to the Ruins of Ullek can drop 2-dose agility potions, which can be decanted into a 4-dose potion.

id: category:items storable in the potion storage
label: Items storable in the potion storage
Agility training
title: Agility training
lead:
Agility training involves a lot of point-clicking and some methods may require a lot of focus to maximise experience gain. Higher Agility level increases one's ability to regenerate run energy and grants access to various shortcuts.

For the fastest rates, players should always run and use stamina potions (or some other form of run energy restoration) to maintain run energy if needed. Keeping weight at 0 or below is helpful, but not necessary. It is recommended to boost the Agility level by using summer pies or agility potions to train on a higher-level course earlier than it is available. Players who are failing obstacles very frequently or have low Hitpoints are advised to bring some food to restore health.

label: Agility/Experience table
title: Agility/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Agility in the game, as well as all interactions that require an Agility level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: Ah Za Rhoon
title: Ah Za Rhoon
lead: Ah Za Rhoon, which means Magnificence Floating on Water in an ancient language, was an ancient temple in Karamja that was built by Zadimus and destroyed by Rashiliyia. After being lost for many years, the temple became a legend, making many doubt its existence. This temple is visited during the Shilo Village quest.

label: Ahmek
title: Ahmek
lead: Ahmek was a ruthless warrior who lived during the Second Age. He crafted the Lightbearer, a powerful ring imbued with unstable energy left behind from Tumeken's sacrifice during the Kharidian–Zarosian War. Ahmek hoped to use this ring to forcibly unite the assorted bands of thieves and mercenaries under his command – and to overthrow Osmumten. On the very night he created it, he was murdered in his sleep and the ring stolen. Soon after, this dreaded item was snatched from the body of a thief by some Menaphite Guards, who presented it to Osmumten.

label: Ahrim the Blighted's equipment
title: Ahrim the Blighted's equipment
lead:
Ahrim the Blighted's equipment is obtainable from the Barrows minigame. A full set consists of Ahrim's robetop, robeskirt, hood, and staff. The set requires 70 Magic and 70 Defence to wear, and 70 Attack to use the staff. Ahrim's robes give Melee Defence bonuses that Magic robes normally don't have, which makes it somewhat popular for PvP situations. The staff is able to autocast spells from the standard spellbook, Arceuus spellbook or from the Ancient Magicks spellbook when a full set is equipped with an Amulet of the damned. The staff is commonly used when facing elemental weaknesses as it allows the use of elemental tomes and is the most accessible one-handed staff with magic damage before the Dragon hunter wand and Purging staff. In such scenarios the set effect specific to the Amulet of the damned can be particularly useful. It can however be in competition with the Elite Void Knight equipment when not using Chaos gauntlets or Tormented bracelet and does not allow the use of a Slayer helmet (i). The equipment degrades over a period of 15 hours of combat, similar to other Barrows equipment.

Ahrim's set offers some of the best Magic bonuses available and is normally recommended for fighting various high level monsters. It is one of the few sets of magical robes that give Defence bonuses against things other than Magic. This is further reinforced by the fact that the robes look like a combination of chainmail and robes. Like chainmail, it is strong against crush attacks; however, more like dragonhide, it is weak to slash and strong against stab. Ahrim's armour provides no Ranged protection. It is also noticeably heavier than other Magic armour; the full set weighs approximately 19 kg, with the top and bottom alone weighing 4.5 and 11.3. This makes it less practical for activities where lots of running is required, such as Chambers of Xeric.

label: Air
title: Air
lead:
Air may refer to:

*The fairy ring code AIR pointing to an island south-east of Ardougne.

label: Air Altar
title: Air Altar
lead:
The Air Altar is a runic altar upon which air runes are crafted from rune essence or pure essence, providing 5 Runecraft experience per essence imbued.

Players may create an air tiara here by using either an air talisman or tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 25 Runecraft experience. An elemental tiara can also be created here by using an elemental talisman and gold tiara, granting 40 Runecraft experience.

label: Air battlestaff
title: Air battlestaff
lead:
The air battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of air runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 66 Crafting by combining an air orb and battlestaff. It can also be upgraded to a mystic air staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries). The mystic air staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.

label: Air elemental
title: Air elemental
lead:
Air elementals are encountered during the Elemental Workshop I quest. It should be noted that players do not actually have to kill any air elementals to complete Elemental Workshop I.

Killing one is a requirement for an Easy Kandarin Diary task.

label: Air orb
title: Air orb
lead:
An air orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Air by using the Charge Air Orb spell, requiring 66 Magic, on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb, 30 air runes, and 3 cosmic runes, yielding 76 Magic experience. The Air Obelisk is located in level 7 Wilderness, north of Edgeville. To get there, climb the ladder north of the black demons in Edgeville Dungeon.

An air orb can be used on a battlestaff, requiring 66 Crafting, yielding an air battlestaff and 137.5 Crafting experience. Charging air orbs is also a hard Wilderness Diary task.

label: Air rune
title: Air rune
lead:
Air runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used in every combat spell and most teleportation spells in the standard spellbook, as well as in many spells from other spellbooks. Because they are used very often, players are recommended to purchase an item that can provide infinite air runes while equipped, such as a staff of air.

A common way for beginning players to obtain air runes is to talk to the magic tutor in Lumbridge. She will give you 30 air and mind runes if you don't have any in your inventory or bank. Air runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops, such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. Non-ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.

label: Air talisman
title: Air talisman
lead:
The air talisman is a talisman that allows players to enter the Air Altar. At the altar, the player can use the Runecraft skill to turn rune essence or pure essence into air runes.

Also at the Air Altar, an air talisman can be combined with a silver tiara to make an air tiara for 25 Runecraft experience by using the tiara on the altar while having an air talisman in the inventory. This consumes the talisman, but the air tiara can be used the same as an air talisman and can be worn, opening an inventory slot to carry another essence.

label: Akhem
title: Akhem
lead: Akhem was a Menaphite, who lived during the Third Age. They were supposedly at Ullek, when a Zamorakian invasion was approaching the city. Sethos hid a chest containing Scabaras artefacts, leaving a stone tablet for Akhem to recover the chest in case the invasion happened.

label: Al Kharid
title: Al Kharid
lead:
Al Kharid is a city in the north of the Kharidian Desert. It is the only desert city open to non-members, and players in the city do not suffer from the desert effect. Al Kharid is ruled by the Emir, although the vast majority of the work has been taken over by Chancellor Hassan since the Emir's son was kidnapped.

Al Kharid contains one of the closest banks to a range as well as two reasonably close fishing spots. It also houses a tanner, Ellis. In free-to-play, Al Kharid's furnace is the second-closest to a bank, after Edgeville's furnace.

label: Al Kharid (music track)
title: Al Kharid (music track)
lead:
Al Kharid is a music track that is unlocked in Al Kharid, at the Al Kharid mine and the Giants' Plateau. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing this track, Arabian, and Arabian 2.

In Classic mode, the track plays in Al Kharid, and the west of the Giants' Plateau.

label: Al Kharid bank
title: Al Kharid bank
lead:
The Al Kharid bank is a bank in western Al Kharid, immediately west of the Al Kharid Palace. The bank is frequently used by free-to-play players while tanning hides or trading. It was added to RuneScape alongside the Catherby bank.

While the bank has no upper level, the roof of the bank is part of the Al Kharid rooftop Agility course.

label: Al Kharid General Store
title: Al Kharid General Store
lead:
The Al Kharid General Store is a general store located in the desert town of Al Kharid.

It mainly stocks the normal general store items. However, many players train their Crafting nearby, because of the crafting store and Tanner that are also in Al Kharid, which often leads to great amounts of leather items, most often hardleather bodies, in the player stock of the store. Silk cannot be sold to this general store.

label: Al Kharid Mine
title: Al Kharid Mine
lead:
The Al Kharid mine (also called Scorpion mine) is a Mining area located just north of the desert city of Al Kharid.

The mine is advantageous because it is near a bank and a furnace and is located in a very low-risk location for its high-value infrequent rocks, such as gold, mithril, and adamantite. In addition, this mine is one of many where three iron rocks can be mined without moving, thus ideal for power-mining.

label: Al Kharid Palace
title: Al Kharid Palace
lead:
The Al Kharid Palace is the southernmost and largest building in the city of Al Kharid, and it is the residence of the Emir and the seat of government for the emirate of Al Kharid. Hassan, the Emir's chancellor, is present in the palace's throne room and features in the Prince Ali Rescue quest. Osman, the emirate's spymaster, is found wandering outside the palace. Members can use an amulet of glory to teleport inside the palace, on the in the southern room.

The palace is primarily important in Prince Ali Rescue. There are several guards that spawn within the palace in the multicombat area, and they can be attacked or pickpocketed, but when one guard is attacked, the others will attempt to attack you as well.

label: Al Kharid warrior
title: Al Kharid warrior
lead:
Al Kharid warriors are guards of Al Kharid found in the palace. When one warrior is attacked, the others will attempt to attack you as well. For Free-to-play and low level players, they are a great place to train Attack, Strength, and Defence, as Al Kharid warriors have high Hitpoints but a low combat level.

Level 25 Thieving is required to pickpocket these warriors. It is very easy to trap an Al Kharid warrior between objects such as beds or tables, immobilising him.

label: Al Kharid–Menaphos War
title: Al Kharid–Menaphos War
lead:
The Al Kharid–Menaphos War was a series of conflicts between the emirate of Al Kharid, located at the northern fringes of the Kharidian Desert, and the great city Menaphos in the far south. Little is known about the war, but it lasted a long time according to Al Kharid's spymaster, Osman.

Currently, a strained peace exists between the two cities.

label: Al Shabim
title: Al Shabim
lead:
Al Shabim is the enigmatic leader of the Bedabin Nomads, a tribe of wandering nomadic people who settle down in different areas when they have exhausted the natural resources around their current camp. Shabim can be found in the larger of their two tents in their camp, south of the oasis.

He is involved with The Tourist Trap quest, in which the players must make a bargain with him to obtain a Tenti pineapple, which are prized by many people in the desert for their succulency. For the pineapple, Al Shabim asks you to steal weapon plans from the Desert Mining Camp, which turn out to be plans to make a deadly throwing dart. He asks you to make a prototype and gives you permission to use the anvils in the north tent of their camp, after which he will give you the pineapple needed for the quest.

label: Al Zaba Bhasim
title: Al Zaba Bhasim
lead:
Al Zaba Bhasim is, according to the Desert Mining Camp mercenaries and their captain, the leader of the notorious desert bandits, although it is unknown which group of desert bandits this refers to. He is described as a nomadic and slippery desert dweller, frequently found at Bedabin Camp. The mercenary captain has been unsuccessfully trying to capture him for years.

The leader of the Bedabin peoples, Al Shabim, claims that Al Zaba Bhasim does not exist, which could be the reason why he has not been captured. Interestingly, Bhasim is an anagram of Shabim.

label: Alan
title: Alan
lead:
Alan may refer to these NPCs:
* Alan (2022 Pride event)
* Alan (Farming Guild)
* Alan (Seers' Village)
* Alan (Scrambled!)

label: Alan Walker
title: Alan Walker
lead: Alan Walker is a Norwegian DJ, record producer and Old School RuneScape player. He collaborated with the Jagex Audio Team to create music for the Sailing skill, including tracks like Scape Sail and Sailing (soundtrack), the latter of which released alongside a music video on his YouTube Channel on 14 November, 2025. The collaboration was sparked after Walker's performance of a Sea Shanty 2 cover at Tomorrowland 2025 that led to communications with the Old School RuneScape team. He later appeared as a guest on OSRS Podcast, Episode 3 (Video link). During his visit to Jagex's headquarters in Cambridge, he described the opportunity to contribute music to the game as a "dream come true."

label: Alchemical chart (interface item)
title: Alchemical chart (interface item)
lead:
The Alchemical chart is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Alchemical chart.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Alchemical Hydra/Strategies
title: Alchemical Hydra/Strategies
lead:
The Alchemical Hydra is a level 95 Slayer boss encountered in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. In order to fight it, players must be assigned a Hydra task.

To reach the boss, players must run north past the Tasakaal, then east past the Hydras. They will then reach the entrance to the lair by Orrvor quo Maten. Alternatively, players with level 88 Agility can reach it safely by using the mysterious pipe just behind Kaal-Ket-Jor.
