**Glorious arena

label: Arena Guard
title: Arena Guard
lead:
Arena Guards are NPCs found throughout the Emir's Arena. It may refer to:
* Arena Guard Beni
* Arena Guard Drakno
* Arena Guard Fawry
* Arena Guard Fronk
* Arena Guard Joby
* Arena Guard Nikkolas
* Arena Guard Rachi
* Arena Guard Yon

label: Arengeesus
title: Arengeesus
lead:
Arengeesus was the Goddess of Luck. Very little was known about the god; her only known follower, Charlie Brown, believed the worship of Arengeesus would grant luck.

As Charlie Brown was removed, Arengeesus is no longer considered canon in Old School RuneScape.

label: Arhein
title: Arhein
lead:
Arhein runs Arhein's General Goods in Catherby, on a pier just south of the bank, near the charter ship. During Current Affairs he attempts to speed up the docking process at Catherby dock with the help of his duck. He also plays a small part in the Merlin's Crystal and the One Small Favour quests.

Arhein owns a ship on the pier, which he uses to deliver candles to Keep Le Faye, a fortress to the south. He does not allow players to ride his ship, although it is possible to sneak aboard it to get to Keep Le Faye by hiding in a crate near the candle shop in Catherby, which is used by the player during Merlin's Crystal.

label: Arhein's General Goods
title: Arhein's General Goods
lead: Arhein's General Goods is a general store in Catherby. It is run by Arhein and is also known as the Catherby General Store.

label: Aris
title: Aris
lead:
Aris Maye is a fortune-teller who resides in a large tent outside Varrock town square.

She is notable for being the start point of the Demon Slayer quest, in addition to being largely featured in Recipe for Disaster.

label: Arkan
title: Arkan
lead:
Arkan is the family name of the Arkan Dynasty of Varlamore.

Arkan may also refer to:

label: Arkney
title: Arkney
lead: Arkney was a settlement from the Fourth Age and hometown of the hero Robert the Strong. Nothing else is known about it, and it presumably no longer exists or goes by a different name. Arkney is only named as part of the riddle on the tomb of Camorra.

label: Armacus
title: Armacus
lead: Armacus is a Guardian of Armadyl. He explains the duty of guarding the Staff of Armadyl, as well as the Incorporealist and Corporealist factions of Armadyleans.

label: Armadyl
title: Armadyl
lead:
Armadyl (Jagex pronunciation: ARM-uh-dill) is the god of justice and law and one of the lesser known gods. His beliefs are very close to those of Saradomin, and so he is usually assumed to be a benevolent deity.

It is rumoured that Armadyl ruled the skies of Gielinor, and possibly parts of Kandarin, during the Second Age. During the God Wars, he ruled from the Empyrean Citadel. After the God Wars, he lost almost all of his influence and followers, and today is almost forgotten, but there are still many items dedicated to him that can be found.

label: Armadyl armour
title: Armadyl armour
lead:
Armadyl armour is a set of armour consisting of the Armadyl helmet, the Armadyl chestplate, the Armadyl chainskirt.

It is dropped by General Kree'arra and his three minions, (Wingman Skree, Flockleader Geerin, and Flight Kilisa) in the God Wars Dungeon. The pieces require 70 Ranged and 70 Defence to wear, and are considered the second best defensive ranged armour in-game, behind fortified masori armour.

label: Armadyl blessed dragonhide armour
title: Armadyl blessed dragonhide armour
lead:
The Armadyl blessed d'hide armour is a set of Ranged armour said to be blessed by Armadyl. Every piece requires 70 Ranged and 40 Defence, except for the blessed chaps and blessed bracers, which do not have the Defence requirement. Blessed dragonhide has better defensive stats and the same offensive stats as the corresponding black dragonhide armour with an additional +1 Prayer bonus. Unlike normal dragonhide armour, a coif and boots are also available. Each piece of armour may be obtained as a reward from hard Treasure Trails.

Wearing any piece of Armadyl blessed d'hide armour will make the Armadyl followers unaggressive within the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon.

label: Armadyl page
title: Armadyl page
lead: Armadyl pages are rewards from Treasure Trails. If a player has all four they can use them to make a Book of law.

label: Armadyl pendant
title: Armadyl pendant
lead:
The Armadyl pendant is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. A Guardian of Armadyl in the Temple of Ikov dungeon gives the player the pendant if the player sides with them. Equipping it allows players to attack Lucien, once he is defeated, the quest is complete.

This pendant is the easiest obtainable protection against Armadyl and followers of Armadyl in the God Wars Dungeon.

label: Armadyl rune armour
title: Armadyl rune armour
lead:
The Armadyl armour set is a set of melee armour affiliated to the god Armadyl. Pieces of the armour provide identical stats as rune armour, except for the kiteshield's ranged attack bonus being -2 (rather than -3), as well as each item having a +1 prayer bonus. Therefore, they require 40 Defence to be worn and the completion of Dragon Slayer I for the platebody.

Each piece of the Armadyl armour set can be obtained by completing hard Treasure Trails, and cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Armadyl shield
title: Armadyl shield
lead:
Armadyl shield may refer to:

*Armadyl d'hide shield
*Armadyl kiteshield
*Book of law

label: Armadyl vestment set
title: Armadyl vestment set
lead: The Armadyl vestment set is a members item set of Prayer armour aligned with Armadyl. The pieces are only obtainable by completing easy and medium Treasure Trails.

label: Armen
title: Armen
lead: Armen was the former leader of the Bandits of the Golden Claw, a criminal organisation based in northern Kandarin, as mentioned in Eagles' Peak. He was well known within the gang for his interest in animals, whom he regularly tried to tame.

label: Armillary sphere (interface item)
title: Armillary sphere (interface item)
lead:
The Armillary sphere is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Armillary sphere.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: armour
title: armour
lead:
.]]
Armour describes any item worn to provide Defence. Defence bonuses decrease a player's chance of being hit. Armour comes in many shapes and forms for all classes giving the player a variety of bonuses to choose from. To wear armour of different metal types, certain Defence levels are required. Good armour is recommended when attacking enemies of a higher level, as the higher defences give the opponent less opportunity to do damage. Players should always have the best armour they can afford and equip although 'the best' may differ from player to player.

label: armour case
title: armour case
lead:
Armour case may refer to:
*Armour case space, Construction hotspot in the Costume Room for storing armour sets.
**Oak armour case, stores up to 25 armour sets
**Teak armour case, stores up to 50 armour sets
**Mahogany armour case, stores all armour sets

label: Armour salesman
title: Armour salesman
lead: Aaron the Armour salesman is the owner of Aaron's Archery Appendages. in the Ranging Guild. His shop sells low level Ranged armour. Players who have achieved 99 Ranged can purchase the Ranged Cape of Accomplishment from him for 99,000 coins.

label: Armour shop
title: Armour shop
lead:
Armour shop may refer to:
*Armour Shop (Jatizso)
*Armour store. (Keldagrim)
*Blair's Armour
*Horvik's Armour Shop
*Oziach (shop)
*Quality Armour Shop
*Salius' Armour Shop

label: Armour stand (disambiguation)
title: Armour stand (disambiguation)
lead:
Armour stand may refer to:
* Armour stand - the common furniture built in the Workshop of a Player-owned house
* Armour stand (PvP World) - unique armour stands found in PvP worlds, which can be used to repair untradeable items with the (broken) suffix after they break in PvP scenarios
* Armour stand (Lovakengj) - decorative armour stands found around Lovakengj
* Armour (scenery) - common decorative armour stands called "armour"
* Various armour displays that can be built in the Skill Hall of a Player-owned house:
** Cw armour 1
** Cw armour 2
** Cw armour 3
** Mithril armour
** Adamantite armour
** Runite armour

label: Armour stand (interface item)
title: Armour stand (interface item)
lead:
The Armour stand is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Armour stand.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Armour/Highest bonuses
title: Armour/Highest bonuses
lead:
This page lists the items with the highest specific bonuses for each slot.

Note that you can not directly compare weapons since they all have different speeds. For instance a setup with a maximum hit of 30 and a speed of 4 should have a damage output roughly equal to a setup with maximum hit of 40 and speed 6. In other words don't consider the weapons listed on this page to be "best" just because they have the highest bonuses, often that means these weapons are also very slow.

label: Armour/Lowest bonuses
title: Armour/Lowest bonuses
lead: This page lists the items with the lowest specific bonuses for each slot.

label: Armour/Magic armour
title: Armour/Magic armour
lead: For the most part, a mage's armour provides little to no Ranged and melee Defence bonuses, but instead serves to harness the wearer's magical abilities. Notable exceptions to this rule include splitbark, lunar, and Ahrim's armour sets, which provide a mediocre amount of melee protection, although even these are still absent of Ranged protection. Generally, the magical defence bonus of this type of equipment directly corresponds to its magic attack bonus. Most magical armours cannot be made by players.

label: Armour/Melee armour
title: Armour/Melee armour
lead:
Melee armour, used in the Attack, Strength, and Defence skills, is generally made out of some kind of metal. There is a "default" (regular) series of armour, consisting of bronze, iron, steel, black/white, mithril, adamant, rune, and dragon (in ascending order of the quality of the armour). For each piece of armour, there is a counterpart made for each other type of metal. Most of these can be made from the Smithing skill, with the exception of black and white armours. The majority of dragon equipment cannot be smithed, with a few exceptions listed below.

All armour items not made from those metal types can be considered "special" and generally cannot be made from the Smithing skill, but rather sold by an NPC or obtained as a monster drop. Some players may consider these more desirable, as they often provide higher bonuses than other forms of armour.

label: Armour/Most expensive
title: Armour/Most expensive
lead: This page lists the items with the highest market value for each slot.

label: Armour/Prayer armour
title: Armour/Prayer armour
lead: Prayer armour is used to slow the rate at which Prayer points drain when praying. Unlike the other three general categories of armour, there are few items within it that can be considered uniquely Prayer-related. Many shields, magic robes, and types of metal armour can also be considered Prayer armour.

label: Armour/Ranged armour
title: Armour/Ranged armour
lead: This is a list of the armour that is generally worn by players who are using the Ranged skill. Ranged armour tends to have high Ranged attack bonuses and good Magic Defence bonuses. Ranged armour is usually made from animal hides, tanned dragonhide, or some other type of leather.

label: Armoured
title: Armoured
lead:
Armoured may refer to:

* Armoured kraken
* Armoured Tortoise Regiment
* Armoured zombie
** Armoured zombie (Zemouregal's Base), found in Zemouregal's Base during and after the Defender of Varrock quest
** Armoured zombie (Defender of Varrock), encountered in Varrock Palace during the same quest
** Armoured zombie (Zemouregal's Fort), found in Zemouregal's Fort during and after The Curse of Arrav quest
** Armoured zombie (The Curse of Arrav), a minion summoned during the boss fight with Arrav during the same quest

label: Armoured Tortoise Regiment
title: Armoured Tortoise Regiment
lead:
The Armoured Tortoise Regiment is a military unit of the Gnome Royal Guard that consists of tortoises, Gnome Drivers, Gnome Archers, and Gnome Mages.

The commanding officer of the regiment is Lieutenant Schepbur. Although the regiment presently contains only two tortoises, more tortoises are being trained in order to expand the regiment's ranks. While the tortoises of the Armoured Tortoise Regiment are currently ridden by a Gnome Driver, Gnome Archer, and Gnome Mage, the gnomes have also been conducting further research into equipping the tortoises with other weapons.

label: Armoured zombie
title: Armoured zombie
lead:
Armoured zombie may refer to:

* Armoured zombie (Zemouregal's Base), found in Zemouregal's Base during and after the Defender of Varrock quest
* Armoured zombie (Defender of Varrock), encountered in Varrock Palace during the same quest
* Armoured zombie (Zemouregal's Fort), found in Zemouregal's Fort during and after The Curse of Arrav quest
* Armoured zombie (The Curse of Arrav), a minion summoned during the boss fight with Arrav during the same quest

label: Armourer
title: Armourer
lead:
Armourer could refer to:

label: Armoury
title: Armoury
lead: Armoury is a shop in the Combat Training Camp. This shop sells various weapons for Melee and Ranged combat. The owner is a shop keeper. Buying from this shop is not recommended because it charges prices 50% higher than other shops that sell the same items.

label: Army of Darkness
title: Army of Darkness
lead:
Army of Darkness is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness and also plays in Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, it plays at Dark Warriors' Fortress as well as Wilderness Bandit Camp.

label: Arposandra
title: Arposandra
lead: Arposandra is a hidden gnome city founded by Glouphrie the Untrusted. Translated from Ancient Gnomish, it means "Rock City". Its exact location is currently unknown, but it is believed to be somewhere beneath the Galarpos Mountains. Ohn's diary further supports this, revealing that the gnomes in Zul-Andra came from a settlement in the mountains to the east of the Poison Waste. Arposandra connects to the Poison Waste Dungeon, which dumps the waste products from their experiments into the Poison Waste.

label: Arposandran War
title: Arposandran War
lead:
The Arposandran War is an unofficial name given to the conflict around which the Gnome quest series revolves. The Arposandran War is currently being waged by Arposandra against the Gnome Empire, although the advanced simian civilisation of Ape Atoll has also become involved.

Until Glough's invasion, the Arposandran Wars saw very little open combat between the two sides and consisted almost entirely of espionage.

label: Arrival
title: Arrival
lead:
Arrival is a music track that can be unlocked inside Falador city walls. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Fanfare and Workshop.

In Classic mode, the track plays west of Falador at the West Falador mine.

label: Arrow shaft
title: Arrow shaft
lead:
An arrow shaft is used in Fletching to make arrows. Arrow shafts can be cut from different types of logs by using a knife on them, each tier yielding 5 additional Fletching experience per set of 15 arrow shafts. 15 Feathers can be attached to 15 arrow shafts at 1 Fletching, yielding 15 experience and 15 headless arrows. Arrowtips are then attached to headless arrows to create arrows. Spider on shaft can be made by using an arrow shaft on a spider carcass with 16 Cooking.

Arrow shafts are purchased for coin at Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild.

label: arrows
title: arrows
lead:
Arrows are standard ranged ammunition used by bows, weapons used in ranged combat. They can be created by members through Fletching, by fletching arrow shafts out of normal logs, and attaching feathers and metal arrowheads to them. Arrows can only be fired from bows that are strong enough to use them.

Arrows can be bought from archery shops owned by NPCs in Varrock (Lowe's Archery Emporium), Rimmington (Brian's Archery Supplies), Catherby (Hickton's Archery Emporium), and the Ranging Guild (level 40 Ranged).

label: Arrows (scenery)
title: Arrows (scenery)
lead: Arrows consist of five arrows hanging on a rack on a wall. The arrows appear to be Steel arrows.

label: arrowtips
title: arrowtips
lead:
Arrowtips are a Members-only item, and are used to make arrows. The Smithing level needed to make the arrowtips from their respective metal bars is shown below, along with the Fletching level needed to attach them to headless arrows to finish the process.

Smithing a set of arrowtips uses 1 bar of the desired metal, and will make 15 arrowtips per bar. To make arrows, these tips need to be combined with headless arrows.

title: Art (disambiguation)
lead:
Art may refer to:

*Crafting
*Skills

label: Arthur
title: Arthur
lead: Arthur may refer to one of the following:

label: Arthur Artimus
title: Arthur Artimus
lead: Arthur Artimus was a member of the Bandits of the Golden Claw and was responsible for leaving behind a journal. The journal describes the gang's final operations prior to their abduction by the Mysterious Old Man and disappearance.

label: Artio/Strategies
title: Artio/Strategies
lead:
Artio is a level 320 bear that can be found inside Hunter's End. She is killed for the valuable voidwaker hilt, though she can also drop claws of callisto, tyrannical ring, Callisto cub, the dragon 2h sword and dragon pickaxe. The hard Wilderness diary is required to fight Artio.

: Artio resides in a singles-plus area and in mid-level Wilderness. You may be attacked at any time during the kill. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose.

label: Artisan
title: Artisan
lead:
Artisan was a proposed skill developed and polled over the course of 2014. Often described as "slayer for skilling", Artisan would have tasked players with gathering and crafting specific items depending on assignments given out by Artisan masters.

The skill was proposed and developed over the course of four developer blogs:
*13 June 2014 - 
*20 June 2014 - 
*10 July 2014 - 
*15 August 2014 -

label: Artur Baryshev
title: Artur Baryshev
lead:
Artur Baryshev is a composer for Old School RuneScape since January 2024. He has composed pieces of music for Old School Runescape, making up
 % of all music in the game.

label: Asgarnia
title: Asgarnia
lead: The Kingdom of Asgarnia is one of the main kingdoms of the Old School RuneScape world, Gielinor. Asgarnia's primary economic activities are crafting, mining, and fishing. It also has a notable navy based in Port Sarim. It is ruled over by the King Vallance, however he has fallen quite ill. With the King unable to stand, Sir Amik Varze manages the Kingdom in his stead.

label: Asgarnian ale
title: Asgarnian ale
lead:
Asgarnian ale is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Strength by 2 while draining Attack by \lfloor Level \times \frac{5}{100} \rfloor + 2 (see table below). It can be obtained through brewing at level 24 Cooking granting 248 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 asgarnian hops, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the Asgarnian ale(m).

4 Asgarnian ales are required during the Recipe for Disaster Dwarf subquest, where they are turned into Asgoldian ale by using a coin on them. One is also required for the Death Plateau quest.

label: Asgarnian ale (interface item)
title: Asgarnian ale (interface item)
lead:
The Asgarnian ale is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Asgarnian ale.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Asgarnian Ice Dungeon
title: Asgarnian Ice Dungeon
lead:
The Asgarnian Ice Dungeon is a moderately large dungeon in Asgarnia. It is found south of Port Sarim and north of Mudskipper Point, , under a trapdoor. Look for the red exclamation sign ( ) on the minimap, which indicates a dungeon. This dungeon is particularly dangerous to low level players, as every single monster within it is aggressive. The dungeon is also crucial to the The Knight's Sword quest as this is the only location in Gielinor that contains blurite rocks, allowing players to mine blurite ore.

Three Agility shortcuts can be found in the dungeon; one just east of the entrance ladder requiring 82 Agility, another in the chamber with muggers requiring 60 Agility, leading them to the ice chamber to the west, and a third right before the ice giants and warriors in the eastern area, requiring 72 Agility. All three are boostable.

label: Ash
title: Ash
lead:
Ash is a troll chef found on Death Plateau. He stands next to Dung at the centre of the plateau, just in front of the cooking pot they both maintain.

When the player searches the cooking pot in My Arm's Big Adventure, the troll cooks will attack with weak ranged attacks, hoping to put you in the stew for dinner.

label: ashes
title: ashes
lead:
Ashes are a common item that are produced when a fire burns out. Ashes are used as a Herblore secondary, and are needed in a number of quests. They are commonly discarded, and can often be found where players are lighting fires for Firemaking training. If a player acquires multiple of Old man's message and starts a new task at the Wise Old Man, the duplicates will explode into ashes when attempting to read them.

Ashes can be crushed into ground ashes using a pestle and mortar.

label: Ashes (disambiguation)
title: Ashes (disambiguation)
lead:
Ashes are the result of burning logs.

Ashes may also refer to:

label: Ashihama
title: Ashihama
lead:
Ashihama is a distant island that is part of the Pincers region of the Wushanko Isles (also known as the Eastern Lands). Not much is known about the island, though it is most known for being the original home of The Nightmare of Ashihama, which is said to have been created in an ancient ritual by shamans on the island.

The Nightmare terrorized the sirens of the island for many years, until Shura's discovery of totems created to combat the Nightmare in the mostly unexplored caves beneath the island allowed her and a group of warriors to finally drive the Nightmare off the island.

lead:

label: Assorted flowers
title: Assorted flowers
lead:
Assorted flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

title: Astral
lead: Astral may refer to:

label: Astral armour
title: Astral armour
lead: Astral armour were a armour set, proposed alongside the Warding skill. They were a mage set that would have required level 65 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. In order to ward the robes, players required level 75 Warding, along with suqah hide.

label: Astronomical chart (interface item)
title: Astronomical chart (interface item)
lead:
The Astronomical chart is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Astronomical chart.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Astronomy book
title: Astronomy book
lead:
The Astronomy book, or The Tale of Scorpius, is obtained during the Observatory Quest. It has a brief history of Scorpius and how he introduced astronomy to Gielinor.

After finding the book, a copy can also be found in the shelves in your house.

label: Asyff
title: Asyff
lead: Asyff Bymajique, the fancy dress shop owner, runs the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock. Players can bring un-noted Hunter furs or hides to him to have him make Hunter clothing for a small fee. He is also involved in the Eagles' Peak quest.

label: Atlas and Meridian
title: Atlas and Meridian
lead: Atlas and Meridian are the names of the two small lizard creatures that surround the minimap on the user interface in fixed screen. Their identities were revealed in the seventh issue of Postbag from the Hedge. Atlas and Meridian, according to the Postbag, saw a job advertisement in the Varrock Herald reading, 'Amazing opportunity for 2 trustworthy beings. Be gazed upon by millions and hold the world in your claws! No previous experience required, but good sense of direction a bonus.' The reality of their job was not what they had expected.

label: Atlax
title: Atlax
lead:
Atlax was a Saradominist wizard who lived some time during the Third Age, when they were one of the workers tasked to restore the remnants of the Temple of the Eye, which had been left in ruins in the aftermath of the invasion of the Fallen Empire, whose assault had inadvertently opened an abyssal rift leading to The Scar. Atlax kept a diary of the time they spent rebuilding the temple, which spans a little over a week from the 15th till the 23rd of Bennath.

In this diary, Atlax describes working under the supervision of Pharana, who had been sent by Aliya, the Justiciar of the Lion, to oversee the work of clearing the site. It would seem however that Aliya had not been fully transparent as to the original purpose of the temple, nor disclosed to Atlax or the other workers why these emergency repairs had to be executed with such haste. When Atlax describes turning over a cache of amulets they had found bearing the symbol of the Eye of Saradomin to Pharana, she reportedly mutters that the Justiciar has some explaining to do, indicating that she had figured out where they had been sent: the sanctuary built to house the Stone of Jas. Unlike their supervisor however, Atlax remains in the dark about the identity of their worksite. As Aliya had originally been instructed to keep all matters relating to the Eye a secret when charged by Zachariah, Justiciar of the Owl, to build the temple, it is likely that Aliya kept to this secrecy even after it had been discovered by the forces of the fallen empire.

label: Atlazora
title: Atlazora
lead: Atlazora, the Jaguar of Night's Shadow was a legendary hero in Varlamorian history. Currently, not much else is known about them, save for the fact that the Atlazora's Rest pub is named after them.

label: Atoll (disambiguation)
title: Atoll (disambiguation)
lead:
Atoll may refer to:

label: Attack
title: Attack
lead: Attack is a player's accuracy in melee combat. As a player raises their Attack level, they can deal damage more consistently as well as wield weapons of stronger materials.

label: Attack 1
title: Attack 1
lead:
Attack 1, is a music track that is unlocked on and to the north-west of the Khazard Battlefield. It also plays at a small area north of West Ardougne. It can also play in the Nightmare Zone when facing the Khazard warlord.

If unlocked, it can be heard in the Nightmare Zone as one of the possible tracks that play when facing the Corsair Traitor, Witch's experiment, Tanglefoot, Trapped Soul, or Chronozon.

label: Attack 2
title: Attack 2
lead:
Attack 2 is a music track that is unlocked in Elvarg's lair in the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon. It can later be heard in Dragon Slayer II, during the cutscene of the Dragonkin battle on Lithkren. It can also play in the Nightmare Zone when facing Elvarg.

If unlocked, it can be heard in the Nightmare Zone as one of the possible tracks that play when facing the Corsair Traitor, Witch's experiment, Tanglefoot, Trapped Soul, or Chronozon.

label: Attack 3
title: Attack 3
lead:
Attack 3 is a music track that is unlocked at the Lava Maze Dungeon and Obor's lair. If unlocked, it can be heard in the Nightmare Zone as one of the possible tracks that play when facing the Corsair Traitor, Witch's experiment, Tanglefoot, Trapped Soul, or Chronozon.

It is the third in a set of six tracks known as the "Attack" series.

label: Attack 4
title: Attack 4
lead:
Attack 4 is a music track that is unlocked during the Fight Arena quest. It can also be unlocked in the Iorwerth Camp cave during Song of the Elves. It can also in the Nightmare Zone when facing Bouncer.

If unlocked, it can be heard in the Nightmare Zone as one of the possible tracks that play when facing the Corsair Traitor, Witch's experiment, Tanglefoot, Trapped Soul, or Chronozon.

label: Attack 5
title: Attack 5
lead:
Attack 5 is a music track that is unlocked at the King Black Dragon's Lair, or in a cutscene at the Lithkren Vault during Dragon Slayer II. If unlocked, it can be heard in the Nightmare Zone as one of the possible tracks that play when facing the Corsair Traitor, Witch's experiment, Tanglefoot, Trapped Soul, or Chronozon.

It is the fifth track in the series of six "Attack" music tracks.

label: Attack 6
title: Attack 6
lead:
Attack 6 is a music track that is unlocked at the Gu'Tanoth Ogre Enclave lair. It can also be unlocked and heard in the quest The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute, when the player fights Cuthbert, Lord of Dread. If unlocked, it can be heard in the Nightmare Zone as one of the possible tracks that play when facing the Corsair Traitor, Witch's experiment, Tanglefoot, Trapped Soul, or Chronozon.

It is the sixth track in the series of six "Attack" music tracks.

label: Attack Level Up!
title: Attack Level Up!
lead: Attack Level Up! is a Jingle for leveling attack.

label: Attack Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Attack Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Attack Level Up! (Unlocks) is a Jingle for leveling Attack.

label: Attack potion
title: Attack potion
lead:
An attack potion is a potion made by using an eye of newt on a guam potion (unf), requiring 3 Herblore, yielding an attack potion(3) and 25 Herblore experience. It is the first available potion to make with the Herblore skill. A dose of attack potion provides a temporary skill boost to Attack equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down. This is less than the super attack's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, roe or caviar can be added to an attack potion(2), requiring 4 Herblore, yielding an attack mix and 8 Herblore experience. An attack mix has 2 doses, boosts Attack equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Attack level, rounded down, and heals 3 Hitpoints per dose.

label: attack range
title: attack range
lead:
The attack range of a weapon or spell is the maximum number of squares away from a target, from which a player wielding the weapon or casting the spell may attack their target and deal damage or other effects. This is measured with , which means that the player will visually be able to fire further when attacking diagonally than cardinally, by a factor of up to \sqrt{2} .

Players may use a weapon's attack range to their advantage to avoid retaliation by hiding behind objects or walls - such areas are known as safespots, and this tactic is known as "safespotting", or "farcasting" when done with magic.

label: attack speed
title: attack speed
lead:
Attack speed is determined by the interval between hits. Hit intervals are measured in game ticks (0.6 seconds). The lower the interval, the faster the attack speed.

The attack speed can not be altered by any consumables, rather it is determined by the type of weapon being used. The tables below show the attack speeds for the respective types.

label: Attack stone
title: Attack stone
lead:
Attack stone may refer to:
*Clay attack stone
*Limestone attack stone
*Marble attack stone

label: Attack types
title: Attack types
lead:
The attack types are the different ways in which a player or NPC may attack another player, another NPC, or a piece of interactive scenery that can be attacked. There are three Melee types (stab, slash, crush), three Ranged types (light, standard, heavy), and one Magic type. Equipment gives players attack bonuses towards and defence bonuses against each of the attack styles, though equipment that gives ranged bonuses gives them to all 3 ranged types.

Attacks can also be typeless, which is a secondary category of attack type conferring their immunity to protection prayers. Most typeless attacks can only be used by NPCs, though the delayed second hit from the ancient godsword's special attack is an example of one that can be used by the player.

label: Attack/Experience table
title: Attack/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Attack in the game, as well as all interactions that require an Attack level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: Attas plant (interface item)
title: Attas plant (interface item)
lead:
The Attas plant is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide representing the Attas plant.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Attention
title: Attention
lead:
Attention is a music track that unlocks around Rimmington. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track and Emperor.

In Classic mode, the track plays at the coastline south of Rimmington and western side of Thurgo Peninsula.

label: Attribute affinities
title: Attribute affinities
lead:
effects.]]
Attribute affinities are bonuses against enemies of a certain monster attribute, such as vampyres, golems, or rats. For the most part, attribute affinities are found on weapons, also known as bane weapons. They can also be found on other equipment such as the salve amulet, spells such as crumble undead, and special effects such as that of pearl bolts (e).

The benefits can extend beyond raw stats of the items, often granting percentage-based boosts to both damage and accuracy when fighting enemies of their chosen attribute. Some weapons also have multiple attribute affinities. For example, silverlight acts as a demonbane weapon, but also as a silver weapon that is effective against low-tier vampyres.

label: attuned corrupted equipment
title: attuned corrupted equipment
lead:
Attuned corrupted equipment is a set of armour and weapons created within The Corrupted Gauntlet. It is the middle tier of the corrupted sets, one tier higher than basic corrupted equipment. It can be upgraded to the perfected corrupted equipment set. Its crystal counterpart is the attuned crystal equipment.

Creating the armour set requires the equivalent basic corrupted equipment, 180 crystal shards and 4 each of linum tirinum, crystal ore and phren bark. Creating each weapon requires its basic tier equivalent and 60 crystal shards.

label: attuned crystal equipment
title: attuned crystal equipment
lead:
Attuned crystal equipment is a set of armour and weapons created within The Gauntlet. It is the middle tier of the crystal sets, one tier higher than basic crystal equipment. It can be upgraded to the perfected crystal equipment set. Its corrupted counterpart is the attuned corrupted equipment.

Creating the armour set requires the equivalent basic crystal equipment, 180 crystal shards and 4 each of linum tirinum, crystal ore and phren bark. Creating each weapon requires its basic tier equivalent and 60 crystal shards.

label: Aubury
title: Aubury
lead:
Layte Aubury is the owner of the Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. He features heavily in the Rune Mysteries quest. He stocks many free-to-play runes, including chaos and death runes. Players who have completed Rune Mysteries can also ask him to be teleported to the rune essence mines. When he teleports players, he utters .

He is a close associate with Archmage Sedridor of the Wizards' Tower, and his research helped re-discover the incantation to teleport to the rune essence mines.

label: Aubury's Rune Shop.
title: Aubury's Rune Shop.
lead:
Aubury's Rune Shop. is a shop located in south-eastern Varrock and owned by Aubury. It is a small building just south of the eastern Varrock bank. The shop's easy to access location makes it one of the most convenient ways for players to buy runes and to teleport to the rune essence mine after the quest Rune Mysteries.

The nearby level 6 Mugger will be aggressive to low level players, however he will not enter the shop.

label: August 2007 Archive of RuneScape
title: August 2007 Archive of RuneScape
lead:
The August 2007 Archive of RuneScape is a backup of the source code of RuneScape that was created on 10 August 2007 which served as the basis for Old School RuneScape. When Old School first launched, it was an exact copy of the original RuneScape as it had existed on that date.

The archive was created during a pivotal time in RuneScape s history: the game was posting its highest membership numbers in mid-2007, a period retrospectively described by Jagex as when RuneScape was at its height . After the backup was made, numerous updates were introduced that would fundamentally change the nature of the game, including the original Bounty Hunter (which was implemented along with the removal of Wilderness PvP), restrictions on trade between players, and the introduction of high-definition graphics.

label: August 2025 Sailing Stress Test
title: August 2025 Sailing Stress Test
lead:
The August 2025 Sailing Stress Test was a limited preview of the Sailing skill, available to all members on special worlds separate from the live game. Running for about 2 hours on 14 August 2025, the purpose of the playtest was to test the performance of the system when many players were sailing simultaneously. During the stress test, players were limited to a small region of water surrounding The Pandemonium and could race in a loop around the island to achieve a time.

The stress test was the third public playtest of Sailing, following the alpha and beta in the preceding months.

label: Auspah
title: Auspah
lead:
The Auspah are a race mentioned in Imcandoria's fall. They are believed to originate from the lands of Acheron in the far north, inhabiting the regions surrounding Imcandoria and the Isle of Garmr. They are described as a collection of tribes associated with fire, and show particular interest in fiery jewellery forged by the giants at the Forge of the Giants.

The only known Auspah is Char, who served the Zarosian Empire but disappeared shortly before the start of the God Wars.

label: Authentic Throwing Weapons.
title: Authentic Throwing Weapons.
lead: Authentic Throwing Weapons is a shop where the Tribal Weapon Salesman sells javelins and throwing axes up to runite. The shop is located in the Ranging Guild, so it can only be accessed by players with a Ranged level of 40 or higher.

label: Auto Retaliate
title: Auto Retaliate
lead:
Auto Retaliate is a Combat toggle that allows the player to choose whether their character fights back when attacked. Players can turn it on or off by going to the Combat Options tab and clicking the icon that says "Auto Retaliate (On)/(Off)".

The player will attempt to automatically retaliate to the attacker 1 tick after they are attacked. When a player is attacked, their attack delay is set to their current weapons attack speed divided by two, rounded up, regardless of what it was prior.

label: autocast
title: autocast
lead:
Autocast is an attack option available for all Magic weapons (except powered staves) that can be activated on the Combat Options interface. This attack option causes players to automatically cast a selected spell when they attack, as opposed to manually selecting the spell and its target each time you wish to cast it. Once autocast has been selected, a player will continue casting spells as their default attack as long as they wield the staff and have the correct amount of runes.

Wherever autocasting is available, there are two options: one with a picture of a shield on the button, and one without it. Selecting the option without the shield will cast magic offensively, granting only Magic experience. Selecting the "shield" option will cast magic defensively, dividing the experience gained between the Defence and Magic skills.

label: Autumn garden (interface item)
title: Autumn garden (interface item)
lead:
The Autumn garden is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide representing the Autumn Garden.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Autumn Voyage
title: Autumn Voyage
lead:
Autumn Voyage is a music track that is unlocked when the player first arrives in Lumbridge. It can also be heard around the Lumbridge Swamp and farmlands. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Book of Spells, Dream, Flute Salad, Harmony, and Yesteryear.

In Classic mode, the track plays in eastern Lumbridge, near the cow calves.

label: Ava (disambiguation)
title: Ava (disambiguation)
lead: Ava may refer to:

label: Ava's device
title: Ava's device
lead:
Ava's devices are a series of backpacks that attract a percentage of the ammunition fired during Ranged combat. They can be obtained from Ava, requiring the quest Animal Magnetism, as well as a minimum ranged level. There are three devices, each attracting a higher percentage of fired ammunition:

* , requiring level 30 Ranged
* , requiring level 50 Ranged
* , requiring level 70 Ranged and a Vorkath's head (obtainable after the quest Dragon Slayer II)

label: Ava's max cape
title: Ava's max cape
lead:
Ava's max cape may refer to:
* Accumulator max cape
* Assembler max cape
* Masori assembler max cape

label: Ava's max hood
title: Ava's max hood
lead:
Ava's max hood may refer to:
*Accumulator max hood
*Assembler max hood
*Masori assembler max hood

label: Avan
title: Avan
lead:
The man found in Al Kharid mine is a non-player character who plays a big role in the Family Crest quest. During the quest it is revealed that his real name is Avan Fitzharmon.

After the quest, he can turn steel gauntlets into goldsmith gauntlets. This is free if players have not previously chosen an enchantment for the gauntlets, but if they have, it will cost . If the Family Pest miniquest has been completed, Avan will give the goldsmith gauntlets directly for free instead. The player can reobtain the goldsmith gauntlets after completion of the quest by right clicking and selecting the "Gauntlets" option, which will allow you to reobtain the gauntlets, even on a F2P world.

label: Avantoe
title: Avantoe
lead:
Avantoe is a mid-level herb, requiring a Herblore level of 48 to clean from the grimy version. It can be obtained as a monster drop or through the Farming skill, with a level of 50, by planting an avantoe seed in a herb patch. It is used to make fishing potions, super energy potions, and hunter potions. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create an avantoe potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, the name means "moment", likely due to its unusual lifecycle caused by the harsh climate of the Kharidian Desert. Avantoe sprouts only after rain and then dies shortly in a matter of days.

label: Avantoe potion (unf)
title: Avantoe potion (unf)
lead: An avantoe potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using an avantoe on a vial of water, requiring 50 Herblore. Using a snape grass on an avantoe potion (unf) with 50 Herblore yields a Fishing potion(3) and 112.5 Herblore experience. Using a mort myre fungus on an avantoe potion (unf) with 52 Herblore yields a super energy(3) and 117.5 Herblore experience. Using a kebbit teeth dust on an avantoe potion (unf) with 53 Herblore yields a Hunter potion(3) and 120 Herblore experience.

label: Avarrocka
title: Avarrocka
lead:
Avarrocka, later known as Varrock, was built in year 700, 4th Age. Varrock is the oldest surviving human settlement outside the Kharidian Desert in Gielinor today. It was founded when a tribe found a baby abandoned, and took it as a good omen. That baby was Arrav, a famous hero.

Somewhere between 700th and 800th year of 4th age, Zemouregal, a powerful Zamorakian Mahjarrat necromancer, invaded Avarrocka with an army of zombies to claim the Shield of Arrav, a powerful shield made by now nearly extinct master smith race, imcando dwarves. His army was slain by none other than the great hero Arrav and the grandson of one of the city's elders with the help of the shield, at the cost of Arrav's life. Zemouregal retreated with undead version of Arrav.

title: Avernic catalyst
lead:
The Avernic catalyst was a scrapped item that was pitched as a reward from the Doom of Mokhaiotl. The catalyst was to be used to combine the primordial boots, pegasian boots, and eternal boots together to create the avernic treads.

Player concerns quickly arose about the requirement of pegasian boots, as ranger boots were much harder to acquire compared to dragon boots and infinity boots respectively. On 11 March 2025, the catalyst was scrapped in favour of Osto-Ayak dropping the treads in a useable state, with the player being able to upgrade the treads with primordial/pegasian/eternal boots.

label: Pages containing information about shelved content
Aviansie (race)
title: Aviansie (race)
lead:
The Aviansie are a race of avian humanoids mostly known for their worship of Armadyl during the Second Age and their involvement in the God Wars on the side of Armadyl during the Third Age. During the God Wars, aviansie were tasked with guarding Armadyl's artefacts, such as the Staff of Armadyl, from enemy control. They were also the creators and protectors of the Godsword. However, the aviansie were unable to stop the theft of the staff and the rise of Zamorak to godhood after he banished Zaros.

The aviansie were believed to have become extinct at some point after the God Wars. However, after the previously frozen God Wars Dungeon was thawed, many combatants of the God Wars were revived, including the aviansie. The God Wars Dungeon is now the only known place left in Gielinor where aviansie can be found.

label: Aviansie/Strategies
title: Aviansie/Strategies
lead: Aviansie are found inside the Armadyl section of God Wars Dungeon, which is at the south-west part of the dungeon and requires 70 Ranged to enter. Alternatively, they can also be found in the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon, making these more dangerous to reach due to the threat of player killers, but they drop noted adamantite bars without the need to do a hard Achievement Diary. Nevertheless, both obstacles of entry in both dungeons require 60 Strength or 60 Agility to navigate.

label: axe
title: axe
lead:
Axes are a weapon and a tool necessary for Woodcutting. It is classified as a melee weapon, available in all varieties of metal, although its power and speed are less favourable than most others. Alternatively, they can be used to slash webs.

Higher-level axes have a greater chance of obtaining logs from a tree and thus are generally faster to woodcut with. However, certain low-level trees become attainable at maximum speed at higher woodcutting levels, even with lower-level axes.

title: Axe cabinet

label: Axe handle (historical)
title: Axe handle (historical)
lead:
Axe handles were items created through a random event that caused axe heads to fly off whilst Woodcutting. Heads and handles were either re-attached or deleted to prevent them from becoming discontinued items.

Dragon axes were included in this event. As they were worth over 2 million at the time, players who were not paying constant attention risked substantial losses. Curiously, although a special version of the Dragon axe handle was added in 2006, it was still possible to combine a Dragon axe head and a regular Axe handle.

label: axe head (random event)
title: axe head (random event)
lead:
An axe head may fly off the handle of a player's axe due to a random event which may occur while a player is woodcutting. To fix their axe, players must collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

Axe heads were removed in an update on 17 July 2007, prior to the release of Old School RuneScape, so have never been obtainable in-game.

label: Axe shops

lead: Axe shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Axe shops sell axes and battleaxes.

label: Aztec

label: B. Anker
title: B. Anker
lead: B. Anker is an Official Representative of the Bank of Gielinor. He responds to a letter sent to the representative of the Gielinor Banking system in the Postbag from the Hedge. Besides being a representative, he also works as a normal banker. According to him the Bank of Gielinor received a tip-off shortly after the events of the The Frozen Door, which led the bank to establish a branch in the Ancient Prison, since they are quite keen on providing good customer service.

label: Baby blue dragon
title: Baby blue dragon
lead:
Baby blue dragons are the young of adult blue dragons found in Taverley Dungeon, the Isle of Souls Dungeon, the bottom floor of the Ruins of Tapoyauik, and in the basement of the Myths' Guild. Unlike their adult forms, they do not breathe fire.

Players who wish to kill baby blue dragons without being attacked by the adult blue dragons can find some in the Taverley Dungeon near the lava eel fishing spot, south of the Agility shortcut. They can also be killed on the east side of the main Taverley Dungeon room as no adult blue dragon will walk there.

title: Baby dragon (unused)
lead:
The Baby dragon was an unused monster that was added in the RuneScape 2 Beta. It did not have any colour, and just used the generic grey baby dragon model with no recolouring. It is unknown what purpose, if any, the monster was intended to serve, yet it remained in the game files for many years and was graphically updated in 2006. Therefore, it was never present in Old School RuneScape, and was deleted entirely from the cache on 10 September 2015.

The model is the same as the baby black dragon.

label: Babydragon bones
title: Babydragon bones
lead:
Babydragon bones are dropped by baby green, blue, red and black dragons. They can also be obtained as a common loot from dragon impling jars and crystal impling jars.

Babydragon bones give 30 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways: 
* 90 XP when casting Sinister Offering.
* 90 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.
* 105 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple. The Temple additionally has a 50% chance to not deplete the bones; effectively doubling the XP to 210 per bone.
* 120 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of Baby dragon bonemeal.
* 120 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 144 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

label: Backporting
title: Backporting
lead:
was brought into Old School RuneScape via backporting.]]
Backporting (or porting) is the process of bringing over content from RuneScape 3, released after the August 2007 Archive, into Old School RuneScape. Currently, the main source of backporting by the Old School team is from a partial backup of RuneScape as it was in May 2012.

Compared to creating new content from scratch, backporting content saves development time and resources by allowing the Old School team to re-use existing assets that were created by prior developers. However, the content is not brought over to Old School as it was in RuneScape 3; various factors, such as how the content was originally received, as well as balancing changes to fit Old School are taken into account. For example, Nex, one of the most difficult boss fights in 2011, was rebalanced in Old School to accommodate the lack of the Summoning skill, among other changes.

label: Bad luck mitigation
title: Bad luck mitigation
lead:
Bad luck mitigation refers to any mechanic that adjusts the drop rate of certain rare items or other events to prevent particularly long dry streaks. This can be accomplished by increasing the chance of a drop after reaching some threshold, or by guaranteeing the drop on a specific kill count, among other methods.

Bad luck mitigation is motivated by the fact that most random drops are rolled independently, so individual kills do not guarantee progress towards the drop (referred to in statistics as being ). Due to the nature of randomness, a small percentage of players would be expected to go dry on getting a drop, potentially several times over the drop rate. For example, a standard 1/100 drop only has a 63% chance of success after after 100 kills, while 1 in 1000 players would need more than 680 kills to receive the drop. label: Bailing bucket
title: Bailing bucket
lead:
A bailing bucket is used in the Fishing Trawler minigame. Its sole purpose is to bail water out of the trawler. It is recommended for all players to have this item before going on a fishing trawler trip, as there is always a need to bail at least once.

Players can obtain bailing buckets from either the Khazard General Store (conveniently close to the Fishing Trawler) and Rasolo west of the Fishing Guild. However, the latter store is not recommended due to the location and stock. If players don't have a bailing bucket when starting a Fishing Trawler run, the crates on the deck of the Trawler can be searched for one. Bailing buckets can be traded with other players but not through the Grand Exchange.

label: Baker
title: Baker
lead:
Bakers run bakery stalls in the East Ardougne market as well as in the Great Kourend market. Players can purchase or steal cakes, bread, and chocolate cake slices from their stalls. Stealing, however, may attract the attention of nearby guards, who will attack the player. If a player attempts to steal from the stall while in the bakers' view, that player will be unsuccessful. One Ardougne baker has a daughter named Ramara du Croissant.

Bakers also sell all the items that can be stolen from their stalls. However, if a player attempts to trade or talk with the bakers having stolen from their stalls within the previous 15 minutes, the bakers will not only refuse to trade or talk with the player; they will alert the guards. If players steal from one baker and then go to the other, they still call the guards.

label: Bakery stall
title: Bakery stall
lead:
Bakery stalls are food stalls that can be stolen from at level 5 Thieving. The stalls are typically found near stores selling baked goods.

A successful steal will reward 16 Thieving experience and either a cake, bread, or chocolate slice. Thieving will fail if the player is spotted by the stall's owner or nearby guard.

label: Balancing ledge (Yanille Agility Dungeon)
title: Balancing ledge (Yanille Agility Dungeon)
lead:
The Balancing ledge is an Agility shortcut. An Agility level of 40 is required to use the shortcut. It is the first obstacle into the Yanille Agility Dungeon, giving access to the Chaos druid warriors. Failing drops the player into a pit of poison spiders.

Some people use the balancing ledge as a low-intensity way to train Agility, as with the right camera placement it is possible to keep the mouse cursor in one spot and continuously click. Players can gain up to 13,200 experience per hour.

It is returned to the boy to complete the quest.

lead:
A ball of wool is used in the Crafting skill. It is made by using a spinning wheel.

Players looking to obtain large numbers of balls of wool often use Neitiznot supplies. in Neitiznot as it has the largest stock of any store with a bank in the same building. After Monkey Madness II, Hamab's Crafting Emporium on Ape Atoll is also located close to a bank.

label: Ballista
title: Ballista
lead: Ballistae are a type of ranged weapon that can be created after Monkey Madness II with materials dropped by tortured or demonic gorillas. Like bows, they are two-handed weapons with ranged strength dependent on the type of ammunition used, except ballistae use javelins with a higher ranged strength bonus as ammunition and have an attack speed one tick slower than crossbows. The light ballista and heavy ballista require Ranged levels of 65 and 75 respectively in order to be wielded. The light ballista and heavy ballista share the same attack speed, range, and special attack, with the main differences between the two being that the heavy ballista has a higher ranged accuracy and provides an extra ranged strength bonus added to that of the type of javelin ammunition used.

title: Ballista (Tree Gnome Village)
lead:
The ballista is a gnome weapon found in the Battlefield of Khazard, north of the Tree Gnome Village. It is used during the Tree Gnome Village quest to pierce through a wall of the Khazard building to the north after the player has obtained the coordinates from three Tracker gnomes. The machine requires three coordinates in order to fire: height, x, and y.

Before the ballista can be fired, repairs must first be made. Commander Montai will request the player's help in obtaining six logs to make the repairs during the Tree Gnome Village quest.

label: Ban
title: Ban
lead:
A ban is a punishment that may be given for repeated or serious violation of the Rules of RuneScape. Bans are issued only by Jagex Moderators. A division of Jagex known as Customer Support handles all bans and blocks.

The status of an account can be checked via the Account Status system. An account is in the green zone if it has no offences, though this changes through orange and red as offences accumulate. Bans may be temporary (for example for 24 hours) or permanent. Banned players are unable to log into the game at all.

label: Banana
title: Banana
lead:
A banana is a type of food that restores 2 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be found on trees in tropical locations, such as Karamja and Ape Atoll, or bought from various stores. Six bananas can be picked at a time from a banana tree grown by planting a banana sapling in a fruit tree patch with 33 Farming. They can also be obtained by using the spell Bones to Bananas, which converts bones of all types in the caster's inventory to bananas.

A single banana is required to cast the standard spellbook Ape Atoll Teleport with 64 Magic. The teleport can be added to a portal chamber or portal nexus, requiring 100 and 1,000 bananas respectively.

label: Banana plantation
title: Banana plantation
lead: Luthas' banana plantation can be found across from Zembo's bar on Musa Point. Players can collect bananas for Luthas and put them in the box outside his hut. When they've filled the box with 10 bananas, Luthas will pay them 30 coins. Luthas is useful if a player forgets their money and cannot go back from the island. There are 33 banana trees in the plantation, each with 5 bananas on each tree. This is a rival money making method to making stew for the guard in a tree in Draynor Village, although it is better to collect the bananas and sell at the Grand Exchange for a much higher price.

label: Banana tree
title: Banana tree
lead:
Banana trees are trees found in tropical areas that grow bananas. Up to 5 bananas can be picked from a tree, after which the tree will be empty and require time to grow more bananas. Banana trees take 5 minutes to regrow. The trees can be found growing in the Musa Point banana plantation, which is owned by Luthas and features prominently in Pirate's Treasure. The trees are also found in the Ape Atoll banana plantation.

A variant of banana trees can be found on Ape Atoll in the Monkey Child's garden, as well as a special tree on the west side of the island that grows red bananas.

label: Bandit Camp (Wilderness)
title: Bandit Camp (Wilderness)
lead:
The Bandit Camp is an outlaw stronghold located within levels 17 to 24 Wilderness. It is most often visited for Treasure Trails and the Curse of the Empty Lord miniquest, as well as to kill bandits for a Krystilia Slayer task and to sell items to the general store.

The camp can only be entered from either the south or the east, as it is surrounded by walls. The south entrance is guarded by level 22 and level 130 bandits. To enter, the player must walk from levels 17 to 19 Wilderness along a narrow pathway with lava on either side, or go through the safer way, from the east where there is a break in the wall. This entrance is guarded by two giant rats, and one of them is of the aggressive level 6 variety.

label: Bandit Camp mine
title: Bandit Camp mine
lead: The Bandit Camp mine (or the Hobgoblin Mine) is a mining site found north-east of the Bandit Camp in the Wilderness from levels 32 to 35 and east of the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon. The mine is occupied by a large number of aggressive hobgoblins, from whom the mine gets its nickname.

label: Bandit Duty Free
title: Bandit Duty Free
lead:
Bandit Duty Free, owned by Noterazzo, is a general store located in the Wilderness Bandit Camp. It offers some of the best prices among general stores, initially buying items at their high alchemy value (60% of the base value) while most others buy at low alchemy value (40%).

If players ask Noterazzo about his store buying at high prices, he will explain that he can do so because the tax collector does not come to his store due to its dangerous location.

label: Bandos
title: Bandos
aliases: Big High War God Big High Idiot
lead:
Bandos (Jagex pronunciation: BAN-doss), also known as the Big High War God, is the god of war. He is highly aggressive, violent, and values obedience and glory through battle above all else. He seems indifferent to the wellbeing of his followers and does not care if large swathes of his armies are wiped out— he fights solely for the sake of battle. Although banished millennia ago, the descendants of his soldiers are many and still highly devoted to their god.

Most creatures that follow Bandos are strong, but are either stupid or refuse to think for themselves by Bandos' own orders. The main exception to this are the goblins, who are not strong, though they make up for their lack of strength with their large numbers. He is lesser-known by the humans of Gielinor, mainly because Bandosians rarely speak of their god with other races. According to Bandosian goblin ideology, referring to him by name is reserved for stronger races like ogres and orks, but not for goblins. Many of his followers seem to obey him out of a sense of awe, respect, and unquestioning loyalty; others were compelled to follow him out of fear. Among the Bandosians, there is a legend of a "Chosen Commander," chosen by Bandos, that will one day lead the Bandosians to victory over the world.

label: Bandos armour
title: Bandos armour
lead:
Bandos armour is a set of armour for members that requires 65 Defence to wear. It is dropped by General Graardor and his bodyguards in the God Wars Dungeon.

Its defence bonuses are between dragon and 3rd age. It has fairly reasonable defensive stats, though the main appeal of the armour is the strength bonus provided by the chestplate and tassets. While it shares the same strength bonuses as blood moon and inquisitors (when not accounting for the helm, as the armour set does not have one), it has superior defence bonuses compared to the two and does not penalise slash or stab styles compared to the latter.

label: Bandos blessed dragonhide armour
title: Bandos blessed dragonhide armour
lead:
The Bandos blessed d'hide armour is a set of Ranged armour said to be blessed by Bandos. Every piece requires 70 Ranged and 40 Defence, except for the blessed chaps and blessed bracers, which do not have the Defence requirement. Blessed dragonhide has better defensive stats and the same offensive stats as the corresponding black dragonhide armour with an additional +1 Prayer bonus. Unlike normal dragonhide armour, a coif and boots are also available. Each piece of armour may be obtained as a reward from hard Treasure Trails.

Wearing any piece of Bandos blessed d'hide armour will make the Bandos followers unaggressive within the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon.

label: Bandos page
title: Bandos page
lead: Bandos pages are rewards from Treasure Trails. If a player has all four they can use them to make a Book of war.

label: Bandos rune armour
title: Bandos rune armour
lead:
The Bandos armour set is a set of melee armour affiliated to the god Bandos. Pieces of the armour provide identical attack and defence stats as Rune armour, except for the kiteshield's ranged attack bonus being -2 (rather than -3), as well as each item having a +1 prayer bonus. As with other rune armour, they require 40 Defence to be equipped.

Each piece of the Bandos armour set can be obtained by completing Hard Treasure Trails, and cannot be made via the Smithing skill. The Bandos platebody cannot be worn without completing the quest Dragon Slayer I.

label: Bandos shield
title: Bandos shield
lead:
Bandos shield may refer to:

*Bandos d'hide shield
*Bandos kiteshield
*Book of war

label: Bandos vestment set
title: Bandos vestment set
lead: The Bandos vestment set is a members item set of Prayer armour aligned with Bandos. The pieces are only obtainable by completing easy and medium Treasure Trails.

label: bank
title: bank
lead:
A bank is a facility that allows players to deposit, store, and withdraw their items. It is indicated on the world map with a dollar ( ) icon. It is usually a standalone building, but sometimes takes the form of a chest or even (rarely) a non-player character.

Within a bank, free-to-play accounts may store up to 400 stacks of items, while members can store up to 900. An additional 20 spaces are given if the player has a Bank PIN, another 20 spaces if they have RuneScape Authenticator activated on their account, and another 20 spaces if their account is linked to a Jagex Account. Players may also increase their bank space by buying blocks of 50 bank spaces, up to 9 times, bringing the highest number of spaces a player can have to 910 on free-to-play worlds or 1,410 on members worlds.

label: Bank booth
title: Bank booth
lead:
Bank booths are found throughout Gielinor in the majority of banks and allow access to the banking system. Bankers can be found behind most booths. Players can left-click the booth to access the bank or right-click the booth and "Collect" to gain access to their Grand Exchange listings where they can withdraw completed trades. However, players cannot make or cancel Grand Exchange offers from this menu.

Several bank booths are permanently closed. These cannot be used.

label: Bank chest
title: Bank chest
lead:
A bank chest is interactive scenery that allows quick access to a player's bank account, usually found in remote locations or places where a normal bank would not fit. Like any other banking facility it is indicated with a bank icon ( ).

Players can access their bank and their Grand Exchange collection boxes at bank-chests, but must visit a Banker to change their PIN settings or Grand Exchange offer notification settings.

label: Bank note
title: Bank note
lead:
A bank note or note is a stackable certificate that represents an item. It is equivalent in value to the item it represents, but cannot be used physically until exchanged for the real thing. Almost all tradeable items can be 'noted' and 'unnoted' in the bank interface, with very few exceptions (such as mysterious emblems).

Notes are useful for players who wish to trade large amounts of items at a time. They can also be used for training magic or for converting into coins via the Low or High Level Alchemy spells.

label: Bank notice board
title: Bank notice board
lead: Bank notice boards can be found at several banks around Gielinor. Despite what the examine text suggests, banks have no other use than depositing and withdrawing items.

label: Bank of Gielinor
title: Bank of Gielinor
lead: The Bank of Gielinor, previously the Bank of RuneScape, is the organisation that administrates the function of every bank, deposit box, bank chest, etc. in Gielinor. It was originally known as the Bank of Varrock because that was its only location; however, it eventually expanded and underwent a name change. It is made up of various branches both on Gielinor and on other planes.

label: Bank PIN
title: Bank PIN
lead:
A Bank PIN (short form for personal identification number) is a security feature that players can use to protect their banks. It was introduced in the Bank PIN update on 19 September 2005.

Trying to find out someone's bank PIN goes against Rule 3 - Password Scamming (see Rules of RuneScape). It is also good to note that an unsuccessful attempt in gaining one's bank PIN is also against the rules and that one can get reported for doing such act.

label: Bank table
title: Bank table
lead: Bank tables are decorative scenery commonly found in banks across Gielinor.

label: Bank table (disambiguation)
title: Bank table (disambiguation)
lead:
Bank table may refer to:
* Bank table - common scenery found across Gielinor
* Bank table (Varrock) - unique bank tables found in Varrock
* Bank table (Keldagrim) - low bank tables found in Keldagrim
* Bank table (Lumbridge Castle) - a unique bank table found in Lumbridge Castle's cellar
* Bank table (Sophanem) - two unique bank tables found in the Sophanem bank
* Bank Table (Neitiznot) - a unique bank table found in Neitiznot
* Bank table (Cam Torum) - low bank tables found in Cam Torum, as well as the outpost of Mistrock on Aldarin
* Bank table (Varlamore) - unique bank tables found in various locations around Varlamore

label: Bank-use item
title: Bank-use item
lead: Bank-use items are items which have a feature that's only accessible when standing in a bank. While the exact reason for bank-use item restrictions is unknown, they most likely exist to prevent players from bringing excess materials into boss or skilling encounters. The limitations on these items are not always consistent; for example, the ring of the elements prevents uncharging outside of a bank, but the Soulbearer can be used to uncharge up to 1,000 soul and blood runes from any place in Gielinor. Coin coffers are not currently known to have any bank tiles around them.

label: Banker
title: Banker
lead:
A banker works in a bank where players can safely store coins and items. Players can use coins on bankers to receive platinum tokens at a static rate of 1,000 coins per token. The bankers can also sell up to 450 bank spaces to the player in sets of 50 at a time, each set increasing in price as the player buys more spaces.

The bankers look different at various banks. Most of them are human, but those in Zanaris are fairies. Bankers in Arceuus are citizens of Arceuus. The ones in Cam Torum, at the Hunter Guild, Keldagrim, and Lovakengj are dwarves. In Port Phasmatys, they are ghost bankers. In Darkmeyer and Ver Sinhaza they are vampyres. On The Great Conch they are tortugans. Those in Lletya are elves; bankers found within the gnomish empire are gnomes; those in Dorgesh-Kaan are cave goblins, and the ones in Mor Ul Rek are TzHaar-Ket. They are not directly part of any quests. Players can speak to a banker either by clicking the banker or by clicking on the bank booth.

label: Banker (Al Kharid)
title: Banker (Al Kharid)
lead: These bankers run the Al Kharid branch of the Bank of Gielinor, and are located in the western part of the city.

label: Banker (Canifis)
title: Banker (Canifis)
lead: Bankers run the Canifis branch of the Bank of Gielinor. Like regular bankers, they provide access to the bank and collecting Grand Exchange offers.
