label: Black
title: Black
lead:
__NOTOC__
Black may refer to:
*Kinshra, or Black Knights, knights clad in the colour black.

label: Black 2h sword
title: Black 2h sword
lead:
The black 2h sword is a two-handed sword stronger than the steel 2h sword, requiring level 10 Attack to wield. Players can purchase this two-handed sword from Gaius' Two Handed Shop in Taverley. It can also be a reward from the Observatory Quest, from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame, completing a Treasure Trail or as a drop from various monsters.

As with all black and white equipment, the black 2h sword cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

label: Black amulet (interface item)
title: Black amulet (interface item)
lead: The black amulet is an interface item. It can be seen in the interface for crafting jewellery. If the player does not have the correct gem to craft an amulet, the black amulet appears in its place as a greyed out version.

label: Black Arm Gang
title: Black Arm Gang
lead:
The Black Arm Gang is a gang at war with the Phoenix Gang. Their headquarters is situated in the south-west of Varrock, near the city's southern entrance. The Black Arm Gang operates under the front of a financial advice company.

According to the Phoenix Gang leader, Straven, the Black Arm Gang was formed when some Phoenix Gang members mutinied and branched off into a separate gang. They broke the Shield of Arrav in two during the process, taking the right half with them.

label: Black Arm Gang Headquarters
title: Black Arm Gang Headquarters
lead:
The Black Arm Gang Headquarters is located in the south-western part of Varrock, near the southern entrance to to city. The building is the headquarters for the ruthless and notorious Black Arm Gang. It is inhabited by three thieves, and Katrine Raven, the leader of the Black Arm Gang. The first two rooms are accessible by any player, however the back room and upstairs are locked for anyone who isn't a Black Arm Gang member.

Players must visit the location to speak to Katrine during the Shield of Arrav quest if they wish to join the Black Arm Gang. During the quest, players who are part of the Black Arm Gang must search the cupboard located upstairs to retrieve the right half of the Shield of Arrav.

label: Black axe
title: Black axe
lead:
A black axe is an item mostly used in the Woodcutting skill. Using this axe requires level 11 Woodcutting. Level 10 Attack is required to equip it. As with all axes, carrying it in your inventory along with the necessary Woodcutting level will work.

The success rate for chopping a log is approximately 225% that of the bronze axe, or 12.5% better than a steel axe.

label: Black axe head
title: Black axe head
lead:
The black axe head is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while Woodcutting. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while Mining, but with a pickaxe head and pickaxe handle.

label: Black battleaxe
title: Black battleaxe
lead:
The black battleaxe is a battleaxe stronger than the steel battleaxe, but weaker than the Mithril battleaxe. It requires 10 Attack to wield. Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim. It can also be received as a drop from a Dark beast, and as a reward from a beginner clue scroll or easy clue scroll.

As with all black and white equipment, the black battleaxe cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

label: black bead
title: black bead
lead:
The Black bead is a bead used in Imp Catcher quest. It is a drop from Imps and is returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with White bead, Red bead and Yellow bead to finish the quest.

The bead can also be used to bait traps when hunting imps.

label: Black bear
title: Black bear
lead:
Black bears are large monsters that can be found in forests and are the weaker, non-aggressive cousins of the aggressive grizzly bear.

Despite their non-aggression, they can pose a threat to newer players who accidentally attack them, although safespots can usually be found for rangers and mages.

label: black beret
title: black beret
lead:
The black beret is a hat that can be obtained from Easy Treasure Trails. They provide no stat bonuses and are worn purely for cosmetic purposes. There's other variants: the white beret, blue beret and red beret.

Black berets can be attached to a mime mask to make a beret mask by talking to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless, along with 500 coins. Doing so requires the completion of Cabin Fever and a book o' piracy.

label: Black candle
title: Black candle
lead:
A black candle is a light source used in the Merlin's Crystal quest.

During Merlin's Crystal, in exchange for sparing Sir Mordred's life, Morgan Le Faye details how to free Merlin, requiring a black candle among other things. The Candle maker in Catherby offers to make one if the player brings him a bucket of wax. Once all the other items are obtained, it is lit with a tinderbox when inside the magical symbol, inside the fence on the north-east side of Camelot Castle. After the remaining items are used, and with the correct incantation, Thrantax the Mighty is summoned for the player to command to free Merlin.

label: Black cape
title: Black cape
lead: A black cape is a low-level cape that is commonly obtained by killing a highwayman. It can also be made by using black dye on any coloured cape, and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis and Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.

label: Black cavalier
title: Black cavalier
lead:
The black cavalier is a piece of headwear. There are no requirements for wearing this cavalier, and they do not confer combat bonuses upon the player.

A cavalier of any colour is a potential reward from hard Treasure Trails.

label: Black chainbody
title: Black chainbody
lead:
The black chainbody is stronger than the steel chainbody, and can be worn by players with 10 Defence. Players can purchase this item at the Keldagrim and Falador Chainmail shops. This item cannot be made using the Smithing skill, and has the same bonuses as a white chainbody, except it lacks a prayer bonus.

Sold at Wayne's Chains shop in southern Falador for 1,440 coins, and at Saro's armour shop in Keldagrim for 1,872 coins.

label: Black Chest
title: Black Chest
lead:
Black Chest can mean any of the following:
* Chests used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame
** Black Chest (red)
** Black Chest (brown)
** Black Chest (crimson)
** Black Chest (black)
** Black Chest (purple)

label: Black chinchompa (interface item)
title: Black chinchompa (interface item)
lead:
The Black chinchompa is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the Black chinchompa

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Black claws
title: Black claws
lead:
Black claws are a fast two-handed melee weapon. To wield them, a player must have at least level 10 Attack. They can only be obtained as a monster drop.

As with all black and white equipment, the black claws cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

label: Black cog
title: Black cog
lead:
The black cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower. It is found in a burning room in the Clock Tower's basement, requiring a bucket of water in the inventory, or ice gloves or smiths gloves (i) equipped to pick up.

It is used to repair the eastern black clock spindle in the basement.

label: Black d'hide body
title: Black d'hide body
lead:
Black d'hide body is a part of the black dragonhide armour set. It requires at least level 70 Ranged and 40 Defence to be worn.

It is the strongest standard dragonhide body and is among the most resilient armours against Magic damage. However, Blessed dragonhide armour provides higher defensive stats while maintaining the same offensive stats.

label: Black d'hide chaps
title: Black d'hide chaps
lead:
Black d'hide chaps are a piece of the black dragonhide armour set, and require level 70 Ranged to wear. Similarly to other dragonhide chaps, they have no Defence level requirement.

A player with 82 Crafting can make them using 2 black dragon leather and 1 thread with a needle, granting 172 experience.

label: Black d'hide gold-trimmed armour
title: Black d'hide gold-trimmed armour
lead: Black d'hide gold-trimmed armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as Black d'hide armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from elite Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: Black d'hide trimmed armour
title: Black d'hide trimmed armour
lead: Black d'hide trimmed armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as black d'hide armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from elite Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: Black d'hide vambraces
title: Black d'hide vambraces
lead:
Black d'hide vambraces are a piece of black d'hide armour worn in the hand slot, which require 70 Ranged to wear.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make black spiky vambraces, requiring a Crafting level of 32.

label: Black dagger
title: Black dagger
lead:
The black dagger is a dagger slightly more accurate than the steel dagger. Like most daggers it can be poisoned, giving an advantage in combat. Like all black weapons, wielding it requires an Attack level of 10.

As with all black and white equipment, the black dagger cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

label: Black dart
title: Black dart
lead:
Black darts are ranged throwing weapons. To wield black darts, players must have at least level 10 Ranged.
Black darts cannot be made with the Fletching skill and instead are obtained through monster drops. The only monsters to drop black darts are Burthorpe soldiers. This makes black darts rather rare and hard to obtain. Black darts can be poisoned and they can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

label: Black demon
title: Black demon
lead:
Black demons are large demons that inhabit various dungeons throughout Gielinor. They are weak to demonbane weapons; as with most demons, they are also weak to magical attacks.

A unique black demon is defeated during The Grand Tree. This demon can be re-fought in the Nightmare Zone after the quest has been completed. Black demons as well as Scarred black demons can be found in The Scar.

label: Black demon (The Grand Tree)
title: Black demon (The Grand Tree)
lead:
A unique Black demon is summoned by Glough during The Grand Tree. This demon can be re-fought in the Nightmare Zone after the quest has been completed.

Players can either fight the demon using melee, or hide in a safespot and use ranged, magic, or a halberd. If the demon is not killed within 8-9 minutes, it will disappear and players will have to start the battle all over again.

label: black dragon
title: black dragon
lead:
Black dragons are the most powerful adult chromatic dragons. As with all adult dragons, protection from dragonfire (such as an anti-dragon shield) is recommended when fighting them, although like other common chromatic dragons, they only use dragonfire at melee range.

Black dragons are the only common chromatic dragons that drop the draconic visage. Notably, the stronger level 247 variant in the Wilderness Slayer Cave drops the draconic visage at a rate of 1/5,000, the most common out of any dragon tied with the King Black Dragon and Vorkath.

label: Black dragon leather
title: Black dragon leather
lead: Black dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make black d'hide armour. It can be created by giving a black dragonhide and 20 coins to a tanner (45 coins at Sbott in Canifis). Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Forthos Dungeon, Canifis, Auburnvale, and the Crafting Guild. Alternatively, black dragon leather can be made using the Tan Leather spell. Crafting any piece of black dragonhide armour will grant the player 86 experience per hide.

label: Black dragonhide
title: Black dragonhide
lead: Black dragonhide (also called Black d'hide by tanners) is a 100% drop from black dragons, brutal black dragons, lava dragons, and the King Black Dragon. The hide can be tanned to become black dragon leather by paying a tanner or by using the Tan Leather lunar spell. A tanner will charge 20 coins for each hide, or 45 in Canifis. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, the Crafting Guild, Auburnvale, and Forthos Dungeon.

label: black dragonhide armour
title: black dragonhide armour
lead:
Black dragonhide armour is a type of Ranged armour. All of the pieces require 70 Ranged to equip. Additionally, the body and shield require 40 Defence to equip. All of the pieces can be made through the Crafting skill from 6 pieces of black dragon leather, or obtained as fairly common rewards from completing Hard clues. It has defence bonuses similar to black and mithril armour, however does not have a negative magic defence bonus and has a considerably lighter weight.

Blessed dragonhide armour pieces have a +1 prayer bonus each.

label: Black equipment
title: Black equipment
lead:
Black equipment is made from black metal. Black equipment is stronger than steel equipment, yet weaker than mithril equipment. As the name suggests, the equipment is black in colour. Black armour requires 10 Defence to wield, melee weapons require 10 Attack to wield and ranged weapons 10 Ranged. Black equipment is almost identical to white equipment, unlocked after the Wanted! quest. However, white equipment is members only and has a slightly higher Prayer bonus than that of black equipment.

Black items cannot be smithed.

label: Black flowers
title: Black flowers
lead:
Black flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds. Players have a 2/1,001 chance of obtaining a black flower when harvesting from a mithril or adamant seed.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

label: Black full helm
title: Black full helm
lead:
The black full helm is a full helmet that requires 10 Defence to equip. As with all black armour, it cannot be made using the Smithing skill. It can be bought at Valaine's Shop of Champions in the Champions' Guild for 1,372 coins. It can also be obtained as a Treasure Trails reward.

A black full helm is used in King's Ransom and, if you're part of the Black Arm Gang, Heroes' Quest.

label: Black full helm (g)
title: Black full helm (g)
lead: Black full helm (g) is a part of black gold-trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Black full helm, and requires level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black full helm (t)
title: Black full helm (t)
lead: Black full helm (t) is a part of black trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal black full helm, and requires level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: black gold-trimmed armour
title: black gold-trimmed armour
lead: Black gold-trimmed armour is a possible reward from easy Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to Black armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill, neither can anything made with black metal as Black bars don't exist in game.

label: Black gold-trimmed wizard robes
title: Black gold-trimmed wizard robes
lead:
Black gold-trimmed wizard robes are a black wizard robe set with a gold trim. The pieces are possible rewards from easy Treasure Trails. This set has the same bonuses as their regular blue counterparts but is worn by players to show a form of wealth. Unlike the regular robes, they cannot be combined with Blue dye to try to create Blue gold-trimmed wizard robes.

This set was released on the 12th of June, 2014 along with the Treasure Trail Expansion update.

label: Black headband
title: Black headband
lead: The black headband is a members only item worn on the head. There are no requirements to wear it. Aside from its use in hard Treasure Trails, it is purely cosmetic, meaning it does not offer any combat bonuses.

label: Black Heather
title: Black Heather
lead:
Black Heather is a member of the leading trio of Bandits in the Wilderness Bandit Camp in levels 24-31 of the Wilderness, along with Donny the lad and Speedy Keith. She, like the other two leaders, wields a steel scimitar.

If players attempt to talk to her, they will receive a message stating, "Black Heather is not interested in talking."

label: Black heraldic armour
title: Black heraldic armour
lead: Black heraldic armour are pieces of the Black armour set that have a heraldic design on them. The heraldic armour set consists of a helm, platebody and shield, which can be only obtained as a reward from easy Treasure Trails. The helms and shields are equivalent, in stats, to the Black full helm and Black kiteshield respectively and requires a Defence level of 10 to equip.

label: Black key
title: Black key
lead:
Black key can refer to five different keys from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame:

*Black key black
*Black key brown
*Black key crimson
*Black key purple
*Black key red

label: Black kiteshield
title: Black kiteshield
lead:
The black kiteshield is a Black Knight kiteshield that requires 10 Defence to wield. The black kiteshield has the same defensive bonuses as a white kiteshield, but without the +1 prayer bonus.

The black kiteshield can be found in trimmed and heraldic forms from Treasure Trails.

label: Black kiteshield (g)
title: Black kiteshield (g)
lead: Black kiteshield (g) is a part of black gold-trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal black kiteshield, except for the ranged attack bonus (-2 rather than -3), and requires level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black kiteshield (t)
title: Black kiteshield (t)
lead: Black kiteshield (t) is a part of black trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Black kiteshield, except for the ranged attack bonus (-2 rather than -3), and requires level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black knife
title: Black knife
lead:
The black knife is a throwing knife that requires a Ranged level of 10 to wield. It is stronger than a steel knife but weaker than a mithril knife. As with all black equipment, this item cannot be made via the Smithing skill. A black knife must either be obtained as a monster drop, or bought from another player. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged.

label: Black Knight
title: Black Knight
lead:
Black knights, also known as the Kinshra, are Zamorakian warriors found mainly in their fortress and stronghold. They are central to the Black Knights' Fortress quest.

Once Wanted! has been completed, black knights can be slain in order to increase the player's White Knight rank. As their rank gets higher, they unlock more white equipment. Even though the quest, as well as white equipment, is only for members, non-members are still able to increase their rank.

label: Black Knight Captain
title: Black Knight Captain
lead:
The Black Knight Captain is a prominent member of the Kinshra order in north-eastern Asgarnia. The captain can be seen in an inaccessible part of the Black Knights' Fortress on Ice Mountain, alongside Greldo, a witch and her black cat.

When players listen through the grills, the above persons can be heard plotting to a make a potion to assist in the destruction of the White Knights. Even in the conversation he has with the witch, the captain does not speak much.

label: Black Knight Titan
title: Black Knight Titan
lead:
The Black Knight Titan is a hill giant encountered during the Holy Grail quest. He is reasonably powerful for his level; but his attacks are inaccurate and very slow. He should be fought with Melee, as he has incredibly high Ranged and Magic defence. He does not move from his tile.

If the player is not holding Excalibur as his hitpoints reach 0, he regenerates back to full hitpoints and players must kill him again. This means either the finishing blow must be dealt using Excalibur, or (if using a delayed attack such as magic or ranged) Excalibur must be switched to before the blow hits him. Since the titan is immobile, players with a fast weapon may employ a hit-and-run technique to kill the titan without being hit. Players can also use a halberd from two squares away to melee him without taking damage.

label: Black Knights
title: Black Knights
lead:
*For a general article about the Asgarnian organisation, see Kinshra.
*For a specific article about the monster, see Black Knight.

label: Black Knights' Base
title: Black Knights' Base
lead:
The Black Knights' Base is a Kinshra base in the far south of Taverley Dungeon. The base has two main areas, and both are swarming with black knights. In the top right of the first area is a kitchen, with a sink and a range. In the far right area of the second compartment is the jail. To gain access to the jail cells, the jailer must be killed; his combat level is 47. Inside the south cell is Velrak the explorer, who can give the player a dusty key which gives access shortcuts in the dungeon. It's also interesting to note that in the rooms on the side of the main hall there are helmet racks, which appear to have helmets on them that look suspiciously like White Knight helmets. Although the base is said to be in Taverley by Solus Dellagar, it is actually underneath the Crafting Guild.

To access the base, the player must enter the trapdoor south of Taverley and run past numerous monsters including chaos dwarves and hill giants. Because of this, it is advised that lower levelled players take food. The base plays a part in the Wanted! quest, where the player must interrogate Lord Daquarius about the whereabouts of Solus Dellagar.

label: Black Knights' Fortress
title: Black Knights' Fortress
lead: The Black Knights are up to no good. You are hired by the white knights to spy on them and destroy their secret weapon.

label: Black Knights' Fortress (location)
title: Black Knights' Fortress (location)
lead:
The Black Knights' Fortress is a castle of the Zamorakian military order of the Kinshra, commonly referred to as the black knights. It plays a central role in the eponymous Black Knights' Fortress quest, and is also visited during the King's Ransom and While Guthix Sleeps quests.

Players attempting to enter the fortress normally will be stopped from doing so by one of the fortress guards. In order to infiltrate the fortress, the player must be wearing one of the following combinations of armour:
*A bronze med helm and an iron chainbody
*A black full helm, black platebody, and black platelegs/black plateskirt
**Black trimmed armour and Black gold-trimmed armour work, as well.
*A set of elite black armour
*The Dark Squall robes

label: Black longsword
title: Black longsword
lead:
The black longsword is a longsword stronger than the steel longsword, but weaker than the mithril longsword. Like all other black weapons, it requires 10 Attack to wield, and cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Players can purchase this longsword from the Varrock Swordshop in Varrock.

The black longsword and the steel longsword have the same strength bonus. Black longswords have the same bonuses as a white longsword, other than the +1 prayer bonus the latter offers.

label: Black mace
title: Black mace
lead:
A black mace is a melee weapon stronger than the steel mace, requiring 10 Attack to wield. It is only obtainable in free-to-play by killing dark warriors, from beginner clue scrolls or from Camdozaal Vault lockboxes. Members can also loot it from bronze chests in the Shade Catacombs in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame or from level 106 Cyclops in the Warriors' Guild basement.

As with most maces, it has a Prayer bonus and like all black equipment it cannot be made from raw materials with Smithing.

label: Black med helm
title: Black med helm
lead: A black med helm is the sixth-strongest med helm. It requires a Defence level of 10 to wear, and can be purchased from Seddu's Adventurers' Store in Nardah for 576 coins. It can be received as an uncommon drop from dark warriors, and a common drop from mutated bloodvelds. It can also be obtained through shade burning, and is quite commonly found at the Digsite.

label: Black naval set
title: Black naval set
lead: The Black naval set is a set of clothing that can be bought from Honest Jimmy. The set consists of a black tricorn hat, black naval shirt, and black navy slacks.

label: Black necklace (interface item)
title: Black necklace (interface item)
lead: The Black necklace is an interface item. It can be seen in the interface for crafting jewellery. If the player does not have the correct gem to craft a necklace, the black necklace appears in its place as a greyed out version.

label: Black platebody
title: Black platebody
lead:
The black platebody is an armour used in melee with the same stat bonuses as a white platebody, excluding the Prayer bonus. It requires 10 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than a black chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

It cannot be made using the Smithing skill, though it's easily obtainable as it can be bought from Horvik, Zenesha or another player.

label: Black platebody (g)
title: Black platebody (g)
lead: Black platebody (g) is a part of black gold-trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Black platebody, and requires level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black platebody (t)
title: Black platebody (t)
lead: Black platebody (t) is a part of black trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. It has the same stats as a normal Black platebody, and requires level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black platelegs
title: Black platelegs
lead:
Black platelegs have the same bonuses as the black plateskirt but weigh more. They require level 10 Defence to wear. They can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid or the Champions' Guild. Like all other black armour, it cannot be made with the Smithing skill.

Black platelegs are used in King's Ransom and Heroes' Quest if you're part of the Black Arm Gang.

label: Black platelegs (g)
title: Black platelegs (g)
lead: Black platelegs (g) is a part of black gold-trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. They have the same stats as regular Black platelegs, and require level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black platelegs (t)
title: Black platelegs (t)
lead: Black platelegs (t) is a part of black trimmed armour and a reward from easy Treasure Trails. They have the same stats as regular Black platelegs, and require level 10 Defence to wear. This item cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Black plateskirt
title: Black plateskirt
lead:
The black plateskirt has the same stats as black platelegs but weighs less. The black plateskirt requires 10 Defence to wear. One can be bought from Ranael's Super Skirt Store in Al Kharid.

As with all black and white equipment, the black plateskirt cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

label: Black ring (interface item)
title: Black ring (interface item)
lead: The Black ring is an interface item. It can be seen in the interface for crafting jewellery. If the player does not have the correct gem to craft a ring, the black ring appears in its place as a greyed out version.

label: Black robe
title: Black robe
lead:
A Black robe is one of the basic pieces of chest armour for low level Magic users. Black robes are often dropped by the dark wizards in the stone circle south of Varrock. It has identical stats to the blue wizard robe, as well as its trimmed and gold-trimmed versions. It can be created by using black dye on a blue wizard robe; similarly, it can also be turned into a blue wizard robe by using blue dye on it.

The black robe is often worn with the black wizard hat and black skirt for aesthetics. The hat has a slightly darker tone than the robes, instead more closely matching the priest gown. This is not the case with the robe's trimmed versions.

label: Black scimitar
title: Black scimitar
lead:
The black scimitar is a scimitar with a slightly higher attack bonus than the steel scimitar. It requires level 10 Attack to wield.

A black scimitar can be found in King Lathas' castle in East Ardougne. The respawn rate of a black scimitar here is about 12 minutes and 30 seconds. It requires level 61 Thieving to access. It can also be bought from Briget's Weapons.

label: Black skirt
title: Black skirt
lead:
Black skirts are one of several skirts available. They are sold by various clothes shops, including Thessalia's shop, Thessalia's Fine Clothes, located in Varrock. They can also be dropped by Forgotten Souls.

Black robe skirts are often worn with black robe tops, in the same way blue skirts are worn with wizard tops. However, they provide no bonuses.

label: Black sq shield
title: Black sq shield
lead: The black square shield (abbreviated in-game as black sq shield) is a square shield made of black metal requiring 10 Defence to equip. Its defensive bonuses are slightly better than those of a steel kiteshield, but slightly inferior to those of a black kiteshield. Like all other black armour, it cannot be made with the Smithing skill.

label: Black sword
title: Black sword
lead:
The black sword is a low-mid level weapon made of black, which is stronger than steel. It requires level 10 Attack to wield.

As with all black equipment, it offers the same bonuses as white equipment, minus the prayer bonus. Similarly, it cannot be smithed using the Smithing skill.

label: Black toy horsey
title: Black toy horsey
lead:
Black toy horseys are items made as a joke by Jagex, poking fun at the requests made by players to have horses. Toy horseys are obtainable from Diango for 150 coins, and come in 4 different colours: white, black, grey, and brown. They can also be made from a plank on any crafting table in a player-owned house, which requires level 10 or higher Crafting.

When you play with the horsey, an animation showing your character playing with it appears, and your character says

label: Black trimmed armour
title: Black trimmed armour
lead: Black trimmed armour is a possible reward from easy Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to Black armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill, neither can anything made with black metal as Black bars don't exist in game.

label: Black trimmed wizard robes
title: Black trimmed wizard robes
lead:
Black trimmed wizard robes are a black wizard robe set with a white trim. The pieces are possible rewards from easy Treasure Trails. This set has the same bonuses as their regular black counterparts but is worn by players to show a form of wealth. Unlike the regular robes, they cannot be combined with Blue dye to try to create Blue trimmed wizard robes.

This set was released on the 12th of June, 2014 along with the Treasure Trail Expansion update.

label: black unicorn
title: black unicorn
lead: The black unicorn is a slightly more dangerous version of the unicorn. These creatures are aggressive to all level players when in the Wilderness, but are low-levelled, so they won't affect high levelled players much. They are a very easy way to obtain unicorn horns in decent quantities, as they are present in greater numbers than normal unicorns. They also have a faster spawn rate and tend to walk around quite a bit in their area, and will sometimes run away when their health is low.

title: Black warhammer
lead:
The black warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the steel warhammer. Members can purchase it from Vigr's Warhammers in Keldagrim and Skulgrimen's Battle Gear in Rellekka. The black warhammer requires 10 Strength to wield.

The black warhammer can be used as a substitute for a regular hammer when banging the big door at the entrance of Bandos' Stronghold in the God Wars Dungeon.

label: Blackhole
title: Blackhole
lead:
The Blackhole, also known as Thordur's blackhole, was Jagex's early punishment system in RuneScape Classic, before the ban system was implemented. Players who misbehaved were sent to the blackhole and would remain there for an undefined amount of time before being removed. It existed throughout most of 2001 until it was removed in December of that same year.

In Old School RuneScape, players are able to visit the blackhole by selecting the "Activate" option on the Disk of returning while in the Dwarven Mines beneath Falador. Here they can interact with Thordur but will be unable to move around. The area and Thordur are not instanced contrary to popular belief, but as there is only 1 available tile in this area, anyone else appearing will be under you. Activating the disk again will return the player to the mines.

label: Blackjack
title: Blackjack
lead:
Blackjacks are a group of members' only melee weapons. They are used in the Thieving skill to lure/knockout certain NPCs located in Pollnivneach. There are three types of blackjack: ordinary, offensive (also known as attack), and defensive. Ordinary blackjacks provide a small bonus to strength, while offensive and defensive raise both strength and their respective crush types.

An ordinary willow blackjack can be purchased from the blackjack seller near the kebab shop in Pollnivneach after completion of The Feud. Other blackjacks are available from Ali Morrisane after the blackjack section of Rogue Trader.

Players can take damage when standing or walking on the same tile as the incoming blade, even at 99 Agility. The message You were hit by the saw blade! will be displayed if this occurs. The amount of damage is based on the player's current health, according to the formula below.

The bladed moon was a scrapped slash-focused shield slot item originally pitched as a reward for the Moons of Peril (then called Perilous Moons) in the Perilous Moons - First Look & Rewards update blog:

label: bladed staff
title: bladed staff
lead:
Bladed staves are a category of magic weapons that typically possess both high melee and magic bonuses and can autocast spells.

Like spears and hastae, bladed staves have options for stab, slash, and crush attack styles. They can be thought of as spears/hastae that have the ability to autocast, much like how staves can be thought of as polestaves that have the ability to autocast; however, bladed staves cannot be poisoned.

title: Blamish oil
lead:
Blamish oil is a quest item used in Heroes' Quest. It is made through the Herblore skill, and it turns a normal fishing rod into an oily fishing rod. Oily fishing rods can only be used at lava fishing spots to catch lava eels or infernal eels.

To make blamish oil, combine blamish snail slime with a harralander potion (unf). It requires level 25 Herblore to be made and gives 80 Herblore experience. Completion of Heroes' Quest is not required to create the blamish oil in this way.

label: Blamish snail slime
title: Blamish snail slime
lead:
Blamish snail slime is a quest item in Heroes' Quest. When added to a vial of water with Harralander it makes blamish oil, which can be used on a fishing rod to make an oily fishing rod. The oily fishing rod can then be used to catch lava eels in the Taverley Dungeon or the Lava Maze, or infernal eels in Mor Ul Rek.

Blamish snail slime can be made by going to Mort Myre Swamp, killing a Myre blamish snail, and grinding the raw snail (thin, lean, and fat all work equally) with a pestle and mortar with an empty sample bottle in the player's inventory. Sample bottles can be obtained from the general store in Canifis or from Rasolo the Wandering Merchant.

label: Blast mine/Strategies
title: Blast mine/Strategies
lead:
To do blast mining efficiently, it is important to:
* Minimise the time wasted waiting for dynamite to explode.
* Minimise the time spent running to and from the deposit sack.
* Minimise the amount of damage taken.

These are much easier if a consistent strategy is used, following a chosen pattern repeatedly. There are many patterns that may be used, with some variation keeping the above points in mind.

label: Blast spells

lead: Blast spells are part of the elemental group of Magic combat spells in the standard spellbook. Elemental staves can be used to cut the costs of these spells. These are free-to-play spells. Like all combat spells, each damage point caused by these spells yields 2 Magic experience and 1.33 Hitpoints experience.

label: Bleed
title: Bleed
lead:
Bleed is a temporary status effect that causes the player to lose a set amount of hitpoints over a short time. Players who are bleeding will be dealt three hitpoints of damage every three ticks.
* Bleed inflicted by custodian stalkers causes the player to lose 9 Hitpoints over 9 seconds (15 ticks). However, if the player is moving, they will take damage every tick.
* Bleed inflicted by Vardorvis causes the player to lose 15 hitpoints over 8.4 seconds (14 ticks) if the player is standing still. However, if the player is moving, they will take damage every tick, causing them to lose a total of 42 hitpoints instead.

Currently, only Vardorvis, the Emissary Enforcer and custodian stalkers (including strange creatures, their quest variant) are capable of inflicting bleed on players. However, Zebak's melee attack uses a similar mechanic.

label: Blessed dragonhide armour
title: Blessed dragonhide armour
lead:
Blessed dragonhide armour is Ranged armour that requires 70 Ranged and 40 Defence to equip the body, coif, boots, and shield, while the chaps and bracers only require 70 Ranged. This armour cannot be made using the Crafting skill; players can only obtain it from hard Treasure Trails or through purchase from other players. Each piece of blessed dragonhide armour has equal offensive stats and better defensive stats compared to its corresponding black dragonhide armour piece, plus a +1 Prayer bonus. Unlike black dragonhide armour, coif and boots are also available.

Blessed dragonhide armour is available in 6 variants, Guthix, Saradomin, Zamorak, Armadyl, Bandos, and Ancient. Every armour piece, except Guthix armour, counts as god-related protection for the corresponding god within the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon.

label: Blessed giant rat
title: Blessed giant rat
lead:
The blessed giant rat is a type of giant rat on the second floor in the Underground Pass.

Due to its 30 Hitpoints and low Defence, the blessed giant rat can be good for training Combat on at low levels. It has no drops other than bones, however, and is not in a prime location compared to other giant rats' locations.

label: blessed gold bowl
title: blessed gold bowl
lead:
The blessed gold bowl is a quest item made during or after the Legends' Quest. It is described by Gujuo as a bowl made of the metal of the sun.

The player must make the gold bowl by using two gold bars and a hammer at an anvil while holding the sketch given to the player by Gujuo to make a gold bowl. The bowl can then be taken back to Gujuo to be blessed (must have 42 prayer points, however they will not be consumed), to make it ready for it to hold the holy water needed to free Ungadulu. It is possible to fail when blessing the bowl causing the player to lose 5 prayer points in the process. If the blessed bowl is filled with the sacred pure water of the Kharazi water pool, it becomes a golden bowl containing sacred pure water that can be used with an enchanted vial to make a vial of holy water: one bowl can fill up to 10 vials. After making one successful golden bowl, the player can smith a gold bowl at any anvil, without need of the sketch, for 30 Smithing experience (though there remains a chance of failure); the bowl can then be taken to Gujuo to have it blessed.

label: Blessed spider
title: Blessed spider
lead:
A blessed spider is a type of spider found only in the Underground Pass. They are found on the west side of the bridge and in the pit where Kalrag is located. They are believed to be blessed or "converted" to Iban. Like most spiders, blessed spiders attack with melee and are weak to crush.

Blessed spiders are initially not aggressive to players with a combat level of 78 or above. However, if Kalrag is killed, they become aggressive to players of all levels, and are able to attack the player simultaneously as if they were in a multicombat area. When Kalrag respawns, they revert to being non-aggressive, except for any that might be attempting to attack the player already.

Bloated toads may only be dropped in the ogre areas east and south of Gu'Tanoth. Once dropped, they have a chance of causing a chompy bird to land, lasting 1 minute before exploding and dealing 1-2 damage to all players within one tile (including diagonally). This damage cannot kill players.

label: blood moon armour
title: blood moon armour
lead:
Blood moon armour is a set of melee equipment that requires level 75 Strength and 50 Defence to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli.

The chest and legs have the same strength bonus as Bandos armour, making it very popular for mid-level players due to its cheap cost and accessibility. The defensive bonuses are much weaker than that of Bandos armour, except its slash defence (which is only slightly lower) and magic defence, which is significantly higher. It is also much lower in weight.

label: Blood rune
title: Blood rune
lead: Blood runes are one of the runes used to cast spells in the Magic skill. They are used in some of the highest level spells, the lowest of which is Ruby Crossbow Bolt Enchant, and the highest is Heal Group. Blood runes are also used in charging the Scythe of Vitur, Sanguinesti staff, Ring of shadows, and soul bearer.

label: Blood spells
title: Blood spells
lead:
Blood spells are one of four types of Ancient Magicks combat spells. Blood spells have a life leech effect which heals the caster by 25% of the damage dealt; the amount healed is based off of damage the spell would have done, allowing players to heal normally from targets with very little remaining health, or immune to damage from the spell. Clever use of blood spells can trivialize dangerous encounters or compensate for player mistakes during hard content, though they are much more expensive than other types of combat magic. Upon activation of the life leech effect of a blood spell, the message You drain some of your opponent's health. will be displayed.

A few enemies are immune to the life leech from blood spells; namely, Zebak, the wights in Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, Sotetseg and both Tumeken's and Elidinis' Warden.

label: Blood tithe
title: Blood tithe
lead:
Blood tithes are rendered periodically by the rulers of Morytania, the vampyres. Officially, a blood tithe is to be taken from every settlement in Morytania, but the only settlement outside of the Sanguinesti region that is both known and useful to the vampyres is Canifis, which is inhabited by werewolves, who use meat sacrifices in most cases; however, sometimes, they are forced to sacrifice one of their own. Port Phasmatys is populated entirely by ghosts, who thus cannot pay the tithe, and nearly every person in Mort'ton is Afflicted by the mists from Castle Drakan; their blood is generally unpleasant, if not poisonous. Burgh de Rott is not yet known to be populated by those rendering the tithe; although the vampyres have demanded the tithes before, it is not known if the people routinely pay them. Therefore, humans in Meiyerditch are practically the only ones in Morytania to be forced to pay the blood tithe. In the ghettos, the blood tithe is more than a periodic tax; humans are farmed for blood, each sector being drained at regular intervals. Humans outside the city are comparatively free and well off.

The vampyres require blood tithes, as blood is their main dietary staple and energy source, similar to the vampyres of popular culture. It also forces some humans to collaborate with the vampyres to protect their families, such as Gadderanks.

label: bloodbark armour
title: bloodbark armour
lead:
Bloodbark armour is a set of members-only magic armour that requires 60 Magic and 60 Defence to wear. Each piece of bloodbark armour can be made by using the corresponding piece of splitbark armour on either the true Blood Altar or Kourend's Blood Altar, and costs a certain amount of blood runes. Infusing splitbark armour into bloodbark armour requires sufficient Runecraft skill, as well as having learned how to do so via reading the Runescroll of bloodbark.
* The gauntlets and boots require 100 blood runes each and 77 Runecraft.
* The helm requires 250 blood runes and 79 Runecraft.
* The body and legs require 500 blood runes each (1,000 runes total) and 81 Runecraft.

Thus, crafting a full Bloodbark armour set requires 1,450 blood runes.

label: Bloom
title: Bloom
lead:
The Bloom spell is learned during the Nature Spirit quest when Filliman Tarlock asks for a silver sickle, which he then blesses.

Every variant of the blessed silver sickle as well as the Ivandis flail and Blisterwood flail can be used to cast Bloom on small bushes, rotting logs, and rotting branches in the Mort Myre Swamp to harvest pears, fungi, and stems respectively. Bloom can also be cast while fighting swamp crabs, causing fungi to blossom from their shells, which will be dropped when they are slain. The druidic spell given to the player during Nature Spirit has a similar effect, but it is single-use and does not cost any Prayer points.

label: Blowpipe
title: Blowpipe
lead:
Blowpipes are two-handed Light Ranged weapons that fire darts. The attack range of blowpipes is 5 tiles, and 7 when using longrange.

In player versus monster encounters, the base attack speed of blowpipes is 3, matching that of darts. However, in player versus player encounters, the base attack speed of blowpipes is 4.

A blue cape may also be among the items you can obtain from chasing Solus Dellagar during the Wanted! quest, the player calls this cape the "Cape of Champions" during the quest because it is sold in the Champions' Guild.

It is used to repair the southern blue clock spindle on the .

label: Blue d'hide body
title: Blue d'hide body
lead:
A blue d'hide body is a piece of blue dragonhide armour worn in the body slot. It is crafted by using 3 blue dragon leather and a needle and thread with level 71 Crafting. To wear a blue d'hide body, a player must have a Ranged level of 50 and a Defence level of 40.

Although players must complete Dragon Slayer I in order to wear the green d'hide body, completion of this quest is not required to equip the blue, red, and black dragonhide bodies.

label: Blue d'hide chaps
title: Blue d'hide chaps
lead:
Blue d'hide chaps are a piece of the blue dragonhide armour set, and require level 50 Ranged to wear. Similarly to other dragonhide chaps, they have no Defence level requirement.

A player with 68 Crafting can make them using 2 blue dragon leather and 1 thread with a needle, granting 140 experience.

label: Blue d'hide gold-trimmed armour
title: Blue d'hide gold-trimmed armour
lead: Blue d'hide gold-trimmed armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as Blue d'hide armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from hard Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: Blue d'hide trimmed armour
title: Blue d'hide trimmed armour
lead: Blue d'hide trimmed armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as blue d'hide armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from hard Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: Blue d'hide vambraces
title: Blue d'hide vambraces
lead:
Blue d'hide vambraces are a piece of blue d'hide armour worn in the hand slot, which require 50 Ranged to wear. They can be made with a Crafting level of 66.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make blue spiky vambraces, requiring a Crafting level of 32.

label: blue door
title: blue door
lead: The Blue door is located in the basement of Melzar's Maze. It must be opened during Dragon Slayer I, using a blue key obtained from killing one of the nearby Zombies.

label: Blue Dragon
title: Blue Dragon
lead:
Blue dragons are the third strongest of the chromatic dragons, behind red dragons and black dragons. Like all dragons, they can breathe dragonfire, which can inflict up to 50 damage if proper protections aren't used. Dragonfire can be mitigated by equipping an anti-dragon shield or a dragonfire shield – alongside the usage of an antifire potion, which will completely negate dragonfire damage. On top of the strong dragonfire breath, they also attack with an accurate slash attack.

Blue dragons are assignable as a Slayer task after starting Dragon Slayer I. Baby blue dragons also count toward blue dragon tasks, and can be found within the Myths' Guild, Isle of Souls, or the Taverley Dungeon. A variant of blue dragons are found in the Ruins of Tapoyauik that are uniquely weak to fire spells, instead of water like most chromatic dragons.

* Blue dragon
* Baby blue dragon
* Brutal blue dragon
* Vorkath

Not to be confused with:
