label: Broken shield
title: Broken shield
lead:
The broken shield is one of the two halves of the restored Shield of Arrav.

In the Shield of Arrav quest, the player must combine both parts of the broken shield to get the complete shield. One player must join the Black Arm Gang and retrieve the right half from a cupboard upstairs in the base. The other player must be in the Phoenix Gang and must get the left half from the chest in the underground base.

label: Broken staff
title: Broken staff
lead:
A broken staff is an item that can be repaired into different kinds of staves at a repair bench or higher in the workshop of a player-owned house. Repairing one gives 14.5 Crafting experience.

Broken staves can be dug up at the Digsite or fished up on the Fishing Trawler.

label: Broken statue
title: Broken statue
lead:
Broken statue may refer to:

* Broken Statue (Hallowed Sepulchre)
* Broken statue (While Guthix Sleeps)

label: Broken wall
title: Broken wall
lead:
Broken wall may refer to:

* Broken wall (Al Kharid), used to enter and exit the back of Al Kharid Palace from the big window
* Broken wall (Burgh de Rott), leads to a Myreque hideout in Burgh de Rott
* Broken wall (Fishing Platform), found on the Fishing Platform, made during Sea Slug quest to help Kennith escape
* Broken wall (Nemus Retreat), Agility shortcuts around Nemus Retreat
* Broken wall (Piscatoris Fishing Colony), found in Piscatoris Fishing Colony, repaired during the Swan Song quest
* Broken wall of the completely destroyed Shades of Mort'ton temple that gets repaired into temple wall

label: bronze
title: bronze
lead: Bronze may refer to:

label: Bronze 2h sword
title: Bronze 2h sword
lead:
The bronze 2h sword is the weakest two-handed sword in Old School RuneScape. Like all bronze weaponry, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

It can be created at level 14 Smithing by using 3 bronze bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory, granting 37.5 Smithing experience.

label: Bronze arrow
title: Bronze arrow
lead:
The bronze arrow is an arrow made of bronze. These arrows are the weakest type of arrows in Old School RuneScape and are compatible with most bows. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

In order to create this item players must first smelt bronze bars. Then using a hammer and anvil, the player must turn the bar into bronze arrowtips. Creating the bronze bar has no Smithing requirement, while a player must have level 5 Smithing to create the arrowheads. Then players should cut logs, and using a knife, turn them into arrow shafts. After attaching feathers to the arrow shafts (creating headless arrows) players can then use the arrowheads on the headless arrows to create bronze arrows. This entire process requires level 1 Fletching.

label: Bronze arrowtips
title: Bronze arrowtips
lead:
Bronze arrowtips are made with a bronze bar requiring 5 Smithing, yielding 12.5 Smithing experience and 15 bronze arrowtips. They are made into bronze arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 1 Fletching, yielding 19.5 Fletching experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for coin at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Armoury in the Combat Training Camp, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the of the Grand Tree, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost.

label: Bronze axe
title: Bronze axe
lead:
The Bronze axe is the weakest axe in Old School RuneScape. It can be wielded for combat, or used to cut trees in Woodcutting. It requires an Attack level of 1 to be equipped, and a Woodcutting level of 1 to be used.

Players can make a bronze axe with the Smithing skill at level 1 using one Bronze bar, giving the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Players can take one for free from logs found at various locations, such as at the chicken farm by the Lumbridge cow field, or Fred the Farmer's house. One can also be obtained by talking to the Woodsman tutor.

label: Bronze axe head
title: Bronze axe head
lead:
The bronze axe head is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while Woodcutting. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while Mining, but with a pickaxe head and pickaxe handle.

label: Bronze bar
title: Bronze bar
lead:
A bronze bar is a bar of refined bronze. It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 1 by using a copper ore and a tin ore on a furnace, granting 6.2 Smithing experience. A bronze bar can be smithed on an anvil through the Smithing skill to create bronze weapons and armour. A list of bronze items that can be smithed from bronze bars and the Smithing levels required can be found here. When smithed, each bar gives 12.5 experience, with a maximum of 62.5 experience given for the bronze platebody.

Members can purchase bronze bars from the Shantay Pass Shop in the Shantay Pass south of Al Kharid for 8gp each, or from Jiminua's Jungle Store north of Tai Bwo Wannai village for 12gp each.

label: bronze battleaxe
title: bronze battleaxe
lead: The bronze battleaxe is a battleaxe made of bronze. The weakest battleaxe in the game, it requires 1 Attack to wield. Players can make a bronze battleaxe with the Smithing skill at level 10 using 3 bronze bars, giving 37.5 experience. It is a slashing weapon, which makes it good for monsters with a slash weakness. Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim.

label: Bronze bolts
title: Bronze bolts
lead:
Bronze bolts are the weakest bolts, and may be shot from any crossbow.

Bronze bolts are crossbow bolts made out of bronze. To make them, a player must smith unfinished bronze bolts. This requires a Smithing level of 3, and for each bronze bar that player smiths they will get 10 unfinished bronze bolts and 12 Smithing experience. Then a player must attach flights to the bolts. Attaching flights to each bolt requires a Fletching level of 9 and 1 feather, granting 0.5 Fletching experience per bolt. They may also be stolen from the crossbow stall in Keldagrim. As with most bolts, they can be poisoned, however this will prevent the addition of bolt tips.

label: Bronze chainbody
title: Bronze chainbody
lead: The bronze chainbody is a chainbody that can be made at an anvil with 3 bronze bars and a hammer with a Smithing level of 11, granting 37.5 Smithing experience. Since it requires a Defence level of 1 to wear, it can be worn by any player. It is one of the weakest armour chest pieces in the game and is seldom worn. The bronze chainbody can be obtained through a spawn located in the Dwarven Mine.

label: Bronze Chest
title: Bronze Chest
lead:
Bronze Chest can mean any of the following:
* Chests used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame
** Bronze Chest (red)
** Bronze Chest (brown)
** Bronze Chest (crimson)
** Bronze Chest (black)
** Bronze Chest (purple)

label: Bronze claws
title: Bronze claws
lead:
Bronze claws are a two-handed melee weapon, and are the weakest set of claws available. They can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

Bronze claws can be obtained either by using the Smithing skill to make a pair, or buying them from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den. The requirements for making them are completing the Death Plateau quest and level 13 Smithing. To make them, use two bronze bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory. This grants 25 experience.

label: Bronze dagger
title: Bronze dagger
lead: The bronze dagger is the most basic dagger in Old School RuneScape, and can be made at an anvil using the Smithing skill. This requires one bronze bar and a hammer, and yields 12.5 Smithing experience. There are no level requirements to create or wield a bronze dagger; like many melee weapons, it can be poisoned.

label: Bronze dart
title: Bronze dart
lead:
Bronze darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from bronze that are only available to members. Bronze darts only require level 1 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Bronze darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Players can smith bronze bars into bronze dart tips with level 4 Smithing after completion of The Tourist Trap. Each bronze bar creates 10 bronze dart tips and gives the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added with at least level 10 Fletching to create the bronze darts. This step does not require the quest to be completed. 1.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per bronze dart.

label: Bronze dart tip
title: Bronze dart tip
lead:
The bronze dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players with at least 4 Smithing can smith 10 dart tips by using a bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory. They can be fletched into bronze darts at level 10 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 18 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must complete the Tourist Trap quest.

label: Bronze equipment
title: Bronze equipment
lead: Bronze equipment are items made from bronze metal. Bronze equipment is the weakest equipment in Old School RuneScape. All bronze items are coloured brown. Bronze armour requires 1 Defence to wield, weapons require 1 Attack.

label: Bronze fire arrow
title: Bronze fire arrow
lead:
Bronze fire arrows are bronze arrows wrapped in an oily cloth, which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox. They, along with any other fire arrow, are primarily used to pierce the rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same Ranged Strength as regular bronze arrows.

label: Bronze full helm
title: Bronze full helm
lead:
The bronze full helmet is the weakest full helmet in Old School RuneScape. The bronze full helmet grants greater defensive bonuses than its medium helmet counterpart, though at a cost of offensive bonuses for Ranged and Magic. There are no Defence requirements for wearing this helmet.

To create a bronze full helmet the player needs at least 7 Smithing, a hammer and 2 bronze bars. To make a helmet use one of the bars on an anvil with the hammer in the inventory. This grants 25 Smithing experience.

label: Bronze gold-trimmed armour
title: Bronze gold-trimmed armour
lead: Bronze gold-trimmed armour is a possible reward from easy Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to Bronze armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Bronze javelin
title: Bronze javelin
lead:
The bronze javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. They are the weakest type of javelin. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching bronze javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 3 Fletching, granting 15 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.

label: Bronze key
title: Bronze key
lead:
Bronze key could refer to:

*The bronze key used during Recruitment Drive
*The bronze key used during Prince Ali Rescue
*The bronze key used during Monkey Madness II
*A bronze key used to open chests in the H.A.M. Dungeon
*Keys from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame
**Bronze key red
**Bronze key brown
**Bronze key crimson
**Bronze key black
**Bronze key purple

label: Bronze key (Prince Ali Rescue)
title: Bronze key (Prince Ali Rescue)
lead:
The bronze key is made by giving a key print and a bronze bar to Osman or by using the same items on any furnace, and it is collected from Leela during Prince Ali Rescue to open the cell door to Prince Ali.

Should players lose the key, they must pay 15 coins to reclaim it from Leela.

label: Bronze kiteshield
title: Bronze kiteshield
lead: The Bronze kiteshield is the weakest smithable kiteshield, requiring 1 Defence to wield. A player with 12 Smithing can make the shield by using 3 bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 37.5 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador.

label: Bronze knife
title: Bronze knife
lead:
Bronze knives are the lowest level throwing knives available, and do not require a Ranged level to wield. They can be poisoned, and due to being one-handed, can be wielded alongside a shield.

Bronze knives can be created from a bronze bar at level . Each bar makes 5 knives, and grants the player 12.5 Smithing experience. The knives can also be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den, requiring and .

label: Bronze longsword
title: Bronze longsword
lead: The bronze longsword is a longsword made of bronze. It is the weakest longsword available, and any player can wield it. It requires 2 bronze bars and level 6 Smithing to make, granting 25 experience. The bronze longsword is available for purchase at Varrock Swordshop in Varrock. It is rarely used due to the existence of the iron longsword, which is stronger and has the same requirements. It can be found as a drop from various monsters.

label: Bronze mace
title: Bronze mace
lead: The Bronze mace is a mace made of bronze. It is the weakest mace in the game, and can be equipped at level 1 Attack. A bronze mace can be created at level 2 Smithing using 1 bronze bar. This item spawns in Sorceress' house in southern Al Kharid, and can be bought at Flynn's Mace Market in Falador.

label: Bronze med helm
title: Bronze med helm
lead:
The bronze med helm is the weakest medium helmet. It can be equipped to give a player small Defence bonuses in combat. Players can make a bronze med helm with a Smithing level of 3 by using one bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory, giving the player 12.5 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this medium helmet from Peksa's Helmet Shop in the Barbarian Village or in the Warrior Guild Armoury from Anton.

A bronze med helm is required for the Black Knights' Fortress, King's Ransom, and While Guthix Sleeps quests. A bronze med helm spawn exists in the south-eastern corner of Draynor Manor. Falador and Edgeville town guards wear these helms as part of their uniform; as well the Black Knights' Fortress' guards.

label: Bronze pick head
title: Bronze pick head
lead:
A bronze pick head was obtained as part of a discontinued random event, in which the bronze pickaxe head flew off the handle while the player was mining. To fix it, the player had to collect it off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

If players were not paying attention when this occurred, the head would disappear from the ground or be picked up by another player, requiring them to purchase another.

label: Bronze pickaxe
title: Bronze pickaxe
lead:
A bronze pickaxe is a pickaxe made of bronze. It is given to players during the Mining part of Tutorial Island and is part of the starting gear given to the player when leaving Tutorial Island. It mines on an 8-tick cycle, making it the slowest pickaxe.

Bronze pickaxes spawn in several locations in Misthalin and Asgarnia, and they can also be bought from various shops. It can also be obtained for free from Monlum, the mining tutor, in the East Lumbridge Swamp mine. A bronze pickaxe is also given to the player by Doric when starting Doric's Quest.

label: Bronze platebody
title: Bronze platebody
lead:
The bronze platebody is an armour used in melee and the weakest of all platebodies. It has no Defence requirement to equip and provides greater protection than a bronze chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 18 Smithing can make one by using 5 bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 62.5 experience. Alternatively, they can be bought from Horvik's Smithy or Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop.

label: Bronze platelegs
title: Bronze platelegs
lead:
Bronze platelegs are leg armour made of bronze, requiring level 1 Defence to wear (as is the same with other bronze and iron items). They share the same defensive stats as a bronze plateskirt but weigh more. They can be made at level 16 Smithing by using a hammer and 3 bronze bars at an anvil.

These can be bought from Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid.

label: Bronze plateskirt
title: Bronze plateskirt
lead: A bronze plateskirt is the weakest plateskirt in Old School RuneScape. It has identical stat bonuses to the bronze platelegs but weighs less. A player with 16 Smithing can make it by using three bronze bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 37.5 smithing experience. They can be bought from Ranael's Super Skirt Store in Al Kharid.

label: Bronze scimitar
title: Bronze scimitar
lead:
The bronze scimitar is a scimitar made of bronze. The weakest scimitar in the game, it requires level 1 Attack to wield. Players can make a bronze scimitar with level 5 Smithing using 2 bronze bars, granting 25 Smithing experience. Players can purchase this scimitar from Zeke's Superior Scimitars in Al Kharid.

One can be found for free on the top floor of a house in Rimmington.

label: Bronze spear
title: Bronze spear
lead:
The bronze spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from bronze and is the weakest spear in Old School RuneScape. Spears are members-only weapons. Bronze spears can also be used to create a scarecrow.

Bronze spears can be easily obtained from low-level monsters such as goblins. There is a bronze spear spawn in the Haunted Mine on the second level near other assorted bronze equipment. A (kp) version can be bought from Tamayu after finishing the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest. Using the Smithing skill, players can create bronze spears. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. It can also be found by digging at Level 3 digging spots at the Digsite, with a specimen brush, specimen jar and trowel in the inventory, or bought from the Fortis Blacksmith.

label: Bronze sq shield
title: Bronze sq shield
lead: The Bronze sq shield is the lowest level defence square shield in Old School RuneScape. It can be equipped to give a player better defence bonuses in combat. Its recommended use is in melee combat. Players can make a bronze square shield with 2 bronze bars at level 8 Smithing, granting 25 Smithing experience. It can also be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop in Falador.

label: Bronze sword
title: Bronze sword
lead:
The bronze sword is a low-level weapon made of bronze. It can be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop, or made at level 4 Smithing using 1 bronze bar, granting 12.5 experience.

A bronze sword is given to the player by Vannaka on Tutorial Island.

label: Bronze thrownaxe
title: Bronze thrownaxe
lead: The bronze thrownaxe is a Ranged throwing weapon. There are no requirements to wield a bronze throwing axe. They can be obtained either by buying from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or trading with another player. The bronze throwing axe can be wielded with a shield or prayer book for protection.

label: Bronze trimmed armour
title: Bronze trimmed armour
lead:
Bronze trimmed armour is a possible reward from easy Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to Bronze armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

Like other Treasure Trails cosmetics, the set can be stored in the Treasure chest in the Costume room.

label: Bronze trophy
title: Bronze trophy
lead:
Bronze trophy may refer to:

* Twisted bronze trophy
* Trailblazer bronze trophy
* Shattered relics bronze trophy
* Trailblazer reloaded bronze trophy
* Raging echoes bronze trophy

label: Bronze warhammer
title: Bronze warhammer
lead:
A bronze warhammer is a warhammer made with 3 bronze bars, requiring 9 Smithing, yielding 37.5 Smithing experience.

It can be purchased from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear and Vigr's Warhammers for coins.

label: bronze wire
title: bronze wire
lead: Bronze wire can be created by players with level 4 in Smithing by using one bronze bar on an anvil with a hammer in your inventory. A total of 7 are used in quests, such as Creature of Fenkenstrain (3 required, unnoted), Recipe for Disaster/Freeing Pirate Pete (3 required) and Shilo Village (1 required).

label: Broodoo shield
title: Broodoo shield
lead:
A Broodoo shield is a special members-only shield requiring 25 Defence & 25 Magic to equip. It is created by using a hammer on a tribal mask with two snakeskins, and eight nails of any type, requiring 35 Crafting, and yielding 100 Crafting experience. A mask of a particular colour produces a shield of the same colour.

Broodoo shields have a unique passive effect in combat, similar to the black mask; when damage is taken, there is a 10% chance of using a charge to drain 1 + 5% levels of a shield-specific combat stat from the opponent. The enemy must have at least 50% Hitpoints and the skill must not already be drained. This occurs even when not retaliating and at any distance. Each broodoo starts with 10 charges and a charge is used for each activation of the passive effect. Broodoo shields cannot be recharged. Having zero charges does not alter the item's stats.

label: Brother Brace
title: Brother Brace
lead: Brother Brace is a Saradominist monk on Tutorial Island who teaches players how to use Prayer. Players can find him in the chapel on Tutorial Island.

label: Brother Cedric
title: Brother Cedric
lead:
Brother Cedric is a drunken monk aided during the Monk's Friend quest.

He is found standing next to his broken cart south of the Ardougne Zoo, just north of the Ardougne Monastery.

label: Brother Jered
title: Brother Jered
lead: Brother Jered is a monk at the Edgeville Monastery. Players may speak to him to have their unblessed symbol blessed one at a time. Since he is on the , only those with a Prayer level of 31 can access him. Players who achieve level 99 Prayer may purchase the Prayer cape from him for 99,000 coins.

label: Brother Kojo
title: Brother Kojo
lead:
Brother Kojo is a monk who oversees the Clock Tower. When the player first meets him, the clock has stopped working, due to the fact that the four cogs that keep the clock running have been taken; players can start the Clock Tower quest to help repair it.

He also makes watches, which the player can obtain from him if they have a sextant and a chart in their inventory. The watches can be used to solve coordinate clues.

label: Brother Omad
title: Brother Omad
lead:
Brother Omad is a monk in the Monastery south of Ardougne. Players can talk to him to start the Monk's Friend quest.

During the quest he wants you to retrieve a child's blanket. After player gives him the blanket he decides to organise a party.

label: Brown
title: Brown
lead:
Brown may refer to:

*Bandos, a god associated with the colour brown.
*Bronze, a brown-coloured metal.

label: Brown apron
title: Brown apron
lead:
Brown aprons are used to enter the Crafting Guild. They can be purchased from several clothing stores, such as Thessalia's Fine Clothes store in the centre of Varrock, for 2 coins.

A brown apron can be obtained from the Tool store 3 built in the Workshop of a player-owned house. Members can also claim them from Malignius Mortifer after the Swan Song quest.

label: Brown headband
title: Brown headband
lead: The brown headband is a members only item worn on the head. There are no requirements to wear it and it is purely cosmetic, meaning it does not offer any combat bonuses.

label: Brown naval set
title: Brown naval set
lead: The brown naval set is a set of clothing that can be bought from Honest Jimmy. The set consists of a brown tricorn hat, brown naval shirt, and brown navy slacks.

label: Brown rug (interface item)
title: Brown rug (interface item)
lead:
The Brown rug is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Brown rug.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Brown toy horsey
title: Brown toy horsey
lead:
Brown toy horseys are items made as a joke by Jagex, poking fun at the requests made by players to have horses. Toy horseys are obtainable from Diango for 150 coins, and come in 4 different colours: white, black, grey, and brown. They can also be made from a plank on any crafting table in a player-owned house, which requires level 10 or higher Crafting.

When you play with the horsey, an animation showing your character playing with it appears, and your character says

label: Brulee
title: Brulee
lead:
Brulee may refer to:

*Brulee (vanilla)
*Brulee (egg)
*Brulee (raw)
*Brulee supreme

label: Bruma
title: Bruma
lead:
Bruma may refer to:
*Bruma herb, used to create rejuvenation potions in Wintertodt
*Bruma kindling, used to light the brazier in Wintertodt
*Bruma root, used to light the brazier in Wintertodt or fletch into kindling
*Bruma roots, the outcrop found that gives bruma roots when chopped
*Bruma torch, a reward from the reward cart that acts as a light source and a pair of warm clothing in Wintertodt

label: Brutal
title: Brutal
lead:
Brutal may refer to:
*Brutal arrows
**Bronze brutal
**Iron brutal
**Steel brutal
**Black brutal
**Mithril brutal
**Adamant brutal
**Rune brutal
*Brutal dragons
**Brutal green dragon
**Brutal blue dragon
**Brutal red dragon
**Brutal black dragon
*Dual macuahuitl

label: Brutal arrows
title: Brutal arrows
lead:
Brutal arrows are a type of arrow that can be created after Sithik Ints teaches you how to make them during the Zogre Flesh Eaters quest. Instead of arrowtips, the brutal arrows use the blunt flat sides of nails, therefore being "brutal". The brutal arrows are stronger than their regular arrow counterpart and have the bonus of being very effective versus zogres and skogres due to their bones easily crumbling beneath the crushing force, as piercing weaponry is ineffective. This ability comes at the cost of not being poisonable. Brutal arrows can also be used to hunt chompy birds.

Partial completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters is required to equip and use brutal arrows.

label: Brutal Black Dragon (interface item)
title: Brutal Black Dragon (interface item)
lead:
The Brutal Black Dragon is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Brutal Black Dragon

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Brutus/Strategies
title: Brutus/Strategies
lead:
After completion of The Ides of Milk, players may fight Brutus as an instanced boss encounter within the Lumbridge cow field.

The easiest way to reach the Lumbridge cow field is by using the cowbell amulet, which teleports players there when charged with air runes. It additionally has a "Ring" option which will cause Brutus to respawn in 13 ticks (7.8s) after a chatbox message appears, rather than 36 ticks (21.6s). Note that ringing the cowbell amulet too late (ex. a few seconds before he's due to respawn) can result in a longer respawn time.

label: Bucket
title: Bucket
lead:
A bucket is one of the most common items available. They can be purchased cheaply from most general stores and can also be found in many locations throughout the game. Buckets are commonly used for skills such as Crafting, Cooking and Farming.

Buckets can contain any of the following items:

label: Bucket (Slayer Tower basement)
title: Bucket (Slayer Tower basement)
lead:
The bucket is examineable scenery in the basement of the Slayer Tower.

Some of them can be used to safespot bloodveld, nechryael, and gargoyles.

label: Bucket of milk
title: Bucket of milk
lead:
A bucket of milk is a Cooking ingredient used to make a variety of drinks and foods such as choc saturdays and cakes, as well as several feeders. Players can use a bucket on a dairy cow or dairy buffalo to create a bucket of milk, or simply click on the cow or buffalo with at least one empty bucket in the inventory.

Players can turn a bucket of milk into chocolatey milk by adding chocolate dust, or add milk to nettle tea (though this does not add any effects). Depending on their Cooking level, Members can use a dairy churn to turn a bucket of milk into a pot of cream, a pat of butter, or a piece of cheese.

label: Bucket of sand
title: Bucket of sand
lead: A bucket of sand can be obtained by using an empty bucket with a sand pit or sand pile. They may also be obtained from Drew by mining sandstone and depositing it in the grinder next to him. They are a key component in creating molten glass, which is often used in Crafting and Construction, either via a furnace along with soda ash or by casting Superglass Make along with soda ash, seaweed or giant seaweed.

label: Bucket of water
title: Bucket of water
lead:
A bucket of water is made by using a bucket on a water source such as a fountain, a sink or a well. A bucket is the only vessel that can be filled from a well.

Like other vessels filled with water, a bucket of water has everyday uses such as transforming clay into soft clay. A bucket of water can also be used to fill a watering can.

label: Bucket of water (disambiguation)
title: Bucket of water (disambiguation)
lead:
Bucket of water may refer to:

*Bucket of water
*Bucket of water (Meiyerditch)
*Bucket of water (Rum Deal)

label: Bucket of wax
title: Bucket of wax
lead:
A bucket of wax is obtained by interacting with a beehive in the apiary south of Seers' Village, west of Catherby. The player must have an empty bucket in their inventory, and either wear full beekeeper's outfit or use insect repellent on the beehive first. This process must be repeated per bucket of wax. It is used in the Merlin's Crystal and Troll Romance quests.

There is a bucket spawn right beside the gate of the apiary.

label: Buffs
title: Buffs
lead: Buffs and debuffs are changes to an individual's capabilities. They include activated prayers and changes in levels of combat skills. A positive change is called a buff, while the negative counterpart is called a debuff.

label: Bugs
title: Bugs
lead:
Bugs is an ogre who is the son of Rantz and brother of Fycie. In Recipe for Disaster, both Bugs and his sister use the ogre boat ride to get to Karamja. Both Bugs and his sister are also featured in Big Chompy Bird Hunting when the player has to cook the Chompy bird to their liking.

Bugs also features briefly in The Corsair Curse, where the player discovers him in the water through a telescope in an attempt to debunk Cabin Boy Colin's theory of the curse affecting Captain Tock's crew. Colin mistook Bugs to be a mermaid and supposedly offended him, resulting in the belief that he was responsible for the curse.

label: Build bank chest
title: Build bank chest
lead:
Build bank chest may refer to

* Chest pieces, found in the Museum Camp after Bone Voyage
* Bank chest space, found on islands discovered by Sailing

label: Builder's costume
title: Builder's costume
lead:
The builder's costume is worn by builders. It is acquired during the Tower of Life quest, and consists of a hard hat, builder's shirt, builder's trousers, and builder's boots. When any piece of the costume is worn, the beckon emote will be enhanced, should the player use it.

While needed during the quest, it is not required when the quest is completed.

label: Building mode
title: Building mode
lead:
Building mode is used when players want to access their player-owned house to start constructing rooms, building furniture, etc. This feature can be accessed from the Options menu in the main game interface. Once "House options" button is chosen, players can toggle Building mode ON and OFF.

When building in OFF mode, house owners can invite friends to visit their houses. Anyone visiting the house will only see furnitures that have already been built. Owners can host parties, duel with others, and serve tea while in this mode. By default, building mode is set to OFF. Pets are not allowed to be out in building mode. Random events do not appear in houses in building mode.

label: Bukalla
title: Bukalla
lead: The Bukalla is an entity exclusively alluded to in Dagannoth Supreme's examine text. Although initially planned to be a lost tribe of vikings vanquished by Dagannoth Supreme, the Bukalla eventually turned out to be a legendary Fremennik warrior.

label: Bullroarer
title: Bullroarer
lead:
The bullroarer is a quest item used during and after the Legends' Quest. During the quest, it is obtained by giving a complete map of Kharazi Jungle to a forester just outside the Kharazi Jungle. The bullroarer is used to summon a local tribesman named Gujuo from the dense jungle at various points during the quest for advice on how to proceed at each point. When used, players swing it around their heads, making a whirring sound.

Sometimes, swinging it near an oomlie bird or a tormented warrior makes them angry for disturbing the jungle's peace, whereupon they attack the player. Also, swinging it not far enough into the jungle makes nothing happen, with a message in the chat box saying, You feel a bit silly at first, but soon it makes an interesting sound. If used in an area other than the Kharazi Jungle, nothing will happen.

label: Bullrushes
title: Bullrushes
lead: Bullrushes are non-interactive scenery, typically found near the edge of water bodies across Gielinor.

label: bunny ears
title: bunny ears
lead:
Bunny ears are an untradeable cosmetic holiday item worn on the head. A pair of bunny ears can be obtained by completing one of the Easter holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Easter.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 14 July to 21 July) as part of a rare item drop.

label: Bunny outfit
title: Bunny outfit
lead:
The bunny outfit is a cosmetic reward obtained during Easter events

The outfit was released over the course of several years, with the bunny ears first being available during the 2014 Easter event, the feet during the 2015 Easter event, and the rest of the outfit being made available during the 2016 Easter event.

label: Burial at Sea
title: Burial at Sea
lead:
Burial at Sea is an unfinished quest not accessible in the game. The quest would have been started by talking to 'Squawking' Steve Beanie. The quest summary is "Hunt down a pair of wannabe pirates and unlock the deep sea diving gear, a useful Sailing tool.". The quest assets were added to the game on 5 November 2025 with the Sailing Technical Pre-Release.

Judging by the assets (which use the config name bas_ ) and the quest summary, the quest appears to be a follow-up to the Pandemonium quest and would have unlocked the deep sea helmet and deep sea apparatus, which would be required for higher level mermaid guide sea charting tasks. The quest would have involved finding and fighting a sickly version of Anne, obtaining deep sea diving gear, diving with Victoria Kebbit-Monkfish, solving a grid puzzle, and discovering a Zarosian laboratory beneath the ocean.

label: Buried skeleton
title: Buried skeleton
lead:
Buried skeleton may refer to:

* Buried skeleton (Digsite), the skeleton found within the Digsite.
* Buried skeleton (Shaman Caves), the skeleton found within the Shaman Caves.
* Buried skeleton (Temple of Ikov), the skeleton found within the Temple of Ikov.

label: Buried skeleton (Digsite)
title: Buried skeleton (Digsite)
lead: Buried skeletons can be found within the training and level 3 digs at the Digsite. Searching the skeleton results in the player finding nothing of interest. Using a trowel on the skeleton with a Digsite workman nearby will provide dialogue of the workman telling the player off.

label: Buried skeleton (Shaman Caves)
title: Buried skeleton (Shaman Caves)
lead: A buried skeleton can be found in the room with the Carved rocks in the Shaman Caves. The skeleton can be searched, which provides a bronze pickaxe if the player is not already holding a pickaxe. The size of the skeleton and the presence of a pickaxe next to it indicates that it likely belongs to a dwarf. Additionally, the examine text says it is "probably dwarven remains", and Ungadulu says his great-grandfather told him dwarves once went down into the caves and never returned.

label: Buried skeleton (Temple of Ikov)
title: Buried skeleton (Temple of Ikov)
lead: A buried skeleton can be found in the icy area of the Temple of Ikov. Searching the skeleton results in the message Nothing interesting happens.

label: Burn
title: Burn
lead:
Burn is a temporary status effect that causes an entity to lose a set amount of hitpoints over a period of time. Players or NPCs who are burning will be dealt one hitpoint of damage every four ticks (2.4 seconds). Over the course of the burn, entities will lose 10 hitpoints over 40 ticks (24 seconds), or 5 hitpoints over 20 ticks (12 seconds) in the case of the scorching bow's special attack.

Up to 5 separate instances of the burn effect can be inflicted at once; in this case the frequency of damage will remain unchanged at once every four ticks, but each time the entity will take damage equal to the number of burn stacks they currently have. After 5 burn stacks, any further burn instances will be discarded; the oldest burn instance with the lowest time remaining will not be replaced.

label: Burning of Avarrocka
title: Burning of Avarrocka
lead:
The Burning of Avarrocka is the unofficial name given to a battle between the goblin armies and the human population of Avarrocka between the years 700 and 800 of 4th Age.

The battle resulted in heavy losses to for the humans. There were only a handful of survivors, and almost all of city was lost. The goblins' losses are unknown.

label: Burnt batta
title: Burnt batta
lead:
Burnt batta is the result of accidentally burning a raw batta while attempting to make a half baked batta. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt batta has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a batta tin. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt bones
title: Burnt bones
lead:
Burnt bones are one of the few bones that free players can bury to train Prayer, with the others being normal bones, big bones, and monkey bones. They can be found in the Kebos Battlefront, the Lizardman Canyon, the Dragon Nest, and various locations in the Wilderness.

Burnt bones give 4.5 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways: 
* 13.5 XP when casting Sinister Offering.
* 13.5 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.
* 15.7 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.
* 18 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of burnt bonemeal.

label: Burnt bread
title: Burnt bread
lead:
Burnt bread is the result of accidentally burning bread dough while attempting to bake bread. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt bread has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt cake
title: Burnt cake
lead:
Burnt cake is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked cake while attempting to bake a cake. The burn rate will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74.

A burnt cake has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt chicken
title: Burnt chicken
lead:
Burnt chicken is the result of accidentally burning a raw chicken while attempting to make cooked chicken. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34. Players can also deliberately make burnt chicken by cooking a piece of cooked chicken, displaying the chatbox message, You deliberately burn the nicely cooked chicken.

Burnt chicken may be used for the Forgettable Tale... quest, in which it may be one of the random items requested by the rowdy dwarf before he will give the player his Kelda seed. It is also one of the items that Gunslik and the rowdy dwarf can request when doing Keldagrim tasks.

label: Burnt crunchies
title: Burnt crunchies
lead:
Burnt crunchies is the result of accidentally burning raw crunchies while attempting to make a half baked crunchy. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt crunchies has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a crunchy tray. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: burnt curry
title: burnt curry
lead:
Burnt curry is the result of accidentally burning uncooked curry while attempting to make curry. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74.

The burnt curry has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim the bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish
title: Burnt fish
lead: Burnt fish may refer to:

label: Burnt fish (anchovies)
title: Burnt fish (anchovies)
lead:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning raw anchovies while attempting to make anchovies. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (herring)
title: Burnt fish (herring)
lead:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning either raw herring or raw mackerel. Cooking herring requires 5 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 41, and mackerel requires 10 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 45.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (sardine)
title: Burnt fish (sardine)
lead:
A burnt fish is the result of burning a raw sardine while attempting to cook a sardine. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt foods, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (trout)
title: Burnt fish (trout)
lead:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning either raw giant carp, raw trout, raw cod, raw pike, or raw salmon. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.
* Giant carp stops being burnt at level 45.
* Trout stops being burnt at level 49.
* Cod stops being burnt at level 51.
* Pike stops being burnt at level 54.
* Salmon stops being burnt at level 58.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt fish (tuna)
title: Burnt fish (tuna)
lead:
Burnt fish is the result of accidentally burning raw tuna or raw bass. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. Tuna requires 30 Cooking to attempt to cook and stops being burnt at level 63, while bass requires 43 Cooking and stops being burnt at level 80.

The burnt fish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt food
title: Burnt food
lead:
Burnt food is the result of a normal occurrence when Cooking. Burning food happens when the player's Cooking level is not high enough to not burn the food, and the chance of burning decreases as the higher Cooking level the player has. Most food will eventually stop burning at a certain cooking level; however, some foods always have a chance to burn unless wearing a Cooking cape. Meat and chicken can also be burnt by trying to cook their cooked variants. When cooking, a fire has the highest chance to burn food, using a range decreases the chance, reduced further with some foods when using the cooking gauntlets, Lumbridge Castle cooking range, or the Hosidius Kitchen.

Although selling burnt food to general stores yields coins and is not tradeable on the Grand Exchange, some player collectors may pay for them, though prices vary and are dependent on the type and quantity of food.

label: Burnt gnomebowl
title: Burnt gnomebowl
lead:
Burnt gnomebowl is the result of accidentally burning a raw gnomebowl while attempting to make a half baked bowl. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 38.

The burnt gnomebowl has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a gnomebowl mould. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt lobster
title: Burnt lobster
lead:
Burnt lobster is the result of accidentally burning a raw lobster while attempting to make a lobster. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 74; wearing cooking gauntlets will stop them from burning at level 64 instead.

The burnt lobster has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt manta ray
title: Burnt manta ray
lead:
Burnt manta ray is the result of accidentally burning a raw manta ray while attempting to make a manta ray. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. There is no level where manta rays stop being burned, although wearing a Cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt manta ray has no use whatsoever, although you can unsuccessfully attempt to eat it. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt meat
title: Burnt meat
lead:
Burnt meat is the result of accidentally burning various raw meat while attempting to make cooked meat. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 34. Players can also deliberately make burnt meat by cooking a piece of cooked meat, displaying the chatbox message "You deliberately burn the nicely cooked meat."

Burnt meat is used for the Witch's Potion quest. It is often dropped by Imps, and is also a reward from Burntmeat after Eadgar's Ruse and My Arm's Big Adventure.

label: burnt oomlie
title: burnt oomlie
lead:
Burnt oomlie is the result of burning a raw oomlie. This requires 50 Cooking, but unless it is wrapped in a palm leaf first, it will always be burnt.

The burnt oomlie has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: burnt oomlie wrap
title: burnt oomlie wrap
lead: Burnt oomlie wrap is the result of accidentally burning a wrapped oomlie while attempting to make a cooked oomlie wrap. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 40 when cooking on a range and level 44 when cooking on a fire.

label: Burnt pie
title: Burnt pie
lead:
Burnt pie is the result of accidentally burning any kind of pie. The burn rate while cooking pies will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels.

The burnt pie has no use whatsoever, but it can be emptied to reclaim a pie dish. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt pitta bread
title: Burnt pitta bread
lead:
Burnt pitta bread is the result of accidentally burning pitta dough while attempting to make pitta bread. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 37.

However, since pitta bread cannot be made until level 58 Cooking, burnt pitta bread cannot be obtained via normal means. The method used to obtain a burnt oomlie wrap cannot be used, since using chill to drain from 58 to 36 Cooking would take longer than it takes to cook a full inventory of pitta bread. Furthermore, pitta dough can only be cooked at a range, which are not found in proximity to areas with the chill effect.

label: burnt pizza
title: burnt pizza
lead:
Burnt pizza is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked pizza while attempting to bake a pizza. The burn rate while baking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 68.

The burnt pizza has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt sea turtle
title: Burnt sea turtle
lead:
Burnt sea turtle is the result of accidentally burning a raw sea turtle while attempting to make a sea turtle. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. There is no level where sea turtles stop being burned, although wearing a Cooking cape will prevent players from burning any food.

The burnt sea turtle has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burnt shark
title: Burnt shark
lead:
Burnt shark is the result of accidentally burning a raw shark while attempting to cook it. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 94 when wearing cooking gauntlets.

The burnt shark has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange. Because of that, some players collect them or resell them to other burnt food collectors.

label: Burnt stew
title: Burnt stew
lead:
Burnt stew is the result of accidentally burning an uncooked stew while attempting to make stew. Cooking stew requires 25 Cooking. Players will stop burning stews at level 58 Cooking.

The burnt stew has no use whatsoever, although it can be emptied to reclaim a bowl. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: burnt swordfish
title: burnt swordfish
lead:
Burnt swordfish is the result of accidentally burning a raw swordfish while attempting to make a swordfish. The burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels, stopping entirely at level 86; wearing cooking gauntlets will stop them from burning at level 81 instead.

The burnt swordfish has no use whatsoever. Like most other burnt food, it is tradeable to other players but not on the Grand Exchange.

label: Burntmeat
title: Burntmeat
lead:
Burntmeat is a troll featured in Eadgar's Ruse and My Arm's Big Adventure. He can be found in the Troll Stronghold kitchen.

Burntmeat is criticised by other trolls for only being able to cook burnt meat; however, he believes that he is a master chef. Should players help him during a quest, he rewards them with burnt meat, which he claims is very valuable.

label: Burrow
title: Burrow
lead: Burrow may refer to:

label: Burst of Strength
title: Burst of Strength
lead:
Burst of Strength is a prayer unlocked at level 4. Burst of Strength increases the player's Strength by 5% when activated, or by 1 level if the player's Strength level is lower than 20.

Like all other stat-affecting prayers, it cannot be used in conjunction with another prayer that increases the player's Strength level, such as Superhuman Strength.

label: Burst spells
title: Burst spells
lead: Burst spells are the weaker group of multi-target damaging Magic spells in the Ancient spellbook, and the second weakest group overall. These spells hit up to nine targets in a 3x3 square area.

label: Burthorpe
title: Burthorpe
lead:
The Principality of Burthorpe, referred to colloquially as Burthorpe, is a military principality north-west of Falador and north of Taverley. It's led by Crown Prince Anlaf and is home to the Burthorpe Imperial Guard, who defend the citadel standing between Burthorpe and Trollheim against trolls in the ongoing Burthorpe–Troll Country War.

Burthorpe is one of the only locations in Asgarnia that isn't directly controlled by the White Knights, who many of Burthorpe's residents believe are taking advantage of Asgarnia's King, the father of Prince Anlaf.

label: Burthorpe Castle
title: Burthorpe Castle
lead: Burthorpe Castle is the central feature of the principality of Burthorpe. Various houses and businesses are lined around the castle, and its lower level contains the Burthorpe Games Room.

label: Burthorpe Imperial Guard
title: Burthorpe Imperial Guard
lead:
The Burthorpe Imperial Guard is an elite military presence and the personal defence force for Prince Anlaf. As the guards of Burthorpe, they are actively engaged in a war with the mountain trolls of Death Plateau, who threaten to destroy the small military city and its neighbouring village of Taverley.

The guards can be found drilling and marching constantly in front of Burthorpe Castle. The Imperial Guard is funded by the White Knights, and according to Denulth, they are looking for an excuse to cut their funding, disband the Imperial Guard, and take control of Burthorpe.

label: Burthorpe Supplies
title: Burthorpe Supplies
lead: Burthorpe Supplies is a general store run by Wistan in Burthorpe. Aside from the shopkeeper, the ground floor has some boxes, a bookcase, and non-interactive shelves and crates. The upper floor has crates, tables, beds, a fireplace, and some bookcases that the player can search.

label: Burthorpe–Troll Country War
title: Burthorpe–Troll Country War
lead:
The Burthorpe–Troll Country War is a series of conflicts that occur between the Burthorpe Imperial Guard and the dangerous and aggressive mountain trolls of Death Plateau. It is of great importance for the Imperial Guard that Burthorpe, the last major settlement in Asgarnia with its own government, win the war in order to prove themselves. Otherwise the White Knights of Falador will take over the town, ending its semi-independence. The war consists mainly of small battles or invasions in and around the Burthorpe area.

The ongoing efforts of the Imperial Guard are lead by Commander Denulth while Crown Prince Anlaf remains in hiding.

label: Bush (The Dig Site)
title: Bush (The Dig Site)
lead: Many searchable bushes are found around the Digsite. One of them contains Teddy, while the rest contain nothing of interest.

label: Bush (Watchtower)
title: Bush (Watchtower)
lead: A large amount of Bushes can be found just north of the Watchtower. They can all be searched, with the majority of them containing nothing, but one contains fingernails which are used during the Watchtower quest. Four of the bushes also contain a Damaged dagger, a Tattered eye patch, an Old robe, and an Unusual armour, none of these items serve any purpose.

label: bush patch
title: bush patch
lead:
Bush patches are a Farming patch in which players can grow bushes that yield berries. Planting a bush requires using one bush seed on any patch. With the exception of poison ivy berries, bushes are also susceptible to disease.

When fully grown, its health must be checked before harvesting. Like fruit trees, calquat trees and cacti, bushes will continue to produce after harvesting. To remove a bush, use a spade on it to dig it up after harvesting. The yield scales with Farming level, with the minimum always being four unless harvested again before it has regrown all berries (within approximately 80 minutes).

Bust may refer to:

label: Butler Jones
title: Butler Jones
lead:
Butler Jones is the butler of the Carnillean family in East Ardougne. During the Hazeel Cult quest the player discovers that he is part of the cult of Hazeel. Should the player side with the Carnilleans against the cult, Butler Jones is arrested; if the player sides with the cultists, he remained with them to await further orders.

In Secrets of the North, should the player have sided with the Carnilleans, Jones' status becomes unknown to the cult. If they sided with the cult, Jones fled following Ceril's murder for reasons unknown, though the family guard believes that he was the prime suspect as Ceril was murdered in his room, which Hazeel found cowardly. Despite his attempts to flee, Jones is eventually apprehended by the authorities. If players sided with the cult, the guard later reveals that Jones was found dead in his cell after quest, having been killed by poison.

label: Butler uniform
title: Butler uniform
lead:
The butler costume consists of two items both named butler's costume which are obtained during the Death on the Isle quest. It can be stored in the Armour case of the costume room in a player-owned house.

If lost, both items can by entering the villa across from Aldrin General Store via its broken south window when the Wandering Guard is far away enough and taking the uniform from the wardrobe to the west of the window.

label: Butler's uniform
title: Butler's uniform
lead:
The butler's uniform consists of two items both named butler's uniform which are obtained during the Death on the Isle quest. It can be stored in the Armour case of the costume room in a player-owned house.

After completing the quest, the uniform can be reobtained from a wardrobe on the of Villa Lucens.

title: Butterfly

label: Butterfly (Hunter)
title: Butterfly (Hunter)
lead:
Butterflies and moths are a type of Hunter creature that can be caught while wielding a butterfly net or magic butterfly net. They can also be caught barehanded, which requires a Hunter level 10 above the normal requirement. Multiple players may attempt to catch a given butterfly at the same time.

When released (or caught without a butterfly jar in the inventory), butterflies will boost the player's combat skills. Catching a butterfly in a jar allows it to be stored away for later. In a multi-combat zone, jarred butterflies may be used on another player to share the effect with them and up to three players within a 5x5 area of the target. They can also be made into hunter's mixes, which affect the consuming player and up to three players within a 5x5 area of them. Players must have Accept Aid toggled on to receive the boost. Using jarred butterflies or hunter's mixes has no level requirements.

label: Butterfly (scenery)
title: Butterfly (scenery)
lead:
Butterflies are insects found throughout Gielinor, primarily in woodland areas.

Unlike other butterflies, they cannot be caught through Hunter. Players can command wily cats to chase them, though this does not reward anything.

label: Butterfly wing
title: Butterfly wing
lead:
Butterfly wings are rare creature parts that may be obtained as part of Hunters' Rumours. There are 5 types:
* Blue butterfly wing
* White butterfly wing
* Black butterfly wing
* Sunlight moth wing
* Moonlight moth wing

label: Buttons
title: Buttons
lead: Buttons are dropped by H.A.M. Guards, thieved from H.A.M. Members in the H.A.M. Hideout behind the Lumbridge General Store, earned from the Fishing Trawler minigame, dug up at the Digsite, or obtained from Ogre Coffins. Polishing them into polished buttons requires 3 Crafting, yielding 5 Crafting experience and the message: "You rub the buttons on your clothes and they become more shiny." Polished buttons are used in the Animal Magnetism quest. Without the required Crafting level the message says: "You rub the buttons on your clothes but they aren't improved by the process."

label: Byrne's Revolt
title: Byrne's Revolt
lead: Byrne's Revolt was a large-scale popular uprising seeking to overthrow Xeric launched and led by the labourer Byrne, who managed to put an end to the mage's hundred-year dominion over the kingdom just seven days after erupting on the 312th day of the 47th decade in Kourend's timeline. Byrne succeeded Xeric as monarch after fighting him back past the borders of the kingdom, prompting the latter's exile to Mount Quidamortem. Excerpts from Byrne's address to the people on the occasion of his victory can be found in Byrne's coronation speech as well as the eighth Chronicle of Xeric.

label: C. P. L-F. Carruthers, Esq (LLB)
title: C. P. L-F. Carruthers, Esq (LLB)
lead:
C. P. L-F. Carruthers, Esq (LLB) is the legal consultant for the weapons division of the renowned law firm Carruthers, Landsbottom and Og. Given that his name appears in the organisation's title, he is likely an important figure. In a Postbag from the Hedge, he replied to a query on behalf of the Consortium of Extra-Planar Merchandise Transferral Specialists.

He is known to own a dragon scimitar, whose special attack he used to kill a goblin trying to steal his pie.

label: Cabbage
title: Cabbage
lead:
A cabbage is a food item that can be picked from fields around Gielinor or grown through the Farming skill at level 7 with cabbage seeds. They heal 1 hitpoint when eaten. When picking cabbages from fields, members may randomly receive 1 cabbage seed.

When eaten, the message You eat the cabbage. Yuck! is displayed. When eaten while below full health, the message It heals some health anyway. is shown as well.

label: Cabbage (Draynor Manor)
title: Cabbage (Draynor Manor)
lead:
A cabbage picked at Draynor Manor is unlike other cabbages; it appears slightly darker, and when eaten, it restores 1 Hitpoint and grants a temporary skill boost to Defence. The item cannot be traded on the Grand Exchange and can only be obtained from one of seven cabbage plants located in between the west side of the house and the fence directly north of the farming patch on the minimap.

When eaten, the messages You eat the cabbage. and It seems to taste nicer than normal. are displayed.

label: Cabbage (scenery)
title: Cabbage (scenery)
lead: Cabbage plants can be picked to obtain cabbages. Rarely, a cabbage seed is awarded in place of a cabbage. Cabbages picked in a field will respawn after 40 to 80 ticks (24 to 48 seconds) depending on world population. Unlike cabbages picked from a Farming allotment, picking cabbages from fields provides no experience.

label: Cabin Boy Jenkins
title: Cabin Boy Jenkins
lead:
Cabin Boy Jenkins is a crew member on the Lady Lumbridge, a ship that a player buys during the Dragon Slayer I quest. Despite the ship's changing hands, Jenkins continued to serve aboard.

He comes with the player and Ned when the Lady Lumbridge sets sail towards to Crandor. However, nearing the island, Elvarg swoops out of the sky and attacks the ship. He is incinerated by Elvarg's dragonfire, along with much of the ship.

label: Cadantine
title: Cadantine
lead:
Clean cadantine is a high level herb. It is used to make super defence potions at level 66 Herblore. Players can obtain it by cleaning a Grimy cadantine at level 65 Herblore, which gives 12.5 Herblore experience for cleaning.

One way to obtain cadantine herbs is through farming Cadantine seeds which requires 67 Farming.

label: Cadantine potion (unf)
title: Cadantine potion (unf)
lead: A cadantine potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a cadantine on a vial of water, requiring 66 Herblore. Using white berries on a cadantine potion (unf) with 66 Herblore yields a super defence(3) and 150 Herblore experience.

label: Cadarn Clan
title: Cadarn Clan
lead: The Cadarn Clan is one of the eight elven clans who were originally brought to Gielinor from Tarddiad by Guthix and Seren in the early First Age. They were renowned for their military prestige, being especially skilled archers, warriors and hunters. They are located south-east of the Tower of Voices in Prifddinas, off the eastern path.

label: Cadava berries
title: Cadava berries
lead:
Cadava berries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting cadavaberry seeds or picked from wild cadava bushes. They are used as payment to protect cactus (x6).

The Apothecary in Varrock will exchange them for four-dose antipoison. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.

label: Cadava potion
title: Cadava potion
lead:
The cadava potion is a quest item used in Romeo & Juliet. It is made by giving Cadava berries to the Apothecary in Varrock. The Apothecary then supposedly adds four other ingredients in order to complete the potion: "Wing of rat, tail of frog. Ear of snake and horn of dog."

The cadava potion is used to fake Juliet's death so Romeo can meet her.

label: Cairn Isle
title: Cairn Isle
lead:
Cairn Isle is an island on the south-west of Karamja, south of Tai Bwo Wannai and west of Shilo Village. To access the island, players must scale a small promontory stood on the Karamjan coastline by climbing up a rockslide (requires 15 Agility), and then walk across the wooden bridge linking up the two islands. In case the player stumbles while climbing the rockslide, they will slide back down and take damage. If the player fails to keep their balance while crossing the bridge, they will fall off and be washed back to the shoreline of Karamja, again taking damage. It is advised to bring food if determined to make it to the island.

The chance of successfully crossing the bridge to Cairn Isle is dependent on the player's Agility level, scaling up to a 98% chance at a safe passage at level 99. Whether the player walks or runs across the bridges does not influence this skill check.

label: Cake
title: Cake
lead:
Cake is a type of food that restores 12 Hitpoints in total, 3 bites each healing for 4. It can be obtained by baking an uncooked cake on a cooking range, requiring level 40 Cooking and granting 180 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt cake. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.

Stealing a cake from the Ardougne Baker's Stall. is an easy Ardougne Diary task.

label: Cake tin
title: Cake tin
lead:
A cake tin is an item used to bake cakes. Players need to add an egg, a pot of flour and a bucket of milk on to the cake tin and used in an oven.

They can be found in the Cooks' Guild, bought from any general store (except for the ones in Port Phasmatys, Ardougne, Port Khazard, Canifis, Keldagrim, and Burthorpe), bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest in Lumbridge, or taken from the wooden shelves from a player-owned house. The cake tin also respawns at the house with an anvil in the level 21 Wilderness.

label: Calamity armour
title: Calamity armour
lead:
Calamity armour is a set of equipment once owned by the Calamity Coven, a trio of Zarosians who, through corruption and abuse of authority, tarnished the reputation of the once glorious Duel Arena. The armour they left behind can be obtained from equipment chests during a match in the now renovated Emir's Arena.

Calamity armour is weaker defensively than typical tank gear, and has lower Ranged and Magic accuracy than dragonhide armour and magic robes at the equivalent tier. The tradeoff here is that players will be able to focus exclusively on swapping out the headgear, rather than messing about switching multiple pieces of equipment. This means saving inventory space and extra clicks in already-intense battles, at the expense of losing out on defensive bonuses compared to opponents wearing the best setups for their build.

label: Calamity Coven
title: Calamity Coven
lead:
The Calamity Coven was a group of three women who were once responsible for running the Duel Arena, now known today as the Emir's Arena. Secretly followers of Zaros, the Calamity Coven stained the reputation of the once glorious Duel Arena, turning it into an immensely corrupt place where they used their positions to accumulate vast amounts of ill-gotten wealth.

Maoma the Corrupt Captain was the captain of the Emir's guard, and was assigned to oversee the fights at the Arena, ensuring that order was upheld. In reality, she abused her authority by taking bribes and rigged fights so that the Coven would get rich at the people's expense.
