label: Clue vessel
title: Clue vessel
lead:
Clue vessels are items obtained while skilling, which can be opened to obtain a clue scroll. Players can toggle whether or not they wish to receive clue vessels by talking to Arthur the Clue Hunter in Lumbridge. The following different types of clue vessels can be obtained:
* Clue bottles while Fishing
* Clue nests while Woodcutting
* Clue geodes while Mining

label: Coal
title: Coal
lead:
Coal can be mined at level 30 Mining providing 50 Mining experience. After coal rocks are mined, it will take 30 seconds until it reappears. Coal is required to smelt all ores above iron (other than gold, silver, lead, and nickel), in increasing amounts.

Members can store 27 pieces of coal in one inventory space by using a coal bag, obtained from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop for 100 golden nuggets at Motherlode Mine.

label: coal rocks
title: coal rocks
lead:
Coal rocks are a rock that contains coal. Players with a Mining level of 30 can mine coal rocks with a pickaxe, granting 50 Mining experience. Coal rocks can be found in numerous mines throughout Gielinor, most abundantly in the Mining Guild.

On rare occasions the rock may give an uncut sapphire, emerald, ruby, or diamond.

label: Coal Truck
title: Coal Truck
lead:
Coal Trucks are used to store coal, and are found by the Coal Trucks mine west of McGrubor's Wood and in the house north of the Forester's Arms Pub in Seers' Village. All coal trucks share the same storage, therefore any coal placed into a coal truck can be removed from any other coal truck. The coal trucks are mainly used by players to deposit the coal mined in the coal trucks mine, then when the coal trucks are full, the coal can be unloaded in Seers' Village and taken to the bank.

The maximum number of coal that can be stored in the coal trucks starts at 120, and increases to 140, 280, and 308 after the easy, medium and hard Kandarin Diaries. Additionally, after the completion of the elite Kandarin Diary, the first 200 coal placed into the coal trucks will automatically be transported to the player's bank.

label: Coal Trucks
title: Coal Trucks
lead:
The Coal Trucks are located north of the Fishing Guild and west of McGrubor's Wood. At the coal truck mining area, there are 18 coal rocks and several carts. Coal can be deposited into the trucks and later retrieved from any truck along the mine track, allowing players to collect and bank their coal from the depot at Seers' Village.

120 coal can be stored in the carts if no Kandarin achievement diaries have been completed, though 158, 280, or 308 pieces of coal can be stored in the trucks if the easy, medium, or hard diary is completed (respectively). With the elite diary, the first 200 coal removed in a day are automatically transported to the player's bank. Though the diary reward says placed, you must first place then attempt to remove the coal from the coal truck to initiate transfer to your bank. An exploit currently exists in which a player can transport 27 additional coal if the trucks are filled up to one less than full, then an entire inventory of coal is placed in the cart.

label: Cockatrice (interface item)
title: Cockatrice (interface item)
lead:
The Cockatrice is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Cockatrice

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Cocktail glass
title: Cocktail glass
lead: Empty cocktail glasses are used to make Gnome cocktails. They can be bought from Heckel Funch in the Grand Tree. There is also a respawn right next to him. They can also be obtained by drinking gnome cocktails or a poison chalice.

label: Cocktail guide
title: Cocktail guide
lead:
The cocktail guide has a collection of recipes for the various gnome cocktails for you to make. It's useful for the Gnome Restaurant minigame or if you just want to make the cocktails for yourself.

You can get the book from Blurberry, Heckel Funch, Rasolo, or from the bookcase in your house. The book will not be available in your bookcase until completing the mixing tutorial with Blurberry.

label: cocktail shaker
title: cocktail shaker
lead:
A cocktail shaker is an item used in Gnome cooking to make cocktails. It can be purchased from Grand Tree Groceries or Funch's Fine Groceries in the Grand Tree for coins, or through dialogue with the Blurberry Bar barmen for coins. One also spawns in Grand Tree Groceries.

Ingredients can not be used on the shaker directly; the "mix-cocktail" option opens an interface where players must click "create" to make the drink. Doing so will create an intermediate mixed drink, still in the shaker, which can then be poured into a cocktail glass while having the appropriate garnish in the inventory.

label: Cocoon
title: Cocoon
lead: Cocoons are objects that can be found in the section of the Kalphite Lair where the Kalphite Queen is found. label: Cod
title: Cod
lead:
Cod is a type of fish that restores 7 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw cod on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 18 Cooking and granting 75 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cod is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 51 on a fire, 49 on a range, or 46 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cod is used as an ingredient in fish pie which requires Cooking level 47 to make.

label: Code of Conduct
title: Code of Conduct
lead:
The Code of Conduct (also called the Rules of Old School RuneScape) is part of the terms and conditions of playing Old School RuneScape. When players make an account, they agree to be bound by the rules and to face punishment (i.e. a ban or a mute) if they do not abide by them.
Jagex's Customer Support team may apply a variety of sanctions against rule breakers, up to a permanent account ban. Lesser offences may result in a warning, temporary ban, or a temporary or permanent mute.

Keeping your account's offences to a minimum contributes to a greater chance of successfully becoming a Player Moderator. If you feel that someone is violating one of the Rules of RuneScape, you can report the offending player using the "Report Abuse" button below the chatbox on the lower-right hand side.

label: Coin pouch glitch
title: Coin pouch glitch
lead:
The coin pouch glitch was a major glitch that occurred after a game update on 12 July 2018.

The code which handles death in game was changed in the update in order to accommodate the coin pouch, but was done incorrectly and wasn't set up to handle stacks of other items, which caused certain items in a player's inventory to become a stack of coins. This is the maximum value a 32-bit signed integer can take, which is the data type RuneScape uses for item quantity.

Coins (also referred to as gold pieces, gp, gold, or simply money) are the most common form of currency in Gielinor. They are used among players and non-player characters alike to exchange for items and services.

Players often refer to one thousand (1,000) coins as 1k and one million (1,000,000) coins as 1m or 1mil. Both can be applied to larger numbers, for example, 10m refers to ten million coins (10,000,000). 1b or 1bil refers to one billion coins (1,000,000,000).

label: Combat Achievements
title: Combat Achievements
lead:
Combat Achievements (commonly abbreviated as CA) are a set of combat-based tasks and challenges released on 21 July 2021. They are intended to test the player's prowess in combat related content, ranging from endurance challenges, killing monsters under a set time limit, and restriction based tasks in which players must kill a monster in a specific manner.

The overview interface for Combat Achievements can be accessed via the Character Summary tab. An overview of bosses can additionally be visited from the Combat Achievements interface.

lead:

For a list of all tasks sorted by boss, see Combat Achievements/Tasks by boss. For a list of all tasks sorted by region, see Combat Achievements/Tasks by region.

label: Combat Achievements/Bosses
title: Combat Achievements/Bosses
lead:
This page shows the overview of each boss as viewed in the in-game Combat Achievements Bosses interface.

Each boss has links pointing to their Combat Achievements task list, where they are located on the world map, and their respective wiki articles. Each one also lists a combat level (in case of raids showing the final boss's level), the player's HiScores kill count, and optionally their personal best time in killing the boss; this personal best can be reset.

label: Combat Achievements/Easy
title: Combat Achievements/Easy
lead: Easy Combat Achievements tasks do not require any significant skill levels to complete, typically involving tasks to kill a low amount of a boss or basic tasks involving killing a monster in a specific manner.

label: Combat Achievements/Elite
title: Combat Achievements/Elite
lead:
Elite Combat Achievements tasks require the player to have high combat levels, having high-level equipment available, as well as good knowledge of dealing with boss mechanics in addition to doing so under difficult restrictions to complete. Speed-based tasks and tasks for raids begin to appear as well.

Non-boss monsters may also have elite tasks, but these are fairly easy tasks, such as killing them for the first time or taking advantage of simple mechanics.

title: Combat Achievements/Free-to-play
lead:

Players without membership cannot claim any rewards or fully complete any tier of the achievements.

label: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster
title: Combat Achievements/Grandmaster
lead:
Grandmaster Combat Achievements tasks require the highest combat levels, the best equipment available, and precise, in-depth knowledge of a boss's mechanics, with the ability to skillfully kill said bosses and deal with their mechanics perfectly without mistakes.
__TOC__

label: Combat Achievements/Hard
title: Combat Achievements/Hard
lead:

__TOC__

label: Combat Achievements/Master
title: Combat Achievements/Master
lead:
Master Combat Achievements tasks require the highest combat levels, some of the best equipment available, and advanced knowledge of a boss's mechanics, with the ability to skillfully kill said bosses and deal with their mechanics with precision, especially within raids.

Very rarely, non-boss monsters may have master-tier combat achievements.
__TOC__

title: combat level
lead:
A player's, monster's, or non-player character's combat level indicates the difficulty in defeating them in combat. For some bosses and most monsters it is reflective of their actual stats as well.

Normally, aggressive non-player characters stop attacking you when you reach higher than double their combat level. There are exceptions, however - for example, almost any monsters, except for Rats, in the Wilderness will be aggressive no matter what your combat level is.

label: Combat only pure
title: Combat only pure
lead:
A combat only pure, or reverse skiller, is a type of pure that only develops combat skills and the Slayer skill. Combat pures keep their skilling stats at level 1, leaving them with a max total level of 808. This makes it more challenging to acquire gear or progress the account as some regions of Gielinor are not accessible, and some content or gear requires quests with skilling involved.

A combat only account type can be played on any game mode but it is most recommended as a Hardcore Ironman, Regular Ironman, or Ultimate Ironman. Each mode will bring their own unique flavour to how a combat only pure progresses their account. As a reminder to those who choose Ultimate Ironman, it is possible to "downgrade" an Ultimate Ironman to a normal Ironman or main account by talking to the Ironman tutor in Lumbridge.

Combat spells are a type of magic spell used by players, mostly in battle, for their offensive capabilities. Combat spells can be separated into three sub-types. The first type of spells, offensive spells, are primarily used to deal magical damage against opponents. The second type, curse spells, are used to disable or debilitate an opponent, and make dealing damage easier or safer for the mage casting them. Finally, there are support spells, which offer a range of benefits to the caster, such as preventing damage, curing poison, and healing other players.

label: Combat triangle
title: Combat triangle
lead:
Old School RuneScape follows the combat triangle, a design philosophy dictating that melee tends to be effective against rangers, ranged tends to be effective against mages, and magic tends to be strong against warriors. This philosophy manifests in the combat bonuses of armour and weapons, the ability of ranged and magic to attack from a distance or safespot, and weapon/armour/spell effects (such as the twisted bow's increased damage against monsters with high magic level.)

In terms of bonuses, melee armour tends to excel in melee defence and ranged defence; ranged armour tends to have substantial ranged attack, high magic defence, and middling melee and ranged defences; and magic armour tends to offer magic attack bonuses and middling magic defence, but little to no ranged or melee defence.

label: Combination
title: Combination
lead:
The combination is an item used in the Death Plateau quest. It is obtained by inspecting the Iou given to the player by Harold in lieu of paying a gambling debt he owes from losing a dice rolling game.

The combination is a cryptic list of clues that give the relative locations of a set of coloured stone balls that must be positioned on a device which locks and unlocks the equipment room in Burthorpe Castle. If lost, the combination can be obtained by talking to Harold again.

label: combination rune
title: combination rune
lead:
A combination rune is any rune made of two other types of rune. A unique combination rune exists for every potential combination of two basic elemental runes, as well as one of catalytic runes (aether runes being soul and cosmic).

Combination runes simultaneously count as one of each type of the runes required to make them. When the player casts a spell with combination runes in their inventory, it will prioritise using those runes first, even while having sufficient runes otherwise.

label: Commander Montai
title: Commander Montai
lead: Commander Montai is the commander of the Gnomic defence at the Khazard Battlefield north of the Tree Gnome Village. Montai directs the battle from behind the trenches at the front line, wearing a red helmet and chestpiece to show his importance. To help ensure victory for his forces on the battlefield against the forces of General Khazard, he has enlisted the help of an adventurer to help him to fix a ballista and retrieve coordinates for the attack from three gnome trackers during the Tree Gnome Village quest. Commander Montai has also ordered the addition of the Tortoise Regiment led by Lieutenant Schepbur. He is spoken to mainly during the Tree Gnome Village quest, but he can be spoken to after the quest as well, where the player will inquire as to how the battle is going, to which he will reply "We're hanging in there, soldier.".

label: Community Event
title: Community Event
lead:
Community Events are special, limited-time game modes that operate in dedicated worlds, similarly to Leagues, and allow players to try new types of gameplay. During Community Events, players earn points which can later be spent at shops on regular worlds. Future Community Events will all access the same Events Reward Shop, and all past rewards will be available for purchase after each event.

The idea of Community Events dates back to 2022, when Jagex began considering a "bingo-type minigame" that would repurpose systems developed for Leagues. After Project Zanaris was indefinitely suspended in 2025, the concept evolved into today's Community Events, and development of the first event began.

They fire at a slightly faster speed than longbows and also have slightly higher accuracy, but they are notably harder to obtain as they are only found from Treasure Trails and cannot be made by Fletching (with the exception of the comp ogre bow). The Crystal bow can be considered a composite bow, given its speed and range, but it generates its own ammo and degrades unlike the others.

The bin functions identically to other compost bins and can be used to create compost, supercompost, ultracompost, and rotten tomatoes. The Port Phasmatys compost bin differs from other compost bins only in appearance, being formed of green coloured wood that matches the swamp setting of Morytania.

Using a bucket on the compost heap returns the message: This compost has sat here for too long - I should make some fresh compost myself.

label: Confuse
title: Confuse
lead:
Confuse is a low-level Magic spell. When cast on an opponent, their Attack level is reduced by 5%. The spell gives experience whether it hits or misses, making it a popular way to gain experience cheaply. The spell can only be cast if an opponent's stats haven't already been lowered, meaning you can not stack stat-reduction with multiple spells in a row.

The spell grants 13 Magic experience and requires three water, two earth, and one body rune in order to be cast.

label: Cook (Lumbridge)
title: Cook (Lumbridge)
lead:
The cook is the head cook of Lumbridge Castle. He usually seems unprepared, but with the player's help, he prepares great food. He is the starting point for the Cook's Assistant and Recipe for Disaster quests. He can be found in the Lumbridge Castle kitchen on the .

When the Cook's Assistant quest is completed, the player is granted use of his special range, which has a lower chance of burning certain foods compared to other ranges.

label: Cook's Assistant
title: Cook's Assistant
lead: Cook's Assistant is the first RuneScape quest ever released and one of the six quests available during the game's launch. In the quest, the player must help the cook of Lumbridge Castle make a birthday cake for Duke Horacio.

label: Cooked chicken
title: Cooked chicken
lead:
Cooked chicken is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw chicken on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt chicken. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked chicken is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked chicken does not require a cooking level to cook, and can be used as an ingredient to make a stew or curry. It is an easily obtainable early food source, as killing chickens at the Lumbridge East Farm is a common activity for a low level player.

label: Cooked chompy
title: Cooked chompy
lead:
Cooked chompy is an ogre delicacy obtained by skewering a raw chompy with an iron spit, then cooking the skewered chompy on a fire, requiring level 30 Cooking and granting 100 experience when successful. Players may burn the chompy while cooking one, resulting in a ruined chompy; the burn rate while cooking these will decrease as players reach higher Cooking levels. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 99.

Cooked chompy heals 10 Hitpoints. If hunting chompy birds, due to the meat's weight of 10 kg, it is recommended to do so south-west of Castle Wars. Big Chompy Bird Hunting is required to hunt them.

label: Cooked meat
title: Cooked meat
lead:
Cooked meat is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking various raw meats on a fire or cooking range, granting 30 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt meat. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Cooked meat is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 34, or 31 when using the Lumbridge range.

Cooked meat is used in the making of stews, pies, and steak sandwiches, or as a topping on pizzas.

label: cooked oomlie wrap
title: cooked oomlie wrap
lead:
Cooked oomlie wrap is a food made from cooking a wrapped oomlie. It heals 14 Hitpoints when eaten, and gives the message "You eat the oomlie meat; it tastes very gamy."

Cooked oomlie wraps can be cooked with a Cooking level of 50 or higher, granting 30 Cooking experience.

label: Cooking
title: Cooking
lead:
Cooking is a skill that allows raw food to be made edible, healing hitpoints when eaten. To do this, the player uses a raw, cookable food on a range or fire.

Depending on the player's Cooking level, food will sometimes burn, becoming unusable. Ranges burn food less often than fires at the same level, and some foods can only be cooked on ranges. Some ranges, such as the one in the Lumbridge Castle or in the Hosidius Kitchen, burn food less often than a normal range.

label: Cooking apple
title: Cooking apple
lead:
Cooking apples are primarily used as an ingredient to make apple pies. They can be obtained from the Cooks' Guild, Culinaromancer's Chest, Logava Gricoller's Cooking Supplies, or alternatively, harvested from an apple tree grown from an apple tree seed in a fruit tree patch by a player with a Farming level of 27.

Baskets of apples (which contain 5 apples each) can be used in the Farming skill to pay farmers to watch planted trees. One basket is needed to watch willows and strawberries, while four baskets are needed to watch a banana tree.

label: Cooking gauntlets
title: Cooking gauntlets
lead:
Cooking gauntlets are a pair of gloves available after completing the Family Crest quest, along with the goldsmith and chaos gauntlets. They can be worn to significantly decrease the likelihood of burning lobsters, swordfish, cooked kyatt, monkfish, sharks, and anglerfish when cooking them. They do not work on other types of food.

In order to obtain this enchantment on your Family Crest gauntlets, one must bring the steel gauntlets that were rewarded from the quest to Caleb in or around the house north of the archery shop in Catherby. (Note: if your gauntlets have a different enchantment on them already, Caleb will charge you 25,000 coins). If the gauntlets are destroyed or lost due to death, these gauntlets may be re-obtained free of charge from Dimintheis in south-east Varrock and will have the same enchantment on them.

One cooking pot appears in the eastern farm house of Lumbridge conveniently close to cows and chickens so that the player may cook their meat drops to recover health when training on them.

As a result, it served no purpose and could not be seen or obtained by players during normal gameplay until the skill guide summaries update in 26 March 2025.

label: Cooking range (Lumbridge Castle)
title: Cooking range (Lumbridge Castle)
lead:
This Cooking range, referred to as the Cook-o-matic 100 by the Lumbridge Cook (more commonly referred to as the Lumbridge Castle Range or simply the Cook's range) is a special range, located in the kitchen, on the of the Lumbridge Castle.

It is notable as it improves the chances of cooking certain foods, especially mushroom and botanical pies. This makes it particularly helpful for players without access to other special cooking ranges, or a cooking cape.

label: Cooks' Guild
title: Cooks' Guild
lead:
The Cooks' Guild (also known as the Cooking Guild or the Chefs' Guild) is a guild for master chefs located in a three-story windmill west of Varrock. To enter the guild, players need at least 32 Cooking and must wear one of the following:
*A chef's hat or golden chef's hat
*A Cooking cape or Cooking hood
*A Max cape or Max hood, or any of their variants
*Varrock armour 3 or 4 (reward from completing the hard or elite Varrock Diary)

Players may remove these items while they are inside the guild without being kicked out.

label: Copper ore
title: Copper ore
lead: Copper ore can be mined at level 1 Mining providing 17.5 Mining experience. After mining copper rocks, it will take 2.4 seconds until it reappears. Copper ore is used with tin ore to smelt bronze bars, or used with nickel ore to smelt Cupronickel bars. Smelting a bronze bar gives 6.2 Smithing experience.

label: copper rocks
title: copper rocks
lead:
Copper rocks are a type of rock that contains copper ore; they can be mined with a Mining level of 1. They are one of the first rocks that can be mined, along with tin rocks. Each time a player successfully mines a copper rock, they gain 17.5 Mining experience.

Mining 14 tin ore and 14 copper ore (wielding the pickaxe as a weapon to free the 28th inventory space) and smelting them to bronze bars is a slow but accessible way to train Mining and Smithing, especially in free-to-play worlds.

label: cormorant
title: cormorant
lead:
Cormorants are a species of large bird native to many coastal regions including Karamja, Fossil Island and Hosidius, and are often found alongside Pelicans. They are carnivorous and feed mainly on fish. Most cormorants cannot be fought or interacted with in any way, essentially making them scenery.

A certain kind of cormorant can be used for aerial fishing, a Hunter technique similar to falconry practiced by Alry the Angler on the small island in Lake Molch. These cormorants will require either some fish offcuts, fine fish offcuts , or king worms on a regular basis to catch fish for the player.

label: Corruption (status)
title: Corruption (status)
lead:
Corruption is a temporary status effect that causes the player to lose a set amount of prayer points over a short time, indicated by a hitsplat ( ) displaying the amount of prayer points that has been drained.
The severity of the corruption is dependent on the type of corruption spells used by the player, which have a 50% chance of inflicting the status on their next successful hit.
* Lesser Corruption drains 6 prayer points over the course of 30 ticks (18s). The first drains 1 prayer point, the second 2 prayer points, and the third drains 3 points.
* Greater Corruption drains 12 prayer points over the course of 30 ticks (18s). The first drains 2 prayer points, the second 4 prayer points, and the third drains 6 prayer points.

Players who become corrupted by another player who has the Mark of Darkness spell active will have corruption occur every 5 ticks instead of 10.

label: Corruption spells
title: Corruption spells
lead:
Corruption spells are a category of offensive spells in the Arceuus spellbook. Requiring completion of A Kingdom Divided to use, these spells provide a chance to inflict corruption on the caster's next successful hit. If a player with corruption spells active attacks an opposing player with Ward of Arceuus active, the attacker's corruption spells will remain active until the target's Ward expires, after which the next successful attack post-expiration will roll the chance for corruption.

Players cannot corrupt a player if they are currently corrupted, nor can they do so while the target is under the effects of the Ward of Arceuus spell. There is no immunity period after corruption wears off on a player. If the caster is under the effect of Mark of Darkness, the corruption has 100% chance to work on the player's next successful hit, up from a 50% chance.

lead:
Corveth was a follower of Zaros. During the Battle of Carrallanger, she was nearly consumed by flames; however, Ablenkian the Dragon rider and his dragon Hekala rescued her.

For unknown reasons, Corveth turned against Ablenkian after Zaros' fall, and hunted down him and his dragon with Ripper Demons. A depiction of these events are accounted firsthand in Ablenkian's escape.

label: Cosmic Altar
title: Cosmic Altar
lead:
The Cosmic Altar is a runic altar upon which cosmic runes are crafted from pure essence, providing 8 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Level 27 Runecraft and completion of the Lost City quest is required to craft cosmic runes.

Players may create a cosmic tiara here by using either a cosmic talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 40 Runecraft experience. A catalytic tiara can also be created here by using a catalytic talisman and gold tiara, granting 60 Runecraft experience.

label: Cosmic rune
title: Cosmic rune
lead:
The cosmic rune is a rune used primarily in enchanting spells. Enchanting spells enchant jewellery, such as rings and amulets, into something that has an effect when worn or operated. For example, when the player casts Lvl-4 Enchant on a diamond ring, the ring will become a ring of life. Cosmic runes are also used for the Lunar spells NPC Contact, Cure Me, Cure Group, and Spellbook Swap and for the resurrection spells in the Arceuus spellbook.

They can be crafted at the Cosmic Altar in Zanaris through the Runecraft skill at level 27 for 8 experience per pure essence after the Lost City quest. They can also be purchased at Lundail's Arena-side Rune Shop in the Mage Arena in the Wilderness, Amlodd's Magical Supplies in Prifddinas after completing Song of the Elves, or from Ali Morrisane after completing The Feud and the Rogue Trader miniquest. At level 59 Runecraft, the amount crafted doubles to two cosmic runes per pure essence. Twisted extracts can also be used to increase the quantity of crafted cosmic runes by 60 per pure essence, requiring partial completion of Desert Treasure II and access to the Scar essence mine.

label: Cosmic talisman
title: Cosmic talisman
lead:
A cosmic talisman is a talisman needed to enter the Cosmic Altar in the southern part of Zanaris. It can be combined with a tiara to make a cosmic tiara for 40 Runecraft experience at the Cosmic Altar by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn. Both the tiara and the talisman allow players to craft cosmic runes at level 27 Runecraft.

To enter the altar the player needs to have completed the Lost City quest or Enter the Abyss if using the Abyss.

label: Cosy Cabin
title: Cosy Cabin
lead:
Cosy Cabin is a house style option for a player-owned house. It is awarded to players after completing Christmas events and requires level 1 Construction. It was originally awarded from completing the 2020 Christmas event.

Players can purchase this house style enhancement from the estate agent for 35,000 gold. It is currently the most expensive housing style available, along with deathly mansion and the Civitas style.

label: Council of Elders
title: Council of Elders
lead:
The Council of Elders was a group formed by the five houses of Great Kourend that rebelled against King Rada III, during the 6th BA an event known as the Rebellion of the Five Houses. They included members from the Arceuus, Hosidius, Lovakengj, Piscarilius, and Shayzien houses, and they used the Tower of Magic as a meeting place.

Sometime during their reign, a famine struck Great Kourend. This resulted in Lord Hosidius writing to the council requesting half the land of each of the other four houses, as agreed to by the other lords, so that Hosidius could grow enough food to stop the famine. The council granted the request, and the famine ended sometime after.

lead: Councillor Halgrive is a councillor in the Ardougne City Council responsible for public health and safety in East Ardougne. He can be found outside the East Ardougne church.

label: Count
title: Count
lead:
Count may refer to:

*Count Check
*Count Check (random event)
*Count Draynor

label: Count Draynor
title: Count Draynor
lead:
Count Draynor Drakan lives in a coffin in the basement of Draynor Manor. He was part of House Drakan, being the younger brother of Lowerniel, Ranis and Vanescula Drakan.

He can be fought in the Nightmare Zone after the quest Vampyre Slayer is complete. A stake is not necessary to kill him in the Nightmare Zone, as he will automatically die upon reaching 0 health.

label: counter
title: counter
lead: Counters can be found inside various shops, and serve no practical purpose. They can be used as a table by putting items on top of them.

label: Counter (Gu'Tanoth)
title: Counter (Gu'Tanoth)
lead: A counter can be found in Gu'Tanoth's market. At level 15 Thieving, and after partial completion of the Watchtower quest, players may steal rock cakes from it. Each successful steal awards 6.4 Thieving experience.

label: Counter (The Toad and Chicken)
title: Counter (The Toad and Chicken)
lead: A counter can be found inside The Toad and Chicken bar in Burthorpe, an Asgarnian ale and a beer glass spawn on it. It looks almost identical to most other counters found in Gielinor, except it is slightly slimmer. The counter functions as a table, allowing for items to be put on it.

label: Courier tasks
title: Courier tasks
lead:
Courier tasks are a type of port task where players deliver crates of cargo between two ports. A task has the following steps:

#Visit a notice board to choose a task.
#Collect cargo from the ledger table (both hands must be free). Some tasks require more than one crate, so multiple trips to the boat may be required.
#Load the cargo hold on a boat with all the crates of cargo.
#Sail to the destination.
#Withdraw all the crates from the cargo hold and deposit them at the ledger table.

label: Cove
title: Cove
lead:
Cove may refer to:

**Corsair Cove Dungeon
**Corsair Cove Resource Area

*Pirates' Cove
*Reeking Cove, a section in the Catacombs of Kourend and Ancient shard teleport option.
*Tempoross Cove

label: cow
title: cow
lead:
Cows are common low level monsters new players train on. They are one of the first NPCs new players see outside of Lumbridge. Cows can help new players earn money, Cooking experience, and combat experience. The cowhides that they drop can be tanned to make leather or hard leather, or they can be sold for coins to players wanting to raise their Crafting level.

While most locations containing cows are crowded, there are some spots usually vacant, like the spot north of the windmill north-west of Lumbridge. Along with cows, you can also find cow calves and dairy cows. Regular cows cannot be milked; attempting to do so using a bucket will display the message Only dairy cows are suitable for milking..

label: cow outfit
title: cow outfit
lead:
The cow outfit is a holiday reward received from Old School RuneScape ' s birthday events. The costume gives no bonus to any stats.

If lost or destroyed, the outfit can be reclaimed from Diango in Draynor Village. In addition, all of the costume items may be stored in the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: cowhide
title: cowhide
lead:
Cowhides are dropped by cows or undead cows when they are killed. If it is brought to a tanner, it can be turned into soft leather for 1 coin or hard leather for 3 coins. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Forthos Dungeon, Canifis, Auburnvale, Neitiznot, Kebos Lowlands, and the Crafting Guild. Soft and hard leathers can then be crafted into various pieces of equipment through the Crafting skill.

It is also used alongside a unicorn horn to generate a unicow in the Tower of Life.

label: Crab trapping
title: Crab trapping
lead: Crab trapping is a Hunter activity in which players trap crabs in permanently-built traps. Unlike other methods, players cannot fail to catch a crab.

label: Crack
title: Crack
lead: Crack colloquially refers to Smelling salts. It may also refer to:

label: Crack the Clue
title: Crack the Clue
lead:
Crack the Clue! was a special clue-seeker event held over the course of four weeks during 2016, where map clues were released on a RuneScape Forums post.

Completion of each clue will grant players pieces of the clue hunter outfit. This event will stay in-game indefinitely.

label: Crack the Clue II
title: Crack the Clue II
lead:
Crack the Clue II is a clue-seeker event which was officially announced after the 6th birthday stream on 22 February 2019. It is a sequel to the original Crack the Clue event, and will similarly stay in the game indefinitely.

Completion of each clue will grant players pieces of the ornate armour.

label: Crack the Clue III
title: Crack the Clue III
lead:
Crack the Clue III is a clue-seeker event available in-game since 23 September 2022. This event will stay in-game indefinitely, similar to the previous Crack the Clue events (I, II).

Completion of Crack the Clue III will grant players pieces of the Robes of Ruin and the infinite money bag. For instructions on how to acquire them, see here.

label: Cracked Jenny's Tea Cup
title: Cracked Jenny's Tea Cup
lead: Cracked Jenny's Tea Cup is a parrot that sits on Cap'n Izzy No-Beard's shoulder, occasionally adding something into the conversation.

label: Cracked sample
title: Cracked sample
lead: A cracked sample is found whilst digging in training digs or searching the chests in the Exam Centre south of the Digsite. If the certification exam has been completed, it can be smashed with a rock pick causing it to disintegrate. It is a useless item; there are no uses for it, it is untradeable, and it is worth nothing.

label: Crafting
title: Crafting
lead:
Crafting is a skill that allows players to create items such as jewellery, pottery, and armour for use or for trade.

The Crafting Guild is located north-west of Rimmington and can be entered at level 40 Crafting while wearing a brown apron.

label: Crafting blood runes
title: Crafting blood runes
lead:
Crafting blood runes may refer to:

*Crafting blood runes in Zeah
*Crafting blood runes at the true Blood Altar

label: Crafting Guild
title: Crafting Guild
lead:
The Crafting Guild is located south-west of Falador and north of Rimmington. It provides top-notch workshops for accomplished crafters. A Crafting level of 40 is required to enter the guild as well as wearing one of the following:

*A brown or golden apron
*A Crafting cape
*A Max cape or any of its variants

label: Crafting Guild mine
title: Crafting Guild mine
lead:
The Crafting Guild mine is a mine accessible only to players who can gain entry to the Crafting Guild. In order to access the guild, players must have at least 40 Crafting and wear either a brown or golden apron, or a Crafting or Max cape.

The nearest bank and furnace are in Falador. Members with level 26 Agility can take a shortcut tunnel under the city wall and go up the west side of the moat. Members who own a crafting cape or have completed at least the hard Falador Diary can access a bank chest and bank deposit box next to the mine, allowing them to bank ore in the guild.

label: Crafting Level Up!
title: Crafting Level Up!
lead: Crafting Level Up! is a Jingle for leveling crafting.

title: Crafting Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Crafting Level Up! (Unlocks) is a jingle for levelling Crafting.

title: crafting shops
lead: A Crafting shop is a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a Icon. Crafting shops sell items used in Crafting. There are 11 Crafting shops in Old School RuneScape.

lead: Below you will find lists of the different actions available through the Crafting skill, with their expected profits.

label: Crandor
title: Crandor
lead:
Crandor is a small volcanic island north of Karamja. Players gain access to the island during Dragon Slayer I, when the Guildmaster tasks them with defeating the mighty dragon Elvarg, who terrorizes the island.

Players are unable to sail to Crandor themselves, as the jagged underwater reef surrounding the island make it impossible for boats of all types to safely approach it. Only boats of Crandorian design, like the Lady Lumbridge, are capable of handling the reefs.

label: Crandor and Karamja Dungeon
title: Crandor and Karamja Dungeon
lead: The Karamja Dungeon is located underneath the Karamja Volcano, and the Crandor Dungeon is located underneath Crandor. Both dungeons are connected to each other. In order for a player to gain full access to the Crandor dungeon, they must have completed or be about to engage in the final fight in the quest Dragon Slayer I. No part of the dungeons are multicombat zones.

label: Crandor map
title: Crandor map
lead:
The Crandor map is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is made by using any two pieces on each other when all three map parts are in the inventory.

It is given to Ned so he can sail the player to Crandor.

label: Crane
title: Crane
lead:
Crane may refer to:
*Fishing Cranes, which can be repaired in Piscarilius for Construction experience
*Crane claw, an item made in the Elemental Workshop II quest
*Crane schematic, used to make the crane claw in the Elemental Workshop II quest
*Loading cranes, hazards during the final fight of the Haunted Mine quest
*Crane (Sea Slug), used during the Sea Slug quest

label: Crane (Sea Slug)
title: Crane (Sea Slug)
lead:
A crane is found on the of the Fishing Platform. After kicking down the badly repaired wall during the Sea Slug quest, players must rotate the crane which initiates a cutscene where they lower Kennith to the platform below.

Once the cutscene is completed, players are not able to rotate the crane, providing a message saying: Maybe I shouldn't be playing with that...

lead:

label: Crashed glider
title: Crashed glider
lead: A crashed glider is a gnome glider that has crashed. One can be found on Karamja and just west of the Digsite, two are located in the Underground Military Glider Hangar, and ten can be found on and around Crash Island.

label: Crashing
title: Crashing
lead:
Crashing may refer to:

*An item plummeting in price, similar to a .
*A player using a spot already in use by another player, sometimes coincides with griefing.
*A problem with the Old School RuneScape game client, such as lag or an unexpected server blackout.

label: Crate
title: Crate
lead:
Crates can be found in many buildings across Gielinor. Crates serve almost no purpose, apart from being used during some Treasure Trails. Clues for Treasure Trails are often hidden inside of them. For example, a clue might say something such as "Search the crate in a house in Varrock." Crates are also used in a few quests.

Strangely, crates cannot be shot over using ranged or magic.

label: crate (Biohazard)
title: crate (Biohazard)
lead: A crate containing a distillator can be found in the storeroom on the of the Mourner Headquarters. The crate is located third from the left on the north side of the storeroom. During the Biohazard quest, the player must search the crate to find a distillator to give to Elena. To access the storeroom in which the crate is found, players must first obtain a key by killing a Mourner in order to unlock the gate. Multiple distillators can be obtained from the crate by drop tricking, however, duplicates will be removed once the player provides one to Elena.

label: Crate (Desert Mining Camp)
title: Crate (Desert Mining Camp)
lead: Crates can be found within the Desert Mining Camp. Searching the crates yields nothing, with the exception of the crate next to the wooden cart during a medium Treasure Trails step providing another clue or a reward casket.

label: Crate (Dwarf Cannon)
title: Crate (Dwarf Cannon)
lead:
The crate is found in the north-western part of the Goblin Cave and must be searched during the Dwarf Cannon quest, in order to find the dwarf child Lollk.

There is a small chance to either receive an uncut red topaz, or spawn an aggressive chicken, rat, or spider whilst searching the crate outside of the quest.

label: Crate (Elemental Workshop I, leather)
title: Crate (Elemental Workshop I, leather)
lead: The crate is scenery found in the north-western part of the entrance room in the Elemental Workshop. It may be searched once for a piece of leather during the Elemental Workshop I quest. It cannot be searched for leather after completion of the quest.

label: Crate (Elemental Workshop I, needle)
title: Crate (Elemental Workshop I, needle)
lead: The crate is scenery found in the north-western corner of the entrance room in the Elemental Workshop. It is able to be searched once for a needle during the Elemental Workshop I quest. It cannot be searched for a needle after completion of the quest, however a different crate within the workshop is able to searched after starting the Elemental Workshop II quest.

label: Crate (Elemental Workshop)
title: Crate (Elemental Workshop)
lead: The crate is scenery found in the north-western corner of the entrance room to the Elemental Workshop. It is able to be searched for a needle after starting the Elemental Workshop II quest, if the player does not have one in their inventory.

label: Crate (Food Store, banana)
title: Crate (Food Store, banana)
lead:
The crate is located at the back of Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim. Searching the crate gives players the option to take a banana. Players can take as many as they want from the crate, one at a time.

During Pirate's Treasure, the player smuggles a karamjan rum into a crate of bananas which is delivered to Wydin's store, where they must retrieve the rum from the crate.

label: Crate (Food Store, cabbage)
title: Crate (Food Store, cabbage)
lead:
The crate is located at the back of Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim. Searching the crate gives players the option to take a cabbage. Players can take as many as they want from the crate, one at a time.

Access to the back of the Food Store requires partial completion of Pirate's Treasure and a white apron equipped.

label: Crate (Food Store, potato)
title: Crate (Food Store, potato)
lead:
The crate is located at the back of Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim. Searching the crate gives players the option to take a potato. Players can take as many as they want from the crate, one at a time.

Access to the back of the Food Store requires partial completion of Pirate's Treasure and a white apron equipped.

label: crate (Gertrude's Cat)
title: crate (Gertrude's Cat)
lead: Six crates can be found around the Sawmill east of Varrock. During the quest Gertrude's Cat, the player must search these crates to find Gertrude's three missing kittens. All three kittens are in one crate, and the crate in which the kittens can be found in is different for every player.

label: Crate (Goblin Cave)
title: Crate (Goblin Cave)
lead:
Crates are scenery found within the Goblin Cave. They can be searched for a small chance to receive an uncut red topaz. Whilst searching, there is a chance for an aggressive chicken, rat, or spider to spawn.

Searching the same crate repeatedly can cause the critters to spawn. Nearby Goblins will also become aggressive to the player upon searching.

label: Crate (Hazeel Cult)
title: Crate (Hazeel Cult)
lead: A crate can be found in the basement of the Carnillean Mansion, located in the south-western corner of East Ardougne. Players who side with Hazeel must search the crate during the Hazeel Cult quest to obtain a key to unlock the chest found upstairs in the secret room.

label: Crate (Lumber Yard)
title: Crate (Lumber Yard)
lead: Crates are scenery objects found in the Lumber Yard, primarily used as decoy locations of Fluffs' kitten during the Gertrude's Cat quest. Only the mewing crates contain the kitten. Outside of a hard clue step, searching the crates will yield nothing.

label: Crate (Merlin's Crystal)
title: Crate (Merlin's Crystal)
lead: A crate that belongs to Arhein is located behind the Candle maker's store in Catherby. During Merlin's Crystal, the player hides in it to stow away on Arhein's ship as it delivers to places along the coast. Although not mentioned, one of the places is Keep Le Faye, which is where the player will arrive after hiding in the crate.

label: Crate (Observatory Dungeon)
title: Crate (Observatory Dungeon)
lead: Crates are scenery found within and at the entrance of the Observatory Dungeon, as well as inside the Elemental Workshop. They can be searched for a small chance to receive an uncut red topaz.

label: Crate (Pirate's Treasure)
title: Crate (Pirate's Treasure)
lead: Musa Point's banana plantation, operated by Luthas, is run through a series of crates which store bananas. The crates are ready to be shipped via the Customs-run shipping lines to Port Sarim. Players may speak to Luthas and take on a job filling the crate, which holds 10 bananas, in exchange for 30 coins. In the Pirate's Treasure quest, the crate is used to smuggle an illegal shipment of Karamjan rum, which is banned by the Customs and Excise Office. There is also a crate on Ape Atoll.

label: Crate (Shaman Caves)
title: Crate (Shaman Caves)
lead: A crate can be found in the first room of the Shaman Caves, south of the circle of fire. During the Legends' Quest the crate can be searched in order to obtain a Scrawled note. After the quest, searching the crate prints the messages You search the crate. and You can't find anything else here.

label: Crate (Shop of Distaste)
title: Crate (Shop of Distaste)
lead:
The crate could previously be found at the Duel Arena bank. It was filled with rotten tomatoes which players could purchase. Clicking on the crate would give the player access to the Shop of Distaste.

With the release of the Emir's Arena in July 2022, the crate was removed, and replaced by a different crate which gives access to Pelters' Veg Stall instead. Since Fadli still runs the Shop of Distaste, this is presumably an oversight.

label: Crate (Tribal Totem)
title: Crate (Tribal Totem)
lead: Crates are scenery objects that can be found in the GPDT depot located in East Ardougne. During the Tribal Totem quest, players must investigate the north-easternmost double-stacked crate in the GPDT Depot to obtain an address label. Players must then affix the label to the single crate containing a teleport block, originally bound for the Wizards' Tower, to be able to gain access to Handelmort Mansion once the crate is delivered.

label: Crate (Underground Pass)
title: Crate (Underground Pass)
lead: A crate is a scenery object located in the Underground Pass. Players can search the crate to obtain two salmon and two meat pies; however, food can only be taken from the crate once.

label: Crate (Zanaris)
title: Crate (Zanaris)
lead: Crates are scenery found around north-western Zanaris, with a few found in the south of Varrock. They can be searched for a small chance to receive an uncut red topaz.

label: Crate (Zemouregal's Fort)
title: Crate (Zemouregal's Fort)
lead: Crates are found in Zemouregal's Fort and Zemouregal's Base.

label: Crates (Falador)
title: Crates (Falador)
lead: Crates are scenery found throughout Falador. Boxes can be searched for a small chance to receive an uncut red topaz. No other items can be obtained from searching.

label: Crates (Food Store, raw chicken)
title: Crates (Food Store, raw chicken)
lead:
The crate is located at the back of Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim. Searching the crate gives players the option to take a raw chicken. Players can take as many as they want from the crate, one at a time.

Access to the back of the Food Store requires partial completion of Pirate's Treasure and a white apron equipped.

label: Crates (Zemouregal's Fort)
title: Crates (Zemouregal's Fort)
lead: Crates are found in Zemouregal's Fort and Zemouregal's Base.

label: Craw
title: Craw
lead:
, the only memento of one of Armadyl's most formidable followers.]]
Craw was a follower of Armadyl and fought for him during the God Wars. They have been described as a formidable archer who personally eliminated some of Armadyl's greatest enemies.

When the God Wars ended, Craw was one of the many soldiers killed in the destruction of Forinthry. Now, an undead Craw can be found amongst the revenants of the Wilderness, still wielding the trusted bow that helped them in the past.

label: Crawling Hand (disambiguation)
title: Crawling Hand (disambiguation)
lead:
Crawling Hands are level 5 Slayer monsters.

Crawling Hand may also refer to:

label: Crawling hand (interface item)
title: Crawling hand (interface item)
lead:
The Crawling hand is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the crawling hand.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Crazy archaeologist/Strategies
title: Crazy archaeologist/Strategies
lead:
The crazy archaeologist is a relatively simple boss, but a simple mistake can cause some damage to you with his area of effect attack.

The most effective way is to use Magic while Protecting from Missiles and avoiding his area of effect attack. His area of effect attack casts 3 books into the air that slowly land and hit a 3x3 area. This area is centred around where the books land. It is preceded by the crazy archaeologist yelling "Rain of knowledge!".

label: Cream boots
title: Cream boots
lead: Cream boots can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the of the Grand Tree.

label: Cream hat
title: Cream hat
lead:
A cream hat can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the of the Grand Tree. These hats are a slight upgrade from Wizard hats, as Gnome hats have 1 more Magic attack and defence.

This item can be obtained when the player is chasing Solus during the Wanted! quest.

label: Cream robe bottoms
title: Cream robe bottoms
lead: Cream robe bottoms can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions. You can find Rometti on the of the Grand Tree, in the north-eastern area.

label: Cream robe top
title: Cream robe top
lead: A cream robe top can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the of the Grand Tree.

label: Creature (disambiguation)

Creature may refer to:

label: Creature Creation
title: Creature Creation
lead:
Creature Creation is a solo activity that involves creating unique hybrid monsters and killing them for their drops. It can be found in the Tower of Life dungeon after completing the Tower of Life quest. A trapdoor on the ground floor of the tower leads to the dungeon. The Builder's costume is not required to enter the tower once the quest has been completed.

Some of the monsters drop multiples of items that are otherwise hard to get or expensive to purchase, such as Unicorn horns, which are used to make Unicorn horn dust for Herblore. Players who have completed the medium tier of the Ardougne diary will receive these drops in noted form.

**Family crest (item), a quest item from Family Crest
*Heraldic crest, the player's family crest which can be viewed or changed by Sir Renitee

title: Crest part
lead:
The crest parts are items obtained during the Family Crest quest. Each part is owned by one of three Fitzharmon brothers, who have all left their family home. Each brother took a separate piece of the crest with him to prevent the other two brothers from inheriting the family fortune.

The player must complete a set of tasks for each of the brothers as follows:

label: Crevice (Shaman Caves, exit)
title: Crevice (Shaman Caves, exit)
lead: A crevice is a piece of scenery found in the Shaman Caves. When entered, it takes players back to the first room of the caves after the player has searched the bookcase. Looking at the crevice results in the message: It looks like a crevice, you could possibly squeeze through.. Searching the crevice results in the message: "You search the crevice. It looks as if you might be able to squeeze through, would you like to try?"

label: Crew Management
title: Crew Management
lead:
Crew management is an interface accessible from the Crew Registrar on The Pandemonium or Port Roberts, where players can distribute tasks whilst Sailing. The interface can alternatively be accessed at the starting points of Barracuda Trials if the boat already has a crew. Once a crew member is recruited, they can be assigned or cleared from the crew without any restrictions.

Different crew members have different levels of Helmsmanship (H), Privateering (P), and Deckhandiness (D) skills. For example, Jobless Jim is unlocked at level 40 Sailing and has H2-P1-D3, while Adventurer Ada is unlocked at level 55 and has H3-P2-D1. Players should choose their crew depending on which facility slots they are using, taking advantage of crew members' specialties.

label: Crew Management/Strategies
title: Crew Management/Strategies
lead:
This page provides guidance for assigning crew mates.

Crew mate stats are abbreviated here as they are in-game, by using the first letter of a stat followed by the level.

label: Crier outfit
title: Crier outfit
lead: The crier outfit can be obtained as a medium clue scroll reward from Treasure Trails. This outfit appears the same as the outfit worn by Town Criers. It provides no beneficial stats and is only worn for cosmetic purposes.

label: Criminal's dagger
title: Criminal's dagger
lead:
The Criminal's dagger is a quest item that is found at the murder scene during the Murder Mystery quest. This dagger cannot be equipped and is used to help gather evidence against the culprit during the quest. In the quest, you must use a pot of flour on the dagger to dust it, then use flypaper on the dagger to get the unknown print. You must do the same with the items belonging to the suspects. Then compare them by using a suspect's fingerprints on the criminal's fingerprint to get the killer's print.

If you lose it, it will respawn in the same place as where you got it.

label: Criminal's thread
title: Criminal's thread
lead:
The Criminal's thread is a quest item that is found at the murder scene during the Murder Mystery quest. It is used again during King's Ransom. It is used to help identify the murderer in the Murder Mystery Quest.

Note: the colour of the thread is different for each person who does Murder Mystery. It can either be red, green, or blue.

label: Crimson
title: Crimson
lead:
Crimson may refer to:
* Crimson fibre, an item used in Desert Treasure II
* Crimson sanguisphera, encountered during Desert Treasure II
* Crimson swift, a Hunter creature
* Crimson Vein, scenery found in the Scar during Desert Treasure II
* Crimsonette van Marr, a pickpocketable vyre

label: crimson kisten
title: crimson kisten
lead: The crimson kisten is a crush weapon that will be dropped by the Maggot King, fought after completion of The Blood Moon Rises. It will require 60 Attack and 85 Strength to wield.

label: Crimson swift (interface item)
title: Crimson swift (interface item)
lead:
The Crimson swift is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the Crimson swift

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Cringe memes (disambiguation)
title: Cringe memes (disambiguation)
lead:
Cringe memes may refer to one of several things removed from the game for being "cringe memes" :

*Charlie Brown
*Arengeesus

label: Crone
title: Crone
lead: The crone is an old woman who appears briefly during a chat scene with the High Priest of Entrana during the Holy Grail quest. She gives information regarding passage to the Fisher Realm. She tells the player to "go to where the six heads face" and "blow the whistle".

label: Cross
title: Cross
lead: A cross is on the wall of the building containing the incinerator in the sheep pen used during Sheep Herder. It can only be examined.

label: crossbow
title: crossbow
lead:
The crossbow is the weakest type of crossbow, along with the Phoenix crossbow, and requires a Ranged level of 1 to wield. It can only fire bronze bolts and mith grapples. The crossbow and the bolts can be bought from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock. There is a crossbow spawn in the Graveyard of Shadows, Bone Yard, and Hugor's house at Land's End (south-west of the Kourend Woodland).

It possesses the longest range of any crossbow in the game, with 10 tiles of range on rapid.

label: crossbow (weapon)
title: crossbow (weapon)
lead:
Crossbows are a category of weapons used in ranged combat that require a certain Ranged level to wield. They are different than bows in that they are horizontal and can be held with one hand (except for the Karil's crossbow, Light ballista and Heavy ballista), allowing a player to carry a shield with the other.

Free-to-play players are recommended to stay with bows as the crossbows available to them are weak, while members have very strong crossbows. Crossbows require ammunition in the form of bolts.

label: Crossbow limbs
title: Crossbow limbs
lead: Crossbow limbs are members-only items used to make crossbows. They can be smithed, but most can also be purchased at the crossbow shops in Keldagrim, White Wolf Mountain, and the Dwarven Mines. The experience and Smithing level needed to make them are as follows:

label: Crossbow shops
title: Crossbow shops
lead: Crossbow shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. Crossbow shops sell crossbow stocks, crossbow limbs, and crossbows. There are 3 crossbow shops in Old School RuneScape, but only the Keldagrim shop keeps parts for an adamant crossbow in stock.

label: Crossbow stock
title: Crossbow stock
lead: A Crossbow stock is the wooden centre of a crossbow. It is required to make a crossbow. They can be fletched by members who have the necessary Fletching level. They can also be purchased or stolen from the crossbow stall in Keldagrim.

label: Crown
title: Crown
lead: Crown may refer to:

label: Crozier
title: Crozier
lead:
Croziers are Magic weapons that have the ability to autocast spells from the standard spellbook. They are similar to battlestaves with an added Prayer bonus, but do not provide an unlimited source of runes of any type.

A crozier is a piece of a vestment set and can be obtained by completing medium or hard Treasure Trails. Each crozier is aligned with a different god: Guthix, Saradomin, Zamorak, Zaros, Bandos and Armadyl.

label: crude raft
title: crude raft
lead: A crude raft can be constructed during the Shilo Village quest to sail on the river out of Ah Za Rhoon. It can be constructed out of the smashed table found close to the entrance to the temple.

label: Crude wooden chair (interface item)
title: Crude wooden chair (interface item)
lead:
The Crude wooden chair is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Crude wooden chair.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Crumble Undead
title: Crumble Undead
lead:
Crumble Undead is a spell on the standard spellbook, requiring level 39 Magic to cast and costing 2 air runes, 2 earth runes, and 1 chaos rune. This spell can only be cast on undead enemies, such as skeletons, zombies, ghosts and shades; trying to cast it a non-undead NPC yields the chatbox message: This spell only affects skeletons, zombies, ghosts and shades.

Crumble Undead can only be autocast by a skull sceptre (i), slayer's staff, slayer's staff (e), staff of the dead, toxic staff of the dead, staff of light, staff of balance, or void knight mace. In particular, the skull sceptre (i) is the only free-to-play weapon that can autocast this spell.

label: Crumbled wall
title: Crumbled wall
lead: The Crumbled wall is located in the northern section of Khazard Battlefield, and can be climbed over to enter the building. During the Tree Gnome Village quest, a Khazard commander will attack you once you enter.

label: Crumbling wall
title: Crumbling wall
lead:
Crumbling wall may refer to:

*Crumbling wall (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course), an Agility obstacle found within the Barbarian Outpost Agility Course
*Crumbling wall (Falador), an Agility shortcut found on the western wall of Falador
*Crumbling wall (Gu'Tanoth), an Agility shortcut found in Gu'Tanoth
*Crumbling wall (Grim Tales), a Thieving obstacle south of the Mind Altar where parts of the Grim Tales quest take place

label: Crumbling wall (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course)
title: Crumbling wall (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course)
lead: The crumbling wall is an Agility obstacle found within the Barbarian Outpost Agility Course. Passing the obstacle requires 35 Agility and will award 13.7 Agility experience.

label: Crumbling wall (Falador)
title: Crumbling wall (Falador)
lead:
The crumbling wall is an Agility shortcut found in Falador, south-west of the western bank. An Agility level of 5 is required to use the shortcut. The shortcut allows players to quickly get between Falador and the mine north of the Dark Wizards' Tower.

Climbing over the wall is a requirement for the Falador Easy diary.

label: Crumpled scroll
title: Crumpled scroll
lead:
The crumpled scroll is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching some sacks in the temple of Ah Za Rhoon. The scroll must be given to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village.

Players can sell the scroll for 100 coins to Yanni Salika after the quest.

label: Crunchies
title: Crunchies
lead:
Crunchies may refer to:
*Chocchip crunchies
*Spicy crunchies
*Toad crunchies
*Worm crunchies

label: crunchy tray
title: crunchy tray
lead: Crunchy trays are items used in gnome cooking. They can be obtained by buying them from the Grand Tree, the Grand Exchange or by trading with other players. The trays can be combined with gianne dough to make raw crunchies.

label: Crush weapons
title: Crush weapons
lead: Crush is an attack type that is used primarily by weapons like mauls, maces and warhammers, and secondarily by weapons like two-handed swords and battleaxes.

label: crushed gem
title: crushed gem
lead:
A crushed gem is produced when a player fails to cut a semi-precious gem (opal, jade and red topaz). Players will gain a small amount of Crafting experience when a gem is crushed. The chance of obtaining crushed gems decreases with higher Crafting levels.

Crushed gems may be one of the items required in the Fairytale I - Growing Pains quest to make the magic secateurs.

label: Crwys Clan
title: Crwys Clan
lead: The Crwys Clan is one of the eight elven clans who were originally brought to Gielinor from Tarddiad by Guthix and Seren in the early First Age. They are skilled in botanic arts such as Farming and Woodcutting. They are located north-east of the Tower of Voices in Prifddinas, off the eastern path.

label: Cry
title: Cry
lead:
Cry is the seventeenth listed emote. Upon use the player puts their hands to their face and cries.

This emote is already unlocked upon making an account.

label: crystal
title: crystal
lead: Crystal is a material used by the elves, which was gifted to them by their goddess Seren. It is infused with some of her divine power, and is an important part of elven culture. It can be shaped, formed, and magically charged into weapons, tools, or other items with magical powers by the use of crystal seeds and crystal shards. Crystal seeds and shards can be transformed via crystal singing, either by using a singing bowl with sufficient Crafting and Smithing levels, or by the service of a crystal singer. Crystal shards can also be ground into crystal dust for use in Herblore, to transform certain combat stat-boosting potions into divine potions.

label: Crystal (Watchtower)
title: Crystal (Watchtower)
lead:
Crystal is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. As the quest opens, ogres have stolen the four crystals needed to power the watchtower and protect Yanille from invasion by the ogres. There are four crystals, each a different colour, and the player must retrieve them by performing various tasks around Gu'Tanoth.

* Yellow Crystal - obtained from Grew in return for Gorad's tooth.
* Magenta Crystal - obtained by completing the dialogue with the Mad skavid after learning bits of the Skavid language.
* Cyan Crystal - obtained from the last Ogre Shaman killed in the Ogre Enclave. (If lost, it is reobtained by picking-up and searching the shaman robe found within the enclave.)
* Grey Crystal - found by mining the Rock of Dalgroth, within the centre of the Ogre Enclave. (Requires all Ogre Shaman to be dead.)

title: Crystal ball (Sorcerer's Tower)
lead:
A Crystal ball is found on the table in the Sorcerer's Tower on the . It presumably belongs to the resident of the tower, Thormac.

When an item is used on the crystal ball, the message "The table appears to be in use." appears in the chatbox, signifying that the crystal ball cannot be used as a table.

title: Crystal Cave
lead: Crystal Cave is a music track that is unlocked anywhere in Zanaris, other than the Fairy Resistance Hideout. To get there, the player must have completed the Lost City quest.

label: crystal chest
title: crystal chest
lead:
The Crystal chest can be found in the house directly south of the witch's house in Taverley. The chest is locked and can only be opened using a crystal key, which is made by combining a loop half of key and a tooth half of key. Attempting to open the chest without the crystal key yields the message: This chest is securely locked shut. Opening the crystal chest grants an uncut dragonstone and possibly a variety of other rewards.

Opening the crystal chest is a task for the medium Falador Diary.

label: crystal equipment
title: crystal equipment
lead:
Crystal equipment is a range of degradable weapons and armour made from elven crystal. Crystal combat equipment requires completion of Roving Elves to use, as well as 50 Agility (although 56 Agility is a boostable requirement to travel through Tirannwn), among other skill requirements unique to each piece. Crystal tools and crystal armour can only be obtained after Song of the Elves. There are also the crystal saw and crystal chime, which are rewards from the quests The Eyes of Glouphrie and The Path of Glouphrie respectively.

Upon death in the Wilderness, the killer will receive the seed form of the crystal equipment.

label: Crystal glider's outfit
title: Crystal glider's outfit
lead:
Crystal glider's outfit is obtained from the chest found in Laguna Aurorae by using the Serrated key. Obtaining the outfit requires level 61 Agility to cross a stepping stone to reach the chest aswell as 72 Sailing to obtain the Serrated key. The outfit can be stored in a magic wardrobe in the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: Crystal key
title: Crystal key
lead:
The crystal key is created by combining a tooth half of key with a loop half of key, displaying the message, "You join the two halves of the key together." Key halves can be obtained as rewards from Barrows, the Gnome Restaurant minigame, Managing Miscellania, Treasure Trails, looting magpie implings, random events, the rare drop table, etc.

It is used to open the crystal chest located inside a house in Taverley. The chest always contains an uncut dragonstone in addition to a variety of other items. Some items of note are 3 runite bars, rune platelegs/plateskirt (depending on the player's gender), or another half of the crystal key. After the key is used, it disappears and the player must use another one if they want to open the chest again.

title: crystal singing
lead: Crystal singing is the process by which items are made from Crystal seeds and Crystal shards. With appropriate Smithing and Crafting levels, the player can sing crystal at a singing bowl; alternatively, a crystal singer can be paid a fee to sing for them.
