label: Crystal Sword
title: Crystal Sword
lead:
Crystal Sword is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness or in Ardougne's eastern sewers. It also plays at Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, the track plays in level 1 Wilderness, north of Varrock as well as Ardougne's eastern sewers.

label: Crystal throne (interface item)
title: Crystal throne (interface item)
lead:
The Crystal throne is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Crystal throne.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Crystal tool
title: Crystal tool
lead:
Crystal tool may refer to:
*Crystal axe
*Crystal harpoon
*Crystal pickaxe
*Crystal tool seed

label: Crystal-flecked waters
title: Crystal-flecked waters
lead:
Crystal-flecked waters are a sailing hazard that are found in the waters near Tirannwn, such as in Porth Gwenith and Porth Neigwl. Unprepared boats that attempt to traverse these waters without an adamant keel or better will be slowed and rapidly dealt 20 damage. Rafts cannot be upgraded to resist this effect, as they do not have a keel.

These waters are the remains of a naval battle that took place during the Siege of Prifddinas, where hundreds of crystal elven vessels were destroyed and scattered in the ocean.

label: Crystalline portal nexus (interface item)
title: Crystalline portal nexus (interface item)
lead:
The Crystalline portal nexus is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Crystalline portal nexus.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Cube part
title: Cube part
lead:
Cube parts were the original components of the Strange box. Although they were in fact items, they could never be obtained by players.

These cube parts were difficult for colour-blind players to identify. As a result in 2006, the Strange box was updated to use numbers instead of colours. As a result, they have never been present in Old School RuneScape - however, they remain in the game cache.

label: Culinaromancer's gloves
title: Culinaromancer's gloves
lead: Culinaromancer's gloves can be bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest after completion of any mini-quest during the Recipe for Disaster quest. The gloves are coloured in the same colours as the metals and the progression of the gloves corresponds with the progression of metals of that colour.

label: Cult
title: Cult
lead:
Cult may refer to:
*Hazeel Cult, a quest.
*The Cult of Hazeel, followers of the Mahjarrat Hazeel.
**Hazeel Cultists, members of the Cult of Hazeel.
*Humans Against Monsters (H.A.M.), a human-supremacist cult.
*Voodoo Cult, a music track unlocked in the Viyeldi caves.

label: Cult of Hazeel
title: Cult of Hazeel
lead:
The Cult of Hazeel are a group of zealots who worship Hazeel, a Zamorakian Mahjarrat. They play a focal part in the Hazeel Cult quest, in which they attempt to resurrect him. Their base is in a sewer found south of Ardougne and east of the Clock Tower. Before the player can enter, they must first correctly manipulate the sewer valves.

In the quest, players have the option to either join the cult or side with the Carnillean family; if the player joins the cult, Hazeel will successfully be resurrected. If the player opposes the cult, Evelot, a member of the Khazard Army, is hired to recover the Hazeel scroll and successfully does so at some point after the events of the quest, leading to Hazeel being resurrected regardless of the player's choice.

label: cup
title: cup
lead:
Cup may refer to any of the following:

;Teacups
*Empty cup
*Cup of tea
*Cup of water
*Cup of hot water
*Cup of milky tea
*Porcelain cup (porcelain)
*Porcelain cup (trimmed)
*Empty cup (clay)
*Cup of tea (Player-owned house)

label: Cup of tea
title: Cup of tea
lead:
A cup of tea is a drink which restores 3 Hitpoints and temporarily boosts Attack by 2 + 2% (rounded down); it will also instantly cancel the effect of the goading potion. Upon drinking a cup of tea, the player will exclaim and an empty cup will remain in the player's inventory.

Tea may be purchased at Ye olde Tea Shoppe in Varrock or stolen at the nearby Tea stall with 5 Thieving.

label: Cup of tea (interface item)
title: Cup of tea (interface item)
lead:
The Cup of tea is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Cup of tea.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Cup of tea (Player-owned house)
title: Cup of tea (Player-owned house)
lead:
A cup of tea is a drink that boosts Construction. There are three different teas available based on the cup the tea is poured into: clay, porcelain, and trimmed porcelain cups which boost Construction by 1, 2, and 3 respectively. Making tea requires 20 Cooking, and a kitchen in a player-owned house with a built stove that isn't a firepit, a larder, a sink, and the appropriate shelves for the right tea cup. Making tea yields 52 Cooking experience, however a servant can also make tea for the player. This type of tea cannot be put into a tea flask.

Note: Leaving the player-owned house will cause all tea-related items to disappear from the inventory.

label: Cupboard
title: Cupboard
lead: Cupboard may refer to:

label: cupboard (Edmond's house)
title: cupboard (Edmond's house)
lead: A cupboard containing a gas mask, found in Alrena and Edmond's house located north-east of the Flying Horse Inn in East Ardougne. Searching the cupboard will yield a gas mask after Alrena has made one during the Plague City quest, provided the player does not currently own one. However, multiple gas masks can be obtained from the cupboard by drop tricking.

label: Cupboard (Hazeel Cult)
title: Cupboard (Hazeel Cult)
lead: A cupboard can be found on the of the Carnillean Mansion, located in the south-western corner of East Ardougne. Players who side with the Carnillean family must search the cupboard during the Hazeel Cult quest to find evidence of Butler Jones's involvement with the cult and finish the quest.

label: cupboard (Heroes' Quest)
title: cupboard (Heroes' Quest)
lead: A cupboard containing Grip's drinks is located within Scarface Pete's mansion in Brimhaven. During the Heroes' Quest, a player who is a Black Arm Gang member must open the cupboard to lure Grip in to the room, allowing a Phoenix Gang member to kill him.

label: Cupboard (Jerico's house)
title: Cupboard (Jerico's house)
lead: A cupboard full of bird feed can be found within Jerico's house, found immediately south of the northern bank in East Ardougne. It is used during the Biohazard quest to retrieve bird feed that is thrown at the West Ardougne watchtower to distract mourner guards with pigeons released from a pigeon cage. Multiple bird feed can be obtained from the cupboard by drop tricking, however, once bird feed is thrown during the quest, the others will be deleted. Searching the cupboard after throwing the bird feed will cause the player to state that they don't need any more bird feed.

label: cupboard (Legends' Quest)
title: cupboard (Legends' Quest)
lead: A cupboard is found inside Sir Radimus Erkle's house in the Legends' Guild courtyard. At the start of the Legends' Quest, Radimus Erkle lets the player search the cupboard for a machete. After the completion of the quest, the player is no longer able to search the cupboard as they will receive the message: "You don't think Radimus Erkle would be very pleased if he caught you rifling through his cupboards without permission."

label: Cupboard (Morgan's home)
title: Cupboard (Morgan's home)
lead: The Cupboard in Morgan's home in Draynor Village can be opened and searched for garlic. The cupboard is located in his second floor, before reaching the bed.

label: Cupboard (Nardah)
title: Cupboard (Nardah)
lead: Cupboards are scenery found near the Elidinis Statuette in Nardah. Players must search the northern cupboard during the Spirits of the Elid quest to obtain a torn robe top and bottom. The cupboards may also be searched for a small chance to receive an uncut red topaz.

label: cupboard (Nurse Sarah's house)
title: cupboard (Nurse Sarah's house)
lead: A cupboard containing a medical gown can be found within Nurse Sarah's house, located in the southern area of West Ardougne. It is used during the Biohazard quest to retrieve medical gown that must be worn to access the Mourner Headquarters. The cupboard is searchable for another gown if the player loses theirs. Multiple gowns can be obtained from the cupboard by drop tricking.

label: cupboard (rock pick)
title: cupboard (rock pick)
lead: A cupboard can be found on the northern wall of the south-western room of the Exam Centre. The cupboard can be searched in order to obtain a rock pick, provided the player does not currently have one in their inventory.

label: Cupboard (Shield of Arrav)
title: Cupboard (Shield of Arrav)
lead: The cupboard is located on the of the Black Arm Gang Headquarters in Varrock, and is used during the quest Shield of Arrav. It is only accessible by members of the Black Arm Gang. During the quest, the player, if they have chosen to join the Black Arm Gang, must search the cupboard to retrieve the right half of the Shield of Arrav.

label: cupboard (specimen jar)
title: cupboard (specimen jar)
lead: A cupboard can be found on the southern wall of the south-western room of the Exam Centre. The cupboard can be searched in order to obtain a specimen jar, provided the player does not currently have one in their inventory.

label: cupboard (The Grand Tree)
title: cupboard (The Grand Tree)
lead: A cupboard is located in Glough's house within the Tree Gnome Stronghold. During The Grand Tree quest, players must search the cupboard to obtain Glough's journal for evidence.

label: Cupboard (The Knight's Sword)
title: Cupboard (The Knight's Sword)
lead: The cupboard is located on the of the White Knights' Castle in Falador, and is used during the quest The Knight's Sword. During the quest, the player must search the cupboard to retrieve a portrait of a paladin. Before the portrait can be found within the cupboard, the player must first talk to the Squire. The cupboard may only be searched if Sir Vyvin is not in the room, otherwise he will stop the player from doing so.

label: Cupboard (witch's house)
title: Cupboard (witch's house)
lead: A cupboard can be found in the basement of the witch's house in Taverley. It is used during the Witch's House quest to retrieve a magnet in order to catch a mouse. In order to access the cupboard, the player must be wearing an appropriate pair of gloves in order to open an electrified gate, and avoid taking damage.

label: Curator Haig Halen
title: Curator Haig Halen
lead:
Haig Halen is the Curator of the Varrock Museum. He can be found on the ground floor. When asked about treasure, he'll tell the player that the museum is "full of treasures" and that anything the museum found took some time to acquire. You can trade him 250 cut rubies, 100 cosmic runes, 500 fire runes and a Digsite pendant for a curator's medallion.

You may speak to him after gaining 50 Kudos to complete an easy achievement diary task. He is also overseeing the construction of the barge, which requires 100 Kudos to assist with.

label: Curling plant
title: Curling plant
lead: Curling plants are scenery highly prominent across southern Karamja, though a single plant may also be found at Musa Point, being the only one that can be interacted with by free-to-play players.

label: Currencies
title: Currencies
lead:
Currencies are items whose primary purpose is to be exchanged (for other items, services, or experience) in a consistent, repeatable fashion, and are primarily used for transactions in Old School RuneScape. Currencies are typically persistent and stackable, and can be traded for a multitude of things in exchange.

Coins (gold pieces or "gp") are the main form of currency and are almost universal, as they are accepted by most shops. All other currencies may only be used at their specific location. Only trading sticks are comparable to gold pieces in that they can be used to buy and sell items in multiple places as well as to trade with other players, although their usage is much more limited than usage of gold pieces.

label: curry
title: curry
lead:
Curry is a type of food that restores 19 Hitpoints when eaten. An empty bowl will remain after consumption. It can be obtained by cooking uncooked curry on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 60 Cooking and granting 280 experience when successful. When cooking, there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt curry. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.

At 50 Construction, a Demon butler can be hired, who can serve curry in Player-owned houses. The number of curries served is equal to the number of people in the house, up to 10.

label: Curse
title: Curse
lead: Curse is a level 19 Magic spell. When cast on an opponent, their defence is reduced by 5%. The spell gives 29 experience whether it hits or misses, making it a popular way to gain experience cheaply. The spell can only be cast if the target's stats haven't already been lowered, meaning you can not stack stat reduction with multiple spells in a row.

label: curse spells
title: curse spells
lead:
Curses are spells mainly used to cause a negative effect to its target other than damage. Stat draining curses are rarely used as they are easily negated with stat restoration items and damage dealing or movement blocking spells are better.

Curse spells can only be used on the same target once the first spell wears off, the curse splashing does not apply the effect, and thus does not count.

label: Cursed
title: Cursed
lead:
Cursed is a music track that is unlocked during the Underground Pass quest.

It plays in the entrance section of the Underground Pass dungeon. It is also played in the Wrath Altar and in the unmarked cave with the rabbit boss, just north of the Gwenith Hunter area.

label: Custodian stalker
title: Custodian stalker
lead:
Custodian stalkers are Slayer monsters found inside the Stalker Den that can be fought after the completion of the Shadows of Custodia quest. They can be assigned by Chaeldar and Nieve. There are multicombat areas where cannons can be placed in the south-western side of the dungeon, and single-combat caverns in the south-eastern and northern parts.

The slayer stalkers all drop broken antlers, which are used to create Atlatl dart tips for creating atlatl darts outside of subduing the Moons of Peril. The mature and elder variants are also able to drop the antler guard, a powerful off-hand weapon boasting offensive stats in all styles, with no defence requirement to wield.

label: Custom Fur Clothing
title: Custom Fur Clothing
lead: Custom Fur Clothing is a service offered by several non-player characters to make players hunter clothing from furs or hides.

label: Customer Support
title: Customer Support
lead: Customer Support is the division of Jagex staff that interacts with players. They normally investigate abuse reports and Black mark appeals. They also help out players with their technical problems and send them messages regarding their RuneScape accounts. Customer Support should NOT be used for quest help, walkthroughs etc. Additionally, the Community Forums are a good place to turn to if you are having problems.

label: Customs officer
title: Customs officer
lead:
A customs officer is found on Karamja at the port at Musa Point. The player must talk to her in order to take a boat back to Port Sarim. It costs 30 coins to depart. If a player is wearing the Karamja gloves, the cost is lowered to 15 coins.

Before the player leaves, she will search the player for any banned substances, such as Karamjan rum. If the player has any on themselves, it will be confiscated. Since this item is necessary in the Pirate's Treasure quest, the player must find some way to smuggle it past her.

label: Cutlass
title: Cutlass
lead: Cutlasses are an uncommon type of medium-speed, one-handed Melee slash weapon similar to scimitars. Unlike scimitars however, they have some defensive bonuses similar to claws and spears, and negative Magic attack bonuses similar to halberds.

label: Cyclops (Ardougne Zoo)
title: Cyclops (Ardougne Zoo)
lead:
A solitary cyclops is located in a cage in the Ardougne Zoo. Unlike all other cyclopes, this cyclops has the same drop table as a regular hill giant.

According to the Zoo keeper, this cyclops was brought to the zoo by an explorer from a far away land, but little else is known because the explorer died shortly thereafter.

label: D'hide body
title: D'hide body
lead: Dragonhide bodies are a type of Ranged armour worn in the torso slot. 40 Defence is required to wear those armour pieces in addition to a certain Ranged level, depending on the type of dragonhide. Dragon Slayer I is also required to wear the green body. They can be crafted using three dragon leathers of appropriate colour.

label: D'hide body (t)
title: D'hide body (t)
lead:
There are four trimmed dragonhide body's:
*Green d'hide body (t)
*Red d'hide body (t)
*Blue d'hide body (t)
*Black d'hide body (t)

label: D'hide chaps
title: D'hide chaps
lead: Dragonhide chaps are a type of Ranged armour worn in the leg slot. Dragonhide chaps only require a certain Ranged level, depending on the type of dragonhide. This means combat pure players can take advantage of their bonuses. They can be crafted using two dragon leathers of appropriate colour.

label: Da Vinci
title: Da Vinci
lead:
Da Vinci is one of three individuals used to smuggle chemicals into Varrock during the Biohazard quest. In the quest, he should be given the ethenea.

Prior to the quest, Da Vinci can only be found near the Chemist's house in Rimmington, working on a painting of a nearby island. After the quest, he can be found in both Rimmington and the Dancing Donkey Inn in Varrock. He is always accompanied by his associates Hops and Chancy.

label: Daconia rock
title: Daconia rock
lead:
A daconia rock is a magical rock that has been hidden in the roots of the Grand Tree in order to poison it.

The Daconia rocks were created by Hazelmere - allegedly as a precaution in case the Grand Tree should grow out of control, and are the only thing that can kill it. Players discover this precaution has been subverted in The Grand Tree quest.

label: Daconia rocks
title: Daconia rocks
lead: Daconia rocks are a scenery object found beneath the Grand Tree, and are a focal point in the quest The Grand Tree. They were created by Hazelmere - allegedly as a precaution in case the Grand Tree should grow out of control, and are the only thing that can kill it.

label: Dad
title: Dad
lead:
Dad is an abnormally large troll that players must fight during the Troll Stronghold quest to gain access to northern Troll Country. After the quest, he can be re-fought in the Nightmare Zone minigame.

If a player tries to open the arena exit without fighting Dad, he will shout "No human pass through arena without defeating Dad!" and attack the player. He will also ignore the player if talked to. Once Dad is defeated, the player can no longer attack him. Trying to attack him yields the message "You don't need to fight him again."

label: Daerig Clod
title: Daerig Clod
lead: Daerig Clod was a resident of Varrock during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. Daerig is mentioned in the Varrock Census found in the Varrock Palace Library. He is described as being unemployed.

label: Daeyalt
title: Daeyalt
lead:
Daeyalt may refer to:

* Daeyalt shard, mined in the daeyalt essence mine, traded for daeyalt essence. Requires 60 Mining
* Daeyalt essence, an alternative, untradeable essence for Runecraft which grants 50% experience bonus
* Daeyalt essence mine, where players may mine daeyalt shards to trade for daeyalt essence

label: Daeyalt mine
title: Daeyalt mine
lead:
Daeyalt mine may refer to:

label: Dagannoth (race)
title: Dagannoth (race)
lead:
dagannoth, found in the Lighthouse and Catacombs of Kourend.]]
Dagannoth (known as daggermouths to the Fremennik) are sea monsters. Many are found near areas inhabited by the Fremennik, who hunt them for their skin and use it to make armour. There are many types of dagannoth, the most powerful being the three Dagannoth Kings. They hatch from eggs as dagannoth spawn. As they grow, they become Dagannoth fledgelings, and later mature into the Dagannoth that is well-known by the Fremennik people.

Dagannoth can be found beneath the Lighthouse, in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon, in the Jormungand's Prison, and all the way over in the Catacombs of Kourend.

label: Dagannoth boss

label: Dagannoth Kings
title: Dagannoth Kings
lead:
The Dagannoth Kings (commonly abbreviated DKs) are a group of three dagannoths that live deep in the cave on Waterbirth Island which is a multiway combat area. They are all level 303, and also represent the combat triangle. Each of the kings uses a different combat style, is weak against the type that defeats them on the combat triangle, and has a high defence against all others. They all have their own, unique ring drops, with Rex having two - these rings give the second best bonuses for their respective combat styles in the ring slot. All three kings have the ability to drop the dragon axe, and also drop dagannoth bones.

*Dagannoth Rex - Attacks with Melee and is weak to Magic. Unique loot includes: berserker ring and warrior ring.
*Dagannoth Prime - Attacks with Magic and is weak to Ranged. Unique loot includes: seers ring and mud battlestaff.
*Dagannoth Supreme - Attacks with Ranged and is weak to Melee. Unique loot includes: archers ring and Seercull.

label: Dagannoth Kings/Strategies
title: Dagannoth Kings/Strategies
lead: Dagannoth Kings are a trio of bosses found in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon, known for their dragon axe, berserker ring, archers ring, warrior ring and seers ring drops. Their bones are also valuable, making them consistently rewarding to kill.

label: dagger
title: dagger
lead:
Daggers are generally small, fast melee weapons. Most daggers are stab swords which primarily use stab attack styles but also have an option for a slashing style; though there are many items thought of as daggers that either belong to different weapon categories or aren't even wieldable.

Interestingly, despite presenting as melee-only weapons, many daggers have a positive magic attack bonus.

label: Dagon'hai robes
title: Dagon'hai robes
lead:
Dagon'hai robes are a set of magic robes worn by members of the Dagon'hai, an ancient Zamorakian organisation. Obtained from Larran's big chest at a rate of 1/256 per piece, they require level 70 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

These robes are Zamorak affiliated items, including when worn in the God Wars Dungeon.

label: Dairy cow
title: Dairy cow
lead:
A dairy cow is a cow that the player can milk with an empty bucket in their inventory to receive a bucket of milk. For more information, Gillie Groats by the northern Lumbridge cow pen will explain more about milking. Dairy cows were introduced because players could attack and kill a cow whilst another player was milking it, preventing them from receiving milk.

Unlike the other cows, dairy cows cannot be attacked or killed. A dairy cow does "talk" to the player during the quest Cold War. During and after completing Cold War, players can steal cowbells from them.

label: Daisies
title: Daisies
lead: Daisies are a common form of scenery found in various areas across Gielinor.

label: Dal's General Ogre Supplies
title: Dal's General Ogre Supplies
lead: Dal's General Ogre Supplies is a general store in Gu'Tanoth owned by an ogre trader named Dal. Dal is the only ogre trader in the area that allows players to trade with him, and accessing the shop requires starting the Watchtower quest.

label: Dalal
title: Dalal
lead: Dalal is one of the people observing the fights at the Emir's Arena, along with Ima.

label: Dalgroth
title: Dalgroth
lead:
Dalgroth is an ogre warrior. It is suggested that Dalgroth is a famous figure amongst ogres, as the ogre guards outside Gu'Tanoth will recognise the ogre relic as a statue of Dalgroth and consider it a token of friendship allowing entry to the city.

The Rock of Dalgroth, found in the centre of the Ogre Enclave is named after them.

label: Damage per second/Magic
title: Damage per second/Magic
lead:
This article is about calculating magic damage output, not to be confused with the Equipment stat Magic Damage. gives a 15% boost to magic damage.]]
Magic damage is affected by the spell used, equipment, prayer, skill boosts and the monster being attacked.

There are various methods by which players can increase their potential Magic damage. The effects of most equipped items can be seen in the stats window (labelled as Magic: +x and Magic damage: +x%).

label: Damage per second/Melee
title: Damage per second/Melee
lead:
This article is about calculating melee damage output.
Melee damage is affected by the Equipment used, prayer, skill boosts and the monster being attacked.

There are various methods by which players can increase their potential Melee damage. The effects of most equipped items can be seen in the stats window (labelled as Stab, Slash, Crush and Melee Strength).

label: Damage per second/Ranged
title: Damage per second/Ranged
lead:
This article is about calculating ranged damage output.
Range damage is affected by the Equipment used, prayer, skill boosts and the monster being attacked.

There are various methods by which players can increase their potential Ranged damage. The effects of most equipped items can be seen in the stats window (labelled as Range: +x and Ranged strength: +x).

label: Damaged armour
title: Damaged armour
lead:
Damaged armour is an item that can be found by digging at the digsite, from the Fishing Trawler minigame, or from pick-pocketing certain monsters (including H.A.M. members). It is also found in ogre coffins (see ogre coffin key), can be telegrabbed inside the Ranging Guild's archery competition spot, and is found in the Uzer Mastaba by searching the first skeleton directly east of the stairs. Players may use the drop trick as a free and quick way to obtain lots of the damaged armour item from this skeleton.

Players may also find damaged armours scattered throughout the world in the form of scenery. However, these may not be picked up.

label: Damaged dagger
title: Damaged dagger
lead:
The damaged dagger is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest and it can be found after the quest's completion. The player can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille. It serves no purpose during the quest and is there as a red herring.

While it cannot be used as a weapon, it can be used to slash webs.

label: Damaged Earth
title: Damaged Earth
lead: Damaged Earth is earth that has been damaged after an unsuccessful attempt at growing a Yommi tree in one of the 6 patches of Fertile Soil in the Kharazi Jungle during the Legends' Quest. It takes about one minute for the earth to become fertile again.

label: Damp sticks
title: Damp sticks
lead: Damp sticks are used with broken glass to make dry sticks in the Sea Slug Quest. The dry sticks can then be used to light a torch. They can be found on the Fishing Platform.

label: Dance
title: Dance
lead: Dance is the thirteenth listed emote, and is unlocked automatically for all accounts. Performing the emote causes the player to swing both arms back and forth in the air and kick their legs one at a time. Performing the emote while wearing flared trousers will instead cause players to perform a disco move and then a split.

label: Dancing Donkey Inn
title: Dancing Donkey Inn
lead: The Dancing Donkey Inn is a small bar found in south-eastern Varrock. Chancy, Hops, and Da Vinci, non-player characters who are involved in the Biohazard quest, are found there. The bar sells beer for 2 coins each.

label: Danger sign (Death Plateau)
title: Danger sign (Death Plateau)
lead: A danger sign is located at the main entry path of Death Plateau. When read a short cutscene plays, pointing the camera at the nearest Thrower Troll, with the troll noticing the camera and throwing a rock at it.

label: Danger sign (Slayer areas)
title: Danger sign (Slayer areas)
lead: Danger signs can be found outside the entrances to some Slayer areas, namely the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon and the Canifis Slayer Tower. The sign reads:

label: Danger sign (Wilderness)
title: Danger sign (Wilderness)
lead:
Danger sign is located outside the entrance to Lava Dragon Isle, all over the Fight arena, near the entrance to the Sheep herder incinerator, on the Khazard Battlefield, and various other locations that seem suitable to warn people of danger.

This is the oldest Danger sign in RuneScape, having been originally added 13 August 2001 to mark the border of the Wilderness. The job of marking the border of the wilderness was given to a redesigned Wilderness Sign on 24 April 2006, but this original sign is still used in many places. It has even been used in newer content, such as its use north of Prifddinas, where a simpler sign was desired.

label: Dangerous
title: Dangerous
lead:
Dangerous is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness and also plays in Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, the track plays in the Wilderness north of Edgeville, and south of the Demonic Ruins.

label: Dargaud's Bow and Arrows.
title: Dargaud's Bow and Arrows.
lead: Dargaud's Bow and Arrows is a shop where Dargaud the Bow and Arrow salesman sells arrow shafts, arrows and arrowheads up to runite, as well as shortbows. He will also buy brutal arrows up to runite. His shop is located in the Ranging Guild.

label: Dark
title: Dark
lead:
Dark is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness and plays in the Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, the track plays north-east of the Wilderness Chaos Temple.

label: Dark cavalier
title: Dark cavalier
lead:
The dark cavalier is a piece of headwear. There are no requirements for wearing this cavalier and they do not confer combat bonuses upon the player.

A cavalier of any colour is a potential reward from hard Treasure Trails.

label: Dark dagger
title: Dark dagger
lead:
The dark dagger is a quest item obtained during Legends' Quest. It is given to the player by the entity Echned Zekin. The dagger can then either be given to Ugandulu for a one-use Holy force spell, or used to kill Viyeldi which converts the dagger into a glowing dagger. It is then given to Echned, who turns out to be the demon.

If players have misplaced their glowing dagger after the quest, it can be reclaimed from Radimus Erkle, and can be investigated via-right click afterwards to switch its appearance between a dark or glowing dagger.

label: Dark hole
title: Dark hole
lead:
Dark hole may refer to:

* Dark hole (Lumbridge Swamp), leading to the Lumbridge Swamp Caves
* Dark hole (Prifddinas Agility Course), Agility obstacle within the Prifddinas Agility Course
* Dark hole (A Soul's Bane), six different holes that need to be looked into during the quest
* Dark hole (Sailing), the entrance to the Charred Island Dungeon

label: Dark Mage
title: Dark Mage
lead: The Dark Mage is a Zamorakian mage that lives in a tower east of the entrance to the Underground Pass in West Ardougne. He provides various services related to Iban's staff.

label: Dark Squall robes
title: Dark Squall robes
lead:
Dark Squall robes are a set of magic robes obtained during the While Guthix Sleeps quest. They offer offensive and defensive Magic stats better than that of Wizard robes but worse than that of Xerician robes. After completion of the quest, the player can reobtain the Dark Squall robes for free from Silif at the White Knights' Castle if they have lost them. They can be stored in the magic wardrobe of the costume room in a player-owned house.

These robes are Zamorak affiliated items, including when worn in the God Wars Dungeon. They can also be used to enter the Black Knights' Fortress.

label: Dark tuxedo outfit
title: Dark tuxedo outfit
lead: The dark tuxedo outfit can be obtained as an elite clue scroll reward from Treasure Trails. The outfit provides no beneficial stats and is only worn for cosmetic purposes.

label: Dark warrior
title: Dark warrior
lead:
Dark warriors are mainly found in the Dark Warriors' Fortress, a castle in level 12 to 16 Wilderness north-west of Edgeville. Some dark warriors can also be found in Great Kourend, accompanying necromancers. The warriors in Great Kourend are different combat levels than those found in the Wilderness.

Dark warriors found in the fortress come in both level 8 and 145 variants, the latter of which only appears in members' worlds. The area is multi-combat and a Dwarf multicannon can be set up in the center of the inner courtyard of the fortress. To speed up a Krystilia Slayer task, it is recommended that the player kills the Level 8 Dark warriors roaming the corridors of the fortress, while leaving the cannon to deal with the Level 145 ones inside the courtyard, making sure to close the courtyard doors so that the warriors don't get out of range of the cannon by going inside the corridors.

label: Dark Warriors' Fortress
title: Dark Warriors' Fortress
lead: The Dark Warriors' Fortress is a castle in level 14 to 16 multi-combat Wilderness, north of Falador. It is populated with level 8 and 145 dark warriors in members worlds, but only level 8 dark warriors in non-members worlds. Caution should be used as these warriors can overwhelm lower level players who don't use Protect from Melee.

label: Dark wizard
title: Dark wizard
lead:
Dark wizards are Zamorakian mages that attack with low-level magic. They can be primarily found around the Varrock stone circle and in the Dark Wizards' Tower, and are notable for frequently dropping runes, as well as black robes and wizard hats. They are also notable for being a considerable threat to very low level players due to their relatively high max hit for their combat level and position next to the southern entrance of Varrock.

They play a small role in the Demon Slayer quest, performing a ritual to summon the demon Delrith.

label: Dark Wizards' Tower
title: Dark Wizards' Tower
lead:
The Dark Wizards' Tower is a tower to the west of Falador in a members-only area. It is due west of Falador, north-west of the Makeover Mage, and south of Taverley and the entrance to the Taverley Dungeon. Level 23 dark wizards occupy all three floors of the tower, and Zandar Horfyre is located on the top floor.

The Tower is involved in Fairytale I - Growing Pains, during which the player must talk to Zandar Horfyre to help cure the Fairy Queen in Zanaris.

label: Dark Wizards' Tower Portal
title: Dark Wizards' Tower Portal
lead: The Dark Wizards' Tower portal is one of the three teleportation portals found on the top floor of the Wizards' Guild. Located on the southern wall of the guild, entering the portal will teleport the player to Dark Wizards' Tower, which is west of Falador and south of Taverley.

label: Darkness
title: Darkness
lead:
Darkness is a game mechanic that darkens the player's screen. Not having a light source in the darkest areas will cause rapid damage from biting insects, and the player will be unable to attack anything. The damage is lethal.

Light sources can dispel darkness to varying degrees, though even the dimmest will prevent damage from biting insects. Some dark areas have environmental hazards or hostile monsters that can extinguish weaker light sources, with higher tier light sources being resistant to these hazards while also being brighter.

title: Darkness (disambiguation)

label: dart
title: dart
lead:
Darts are a type of members only ranged throwing weapon that target a monster's light ranged defence. They can be fletched by members with the required Fletching level. However, in order to smith dart tips, the player must have the required Smithing level and completed the Tourist Trap quest. They are made from dart tips and feathers and have an attack range of 3 tiles, 5 with longrange. They can be poisoned and are one-handed, so they can be wielded along with a shield or god book for protection.

Darts, alongside throwing knives, are the quickest ranged weapons in the game making them a fairly popular weapon for Ranged training. The only difference between darts and throwing knives is that knives have small ranged accuracy bonuses, have a slightly longer attack range (4/6 tiles), and are stronger than their dart counterparts; however knives are generally more expensive and traded less often compared to darts.

label: dart tip
title: dart tip
lead: Dart tips are a members-only item, and are used to make darts. Metal dart tips can be smithed in sets of 10 per bar after completing The Tourist Trap quest. Amethyst dart tips can be crafted in sets of 8 and do not require completion of The Tourist Trap. Each tip requires a feather to make it into a dart; feathering dart tips does not require completion of The Tourist Trap.

label: Dartboard (interface item)
title: Dartboard (interface item)
lead:
The Dartboard is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Dartboard.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Dathero Raispher
title: Dathero Raispher
lead: Dathero Raispher was one of the founding members of the Elders of Avarrocka. He has two known descendants, Lucinda and Aeonisig Raispher.

label: Dave the beard
title: Dave the beard
lead: Dave the beard is the beard of a moss giant, mentioned in the 6th Postbag from the Hedge. Moss giants were asked whether their beards had a life of their own, and Dave answered affirmatively.

label: Davey (Eagles' Peak)
title: Davey (Eagles' Peak)
lead: Davey was a member of the Bandits of the Golden Claw, a criminal organisation based in northern Kandarin. The gang's abduction by the Mysterious Old Man during the Eagles' Peak quest leaves his fate unknown.

label: David
title: David
lead:
David may refer to these NPCs:
* David (Fossil Island), who is involved in the quest Bone Voyage
* David (Murder Mystery), who is involved in the quest Murder Mystery
* David (Varrock Museum), who is found in the paleontology floor in the Varrock Museum
* David Andrews, the head councillor of the Kourend Council

label: David (Murder Mystery)
title: David (Murder Mystery)
lead:
David Sinclair is one of Lord Sinclair's children. He is a suspect during the Murder Mystery quest. He is also involved in King's Ransom.

According to the Gossip, he has anger management problems, shouting at the household servants when he is angry. As much as they fear his anger, they do not dare to report his behaviour to his father as it would get him kicked out of the house.

label: David's barrel
title: David's barrel
lead: David's barrel can be found inside the Sinclair Mansion in David's bedroom. During the Murder Mystery quest, the player must search the barrel to find his silver book.

label: David's print
title: David's print
lead: David's print is a quest item in the Murder Mystery quest. It is created by using flypaper on the silver book after dusting it with a pot of flour. If the prints match those of the unknown print, it will become a killer's print, meaning David is the killer.

label: Davon
title: Davon
lead: Davon is a merchant found standing along the southern shore of Brimhaven towards the fence. He runs Davon's Amulet Store - apparently out of his pockets (in true underworld style), because he has neither a building nor a stall. The price of items is affected by wearing Karamja gloves.

label: Davon's Amulet Store.
title: Davon's Amulet Store.
lead:
Davon's Amulet Store is a jewellery store in Brimhaven, owned by Davon. It stocks enchanted gem amulets, as well as holy symbols. It has a higher buying price and lower selling price to players wearing Karamja gloves 1 or higher.

The shop has no inventory of its own to sell, making it useful for getting rid of enchanted amulets as it will buy them for a higher price than other shops. Ironmen cannot buy from this shop because any amulets that he has available for purchase will always be overstocked.

label: Dawn Ascent
title: Dawn Ascent
lead:
Dawn Ascent was the name of covert military operation carried out by the White Knights in the Fifth Age that resulted in the death of the Kinshra officer Iban. After the battle, Iban's dead body was salvaged and resurrected by the witch Kardia in the Underground Pass. The event is only mentioned by name in Kardia's History of iban found in the Underground Pass.

The exact date of the Dawn Ascent remains unknown, but based on the context Kardia's history supplies, it occurred after Lord Daquarius Rennard rose to power.

label: Dawn scarab
title: Dawn scarab
lead:
, the last remaining dawn scarab, though only a shell of her former self.]]
Dawn scarabs are a species of giant scarab beetles, known for their intelligence and long lifespans. They supposedly lived in the Kharidian Desert until they were wiped out during the Kharidian–Zarosian War. Following this, the sole survivor of the race was a female known as Kephri. Kephri however made a deal with Amascut for her to produce offspring. Amascut used this deal to wipe out Kephri's mind, making her a mindless husk. Kephri's offspring were however not the same race as their mother, rather being a creation of Amascut herself.

After an adventurer slew Kephri to free Scabaras from Amascut's grip, they decided to collect her dung. Upon cleaning it, they found a dawn scarab egg amidst the waste and gave it to the High Priest of Scabaras to care for, leaving the current fate of the species unknown.

label: Dead coral (Sailing Beta)
title: Dead coral (Sailing Beta)
lead: Dead coral was a Farming plant found in the Sailing alpha game files. Though coral farming was not accessible during the alpha, it was likely intended to be the dead form of elkhorn, pillar, and umbral coral planted in a coral patch. In the actual release of coral farming, each type of coral has distinct dead variants, so the alpha variants were never released.

label: Dead Man's Chest
title: Dead Man's Chest
lead: The Dead Man's Chest is a bar in Brimhaven. (located in northern Karamja) Players can buy grog for 3 coins and Karamjan rum for 27 coins from the Bartender. It also plays a role in Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl miniquest, in which the player must drink Supergrog. There are some beer and empty beer glass as well as a bronze axe respawns on some of the tables. There are some barrels located by the north wall and in the south-west corner that beer glasses can be refilled at.

label: dead orb
title: dead orb
lead:
A dead orb is an unobtainable item released alongside the Underground Pass quest. Previously, it was a fifth orb of light that could not be obtained, and it was silently renamed to "Dead orb" in an update on 15 June 2017.

During the Underground Pass quest, the player is required to collect four orbs of light. The first three spawn on the ground and can easily be picked up, however the fourth is in front of a swinging log that must be disarmed. The item that appeared on the ground was a fake orb that was actually an object, and was programmed to trigger the trap if players attempted to pick it up. To give the illusion of being real, an invisible Orb of light item was set to spawn on the same tile, so a red dot would appear on the minimap.

label: Dead Quiet
title: Dead Quiet
lead:
Dead Quiet is a music track that is unlocked in the Mort Myre Swamp. It can also be unlocked while Temple Trekking, during the Bog puzzle, when battling the Swamp snakes, or during combat events with two escape routes. In the Mort Myre Swamp area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track, Stagnant and Waterlogged.

In Classic mode, the unlock area in the Mort Myre Swamp is limited to the south-eastern part of Mort Myre Swamp. With this setting, it is also possible to unlock it at the shore east of the Digsite.

label: Dead tree
title: Dead tree
lead:
Dead trees can be chopped down to provide logs and 25 Woodcutting experience. They are the same as normal trees but with a different look.

There are a few special types of dead trees. Some types of burnt dead trees provide charcoal when chopped down, instead of logs. Some undead trees at Draynor Manor attack unsuspecting players for up to 3 damage.

label: Dead tree (burnt)
title: Dead tree (burnt)
lead:
Burnt dead trees require level 1 Woodcutting to cut and give charcoal when chopped down. They look the same as some types of dead tree, except have a slightly darker tone. Burnt trees are found in the Wilderness south of the Demonic Ruins near Callisto's Den, in the Death Altar and several locations in Great Kourend, such as the Fishing Hamlet, the east side of Lizardman Canyon and the area just north of Kourend Castle.

A similar variant of tree called burnt tree can be found on Fossil Island and also give charcoal when chopped. These trees have a different appearance but otherwise function the same.

label: Dead tree (disambiguation)
title: Dead tree (disambiguation)
lead: Dead tree may refer to:

label: Dead tree (Gravedigger)
title: Dead tree (Gravedigger)
lead: Dead trees are scenery found in the Gravedigger random event area. There are 5 trees in the area, as well as one tree stump. They are identical to other dead trees around the world, but cannot be chopped down to obtain logs. Using an axe on them will show You don't need any wood. What are you planning on doing, making them a fresh coffin?

label: Dead tree (Kharidian Desert)
title: Dead tree (Kharidian Desert)
lead: Dead tree is a unique tree found in the Kharidian Desert. The tree is found in only one location to the north-west of the Bandit Camp Quarry. It has no interaction options and is purely decorative.

label: Dead tree (old)
title: Dead tree (old)
lead:
Old dead trees are a variant of dead trees that be chopped down to provide logs and 25 Woodcutting experience. They are the same as normal trees but with a different appearance.

When chopped down, the tree is replaced by a tree stump. After a few seconds, it will respawn into a dead tree.

label: Dead tree (parasitic)
title: Dead tree (parasitic)
lead: The parasitic dead tree is an unused scenery object that appears to be a dead tree with a red vine tangled around it. The red vine is described as a parasitic plant, and has a similar appearance to several other unused red vine objects found in the game cache. The parasitic vines may have been intended for use in Karamja or other tropical areas.

label: Dead tree (sickly sweet)
title: Dead tree (sickly sweet)
lead: Dead tree is an unused scenery object that appears to have an unusual twisted trunk with yellow sap dripping from its branches. Based on the location in the cache, it may have been intended for use on Mount Karuulm, but is otherwise not a close match for the art style of the mountain.

label: Dead tree (snowy)
title: Dead tree (snowy)
lead:
Snowy dead trees are a variant of dead trees that be chopped down to provide logs and 25 Woodcutting experience. They are the same as normal trees but with a different appearance.

When chopped down, the tree is replaced by a tree stump. After a few seconds, it will respawn into a dead tree.

label: Dead tree (swampy)
title: Dead tree (swampy)
lead:
Swampy dead trees are a variant of dead trees that can be chopped down to provide logs and 25 Woodcutting experience. They are the same as normal trees besides their appearance. Swampy dead trees can be found in various swamp environments, including the Lumbridge swamp and Morytania.

When chopped down, the tree is replaced by a tree stump. After a few seconds, it will respawn into a dead tree.

label: Dead Tree (Waterfall Dungeon)
title: Dead Tree (Waterfall Dungeon)
lead:
Dead tree is a tree located on a small islet in the middle of the River Dougne, directly above the entrance to the Waterfall Dungeon. In order to reach the dungeon, a rope must be used on the tree, which will allow the player to climb down to the entrance. The tree also has a climb option, but attempting to climb the tree will always fail. Instead, the player will be washed down the river and arrive on the riverbank some distance to the south.

The dead tree cannot be chopped with an axe.

label: Dead tree (weathered)
title: Dead tree (weathered)
lead:
Weathered dead trees are a variant of dead trees that can be chopped down to provide logs, awarding 25 Woodcutting experience. They are the same as normal trees but with a different appearance.

When chopped down, the tree is replaced by a tree stump. After a few seconds, it will respawn into a dead tree.

label: Dead tree (web)
title: Dead tree (web)
lead: Dead trees are trees found in the Wilderness holding up slashable webs. They can be found in the Lava Maze and at the entrance to the Deserted Keep. The dead trees have no interaction options and are purely decorative.

label: Dead tree stump
title: Dead tree stump
lead: A dead tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a burnt tree has been chopped down. A dead tree stump will respawn into a burnt tree after a short amount of time. The stump has no interaction options.

label: deadly red spider
title: deadly red spider
lead: Deadly red spiders are an aggressive species of spider. Their eggs can usually be found nearby. The spiders found in Varrock Sewers are a popular training spot for free-to-play, as they reside in a multicombat area and are aggressive to low levels (up to level 68 combat). Bringing a knife or slash weapon is mandatory to access the area.

label: Deadman: All Stars
title: Deadman: All Stars
lead: Deadman: All Stars is a recurring invite-only version of Deadman Mode. Created by content creator Solo Mission in collaboration with Jagex, each season involves several teams of invited participants in a private world with boosted experience and drop rates. Teams have a limited number of days to build accounts and gather gear for a finale in which each team faces off against the others. Like in Deadman Mode, PvP is enabled in most areas of the game and breaches spawn on a regular schedule.

label: Deadman: All Stars Season 1
title: Deadman: All Stars Season 1
lead:
Deadman: All Stars Season 1 was the first season of Deadman: All Stars, an invite-only variant of Deadman Mode that ran from 14 June 2024 until 22 June 2024. It was hosted on World 400 and spearheaded by content creator Solo Mission, in collaboration with Jagex. 30 content creators, drafted into 6 teams of 5 members each, were invited to participate in this event.

The finale was streamed live on the official Old School RuneScape Twitch channel at 5:00 PM UTC on 22 June 2024, with the winners receiving Deadman All Stars trophies, a guaranteed invite to future events, and the Deadman's Stake, which contained 18.4 billion coins.

label: Deadman armour
title: Deadman armour
lead:
Deadman armour is a set of cosmetic armour purchased from Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing for 160 Last Man Standing points per piece, costing a total of 480 points. Players can store a complete set of Deadman armour in the armour case of the costume room of their player-owned house.

In Deadman mode, it is obtained by using blood money on Nigel, costing 1 per piece totalling at 3 for the set. The armour pieces share their stats with a regular cape, iron platebody and platelegs. In order to purchase deadman armour in Deadman mode, players must use the blood money on Nigel, instead of speaking to him, as there are no dialogue options for purchasing the armour.

label: Deadman Mode
title: Deadman Mode
lead:
Deadman Mode (commonly abbreviated as DMM) is a variant of Old School RuneScape that released on 29 October 2015. A separate server is hosted featuring an open PvP environment, with some exceptions. Players in-game can speak to Nigel in Lumbridge Graveyard for information about Deadman Mode.

Experience gained in permanent Deadman Mode is 5x to 20x more than usual depending on the level and protection status. Experience is capped to 2x in most instanced areas (such as the Nightmare Zone and TzHaar Fight Caves).

label: Deadman Mode Betas
title: Deadman Mode Betas
lead:
In preparation of the Deadman Spring Invitational planned on March 25th, players were able to log in to the beta world to test how the final hour of the Invitational will run at 14:00 GMT. Instead of a creeping lethal fog, large chunks of the map would be taken away at a time instead.

During the final hour, an overlay is always visible telling players whether they are safe or not, and giving them ample time to move to a safe area. This was done so that players are more likely to die to other players rather than the environment.

label: Deadman rug (interface item)
title: Deadman rug (interface item)
lead:
The Deadman rug is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Deadman rug.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Deadman sigil
title: Deadman sigil
lead:
Deadman Sigil may refer to one of the following:

* Sigils in Deadman: Armageddon
* Sigils in Deadman: Apocalypse
* Sigils in Deadman: Reborn

label: Deadman: All Stars Season 2
title: Deadman: All Stars Season 2
lead:
Deadman: All Stars Season 2 was the second season of Deadman: All Stars, an invite-only variant of Deadman Mode that ran from 30 May 2025 to 8 June 2025. As with Deadman: All Stars Season 1, it was hosted and spearheaded by content creator Solo Mission, in collaboration with Jagex. 30 content creators drafted into 6 teams of 5 members each participated in this event.

The finale was streamed live on the official Old School Runescape Twitch channel starting at 16:00 UTC on 8 June 2025, with the winners receiving Deadman: All Stars Season 2 trophies and a guaranteed invite to future events.

label: Deadman: All Stars Season 3
title: Deadman: All Stars Season 3
lead:
Deadman: All Stars Season 3 is the upcoming third season of Deadman: All Stars, an invite-only variant of Deadman Mode planned to run from 6 June 2026 to 15 June 2026. As with seasons 1 and 2, it was hosted and spearheaded by content creator Solo Mission, in collaboration with Jagex.

The finale is planned for 20 June 2026; it will be held at a live in-person event at the Rosemont Theatre in Rosemont, USA, near Chicago.

label: Deadman: Annihilation
title: Deadman: Annihilation
lead:
Deadman: Annihilation was an updated variant of Deadman Mode that released on 30 January 2026 at 17:00 UTC, that lasted until 20 February 2026. This variant of Deadman was announced during RuneFest Summit 2025.

Notable differences from previous Deadman Mode variants include:
*The removal of bank keys
*A reworked sigil system (where some sigils are now permanent unlocks instead of items that need to be toggled)
*The addition of the dogsword, the thunder khopesh, and the Ruinous Powers

label: Deadman: Annihilation/Points
title: Deadman: Annihilation/Points
lead:
Skull Points can be earned through a variety of activities during Deadman: Annihilation, then spent on sigils and quest lamps in the Deadman's Skull Store inside the Deadman's skull item. The Deadman tab of the character summary interface shows the total number of points earned, while the Skull Store interface shows the current balance.

At the conclusion of the tournament, the total Skull Points earned (not the current balance) will be converted into an equal number of Deadman Points. These can be redeemed on regular worlds at the Deadman Reward Store for various rewards, including those from previous Deadman seasons. To earn each of the Annihilation rewards, one would need to earn 37,000 points.

label: Deadman: Annihilation/Skull shop
title: Deadman: Annihilation/Skull shop
lead: In Deadman: Annihilation, sigils and quest lamps can be bought from the Deadman's skull for various amounts of skull points. An unlimited amount of sigils from the Permanent and Toggle tab may be active at any time, while up to three sigils from the Attune tab may be active at any one time. Excluding the starting sigil, duplicate sigils can be sold back to the shop by using them on the Deadman's skull.

label: Deadman: Apocalypse
title: Deadman: Apocalypse
lead:
Deadman: Apocalypse is an updated variant of Deadman Mode released on 25 August 2023 that lasted until 16 September 2023. In this variant, "breaches" occurred at regular intervals throughout the day in which monsters breach through to the over world and wreak havoc. Players who output enough damage to contain the breach will score exclusive and extremely powerful loot.

Players need to wipe any permanent Deadman Mode progress they have in order to play Deadman: Apocalypse.

label: Deadman: Apocalypse/Emblem Trader Shop
title: Deadman: Apocalypse/Emblem Trader Shop
lead:
The Emblem Trader can be found within safe confines of the Grand Exchange on Deadman Apocalypse servers, where he runs a version of the Bounty Hunter Shop unique to the game mode.

Archaic emblems can be handed in at the Emblem Trader in exchange for store credit, which can spent on a wide variety of supplies and equipment.

label: Deadman: Apocalypse/Global loot table
title: Deadman: Apocalypse/Global loot table
lead:
The global loot table for Deadman: Apocalypse is accessed by nearly all monsters killed during the game mode, except for raids and Nightmare Zone.
__NOTOC__

label: Deadman: Apocalypse/Points
title: Deadman: Apocalypse/Points
lead: Points can be earned through a variety of activities during Deadman: Apocalypse, allowing players to climb up the dedicated leaderboard, in addition to earning a chance of partaking in the prize money, which is distributed to randomly selected players among those who earned the highest number of points.

label: Deadman: Apocalypse/Sigils
title: Deadman: Apocalypse/Sigils
lead:
In Deadman: Apocalypse, Sigils are powerful buffs that are obtained through killing monsters or through other players in the Grand Exchange.

Upon starting Deadman: Apocalypse for the first time, players are presented with the following selection of Tier 2 sigils to choose from. The selection is the same for all players.

label: Deadman: Apocalypse/Unique item drops
title: Deadman: Apocalypse/Unique item drops
lead: A pre-arranged list of unique items are dropped at a higher rate in the Deadman: Apocalypse game mode, depending on the combat bracket world the player has access to. Items on this list are dropped at 2x the regular rate upon entering the level 51+ combat bracket, increasing to 3x the normal rate when entering the level 71+ bracket, and finally to 4x the standard rate on reaching the level 111+ combat bracket.

label: Deadman: Armageddon
title: Deadman: Armageddon
lead: Deadman: Armageddon is an updated variant of Deadman Mode released on 19 July 2024 that lasted until 3 August 2024. This variant of Deadman was announced during the 2024 Winter Summit. During the summit, it was stated that this variant will have larger breach events, the return of sigils with improvements, keys and other additional content.

label: Deadman: Armageddon/Points
title: Deadman: Armageddon/Points
lead: Similarly to Deadman: Apocalypse, points can be earned through a variety of activities during Deadman: Armageddon, allowing players to climb up the dedicated leaderboard, in addition to earning a chance of partaking in the prize money, which is distributed to randomly selected players among those who earned the highest number of points. They can also be used to purchase rewards from the Deadman Reward Store.

label: Deadman: Armageddon/Sigils
title: Deadman: Armageddon/Sigils
lead:
In Deadman: Armageddon, sigils are powerful buffs that are obtained through killing monsters, training gathering skills, or by trading with other players at the Grand Exchange. Up to three sigils may be active at any one time.

Sigils may only be attuned while in a bank, causing them to become untradeable. Unattuning the sigil must also be done in a bank, which makes it tradeable once more. Some sigils can be activated from the inventory.

label: Deadman: Factions
title: Deadman: Factions
lead:
Deadman: Factions was an invite-only variant of Deadman Mode based on Deadman: Annihilation. It started at 4pm UTC on 25 January 2026 and ran for 3 hours ahead of the Winter Summit 2026. Due to its very short duration, it featured boosts such as 1000x experience and 1000x drop rate multipliers.

The event features 150 content creators split amongst 4 factions, each themed around a god: Saradomin, Zamorak, Bandos, and Armadyl. Each faction had three hours and 20 minutes to prepare for the finale, where everyone was teleported to the Daimon's Crater to fight it out in multicombat, with the last faction standing being crowned the winner. Killing a player during the event resulted in an additional 15 sharks, 3 Sanfew serums, 1 ranging potion, and 1 super combat potion dropping along with their loot.

label: Deadman: Reborn
title: Deadman: Reborn
lead: Deadman: Reborn was an updated variant of Old School RuneScape s Deadman Mode, released on 25 August 2021 that lasted until 16 September 2021. In this variant, players received accelerated experience rates, increased drop rates of rare items, and most of Gielinor was classified as PvP areas. Many other small differences exist between Deadman: Reborn and the standard game, which are detailed below.

label: Deadman: Reborn drop table
title: Deadman: Reborn drop table
lead: The drop table for Deadman: Reborn is accessed by nearly all monsters killed during the game mode, except for raids and Nightmare Zone.

label: Deadman: Reborn/Sigils
title: Deadman: Reborn/Sigils
lead:
In Deadman: Reborn, Sigils are powerful buffs that are obtained through killing monsters or through other players in the Grand Exchange. There are 53 sigils available across all tiers.

Upon starting Deadman: Reborn for the first time (and also after all lives are lost), players are presented with the following selection of Tier 2 sigils to choose from. The selection is the same for all players.

label: death
title: death
lead: Death occurs when a player's Hitpoints reach zero; a message in the Chat Interface will inform them: Oh dear, you are dead!. There are other alternatives of death which occur when specific criteria are met, such as being completely frozen at the Wintertodt, which causes the player's death despite not losing any Hitpoints. After death, the player will respawn at another location and potentially lose some items depending on the circumstances.

label: Death (disambiguation)
title: Death (disambiguation)
lead:
__NOTOC__
Death may refer to:
*Death, having run out of Hitpoints
*Deadman Mode, a variant game mode

label: Death Plateau
title: Death Plateau
lead: Death Plateau is a short quest wherein you are to help the Burthorpe Imperial Guard gain access to the Death Plateau in order to defeat the hostile trolls.

label: Death Plateau (location)
title: Death Plateau (location)
lead:
The Death Plateau is a tall, flat land formation, surrounded by steep ascents, north-west of Burthorpe and directly north of the Warriors' Guild. This area is inhabited by various trolls. Though the plateau is not a multi-combat area, the path leading around the plateau is riddled with thrower trolls and is multi-combat. Extreme caution is advised here, and players should take advantage of Protection prayers as certain monsters can hit very high here.

A Dwarf multicannon may be used here.

label: Death rune
title: Death rune
lead:
Death runes are one of the runes used to cast spells in the Magic skill. They are required to cast medium-level missile spells, like Wind Blast, Water Blast, Earth Blast, and Fire Blast. Members with 65 Runecraft and who have completed Mourning's End Part II can craft death runes at the Death Altar by using pure essence on it, with each essence yielding one death rune. Each death rune yields 10 Runecraft experience. Players with 99 Runecraft will always craft two death runes per essence. Crafting death runes from essence is a requirement for the Hard Ardougne Diary.

Death runes can be bought from most Magic shops. Several monsters, such as ankous, nechryael, and dark beasts, commonly drop death runes. They can also be found in the Barrows Chest with at least 631 rewards potential.

label: Death to the Dorgeshuun/Quick guide
title: Death to the Dorgeshuun/Quick guide
lead: If you are planning to do this quest and obtain the robes yourself, make sure to first start the quest since this improves your chances to obtain robes. Because of this, it is not recommended to prepare for the quest by collecting the robes in advance.

label: Death wing
title: Death wing
lead:
Death wings are flying monsters that appear in the Legends' Quest. The death wings are located in a remote area, and have no drops, so very few players train on them. Killing a death wing is one of the hard tasks in the Karamja Diary.

Death wings can only be found in the Shaman Caves, which is unlocked during the Legends' Quest. To reach them, players should bring one or more lockpicks, a machete, any axe and any pickaxe. The dungeon can be found in the north-west of the Kharazi Jungle by searching the mossy rocks, after which the player should search the bookshelf north of Ungadulu and choose to squeeze through there, picklock the ancient door, mine the rocks and open another door to reach the death wings. Death wings can also sometimes be found inside barrels in the dungeon.

label: Deathly mansion
title: Deathly mansion
lead:
Deathly mansion is a House style option for a player-owned house.

This house style is awarded to players after completing Halloween events and requires level 1 Construction to use in a player's house. It was originally awarded from completing the 2015 Halloween event.

label: Debug Console
title: Debug Console
lead:
The Debug Console is a tool exclusive to the Official Client and, formerly, the iOS closed beta client. It has a set of commands that may prove useful for debugging technical issues on the client or setting several preferences. A list of commands can be viewed by typing ? in the console.

To open the console on desktop, hold down and then press (grave accent). The console could be opened on the iOS beta client by swiping down 4 fingers.

label: Decanting
title: Decanting
lead:
Decanting is the method of combining partially full potions of the same kind. Potions may be decanted into any number of doses. For example, combining a 3 dose potion with a 1 dose potion will leave the player with a 4 dose potion and an empty vial, while combining a 1 dose potion with a 2 dose potion will create a 3 dose potion.

Occasionally it is required or recommended for potions to be in fewer doses rather than four:
*Barbarian mix potions can only be made from 2-dose potions.
*Not taking excess doses can reduce unnecessary monetary loss:
**In the Wilderness, where player killers may interrupt killing a boss – taking a 2-dose super combat potion instead of 4-dose when the player only plans to kill a few bosses per trip, for example
**At Vorkath, players typically only need two doses of super antifire per trip, and using a 2-dose potion allows an extra item of loot to be collected
**At Chambers of Xeric, if the raid is already scouted, players may know how many doses of a stat-boosting potion are enough before a potion drop is received
*When drinking potions at a bank before going to an extended activity to save inventory space ("pre-potting"), or when training some skills, 1-dose potions may be convenient
*When making potions with stackable secondaries (like stamina potions), decanting the base potion to less than 4 doses may be convenient to activate the effect of the Amulet of chemistry (or Alchemist's amulet), allowing the player to get extra doses

label: Decay
title: Decay
lead:
Decay may refer to:

*Degradation of equipment
*Item decay, the rate at which an item dropped on the ground by a creature or player disappears if not picked up

Deep sea trawling is an intensive mid-level Fishing and Sailing activity which involves catching fish from shoals out at sea with a trawling net. Though providing low experience per hour compared to other training methods, the quantity of deep sea fish obtained is much higher to compensate for the amount of effort required, especially with higher tier trawling nets.

label: Deep sea trawling/Strategies
title: Deep sea trawling/Strategies
lead:
Deep sea trawling is a Fishing and Sailing activity which is more intensive than traditional fishing, by chasing fish shoals out at sea with a boat to catch deep sea fish. Fishing and Sailing experience per hour for are very poor for an intensive activity, but the quantity of deep sea fish obtained per hour is much higher to compensate for the amount of effort required, especially with better boat facilities.

As such, deep sea trawling is chiefly used to acquire high-value fish in bulk that cannot be obtained elsewhere. Players will need a minimum of level 69 Fishing to trawl fish shoals, but 83 (the level needed to catch raw halibut) is recommended instead as the limited utility of the low level deep sea fish makes them largely impractical for the effort required.

label: Deep Wilderness Dungeon
title: Deep Wilderness Dungeon
lead:
The Deep Wilderness Dungeon can be found in level 51 Wilderness. The entrance is via stairs in a broken house west of the Mage Arena. It is entirely single-way combat and covers level 49 to 56 Wilderness.

The main attractions here are the wine of Zamorak spawn found at the end of the dungeon, which respawns every 3-7 ticks (and are obtained in noted form if players have completed the hard Wilderness Diary), as well as the fire giants which can be assigned as a Wilderness Slayer task by Krystilia, this being their only location in the Wilderness. A cannon can be used within the dungeon.

label: Defence
title: Defence
lead: Defence is a skill that grants players protection in all forms of combat. Defence level also determines which equipment players are able to wear, as most pieces of armour or other equipment have a Defence level requirement.

label: Defence Level Up!
title: Defence Level Up!
lead: Defence Level Up! is a Jingle for leveling defence.

label: defence potion
title: defence potion
lead:
A Defence potion is a potion made by using white berries on a ranarr potion (unf), requiring 30 Herblore, yielding a Defence potion(3) and 75 Herblore experience. A dose of Defence potion provides a temporary skill boost to Defence equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down. This is less than the super Defence's boost of 5 + 15% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a Defence potion(2), requiring 33 Herblore, yielding a Defence mix and 25 Herblore experience. A Defence mix has 2 doses, boosts Defence equal to 3 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down, and heals 6 Hitpoints.

label: Defence pure
title: Defence pure
lead:
A Defence pure maintains a low Combat level while having a high Defence in order to equip endgame armour in low combat brackets. When player-killing, other players have a large window of opportunity to escape from a Defence pure due to their weak attacks. However, other players also find it difficult to kill Defence pures due to their ability to tank hits.

Additional sources of damage for Defence pures are poisoned daggers, such as the iron and bone daggers, and the Dragonfire shield. The poison deals six damage every 15 seconds, and the Dragonfire shield special attack deals from 15 to 25 damage and can be used every 192 game ticks, or about 1 minute and 56 seconds. The shield’s accuracy is dependent upon the user's Defence level vs. the opponent’s Magic Defence bonus.

label: Defence pure (free-to-play)
title: Defence pure (free-to-play)
lead:
A defence pure is a type of free-to-play combat pure account that focuses on training Defence. Defence pures are very difficult to kill within their combat level brackets due to their extremely high defensive capabilities. This makes them very useful as scouts and tanks for their teams.

Free-to-play defence pures lack the members-only offensive options such as using poisoned weapons, ring of recoil, or the dragonfire shield special attack. However, they are still useful for clans in the deep Wilderness, as they often carry supplies and perform tasks such as world hopping or luring.

title: degradation
lead: Degradation is the process by which some armour, weapons, and tools gradually wear down with use until they either break completely or reach a "charge" of zero. Degradable items can degrade in one of a few ways, and some items are repairable or rechargeable at a cost while others are not and crumble to dust. A repairable or rechargeable item will either become unusable or will have reduced stats until it has been repaired or recharged.

label: Delrith
title: Delrith
lead:
Delrith is a Zamorakian demon summoned by dark wizards from a stone table during the Demon Slayer quest. Delrith is relatively easy to kill and players can evade the wizards if they take their time. Low-levelled players should exercise caution, however as the wizards will deal significant damage against them.

All damage dealt to Delrith is doubled when Silverlight is equipped. Ring of recoil damage will therefore always inflict 2 on Delrith when he lands a successful hit on the player. When using a ring of recoil to lower Delrith's hitpoints, it's not necessary to deal any damage to him directly in order to finish the quest; you must simply have Silverlight equipped.

label: Demon spade
title: Demon spade
lead:
The demon spade was a proposed reward from the Doom of Mokhaiotl which would allow harvesting farming patches instantly. The item was originally proposed as the demonic digger before being renamed. It would have allowed instant harvesting at herbs, hops, allotments, dead plants, tree roots, and Chambers of Xeric patches.

After being proposed there were concerns that harvesting allotments such as snape grass and watermelons would offer higher experience per hour than trees due to the reduced time spent harvesting. The harvesting speed was then proposed to be double harvesting speed rather than instant. After further community feedback and concerns about a skilling upgrade coming from an end-game PvM encounter the demon spade was removed from the rewards.

label: Demonbane spells
title: Demonbane spells
lead:
Demonbane spells are a category of offensive spells in the Arceuus spellbook. Requiring completion of A Kingdom Divided to use (excluding Inferior Demonbane), these spells deal damage much like any other offensive spells, but can only be cast on demonic creatures. Demonbane spells can only be autocast by certain staves.

By default, demonbane spells have an accuracy bonus of 20%, but can be doubled to 40% when the Mark of Darkness spell is active, which additionally gives a 25% damage bonus. If attacking with a purging staff, this is further doubled to an 80% accuracy and 50% damage bonus when under the effects of the Mark of Darkness. All of these bonuses are calculated after the player's own magic damage bonuses from their equipment.

label: Demonic Pacts League
title: Demonic Pacts League
lead:
The Demonic Pacts League is Old School RuneScape's sixth league. It started on 15 April 2026 at 11:45 AM BST and will run for 8 weeks, ending on 10 June 2026. It is themed around Yama and his pacts.

The name was revealed with a teaser trailer at the New Game+ Showcase 2026 on 8 January 2026, with further details coming as part of the Winter Summit 2026.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Areas
title: Demonic Pacts League/Areas
lead:
In the Demonic Pacts League, players will be locked to only certain areas in the game. All players begin locked to Varlamore and will unlock Karamja for free when they achieve their first region unlock after completing 80 tasks. Up to 3 other regions of their choice can be unlocked through completing 200, 300, and 450 tasks, respectively.

Travel between regions is restricted by barriers unless a player has access to the appropriate areas. Death's office, the player-owned house, random events, Zanaris and the Abyssal Area will be accessible from all areas. Use of transportation methods such as charter ships, fairy rings, gnome gliders, etc. will require the destination area be unlocked before they can be used.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Asgarnia/Summary
title: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Asgarnia/Summary
lead: The Asgarnia area covers the entire Kingdom of Asgarnia along with the island of Entrana, the Pest Control islands, and Troll Country. Instances of areas in Asgarnia and underground areas with an entrance in Asgarnia will also be included. Access to Catherby from White Wolf Mountain will be restricted and prevented through the use of magical barriers, as it is considered part of the Kandarin region.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Fremennik/Summary
title: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Fremennik/Summary
lead: The Fremennik Province area covers the entire Fremennik Province (including the Fremennik Isles) along with Lunar Isle and Weiss. Its southern border is defined by the river south of Rellekka, with the lighthouse included. Instances of areas in the Fremennik Province and underground areas with an entrance in the Fremennik Province will also be included. Access to Kandarin via the bridge south of Rellekka will be blocked by magical barriers.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/General/Summary
title: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/General/Summary
lead: General covers miscellaneous areas available to everyone outside of Varlamore and Karamja. This covers areas accessible only via fairy rings, including the Abyssal Area, Abyssal Nexus, Zanaris, Gorak Plane, Enchanted Valley, and Cosmic entity's plane.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Kandarin/Summary
title: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Kandarin/Summary
lead:
The Kandarin area covers the entire Kingdom of Kandarin, along with the Feldip Hills, Ape Atoll and Crash Island. Instances of areas in Kandarin and underground areas with an entrance in Kandarin will also be included (with the exception of Taverley Dungeon and the Underground Pass).

Access to Nightmare Zone is restricted. To obtain Nightmare Zone points, speak to Dominic Onion and purchase them for 1 gp each.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Karamja/Summary
title: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Karamja/Summary
lead: The Karamja area covers the entire island of Karamja along with the island of Crandor and the Realm of the Fisher King. Instances of areas in Karamja and underground areas with an entrance in Karamja will also be included.

title: Demonic Pacts League/Areas/Varlamore
lead: Varlamore covers the entirety of Varlamore, including the island of Aldarin as well as the Stranglewood. It is the starting area for the Demonic Pacts League.
