label: Demonic Pacts League/Boosted drops
title: Demonic Pacts League/Boosted drops
lead: Items from certain sources are given a boosted drop rate in Demonic Pacts League. All players receive a 2x drop rate multiplier after unlocking their first relic, this is further boosted to 5x upon reaching the fourth tier of relics.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Demonic Pacts
title: Demonic Pacts League/Demonic Pacts
lead:
Demonic Pacts are a complementary system to relics that focuses purely on providing powerful and unique combat boosts across the three main styles. Pacts are similar to combat masteries from past events, however the progression is less linear and has many more options.

There are over 130 individual nodes in the pact tree which are allocated with Pact Points. Although a total of 44 Pact Points can be acquired from any three regions (not including Varlamore, Karamja and general tasks), players can only spend up to 40 of these pacts. Two of these are given during the Leagues tutorial. Demonic Pact tasks are indicated with a demon's head inside the helm.

id: page:demonic pacts league/echo bosses and echo equipment
label: Demonic Pacts League/Echo bosses and echo equipment
title: Demonic Pacts League/Echo bosses and echo equipment
lead: Echo bosses are a returning system from Raging Echoes League that grant players the opportunity to fight challenging variants of existing bosses, targeting difficulty levels more suited to the power level that players attain during Leagues.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Guide
title: Demonic Pacts League/Guide
lead: The Demonic Pacts League presents unique decisions and challenges compared to other content and game modes in Old School RuneScape. Since players are restricted to just 5 of the 10 available regions in the game, sacrifices have to be made regarding training skills, acquiring gear, and making money. This guide aims to provide information about the league mechanics, different training methods, and money making guides based on the constraints within the league.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Guide/Collection Log
title: Demonic Pacts League/Guide/Collection Log
lead: Many tasks in Demonic Pacts League are related to completing collection log slots. The following can be used to view possible collection log slots by region requirements.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Guide/Skills
title: Demonic Pacts League/Guide/Skills
lead:
All skills other than Sailing are available in the Demonic Pacts League. As all accounts are ironmen, skill training is often more similar to ironman training methods than pay-to-play ones. Training methods available will vary widely depending on what relics and areas are unlocked.

All players begin with level 3 Herblore and level 5 Runecraft, with all other skills at level 1. Experience rates begin at 5x the usual rate and increase as relic tiers are unlocked. Experience rewards such as quest rewards and experience lamps will be multiplied by this multiplier.

label: Demonic Pacts League/New player guide
title: Demonic Pacts League/New player guide
lead:
Welcome to the Demonic Pacts League! This guide is aimed primarily at those who have never participated in one of the Leagues before and are looking for an overview of what the league is, how it works, and how to play.

For more specific info, many guides are available from the main Demonic Pacts League page.

label: Demonic Pacts League/Relics
title: Demonic Pacts League/Relics
lead:
Relics are powerful buffs which are unlocked with League Points. Relics offer bonuses that boost actions related to gathering, processing, teleportation, and combat. Upon completing the league tutorial, players are presented with the choice of their first relic between three. Additional relics can be unlocked as players reach certain point thresholds and unlock new tiers.

Once players choose a relic from a tier, it will be permanently unlocked and another relic cannot be chosen from that tier.

lead:
This page contains a list of all the tasks in the Demonic Pacts League. Completing tasks during the league allows players to earn league points and unlock relics and areas containing new content and tasks. Tasks span five difficulty levels: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite, and Master. Completing a task requires its respective area to be unlocked, unless otherwise stated.

For a list of only tasks that grant Demonic Pact points click here.

label: Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T1)
title: Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T1)
lead: The Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T1) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing the Demonic Pacts League. It can be purchased for 1,000 League points from the Leagues Reward Shop. It consists of a hood, robe top, robe bottom, and boots.

label: Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T2)
title: Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T2)
lead: The Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T2) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing the Demonic Pacts League. It can be purchased for 5,000 League points from the Leagues Reward Shop. It consists of a hood, robe top, robe bottom, and boots.

label: Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T3)
title: Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T3)
lead: The Demonic Pacts Relic Hunter (T3) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing the Demonic Pacts League. It can be purchased for 20,000 League points from the Leagues Reward Shop. It consists of a hood, robe top, robe bottom, and boots.

label: Demonic Ruins
title: Demonic Ruins
lead:
The Demonic Ruins, originally known as Annakarl during the rule of Zaros, is a desecrated temple that is located in level 44-48 Wilderness. Players within range of the ruins will have their Prayer points passively recharged. As with all locations in the Wilderness, . The entire area is multicombat.

The ruins are notable for being the only place to find greater demons on free-to-play worlds. All four demons are level 92.

label: Demonic throne (interface item)
title: Demonic throne (interface item)
lead:
The Demonic throne is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Demonic throne.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Demonikin
title: Demonikin
lead: Demonikin is an expletive used in Gielinor. This expletive is used by Zavistic Rarve during Zogre Flesh Eaters when shown the Sithik portrait (bad), by the player during One Small Favour when asking Captain Bleemadge about T.R.A.S.H. and when talking to Wizard Cromperty about freeing people stuck in rockfaces. Just east of the bank in Draynor Village, the guard perched on a tree will use the term to admonish the player if an axe is used on the tree his feet dangle out of.

label: demons
title: demons
lead:
Demons are a category of creature characterized by a beastly appearance, and often a red or black colouration. Most demons are followers of Zamorak, the god of chaos, and as such, are often considered to be evil. Demons prefer attacking with melee, although a few are also known to use ranged and magical attacks. When a demon dies, they typically leave behind demonic ashes instead of bones. Demons originate from their home world of Infernus, also known as the Infernal Dimensions.

A wide variety of creatures are encompassed in this category, including many which are not explicitly referred to as demons in-game. Some demons are considered sub-classes of other varieties, and thus will count towards a Slayer task for the primary class. These cases are labelled in parenthesis. There are multiple types of demons: Avernic demons, such as Thammaron, Tsutsaroth demons (a tribe of Avernic demons), such as K'ril Tsutsaroth and Porazdir, and Chthonian demons, such as Duke Sucellus and Duke Mephitis.

label: Dentristus
title: Dentristus
lead:
Dentristus was a farm hand who was in love with his lord's daughter, Arastasia, though he knew he would never win her hand. During a harsh winter, the Wintertodt was drawn from the north devouring animals and crops, devastating villages along its path. He vowed to stop the Wintertodt, for he could not bear to see Arastasia in despair. The lord offered Arastasia's hand in marriage if he were to be successful.

Geared with his lord's best armour and weapon, he followed the trail of destruction that the Wintertodt had left behind. Destrius lay dead before he ever saw the wintertodt, frozen to the bone. A grim reminder the Wintertodt could not be fought alone.

label: Denulth
title: Denulth
lead:
Commander Denulth is the forefront of the Burthorpe Imperial Guard in the Principality of Burthorpe, and acting leader during Prince Anlaf's sudden illness, as well as a commander in the Burthorpe–Troll Country War.

Talking to him is required to start the Death Plateau and Troll Stronghold quests. He can be found at the training grounds by a rectangular tent, near The Toad and Chicken inn.

label: Deranged archaeologist/Strategies
title: Deranged archaeologist/Strategies
lead:
The Deranged archaeologist is a demi-boss located on Fossil Island. A simple mistake during the fight can cause instant death due to his special attack.

He attacks with both Ranged and melee but will use only Ranged if the player does not stand in melee distance. Although his Magic defence stat is quite high, his Magic level is very low, which makes him very easy to hit with Magic. The most effective way to kill the archaeologist is to use Magic from several tiles away while using Protect from Missiles and avoiding his special attack. Note that the archaeologist can use melee attacks on tiles immediately diagonal to him.

label: Derril
title: Derril
lead:
Derril is a character mentioned only on page 21 of my notes, a collection of pages recovered by the player during and after the Barbarian Training miniquest. He does not appear in-game, although some details regarding his history can be gleaned from the notes.

According to the page, Derril was involved with a group of explorers that entered the Ancient Cavern beneath Baxtorian Falls at an undetermined point in the past. The notes suggest that the group attempted to open the mithril door found near the cave's centre through a variety of methods, including the fishing explosives normally utilised in the Slayer skill to kill mogres. Evidently Derril was the one that suggested the group use the explosives, although whether he was part of the expedition or merely offered them advice prior to their entry is unknown.

label: Derygull Templeton
title: Derygull Templeton
lead:
Derygull Templeton was one of the seven priestly warriors who died fighting the Morytanian hordes at Silvarea. He came from Falador.

He is described in The Sleeping Seven as "A great oak of a man, so well imbued with Saradomin's will and martial ability that he fair commanded people's respect and admiration and they eagerly followed him into battle. His booming voice rallied man in times of fierce fighting, this allowing them to regroup and focus their brutal, savage violence and force capitulation from writhing, cowardly, evil hordes."

label: Deryk Paulson
title: Deryk Paulson
lead: Deryk Paulson is the writer of the Varlamore envoy, found in the Grand Library in Arceuus. No information about his status, race, location or involvement in the events that are mentioned in the book are currently known.

label: Desert boots
title: Desert boots
lead:
Desert boots are boots suitable for desert environments such as the Kharidian Desert south of Shantay Pass. Wearing the boots delays the desert heat effect by 6 additional seconds. The boots have no other bonuses.

A full set of desert clothing is needed for the The Tourist Trap quest. They are given to a slave miner in exchange for a set of slave robes which permit the player to access a deeper area of the mining camp.

label: Desert camouflage gear
title: Desert camouflage gear
lead:
Desert camouflage gear is a set of hunter gear made at the Fancy Dress Shop in Varrock or Pellem's Fur Store in the Hunter Guild, with desert devil fur. Contrary to popular belief, these do not improve catch rates of any hunter creatures.

To make desert camo tops and legs, bring 4 desert devil fur and 40 coins to the Fancy Dress Shop or Pellem's Fur Store. Desert devil furs are obtained by hunting Desert devils in the Uzer hunting area, requiring at least 13 Hunter to trap. The set may be stored in a costume room's armour case.

label: Desert heat
title: Desert heat
lead:
Desert heat is a game mechanic occurring in the Kharidian Desert south of the Shantay Pass. Every 24-132 seconds (depending on armour worn) a player spends in the desert, they will drink 1 dose of water from a waterskin in their inventory. Without any water to drink, the player takes 1-10 damage. Wearing armour will decrease the interval from 90 seconds (when wearing no armour items) down to a minimum 24 seconds with full armour. Equipment without a negative heat resistance include magic robes, vambraces (gloves however do have negative resistance), non-metal boots (fancy and fighting boots are considered metal) and capes.

The heat of the desert will also evaporate water from bowls of water, buckets of water, jugs of water, and vials of water on the same timer.

label: Desert Mining Camp
title: Desert Mining Camp
lead:
The Desert Mining Camp is a slave camp located south of Al Kharid in the Kharidian Desert. It features prominently in The Tourist Trap quest.

Run by Captain Siad, prisoners from Al Kharid are sent to the mining camp to serve out their sentences in the mines.

label: Desert outfit
title: Desert outfit
lead:
The Desert outfit consists of two sets of members-only clothing that are suitable for desert environments, like the Kharidian Desert south of Shantay Pass.

The following pieces of the desert outfit individually delay the desert heat effect:
*Fez - 12 additional seconds
*Desert top - 12 additional seconds
*Desert top (overcoat) - 12 additional seconds
*Desert legs - 12 additional seconds
*Desert robes - 12 additional seconds

label: Desert robe
title: Desert robe
lead:
Desert robes are suitable for desert environments, like the Kharidian Desert south of Shantay Pass. When worn, this clothing item delays the desert heat effect by 12 additional seconds. It has no other bonuses.

A full set of desert clothing is needed for the The Tourist Trap quest. They are given to a slave miner in exchange for a set of slave robes to allow the player access to a deeper area of the mining camp.

label: Desert shirt
title: Desert shirt
lead:

A full set of desert clothing is needed for the The Tourist Trap quest. They are given to a slave miner in exchange for a set of slave robes to allow the player access to a deeper area of the mining camp.

label: Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire
Desert Treasure II Rewards Beta
title: Desert Treasure II Rewards Beta
lead:
The Desert Treasure II Rewards Beta ran to test various rewards that have passed the Community Consultation polls for Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire for play testing in a separate game save. This is so that players can try out the rewards and give feedback before a second poll is brought forward to ask players whether they'd like the rewards in question to be implemented in the live game as a reward from the post-quest bosses.

Notably, players are given a boss helper tool, which allows players to switch to the Ruinous Powers prayer book, as well as a variety of functions.

label: Desert Voyage
title: Desert Voyage
lead:
Desert Voyage is a music track unlocked in members parts of Kharidian Desert. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing this track, Arabian 3, Desert Heat, The Desert, Egypt, Scarab, Sphinx and Sunburn.

In Classic mode, the track plays around the Desert Mining Camp, or the entrance to the Smoke Dungeon.

label: Desert Wolf
title: Desert Wolf
lead:
A desert wolf is a type of wolf that is located all over the north-west of the Kharidian Desert, as well as in the Necropolis. Players who wish to kill desert wolves should bring protection from desert heat, such as waterskins, the circlet of water, or the Desert amulet 4.

They are aggressive to players level 54 Combat and below.

label: Deserted Keep
title: Deserted Keep
lead:
The Deserted Keep is an abandoned surrounded by lava, located deep in the Wilderness. It spans level 50 to 54, and is found to the east of the Mage Arena. A web blocks the entrance to the keep, so unless someone else has slashed it recently, players will need a knife or a weapon with a slash attack style to enter or exit the keep.

East of the keep lies the Resource Area and the Chaos Elemental.

label: Destroy
title: Destroy
lead:
Destroy is a feature in Old School RuneScape for certain quest-related items, discontinued items and holiday drops that replaces the usual "Drop" option available to all other items. It most often applies to items which cannot be traded.

When destroying items, players can use either the '1' or 'Y' key on their keyboard to select the 'Yes' option, or the '2' or 'N' option on their keyboard to select the 'No' option.

label: Developer Blogs
title: Developer Blogs
lead: Developer Blogs, or Dev Blogs are newsposts which are released prior to notable content updates, typically describing the direction or development process behind the upcoming update. Many developer blogs are marked as website updates.

label: Dharok the Wretched's equipment
title: Dharok the Wretched's equipment
lead: Dharok the Wretched's equipment is obtainable from the Barrows Minigame. Note that completing the minigame does not guarantee you will get a Barrows item. Like all Barrows equipment, Dharok's armour requires 70 Defence to wear, while the Greataxe requires 70 Attack and Strength to wield. Like all Barrows items, the armour will degrade over time while in combat. Once it degrades, displaying a durability rating of 100, 75, 50, or 25, it is no longer tradeable. Only non-degraded and fully degraded versions are tradeable.

label: Diabolical aegis
title: Diabolical aegis
lead:
The diabolical aegis was a scrapped two-handed melee weapon pitched as a reward from the Doom of Mokhaiotl. It would have required 70 Attack, 75 Strength, and 75 Defence to wield.

With an attack speed of 4, the aegis would have had both a 25% demonbane effect, as well as a 25% "demonward" effect, which would reduce damage taken from demons by 25%. It also would have a passive effect of resetting attack delay if used to finish off any demonic enemy. Additionally, it would have split its damage into two hitsplats like Torag's hammers and the dual macuahuitl.

label: Diamond
title: Diamond
lead:
Diamonds are precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut diamonds with a chisel at level 43 Crafting, yielding 107.5 experience.

A diamond is required to enter the Zanaris marketplace.

label: Diamond amulet
title: Diamond amulet
lead:
A diamond amulet is an amulet created by using a ball of wool on a diamond amulet (u). The unstrung diamond amulet is created by using a gold bar and a diamond on a furnace with an amulet mould in the inventory. It is the fourth highest level amulet that can be created. This requires a Crafting level of 70 and provides 100 Crafting experience when made.

It can be turned into an amulet of power with Lvl-4 Enchant.

label: Diamond amulet (u)
title: Diamond amulet (u)
lead:
A diamond amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular diamond amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut diamond and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 70 Crafting is required to make one, yielding 100 experience. When used with a ball of wool, it becomes a diamond amulet, giving 4 experience. After it is strung, it can be enchanted into an amulet of power, requiring level 57 Magic and yielding 67 experience.

label: Diamond necklace
title: Diamond necklace
lead:
A Diamond necklace is made by using a gold bar, a diamond, and a necklace mould on a furnace. This requires level 56 Crafting and gives 90 Crafting experience.

A diamond necklace can be enchanted into a phoenix necklace by using the Lvl-4 Enchant spell. This requires level 57 Magic, one cosmic rune, and ten earth runes.

label: Diamond ring
title: Diamond ring
lead:
The diamond ring is made by using a gold bar, a cut diamond and a ring mould on a furnace. Making it requires a Crafting level of 43, and gives 85 experience.

The diamond ring can be enchanted into a ring of life by members through the use of the Lvl-4 Enchant spell.

label: Diamonds of Azzanadra
title: Diamonds of Azzanadra
lead:
The Diamonds of Azzanadra consist of four diamonds that play a role in the Desert Treasure I quest. A player must collect all four gems from each of the four guardians (Kamil, Damis, Fareed and Malak) in order to free Azzanadra, a mahjarrat. Each diamond represents a part of the Mahjarrat's soul, and may be found in locations representative of their different themes. The diamonds, with the exception of the blood diamond, are obtained by killing each of the guardians after the player has looked into the mirrors to find their locations; the blood diamond is obtained by killing a rival of the guardian rather than the guardian himself.

Should the player wish to keep copies of the diamonds after the quest, before putting the last diamond into the pyramid's final unpowered obelisk, the player should drop the duplicates. After this, the quest can be safely completed without having the diamonds be automatically removed from one's inventory or bank.

label: Diango
title: Diango
lead:
Diango is a merchant located in Draynor Village who sells toys and other commemorative items in his store, Diango's Toy Store. He is able to replace lost holiday items that the player has previously earned from holiday events.

He was originally added as part of an April Fools' joke. Players had been requesting horses in the game for some time, and were excited to find out that Diango was to be added to sell "horses" in his store. However, Diango actually sells toy horseys, which are not rideable and are mostly useless. He has since been a part of several holiday events, such as the 2013 Halloween event.

label: Diango's Toy Store
title: Diango's Toy Store
lead: Diango's Toy Store is located in Draynor Village market, run by Diango next to his Toy Stall. Many holiday events are centred around Diango and his store. Players who have lost a non-tradeable holiday item can visit this store to have it replaced free of charge.

It reveals information on some of the witch's experiments, giving the player clues on how to get into the back yard and what to expect during the fight.

label: Did you know?

lead:
"Did you know?" are a series of game facts that are displayed in the chat interface upon login. The feature is enabled for all accounts by default. It can be toggled off in the settings. Its chat message colours can also be adjusted there.

They were added on 23 April 2025 in the Poll 84: Misc Mayhem update. More facts are intended to be added at a later date.

label: Digsite
title: Digsite
lead:
The Digsite is an archaeological excavation area just east of Varrock. Players need to proceed far enough into the Dig Site quest in order to fully use it. This area is a members-only location. It is visited during several quests.

During The Dig Site quest, players learn that the area was once Senntisten, the capital of the Zarosian Empire during the Second Age. During the quest, players find an ancient talisman and a stone tablet telling all mortals to tremble before the power of Zaros. This area is said to be part of a city three times bigger than Varrock which supposedly reached to Edgeville (then known as Paddewwa). It was destroyed during the God Wars and replaced by Saranthium, which was destroyed several hundred years before Avarrocka was established in 700 of the Fourth Age.

label: Digsite Dungeon
title: Digsite Dungeon
lead:
The Digsite Dungeon is below the Digsite and can only be accessed during and after The Dig Site quest. It appears to have once been a temple of Zaros.

Players rarely use the dungeon after the quest, because of the dungeon's distance from a bank, though it has several iron pickaxe and bucket spawns and five silver rocks.

label: Digsite workman
title: Digsite workman
lead:
The Digsite workmen can be found in and around the Digsite, as well as carrying rocks to the Varrock Museum. They can also be pickpocketed, giving 10.4 Thieving experience if successful.

They play an important role in The Dig Site quest as one may steal an animal skull from them. Also, players who come to work at the Digsite without the necessary tools can pickpocket the workmen and eventually gain most of the items needed, although this can take some time.

label: Dimintheis
title: Dimintheis
lead: Dimintheis Fitzharmon is a noble of Varrock. He is featured heavily in the quest Family Crest, and plays a crucial role in the quest Defender of Varrock. He is a descendant of an important Elder of Avarrocka, and is the father of Avan, Caleb, and Johnathon Fitzharmon. His house is located south of Varrock's east gate, north of the Fancy dress shop in the fenced off area.

label: Dinh
title: Dinh
lead:
, a tool of the legendary smith.]]
Dinh was a legendary and renowned dwarven master smith from Lovakengj. He presumably lived during the Fourth Age before Xeric took power over Great Kourend. Dinh is described as the greatest smith of all time, imbuing the power of the Dark Altar into his work, and some of his work still persists to this day. One of Dinh's greatest accomplishments was forging the Doors of Dinh, which were made to contain the Wintertodt and have lasted for centuries. Dinh resided in a remote tower of his own design named Dinh's Redoubt, today more commonly named the Forsaken Tower, on a small peninsula just west of Lovakengj. The tower was where Dinh made and stored some of his greatest creations such as Dinh's bulwark.

The tower was eventually raided by Xamphur and a group of raiders on Xeric's order, who tarnished Dinh's legacy and stole most of his inventions and took them to Mount Quidamortem. Dinh's fabled hammer was recovered from the tower by an adventurer, who was sent to recover the hammer for the dwarven smith Undor. It was considered the only tool capable of fixing the Doors of Dinh, which for the first time since their creation was starting to fail, due to sabotage.

label: Disciple of Iban
title: Disciple of Iban
lead:
Disciples of Iban are cultists who worship Iban, and are located in the Underground Pass. They drop Zamorak monk robes, which must be worn to enter Iban's temple during the Underground Pass quest. After Iban is killed, they disappear permanently.

Formerly, Disciples of Iban would drop a broken Iban's staff if the player lost theirs. With the release of Song of the Elves, this is no longer the case. To retrieve a new staff, you must now talk to Koftik at the entrance of the Underground Pass.

label: Disease
title: Disease
lead:
Disease is a status effect which can be caused by any monster found in the crypts of Jiggig: zogres, skogres, the zombie with the ruined backpack and Slash Bash as well as fever spiders. It can also be caused by failing to pick the lock on an Ogre Coffin at Jiggig, by failing to cut a scrapey tree in Trouble Brewing or sailing through the fetid waters without the innoculation station facility. Additionally, the Bottle of zogre's sloppy kisses found while charting will disease as well as poison the player. Every 1.5 minutes, its strength will reduce by 1. It can be reapplied and will reset the disease amount to the max value applied by the source.

When a player has disease, shown by a yellow hitsplat ( ), one of the player's skills, excluding Hitpoints and Prayer, is reduced by the number on the hitsplat every 18 seconds. Stats are restored one level every minute meaning it can take a long time to naturally recover from reduced stats. If the targeted skill is already level 1, then it will instead reduce the player's Hitpoints.

label: Disease (farming)
title: Disease (farming)
lead:
Disease is a condition that can afflict most crops grown through the Farming skill.
When a healthy crop ends a growth cycle, there is a chance it may become diseased. While diseased, the crop stops growing and does not advance to the next stage. Crops do not recover from disease on their own, and may die at the end of the diseased cycle if left uncured. The cycle length of a diseased crop will tend to become one tier slower than if it were healthy, using the next slowest growth tick than typical for the crop. Dead crops yield no experience and require use of a spade to dig up their remains before planting another crop in the patch.

Players may treat plants in diseased herb, flower, allotment, hops, hardwood tree, celastrus, belladonna, cactus, and mushroom patches with plant cure to restore the crop to health. Doing so may let the crop advance to the next growth stage normally upon the end of the cycle, although it is possible that it may become diseased again. For diseased trees, fruit trees, spirit trees and bushes, the player may use secateurs on the plant to trim the diseased branch and restore the crop to health. Alternatively, if a player has access to the Lunar Magic spellbook they may use the Cure Plant spell instead, which saves the player valuable inventory space during Farming runs.

label: Diseased coral (Sailing Beta)
title: Diseased coral (Sailing Beta)
lead: Diseased coral was a Farming plant found in the Sailing alpha game files. Though coral farming was not accessible during the alpha, it was likely intended to be the diseased form of elkhorn, pillar, and umbral coral planted in a coral patch. It has a prune option to return the coral to health, or else it will eventually turn into dead coral. In the actual release of coral farming, each type of coral has distinct diseased variants, so the alpha variants were never released.

label: Disk of returning
title: Disk of returning
lead:
The disk of returning is an item purchased from Diango's Toy Store for coins. Players can activate the disk, which requires them to be inside the Dwarven Mine; when activated, the player is teleported into the Blackhole, where Thordur resides. To leave, simply activate the disk again. This will cause players to reappear in the Dwarven Mine, next to Boot and the sign in the north-western corner of the mine. This means it could conceivably be used to quickly travel from the south-eastern part of the mine to the north-western part. This can be useful for Free-to-play Ultimate Ironmen to train their Smithing with Superheat Item in the mines, by accessing the anvils next to the respawn location after leaving the black hole, or for players running from Falador to the Ruins of Camdozaal.

The 'blackout' option on the disk may also be used in the easternmost part of the White Knights' Castle Crypt, although the 'activate' option does not work. This may be used to quickly reach certain clue step locations by teleporting to Falador, entering the crypt, and then entering and leaving the blackhole.

label: Display case

label: Display name glitch
title: Display name glitch
lead:
The display name glitch was a major glitch that occurred on 27 February 2024. After scheduled maintenance took place and the servers were brought back online, an issue was identified with player display names. Players were able to change their display name and to display names already in use by other players - this was quickly abused to take the names of renowned players, or those with very short character length names, with the same issue also affecting newly created characters.

Jagex took the game and some other systems (including the ability to change display names) offline, and worked on reverting the name changes back to their state at 9:30AM GMT. They also refunded name change credits to players affected by the incorrect name changes.

label: Distillator
title: Distillator
lead:
The distillator is a quest item used only in Biohazard. It is found in a crate within the storeroom on the of the Mourner Headquarters. Players are able to access the storeroom after killing the level 13 Mourner to obtain a key used to unlock the gate.

It is returned to Elena in order to run some tests.

label: Distractions and Diversions
title: Distractions and Diversions
lead:
.]]

Distractions and Diversions, also known as DNDs or D&Ds, are sporadic activities that, as the name suggests, are distractions and diversions from other content players may be engaged with. Unlike minigames, Distractions and Diversions are typically encountered by chance, and may not always be specifically sought after. For instance, a player may receive a Champion's scroll or Clue scroll while training Slayer, or encounter Shooting Stars while Questing.

label: Diversity & Inclusion updates
title: Diversity & Inclusion updates
lead: Diversity & Inclusion updates (also known as D&I changes) are unpolled changes to Old School RuneScape that are introduced by updating various content from decades past to reflect the social norms of today, ensuring the game remains an accepting and inclusive space for all players. Like game integrity updates, D&I updates are not voted on by players and cannot be vetoed by the community.

label: Divine potion
title: Divine potion
lead:
Divine potions are stat-boosting potions that increase the player's level in one or more skills for 5 minutes. Drinking these will inflict 10 damage to the player but provide the stat boost for five minutes. Natural stat decay is disabled for the stats affected by the divine potion. They are made by using crystal dust as a tertiary ingredient on some decaying stat-boosting potions, such as the super attack potion.

Each divine potion will fill a specific stat boost, which can still be drained through various means such as Saradomin brews. Even if the stats are drained, if the player drinks a corresponding potion, including a non-divine one, the player can still maintain the boost. For example, if the player drank a divine ranging potion, drank a few Saradomin brews, restored the stat drain with a super restore and then drank a normal ranging potion, the player would still benefit from the divine ranging potion's effect. Once the five minutes provided by the potion expires, the boosted stat is returned to the player's normal level.

label: Dizana
title: Dizana
lead:
Dizana was a legendary hero of Varlamore, also known as the Heroine of the Hunt. Replicas of her quiver are given to players as a reward for completing the Fortis Colosseum; a replica is also on display at the Grand Museum in Civitas illa Fortis. Other than this, not much is known about her.

Statues of Dizana can be seen throughout Fortis.

label: Doctor Orbon
title: Doctor Orbon
lead:
Doctor Orbon is located in the East Ardougne chapel, and is involved in the Sheep Herder Quest. He sells the plague set, consisting of a plague jacket and a pair of plague trousers, that protects players from the poisonous sheep. He seems to be a scientist who has invented a suit that helps protect people from the infected sheep around the north of East Ardougne. The quest cannot be completed without his help.

If talked to while wearing full mourner clothes, he will ask for his payment, saying 'he won't keep the charade any longer for free', and asks to tell the head mourner about it. This implies that he is part of the Mourners or is working for them.

label: Dodge
title: Dodge
lead: Dodge is a combat effect that allows players to negate damage from any non-typeless attack. This effect has only ever applied to the Masori armour during the Nex Weapons Beta where players could test its effects. The Masori armour in its current form no longer utilises the dodge effect.

label: dog
title: dog
lead:
A dog can be found on the farm south of Falador, and in the caves under The Hollows. The dog in Falador farm is kept as a pet by Sarah, the farm's owner, along with Sadie and a sheepdog that lives inside the house. He roams the chicken pen on the farm's western side. Two additional dogs are located within a small cave accessible after entering the tunnels during In Search of the Myreque. Take the middle tunnel on the western wall to see them.

Players can pet the dog, resulting in the player saying and a chatbox message stating He tries to lick your hands as you pet him.

label: Doll of iban
title: Doll of iban
lead:
The doll of iban is a quest item used in the later stages of the Underground Pass quest. It is initially obtained by searching the chest belonging to Kardia the witch in her house deep in the underground pass, west of West Ardougne.

The doll is turned into an effigy of Iban by using Iban's shadow, Iban's ashes, Iban's blood and Iban's dove on it, all of which have to be obtained by completing various tasks in the dungeon. Progress on the doll is saved if it is lost. At the end of the quest, the doll is thrown down the Well of Voyage to banish Iban from Gielinor.

label: Dolmen
title: Dolmen
lead: Dolmens are burial tombs used by gnomes, that can be found south of the Tree Gnome Stronghold and inside the Tree Gnome Village. Due to the gnomes' smaller size, the dolmen resembles a table for humans.

label: Dommik
title: Dommik
lead:
Dommik is the owner of Dommik's Crafting Store., a Crafting shop in Al Kharid. Most players use him to purchase needles and thread used in the Crafting skill.

Due to the fact that a cow field is nearby, he's useful for running the dropped cowhides from Lumbridge to the tanner in Al Kharid, to his crafting shop to buy supplies for making items out of leather.

label: Dommik's Crafting Store.
title: Dommik's Crafting Store.
lead:
Dommik's Crafting Store is a Crafting supplies store owned by Dommik located in north-eastern Al Kharid. It is a convenient place to buy Crafting supplies due to its close proximity to a bank and a tanner.

Dommik's Crafting Store has an identical stock to that of Rommik's Crafty Supplies in Rimmington.

label: Donkey
title: Donkey
lead:
depicts a donkey ballerina.]]
Donkeys are domesticated equines that are used as working animals in Gielinor, such as for the purposes of pulling carts. Not much else is known of them, as they are only directly referenced during the What Lies Below quest when the player character mistakes a rickshaw cart for a donkey cart.

However, they are also indirectly referenced on a number of other occasions:

label: Donny the lad
title: Donny the lad
lead: Donny the lad is one of the three Bandits that lead the Wilderness Bandit Camp. Players cannot talk to Donny, any attempt to will give the player a message that states: "Donny the Lad is not interested in talking". Speedy Keith and Black Heather are the other two leaders of the Wilderness Bandit Camp.

label: Donovan the Family Handyman
title: Donovan the Family Handyman
lead: Donovan the Family Handyman is one of the murder suspects in Murder Mystery. He can be found on the top floor of the Sinclair Mansion, wandering around.

label: Doogle leaves
title: Doogle leaves
lead:
Doogle leaves are herbs that players can use on a raw sardine to make a seasoned sardine. They then feed the seasoned sardine to Fluffs, a cat in the Gertrude's Cat quest. After the quest, players may still season sardines with the leaves, but the doogle sardines can not be used to feed player-owned kittens.

It may also be needed for the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest as a possible seasoning for Fycie, Bugs or Rantz.

label: Doom of Mokhaiotl/Strategies
title: Doom of Mokhaiotl/Strategies
lead:
After completion of The Final Dawn, players can challenge the Doom of Mokhaiotl, who is found in the Ruins of Mokhaiotl by returning through the northernmost entrance.

Similar to Yama, players who die fighting the Doom are sent back to the lobby area instead of their respawn point, where their graves are also located. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have 20 total delves, after which the standard death cost will apply.

label: Doomion
title: Doomion
lead:
Doomion is a demon encountered during the Underground Pass quest. When killed, it drops the amulet of doomion, which is needed to obtain Iban's shadow. Protect from Melee should be used during this part of the quest to save hitpoints for coping with its attacks.

It is possible to use the small bridges connecting the platforms as a safespot to attack using Ranged, Magic, or with a halberd. In the quest, the player must also kill the other demons, Othainian and Holthion.

label: door
title: door
lead:
A door or a gate is an entrance (or exit) in a wall or fence, which sometimes acts as a passage through a physical boundary. It could be an entrance into a city, into a building, into a room, or into a field (especially when outdoors). The names of particular doors or gates may include an or other qualifier. For example, the guards' entrance to the Black Knights' Fortress is marked by a sturdy door.

The buildings in Al Kharid and the Kharidian Desert have a curtain that serves in place of a door. A trapdoor is a similar concept, except that it allows passage vertically downwards from one story to another. It always has a ladder, a staircase, steps or a rope below to allow passage back up again.

label: Door (Ardougne Castle)
title: Door (Ardougne Castle)
lead: The doors in the north and south wings of the Ardougne Castle's require a Thieving level of 61 to open. They guard entrance to rooms containing the Ardougne Castle chests, and a black scimitar also spawns behind the southern door.

label: Door (Chaos Druid Tower)
title: Door (Chaos Druid Tower)
lead: The door is the entrance to the Chaos Druid Tower. Unlocking the door requires level 46 Thieving and grants 37.5 experience.

label: Door (Lumbridge Swamp)
title: Door (Lumbridge Swamp)
lead:
The door can be used to enter the shed in Lumbridge Swamp or Zanaris. The door never visually opens when interacted with.

If entered with a dramen staff equipped and obtained during the Lost City quest, players are instead transported to Zanaris. If the elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary is completed, a dramen staff is not needed and simply opening the door transports players, thus making the shed normally inaccessible. However, when on a certain easy clue step which requires players to dance within the shed, opening the door instead prompts players if they want to go Zanaris or not, making the shed accessible as long as players have the clue scroll.

label: Door (Magic axe hut)
title: Door (Magic axe hut)
lead: The door is the entrance to the Magic axe hut located in the Wilderness. A lockpick and level 23 Thieving are required to unlock the door.

label: Door (McGrubor's Wood)
title: Door (McGrubor's Wood)
lead:
The door in the shack in McGrubor's Wood can be opened after completion of the Temple of Ikov quest by using the shiny key on the door, or by left-clicking the door while having the key in the inventory.

In the shack is an entrance to the Temple of Ikov dungeon leading to the section with lesser demons.

label: Door (Mourner Basement)
title: Door (Mourner Basement)
lead: This door is found in the basement of the Mourner Headquarters. It provides access to the Mourner Tunnels. A new key is required to open it until the removal of the Mourners from the basement.

label: Door (Nulodion)
title: Door (Nulodion)
lead:
The Door is the entrance to the western house at the entrance to the Dwarven Mine on Ice Mountain. It is locked until the Dwarf Cannon quest has progressed until the player has been ordered to pick up items from Nulodion, the cannon engineer. The door automatically closes after the player walks through it.

Nulodion is inside and gives the player an ammo mould and Nulodion's notes to bring back to Captain Lawgof during the quest. After the quest, he sells the Dwarf multicannon.

label: Door (Pirates' Hideout)
title: Door (Pirates' Hideout)
lead: The door is the entrance to the Pirates' Hideout located in the Wilderness. A lockpick and level 39 Thieving are required to unlock the door.

label: Door (Ross' House)
title: Door (Ross' House)
lead:
The door is the entrance to Ross' house. Unlocking the door requires level 13 Thieving and grants 15 experience. Whether you succeed or fail in unlocking the door, there is a chance (between ~77% at level 13 and ~2% at level 99) that you will lose 10% (rounded down) of your current Hitpoints. You will not receive any damage if you have ten Hitpoints or less. The chance to both avoid damage and unlock the door scales between 0.7% at level 13 and 15% at level 99.

When given a Mahogany Homes contract for Ross' house, the player can open the door without needing to unlock it.

label: Door (Yanille Dungeon)
title: Door (Yanille Dungeon)
lead: The door is an alternate entrance to the Yanille Agility Dungeon located in the basement of a house in south-east Yanille. To pick the lock and open the door, players must have a lockpick and a Thieving level of 82. Picking this lock is a requirement of the Ardougne Elite Diary. There seems to be about a 10-15% chance of success to open the door every attempt.

label: Door key
title: Door key
lead:
Door key can refer to the following:

*Door key (Darkness of Hallowvale) - A key acquired during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest.
*Door key (Witch's House) - A key acquired during the Witch's House quest to open said house. May also be required for Mourning's End Part II.

label: Door key (Witch's House)
title: Door key (Witch's House)
lead:
The Door key is a quest item used in Witch's House, Grim Tales, and Mourning's End Part II. It is found by searching under a potted plant left of the front door of the witch's house in Taverley. Additionally, another key spawns on the of Nora T. Hagg's house. In Grim Tales, a key may be obtained from Princess Miazrqa after Rupert has been freed.

In Witch's House and Grim Tales, it is used to open the front door of Nora T. Hagg's house. In Mourning's End Part II, it may be needed to obtain the death talisman.

label: Door man
title: Door man
lead: Door men are unused NPCs who could originally be found guarding the entrance to the marketplace in Zanaris. In 2006, Zanaris was graphically updated, and the door men were replaced by Gatekeepers. As a result, they have never been present in Old School RuneScape.

title: Doorways
lead:
Doorways is a music track that can be unlocked at locations outside Varrock city walls, including the Cooks' Guild, Champions' Guild, and Jolly Boar Inn. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Expanse, Greatness, and Still Night. It can also be unlocked on the Isle of Souls.

If using Classic music mode in free-to-play area, it only plays at the Jolly Boar Inn or the Lumberyard.

label: Dorgeshuun
title: Dorgeshuun
lead:
, a prominent Dorgeshuun cave goblin.]]

The Dorgeshuun, often referred to as cave goblins or the "lost tribe", are a race and tribe of subterranean goblins that inhabit the tunnel network beneath southern Misthalin. Dorgesh-Kaan is their capital city, founded 2900 years ago. Their name, in the ancient goblin language, translates to "Goblins of the Strong Spears."

label: Dorgeshuun Civil War
title: Dorgeshuun Civil War
lead: The Dorgeshuun Civil War was an internal conflict in the Dorgeshuun tribe in Dorgesh-Kaan.

label: Dorgeshuun weapons
title: Dorgeshuun weapons
lead: Dorgeshuun weapons are weapons made of bone, used by Dorgeshuun tribe. Most of them may be purchased from Nardok in Dorgeshuun Mines Nardok's Bone Weapons shop after completing The Lost Tribe quest.

label: Doric
title: Doric
lead:
Doric is a dwarf that lives in a small hut north of Falador and directly east of the Taverley gate. He plays a minor role in the Devious Minds quest but is mostly known for his quest called Doric's Quest. His hut contains an anvil and a whetstone.

Doric's anvils are the closest to the Dwarven Mine. He has a steel pickaxe on his back. He is the self-proclaimed best maker of pickaxes in Gielinor, but he has a running order with Nurmof and will not sell the player any.

label: Doric's hut
title: Doric's hut
lead:
Doric's hut is a small hut located south of Goblin Village, just east of the gate to Taverley. There is a small wheat field just south of it. The only inhabitant, Doric, is a dwarf who specialises in the Smithing skill.

As the name implies, this hut is the starting location of Doric's Quest, and can be started by talking to Doric. After the quest, players can use the 2 anvils inside the hut; currently the closest anvils to any banks in Falador.

label: Doric's Quest
title: Doric's Quest
lead: Doric's Quest is a quest involving Doric the dwarf, who is happy to let the player use his anvils but first requests an errand.

label: Double Trouble (disambiguation)

label: Dr Foster

's certificate of Advanced Healing, signed by Dr Foster.]]
Dr Foster-MMD, PRD, is or used to be the Head of Magical Healing at PoxStead College over 200 years ago, as noted by their signature on Fairy Nuff's certificate of Advanced Healing.

label: Dr Harlow
title: Dr Harlow
lead:
Dr Randulf Harlow is a retired vampyre slayer in the Blue Moon Inn in Varrock. If a player has started Vampyre Slayer, they must buy him a beer in order to convince him to teach them how to kill Count Draynor. Dr Harlow will then give players a stake. After completing the quest, Dr Harlow will go back to what he was saying before ("Buy me a beer pleash").

During the 2021 Halloween event, he and other bar attendants respond with fear to the arrival of Death in a cutscene.

label: Dr. Darius Gnomalus
title: Dr. Darius Gnomalus
lead:
Dr. Darius Gnomalus is a gnome and Head of Psychology at the Gnome Institute of Knowledge, a scientific research organisation. He was interviewed for the paper , a text about gnomish humour.

During the interview, Dr. Gnomalus was asked about his opinion as to whether gnomes used humour as a self defence mechanism against insecurity, primarily their height insecurity. He responded negatively, attacking the idea and claiming gnomes could be serious, before he exploded, sending bits of gnome everywhere. Dr. Gnomalus then revealed that it was a synthetic replica he had created as a joke and made comments about the interviewer's gullibility and possible oxygen deprivation, causing the interviewer to terminate the interview in disgust.

label: Draconic (attribute)
title: Draconic (attribute)
lead:
Draconic is an attribute that confers a vulnerability to dragonbane weapons.

Most monsters created from dragonkin experiments are draconic, including dragons, hydras, drakes, wyrms, wyverns, and the Great Olm. The exceptions are listed below.

label: Draconic shield
title: Draconic shield
lead:
Draconic shield may refer to:
* Ancient wyvern shield
* Dragonfire shield
* Dragonfire ward

title: dragon
lead:
Dragon may refer to:

*Dragon (race)
*Dragon equipment

*Dragonkin - ancient race responsible for the creation of dragons and dragon equipment

label: Dragon (race)
title: Dragon (race)
lead:
A dragon (Draconis Rex ) is a large, winged, reptilian monster which possesses the ability to exhale dragonfire. Since a dragon's fiery breath attack can hit up to 50 damage, to safely fight them, an anti-dragon shield or anti-fire potion is almost always required. If both the shield and the potion are used, 100% of the damage is prevented in most cases.

Dragons drop dragonhide of their particular colour if [[#Chromatic dragons|chromatic]], and metal bars in their metal type if [[#Metal dragons|metallic]]. All dragons drop some variant of valuable dragon bones. [[#Brutal dragons|Brutal dragons]], the King Black Dragon, and Vorkath drop two hides instead of one. Dragons are weak to dragonbane weapons.

label: Dragon armour set
title: Dragon armour set
lead:
Dragon armour set may refer to:

*Dragon armour set (lg)
*Dragon armour set (sk)

label: dragon battleaxe
title: dragon battleaxe
lead:
The dragon battleaxe is the third strongest battleaxe, behind the leaf-bladed battleaxe and the zombie axe. It requires 60 Attack and the completion of Heroes' Quest to wield.

The battleaxe is not commonly used as a primary weapon, however it has a useful strength-boosting special attack that can be activated before switching to a more powerful weapon to attack with.

label: Dragon bitter
title: Dragon bitter
lead: Dragon bitter is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Strength by 2 while draining Attack by 5% + 2. It can be obtained through brewing at level 39 Cooking granting 347 experience. It is brewed using 4 krandorian hops, 2 buckets of water, 2 lots of barley, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the dragon bitter(m).

label: Dragon bitter (barrel) (interface item)
title: Dragon bitter (barrel) (interface item)
lead:
The Dragon bitter (barrel) is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Dragon bitter (barrel).

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: dragon bones
title: dragon bones
lead:
Dragon bones are bones dropped by most adult dragons, which give 72 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways: 
* 216 XP when casting Sinister Offering.
* 216 XP when offered at the sacred bone burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.
* 252 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple. The Temple additionally has a 50% chance to not deplete the bones; effectively doubling the XP to 504 per bone.
* 288 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of dragon bonemeal.
* 290 XP when blessed and broken down into blessed bone shards and offered at the libation bowl, or 348 XP when offered with a jug of blessed sunfire wine. Virilis outside the altar will exchange noted bones for 10 coins each.

The relative ease of collecting dragon bones, combined with the amount of experience earned from them, makes them widely viewed as a fast, cost-effective way to train Prayer.

label: Dragon boss
title: Dragon boss
lead:
Dragon boss refers to a boss that is susceptible to dragonbane weapons. It may refer to one of the following:

*Elvarg, a strong green dragon fought at the end of Dragon Slayer I
*Galvek, an extremely powerful dragon fought at the end of Dragon Slayer II
*Great Olm, a large white salamander and final boss in the Chambers of Xeric raid
*King Black Dragon, a powerful black dragon fought in his lair
*Vorkath, a very powerful blue dragon encountered during Dragon Slayer II and afterwards
*Alchemical Hydra, a boss version of hydra found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon
*Hueycoatl, a boss residing in the Hailstorm Mountains

label: Dragon chainbody
title: Dragon chainbody
lead:
The dragon chainbody is the highest tier of chainbody in the game, requiring a Defence level of 60 to equip. As with most dragon armour, players cannot make this item using the Smithing skill.

Prior to the release of Barrows armour, the chainbody was an extremely rare item, and was a status symbol for accomplished players. Today, the chainbody is not nearly as prestigious as it once was, and its lack of a strength bonus means it is often substituted with armour such as the fighter torso for Slayer tasks and general melee training, where maximising one's damage output takes precedence over defensive bonuses.

label: Dragon dagger
title: Dragon dagger
lead:
The dragon dagger is the second-strongest dagger available in Old School RuneScape, behind the abyssal dagger. It can be wielded by players with at least 60 Attack after completion of the Lost City quest. As with most daggers, it can be poisoned.

If casting either of the alchemy spells on a dragon dagger, use a cleaning cloth on poisoned versions to make more profit, as the value of the unpoisoned dagger is higher than any of the poisoned versions: compared to .

label: Dragon equipment
title: Dragon equipment
lead:
Dragon equipment is a range of tier 60 equipment available to members. With the exception of dragon arrows, dragon darts and dragon javelins, dragon items are made of a hard, dark-red metal called Orikalkum, with the former three being made of dragon talons rather than Orikalkum.

The dragonkin are the original creators of Orikalkum armour and weaponry, which is nicknamed by adventurers as dragon equipment.

label: Dragon gold-trimmed armour
title: Dragon gold-trimmed armour
lead: Dragon gold-trimmed equipment can be created by using ornament kits, a potential reward from elite Treasure Trails, on Dragon equipment. The equipment has identical stats to their unornamented counterparts, and the pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Dragon head
title: Dragon head
lead:
Dragon head may refer to:

*Dragon med helm
*Dragon full helm
*Elvarg's head
*Ensouled dragon head
*Kbd heads, its stuffed and mounted versions.
*Vorkath's head, its stuffed and mounted versions.

label: Dragon Inn
title: Dragon Inn
lead:
The Dragon Inn is the only bar in Yanille. It is located in the south-west of the city, between the Hunter store and a small lake. The bar is one of the two places in RuneScape where you can buy dragon bitter and one of four places you can buy a Greenman's ale. The sign out the front of the inn is a picture of a red dragon head from front on. The name of the inn probably comes from the two stuffed dragon heads mounted about the counter of the bar.

The of the inn is the bar. The bar is furnished with a table and chairs and four barstools around the bar. The bar has barpumps, though the bartender never uses them. There are stairs to the in the south-west corner of the room. The of the inn contains two room for people staying in the inn. Each room contains a bed and a bedside table, with the north room also containing a hat stand.

label: Dragon Slayer I
title: Dragon Slayer I
lead:
Dragon Slayer I is a quest that focuses on the player's journey to slay Elvarg, the dragon of Crandor. Often described as the hardest, yet most rewarding quest available to free-to-play players, those who successfully complete it gain the ability to equip the rune platebody and green d'hide body (as well as their many variations), in addition to the dragon platebody.

Starting this quest is required to use any dragonfire protection, although it does not need to be completed. It also allows dragons to be received as a Slayer task.

label: dragon leather
title: dragon leather
lead:
Dragon leather may refer to:
*Green dragon leather
*Blue dragon leather
*Red dragon leather
*Black dragon leather

label: dragon longsword
title: dragon longsword
lead:
The dragon longsword is the third-strongest longsword available in Old School RuneScape, and can only be wielded by players who have at least 60 Attack and have completed the Lost City quest.

As with all dragon weapons, players cannot make this item using the Smithing skill. However, it can be purchased in the Zanaris marketplace from Jukat for 100,000 coins (requires a Diamond for entry). The weapon can also be received as a reward from elite Treasure Trails.

label: Dragon mace
title: Dragon mace
lead:
The dragon mace is the fifth-strongest mace stat-wise after the Tzhaar-ket-em, Sarachnis cudgel, Viggora's chainmace, and Inquisitor's mace. It can only be wielded by players who have an Attack level of at least 60 and who have completed the Heroes' Quest.

The mace can be purchased for 50,000 coins at the Happy Heroes' H'emporium in the Heroes' Guild, or from other players.

label: Dragon mask
title: Dragon mask
lead:
Dragon masks are possible rewards from Treasure Trails and can be worn in the head slot. Chromatic dragon masks can be obtained from hard Treasure Trails, while metal and lava dragon masks can be obtained from elite Treasure Trails.

All of the dragon masks can be stored independently from each other in the treasure chest of a player's costume room.

label: Dragon med helm
title: Dragon med helm
lead:
The dragon med helm is a piece of armour which requires 60 Defence to equip. It was the first piece of dragon armour to be released.

Zulrah, revenants, Sarachnis and some dragons can drop the dragon med helm. Any monster that has access to the standard rare drop table can also drop the dragon med helm. It can also be found in the Barrows chest as a separate item with 1012 rewards potential and all brothers killed.

label: Dragon necklace
title: Dragon necklace
lead:
A dragon necklace, also known as a dragonstone necklace is a necklace made by using a gold bar, a dragonstone and a necklace mould on a furnace, requiring a Crafting level of 72 and providing 105 experience when made. It can also be obtained as a reward from elite clue scrolls.

The dragon necklace can be enchanted into a skills necklace with the Lvl-5 Enchant spell. This requires level 68 Magic, one cosmic rune, fifteen earth runes and fifteen water runes.

label: Dragon pet
title: Dragon pet
lead:
Dragon pet can refer to one of the following:
* The following pets for dragon bosses:
** Prince black dragon
** Vorki
* The following pets for other draconic bosses:
** Ikkle hydra
** Pet snakeling
** Olmlet
** Huberte
* Baby dragons
* Fairy dragons

label: Dragon pickaxe (disambiguation)
title: Dragon pickaxe (disambiguation)
lead:
Dragon pickaxe may refer to:

* 
* , a cosmetic variant made by using a dragon pickaxe upgrade kit.
* , a cosmetic variant made by using a Zalcano shard.
* , a cosmetic variant made by using a Trailblazer tool ornament kit. 
* , a rare loot obtained from Volcanic Mine ore packs, which can be repaired to create a Dragon pickaxe.

label: Dragon scale dust
title: Dragon scale dust
lead:
Dragon scale dust is the result of using a pestle and mortar on a blue dragon scale. It is used in Herblore for mixing weapon poisons and antifire potions.

Wesley (in Nardah) will crush unnoted or noted herblore secondary items for 50 coins per item.

label: Dragon shield
title: Dragon shield
lead:
Dragon shield may refer to:

*Anti-dragon shield
*Dragon sq shield
**Shield left half
**Shield right half
*Dragon kiteshield
*Dragonfire shield
*Dragonfire ward
*Wyvern shield

label: Dragon spear
title: Dragon spear
lead:
The dragon spear is a two-handed melee weapon that requires level 60 Attack to wield. It does not require the completion of a quest to equip. Like most spears, it can be poisoned.

The spear is a rare drop from both the rare and gem drop tables. On the gem drop table, the spear will only drop if the Legends' Quest has been completed, otherwise a talisman will be dropped in its place. However, the rare drop table does not require the quest's completion in order to be able to receive it as a drop. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from both tables.

label: Dragon sq shield
title: Dragon sq shield
lead:
The dragon sq shield is the strongest square shield in Old School RuneScape. It requires 60 Defence to wield, along with completion of Legends' Quest. The dragon square shield is created by combining the shield left half, a mega-rare drop from the rare drop table, and the shield right half, which must be purchased for 750,000 coins from Siegfried Erkle in the Legends' Guild or Erdan in the Myths' Guild. The two shield halves are combined at any anvil with a hammer in the inventory to produce the dragon square shield, a process that requires level 60 Smithing and grants 75 experience.

Smithing this shield in West Ardougne is a task required in the hard set of the Ardougne Diary.

label: Dragon trophy
title: Dragon trophy
lead:
Dragon trophy may refer to:

* Twisted dragon trophy
* Trailblazer dragon trophy
* Shattered relics dragon trophy
* Trailblazer reloaded dragon trophy
* Raging echoes dragon trophy
* Demonic pacts dragon trophy

label: Dragonbane weapons
title: Dragonbane weapons
lead:
Dragonbane weapons are a class of weapons that are more effective against draconic creatures than other monsters.

There are three dragonbane weapons currently available to players:

label: dragonfire
title: dragonfire
lead:
Dragonfire is the fiery breath attack used by most dragons, hence the name. While it can deal considerable damage to unprepared players, the damage may be [[#Protection|negated or reduced]] with certain shields, (super) antifire potions and Protect from Magic.

Since dragonfire attacks usually roll with the monster's Magic accuracy against the player's Magic defence , dragonfire can be thought of as a magic attack that can be typeless or not depending on its source.

label: dragonhide
title: dragonhide
lead:
Dragonhide, often shortened "D'hide", is a general name for green dragonhide, blue dragonhide, red dragonhide, black dragonhide or anything made from them.

Dragonhides are a 100% drop from non-metal dragons along with dragon bones. They can also be obtained from looting impling jars. Adult dragons drop dragonhide of their respective colour, meaning green dragons drop green dragonhide, while black dragons drop black dragonhide. However, baby dragons do not drop dragonhide of any colour.

label: dragonhide armour
title: dragonhide armour
lead:
Dragonhide armour is worn by rangers and is made from the hide of dragons through the Crafting skill. It provides decent defensive bonuses for melee and ranged, with good defensive bonuses against magic. As such, it is commonly worn in situations where a strong defence against magical attacks is required, including elemental Slayer monsters and player killing. Dragonhide armour comes in different colours depending on the hide it was made from, with different colours offering different bonuses. Each colour of dragonhide armour has vambraces, a body, and chaps.

The colours of dragonhide, in order of ranged strength, are:
* 
* 
* 
*

label: Dragonhide Leather
title: Dragonhide Leather
lead:
The Dragonhide Leather is an unreleased scenery object that was meant to be in the Ranging Guild.

It is possible that it was meant to appear in a room alongside the Leatherworker. However, when the Weapon poison salesman was removed (before release), the Leatherworker was moved to his stall instead, and the Dragonhide Leather was never included in the game.

label: Dragonkin
title: Dragonkin
lead:
The dragonkin are a race of powerful and intelligent dragon-like creatures who were known to humans as powerful and malevolent creatures that spread destruction wherever they went. In battle, they have been seen to use exceptionally powerful dragonbreath.

The dragonkin are the original creators of armour and weaponry based on Orikalkum, a material which is known by adventurers as dragon equipment. They are also the creators of dragons and other related species. Supposedly, they are also responsible for creating the draconic visage.

label: Dragonkin Conflicts
title: Dragonkin Conflicts
lead:
The Dragonkin Conflicts were a series of attacks by the Necrosyrtes, a group of Dragonkin who spread terror to cool their rage. The attacks started immediately after the God Wars and lasted for approximately a hundred years.

After the abuse of the Stone of Jas by Saradomin and Zamorak during the God Wars, the Dragonkin, unable to stop them, were tortured by Jas' curse and thus cooled their rage by attacking human settlements as the Fourth Age began. Being largely resistant to conventional weapons, the Dragonkin were left unchecked.

label: Dragonstone
title: Dragonstone
lead:
Dragonstones are rare gems which can be cut from uncut dragonstones, requiring 55 Crafting and yielding 137.5 experience. It can then be made into dragonstone jewellery by using a furnace along with a gold bar and a mould.

Monsters with access to the rare drop table have a chance to drop cut dragonstones.

label: Dragonstone amulet
title: Dragonstone amulet
lead:
The dragonstone amulet is an amulet worn in the neck slot. It is made by stringing an unstrung dragonstone amulet with a ball of wool or the String Jewellery spell. The unstrung amulet requires 80 Crafting and is made by using a gold bar on a furnace with a cut dragonstone and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Crafting one in the Neitiznot furnace is a task in the Elite Fremennik Diary.

label: Dragonstone amulet (u)
title: Dragonstone amulet (u)
lead:
A dragonstone amulet (u) is the unstrung version of the regular dragonstone amulet. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace, while having a cut dragonstone and an amulet mould in the inventory.

Level 80 Crafting is required to make one, and crafting this item grants 150 experience. Stringing this item using a ball of wool gives 4 experience.

label: Dragonstone armour
title: Dragonstone armour
lead:
Dragonstone armour pieces are rewards from the Elven Crystal Chest. The stats of the dragonstone armour are exactly the same as rune equipment. All pieces require level 40 Defence to equip, with the dragonstone platebody requiring the completion of Dragon Slayer I to wear.

This set can be stored in the armour case space of a costume room in a player-owned house. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

label: Dragonstone ring
title: Dragonstone ring
lead:
The dragonstone ring is made by using a gold bar, a dragonstone, and a ring mould on a furnace. It requires a Crafting level of 55 and provides 100 Crafting experience when made.

The dragonstone ring can be enchanted into a ring of wealth through the use of the Lvl-5 Enchant spell at level 68 Magic, requiring 15 earth runes, 15 water runes, and 1 cosmic rune.

label: Drain
title: Drain
lead: Drain may refer to:

label: Drain (Demon Slayer)
title: Drain (Demon Slayer)
lead:
The drain is located outside the north-eastern corner of Varrock Palace's kitchen. During the Demon Slayer quest, the player must use a bucket of water on the drain in order to flush Sir Prysin's lost key in to the sewer below.

Searching the drain prior to flushing out the key results in the player mentioning that they can see a key inside the drain.

label: Drake (disambiguation)
title: Drake (disambiguation)
lead:
Drake is a Slayer monster in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon.

Drake may also refer to:

label: Drake (interface item)
title: Drake (interface item)
lead:
The Drake is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Drake.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Dramen
title: Dramen
lead:
Dramen may refer to:

*Dramen staff, a staff required to use fairy ring teleportation
*Dramen branch, a branch cut from the dramen tree, used in Lost City and Recipe for Disaster quests
*Dramen tree, a tree featured in Lost City quest
*Dramen Tree Spirit, a monster required to be killed to cut dramen branches

label: Dramen branch
title: Dramen branch
lead:
The Dramen branch is cut from the Dramen tree found in the dungeon below Entrana island. Cutting it from the Dramen tree requires 36 Woodcutting. It can be crafted into a Dramen staff with a knife and 31 Crafting, allowing access to the lost city of Zanaris and to the fairy ring transportation network.

The branch can only be obtained after starting the Lost City quest and having Shamus the leprechaun explain the Dramen Staff. Otherwise, the player will receive the message, "The tree seems to have an ominous aura to it. You do not feel like chopping it down," when attempting to chop it down.

label: Dramen staff
title: Dramen staff
lead:
The dramen staff allows players to enter Zanaris from the shed in the Lumbridge Swamp after completion of the Lost City quest. Players can obtain the staff by using a knife on a dramen branch, which requires a Crafting level of 31. It is possible to return to Entrana and cut more branches from the Dramen tree, although it is advised players make multiple staves upon completion of the quest, as this prevents the need for a return trip should the staff be lost. It is a blunt weapon and cannot autocast spells.

The dramen staff is required to use the fairy ring transport system, which requires partial completion of the Fairytale II - Cure a Queen quest. Players who have completed the Elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary can use them without the staff.

label: Dramen tree
title: Dramen tree
lead: The Dramen tree is a special tree which is featured in the Lost City and Recipe for Disaster quests. It is located in the Entrana Dungeon, a location where players cannot bring any weapons or armour. It requires level 36 Woodcutting to cut.

label: Drawers
title: Drawers
lead:
Drawers may refer to:

* Oak drawers
* Oak drawers (flatpack)
* Teak drawers
* Teak drawers (flatpack)

label: Drawers (white)
title: Drawers (white)
lead: White drawers are scenery found in the hospital at Emir's Arena as well as in western Great Kourend. The drawers can be searched for a small chance to receive an uncut red topaz. No other items can be obtained from searching.

label: Draynor bank
title: Draynor bank
lead:
The Draynor bank is the only bank in Draynor Village. It was added alongside the Varrock east bank.

The bank is a popular location for free-to-play players who are fishing or chopping the nearby willows. Note that this bank may not always be safe for players under level 15 combat, due to the fact it is possible for other players to lure the nearby dark wizard into the bank.

label: Draynor Bank Robbery
title: Draynor Bank Robbery
lead:
The Draynor bank robbery was a severe break-in at Draynor bank, accompanied by criminal damage and several murders. The only suspect is the Wise Old Man, although there are some theories that Cool Mom227 aided him.

The main source of evidence is a security tape from inside the bank. Players can watch this recording by talking to the bank guard standing outside by the broken wall. The recording can be viewed again by paying the guard 50 coins.

label: Draynor farm
title: Draynor farm
lead: The Draynor farm is a large farm field in eastern Draynor, just west of Mill Lane Mill. The farm features a large wheat field, a large potato field, two un-interactable farmers, and a barn with many goblins. The barn is commonly used by players hoping to use a cannon to quickly obtain the goblin champion scroll.

label: Draynor jail
title: Draynor jail
lead:
The Draynor jail is a small jail run by Lady Keli, patrolled by several aggressive jail guards who will attack anyone under level 53. The jail is a multi-combat area, which makes it a very dangerous place for lower levels. Approaching from the east normally allows a quicker entry to the jail, with less exposure to the guards. The jail is mainly featured in the Prince Ali Rescue quest.

Within the jail compound are a few nettles growing on the eastern and southern sides of the building, which can be picked when wearing some form of gloves. Just west of the jail building, a second trapdoor entrance to the Draynor Sewers can also be found. There is an inaccessible guard tower found on the southern side. Osman's daughter, Leela, can be found north-west just beyond the compound by the wheat field.

label: Draynor Manor
title: Draynor Manor
lead:
Draynor Manor is a large, haunted, mansion located north of Draynor Village owned by Count Draynor Drakan. The manor contains 4 floors and is a central location for 4 quests: Ernest the Chicken, Vampyre Slayer, Animal Magnetism, and is visited briefly during Fairytale I - Growing Pains. It also holds a portal that grants access to the dimension where killerwatts reside.

There is a Belladonna patch outside the manor, towards the west and within the fence.

label: Draynor Village
title: Draynor Village
lead: Draynor Village, often shortened to Draynor, is a small village located between Falador and Lumbridge. The village is featured in many quests, and is a popular training location due to its willow trees and master farmers.

label: Dreaded Years of Tragedy
title: Dreaded Years of Tragedy
lead:
The Dreaded Years of Tragedy (sometimes also called 'Dread' and 'Dreadful') was a period of conflict in Ardougne from approximately 95 to 98 of the Fifth Age, wherein a group of Zamorakians had moved into an abandoned Outpost to the north-west of the city and began to cause chaos. Their acts included theft and petty vandalism, as well as magical tricks and charms. They also convinced others, such as Drozal, to join their evil acts.

Though the acts of the Zamorakians seem petty and humorous, great distress was caused to the people of Ardougne and the conflict led to their calling on a Saradominist army to get rid of the Zamorakians in 98, a battle which would later become known as The Great Battle, in which all but one from each side were killed. This in turn led to the founding of the Ardignas line of kings in the new kingdom of Kandarin, which still rules to the present day, and the Equal Trade Market.

label: Dream (disambiguation)
title: Dream (disambiguation)
lead:
Dream may refer to:

label: Dream (music track)
title: Dream (music track)
lead:
Dream is a music track that is unlocked when the player first arrives in Lumbridge. It can also be heard around the Lumbridge Swamp and farmlands. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Autumn Voyage, Book of Spells, Flute Salad, Harmony, and Yesteryear.

In Classic mode, the track plays on the path from Lumbridge to Draynor Village.
