label: Drezel
title: Drezel
lead:
Drezel is a monk who lives in Silvarea, the passage bordering Morytania and the forest east of Varrock, under Paterdomus. He is heavily involved with the Priest in Peril quest, where you must help him escape from jail, and once Priest in Peril and The Restless Ghost are completed, players can talk to him to start the Nature Spirit quest.

Players can quickly reach him by taking a fairy ring to or using a Salve Graveyard Teleport, and then running northwest across the bridge and into the trapdoor.

label: drift net fishing
title: drift net fishing
lead: Drift net fishing is a skilling method that requires 44 Hunter and 47 Fishing, rewarding experience in both. Drift nets are used to catch fish shoals in the Underwater area of Fossil Island. This method offers fairly high experience rates in both skills at the cost of drift nets, and requires more attention than other passive fishing methods.

label: Drinks
title: Drinks
lead: Drinks are consumable items that come from a cup, tankard, beer glass, cocktail glass, or other container, excluding vials for potions.

label: Drogo dwarf
title: Drogo dwarf
lead: Drogo is a dwarf in the Dwarven Mine, who runs Drogo's Mining Emporium, which sells pickaxes. In the past, Drogo's store often had a large stock of iron and other ores on free worlds, primarily because his store is in close proximity to two iron rocks.

label: Drogo's Mining Emporium.
title: Drogo's Mining Emporium.
lead: Drogo's Mining Emporium is located in the Dwarven Mines, run by Drogo. Although labelled as a mining shop, it only sells hammers and bronze pickaxes. It does provide a place for players to sell their ores or bars, but it is relatively unpopular due to its inconvenient location.

label: Drogokishuun
title: Drogokishuun
lead:
The Drogokishuun is a goblin tribe. Like all other goblins, they were called upon by the god Bandos to fight in his name during the God Wars.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Goblins of the Fierce Blades".

label: Drop
title: Drop
lead:
The drop function is the action in which a player removes an item from their inventory, placing it on the ground. The drop function is one of the default right-click options (sometimes replaced with destroy for most untradeable, holiday, and quest related items) but can be made into the left-click option by toggling Shift Click to Drop in the Controls tab of the Options menu, this enables the player to drop items by holding the left-shift key and left-clicking. A dropped item does appear on the ground where the player was standing, and can be recovered at any time. Every item holds this function, except for certain untradeable items (such as event rewards) where the drop function is replaced by 'destroy' and items that cannot be dropped or destroyed such as bonds. Destroyed items do not appear where the player was standing, and to recover it, the player will have to return to the original source of the item (or a special NPC that replaces them) unless the item is permanently lost and cannot be reclaimed.

The limit to the number of different items that can fit on one game tile is 128, with stackable items such as coins and noted items counting as one. However, items dropped on the ground disappear after a certain time. In general:

label: Drop party
title: Drop party
lead:
Drop parties are events in which players drop items for fun, and other players try to pick them up first. While drop parties were traditionally held in the Falador Party Room, they can now be held anywhere in Gielinor on any world.

Drop parties are often advertised at the Grand Exchange. Some scammers falsely advertise drop parties in order to obtain donations from other players to drop, or lure unsuspecting players into dangerous locations like the Wilderness, but many drop parties are legitimate. Drops at drop parties may range from junk, like tin ore, to extremely valuable items, such as dragon, Barrows items, and godswords.

label: Drop rate
title: Drop rate
lead:
The drop rate is the frequency at which a monster is expected to yield a certain item when killed by players. When calculating a drop rate, divide the number of times you have gotten the certain item, by the total number of that monster that you have killed. For example:
*Bones have a 100% drop rate from chickens.
*Feathers have approximately a 75% drop rate from chickens.

label: drop table
title: drop table
lead: A drop table represents a list of drops that a monster is able to drop. Most monsters have their own drop table that is largely determined by the requirements to reach them, their difficulty to kill, and how quickly they are killed; for example, most slayer bosses have a fairly generous drop table as they can only be killed while on the appropriate Slayer task.

label: Drop trick
title: Drop trick
lead:
The drop trick is a technique used to gain multiples of an item that can normally be obtained only once. These items are not awarded to the player if they are already in the player's bank, house, or inventory, or in some cases, dropped where they stand.

The drop trick involves repeating the action that first obtained the item and doing the following:

label: drops
title: drops
lead:
Drops, also known as monster drops or loot, are the items monsters leave for the killer when they are defeated or die. Drops can be picked up by players. Drops often include bones, coins or other items. A lot of monsters have "100% drops", which is an item or items that are always dropped by that monster. 100% drops are more commonly bones or ashes. Certain monsters have more than one type of 100% drops. A good example of monsters who have more than one type of 100% drops are metal dragons, who drop bones and also, metal bars of the type of metal they're made of.

Large monsters (that take up more than one square) will always drop their drops in the south-westernmost square. This also applies to any Ranged ammunition that falls to the ground when ranging those monsters.

label: Drozal
title: Drozal
lead: Drozal was an Ardougnese man who joined the Zamorakians terrorising the city during the Dreaded Years of Tragedy. Some of their actions included poisoning the city's water supply and turning all children invisible. Eventually, the Saradominists revolted, causing a massive battle to erupt near an outpost. All those who participated in this battle died, except for one soldier of each side. At some point prior to the battle, Drozal had hidden his journal in a chest, which he buried near the Observatory.

label: Druid
title: Druid
lead: Druids are level 33 non-player characters found in the druidic village of Taverley, a small settlement in western Asgarnia. They attack with both Melee and Magic (similar in appearance to Entangle). These druids are sometimes fought for the herbs that they carry, although chaos druids are a better source of herbs.

label: Druid (disambiguation)
title: Druid (disambiguation)
lead:
Druid may refer to:

NPC types:
*Druid (enriched snapdragon patch)
*Druid (super truth serum)
*Druid spirit
*Elder Chaos druid (NPC)

label: Druid pouch
title: Druid pouch
lead:
The druid pouch is an item first obtained during the Nature Spirit quest. Its main use is to protect the player against the ghasts that haunt the Mort Myre Swamp.

If lost, an empty druid pouch can be reclaimed from the inside of the Nature Spirit's grotto - one respawns near the grotto pool.

label: Druid's robe
title: Druid's robe
lead: The druid's robe (bottom) is part of the druid's robes set. Pieces of the druid robes can be obtained by killing druids in Taverley.

label: Druid's robe top
title: Druid's robe top
lead: The druid's robe top is part of the druid's robes set. Pieces of the druid robes can be obtained by killing druids in Taverley.

label: Druid's robes
title: Druid's robes
lead: Druid's robes are a set of two items (top and bottom) which are dropped by Druids. They are essentially identical in appearance to desert clothing, although they do not provide protection from desert heat.

label: Druid's robes (scenery)
title: Druid's robes (scenery)
lead: A washing line of Druid's robes can be found in Taverley, nearby Tegid washing laundry in the lake.

label: Druidic
title: Druidic
lead:
Druidic may refer to:
* Druidic Ritual, a novice quest that unlocks the Herblore skill
* Druidic spell, used in Nature Spirit
* Druidic wreath, a holiday item that originated from the 2014 Midsummer event
* 3rd Age Druidic robes, a set of 3rd age equipment obtained from Master Treasure Trails
** 3rd age druidic robe top
** 3rd age druidic robe bottoms
** 3rd age druidic cloak
** 3rd age druidic staff

label: Druidic Ritual
title: Druidic Ritual
lead: Druidic Ritual is a novice quest that serves as the introduction to the Herblore skill. It takes place entirely in the vicinity of Taverley and is a fairly short quest.

label: Druidic spell
title: Druidic spell
lead:
The druidic spell is a spell scroll that can cast Bloom on rotten logs in Mort Myre Swamp to grow Mort myre fungi.

The spell is given to the player by Filliman Tarlock during the Nature Spirit quest and can be used only once, after which it turns into a used spell. The spell can only be used once the player has been blessed by Drezel during the quest. Attempting to use the spell before receiving Drezel's blessing will yield the message, "You need to be blessed before you can cast this spell." However, after completing the quest, the player can cast Bloom using a Silver sickle(b), or any of: Emerald sickle (b), Enchanted emerald sickle (b), Ruby sickle (b), Enchanted ruby sickle (b), Blisterwood sickle, Ivandis flail, or Blisterwood flail. For collectors, be cautious about dropping this item inside the grotto right before the quest's end. If left on the ground, it will disappear when the grotto shifts.

label: Drunk
title: Drunk
lead: Drunk may refer to:

label: Drunk dragon
title: Drunk dragon
lead:
Drunk dragon is a drink that can be made at level 32 Cooking, granting 160 Cooking experience.

It heals 5 Hitpoints, lowers your Attack by 2% - 3 levels, and raises your Strength by 5% + 2 levels.

label: Drunken Dwarf
title: Drunken Dwarf
lead: The drunken dwarf is a random event who occasionally appears and talks to players. If the player responds, the dwarf will give them a kebab and a beer.

label: Dry sticks
title: Dry sticks
lead: Dry sticks are the result of using broken glass on damp sticks. They are used in the Sea Slug quest to light a torch on the Fishing Platform. They can be kept after the quest, and with 30 Firemaking can be used at any time to light a torch by selecting the "rub-together" option. Unlike a tinderbox, clicking to use the sticks on an unlit torch has no effect.

label: Dryad (unused)
title: Dryad (unused)
lead:
Dryads are a cut race planned to be added to RuneScape 2. Unlike other cut creatures, they were most likely scrapped very early on. They lack any interaction options and their combat level is the default, while they were not mentioned as one of the planned updates in March 2004.

Their model was later reused for the Tree spirit random event, while Wood Dryads were eventually released in July 2006. The original Dryads have never been present in Old School RuneScape, but remain in the game files.

label: duck
title: duck
lead:
Ducks are small animals that can be found in rivers or lakes. They are a fairly good way to start training the Magic skill with low-level Curse spells and even Strike spells.

If ducks are next to the shore, it is possible to hit with a long-range melee weapon such as a halberd; however, it is uncommon for them to be there with the exception of the Fishing Guild docks, Falador Park, and the River Lum in Lumbridge.

label: duckling
title: duckling
lead: Ducklings are smaller versions of ducks found swimming in the pond north-west of Lumbridge, by Farmer Fred's farm, and in the western wing of the Farming Guild. They will only follow female ducks. Occasionally, the female duck will say: , to which any following ducklings respond with: . If the female duck they're following is killed, the ducklings will say: , followed by: and attempt to swim away.

label: Duel Arena
title: Duel Arena
lead:
The Al Kharid Duel Arena was a place where players could go to engage in one-on-one Combat. The Duel Arena was available to both members and free-to-play, though there was a limit to how much you can stake in both members and free-to-play.

Duel Arena challenge areas were identified upon entering by a battleaxe ( ) which appeared in the bottom right hand corner of the interface, during a duel this was changed to a skull ( ).

label: Duke (disambiguation)
title: Duke (disambiguation)
lead:
Duke may refer to:

* Duke (monkey), Kruk's successor as head of the Ninja Monkey Guards of Marim
* Duke Horacio, duke of Lumbridge
* Duke Rabbacio, duke of Bunbridge
* Duke Polonius, first duke of Lumbridge
* Duke Sucellus, a boss featured in Desert Treasure II
* Duke (dog), a dog featured in the 2024 Christmas event

label: Duke Horacio
title: Duke Horacio
lead: Duke Horacio is the duke of Lumbridge and the surrounding area. He lives on the of the Lumbridge Castle in a room with a quest marker in it. He also hands out anti-dragon shields to players during the Dragon Slayer I quest. More shields can be obtained via the drop trick.

label: Duke Mephitis
title: Duke Mephitis
lead:
Duke Mephitis was a chthonian demon who served as a legatus in the Zarosian Empire. He remained loyal to Zaros after Zamorak's betrayal, and lead the garrison at the fortress of Paddewwa at some point prior to its destruction in the Third Age.

The golem encountered during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire's most recent information prior to its deactivation indicates that a bandosian force lead by General Graardor marched on Paddewwa while it was under Mephitis's control, but the outcome of this encounter is unknown.

label: Duke of Bridgelum
title: Duke of Bridgelum
lead:
Duke of Bridgelum was a scrapped random event that involved going to ScapeRune to help the Duke of Bridgelum reassemble dead cows from their component parts. The player would have to select certain cow parts (udders, hind legs, etc.) from an interface.

The random event was scrapped because during testing, it was pointed out that the dismembered cow parts looked too grotesque. The reward would have been pieces of the cow outfit, which are now given out as rewards during birthday events.

label: Duke Polonius
title: Duke Polonius
lead:
Duke Polonius was the first Duke of Lumbridge. Polonius was given the land by King Claudius, the King of Misthalin at the time, and is a direct ancestor of Duke Horacio.

Polonius built Lumbridge Castle in the place of a wooden fort that had stood as a temporary fortress.

label: Duke Sucellus/Strategies
title: Duke Sucellus/Strategies
lead:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of Duke Sucellus. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by entering the asylum gates with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted.

If the player dies while fighting Duke Sucellus, their grave will appear by the asylum gates. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

label: Dummy
title: Dummy
lead:
A dummy is a sandbag that players can train on. Different types of dummy provide different amounts of Attack experience per hit, but it does not deal any damage and does not provide any hitpoints experience. This makes it ideal for players just starting out, if they are trying to keep their hitpoints level as low as possible.

Dummies in Varrock can be found in the building north of Varrock's East Bank, as well as on the top floor of Varrock Castle. Similar types of dummies can be found in Burthorpe, with soldiers training on them, as well as in the Kualti Headquarters in Civitas illa Fortis. All of these dummies will provide 5 Attack experience per hit, up to and including level 7. Players with level 8 or higher in Attack will receive no experience, instead receiving the message There is nothing more you can learn from hitting a dummy..

label: Dung
title: Dung
lead:
Dung is a troll chef found on Death Plateau. He stands next to Ash at the centre of the plateau, just in front of the cooking pot they both maintain.

When the player searches the cooking pot in My Arm's Big Adventure, the troll cooks will attack with weak ranged attacks, hoping to put you in the stew for dinner.

title: Dungeon entrance (interface item)

The Dungeon entrance is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Dungeon entrance.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Dungeon rat
title: Dungeon rat
lead: Dungeon rats are rare monsters found only in select members' dungeons. They play a key role in the Clock Tower quest in which players poison their food trough so that they attempt to escape by chewing away a railing, which allows the player to grab the white cog.

label: Dunjun
title: Dunjun
lead: Dunjun is a music track that is unlocked in Taverley Dungeon after passing the Magic axe room or by entering the Crypt under the White Knights' Castle.

label: Dunstan
title: Dunstan
lead: Dunstan is the local smith for Burthorpe. He can be found near the anvil symbol.

label: Duplicates
title: Duplicates
lead:
rewarding duplicate ham joints.]]
Duplicates or "dupes" are items that players receive in quantities greater than what is necessary or useful. In many instances, a rare drop received from a boss or minigame is valuable, but receiving the same drop multiple times is not. For example, at Wintertodt, players may receive multiple pairs of warm gloves, but only have one pair of hands to put them on, so subsequent drops serve no purpose.

Surplus warm gloves can be traded to Ignisia for an extra supply crate or 50 burnt pages, and indeed many duplicate drops can be exchanged with NPCs, sold to shops, or used on special scenery objects for experience or more useful items.

label: Dust
title: Dust
lead:
Dust may refer to:

*Pestle and mortar, used to crush (or dust) items.

label: Dust Devil (interface item)
title: Dust Devil (interface item)
lead:
The Dust Devil is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Dust Devil

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: dusty key
title: dusty key
lead:
The dusty key is a key that unlocks a gate to the Taverley Dungeon, allowing passage into the deeper parts of dungeon from the Lesser demon area to the Blue dragon area.

The player can get the key from Velrak the explorer, who is imprisoned in the Black Knight headquarters in the southern part of the Taverley Dungeon. Kill the jailer to get a key to enter Velrak's cell and talk to him, but do not ask for a reward!

label: Dusty scroll
title: Dusty scroll
lead:
Dusty scroll may refer to:

* Dusty scroll (In Aid of the Myreque), an item obtained during the quest In Aid of the Myreque.
* Dusty scroll (Secrets of the North), an item used during the quest Secrets of the North.

label: dwarf
title: dwarf
lead: Dwarves are low-levelled monsters often found in mines and dwarven settlements. They can occasionally be assigned as Slayer tasks by Turael and Spria.

label: Dwarf (Dwarven shopping store)
title: Dwarf (Dwarven shopping store)
lead: A dwarf is the shopkeeper of the Dwarven shopping store in the Dwarven Mine. He wears red clothes and is always holding a pickaxe. He sells some basic items in his store.

label: Dwarf (Mining Guild)
title: Dwarf (Mining Guild)
lead: Dwarves are located by the entrances to the Mining Guild, both on the surface in Falador alongside Gadrin, and within the Dwarven Mine. They are also located inside the guild, by the entrances to the members' area of the guild.

label: Dwarf (race)
title: Dwarf (race)
lead:
Dwarves are one of many races in Gielinor. They live predominately in Keldagrim, their capital city, and the city of Lovakengj on Great Kourend, but are also found in various mines and settlements across Gielinor.
In stature, Dwarves tend to be shorter than humans, usually being slightly above human-waist height, but considerably stockier. They are long-lived, although they tend to be gruff and short in temper. They are particularly fond of ale and often have long beards. Dwarves are particularly well known for being excellent blacksmiths, miners, and craftsmen, but usually a dwarf specialises in one area. Dwarves primarily use power-based weapons in combat, such as battleaxes, warhammers and crossbows.

label: Dwarf brew
title: Dwarf brew
lead:
Dwarf brew is a potent spirit made by Kamen. It is used in the later stages of the Underground Pass quest. It is obtained by using an empty bucket on the brew barrel inside Klank's house, found deep inside the Underground Pass.

The brew is used to light a pyre over the tomb of Iban, cremating his remains and turning them into Iban's ashes which must then be used on the doll of iban to create his effigy. The brew only needs to be used once on the tomb, after which it can be lit as many times the player likes as long as they don't possess the ashes in their inventory or have used such ashes on the doll.

label: Dwarf Cannon
title: Dwarf Cannon
lead: Dwarf Cannon is a short quest about the conflict between the dwarven outpost at the Coal truck mining site and local goblins. The quest provides access to the Dwarf multicannon, a powerful Ranged weapon.

label: dwarf multicannon
title: dwarf multicannon
lead:
The dwarf multicannon (or simply cannon) is a unique type of Ranged weapon that acts as a deployable turret using steel cannonballs or granite cannonballs as ammunition. Once deployed and loaded with ammunition, the cannon will fire at targets within its line-of-sight and range. The cannon acts as a supplemental source of damage alongside the player, and is commonly used to speed up Slayer tasks. Damage with the cannon gives reduced experience. The cannon's accuracy depends heavily on the player's current equipment, attack style and levels.

The cannon has four parts which it can be assembled from. A player may only have one cannon assembled at a time. There are many locations where setting up a cannon will be automatically prevented, as well as bosses which will destroy the cannon. If a cannon is destroyed, Nulodion will provide a free replacement.

label: Dwarf remains
title: Dwarf remains
lead:
Dwarf remains are a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. The remains are those of Gilob, and are given to Captain Lawgof after recovering them during the quest. It is found on the of the watchtower south of the Coal Trucks.

Duplicates cannot be obtained, as it does not respawn after the player has picked it up for the first time.

label: Dwarf statue (Falador)
title: Dwarf statue (Falador)
lead: Dwarf statue is a scenery object found in Falador near the entrance of the Mining Guild. Players cannot interact with this statue, but they can examine it.

label: Dwarf statue (Underground Pass)
title: Dwarf statue (Underground Pass)
lead: Dwarf statue is a scenery object found in the dwarf settlement beneath Iban's Temple in the Underground Pass. Two of these statues stand outside of the main building of the dwarf settlement. Players cannot interact with these statues, but they can examine them.

label: Dwarf Theme
title: Dwarf Theme
lead:
Dwarf Theme is a music track that is unlocked near the surface camp above the Dwarven Mine.

In Classic mode, the track plays in a wider area around the Dwarven Mine, on the path between Falador and the Barbarian Village.

label: Dwarf weed
title: Dwarf weed
lead:
Dwarf weed is the second highest level herb. Cleaning dwarf weed requires level 70 herblore and yields 13.8 Herblore experience. It is used with wine of Zamorak to create ranging potions. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a dwarf weed potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

One way to obtain dwarf weed is by planting dwarf weed seed in a herb patch at level 79 Farming. This gives you grimy dwarf weed which you can clean to obtain clean dwarf weed.

label: Dwarf weed potion (unf)
title: Dwarf weed potion (unf)
lead: A dwarf weed potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a dwarf weed on a vial of water, requiring 72 Herblore. Using a wine of zamorak on a dwarf weed potion (unf) with 72 Herblore yields a ranging potion(3) and 162.5 Herblore experience. Using nihil dust on a dwarf weed potion (unf) with 85 Herblore yields an ancient brew(3) and 190 Herblore experience. Using a lily of the sands on a dwarf weed potion (unf) with 88 Herblore yields a Menaphite remedy(3) and 200 Herblore experience.

label: Dwarven Mine
title: Dwarven Mine
lead:
The Dwarven Mine is a large mine ran by dwarves located beneath Asgarnia. It contains a variety of ores and can be accessed from the entrance south of Ice Mountain or from the two entrances located in Falador. The Dwarven Mine also connects to both the Mining Guild and the Motherlode Mine, which are located at the southern end of the mine.

At the southern end of the mine, there is a severe infestation of scorpions and King Scorpions that will trouble those with lower combat levels. You need a combat level of 65 in order to be left alone by the King Scorpions. North of the scorpions is an Agility shortcut (narrow crevice in the wall) requiring level 42 Agility. The Mining Guild can be found in the southern part of the mine, requiring 60 Mining to access. The entrance to the Motherlode Mine can be found in the south-eastern section of the Dwarven Mine marked by a dungeon icon ( ). To make use of the Motherlode Mine, players require a minimum of 30 Mining, with 57 Mining required to access the upper level.

label: Dwarven Realm
title: Dwarven Realm
lead: The Dwarven Realm is the region of the mainland continent on Gielinor controlled by the dwarven race.

label: Dwarven Shopping Store
title: Dwarven Shopping Store
lead: The Dwarven shopping store is a general store run by a dwarf in the Dwarven Mine. It is almost never visited, mainly because of its location; there are many general stores nearby (such as the ones in Falador or Edgeville) which are much easier to reach.

label: dwarven stout
title: dwarven stout
lead:
Dwarven stout is a type of ale that restores 1 Hitpoint and temporarily boosts Mining and Smithing by 1 while draining Attack, Strength and Defence by 4% + 2. It can be obtained through brewing at level 19 Cooking, granting 215 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 hammerstone hops, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the dwarven stout(m).

Drinking a dwarven stout will give the messages: You drink the Dwarven Stout. It tastes foul. It tastes pretty strong too.

label: Dwellberries
title: Dwellberries
lead:
Dwellberries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting dwellberry seeds. They are used in quests and gnome cooking.

Dwellberries heal 2 hitpoints when eaten. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.

label: dye
title: dye
lead: Dye exists in seven hues, plus the black dye. Dye is used to colour items: most commonly capes, but also certain quest items. Dyes can be made quickly by using the required ingredients on the person making the dye, given you have enough of the item and the required coins in your inventory.

label: Dye shop
title: Dye shop
lead: Dye shops are a type of store sparsely dotted over Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Dye shops sell various hues of dyes, and may also occasionally stock crafting items used in the fashioning of garments. There are three regular dye shops in Old School RuneScape, and three that are dialogue-only.

label: Dyer
title: Dyer
lead:
A dyer either makes or sells dyes. There are four:

*Aggie, the witch who lives in Draynor Village
*Ali the dyer, one of many Alis that live in Pollnivneach
*Betty, who specialises in pink dye and runs the Port Sarim magic shop
*Oronwen, who sells six colours of dye and runs the Lletya Seamstress crafting store in Lletya

label: Eadburg
title: Eadburg
lead: Eadburg is the Burthorpe Castle chef, and can be found wandering around the of the castle. She will sometimes wander outside the castle and into the courtyard.

label: Eadgar
title: Eadgar
lead:
"Mad" Eadgar lives in a cave at the top of Trollheim. He plays a very small part in the Troll Stronghold quest, where players free him from his cell. He also plays a central role in Eadgar's Ruse, acting as an advisor to the player, helping them craft a ruse with a parrot to fool the trolls into believing it to be a human.

Eadgar will give players a bowl of mountain goat stew in exchange for some logs that he can use for firewood. The mountain goat stew heals 20 Hitpoints after you exit the chatbox; it is not a physical item.

label: eagle transport system
title: eagle transport system
lead:
The eagle transport system is unlocked after completion of the Eagles' Peak quest. Players may use it to travel quickly to different Hunter areas. There are eyries in four locations: Eagles' Peak, Rellekka Hunter area, Uzer, and Feldip Hills.

A rope is required to travel using the eagles. Rope spawns are found in the Rellekka and Uzer eyries.

label: Earth Altar
title: Earth Altar
lead:
The Earth Altar is a runic altar upon which earth runes are crafted from rune essence or pure essence, providing 6.5 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Level 9 Runecraft is required to craft earth runes.

Players may create an earth tiara here by using either an earth talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 32.5 Runecraft experience. An elemental tiara can also be created here by using an elemental talisman and gold tiara, granting 40 Runecraft experience.

label: Earth battlestaff
title: Earth battlestaff
lead:
The earth battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of earth runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 58 Crafting by combining an earth orb and battlestaff. It can also be upgraded to a mystic earth staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries). The mystic earth staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.

label: Earth Blast
title: Earth Blast
lead:
Earth Blast is an earth-based blast spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 53 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

It is the strongest earth spell available to free-to-play players.

label: Earth Bolt
title: Earth Bolt
lead: Earth Bolt is an earth-based bolt spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 29 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

label: Earth elemental
title: Earth elemental
lead:
Earth elementals are found beneath Seers' Village during the Elemental Workshop I and Elemental Workshop II quests. There are several roaming around in the quest area, but the player can also cause one to appear by mining a rock in the earth room.

There are two types of Earth elementals: the ones roaming around and the ones that can be mined. Only the latter will drop elemental ores.

label: Earth orb
title: Earth orb
lead:
An earth orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Earth by using the Charge Earth Orb spell, requiring 60 Magic, on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb, 30 earth runes, and 3 cosmic runes, yielding 70 Magic experience. The Earth Obelisk is located in the Edgeville Dungeon, south of the black demons beyond the poison spiders and Chronozon.

An earth orb can be used on a battlestaff, requiring 58 Crafting, yielding an earth battlestaff and 112.5 Crafting experience.

label: Earth rune
title: Earth rune
lead: Earth runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used to cast earth-based combat spells in the standard spellbook, as well as many spells found in other spellbooks; Earth runes are used especially often for spells in the Lunar spellbook. The Confuse, Weaken, and Curse spells, often regarded as an inexpensive source of Magic experience, require earth runes in conjunction with body and water runes to cast. Some items, such as a staff of earth, provide infinite earth runes while equipped.

label: earth spells
title: earth spells
lead: Earth spells may refer to:

label: Earth Strike
title: Earth Strike
lead: Earth Strike is an earth-based strike spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 9 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

label: Earth talisman
title: Earth talisman
lead: An earth talisman is a type of talisman that lets the player access the Earth Altar. Use the talisman on the altar to get inside to create earth runes. You can also access the Earth Altar by using an earth tiara, which can be equipped to save inventory space and is made using the earth talisman. When you make an earth tiara, you are granted 32.5 Runecraft experience. If you are a member, it can be used to runecraft dust runes at the Air Altar, mud runes at the Water Altar, or lava rune at the Fire Altar. The earth talisman is consumed in the process.

label: earth warrior
title: earth warrior
lead:
Earth warriors are a type of humanoid earth elemental found in a dirt-lined chamber in the Edgeville Dungeon. This area is in the Wilderness so it is advised to come prepared for player killers. Earth warriors can be safe-spotted in the bottom right corner or top of the first chamber.

Their chamber requires the player to climb across a set of monkey bars, which requires 15 Agility. It is not possible to fail the set of monkey bars.

label: Earth Wave
title: Earth Wave
lead:
Earth Wave is an earth-based wave spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 70 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

It is the second-strongest earth spell in the game, with the strongest being Earth Surge.

label: Easel
title: Easel
lead:
Easel may refer to one of the following:
* Shield easel, built in a player-owned house Workshop.
* Banner easel, an upgraded version of the shield easel.
* Easel (scenery), a non-interactive object

label: East Ardougne
title: East Ardougne
lead:
East Ardougne is the eastern of the two districts that form Ardougne, the capital of Kandarin. It is in the members area of Gielinor.

Its neighbour, West Ardougne, governed by King Tyras, is closed off to the general public because of a plague affecting the inhabitants, but players may gain access by finishing parts of the Plague City quest. East Ardougne is most known for its wealth, zoo and the theft-stricken marketplace. East Ardougne is currently governed by King Lathas.

label: Easter egg
title: Easter egg
lead:
Easter eggs are edible holiday items. Two easter eggs can be obtained by completing one of the Easter holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Easter.

Consuming an easter egg will restore 14 hitpoints, which is the same amount of hitpoints as swordfish and pumpkins. Due to their limited availability and resulting price, easter eggs are not recommended as food.

label: Easter event
title: Easter event
lead: Easter events are annual holiday events that commemorate Easter, which typically occur towards the end of March or early April.

label: Ebel Lum
title: Ebel Lum
lead: Ebel Lum is Sir Tiffy Cashien's grandson, mentioned only in the 2016 Birthday event. Sir Tiffy hopes that he will follow in his footsteps and become a White Knight. Were he to do so, his name would be Sir Ebel Lum, which is a play on words like the names of most White Knights, meaning "cerebellum".

label: Echo orb
title: Echo orb
lead:
Echo orbs are drops from certain bosses during Leagues that allow players to fight their more difficult echo boss variants. The echo bosses have a chance to drop unique and powerful echo items.

In order to access an echo boss, the player must acquire the region's echo orb from the non-echo variant of the boss and have it in their inventory while entering the boss area. Unlike Awakener's orbs, echo orbs are not consumed upon entry, and only one orb is needed for access to the boss for the entire League.

label: Echo Virtus robes
title: Echo Virtus robes
lead:
Echo Virtus robes can be obtained by attaching echo Virtus ornament kits to Virtus robes. Their stats are identical to those of the virtus robes. Each piece of virtus robes gives a 2% magic damage bonus for a total of 6%. When using combat spells from Ancient Magicks, an additional 3% magic damage is given per piece, taking the bonus to 5% per piece for a total of 15% for the full set.

Therefore, equipping the robes requires level 78 Magic and 75 Defence. Each piece of Virtus robes gives a 2% magic damage bonus for a total of 6%. When using combat spells from Ancient Magicks, an additional 3% magic damage is given per piece, taking the bonus to 5% per piece for a total of 15% for the full set.

label: Eclipse moon armour
title: Eclipse moon armour
lead:
Eclipse moon armour is a set of ranged equipment that requires level 75 Ranged and 50 Defence to equip, which is obtained as a possible reward from the Lunar Chest in Neypotzli.

It has similar defensive stats to steel armour, but with higher crush and magic defence.

label: Economy
title: Economy
lead:
The economy in Old School RuneScape bears many similarities to economies in the real world. In RuneScape, items can be produced, exchanged and used by players. Players can exchange these items through trading or via the Grand Exchange (the market). Grand Exchange prices vary due to many factors, the most basic one being . This can have a big influence on the behaviour of players.

Real world economies behave differently from RuneScape's in some respects, particularly because of the limited time many have to play the game, which renders the availability of financial organisations such as player-owned banks, shops, stocks, or insurance companies difficult. A difference between the two economies is that median prices on the Grand Exchange only update, on average, once every 24 hours, usually resulting in a change in the price of an item of no more than 5% either way, whereas in unrestricted economies, s may change in real time, and there is no limit to how much the price can rise or fall in a given time. On top of this, there is a fundamental computer system limit on how many of an item, in this case coins, can be in one stack. The maximum number of an item that a player can hold in a stack is 2,147,483,647, as limited by a signed (positive and negative) 32-bit , i.e. 2 31 - 1, thus this the highest amount an item can be valued at. See stackable items.

label: Edgeville
title: Edgeville
lead:
Edgeville is a small town located at the border of the Wilderness. Edgeville is a popular town to trade player killing-related items, and the bank is popular among players training Runecraft via the Abyss. Edgeville is also popular with members who own amulets of glory, as it is a fast bank to get to via a teleport.

In the early development of RuneScape Classic, Edgeville only had empty buildings; it was commonly referred to as "Ghost Town" until items were placed in the buildings and the town was given its official name.

label: Edgeville bank
title: Edgeville bank
lead:
The Edgeville bank, also known as edge bank, is a popular bank found in Edgeville, east of the Grand Exchange and just below the Wilderness ditch.

On the north wall of the Edgeville bank players can find the Wilderness Statistics board, displaying their kill to death ratio in the Wilderness, as well as the ratios of nearby players. There is also a loot chest for player killers.

label: Edgeville Dungeon
title: Edgeville Dungeon
lead:
The Edgeville Dungeon is a dungeon in Edgeville. It contains a large variety of monsters spanning across a wide range of levels, as well as the Slayer master Vannaka. It can be accessed by a trapdoor south of the Edgeville bank, or a locked shed (requiring a Brass key to open) west of the Cooks' Guild.

The southern half of the dungeon is free-to-play, and is a popular location for killing Hill Giants on free-to-play worlds. The northern half is members-only, and is in the Wilderness, so anyone who wishes to explore the deeper parts of this dungeon should watch out for PK'ers and only bring items that they are willing to lose. The Members' area is a popular location for killing Chaos druids.

label: Edgeville Dungeon mine
title: Edgeville Dungeon mine
lead:
The Edgeville Dungeon mine is a mine near the centre of the Edgeville Dungeon. The mine itself is north of the hill giants and the ladder near the brass key. It is south of Vannaka and the Agility shortcut to Varrock Sewers. It is sometimes called the Skeleton Mine by some; similar to how several other mines guarded by skeletons are called the same, such as the Southern Wilderness mine. Due to being so far out of the way, the mine is almost never used by non-Free-to-play players.

It is a compact mine with a variety of ores. The resident skeletons and the occasionally visiting hobgoblin may be dangerous for players with low combat levels.

label: Edgeville General Store
title: Edgeville General Store
lead: The Edgeville General Store is a general store located in Edgeville.

label: Edgeville Incident
title: Edgeville Incident
lead:
The Edgeville incident was a military conflict that occurred in Edgeville between the Kinshra, White Knights, Temple Knights, and Solus Dellagar. Over 800 civilians, as well as the same number of white knights and black knights were killed during the battle, earning Solus Dellagar the nicknames 'Murder-mage' and 'Mad Solus.' Solus Dellagar was captured by the Temple Knights during the incident. The event is referenced heavily in the Commorb dossiers during and after the Wanted! quest.

After the death of Lord Shadwell during the battle, Lord Daquarius was unanimously voted into leadership by the Kinshra. He was the youngest ever Black Knight to the leader of the Kinshra.

label: Edgeville Mausoleum
title: Edgeville Mausoleum
lead:
The Edgeville Mausoleum is a ruin of a mausoleum just south of the village of Edgeville.

The Edgeville Mausoleum contains an entrance to the Edgeville Dungeon as well as two yew trees in the garden on the left side of the building. There is also a lever here that can teleport players to the Deserted Keep in the deep Wilderness, much like East Ardougne's lever. The lever in the Deserted Keep teleports the player to Ardougne, not back to Edgeville, unless the player has completed the easy Wilderness Diary.

label: Edgeville Monastery
title: Edgeville Monastery
lead:
The Edgeville Monastery is a two-story building north-east of Falador, east of the Black Knights' Fortress and west of Edgeville. A combat bracelet can be used to teleport inside the monastery, and is the fastest method to get there. Five monks wander inside, both in the courtyard and inside the building.

The four monks that spawn around the courtyard are an extremely popular training spot for Defence pures due to the monks' high health and low Defence, as well as their healing powers; pures could train indefinitely without food. It is recommended for most free-to-play pures as a safe and effective training method.

label: edible seaweed
title: edible seaweed
lead:
Edible seaweed is an edible version of seaweed that restore 4 Hitpoints. Edible seaweed can be cooked on a range or fire to create soda ash (an ingredient in molten glass), granting no experience.

The item is one of the possible random items required during the quest Fairytale I - Growing Pains.

label: Edicts of Guthix
title: Edicts of Guthix
lead:
The Edicts of Guthix, most prominently alluded to in the Darkness of Hallowvale quest, are a series of decrees Guthix created for the world after the last God War. At the time of this writing, there is "balance" in Gielinor between the god of order, Saradomin, and the god of chaos, Zamorak. If either god were to upset this balance by attempting to invade the other, then the other god would potentially call on reinforcements from other realms. This would escalate the crisis and lead to another devastating God War. Guthix, according to legend of his followers, would then awake and wreak justice on Gielinor, remaking the world as it has never been but destroying it in the process.

The Edicts of Guthix are being investigated by Saradomin scholars for a loophole after the revelation that werewolves had crossed the Salve and kidnapped humans for blood tithes.

label: Edmond
title: Edmond
lead:
Edmond is a civilian of East Ardougne, the husband of Alrena, and the father of Elena. He lives north of the Flying Horse Inn.

His daughter was captured by mourners during the Plague City quest. Players start this quest by speaking to him, and he plays a large role in the quest's storyline.

label: Edwina Halen
title: Edwina Halen
lead: Edwina Halen was a former Varrockian belonging to the Halen family, descending from the Elders of Avarrocka. She was the last blood descendant of Marv Halen within the family. She married into the Fitzharmon family.

label: Eek C'ho
title: Eek C'ho
lead: Eek C'ho is a lizardman mentioned only in the story . Eek was assigned the job of guarding the prisoner Magnus Rimor within the Tower of Magic. Magnus eventually opens up to Eek, and requests he bring him a journal and something to write with, which Eek complies. After a few months, Magnus asks Eek to get the warnings he wrote in the journal outside to the rest of Kourend, because "they have to know". Before Eek could do so, the Yo'kal ahk, Xamphur, took the journal from Eek, thanking the lizardman for getting Magnus to talk. The next day, Eek was promoted to a member of Xamphur's personal guard.

label: Effective Experience
title: Effective Experience
lead: Effective Experience or eXP describes the amount of experience points a player is able to accumulate within a period of time (usually 1 hour) while taking the value of a player's time into account. Effective Experience rates can be used to compare various training methods that differ in both GP/h and XP/h.

label: Efficiency
title: Efficiency
lead:
Efficiency is a measure of the cost per experience of a training method, factoring in opportunity cost (the amount of profit that was sacrificed by pursuing the training method instead of spending the same amount of time earning money). A simple formula can be used to decide whether or not it's worthwhile to spend more money on a faster training method.

Efficiency is often used in the context of evaluating, based on how valuable you perceive your time to be, two different methods to train a skill for which their experience per hour and profit per hour are known. If one method gives more experience per hour than the other and also costs less (or gives more profit), then there is no question which method is more efficient. However, if one method gives faster experience than the other but costs more (or gives less profit), then the most efficient method depends on how much the player perceives their value of time to be. It is possible to calculate which method is more efficient for a player with a known value of time. It's also possible to calculate at what value of time the two methods are equally efficient.

label: Efficient training
title: Efficient training
lead:
Efficient training refers to minimising the time spent actively training a skill by using the fastest methods available. For example, players looking to train Woodcutting with this playstyle would use tick manipulation to chop two teak logs every 3 game ticks.

Players factor efficiency into their playstyle at various degrees. Players looking to max their account might opt for methods that train multiple skills at once, whereas players looking solely to train a specific skill might use a method that's less efficient overall, but faster at training that specific skill. For example, someone looking to train Fishing efficiently might use tick manipulation to increase their chance of rolling for fish at harpoon spots; however, a player focusing on overall efficiency would do drift net fishing instead, to gain experience in both Fishing and Hunter.

Egypt is a music track unlocked in members parts of Kharidian Desert. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing this track, Arabian 3, Desert Heat, Desert Voyage, The Desert, Scarab, Sphinx and Sunburn.

In Classic mode, the track plays in and around the Shantay Pass. As such, free-to-play players can only unlock the track while on Classic mode.

label: Eirlys Cadarn
title: Eirlys Cadarn
lead: Eirlys Cadarn was an elf born to King Baxtorian and Queen Glarial sometime in the late Fourth Age. She became a mother to Islwyn before dying as a result of the Baxtorian campaign. Eirlys is only mentioned during Song of the Elves.

label: Ekeleshuun
title: Ekeleshuun
lead:
The Ekeleshuun are a goblin tribe found while doing the Land of the Goblins quest, who wear blue goblin mail. Like the other tribes found in the temple, they were called upon by the god Bandos to fight in his name during the God Wars.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Goblins of the East". They are also part of The Lost Tribe quest; on certain rocks, their logo is placed to tell the player where to go.

label: Elder chaos druid robes
title: Elder chaos druid robes
lead:
Elder chaos robes can be obtained as rare drop from Elder Chaos druids. Equipping the robes requires level 40 in Magic, with no Defence requirements. Each piece gives a Magic damage bonus of 1% for a total of 3%.

The robes can be stored in a player's magic wardrobe within their costume room.

label: Elder Dag'eth
title: Elder Dag'eth
lead: Elder Dag'eth was one of the leaders of the Zamorakian Dagon'hai in the early Fifth Age. He was presumably killed when the Dagon'hai were forced to flee Varrock following the burning of the first Wizards' Tower in the Year 70.

label: Elder Kree'nag
title: Elder Kree'nag
lead:
Elder Kree'nag was a leader of the Zamorakian Dagon'hai cult prior to their exile from Varrock in the Year 70 of the Fifth Age. He was killed, alongside the rest of the cult's elders, when they were forced from Varrock.

The death of Kree'nag and the rest of the elders would later open the position for Sin'keth Magis, the father of the Dagon'hai's current leader, Surok Magis.

label: Elder La'nou
title: Elder La'nou
lead:
Elder La'nou was one of the leaders of the Zamorakian Dagon'hai group prior to their exile from Varrock during the Year 70 of the Fifth Age. He died during the final conflict between the city guard and the Dagon'hai.

According to Sin'keth's Diary, written by Sin'keth Magis, La'nou was killed when the Dagon'hai fled the city, alongside many others. Elder Dag'eth and Elder Kree'nag also fell in the struggle, leaving the position of leader to Sin'keth.

label: Elder Weapon Beta
title: Elder Weapon Beta
lead:
The Elder Beta was open to all members. Along with the regular facilities that an unrestricted world supplied (Clan Wars portal, free-for-all portal, spellbook altar, etc.), players could obtain an elder wand and maul from the supplies table.

South-east of the bank chest, there was a boss portal that allowed players to enter an instanced encounter with monsters weak to crush attacks (Cerberus, Chaos Elemental, Kalphite Queen, and three waterfiends), along with the option to be on a Slayer task with that particular monster. It should be noted that Cerberus' area-of-effect attack will do no damage, and the Kalphite Queen can only be fought in her first form.

label: Elder-dragons
title: Elder-dragons
lead:
The elder-dragons are a world creation theory proposed in a book of folklore. The theory links the creation and 'life-force' of Gielinor to the existence of an ancient race of creatures known as the elder-dragons. As long as those dragons lived, the world would continue. Erasing the whole race would result in the 'end of the world'.

The elder-dragon theory is not widely known, nor popular with sceptics, believing it to have been created to throw doubt on the idea of Gielinor being devoid of life before the gods first arrived.

label: Elders of Avarrocka
title: Elders of Avarrocka
lead:
The Elders of Avarrocka also known as The Council of Varrock were a small group of men that ruled the town of Avarrocka, now called Varrock, during its early days in the Fourth Age.

The Elders were at first the leaders of a small wandering tribe, one of the many nomadic tribes of humans that wandered Gielinor during the Fourth Age. When they discovered the child Arrav in the forests of modern-day Misthalin, they saw him as a good omen and established the city of Avarrocka where they found him.

label: Elegant clothing
title: Elegant clothing
lead:
Elegant costumes (also known as Ele' costumes) are formal fancy clothing that come in sets of different colours (red, blue, green, purple, pink, gold, white and black) and in male and female varieties. These costumes are obtained as rewards from Easy to Medium Treasure Trails. A full costume set can be stored in the Costume room of a Player-owned house.

The red, green, and blue costumes can be obtained from easy Treasure Trails, and the purple, pink, gold, white, and black costumes from medium Treasure Trails. As some of the costume colours may be desired more than others, the prices vary between each costume colour, sometimes greatly. The perceived gender of clothing also influences the prices between the costumes.

label: Elemental metal
title: Elemental metal
lead:
Elemental metal is a metal bar that is used in the quests Elemental Workshop I and Elemental Workshop II. It is made by using one elemental ore and four coal on the furnace on the south side of the first floor of the Elemental Workshop. Each bar must be made individually.

The elemental metal can be used to make an elemental shield or an elemental helmet. During Elemental Workshop II, it is also used to make an elemental claw and is processed into a primed bar in the second level of the Elemental Workshop.

label: Elemental obelisks
title: Elemental obelisks
lead:
Elemental Obelisks can be used to charge unpowered orbs into elemental orbs which may then be attached to a plain battlestaff to make fire, water, earth or air battlestaffs.

To charge an unpowered orb it must be taken to the obelisk of the respective element that the player wishes to have the orb charged to, as well as the required runes to charge the orb.

label: Elemental ore
title: Elemental ore
lead:
Elemental ore is an ore that may only be obtained by killing a level 35 earth elemental after trying to mine the elemental rock. This ore can only be obtained during and after the Elemental Workshop I quest, and turned into elemental metals. Elemental ore is only found in the Elemental Workshop dungeon beneath the Seers' Village, in the house with the anvil, next to the bank. Earth elementals are found in the western area on the first level of the workshop.

The second level is to make bars, and repairs are needed here too. One elemental ore and four coal may be smelted into a bar of elemental metal using the blast furnace in the southern area of the Elemental Workshop (level 20 Smithing is required). This bar is used to smith the elemental shield and helmet.

label: elemental shield
title: elemental shield
lead:
The elemental shield may be made during and after the Elemental Workshop I quest in the Elemental Workshop dungeon.

To make the shield, players must have a Smithing level of 20, an elemental metal, a hammer, and either a battered book or slashed book in their inventory. Use the elemental metal on a workbench in the elemental workshop to make the shield. Smithing the shield grants the player 20 Smithing experience. To equip the shield, players must have completed the Elemental Workshop I quest.

label: Elemental sphere (interface item)
title: Elemental sphere (interface item)
lead:
The Elemental sphere is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Elemental sphere.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: elemental staves
title: elemental staves
lead:
Elemental staves provide an unlimited amount of one of the basic elemental runes (air, water, earth, and fire) or a combination rune (lava, mud, steam, smoke, mist, and dust) and the autocast option when equipped. The staves come in three different types:
*Basic elemental staves have no requirements to wield. They can be obtained from various sources, including several shops.
*Battlestaves require 30 Magic and Attack to wield. They can be obtained from various sources, such as Zaff's Superior Staffs! (after completing the quest What Lies Below), and also created by players with the Crafting skill. Battlestaves that provide combination runes cannot be created by players and are only obtainable through trading or monster drops.
*Mystic staves require 40 Magic and Attack to wield. They can be created by paying Thormac and giving him a charged battlestaff of the type the player wants (after completing the quest Scorpion Catcher). They can also be obtained through trading or monster drops.

label: Elemental weakness
title: Elemental weakness
lead:
Elemental weakness is a stat assigned to monsters that makes them weak to the elemental spells from the standard spellbook. The elemental spells include the strike, bolt, blast, wave, and surge spells. It does not include spells which could be viewed as elemental, such as Flames of Zamorak, or spells from other spellbooks, such as Ice Rush.

For every percentage point of elemental weakness that an NPC has, the player will gain an extra 1% magic damage and 1% magic accuracy to their attacks. The bonus to magic damage is added after all previous magic damage sources, such as equipment or bonuses from the Slayer helmet (i) or Salve amulet (i).

label: Elemental Workshop (location)
title: Elemental Workshop (location)
lead: The Elemental Workshop is a dungeon that players can progressively explore more of as they complete the Elemental Workshop quest series. It is accessed by opening the odd looking wall, by using battered key, in the building west of the Seers' Village bank with the anvil icon and going down the stairs.

label: Elemental Workshop I
title: Elemental Workshop I
lead: Elemental Workshop I is a quest in which you find a mysterious book in Seers' Village, guiding along the rediscovery of the eponymous workshop and the lost magical elemental ore.

label: Elemental Workshop quest series
title: Elemental Workshop quest series
lead: The Elemental Workshop quest series is a series of quests revolving around the eponymous workshop and its various levels. It explores the Elemental and Mind workshops. The player first repairs the workshops and then learns how to craft the metals into shields, then helmets.

label: Elena
title: Elena
lead: Elena is a healer from Ardougne, particular skilled in (bio)chemistry and epidemiology, and heavily involved in the Elf quest series. In Plague City, the player is to save her from her entrapment by the mourners in West Ardougne. In Biohazard, you are to aid her deliver 3 different chemicals and a sample of the West Ardougne plague to her mentor in south-east Varrock. After Plague City, you may find her in her house in north-west of East Ardougne. After the Ardougne Revolution and the escape from Lord Iorwerth during Song of the Elves she can be found by the pond and farming patch in the south-western corner of Lletya. Following the events of Song of the Elves, Elena can be found among the Meilyr Clan within Prifddinas, being the first human to have settled in the elven capital.

label: elf
title: elf
lead: Elves are among the longest living races in Gielinor. They are noted as being tall, graceful humanoids, with elongated ears. Female elves are also renowned for their beauty. They follow the crystalline goddess Seren, who journeyed to Gielinor with them from their ancestral homeland Tarddiad. Elves have no need for human technology or magic, but instead opt for crystal-based weaponry, technology and magic power, granted by Seren. Due to their many years of isolation brought on by their beliefs and a civil war, elves are generally regarded as a mere myth by humans, most of whom have not interacted with elves in centuries and believe them to have gone. All elves are associated with a clan, each of which originated from the first eight elven families of Gielinor.

label: Elf (Thieving)
title: Elf (Thieving)
lead:
Elves are citizens of Lletya and Prifddinas that can be talked to as well as pickpocketed from with level 85 Thieving. A player can only access the Lletya elves after starting Mourning's End Part I and the Prifddinas elves after completing Song of the Elves.

Pickpocketing an Elf is a task for the elite Western Provinces Diary.

label: Elidinis
title: Elidinis
lead:
with an illustration of a hippopotamus engraved on it, representing Elidinis.|class=notpageimage]]
Elidinis (Jagex pronunciation: eh-LID-in-iss), is the Menaphite Goddess of fertility and growth, she is also heavily associated with the River Elid. The River Elid is named in her honour, for it brings life to the whole region. There are some who believe the river to be Elidinis herself, according to the Sphinx in Sophanem. The three Spirits of the River Elid explain that "Elidinis is the goddess of the river" and that they were "bound to her river" when Elidinis came to the desert. This contradicts the belief that the river is Elidinis herself, however it does not exclude the possibility that the river is part of Elidinis, which is underlined by the Spirits of the River when they describe that they "have become one with the river and have become full of power of Elidinis that was in her river."

She is also the wife of Tumeken, with whom she created Icthlarin and Amascut from their divine essence, and one of the four major gods of the Menaphite Pantheon. Elidinis is mainly worshipped by the peoples of the desert. The centre of her worship is the town of Nardah, although there are priestesses of hers in Menaphos as well. In Nardah, there is a shrine to Elidinis (the Elidinis Statuette), provided by the goddess herself to Nardarine, a refugee of the God Wars, who went on to found and lead Nardah.

title: Elite black armour
lead:
Elite black armour is a set of armour requiring 40 Defence to equip, obtained from killing Elite Black Knights. A set is guaranteed while killing the knights, and another set can be pilfered in the inner section of the base, though one of these is eventually given away to Silif. Further pieces can be obtained afterwards by killing more Elite Black Knights. They can be stored in the armour case of the costume room in a player-owned house.

They have defensive stats equivalent to the Initiate armour, but the same prayer bonus as Proselyte armour. They can also be used to enter the Black Knights' Fortress.

title: Elite hidey hole (interface item)
lead:
The Elite hidey hole is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the STASH.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Elite Void Knight equipment
title: Elite Void Knight equipment
lead:
Elite Void Knight equipment, commonly called elite void, is a reward from the Pest Control minigame, and the upgraded version of regular Void Knight equipment. The set has two pieces, the elite void top and elite void robe, and becomes available after completing the hard Western Provinces Diary.

Upgrading to elite void costs 200 commendation points for each piece, for a total of 400 points to upgrade both the top and bottom. Players can upgrade their equipment by speaking to the Elite Void Knight at the Void Knights' Outpost. The regular Void Knight top and bottom are required for the upgrade.

label: Elizabeth
title: Elizabeth
lead:
Elizabeth Sinclair is one of Lord Sinclair's children. She is a suspect during the Murder Mystery quest.

According to the Gossip, it is hinted she suffers from kleptomania and stole her father's silver needle.

label: Elizabeth's barrel
title: Elizabeth's barrel
lead: Elizabeth's barrel can be found inside the Sinclair Mansion in Elizabeth's bedroom. During the Murder Mystery quest, the player must search the barrel to find her silver needle.

label: Elizabeth's print
title: Elizabeth's print
lead: Elizabeth's print is a quest item in the Murder Mystery quest. It is created by using flypaper on the silver needle after dusting it with a pot of flour. If the prints match those of the unknown print, it will become a killer's print, meaning Elizabeth is the killer.

label: Elkhorn
title: Elkhorn

label: Elkoy
title: Elkoy
lead: Elkoy is a gnome from the Tree Gnome Village who guides people through the Tree Gnome Maze both to and from the Tree Gnome Village after starting the Tree Gnome Village quest. To start the quest you have to speak to King Bolren in the Tree Gnome Village. If you right click on him it will say "follow", click it and you will be escorted through the maze quickly and safely. He can be found at the north-west entrance to the maze.

label: Ellemar
title: Ellemar
lead:
Ellemar was a Saradominist demonologist who performed demonic rituals. He read tomes on demon lore in order to better understand the race so that they could be fought more effectively, despite the fact that this had been forbidden by the Church of Saradomin.

At some point, Ellemar read about the weather demon Agrith Naar and discovered that he would not be able to exercise his powers on Gielinor if he were to be removed from Infernus. Therefore he and seven other people performed a summoning ritual, which was successful. With great effort they managed to imprison Agrith Naar in a cage but were unable to slay him. Because the cage was steadily weakening, they decided to trap the demon inside a human body, the result of which was Denath.

label: Elvarg
title: Elvarg
lead: Elvarg is the dragon that players have to kill in the Dragon Slayer I quest. She resides in the dungeon below Crandor. She is a green dragon, and is considerably stronger than the usual kind. Unlike other chromatic dragons, Elvarg has a ranged dragonfire attack. Despite being a dragon, she is not vulnerable to dragonbane weapons.

label: Elven Civil War
title: Elven Civil War
lead: The Elven Civil War was a centuries-long conflict between the Iorwerth clan and the seven other elven clans. It began with the siege of Prifddinas and the subsequent Baxtorian campaign. Because Lord Iorwerth and his forces had the advantage of the city walls, they were ultimately able to defeat King Baxtorian's army, many of which further perished in the forest of Isafdar and in the Underground Pass following an ambush. With no way to retake Prifddinas, Baxtorian and the other clan elders reverted it to a crystal seed, where it remained until the day it would be restored.

label: Elven clan leader
title: Elven clan leader
lead:
There are eight elven clan leaders (also referred to as the Prifddinas Elders or Council of Elders) found in the eight districts of Prifddinas, each in charge of their respective clan and all equal leaders of the city and the land of Tirannwn. Clan leadership is not based solely on heritage; neither Morvran Iorwerth nor Islwyn Cadarn are clan leaders, despite being the heirs of previous leaders, and Kelyn was chosen as clan leader due to her love of architecture.

The elves have had clan leaders since their time on Tarddiad. When the elves were brought to Gielinor by Seren and Guthix during the First Age, Seren established the eight clan leaders as equal rulers of Prifddinas, each with their own district and a crystal tower connected to Seren's abode, the Tower of Voices. It is unknown how much political power Seren had, but she was universally adored and respected by the elves and the clan leaders could enter the tower to consult her.

label: elven clans
title: elven clans
lead: The elven clans are a collection of elven families. Each clan specializes in certain skills and crafts to complement each other. Each clan is led by an elf with the title of Lord or Lady.

label: Elven outfit
title: Elven outfit
lead:
The Elven outfit is a set of cosmetic clothing worn by elves.

The outfit can be bought from Lliann in Prifddinas. All components except the gloves and boots can be traded on free-to-play worlds.

label: Emerald
title: Emerald
lead: Emeralds are precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut emeralds with a chisel at level 27 Crafting, yielding 67.5 experience.

label: Emerald amulet
title: Emerald amulet
lead:
The emerald amulet is created by using a gold bar on a furnace while also carrying a cut emerald and an amulet mould. This requires 31 Crafting and grants 70 Crafting experience. The resulting unstrung amulet is then used with a ball of wool, granting an additional 4 experience.

It has no stat bonuses, but can be enchanted with the Lvl-2 Enchant spell to become an Amulet of defence which gives some defensive bonuses.

label: Emerald amulet (u)
title: Emerald amulet (u)
lead:
An emerald amulet (u) can be made at level 31 Crafting by using a gold bar on a furnace while carrying a cut emerald and an amulet mould. This grants the player 70 Crafting experience. The amulet can then be strung with a ball of wool to create a strung emerald amulet, granting an additional 4 experience. The strung amulet can be enchanted into an amulet of defence using the Lvl-2 Enchant spell, requiring level 27 Magic.

This amulet can also be strung with a magic string instead, turning it into a pre-nature amulet. This amulet can then be enchanted into an amulet of nature.

label: Emerald necklace
title: Emerald necklace
lead:
The emerald necklace is made by using a gold bar on a furnace with an emerald and a necklace mould in your inventory. It requires a Crafting level of 29 and provides 60 experience when made.

The emerald necklace can be enchanted into a binding necklace by casting Lvl-2 Enchant. This requires a Magic level of 27, a cosmic rune and three air runes.

label: Emerald ring
title: Emerald ring
lead:
The Emerald ring is made by using a gold bar on a furnace whilst having an emerald and ring mould in the inventory. Making it requires a Crafting level of 27, and gives 55 experience.

The ring has no stats but can be enchanted using Lvl-2 Enchant ( ) to make a ring of dueling.

label: Emir
title: Emir
lead:
The Emir is the ruler of Al Kharid, a city on the northern fringe of the massive Kharidian Desert. Since his son's kidnapping, the Emir has been in no state to directly govern Al Kharid, and he has retreated to his private chambers where only Chancellor Hassan may see him. He has ruled the desert town for many years, and it is his only wish that his son, Prince Ali, might be raised to run the state with the same good hand.

After the rescue of his son, the Emir was unable to thank the adventurer in person due to his age and poor health. He now spends most of his time resting.

label: Emote enhancers
title: Emote enhancers
lead: Emote enhancers are special clothing that, when worn, change a certain emote if it is performed.

label: Emotes
title: Emotes
lead:
Emotes are a selection of movements that a player can perform. Some emotes are unlocked by default, to be unlocked through random events, quests, the Stronghold of Security, holiday events, or obtaining a skillcape. The majority of emotes can be looped so that they will be played continuously until they interact with the overworld or perform another emote. Emotes are currently the only way one can communicate as a muted player.

Emotes are depicted as characters in the Emotes tab. In order of appearance; someone in full white armour with a white medium helmet, a man with the default player outfit and brown hair, a woman wearing what appears to be a woven top and skirt, a jester, Romeo, a goblin, a Mime, a woman wearing a bronze platebody and dragon plateskirt, a zombie, and a skillcape-wearer.

label: Emotion
title: Emotion
lead: Emotion is a music track that is unlocked at the Tree Gnome Village maze, and in the corrupted version of the Fisher Realm. It also plays in the Nightmare Zone when facing the Black Knight Titan in Practice or Endurance mode.

label: Emperor
title: Emperor
lead:
Emperor is a music track that unlocks around Rimmington. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track and Attention.

In Classic mode, the track plays around Melzar's Maze and (since an update in 2022) at a small area south-west of Rommik's Crafty Supplies. The map below represents post-2022 unlock area on Classic mode. The area before 2021 and on Classic mode in 2021-2022 only covers excluding Melzar's Maze.

label: Empty cup
title: Empty cup
lead: An empty cup is an item that is obtained after drinking a cup of tea or a cup of nettle tea. To obtain an empty cup, players can buy or steal a cup of tea from the tea stall in east Varrock. Having a conversation with Galahad will also involve him giving the player a cup of tea, after which it can be drunk to get an empty tea cup.

label: Empty oyster
title: Empty oyster
lead: An empty oyster is an oyster which has been opened and does not contain a pearl. It has no known use, but is collected by some players who like accumulating large amounts of difficult to obtain items such as burnt food and crushed gems. These items are not traded on the Grand Exchange, and are often discarded by players because they serve no real purpose.

label: Empyrean Citadel
title: Empyrean Citadel
lead: The Empyrean Citadel was a location that the god Armadyl commanded his forces from during the Third Age. Not much is known about it, as it is only referenced by the golem in Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire.

label: Enchant Crossbow Bolt
title: Enchant Crossbow Bolt
lead:
The Enchant Crossbow Bolt spell is a members-only spell used to give gem-tipped crossbow bolts special powers that have a chance of activating upon impact.

Although Enchant Crossbow Bolt is listed as one spell in a player's spellbook requiring 4 Magic to cast, the only bolts that can be enchanted at this level are Opal bolts. When attempting to cast Enchant Crossbow Bolt, an interface will appear, asking you to choose from up to 10 different spells. Each of these spells requires a different Magic level, different runes, and grants different amounts of experience. When successfully cast, the message The magic of the runes coaxes out the true nature of the gem tips. is displayed.

label: Enchanted bear
title: Enchanted bear
lead:
Enchanted bear is a quest item used only in Druidic Ritual. It is made by dipping raw bear meat into the Cauldron of Thunder.

It is given to Sanfew to create a potion.

label: Enchanted beef
title: Enchanted beef
lead:
Enchanted beef is a quest item used only in Druidic Ritual. It is made by dipping raw beef into the Cauldron of Thunder.

It is given to Sanfew to create a potion.

label: enchanted bolts
title: enchanted bolts
lead:
Enchanted bolts are gem-tipped crossbow bolts enchanted through the Enchant Crossbow Bolt spell to obtain a secondary effect. All enchanted bolts can be traded, with the exception of enchanted jade bolts.

While players can only add certain gem bolt tips to specific metal bolts, dragon bolts can have any type of gem bolt tips added to them.

label: Enchanted chicken
title: Enchanted chicken

Enchanted chicken is a quest item used only in Druidic Ritual. It is made by dipping raw chicken into the Cauldron of Thunder.

It is given to Sanfew to create a potion.

title: Enchanted rat
