Enchanted rat meat is a quest item used only in Druidic Ritual. It is made by dipping raw rat meat into the Cauldron of Thunder.

It is given to Sanfew to create a potion.

label: Enchanted robes
title: Enchanted robes
lead:
Enchanted robes is a set of magic robes. To wear these robes, the player must have at least 20 Defence and 40 Magic. To obtain enchanted robes the player can either complete a hard Treasure Trail or buy them from another player. The pieces have the same stats as their corresponding mystic counterparts.

Enchanted robes may be placed in a mahogany treasure chest the costume room in a house, so the player may own them without taking up bank space.

label: Enchanted vial
title: Enchanted vial
lead:
An enchanted vial is made when using the binding book on an empty glass vial. The vial can be filled with water from the golden bowl (provides enough water to fill ten vials) to make holy water. They cannot be used as normal water vessels, nor for Herblore. Holy water is a usually weak ranged weapon, and is only effective on demons.

The process of making enchanted vials drains 5 Prayer and Magic levels. It is therefore recommended to make them near an altar and a bank (for stat restore potions). The free-for-all portal in the Clan Wars building of the Ferox Enclave may also be used. Exiting the portal will recharge one's Prayer and stats, and the Ferox Enclave bank is close by.

label: Enchantment spells
title: Enchantment spells
lead:
Enchant spells use cosmic runes to give an item new properties. For the enchant orb group of spells, a player needs to travel to the appropriate Obelisk and cast the spell on that. Similarly with the jewellery spells, the player must have a piece of jewellery to cast the spell on.

Content in italics denote members only content.

label: Enclave guard
title: Enclave guard
lead:
Enclave guards are ogres that guard the Ogre Enclave dungeon in the heart of Gu'Tanoth. During the Watchtower quest, players must use a cave nightshade on them twice (on different occasions) in order to be able to enter the enclave. After the quest, a cave nightshade does not have to be used to enter the cave, but the following message will appear: You run past the guard while he's busy.

Players can kill enclave guards towards an ogre Slayer task. Due to their lacklustre drops and being more difficult to kill compared to standard ogres, players usually avoid killing them.

label: Energy
title: Energy
lead:
Energy (sometimes called run energy, running energy, or stamina) allows players to run rather than walk. Players move one tile per game tick while walking, but move two tiles per game tick while running, making running twice as fast as walking. Run energy depletes while running, and turning on Run is only possible while a player has 1% energy or more.

Each player has at fewest 0 units of energy and up to 10,000 units of energy, displayed as a percentage in-game rounded down. For instance, the game shows 100% when a player has the full 10,000 units of energy and 0% when a player has fewer than 100 units of energy. The energy percentage is displayed in the game's Settings screen and by the Minimap if the Data orb option is enabled. Players can toggle this option to continuously run, or they can run to one particular destination by holding down the Control key when they click to move, if run energy is toggled to walk. Conversely, players can walk to one particular tile using the Control key while Run is enabled (see Game controls).

label: Energy potion
title: Energy potion
lead:
An Energy potion restores 10% of the player's run energy.

It can be purchased from the Apothecary in Varrock for 1 chocolate dust and 2 limpwurt roots. Members can also make them using the Herblore skill by mixing Harralander in a vial of water and then adding chocolate dust. This requires level 26 Herblore, and gives 67.5 Herblore experience.

label: Enfeeble
title: Enfeeble
lead: Enfeeble is a level 73 Magic spell. When cast on an opponent, their Strength level is reduced by 10%. Casting Enfeeble grants 83 Magic experience and requires 1 Soul, 8 Earth, and 8 Water runes to be cast. The spell can only be cast if the opponent's stats haven't already been lowered, meaning you cannot stack the 10% Strength reduction with multiple spells in a row.

label: Engineered terrorbird
title: Engineered terrorbird
lead:
Engineered terrorbirds are terrorbirds that have achieved sapience as a result of Arposandra's experiments. Unlike standard terrorbirds, they are bipedal and capable of speech. They serve Arposandra's gnomish residents, who they refer to as the masters. They are known to inhabit the lower areas of Arposandra, where they perform jobs such as guarding. They lack names, and instead refer to themselves by their occupation and number. While they are supposed to have been created with the inability to sleep, this has been shown to not actually be the case.

The process that creates them is not always successful, and instead often creates warped terrorbirds, which are then dumped into the Poison Waste Dungeon.

label: Ensouled head
title: Ensouled head
lead:
Ensouled heads are items that can be dropped by their respective monsters. These heads can be reanimated by using the appropriate spell within the Arceuus spellbook on the head, consuming the head in the process. Reanimation can be cast on any ensouled head within a 31x31 area where that head was dropped by a monster. This will work indefinitely, even if the ensouled head is picked up, so long as it is not put into the bank, trade screen, Grand Exchange, or price checker. If the player has put the head into the bank, trade screen, Grand Exchange, or price checker, the reanimation spell will only work within range of the Dark Altar.

When reanimated, the monster will attack after the animation completes, and they will override Single-way combat rules. Upon killing the monster, Prayer experience will be rewarded. The amount of Prayer experience gained increases with higher-levelled heads. Reanimation spells are divided into four tiers, which determines the Magic level required in order to use the spell. Some reanimated monsters do have additional requirements, so players should take note of this before reanimating a head.

label: Ent (disambiguation)
title: Ent (disambiguation)
lead: Ent may refer to:

label: Ent (race)
title: Ent (race)
lead:
Ents are large, intelligent, and ancient beings made of living wood that resemble trees. They draw their energy directly from nature. Not much is known about their origins, but they are known to be a very old race. At least one ent, Derwen, is known to be a follower of Guthix.

Although they can be found anywhere in the world where trees are in the form of entlings, grown ents can primarily be found in the forests of the south-eastern Wilderness, in a dungeon beneath the Woodcutting Guild, and in the Auburn Valley. The appearance of an ent tends to match that of their environment. The life cycle of an ent appears to begin with an ent seed, which grows into an entling, and later into a fully grown ent.

label: Ent (random event)
title: Ent (random event)
lead:
Ents were a RuneScape 2 random event. When a player tried to chop a tree, the tree had a chance of becoming an ent, also known as a "dancing tree" to some players. Like most random events, its purpose was to stop macro users. Since the ent could appear for each player chopping the tree, the odds of it showing up increased when woodcutting with more players. However, once it appeared, it influenced all players chopping that tree.

If the character continued chopping at the ent, the woodcutting axe became broken and useless. Once broken, a player could go to Bob's Brilliant Axes in Lumbridge to get the broken axe fixed. Bob fixed bronze, iron, and steel axes free of charge, and other woodcutting axe types (mithril and above) for a small fee. The stronger the woodcutting axe, the higher the repair cost. Alternately, the axe could be repaired in a player-owned house, reducing the cost.

label: Entangle
title: Entangle
lead:
Entangle is a members-only spell that requires level 79 Magic to cast. Casting Entangle will hold your target in place for 24 ticks (14.4 seconds) and grants 89 Magic experience (in addition to 2 experience per damage dealt). A successful hit, without any damage boosting items, can deal up to 5 damage. When used on a player and the entanglement is about to wear off, the entangled player will receive this message in their chatbox: The holding effect is beginning to fade. Players can increase the binding duration by equipping swampbark armour; the helm, body, and legs will increase the duration by 2 ticks (1.2 seconds) each, up to a maximum of 30 ticks (18.0 seconds).

Once the spell wears off, the target has 5 ticks (3 seconds) of immunity before they can be entangled again.

label: Entrana
title: Entrana
lead: Entrana is a large island south-west of Taverley, occupied by Saradominist monks. When entering Entrana, adventurers are prohibited from bringing most weapons or armour with them.

label: Entrana church
title: Entrana church
lead:
The Entrana church is a Saradomin church led by the High Priest and is the focal point of Entrana. In addition to offering an altar and characters who play roles in such quests as Desert Treasure I, if you are injured, you can talk to a level 5 monk and select the option "Can you heal me? I'm injured" to be nursed back to full health. From the candle stall, you can steal candles, granting 20 Thieving experience each. You may fail, giving the message "A high power smites you" and inflicting 1 damage.

Upstairs, the player can find an organ on which they can play a melody.

label: Entrana Dungeon
title: Entrana Dungeon
lead:
The Entrana Dungeon is found on the north-west corner of Entrana. After entering the dungeon, it is not possible to climb back up to Entrana.

It is used during the Lost City and Recipe for Disaster quests.

label: Entrana firebird
title: Entrana firebird
lead: The Entrana firebird is a unique bird found only on the holy isle of Entrana, on the northern part of the island. During Heroes' Quest, the player must kill it to receive the fire feather. You must have ice gloves to pick up the feather it drops.

label: Entrana homestead
title: Entrana homestead
lead: The Entrana homestead is a small farm on the island of Entrana. It is surrounded by unicorns.

lead: Eohric is the head servant for Prince Anlaf. He is located on the top floor of Burthorpe castle.

label: Equa leaves
title: Equa leaves
lead:
Equa leaves are ingredients utilised in gnome cooking that heal 1 hitpoint each. They are used in almost all gnome food, and have little other use, besides possibly in the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest.

They can be purchased at the two food stores on the of the Grand Tree in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. Several respawn points are located in the south-east of Feldip Hills.

label: Equa toad's legs
title: Equa toad's legs
lead:
Equa toad's legs was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Toad batta. It could be made by adding Equa leaves to Toad's legs. Gnome spice was then added to these in order to create Seasoned legs, an ingredient in the Toad batta.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the toad's legs, equa leaves and gnome spice are all automatically added at once to create a Half made crunchy. If the player attempts to add equa leaves to toad's legs, nothing happens.

label: Equipable tool
title: Equipable tool
lead:
Several tools that are normally used from the inventory have an equipable variant. Typically, these can be obtained by participating in activities related to the skill the tool is used in. This page only lists tools that are not normally equipable.

The following items are completely equivalent to the base tool, except being equipable:

** and its oily variant, equivalent to an (oily) fishing rod

** , equivalent to a Barbarian rod
* , equivalent to a harpoon
* , equivalent to a teasing stick

label: Equipment Rebalancing Beta
title: Equipment Rebalancing Beta
lead:
Two beta worlds (401 and 407) were opened to test newly adjusted crystal armour, black dragonhide armour, and toxic blowpipe as proposed in the Equipment Rebalancing Changes blog. As the beta was intended to test the rewards against various scenarios, players were allowed complete access to the world, including the Inferno.

As the previous open beta was The Nightmare Rewards Beta, when Clan Wars was still in the Giants' Plateau, unrestricted worlds now logs players in Ferox Enclave, where similar features were added. Supply tables in the Clan Wars building in Ferox Enclave gave players the test equipment (which were given a (beta) suffix) as well as many weapons, armour, teleport items, food, and potions. The altar in Ferox Enclave can change a player's spellbook as well, and two handy portals can be found just outside the Last Man Standing building (coloured blue), and one just west of the bank chest (coloured yellow).

label: Equipment Stats
title: Equipment Stats
lead: Equipment Stats (also called equipment bonuses, combat stats, or bonuses) are the bonuses given by the armour and weapons that a player is wearing. The bonuses of a player can be found in the Worn Equipment section of the player interface. In general, higher level items give greater bonuses than their lower-level counterparts. Some items that can be equipped do not actually possess any bonuses, e.g. the brass necklace. The bonuses an item provides are placed into three different categories: Attack bonus, Defence bonus, and Other bonuses. These bonuses, in addition to level of the player's relevant combat skills and the attack style used, are used to calculate both the damage dealt and received during combat, and the likelihood of an attack being successful.

label: Ernest
title: Ernest
lead:
Ernest is the fiancé of Veronica and a central character in the quest Ernest the Chicken. While travelling to Falador, they got lost and ended up outside Draynor Manor. Ernest went inside to ask for directions and ended up testing Professor Oddenstein's latest invention, being turned into a chicken. After an hour Veronica begged a passing adventurer to look for Ernest. The machine was damaged by poltergeists, rendering Professor Oddenstein incapable of reverting the results of the experiment. The adventurer managed to retrieve all the pieces needed to restore Ernest to human form, much to the delight of Veronica.

After completing Ernest the Chicken he will give you 300 coins as a reward. He is not seen after completion of the quest, Veronica states that he went off to speak with a "green warty guy", but that she's expecting him to return soon.

label: Ernest the Chicken
title: Ernest the Chicken
lead:
Ernest the Chicken is a free-to-play quest where players must discover what happened to the missing Ernest, who went into Draynor Manor to ask for directions and never returned.

It was one of the first quests developed and the first quest released after RuneScape's initial launch.

label: Erysail the Pious
title: Erysail the Pious
lead:
Erysail the Pious was one of the seven priestly warriors who died fighting the Morytanian hordes at Silvarea. She came from Rimmington.

She is described in The Sleeping Seven as "A woman of such noble and just nature that she commanded the will of Misthalinian fighters high and right, ever at the front of battle displaying courage and aiding those in need."

label: Escape
title: Escape
lead: Escape is a music track that can be unlocked within the Witchaven Dungeon.

label: Escaping slave
title: Escaping slave
lead: An escaping slave is a male slave that has been given a set of desert robes during the Tourist Trap quest. After you pick the male slave's handcuffs, he will trade you his slave robes for the desert robes, and he will put them on. After a few minutes, or after talking to the escaping slave, he will turn back into a male slave, having been caught.

label: Eski
title: Eski
lead:
Eski is a small pet green dragon owned by Tim and Crunchy, typically seen holding or nearby a dice block. It first appeared beneath the table Tim and Crunchy are sitting at in the "Warrior and Skeleton" wallpaper, which also appeared on the cover of RuneScape- The Official Handbook, although Eski is mostly out of frame on the book. In this appearance, it is depicted holding a dice block and wearing a collar connected to a leash held by Tim.

and "Wish You Were Here" wallpaper.]]
It subsequently appeared and was named in the 14th issue of Postbag from the Hedge , where it is described as sitting under the table drooling on Postie Pete's mail bag before Crunchy's left hand falls off, which it then runs off with. The postbag also contained a postcard that depicted Eski relaxing at a beach alongside Tim and Crunchy, which was also released as the "Wish You Were Here" wallpaper. In the postcard and wallpaper, Eski was depicted snoozing under a parasol near a sandcastle, with its dice block nearby, and was also redesigned to more closely resemble the current appearance of baby dragons.

label: Eski the Bloated
title: Eski the Bloated
lead:
Eski the Bloated was a dragonkin mentioned in the original design document for Fossil Island, written in October 2006 . He would have been the first of the Dragonkin brought to Gielinor by the Stone of Jas, and their leader. He would have been found in a dragonkin outpost atop the island's central mountain, and players would be unable to reach him, but would still be able to converse with from a distance. The document describes him as sitting atop the mountain "brooding and looking bloody impressive ... scarred from torture and abuse and exposure to the sun".

His role as the dragonkin on Fossil Island was ultimately replaced by Skeka.

title: Essence mine
lead:
Essence mine may refer to:

* Rune essence mine, containing rune essence rocks
* Lunar Isle mine, containing a rune essence rock
* Dense essence mine, containing dense runestone rocks
* Daeyalt essence mine, containing daeyalt essence rocks

label: Essence pouch
title: Essence pouch
lead:
Essence pouches are bags that can hold varying amounts of rune, pure, daeyalt, or guardian essence for use in the Runecraft skill. Essence pouches allow the player to take larger loads when crafting runes or mining pure essence, which saves a significant amount of transit time.

Essence pouches are made from superfluous organs of creatures from the Abyss. As such, most pouches are dropped by monsters in the Abyss and the Abyssal Area, accessible after completing Enter the Abyss or by fairy ring code , and can also be received from the Guardians of the Rift minigame as loot from the Rewards Guardian.

label: Essiandar Gar
title: Essiandar Gar
lead:
Essiandar Gar was one of the Seven Priestly Warriors who died fighting the Morytanian hordes at Silvarea. She came from Draynor Village. Her description suggests that she may have been an older woman.

She is described in The Sleeping Seven as "A fearless woman at even such a worthy age. It was said that her indignation at the evil scourge was enough to make the most cowardly of men in her ranks act like lions in the fiercest fighting."

label: Eternal
title: Eternal
lead:
Eternal may refer to:

* Amulet of eternal glory, an amulet of glory with unlimited charges.
* Eternal crystal, an item used to create eternal boots.
* Eternal boots, a pair of magic boots.
* Eternal gem, an item used to create eternal slayer rings.
* Eternal teleport crystal, a teleport crystal with unlimited charges.
* Fire of Eternal Light, a type of fire pit that acts as a light source.
* Ode to eternity, a book obtained during the quest Song of the Elves.
* Sigil of the eternal jeweller, a type of sigil in Deadman: Reborn.
* Slayer ring (eternal), a slayer ring with unlimited charges.

label: Eternal cold
title: Eternal cold
lead: Eternal cold is a sailing hazard found in the Forgotten Ocean. It is currently not possible to traverse these seas, as even the eternal brazier is not strong enough to protect players and their ship. If the eternal cold seas are traversed players will receive a chatbox message: You feel the warmth sap from your body. No boat can withstand these waters! and their ship will be slowed and take 50 damage every few seconds. Crew will be frozen, cancelling actions. Player will be frozen soon afterwards and take increasing damage over time if area is not left with the chatbox message: The endless winter freezes you in place. No boat can withstand these waters!; damage is significantly higher than icy seas.

label: Eternal teleport
title: Eternal teleport
lead:
Eternal teleport may refer to:

*Amulet of eternal glory
*Eternal teleport crystal
*Slayer ring (eternal)

label: Ethel Prim
title: Ethel Prim
lead: Ethel Prim was a resident of Varrock in the Year 160 of the Fifth Age mentioned in the Varrock Census. According to the Varrock Census, she was a servant. She may be related to Hartwin Prim.

label: ethenea
title: ethenea
lead:
Ethenea is a quest item used only in Biohazard. It is obtained from Elena after returning her distillator to her.

It is first given to Da Vinci, who will smuggle it into the Dancing Donkey Inn, past the Guard conducting body searches. After retrieving it from Da Vinci, it is given to Guidor in south-east Varrock, alongside plague sample, liquid honey, sulphuric broline, and touch paper.

label: Eustace Forthwright
title: Eustace Forthwright
lead: Eustace Forthwright was a resident of Varrock during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. According to the Varrock Census of that year, he was a guard.

label: Event rewards
title: Event rewards
lead:
Event rewards are items in-game that are only available for a limited amount of time. As a result, the number in-game is limited, although most of these items can still be obtained through participating in corresponding holiday events or trading with other players.

These items were initially released in a way similar to the holiday drops in s early years; Jagex moderators would give hints as to the location of a discontinued item and only one was available. When it was picked up, another would spawn in its place in a random location.

label: events
title: events
lead:
Events may refer to:

*Random events, an event that can happen randomly whilst playing
*Holiday events, seasonal and community events that happen periodically throughout the year
**Valentine's Day, a one-off event in celebration of Valentine's Day
**Anniversary event, a seasonal event celebrating the anniversary of

**April Fools', a minor seasonal event

**Halloween event, a seasonal event celebrating Halloween
**Thanksgiving event, a seasonal event held during Thanksgiving
**Christmas event, a seasonal event celebrating Christmas
*Repeatable events, tasks that can be repeated periodically for experience, coins, or item reward
*Unannounced phenomena, events usually hinting at a future update

label: Everard Grafham
title: Everard Grafham
lead: Everard Grafham was a resident of Varrock known to have lived during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. Grafham is mentioned in the Varrock Census of 160, found in the Varrock Palace's library. He was a natural historian.

label: Evergreen tree
title: Evergreen tree
lead:
Evergreen trees can be chopped down to provide logs and 25 Woodcutting experience.

Buckets of sap can be acquired by using a knife on an evergreen tree while having a bucket in your inventory. This is required for The Eyes of Glouphrie and Icthlarin's Little Helper quests.

label: Evergreen tree (disambiguation)
title: Evergreen tree (disambiguation)
lead:
Evergreen may refer to:

* Evergreen tree, a common tree
* Evergreen tree (Mac), an obstacle on the path to Mac
* Evergreen (2021 Halloween event)
* Evergreen (Big Cats & WWF)
* Evergreen (Big Cats & WWF, grown)

label: Everlight
title: Everlight
lead:
The Everlight was a lighthouse in Hallowvale, found east of the Icyene Graveyard and what is now Ver Sinhaza. At its peak, it covered much of the region with the light of Saradomin, soothing the Icyene and repelling the vampyres. The light of the Everlight was deadly to vyres, capable of reducing one to ashes if caught in it, but its main purpose was for the comfort of the Icyenes who were used to always living in daylight on their homeworld.

At some point, the Everlight was destroyed and now rests somewhere beneath the ocean.

label: Evil chicken outfit
title: Evil chicken outfit
lead:
The evil chicken outfit is a members-only cosmetic outfit that can be obtained by offering bird's eggs to the Shrine found in the Woodcutting Guild. Each piece of the evil chicken outfit has a 1/1200 chance of being awarded, resulting in a 1/300 chance of receiving any outfit piece. Any outfit piece will replace a nest, so a full inventory will not compromise receiving the outfit piece. There is no duplicate protection for pieces of the outfit.

Like the chicken outfit, if the Flap emote has been unlocked from the Stronghold of Security, when wearing all the pieces of the set, players can do an enhanced "Flap" emote, in which their character lifts off the ground slightly as if flying. The outfit can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player's costume room.

label: Exam Centre
title: Exam Centre
lead:
The Exam Centre is a location in Misthalin (found south-east of Varrock, directly south of the Digsite) that is central to several quests. Its access is limited to members only.

Players can identify a liquid, collected from the barrel in the Digsite by giving it to Terry Balando here. The identified liquid - Nitroglycerin - is commonly used with Dharok the Wretched's equipment in the Pest Control minigame.

label: Examine
title: Examine
lead:
Examine is a feature in Old School RuneScape that allows players to inspect objects closely. Almost anything in Gielinor can be examined, whether it be items, non-player characters or scenery. To examine an object, right-click it and click on "Examine" (see Game controls). The examine option is usually the last option on an object or NPC's right-click menu. If a monster's combat level is higher than a player's, or if they have set their NPC 'Attack' option to always right click, then the examine option will appear for them as second to last.

Upon choosing the Examine option, a short description of the object will appear on the chat interface. If it is a stack of 100,000 or more items (such as a large stack of coins), the text will instead state the exact number of items in the stack, e.g. 111,237 x Coins.

label: Examiner
title: Examiner
lead: Examiner is a worker in the Exam Centre. They can be found in the east building.

label: Excalibur
title: Excalibur
lead:
Excalibur is a one-handed sword and a quest item obtained from the Merlin's Crystal quest and used in the Holy Grail quest. It requires 20 Attack to wield and has similar stats to the adamant longsword, except for 6 less strength bonus and 1 more magic defence.

In the Merlin's Crystal quest, the player must use Excalibur on the crystal to smash and free Merlin. It is obtained from Lady of the Lake after she tests the purity of the player's spirit when giving a beggar bread at Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim.

label: Exit door
title: Exit door
lead: An exit door is in the north-east corner on the ground floor of Melzar's Maze. Opening the door leads to a ladder that players can use to exit the maze.

label: Exit portal (interface item)
title: Exit portal (interface item)
lead:
The Exit portal is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Exit portal.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Expanse
title: Expanse
lead:
Expanse is a music track that can be unlocked at locations outside Varrock city walls, including the Cooks' Guild, Champions' Guild, and Jolly Boar Inn. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Doorways, Greatness, and Still Night.

In Classic mode, this track plays south of Varrock and in the Phoenix Gang Hideout.

label: Expecting
title: Expecting
lead: Expecting is a music track that is unlocked near the Ourania Altar, underneath the Chaos Druid Tower, or by falling through the swamp or from the rope swing in the Underground Pass.

label: Expedition
title: Expedition
lead: Expedition is a music track that can unlocked in the Observatory Dungeon. It can also be unlocked in the passage between the Troll arena and Trollheim.

label: experience
title: experience
lead:
Experience, commonly abbreviated as EXP or XP, is a measure of progress for skills. It is obtained by performing tasks related to that skill. Experience can also be gained through other means, such as quests, the book of knowledge from the Surprise Exam random event, a lamp from the genie random event, certain minigames, and lamps for completing parts of the Achievement Diary and Combat Achievements.

After gaining a certain amount of experience, players will advance to the next level in that skill, which can result in new abilities, and the chance to try more quests. The amount of experience needed for the next level is approximately 10% more than the last level. For example, 83 experience is required for advancement to level 2, while 91 experience is required for advancement to level 3. Reaching level 99 in a skill requires a total of 13,034,431 experience. By around level 30, the exponential factor predominates, so that the amount of experience required doubles for each 7th level. Accordingly, level 92 is nearly the exact halfway mark to level 99, requiring 6,517,253 experience, and level 85 requires very nearly one quarter of the experience needed for level 99. The "92 is half of 99" rule can be seen visually below.

label: Experience item
title: Experience item
lead: Experience items are items which directly grant experience when used from the inventory and which are not typically used when training a skill, e.g. grimy herbs and bones. These usually allow the player to choose a skill in which to gain experience and are often received as rewards from Achievement Diaries, quests, and other non-repeatable content, as well as random events.

label: experience lamp
title: experience lamp
lead: An experience lamp can refer to any one of the multiple lamps which give experience in one or more skills. They are:

label: Experience multiplier
title: Experience multiplier
lead: Experience multipliers cause the default experience of an action to be multiplied. For example, something that gives an experience multiplier of 10 will cause each oak log being chopped to give 375 experience instead of the normal 37.5 experience that an oak log normally gives.

label: experience rate
title: experience rate
lead:
Experience rates refer to the hourly rates at which experience can be obtained through training a specific skill.

Some of the quicker and easier skills to train (such as Cooking and Fletching) can get experience rates upwards of 800,000 per hour, whilst some of the slowest and most tedious skills to train (such as Slayer, Runecraft and Agility) get maximum experience rates between 20,000–75,000 per hour, making them slower to train in comparison to the quicker and easier skills. In all cases, tediousness and "difficulty" of a skill is subjective; however, faster skills tend to be considered easier, with some exceptions such as Thieving due to its high intensity of clicking.

label: exploding rock
title: exploding rock
lead:
The exploding rock random event (AKA: "smoking rock" or "gas") is a Mining random event that occasionally happens when a player tries to mine a rock after the point at which it begins to "steam/smoke/bubble". When this happens, the player should stop mining the affected rock immediately. After mining that rock for more than a few more seconds, the rock will explode which will break the player's pickaxe (see broken pickaxe) making it unusable. It will also damage the player for a number of Hitpoints (based on the player's Hitpoints total) and it may even kill them if their Hitpoints were already greatly reduced.

Explosion of an exploding rock does not cease the smoke from puffing and therefore an exploding rock can explode again if it were mined again or mined by another player.

label: Exploding vial (animation item)
title: Exploding vial (animation item)
lead: The Exploding vial is an animation item used during the Watchtower. It is temporarily wielded during an animation if the player makes a mistake while creating the Magic ogre potion. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.

*Explorer's ring 4

*Explorer's notes

label: explorer's ring
title: explorer's ring
lead:
Explorer's rings are rewards from the Lumbridge & Draynor Diary obtained by speaking to Hatius Cosaintus in Lumbridge. The different upgrades of Explorer's rings are:

*Explorer's ring 1, from the easy tasks set

Items:
* Castle Wars explosive potions, used to destroy barricades

* Elena's explosive potion, a potion used during Song of the Elves

label: Extra weapons rack (interface item)
title: Extra weapons rack (interface item)
lead:
The Extra weapons rack is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Extra weapons rack.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Extreme heat
title: Extreme heat
lead:
Extreme heat is a game mechanic occurring in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon beyond the entrance chamber. It causes the player to take 4 damage every tick, which can quickly kill the player.

Wearing boots of stone, boots of brimstone or granite boots will prevent the extreme heat from ever damaging the player. Players will be warned if they attempt to explore beyond the entrance chamber without one of these boots.

title: Eye (disambiguation)
lead: Eye may refer to:

label: Eye decoration
title: Eye decoration
lead: The eye decoration is the symbol of the Order of Wizards. It can be found on the outside wall of the Wizards' Tower and on the of Zeke's Superior Scimitars in Al Kharid. Another can be found atop the portal leading to the Temple of the Eye from the Wizards' Tower.

label: Eye of newt
title: Eye of newt
lead: An eye of newt is used in Herblore to make attack potions and super attack potions. One eye of newt is needed for the Witch's Potion and Recipe for Disaster quests. After completing Tower of Life, it can be used in the Creature Creation minigame together with a feather to create a newtroost.

label: Ezekiel
title: Ezekiel
lead: Ezekiel is one of the bosses planned for The Fractured Archive raid. He is a follower of Saradomin who came to the Fractured Archive seeking artefacts worthy of Saradomin.

label: facilities
title: facilities
lead:
Facilities are structures or devices that can be built on boats with various useful features. Facilities can be added to a boat at the shipyard and require both Sailing and Construction levels to build. A saw and a hammer are required to build or modify facilities. Facilities can be stored in facility bottles, which allows the stored facility to be moved to a different hotspot or even moved between boats. Constructing a facility this way still requires a hammer and saw.

Different types of boats have different numbers and types of facility hotspots available. Not all facilities can be built on all boats. For example, trawling nets cannot be built on rafts.

label: Fade Test
title: Fade Test
lead:
"Fade Test" was the filename of an unused music track that could be previously found in the cache. The track is a longer version of Ambience 4. It was added in the Runescape 2 beta, but it is unknown where it was intended to play. It was removed from the game files on 26 September 2019.

The track has a copyright date of 2002 rather than the usual 2002-04, as it was not updated when the Music Player was released.

label: Fadli
title: Fadli
lead:
Fadli is the banker at the Emir's Arena. He is also the owner of the Shop of Distaste, where you can buy rotten tomatoes for 1 coin each, these can be thrown at other players. Fadli also serves as a collection point for your Grand Exchange items.

According to Fadli, he is the best warrior in Al Kharid. He wears leather gloves, leather boots, and a hardleather body.

label: Faerdhinen
title: Faerdhinen
lead: Faerdhinen was an elite elven warrior and the sister of Saeldor. She wielded the bow of Faerdhinen, but little else is currently known about her.

label: Faerie
title: Faerie
lead:
Faerie is a music track that is unlocked anywhere in Zanaris, other than the Fairy Resistance Hideout. To get there, the player must have completed the Lost City quest.

Playing this song to Cecilia may be required for a Medium Clue step.

label: Fairy
title: Fairy
lead: Fairies are small race of winged humanoids that occupy Zanaris, along with the mindslayers and otherworldly beings.

label: Fairy (disambiguation)
title: Fairy (disambiguation)
lead: Fairy may refer to:

label: Fairy (race)
title: Fairy (race)
lead:
The Fairies are a small race of winged humanoids that occupy Zanaris, along with the mindslayers and otherworldly beings. Pixies are a type of fairy, hired out by the Fairy Godfather to work jobs on Gielinor for gold.

The Fairies often travel to the world of Gielinor, being in charge of maintaining the world's weather, the growth of crops, and the passing of seasons. They operate from Gielinor's moon, Zanaris, and are co-ordinated jobs by the Co-ordinator, with jobs such as Autumn Fairy, Winter Fairy, Weather Fairy, and Tooth Fairy.

label: Fairy (Zanaris market)
title: Fairy (Zanaris market)
lead: The fairy explains the nearby fairy ring's use. It is a one-way teleport to slightly west of the Al Kharid bank.

label: Fairy bank
title: Fairy bank
lead: Fairy bank can be found in the bank of Zanaris. Players cannot interact with the object, but they can examine it.

label: Fairy Cake
title: Fairy Cake
lead: Fairy Cake is a fairy of Zanaris. She has not been seen since she went to talk to the Fairy Godfather around the time he attacked the city.

label: Fairy dragon
title: Fairy dragon
lead: Fairy dragons are a near-extinct race of dragons. Little is known about them, although them being dragons suggests that they may have been created by the Dragonkin. The only known fairy dragon is K'klik, who is summoned in the Freeing Sir Amik Varze subquest of Recipe for Disaster by rubbing a dragon token.

label: fairy market stall
title: fairy market stall
lead:
Fairy market stalls are stalls which are only found in the Zanaris market place. They can be found next to Jukat and Irksol. To be able to enter the marketplace, players must pay a fee of one diamond.

Although these are stalls, they cannot be thieved from.

label: Fairy Queen
title: Fairy Queen
lead:
The Fairy Queen is the ruler of Zanaris and the fairies, and she plays a key role in the Fairy Tale quest series.

In Fairytale I - Growing Pains the Fairy Godfather has stolen the Queen's secateurs. Players must save the Queen by returning her secateurs which Tanglefoot (a level 111 tree-like monster) drops.

label: Fairy ring (interface item)
title: Fairy ring (interface item)
lead:
The Fairy ring is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Fairy ring.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fairy shop assistant
title: Fairy shop assistant
lead: The fairy shop assistant runs the Zanaris General Store together with the fairy shop keeper.

label: Fairy shop keeper
title: Fairy shop keeper
lead: The fairy shop keeper runs the Zanaris General Store together with the fairy shop assistant.

label: Fairy Tale quest series
title: Fairy Tale quest series
lead: The Fairy Tale quest series is a series of three quests so far. It involves the fairies and is centred on Zanaris. It reveals a plot against the Fairy Queen and shows a group of fairies struggling to reclaim their city.

label: Falador
title: Falador
lead: Falador is the capital city of the Kingdom of Asgarnia. It is home to the iconic White Knight's Castle, and is one of the largest and most major cities, only slightly smaller than Varrock. It plays a key role in the Gielinor ore trade because it houses the Mining Guild, the Motherlode Mine, and a portion of the large Dwarven mine underground.

label: Falador east bank
title: Falador east bank
lead:
The Falador east bank, also known as Falador east or fally east, is a bank found in east Falador, south of the Falador Park. The bank was popular prior to the introduction of the Grand Exchange, and is commonly used before and after drop parties.

There is a Deadman chest in the bank.

label: Falador General Store
title: Falador General Store
lead:
The Falador General Store mainly consists of useful low level items. It is the first building on the west side when entering through the north gate. The ground floor of the general store contains the shop keeper and the shop assistant.

There is a ladder in the store that players can climb up to find Perdu. There are two more floors above him that can be reached by ladders, both of which contain nothing.

label: Falador Park
title: Falador Park
lead: The Falador Park is a large, fenced-in park found in Falador. Several gardeners maintain the plants and ponds located here. It is the entrance to the lair of the Giant Mole, and is a key location in the members' quest Wanted!, as well as the free-to-play quest Pirate's Treasure which requires the player to dig the ground at Falador Park. Multiple Treasure Trails clue scrolls will also lead the player to Falador Park in order to talk to Wyson the gardener or play music for Cecilia. Sir Tiffy Cashien can also be found in the park. He is involved in several quests.

label: Falador shield
title: Falador shield
lead:
Falador shield is a reward from completing parts of the Falador Diary. There are four types, depending on which part of the diary the player has completed. Those are:

*Falador shield 1, from the easy tasks set
*Falador shield 2, from the medium tasks set
*Falador shield 3, from the hard tasks set
*Falador shield 4, from the elite tasks set

label: Falador Teleport
title: Falador Teleport
lead:
Falador Teleport is a Magic spell that teleports the caster to Falador.

Like most teleports, this spell cannot be used past level 20 Wilderness.

label: Falador west bank
title: Falador west bank
lead:
The Falador west bank, also known as Falador west, fally west, and formerly Falador bank, is a popular bank found in north-west Falador.

The bank has a , although there is no way for players to access it. There is a Deadman chest in the bank.

label: Falconry
title: Falconry
lead:
Falconry is a Hunter technique requiring 43 Hunter. The falconry technique can be used to catch three different types of kebbits. With the required Hunter level and a gyr falcon, clicking on a kebbit will send the falcon towards the kebbit. When the falcon catches the kebbit, the hunter needs to retrieve both the falcon and the drops. A yellow arrow marks the location of the falcon with its catch. If the falcon is not retrieved within a short time, the player will get the message, "Your falcon has left its prey. You see it heading back toward the falconer." As long as the player is inside the falconry area, they may talk with the Matthias to get their falcon back without cost; however, no experience is given for the lost prey.

For a fee of 500 coins, hunters can rent a gyr falcon and a falconer's glove from the falcon expert Matthias at the Piscatoris falconry area. Both hands must be free for falconry, which means no items may be carried in the weapon, shield, or gloves slots (the ring slot does NOT need to be empty.) Players may invest in Matthias' operation for a one-time fee of 500,000 coins, allowing for subsequent falcons to be used for free.

label: Fallen tree
title: Fallen tree
lead: Fallen trees are found in various locations across Gielinor. The tree north of Draynor Village serves as a replacement for Sarah's damaged cart after the quest A Porcine of Interest is completed.

label: Family Crest
title: Family Crest
lead: Family Crest is a quest in which the player must retrieve three family crest pieces from the Fitzharmon brothers and return the crest to their father.

label: Family crest (item)
title: Family crest (item)
lead:
The Family crest is a quest item obtained during the Family Crest quest. It is made by combining the three crest parts given to the player by the Fitzharmon brothers, Avan, Caleb, and Johnathon, in return for performing a set of tasks for each brother.

If a player tries to put the crest back together with only two pieces, they will receive a message saying You still need one more piece of the crest.

label: Fancy
title: Fancy
lead:
Fancy may refer to:

*Asyff, owner of the Fancy Clothes Store.
*Fancy Clothes Store, a clothes shop in Varrock.
*Fancy Dan, a team leader in the Trouble Brewing minigame.
*Fancy stone, a type of wallkit for a Player-owned house.

label: Fancy Clothes Store
title: Fancy Clothes Store
lead: The Fancy Clothes Store is a shop in south-eastern Varrock. It is owned and run by Asyff. The shop sells needles and thread and different kinds of clothes such as gloves, boots, capes and hats. The store is also one of the places where players can obtain hunter clothing, through the Custom Fur Clothing panel, some of which increases one's Thieving abilities or provides weight reduction.

label: fancy dress box
title: fancy dress box
lead:
Fancy dress box may refer to:
*Fancy dress box space
*Mahogany fancy dress box
*Oak fancy dress box
*Teak fancy dress box

label: Fancy hedge (interface item)
title: Fancy hedge (interface item)
lead:
The Fancy hedge is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Fancy hedge.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fancy jewellery box (interface item)
title: Fancy jewellery box (interface item)
lead:
The Fancy jewellery box is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Fancy jewellery box.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fancy rejuvenation pool (interface item)
title: Fancy rejuvenation pool (interface item)
lead:
The Fancy rejuvenation pool is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Fancy rejuvenation pool.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fancy stone
title: Fancy stone
lead:
Fancy stone is a House style option for a player-owned house.

When level 50 Construction is reached, this can be chosen as a house template for Player-owned house. Players can purchase this house style enhancement from the Estate agent for 25,000 gold.

label: Fancy teak dresser (interface item)
title: Fancy teak dresser (interface item)
lead:
The Fancy teak dresser is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Fancy teak dresser.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fanfare
title: Fanfare
lead:
Fanfare is a music track that can be unlocked inside Falador city walls. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Arrival and Workshop.

In Classic mode, the track plays in western Falador.

label: Fanfare 2
title: Fanfare 2
lead:
Fanfare 2 is a music track unlocked in the Karamja Ship Yard. The song has a cheerful sound.

In Classic mode, the track plays in a larger area around the Ship Yard.

label: Fanfare 3
title: Fanfare 3
lead: Fanfare 3 is a music track that is unlocked in and around Port Khazard.

label: Fang (disambiguation)
title: Fang (disambiguation)
lead:
Osmumten's fang, commonly referred to as just the fang, is a rare reward from the Tombs of Amascut.

Fang may also refer to:

label: Farm
title: Farm
lead: A farm in Old School RuneScape is an area of land dedicated to agriculture or livestock. Farms often have chickens or cows, as well as various vegetables which players can pick and eat. Some farms have owners which can be talked to, while other farms have no apparent owner. Several locations, such as the Vinery and the Winery, are not farms in the traditional sense, but are classified as such on this page.

label: Farmer
title: Farmer
lead: Farmers are level 7 humans found on farms. Farmers are fairly weak and can be fair melee training for lower levels. Players with level 10 Thieving can pickpocket farmers, gaining 14.5 experience.

label: Farmer (disambiguation)
title: Farmer (disambiguation)
lead:
Farmer may refer to:

* Cabbage Farmer, the farmer who spawns when the cabbage patch in northern Aldarin is picked empty
* Farmer, level 7 monsters that can be pickpocketed with level 10 Thieving
* Farmer (Misthalin), NPCs tending Groats' farm and Draynor farm in Misthalin
* Farmer (Hosidius), NPCs tending farms around Hosidius
* Farmer (Kastori), NPCs in Kastori that can be pickpocketed with level 10 Thieving
* Farmer (Shayzien), the lone farmer found in the Cloak and Stagger
* Farmer (The Golden Field), the farmers in The Golden Field tavern
* Farmer (Varlamore), the farmers in Varlamore
* Master Farmer, any of several NPCs who can be pickpocketed with level 38 Thieving

label: Farmer (Misthalin)
title: Farmer (Misthalin)
lead: Farmers are non-player characters located in Misthalin. They can be found tilling the soil of various crop fields such as wheat or potatoes in Lumbridge and Draynor Village.

label: Farmer Brumty
title: Farmer Brumty
lead:
Farmer Brumty is involved in the Sheep Herder quest. He is the owner of the sick-looking sheep and will aid players in their attempt to combat the plague. Like the other normal citizens in East Ardougne, he is oblivious to the plague hoax that King Lathas has created.

In order to enter Farmer Brumty's enclosure players must be wearing both a plague jacket and plague trousers.

label: Farmer's fork
title: Farmer's fork
lead:
The Farmer's fork is an unobtainable item added to the game with the release of RuneScape 2. Although it is classified internally as a weapon, it lacks a wield option and does not have any equip animations defined.

It is very similar, but not identical, to the forks that are wielded by farmers.

label: Farmer's outfit
title: Farmer's outfit
lead:
The farmer's outfit is an experience-boosting set that grants bonus Farming experience when worn. A Farming level of 34 is required to wear any of the pieces, as pieces of the outfit are purchased from the Tithe Farm shop. The outfit costs a total of 400 points to purchase. The outfit is significantly different for body type A and B: in addition to the other pieces having a different appearance, body type A characters obtain the farmer's jacket while body type B characters obtain the farmer's shirt. Attempting to change body type at the Makeover Mage while wearing any of the pieces will result in them saying "'Fraid I can't see you under all that dirt from farming. You'll have to take your farmer's outfit off before I can give you a makeover.".

A reasonably efficient player can earn about 76 points per hour, meaning it takes approximately five and a half hours of Tithe Farm to earn the full farmer's outfit. If earned at low levels, this will save the player approximately 326,000 experience over the course of getting 99 Farming. In obtaining the outfit, 569,692 experience is gained from the Tithe Farm minigame if using Logavano to gain 400 points and getting a perfect score (26 points). This is the equivalent of earning 62,000 (without counting Tithe Farm experience) or 166,000 (with Tithe Farm experience using Logavano) experience per hour. As such, players aiming for 99 Farming should consider if this rate is less than what one might earn doing other more efficient tasks such as tree runs.

label: Farming Guild Door
title: Farming Guild Door
lead:
The Farming Guild Door is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Farming Guild Gate
title: Farming Guild Gate
lead:
The Farming Guild Gate is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Farming runs
title: Farming runs
lead:
Farming runs, sometimes referred to as farm runs, are the act of visiting farming locations in sequence to efficiently harvest crops. Farming runs are the most effective way to gain Farming experience, compared to waiting for growing crops to complete.

Farming runs can be combined with activities such as item alchemising or bolt fletching.

label: Farming shops
title: Farming shops
lead: Farming shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. The majority of farming shops sell tools that players need to start Farming, while some sell seeds. There are 13 Farming shops in Old School RuneScape. Most are located near an allotment farming patch.

label: Farming training
title: Farming training
lead:
Farming training focuses heavily on doing tree runs, which is a recurring training method. Much like daily events and recurring money making methods, tree runs give Farming experience passively over time since it is possible to only do 1 or 2 runs per day. Instead of actively training the skill for hours, players only spend a few minutes to do a run, gaining a lot of Farming experience during that short amount of time, and then do other activities while waiting for the patches to grow. While trees take a very long while to grow in real time, players spend very little time actively doing tree runs.

Doing tree runs costs money, and certain saplings and protection payments can be quite expensive. It is recommended to have a decent amount of money to be able to buy a lot of Farming supplies at once, and have a good money making method to sustain the cost of doing tree runs. Herb runs are often highly profitable and they also offer a fair amount of Farming experience, but usually it is better to look into money making alternatives that offer better profit.

label: Farming/Experience table
title: Farming/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Farming in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Farming level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: Fastest bank teleports
title: Fastest bank teleports
lead:
This page contains information on the fastest bank teleports in Old School RuneScape. It only includes banks within 40 tiles of a teleport or less; consult the list of banks for a full list of all bank locations. Bank deposit boxes are listed in their own table below, for the purposes of quick deposits while skilling.

While running, a player can travel 2 tiles in 0.6 seconds, one game tick. In addition, for locations with a banker, using the "Bank" option on bankers allows the user to bank one tile sooner.

label: Fat Tony
title: Fat Tony
lead: Fat Tony is the owner of Tony's Pizza Bases, he is located in the Wilderness Bandit Camp. He is an outlaw after being accused of giving the king food poisoning. He denies it and fled the kingdom of Misthalin. The bandits give him refuge so long as he cooks for them.

label: Father Aereck
title: Father Aereck
lead:
Father Aereck is a Saradominist priest who maintains the over 230-year-old church of Lumbridge.

He is the person players must speak with to start The Restless Ghost quest.

label: Father Lawrence
title: Father Lawrence
lead: Father Lawrence Lambare is a priest who worships Saradomin in his church in north-east Varrock. He is often drunk when talked to and also claims that he is holding a congregation, although both of his followers, Martina Scorsby and Jeremy Clerksin, are asleep in their seats. He is a close friend to Romeo and he knows a lot about the struggles between Romeo's and Juliet's families. Father Lawrence is the person who suggests that you make a cadava potion during the Romeo & Juliet quest to help Romeo marry the love of his life, Juliet.

label: Father Urhney
title: Father Urhney
lead:
Father Urhney is an irritable priest who lives as a hermit in the Lumbridge Swamp. He has left Lumbridge to perform a full two-years meditation and retreat. Father Urhney never stops meditating, however, since he is constantly interrupted by people asking for amulets or claiming they have come to repossess his house. He suspects they are part of 'a bizarre conspiracy by some fiendish cult.'

Father Urhney plays a role in The Restless Ghost, giving the player a Ghostspeak amulet, which is required to speak to the Restless ghost in Lumbridge. If the player loses the Ghostspeak amulet, even after the quest is done, he will provide the player with a new amulet.

label: Favour certificate
title: Favour certificate
lead:
Favour certificate can refer to one of the following:

*Kourend favour certificate
*Hosidius favour certificate
*Piscarilius favour certificate
*Shayzien favour certificate
*Lovakengj favour certificate
*Arceuus favour certificate

title: fayrg
lead:
