Fayrgs are an extinct race of creatures in the service of Bandos that were likely wiped out during the cataclysmic God Wars. Their remains, Fayrg bones, can be found in the coffins at Jiggig.

The appearance and nature of Fayrgs is largely unknown, they are however suspected to be similar to ogres, orks, raurgs and ourgs.

label: Feather
title: Feather
lead:
Feathers are used in the Fishing and Fletching skills. In Fishing, feathers are used as lures for fly fishing. Feathers may also be used as bait for barbarian heavy-rod fishing, as a cheaper alternative to fishing bait. In Fletching, feathers are used to make arrows, darts, and bolts. Feathers cannot be noted, as they are stackable.

These are the only feathers that can be used to summon a newtroost during the Creature Creation activity in the Tower of Life, as coloured feathers are not accepted by the altar.

label: Feather (disambiguation)
title: Feather (disambiguation)
lead:
Feather usually refers to Feather, dropped by Chickens and used in the Fletching and Fishing skills.

However, it may also refer to various quest items or coloured feathers dropped from Hunter creatures.

label: Feet slot table
title: Feet slot table
lead: Click a column header icon to sort the table by that column. Use SHIFT click to sort by multiple columns.

label: Feldip Hills
title: Feldip Hills
lead: The Feldip Hills are positioned to the south of Yanille and south-east of the Castle Wars arena. The main city of Feldip Hills is Gu'Tanoth—to the west of Gu'Tanoth is Jiggig. Jiggig is filled with zogres and skogres. In the southern areas is a Hunter training area. After completing the quest Big Chompy Bird Hunting, the hunting area can be used to hunt chompy. After speaking to Haris with Dragon Slayer I completed, the Corsair Cove Resource Area in the south-west of Feldip Hills can be unlocked and used as a spot to harpoon fish for tuna and swordfish, cage fish for lobster, or cut yew and maple trees.

label: Feldip Hills Civil War
title: Feldip Hills Civil War
lead:
The Feldip Hills Civil War was a major conflict between Bandosians living in the Feldip Hills near the beginning of the Fourth Age. After the end of the God Wars, Bandos was banished from Gielinor and the remaining followers of Bandos were left without guidance, causing them to fall into a bloody civil war. Soon enough, the much more powerful ogres united against the weaker goblins living in the area and effectively began a mass of the goblins, prompting them to retreat north.

It was at this point that King Baxtorian and his Cadarn Clan began to settle in what is now Kandarin, having crossed the Galarpos Mountains. After establishing peace treaties with the Tree Gnome Stronghold and local human tribes, the elves approached the ogres, but quickly left the Feldip Hills after realising the warring nation could not be reasoned with. Although the elves soon established a stable kingdom, they suffered on a small scale due to raids from the goblins fleeing northwards, which apparently lasted several decades. Eventually, the goblin tribes, minus the Dorgeshuun, all came together in what is now Hemenster where the scarce food and constantly diminishing living space triggered the events that would lead to the Battle of the Plain of Mud around the middle of the Fourth Age.

label: Felling axe
title: Felling axe
lead:
Felling axes are 2-handed tools used in the Woodcutting skill. When used with Forester's rations in their inventory or inside their Forestry kit they offer 10% more Woodcutting experience than regular axes while also having a 20% chance to not obtain a log. Note that felling axes can use Forester's rations even if the felling axe is not wielded. This effect will also apply to sulliusceps. One ration is consumed every time the player completes an action (e.g. receiving a log or extra Woodcutting experience). The experience boost stacks multiplicatively with the lumberjack outfit. When missing out on receiving a log, a roll for the beaver pet will still be made. If the player has no Forester's rations, the felling axe will function like a regular axe of the same tier.

Felling axes chop wood at the same tick frequency and have the same success rates as their standard counterparts. Higher-tier axes have a greater chance of obtaining logs from a tree and thus are generally faster to woodcut with. However, with a high Woodcutting level, a 100% success rate at certain low-level trees becomes attainable even with lower-tier axes.

label: Female H.A.M. (interface item)
title: Female H.A.M. (interface item)
lead:
The Female H.A.M. is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide representing H.A.M. Members.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Female slave
title: Female slave
lead:
Female slaves can be found working the mines at the Desert Mining Camp.

The generic female slaves (along with male slaves) complain a lot about being there and about their work. They can be spoken to, but no dialogue pops up, they will exclaim and the player will get thrown in jail if done enough times. After completion of The Tourist Trap, it's no longer possible to get thrown in the jail and the slaves can be talked to freely.

label: Femi
title: Femi
lead:
Femi is a gnome trader located outside the gate leading into the Tree Gnome Stronghold. When attempting to enter the gate for the first time, Femi will ask the player if they can help load some boxes into her cart. If the player helps load the boxes, she will later smuggle the player into the Tree Gnome Stronghold for free during The Grand Tree quest. If the player declines to help load the boxes, she will require a fee of 1,000 coins to smuggle the player in during the quest.

If the player has never spoken to Femi before The Grand Tree quest (by always entering the Tree Gnome Stronghold via a spirit tree), she will act as if the player had already assisted her and allow entry for free.

label: Fence
title: Fence
lead: Fence may refer to:

label: Fence (Biohazard)
title: Fence (Biohazard)
lead: A fence can be found at the back of the Mourner Headquarters in West Ardougne. Players must squeeze-through the fence during the Biohazard quest to throw a rotten apple in the cauldron located in the garden of the headquarters.

label: Fence (Construction)
title: Fence (Construction)
lead: Fences are built using the Construction skill in a formal garden of a player-owned house. There are seven different types of fences that can be built into a player-owned house:

label: Fencing ring (interface item)
title: Fencing ring (interface item)
lead:
The Fencing ring is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Fencing ring.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: fern
title: fern
lead:
Fern may refer to:
*Fern (scenery)
*Ferns used in Construction:
**Fern (big plant)
**Fern (small plant)
**Small fern
*Fernahei, owner of Fernahei's Fishing Hut

label: Fern (scenery)
title: Fern (scenery)
lead: Ferns can be found almost anywhere with plant life. The common fern is ubiquitous throughout Gielinor, and can be found as far as Zeah and even on Zanaris. There is no way to interact with ferns other than to examine them. Ferns prevent fires from being lit on tile which they occupy, but are otherwise simply decorative.

label: Fernahei
title: Fernahei
lead: Fernahei runs Fernahei's Fishing Hut in Shilo Village. Players often buy feathers from him, and sell him fish. Shop prices are affected by the use of Karamja gloves.

label: Fernahei's Fishing Hut.
title: Fernahei's Fishing Hut.
lead: Fernahei's Fishing Hut is a fishing shop in Shilo Village run by Fernahei. The shop is filled with items related to fly Fishing, which is what Shilo Village is most popular with players for aside from the highest level Slayer Master, Duradel. It is common for players preparing to begin fly Fishing in the village to purchase the feathers here, unless they have purchased beforehand.

label: Fertile Soil (scenery)
title: Fertile Soil (scenery)
lead: Fertile Soil refers to 6 patches of soil in the Kharazi Jungle which are suitible for planting a Yommi tree during the Legends' Quest. Before planting, Fertile Soil must be treated by a golden bowl filled with holy water from the Kharazi water pool.

label: Fertiliser
title: Fertiliser
lead:
Fertiliser may refer to:

*Compost
*Fertile Soil
*Gricoller's fertiliser
*Sulphurous fertiliser
*Supercompost
*Ultracompost

label: Festival of Zamorak
title: Festival of Zamorak
lead:
The Festival of Zamorak is a social and holiday observed by the werewolves of Morytania, although it may be celebrated more secretly by other Zamorakians.

The werewolves of Canifis celebrate the event annually as an enjoyable sign of fealty to Zamorak, the patron god whom the majority of Morytanians worship.

label: Fetid waters
title: Fetid waters
lead:
Fetid waters are a sailing hazard which inflicts disease when players sail into the water. Entering Fetid water also inflicts 5 player damage every few seconds and severely slows your boat down if you enter without an Innoculation station. There is a short grace period in which players can exit the waters, before becoming diseased. It can be prevented by an Innoculation station.

Consuming a Sanfew serum will prevent the player from becoming diseased, but they will still take 5 damage every few seconds while remaining in the fetid waters.

label: Fever spider (interface item)
title: Fever spider (interface item)
lead:
The Fever spider is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Fever spider

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fidelio
title: Fidelio
lead: Fidelio is the owner of the general store in Canifis. Like all the residents of Canifis, he is a werewolf, but is not aggressive to the player. He claims that the items he sells are "rare human artefacts which I went to great lengths of danger to acquire!" He speaks with a stutter.

label: Field
title: Field
lead:
Fields may refer to:

* Potato fields
* Onion fields
* Cabbage fields
** Draynor cabbage field
* Wheat fields
* Flax fields
* Sweetcorn fields

label: Fiend
title: Fiend
lead:
Fiend may refer to various demons:

*Icefiend, found in colder areas.
*Pyrefiend, Slayer monsters that require 30 Slayer to be harmed.
*Pyrelord, a stronger variant of pyrefiends.
*Flaming pyrelord, the superior variant of pyrefiends.
*Infernal pyrelord, the superior variant of pyrelords.
*Waterfiend, which reside in the Ancient Cavern and Kraken Cove.

label: Fiery (attribute)
title: Fiery (attribute)
lead:
Fiery is an attribute assigned to monsters that are weak to the special effect of pearl bolts (e).

Dragons usually have the fiery attribute, however non-dragon dragonkin experiments with the draconic attribute are often not fiery.

label: Fifth Age
title: Fifth Age
lead: The Fifth Age, also known as The Age of Man or The Age of Humans, is the current age of Gielinor. The Fifth Age is a time of amazing strides for the human race, granting many humans dominance throughout central Gielinor largely due to the discovery of runes at the end of the Fourth Age. Positive advances in humanity's lifestyle include military, technological, theological, philosophical, political, and economic strides.

label: Fight Arena
title: Fight Arena
lead: Fight Arena is an intermediate quest. The quest is started south of Ardougne by the titular Fight Arena by talking to Lady Servil.

label: Fight Arena (location)
title: Fight Arena (location)
lead:
The Fight Arena is a large structure south of Ardougne. It is here that General Khazard forces captured creatures and people (called fight slaves) to fight in violent clashes that always result in death. Some of these creatures were most likely imported by ship through Port Khazard from other regions.

The Fight Arena plays a large role in the quest Fight Arena. The only useful facilities that can be found here are the 4 water supplies and the bar to the west. Khazard armour can be obtained here by searching the armoury in the north-eastern house. Other than this, the area has no other use and cannot be accessed again after completing the quest. If attempted, the doorman will say "You're [him/her/them]! The one who murdered the General's pet. Leave this place at once!".

label: Fight Arena Bar
title: Fight Arena Bar
lead:
The Fight Arena Bar is a single-floored pub located in the south-western corner of the Fight Arena. The pub heavily relies on the Arena for its business, as it draws many customers ranging from spectators to guards.

The bar is the only place in RuneScape where players can purchase the Khali brew, which sells for 5 coins each. However, it has no drink option so players cannot consume it, and it is also untradeable. Regular beer is also available for 2 coins each.

label: Fight Arena mine
title: Fight Arena mine
lead: The Fight Arena mine is a mining area located between Port Khazard and Yanille, near the Fight Arena. It has a large variety of rocks, and it is close to the nearby Yanille bank as well as a bank deposit box and chest at Port Khazard. Also, the mine is a good source for iron ore.

label: Filled Recess
title: Filled Recess
lead: The Filled Recess is created when the player uses the activated heart crystal on the recess next to the shimmering field in order to pass through it. This can only be done during Legends' Quest.

label: Filliman Tarlock
title: Filliman Tarlock
lead:
Filliman Tarlock is the central character of the Nature Spirit quest. Players must wear the ghostspeak amulet to speak to him. During the quest, the player helps him transform from a ghost into a nature spirit. After the quest, he will disappear and reemerge during the quests, Fairytale I - Growing Pains and A Night at the Theatre.

He lives in his grotto in Mort Myre Swamp where an Altar of nature can be found after completing the quest. To reach his grotto, the most efficient way is to run all the way south of the western coast of the swamp.

label: Financial Advisor
title: Financial Advisor
lead:
The financial advisor was a man found in the Tutorial Island's bank. He taught players about ways to make money.
He told you that there were three basic ways of making money in Old School RuneScape:
*Combat, by picking up monster drops.
*Quests, by receiving their rewards.
*Trading with other players.
He said that he had to run through it quickly so you wouldn't get much out of him.

As he was not deemed useful, he was fired and replaced by the Account Guide in an update on 18 October 2018, although they both share the same appearance.

label: Fine Fashions
title: Fine Fashions
lead:
Fine Fashions is a store in the Grand Tree that is owned by Rometti. He can be found north-east on the . He sells an assortment of gnome robes sets in five pastel colours. These colours are pink, green, blue, cream, and turquoise.

Some of these items are used in Treasure Trails emote clues.

label: Fingernails
title: Fingernails
lead:
Fingernails is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. During the quest, the player can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille.

The fingernails must be given to the wizard in the Watchtower in order for him to be able to identify who stole the power crystals that make the tower operate.

label: Finnigan
title: Finnigan
lead:
Finnigan is a member of the Zamorak Magical Institute (Z.M.I.) mentioned by Hagus.

According to Hagus, Finnigan, Herbert, and himself were all assigned important missions, but he refuses to elaborate what those missions are or who Finnigan is.

label: Fionella
title: Fionella
lead:
Fionella is a non-player character that can be found on the of the Legends' Guild. She runs the Legends Guild General Store.

In a letter from the Postbag from the Hedge, it is revealed that she is the wife of Radimus Erkle. Despite selling items within the Legends' Guild, she is not an actual member as with the bankers in the guild.

label: fire
title: fire
lead: A fire is a pile of burning logs lit on fire using the Firemaking skill. Many foods can be cooked on a fire, given the player has the required Cooking level.

label: Fire (disambiguation)
title: Fire (disambiguation)
lead:
Fire may refer to:

*Fire, the result of using logs with a tinderbox.
** Fire (scenery), naturally occurring fires
*Firemaking, the skill used to light said fires.

label: Fire (Goblin Settlement)
title: Fire (Goblin Settlement)
lead: Fire is located in the Goblin settlement east of the Observatory. The fire is being tended by the goblins Greasycheeks and Smellytoes, but players may still use it for cooking.

label: Fire Altar
title: Fire Altar
lead:
The Fire Altar is a runic altar upon which fire runes are crafted from rune essence or pure essence, providing 7 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Level 14 Runecraft is required to craft fire runes.

Players may create a fire tiara here by using either a fire talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 35 Runecraft experience. An elemental tiara can also be created here by using an elemental talisman and gold tiara, granting 40 Runecraft experience.

label: Fire arrows
title: Fire arrows
lead:
Fire arrows are used to access the Underground Pass starting with the Underground Pass quest, in order to burn down the ropes holding up a bridge allowing one into the pass maze proper.

Fire arrows are created by using an oily cloth on most untreated arrows, then by using them on a tinderbox or any fire. There is a perpetual fire in the Underground Pass near Koftik for ease of access. Lit fire arrows can also set mummies ablaze inside the Ancient Pyramid. Apart from that, they are no different from normal arrows in combat.

label: Fire battlestaff
title: Fire battlestaff
lead:
The fire battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 62 Crafting by combining a fire orb and battlestaff. It can also be upgraded to a mystic fire staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries). The mystic fire staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.

label: Fire Blast
title: Fire Blast
lead:
Fire Blast is a fire-based blast spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 59 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

It is the strongest fire spell available to free-to-play players.

label: Fire Bolt
title: Fire Bolt
lead: Fire Bolt is a fire-based bolt spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 35 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

label: Fire elemental
title: Fire elemental
lead:
Fire elementals are one of the elementals featured in the Elemental Workshop quest series, along with the air, earth, and water elementals. They reside within the Elemental Workshop and the Smoke Dungeon.

Killing one is a requirement for an Easy Kandarin Diary task.

label: Fire feather
title: Fire feather
lead:
The fire feather is a quest item dropped by the Entrana firebird. Players need to obtain the fire feather as part of Heroes' Quest. In order to pick up the feather, the player must be wearing the Ice gloves, or else the player will fail to pick it up and take about 1/8 of their current HP in damage. After Heroes' Quest is completed, the fire feather cannot be re-obtained. If a player tries to pick up the fire feather before starting Heroes' Quest, they will receive the message: "It looks dangerously hot, and you have no reason to take it."

It is impossible to telegrab this item, even if the player is wearing the ice gloves. When a player attempts to telegrab the feather, they will receive the message: "I can't use Telekinetic Grab on this object.".

label: Fire Giant
title: Fire Giant
lead:
Fire giants are powerful giants that are popular for training Ranged and Slayer. They are also the strongest of the standard giants, being significantly stronger than their Ice, Moss, and Hill giant relatives.

Fire giants are assigned by a multitude of Slayer Masters, providing fairly decent experience for both combat and Slayer. They're also frequently killed by Ironman players early on due to their signature rune scimitar drop, as they are fairly easy to access with numerous safespots. Low-level players may find enchanted pearl bolts helpful when training Ranged against these enemies. Although there are many locations where cannons can be used, only the Charred Dungeon spawns are in a multicombat area.

label: Fire of Dehumidification (interface item)
title: Fire of Dehumidification (interface item)
lead:
The Fire of Dehumidification is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction and Firemaking skill guides representing the Fire of Dehumidification.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fire of Eternal Light (interface item)
title: Fire of Eternal Light (interface item)
lead:
The Fire of Eternal Light is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction and Firemaking skill guides representing the Fire of Eternal Light.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fire of Nourishment (interface item)
title: Fire of Nourishment (interface item)
lead:
The Fire of Nourishment is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction and Firemaking skill guides representing the Fire of Nourishment.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fire of Unseasonal Warmth (interface item)
title: Fire of Unseasonal Warmth (interface item)
lead:
The Fire of Unseasonal Warmth is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction and Firemaking skill guides representing the Fire of Unseasonal Warmth.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fire orb
title: Fire orb
lead:
A fire orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Fire by using the Charge Fire Orb spell, requiring 63 Magic, on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb, 30 fire runes, and 3 cosmic runes, yielding 73 Magic experience. The Fire Obelisk is located at the end of Taverley Dungeon, west of the black dragons.

A fire orb can be used on a battlestaff, requiring 62 Crafting, yielding a fire battlestaff and 125 Crafting experience.

label: fire pit
title: fire pit
lead:
Fire pits are rebuilt old fire pits in which special permanent fires are lit using a combination of salts. All fires require 66 Firemaking, but the required Construction level varies. These fires grant the player certain conveniences, such as serving as an inextinguishable light source, removing the need for a player to bring one themselves.

Fire pits can only be built and lit after the completion of the quest Making Friends with My Arm. Players cannot cook on these fire pits.

label: Fire remains
title: Fire remains
lead:
Fire remains may refer to:

* Fiyr remains
* Fire remains (Royal Trouble)
* Fire remains (Monkey Madness II)

label: Fire rune
title: Fire rune
lead: Fire runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used to cast fire-based combat spells in the standard spellbook, as well as casting many spells from other spellbooks. Some notable use cases for fire runes include casting alchemy spells to convert items into coins, charging a trident of the seas or trident of the swamp, and resurrecting high level thralls. Several items throughout the game, such as the staff of fire, provide infinite fire runes while equipped. Fire runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops, such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. Non-ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.

label: fire spells
title: fire spells
lead: Fire spells may refer to:

label: Fire Strike
title: Fire Strike
lead: Fire Strike is a fire-based strike spell in the standard spellbook, available at level 13 Magic. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

label: Fire talisman
title: Fire talisman
lead:
The fire talisman is a talisman used in the Runecraft skill to enter the Fire Altar north of Al Kharid. It can also be combined with a tiara to create a fire tiara, which grants you 35 Runecraft experience.

It is dropped by a variety of monsters, including skeletons, fire wizards (1/20), dark wizards, creatures in the Abyss and lava dragons. The drop rate is noted to be slightly higher from dark wizards than regular wizards but more commonly by fire wizards and creatures in the Abyss.

label: Fire wall
title: Fire wall
lead: Fire Walls are found in the Shaman Caves in the form of an octagram, sealing Ungadulu inside. During the Legends' Quest, the player must obtain a bowl of pure water and use it on the fire wall in order to extinguish a part of it and walk through. After the player has defeated Nezikchened inside the octagram of fire, Ungadulu casts a spell on the player, allowing them to freely walk through the fire wall by either attempting to touch it or by investigating it.

label: Fire Warrior of Lesarkus
title: Fire Warrior of Lesarkus
lead:
Leka, the Fire Warrior of Lesarkus, is a temple guardian encountered while exploring during the Temple of Ikov quest. He guards a door leading to Winelda the witch.

When a player attempts to open the door, he will appear and demand to know their identity. If the player chooses to identify themselves as a humble pilgrim, he will comment that no pilgrims have been to the temple for thousands of years, and will tell the player that the temple is closed. Otherwise, if the player instead states that they are a mighty hero, he will become enraged and attack. He uses fire-based magic attacks. If the player takes too long to kill him, he will simply disappear and the player will have to make him appear again.

label: Fire Wave
title: Fire Wave
lead:
Fire Wave is a fire-based wave spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 75 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

It is the second-strongest fire spell in the game, with the strongest being Fire Surge.

label: Firemaking
title: Firemaking
lead:
Firemaking is a skill used to light fires, among other things. It is the artisan companion skill of Woodcutting. Firemaking is trained by players to complete quests or participate in minigames. Several quests with quality rewards require Firemaking levels, such as Recipe for Disaster and Desert Treasure I. Similarly, Firemaking-oriented minigames with useful rewards include Shades of Mort'ton and the Wintertodt boss. Firemaking allows players to light logs to cook food anywhere, albeit with a higher burn chance than with a range. Wintertodt is a solid way to train Firemaking whilst also being profitable. Subduing the Wintertodt is the only way to obtain the pyromancer outfit.

Burnt-out fires leave behind ashes which some members may use to train Herblore with by making Serum 207. Players can turn a profit from burning cheaper logs and collecting the ashes, though at the cost of experience per hour.

label: Firemaking Level Up!
title: Firemaking Level Up!
lead: Firemaking Level Up! is a jingle for levelling Firemaking.

label: Firemaking Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Firemaking Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Firemaking Level Up! (Unlocks) is a Jingle for leveling Firemaking.

label: Firemaking/Experience table
title: Firemaking/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Firemaking in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Firemaking level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: Firepit (interface item)
title: Firepit (interface item)
lead:
The Firepit is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Firepit.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Firepit with hook (interface item)
title: Firepit with hook (interface item)
lead:
The Firepit with hook is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Firepit with hook.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Firepit with pot (interface item)
title: Firepit with pot (interface item)
lead:
The Firepit with pot is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Firepit with pot.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fireplace
title: Fireplace
lead:
Fireplaces are interactive scenery items found inside many buildings in Old School RuneScape. The fireplace can be used like a camping fire to cook any meat, fish, or seafood and carries the same burn rate as a regular fire.

While the fire in the fireplace remains always lit, it does not allow players to bake or cook food that requires a range such as bread, stews, cakes, pies or pizzas due to the fact that it is similar to a normal fire. Players can also build a clay fireplace, stone fireplace, or a marble fireplace in their homes using the Construction skill at levels 3, 33, and 63 respectively, and can light them with logs and a tinderbox.

label: Firework
title: Firework
lead: A firework is an unobtainable potion released alongside snapdragon and the Brimhaven Agility Arena. It was presumably intended to be a cosmetic potion created from snapdragons, but was scrapped for unknown reasons.

label: First Age
title: First Age
lead: The First Age, also known as The Age of Creation, is the first era of the history of Gielinor. It is estimated to have been around 4,000 years long.

label: fish
title: fish
lead: Fish and other marine life are found throughout Gielinor. Conventional fish can be caught using a number of methods with the Fishing skill, and then cooked with the Cooking skill for food. There are unique fish that are obtained by ways other than fishing.

label: Fish (disambiguation)
title: Fish (disambiguation)
lead:
Fish may refer to:
*Fish caught using the Fishing skill
*Goblin fish or loach
*Fishing is a skill used to catch edible sea creatures and other items
*Fishing items are useful items concerned with fishing, including a list of fish that players can catch
*Several types of fish found underwater on Fossil Island or at the Mogre Camp:
**Fish (angel fish)
**Fish (black moor fantail)
**Fish (discus)
**Fish (harlequin)
**Fish (neon tetra)
**Fish (paradise)
**Fish (pearl danio)
**Fish (red fantail)
*Fresh fish, a discontinued item
*Fishy salvage

label: Fish food
title: Fish food
lead:
Fish food is used in the Ernest the Chicken quest, used to feed fish that members can obtain as pets, and used in a step as part of Crack the Clue III. The poison found in the kitchen of Draynor Manor can be combined with the fish food to create poisoned fish food, which is used to kill the piranhas in the fountain south-west of Draynor Manor, allowing the player to retrieve a pressure gauge needed for the quest.

It can be found on the second level of Draynor Manor in the room with the ghost, south of the stairs.

label: Fisher Realm
title: Fisher Realm
lead:
The Realm of the Fisher King is the name given to a small kingdom located on an inter-dimensional plane alongside that of Gielinor's. The area plays a key role in the Holy Grail quest, in which the player is tasked with returning the grail to The Knights of the Round Table following Sir Galahad's choice to pardon himself from the order so he could become a monk.

Prior to completion of the quest, the area is ruled by The Fisher King; however, he is eventually succeeded by Sir Percival upon completion of the quest.

label: Fisherman
title: Fisherman
lead:
Fisherman may refer to:
*Fisherman (Holy Grail)
*Fisherman (Fishing Platform)
*Fisherman (Rellekka)
*Fisherman (Port Piscarilius)
*Fisherman Frodi
*Witchaven villager

label: Fisherman (Fishing Platform)
title: Fisherman (Fishing Platform)
lead:
The Fishermen of the Fishing Platform were attacked and possessed by sea slugs, they have yellowish skin and make bizarre comments.

During the Sea Slug quest, they scare Kennith into hiding.

label: Fisherman (Holy Grail)
title: Fisherman (Holy Grail)
lead: The Fisherman is a subject of the Fisher Realm and one of the few people present that follow The Fisher King. During the quest Holy Grail, you must ask him how to enter the Grail Castle, which is by ringing the grail bell found outside. He disappears after Percival has become king for reasons unknown. He wears an eyepatch.

label: Fishing
title: Fishing
lead: Fishing is a skill which involves catching fish from selected spots around Gielinor. Higher Fishing levels enable different mechanisms of Fishing, the ability to catch a larger selection of fish and increases a player's catch rate. Caught fish may be cooked through the Cooking skill to create food which may be used later to regain hitpoints during combat. Alternatively, many players sell their excess stock of catches for gold.

label: Fishing (music track)
title: Fishing (music track)
lead:
Fishing is a music track that is unlocked in Catherby. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track and Lightwalk.

In Classic music mode, this track only plays on the east side of Catherby or on the northern shore of Entrana.

label: Fishing bait
title: Fishing bait
lead:
Fishing bait is an item used with the fishing rod. It is used to fish in any fishing spot as long as the spot has the Bait Fishing Spot option. Each successful catch uses up one piece of bait, so bring an appropriate amount in your inventory if you wish to catch a lot of fish.

Fishing bait can also be used for barbarian fishing, replacing feathers as bait.

label: Fishing Contest
title: Fishing Contest
lead: Fishing Contest is a quest in which the player has to earn the friendship of two dwarven brothers by securing a fishing trophy for them. Afterwards, they allow the player to use the dwarven passage underneath the mountain.

label: Fishing enhancers
title: Fishing enhancers
lead: Fishing enhancers are items that aid the player in Fishing. Their benefits range from giving a chance to catch an extra fish, to increasing the odds of catching specific fish. The effects of fishing enhancers stack with each other.

label: Fishing explosive (interface item)
title: Fishing explosive (interface item)
lead:
The Fishing explosive is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Fishing explosive

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fishing Guild
title: Fishing Guild
lead:
The Fishing Guild is a members-only guild located in a fenced area north of East Ardougne; west of Hemenster, which was released on 17 June 2002. To enter, players must have a Fishing level of 68; temporary boosts can be used to boost one's level in order to enter the guild, making the lowest level to possibly enter 62 using a super fishing potion.

Historically, aside from Catherby, the Fishing Guild has been one of the most popular places to fish because of the nearby bank.

label: Fishing Guild bank
title: Fishing Guild bank
lead:
The Fishing Guild bank is a bank located in the Fishing Guild. It was the first bank to be added in RuneScape 2.

Players must have to enter the guild, although it can be boosted from as low as 63 with an admiral pie. The bank is commonly used by ironmen, as well as for people completing the Fishing Guild Treasure Trails step.

label: Fishing Guild Shop.
title: Fishing Guild Shop.
lead: The Fishing Guild Shop is a store located in the Fishing Guild, owned by Roachey. It sells fishing bait and feathers, and will buy fish from players. The guild requires 68 Fishing to enter.

label: Fishing Level Up!
title: Fishing Level Up!
lead: Fishing Level Up! is a jingle for levelling Fishing.

label: Fishing Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Fishing Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Fishing Level Up! (Unlocks) is a jingle for levelling Fishing.

label: Fishing net
title: Fishing net
lead:
Fishing net may refer to:

*Small fishing net, an item that beginners use to catch small fish for food
*Big fishing net, used by more advanced fishers to catch larger sea creatures
*Drift net, used in Drift net fishing in the underwater area of Fossil Island
*Tiny net, used to obtain a pet fish in Catherby

label: Fishing pass
title: Fishing pass
lead:
The fishing pass is a quest item used only in Fishing Contest. It is obtained from Austri or Vestri upon starting the quest.

It is shown to Morris to enter the competition area each time.

label: Fishing Platform
title: Fishing Platform
lead: The Fishing Platform is located in the ocean due east of Witchaven. Players can travel here during and after the Sea Slug quest.

label: fishing potion
title: fishing potion
lead:
A Fishing potion is a potion made by using snape grass on an avantoe potion (unf), requiring 50 Herblore, yielding a Fishing potion(3) and 112.5 Herblore experience. A dose of Fishing potion provides a temporary skill boost to Fishing of +3. It can be stored in a tackle box.

After Barbarian Herblore Training, caviar can be added to a Fishing potion(2), requiring 53 Herblore, yielding a Fishing mix and 38 Herblore experience. A Fishing mix has 2 doses, boosts Fishing by 3, and heals 6 Hitpoints.

label: Fishing rod
title: Fishing rod
lead:
The fishing rod is an item used to catch fish through the Fishing skill. It can be bought from various fishing shops. To use a fishing rod, one will need fishing bait (except sandworms for anglerfish) to catch fish. It can be bought from fishing stores for 5 coins. There is also a fishing rod spawn in a house on south-eastern side of Entrana.

The equipable version of the fishing rod, the pearl fishing rod, can be bought with molch pearls from Alry the Angler.

label: fishing shops
title: fishing shops
lead: Fishing shops are a type of store found throughout RuneScape. The stores are represented by a . Fishing shops sell fishing equipment, fishing bait, feathers, and raw fish.

label: Fishing spot (big net, harpoon)
title: Fishing spot (big net, harpoon)
lead: Fishing spots can be found throughout Gielinor typically along coastal areas. They can be fished for raw mackerel, raw cod, raw bass, big bass, raw shark, and big shark. There are also non-fish items such as casket, leather boots, leather gloves, oyster, and seaweed.

label: Fishing spot (cage, harpoon)
title: Fishing spot (cage, harpoon)
lead: Fishing spots can be found throughout Gielinor typically at coastal areas or docks. They can be fished at with lobster pots or harpoons for raw lobster, raw tuna, raw swordfish or Big Swordfish depending on the tool used.

label: Fishing spot (Hemenster)
title: Fishing spot (Hemenster)
lead: Fishing spots can be found in Hemenster during the Fishing Contest quest. These spots are used to catch a raw giant carp.

label: Fishing spot (lava eel)
title: Fishing spot (lava eel)
lead: Fishing spots can be found in three locations. These spots are used to fish Lava eels which are primarily used for the completion of the Heroes' Quest.

label: Fishing spot (small net, bait)
title: Fishing spot (small net, bait)
lead: The fishing spot with small net and bait options is commonly found in many fishing locations. Fish can be caught at them with either a small net or a fishing rod and bait.

label: Fishing spot (Tutorial Island)
title: Fishing spot (Tutorial Island)
lead: Fishing spots can be found on Tutorial Island. These spots are used to introduce the player to fishing and only shrimps can be caught.

label: fishing spots
title: fishing spots
lead: There are several different types of fishing spots in Old School RuneScape. The most common types are 'Net/Bait', 'Lure/Bait', 'Cage/Harpoon', and 'Net/Harpoon'. Most fishing spots take a minimum of 250 ticks (2.5 minutes) to move, and a maximum of 530 ticks (around 5 minutes) . There are some exceptions: fishing spots for Karambwan, the big net spot in Civitas illa Fortis, and the Dark Crab spots in the Wilderness Resource Area never move, fishing spots for Sacred eel and Infernal eel move between 100 ticks (1 minute) and 300 ticks (3 minutes), and fishing spots for Anglerfish move between 8 ticks (5 seconds) and 830 ticks (8.3 minutes).

label: Fishing Trawler
title: Fishing Trawler
lead:
Fishing Trawler is a Fishing minigame run by Murphy in Port Khazard. It can be played at any level, but 15 Fishing is required to receive any rewards. To play, board Murphy's trawling boat and work to prevent it from sinking for 5 minutes as it trawls the sea.

It can be played solo or in small groups for higher non-unique rewards (and therefore higher Fishing experience), but it is slightly faster and much more relaxed to obtain the angler's outfit working with others, especially on the official Fishing Trawler worlds.

label: Fishing trophy
title: Fishing trophy
lead:
The fishing trophy is a quest item used only in Fishing Contest. It is obtained from Bonzo after catching a raw giant carp.

It is given to either Austri or Vestri to complete the quest.

label: Fishing/Experience table
title: Fishing/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Fishing in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Fishing level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: fissure
title: fissure
lead:
The fissure entrance to the temple of Ah Za Rhoon in Karamja is revealed by using a spade on the mound of earth during the Shilo Village quest.

Once revealed, a lit torch or candle can be used on it to drop it into the fissure to see that is a large drop and to find an anchor point for a rope. Once a rope is used on it and attached, the fissure can be searched to crawl through the hole and down below into the temple.

label: Flagpole
title: Flagpole
lead: Flagpoles are scenery objects found in various towns and cities throughout Gielinor. Players cannot interact with these flagpoles, but they can examine them.

label: Flags
title: Flags
lead: The flag is a core boat part, used in shipbuilding as a cosmetic for the player's boat. The flags can be created with 4 oak logs, 1 rope and a fabric roll obtained from achieving the Marlin rank at various Barracuda Trials. The fabric rolls are not consumed upon construction of the flag.

label: Flail
title: Flail
lead:
Flail may refer to:

*Blisterwood flail, an enhanced version of Ivandis flail
*Ivandis flail, a weapon used in A Taste of Hope
*Verac's flail, a two-handed flail comprising part of Verac the Defiled's set
*Viggora's chainmace, a Wilderness weapon charged with revenant ether

label: Flail Upgrade
title: Flail Upgrade
lead:
The Flail Upgrade is a one-handed melee weapon to be created during The Blood Moon Rises quest using the remnants of a blisterwood flail.

This flail requires an Attack level of 50 to wield, and gives a 25% damage and accuracy bonus against vampyres. Compared to the blisterwood flail, it changes from a crush weapon to a slash weapon, loses some of its defensive bonuses, and keeps the same special attack, but attacks faster, has a more potent special effect, and gains a little Prayer and Magic bonuses.

label: Flame pit (interface item)
title: Flame pit (interface item)
lead:
The Flame pit is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Flame pit.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Flames of Lloigh-enn
title: Flames of Lloigh-enn
lead:
The flames of Lloigh-enn are a legendary barrier between dimensions created at some point in the ancient past, and are primarily featured on the login screen of Old School RuneScape. In Issue 23 of the God letters, Zamorak discussed their use and history. The flames of Lloigh-enn (a pun on the word "login") are the pair of torches players can see on the login screen. They allow the player to journey to Gielinor if they recite their unique "spell" for access (i.e. their username and password).

Obviously, the real flames of Lloigh-enn do not appear in-game. However, look-alikes of the braziers (or at least their top halves) can be found flanking the staircase that leads into and out of the crypt beneath the White Knights' Castle in Falador. Look-alikes can also be found in the Old School Museum, and were present in the Falador Party Room during the 2018 Birthday event.

label: Flames of Zamorak
title: Flames of Zamorak
lead:
Flames of Zamorak is a combat spell in the standard spellbook, requiring 60 Magic and the completion of Mage Arena I to cast. In addition, players must also be wielding a Zamorak staff, staff of the dead, Thammaron's sceptre (a), accursed sceptre (a), or toxic staff of the dead; all except the Zamorak staff are able to autocast the spell.

Initially, the spell can only be cast within the Mage Arena against the battle mages. Upon casting the spell 100 times (regardless of whether it was a successful hit or not), the spell becomes usable outside the arena.

label: Flash
title: Flash
lead:
Flash may refer to:

* Flash powder
* Prayer Flash
* The flash chat effects

label: Flash Mob
title: Flash Mob
lead:
The Flash Mob is an angry mob that appears on Entrana during the Enlightened Journey quest.

According to Auguste, the Flash Mob was placed on Gielinor by the gods to ensure that technology never advanced too far. During the quest, the flash mob destroys the players' origami balloon because they fear it is too advanced. However, the factuality of this is doubtful as they are not seen anywhere else, and was most likely just a joke by Jagex.

label: Flat armour
title: Flat armour
lead:
Flat armour is a stat which modifies the damage a target receives from successful melee and ranged attacks, through subtracting the flat armour value from the attack's final damage roll. For example, if a target has 4 flat armour then an attack that would usually deal 10 damage would instead deal 6. Negative flat armour values will increase the damage a target receives, but again this only affects successful attacks. Attacks that miss will still deal 0 damage.

Flat armour primarily affects the player's standard attacks, and does not affect other sources of damage such as:
* Thralls
* Poison or venom
* Burn effects
* Recoil effects, like Vengeance and rings of recoil
* Poison dynamite

label: Flat rock
title: Flat rock
lead:
Flat rocks are an obstacle that can be found within Underground Pass dungeon. During the Underground Pass quest, players must use a plank on the flat rocks in order to traverse the obstacle and reach the orb of lights. A set of flat rocks are also encountered further into the dungeon.

The plank remains in the player's inventory after use, eliminating the need to pick it up again or have multiple planks.

label: Flat rock (trap)
title: Flat rock (trap)
lead: A flat rock is a trap that can be found within the Underground Pass dungeon. Players will encounter the trap during the Underground Pass quest whilst collecting the four orbs of light. Players must first search the flat rock to disarm the trap before taking the orb of light on top of it. It is possible to fail disarming the trap, triggering a swinging log, which can damage 6 to 13 Hitpoints.

label: Flatpack
title: Flatpack
lead:
Flatpacks are pre-packaged furniture built with the Construction skill on a workbench in the Workshop of a player-owned house. Flatpacks allow players to install the furniture inside their player-owned house without the necessary level required to build the furniture from scratch. A hammer and Saw are required to install flatpacked furniture. An example would be a level 42 builder adding a Costume Room to their house and using an oak toy box flatpack on a Toy box space. No experience is received when using a flatpack on a building hotspot.

Flatpack items can be created with building mode either on or off. A hammer and a saw are needed in your inventory to create flatpack items, and they are always created un-noted. Each flatpack takes 8 game ticks (4.8 seconds) to create. Creating flatpacks still requires the same amount of materials needed to construct the furniture at the hotspot. The advantage of making flatpack items is that there is no need to enter building mode or remove any furniture from a hotspot to create them, although players must still enter building mode and remove existing furniture from a hotspot before using a flatpack on the empty hotspot.

label: Flatpak Jones
title: Flatpak Jones
lead: Flatpak Jones is the CEO of the Karamja Box Company, who replied to a letter in the 8th Postbag from the Hedge. His name is a reference to flatpacks, used in Construction.

label: Flax
title: Flax
lead:
Flax is a resource that can be picked from plants in various locations around Gielinor. Multiple can be collected from the same plant. Flax can also be harvested from a hops patch after planting flax seeds with 18 Farming.

It is used to make bow strings at a spinning wheel, requiring 10 Crafting, yielding 15 Crafting experience. Flax can also be spun via the Spin Flax Lunar spell. It is also used to spin linen yarn or as payment to protect hemp plants (x6). Linen yarn can be used to build a linen trawling net or woven into bolts of linen, which can be used to upgrade masts and sails on a player's boat.

label: Flax (plant)
title: Flax (plant)
lead:
Flax plants can be picked to obtain flax, which can then be spun into bowstrings and linen yarn. There are six flax fields where many flax plants are located, in addition to many isolated plants.

There is a 3/16 (18.75%) chance that flax will disappear when picked, after which the plant will respawn after 10 game ticks (6 seconds).

label: Flax field
title: Flax field
lead:
A flax field is a location where many flax plants are located together. Each of these spots has a random number of flax, and a flax spot disappears when all the flax in that spot is picked. They reappear later after approximately five seconds in the same spot. They can be picked by members, and may then be spun into bow strings. This gives 15 Crafting experience.

Currently, there are six flax fields located in Gielinor.

label: Fletching
title: Fletching
lead:
Fletching is a skill which allows the player to create various types of ranged weapons and their ammunition. The products of this skill are primarily used in the combat skill, Ranged. It also provides some of the most popular materials used for High Alchemy, which is a commonly used method for training the Magic skill.

At a higher Fletching level, the skill can be trained without losing any coins, although a decent amount of working capital is very useful. Money can usually be generated at higher Fletching levels. Alternatively, it can be extremely fast with more expensive methods.

label: Flighted ogre arrow
title: Flighted ogre arrow
lead:
Flighted ogre arrows are made by using a knife on achey logs to make ogre arrow shafts, and then using 4 feathers per arrow shaft made. Doing so requires level 5 Fletching, granting 0.9 Fletching experience per flighted arrow.

Adding wolfbone arrowtips makes ogre arrows, while adding nails with a hammer will make brutal arrows instead.

label: Flinching
title: Flinching
lead:
.]]
Flinching (also hit-and-run or hit-and-hide) is a combat tactic that entails attacking an opponent while it is out of combat and going to a safespot before the monster can retaliate. The player then waits while making sure the opponent does not attack until it is "out of combat" again. Usually, this is when its health bar disappears from the screen. After this, the cycle can be repeated until the opponent is dead.

label: Flour (unobtainable item)
title: Flour (unobtainable item)
lead:
Flour was an item that could be obtained by killing black knights in RuneScape Classic. It could not normally be picked up, and players were intended to use a pot on it in order to obtain a pot of flour. However, it was possible to obtain the heap of flour by casting Telekinetic Grab. Upon the release of RuneScape 2, knights were changed to drop a regular pot of flour instead, initially making it one of the rarest discontinued items in the game.

Flour was inadvertently made obtainable again with the release of Player-owned Houses, as the Teak larder gave this item instead due to an oversight. Since it was useless in cooking, players could only bake by dropping the flour and picking it up with a pot.

label: Flower (original scenery)
title: Flower (original scenery)
lead: Flowers are a common form of scenery decoration found all throughout Gielinor, with these being the most common having over 1200 collectively logged individual flowers.

label: flower patch
title: flower patch
lead:
A flower patch is a type of patch used in the Farming skill to place scarecrows or to grow different kinds of flowers. With the exception of woad and limpwurt plants, flowers and scarecrows placed in this patch offer some degree of protection from disease over nearby allotment patches.

Flower patches are usually found alongside allotment patches, except for the allotment patch on Harmony Island and the flower patch in Kastori.

label: Fluffs' kitten
title: Fluffs' kitten
lead:
Fluffs' kitten is a quest item used only in Gertrude's Cat. It is found in one of the mewing crates in the Lumber Yard.

The kitten must be used on Fluffs to progress. If the player drop the kitten, it will become an NPC and run off into crates again, forcing the player to search for it again.

label: Flute Salad
title: Flute Salad
lead:
Flute Salad is a music track that is unlocked when the player first arrives in Lumbridge. It can also be heard around the Lumbridge Swamp and farmlands. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Autumn Voyage, Book of Spells, Dream, Harmony, and Yesteryear.

In Classic mode, the track plays around Mill Lane Mill and Fred the Farmer's house.

label: Fly fishing rod
title: Fly fishing rod
lead:
A fly fishing rod can be used to fish trout, salmon (both with feathers), and rainbow fish (with stripy feathers). They can be bought from various fishing shops. Fly fishing rods are used at fishing spots with the lure option. Popular fishing spots include the Barbarian Village, the Grand Tree, and Shilo Village. Fly fishing rods use feathers as bait. Feathers are dropped frequently from chickens or purchased from fishing shops.

The equipable version of the fly fishing rod, the pearl fly fishing rod, can be bought with molch pearls from Alry the Angler.

label: Fly trap
title: Fly trap
lead:
A fly trap is a stationary, carnivorous plant found only on Karamja. Like undead trees, they can attack players next to them every 5 ticks for up to 2 damage. They cannot be attacked and inflict melee damage that can be prevented with Protect from Melee.

Their stats are: 15 Attack, 15 Strength, 30 Defence, 100 Hitpoints with 45 crush defence, 30 stab defence, and 8 slash defence.

label: Flyer
title: Flyer
lead:
A flyer is a virtually useless item that, when examined, advertises Bob's Brilliant Axes. It is one of the possible required items that must be traded for a Kelda seed in the Forgettable Tale... quest. Additionally, it is one of the items that can be requested by Gunslik or the rowdy dwarf when doing Keldagrim tasks.

It can be dropped by barbarians and imps or obtained as a reward from a mystery box from the Quiz Master random event. Talking to men or women has a 1/128 chance of being offered a flyer.

label: Flying (attribute)
title: Flying (attribute)
lead: Flying is an attribute assigned to monsters that are immune to melee damage except for polearms.

label: Flying Horse Inn
title: Flying Horse Inn
lead:
The Flying Horse Inn is a bar found north of Ardougne Castle, in the north-western part of East Ardougne. The bartender sells beer to thirsty adventurers for two coins per pint, and there are several small rooms to rest in upstairs (though these are non-functional).

Lucien can be found around the inn; he serves as the start point of the Temple of Ikov quest. Two-pints can also be found at the inn, where she acts as the taskmaster for the Ardougne Diary.

label: Flynn
title: Flynn
lead:
Flynn is the owner of the Flynn's Mace Market in Falador.

His shop is located between the barbershop and the general store which is just west of Falador's town square. He sells bronze, iron, steel, mithril, and adamant maces.

label: Flynn's Mace Market.
title: Flynn's Mace Market.
lead: Flynn's Mace Market is a mace shop owned by Flynn in Falador. It is located between the Falador General Store and the Hairdresser in the north-western part of the city.

label: flypaper
title: flypaper
lead: Flypaper can be taken from sacks in the gardening shed on the west end of Sinclair Mansion. It is used during the Murder Mystery quest to lift fingerprints from a number of silver items that belong to the people suspected of committing the murder of Lord Sinclair.

label: food
title: food
lead:
Food is a type of item primarily used to restore the player's Hitpoints, though some foods may have other effects. Food can be obtained through the Cooking skill, as a drop from certain monsters, from some random events such as the Sandwich lady, from other players, or from non-player characters. There are also foods which can be grown with the Farming skill or found in some farm areas such as potatoes, cabbages, and onions. Lastly, there are holiday food items such as pumpkins and easter eggs. It is not advised to eat one of these holiday items due to their low availability and high price.

There are many different kinds of food, such as fish and meat, bread, cakes, pies, and pizza. Some food items, such as pies and pizzas, have two or more "bites" or "slices" meaning they can be eaten multiple times.

label: Food pot (scenery)
title: Food pot (scenery)
lead:
Food pots are decorative scenery found throughout Varlamore. They have no interaction options and cannot be searched.

A specific searchable food pot found in the Hunter Guild is used in an easy clue.

label: Food shops
title: Food shops
lead: Food shops are a type of shop throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Food shops sell a variety of foods, drinks, and other related items. There are 19 Food shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Food Store
title: Food Store
lead:
The Food Store, operated by Wydin, sells a variety of fresh food, and is located in Port Sarim. It plays a notable role in the Pirate's Treasure quest - it is the drop off point between Karamja and Asgarnia to find the otherwise illegal beverage Karamjan rum, after smuggling it from Karamja.

Starting the quest is not required to access the store. However, to access the back room of the store, the player must have progressed far enough into the quest and be wearing a white apron (which can be taken from the Fishing shop to the north). The back room contains various crates: a crate of cabbages, crate of potatoes, crates of raw chicken, and a crate of bananas.

label: Food trough (Clock Tower)
title: Food trough (Clock Tower)
lead:
Food trough is a part of the Clock Tower quest, and is located in Clock Tower Dungeon, inside the room with dungeon rats.

During the quest, in order to obtain the white cog, the player has to put rat poison inside the food trough. After doing so, the rats inside the room will eat from the trough and die, after which the player will find the gate guarding the white cog unhinged.

label: Food Trough (Troll Stronghold)
title: Food Trough (Troll Stronghold)
lead: The Food Trough is located in the Mountain goat pen in the Burntmeat's Troll kitchen, in the Troll Stronghold.

label: Food/Fast foods
title: Food/Fast foods
lead: Fast foods refer to a subtype of food that incur non-standard attack or eating delays when they are consumed. This means you may be able to eat them faster, or attack more quickly after eating one than you could with standard foods.

Forbidden is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness and also plays in Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, the track could be unlocked near the Wilderness ditch, north of the Lumber Yard.

label: Forcae
title: Forcae
lead: Forcae is a dragonkin who is thought to have created lower tier metal dragons (bronze, iron, steel and mithril). He is mentioned in some of Zorgoth's notes as the first to inject dragon eggs with metals, leading Zorgoth to do the same, in turn creating adamant and rune dragons. He is also mentioned at a shrine found in the northern portion of the Wyvern Cave. Examining the shrine will state "Forcae castil draekeun. Ortha lokur. Lith kletter ortha lokur. Draekeun fia Lithkren." This can be roughly translated as "Forcae combine dragon. First steel. Superior green first steel. Dragon safe from Lithkren." He is also mentioned in the Lithkren vault notes.

label: Foreman
title: Foreman
lead:
The foreman looks after the Ship Yard on Karamja. He can be found walking around on the southern tip of the docks.

During The Grand Tree, players need to either talk to him or kill him to get the lumber order. His combat level is 23. If the player decides to talk to him, he will ask three questions to which players must answer correctly to proceed.

label: Forester's Arms
title: Forester's Arms
lead:
Forester's Arms is the tavern in Seers' Village. The place is featured in the Bar Crawl, selling a Liverbane Ale for 18 coins; the ale temporarily lowers Attack, Defence, Fletching, Firemaking and Woodcutting by 6 levels, so don't plan to pursue those skills after running the Bar Crawl here. In addition to beer, the bartender sells meat pie for 16 coins and bowls of stew for 20 coins. These are good prices but there's a bit of dialogue to go through for each one bought, so it's rather slow if large quantities are wanted. Buying a bowl of stew is also an easy task for the Kandarin Diary.

The Poison salesman works his trade here; he features in the Murder Mystery and Fremennik trials quests. There are a number of NPCs (men and women) to train on.

label: Forestry outfit
title: Forestry outfit
lead:
The Forestry outfit is a cosmetic override for the Lumberjack outfit. Like the Lumberjack outfit, it is an experience-boosting clothing set that grants additional experience when worn while Woodcutting, but will not provide any additional experience bonus above the Lumberjack outfit. Equipping any piece of the outfit requires 44 Woodcutting.

Each piece equipped increases Woodcutting experience by 0.2-0.8% (depends on piece); wearing the complete set grants an additional set bonus of 0.5%, resulting in a total of 2.5% for the entire set. This does stack with the bonus 10% experience when cutting maples from the Kandarin Diary medium reward, as well as the bonus 10% experience when using a felling axe with Forester's rations in the player's Forestry kit. Pieces of the Lumberjack outfit will act as Forestry pieces for the purpose of obtaining the set bonus.

label: Fortis Colosseum/Strategies
title: Fortis Colosseum/Strategies
lead:
The Fortis Colosseum is a very difficult solo PvM challenge, being a spiritual successor of the Inferno. Players who are successful will be rewarded with Dizana's quiver.

Before attempting it, it is highly recommended that you have the best gear that you can afford and maxed or very high combat stats. However, completions are possible with inexpensive gear, though at least a bow of Faerdhinen with full crystal armour along with an abyssal tentacle is recommended for a first quiver. More importantly, do not expect to complete it on your first few attempts; be mentally prepared to fail a lot and learn from your mistakes.

lead:
Fortress may refer to:

** Black Knights' Fortress, a quest

* Dark Warriors' Fortress, a castle in levels 14, 15 and 16 multi-combat Wilderness north of Falador.

* Zamorak's Fortress, a God chamber in the God Wars Dungeon containing K'ril Tsutsaroth, Balfrug Kreeyath, Tstanon Karlak, and Zakl'n Gritch

label: Forum moderator
title: Forum moderator
lead:
A Forum Moderator was a regular player selected by Jagex staff to enforce and promote the community on the RuneScape Forums. As of 2017, there were around 60 Forum Moderators; ; this number had dropped down to around 30 in 2024, just before the removal of the Forums. Forum Moderators had a green glow around their posts and green avatar background when they commented on the Forums; they had no powers in-game and received no further benefits. Other types of moderators include Player Moderators and Jagex Moderators.

If a player was selected to become a Forum Moderator, they would be notified only via a message in their account inbox. Forum Moderators were chosen primarily on the quality (not quantity) of their posts. When selected, new Forum Moderators were subject to a training period; many applicants did not pass this period. There was also a section of the RuneScape Forums that could only be accessed by Forum Moderators and Jagex Moderators.

label: Fossil Island fossil
title: Fossil Island fossil
lead: Fossils are items on Fossil Island that are used to build displays on the bottom floor of the Varrock Museum (below the natural history floor). Completing a display requires a complete set of one type of fossil (i.e. small/medium/large) and grants 2 Kudos and an experience lamp based on the type of category of the fossils. They can be sold to the Fossil Collector in exchange for numulites, or used on the mycelium pool to create enriched bones which can be further processed to eventually gain some Prayer experience.

label: Fossil island wyvern (interface item)
title: Fossil island wyvern (interface item)
lead:
The Fossil island wyvern is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Fossil island wyvern.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Fountain
title: Fountain
lead:
Fountains are decorative scenery that can be found throughout Gielinor. Players may use various containers on them, such as buckets, vials, or waterskins in order to fill them with water. They are usually indicated on the map by a symbol.

While the vast majority of fountains have the common appearance, some towns and cities have different styled fountains. A unique golden fountain can be found in the Ratcatchers Mansion, that has an identical appearance to the Fountain of Heroes.

label: Fountain (disambiguation)
title: Fountain (disambiguation)
lead:
Fountains are decorative scenery that can be found throughout Gielinor.

Fountain may also refer to:
* Fountain (Aldarin), at the centre of the island
* Fountain (Darkmeyer), found around the city
* Fountain (Draynor Manor), used in the Ernest the Chicken quest

label: Fountain (Draynor Manor)
title: Fountain (Draynor Manor)
lead:
Fountain is used in Ernest the Chicken quest, and is located outside Draynor Manor in the south-west corner.

During the quest, a pressure gauge can be found inside the fountain. However, it is guarded by piranhas that are inside the fountain, and in order to obtain the pressure gauge players must kill the piranhas by using poisoned fish food on the fountain.

label: Fountain (witch's house)
title: Fountain (witch's house)
lead: A fountain can be found in the garden of the witch's house. During the quest, players must search this fountain in order to find the key to the witch's shed. Unlike other fountains, it cannot be used as a water source.

label: Fountain of Heroes
title: Fountain of Heroes
lead:
The Fountain of Heroes is a magical fountain found in a small side passage of the Heroes' Guild, downstairs inside the mine, near the runite ore rocks.

Using an amulet of glory on the fountain will cause all unnoted amulets of glory that players have in their inventory or equipped on their character to be recharged to an amulet of glory (4). Amulets can be recharged even if they are not completely depleted.

label: Fourth Age
title: Fourth Age
lead: The Fourth Age, also known as The Age of Mortals, was when the surviving races began to rebuild and flourish amongst the world. Heroes from this age include Arrav and Camorra, both of whom have a statue in the Heroes' Guild. The age lasted for around 2,000 years.

label: Fourth wall
title: Fourth wall
lead: In a traditional theatre, the "fourth wall" is the imaginary "wall" at the front of the stage, through which the audience sees the action of the play. In video games, television, etc., speaking directly to or otherwise acknowledging the audience/player or real world can be referred to as "breaking the fourth wall," as it "deconstructs" the boundaries of the fictional world.

label: Fragment Hunt
title: Fragment Hunt
lead:
Fragment Hunt is a special event with clues being on the Old School RuneScape Twitter in December 2021, with each clue eventually leading to a name of a Fragment in the upcoming Shattered Relics League.

The first person to @JagexSarnie on Twitter, with #FragmentHunt and solve the name wins 6 months of Membership. This was confirmed solved by Jagex in their day 5 tweet on 22 December 2021, at 12:00 PM.

Frags are the equivalent of seeds for farming coral at the Coral Nurseries off the coast of The Great Conch. The types of frags are:
