label: Franizzard Van Lumbcook
title: Franizzard Van Lumbcook
lead:
Franizzard Van Lumbcook is a famous ancestor of the current Cook of Lumbridge Castle. He served as an assistant to the Culinaromancer (who worked as a cook in the Lumbridge Castle for the then Duke) and helped prepare a banquet one hundred years ago for the Lumbridge Secret Council.

During the banquet, the Culinaromancer threatened the attendees of the banquet with death. Franizzard foiled the Culinaromancer's plan and trapped him in another dimension. As a result of his action, Franizzard was offered a job for life as head cook of Lumbridge Castle, for himself and all his descendants.

label: Frank
title: Frank
lead:
Frank Sinclair is one of Lord Sinclair's children. He is one of the suspects during the Murder Mystery quest. Frank is not involved in King's Ransom.

According to the Gossip, he is a chronic gambler and in order to cover his debts, Frank has stolen and sold a couple of his father's rare paintings.

label: Frank's barrel
title: Frank's barrel
lead: Frank's barrel can be found inside the Sinclair Mansion in Frank's bedroom. During the Murder Mystery quest, the player must search the barrel to find his silver pot.

label: Frank's print
title: Frank's print
lead: Frank's print is a quest item in the Murder Mystery quest. It is created by using flypaper on the silver pot after dusting it with a pot of flour. If the prints match those of the unknown print, it will become a killer's print, meaning Frank is the killer.

label: Fred Parks
title: Fred Parks
lead: Fred Parks was a resident of Varrock during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. According to the Varrock Census of that year, he was retired. He is the husband of Elsie Parks, who calls him "Freddie".

label: Fred the Farmer
title: Fred the Farmer
lead:
Fred the Farmer is an agriculturalist that features in the Sheep Shearer, One Small Favour, and Cold War quests. Players can find Fred at the farmhouse north-west of Lumbridge, south of the windmill and to the west of the Lumbridge sheep pen. His farm is where you can find onions, which can be hard to find, especially for non-members.

If the player talks to him and says that they have seen the "Thing" (which is actually just two penguins), he will start to go on about grabbing chickens and running to the hills. In the end, the player will say that it is two penguins disguised as a sheep. He will ask if the player is feeling alright.

label: Fred's farm
title: Fred's farm
lead: Fred's farm, also known as the Lumbridge farm, is a large farm in Lumbridge found north of the Lumbridge Castle. The farm is owned by Fred the Farmer, and is worked by Fred and several farmers.

label: Free-to-play
title: Free-to-play
lead:
. Pay-to-play areas and activities in red. [ Full resolution image].]]

Free-to-play, also known as F2P, is the free version of Old School RuneScape where no payment to Jagex is required to play. Players who play the free version are known as "Free players", "F2Pers", or "Non-members". This is in contrast to members, who pay a fee for access to a much larger map and a multitude of skills, items, quests, and activities that are unavailable to free-to-play users.

label: Free-to-play account builds
title: Free-to-play account builds
lead: This article lists the major account builds followed by players restricted to the free-to-play game mode.

label: Free-to-play combat pure guide
title: Free-to-play combat pure guide
lead: Free-to-play combat pures are accounts designed to excel in player versus player combat. They are often created with the specific goal of engaging in player versus player activities in the free-to-play worlds. To gain an advantage in their respective combat level brackets, training of these accounts is often focused on the offensive skills, maximising the damage output at the cost of sacrificing the defensive capabilities.

label: Free-to-play combat pure training
title: Free-to-play combat pure training
lead:
This article describes how to effectively train combat skills of the so-called free-to-play combat pures, or accounts suitable for free-to-play PvP.

While many optimal training methods are only available for members, this guide assumes that the accounts are mostly trained in the free-to-play worlds.

label: Free-to-play cosmetic items
title: Free-to-play cosmetic items
lead:
The following article lists cosmetic items equipable on Free-to-play worlds that are tradeable or contain combat bonuses. Note that unfinished items (such as Emerald amulet or Unblessed symbol), as well as quest- and skill-related items (such as tiaras, Chef's hat or Brown apron) are not included. Rings and arrows were also omitted, since they cannot be seen on the character model.

An item is considered cosmetic if it has no combat bonuses and is used only for its looks, or if it is a rarer reskinned variation of an item (e.g. gold-trimmed armour). Cosmetic items usually offer no or very small advantages over the original items, but they can be much more expensive due to their rarity. Note that untradeable items without combat bonuses were excluded from this list.

label: Free-to-play Crafting training
title: Free-to-play Crafting training
lead: This guide outlines the best methods and alternative options for training the Crafting skill in free-to-play.

label: Free-to-play Fishing training
title: Free-to-play Fishing training
lead: There are several ways to train Fishing in free-to-play. Depending on the desired goals of the player, they can choose between methods favouring experience rates or profit. If you choose to go with making a profit, be sure to sell your catch at the Grand Exchange and not a General store in order to maximize your profits. Keep in mind, since the Grand Exchange acts as an in-game stock market, that means the prices are always changing. You can find the latest prices on the Grand Exchange here.

label: Free-to-play Hitpoints training
title: Free-to-play Hitpoints training
lead:
Hitpoints is almost always trained through combat with any of the combat styles, melee, ranged, or magic. The ratio of combat experience to hitpoint experience is 3:1 for melee and ranged. For magic it is dependent on the spell being used, the magic defence of the target, and the attack style used. Skill pures, also known as skillers, can train Hitpoints with experience lamps to avoid combat, the only way to do so in free-to-play.

* Melee training
* Magic training
* Ranged training

label: Free-to-play Ironman guide
title: Free-to-play Ironman guide
lead:
This article contains information on free-to-play Standard Ironman, Hardcore Ironman and Ultimate Ironman Mode training, all of which differ significantly from normal skill training.

Group ironmen and hardcore group ironmen can take advantage of training together in various ways such as collecting resources from one training method for another teammate's training session for faster experience. Hardcore group ironmen share lives with the number of players in the group and may take risks that solo hardcore ironmen may not take but hardcore group ironmen should be cautious doing what would be safe-death activities as their lives are not protected from safe deaths.

label: Free-to-play Magic training
title: Free-to-play Magic training
lead: Magic is a useful skill in Old School RuneScape, and especially in free to play, because there is no access to magic tablets, so many teleports are only available by levelling Magic.

label: Free-to-play melee training
title: Free-to-play melee training
lead:
This article provides information about effective ways to train Attack, Strength, Defence, and Hitpoints through melee combat in free-to-play.

This guide is organised into sections based on skill levels. For example, if the section header is Levels 20 to 30, you should begin training at the area with an Attack and Strength level of at least 20. Defence is also preferred to be at that level, but is not always required. The solution to lower Defence is to bring more food, or use food that heals more.

label: Free-to-play Mining training
title: Free-to-play Mining training
lead: This guide outlines the best methods for training the Mining skill in free-to-play. Even though mining runite ore with 85 Mining is one of the fastest free-to-play money making methods, profit from lower level ores is very low so it is more efficient to drop mined ores when training and use the saved time for other money making methods.

label: Free-to-play Prayer training
title: Free-to-play Prayer training
lead: Prayer is regarded to be the most difficult skill to train in free-to-play due to the expense involved in purchasing large numbers of remains from the Grand Exchange, low experience rates, and the high amount of clicking required to train the skill.

label: Free-to-play PvP
title: Free-to-play PvP
lead: This article serves as an overview of the free-to-play guides on player-versus-player activities, account builds, and other related topics.

label: Free-to-play PvP culture
title: Free-to-play PvP culture
lead: This article aims to document various parts of the free-to-play player-versus-player culture, including practices and behaviours, common locations and hot spots, as well as the used slang.

label: Free-to-play PvP equipment
title: Free-to-play PvP equipment
lead: This article describes the items commonly used in player-versus-player combat in the free-to-play worlds, including detailed comparisons of available equipment, as well as common inventory setups.

label: Free-to-play PvP techniques
title: Free-to-play PvP techniques
lead: Free-to-play player-versus-player combat involves applying certain techniques to improve the chances of a successful knockout or the likelihood of survival. They are commonly used in both 1-vs-1 combat and multicombat by combat pures and other player killers alike. This article aims to be an overview of these methods.

label: Free-to-play Ranged training
title: Free-to-play Ranged training
lead:
Ranged in the free-to-play worlds, while having less equipment and features than in member's worlds, provides some fun with the ability to battle monsters and players who would otherwise be out of reach.

This guide will provide advice for the equipment, attack style, and training locations to use to maximise Ranged experience gained in free-to-play.

label: Free-to-play Runecraft training
title: Free-to-play Runecraft training
lead:
When crafting runes at a runic altar, it is a good idea to wear the corresponding tiara in your head slot. This acts as an equipable talisman, saving an inventory space over a normal talisman. It also allows the player to enter a particular runic altar by left-clicking on the corresponding mysterious ruins, as opposed to having to use the talisman on them, thereby saving time. Talisman tiaras may be purchased from the Grand Exchange, from other players, or crafted by a player themselves. To create a talisman tiara, the player must have a plain tiara and the corresponding talisman in their inventory, and use the tiara on the altar of that particular talisman. For example, a player who wishes to create an air tiara must enter the Air Altar ruins, and use the tiara on the altar with an air talisman in their inventory. The talisman itself is lost in the process.

All runes craftable by free-to-play RuneScape players may be crafted from either rune essence, pure essence or Runecrafting cores. Body cores give the most experience, but they are very hard to obtain in large quantities. To obtain enough, one needs to spend most of their combat training by killing Body Golems.

label: Free-to-play Smithing training
title: Free-to-play Smithing training
lead: This guide outlines the best methods for training the Smithing skill in free-to-play. There are a few ways to profit with Smithing in free-to-play, such as smelting bars or making rune equipment, however it is more beneficial to simply perform the fastest experience methods and use the saved time to make money from alternative methods.

label: Free-to-play transportation
title: Free-to-play transportation
lead: This article lists and describes all free-to-play transportation methods that allow to quickly travel between available areas.

label: Free-to-play Woodcutting training
title: Free-to-play Woodcutting training
lead: This guide outlines the best methods for training the Woodcutting skill in free-to-play.

label: Fremennik
title: Fremennik
lead:
The Fremennik are a group of humans who live primarily in the Fremennik Province, in northern Gielinor. All humans across Gielinor originated from the Fremennik.

They are not one unified group, but rather several different groups that have split-off over time. These groups tend to fight with each other as well as amongst themselves, often for trivial reasons. The Fremennik are also in conflict with the magical Moon Clan of Lunar Isle, because of a difference of opinion when it comes to Runecrafting. The Fremennik do not approve of the crafting of runes, and think that humans should only use the runes they were given by the gods. The tension between the two clans is lessened during the Lunar Diplomacy quest.

label: Fremennik armour
title: Fremennik armour
lead: Fremennik armour includes several types of armour that are obtained within the Fremennik Province. There are several different categories of Fremennik armour, focused around the different combat styles.

label: Fremennik citizen
title: Fremennik citizen
lead:
Fremennik citizens are citizens of Rellekka that can be talked to as well as pickpocketed. They can only be pickpocketed after completion of The Fremennik Trials and require level 45 Thieving to do so. A successful pickpocket yields 40 coins and 65 Thieving experience. If you are caught pickpocketing a Fremennik citizen, they say a number of different things, including "You have betrayed your heritage," or "You shame us." If you are caught, they will sometimes address you with your Fremennik name.

Most citizens are found in the marketplace of Rellekka, west of the long hall.

label: Fremennik name
title: Fremennik name
lead:
Fremennik names are given to the player at the end of The Fremennik Trials quest, this is a form of in-game Title. The name is used to call the players while they are in Rellekka, Lunar Isle, Mountain Camp, Miscellania, and Etceteria (except if previously crowned), Neitiznot, Jatizso, and Waterbirth Island. Using the power of the ring of charos (a), players may ask Brundt the Chieftain for the Fremennik name to be changed. Doing so yields a new random name for that player.

Names are not gender-specific, and are generated by using one of 16 different prefixes and one of 16 different suffixes, for a total of 256 different Fremennik names that can be given to the player. Wearing certain equipment or completing The Fremennik Exiles will add a title to the player's Fremennik name.

label: Fremennik-style wood
title: Fremennik-style wood
lead:
Fremennik-style wood is a House style option for a player-owned house.

When level 30 Construction is reached, this can be chosen as a house template for Player-owned house.

label: Fremennik ring icons
title: Fremennik ring icons
lead:
The Fremennik ring icons can be created from the Fremennik rings with a chisel, 80 Crafting and completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire.

After learning the process from Peer the Seer, the icons can be combined with the corresponding Ancient vestige, dropped by Duke Sucellus, The Leviathan, The Whisperer or Vardorvis, to create Ancient icons, part of the Ancient rings.

label: Fremennik rings
title: Fremennik rings
lead:
The Fremennik rings provide offensive and defensive bonuses corresponding to their respective combat styles.

They are obtained from the Dagannoth Kings, found on the deepest level of the Waterbirth Island Dungeon. Dagannoth Rex drops the Berserker and Warrior melee rings, Dagannoth Prime drops the Seers ring, and Dagannoth Supreme drops the Archers ring.

label: Fremennik sea boots
title: Fremennik sea boots
lead:
Fremennik sea boots is a reward from completing parts of the Fremennik Diary. There are four types, depending on which part of the diary the player has completed. Those are:

*Fremennik sea boots 1, from the easy tasks set
*Fremennik sea boots 2, from the medium tasks set
*Fremennik sea boots 3, from the hard tasks set
*Fremennik sea boots 4, from the elite tasks set

label: Fremennik warband
title: Fremennik warband
lead:
The Fremennik warband is a trio of enemies that spawn in during the Fortis Colosseum. Its members include:

Attacking a warband member with the style they are weakest to will always result in a successful hit and will deal your maximum hit against them.

label: Freneskae
title: Freneskae
lead:
Freneskae (or Frenaskrae) is a mysterious plane of existence from which the Mahjarrat are believed to have originated. According to the Wise Old Man, very little else is known about the realm.

During the Kharidian–Zarosian War, when Icthlarin and Amascut were seeking allies to turn the tide against the armies of the Zarosian Empire, they travelled to the home of the Mahjarrat (presumably Freneskae) and brought them to Gielinor, where they were known as Icthlarin's Stern Judges.

label: Frenita
title: Frenita
lead: Frenita runs Frenita's Cookery Shop in Yanille. She sells various cooking utensils and some ingredients for advanced recipes such as cakes and pies. Her shop also houses a range, a sink and a churn.

label: Frenita's Cookery Shop.
title: Frenita's Cookery Shop.
lead: Frenita's Cookery Shop is a Cooking shop in Yanille run by Frenita. There is also a range, sink, and churn inside the building and dairy cows just north of Yanille.

label: Fresh Start Worlds
title: Fresh Start Worlds
lead:
Fresh Start Worlds was a seasonal event that started on 19 October 2022 and ended on 18 April 2023. It ran on a separate set of servers than the standard worlds, requiring a new account that did not play Old School RuneScape before. Both free-to-play players and members could play on Fresh Start Worlds.

Unlike the RuneScape counterpart, Fresh Start Worlds did not feature any increased experience rates, in-game buffs, or rewards. They did however feature "Achievement Points", earned through completing quests, bossing, achievement diaries, or clue scrolls. These points were solely to help keep players motivated and were not redeemable for anything.

label: Friar Twiblick
title: Friar Twiblick
lead:
Friar Twiblick came from Taverley and was one of the seven priestly warriors who fought against the Morytanian hordes at Silvarea.

He is described in The Sleeping Seven as "A devout man of worship whose brave talks and uncommon speeches raised the spirits and abilities of men above that of mortals so they fought as though Guthix himself were at their side, redressing the balance that 'his-dark-self' has spoilt."

label: Friends List
title: Friends List
lead:
The Friends List tab can be used to send private messages to other players, and to see which worlds they are currently on. If a player's private chat is set to 'off', then they will always appear as offline and it will not be possible to send them a private message. If their private chat is set to 'friends', then only people on their Friends List will be able to send them private messages. The Ignore List can be accessed here by clicking on the red sad face on the top right of the tab.

To add a player to your Friends List, click the 'Add Friend' button in the Friends List interface, type the player's display name, and press enter or simply right-click their name in the chat box and select 'Add friend'. To delete a friend from the friend list, either right-click their name on the friend list and click 'Delete', or click the 'Del Friend' button, type their name and press enter. The Friends List in Old School RuneScape can hold up to 200 names for free-to-play players, and 400 names for members.

label: Frincos
title: Frincos
lead: Frincos is a monk who runs Frincos' Fabulous Herb Store on south-western Entrana. His shop sells Herblore supplies such as eyes of newt and vials, as well as packs of them.

label: Frincos' Fabulous Herb Store.
title: Frincos' Fabulous Herb Store.
lead: Frincos' Fabulous Herb Store is a Herblore shop on Entrana. Frincos sells eyes of newt and vials both individually and in packs. He also sells pestle and mortars. His shop contains a sink and two vial respawns. The shop is also next to a hops patch.

label: Frog (disambiguation)
title: Frog (disambiguation)
lead: Frog may refer to any of the following:

label: Frog-leather armour
title: Frog-leather armour
lead:
Frog-leather armour (also known as Frog-skin armour) is a Ranged armour made by the Dorgeshuun goblins. Frog-leather armour is members-only, and players must have level 25 Ranged and level 25 Defence. This armour is bought from Reldak in Dorgesh-Kaan.

Although they are not a particularly war-like race, the Dorgeshuun see the value of their skills and are not completely against fashioning armour to fit the humans that come to visit their city.

label: Frost dragon/Strategies
title: Frost dragon/Strategies
lead:
With Sailing, Frost dragons can be fought within the Grimstone Dungeon.

They may be assigned as a Slayer task by Nieve/Steve or Duradel/Kuradal. Being on task increases the drop rate of dragon metal sheets from 1/200 to 1/55.

label: Frostenhorn
title: Frostenhorn
lead:
The Frostenhorn is a magical artefact that amplified power to "unimaginable levels". During the Second Age, it was possessed by the Zarosian Empire and located in their capital, Senntisten.

During the God Wars, it disappeared from Senntisten, around the same time that Azzanadra, the Pontifex Maximus of the Zarosian Empire, was imprisoned by Saradominist and Zamorakian forces. It eventually made its way to Ghorrock Prison, sometime before the Fifth Age. During the quest Desert Treasure II, the artefact is destroyed by Sliske, disguised as an assassin.

label: Frozen key
title: Frozen key
lead:
Frozen key may refer to:

* Frozen key (The Fremennik Trials), an item used during The Fremennik Trials quest.
* Frozen key (The Frozen Door), an item used during The Frozen Door miniquest.

label: Frozen key piece
title: Frozen key piece
lead:
Frozen key piece may refer to:

* Frozen key piece (armadyl)
* Frozen key piece (bandos)
* Frozen key piece (saradomin)
* Frozen key piece (zamorak)

label: Frozen Waste Plateau
title: Frozen Waste Plateau
lead:
The Frozen Waste Plateau, also known as Ice Plateau (or historically Ghorrock), is located in the north-west corner of the Wilderness. The area spans both free-to-play and members areas. It contains ice giants and ice warriors in the free-to-play area. In the member's area, ice spiders can also be found. There are also spawns of water runes and cosmic runes.

Notably, three runite rocks can be found in the members' only area of the plateau.

label: fruit
title: fruit
lead:
Fruit refers to a variety of food. Players can eat some fruits to regain hitpoints, or use them as ingredients in other food items with the Cooking skill.

Members can grow some fruits with the Farming skill, often in a fruit tree patch. However, most berries are grown in a bush patch, and some fruits are grown in allotments.

label: Fruit batta
title: Fruit batta
lead:
A fruit batta is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 11 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade fuit battas are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 120 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a fruit batta via gnome cooking with 25 Cooking, yielding 150 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Fruit blast
title: Fruit blast
lead:
A fruit blast is a type of drink that restores 9 Hitpoints when consumed. It can be obtained by mixing 1 pineapple, 1 orange, and 1 lemon. You must then finish the cocktail by adding lemon slices as a garnish, requiring level 6 Cooking to complete. To create the cocktail, click "Mix-cocktail" on a cocktail shaker. All ingredients and tools can be bought from Funch's Fine Groceries just east of the Blurberry Bar.

Ashes can be added to a fruit blast to create a dirty blast, which is a requirement for the first part of Recipe for Disaster.

label: fruit tree patch
title: fruit tree patch
lead:
Fruit tree patches are Farming patches used to grow fruit-bearing trees. There are a total of 7 Fruit tree patches currently. Growing fruit trees are somewhat different to other plants, in that there is an intermediate growing stage where the seed must be grown into a sapling before being planted into a cleared fruit tree patch.

The necessary seeds to grow them can be obtained from bird nests, drops from monsters, farming contracts, or by other means. Sources of seeds may be found in the Farming skill guide.

label: Fruit tree sapling
title: Fruit tree sapling
lead: Refers to any fruit tree sapling grown in a fruit tree patch through the Farming skill.

label: Fruit tree seedling
title: Fruit tree seedling
lead:
Fruit tree seedling may refer to:

* Apple seedling
* Banana seedling
* Orange seedling
* Curry seedling
* Pineapple seedling
* Papaya seedling
* Palm seedling
* Dragonfruit seedling

label: Fukong Interactive Entertainment
title: Fukong Interactive Entertainment
lead:
Shanghai Fukong Interactive Entertainment (chinese: 富控互动 ), previously known as Zhongji Holding , is a venture capital firm that started in June 2016 and bought all investments from Insight Venture partners, The Raine Group and Spectrum Venture partners for a 100% stake in Jagex for $300,000,000 USD.

It was formed by employees of Shandong Hongda who originally put forward the intent to buyout all stakes in Jagex for $300,000,000 USD in April 2016.

label: Ful
title: Ful
lead:
Ful is the likely name of the deity served by the Tasakaal, whose instructions they await.

The only mention of the name "Ful" in Old School RuneScape is in the name of the song Ful to the Brim, which plays inside the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon.

label: Full fishing net
title: Full fishing net
lead: Full fishing nets are mainly found in Port Sarim. They can also be found in the ports of Brimhaven, Fishing Guild, Corsair Cove, Lunar Isle, and Fishing Hamlet.

label: full helmet
title: full helmet
lead:
A Full helmet is armour worn in the headwear slot. Full helmets are stronger than medium helmets, providing a higher defence bonus, and are used primarily by warriors. The helmets, as with all melee-oriented gear, give good defence against ranged attacks, but are weak against magic.

Full helms are heavier than medium helmets, some full helmets and their trimmed parts do have plumes. Trimmed and gold-trimmed armours have grey and gold plumes respectively, and the god helmets have plume colours representing the god to which they are aligned.

label: Fun weapons
title: Fun weapons
lead:
Fun weapons are wieldable objects that are intended for fun use and have negative bonuses. There is a restriction in legacy duels within the Emir's Arena that can be set so only fun weapons may be used in the fight. Fun weapons are generally released for holiday rewards, as the point of the holiday events are for entertainment, without a reward that would give advantages to participants as opposed to non-participants. Some fun items such as Diango's claws are not equipable and as such aren't really considered a weapon.

The Cursed goblin hammer, Hunting knife, Nutcracker staff, and Skis cannot be used as fun weapons in the Emir's Arena legacy duels.

label: Funch's Fine Groceries
title: Funch's Fine Groceries
lead: Funch's Fine Groceries is a shop owned by Heckel Funch in the Grand Tree. It sells items needed for Gnome cooking. The store is located on the east side of the Grand Tree's , east of Blurberry's Bar.

label: Fungi
title: Fungi
lead:
Fungi may refer to:
*Zygomite in their fungi form
*Ancient Zygomite in their ancient fungi form
*Mort myre fungus
*Mushroom
*Fungicide
*Fungicide spray
*Fungi (scenery), found mainly on Fossil Island

label: Fungus
title: Fungus
lead: Fungus may refer to any of the following:

label: Fungus (common)
title: Fungus (common)
lead: Fungus is a common scenery decoration found in many places all across Gielinor.

label: Fungus covered Cavern wall
title: Fungus covered Cavern wall
lead:
Fungus covered Cavern walls are located within the Pothole Dungeon on Karamja, and can be searched for a Grimy rogue's purse. In the Jungle Potion quest, these walls must be searched for a rogue's purse, as Trufitus will not accept one obtained as a drop. Players must be told by Trufitus about where to find rogue's purse first, or else searching the walls will yield nothing.

After the rogue's purse has been picked, the wall becomes a Fungus pattern and cannot be picked from again until it turns back after about 100 ticks, or 60 seconds.

label: Fur (disambiguation)
title: Fur (disambiguation)
lead: Fur may refer to:

label: Fur pouch
title: Fur pouch
lead:
Fur pouch may refer to:
* Small fur pouch, which can store up to 14 pieces of fur from hunter creatures
* Medium fur pouch, which can store up to 21 pieces of fur from hunter creatures
* Large fur pouch, which can store up to 28 pieces of fur from hunter creatures

label: Fur stall
title: Fur stall
lead:
A fur stall is a stall that requires 35 Thieving to loot and grants 45 experience. Successfully looting a fur stall will give the player a piece of grey wolf fur. The thievable stalls are located in Ardougne, Rellekka, and Civitas illa Fortis.

In Civitas Illa Fortis, players can safely steal from the stall by luring Molossus (the dog) to the west-side corner of the stall. This prevents the guards from attacking the player as the guards will be blocked by Molossus.

label: Fur stall (disambiguation)
title: Fur stall (disambiguation)
lead:
Fur stall may refer to:
* Fur stall, the Thieving stall
* Fur stall (Port Roberts), the Thieving stall in Port Roberts
* Fur stall (Varrock), the decorative stall run by Baraek
* Fur stall (The Fremennik Exiles), a non-thievable variant of the Rellekka stall
* Fur stall (Sophanem), an unused decorative stall

label: Fur stall (Varrock)
title: Fur stall (Varrock)
lead: Fur stall is a decorative stall found in Varrock Square near Baraek. Unlike other fur stalls, the stall in Varrock cannot be stolen from.

label: Fur trader (East Ardougne)
title: Fur trader (East Ardougne)
lead:
The Fur trader runs the Ardougne Fur Stall. in the East Ardougne market. If stock is stolen from his stall, he refuses to do business for 10 minutes. He buys bear furs for 3 coins each.

He appears alongside other residents of East Ardougne in the Ratcatchers mansion.

label: Fur traders
title: Fur traders
lead: Fur traders are a type of store found in Old School RuneScape. The stores are represented by an icon. Fur traders buy and sell different types of furs.

label: furnace
title: furnace
lead:
A furnace is an interactive scenery object primarily used in Smithing to smelt various ores into metal bars. Furnaces around Gielinor are identified with the furnace icon on the world map and minimap.

Furnaces are also used for Crafting from metal bars. With the appropriate mould in their inventory and the required Crafting level, players can use the furnace to craft gold or silver bars into jewellery such as rings or holy symbols, assuming they have the appropriate mould in their inventory and the required Crafting level. Players may also make molten glass by smelting soda ash and a bucket of sand.

label: Furnace (Elemental Workshop)
title: Furnace (Elemental Workshop)
lead:
The furnace found in the elemental workshop near the fire elementals is used to melt elemental ore into elemental metal during the Elemental Workshop I and Elemental Workshop II quests.

For the furnace to work properly, the bellows and Water wheel need to be working as well.

label: Furnace (Viyeldi caves)
title: Furnace (Viyeldi caves)
lead: A Furnace can be found in the Viyeldi caves. During the Legends' Quest the player must use the lump, hunk, and chunk of crystal on it, in order to combine them into a Heart crystal which can then be activated by using it on the mossy rock.

label: Fycie
title: Fycie
lead: Fycie is the daughter of Rantz. She has a brother named Bugs. She lives in Rantz's Cave, and sells feathers during Big Chompy Bird Hunting. In Recipe for Disaster, both Fycie and her brother Bugs use the ogre boat ride to get to Karamja. During some Treasure Trails, she has to be talked to. When doing so, she says 'Human done good!', and gives you your next clue, or the reward. One method of getting to her is to take a fairy ring to and running east.

label: Gaffit Malore
title: Gaffit Malore
lead: Gaffit Malore was a resident of Varrock during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. According to the Varrock Census of that year, he was a librarian. He may be related to Mabel Malore.

label: Gaius
title: Gaius
lead: Gaius is a male non-player character who is located in Taverley. He owns a shop called Gaius' Two-Handed Shop, which sells two-handed swords.

label: Gaius' Two Handed Shop.
title: Gaius' Two Handed Shop.
lead: Gaius' Two Handed Shop is a shop in Taverley owned by Gaius that has a variety of two-handed swords ranging from bronze to adamant. This store does not sell the rune or dragon two-handed sword. It can be used as an easy source for the adamant two-handed sword needed for a hard emote clue scroll.

label: Galahad
title: Galahad
lead:
Brother Galahad was formerly a knight of King Arthur's Round Table and one of the three achievers of the Holy Grail. He now lives in a house west of McGrubor's Wood and does not mind somebody stopping by to talk to once and a while, stating that it is rare that this happens. During the conversation he may give players a cup of tea.

During the Holy Grail quest, he will give the player the holy table napkin which is used to get the magic whistle in Draynor Manor. The whistle is used to go to the Fisher Realm. The alternative to go to Fisher Realm is by use of the fairy ring code . Letting him make you a cup of tea is a task in the Kandarin Easy Achievement Diary.

label: Galarpos Mountains
title: Galarpos Mountains
lead:
The Galarpos Mountains are part of a mountain range in Western Kandarin and Eastern Tirannwn, which separates Tirannwn from the rest of the mainland. For a long time, the mountains were largely thought to be impassable. The only routes available past the mountains are either through the Underground Pass or through the Arandar mountain pass.

Arposandra, translating in ancient gnomish to "Rock City", is located somewhere beneath the mountain range.

label: game client
title: game client
lead:
There are several game clients, both official and unofficial, that are allowed for playing Old School RuneScape.

The official clients are:
* The Official Client, a conversion of the legacy java client, originally released on the gaming platform, and now also available on the Jagex Launcher.
* Old School RuneScape Mobile, the client for Android and iOS.

label: Game controls
title: Game controls
lead: Game controls are mostly mouse driven, with occasional use of the keyboard. Familiarity with the game interface should be achieved during the introduction at Tutorial Island. Controls can be configured in Settings.

label: Game Integrity updates
title: Game Integrity updates
lead:
s now requires partial completion of the quest Eagles' Peak. As with many game integrity changes, this was intended to combat botting.]]
Game Integrity updates or balancing changes are unpolled permanent changes to Old School RuneScape that are introduced to the game in order to combat rule-breaking or change elements of gameplay that are considered unfair or counterproductive to the game's long-term health. Apart from holiday events, bug fixes, and minor quality of life changes, game integrity updates are the only updates not voted on by players and cannot be vetoed by the community. However, they are sometimes announced ahead of time by Jagex to take community feedback on effective ways to combat the problem without impacting the game negatively for legitimate players.

Often, these unpolled updates were either perceived by the development team to be unlikely to pass a community poll or had already failed one. For example, the anti-dragon shield being gated behind the start of Dragon Slayer I failed a poll before being introduced as a game integrity update.

label: Game Intro 1
title: Game Intro 1
lead:
"Game Intro 1" was the filename of an unused music track that could be previously found in the cache. Its name suggests it would have played on the title screen, but was replaced by Scape Original instead. It was removed from the game files on 26 September 2019.

The track has a copyright date of 2003 rather than the usual 2003-04, as it was not updated when the Music Player was released.

label: Game Jam
title: Game Jam
lead:
Game Jams are semiannual events hosted by Jagex where Jagex Moderators develop content prototypes to workshop potential new additions to the game. These events were a replacement for the ideation days that Jagex Moderators previously had.

Projects developed during a Game Jam are only concepts; they will not necessarily be polled or even added to the game at all.

label: Game Jam I
title: Game Jam I
lead:
Game Jam I was a Game Jam that took place during the week of 4 April 2022, and the first of a now bi-annual tradition.

Most of the projects were listed in the April 2022 Gielinor Gazette, and discussed during a livestream event on 12 May 2022.

label: Game Jam II
title: Game Jam II
lead:
Game Jam II was a Game Jam that took place during the week of 31 October 2022.

Most of the projects were listed in the November 2022 Gielinor Gazette.

label: Game Jam III
title: Game Jam III
lead:
Game Jam III was a Game Jam that took place during the week of 24 April 2023.

Most of the projects were listed in a dedicated post.

label: Game Jam IV
title: Game Jam IV
lead:
Game Jam IV was a Game Jam that took place between 2 October 2023 and 12 October 2023.

Notably, the jam's theme was "Sailing", as the Sailing skill had been in development during the time the jam took place.

label: Game Jam V
title: Game Jam V

Game Jam V was a Game Jam that took place between 22 April 2024 and 6 May 2024.

Most of the projects were listed in a dedicated post.

label: Game Jam VI

Game Jam VI was a Game Jam that took place between 21 October 2024 and 1 November 2024.

Most of the projects were listed in a dedicated post.

label: Game Jam VII

lead:
Game Jam VII was a Game Jam that took place at the beginning of 2026.

Most of the projects were listed in a dedicated post.

label: Game Requirements
title: Game Requirements
lead: To be able to play Old School RuneScape, we recommend having the following:

label: Game square
title: Game square
lead:
Game squares, also known as tiles, spaces, or steps are the basic unit of area that divide the Old School RuneScape overworld. The game squares form a grid, dictating where objects may be. All objects' locations will be defined by a single square. All locations and sizes can only be integer numbers.

Every entity on the overworld occupies at least one game square. Players and dropped items occupy one square. Larger monsters, such as the King Black Dragon occupy multiple squares. For these larger monsters, their location is defined by the south-westernmost square they occupy. This is the location used by most calculations, such as where items drop.

label: Game tick
title: Game tick
lead:
The game tick, also known as the server cycle, is the fundamental unit of time used in Old School RuneScape, equal to 0.6 seconds. All actions that require server processing are governed by this value. Purely client-side actions, such as opening a right-click menu or switching interface tabs, are processed separately with a 20 millisecond tick rate.

Each action registered within one tick will start to take place by the beginning of the next tick. This can cause your action to be carried out instantaneously, or after a delay of nearly 0.6 seconds, depending on how long you had to wait until the next tick.

label: Game updates
title: Game updates
lead:
Game updates are updates which generally affect gameplay by adding extra content (quests, minigames, etc.) or small to large changes of existing gameplay elements.
Game updates occur on Wednesdays at 11:30 AM (in British time) and have no downtime, unless noted otherwise prior to the update.

label: Games
title: Games
lead:
Games may refer to:

* Games necklace
* Minigames
* The [ Runescape] games.
* Games room

label: Gang
title: Gang
lead: Gang may refer to:

label: gangplank
title: gangplank
lead: Gangplanks are scenery used to cross on and off of boats. Gangplanks can be found at most docks and have an option to cross onto nearby boats. In most cases travelling by boat is activated by talking to a nearby NPC, and crossing the gangplank isn't necessary.

label: Gaol
title: Gaol
lead: Gaol is a music track that is unlocked either in Gu'Tanoth or in the Skavid caves. Prior to the track's removal from an area north of the Bandit Camp in the Wilderness in 2021, this track was accessible to free-to-play players.

label: Gap
title: Gap
lead:
Gap may refer to:

* The distance in which a player killer or bounty hunter is too far away to attack someone with Ranged or Magic (i.e. The player or victim who cannot be attacked in this situation is said to have "gap" over the attacker.)
* The hole in a bridge inside Gu'Tanoth

label: Gap (Gu'Tanoth)
title: Gap (Gu'Tanoth)
lead:
The gap is a hole in a bridge inside Gu'Tanoth. Partial completion of the Watchtower quest along with a rock cake is necessary to access this bridge for the first time. Jumping the gap from the south will grant the player 5 experience in Agility at the cost of coins each time. Level 25 Agility is required to do so. No experience is awarded when jumping the gap in the opposite direction.

While players no longer will have to bribe the ogre guards at the second checkpoint with a rock cake on subsequent visits to Gu'Tanoth, jumping back over the gap after having crossed it will reset the player's payment status, leading the guards to demand another bribe the following visit. However, if the player teleports out rather than jump back across, they will not be prompted to pay a bribe on their next attempt to cross the bridge. It is possible that this behaviour is the result of a misconception when the ogre city was converted from RuneScape Classic.

label: Garagorshuun
title: Garagorshuun
lead:
The Garagorshuun are a goblin tribe that live in Goblin Village and wear green goblin mail. In the Goblin Diplomacy quest, players make peace between the Garagorshuun and the Thorobshuun.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Goblins of the Sea".

label: Garak
title: Garak
lead:
Garak was a dragonkin who was known to have destroyed a number of small settlements near the border of the Wilderness during the Dragonkin Conflicts in the Fourth Age. A common misconception exists in which Garak was a particularly ferocious dragon; this is due to Archibald Malore's translations that standardised the poems describing it and being written as being a dragon.

Camorra Shayzien, then a little-known heroine, slayed Garak, and it is this act that subsequently placed her among the most famous heroes of the period, such as Arrav and Robert the Strong.

label: Garb
title: Garb
lead:
Garb may refer to:
*Clue hunter garb, the body part of the clue hunter outfit
*Pyromancer garb, the body part of the pyromancer outfit.
*Garbek quo Maten

label: Garden (disambiguation)
title: Garden (disambiguation)
lead: Garden may refer to:

label: Garden (music track)
title: Garden (music track)
lead:
Garden is a music track that can be unlocked inside Varrock city walls, excluding the Grand Exchange. It also plays in the Phoenix Gang Hideout and in the basement of the Blue Moon Inn. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Adventure, Medieval, and Spirit. This track was one of the first released in RuneScape.

In Classic mode, this track plays in the centre of Varrock and in the basement of the Blue Moon Inn.

label: Garden fence (interface item)
title: Garden fence (interface item)
lead:
The Garden fence is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Garden fence.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Garlic
title: Garlic
lead: Garlic is an item used in several quests. Although it cannot be eaten on its own, it is used in Cooking in making Spicy sauce and in Herblore in making Guthix balance potions.

label: Garv
title: Garv
lead: Garv guards Scarface Pete's mansion in Brimhaven. Only players who are aligned with the Black Arm Gang can infiltrate this hideout by disguising themself as Hartigen via black knight's armour and Id papers from Trobert, which is done during the Heroes' Quest.

label: Gas mask
title: Gas mask
lead:
The gas mask is a quest item used in Plague City and Biohazard. It is made by giving dwellberries to Alrena in East Ardougne. The mask is required to be worn to enter West Ardougne before completion of Biohazard. Gas masks are also dropped by the mourners who are present in Mourning's End Part I.

Gas masks serve as a way to protect player from damage in the Smokey Dungeon and Smoke Devil Dungeon. The mask also reduces damage from the clouds whilst sulphur mining in Lovakengj, and prevents infection from Nex's virus attack, which makes them useful even after their intended quest use.

label: Gate
title: Gate
lead: Gate may refer to:

label: Gate (Al Kharid)
title: Gate (Al Kharid)
lead: The Al Kharid gate is the gate between Lumbridge and Al Kharid. Four border guards are guarding the gate, two on each side.

label: Gate (Ardougne Sewers)
title: Gate (Ardougne Sewers)
lead: The gates in the Ardougne Sewers block the path to the Ardougne Sewers mine and the Rat Pits. Unlocking the gate requires level 31 Thieving and grants 25 experience.

label: Gate (Biohazard)
title: Gate (Biohazard)
lead: Gates can be found on the of the Mourner Headquarters in West Ardougne. The gates are locked and require a key that is automatically obtained after killing the Mourner positioned outside the gates. During the Biohazard quest, players must access the storeroom behind the gates in order to obtain a distillator from one of the crates.

label: Gate (Desert Mining Camp)
title: Gate (Desert Mining Camp)
lead: The gate is the entrance to the Desert Mining Camp. Players must have the metal key in their inventory to open the gate. The metal key is obtained in the Tourist Trap quest by fighting the Mercenary Captain. Players can also search the gate to find out more information about the Desert Mining Camp.

label: Gate (Secrets of the North)
title: Gate (Secrets of the North)
lead:
Gate (Secrets of the North) may refer to:

* Gate (Secrets of the North, unlocked), the gates unlocked at all times
* Gate (Secrets of the North, assassin), the gate used to escape the Assassin fight
* Gate (Secrets of the North, direction lock), the northern gate with a direction puzzle lock
* Gate (Secrets of the North, word lock), the central gate with a word puzzle lock
* Gate (Secrets of the North, icy key), the south-west gate opened with the icy key
* Gate (Secrets of the North, open), the gate temporarily seen while walking through a solved puzzle gate
* Gate (Secrets of the North, completed), the open gates that replace the puzzle gates after completion of the quest

label: Gate (Ship Yard)
title: Gate (Ship Yard)
lead: A gate is the entrance to the Ship Yard. To pass through the gate, players must speak the password (Ka, Lu, Min) they learn during The Grand Tree quest. During the Monkey Madness I quest, the player must have a gnome royal seal to enter the Ship Yard. After completing the quest the gnome royal seal is no longer required.

label: Gate (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
title: Gate (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
lead: The gate is the entrance to the Tree Gnome Stronghold. Prior to partial completion of The Grand Tree quest, on the first time the player attempts to open the gate, Femi will ask for assistance to lift some boxes on to her cart. If the player helps load the boxes, she will smuggle the player in to the Tree Gnome Stronghold for free when they are stopped from entering during The Grand Tree. If she wasn't helped with loading her boxes, she will require a fee of 1,000 coins to be smuggled in during the quest. Players are freely allowed to enter the gate without interruption outside of that section of the quest once the initial dialogue is completed.

label: Gate (Underground Pass Shortcut)
title: Gate (Underground Pass Shortcut)
lead: Two gates are located in the Underground Pass that block the entrance and exit of a path around an obstacle maze. These gates can only be successfully unlocked with level 50 Thieving.

label: Gate (witch's house)
title: Gate (witch's house)
lead: The gate in the basement of the witch's house can only be opened with certain gloves. During the Witch's House quest, it must be passed in order to get the magnet from the cupboard. Without the correct gloves, attempting to open the gate will deal 20% of your current Hitpoints.

label: Gauntlets
title: Gauntlets
lead: These are the different types of gauntlets that players can wear in Old School RuneScape.

label: Gazebo (interface item)
title: Gazebo (interface item)
lead:
The Gazebo is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gazebo.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Gazulibird
title: Gazulibird
lead:
Gazulibirds were an avian species that once inhabited Gielinor but are now extinct. They are mentioned only in the fifth Postbag from the Hedge.

The Makeover Mage killed a nest of them, in which they found a yin yang amulet. It is from this amulet that their gender-altering powers are derived.

label: gem drop table
title: gem drop table
lead:
The gem drop table or GDT is a drop table that is accessed by monsters of all kinds. The table mainly drops gems and talismans. The rare drop table also has access to the gem drop table. The gem drop table also has a chance at rolling the Mega-rare drop table.

The Mega-rare drop table contains mostly empty drops, but also the rune spear, dragon spear and shield left half. The Legends' Quest must be completed to obtain one of the mega-rare drops. Wearing a ring of wealth will remove all empty slots from the table.

label: Gem drop table/Sources
title: Gem drop table/Sources
lead: The following is a list of monsters that directly access the gem drop table. Several more sources indirectly access this table via the rare drop table; that list can be found at Rare drop table/Sources.

label: Gem machete
title: Gem machete
lead:
Gem machete may refer to:

*Opal machete
*Jade machete
*Red topaz machete

label: Gem merchant
title: Gem merchant
lead:
The gem merchant runs the Ardougne Gem Stall. in East Ardougne. He sells sapphires, emeralds, rubies, and diamonds.

He appears alongside other residents of East Ardougne in the Ratcatchers mansion.

label: gem rocks
title: gem rocks
lead:
Gem rocks can be mined through the Mining skill. A Mining level of 40 is required to mine gem rocks, granting 65 Mining experience per gem.

Normal gem rocks can be mined in Shilo Village after a player has completed the Shilo Village quest, in the Lunar Isle mine after Lunar Diplomacy, or on The Onyx Crest after 47 Sailing. The rocks regenerate 99 ticks (59.4 seconds) after being mined. Wearing a charged amulet of glory triples the success rate of mining these gem rocks. There is also another kind of gem rock which randomly appears during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame with a 5% chance per event. These rocks can be mined three times before they despawn.

label: Gem shops
title: Gem shops
lead: Gem shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Gem shops sell gems. There are twelve gem shops in total throughout Old School RuneScape.

label: gem stall
title: gem stall
lead:
A gem stall is a stall, which may be stolen from at level 75 Thieving, granting 408 Thieving experience. There is a respawn time of 60 seconds.

Thieving from the Green Gemstone Gems stall is a requirement for the Fremennik Hard Diary.

label: Gem stall (Al Kharid)
title: Gem stall (Al Kharid)
lead: Gem stall is scenery found in northern Al Kharid near the Gem trader. Unlike standard gem stalls, the Al Kharid variant cannot be stolen from.

label: Gem stall (disambiguation)
title: Gem stall (disambiguation)
lead:
Gem stall may refer to:

* Gem stall, the thievable stalls.
* Gem stall (Port Roberts), the thievable stall in Port Roberts.
* Shop Counter (gems), the thievable stall in Mor Ul Rek.
* Gem stall (Al Kharid), the decorative stall in Al Kharid.
* Gem stall (Aldarin), decorative scenery in Aldarin.
* Gem stall (Sophanem), unused scenery intended for Sophanem.
* Gem stall (unused), unused scenery potentially intended for A Kingdom Divided.

label: Gem stall (unused)
title: Gem stall (unused)
lead: Gem stall is an unused variant of thievable gem stalls. The unused stall has no Steal-from option, but is otherwise identical to the standard thieving stall. It may have been intended to be shown during a cutscene in A Kingdom Divided.

label: Gem tipped bolts
title: Gem tipped bolts
lead:
Gem tipped bolts are heavy ranged ammunition used by crossbows, weapons used in ranged combat. They can be created by members through Fletching, by attaching bolt tips on bolts.

Attaching gem tips doesn't improve the stats of the bolt. Most players use the Enchant Crossbow Bolt spell on a gem tipped bolt to create an Enchanted bolt, a bolt with an additional special effect.

label: Gem trader
title: Gem trader
lead:
The gem trader runs the Gem Trader stall in Al Kharid. He buys and sells sapphires, emeralds, rubies, and diamonds and their uncut versions as well. His shop isn't frequently used by most players due to the predominance of the Grand Exchange, where sellers can receive more money for the gems, cut or uncut. However, it is popular with ironmen. In the Family Crest quest, he directs the player to Avan at the Al Kharid mine.

Prior to the release of the Grand Exchange pre-late 2007, it was common for the gem trader to have a fairly full stock on free-to-play worlds as his shop was the easiest way for newer players to sell their gems. Newer players were also able to make small profits by buying uncut gems from the gem trader, cutting them, then selling back for a higher price.

label: Gem Trader.
title: Gem Trader.
lead: Gem Trader is a gem shop run by the Gem trader in northern Al Kharid. It is a stall, but cannot be stolen from using the Thieving skill, unlike the gem stalls in Keldagrim, Ardougne, and Mor Ul Rek.

label: Gemelli twins
title: Gemelli twins
lead: The Gemelli twins are two penguins that are members of the Fettuccine Mafia, first mentioned in the 19th Postbag from the Hedge. Noodle explains that if the player asked the Gemelli twins about the funny way they talk, they would end up "eatin' wi' the fishes."

label: gems
title: gems
lead:
Gems are valuable stones that are primarily used in Crafting. They can be obtained from Mining (either randomly while mining other ores or from gem rocks), as a frequent drop from a wide range of monsters via part of the rare drop table or occasionally given out as gifts from various random events. Many types of gems can be purchased or sold (or stolen) at gem shops, identified with a red gem icon on the map ( ).

While mining most ore rocks or Motherlode Mine ore veins, players have a 1/256 chance of receiving a gem instead of an ore; this does not deplete the ore rock. Wearing a charged amulet of glory (of any number of charges other than 0) increases this chance to 1/86; wearing one while mining gem rocks increases the speed at which they are mined. It may be worth noting that the gems found randomly whilst mining most ores do not grant any additional Mining experience. Mining gems from gem rocks, however, does grant experience.

label: Gender
title: Gender
lead:
can change a player's gender (and skin colour) free of charge.]]
Gender refers to whether a character in RuneScape is male or female. Like race, it is an attribute that applies to all player characters and many non-player characters (NPCs). Gender in RuneScape is purely cosmetic and does not affect a player's skills or restrict their abilities in any way.

Prior to the August 14th 2024 update, a player would select a gender at character creation; this was replaced by body type and pronoun selection.

label: General
title: General
lead:
General may refer to:

*General stores

label: General Bentnoze
title: General Bentnoze
lead:
General Bentnoze is a member of the Thorobshuun tribe and one of the two goblin generals found in the northernmost part of Goblin Village. He plays a major role in the quest Goblin Diplomacy.

He is always found standing next to his rival general, General Wartface, whom he constantly argues with over armour colours. He favours the colour red while his opponent prefers the colour green.

label: General Bloodfist
title: General Bloodfist
lead:
General Bloodfist was the leader of the Dorgeshuun goblin tribe at one point during the God Wars. He was the goblin that led the Dorgeshuun from the control of Bandos.

Since Bandos had taken the goblins from the peaceful world of Yu'biusk, he had used them wastefully, forcing them to fight in battles they could not possibly win. Millions of goblins died in this way.

label: General Bonehelm
title: General Bonehelm
lead: General Bonehelm was the last of the Dorgeshuun tribe generals. He was the leader of the tribe until they voted to become a republic, but he refused to give up his power, resulting in a civil war between the military and republican factions. The military tribe was driven out of the city, and dug out a base in the nearby caves. His army attacked Dorgesh-Kaan again, but was again driven out. However, the mining had weakened the stone around the base, and the footsteps of the retreating army caused the tunnels to collapse on them, crushing the entire army.

label: General Graardor/Strategies
title: General Graardor/Strategies
lead:
This is a guide for killing General Graardor with Melee and Ranged. It has the basics of attacking and tanking, as well as providing a few examples of what equipment to bring.

Note that ranged is the most straightforward combat style to use for solo players, since with proper play it is possible to avoid all damage from Graardor. In teams, it is recommended to have one player tank with melee while the rest of the party uses either melee or ranged.

label: General Khazard
title: General Khazard
lead:
General Khazard, also known as Khazard, is the leader of the Khazard Army. He is a Zamorakian Mahjarrat, and the son of Palkeera. He has established a large territory between Ardougne and Yanille and is at war with the gnomes.

He may be fought during the Fight Arena quest after killing Bouncer, his pet hellhound, though it is not required. He is spoken to frequently during The General's Shadow and Secrets of the North.

label: general store
title: general store
lead: The general store is a type of shop placed in many locations in Gielinor. Unlike specialty shops, general stores usually accept all tradeable items, making them a useful place to sell miscellaneous goods that do not have a dedicated store. General stores are identified on the map by a pot icon. Many general stores have both a shop keeper and a shop assistant, both of which can be used to access the shop stock.

label: General Store (Canifis)
title: General Store (Canifis)
lead: The Canifis General Store is located in north-western Canifis and is owned by Fidelio. Its wares are double the price of other general stores, and it always offers to buy items at the lowest price (as if the store has a full stock of the item). However, unlike other stores, the Canifis General Store also sells needles and thread.

label: General Wartface
title: General Wartface
lead:
General Wartface is a member of the Garagorshuun tribe and one of the two goblin generals found in the northernmost building in Goblin Village. He plays a major role in the Goblin Diplomacy quest.

He is always found standing next to his rival general, General Bentnoze, whom he constantly argues with over armour colours. He favours the colour green while his opponent prefers the colour red.

label: General Wartface (historical)
title: General Wartface (historical)
lead: General Wartface is an unused historical variant of General Wartface that appeared during Goblin Diplomacy. Despite the historical variant being unused since the graphics were updated in 2006, the NPC model and data remains in the game cache. The old variant retains the old graphical style.

label: Genie
title: Genie
lead:
The Genie appears as a random event. The Genie appears near players and gives them an experience lamp, which may be rubbed to raise a selected skill's experience by 10 times the current level of the particular. For example, if the player has level 30 in Herblore, they would gain 300 Herblore experience if the skill is chosen.

The lamp is generally best used on skills that take longer to level up, such as Runecraft or Agility. Alternatively, they can be used for skills that are expensive to train, such as Construction.

label: Gentleman Mallard
title: Gentleman Mallard
lead: Gentleman Mallard is a famed privateer, first heard of when attempting to buy his rapier from Smith.

label: Gerald
title: Gerald
lead:
Gerald is a man wandering near the banks of the River Dougne, south of the massive chain of rapids known as Baxtorian Falls. Gerald appears to be a fisherman looking to harvest the native trout and salmon that make their home in the nearby stretch of water.

Gerald can be found very close to where a player will wash up if they attempt to traverse Baxtorian Falls' rapids without a rope. If spoken to, Gerald will discuss some of the area's tourist attractions. He also makes a brief mention of the legendary treasure said to have been left in the falls by the elven king Baxtorian some 200 years ago, in the late days of the Fourth Age. He says that, although many adventurers come searching for it, none have found any trace of Baxtorian's legendary tomb.

label: Gerrant
title: Gerrant
lead: Gerrant is the owner of Gerrant's Fishy Business in Port Sarim. He is seen wearing a white apron and toting a fishing pole around and he also wears a beige fishing hat. A white apron respawns in his shop. He sells feathers, fishing bait, fishing poles (bait and lure), harpoons, lobster pots, and all raw free-to-play fish. In the Heroes' Quest, Gerrant teaches the player how to make an oily fishing rod.

label: Gerrant's Fishy Business.
title: Gerrant's Fishy Business.
lead:
Gerrant's Fishy Business is located in Port Sarim. The shop sells Fishing supplies. It is run by Gerrant.

Near the back of the store there is a white apron respawn, potentially useful for those doing the Pirate's Treasure quest.

label: Gertrude
title: Gertrude
lead:
Gertrude Fairweather is a woman living in a house just west of Varrock. She is the starting point for both the Gertrude's Cat and Ratcatchers quests. She has four sons: Wilough, Shilop, Philop, and Kanel. Her husband, Walter Fairweather, is a travelling merchant, and is not present ingame.

Once your cat has become overgrown, she will sell you kittens for , but keep in mind you can only have one kitten at a time. When you have a normal cat in your inventory or in your bank, she won't give you a kitten. If you store your normal cats in your POH, she will sell you a new kitten. The colour of the kitten is random unless you have an activated ring of charos, then you will be able to charm Gertrude into letting you choose the colour of the kitten. Doing so the first time completes a medium Varrock Diary task.

label: Gertrude's Cat
title: Gertrude's Cat
lead: Gertrude's Cat is a short quest in which you have to find Fluffs, a lost pet cat owned by Gertrude. Completion of the quest allows you to adopt a feline companion of your very own.

label: Gertrude's cat (NPC)
title: Gertrude's cat (NPC)
lead:
Fluffs is a cat that belongs to Gertrude, and is the cat that a player must find for her within the Gertrude's Cat quest. After the quest has been completed, she can be seen in the Varrock Rat Pits or up the ladder in the Lumber Yard. According to Gertrude, she is the mother of all the kittens players can buy from her.

*If you have a cat or kitten within your bank and you talk to her it can lead to her scratching you, dealing 3 damage.
*If you use milk and fish (with the exception of cooked fish or tuna and trout) or any other type of food with Fluffs, she will eagerly devour it.
*If you speak to Fluffs while having a kitten/cat following you, they will briefly converse.

label: Ghommal's hilt
title: Ghommal's hilt
lead:
Ghommal's hilts are rewards from the Combat Achievements system obtained by speaking to Ghommal (or Laidee Gnonock after the completion of While Guthix Sleeps) at the Warriors' Guild entrance. If new tasks are introduced after a player has already obtained a certain upgrade for the hilt, even if they then have no longer completed enough points from tasks for the corresponding tier, they can keep that version of the hilt, but it will only provide the benefits of the highest tier the player has achieved, and it will also not be possible to obtain more of them until they have completed the newly introduced tasks.

The different upgrades of Ghommal's hilt are:

label: ghost
title: ghost
lead:
A ghost is an undead monster that is found in various places and dungeons. As they are undead, Crumble Undead and the salve amulet work well on them. Ghosts are rarely used for training, because they drop nothing in most locations.

Players must kill ghosts in Melzar's Maze to progress through a level of the maze. The ghosts in Melzar's Maze can be spoken to with a Ghostspeak amulet; their speech hints that they were victims of Elvarg the dragon.

label: Ghost's skull
title: Ghost's skull
lead:
The ghost's skull is a quest item used only in The Restless Ghost. It is found in the Wizards' Tower basement by searching the altar.

After searching the altar a skeleton will appear. Killing it is optional, and the player may run if desired. Putting the skull back into the restless ghost's coffin will complete the quest.

label: GPDT employee
title: GPDT employee
lead:
GPDT employees are, as suggested by their names, employees of the Gielinor Parcel Delivery Team, the only known postal service on Gielinor. They are involved with the Tribal Totem quest.

GPDT employees can be found south of the southern bank in East Ardougne.

label: Ghost (disambiguation)
title: Ghost (disambiguation)
lead:
Ghost may refer to:
*Ghost
