 titlematch = Ghost (%)
 category = Monsters | Non-player characters

label: Ghost (Grave of Scorpius)
title: Ghost (Grave of Scorpius)
lead: Several ghosts can be found near the Grave of Scorpius, where the Spirit of Scorpius can also be found. These ghosts can be talked to, even without wearing a ghostspeak amulet. Talking to them will cause them to say "We are waiting for you to join us.", and then attack the player.

label: Ghost (Melzar's Maze)
title: Ghost (Melzar's Maze)
lead:
A room full of ghosts can be found on the of Melzar's Maze. They must be killed in order to obtain the orange key, which can unlock the orange doors and progress through the maze.

The orange key is always dropped by the hooded ghost with no cape, and will never be dropped by the other ghosts.

label: Ghostly robes
title: Ghostly robes
lead:
Ghostly robes are a members-only set of magic armour that makes the wearer translucent, which can be obtained by speaking to various ghosts throughout Gielinor after a player has a ring of visibility from Desert Treasure I.

Speaking to the ghosts will start a miniquest, the Curse of the Empty Lord, in which each ghost will tell you their story, direct you on to the next ghost, and give you a piece of the ghostly robes set. To talk to the ghosts, a player must be wearing a ring of visibility, which is obtained during the Desert Treasure I quest, as well as a ghostspeak amulet, which is obtained during The Restless Ghost quest. Many of the ghosts are found in the Wilderness; locations will vary for each player.

label: Ghostly thrall
title: Ghostly thrall
lead:
Ghostly thrall may refer to one of the following:

* Lesser ghostly thrall
* Superior ghostly thrall
* Greater ghostly thrall

label: Ghostspeak amulet
title: Ghostspeak amulet
lead:
A ghostspeak amulet is an item worn in the neck slot that enables the wearer to talk to ghosts. Partial completion of The Restless Ghost is required to obtain the item, as it is given to players by Father Urhney in order to speak to the ghost haunting the Lumbridge graveyard during the quest. Normally players can only get one ghostspeak amulet as Father Urhney will not give an amulet to players who have one in their possession, although the drop trick can be used to obtain more.

An enchanted ghostspeak amulet is given to players by the old crone in order to control Necrovarus during the Ghosts Ahoy quest.

label: Gianne dough
title: Gianne dough
lead: Gianne dough is an ingredient in gnome cooking used to make gnomebowls, gnome crunchies, and gnome battas. It can be bought from Hudo in the Grand Tree. Gianne dough cannot be cooked by itself; instead, players must use the dough on a crunchy tray, batta tin, or gnomebowl mould and then precook it on a range. It was probably named after Aluft Gianne snr., the gnome cook. 100 Gianne dough is also given as a reward for completing the Gnome Restaurant training.

label: Gianne's cook book
title: Gianne's cook book
lead:
Gianne's cook book is a cook book written by Aluft Gianne. It is full of Gnome recipes, and useful for the Gnome Restaurant minigame, or if players want to make gnome foods for themselves.

The cook book can be obtained from Aluft Gianne himself, Hudo the nearby grocer, or from the bookcase in a player-owned house. The book will not be available in your bookcase until completing the cooking tutorial with Aluft Gianne snr.. It mentions Pukkamay, a great Gnome cook.

label: Gianne's Restaurant
title: Gianne's Restaurant
lead:
Gianne's Restaurant is a food store located on the west side of the of the Grand Tree, owned by Aluft Gianne snr. and operated by the Gnome Waiters. It sells premade gnome food, which cannot be used for the Gnome Restaurant minigame.

All food bought from the restaurant can be combo eaten. This mechanic is shared with the cooked karambwan.

label: giant
title: giant
lead: Giant may refer to:

label: Giant (race)
title: Giant (race)
lead:
Giants are a race of gigantic humanoid beings that reside in Gielinor. They are mostly aggressive, unintelligent, mute beings with mysterious origins. Five subgroups of giants are known to exist: hill giants, moss giants, ice giants, fire giants, and cloud giants. The one-eyed cyclopes form another potential subgroup. A few giants are referred to as 'titans', such as the Cloud Titan, the Royal Titans, Obor "the Hill Titan", and the Black Knight Titan.

It is not known whether the subgroups of giants have a common heritage, or whether they have separate histories. All giant subgroups seem to at least have some basic knowledge of using tools, weapons and armour, and they live in groups together, but there is very little indication that they currently form any kind of civilised society amongst themselves. They can be found in almost all kingdoms and continents.

label: Giant Anvil
title: Giant Anvil
lead:
Giant Anvil may refer to:
* Giant Anvil (Chambers of Xeric), the anvil in Tekton's room within the Chambers of Xeric
* Giant anvil (Giants' Plateau), a decorative anvil near the entrance to the Giants' Foundry on the Giants' Plateau

label: Giant bat
title: Giant bat
lead:
Giant bats are relatively low-level flying monsters found throughout dungeons and across the surface of Gielinor. Despite them being generally weak monsters they may sometimes pose a threat to players due to their aggressiveness toward any players level 54 or lower. Giant bats can be used as a slightly higher-level alternative for regular Bats for Slayer assignments.

Notably, the bats in Arceuus and around the Dark Altar are not aggressive to players, making it safe to traverse the area and craft runes at the nearby altars even at a low combat level.

label: Giant bat (disambiguation)
title: Giant bat (disambiguation)
lead:
Giant bat may refer to:

*Giant bat - the common monster
*Giant bat (Brine Rat Cavern) - giant bats with a unique appearance found in the Brine Rat Cavern
*Giant bat (Iban's Temple) - decorative NPCs flying near Iban's Temple in the Underground Pass
*Giant bat (Brimhaven Agility Arena) - decorative NPCs flying around the pillars of the Brimhaven Agility Arena

label: Giant bat (Iban's Temple)
title: Giant bat (Iban's Temple)
lead: Giant bats are decorative NPCs that fly around Iban's Temple in the final area of the Underground Pass. Unlike regular giant bats, these ones are not monsters and can not be attacked.

label: Giant bosses
title: Giant bosses
lead:
Giant bosses may refer to:
*Obor, the Hill giant boss.
*Bryophyta, the Moss giant boss.
*The Royal Titans, a duo encounter with Eldric and Branda, the Ice giant and Fire giant bosses.
* Giant Champion, requiring a Giant champion scroll

label: Giant carp
title: Giant carp
lead:
Giant carp are a type of fish that restores 6 Hitpoints when eaten. They can be obtained by cooking a raw giant carp on a fire or cooking range, giving no Cooking experience. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Giant carp is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 45, or 41 when using the Lumbridge range.

Raw giant carp can only be caught as part of the Fishing Contest quest before receiving the fishing trophy during the quest. Level 10 Fishing is required, along with a fishing rod and red vine worms for bait — the latter can be dug up in McGrubor's Wood with a spade.

label: Giant crystal
title: Giant crystal
lead:
Giant crystal is a large crystal that Merlin is trapped in. Merlin is freed from the crystal by the player during the Merlin's Crystal quest.

The crystal remains after the quest, and attempting to smash it again will give the message You have already freed Merlin from the giant crystal.

label: Giant eagle (interface item)
title: Giant eagle (interface item)
lead:
The Giant eagle is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the giant eagle.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Giant Mole/Strategies
title: Giant Mole/Strategies
lead: The Giant Mole is a fairly simple low-level boss that can be found under Falador. It is killed for its mole claw, mole skin and Baby mole drops.

label: giant rat
title: giant rat
lead:
Giant rats are common, low-levelled monsters. They can often be found in swamps and sewers, and are sometimes killed by low-levelled players training their Combat skills as they are weak and can be easily found around Lumbridge and Varrock.

One of two giant rats found near Damis during Desert Treasure I can be used to safespot him by luring Damis and the other aggressive monsters behind it, making the fight considerably easier.

label: Giant rat (Tutorial Island)
title: Giant rat (Tutorial Island)
lead:
Giant rats are a variant of giant rats used exclusively on Tutorial Island. They are the first monster a player will defeat in Old School RuneScape, as Vannaka will task them with defeating one.

Two variants of Tutorial Island giant rats exist in the cache but are not used in-game. Another variant was used for an alternate version of Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.

label: Giant skeleton
title: Giant skeleton
lead:
Giant skeleton may refer to:

*Giant skeleton (Tarn's Lair)
*Giant skeleton (Shadow Dungeon)

label: Giant spider
title: Giant spider
lead: Giant spiders are very large spiders most commonly seen around Lumbridge.

label: Giants' Foundry/Mould List
title: Giants' Foundry/Mould List
lead: These are the moulds used in the Giant's Foundry minigame for forging swords.

label: Giants' Foundry/Strategies
title: Giants' Foundry/Strategies
lead: This guide provides detailed information as to recommended equipment and alloys, the acquisition of materials and workings of refinement of a preform in the Giants' Foundry.

label: Gielinor
title: Gielinor
lead:
Gielinor ( ) is the fictional world in which Old School RuneScape takes place. It was discovered and given its name by Guthix. It is orbited by a single moon, which is the realm of Zanaris.

Two of its continents, the mainland and Zeah, are accessible to players. Five of its nine oceans, along with parts of a sixth ocean, are accessible through the Sailing skill.

label: Gielinor Gazette
title: Gielinor Gazette
lead:
The Gielinor Gazette is a monthly blog series published by Jagex. Originally started in 2020, editions were published monthly from February-September 2020 and once thereafter before becoming a regular monthly feature again beginning in October 2021.

The Gazette features behind the scenes material which documents ongoing projects being worked on by the Old School development team. It is the home of the Postbag From the Hedge, which allows players to write letters to in-game NPCs and receive responses. It also includes the Player Showcase Gallery, which shows RuneScape fan artwork submitted by players.

label: Gielinor Guide
title: Gielinor Guide
lead:
The Gielinor Guide (formerly RuneScape Guide) is the first non-player character (NPC) that players meet in the game. He is found in his house on Tutorial Island. He gives a brief but informative chat about the game.

At this NPC, a player is required to choose their character's looks.
These include:
*Body type
*Hair style / colour
*Body style / colour
*Legs style / colour
*Arms style
*Feet style / colour (brown or black)

label: Gielinor Parcel Delivery Team
title: Gielinor Parcel Delivery Team
lead:
The Gielinor Parcel Delivery Team (GPDT) is an organisation that specialises in delivering things. According to Wizard Cromperty, their motto is "We aim to deliver your stuff at some point after you have paid us".

It is the only known postal service in Gielinor with a branch located in East Ardougne; it is south of the eastern bank. The building is scattered with boxes used in Tribal Totem quest. Their employees are extremely inefficient, as they forget to deliver a lot of their packages.

label: Gielinor's Flora
title: Gielinor's Flora
lead:
Gielinor's Flora is a series of books detailing the various flora that exist within Gielinor. The information found within the books are more often than not just flavour text, and do not reflect their properties or uses within the game itself, though the order each book describes its respective plants do reflect the order that each produce is unlocked from Farming (for example, potatoes are the first allotment plant players can grow, and so are listed first in the allotments book; snape grass is the last allotment unlocked, and as such are listed last). This is true of each book.

Special produce, such as mushrooms and cacti, do not have a book associated with them.

title: Gilded 4-poster (interface item)
lead:
The Gilded 4-poster is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gilded 4-poster.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Gilded dragonhide armour
title: Gilded dragonhide armour
lead:
Gilded dragonhide armour has the same offensive bonuses as the green dragonhide armour, but offers notably higher defensive bonuses. Like green dragonhide armour, level 40 Ranged is required to equip each piece. The gilded d'hide body also requires level 40 Defence and completion of Dragon Slayer I to equip. Each piece is a possible reward from completing elite Treasure Trails.

Since the additional defensive bonuses makes this an upgrade from regular green dragonhide armour, it is the best ranged armour available in free-to-play. While most pieces of the armour are available in the free-to-play worlds, the coif is a members-only item.

label: Gilded dresser (interface item)
title: Gilded dresser (interface item)
lead:
The Gilded dresser is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gilded dresser.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Gilded equipment
title: Gilded equipment
lead: Gilded equipment pieces are potential rewards from hard, elite and master tier Treasure Trails. It is essentially gold-plated rune equipment, as stat bonuses between any gilded piece and its regular counterpart are identical. Gilded items are mostly worn as status symbols of wealth, due to their high prices with no advantage in combat over their regular rune counterparts.

label: Gilded magic wardrobe (interface item)
title: Gilded magic wardrobe (interface item)
lead:
The Gilded magic wardrobe is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gilded magic wardrobe.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Gilded mounted head display (interface item)
title: Gilded mounted head display (interface item)
lead:
The Gilded mounted head display is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the a mounted King Black Dragon head.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Gilded portal nexus (interface item)
title: Gilded portal nexus (interface item)
lead:
The Gilded portal nexus is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gilded portal nexus.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Gilded throne (interface item)
title: Gilded throne (interface item)
lead:
The Gilded throne is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gilded throne.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: gilded totem
title: gilded totem
lead:
The gilded totem is a quest item obtained during the Legends' Quest quest. At the very start of the quest, the player is asked to get one from the inhabitants of Kharazi Jungle by Radimus Erkle so that it may be displayed it in the main hall of the Legends' Guild.

Gujuo of the Kharazi tribe rewards the player with the gilded totem after they successfully carve a Yommi totem and replace the corrupted totem after defeating the demon Nezikchened. After completing the quest, the gilded totem, now displayed in the Legends' Guild as the totem pole, can be used to recharge the Skills necklace and the Combat bracelet by using them on the totem pole.

label: Gilded wardrobe (interface item)
title: Gilded wardrobe (interface item)
lead:
The Gilded wardrobe is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gilded wardrobe.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Giles
title: Giles
lead: Giles is the brother of Miles and Niles. Like his brothers, he may appear to initiate the Certer random event, in which he will ask players to identify an item, such as a fish, with three possible choices of what the object is. If the player correctly identifies the item, Giles will give the player a reward of either coins, a gem (uncut, up to diamond), a cosmic talisman, a half key, a spinach roll, or a kebab.

label: Gilob
title: Gilob
lead: Gilob was a former watchman for the Black Guard at the Coal Trucks. His watchtower south of the Coal Trucks was overrun by goblins and he was slain. His son, Lollk, was kidnapped but is recovered later in the Dwarf Cannon quest. The player must bring Gilob's remains to Captain Lawgof in the aforementioned quest.

label: gin
title: gin
lead:
Gin is an alcoholic drink used in making gnome cocktails. It heals 5 hitpoints, increases a player's Strength by 5% + 1, and decreases Attack by 2% + 3 when drunk.

It can be found at Blurberry's bar in the Grand Tree and Jossik's shop in the Lighthouse.

label: Gingerbread shields
title: Gingerbread shields
lead:
Gingerbread shields could refer to:

*Gingerbread shield
*Iced gingerbread shield
*Green gingerbread shield
*Red gingerbread shield
*Blue gingerbread shield

label: Girlfriend
title: Girlfriend
lead:
A girlfriend may refer to one of the following NPCs:

* Aga – a female troll, which must be convinced to change boyfriends in the Troll Romance quest
* Anita – Glough's girlfriend
* Lantania – a girlfriend of Sialathin referred to in a dusty scroll
* Neite – the girlfriend of Bob
* Princess Astrid – the player can choose to pursue her romantically during the Throne of Miscellania quest.
* Sylvia and Marsha – female girlfriends of each other

label: Gland
title: Gland
lead:
Gland may refer to:

* , a drop from Tormented Demons
* , obtained during The Fremennik Exiles quest

label: Glarial
title: Glarial
lead:
Queen Glarial was a legendary elven queen of the Fourth Age. She was the wife of King Baxtorian, mother of Eirlys and grandmother of Islwyn. She is mentioned in the Waterfall Quest and Roving Elves quest.

Her tomb is located near the Baxtorian Falls.

label: Glarial's amulet
title: Glarial's amulet
lead:
Glarial's amulet is used during the Waterfall Quest to grant access to the Waterfall Dungeon. Attempting to enter the dungeon during the quest without the amulet results in the player taking damage, being swept away to downstream from the door. After the quest, the amulet is not needed to enter the dungeon.

The amulet can be recovered in the western chest inside Glarial's Tomb if lost. Players may enter the tomb by having Glarial's pebble and having no armour, weapons, or runes equipped or in their inventory. Beware of the moss guardians in the tomb. Players may obtain more than one amulet through the drop trick.

label: Glarial's pebble
title: Glarial's pebble
lead:
Glarial's pebble is an item used in the Waterfall Quest and Roving Elves. It is given to the player by Golrie as a reward for freeing him from the dungeon under the Tree Gnome Village. If you lose this pebble all you have to do is go back to Golrie to obtain another.

The pebble is used to gain access to the Glarial's Tomb dungeon near the Baxtorian Falls. Note that in order to enter the dungeon, the player may not be carrying weapons, armour, runes, or various other items. See the Glarial's Tomb page for a more comprehensive list of disallowed items.

label: Glarial's Tomb
title: Glarial's Tomb
lead:
Glarial's Tomb is a dungeon underneath the tombstone near the Baxtorian Falls and the Kingdom of Kandarin. To enter, the player needs Glarial's pebble, which is obtained during the Waterfall Quest, and must not have any weapons, armour or runes either equipped or in their inventory. Level 84 moss guardians roam here.

The location is close to the Fishing Guild; use Glarial's pebble on her tombstone and you may enter. Players can get Glarial's amulet in the west chest. This location can be re-entered after the Waterfall Quest has been completed in order to obtain Glarial's amulet once again.

label: Glarial's tomb (scenery)
title: Glarial's tomb (scenery)
lead: Glarial's tomb is found within Glarial's Tomb, the player searches the tomb during Waterfall Quest to retrieve Glarial's urn.

label: Glarial's Tombstone
title: Glarial's Tombstone
lead:
Glarial's tombstone is a gravestone that serves as the entrance to Glarial's Tomb. The door can only be opened by using Glarial's pebble on it. It is located north-west of the Fishing Guild.

The tomb is involved in the Waterfall Quest and Roving Elves.

label: Glarial's urn
title: Glarial's urn
lead: Glarial's urn is an item used in the Waterfall Quest and has no known use after the quest. The urn can obtained by searching the tomb in the Glarial's tomb. After the completion of the Waterfall Quest, the urn becomes empty.

label: Glass Box
title: Glass Box
lead:
Glass Box is one of four Mime emotes unlocked as a Random event reward.

Upon completing a Mime event, players are returned to their previous location in game, with a new mime emote unlocked. Players cannot choose which of the four emotes unlock since this is random.

label: Glass Wall
title: Glass Wall
lead:
Glass Wall is one of four Mime emotes unlocked upon completing a Mime event. After the event, players are returned to their previous location with a random new mime emote unlocked.

Upon use the player pretends to be behind a glass wall.

label: Glassblowing pipe
title: Glassblowing pipe
lead: A glassblowing pipe is a tool used to make items from molten glass using the Crafting skill. It is required to make glass items. The item can be obtained from Fritz the Glassblower's house found in the south-western area of Entrana, taken from a tool store 3 in a player-owned house (required 35 Construction), from Grandpa Jack's house (from Fishing Contest quest), bought from the Piscatoris Fishing Colony after finishing Swan Song, or bought from charter ship locations (from the crew).

label: Glasses
title: Glasses
lead:
Glasses may refer to:

*Spyglass, used in sea charting
*Half moon spectacles
*Monocle
*Partyhat & specs
*Sagacious spectacles
*Odd spectacles
*Prescription goggles

label: glitch
title: glitch
lead:
A glitch (also known as a bug) is a fault in a program that causes it to function improperly. The severity of glitches can vary. Most glitches are merely annoying and don't benefit players. In rare cases, however, a major glitch might cause Jagex to do a complete shutdown of the game making all worlds offline, followed by banning the players who abused such a glitch or rolling back the game state to a previous point.

Glitches can be reported directly to Jagex by right-clicking the Report button and selecting "Report game bug". This in-game bug report form also contains a listing of known issues to prevent duplicate reports.

label: Globe (disambiguation)
title: Globe (disambiguation)
lead: Globes are built in the study of a player-owned house as a decoration.

label: Globe (interface item)
title: Globe (interface item)
lead:
The Globe is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Globe.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Glorious arena (interface item)
title: Glorious arena (interface item)
lead:
The Glorious arena is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Glorious arena.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Glory
title: Glory
lead:
Glory is an intangible reward obtained from the Fortis Colosseum. Players must complete Children of the Sun to gain access to the Colosseum and increase their Glory.

Every time the player completes a wave, they will earn Glory, in which the amount gained is dependent on the player's performance - damage taken, time spent, errors made, and types of handicaps selected. The player will retain Glory even if they die during a subsequent wave, but not if they teleport out.

label: Glough
title: Glough
lead:
Glough ( ) is an ill-natured, misanthropic gnome who attempts to start a war against the humans. In The Grand Tree quest, he can be found in his house up a ladder just south-east of the ramp leading to the Grand Tree.

Glough's schemes are thwarted in The Grand Tree quest, and once again in Monkey Madness I. He was originally the head tree guardian of the Tree Gnome Stronghold until his first plot was thwarted by the player. He makes his first unsuccessful attempt on the player's life when he summons a black demon to kill them in The Grand Tree, and is indirectly responsible for the second attempt in Monkey Madness I, where he provides a powerful spell and a Jungle Demon to Awowogei, which is used in an attempt to trap the 10th Squad, but is defeated by the player. During Monkey Madness II, the player manages to break the alliance between Glough and the monkeys by sabotaging Awowogei's forces, along with his alliance between the ogres and trolls. Becoming increasingly deranged and desperate, Glough launches an attack on the Grand Tree by himself. He eventually meets his end at the hands of the player after a great skirmish, but not before killing Nieve.

label: Glough's experiments
title: Glough's experiments
lead:
Glough's experiments may refer to:

* Tortured gorilla
* Demonic gorilla
* Maniacal monkey

label: Glough's journal
title: Glough's journal
lead:
Glough's journal is found during The Grand Tree quest by searching a cupboard within Glough's house. The journal looks a little deeper into the mind and motives of Glough the gnome. It's used as a key piece of evidence as to what he's planning.

After finishing the quest, the book can be found on the shelves in your house.

label: Glough's key
title: Glough's key
lead:
Glough's key is an item used during The Grand Tree quest. It opens a chest in Glough's home just south of the Grand Tree. The player finds invasion plans in the chest which can then be shown to King Narnode Shareen as evidence.

Players obtain this item by talking to Anita in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. Her home is in the north-west of the stronghold, just west of the swamp. The key has no use after the quest.

label: Glouphrie (disambiguation)
title: Glouphrie (disambiguation)
lead: Glouphrie can mean any of the following:

label: Glove rack (interface item)
title: Glove rack (interface item)
lead:
The Glove rack is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Glove rack.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: gloves
title: gloves
lead: Gloves are pieces of armour that players can wear in the hands slot. These are the many different types of gloves that players can wear in Old School RuneScape.

label: glowing dagger
title: glowing dagger
lead:
The glowing dagger is a quest item obtained and used during the Legends' Quest. It has the same combat stats as an iron dagger, only lacking the +4 strength bonus.

It is created when players are given the dark dagger by Echned Zekin, requesting them to kill Viyeldi because he was the one that murdered him and wants revenge. Once the dagger is used to kill Viyeldi, it will convert into a glowing dagger. It must then be taken back to Echned Zekin, who will reveal his true form - the demon Nezikchened.

label: Glue
title: Glue
lead:
Glue may refer to:

*Magic glue, an item used in The Eyes of Glouphrie quest.
*Sea slug glue, an item used in The Slug Menace quest.

label: Glyphs
title: Glyphs
lead: Glyphs are pieces of scenery found in almost every house in Al Kharid. The symbols depict ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs, but have no relation to any Kharidian lore. They can only be examined.

label: gnome
title: gnome
lead:
Gnomes are a race of small humanoids found in various parts of Gielinor. They can be found primarily in the Kandarin region, being most common in the Tree Gnome Village, Tree Gnome Stronghold, and Battlefield of Khazard. Gnomes fight with primarily either ranged or melee attacks, depending on the weapon they wield. They have different coloured hoods.

Gnomes can be pickpocketed at level 75 Thieving yielding 133.3 Thieving experience. It is a good source of medium clue scrolls, but keep in mind that you will not receive a clue from pickpocketing an NPC if your inventory is full, and you have not completed X Marks the Spot. If you have completed X Marks the Spot and obtained at least one scroll box in your inventory, then you will continue to obtain more to your stack without emptying your inventory of other loot. Pickpocketing gnomes can also be very convenient for those doing Gnome Restaurant, so you do not need to leave to get more king worms or toad legs.

label: Gnome (A Tail of Two Cats)
title: Gnome (A Tail of Two Cats)
lead: Two gnomes were planned to appear in a cutscene in the A Tail of Two Cats quest. Due to the quest developer resigning before the quest could be completed, the cutscene was never implemented, leaving the gnomes and the other NPCs that were intended to appear in the cutscene unused within the game cache.

label: Gnome (race)
title: Gnome (race)
lead: Gnomes are one of several intelligent races that inhabit Gielinor, with an extensive civilisation and culture. Not only do the gnomes have their own empire, but they also have their own cuisine, clothes, methods of transportation (spirit trees and gnome gliders), quests, and minigames (Gnome Ball and Gnome Restaurant). Most gnomes are found in Kandarin, but gnome explorers can be found all over Gielinor.

label: Gnome Air
title: Gnome Air
lead:
Gnome Air is a gnomish airline that is the primary overseer and manager of air travel in Gielinor. It uses gnome gliders, first invented by Oaknock the Engineer and his son Yewnock at the beginning of the Fifth Age. Until the arrest of the misanthropic Glough, Gnome Air would only take gnomes, but now they also fly humans.

Whilst Gnome Air dominates long-distance air travel across the globe, Ali Morrisane's fleet of magic carpets is the main mode of transportation over shorter distances in the desert. When Ali announced his new venture, a PR executive for Gnome Air replied that 'it [would] never take off.' In fact, the gnomes have filed lawsuits against Ali to the Supreme Rune Court, the result of which is not known.

label: Gnome amulet
title: Gnome amulet
lead:
The gnome amulet is awarded to players by King Bolren after completion of the Tree Gnome Village quest. Should the player happen to lose the amulet, another can be obtained for free from King Bolren. It is made from the same material as the orbs of protection that are retrieved during the quest.

It functions as a melee-only amulet of defence, having +13 in all melee defences but no magic and ranged defence. For melee-only situations, this amulet is recommended over the amulet of defence.

label: Gnome Ball
title: Gnome Ball
lead:
Gnome Ball is a minigame in which one or more players attempt to score goals against gnomes. Goals are scored by throwing the gnomeball into the goal, and the game is won when five goals are scored. Players earn some Ranged and Agility experience upon scoring a goal and winning the game.

When a player first enters the field, they should talk to the gnome ball referee to gain the ball.

label: Gnome ball referee
title: Gnome ball referee
lead: The Gnome ball referee runs the members-only Gnome Ball minigame.

label: Gnome baller
title: Gnome baller
lead:
Gnome Ballers are gnomes found in the Tree Gnome Stronghold Gnome Ball pitch. While competing in Gnome Ball, the gnome ballers may try to tackle and take possession of the ball. The gnome ballers have a Tackle option which, when successful, knocks them to the ground and recovers possession of the ball.

The chance of getting successfully tackled by a gnome baller is dependent on a player's Agility level, but is not influenced by the colour of the uniform worn by a gnome baller. In contrast, the chance of tackling a gnome baller as a player depends on a number of factors, as described in the section below.

label: Gnome banker
title: Gnome banker
lead: Gnome bankers run the Tree Gnome Stronghold branch of the Bank of Gielinor.

label: Gnome bench (interface item)
title: Gnome bench (interface item)
lead:
The Gnome bench is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gnome bench.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Gnome boots
title: Gnome boots
lead:
Gnome boots may refer to:

*Blue boots
*Cream boots
*Green boots
*Pink boots
*Turquoise boots

label: Gnome child
title: Gnome child
lead:
Gnome children are young gnomes found in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. Like adult gnomes, they can be killed or pickpocketed. All of them use melee unlike their adult counterparts.

Gnome children can be pickpocketed at level 75 Thieving; doing so yields 133.5 Thieving experience. It is recommended not to pickpocket them until the player has level 85 Thieving, because even with gloves of silence, the player will fail most of the time.

label: gnome cooking
title: gnome cooking
lead:
Gnome cooking is a specialised part of the Cooking skill that is available to members. Like standard cooking, players may burn various gnome cuisine, stopping entirely at level 38. Special equipment and ingredients are required for gnomish cooking, all of which can be obtained either by purchasing from Hudo or Heckel Funch, or by picking up respawns around the Grand Tree in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Cooking tutorials can be given by Aluft Gianne snr. and Blurberry, but are not required to begin making the food. These tutorials are however required to start the Gnome Restaurant minigame, as Gianne jnr. will request recommendations from both of them before it is possible to begin.

label: Gnome Empire
title: Gnome Empire
lead:
The Gnome Empire is a monarchical region bordering and within the human nation of Kandarin. The Empire is not referred to as such on the world map and is often not recognised by players, but it has been named as such by various characters, the most prominent of which is perhaps Glouphrie. The empire is considered part of Kandarin on maps, but it isn't known what the exact relationship and governmental structures are between the Kingdom and the Empire.

Although it was once much larger, as of the year 169 of the Fifth Age, the Gnome Empire consists mostly of two settlements; the Tree Gnome Stronghold (north-west of Ardougne) and Tree Gnome Village (south of Ardougne). Despite being considered one empire, both settlements have a monarch.

label: Gnome Glider
title: Gnome Glider
lead:
Gnome gliders are a method of transportation available after completing The Grand Tree quest. They can fly to many locations and can be used in combination with teleport spells, spirit trees, and the fairy ring network to quickly travel across Gielinor.

The fastest way to access the glider network is by either taking the royal seed pod and climbing up to the top floor with the right-click option (requiring Monkey Madness II, takes approximately 10 seconds), or using a ring of dueling to teleport to Emir's Arena and running south-west (takes approximately 13 seconds).

label: Gnome goal
title: Gnome goal
lead: The Gnome goal is the target for the Gnome Ball minigame. Shooting and making a goal will give the player's team a point.

label: Gnome guard
title: Gnome guard
lead: Gnome guards are gnome warriors in and around the Tree Gnome Stronghold, including in the Grand Tree. They have either a halberd or a sword and shield equipped. They have relatively high Hitpoints for their level and their attacks aren't very accurate.

label: Gnome hat
title: Gnome hat
lead:
Gnome hats may refer to:

*Blue hat
*Cream hat
*Green hat
*Pink hat
*Turquoise hat
*Gnome child hat

label: Gnome Institute of Knowledge
title: Gnome Institute of Knowledge
lead:
The Gnome Institute of Knowledge is a gnome research organisation. The institute is only briefly mentioned in , a lore found on the official RuneScape website, and has not made an appearance in-game.

The only known field of study is psychology. Dr. Darius Gnomalus, who is interviewed by a human, was Head of Psychology when the account was written a few years ago. It is possible that he still holds the position today.

label: Gnome King
title: Gnome King
lead: Gnome King is a music track that is unlocked in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

label: Gnome Liaison Officer
title: Gnome Liaison Officer
lead: Gnome Liaison Officer was a position created by Glough to act as a middleman between the Gnome and human workers in the Karamja Shipyard.

label: Gnome Maze
title: Gnome Maze
lead:
The gnome maze is a large hedge maze that makes up the exterior part of the Tree Gnome Village. The maze must be solved at least once in order to start the Tree Gnome Village quest.

After the first completion, Elkoy will be available as an escort through the maze both to and from the village, although only if players have started the quest. The maze is also involved in other quests, such as Waterfall Quest (where the player enters the maze dungeon) and Regicide.

label: Gnome pilot
title: Gnome pilot
lead:
Gnome pilot may refer to:
*Captain Bleemadge
*Captain Daerkin
*Captain Dalbur
*Captain Errdo
*Captain Klemfoodle
*Captain Lamdoo
*Captain Ninto
*Captain Shoracks
*Waydar

label: Gnome pilot (historical)
title: Gnome pilot (historical)
lead: Gnome pilots were gnomes who could originally be found piloting the gnome gliders. With the release of the revamped Gnome Restaurant minigame, they were replaced by four updated pilots with unique names on 7 August 2006. However, one pilot remained at the crashed glider west of the Digsite, until he too was replaced by an embarrassed Captain Errdo in a hidden update in January 2007. As a result, they have never been present in Old School RuneScape.

label: Gnome quest series
title: Gnome quest series
lead: The Gnome quest series is a series of quests centring around the race of gnomes. The main theme of the quest series is traitors and enemies of the gnomes attempting to destroy them. The player fights to stop this. The storyline of the series varies greatly by quest, and two quest series can be distinguished. One is the Glough quest series, of which The Grand Tree, Monkey Madness I, and Monkey Madness II are a part of. The other is the Glouphrie quest series, which includes The Eyes of Glouphrie and The Path of Glouphrie. Tree Gnome Village doesn't belong to either storyline but is still a gnome quest.

label: Gnome robe bottoms
title: Gnome robe bottoms
lead:
Gnome robe bottoms may refer to:

*Blue robe bottoms
*Cream robe bottoms
*Green robe bottoms
*Pink robe bottoms
*Turquoise robe bottoms

label: Gnome robe top
title: Gnome robe top
lead:
Gnome robe top may refer to:

*Blue robe top
*Cream robe top
*Green robe top
*Pink robe top
*Turquoise robe top

label: Gnome robes
title: Gnome robes
lead: Gnome robes can only be purchased from Fine Fashions in the Gnome Stronghold. The set includes: Robe top, Robe bottoms, Hat, and Boots. The colours they come in are pastel pink, pastel green, blue, turquoise and cream. Gnome robes are used as cheap magic gear or required to complete some low level Treasure Trails clues.

label: Gnome Royal Guard
title: Gnome Royal Guard
lead:
The Royal Guard is the primary military force of the Gnome Empire. The Royal Guard maintains a strong presence throughout the Empire, although its activities can be seen most primarily in areas such as the Tree Gnome Stronghold and Battlefield of Khazard. The term Royal Guard is used somewhat rarely in-game, although during the Monkey Madness I quest it is referred to as such very frequently.

The Royal Guard was likely established in some form by the gnomish race in the early Fourth Age, after it re-emerged from its God Wars-era hiding. It has since allowed the Gnome Empire to grow in strength and political prominence, and has defended the Empire during recent conflicts such as the Arposandran War and Khazard - Gnome War.

label: Gnome shop keeper
title: Gnome shop keeper
lead:
The Gnome shop keeper is an unused character who was added to the game during the RuneScape 2 beta. Presumably, he would have been a generic character in the Tree Gnome Stronghold or Tree Gnome Village, similar to the Gnome banker. He has a very similar appearance to Bolkoy, who runs the general store in the Tree Gnome Village.

The character was not added to the game since every gnome shop is run by a unique character. Most likely, he was scrapped relatively early on due to lacking any interaction options.

label: gnome spice
title: gnome spice
lead:
Gnome Spice is an ingredient used to make spicy sauce and certain gnome foods. It can be bought from Grand Tree Groceries, run by Hudo in the Grand Tree. It will never run out while making Gnome foods.

To create spicy sauce, gnome spice is used with chopped garlic. This uses up the gnome spice.

label: Gnome Statue (Port Khazard mine)
title: Gnome Statue (Port Khazard mine)
lead: This gnome statue is a scenery object found south of the Port Khazard mine. Players cannot interact with the statue, but they can examine it.

label: Gnome Stronghold Agility Course
title: Gnome Stronghold Agility Course
lead:
The Tree Gnome Stronghold Agility Course is an Agility course in which the player must traverse obstacles consisting of a log balance, obstacle nets, tightropes, and pipes. It is located south of the Grand Tree in the Tree Gnome Stronghold, which is north-west of East Ardougne. This Agility course is the lowest level course that can be accessed and has no requirements. It is impossible to fail any of the obstacles at this course, so it is not necessary to bring any food. Players gain 110.5 experience points for a complete circuit, and can receive marks of grace during this course.

Completing a lap of the Gnome Stronghold Agility Course is a requirement for the easy Western Provinces Diary.

label: Gnome Stronghold north bank
title: Gnome Stronghold north bank
lead:
The Gnome Stronghold north bank, also known as the Grand Tree bank, is a bank found on the second level of the Grand Tree, in the Gnome Stronghold. Players do not need to have completed The Grand Tree to enter the stronghold or use the bank.

The Grand Tree bank is popular for players teleporting from the Wilderness with a royal seed pod, as the pod takes them just one level below. There is also a loot chest, which player-killers use to cash in loot keys from players they killed.

label: Gnome Stronghold south bank
title: Gnome Stronghold south bank
lead:
The Gnome Stronghold south bank, also known as the Stronghold Cave bank or the Nieve bank, is a bank found in the southern part of the Gnome Stronghold. Players do not need to have completed The Grand Tree to enter the stronghold or use the bank.

The Nieve bank is popular for players using the nearby Stronghold Slayer Cave, as well as for players restocking during farm runs.

label: Gnome trainer
title: Gnome trainer
lead: Gnome trainers are rather unfriendly gnomes that shout insults at players training agility at the agility course in the Tree Gnome Stronghold such as "My granny is faster than you!"

label: Gnome troop
title: Gnome troop
lead:
Gnome troops are soldiers of the Gnome Army found on the Khazard Battlefield and within the Tree Gnome Stronghold. At Khazard Battlefield, they can be found swamping the Khazard troopers most of the time. When they are attacking or being attacked by Khazard troopers, they will say phrases such as "You will never get us without a fight!" and "Tally ho!"

While in the Tree Gnome Stronghold, they have a Talk-to option, and will talk to players about the Khazard Battlefield and ask to join them in their cause.

label: Gnome Village
title: Gnome Village
lead:
Gnome Village may refer to:

* The quest Tree Gnome Village
* Music tracks:
** Gnome Village
** Gnome Village 2
* Locations:
** Tree Gnome Village (location)
** Tree Gnome Village Dungeon
** Tree Gnome Stronghold

label: Gnome Village 2
title: Gnome Village 2
lead: Gnome Village 2 is a music track that is unlocked in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

label: gnome waiter
title: gnome waiter
lead:
Gnome Waiters run the shop Gianne's Restaurant that sells premade gnome cuisine, such as crunchies, battas and gnomebowls. The food they sell cannot be used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. They are located on the of the Grand Tree north of the bank.

They seem to be sad about the food being made by a human assistant chef, as it was not up to the Chef's exacting standards, and claims the food may not be accepted as the 'real' thing, which is true, as premade food cannot be used when doing Gnome Restaurant.

label: Gnome winger
title: Gnome winger
lead: Gnome wingers are found in the Gnome Ball pitch. They are on the same team as the player, and passing the Gnomeball to them will let them pass it back to you after a few seconds. This could be used to pass some Gnome ballers who will normally try to take possession of the ball.

label: gnome woman
title: gnome woman
lead:
Gnome women are female gnomes that may be found in the Gnome Stronghold. They may be pickpocketed with 75 Thieving; doing so yields 133.5 Thieving experience.

Gnome women will occasionally give the player a King worm when spoken to.

label: Gnomeball
title: Gnomeball
lead:
Gnomeballs are received by winning 5 points in a game of Gnome Ball, from the gnome restaurant minigame, or as a drop from dolphins. With the item in your inventory, you can click "Use" with it, and click another player. If that player has their right hand empty, they will catch the ball, and it will end up in their weapon slot. It is not advised that you throw it to a player you do not know, as they can very easily walk away with it.

Gnomeballs cannot be used on or by Ironman Mode players.

label: Gnomeball (music track)
title: Gnomeball (music track)
lead: Gnomeball is a music track that is unlocked at the Gnome Ball Field.

label: gnomebowl mould
title: gnomebowl mould
lead:
A gnomebowl mould is an item used in gnome cooking. It can be bought in the Grand Tree by talking to Hudo in the north-west corner on the , or it can be acquired for free by searching the tree gnome kitchen cabinet at the northernmost part of the Grand Tree for a "gnome bowl".

Adding gianne dough to the mould will create a raw gnomebowl, the basis for gnomebowl cooking.

label: gnomish firelighters
title: gnomish firelighters
lead:
Gnomish firelighters are stackable rewards from Treasure Trails. They can be used on regular logs to produce coloured logs, or on a gnomish firelighter to fill it. When used on logs, a message in the chatbox will state You coat the logs with the [colour] chemicals. When the coloured logs are used with a tinderbox, the flame will either be blue, red, purple, white, or green, depending on the colour of the firelighter used.

When burning the logs, the experience gained is increased by 10 points, for a total of 50. Additionally, the fire will always be lit on the first try; burning coloured logs can be a slight time-saver on early Firemaking training over regular logs and even oak logs.

label: Goat (disambiguation)
title: Goat (disambiguation)
lead:
Goat may refer to:
*Goat
*Billy Goat
*Billy
*Mountain goat
*Goat Poo

*Desert goat horn
**Goat horn dust
*Goat dung

label: goblin
title: goblin
lead:
Goblins are one of the most common, low-level monsters found around Gielinor. They are popularly killed by low-level players training their combat skills.

Goblins are often one of the first monsters a player will encounter, as they inhabit much of the area around Lumbridge.

label: Goblin (disambiguation)
title: Goblin (disambiguation)
lead:
Goblin may refer to:
* The race of goblins

label: Goblin (historical)
title: Goblin (historical)
lead:
Goblins could originally be found in the Goblin Village and were encountered during the Goblin Diplomacy quest. Twice in 2005 and 2006, goblins were graphically updated and new versions were added. However, the original versions remained in the game cache.

The 2005 versions were graphically updated alongside other goblins in 2007, despite already having been removed from the game. The original versions however were not updated.

label: goblin (race)
title: goblin (race)
lead: Goblins are small, green, humanoid creatures. Though lacking intelligence and strength, goblins make up for this with overwhelming numbers. They are followers of the god Bandos, who they refer to as the "Big High War God". Goblins are frequently at war with the other races of Gielinor, in particular dwarves and gnomes.

label: Goblin Cave
title: Goblin Cave
lead:
The Goblin Cave, known to the goblins as the Plain of Mud, is a dungeon filled with goblins located east of the Fishing Guild and south of Hemenster. Some of its inhabitants are aggressive no matter what level you are.

The cave contains the entrance to the Goblin Temple, built by goblin tribes for Bandos during the Fourth Age after the Battle of Plain of Mud.

label: Goblin Diplomacy
title: Goblin Diplomacy
lead: Goblin Diplomacy is the 15 th quest released in RuneScape. During the quest, the player resolves a long-standing dispute among the goblins of Goblin Village.

label: Goblin general
title: Goblin general
lead:
Goblin general may refer to:

*General Graardor, leader of the Bandos forces in the God wars dungeon.

label: Goblin guard
title: Goblin guard
lead: The Goblin guard (known as Sleeping guard before being woken up) is a level 42 goblin with 43 hitpoints, who is guarding the kitchen gate in the dungeon near the Observatory. During the Observatory Quest players must "prod" him to wake him up, he then attacks the player while saying "Oi, how dare you wake me up!". He can be fought after the quest is complete as he respawns in the same place.

label: Goblin Invasion
title: Goblin Invasion
lead:
Goblin Invasion may refer to the following events:

*2013 Goblin Invasion
*2014 Goblin Invasion

label: Goblin kitchen key
title: Goblin kitchen key
lead:
The goblin kitchen key is a quest item in the Observatory Quest. It found in a chest in the Observatory Dungeon and is used to open the Kitchen gate in the same dungeon. The chest in which the key is found is different for every player, but remains the same once found. Attempting to obtain another from the chest while one is in the inventory yields the message: Another one will be of little use. However, it is possible to obtain duplicates if it is banked. It can be reobtained after the quest.

It cannot be added to the key ring.

label: goblin mail
title: goblin mail
lead:
Goblin mail is armour for goblins. Although this item has the "Wear" option, this item cannot be equipped by players as it is too small to fit humans. However, during the Land of the Goblins quest, the player can turn into a goblin using a transmogrification potion and wear the goblin mail.

It can be dyed into various colours, in which certain colours are used for the Land of the Goblins quest.

label: Goblin name
title: Goblin name
lead:
Goblin names are given to the player by goblin guards during the quest Land of the Goblins. When talking to them after transforming into a goblin, they will try to guess your goblin name.

If players don't like the goblin name they're given, they can ask the goblin guards to guess their name again to be given another name.

label: Goblin priest (disambiguation)
title: Goblin priest (disambiguation)
lead:
Goblin priest may refer to:

* High Priest Bighead, the current goblin high priest
* Priest (Goblin), one of the tribal priests found in the Goblin Temple
* One of the past priests encountered during Land of the Goblins:
** Snothead
** Snailfeet
** Mosschin
** Redeyes
** Strongbones
* High Priest (2013 Goblin Invasion)
* Goblin priest (from the 2013 Goblin Invasion)

label: goblin settlement
title: goblin settlement
lead:
The Goblin settlement can be found in the ruins east of the Observatory, and is home to a number of named Goblins. During the Observatory Quest, the Observatory professor tells the player that the goblins have been causing trouble in the region, and have stolen parts from the Observatory.

The goblin settlement also has one of the entrances to the Observatory Dungeon, which is similarly overrun by goblins.

label: Goblin Village
title: Goblin Village
lead: Goblin Village is the main settlement of goblins in Asgarnia. The Goblin Village is ruled by two generals, General Bentnoze and General Wartface, whose differences cause the village to fall into conflict and its inhabitants to attack each other. The only entrance to Goblin Village is from the south, along the path that runs from the gate to Taverley. To enter the village, take the path north of Doric's hut.

label: Goblin Village (music track)
title: Goblin Village (music track)
lead: Goblin Village is a music track that is unlocked at the Goblin Village. It has a tribe-ish, simple tune to emphasise to primitiveness of the goblins. The track is quoted in several other music tracks, such as Bandos Battalion.

label: God Alignments
title: God Alignments
lead:
God Alignments are proposed prayers which act as additions to the existing prayer book. A set of alignments would be themed toward one of the many gods in the game, and players can only have one set active at any time. Following initial feedback, they were shelved and have no projected release date.

Details concerning how they're unlocked, as well as the specifics of what each prayer does, are not currently set in stone and are subject to change. The current proposal suggests that each set of prayers would be unlocked for completion of a corresponding grandmaster quest, but it may be that completion of the quest may only unlock a portion of each alignment, and completion of additional content may be required.

label: God blessing
title: God blessing
lead:
God blessings can be found as a reward from all levels of Treasure Trails, except beginner. Each God blessing comes colour coded to represent their respective gods. Saradomin is blue, Guthix is green, Zamorak is red, Armadyl is silver, Zaros is purple, and Bandos is brown.

Each god blessing has a +1 prayer bonus in the ammunition slot, and will also provide protection within the God Wars Dungeon (excluding the peaceful blessing).

label: God book
title: God book
lead: The 6 god books are books held in place of a shield. A player first receives a damaged book and needs to add 4 god pages to make a complete god book. Once a page has been put into a god book, the page cannot be retrieved.

label: God book (or)
title: God book (or)
lead:
God book (or) may refer to:

*Holy book (or)
*Unholy book (or)
*Book of balance (or)
*Book of war (or)
*Book of law (or)
*Book of darkness (or)

label: God capes
title: God capes
lead:
__NOTOC__

The God capes are a set of magic capes awarded from the Mage Arena I miniquest. After defeating Kolodion, the player can speak to him and step through the sparkling pool to a cave where they can pray to one of three gods: Saradomin, Zamorak, or Guthix. After praying to a god, the corresponding cape will appear at the statue's feet and may be picked up. After claiming their first cape, players can talk to the Chamber guardian to claim the corresponding god staff. Multiple capes from the same statue can be obtained.

label: God Letters
title: God Letters
lead:
The God letters were a feature in RuneScape where a player could send a letter through post or e-mail to Jagex, who would pass it on to one of the three major gods: Guthix, Saradomin, or Zamorak. These three gods would then respond to the letters, much like Postbag from the Hedge. The last issue was released on 9 December 2004.

Saradomin would answer in a polite yet somewhat egotistical manner, though his answers were generally accurate; Zamorak would respond to letters with frequent insults and would belittle players' questions; and Guthix would speak in an unbiased tone but would occasionally hide things from the players. Guthix would also use old-fashioned dialects with words and phrases not used in modern English.

label: God page
title: God page
lead: God pages (also known as torn pages) are possible rewards from all tiers of Treasure Trails except beginner clues. Each god page is coloured to represent their respective god: Armadyl is silver, Bandos is brown, Guthix is green, Saradomin is blue, Zamorak is red, and Zaros is purple. Four god pages, numbered 1 through 4, must be put in their respective damaged book to complete the god book, however all four are not required at the same time to add pages to the book.

label: God spells
title: God spells
lead:
God spells refer to the three combat spells unlocked at the Mage Arena. Each spell requires a staff that corresponds to its respective god, and players must have cast the spell at least 100 times within the Mage Arena before being able to cast it anywhere else. Being able to cast all three god spells anywhere is a requirement to start the Mage Arena II miniquest.

Casting one of these spells on another player in the Wilderness is a requirement for the hard Wilderness diary. Splashing the spell will not fulfil the requirement.

label: God Wars
title: God Wars
lead:
, a remnant of the conflict of the God Wars, where four godly factions fight.]]
The God Wars was a time of great calamity in Gielinor. The war lasted approximately 4,000 years, spanning the entire Third Age, which is synonymous with the God Wars.

During the Second Age, Zaros and his empire had almost complete control of the world. When he was betrayed and defeated by Zamorak, the Second Age ended, and the other gods began fighting for power, land and influence. However, many gods, the most significant being Saradomin and Zamorak, wanted complete control.

label: God Wars Dungeon (disambiguation)
title: God Wars Dungeon (disambiguation)
lead:
There are two discrete God Wars Dungeons in Old School Runescape:

* The main God Wars Dungeon, whose entrance is situated north of Trollheim and which contains the five God Wars bosses; and
* The Wilderness God Wars Dungeon, whose entrance is located in the middle of the Wilderness and which does not contain any bosses.

id: page:god wars dungeon-variant rare drop table
label: God Wars Dungeon-variant rare drop table
title: God Wars Dungeon-variant rare drop table
lead:
The God Wars Dungeon-variant rare drop tables refer to two special drop tables of items. When slain, the four bosses in the God Wars Dungeon have a chance to give loot from one of the rare drop tables instead of loot from their own unique drop table. These rare drop tables consist of the God Wars Dungeon-variant rare drop table (GWDRDT) and the God Wars Dungeon-variant gem drop table (GWDGDT). The chance to access the GWDRDT is 8/127. The chance to access the GWDGDT is 2/127, additionally the GWDRDT has a 20/128 chance to roll a drop on the GWDGDT.

The God Wars Dungeon-variant rare drop table has three tables: the Standard rare drop table (GWDRDT), the Gem drop table (GWDGDT) and the Mega-rare drop table. Both the GWDRDT and the GWDGDT have a chance at rolling the Mega-rare drop table.

label: Godric
title: Godric
lead:
Godric is the son of Dunstan, Burthorpe's local blacksmith and is a soldier in the Imperial Guard.

After the player finds an alternate route up the Death Plateau in the Death Plateau quest, the Imperial Guard uses it to plan a surprise attack on the trolls. However, they encounter resistance from the trolls in the area and their forces are decimated. Some of the Guard just escape with their lives. Godric isn't so lucky and is taken prisoner by the trolls to their Stronghold next to Trollheim, where they plan to make him part of their stew. The Troll Stronghold quest centres in the player rescuing Godric from the clutches of the trolls. The player can free him and a strange hermit known as Eadgar from the Stronghold. After their rescue, they take different paths: Godric returns to Burthorpe, while Eadgar returns to his cave at the top of Trollheim. He resumes his training with the Imperial Guard and is promoted to corporal.

label: Gods
title: Gods
lead:
Gods and goddesses are divine beings of various races who have ascended beyond mortality. Many different gods have come and gone from Gielinor throughout its history, some leaving a bigger mark on it than others. The power of the gods varies, but they are all considered to be more powerful than any mortal. Most origins of the gods are unknown, but a few are known to have ascended from mortality to divinity, gaining great powers in doing so, and some are known to have been created intentionally or unintentionally by other gods.

Most gods represent a philosophy or a world view, which affect the titles they have taken or been given by their followers. They are not embodiments of the elements they are attributed, but merely use it as a reflection of what they believe. These philosophies and their interpretations have led to many triumphs and achievements, but also to conflict and war, with the most widely known example being the God Wars, where several different godly factions fought each other for power, territory, etc. The end of the God Wars, established by the creation of the Edicts of Guthix, resulted in the gods being unable to directly influence their followers, thus leaving the mortals to their own interpretation and understanding of the gods.

label: Godsword
title: Godsword
lead:
Godswords are powerful two-handed swords that were originally released on 28 August 2007, along with the God Wars Dungeon. They were added to Old School RuneScape on 17 October 2013. Requiring 75 Attack to wield, godswords have the second highest slash bonus of any weapon after the Soulreaper axe. The godsword consists of a godsword blade, to which a godsword hilt is attached. One hilt exists for each of the gods whose armies still fight in the God Wars Dungeon: Armadyl, Bandos, Saradomin, Zamorak, and Zaros. Consequently, there are five different godswords: the Ancient godsword, Armadyl godsword, the Bandos godsword, the Saradomin godsword, and the Zamorak godsword. All five godswords have identical stats, but each has a different special attack, as detailed below.

Godswords are created by smithing the three different godsword shards into a godsword blade at an anvil. Doing so requires 80 Smithing, and gives a total of 200 Smithing experience. A godsword hilt is then attached to the godsword blade, which requires no stats and can be done by any player. Hilts can be attached or removed at will, at any time. Godsword hilts are dropped exclusively by the generals within the God Wars Dungeon, while godsword shards are dropped by the generals and their bodyguards.

label: Godsword hilt
title: Godsword hilt
lead:
A Godsword hilt is an item dropped by the five Bosses (but not any of the sub-bosses) of each God from the God Wars Dungeon. The hilts come in 5 different varieties, Zamorakian, Saradominist, Bandosian, Armadylean, and Zarosian Godsword hilts may be attached to a Godsword blade to create either an Armadyl godsword, a Bandos godsword, a Saradomin godsword, Ancient godsword or a Zamorak godsword.

Changing a hilt only changes the Godsword's appearance and Special attack - its bonuses do not change.

label: Godsword ornament kit
title: Godsword ornament kit
lead:
Godsword ornament kit may refer to:

*Armadyl godsword ornament kit
*Bandos godsword ornament kit
*Saradomin godsword ornament kit
*Zamorak godsword ornament kit

label: Godsword shard
title: Godsword shard
lead:
Godsword shard may refer to:
* Godsword shard 1
* Godsword shard 2
* Godsword shard 3

label: Godsword shards
title: Godsword shards
lead:
Godsword shards are obtained by combining two different Godsword shards.

*Godsword shards 1 & 2
*Godsword shards 2 & 3
*Godsword shards 1 & 3

label: Goggles
title: Goggles
lead:
Goggles may refer to:

* Reinforced goggles, the headgear used to fight Sourhogs and as part of the creation of a Slayer Helmet
* Prescription goggles, the secondary saving reward from the Mastering Mixology minigame
* Gnome goggles, the cosmetic reward from the Gnome Restaurant minigame

label: Gold
title: Gold
lead: Gold may refer to:

label: Gold amulet
title: Gold amulet
lead:
Gold amulet is a piece of jewellery that is worn in the neck slot. It is made by using a gold bar on a furnace with an amulet mould, followed by using a ball of wool on the resulting Gold amulet (u). This requires level 8 Crafting and the player receives 30 experience for making the amulet and an additional 4 experience for stringing it.

The gold amulet cannot be enchanted, making it purely cosmetic. However, it can be sold to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim for 245 coins or at the Grand Exchange.

label: Gold amulet (u)
title: Gold amulet (u)
lead:
A Gold amulet (u) is made with the Crafting skill by using a gold bar on a furnace while carrying an amulet mould. Following that, it can be strung with a ball of wool, resulting in a strung gold amulet. Making a gold amulet (u) requires level 8 Crafting and players gain 30 experience for making the amulet, and then 4 experience for stringing it.

Unlike gem amulets, gold amulets cannot be enchanted, making them purely cosmetic.

label: gold bar
title: gold bar
lead:
A gold bar is a bar of refined gold created through the Smithing skill at level 40 by using a gold ore with a furnace, or by casting Superheat Item on it. By default, this gives 22.5 Smithing experience per bar, but if the goldsmith gauntlets from the Family Crest quest are worn, the experience given is boosted to 56.2.

The primary use of gold bars is to create jewellery through the Crafting skill. To craft gold bars into jewellery, players must use a gold bar on a furnace with the proper mould in their inventory. If players wish to craft jewellery with gems inset, they must also have the respective cut gems.

label: gold bowl
title: gold bowl
lead:
The gold bowl is a quest item used during the Legends' Quest. According to Gujuo, the required vessel for holy water is a bowl "made from the metal of the sun", referring to gold. The bowl is made by using two gold bars on an anvil while holding the sketch given to the player by Gujuo; after completion of the quest, it is possible to make the bowl without the sketch, though there remains a chance of failing. This gives 30 Smithing experience per bowl. The bowl must then be blessed with Gujuo's help to turn it into a blessed gold bowl. The blessed version is the only vessel capable of holding water with holy properties; trying to fill a normal gold bowl with the pure spring's water will yield a message along the lines of having mere normal water. A successful fill will result in a message saying that "the water seems to bubble and sparkle as if alive."

There is a chance that the player will fail in making the gold bowl, causing one or two gold bars to be destroyed without a resultant bowl. When successfully made, 30 Smithing experience is gained and a message of the achievement appears in the chat box.

label: Gold candlesticks (interface item)
title: Gold candlesticks (interface item)
lead:
The Gold candlesticks is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gold candlesticks.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: gold chest
title: gold chest
lead:
Gold Chest can mean any of the following:
* Chests used in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame
** Gold Chest (red)
** Gold Chest (brown)
** Gold Chest (crimson)
** Gold Chest (black)
** Gold Chest (purple)
* Grand Gold Chest

label: Gold decorative armour
title: Gold decorative armour
lead:
Gold decorative equipment is a reward from the Castle Wars minigame. The armour set requires 30 Defence to equip and the sword requires 30 Attack to wield.

To purchase all pieces of the Gold Decorative Armour set, it would cost 4,400 Castle wars tickets. These calculations are excluding time waiting between each game.

label: Gold key
title: Gold key
lead:
Gold key could refer to:

* Golden key, key used in the Priest in Peril quest
* Gold keys from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame
** Gold key red
** Gold key brown
** Gold key crimson
** Gold key black
** Gold key purple

label: Gold necklace
title: Gold necklace
lead:
The gold necklace is a piece of gold jewellery.

It has no stats and cannot be enchanted, making it purely cosmetic. However, it can be sold for 45-315 coins to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim, depending on how many he already has.

label: gold ore
title: gold ore
lead:
Gold ore can be mined from gold rocks at level 40 Mining, providing 65 Mining experience. After it is mined, it takes 60 seconds to regenerate. Gold ore is used to smelt gold bars at a furnace. Smelting a gold bar gives 22.5 Smithing experience, or 56.2 with goldsmith gauntlets equipped. The bar can then be used again on a furnace to craft various types of jewellery, with sufficient Crafting skill, and an appropriate mould. An anvil is only used to make a gold helmet, and golden bowl for the quests Between a Rock... and Legends' Quest respectively.

A frequently occurring item, gold ore can be acquired through various means, beyond mining. It can be bought from shops, obtained from monster drops and pick-pocketing, as a reward from a variety of chests and reward crates, through the Gnome Restaurant and Volcanic Mine minigames, and can also be obtained by handing in nuggets to Terry Balando at the Digsite.

label: Gold ring
title: Gold ring
lead:
A gold ring can be worn in the ring slot, but does not give bonuses and does not provide any functions to the player, teleports or otherwise. Like all rings, they are not visible on player characters. They can be sold for up to coins to Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim.

Gold rings can be obtained as a reward from the Casket from the Pirate's Treasure quest, as a possible reward from the Capt' Arnav's Chest random event, from bird nests, from salvaging, or from crafting.

label: gold rocks
title: gold rocks
lead:
Gold rocks are a type of rock that contains gold ore; a Mining level of 40 or higher is required to mine them, granting 65 Mining experience for each ore mined. Once mined, a gold rock takes about a minute to respawn.

The Arzinian Mine, after completing Between a Rock..., and Crafting Guild, after completing the Hard Falador Diary, are the ideal places to mine gold.

label: Gold sink (interface item)
title: Gold sink (interface item)
lead:
The Gold sink is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Gold sink.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Gold-trimmed leather armour
title: Gold-trimmed leather armour
lead: Gold-trimmed leather armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as Leather armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from easy Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: Gold-trimmed monk's robes
title: Gold-trimmed monk's robes
lead: Gold-trimmed monk's robes are possible rewards from Easy Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to monk's robes.

label: Gold-trimmed studded leather armour
title: Gold-trimmed studded leather armour
lead: Gold-trimmed studded leather armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as Studded leather armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from easy Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: golden bowl
title: golden bowl
lead:
The golden bowl is a quest item used during the Legends' Quest. It is made by first smithing a gold bowl from 2 gold bars, granting 30 Smithing exp, and then giving it to Gujuo in the Kharazi Jungle to bless it, making it into a blessed gold bowl. The player must then head to the pond in the middle of the jungle, cut a hollow reed by using a machete on the tall reeds next to the pond, and use the reed on the pond to turn the bowl into a golden bowl containing sacred pure water.

Note: Filling an unblessed gold bowl from the Kharazi water pool will also create a golden bowl, but the examine information will reveal that the water is pure but no longer sacred. Filling a gold bowl or a blessed gold bowl with plain water from some other water source will likewise cause it to be renamed a golden bowl, but the examine information will reveal that the water is only plain water.

label: Golden candle
title: Golden candle
lead:
A golden candle is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a candle (extinguished) on the north-west Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used as a light source in a dark area. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

label: Golden feather
title: Golden feather
lead:
Golden feather or gold feather may refer to:

*Golden feather (Eagles' Peak), a quest item from Eagles' Peak
*Golden feather (Priest in Peril), a quest item from Priest in Peril
*Magic gold feather, a quest item from Holy Grail

label: Golden feather (Priest in Peril)
title: Golden feather (Priest in Peril)
lead:
A Golden feather is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a feather on the east Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used in Fishing or Fletching. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

title: Golden God (Raging Echoes League)/Calculators
lead: __TOC__
