label: Golden hammer
title: Golden hammer
lead:
A golden hammer is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a hammer on the north Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used in Smithing, Construction, or for opening the Bandos door in the God Wars Dungeon. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

label: Golden key
title: Golden key
lead:
The golden key is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is dropped by a hooded Level 30 Monk of Zamorak in the Paterdomus Temple.

It is used to open the first gate under Paterdomus after killing the Temple Guardian and then it is exchanged for the iron key by using it on the southern monument (the one referencing to "Saradomin being the key"). After unlocking the first gate for the first time, it is not required to be in the inventory to open the gate again.

label: Golden Monkey of Tee-Tah-Toh
title: Golden Monkey of Tee-Tah-Toh
lead:
at Marim, not the Golden Monkey of Tee-Tah-Toh]]
The Golden Monkey of Tee-Tah-Toh is a Karamjan artefact that was supposedly discovered by the archaeologist Asgarnia Smith. After the completion of Desert Treasure I, Smith will tell the player the story of his discovery. According to Smith, the artefact resided inside of a "spooky old temple" he happened upon one day in the middle of the Karamjan jungle. Covered in vines, Smith discovered a secret entrance to the temple, only to find himself surrounded by zombies and hostile tribesmen. After reportedly fighting his way through the corridors, all the while dodging various traps, the Golden Monkey of Tee-Tah-Toh was found sat on a great pedestal at the heart of the temple. Paying little heed to the archaeological provenience of the artefact, Asgarnia Smith at once lifted up the statuette from its original context, thereby triggering a trapdoor to open up beneath him, plunging him into a great dark pit below. A tribesman of significant proportion assaulted him, but was overcame due to Asgarnia hiding behind a nearby stalactite and shooting him down with a shortbow – a reference to the popular mechanic of safespotting. Though the archaeologist reports to have hidden behind a stalactite, which refers to a mineral formation that hangs from the ceiling, it is possible that he might have meant a stalagmite instead.

The temple mentioned in this account might be Rashiliyia's Tomb, which the player visits as a part of Shilo Village. Its entrance is similarly hidden deep in the Karamjan jungle and covered in vines, and is populated by traps and undead ones on the inside, which Smith might be referring to as 'zombies'. However, no tribesmen can be encountered there, nor does it seem to contain the pedestal the Golden Monkey rested on. The original location of the artefact may therefore very well be another temple hidden in the tropical forests of the island, perhaps not featured in-game.

label: Golden needle
title: Golden needle
lead:
A golden needle is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a needle on the south Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used in Crafting. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High Alchemy on it.

label: Golden pot
title: Golden pot
lead:
A golden pot is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a pot on the west Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used for storing any materials. However, players can cast Low Alchemy or High alchemy on it.

label: Golden tinderbox
title: Golden tinderbox
lead:
A golden tinderbox is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a tinderbox on the south-east Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It serves no purpose in the quest, and has no uses outside the quest, as it cannot be used for lighting fires. However, players can cast Low or High Level Alchemy on it.

label: Golden warbler (interface item)
title: Golden warbler (interface item)
lead:
The Golden warbler is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the Golden warbler

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Goldsmith gauntlets
title: Goldsmith gauntlets
lead:
Goldsmith gauntlets are one of the three possible glove rewards from Family Crest quest, along with Chaos gauntlets and Cooking gauntlets. They can be obtained by bringing the magical steel gauntlets (along with 25,000 coins) to Avan, who can be found in the Al Kharid mine (no cost if the gauntlets are still steel). The message "Avan takes your gauntlets, takes out a small hammer, and pounds them into a slightly new shape, then hands them to you." appears as this happens. The Goldsmith gauntlets increase the experience gained from smelting gold ore into a gold bar, from 22.5 to 56.2 experience — about 2.5 times as much as without the gauntlets.

Casting the Superheat Item spell on a gold ore while wearing the gauntlets gives 56.2 Smithing experience and 53 Magic experience.

label: golem
title: golem
lead:
The Golem is a quest centred around a golem and the desert city of Uzer.

Golem may also refer to:

label: Golem (attribute)
title: Golem (attribute)
lead: The golem attribute is assigned to monsters that are weak to golembane weapons.

label: Golem (Ruins of Camdozaal)
title: Golem (Ruins of Camdozaal)
lead:
A golem in the Ruins of Camdozaal is any of the following four types of golems:
* Flawed Golem, a level 13 golem.
* Mind Golem, a level 30 golem associated to mind runes and the Mind Altar
* Body Golem, a level 50 golem associated to body runes and the Body Altar
* Chaos Golem, a level 70 golem associated to chaos runes and the Chaos Altar (members only)
They can be found by awakening a pile of rubble located in the east and south-east section of the ruins. Each type of golem resides in a specific part; see the image to the right.

These golems are notable for dropping Runecrafting cores and the Barronite guard. This guard is a part of the Barronite mace, a weapon to which these golems are susceptible.

label: Golem (unused NPC)
title: Golem (unused NPC)
lead: The Golem is a cut race originally added during the RuneScape 2 beta. Although it was never added to the game, their appearance was reused for the Rock golem random event, while the concept was later recycled for the Clay golem.

label: Golembane weapons
title: Golembane weapons
lead:
Golembane weapons are a class of weapons that are more effective against golem-type monsters.

There are two golembane weapons currently available to players:

label: Gollwyn
title: Gollwyn
lead:
Gollwyn was an elf and soldier in Baxtorian's army that fought against Iorwerth's forces during the Baxtorian campaign.

In his book, Gollwyn's final statement, he describes the assault at the gates of Prifddinas by Iorwerth's forces, which resulted in the loss of more than half of Baxtorian's army, and how this led to him becoming lost in the Underground Pass. Unable to find a way out, he writes an apology to his son, Arianwyn, and soon succumbs to the voices (whispers from the fragment of Seren) drawing him to enter the Well of Voyage.

label: Golrie
title: Golrie
lead:
Golrie is a gnome found in the jail of the Tree Gnome Village dungeon. He is the grandson of King Bolrie and grand-nephew of King Bolren. He locked himself in a room to avoid some hobgoblins, but managed to leave the key to unlock the door elsewhere, outside the room. He was not planning on leaving until the hobgoblins departed, but does ask the player to help him solve his dilemma in the Waterfall Quest.

The key can be located by searching some crates on the east side of the dungeon, the crate is on the east side of the room as you first enter, and it is slightly a different colour than the others.

label: Gorad
title: Gorad
lead:
Gorad is an ogre who lives on an island north of Feldip Hills. He is killed during the Watchtower quest. He always drops the Ogre tooth required to get the second part of the Ogre relic. Upon killing Gorad, the Ogre tooth appears in your inventory and not on the ground, so you must have an empty inventory space to receive it.

Should you speak with him and insult him at any point outside the quest section for the ogre tooth, he will deal 12 damage upon the dialogue's completion (Note: if lacking sufficient hitpoints, the damage will kill you!)

label: Gossip
title: Gossip
lead: The Gossip starts the King's Ransom quest and is partially involved with Murder Mystery. He does not talk much to players. During King's Ransom, he provides important background history on the Sinclair family, as well as Anna Sinclair. He can be found just around the guard you speak to in Murder Mystery. When you speak to him in Murder Mystery, he will tell you that he saw a poison salesman who came in the village and gave a huge sale on poison to the family.

label: Gout tuber/Strategies
title: Gout tuber/Strategies
lead: Gout tubers are a rare seed and food obtained from Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup. A gout tuber is required to complete the medium Karamja Diary. Gout tubers are tradeable on the Grand Exchange, currently priced at coins, due to the diary requirement and how difficult they are to obtain.

label: Goutweed Crate
title: Goutweed Crate
lead: Goutweed Crates are crates that can be searched to obtain the herb Goutweed. The crates are located in the Goutweed store accessed from the stairs going down from the Troll kitchen, located within the Troll Stronghold.

label: Graahk hunter gear
title: Graahk hunter gear
lead:
Graahk hunter gear is a set of hunter gear made at the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, Pellem's Fur Store in the Hunter Guild and Prifddinas' Seamstress in Prifddinas, with either tattered or perfect graahk furs, and requires 38 Hunter to wear.

When the full set is worn, players will take 40% less damage from Hunter creatures. Contrary to popular belief, these do not improve catch rates of any hunter creatures.

label: Graahks brothers
title: Graahks brothers
lead:
The Graahks brothers are a group of graahks that responded to a letter in the 14th Postbag from the Hedge about why graahks don't jump over pits. The name is a reference to the Marx brothers, and while Chico and Groucho were members of the Marx brothers, Karl Marx was a philosopher who founded communism, and had nothing to do with the Marx brothers.

*Carl is a communist graahk that says that the graahks die in protest over injust government. He is a reference to Karl Marx.
*Chico pokes Carl in the eye during the letter, interrupting him. He is a reference to Chico Marx.
*Groucho is a comedian based on Groucho Marx.

label: Graceful outfit
title: Graceful outfit
lead:
Graceful clothing is weight-reducing gear that can be bought from Grace found in the Rogues' Den beneath The Toad and Chicken in Burthorpe. The pieces are bought at Grace's Graceful Clothing with marks of grace, which are obtained by completing Agility Courses and Rooftop Agility Courses.

While individual pieces of the graceful outfit will increase the rate of the player's natural run energy restoration (adding up to 20%), wearing the full graceful outfit gives an additional 10% bonus, giving a total of 30% increased natural run energy restoration. Note that other items, such as the boots of lightness, spottier cape, and penance gloves, reduce more weight than their graceful counterparts, but they do not grant the run energy restoration bonus. The Agility cape is an exception to this and can be used as a substitute for the graceful cape for the graceful set effect.

label: Grail
title: Grail
lead:
Grail may refer to:
*Crystal grail
*Holy Grail (quest)
*Holy grail (item)
*Grail bell

label: Grail bell
title: Grail bell
lead:
The grail bell is a quest item in the Holy Grail quest. It spawns just outside of castle in the Fisher Realm. When the bell is rung near the castle, a message will appear in the chatbox saying "Somehow you are now inside the castle." and the player will enter the castle.

Only one can be owned at a time; players cannot obtain another bell after completing the quest.

label: Grail Maiden
title: Grail Maiden
lead:
Grail Maidens are women who serve the Holy Grail. They can only be found in Grail Castle in the Fisher Realm.

They play a minor part in the Holy Grail quest, where they let the player inside the Fisher King's castle when the bell is rung.

label: grain
title: grain
lead:
Grain is obtained by picking from wheat fields growing in many places in RuneScape. They are also dropped by goblins and imps. It is used for Cooking. Six grain can be given to nearby gardeners to watch over flax grown in a hops patch.

One quick way is to get grain next to the hops patch in Yanille and go east to the bank in Yanille. Another is to use the canoe transport system on the River Lum. One could take the canoe to the Champions' Guild wheat field, then fill their inventory, then return to Edgeville to bank the wheat using the canoe. The wheat fields are also used to access Puro-Puro.

label: Gramophone (Sinclair Mansion)
title: Gramophone (Sinclair Mansion)
lead: Gramophone is a scenery object found in the Sinclair Mansion. Unlike the gramophone found in the witch's house in Taverley, players cannot interact with or play music from the gramophone.

label: Grand

*Grand Exchange
*Grand Library
*Grand Tree
*Grand seed pod
*The Grand Tree, quest
*Grand Tree Groceries
*Grand Hallowed Coffin

label: Grand Exchange Database
title: Grand Exchange Database
lead:
The Grand Exchange Database, very similar to this wiki's own Grand Exchange Market Watch, is a feature on the RuneScape website, allowing players, both free and members, to view price changes of a specific item over the previous 180 days.

There are many features in the Grand Exchange Database that resemble the stock market or the stock exchange. Examples are the price graph, and the scrolling prices in the Grand Exchange banner at the top of the page. While most people easily identify with the concept of a stock market, the Grand Exchange is actually a commodities exchange.

label: Grand Exchange/Non-tradeable items
title: Grand Exchange/Non-tradeable items
lead:
Non-tradeable items, in terms of the Grand Exchange, are items that are tradeable, but not on the Grand Exchange. These items must therefore be exchanged via the standard trading interface.

Because of this, it may be difficult to obtain significant quantities of these items. Although most non-tradeable items are quest-related items or otherwise low in value when sold to shops, certain players seek them for collecting purposes. An example of this is players collecting burnt food.

label: Grand Lord
title: Grand Lord
lead: The Grand Lord was a title given to the leader of Great Kourend after the signing of the royal accord of twill, the guidelines for Grand Lord were set by Lord Ethrain Hosidius I, Lord Seabry Shayzien, Lord Ret Piscarilius, Lord Solange Lovakengj, and Lord Bourath Arceuus. This titled was passed from lord to lord for 12 decades before King Shayzien III breached the accord, seizing control of Kourend with the military under his command.

label: Grand Tree
title: Grand Tree
lead:
The Grand Tree, or Ta Quir Priw in gnomish language, is home to a gnome community and is built inside a tree in the north-east of the Tree Gnome Stronghold. It contains Blurberry's Bar, Heckel Funch's Shop, Rometti's Fine Fashions, and Gulluck's weapon shop.

The Grand Tree includes two of the three banks in Tree Gnome Stronghold, several shops, and a bar and restaurant. The Gnome Restaurant minigame is on second level, and players who have completed The Grand Tree quest can access the Grand Tree Mine. There is an Agility shortcut north-east of the Grand Tree, which can be very useful for players training barbarian fishing.

label: Grand Tree Groceries
title: Grand Tree Groceries
lead: Grand Tree Groceries is a shop run by Hudo that sells food supplies used in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. It is located on the in the north-western corner of the Grand Tree.

label: Grand Tree mine
title: Grand Tree mine
lead:
The Grand Tree mine is an area in the northern part of the Grand Tree Tunnels and is only accessible after The Grand Tree quest. Players can enter the mine after the quest by pushing the roots that block access from the central area. No axe or other equipment is required to push the roots aside.

Within the mine lie two slightly separated mining areas, one to the east and one to the west.

label: Grand Tree Tunnels
title: Grand Tree Tunnels
lead: The Grand Tree Tunnels is a dungeon located beneath the Grand Tree and is only accessible during and after The Grand Tree quest.

label: Grandfather Clock
title: Grandfather Clock
lead: Grandfather clocks are found in many places across Gielinor, often in larger houses.

label: Grandpa Jack
title: Grandpa Jack
lead:
Grandpa Jack tells the player about his fishing experiences during the quest Fishing Contest, revealing how to win the contest. He lives in the house slightly north-east of Hemenster where a glassblowing pipe respawns.

He will also sell you his "competition winning" fishing rod for 5 coins, however it has no special properties and is just a regular rod.

label: Granite equipment
title: Granite equipment
lead:
Granite equipment is a set of equipment made from granite. They are members only items. As most pieces of the granite set are dropped only by monsters which require medium-high Slayer levels to kill and are fairly rare drops, many players choose to simply buy the set rather than attempting to obtain the items as drops.

To wear pieces of granite armour, 50 Defence and 50 Strength are required; 50 Attack and 50 Strength are needed to wield the granite weapons. Granite armour and weapons are also notable for being much heavier than other pieces of equipment (Granite platelegs have a mass of 15 kg, compared to rune platelegs which have a mass of 9 kg).

label: granite shield
title: granite shield
lead:
The granite shield is a shield made of granite. It requires 50 Defence and 50 Strength to equip. It has defensive stats equal to the Toktz-ket-xil, minus the +5 strength bonus, and isn't commonly used for melee combat as a result.

It can be used in place of the rune kiteshield due to its superior ranged defence bonus. However, some players choose not to use it due to its weight and slightly lower melee defence bonuses.

label: Grapes
title: Grapes
lead:
Grapes can be produced through planting grape seeds at the Hosidius Vinery, requiring level 36 in Farming. They are also dropped in noted form by several bosses. They can also be obtained from the Vineyard foreman in Aldarin by harvesting his Grapevines for him.

They are an ingredient for making a jug of wine at level 35 Cooking by using them on a jug of water, which grants 200 Cooking experience when fermented after a short period. If fermentation fails, a jug of bad wine will be created instead. Players stop creating jugs of bad wine when they reach 68 Cooking.

label: Graphical updates
title: Graphical updates
lead:
Graphical updates are updates that change the appearance of non-player characters, monsters, items, chatheads, and animations from one version to another. Despite the old-school graphics of Old School RuneScape, many graphical updates have occurred, particularly with new content since its launch being updated.

Graphical updates mostly occur due to player feedback, and are often updated after having the items/NPC's graphic update pass a poll. On occasion, Jagex may implement graphical updates without a poll due to player feedback, such as the fire max cape and Cerberus' summoned souls, or to fix graphical issues caused by clipping or a model's polygon count, such as the Fremennik sea boots, druidic wreath, and the malediction ward (or).

label: Graphical updates (historical)
title: Graphical updates (historical)
lead:
Graphical updates are updates that change the appearance of non-player characters, monsters, items, chatheads, and animations from one version to another. While Old School RuneScape is noted for the older graphics used, there have been numerous graphical updates since the release of RuneScape 2, starting with a graphical update of Lumbridge in 2005. By the time of the August 2007 Archive of RuneScape, the process of graphically updating and reworking free-to-play content had been mostly completed.

The following is a list of graphical changes that occurred between January 2005 and August 2007 that, while consistent with the style, have never been present in Old School RuneScape.

label: Grapple

lead: Grapple may refer to one of the following:

label: Grasp spells
title: Grasp spells
lead:
Grasp spells are a category of offensive spells in the Arceuus spellbook. Requiring completion of A Kingdom Divided to use (excluding Ghostly Grasp), these spells deal damage and provide a chance to stop the target from moving for a short time; streak marks mid-animation indicate a successful bind on the target.

The bind chance of a grasp spell is doubled if the Mark of Darkness spell is active, though this will not increase the duration of the bind. However, if the target is under the effect of the Ward of Arceuus spell, they will only be bound in place for 0.6 seconds if successfully bound by the caster. Note that the chance to bind an opponent is only provided upon a successful hit, which means that a bind will not be rolled for if a grasp spell fails the accuracy roll.

label: Grass
title: Grass
lead: Grass is a common piece of decorative scenery, found across the surface of Gielinor. Examinable grass scenery is widespread in Morytania, but can also be found in patches atop Trollheim, near Land's End, and on Crandor.

label: Grassland habitat (interface item)
title: Grassland habitat (interface item)
lead:
The Grassland habitat is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Grassland habitat.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Grave marker
title: Grave marker
lead: Grave markers are mostly found in the many graveyards of Gielinor. Players cannot interact with the markers, but they can examine them.

label: Grave of Scorpius
title: Grave of Scorpius
lead:
The Grave of Scorpius, also known as the Shrine of Scorpius, is found south of West Ardougne in some crumbling ruins atop a hill. Here the Spirit of Scorpius lurks around his gravestone. There are also some ghosts, grave scorpions, and dead trees, as well as thirteen bone spawns. The Shrine has a Celtic cross on it. The Ourania Cave (and Ourania Altar) is found north of the grave.

By talking to Scorpius, players can get an Unholy mould and have their Unholy symbols blessed. A ghostspeak amulet is not needed to talk to Scorpius, but he will only talk to players who have "seen beyond the stars" (finished the Observatory Quest).

label: Grave scorpion
title: Grave scorpion
lead: Grave scorpions are low-level monsters found by the Grave of Scorpius, south of West Ardougne. It is worth noting that their hitpoints are lower than standard scorpions, so they may be useful to kill if the player wants to finish a Slayer task of scorpions quickly.

label: Gravedigger outfit
title: Gravedigger outfit
lead:
The Gravedigger outfit was a holiday reward received from the 2015 Halloween event. The costume gives no bonus to any stats. Its appearance changes depending on gender.

This costume is the undead version of Leo, the Gravedigger random event starter.

label: Gravestone (Draynor Manor)
title: Gravestone (Draynor Manor)

label: Graveyard of Shadows
title: Graveyard of Shadows
lead: The Graveyard of Shadows, located at levels 18–21 in the Wilderness, occupies a section of what was once the Zarosian fortress of Carrallanger. This area is a large, seemingly forgotten graveyard filled with dead trees, wandering zombies, and derelict gravestones. Within the graveyard lies the Skeletal Tomb, the lair of Calvar'ion.

label: Great Carpet Crash of '76
title: Great Carpet Crash of '76
lead:
The Great Carpet Crash of '76 was an incident that resulted in the death of the Sultan of Al Kharid. The exact date is unknown but is likely to be the very late Fourth Age, since the only year ending in 76 in the Fifth Age is 76 itself, which is precluded by the apostrophe.

The crash occurred when the Sultan, looking forward to riding his racing Magic Carpet, accidentally took an unenchanted doormat from the floor of his chamber. After jumping from a high tower of Al Kharid palace, he fell to his death, a loss that shook Al Kharid. The people of the city called upon a ban on magic carpets, and although this was never written down as law, magic carpets fell from use for many years. Only a century and a half into the Fifth Age did they resurface under the direction of the famed merchant Ali Morrisane.

label: Great fire of '86
title: Great fire of '86
lead:
The great fire of '86 was a major conflagration that occurred at the royal library of the Varrock Palace, and was later recounted by the current palace librarian, Reldo, in a letter published in the Postbag from the Hedge. The exact date of the incident is unclear, but the fire is likely to have swept the castle at some point during the late Fourth Age, since the only year ending in 86 in the Fifth Age is the year 86 itself, which is presumably precluded by the presence of an apostrophe.

According to Reldo, a neglectful cataloguing system is ultimately to be blamed for sparking the great fire, which ignited after a small collection of works on spontaneous combustion was carelessly placed right next a "rather lively tome on literary sentience" on the library shelves. This characterisation of the latter tome as being unusually animated implies that it didn't merely contain a discourse on textual consciousness, but had become a conscious text itself. Although the terse account of events given by Reldo leaves it up to the reader to fill in the blanks, it is likewise implied that the tome then learned about the intricacies of self-immolation by studying its adjacent volumes, and consequently acted on that knowledge.

label: Great Kourend quest series
title: Great Kourend quest series
lead: The Great Kourend quest series is a series of quests involving various events surrounding the kingdom of Great Kourend.

title: greater demon
lead:
Greater demons are large demonic monsters. They are well known for their rune full helm and hard clue scroll drops.

K'ril Tsutsaroth, the Zamorakian general in the God Wars Dungeon, and his bodyguard Tstanon Karlak; Skotizo, the demi-boss in the Catacombs of Kourend; as well as Tormented Demons are considered greater demons for the purpose of a Slayer task.

label: Greatness
title: Greatness
lead:
Greatness is a music track that can be unlocked at locations outside Varrock city walls, including the Cooks' Guild, Champions' Guild, and Jolly Boar Inn. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Doorways, Expanse, and Still Night.

In Classic mode, this track plays near the Champions' Guild.

label: greegree
title: greegree
lead:
Greegrees are used for transforming into monkeys; however, their use is limited to the island of Ape Atoll, as Zooknock cannot use his magic over long distances (except for the Ardougne Zoo). When in monkey form, all monsters on the island become non-aggressive. Be advised that greegrees may not be equipped while in combat.

They are required during the Monkey Madness I and Monkey Madness II quests, as well as the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest. To begin making greegrees, the player must first obtain a monkey talisman by speaking to the Monkey Child on Ape Atoll while wearing a m'speak amulet. The talisman can then be enchanted by Zooknock with the remains of various monkeys and gorillas. Once Zooknock enchants this talisman, additional talismans can be bought from Tutab's Magical Market for each.
