label: Hanging banner
title: Hanging banner
lead: The Hanging banner is a heraldic banner found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The banner features a and three small symbols of Saradomin on the left, a large symbol of Saradomin in the centre, and a castle with two crossed swords below it on the right. Despite the banner depicting the symbol of Saradomin, multiple banners can be found in the Black Knights' Fortress, despite the Kinshra being Zamorakians. The coat of arms on the banner vaguely resembles the symbol of Lumbridge.

label: Hanging meat
title: Hanging meat
lead: Hanging meat is butchered meat hanging from a rack and can be found in various locations, but primarily kitchens and food shops. The meat has no functionality and exists purely for aesthetics.

label: Hanging skeleton (interface item)
title: Hanging skeleton (interface item)
lead:
The Hanging skeleton is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Hanging skeleton.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Hanging wheel
title: Hanging wheel
lead: Hanging wheels can be found in several locations over Gielinor that are somewhat connected to the sea, such as Port Sarim. Players cannot interact with the wheels, but they can examine them.

label: Hangman (interface item)
title: Hangman (interface item)
lead:
The Hangman is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Hangman.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Hangover cure
title: Hangover cure
lead:
A hangover cure is made by adding chocolate dust, obtained by grinding a chocolate bar down with a Pestle and mortar (or cut with a knife), to a bucket of milk, and then mixing in snape grass to the chocolatey milk. Hangover cure is used during the Plague City quest, in which the player must give one to Bravek, city warder of West Ardougne, found in the Civic Office of West Ardougne. Players may then obtain a warrant from him which will allow the player to enter the "plague-house" in the south-east corner of the city.

A hangover cure is also given to Skippy, a washed-up fisherman on the coast of Rimmington, in the miniquest Skippy and the Mogres. Once cured, he will explain the "creature" he saw in the water, which eventually turns out to be a mogre. This miniquest is required for players to kill mogres as Slayer monsters.

label: Hannibus
title: Hannibus
lead: Hannibus was a Dragon rider, who served Zaros near the end of the Second Age. When Zaros was betrayed by his general Zamorak, some of the Dragon riders remained loyal to Zaros, while others joined Zamorak's rebellion. Hannibus, however tried to remain neutral, by not declaring loyalty to either faction, despite still being branded as a traitor after fleeing from the Senntisten. His fate following after that is unknown.

label: Hans
title: Hans
lead:
Hans is the servant of Duke Horacio and can be found walking in circles around the Lumbridge Castle courtyard. He is easily scared, screaming and running away in fright when threatened. He can tell players how old their accounts are or how long they've spent online by talking to him.

Hans can also be spoken to by selecting "random contact" on the NPC Contact spell. If Hans is contacted, your character will claim you are a knight coming to kill everyone in Lumbridge Castle. Hans panics in response.

label: Happy Heroes' H'emporium.
title: Happy Heroes' H'emporium.
lead: Happy Heroes' H'emporium is a shop run by Helemos, who resides within the Heroes' Guild. As such, the shop can only be accessed after completion of the Heroes' Quest. This is one out of the two shops (the other being the Myths' Guild Weaponry shop) that sells the dragon battleaxe and dragon mace.

label: Hard leather
title: Hard leather
lead:
Hard leather is made by taking cowhides to a tanner. The lunar spell Tan Leather can also be used at level 78 Magic, and tans up to 5 cowhides at once into hard leather.

Combined with thread and a needle, it can be used to make hardleather bodies at level 28 Crafting, granting 35 crafting experience.
With a hammer and 15 bronze nails, members can attach two hard leathers onto an oak shield to create a hard leather shield. Doing so requires level 41 Crafting and grants 70 experience.

label: Hard mode
title: Hard mode
lead: Hard mode is a modified version of content that is meant to be more challenging than normal mode. The term is most often applied for boss encounters, and in most cases, completing hard mode gives more lucrative rewards. Several combat achievements are only completable in hard mode, and their kill count is tracked separately from other modes.

label: Hardcore group ironman armour
title: Hardcore group ironman armour
lead:
Hardcore group ironman armour is obtainable only by players who chose to be Hardcore group ironmen in Ironman Mode. It can be obtained by speaking to the Group Ironman tutor on The Node or from Adam after leaving Tutorial Island, after choosing to be a Group ironman. Players may obtain a new set by speaking to either of them if they lose their set.

The armour pieces share their stats with the iron full helm, platebody and platelegs.

label: Hardcore ironman armour
title: Hardcore ironman armour
lead:
The Hardcore ironman armour is a set of armour obtainable only by players who chose to be a Hardcore ironman in Ironman Mode. It is obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island, after choosing to be a Hardcore ironman. Players may obtain a new set by speaking to him if they lose their set.

The armour pieces share their stats with the iron full helm, platebody and platelegs.

label: Hardleather body
title: Hardleather body
lead: The hardleather body is low-level ranged armour. It may be equipped in the torso slot by players with 1 Ranged and 10 Defence. It provides better protection from melee, Magic, and Ranged attacks than the leather body and grants a modest boost to one's Ranged accuracy.

title: Harmony (music track)
lead:
Harmony is a music track that is unlocked when the player first arrives in Lumbridge. It can also be heard around the Lumbridge Swamp and farmlands. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Autumn Voyage, Book of Spells, Dream, Flute Salad, and Yesteryear. It can also be heard in the dining room during Recipe for Disaster.

In Classic mode, the track plays at Lumbridge Castle.

label: Harold

lead:
Harold is an off-duty Burthorpe Imperial Guard featured in the Death Plateau quest.

During the quest, players must converse with him, buy him drinks, and gamble with him until he is broke, forcing him to write an IOU letter with the only available piece of paper he had on his persons, which happens to have the combination on the back.

label: Harpoon
title: Harpoon
lead:
A harpoon is an item used in the Fishing skill. It can first be used at level 35 Fishing to catch tuna. Then, at level 50, you will begin to catch an array of tuna and swordfish. Eventually at level 76, you can harpoon sharks. Swordfish and tuna are caught in Cage/Harpoon fishing spots while sharks are caught in Net/Harpoon spots. Harpoons are also used at harpoon fishing spots on Tempoross Cove to catch harpoonfish when fighting Tempoross. It can be stored in a tackle box.

For pay-to-play players, wieldable alternatives, specifically the barb-tail harpoon and dragon harpoon, can be used. The dragon harpoon also has a 20% increased catch rate compared to other harpoons. Additionally, players can learn Barbarian fishing to do barehanded Fishing (48 Fishing, 15 Agility, 15 Strength to start/55 Fishing, 35 Strength to complete).

label: Harpoon (weapon)
title: Harpoon (weapon)
lead:
Harpoons are wieldable Fishing equipment that double as stab weapons. They are similar to swords, though notably weaker.

They are mainly used to free an inventory space for an extra Fishing resource, and rarely see use in combat.

label: Harralander
title: Harralander
lead:
Harralander is a herb that can be cleaned at level 20 Herblore. It can be obtained as a monster drop or through the Farming skill, with a level of 26, by planting a harralander seed in a herb patch. It is used to make Guthix rest potions, compost potions, restore potions, blamish oil, energy potions, Greenman's ale, combat potions, harralander tar and goading potions. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a harralander potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, harralander naturally grows on rocky crevices, and upon reaching maturity, its root system often causes large cracks to form in the rock.

label: Harralander potion (unf)
title: Harralander potion (unf)
lead: A harralander potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a harralander on a vial of water, requiring 22 Herblore. Using a volcanic ash on a harralander potion (unf) with 22 Herblore yields a compost potion(3) and 60 Herblore experience. Using a red spiders' eggs on a harralander potion (unf) with 22 Herblore yields a restore potion(3) and 62.5 Herblore experience. Using blamish snail slime on a harralander potion (unf) with 25 Herblore yields blamish oil and 80 Herblore experience. Using a chocolate dust on a harralander potion (unf) with 26 Herblore yields an energy potion(3) and 67.5 Herblore experience. Using a goat horn dust on a harralander potion (unf) with 36 Herblore yields a combat potion(3) and 84 Herblore experience.

label: Harry
title: Harry
lead: Harry is the owner of Harry's Fishing Shop, located in Catherby. He sells fishing equipment and a wide variety of raw fish. Harry also sells pet fish. Players may use a tiny net to catch one in his shop.

label: Harry's Fishing Shop.
title: Harry's Fishing Shop.
lead:
Harry's Fishing Shop is located in eastern Catherby. It is run by Harry. It is a convenient location for players because it is close to many Fishing spots. Players can sell their unwanted fish here.

Harry sells basic fishing equipment including small fishing nets, fishing rods, Harpoons, Lobster pots, fishing bait, and big fishing nets.

label: Hartigen
title: Hartigen
lead: Hartigen is a former member of the Kinshra. He deserted his position at the Black Knights' Fortress and sought new employment in Brimhaven as deputy for Grip, Scarface Pete's head guard. Hartigen was waylaid on his journey to Brimhaven by members of the Black Arm Gang who stole his Id papers. His current whereabouts are unknown, with his ID papers in the possession of Trobert.

label: Hartwin Prim
title: Hartwin Prim
lead: Hartwin Prim was a resident of Varrock in the Year 160 of the Fifth Age mentioned in the Varrock Census. According to the Varrock Census, he was a student. He may be related to Ethel Prim.

label: hasta
title: hasta
lead:
Hastae are one-handed melee weapons that are similar to spears with slightly lower stats. Hastae can be obtained either by trading with another player or using the Smithing skill. Most hastae (excluding the Zamorakian hasta, Gilded hasta, and Dragon hunter lance) can be poisoned with either normal weapon poisons or karambwan paste. They can only be wielded and created by those who have completed the Smithing portion of Otto Godblessed's Barbarian Training.

Due to their one-handed aspect and design hastae are similar to, but should not be confused with, the mjolnirs.

label: Hat
title: Hat
lead: Hats are head slot items in Old School RuneScape. They include cosmetic items, Skilling equipment, Treasure Trails, quest items, Achievement Diary rewards, Holiday and Event rewards.

label: Hat stand
title: Hat stand
lead:
Hat stands are pieces of furniture that can be found around Gielinor used to hold hats.
* Using most head-slot objects on the stand triggers a chatbox message Oops - it fell off the hatstand! and causes the item to fall to the floor.
* Most items with a destroy option instead produce It'll probably fall off if you do that., with the item staying in the inventory. Some destroyable items (including the progress hat and Shayzien helm) can be dropped.
* Using a ram skull helm on the stand gives the message That is too valuable to use here. What if it fell off?.
* Attempting to use a non-hat item on the hat stand gives the chat message You can't put that on a hatstand.

In the past, hat stands did not have the destroy restrictions. They were sometimes used to make the drop trick work for destroyable head slot items, including the hats from the 2005 Christmas event, bunny ears, and the ram skull helm.

label: Hats and scarves
title: Hats and scarves
lead:
Hats and scarves are untradeable cosmetic items. They can be obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Christmas. They come in four different varieties. If a player destroys or loses their hats and scarves, they can get replacements from Diango in Draynor Village.

During the Old School Q&A Livestream on 08/10/2016, the items were confirmed to be "warm", and thus allows the player to take less passive damage within the Wintertodt boss room.

label: Hattori Hanzo
title: Hattori Hanzo
lead: Hattori Hanzo is a weaponsmith from the Wushanko Isles. Little is known about them, besides that they are responsible for creating the katana that can be obtained from elite Treasure Trails.

label: Hauberk
title: Hauberk
lead:
Hauberk may refer to:

*Initiate hauberk, Temple Knight armour equipable after Recruitment Drive
*Proselyte hauberk, Temple Knight armour equipable after Slug Menace
*Inquisitor's hauberk, Inquisitor armour obtainable from The Nightmare

label: hay bale
title: hay bale
lead:
Hay bales are a form of interactive scenery found throughout many locations, especially near farms. Players can use a sack with a Hay bale or a haystack to get a hay sack, needed to craft a Scarecrow.

Hay bales can be searched with a 10% chance to find a needle. When this occurs, the player will say "Wow! A needle! Now what are the chances of finding that?" However, there is a 2% chance that players will get pricked with the needle, causing them to lose one hitpoint.

label: Hay bale (scenery)
title: Hay bale (scenery)
lead: Hay bales are decorative scenery found in many locations, especially near farms. Unlike the searchable hay bales, these hay bales cannot be searched to find needles despite the examine text mentioning them. Most hay bales (besides variant 3) can be used as a source of hay by using an empty sack to produce a hay sack.

label: haystack
title: haystack
lead:
Haystacks are piles of hay found throughout Gielinor, especially on farms. If an empty sack is used on a haystack (or hay bale), a player will get a hay sack, which can be used for a scarecrow. One hay bale can be found just north-east of Draynor.

Haystacks can be searched, often resulting in nothing. However, there is a 10% chance that players will find a needle. When this occurs, the player will say "Wow! A needle! Now what are the chances of finding that?" However, there is a 2% chance that players will get pricked with the needle, causing them to lose one hitpoint.

label: Hazeel
title: Hazeel
lead: Hazeel is a Zamorakian Mahjarrat, featured in the quests Hazeel Cult and Secrets of the North. He was recently revived after having been defeated in the early Fifth Age.

label: Hazeel Cult
title: Hazeel Cult
lead:
Hazeel Cult is a novice quest that was released on 15 August 2002. It was the second quest to feature a Mahjarrat, and introduces Hazeel, a Zamorakian Mahjarrat that has been put into a state of torpor, and his followers are attempting to revive him in time for the next Ritual of Rejuvenation.

This quest is notable in that it has two sides, a "good" side and an "evil" side, sharing this trait with Temple of Ikov, another Mahjarrat quest. In the "good" side, the player foils the cultists in their attempt to resurrect Hazeel, and in the "evil" side, the player joins the cult and assists them in resurrecting Hazeel.

label: Hazeel Cultist
title: Hazeel Cultist
lead: Hazeel Cultists are followers of the Zamorakian Mahjarrat, Hazeel, located in the southern Ardougne Sewers. Accessing their location requires starting the Hazeel Cult quest and correctly turning the five sewer valves outside. The cultists are eager to resurrect their lord, which the player helps with or refuses.

label: Hazeel scroll
title: Hazeel scroll
lead: The Hazeel scroll is a scroll containing the incantation used to free Hazeel in the evil side of the Hazeel Cult quest. The scroll is located up in a secret room on the of the Carnillean Mansion in a locked chest which can only be opened with a chest key. It is used by Alomone to reconstruct Hazeel's body.

label: Hazeel's mark
title: Hazeel's mark
lead: Hazeel's mark is a quest item from the quest Hazeel Cult. The item is only obtained when you choose Hazeel's side. It does not give any stat bonuses and is not used in any other quests.

label: Hazelmere
title: Hazelmere
lead:
Hazelmere is a gnome who lives on the Yanille Chain just east of Yanille. Hazelmere was the last surviving creator of the Grand Tree, a massive living fortress within the Gnome Stronghold. He was also an accomplished battle mage, the third advisor to King Healthorg, tree whisperer, soothsayer, and telepath with a great knowledge of history and culture. Hazelmere plays a prominent role in The Grand Tree, The Eyes of Glouphrie, The Path of Glouphrie, and While Guthix Sleeps quests.

There is a fairy ring near his house, the code being .

label: Hazelmere's scroll
title: Hazelmere's scroll
lead:
Hazelmere's scroll is an item used during The Grand Tree. Players obtain it by using the bark sample on Hazelmere. Hazelmere writes on the scroll in gnome language, and gives it to the player.

Players must then deliver this message back to King Narnode Shareen.

label: HD
title: HD
lead:
HD may refer to:

*The upcoming Official HD Mode.
*The 117 HD plugin for RuneLite, which enhances graphics within the RuneLite client.
*HDOS, a third-party client that offers high-definition graphics meant to emulate the era of RuneScape HD.

label: HDOS
title: HDOS
lead:
HDOS, or High-Detail Old School, is a closed-source third-party client for Old School RuneScape. It is one of two non-Jagex clients on the approved client list that players are permitted to use, along with RuneLite. When installed, HDOS can be launched as a standalone client or through the official Jagex Launcher.

The stated goal of HDOS is to emulate the era of RuneScape HD that was originally released 1 July 2008.

label: Head
title: Head
lead:
Head may refer to:

*Ensouled heads, used for reanimation spells
*Head (Temple Trekking), monster fought during Temple Trekking
*Head (Temple of the Eye), seen on the ocean floor near the Temple of the Eye
*Heads dropped by slayer or boss monsters for stuffing as trophies:
** 
** 
** 
** 
** 
** 
** 
** 
**

label: Head (disambiguation)
title: Head (disambiguation)
lead:
__NOTOC__
The term "Head" may refer to any of the following:

label: Head chef
title: Head chef
lead:
The Head Chef is the head of the Cooks' Guild between Varrock and Barbarian Village. He will allow entrance to those with a Cooking level of 32 and wearing a chef's hat.

As the master of Cooking, he sells the Cooking cape for , along with a matching hood to players who have achieved 99 Cooking.

label: Head Guard (Fight Arena)
title: Head Guard (Fight Arena)
lead: The Head Guard is a guard found in the Fight Arena and is involved in the quest of the same name. Players must get him drunk with a Khali brew during the quest and steal the Khazard cell keys from him.

label: Head Mourner
title: Head Mourner
lead:
The head mourner is an elf pretending to be the leader of the mourners in West Ardougne. This is presumably because the real head mourner, Essyllt is located in the underground headquarters near the Mourner Tunnels.

He claims to work for King Lathas to keep the West Ardougne plague in check. He has the same authority as city warder Bravek and is mostly in charge of the "official" paperwork and administration, whereas the real head mourner leads the mining operations to the Temple of Light by slaves from the city.

label: Head slot table
title: Head slot table
lead: Click a column header icon to sort the table by that column. Use SHIFT click to sort by multiple columns.

label: Head Thief
title: Head Thief
lead: The Head Thief is the leader of a small band of thieves that operate in the Kandarin area, just south of Ardougne. The thief and his group are involved in the Monk's Friend quest, where it is revealed that they have stolen a Child's blanket from one of the monks' sons. When infiltrating the thieves' lair to retrieve the blanket, the Head Thief can be found guarding the blanket, though you do not need to fight him to complete the quest.

label: Headband
title: Headband
lead:
A headband is a members-only headwear item. There are no requirements for wearing headbands, and they do not confer bonuses upon the player. To obtain headbands, the player can either trade with another player or receive one as medium Treasure Trails reward. Headbands can be stored in the costume room of a player-owned house.

There are eight colours of headbands:

label: Headless
title: Headless
lead:
Headless may refer to one of the following:
* Headless arrow, an arrow shaft with feathers
* Headless head, a Halloween event reward
* Headless Beast, a quest boss in Getting Ahead
** Headless Beast (Nightmare Zone), the version fought within the Nightmare Zone

label: headless arrow
title: headless arrow
lead:
A headless arrow is used in Fletching to make arrows. Attaching 15 feathers to 15 arrow shafts, requiring 1 Fletching, yielding 15 Fletching experience and 15 headless arrows. 15 arrowtips can be attached to headless arrows to make arrows.

There are several item spawns of headless arrows in the Scorpion Pit, deep in the Wilderness.

label: Headquarters
title: Headquarters
lead:
Headquarters may refer to:

* KGP Headquarters, located within the Iceberg during Cold War
* Kualti Headquarters, located in Varlamore
* Mourner Headquarters, located in West Ardougne (requires partial completion of Biohazard)

label: Healer
title: Healer
lead:
Healer may refer to:
* Yt-HurKot, the creature which heals TzTok-Jad in the TzHaar Fight Cave and JalTok-Jad in the Inferno and TzHaar-Ket-Rak's Challenges
* Jal-MejJak, the creature which heals TzKal-Zuk in the Inferno
* Penance Healer, the creature encountered in the Barbarian Assault minigame
* The Healer role in Barbarian Assault, tasked with killing the Penance Healers

label: Healers (disambiguation)
title: Healers (disambiguation)
lead:
Healers may refer to:

* Penance healers, a monster fought during Barbarian Assault
* Yt-HurKot, monsters which heal when a Jad reaches half health, and begin to heal him
* Jal-MejJak, monsters which heal TzKal-Zuk when it reaches 20% health for the first time

label: Heart
title: Heart
lead:
Heart can refer to:
* , an item dropped by Porazdir during Mage Arena II, used to upgrade the relevant God capes.
* , a quest item created during Legends' Quest using parts obtained from the three undead knights in the Viyeldi caves.
* , the third quest in the Twilight Emissaries series.
* , an item required for building the crystal extractor.
* , an item dropped by hydras and the Alchemical Hydra, used in creating the brimstone ring.
* , a magic-boosting item dropped by superior Slayer monsters.
* , the imbued heart's upgraded variant.
* , a single-use stat boost item dropped by tormented demons.

label: Heart (disambiguation)
title: Heart (disambiguation)
lead: Heart may refer to:

label: Heart and Mind
title: Heart and Mind
lead: Heart and Mind is a music track that is unlocked inside the Body Altar, which is south of the Edgeville Monastery.

label: Heart crystal
title: Heart crystal
lead:
The heart crystal is a quest item used in the Legends' Quest. It's created by killing the three knights Ranalph Devere, Irvig Senay and San Tojalon in the Viyeldi caves dungeon within Kharazi Jungle to obtain a lump of crystal, a hunk of crystal and a chunk of crystal respectively, which can then be combined to form the heart crystal by using them on the furnace. Once combined, the crystal must be activated by using it on the mossy rock in the caves, before it can be used on the recess in order to fill it, which deactivates the Shimmering fields.

It is not possible to obtain the heart fragments after filling the recess, or while in possession of a either a heart crystal or a knight's respective piece drop, even if stored within the bank or the nearby furnace. However, duplicate parts as well as the full crystal can be obtained before this point in Legend's Quest by utilising the drop trick. If the player does this, they are able to create multiple (albeit useless) heart crystals even after completing the quest.

label: Heather (scenery)
title: Heather (scenery)
lead: Heather is non-interactable scenery found across Gielinor.

label: Heavy Ranged weapons
title: Heavy Ranged weapons
lead: Heavy ranged weapons typically use slower, higher hitting attacks than other ranged weapons, although faster hitting Chinchompas are also heavy ranged weaponry. The most common heavy ranged weaponry in use is crossbows.

label: Heckel Funch
title: Heckel Funch
lead:
Heckel Funch is a shopkeeper who sells ingredients for gnome cooking. His shop, Funch's Fine Groceries, is on the east side of the Grand Tree on the , near Blurberry's Bar.

Heckel sells various ingredients from drinks (vodka, whiskey etc.) to fruits and berries. Players can also buy pineapples from there that can be used in the farming skill to create supercompost.

label: Hedge
title: Hedge
lead: Hedges are common decorative scenery found in many locations across Gielinor. During the quest Witch's House, if the hedge is in between the player and the witch, she will not be able to see the player. The same is also true for the guards in Ratcatchers.

label: Hefin Clan
title: Hefin Clan
lead: The Hefin Clan is one of the eight elven clans who were originally brought to Gielinor from Tarddiad by Guthix and Seren in the early First Age. They are a clan of spiritualists skilled in Prayer and Agility. They are located north-west of the Tower of Voices in Prifddinas, off the northern path.

label: Hekala
title: Hekala
lead: Hekala was the dragon steed of Ablenkian, a dragon rider. During the Second and Third Age the pair served Zaros loyally and had saved many of their allies in conflicts. During the battle of Carrallanger in the early Third Age, Ablenkian rode Hekala into battle, saving Corveth from a burning tower. Eventually however, this led to her demise, as Corveth would later betray Ablenkian.

label: Helemos
title: Helemos
lead: Helemos is a retired adventurer and the owner of Happy Heroes' H'emporium., a shop located on the of the Heroes' Guild which sells dragon battleaxes and dragon maces exclusively. When talked to, he begins by welcoming the player to the Heroes' Guild.

label: Hell
title: Hell
lead:
Hell may refer to:

*Hellcats, a type of cat players can obtain after starting the Evil Dave section of Recipe for Disaster
*Hellhounds, monsters commonly fought for hard clue scrolls or Slayer tasks
*Hell-Rats, a type of rat caught in Evil Dave's basement of doom
*Hells Bells, a music track
*The Infernal Dimensions (also known as Infernus), the demon homeworld
**Abyssal Space, a plane home to some demons

label: hellhound
title: hellhound
lead:
Hellhounds are monsters that are often given as a Slayer task to mid-to-high level players. Hellhounds are primarily killed for their hard clue scroll drops, as they drop them at a much higher rate compared to most other non-boss/superior monsters.

In order to be assigned them as a slayer task, the player must have 75 combat (unless it is not counted). Players with 91 Slayer may also kill Cerberus as an alternative to a hellhound task. Other alternatives include the skeleton hellhounds from Calvar'ion and Vet'ion, or reanimated hellhounds spawned by using Expert Reanimation on an ensouled hellhound head.

label: Hellhound (disambiguation)
title: Hellhound (disambiguation)
lead:
Hellhound may refer to:

* Hellhound, the regular Slayer monster

label: Hellhound (interface item)
title: Hellhound (interface item)
lead:
The Hellhound is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the hellhound.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Helm
title: Helm
lead:
Helms are a core boat part used in shipbuilding in the Sailing skill. Players can use the "navigate" option of the helm to control the ship they're on, which changes the control scheme from click-pathing to move the player, to a heading selector which changes the boat's travel direction. An "escape" option is also present on the helm, which allows players to evacuate the boat and return to their docked port.

There are helms of each smithable metal that are crafted with bars, as well as a dragon helm that requires dragon metal sheets to make. Helms require specific Sailing and Construction levels to create, and can be attached to any tier of boat. They are built at the Shipyard by interacting with the boat schematics boards.

label: helmet
title: helmet
lead:
A helmet is a piece of equipment that protects player's head. There are many helmets in Old School RuneScape. A helmet may refer to:

*Metal helmets:
**Medium helmets
**Full helmets

label: Helmet Shop.
title: Helmet Shop.
lead: The Helmet Shop is a shop run by Peksa located in central Barbarian Village. The shop offers medium and full helmets ranging from bronze to adamant, with the exception of black helms. It is the only shop in the Barbarian Village. The shop also contains a permanent fire.

label: Helmet shops
title: Helmet shops
lead: Helmet shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Helmet shops sell assorted helmets, such as medium helmets, full helmets and Fremennik helmets. There are 3 dedicated helmet shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Hemenster
title: Hemenster
lead: Hemenster is a small fishing town in Kandarin, located on the road between Seers' Village and East Ardougne.

label: Hendry Jamison
title: Hendry Jamison
lead: Hendry Jamison was a citizen of Varrock in the year 160. According to the Varrock Census, Jamison was a bartender.

label: Hengrad
title: Hengrad
lead: Hengrad is a prisoner found in the Fight Arena. He plays a minor role in the Fight Arena quest, where he reveals that General Khazard captured him when he was just a child and he has survived the arena for almost all his living years.

label: Henryeta Carnillean
title: Henryeta Carnillean
lead: Lady Henryeta Carnillean is the wife of Sir Ceril Carnillean, a wealthy nobleman of Ardougne, and the head of the Carnillean family. Henryeta lives in Carnillean Mansion, in the south-western end of East Ardougne, where she features briefly in the Hazeel Cult. She and Ceril have a son, Philipe Carnillean, who is very spoiled.

label: Heraldic armour
title: Heraldic armour
lead:
Heraldic armour may refer to:

*Heraldic armour, reward from Treasure Trails.
**Black heraldic armour, equipment obtained from easy Treasure Trails and requiring 10 Defence
**Adamant heraldic armour, equipment obtained from medium Treasure Trails and requiring 30 Defence
**Rune heraldic armour, equipment obtained from hard Treasure Trails and requiring 40 Defence
*Painted heraldic armour, armour painted with heraldic crests in the Heraldry space of a Workshop in a player-owned house.
**Heraldic helmet
**Heraldic kiteshield

label: Heraldic armour (Treasure Trails)
title: Heraldic armour (Treasure Trails)
lead: Heraldic armours are cosmetic armour rewards from Easy to Hard Treasure Trails. Heraldic armour come in black, adamant, and rune varieties. The armour set only includes a helmet, platebody and a shield, whose stats are equivalent to the full helm, platebody and kiteshield of the equivalent metal. There are five different heraldic designs in total.

label: Heraldic crest
title: Heraldic crest
lead: A heraldic crest, also known as the player's family crest is the insignia used by the player to identify their family ancestry. Heraldic crests are primarily used as an extension of the Construction skill and do not play a role in any quests.

label: Heraldic helmet (Construction)
title: Heraldic helmet (Construction)
lead:
A heraldic helmet is a decorative steel, adamant or rune full helm. Players can paint them on a pluming stand, shield easel, or banner easel in a player-owned house if they have level 38 Crafting or higher and have been assigned a crest by Sir Renitee in the White Knights' Castle. Sir Renitee will not assign a crest unless the player has level 16 Construction or above. A player's first crest assignment is free, and it costs 5k to change their crest to another one. It should be noted that some crests have other requirements; such requirements are detailed below. Players can use a pluming stand in another player's house if they do not have one in theirs. The helmets have exactly the same stats as their regular counterparts.

If a player is killed by another player, the helm will convert into a steel/adamant/rune full helm if it is not protected upon death, depending on the helm the player used to make the heraldic helm.

label: Heraldic kiteshield (Construction)
title: Heraldic kiteshield (Construction)
lead:
A heraldic kiteshield is a decorative steel, adamant or rune kiteshield. Players can paint them on a shield easel or banner easel in a player-owned house if they have level 43 Crafting or higher and have been assigned a crest by Sir Renitee in the White Knights' Castle. Sir Renitee will not assign a crest unless the player has over level 16 Construction. A player's first crest assignment is free, and it costs 5,000 coins to change your crest to another one, however some crests have other requirements, detailed below. Players can use a shield easel in another players house if they do not have one in theirs. The shields have exactly the same stats as their steel, adamant or rune counterparts. These shields do not work for clues requiring heraldic armour.

If a player is killed by another player, the shield will convert into a steel/adamant/rune kiteshield if it is not protected upon death, depending on the shield the player used to make the heraldic kiteshield.

label: herb
title: herb
lead:
Herbs are items used to make most potions with the Herblore skill. There are many herbs, each of which have a "clean" and "grimy" state. Herbs must be clean to be used in potions. Players can clean grimy herbs, provided that they have the minimum required Herblore level (see below).

When making potions, players must combine a clean herb with a vial of water, coconut milk, vial of blood or potentially other finished potions before adding a secondary ingredient if necessary. The majority of herbs can be used to make more than one type of potion, the exceptions being guam leaf, marrentill, rogue's purse, and snapdragon.

label: Herb bowl (animation item)
title: Herb bowl (animation item)
lead: The Herb bowl is an animation item used during Herblore. It is temporarily wielded during animations where the player uses a pestle and mortar, and when creating potions. Aside from this, it cannot be obtained.

label: Herb drop table/Sources
title: Herb drop table/Sources
lead: The following is a list of monsters that access the herb drop table.

label: Herb patch
title: Herb patch
lead:
Herb patches are farming patches in which players can grow herbs. Currently, there are a total of 10 Herb patches. Herbs are primarily used in the Herblore skill. Most herb patches also have a compost bin, a tool leprechaun, an allotment, and a flower patch nearby. All herbs take approximately 80 minutes to fully grow. Each patch requires one seed to begin growing that herb type. A seed dibber is required to plant a herb seed (unless the player has completed the farming subsection of Barbarian Training) and a spade to harvest herbs.

Unlike allotments, there is no way to protect herbs from disease, except by using a disease-free patch. Players can check on herbs regularly and apply plant cure if necessary to save a diseased plant. Using the Lunar Spellbook, players can also cure diseased plants with the spell Cure Plant, and instantly check the status of all farming patches by casting the spell Geomancy. It is highly recommended to use ultracompost on valuable herb crops, as this will not only greatly decrease the risk of death, but also increase the minimum yield to 6 herbs per seed. Yield boosting equipment such as the magic secateurs is also highly recommended.

label: Herbert Dunwich
title: Herbert Dunwich
lead: Herbert Dunwich was an adventurer and the author of The weeping. He lived sometime during the God Wars and described himself as neutral towards the conflict, weary of the immense loss of life it had caused. The weeping recounts his experience with a mysterious weeping creature he encountered in a pit beneath the northern shore of Forinthry.

label: Herbert Spiccanspan
title: Herbert Spiccanspan
lead:
Herbert Spiccanspan was a resident of Varrock during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. According to the Varrock Census of that year, he was a street cleaner.

Herbert may be the cleaner found near Varrock's West bank.

label: Herbi Flax
title: Herbi Flax
lead:
Herbi Flax was a resident of Mort'ton, a small human settlement in southern Morytania. Flax lived during the town's final days in the recent Fifth Age, when an infectious plague from the Sanguinesti region wiped out the town's populace, putting them in a zombie-like state.

Herbi Flax and his assistant Liornish Stemplehair were amongst the first to research a cure for the plague, successfully creating multiple serums that could weaken or temporarily cure the plague. Flax also heard the legends of the power Flamtaer Temple, which he was very skeptical about, even though its power could be used to fight against the virus. Ultimately, though, his efforts failed, descending into madness at the hands of the plague and never finding an effective cure.

label: Herbiboar (interface item)
title: Herbiboar (interface item)
lead:
The Herbiboar is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter and Herblore skill guides.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Herblore
title: Herblore
lead:
Herblore is a members-only skill that allows players to make their own potions from herbs and various secondary ingredients.

Potions created with the Herblore skill have a variety of effects. Most potions can be drank to give players temporary skill boosts or other status effects, such as antifire or antipoison. Effects of temporary skill boosts degrade at roughly 1 level per minute until the potion completely wears off.

label: Herblore Level Up!
title: Herblore Level Up!
lead: Herblore Level Up! is a Jingle for leveling Herblore.

label: Herblore Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Herblore Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Herblore Level Up! (Unlocks) is a jingle for levelling Herblore.

label: Herblore secondaries
title: Herblore secondaries
lead:
Herblore secondaries, or secondary ingredients, are items used in Herblore to complete potions. They are commonly used on an unfinished potion, with the "primary ingredient" being the herb used to create the unfinished potion. A small number of them can also be given to the Varrock Apothecary to create potions without the use of herbs.

Two rewards from the Mastering Mixology activity interact with Herblore secondaries: the reagent pouch is able to store up to 26 of each secondary ingredient in a single inventory space, while the prescription goggles give a 10% chance to save a secondary ingredient when worn while brewing potions, except when using crystal dust or lily of the sands.

label: Herblore shops
title: Herblore shops
lead: Herblore shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Herblore shops sell items used in the Herblore skill. There are 7 stores in Old School RuneScape.

label: Herblore training
title: Herblore training
lead:
Herblore training usually involves making potions which can only begin after completing the Druidic Ritual quest granting the player level 3 Herblore. To make a potion, the player will have to gather the required ingredients, usually a herb of some sort along with a secondary ingredient, and use them on a vial of water, blood, or coconut milk.

The fastest way to train Herblore is to add secondary ingredients to unfinished potions. If the player banks fairly quickly after each inventory of potions, they can expect to make around 2,500 potions per hour.

label: Herblore/Experience table
title: Herblore/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Herblore in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Herblore level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions.

label: Hermit
title: Hermit
lead: Hermit is a music track that is unlocked in Saba's cave during the Death Plateau quest.

label: Hero
title: Hero
lead:
Heroes can be found in East Ardougne. They wear what appears to be a lighter coloured rune platebody and platelegs. They also wear leather gloves, boots and wield a rune longsword and square shield. Heroes can be pickpocketed by players with level 80 or greater Thieving, which gives 163.3 experience plus coins or other items. Pickpocketing a hero is a requirement for the Elite Ardougne Diary.

They are often present near the marketplace in East Ardougne, or the south-east bank. One of them is also near the entrance of the Ardougne Zoo. Heroes attack players when they steal from the gem stall. They also attack when the player steals from a stall and tries to trade the stall owner. One of them is always near a bakery stall, so the player can easily steal food to heal from failed pickpocketing attempts. Unlike most thievable NPCs, players can be stunned frequently when pickpocketing heroes even at level 99 Thieving. A successful pickpocket attempt usually gains between 200 and 300 coins.

label: Heroes' Guild
title: Heroes' Guild
lead: The Heroes' Guild is located just south of Burthorpe. The guild is only accessible to members who have completed the Heroes' Quest. Dragon maces and dragon battleaxes can be purchased here, and amulets of glory can be recharged at the fountain in the basement of the guild.

label: Heroes' Guild mine
title: Heroes' Guild mine
lead:
The Heroes' Guild mine is a mine located in the basement of the Heroes' Guild. Players must have completed the Heroes' Quest to enter.

There are several non-aggressive giant bats, as well as a caged blue dragon. The nearest bank is in the Rogues' Den or the Warriors' Guild, though a teleport may be a better idea if using a Games necklace to return to Burthorpe.

label: Heroes' Quest
title: Heroes' Quest
lead:
Heroes' Quest is a quest that gives access to the Heroes' Guild in Burthorpe, by completing the guildmaster's rigorous initiation test.

Note: This quest requires another player to complete. Players may use the Grouping interface's "Join" button on the Shield of Arrav category to enter a chat-channel for finding a partner.

label: Herquin
title: Herquin
lead:
Herquin owns the shop Herquin's Gems in the city of Falador. He can be found in his shop south of the western Falador bank.

Herquin was visited during the 2018 Birthday event, helping the player with finding a semi-precious blue gem to use for their prop sword.

label: Herquin's Gems.
title: Herquin's Gems.
lead:
Herquin's Gems is located on the west side of Falador, just south of the west bank. It is owned by Herquin.

This shop only stocks one uncut sapphire and one sapphire; all of its other gems are stocked when players sell them to him. Because other players will usually pay more for gems than this shop will, players tend not to sell their gems to it and as such his shop is often empty.

label: Herring
title: Herring
lead: Herring is a type of fish that restores 5 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw herring on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 5 Cooking and granting 50 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt herring. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Herring is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 41, or 38 when using the Lumbridge range.

Hespori can be periodically killed in the Farming Guild, grown from a hespori seed.

label: Hetty
title: Hetty

label: Hickton
title: Hickton

The High Priest of Entrana is one of the most powerful holy men in the Saradominist religion. He plays a role in Desert Treasure I, a large role in Devious Minds, and minor roles in the Heroes' Quest and Holy Grail quests.

Players can also give him a holy sheet to obtain an unlimited supply of Saradominist paint.

In Classic mode, the track only plays around the Brimhaven town centre.

label: Highwayman
title: Highwayman
lead: Highwaymen are a level five NPC which are aggressive towards players below a combat level of 11. One will always exclaim when they target a player. Players with a Combat level below 11 are advised to quickly run past when encountering them.

label: Highwayman mask
title: Highwayman mask
lead:
The highwayman mask is a black mask similar to the ones highwaymen wear. It can be obtained from Easy Treasure Trails. Some players argue that it is very different, but when shown on a player while in game, they look almost identical to the ones worn by the NPC highwaymen. However, the only highwayman to be featured in chat is Rick Turpentine, who looks like the player in chat.

These masks, like many other accessories, do not give any combat bonuses. Players who have completed the Cabin Fever quest can take the mask and a Black cavalier to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless, and have them sewn together to create a Cavalier and mask for 500 coins. The highwayman mask can be worn along with a plain black Cape, brown Fremennik shirt, and Steel sword to resemble the highwayman himself.

label: Highwayman mask (unobtainable item)
title: Highwayman mask (unobtainable item)
lead:
The Highwayman mask is an unobtainable item that was added to the RuneScape 2 beta. It has an identical name and appearance to the Highwayman mask obtainable from Treasure Trails.

Its purpose is unknown, though it may have been accidentally added to the game early when the Highwayman mask's model was added to the level up screen for Thieving.

label: Hild
title: Hild
lead: Hild is a woman that lives in the small city of Burthorpe in the north-eastern corner. She has a small involvement in A Tail of Two Cats. She enchants the catspeak amulet for five death runes.

label: Hill giant
title: Hill giant
lead:
A Hill Giant is a type of giant found in several locations around Gielinor. For free-to-play, the Edgeville Dungeon offers the most spawns, while for members, the Shayzien Giant Pit also has numerous spawns. The Edgeville dungeon may be accessed through the entrance located in the house north-east of Barbarian Village and west of the Cooks' Guild if the player has a brass key. The Edgeville Dungeon area is usually very crowded in free-to-play worlds, as players like to gather big bones to bury them for Prayer experience. Another free-to-play hill giants area was added at the Giants' Plateau, near Al Kharid (located east of the Al Kharid General Store and Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar., east past the gap in the gate). They are aggressive to players below combat level 57.

There are two Hill Giants in level 17-18 Wilderness, but the area is unsuitable for training due to the possibility of player killers and its long distance from the nearest bank, found in Ferox Enclave.

label: Hit delay
title: Hit delay
lead:
Hit delay is measured in game ticks and is the amount of time an attack will be queued to an entity (player or NPC) without doing damage. Specifically, hit delay measures the amount of ticks an attack is processed on an entity without damaging it. Melee attacks damage an entity the very first tick that they are processed, and as such, are defined to have a hit delay of 0.

The hit delay of distance attacks is typically variable based on the between the entity dealing the attack and the entity receiving the attack. The distance is typically measured edge-to-edge in game squares, using the same edge for both entities. I.e. distance will be calculated using an NPC's closest edge to the player, and the player's furthest edge from the NPC. However, barrage spells are a notable exception in that they calculate distance from the player to an NPC's south-west tile, which causes abnormally long hit delay when attacking a large NPC from the north or east.

label: Hitpoints
title: Hitpoints
lead: Hitpoints (also known as "health" or "HP") represent a player's health. If they reach zero, the player will die. Hitpoints is the only skill for which players start with any experience initially - with 1,154 experience points, placing them at exactly level 10 on Tutorial Island.

label: hitsplat
title: hitsplat
lead: Hitsplat is a term used to refer to the damage icon appearing above a player, an NPC, or a monster, while in combat. A hitsplat usually results in the reduction of hitpoints. A splat of disease usually results in a loss of skill points, but can also affect hitpoints. All hitsplats have a number in the centre, which displays the numerical positive or negative effect on a player's hit points or skill levels.

They come in two variations outside of the God Wars Dungeon, with the level 28 variant usually unarmed and the level 42 variant wielding a spear, although some level 28 hobgoblins found north-east of the Vinery in Hosidius as well as one west of the Crafting Guild wield spears too. The narrow strip of land alongside the peninsula west of the Crafting Guild, and Tree Gnome Village dungeon (requires a key), contain many level 28 hobgoblins with no level 42 variants present.

It is crawling with several level 28 hobgoblins. On members servers, it spawns 3 snape grass in the sand pit near the end of the island. Some players gather the snape grass for a small profit, but since the peninsula is far away from a bank, this is not done by many players. The quickest way to get there is via the skills necklace teleport to the Crafting Guild.

label: Holgart
title: Holgart
lead:
Holgart can be found north of Witchaven near Caroline and Jeb, just outside of Caroline's house, and he sails the player to and from the Fishing Platform prior to the completion of Slug Menace after the player has helped him by repairing his boat with swamp paste. If players start The Slug Menace quest, he will no longer take them to the Fishing Platform as he is replaced by the sea slug-controlled Jeb since Mayor Hobb confiscated Holgart's boat and gave it to Jeb. As Holgart's skill is only sailing, he laments that he "don't know what to do without his boat".

Throughout the entire Sea Slug quest series, he is one of the few remaining villagers of Witchaven who is not possessed by sea slugs.

label: holiday events
title: holiday events
lead: Holiday events are special themed events released around the time of a special event or celebration. They are often quest-based, and will reward players with song tracks, themed items (also including ones from previous events of that particular holiday) and/or emotes. These rewards are usually unique to the event they were obtained from, including ones original to Old School RuneScape as well as historic ones from previous iterations of the game.

label: hollow reed
title: hollow reed
lead:
A hollow reed is an item obtained by using a machete or knife on the tall reeds in various areas: in the pure water spring in the centre of the Kharazi Jungle, at the start of the blessed River Salve near Paterdomus, and from the reeds found at a pool in the Kourend Woodland.

The reed is used during the Legends' Quest, where it must be used on the pure water spring in the Kharazi Jungle to obtain a golden bowl filled with pure water.

label: Hollow reed (unobtainable item)
title: Hollow reed (unobtainable item)
lead:
A Hollow reed is an unobtainable version of the Hollow reed. Reeds could previously be traded and turned into bank notes; however, they were made untradeable in 2007 due to frequent use in scams. Any player who had a noted Hollow reed was given this now discontinued item. Originally, it was identical to the real reed, except stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

It is possible to use the small bridges connecting the platforms as a safespot to attack using Ranged, Magic, or with a halberd. In the quest, the player must also kill the other demons, Othainian and Doomion.

label: Holy grail (item)
title: Holy grail (item)
lead:
The Holy grail is a quest item in both the Holy Grail and King's Ransom quests.

During the Holy Grail quest, the main objective is to retrieve it from a table on the of the east side of the Fisher King's castle in the Fisher Realm. During the quest, King Arthur informs you that it has just passed between dimensions into Gielinor. Should you choose to accept the quest and retrieve the Holy grail, you must travel to the Fisher Realm. If you attempt to take it before it's time, you will receive a message saying that you're not worthy of it. It is used to finish the quest by speaking to King Arthur while in your possession.

label: Holy Lake

lead:
The Holy Lake is a small body of water located south of Tai Bwo Wannai on the island of Karamja. It is the only place where karambwanji fish may be caught. The western end of the lake flows into a cave, on the other end of which it emerges into the Ardent Ocean. A number of hobgoblins can be found along the Holy Lake's southern shore.

The lake's name is only used by Lubufu the fisherman during Tai Bwo Wannai Trio.

label: Holy mould
title: Holy mould
lead:

They can be purchased from Rasolo, north-west of East Ardougne, Jamila's Craft Stall in Sophanem, Dommik's Crafting Store in north-eastern Al Kharid, or from Rommik's Crafty Supplies in Rimmington. An unlimited amount can be taken from a player-owned house tool store 4.

label: Holy symbol
title: Holy symbol
lead:
A holy symbol is an amulet donning the symbol of Saradomin. They are made by having an unblessed symbol blessed by Brother Jered in the Edgeville Monastery, or by blessing it via using a holy book or book of balance on an unblessed symbol at 50 Prayer, requiring a few prayer points. As Brother Jered is located on the upper floor of the monastery, blessing the symbol effectively requires a minimum of level 31 Prayer due to the entry requirement.

It has the third highest prayer bonus for an amulet in game (after god stoles and the dragonbone necklace). It is cheap, easy to obtain, and is commonly used in conjunction with Proselyte armour and other high prayer granting armour when using protect prayers as a form of defence while training.

label: Holy table napkin
title: Holy table napkin
lead:
The holy table napkin is a quest item obtained from Galahad in the Holy Grail quest. It is used to see the magic whistle spawn in Draynor Manor's top floor.

If the player wants to return to the Fisher Realm, it can be safely dropped if the player has access to fairy rings or keeps the magic whistle from the quest.

label: holy water
title: holy water
lead:
Holy water is a Ranged weapon that is used just like throwing knives and darts; however, it will only deal damage against demons. Throwing holy water will cause the vial to break, dropping smashed glass on the floor. This makes holy water a single-use weapon. Holy water is non-tradeable and has a +6 Ranged attack bonus when wielded. As a demonbane weapon, it has an attribute affinity for demons; the item's max hit is increased by 60% in a similar fashion to that of Silverlight. On top of that, it gains an additional +5 damage bonus if the demon is Nezikchened. Upon a successful hit, it will drain the opponent's Defence level by 5%, provided it is a demon. Multiple holy water hits will not stack their Defence reduction.

Holy water uses a different form of damage calculation compared to how regular maximum Ranged hits are determined, which ignores some factors that normally serve to increase Ranged damage. For instance, while boosting one's visible Ranged level will result in an increased maximum hit when using holy water, the use of stat-boosting prayers such as Eagle Eye or Rigour will not, nor does the set effect of Void ranger armour apply to holy water.

label: Home teleport
title: Home teleport
lead:
Home Teleports are spells that provide players with a free teleport every half an hour to a location dependent on the active spellbook. They require no runes but take 22 (or 18 with Speedy) ticks (around 13 seconds or 10 seconds with Speedy) to cast. The teleport can be interrupted at any time by most actions, including combat, and only can be cast 10 seconds or more after combat has ended (similar to logging out). If a player tries to cast a home teleport a second time before 30 minutes have elapsed, they are notified with the remaining time in minutes in the chat box. Free-to-play can only home teleport to Lumbridge.

This cooldown is shared with that of other home teleports. Switching spellbook will not allow you to use a different home teleport spell until 30 minutes has elapsed. However, the cooldown is not shared with Minigame Teleport.
