label: Hops (Biohazard)
title: Hops (Biohazard)
lead:
Hops is one of the three individuals used in the Biohazard quest to deliver the dangerous chemicals to Varrock. During Biohazard, you need to give him the sulphuric broline.

Prior to the quest, Hops can only be found near the Chemist's house in Rimmington, wandering back and forth and drinking. After the quest, he can be found in both Rimmington and the Dancing Donkey Inn in Varrock. He is always accompanied by his associates Da Vinci and Chancy.

label: Hops patch
title: Hops patch
lead:
Hops patches are used with the Farming skill to grow hops and barley used for brewing, and fibre crops used for spinning and weaving. Players can pay a nearby farmer to eliminate disease risk altogether, or alternatively use various types of compost and water the patch to reduce (but not eliminate) the chance of disease. The number of seeds required for hops patches varies; with fibre crops requiring 3, while hops and barley require 4.

Harvesting a plant grown in the hops patch tends to result in a relatively high yield, similar to most produce grown in allotments (see variable crop yield). At level 99, using both ultracompost and a pair of magic secateurs, a hops patch can be expected to yield 27 crops on average. Flax, Hemp, and Cotton may yield more/less (35/25/15 respectively) per sailing resource poll. After a hops patch has been harvested, the patch has to be re-planted. Hops on average give less experience in planting and harvesting than allotments. Hop plants are generally more susceptible to disease than herbs, although they are more hardy than crops grown in an allotment patch. Hops patches do not have a compost bin nearby but do have a Tool Leprechaun.

label: Horacio
title: Horacio
lead: Horacio Dobson is the gardener to Lord Handelmort, tending the grounds of his house in East Ardougne. He plays a minor role in the Tribal Totem quest.

label: Horizon
title: Horizon
lead:
Horizon is a music track that is unlocked in Taverley, or during the Bee keeper random event. In this area, the music area will shuffle between playing this track and Splendour.

In Classic music mode outside the Bee keeper random event, the music will play in southern Taverley.

label: Horn
title: Horn
lead: Horn may refer to:

label: Horogothgar
title: Horogothgar
lead:
The Horogothgar are a goblin tribe found while doing the Land of the Goblins quest, who wear purple goblin mail. Like the other tribes found in the temple, they were called upon by the god Bandos to fight in his name during the God Wars.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Eaters of Manflesh".

label: Horror
title: Horror
lead: Horror could refer to any of the following:

label: Horror (race)
title: Horror (race)
lead:
Horrors are emaciated ape-like creatures that can be found on the island of Mos Le'Harmless and inside the Mos Le'Harmless Cave. Jungle horrors can be found on the surface of the island, whereas cave horrors can be found inside the cave.

Their sizes and appearances reveal their ages and roles in their society. Younger horrors are smaller than the adults, and the workers are more plain looking. Jungle horror warriors have spikes on their backs and chins, and cave horror guards and alphas wear necklaces with bones on them. Cave horrors are stronger than jungle horrors, and they wear black masks, which enhance their howls into a magical sound which can only be protected from by wearing a witchwood icon.

label: Horse
title: Horse
lead:
from the 2018 Halloween event.|right|thumb|upright=0.75]]
The horse is a creature that does not exist. However, there are many in-game references to this mythical creature.

label: Horvik
title: Horvik
lead:
Horvik Ravitz is an armoursmith located north-east of the Varrock square. The building he is located in is called Horvik's Smithy, and is the owner of Horvik's Armour Shop.

During One Small Favour, he is asked by the player to create some chicken cages for Seth Groats. He does this in return for a herbal antidote, for his illness, and some pigeon cages to make the chicken cages from.

label: Horvik's Armour Shop.
title: Horvik's Armour Shop.
lead: Horvik's Armour Shop is located near central Varrock. It is operated by Horvik, and he specialises in selling chainbodies and platebodies. The shop is unusual because the building also houses an anvil. This makes it a convenient place for a player to sell armour as they smith it. By default, Horvik's stock consists of bronze, iron, steel, and mithril chainbodies; bronze, iron, steel, black, and mithril platebodies; and studded body and chaps.

label: Hosidius (disambiguation)
title: Hosidius (disambiguation)
lead:
Hosidius may refer to:

*The city of Hosidius

label: Hosidius house
title: Hosidius house
lead:
Hosidius house is a House style option for a player-owned house.

This house style can be used by owning the hosidius blueprints and requires level 1 Construction to use in a player's house. The blueprints are an untradeable reward from the Mahogany Homes minigame, requiring 2,000 carpenter points to purchase.

label: Hosidius windmill
title: Hosidius windmill
lead:
The Hosidius windmill is a windmill located in Hosidius, south of the city centre and north of the POH portal. The windmill can be used to grind grain into flour. There is a wheat field located directly south of the windmill.

On the of the mill there is a flour bin into which all the milled flour is poured. On the there are millstones, which grind grain to make flour. On the there is the hopper into which grain is put and the hopper controls which control the flow of the grain from the hopper to the millstones. To mill flour, a player will need grain and an empty pot to collect the flour.

label: Hosidius/Historical
title: Hosidius/Historical
lead:
Earning Hosidius favour can be done by helping with the production of farmed foods and preparing food for soldiers. Once you have earned Hosidius favour, you will gain access to both the city kitchens, which reduces the chance of burning food when cooking using their ranges by 5%, access to a new spirit tree patch, access to the Woodcutting Guild and Farming Guild, and the ability to play the Tithe Farm minigame, which focuses on gaining Farming experience.

To progress in the Architectural Alliance miniquest, players must gain 100% Hosidius favour and speak to Hosa by the statue in the Kourend Castle courtyard.

label: Hot Coals
title: Hot Coals
lead:
Hot Coals are a scenery object that can be found in the Port Sarim Jail and next to a Lovakengj Engineer at the Battlefront. They cannot be interacted with.

Based on their placements, the one in the jail is likely used to torture prisoners, whereas the one at the Battlefront is involved in smithing.

label: hotspot
title: hotspot
lead:
A hotspot is a pre-defined place to build a specific type of furniture in a player-owned house, Chambers of Xeric, or Mahogany Homes used in the Construction skill. Hotspot locations cannot be changed by players, unless the room is removed and rebuilt in a different way.

When the player is in Building mode, vacant hotspots appear as ghostly figures of the lowest piece of furniture that can be built there. Unbuilt hotspots do not appear while Building mode is OFF.

label: Hourglass
title: Hourglass
lead:
Hourglass may refer to:

*Hourglass (2014), an item from the 2014 Halloween event
*Hourglass (Recruitment Drive), a quest item from Recruitment Drive

label: House advertisement (interface item)
title: House advertisement (interface item)
lead:
The Advertisement noticeboard is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the House advertising board.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: House keys (interface item)
title: House keys (interface item)
lead:
The House keys is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide representing house keys.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: House party
title: House party
lead: House parties are parties that members can hold at their or someone else's player-owned house.

label: House styles
title: House styles
lead:
House styles are themes that may be applied to a player-owned house (POH). Redecorating a house will modify the appearance of the outside ground, walls, doors, windows, floors, and roofs of the house but will not affect the house's layout or content. Many of the styles reflect the architectural style of houses and buildings within various towns and cities throughout Gielinor, and each house style also has a unique musical jingle that plays upon entering the house.

Upon first creating a house, it will have a default style of Basic wood. Redecoration can be done by speaking to any estate agent, and usually requires a fee and a certain Construction level.

label: Hudo
title: Hudo
lead:
Hudo Glenfad is a gnome who operates Grand Tree Groceries. His store is located in the north-west corner of the in the Grand Tree, which is in Gnome Stronghold.

His store is essential for preparing the gnome cuisine dishes in the Gnome Restaurant minigame. He sells Gianne dough among many other food items. He is generally only used by players playing the minigame, although he provides the most food items of any food shop. On the players can find some tools in the Kitchen cabinet that needed to make Gnome cooking.

label: Hudon
title: Hudon
lead: Hudon is a child involved with the Waterfall Quest. His mother is Almera who is the starting point for the quest. He ran away from his mother's house to look for the treasure under the Baxtorian Falls. However, he is never rescued from the falls during the quest and cannot be rescued, despite this being the initial objective of the quest at first. If you talk to him after you finish the quest, he will claim that you stole his treasure.

label: Hueycoatl hide armour
title: Hueycoatl hide armour
lead:
Hueycoatl hide armour is a set of Ranged armour. All the pieces of armour require 70 Ranged to equip. Additionally, the body and head require 40 Defence to equip.

The pieces can be crafted from Hueycoatl hide, obtained from the Hueycoatl, requiring level 76-78 Crafting (boostable) depending on the item.

label: Huge Mushroom
title: Huge Mushroom
lead: Huge mushrooms are examineable scenery.

label: Huge spider (interface item)
title: Huge spider (interface item)
lead:
The Huge spider is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Huge spider.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Hull
title: Hull
lead:
The hull is a core boat part, used in shipbuilding to make boats for Sailing. The level of hull affects the ship's hitpoints, speed and defence, with higher-tier woods giving more health, faster movement and less chance to be hit.

They are built at the Shipyard by interacting with the boat schematics board.

label: Hull parts
title: Hull parts
lead:
Hull parts are a core ship part used to upgrade the hull of your ship while shipbuilding for Sailing. They can be made using a hammer and saw at a shipwrights' workbench, then used at the boat schematics board in the shipyard. There are two types of hull parts:
* Regular hull parts, created using five planks of the appropriate wood. These are used to upgrade or build the Skiff, with 10 of each hull part (for a total of 50 planks) for the complete hull.
* Large hull parts, created using five of the corresponding type of regular hull parts. These are used to upgrade or build the Sloop, with 16 of each large hull part (total 80 regular hull parts, or 400 planks) for the complete hull.

The raft is built by lashing together logs with rope, so it doesn't require hull parts.

label: Human
title: Human
lead: Humans are the dominant race of Gielinor. Humans can be found in almost every settlement in Gielinor and are responsible for the creation of many of the major kingdoms. Humans tend to worship a large variety of gods, most notably Saradomin, Zamorak, and Guthix, and have a level of intelligence which is lower than races such as gnomes and elves, but higher than goblins and other "brutish" races.

label: hunk of crystal
title: hunk of crystal
lead:
The hunk of crystal is a quest item used during the Legends' Quest. It is obtained by defeating Irvig Senay in the Viyeldi caves beneath the Kharazi Jungle. When combined with the chunk of crystal and the lump of crystal (obtained by defeating the other two warriors) at the furnace, they form the heart crystal required to unlock a door that leads further into the caves.

It is not possible to obtain the heart fragments after completing the quest; killing the knights again does not provide the player with the fragments. However, duplicate parts of the crystal can be obtained during the quest by utilising the drop trick. If the player does this, they are able to create another (albeit useless) heart crystal after completing the quest.

label: Hunter creatures
title: Hunter creatures
lead: Here is a full list of huntable creatures via the Hunter skill.

label: Hunter gear
title: Hunter gear
lead: Hunter gear is armour made with furs obtained from catching creatures with tracking or pitfalls using the Hunter skill. It cannot be crafted by players, instead requiring the use of the Custom Fur Clothing interface at the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock, Pellem's Fur Store in the Hunter Guild, or Prifddinas' Seamstress. It does not increase the chance of successfully catching creatures. It can provide warm clothing bonuses in Wintertodt.

label: Hunter meat
title: Hunter meat
lead:
Hunter meats are a type of food with the special effect of healing twice: once immediately and then again after 7 ticks (4.2 seconds). Some have additional effects beyond that, like restoring energy. Some hunter meats require having done a number of Hunters' Rumours to cook, though they can still be eaten regardless of rumours completed.

Not all meat obtained from the Hunter skill qualifies as hunter meat, only the specific meats listed below. Notably, bird meat is not a hunter meat.

label: Hunter pouch
title: Hunter pouch
lead:
Hunter pouches may refer to one of the following items, used to store items obtained from hunter creatures:
* Hunter fur pouches:
** Small fur pouch - stores up to 14 hunter furs
** Medium fur pouch - stores up to 21 hunter furs
** Large fur pouch - stores up to 28 hunter furs
* Hunter meat pouches:
** Small meat pouch - stores up to 14 hunter meats
** Large meat pouch - stores up to 28 hunter meats

label: Hunter shops
title: Hunter shops
lead: Hunter shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Hunter shops sell items used in the Hunter skill. There are 4 Hunter shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Hunter top
title: Hunter top
lead:
Hunter top may refer to:

*Desert camo top
*Graahk top
*Guild hunter top
*Jungle camo top
*Kyatt top
*Larupia top
*Polar camo top
*Wood camo top

label: Hunter training
title: Hunter training
lead: This guide describes the most effective methods to train the Hunter skill.

label: Hunter's mix
title: Hunter's mix
lead:
Hunter's mixes are consumable items created by using a jarred butterfly or moth with raw hunter meat, whilst having a pestle and mortar in your inventory. Cooked Hunter meats cannot be used. Upon creating the mix, the player will receive the following chatbox message: You mix the meat into the butterfly jar... Don't think too hard about it.

Each mix has two doses upon creation. Unlike barbarian mixes, Hunter mixes do not have an added healing effect, but in multicombat areas they apply the effect of the mix to the drinker and up to three players adjacent to them (who have Accept Aid toggled on). Hunter mixes share a 3 tick (1.8 second) consumption cooldown with potions, and do not incur an eating or attack delay.

label: Hunter/Experience table
title: Hunter/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Hunter in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Hunter level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: Hunters' loot sack
title: Hunters' loot sack
lead:
Hunters' loot sacks are an item rewarded from completing Hunters' Rumours. The loot sacks come in the following tiers:
* Hunters' loot sack (basic)
* Hunters' loot sack (adept)
* Hunters' loot sack (expert)
* Hunters' loot sack (master)

A hunters' loot sack (supplies) can be obtained by trading in uniques from the above sacks to Guild Scribe Verity.

label: Hunters' Rumours
title: Hunters' Rumours
lead:
Hunters' Rumours are unlocked at 46 Hunter after speaking to Guild Scribe Verity in the Burrow under the Hunter Guild. Players are assigned a rumour from a Guild Hunter which requires them to hunt a specific hunter creature until a rare creature part is received. When a player finds the rare part, a jingle is played and the player receives the message You find a rare piece of the creature! You should take it back to the Hunter Guild.

The quest At First Light offers an introduction to the Hunter Guild and unlocks the ability to complete Master Tier rumours at 91 Hunter, although no other tier of rumour requires completion of this quest.

label: Hunting expert (disambiguation)
title: Hunting expert (disambiguation)
lead:
Hunting expert may refer to:

*Hunting expert, the NPC who sells the Hunter cape.
*Hunting expert (Rellekka Hunter area)
*Hunting expert (Red chinchompa hunting ground)
*Guild Hunter Aco (Expert)
*Guild Hunter Teco (Expert)

label: Huzamogaarb
title: Huzamogaarb
lead:
The Huzamogaarb are a goblin tribe found while doing the Land of the Goblins quest, who wear black goblin mail. Unlike the other tribes found in the temple, they were sold to Zamorak and fought in his name during the God Wars. Despite their subservience to Zamorak in the God Wars, they appear to be worshippers of Bandos in the modern day.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Live-Flesh Eaters of the Chaos God".

label: Hybrid boots
title: Hybrid boots
lead:
Hybrid boots may refer to a few types of boots that provide positive stats for multiple combat styles:

* Aranea boots
* Boots of brimstone
* Fremennik sea boots 4
* Mixed hide boots
* Runner boots

label: Hydra (disambiguation)
title: Hydra (disambiguation)
lead: Hydra may refer to:

label: Hyeraph
title: Hyeraph
lead: Hyeraph is a term that appears in Sin'keth's diary. It appears to be a rank within the Dagon'hai. The only known person that was a Hyeraph is Sin'keth Magis who presumably went to on to become High Elder at a later date. The role seems to revolve around leading an incantation of some type, although the nature of it is unknown.

label: Hygd
title: Hygd
lead: Hygd is a citizen of Burthorpe. She tells the player a little of what is going on in the town.

label: Iain Hetherington
title: Iain Hetherington
lead:
Iain Hetherington was an audio developer at Jagex. He has composed pieces of music for Old School Runescape, making up
 % of all music in the game.

label: Ian Gower
title: Ian Gower
lead:
Ian Gower is the brother of Andrew Gower and Paul Gower. He helped create an early version of RuneScape, , in 1998. He did the graphics and three-dimensional modeling.

In addition, he originally did the conversion for the quests Goblin Diplomacy and Fight Arena. He also developed the Hunter skill, Haunted Mine, Recipe for Disaster: Freeing the Goblin generals and Eagles' Peak.

label: Iasor plant (interface item)
title: Iasor plant (interface item)
lead:
The Iasor plant is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide representing the Iasor plant.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Iban
title: Iban
lead: Iban is a former Kinshra knight and self-proclaimed son of Zamorak. He rules over the Underground Pass and is the primary adversary in the quest of the same name.

label: Iban (music track)
title: Iban (music track)
lead: Iban is a music track unlocked in Iban's lair during the Underground Pass quest.

label: Iban Blast
title: Iban Blast
lead:
Iban Blast is a combat spell that can be cast at 50 Magic while on the standard spellbook. Without Magic damage boosts, it can inflict up to 25 damage. Because of its very high max hit compared to other spells on the standard spellbook, it is often recommended for casters in situations where another staff is not required.

To cast this spell, the player must be wielding Iban's staff; thus, the player must complete Underground Pass and have level 50 Attack in order to be able to cast this spell. Each cast consumes one charge from Iban's staff when cast on an NPC, or two charges if cast on another player. Thus this spell can be cast a total of 120 times (60 in PvP) before the staff must be recharged. This is increased to 2,500 (1,250 in PvP) with Iban's upgraded staff.

label: Iban's ashes
title: Iban's ashes
lead:
Iban's ashes is a quest item used in the later stages of the Underground Pass quest. It is obtained by emptying a bucket of dwarf brew over Iban's tomb and lighting it on fire. This cremates Iban's remains, leaving his ashes behind.

The ashes are used on the doll of Iban, along with other things, to banish the evil wizard, Iban, from Gielinor.

label: Iban's dove
title: Iban's dove
lead:
Iban's dove is an item used in the later stages of the Underground Pass quest. It is obtained by searching cages of half-soulless deep in the dungeon west of West Ardougne.

It is wise for anyone doing the Underground Pass quest to remember to wear their Klank's gauntlets while searching the cages of the soulless. They will bite players who searching the cages, however, if the player is wearing the gauntlets, the player will take no damage. Searching the cages without wearing the gloves will result in losing 10 hitpoints.

label: Iban's shadow
title: Iban's shadow
lead:
Iban's shadow is a quest item used in the later stages of the Underground Pass quest. It is obtained by killing the level 91 demons Doomion, Othanian, and Holthion and then using the amulets that they drop on the chest near where they are found. Reopening the chest, while in possession of the item or having had used it on the doll, will show that it is empty.

The shadow is used on the doll of iban obtained earlier in the quest in order to banish the evil wizard, Iban, from Gielinor.

label: Iban's staff
title: Iban's staff
lead:
Iban's staff is a staff used to cast Iban Blast. It is obtained by defeating the evil mage Iban at the end of the Underground Pass quest. Iban's staff requires 50 Magic and 50 Attack to wield. Casting Iban Blast on a monster consumes one charge from the staff and casting it on another player consumes two charges. Casting other spells, like Fire Blast, does not consume any charges.

If Iban's staff is lost, Koftik will give a broken staff to the player. It must then be brought to the Dark Mage with to repair it.

label: Iban's Temple
title: Iban's Temple
lead:
Iban's Temple is a small building located at the end of the Underground Pass. It is visited briefly during the Underground Pass quest. During the quest, players must throw the Doll of Iban into the well at the centre of the temple while being hit by Iban's spells. After the quest is complete, once Regicide is started, players can use the Well of Voyage found within the temple to travel to Tirannwn, the land of the elves. Prior to Regicide, it was possible to go back to Iban's Temple and try to throw a second doll into the well, yielding the message, "Iban is already dead...", even though Iban was still in the room as if nothing had happened.

This temple was created by Iban, Zamorak's disciple, as a stronghold. It is possible he knew of the powers of the Well of Voyage, but in any case, he corrupted the well and turned it into the Well of the Damned.

label: Iban's Throne
title: Iban's Throne
lead: Iban's Throne is the throne of Iban, ruler of the Underground Pass and self-proclaimed son of Zamorak. Directly in front of the throne lies the Well of Voyage, which provides passage to Isafdar. At the end of the Underground Pass quest, the throne is destroyed when the temple collapses.

label: Ice
title: Ice
lead: Ice may refer to:

label: Ice arrows
title: Ice arrows
lead:
Ice arrows are a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. They have the same Ranged Strength as steel arrows, but must be fired from a yew bow or better.

In the Temple of Ikov quest, they are collected randomly when searching chests in the eastern Temple of Ikov dungeon and required to defeat the Fire Warrior of Lesarkus. While not required, ice arrows can also be used to defeat Fareed from the Desert Treasure I quest, as all other ammunition will drop to the floor as ashes, bypassing the ammo-saving effect of Ava's devices.

label: Ice chunks (disambiguation)
title: Ice chunks (disambiguation)
lead:
Ice chunks may refer to:

* Ice chunks (Astral Altar), scenery found surrounding the Astral Altar on the south-east tip of Lunar Isle.
* Ice chunks (Ruins of Tapoyauik), scenery found throughout the Ruins of Tapoyauik.
* Ice chunks (Vorkath), a terrain obstruction blocking the entrance to Vorkath's crater on Ungael.

label: Ice Column
title: Ice Column
lead: Two Ice Columns can be found within the throne room of the Ice Queen's Lair, which is under White Wolf Mountain. They have no use outside of scenery.

label: Ice giant
title: Ice giant
lead:
Ice giants are tall, light blue giants that appear at certain icy areas of the game. They are the second strongest giant type out of the standard giants, weaker than Fire giants, but stronger than Moss and Hill giants.

Ice giants are assigned only by Vannaka and Krystilia, although they aren't often killed by players outside of Wilderness slayer due to their poor loot compared to the weaker moss giants and hill giants. Ice giants have separate variants where they appear to be holding different weapons; a longsword, a warhammer, or a macuahuitl.

label: Ice gloves
title: Ice gloves
lead:
Ice gloves are a piece of armour dropped by the Ice Queen under White Wolf Mountain. The gloves are required for multiple quests, as well as several skilling activities. They can be combined with Smiths gloves to combine the effects of both in Smiths gloves (i). This process is reversible.

Although the Ice Queen is a high level, she is very easy to kill, especially when using Protect from Melee. You do not need to start Heroes' Quest to obtain the ice gloves, and the gloves can be obtained as many times as desired. The gloves are obtainable at level 3; however, a boostable level of 50 Mining is required to mine an obstacle on the path to her lair.

label: Ice Light
title: Ice Light
lead: Ice lights are examinable scenery in the Ice Queen's Lair under White Wolf Mountain.

label: Ice Melody
title: Ice Melody
lead: Ice Melody is a music track that is unlocked on White Wolf Mountain.

label: Ice Mountain
title: Ice Mountain
lead: Ice Mountain is located just north-west of Barbarian Village, and the main entrance to the Dwarven Mine is located on its lower southern slope. It dominates northern Asgarnia, and is Asgarnia's only remaining region in which it snows year-round.

label: Ice Queen
title: Ice Queen
lead:
The Ice Queen is a monster found beneath White Wolf Mountain, known for dropping ice gloves. A boostable level of 50 Mining is required to reach her.

Players must fight the Ice Queen to obtain ice gloves for Heroes' Quest, but it is not required to start the quest to be able to fight her, making it possible for skillers to obtain the gloves. A method of fighting the queen while gaining minimal combat experience is shown below.

label: Ice Queen's Lair
title: Ice Queen's Lair
lead:
The Ice Queen's Lair is a dungeon located under the White Wolf Mountain. The entrance is blocked by a rock slide requiring a pickaxe and level 50 Mining to remove. The rock slide can not be mined by another player. The lair plays a major role in Heroes' Quest, where players must kill the Ice Queen to obtain ice gloves. Player can get there quickly via the gnome glider.

If a player loses their ice gloves, they may acquire a new pair by slaying the queen again, but because the dungeon is out of the way, it's recommended to get multiple pairs during the quest.

label: Ice resistance
title: Ice resistance
lead:
Ice resistance may refer to:
* Ice breath resistance, a type of dragonfire used by wyverns.
* Icy seas resistance, a sailing hazard present in the Northern Ocean.

label: Ice spells
title: Ice spells
lead:
Ice spells are one of four types of Ancient Magicks combat spells. In addition to dealing damage, these spells freeze the target in place, preventing it from moving.

Ice spells may refer to:

label: Ice spider
title: Ice spider
lead:
Ice spiders are one of the stronger species of spider. They are seldom killed due to having very few drops except when on a Wilderness Slayer task.

They do not appear on the player's minimap.

label: Ice Throne
title: Ice Throne
lead: Ice Throne is the throne used by the Ice Queen, found in her lair.

label: ID
title: ID
lead: ID may refer to:

label: Ice troll (disambiguation)
title: Ice troll (disambiguation)
lead:
Ice troll can refer to:

*Ice trolls found east of the Ice Gate along the Ice Path
**Ice troll (Desert Treasure I), a friendly ice troll near aforementioned monsters encountered during the Desert Treasure I quest
*Ice trolls in the Fremennik Isles:
**Ice troll runt
**Ice troll female
**Ice troll grunt
**Ice troll male
*Ice trolls in the Ice Troll Caves
**Frenzied ice troll runt
**Frenzied ice troll female
**Frenzied ice troll grunt
**Frenzied ice troll male
**Ice Troll King
*Ice trolls of Weiss:
**Boulder
**Butterfly
**Don't Know What
**Driftwood
**Goat Poo
**Icicle
**Mother
**Odd Mushroom
**Odd Stone
**Pebble
**Root
**Snowflake
**Squirrel
**Yellow Snow

label: Ice warrior
title: Ice warrior
lead:
Ice warriors are mid-level elemental warriors. Ice warriors can be formidable foes to those with low levels. Ice warriors can be assigned by Krystilia for a Wilderness Slayer task, or by Vannaka or Mazchna for normal tasks.

Ice warriors have 100% elemental weakness to fire spells.

label: Icicle (disambiguation)
title: Icicle (disambiguation)
lead:
Icicle may refer to:
* Icicle, an ice troll resident of Weiss
* Icicles (Penguin Agility Course), an agility obstacle at the Penguin Agility Course
* Icicles (Royal Titans), obstacles conjured by Eldric the Ice King during the fight against the Royal Titans

label: icon
title: icon
lead: Icons are symbols on a player's map (minimap or world map) representing certain buildings and locations.

label: Icon (disambiguation)
title: Icon (disambiguation)
lead: Icon may refer to:

label: Icy seas
title: Icy seas
lead: Icy seas are a sailing hazard found in the Northern Ocean. An eternal brazier is required to traverse the seas, otherwise crew will be frozen, cancelling actions, players will receive a chatbox message: Without a brazier's warmth, the icy seas will soon freeze you to your core! and be frozen soon afterwards and both they and ship will take increasing damage over time if area is not left indicated by the chatbox message: Without a brazier's warmth, the icy seas freeze you to your core, locking you in place!

label: icyene
title: icyene
lead: The Icyene (Jagex pronunciation: ) are an ancient race of winged humanoids aligned to the god Saradomin. While now nearly extinct, they were some of his most powerful followers.

label: Id papers
title: Id papers
lead: The id papers is needed to get into ScarFace Pete's mansion during the Heroes' Quest. Using it while the player is dressed in full Black armour will allow the player to pass themself off as a Black Knight called Hartigen. The ID paper can be obtained by talking to Trobert.

label: Idithuun
title: Idithuun
lead:
The Idithuun are a goblin tribe. Like the other goblin tribes, they were called upon by the god Bandos to fight in his name during the God Wars.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Goblins of the South".

label: Idle
title: Idle
lead:
Idling, also known as being AFK (away from keyboard), describes periods when a player is not actively interacting with the game. However, idling doesn't always mean the player is absent – many activities, like cutting trees for Woodcutting experience, require minimal attention and can be performed while partially disengaged.

Note that idle training is distinct from passive training, which includes click-intensive methods such as zero-time fletching or casting High Level Alchemy in between agility obstacles.

label: Idol
title: Idol
lead:
Idol may refer to:

*Idol of balance, an item used during the 2018 Easter event
*Idol of chaos, an item used during the 2018 Easter event
*Idol of light, an item used during the 2018 Easter event
*Revitalising idol, an item used during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire

label: Idonea Ramlock
title: Idonea Ramlock
lead: Idonea Ramlock was a resident of Varrock during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. According to the Varrock Census of that year, she was a teacher. She may be related to Trevick Ramlock.

label: Ignore List
title: Ignore List
lead:
The Ignore List tab is found in the Friends List tab by clicking on the red sad face on the top right of the tab.

It is used to block messages from certain players. A player "ignoring" a specific person cannot hear that person in public or private chat. However, unlike turning Private Chat "off", the player doing the ignoring does not appear offline to the person being ignored.

label: Ilujanka
title: Ilujanka
lead:
, one of the few remaining accounts of the Dragon riders.]]
The ilujanka, nicknamed as the dragon riders, were a race of beings that served Zaros during the Second Age. Little is known about them other than that they had a unique talent for taming and riding dragons, which was considered an impossible feat, thus making them formidable and dangerous opponents. They were known to be very skilled in combat and a few served as honour guards of Zamorak after defecting. There are no known dragon riders alive today.

label: Ima
title: Ima
lead: Ima is one of the people observing the fights at the Emir's Arena. He says few lines with some importance though usually just random chitchat. He also walks around Dalal.

label: Imafore Tullus
title: Imafore Tullus
lead:
, which has been beheaded.]]
Imafore Tullus was an Emperor of Varlamore roughly 100 years ago. Not much is known about his early life, except that he had an abusive father and were prone to fits of rage, which once culminated in a young Imafore breaking the arm of his cousin Mezpah Arkan.

When Imafore took the throne, he was responsible for transforming the region into the Varlamorian Empire. Although his rule was initally peaceful, he is most remembered for causing the War of Betrayal by killing the Kourend royal family. As the war with Kourend progressed, Imafore lost popularity within Varlamore thanks to his cruel and extreme conduct, such as his plan to burn the entirety of Auburn Valley to stop the progress of Kourend's troops and his subsequent execution of General Nemus for refusing to carry out said plan.

label: Imbue scroll
title: Imbue scroll
lead:
Imbue scroll may refer to:

*Magic shortbow scroll, used to create the Magic shortbow (i)
*Scroll of imbuing, a reward from the Emir's Arena used to imbue various pieces of armour
*Scroll of imbuing (beta), a version of the Scroll of imbuing available during the Emir's Arena beta
*Ring of wealth scroll, used to create the Ring of wealth (i)

** Dark bow imbue scroll
** Barrelchest anchor imbue scroll

label: Imbuing
title: Imbuing
lead: Imbuing is the process of upgrading or enhancing certain items. Most imbues are rewards from Nightmare Zone, whilst others are imbued by other means.

label: Imcando dwarf
title: Imcando dwarf
lead:
, an Imcando dwarf.]]
The Imcando dwarves are an ancient clan of dwarves, related to the ordinary dwarves. They once inhabited Camdozaal, a now ruined-city below Ice Mountain, but were believed to be extinct after the Runecrafting Crusades. They are well-known for their masterful Smithing skill, having created the original sword of Sir Vyvin's family and the Shield of Arrav , as well as their love of redberry pie. Additionally, most of the ancient Imcando dwarves were followers of Saradomin. For many hundreds of years, they were the world's most renowned smiths. The techniques used by the Imcando were secret, passed down from generation to generation, and any devices created by the Imcando are very hard to replicate; however, it is known that they incorporate magic in their techniques.

label: Imcandoria
title: Imcandoria
lead: Imcandoria was the former city of the Imcando dwarves, located on Acheron. The region around Imcandoria was also home to a group of unspecified giants who were metalworkers, as well as several Auspah tribes; in addition, they are known to have traded with Fremennik tribes.

label: imp
title: imp
lead:
Imps are amongst the smallest creatures in Gielinor. They are central in the Imp Catcher quest due to their unique bead drops. Every 30–120 seconds there is a 25% chance for an imp to disappear into a puff of smoke and teleport a short distance away. At level 71 Hunter players may catch imps with magic boxes, including imps found in the God Wars Dungeon.

Outside of the bead drops, imps are primarily killed to obtain God Wars Dungeon Zamorak kill-count, and for their extremely rare Imp champion scroll drop.

label: Imp (interface item)
title: Imp (interface item)
lead:
The Imp is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the Imp

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Imp (unused)
title: Imp (unused)
lead:
Level 3 Imps are unused non-player characters that previously appeared in the Imp Catcher quest. Originally, Wizard Grayzag had a combat level of 41 and could be fought by the player, during which he would summon stronger variants of Imps. In 2006, the quest was reworked; from now on players could only talk to Grayzag instead of fighting him. Therefore, the stronger imps could no longer be encountered in game, although they remained in the game files and were graphically updated several months later.

As they became discontinued before August 2007, they have never been present in Old School RuneScape. Ultimately, they were removed from the game files altogether on 6 January 2021.

label: Imp Catcher
title: Imp Catcher
lead: The Wizard Grayzag has summoned hundreds of little imps. They have stolen a lot of things belonging to the Wizard Mizgog including his magic beads.

label: Imp statue (interface item)
title: Imp statue (interface item)
lead:
The Imp statue is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Imp statue.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Impending Chaos
title: Impending Chaos
lead:
Impending Chaos is an unfinished quest not accessible in the game. The quest would have been started by talking to Citlalli who has a basement full of imps causing issues. The quest summary is "Deal with some troublesome imps causing problems in Kastori." The quest assets were added to the game on 23 July 2025 with the release of Varlamore: The Final Dawn which included four quests, and another unfinished quest, An Existential Crisis.

Judging from its config name ( ic_ecatl ), Ecatl, a non-player character, is believed to be involved in the quest.

label: Impling
title: Impling
lead:
Implings are Hunter creatures that are featured in the minigame Impetuous Impulses. They are mainly found in Puro-Puro, but they can be found commonly across Gielinor. Higher level requirement implings typically have more valuable loot.

Players must wield a butterfly net or magic butterfly net to be able to catch implings, but doing so with an empty impling jar in their inventory allows players to keep them (either to open later or sell at the Grand Exchange). Players can also catch implings barehanded, but this requires 10 Hunter levels above the requirement for catching that impling (for example, ninja implings barehanded requires level 84 Hunter instead of the normal 74). Implings caught without an impling jar will be looted immediately. An impling jar is required to catch implings in Puro-Puro. However, if you have a jar in your inventory, you can barehand the impling into the jar. Grabbing an impling with your bare hands has the same success rate as attempting to catch one with a magic butterfly net.

label: Improved Reflexes
title: Improved Reflexes
lead:
Improved Reflexes is a prayer unlocked at level 16 Prayer. It increases the player's Attack by 10%.

Like all other Melee-boosting prayers, it cannot be used with any Ranged or Magic prayers nor can it be used in conjunction with another prayer that increases the player's Attack level, such as Incredible Reflexes.

title: In the Manor
lead: In the Manor is a music track that is unlocked south of Yanille.

label: Inaccessible areas
title: Inaccessible areas
lead:
Inaccessible areas are locations that, although existing ingame, cannot currently be accessed by players. Some are visible on the World map, while others can only be seen ingame by using an Orb of oculus.

These locations exist for a variety of reasons. Some are areas that were previously accessible but were closed off before August 2007, others are placeholders or hints for potential future content releases, while some are debug areas not normally supposed to be seen by players.

label: Incantations
title: Incantations
lead:
Incantations were ammunition-slot items proposed as part of the Warding skill that would have granted small magic bonuses. Players would have required papyrus, the appropriate talisman and certain vis to create incantations.

The incantations would have had the following stats:

label: Incense burner (Mahogany) (interface item)
title: Incense burner (Mahogany) (interface item)
lead:
The Incense burner (Mahogany) is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the mahogany incense burner.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

title: Incense burner (Marble) (interface item)
lead:
The Incense burner (Marble) is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the marble incense burner.

lead:
The Incense burner (Oak) is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the oak incense burner.

label: Incinerator (Sheep Herder)
title: Incinerator (Sheep Herder)
lead:
The Incinerator is used during the Sheep Herder quest to dispose of bones from the surrounding "infected" sheep.

It is later uncovered during Biohazard that the plague was fake.

label: Incomplete pizza
title: Incomplete pizza
lead:
An Incomplete pizza is an item that players will usually make only intermittently whilst making a plain pizza. It is made by using a tomato with a pizza base.

As the examine text implies, players will usually use this with cheese to make an uncooked pizza, which they will then cook on a range to make a plain pizza. This requires level 35 Cooking, and is open to members and non-members.

label: Incomplete stew
title: Incomplete stew
lead: Incomplete stew is made by using a potato, cooked meat, or a cooked chicken on a bowl of water, requiring level 25 Cooking. The final product is the same regardless of which of the two types of meat is used. The ingredients can be added in any order. Adding the last ingredient creates an uncooked stew.

label: Incredible Reflexes
title: Incredible Reflexes
lead:
Incredible Reflexes is a prayer unlocked at level 34 Prayer. Incredible Reflexes increases the player's Attack by 15%. It is commonly used by players in mini-games, such as Castle Wars and the Emir's Arena, due to the fact that the player's prayer points are instantly refunded at the end of each scrimmage.

Like all other stat-affecting prayers, it cannot be used in conjunction with another prayer that increases the player's Attack level, such as Piety.

The Infernal chart is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Infernal chart.

label: Infernal Dimensions
title: Infernal Dimensions
lead:
The Infernal Dimensions, together known as Infernus, is the original home world of the demons. The realm seems to be ruled by demon lords, such as the Tsutsaroth demon Thammaron. The throne room of Thammaron, which is visited in the quests The Golem and Shadow of the Storm, is likely to be in the Infernal Dimensions. It is, however, not possible to exit beyond the throne room and explore the dimension any further.

The Infernal Dimensions contain ore not found elsewhere, and sustain the unique conditions required for advanced Smithing techniques. Avernic weaponry, such as the Avernic defender, was crafted by Avernic smiths in the liquid fires of Infernus. Additionally, Oathplate armour is forged with a metal made from an ore found only in Infernus. The bottom of the Chasm of Fire seems to experience similar conditions of that of Infernus, with infernal shale forming under the high pressure, capable of fueling the nearby furnace to the extreme temperatures required to melt down oathplate shards.

label: Infernal mage (interface item)
title: Infernal mage (interface item)
lead:
The Infernal mage is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the infernal mage.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Infernal tool

lead:
Infernal tool may refer to:
