label: Inferno/Strategies
title: Inferno/Strategies
lead:
The Inferno is a very difficult solo PVM challenge, with the goal of completing all 69 waves and killing TzKal-Zuk. Players who are successful will be rewarded with the infernal cape.

Before attempting it, it is highly recommended that you have the best gear that you can afford and maxed or very high combat stats. More importantly, do not expect to complete it on your first few attempts: be mentally prepared to fail a lot and learn from your mistakes.

label: Infinity colour kit
title: Infinity colour kit
lead:
Infinity colour kit may refer to:

*Light infinity colour kit
*Dark infinity colour kit

label: Infinity robes
title: Infinity robes
lead:
Infinity robes are a set of magic armour that are rewards from the Mage Training Arena minigame. Each piece of the robes can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian on the top floor of the arena in exchange for Pizazz points. Infinity robes require 25 Defence and 50 Magic to wear. The hat, top and bottom gives a 1% Magic damage bonus for a total of 3%.

To buy full infinity robes with Pizazz points requires 1,495 Telekinetic, 1,695 Alchemist, 14,700 Enchantment and 1,495 Graveyard points. It can be stored in a magic wardrobe in a player-owned house.

label: Initiate armour
title: Initiate armour
lead:
Initiate armour is white-plate, gold-trimmed plate armour that can be purchased from Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador Park after completing Recruitment Drive, requiring 20 Defence and 10 Prayer to equip. The items have a small Prayer bonus equivalent to monk's robes and other bonuses equivalent to mithril armour. The hauberk and cuisse are commonly used on Slayer tasks when using Prayer to slow the drain on Prayer points, saving on Prayer potions.

A full set can be bought from Sir Tiffy Cashien for 20,000 coins, while the individual pieces can be purchased for a total of 24,000 coins: 6,000 for an initiate sallet, 8,000 for an initiate cuisse, and 10,000 for an initiate hauberk. Although Recruitment Drive rewards an initiate sallet, buying the full set is still cheaper, as the second sallet can be high alched for 3,600 effectively making this route cost 1,600 less coins than buying the hauberk and cuisse individually. Alternatively, purchasing the full set from the Grand Exchange costs while the separate pieces total .

label: Inquisitor
title: Inquisitor
lead: Inquisitor may refer to:

label: Inquisitor's armour
title: Inquisitor's armour
lead:
The Inquisitor's armour is a set of armour requiring 70 Strength and 30 Defence to equip. While the armour has unimpressive defensive stats, around adamant equipment's values, it shares the same strength bonuses as Bandos armour and specializes in crush attack and defence, but penalises accuracy with slash and stab weapons. It also has a higher prayer bonus than Bandos armour. The pieces can be obtained as a potential reward from The Nightmare and its harder counterpart, Phosani's Nightmare.

The armour once belonged to Phosani, the Justiciar of the Wolf, who defected to Zamorak and founded Slepe after; the armour had remained sealed in the Sisterhood Sanctuary deep beneath Slepe until The Nightmare's arrival unearthed it. As such, the set pieces count as Zamorakian items for the God Wars Dungeon.

label: Insect Queen
title: Insect Queen
lead: Insect Queen is a music track that is unlocked in the Kalphite lair and the Kalphite cave.

label: Insect repellent
title: Insect repellent
lead:
Insect repellent is a container of bug spray that can be used on beehives, large mosquitoes, and mosquito swarms.

Using insect repellent on beehives, located in the apiary west of Catherby and in southern Seers' Village, causes the bees to leave. Using a bucket on the beehive then gives a bucket of wax, which is used in Merlin's Crystal and Troll Romance. Insect repellent must be used on the beehive every time, otherwise the bees will have returned and no wax will be collected.

label: Insela
title: Insela
lead: Insela was a member of the Sisterhood, a ballistics expert, and one of Phosani's closest companions. When the kingdom of Hallowvale fell to Lord Drakan's forces in the Third Age, Insela, along with Phosani and Otrava, swore allegiance to Zamorak and the vampyres and handed over their remaining squadrons to the invaders. Insela followed Phosani in founding the town that would later be known as Slepe in east Morytania. Insela most likely wrote the Explosive discovery, after discovering a volatile gourd that could be used as an explosive if blood was added to it. Insela supposedly also drank the Elixir of Everlasting like Phosani to extend her life, but succumbed to the same eternal slumber as her, and Insela's body was supposedly taken into the Sisterhood Sanctuary.

label: Inspiration
title: Inspiration
lead:
Inspiration is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness and also plays in Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, the track plays north-east of the Black Knights' Fortress in the Wilderness.

label: instance
title: instance
lead:
An instance is a special area, typically a quest area, that generates a new copy of the location for each player or group that enters the area. Players cannot see other players in instanced areas unless it's a group instanced area—in which case, the group cannot see any other groups.

Instanced areas can take place in entirely new areas that cannot be accessed without the instance or in areas that are normally not instanced. Most non-quest boss instances will require the player to pay a specific sum of money or have an item in their inventory in order to access the instance.

label: Instruction manual
title: Instruction manual
lead:
The Instruction manual, or Dwarf Multicannon Manual, is a book that details how to set up and fire the dwarf multicannon, how to create cannonballs, and includes warranty information for the dwarf multicannon.

After completion Dwarf Cannon, it is found on a bookshelf in a player-owned house or is purchasable from Multicannon parts for sale for coins or Rasolo the Wandering Merchant for coins.

label: Intel report
title: Intel report
lead: Intel report is obtained during the Shield of Arrav quest by killing the Jonny the Beard. It needs to be taken to Straven for admission to Phoenix Gang.

label: Interface
title: Interface
lead:
fixed screen interface]]
The interface is the screen containing different buttons which, when clicked, display different pieces of information. Some parts of the interface are permanently open, for example, the minimap.

label: Interface items
title: Interface items
lead:
Interface items are items that appear in an interface or an animation, but cannot otherwise be obtained. Unlike unobtainable items, the majority of these 
items can be seen ingame in some form.

label: Intrepid
title: Intrepid
lead: Intrepid is a music track that is unlocked in lower floor of Iban's lair during the Underground Pass quest.

label: Invasion of Avarrocka
title: Invasion of Avarrocka
lead:
The Invasion of Avarrocka was an attack against Avarrocka led by Zemouregal, a Zamorakian Mahjarrat necromancer. Zemouregal sought the Shield of Arrav, a powerful shield made by the Imcando dwarves.

The invasion happened in the 4th Age sometime between the years 700 and 800, on the lands now called Varrock. The battle between Zemouregal's undead army and Avarrocka knights resulted in the defeat of the invaders. The incursion was successfully stopped by the mighty hero Arrav and the grandson of one of the city's elders with the help of Arrav's legendary shield, at the cost of Arrav's life.

label: Invasion of Lletya
title: Invasion of Lletya
lead:
The invasion of Lletya took place during Song of the Elves. Once Arianwyn hears that Lord Iorwerth's claims are true, he questions everything he fought for. In turn, he joins Iorwerth and betrays the resistance, disclosing the location of Lletya and the secret tunnel into the Temple of Light.

Iorwerth, knowing the orb of light was taken from his camp, has the village set on fire, and his clan attacks its citizens. He comes to reclaim the orb from Baxtorian, who refuses until he threatens to take the life of an elven child. Ysgawyn tries to stop Iorwerth from leaving, but Essyllt kills him. With the orb back in their possession, the Iorwerth clan departs for the tunnel in the Underground Pass.

label: Invasion plans
title: Invasion plans
lead:
The invasion plans are an item used during the The Grand Tree quest. Players obtain it by using Glough's key on the locked chest in Glough's home just south of the Grand Tree.

Along with the lumber order, players should take this to King Narnode Shareen as evidence against Glough.

label: Inventory
title: Inventory
lead: A player's inventory is a term for all of the items they are carrying. The game interface splits the inventory into two sections: the backpack inventory and the equipped inventory.

label: Inventory blocking food
title: Inventory blocking food
lead:
is a cheap high healing inventory blocking food frequently used when fighting the Chaos Elemental.]]

Inventory blocking food is food that leaves behind an item in the inventory after it is consumed. It is commonly used while fighting the Chaos Elemental, Chaos Fanatic, and used while Blackjacking in Pollinveach. Blocking food is generally used when it is desirable to keep the players inventory full. This can be to counteract a disarming special attack or to prevent the player from accidentally taking certain actions while rapidly clicking such as pickpocketing Menaphite thugs.

label: Inventory Expansion
title: Inventory Expansion
lead:
Inventory Expansion refers to the player's ability to increase the number of certain items that can be held within their inventory; by use of various items in Old School RuneScape.

While there are many items that have their own inventory, when held or equipped, there is no way to permanently increase the player's backpack inventory above the default 28 slots.

label: Invitation letter
title: Invitation letter
lead:
The invitation letter is a quest item used in The Dig Site to gain access to the winches. It is obtained from Terry Balando after the player has brought him the Ancient talisman. Giving it to any digsite workman grants them access to the dig shafts.

It is possible to obtain multiple letters by using the drop trick. Should the player use another letter on a workman, they will ask "What an earth are you giving me another scroll for?"

label: Invrigar the Necromancer
title: Invrigar the Necromancer
lead: Invrigar is a necromancer found on the top floor of the Necromancer Tower. He will use magic to attack the player and will sometimes summon a level 13 Summoned Zombie to fight with him.

label: Iorwerth Clan
title: Iorwerth Clan
lead:
The Iorwerth Clan is one of the eight elven clans who were originally brought to Gielinor from Tarddiad by Guthix and Seren in the early First Age. Their former leader, Warmaster Lord Iorwerth, was the initiator of the Elven Civil War due to conquering Prifddinas and seizing the Tower of Voices and the Grand Library, denying access to the city to non-Iorwerth elves. The civil war, which has caused the deaths of thousands of elves, is the reason for the Iorwerth Clan being regarded as an enemy to elven society. Although followers of Seren, their plan to summon the Dark Lord had misled the other elves to believe that they worshipped Zamorak, as the Dark Lord was a name Lord Iorwerth used to sway King Lathas, a secret worshipper of Zamorak, to help the Iorwerth Clan to free the Fragment of Seren.

They are a clan of skilled warriors, assassins and slayers. They are located south-west of the Tower of Voices in Prifddinas, off the southern path.

label: Iou
title: Iou
lead:
The iou is a quest item that appears in the Death Plateau quest. Harold gives it to the player in lieu of payment for a gambling debt he owes from a dice rolling game.

When the player inspects the back of the IOU, they will discover that it is really the combination to the equipment room in Burthorpe Castle. This item is lost at the completion of Death Plateau quest.

label: Iqbar Ali-Abdula
title: Iqbar Ali-Abdula
lead:
Iqbar Ali-Abdula is the name of the famed bug hunter and researcher who first studied the Kalphite species in the Kharidian Desert. Apparently, this research drove him insane. Whether he is still alive is uncertain, however it is implied that he may be the Weird Old Man found outside the Kalphite Lair.

He is mentioned only in the Varrock Museum by one of the natural historians, when discussing the Kalphite Queen near her display.

label: Irena
title: Irena
lead: Irena is a woman from Al Kharid, and the mother of Ana, an eager explorer/tourist. Recently, she went down into the Kharidian Desert and Irena hasn't seen her since, so she waits and sobs at the gates of the Shantay Pass, waiting for Ana to return, and waiting for an adventurer to arrive and help her. A player can talk to her to begin The Tourist Trap.

label: Iriandul Caistlyn
title: Iriandul Caistlyn
lead:
Iriandul Caistlyn was one of the Seven Priestly Warriors who died fighting the Morytanian hordes at Silvarea. He came from Varrock.

He is described in The Sleeping Seven as "A true leader of the holy seven, though rarely ever a footfall in front of Ivandis, who was ever eager to smash the evil and force the tide back into Morytania."

label: Irit leaf
title: Irit leaf
lead:
Irit leaf ( ) is a mid level herb that can be cleaned at level 40 Herblore. Each cleaned irit leaf yields 8.8 Herblore experience. It is commonly dropped while fighting chaos druids, but can be dropped by almost every monster capable of dropping herbs.

To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create an irit potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient. You can create super attack potions by adding an eye of newt. Creating super attack potions is considered one of the easiest methods to train Herblore, especially for ironmen, as eyes of newt are very easy to obtain, and the finished product is very useful for combat purposes. Eye of newt packs can be bought for 300 gp at various shops, and contain 100 eyes of newt. You can also create superantipoison potions by adding unicorn horn dust. In order to create an antidote++ however, you need to add the irit leaf to a vial of coconut milk, creating antidote++ (unf), and add magic roots as secondary ingredients.

label: Irit potion (unf)
title: Irit potion (unf)
lead: An irit potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using an irit leaf on a vial of water, requiring 45 Herblore. Using an eye of newt on an irit potion (unf) with 45 Herblore yields a super attack(3) and 100 Herblore experience. Using a unicorn horn dust on an irit potion (unf) with 48 Herblore yields a superantipoison(3) and 106.3 Herblore experience.

label: Irksol
title: Irksol
lead: Irksol is an otherworldly being selling ruby rings at his shop in the Zanaris market.

label: Irksol (shop)
title: Irksol (shop)
lead: Irksol is a store run by Irksol in the Zanaris marketplace. The shop only sells ruby rings, and it is decorated with fairy market stalls.

label: Iron
title: Iron
lead:
Iron may refer to:
*Ironman, the game mode
*Iron bar, the Smithing material
*Iron dragons, the second weakest tier of the six metallic dragons
*Iron equipment, the equipable pieces of gear
*Iron ore, the Mining product
*Iron rocks, the rock the player obtains iron ore from

label: Iron 2h sword
title: Iron 2h sword
lead:
The iron 2h sword is a two-handed sword that is stronger than the bronze 2h sword. As with other iron weaponry, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

Players can make an iron 2h sword with the Smithing skill at level 29 using 3 iron bars, giving the player 75 Smithing experience.

label: Iron arrow
title: Iron arrow
lead:
Iron arrows are stronger than bronze arrows, and are compatible with most bows. Iron arrows can be made at level 15 Fletching by using 15 iron arrowtips on 15 headless arrows, granting 37.5 Fletching experience. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Iron arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock.

label: Iron arrowtips
title: Iron arrowtips
lead:
Iron arrowtips are made with an iron bar requiring 20 Smithing, yielding Smithing 25 experience and 15 iron arrowtips. They are made into iron arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 15 Fletching, yielding 37.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the of the Grand Tree, Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost, and Ava's Odds and Ends in Draynor Manor. They are purchased for coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp.

label: Iron axe
title: Iron axe
lead:
The iron axe is the second weakest axe in Old School RuneScape, being slightly better than the bronze axe. It can be used in combat or in Woodcutting to cut trees. An iron axe has the same level requirements as a bronze axe, making it the better choice for new players.

The success rate for chopping a log is approximately 150% that of the Bronze axe.

label: Iron axe head
title: Iron axe head
lead:
The iron axe head is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's axe while Woodcutting. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while Mining, but with a pickaxe head and pickaxe handle.

label: Iron bar
title: Iron bar
lead:
An iron bar is a bar of refined iron. It can be created through the Smithing skill at level 15 by using iron ore on a furnace, granting 12.5 Smithing experience. When smelting iron ore, there is a 50% chance that it will be too impure; it disappears, yielding no Smithing experience nor an iron bar. However, wearing a ring of forging, casting Superheat Item, or using the Blast Furnace would give a 100% success rate.

An iron bar can be smithed on an anvil through the Smithing skill to create iron weapons and armour. When smithed, each bar grants 25 experience, with a maximum of 125 being given for the iron platebody.

label: Iron battleaxe
title: Iron battleaxe
lead:
The iron battleaxe is the second-weakest battleaxe in Old School RuneScape, being more powerful than the bronze battleaxe. Like all iron weapons, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack.

Players can make an iron battleaxe with level 25 Smithing using three iron bars, giving 75 experience. It is a slashing weapon, which makes it good for monsters with a slash weakness. Players can purchase this battleaxe from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim and Bob's Brilliant Axes shop in Lumbridge.

label: Iron chainbody
title: Iron chainbody
lead:
The iron chainbody is the second weakest chainbody, and can be worn by a player with 1 Defence. A player with 26 Smithing can make the chainbody by using three iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 75 Smithing experience.

An iron chainbody is required for the Black Knights' Fortress, King's Ransom, and While Guthix Sleeps quests.

label: Iron claws
title: Iron claws
lead:
Iron claws are a two-handed melee weapon. They are the second weakest claws available and can be wielded at 1 Attack.

Iron claws can be obtained by making them using the Smithing skill, or buying them from Martin Thwait in the Rogues' Den. The requirements for making them are completing the Death Plateau quest and 28 Smithing. To make them, use two iron bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory. This will grant the player 50 Smithing experience.

label: Iron dagger
title: Iron dagger
lead:
The iron dagger is a dagger stronger than the bronze dagger. Players can make an iron dagger with the Smithing skill at level 15 using 1 iron bar, giving the player 25 Smithing experience. Members can poison this weapon, giving them an advantage in combat. Players can purchase this dagger from the Varrock Swordshop. There are also several spawn points throughout the map. As with most daggers, it can be poisoned.

Players with at least level 32 Thieving can get an iron dagger (p) by pickpocketing Rogues. Rogues are located south-west of the deep Wilderness Mage Arena.

label: Iron dart
title: Iron dart
lead:
Iron darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from iron. Iron darts can be wielded at level 1 Ranged. They can be obtained by using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Iron darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

To create iron darts the player must have completed the Tourist Trap quest and have at least level 19 Smithing and level 22 Fletching. Players can smith iron bars into iron dart tips. Each iron bar creates 10 iron dart tips and gives the player 25 Smithing experience. Feathers then must be added to create the iron darts. 3.8 Fletching experience is rewarded per iron dart fletched.

label: Iron dart tip
title: Iron dart tip
lead:
The iron dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players can craft this item using an iron bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory and a Smithing level of 19. Each iron bar creates 10 iron dart tips and gives the player 25 Smithing experience. They can be fletched into iron darts at level 22 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 38 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, one must complete the Tourist Trap quest.

label: Iron equipment
title: Iron equipment
lead: Iron equipment are items made from iron metal. Iron equipment is stronger than bronze equipment, but weaker than steel equipment. All iron items are coloured dark-grey. Iron armour requires 1 Defence to wield, weapons require 1 Attack, which makes it a suitable alternative to bronze equipment, which has the same requirements.

label: Iron fire arrow
title: Iron fire arrow
lead:
Iron fire arrows are iron arrows wrapped in an oily cloth, which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox. They, along with any other fire arrow, are primarily used to pierce the rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same Ranged Strength as regular iron arrows.

label: iron full helm
title: iron full helm
lead:
The Iron full helm is a full helm made of iron. It is the second weakest full helmet available. While it grants greater defensive stats than its medium helmet counterpart, it has worse magic and ranged attack stats. There are no Defence requirements for wearing this helmet.

Players with level 22 Smithing can create an iron full helm by using two iron bars on an anvil while having a hammer in their inventory. Doing so will grant the player 50 Smithing experience.

label: Iron gold-trimmed armour
title: Iron gold-trimmed armour
lead: Iron gold-trimmed armour is a possible reward from easy Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to Iron armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Iron javelin
title: Iron javelin
lead:
The iron javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. They are the second weakest type of javelin. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching iron javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 17 Fletching, granting 30 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.

label: Iron key
title: Iron key
lead:
The iron key is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It is obtained by using a golden key on the southern Monument in the Paterdomus mausoleum.

It is used to unlock the cell Drezel is detained in.

label: Iron kiteshield
title: Iron kiteshield
lead:
The Iron kiteshield is the second-weakest smithable kiteshield, requiring 1 Defence to wield. A player with 27 Smithing can make the shield by using three iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 75 Smithing experience. It cannot be bought from Cassie's Shield Shop for ironmen, as there is no stock available.

The iron kiteshield yields the highest melee defence bonuses for any shield slot item at 1 Defence.

label: Iron knife
title: Iron knife
lead:
The iron knife is a throwing knife that does not require a Ranged level to wield. It is stronger than a bronze knife but weaker than a steel knife. To create iron knives, the player must have at least 22 Smithing. Each iron bar will create 5 iron knives and give the player 25 Smithing experience. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged. Iron knives can be purchased from Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop in the Rogues' Den with 50 Thieving and 50 Agility.

label: Iron longsword
title: Iron longsword
lead: The iron longsword is a longsword stronger than the bronze longsword, but weaker than the steel longsword. Like all other iron weapons, it can be wielded at level 1 Attack. It can be created at level 21 Smithing using two iron bars, granting 50 experience. This longsword can be purchased at Varrock Swordshop.

label: Iron mace
title: Iron mace
lead:
The Iron mace is a mace made of iron. It is the second weakest mace available in the game. It requires level 1 Attack to wield, and can be created by using an iron bar on an anvil (as long as the player has level 17 Smithing). It can be bought at Flynn's Mace Market in Falador.

It can be found in the Edgeville jail and in a house to the east of the Ardougne market.

label: Iron med helm
title: Iron med helm
lead: The iron med helm is the second weakest medium helmet. A player with 18 Smithing can make the helmet by using one iron bar on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 25 Smithing experience.

label: Iron ore
title: Iron ore
lead: Iron ore can be mined from iron rocks at level 15 Mining, providing 35 Mining experience. It can be smelted at a furnace into an iron bar at level 15 Smithing, or along with two coal into a steel bar at level 30 Smithing. Smelting iron bars has a 50% success rate, unless the player is wearing a ring of forging, using the Superheat Item spell, or using the Blast Furnace. Smelting iron ore into a bar gives 12.5 Smithing experience, and smelting a steel bar gives 17.5 Smithing experience.

label: Iron pick head
title: Iron pick head
lead:
An iron pick head was obtained as part of a discontinued random event, in which the iron pickaxe head flew off the handle while the player was mining. To fix it, the player had to collect it off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

If players were not paying attention when this occurred, the head would disappear from the ground or be picked up by another player, requiring them to purchase another.

label: Iron pickaxe
title: Iron pickaxe
lead:
The iron pickaxe is a pickaxe that mines on a 7-tick cycle, 1-tick faster than the bronze pickaxe. It can be used in combat or to mine rocks.

As with all pickaxes, players cannot smith an iron pickaxe.

label: Iron pickaxe (Chambers of Xeric)
title: Iron pickaxe (Chambers of Xeric)
lead: Iron pickaxe is scenery found in the Chambers of Xeric that is used to provide an item spawn of an iron pickaxe. The spawn can be found in Guardian rooms. It has the appearance of an item including an orange name and red dot on the minimap, but unlike normal item spawns does not disappear after being picked up.

label: Iron platebody
title: Iron platebody
lead:
The iron platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between bronze and steel. It has no Defence requirement to equip, which makes it the best platebody for players just starting out. It also provides greater protection than an iron chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

If playing as an Ironman, an ironman platebody with equivalent stats can be acquired by talking to the Ironman tutor in Lumbridge.

label: Iron platelegs
title: Iron platelegs
lead:
Iron platelegs are melee leg armour made of iron. There is no Defence requirement to wear them, as is the same with bronze armour. As such, it is recommended to skip bronze tier items and start out with iron tier items. They have the same defensive stats as an iron plateskirt but weigh more.

They can be made at level 31 Smithing with 3 iron bars, granting 75 experience.

label: Iron plateskirt
title: Iron plateskirt
lead:
The iron plateskirt is a plateskirt made from iron. It has the same stats as iron platelegs but weighs less.

They can be made at level 31 Smithing with 3 iron bars, granting 75 experience.

label: Iron railings (interface item)
title: Iron railings (interface item)
lead:
The Iron railings is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Iron railings.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Iron rocks
title: Iron rocks
lead:
Iron rocks are a type of protruding rock that contains iron ore. Players with a Mining level of 15 or higher can mine iron ore from rocks found in various mines, granting 35 Mining experience for each ore mined. After being mined, an iron rock takes 5.4 seconds to respawn. When inside the members' area of the Mining Guild, that time is reduced to 2.4 seconds; the faster respawn time makes it the best place to power-mine iron, with an experience rate of up to 70k xp/h.

Iron is the most popular ore that free-to-play players power-mine for experience. For locations where there are three rocks in a triangle formation suitable for proper power-mining, see here.

label: Iron scimitar
title: Iron scimitar
lead: The iron scimitar is a melee weapon that can be used in combat. It is stronger than the bronze scimitar. Players can make an iron scimitar with 20 Smithing using 2 iron bars, giving 50 experience.

label: Iron shield
title: Iron shield
lead:
Iron shield may refer to:

*Iron sq shield
*Iron kiteshield

label: Iron spear
title: Iron spear
lead: The iron spear is a members-only two-handed melee weapon. An iron spear can be obtained by buying one from the Fortis Blacksmith, buying one from another player, or receiving it as a monster drop. The only way it can be created using the Smithing skill is through Barbarian Training after completing Tai Bwo Wannai Trio. It can be poisoned.

label: Iron sq shield
title: Iron sq shield
lead: An Iron square shield is the second weakest square shield. A player with 23 Smithing can make the shield by using two iron bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 50 experience. This shield can also be bought at Cassie's Shield Shop in northern Falador.

label: Iron sword
title: Iron sword
lead: The iron sword is a low-level weapon made of iron, stronger than the bronze sword. It can be purchased from Varrock Swordshop or made at level 19 Smithing with 1 iron bar, granting 25 experience.

label: Iron thrownaxe
title: Iron thrownaxe
lead: The iron thrownaxe is a thrownaxe made of iron. They can be wielded by players at any Ranged level. They can be bought from the Tribal Weapons Salesman in the Ranging Guild. Thrownaxes cannot be smithed.

label: Iron trimmed armour
title: Iron trimmed armour
lead: Iron trimmed armour is a possible reward from easy Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to Iron armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Iron trophy
title: Iron trophy
lead:
Iron trophy may refer to:

* Twisted iron trophy
* Trailblazer iron trophy
* Shattered relics iron trophy
* Trailblazer reloaded iron trophy
* Raging echoes iron trophy

label: Iron warhammer
title: Iron warhammer
lead:
The iron warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the bronze warhammer. It can be wielded at level 1 Strength. Players can make an iron warhammer with the Smithing skill at level 24 using 3 iron bars, giving 75 Smithing experience.

One spawns in the ruined castle near the bandits just south-west of the Hosidius Mess.

label: Ironman armour
title: Ironman armour
lead:
Ironman armour is a set of armour obtainable only by players who chose to be a standard ironman in Ironman Mode. It is obtained by speaking to Adam after leaving Tutorial Island, after choosing to be a standard ironman. Players may obtain a new set by speaking to him if they lose their set.

The armour pieces share their stats with the iron full helm, platebody and platelegs.

label: Ironman guide
title: Ironman guide
lead: This guide aims to give general advice, tips, and suggestions for regular and Hardcore Ironmen. Ultimate Ironmen have their own guide here.

label: Ironman Guide/Agility
title: Ironman Guide/Agility
lead:
Agility training on an ironman is not very different from training it on a regular account. A variety of agility courses can be used, with the majority of them requiring little to no inventory or equipment considerations. As a skill, Agility is very useful to train for its passive energy restoration effect, which speeds up many training methods, quest completion, and travel around the world in general. Agility also provides access to the graceful outfit, one of the best all-around equipment sets for almost any non-combat situation. Because Agility has very few inventory requirements to train, it is a good skill to train in tandem with other skills that use the inventory space, such as Magic or Fletching.

Ultimate Ironmen may find it difficult to fully take advantage of the Hallowed Sepulchre, though given how important the Ring of endurance is to run energy management it is recommended to always loot the Grand Hallowed Coffin.

label: Ironman Guide/Construction
title: Ironman Guide/Construction
lead: Construction training on an Ironman is not very different from training the skill normally; however, sourcing the required logs and/or planks does require additional planning.

label: Ironman Guide/Cooking
title: Ironman Guide/Cooking
lead: Cooking is most often trained by ironmen alongside Fishing, both to maximise efficiency of resources and for food.

label: Ironman Guide/Crafting
title: Ironman Guide/Crafting
lead: Crafting is a skill that Ironmen typically train through glassblowing, due to its low cost and availability. Many pieces of important jewellery require Crafting, such as teleportation jewellery and amulets of glory.

label: Ironman Guide/Defence
title: Ironman Guide/Defence
lead:
Defence is most often trained through combat. For more information about combat training on an Ironman, see:
*Ironman Guide/Melee
*Ironman Guide/Ranged
*Ironman Guide/Magic

label: Ironman guide/Efficient herb run guide
title: Ironman guide/Efficient herb run guide
lead:
Please note – this is a guide for those looking to make their farming runs more efficient – not a guide for someone who has never done any farming before.

This guide assumes you have the Farming level for watermelons. If you do not have the level for watermelons, use charter ships to buy pineapples and use them to fill compost bins.

label: Ironman Guide/Farming
title: Ironman Guide/Farming
lead: Farming is a skill trained primarily through Farming runs. The major difference for ironmen compared to normal Farming training is the difficulty in getting seeds, particularly for those early on in their journey.

label: Ironman Guide/Firemaking
title: Ironman Guide/Firemaking
lead: Firemaking is a skill trained simultaneously with Woodcutting in the lower levels. At level 50, players gain access to Wintertodt, which is ideal for Firemaking training, leaving the logs obtained through Woodcutting available to be used for birdhouse trapping, fletching or construction.

label: Ironman Guide/Fishing
title: Ironman Guide/Fishing
lead: Fishing is most often trained through "powerfishing", where the caught fish are dropped rather than banked. While the skill is classically a good source of food for combat training, the required time investment to catch and cook fish makes it less useful for Ironman players when compared to buyable food (such as cooked karambwans, jugs of wine, and potatoes with cheese) or Saradomin brews. At high Fishing levels, it is possible to get large amounts of raw sharks from fishing minnows, which can be a solid food choice once cooked.

label: Ironman Guide/Fletching
title: Ironman Guide/Fletching
lead:
The Fletching skill is most often trained by ironmen while working on other skills, as the ability to purchase all ingredients, as well as their stackability, makes them easy to bring to different training locations. Common skills Fletching is trained alongside are Runecraft, Agility, and Farming. Players also train Fletching while completing quests.

Fletching is also used for making high-level darts and arrows for use in Ranged combat. It can also be useful as a source of mid-tier Ranged armour or weaponry, depending on the player's Fletching level. Players looking to train Slayer will need large amounts of arrows if they plan to use Ranged in combat.

label: Ironman Guide/Herblore
title: Ironman Guide/Herblore
lead: Herblore is arguably the hardest skill to train on an ironman since collecting the herbs and most of the secondary ingredients can be slow and time-consuming. Therefore, it is advised to put the rewards of every experience lamp and book of knowledge into Herblore if possible. By the time all hard diaries are completed, if making all potions obtained along the way, the player should have around level 67–69 Herblore, just enough to start boosting to make ranging potions.

label: Ironman Guide/Hitpoints
title: Ironman Guide/Hitpoints
lead:
Hitpoints training is not significantly different on an ironman than a main account and is most often trained through combat. For more information about combat training on an Ironman, see:
*Ironman Guide/Melee
*Ironman Guide/Ranged
*Ironman Guide/Magic

For general Hitpoints training advice, including non-combat methods, see pay-to-play Hitpoints training.

label: Ironman Guide/Hunter
title: Ironman Guide/Hunter
lead:
Hunter is a skill that is commonly trained mostly as normal, however, an emphasis is placed on gathering ingredients for Herblore and Ranged, with bird house trapping, Herbiboar and hunter rumours all providing useful resources.

At higher levels, ironmen will often hunt chinchompas to aid in ranged training.

label: Ironman Guide/Magic
title: Ironman Guide/Magic
lead: Magic training for Ironmen is often similar to the normal training methods. However, due to the increased difficulty in obtaining runes, there is a heavier emphasis on Slayer in early training, as well as the conservation of runes and the value of drops.

label: Ironman Guide/Melee
title: Ironman Guide/Melee
lead: Melee training involves training Attack, Strength, Defence, and Hitpoints through combat. Ironman melee training is similar to the normal training methods, with a heavy emphasis on Slayer for resources.

label: Ironman Guide/Mining
title: Ironman Guide/Mining
lead:
Training Mining on an ironman is not very different from training it normally. In addition to the normal training methods, players will need to mine volcanic ash for making ultracompost and gem rocks for making expeditious bracelets at some point.

Pickaxes up to rune can be bought from Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop. A dragon pickaxe can only be obtained as a rare drop from Artio, Chaos Elemental, Callisto, Calvar'ion, Kalphite Queen, Spindel, Venenatis and Vet'ion, or as a very rare drop from King Black Dragon. A broken dragon pickaxe is a 1% chance to drop from an ore pack bought from Petrified Pete's Ore Shop at the Volcanic Mine for 4000 points. It must be repaired by taking it to Nurmof in the Dwarven Mine for a fee of coins.

label: Ironman Guide/Prayer
title: Ironman Guide/Prayer
lead:
Prayer is a slower skill to train for ironmen due to having to obtain bones themselves. Ideally, it is best to use every bone on an experience boosting altar, such as the Chaos Altar, Ectofuntus, Libation bowl, or with high Construction, a gilded altar in the chapel of your player-owned house. A bone crusher or ash sanctifier can be used for passive experience while training when the bones dropped are not worth picking up.

Early Prayer goals include level 43 for , and , and level 45 for all stat-boosting Prayers up to .

label: Ironman Guide/Ranged
title: Ironman Guide/Ranged
lead: Ranged is trained by Ironmen similar to the normal training methods, however an emphasis is placed on affordable and easily obtainable ammunition, particularly in the early-game. Notably, this does not recommend using a dwarf multicannon.

label: Ironman Guide/Runecraft
title: Ironman Guide/Runecraft
lead: Runecraft is mostly trained as normal, especially if training Runecraft through non-essence methods. However, essence-based training methods can be troublesome for ironmen due to lack of buying essence from the Grand Exchange and instead, ironmen would have to either passively obtain large quantities of pure essences in bulk from other activities or actively [[#Acquiring essence|gather essence]]. Fortunately, ironmen can effectively reach through non-essence training methods.

label: Ironman Guide/Sailing
title: Ironman Guide/Sailing
lead: Training Sailing on an Ironman is not substantially different from training the skill normally. Due to account limitations, gathering resources for ship and facility upgrades, along with cannonballs, may prove difficult.

label: Ironman Guide/Slayer
title: Ironman Guide/Slayer
lead:
Completing Slayer tasks is the sole way for Ironmen to acquire or upgrade several best-in-slot items, such as the abyssal whip, dragon boots, trident of the seas, occult necklace, and dragon hunter lance. High-level Slayer can also be an excellent way to earn money through valuable alchables.

Duradel is generally the best Slayer master to use. Konar quo Maten should be used for every milestone task for the extra Slayer reward points.

label: Ironman Guide/Smithing
title: Ironman Guide/Smithing
lead: Smithing is a skill most efficiently trained by buying ores from Ordan, and smelting them at the Blast Furnace. A decent amount of experience also comes from smelting ores and forging bars obtained from monster drops. Alternatively, the Giants' Foundry minigame is a slower but cheaper and more accessible alternative training, and can be profitable.

label: Ironman Guide/Thieving
title: Ironman Guide/Thieving
lead: Thieving training on an ironman is not very different from training it normally. Certain methods, such as pickpocketing Master Farmers, are favoured due to their valuable drops.

label: Ironman Guide/Woodcutting
title: Ironman Guide/Woodcutting
lead:
Woodcutting is a skill trained simultaneously with Firemaking in the lower levels. At higher levels, bank the logs necessary for Construction training. Otherwise the skill is trained as normal.

Ironman training is not substantially different from normal, however a large amount of mid-level experience comes from Wintertodt.

label: Ironman Mode
title: Ironman Mode
lead:
Ironman mode is an official game mode that players can choose to assign themselves. There are currently six types of ironmen, each with their own set of rules, armour (equivalent to iron equipment) and chat badge to denote their status (displayed in the table below.) There are also five separate HiScores for ironmen, one for each of the modes (excluding Unranked Group Ironman mode.)

These restrictions can be applied at the end of Tutorial Island by speaking to the Ironman tutor before being teleported by the Magic Instructor. At any point after Tutorial Island, players will have the option to convert their account to a standard unrestricted account ("main"), or to a regular Ironman in the case of a Hardcore or Ultimate Ironman, by talking to the other Ironman tutor in Lumbridge. However, this conversion is permanent and these restrictions cannot be retroactively imposed. After confirming to toggle a mode off, there will be a 7-day waiting period before the toggle will take effect, during which time the player may cancel the change if they change their mind or if their account had been hijacked; the change is also cancelled if a Hardcore Ironman dies during the waiting period to become a standard account.

label: Ironman Mode/Hardcore ironman firsts
title: Ironman Mode/Hardcore ironman firsts
lead: Hardcore ironman mode was released on November 10th of 2016; and this list contains documentation of the first hardcore ironman players to achieve specific goals. All of the first achievements that are listed on Jagex's official website, have been listed here, with the great addition of the first 99s achieved. Moreover, the lists here are sorted by date, while Jagex's aren't.

label: Ironman money making guide
title: Ironman money making guide
lead:
Making money as an Ironman can be difficult. Unlike regular accounts, Ironmen cannot generate coins passively by obtaining valuable items from skilling, bossing, or other sources, and simply selling them on the Grand Exchange. Instead, they must generate coins themselves, usually in less efficient ways.

This is important because many Ironman account goals are expensive. Large amounts of Coins are needed to purchase runes and skilling supplies, for instance. An Ironman's ability to make money can be a rate-limiting step which determines how quickly they are able to accomplish their other goals.

label: Irvig Senay
title: Irvig Senay
lead: Irvig Senay is one of the three long-dead warriors alongside San Tojalon and Ranalph Devere that are required to be killed to collect a piece of the heart crystal for the Legends' Quest. He is hostile until you kill him to obtain the hunk of crystal, but you can still attack him afterwards and he will fight back. He attacks with melee.

label: Isafdar conflict
title: Isafdar conflict
lead:
The Isafdar conflict began after the Baxtorian campaign and lasted several decades. It was a long and drawn-out struggle between the rebel elves and clan Iorwerth.

As part of the Elven Civil War, Prifddinas was lost. The elves that remained dispersed into the forest of Isafdar, settling into either the Iorwerth Camp or Lletya. Lord Iorwerth and his followers were willing to kill any opposing elf that stood in their way. Eventually, the rebel elves discovered that Iorwerth intended to summon Zamorak, whom they called the 'Dark Lord'. This, however, was not his true intention, as they found out in the quest Song of the Elves, where he reveals the truth to them: that Seren is the one he's been trying to free.

label: Island amenity
title: Island amenity
lead:
Island amenities are facilities players can construct on various islands accessed by Sailing. Amenities include anvils, bank chests, cooking pots, furnaces, looms, potter's wheels, pottery ovens, rowboats, spinning wheels, and water pumps. Each amenity requires a certain Construction level to build and awards some Construction experience. A hammer and saw are required to build any amenities, as well as other materials that differ by amenity.

Some island amenities have "very obvious purposes" whereas other island amenities "just exist for purposes."

label: Isle of Garmr
title: Isle of Garmr
lead:
The Isle of Garmr is an island mentioned in Imcandoria's fall. It supposedly lies somewhere in the Northern Ocean, possibly near Acheron. The island housed an Imcando dwarf settlement before it was abandoned after the destruction of Imcandoria. It was also home to a group of unspecified giants as well as several Auspah tribes.

Freja, an adventurer and member of the Myths' Guild, explored the island once, and brought back the transcript of Imcandoria's fall. She is planning an expedition to Acheron, but also mentions the Isle of Garmr, hinting the two locations are near each other.

label: Item IDs
title: Item IDs
lead: Each unique item has an in-game ID associated with it which can be used by tools such as plugins or the online interactive world map.

label: Item pack
title: Item pack
lead:
Item packs facilitate the buying of large quantities of items from a shop. The pack has a simple left-click open option. If a player has multiple packs, opening one will automatically open the remaining packs at a very slow pace of 1 pack every 1 or 2 game ticks. This can be sped up by manually opening them individually.

Item packs open all their items as "noted" when unpacked, unless the item is already stackable.

label: Item Retrieval Service
title: Item Retrieval Service
lead:
Item Retrieval Services, commonly known as deathbanks, are in-game services offered outside of dangerous, instanced boss fights and other challenges. If a player dies during one of these activities, their items will be saved and made available to retrieve at a later time, usually after the player pays a certain fee. This system prevents the player from permanently losing items due to an instanced area ceasing to exist after the player dies. Any items stored at an Item Retrieval Service will be permanently lost should the player die anywhere in an unsafe death. Thus it is recommended that players retrieve their items as soon as possible if planning to continue dangerous activities. Dying in an activity with an Item Retrieval Service will let the player keep their three most valuable items (affected by skull and Protect Item) but not additional untradeable items, unlike standard deaths outside PvP scenarios.

Retrieval fees can be paid using Death's Coffer. Fees will be first taken from the coffer and any remaining amount from your bank, or from currency stored within the deathbank.

label: item set
title: item set
lead: Item sets are used in the Grand Exchange to "compress" several components into a set. This makes it possible to trade an entire set at once, instead of trading each component individually. The only way to create sets from individual components is by swapping the pieces for the set via right-clicking a Grand Exchange clerk and select the "Sets" option to exchange item sets.

label: item spawn
title: item spawn
lead:
An item spawn is an exact location at which a specific item appears at regular intervals, free for any player to take. Although many item spawns are almost useless, some can be quite valuable. Secondary Herblore ingredients are often item spawns, such as snape grass or red spiders' eggs.

Some items are very fast to spawn, such as white berries, but others, like the sapphire spawn in level 46 Wilderness, are very slow. The respawn rate changes depending on the number of players logged into your current world according to the following formula: \left\lfloor \text{BaseRate} \frac{4000 - \text{Population}}{4000} \right\rfloor , where the \text{BaseRate} is the respawn duration on an empty world. If the world is full, the respawn interval is halved.

label: Items
title: Items
lead: In Old School RuneScape, items are physical objects that a player may have in their inventory or bank. Players distinguish them by their names and graphics. The game internally distinguishes items by unique ID numbers and config names that are not visible to players in-game.

label: Items Kept on Death
title: Items Kept on Death
lead:
When players die an unsafe death, some or all of their items will become lost or broken. The page lists the various rules that determine what happens to each item. Players should frequently familiarise themselves with what items they are risking by navigating to the Worn Equipment interface tab and clicking 
 View items kept on death. This interface has more comprehensive coverage of the rules listed below.

Important note: Ultimate Ironmen follow different item-loss rules to standard Ironmen and will drop all tradeable and untradeable items on the ground upon unsafe death. They are also unable to benefit from Protect Item despite being able to activate it. They have 60 minutes in game time to reclaim the items either on the tile they died on, or if that was in an instance, the tile other players would find their gravestone.

label: Items Kept on Death (Interface)
title: Items Kept on Death (Interface)
lead:
Items Kept on Death is an interface players can use to familiarise themselves with what will happen to their items upon unsafe death. The interface is located within the Worn Equipment tab. There are various rules that go into determining what happens to your items upon death.

Items outlined in white will become broken.

label: Ithell Clan
title: Ithell Clan
lead: The Ithell Clan is one of the eight elven clans who were originally brought to Gielinor from Tarddiad by Guthix and Seren in the early First Age. They are located south-west of the Tower of Voices in Prifddinas, off the western path. They are artisans skilled in Construction and Crafting and they are the most skilled crystal-chanters with most crystal-chanters hailing from this particular clan.

label: Ivandis Seergaze
title: Ivandis Seergaze
lead:
Ivandis Seergaze was one of the seven priestly warriors who fought against Lord Drakan and his forces.

They all died and were buried at Paterdomus, but rumours say that Ivandis was buried in a secret cave somewhere in Morytania. It is then found to be in an offshoot of the Myreque Hideout by removing the planks boarding up the entrance. His weapon was the rod of ivandis, made of a silver and mithril alloy and a sapphire. The rod is imbued with magic and blessed by the holiness of the River Salve. Ivandis battled Drakan's creatures with his staff, and after trapping them with his staff, he would then use a Serum of Guthix.

label: Jade
title: Jade
lead:
Jade is a semi-precious gem used mainly in Crafting. It can be cut from an uncut jade with a chisel at level 13 Crafting, yielding 20 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the jade, resulting in a crushed gem and 5 experience.

One jade is used in the Legends' Quest.

label: Jadid
title: Jadid
lead: Jadid is one of the people observing the fights at the Emir's Arena. He can be found on top of the walls and is near the Gnome Restaurant customer and drunken off-duty pilot, Captain Daerkin.

label: Jagex
title: Jagex
lead: Jagex Limited (pronounced ), also known as Jagex Software or JaGeX Games Studio, and currently stylised as Jagex: The RuneScape Company, is a British video game developer and publisher, best known for its MMORPGs RuneScape and Old School RuneScape. The company's name is contracted from "Java Gaming Experts" or "Just About the Gaming Experience".

label: Jagex Account
title: Jagex Account
lead: Jagex Accounts are a method used to access Jagex games. They aim to be a successor to the pre-2023 login system of RuneScape and Old School RuneScape and the RuneScape Authenticator. These accounts provide increased security and stability, using modern industry-standard technology . To play the game, a Jagex Account may only be logged in to through the Jagex Launcher.

label: Jagex Account Guardian
title: Jagex Account Guardian
lead:
The Jagex Account Guardian was an account security feature that provided enhanced security, blocking unknown devices from accessing a player's account. Although the functionality of the system remained undisclosed as stated by Jagex, it seemed to use modern device-recognising technologies to authenticate a user trying to log in. This included a combination of the user's MAC address, their IP address, an encrypted security token saved on the user's system, as well as other unstated properties. Its aim was to prevent against and hijacking; additionally, it discouraged account sharing. It has since been superseded by the RuneScape Authenticator.

A player chose the device(s) that they wish to grant access to for the account. Unknown devices required to pass email and security checks before access was permitted.

label: Jagex Audio Team
title: Jagex Audio Team
lead:
The Jagex Audio Team is a team of Jagex employees compose and create the various sounds and music across all jagex games. There are currently music tracks, (855 when including unlisted and unused music, and 1169 when including Jingles) in the game, each composed by various different people. The way the team works on projects is that they choose from a list of available projects and do them one at a time.

The audio team works on all audio, not just music. Which can include sound effects or sound systems within the game, while some are purely composers for music.

label: Jagex Clan Cup 2013
title: Jagex Clan Cup 2013
lead: The Old School Clan Cup was a tournament that was hosted by Jagex during 2013. Clans competed in eight different tournaments with teams of varying sizes and styles. Rules, rosters, and results were all hosted on a dedicated website.

label: Jagex Clan Cup 2014
title: Jagex Clan Cup 2014
lead: The 2014 Clan Cup was a tournament that was hosted by Jagex during the summer of 2014. Clans across Old School RuneScape competed in various Player killing, Monster killing, or skilling events to see which clan was the best. There were three categories of events during the cup.

label: Jagex Launcher
title: Jagex Launcher
lead:
The Jagex Launcher is an official game launcher for Old School RuneScape and . It was launched on 14 March 2022 through an open beta.

Currently, it is available for installation on and . Whilst systems are not officially supported, third-party workarounds are available.

Jagex Moderators, also known as Staff Moderators, Jagex Mods, JMods, or admins, are employees working for Jagex Ltd. Jagex Moderator accounts are only used for work purposes such as play-testing, debugging, and dealing with in-game situations.

label: Jagged reefs
title: Jagged reefs
lead: Jagged reefs are a sailing hazard found around the island of Crandor and in Aehecatl. Attempting to traverse these waters will significantly slow the player's boat and continuously damage it (5 damage around Crandor and 20 damage in Aehecatl). It will also give the chatbox message The jagged reefs here shred the underside of the boat! No hull nor keel can withstand them! Currently, there is no way to mitigate the effects of jagged reefs.

label: Jagged wall
title: Jagged wall
lead: The Jagged wall is a scenery object located at the Shaman Caves during and after the Legends' Quest. It can be jumped over to access the next part of the dungeon, which requires level 50 Agility and can be failed, dealing damage.

label: Jail guard
title: Jail guard
lead:
Jail guards are aggressive bandits found around the Draynor Village jail. They are level 26 and can be dangerous to low level players, especially in numbers, as they are able to wander quite far from the jail and may pursue players on the nearby road or partially into the village. They are equipped with a steel mace, leather body, and leather gloves.

The jail guard with blonde hair is not initially aggressive.

label: Jail key
title: Jail key
lead:
The jail key is dropped by the Jailer, found in the Black Knights' Base, deep within Taverley Dungeon. The key gives access to the jail cell containing Velrak the explorer, who will in turn give players the Dusty key which may be used to travel deeper into the dungeon. It can also be used to unlock the door that holds two dwarves, opposite to Velrak the explorer's cell.

The jail key is also one of the fifty required items to hand the dwarf in the Mourning's End Part II quest if you need a death talisman.

label: Jailer
title: Jailer
lead: The jailer is found in the Black Knights' Base in Taverley Dungeon. He guards the jail holding Velrak the explorer, who has the dusty key, required to access the deeper parts of the dungeon. Players who are navigating the dungeon for the first time must kill the jailer to obtain the jail key, which can be used to unlock Velrak's cell. The jailer can be safespotted using Ranged or Magic by standing behind the table at the eastern end of the hallway.

label: Jal
title: Jal
lead:
Jal may refer to:

*TzHaar-Mej-Jal, a TzHaar guarding the TzHaar Fight Cave.

label: Jangerberries
title: Jangerberries
lead:
Jangerberries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting jangerberry seeds. They are used in Herblore to make Zamorak brews or as protection payment for snape grass (x5).

Jangerberries restore 2 hitpoints, 1 prayer point, temporarily boosts Attack by 2 and Strength by 1, and reduces Defence by 1. Adding them to a compost bin makes supercompost, though this is not recommended as watermelons or pineapples are far cheaper and have the same effect.

label: Jaraah
title: Jaraah
lead: Jaraah also known as "The Butcher" is one of the two surgeons at the Emir's Arena. Jaraah, along with Surgeon General Tafani, and the two nurses (Sabreen and A'abla), are able to heal players, restoring all their hitpoints for no cost, but cannot cure poison. Players must right-click (and choose "Heal" from the Choose Option menu) or talk to these NPCs to benefit from this.

label: Jareesh
title: Jareesh
lead:
Jareesh was a citizen of Nardah. Because there was a drought brought upon by a curse, he travelled to the Water Ravine Dungeon with the hopes of appealing to Elidinis and breaking the curse. His story is written in a ballad.

He failed to reach his goal, but in the form of his ballad, the player gained helpful clues to pass through the dungeon and break the curse. His current fate is unknown.

label: Jas
title: Jas
lead: Jas is an ancient and enigmatic deity responsible for the creation of the Stone of Jas, which has played a significant role in the history of Gielinor, most notably as a central cause of the God Wars. Jas magically bound the Dragonkin to the stone, forcing them to unwillingly operate as a defence mechanism against anyone who attempts to wield its power.

label: Jatix
title: Jatix
lead: Jatix is a druid and citizen of Taverley, a small village located south of Burthorpe. He owns Jatix's Herblore Shop shop, located just west of the Tree Patch.

label: Jatix's Herblore Shop.
title: Jatix's Herblore Shop.
lead:
Jatix's Herblore Shop is a shop in Taverley owned by Jatix that sells Herblore supplies. This shop sells empty vials and eyes of newt in packs.

Sanfew, who plays a part in various quests, is upstairs on the .

label: Jatizso (person)
title: Jatizso (person)
lead:
Jatizso was the founder of Jatizso, a Fremennik island. He was one of the youngest sons of an unnamed king, and the brother of Neitiznot, Neitiznot's namesake and founder; they were both exiled by their father due to their feuds, which are still manifested in the feuds between native islanders.

The current king of Jatizso, King Gjuki Sorvott IV, is descended from him.

label: Java
title: Java
lead:
Java is an object-oriented originally developed by at . It was released in 1995 as a core component of Sun Microsystems' Java platform. currently develops the language and JVM for Windows, Solaris, Linux and macOS.

Java can run on most popular operating systems as it compiles code into platform independent, low-level byte-code via the Java Virtual Machine that (which is platform specific) translates this byte-code into native instructions.

label: Java Client
title: Java Client
lead:
The Java Client or Legacy Java Client was an Old School RuneScape client built by Jagex for desktop platforms. In the past, the client was an alternative to playing the game in a browser. However, due to multiple browsers discontinuing support for s, Jagex was forced to drop support for browser play. The client does not support , and is limited to 1 processor core and 50 frames per second.

The Legacy Java Client was no longer the default client on 20 July 2023 and was announced to be fully deprecated since 24 July 2024 despite getting updates up until 1 October 2025. As of 28 January 2026, the Legacy Java Client can no longer be used , although it is still available for download from the Old School RuneScape website for Windows and macOS. It was possible to run the Java client on Linux, although not officially supported.

label: javelin
title: javelin
lead:
Javelins are a type of heavy ranged ammunition used by light and heavy ballistae. Javelins can be fletched by combining javelin tips with javelin shafts.

Most javelins can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store, or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after completion of Monkey Madness II. Amethyst, dragon, and Morrigan's javelins cannot be found in any store.

label: Javelin (scenery)
title: Javelin (scenery)
lead: Javelin consist of two javelins hanging on a wall in the shape of an X. The javelins appear to be steel javelins.

label: Javelin (unobtainable item)
title: Javelin (unobtainable item)
lead:
The javelin is an unobtainable item release alongside RuneScape 2. Although it is classified internally as a weapon, it lacks a wield option and does not have any equip animations defined.

It was presumably a leftover from development, created to test the implementation of the new javelin weapons in RuneScape 2.

label: Javelin tip
title: Javelin tip
lead:
Javelin tips are a members-only item, and are used to make javelins. Smithing a metal bar or cutting an amethyst will yield 5 javelin tips. Each head requires a javelin shaft to make it into a javelin.

label: Jerico
title: Jerico
lead:
Jerico is a pigeon enthusiast living between the chapel and the northern bank of East Ardougne. He owns several pigeons, which he uses to communicate with the quarantined West Ardougne. If the player chooses to, he will eagerly engage them in conversation about pigeons.

He has several friends in Ardougne, such as Edmond, Omart, and Kilron. When Elena wanted to study the plague, he helped the adventurer who rescued her to sneak over the wall in order to retrieve her distillator, which had been stolen by the mourners. He distracted the mourners watching the gate by releasing several of his pigeons, allowing the adventurer to climb over and into the quarantined city.

label: Jester (interface item)
title: Jester (interface item)
lead:
The Jester is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Jester.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Jethick
title: Jethick
lead: Jethick is an elderly citizen of West Ardougne unaffected by the plague. He can be found in the town square of West Ardougne or in the basement of the Rehnison household during part of the Song of the Elves quest.

label: jewellery
title: jewellery
lead:
Jewellery is any item worn in the ring slot or neck slot of the Worn Equipment tab; members can wear bracelets in the hand slot. Most jewellery can be created using Crafting, and enchanted with Magic to gain special properties such as teleportation, combat stats enhancement, and skilling utility. Unenchanted jewellery is purely decorative.

Access to jewellery in free-to-play is significantly limited: the availability of amulets, rings, and necklaces is restricted to sapphire through diamond, there are no bracelets available, and the only available enchanted jewellery is the ring of forging.

label: Jewellery Enchantments
title: Jewellery Enchantments
lead:
Jewellery Enchantments are a set of enchantment spells on the standard spellbook used specifically for gold and silver jewellery with gemstones to give the item new properties.

Unlike Enchant Crossbow Bolt, Jewellery Enchantments is not a single spell, but exists as a subpage of the standard spellbook, and houses the seven enchantment spells used for jewellery. Each spell requires different Magic levels for casting, as well as a suitable jewellery item. It is accessible for both free-to-play and members, though free-to-play players may only use the first four levels of enchantments and can only enchant into items that are also free-to-play.

label: Jiminua
title: Jiminua
lead:
Jiminua is a lady on the north side of Tai Bwo Wannai village. She runs Jiminua's Jungle Store.

Interestingly, she sells cooked beef for more money than cooked bread, although the bread heals more.

label: Jiminua's Jungle Store.
title: Jiminua's Jungle Store.
lead:
Jiminua's Jungle Store is a general store that sells many useful items for those adventuring in the Karamjan jungle, such as antipoison, pickaxes, machetes, and axes. It is also notable for being one of the few places to obtain both charcoal and papyrus. Because of the items it stocks, this shop is useful for the nearby minigame Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup.

Along with its functionality as a general store, the building houses Aisles, an NPC who will un-note players' noted items for a fee of five coins per item.

label: Jingles
title: Jingles
lead:
Jingles are short tracks played during specific occasions, such as completing a quest, levelling up, or winning a minigame.

Jingles will play on top of default music, and the Music Player will display the name of the previous track that was playing. As such, jingles have no name that is visible in-game.

label: Joe (Fight Arena)
title: Joe (Fight Arena)
lead: Joe is a prisoner found in the Fight Arena, trapped along with Kelvin in the south-western cell. He and Kelvin are fightslaves in the arena.

label: Joe (jail)
title: Joe (jail)
lead:
Joe is Lady Keli's talkative head bodyguard in the jail east of Draynor Village. During the Prince Ali Rescue quest, the player must incapacitate him so they can then tie up Lady Keli and rescue Prince Ali. This is done by getting him drunk on beer. To do this, use three beers on him until he gets too drunk to guard the prince. Prince Ali can then be rescued if the player has the correct materials, namely some rope and a bronze key. Should the player attempt to tie up Lady Keli before Joe is drunk, he will intervene.

Joe seemed to be wearing a steel mace, steel platelegs, leather boots, leather gloves, and an iron chainbody.

label: Jogre
title: Jogre
lead:
Jogres are a type of ogre that live in the jungles of Karamja. Their attacks are slow but powerful, however their low defence allows them to be killed quickly. They are a threat mostly to lower-level players exploring Karamja due to their high damage hits.

Jogres can also be found within the God Wars Dungeon, located to the north of Trollheim. As with other Bandosian followers in the dungeon, wearing a piece of Bandos-aligned equipment will make them unaggressive to the player.

label: Jogre bones
title: Jogre bones
lead:
Jogre bones are bones dropped by jogres, which give 15 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways: 
* 45 XP when casting Sinister Offering.
* 45 XP when offered at the Sacred Bone Burner after the appropriate faith level has been achieved.
* 52.5 XP when offered at a gilded altar with two burners lit or at the Chaos Temple.
* 60 XP when offered at the Ectofuntus in the form of jogre bonemeal.

They can be lit with a tinderbox at level 30 Firemaking to make burnt jogre bones, granting 90 Firemaking experience. Burnt jogre bones are used with karambwanji paste during the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest to make marinated j' bones.

label: Johnathon
title: Johnathon
lead:
Johnathon Fitzharmon is the brother of Caleb and Avan and one of the sons of Dimintheis. He can be found on the of the Jolly Boar Inn. Johnathon plays a role in the Family Crest quest: he was fighting Chronozon, a powerful demon in the Edgeville Dungeon, but began losing the fight and tried to retreat. In his way was a poison spider, which bit him, poisoning him. When the player meets him, he will ask for an antipoison to cure himself.

After the player brings him an antipoison, he tells the player that in order to beat Chronozon, the player must cast all four blast spells at least once. After the quest is complete, he offers to enchant the steel gauntlets into chaos gauntlets, which increase the maximum damage of all bolt spells by 3. If the gauntlets are already imbued with another power, Johnathon will ask for 25,000 coins to re-enchant them. If the Family Pest miniquest has been completed, Johnathon will give the chaos gauntlets directly for free instead.

label: Jolly Boar Inn
title: Jolly Boar Inn
lead:
The Jolly Boar Inn is a two-story bar and inn located north-east of Varrock, on the southern border of the Wilderness. It contains a range and a spawn point for thread. The bartender only sells (ordinary) beer for 2 coins each.

The bar contains Johnathon from the Family Crest quest. In the early days of RuneScape 2, this bar was the location of Dr Harlow, an important character in the Vampyre Slayer quest. He was moved to the Blue Moon Inn because newer players had a hard time finding the bar and would often wander into the nearby Wilderness. A man upstairs and a woman downstairs, though they both walk normally, act drunk when you talk to them, conversing with a player about how there are two of them and mumbling about "giant hairy cabbages". A Black Knight and a Thief also wander around the inn, but the knight is not aggressive, unlike those at the Black Knights' Fortress. The Bartender of the Jolly Boar Inn will say that the Bartender of the Blue Moon Inn is crazy because he thinks RuneScape is in a computer game. A quite-unfriendly Cook resides in the inn, on the south-east corner, cooking something on the range.

label: Jolly R
title: Jolly R
lead:
Jolly R is a music track that is unlocked in Brimhaven, including on the island accessible by fairy ring code . In this area, the music player will shuffle between this track, High Seas and Landlubber.

In Classic mode, the track only plays in the northern docks area of Brimhaven.

label: Jolly Roger
title: Jolly Roger
lead: Jolly Roger is a pirate flag adorning the walls of the pub Dead Man's Chest in Brimhaven.

label: Jonah who is 7 3/4
title: Jonah who is 7 3/4
lead:
Jonah who is 7 3/4 was a child who was kidnapped by Gublinches and later rescued during the course of the 2013 Christmas event. He is written to by a player in a Postbag from the Hedge where he responds with a thank you.

He is asked why he is always jumping without a break, and he explains he prefers jumping to mining. He also states that jumping helps to forget things because "memmerys start to leap outta yer ears" and that it makes one look taller.

label: Jones
title: Jones
lead:
Jones may also refer to:
*Anna Jones, a former archaeologist found in What Lies Below
*Beedy Eye Jones, a pirate aboard the Lady Zay
*Butler Jones, the Carnillean family's butler
*Dallas Jones, an NPC involved in Dragon Slayer II

label: Jonny the Beard
title: Jonny the Beard
lead:
Jonny the Beard is a notorious mass murderer and pirate captain who can be found in the Blue Moon Inn in southern Varrock. He came to Varrock from Port Sarim to meet with the Black Arm Gang; those who wish to join the Phoenix Gang during the Shield of Arrav quest must kill him and bring the intel report he drops to Straven.

He can only be attacked once the player is tasked by Straven to kill him, and he permanently disappears after the quest for those who killed him.

label: Josef
title: Josef
lead:
Josef was a follower of Agrith-Naar in the Shadow of the Storm quest and was one of the dark wizards recruited by Denath to summon the Agrith-Naar demon. The Demonic tome can be found on the ruined kilns around Uzer.

Josef ran away from the temple in the background of the quest, and his friend, Matthew, is worried about his fate. What happened to him was that he turned to dust because of a spell caused by Denath.

label: Joshua
title: Joshua
lead: Joshua is one of the competitors during the Fishing Contest quest. He informs the player about Grandpa Jack and his inability to keep secrets. He speaks with a younger accent calling the player "dude" and wears a yin yang amulet, but how he came to own it is unknown.

label: Journal
title: Journal

label: Journal (Filliman Tarlock)
title: Journal (Filliman Tarlock)
lead:
Filliman Tarlock's journal is one of a number of items that are simply called 'Journal' in the inventory. This particular journal is obtained by searching the tree in the middle of Filliman's grotto south of Mort Myre Swamp during the Nature Spirit quest. The player must read the journal to find vague instructions on how Filliman can transcend his current ghostly form to become a nature spirit.

The journal is not available from the tree after the quest. It is not found in the bookcase in a player-owned house.

label: Jug
title: Jug
lead:
A Jug is an item that can be filled with water to create a jug of water. Wine can also be made by adding grapes to a jug of water.

Jugs can be bought at general stores for one coin each. Jugs are not sold at the Catherby, East Ardougne, or West Ardougne general store. However, jugs are sold by the charter crew members in Catherby. Wine Shop in Draynor Village sells them for the same price as the general stores, and they can be thieved from the stall. Hassan at the Al Kharid palace may also give free jugs of water if the player has not completed Prince Ali Rescue.

label: Jug (disambiguation)
title: Jug (disambiguation)
lead:
A jug may refer to:

* Empty jug pack
* Half full wine jug
* Jug

* Jug of blessed wine
