label: Keldagrim Mine
title: Keldagrim Mine
lead:
Keldagrim Mine may refer to:

*Dondakan's mine, also known as the Arzinian Mine, a site unlocked during Between a Rock... that contains 146 gold rocks
*Keldagrim entrance mining site, a surface-level mining site outside Keldagrim's entrance, in the eastern Fremennik Province
*Keldagrim north-east mine, a site near the Keldagrim Blast Furnace that contains nine coal rocks
*Keldagrim south-west mine, a large mining area outside Keldagrim that houses small deposits of copper, tin, iron, and gold

label: Keldagrim minecart system
title: Keldagrim minecart system
lead:
.]]
Keldagrim minecarts are a system of transportation often used to travel to and from the dwarven capital, Keldagrim. Players must have started The Giant Dwarf quest to use this travel method. It is one of three ways to enter Keldagrim directly.

The cart conductors charge a small fee (100 to 150 coins, halved while wearing a Ring of charos (a)) to travel using the minecart system. Travels from the Grand Exchange to Keldagrim and vice versa are free of charge.

label: Keldagrim Trading
title: Keldagrim Trading
lead:
Trade Octagon, where the minigame would have taken place.]]
Keldagrim Trading was an unreleased minigame developed by Mod Vincent and later Mod Greg, planned for the Trade Octagon on the first floor of Keldagrim Palace. The minigame would have focused on merchanting, and involved speculating on the fluctuating prices of the items sold by the dwarven traders.

label: Keldagrim–Troll Country War
title: Keldagrim–Troll Country War
lead:
The Keldagrim–Troll Country War is a longstanding conflict between the two nations from which its name is derived.

Keldagrim was founded during the Third Age, when a dwarven tribe fled beneath the mountain range east of the Fremennik Province in order to escape the God Wars. Cut off from the world above, the dwarves remained ignorant of the end of the God Wars. This changed when the Trolls launched an invasion against the city sometime in the Fourth Age, thus beginning the Keldagrim-Troll Country War.

label: Kelvin
title: Kelvin
lead: Kelvin is a prisoner found in the Fight Arena, trapped along with Joe in the south-western cell. He and Joe are fightslaves in the arena.

label: Kennith
title: Kennith
lead:
Kennith is a boy who features in the Sea Slug quest. During the quest, the player is enlisted by Kennith's mother, Caroline, to find him after he and his father went to the fishing platform and did not return.

After the quest, he can be found at his house in Witchaven with his parents Kent and Caroline. He and his parents, as well as Holgart and Ezekial Lovecraft are the only people in Witchaven who are not possessed by sea slugs by the end of Slug Menace.

label: Kent
title: Kent
lead: Kent features in the Sea Slug quest. During the quest he is found on an unknown island; when the quest is done he is back at Witchaven. He has a wife Caroline and a son Kennith.

label: Keorgius Feryis
title: Keorgius Feryis
lead:
Keorgius Feryis was a brother-in-arms loyal to Ivandis Seergaze in the aftermath of the Fourth Age Misthalin - Morytania War. Keorgius was amongst those responsible for burying the deceased Seergaze in a cavern connected to a large tunnel network running beneath Mort Myre Swamp. He is known to have lived in approximately 1200 of the Fourth Age.

Keorgius was amongst those veterans of the war to continue into Morytania with Seergaze. Seergaze was killed at some point while combatting the tyranny of Lord Drakan, leaving his men to bury him. Keorgius and the rest of Seergaze's followers buried him with his staff, marking the cavern so as to deter looters and explorers. The group returned to Misthalin through Paterdomus, where Keorgius contributed to a document describing their time in Morytania.

label: Kerapac
title: Kerapac
lead: Kerapac is an influential dragonkin mentioned in the old notes in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. He primarily focused on creating dragons and did not believe in offshoots. Whatever he said was law, and he had enough influence to make sure that none of the Dragonkin working with him would disobey his orders, something which Karuulm disliked.

label: Kethsi
title: Kethsi
lead: Kethsi is a location mentioned by Zorgoth in the Lithkren vault notes. According to Zorgoth, multiple Necrosyrte dragonkin were slain on Kethsi by humans who had obtained weapons capable of killing dragonkin. The exact location of Kethsi is currently unknown.

label: Key (Biohazard)
title: Key (Biohazard)
lead:
The Key is a quest item used only in Biohazard. It is automatically placed into the player's inventory after killing the level-13 Mourner on the of the Mourner Headquarters in West Ardougne.

It is used to open a gate to access a stockroom full of crates, one of which holds a distillator.

label: Key (blue)
title: Key (blue)
lead:
The blue key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by one of the two zombies in the basement of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the blue door, where it will disintegrate upon being used.

label: Key (disambiguation)
title: Key (disambiguation)
lead:
Key may refer to several items, most of which are used in quests:
*List of keys

Key may also refer to items named key:
*Key (Biohazard)
*Key (Elemental Workshop II)
*Key (Ernest the Chicken)
*Key (Melzar's Maze)
*Key (Olaf's Quest)
*Key (The Lost Tribe)
*Key (Treasure Trails)
*Key (Witch's House)
*Key (Waterfall Dungeon)

label: Key (Ernest the Chicken)
title: Key (Ernest the Chicken)
lead:
The Key is a quest item used only in Ernest the Chicken. It is found by using a spade on the compost heap inside Draynor Manor's west wall during the quest.

It is used to open the door to the room containing a skeleton and the rubber tube. It can only be obtained during the quest and is kept upon completion.

label: Key (green)
title: Key (green)
lead:
The green key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by the lesser demon in the basement of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the green door, where it will disintegrate upon being used.

label: Key (magenta)
title: Key (magenta)
lead:
The magenta key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by Melzar the Mad in the basement of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the magenta door, where it will disintegrate upon being used.

label: Key (Melzar's Maze)
title: Key (Melzar's Maze)
lead: Keys of various colours are used to unlock doors and progress further in Melzar's Maze during the Dragon Slayer I quest. They are obtained by killing the creatures in the maze in order to unlock doors of the corresponding colour. Players must obtain each of the different coloured keys to retrieve the map piece located at the end of the maze needed to complete the quest. Once used, the keys will disintegrate. Entry into Melzar's Maze requires a maze key, obtained from the Guildmaster in the Champions' Guild.

label: Key (orange)
title: Key (orange)
lead:
The orange key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by the ghost wearing a hood and no cape on the floor of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the orange doors, where it will disintegrate upon being used.

label: Key (red)
title: Key (red)
lead:
The red key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by the small zombie rat with the long tail on the floor of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the red doors, where it will disintegrate upon being used.

label: Key (Treasure Trails)
title: Key (Treasure Trails)
lead:
A key is an item needed to unlock a chest or drawer during a Treasure Trail.

There will be a clue telling you where to get it. The key is a drop only when carrying the clue scroll. It disappears when used to open the chest or drawer. Keys are non-tradeable objects, specific to the player who finds them. They are used on all levels of treasure trails.

label: Key (Tree Gnome Village Dungeon)
title: Key (Tree Gnome Village Dungeon)
lead:
The key is an item found in the Tree Gnome Village Dungeon. Prior to starting the Roving Elves quest, it can be found in a crate in the storeroom to the north-east of the dungeon entrance. It opens the door to the jail, found north-west of the dungeon entrance. Upon finding it, the player will receive the message "You found a large key". The crate can be searched for another key if the player loses it. It cannot be stored on a Steel key ring.

Note that if a player has a low combat level, they will likely receive damage from the surrounding monsters whilst searching the crates for the key.

label: Key (Waterfall Dungeon)
title: Key (Waterfall Dungeon)
lead:
Key is an item found in the Waterfall Dungeon by searching a crate in the eastern chamber of the dungeon. It is used to open the two doors in western part of the dungeon, towards the Chalice of Eternity. It also spawns in the chamber between these two doors, allowing the player to pass back through the door if they were to drop it.

The key is used in several quests. It cannot be stored on a steel key ring.

label: Key (Witch's House)
title: Key (Witch's House)
lead:
The key is a quest item used during the Witch's House quest to open the shed door and retrieve the ball. It is found by searching the fountain in Nora T. Hagg's garden.

Duplicates can be drop tricked by searching the fountain to obtain another. This key cannot be added to a steel key ring.

label: Key (yellow)
title: Key (yellow)
lead:
The yellow key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is dropped by the skeleton wielding a round shield on the floor of Melzar's Maze.

Is it used to unlock the yellow doors, where it will disintegrate upon being used.

label: Key piece
title: Key piece
lead:
Key piece may refer to:

* Dragon key piece
* Frozen key piece (armadyl)
* Frozen key piece (bandos)
* Frozen key piece (saradomin)
* Frozen key piece (zamorak)
* Loop half of key
* Tooth half of key

label: Key print
title: Key print
lead:
A key print is a quest item in the Prince Ali Rescue quest. It is obtained by pressing Lady Keli's cell key into soft clay. The key print is used to make a bronze key that unlocks the cell door.

If lost, you must speak to Lady Keli again with soft clay, pink skirt, paste, and a dyed yellow wig in your inventory to obtain a new key print.

label: Khali brew
title: Khali brew
lead: Khali brew is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest. Once the player has spoken to the Head Guard in the south-eastern room of the jail, it is possible to buy the beer for coins from the Khazard barman in the bar in the south-west corner of the Fight Arena. The Khazard barman suggests lying down before drinking it so there is less distance to collapse; however, there is no option for the player to drink it. Giving it to the Head Guard will get him drunk and allow you to steal the Khazard cell keys.

label: Kharazi Dungeon
title: Kharazi Dungeon
lead:
Kharazi Dungeon may refer to:
* Shaman Caves, the upper level of the cave system.
* Viyeldi caves, the lower level of the cave system.

label: Kharazi Jungle
title: Kharazi Jungle
lead:
The Kharazi Jungle is an area south of Shilo Village on Karamja. This is where most of the Legends' Quest takes place, and it is necessary to start the quest in order to enter the jungle (you only have to talk to Radimus Erkle and receive Radimus notes). A machete and a Woodcutting axe are required to hack through the dense jungle blocking the path along with the notes. Radimus notes is required to navigate it if players have not completed Legends' Quest.

The jungle often serves as the location for Treasure Trail co-ordinates.

label: Kharazi tribe
title: Kharazi tribe
lead:
The Kharazi Tribe is a large and spread-out tribe of warriors located in the Kharazi Jungle, located in the south of the large island Karamja. During the Legends' Quest, players commune with the Kharazi Tribe in order to gain access to the Legends' Guild, though the task proves much greater when a proud member of the tribe, Gujuo, tells the player that they must exorcise an evil demon called Nezikchened who has taken to dwelling in their totems.

The members of the Kharazi Tribe meet around these various totems, which are made from a valuable and rare tree called the Yommi tree, which are grown only in patches of fertile soil in the Kharazi Jungle. In addition to their sacred trees, they regard a small pool of water in the middle of the jungle as holy, and it is worthy of note that they consider the metal gold as blessed, calling it "sun-metal". This attitude toward gold mirrors that of the real-world Aztecs and Incas.

label: Kharid Scorpion
title: Kharid Scorpion
lead:
Kharid Scorpions are a rare species of scorpion native to the Kharidian Desert. They play a prominent role in the Scorpion Catcher quest, during which players must capture three that escaped from the wizard Thormac. Players can catch them during the Scorpion Catcher with a scorpion cage. Locations are as follows:
*One roams freely on the of the Edgeville Monastery.
*Another can be found in the beginning of the Taverley Dungeon. The scorpion in Taverley Dungeon is behind a disguised wall that can only be opened after starting the quest.
*The final one is found in the Barbarian Agility area at the Barbarian Outpost.

None of these scorpions are attackable. If players attempt to pick them up, they will always suffer 3 Hitpoints of typeless damage, and the message The scorpion stings you! will be displayed. This damage can kill the player if they have 3 HP or less when attempting to pick one up. The scorpion damage is not poisonous, though it is typeless (similar to damage from failing to pickpocket) and therefore unaffected by protection prayers. Some players may use them as a form of suicide when they have low Hitpoints or are in need of stat healing.

label: Kharidian cactus
title: Kharidian cactus
lead:
Kharidian cacti can be found around the Kharidian Desert. They can be used to fill waterskins, increasing them by one dose, but not other types of containers. Similar to webs, a knife or a slash weapon is needed to cut them open.

Successfully cutting a cactus and filling a waterskin will display the text You top up your skin with water from the cactus and award 10 Woodcutting experience. Failing to do so will display the text You fail to cut the cactus correctly and it gives no water this time and award 0.4 Woodcutting experience. If the player successfully cuts a cactus but has no waterskin, the chatbox will display You have no empty waterskins to put the water in.. There is currently no way to increase the chance of success. A dry cactus will become healthy again after 1 minute. Refilling a waterskin this way is a requirement for the Easy Desert Diary.

label: Kharidian Desert
title: Kharidian Desert
lead:
The Kharidian Desert is an expansive region located south of the nations of Misthalin and Morytania. The desert becomes a dangerous region south of the Shantay Pass, requiring a player to drink from waterskins or other sources of water to avoid dehydration. The player will automatically drink every 90 seconds if they have a waterskin with charges in their inventory; the time between drinks can be extended by wearing heat-resistant gear. Failing to drink will cause the player to periodically lose hitpoints. Within the boundaries of towns, players are immune to the desert heat and do not need to drink.

Players may quickly travel to certain locations by using magic carpet rides, though some destinations are unavailable until certain quests have been completed.

label: Kharidian Desert Campaign
title: Kharidian Desert Campaign
lead:
The Kharidian Desert Campaign is an unofficial name given to a prolonged period of battles and skirmishes that occurred during the late Third Age as part of the cataclysmic God Wars. The Campaign was amongst the most violent and devastating of the God Wars, and saw some of the most intense conflict of the period.

Unlike the rest of Gielinor, the Kharidian Desert managed to avoid most conflict during the first 3,000 years of the God Wars. It was only during the last thousand years of the Wars that primarily Saradominist and Zamorakian military forces began to invade the region searching new land and resources. Although the forces that entered the region initially focused mainly on fighting each other, the native Menaphite people were often slain in the battles and eventually became the direct target of mainly Zamorakian hostilities.

label: Kharidian Empire
title: Kharidian Empire
lead:
The Kharidian Empire was founded in Second Age by Elidinis, Tumeken, Amascut and Icthlarin in the Second Age. The Empire's lands were located in the land currently known as the Kharidian Desert.

The Kharidian Empire built cities and big structures all over the desert, most notably the still-standing Emir's Arena.

label: Kharidian–Zarosian War
title: Kharidian–Zarosian War
lead:
The Kharidian–Zarosian War was a series of major battles in the northern Kharidian Lands in the Second Age. Zaros had been expanding his empire which shared a border with the Kharidian lands, which were ruled over by a group of gods called the Menaphite Pantheon.

The war started from simple border skirmishes, that broke out due to the Menaphites fear of the expanding Zarosian Empire, whom the Menaphites named the "Ruinous Powers". To hold back the Zarosian forces, the gods of the Menaphite Pantheon granted their people powerful weapons. Despite this, the Zarosians remained on the winning side, quickly conquering the Menaphite's terrain.

label: Kharshai
title: Kharshai
lead:
Kharshai is a Mahjarrat of unknown allegiance mentioned by the golem during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire and in the Mahjarrat notes.

Kharshai disappeared early during the God Wars, after his loyalty towards the Zarosian Empire was under investigation.

label: Kharyrll
title: Kharyrll
lead:
Kharyrll was once a fortress of the Zarosian Empire during the Second and early Third Ages. It was destroyed during the God Wars by Zamorakian forces. The modern-day town of Canifis now stands where the fortress once stood.

If the player has access to the Ancient Magicks spellbook, the Kharyrll Teleport, once used by Zarosians, can be used to teleport directly into the Hair of the Dog pub, using two law runes and one blood rune (66 Magic required).

label: Khazard armour
title: Khazard armour
lead:
A Khazard armour is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest. It is a dark coloured platebody that is part of the Khazard armour set. It has stats worse than a bronze platebody, but unlike most melee armours, it does not have a penalty to Magic or Ranged accuracy, nor does it interfere with Ava's devices, making it a viable choice for mages and rangers. It also weighs far less than a typical platebody. Another nearby quest item, Carnillean armour, has over double the stab defence and +3 slash defence bonuses, at the cost of -2 crush defence and nearly 20x the weight.

In the Fight Arena quest, a Khazard helmet and Khazard armour can only be found by searching the chest in a building north of the Fight Arena. They both must be worn to enter the Khazard prisons. Unequipping either the helmet or armour inside the jail causes the guards to kick the player out.

label: Khazard armour set
title: Khazard armour set
lead:
The Khazard armour set is a set of armour which consists of the Khazard helmet and Khazard armour.

Both the helmet and the platebody are obtained during the Fight Arena quest and are used primarily as a disguise. A Defence level of 1 is required to wear them and is currently one of the poorest melee armours in the game, with comparable defensive bonuses to bronze. The set cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

label: Khazard Army
title: Khazard Army
lead:
The Khazard Army is a group of armed forces consisting of humans that fight for the Zamorakian Mahjarrat known as General Khazard. They are mainly situated in the area around Port Khazard, the Fight Arena and the Battlefield. Some members can also be found stationed in the Ghorrock Dungeon to secure the area after Secrets of the North.

The army operates under the approval of King Lathas, having a good relationship, and even once performing a peacekeeping job for him, though King Thoros seeks to slowly distance himself from Khazard. They are also extremely loyal to their Mahjarrat leader, and, like the General himself, are quite fond of his pet hellhound Bouncer. They seem to have a particular hatred of gnomes, showing no mercy to them, and during the Tree Gnome Village quest, a group of them attack the Tree Gnome Village, slaughtering many unarmed gnomes inside, including women and children.

label: Khazard Barman
title: Khazard Barman
lead: Angor, the Khazard Barman, runs the Fight Arena Bar in Khazard. The barman sells beer and Khali brew, which is needed for the Fight Arena quest.

label: Khazard cell keys
title: Khazard cell keys
lead: Khazard cell keys are a quest item in the Fight Arena quest. They are obtained by giving a Khali brew to the Head Guard in the south-eastern room of the jail at the Fight Arena, north of Yanille. The keys are used to unlock the door to the cell that holds Sammy Servil prisoner.

label: Khazard commander
title: Khazard commander
lead: The Khazard commander can be found in the Battlefield of Khazard (located south of West Ardougne). He is encountered during the Tree Gnome Village quest. To be able to get to him, players must have fired the ballista during the Tree Gnome Village quest. By firing the ballista, it will break the stronghold allowing the player to climb over the wall to attack him. The commander can not be attacked from outside of the stronghold, even with ranged or magic.

label: Khazard General Store
title: Khazard General Store
lead: The Khazard General Store is a general store with two locations sharing the same stock in Port Khazard. The store has stock consistent with other general stores, as well as a few items that are unique to the Fishing Trawler minigame.

label: Khazard Guard
title: Khazard Guard
lead: Khazard Guards are members of the Khazard Army found in and around General Khazard's Fight Arena, south of Ardougne. Talking to them after killing Bouncer in the Fight Arena quest will cause them to exclaim and start attacking.

label: Khazard Guard (Arena escort)
title: Khazard Guard (Arena escort)
lead:
The Khazard Guard was a member of the Khazard Army that appeared in the Fight Arena quest. After players were captured by General Khazard and forced to become one of his fight slaves, this guard would escort players to the Fight Arena prison.

Despite not being attackable, he had a combat level of 25.

label: Khazard Guard (Off duty)
title: Khazard Guard (Off duty)
lead: The Khazard Guard is an off-duty member of the Khazard Army living in the north-eastern house at the Fight Arena. The chest in his house can be opened and searched for the Khazard armour and helmet during the Fight Arena quest.

label: Khazard helmet
title: Khazard helmet
lead:
A Khazard helmet is a quest item in the Fight Arena quest. It is a dark coloured medium helmet that is part of the Khazard armour set. It has stats similar to an iron med helm, except unlike most medium helmets, it does not have a penalty to Magic, making it a viable choice for mages and rangers.

In the Fight Arena quest, a Khazard helmet and Khazard armour can only be found by searching the chest in a building north of the Fight Arena. They both must be worn to enter the Khazard prisons. Unequipping either the helmet or armour inside the jail causes the guards to kick the player out.

label: Khazard Ogre
title: Khazard Ogre
lead: The Khazard Ogre is a monster fought during Fight Arena. After it is defeated, General Khazard will send out a Khazard Scorpion to fight next. This is General Khazard's 4th best creature who is used to fight against the Slave fighters along with Bouncer and the Khazard Scorpion.

label: Khazard Scorpion
title: Khazard Scorpion
lead: The Khazard Scorpion is a monster fought during Fight Arena. After it is defeated, General Khazard will send out Bouncer to fight next. This is General Khazard's 3rd best creature who is used to fight against the Slave fighters along with Bouncer and the Khazard Ogre.

label: Khazard trooper
title: Khazard trooper
lead:
Khazard troopers are the foot soldiers of the Khazard Army. They can be found fighting gnomes in the Khazard Battlefield near West Ardougne and spectating at the Fight Arena.

While fighting gnomes, the troopers will say phrases such as "Get off of me, ya little pest!" and "Arrgh! Get the gnome!".

label: Khazard warlord
title: Khazard warlord
lead:
The Khazard warlord is fought during the Tree Gnome Village quest. After he is defeated, players can search his satchel to find the the remaining orbs of protection needed for the spirit tree. The player must then these bring back to King Bolren to complete the quest. Players can fight him in the Nightmare Zone after the quest is complete.

Even though the warlord attacks with a warhammer, he has the attacking speed of a scimitar, meaning that low-level players can take a lot of damage very quickly. Protect from Melee will render him harmless, and he can also be bound with magic. Players choosing to use melee and can't use Prayers are advised to have adamant armour or better when fighting him, as well as good food.

label: Khazard–Gnome War
title: Khazard–Gnome War
lead:
The Khazard–Gnome War is an ongoing military conflict between the Northern and Southern Gnome Empire and the army of the Mahjarrat General Khazard, centred at the Battlefield. The war is featured in the Gnome quest series. The cause of the war is currently unknown. However, it does appear that fighting between the gnomish and Khazard forces began in earnest due to killings carried out by the Khazard against the gnomes. These attacks themselves may have been in response to gnomish expansion into the region after the gnomes emerged from underground following the end of the God Wars.

At one point the Gnome army got desperate enough to send one of their orbs of protection to the Battlefield. However this left their Village vulnerable, and a group of Khazard soldiers managed to navigate the maze, attack the village (killing King Bolren's wife and many other gnomes), and steal the other orbs. An adventurer managed to recover the orbs, defeating a Khazard warlord who was in possession of one of the orbs.

label: Khom Prysin
title: Khom Prysin
lead: Khom Prysin was one of the founding members of the Elders of Avarrocka. Rhee Prysin and Sir Prysin are his descendants. He is a founder of Avarrocka.

label: Kick
title: Kick
lead:
Kick may refer to:

*Kick, an unarmed fighting style in Combat Options
*Kicking, the temporary removal of players from a clan chat by a corporal or higher rank granted the kicking ability

label: kill count
title: kill count
lead: Kill count, or killcount (also referred to as KC), is a unique system in both Barrows and the God Wars Dungeon (referred to as essence).

label: Kill credit
title: Kill credit
lead: Kill credit is a game mechanic that determines whether the player will receive credit and/or loot for defeating a monster. Kill credit can be measured in various ways, depending on the activity and game mode played in. Normal users will generally receive kill credit for dealing the final hit to the monster. Specific achievements will have different requirements, such as using a specific weapon for the final hit or killing the monster without taking any specific damage.

label: killer's print
title: killer's print
lead: The killer's print is an item used in Murder Mystery, found by using the criminal's dagger on a pot of flour and some flypaper. Players compare this item to the prints of the Sinclair family, and find out who the killer is.

label: Killerwatt (interface item)
title: Killerwatt (interface item)
lead:
The Killerwatt is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Killerwatt

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Kilron
title: Kilron
lead:
Kilron is found on the south-west side of the wall separating east and West Ardougne.

He plays a minor role in the Biohazard quest by helping the player leave West Ardougne without alerting the mourners by using a rope ladder to climb over the wall.

label: Kilt
title: Kilt
lead:
Kilt may refer to:

* 
* 
*

label: King
title: King
lead: King may refer to:

label: King Agata IV
title: King Agata IV
lead: King Agata IV was the ruler of Great Kourend during the 117th to 120th decade. Known as a gluttonous king, his mismanagement of the kingdom during his reign left it ravaged by famine, which likely resulted in him being overthrown by the leaders of the five Houses. Shortly after, the War of the Five Houses began.

label: King Alvis
title: King Alvis
lead: King Alvis was a king of Keldagrim, the capital of the Dwarven Realm. He passed away roughly 500 years ago, but remains amongst the dwarves' most significant historical figures. His legacy is honoured by a statue on the River Kelda, which is relevant in The Giant Dwarf quest.

label: King Arthur
title: King Arthur
lead:
King Arthur is the king of Camelot Castle which is east of Seers' Village. Arthur is the leader of the Knights of the Round Table and an ally of the White Knights. King Arthur is found on the ground floor and is involved in three quests: Holy Grail, Merlin's Crystal, and King's Ransom.

After completing the Holy Grail, players can mount a painting of King Arthur on a wall in their player-owned house.

label: King Ascertes
title: King Ascertes
lead:
King Ascertes Hallow was the human husband and consort of Queen Efaritay, the Icyene queen of Hallowland and father of their children Safalaan and Larina Hallow. Very little is known about Ascertes, but he was presumably born in the Third Age and married the queen some time before the Zamorakian invasion led by Lord Drakan. Ascertes was captured by Ranis Drakan and Verzik Vitur, who brought him to Lord Drakan.
In Sins of the Father, it is revealed that Ascertes was turned into a vampyre during the Hallowvale invasion, in an attempt to end the ongoing war and force the queen to surrender to the Zamorakian invaders. After his vampyrification, he became known as Vanstrom Klause, and became one of Drakan's henchmen.

label: King Black Dragon
title: King Black Dragon
lead:
The King Black Dragon, commonly referred to as KBD, is a three-headed dragon located in his lair, accessible only through the deep Wilderness. Although the lair itself is not in the Wilderness, KBD is still considered a Wilderness boss by designation, as players must enter the Wilderness to fight him. The King Black Dragon has a combat level of 276, which makes him one of the strongest dragons in Old School RuneScape. Players should not take this foe lightly, and they should always take an anti-dragon shield as his dragonfire breath is very deadly without protection. The King Black Dragon can also be killed as an alternative for a black dragon Slayer task, except when assigned by Krystilia.

Although he will always fight back when attacked, he has gotten bored over the centuries from adventurers attacking him, as he revealed to his good friend Bob the cat. If you're going there for the first time, please note that KBD is aggressive and will aggro you, dealing damage from a distance through even super antifire potions, dragonfire shields, and protect from magic.

label: King Black Dragon (PvM Arena)
title: King Black Dragon (PvM Arena)
lead: King Black Dragon is one of the bosses fought in the PvM Arena, originally added for the 2015 Clan Cup. He has the same stats as his standard version.

label: King Black Dragon Lair
title: King Black Dragon Lair
lead:
The King Black Dragon Lair, abbreviated as the KBD lair, is a multi-combat area, allowing groups of players to fight him simultaneously. The lair can be accessed via the western entrance to the Lava Maze Dungeon in level 42 Wilderness near the Lava Maze, however the lair itself is not the Wilderness. The lair is additionally visited by players completing an elite or master clue scroll step; the elite one requires players to kill the dragon, while the master clue has an emote clue that must be performed in the cave.

: Watch out for player-killers on the way to the lair. The dungeon may be accessed via a ladder in a fenced area on the west end of the Lava Maze containing four lesser demons. The ladder leads to an area with poison spiders, and a lever which will teleport the player to the King Black Dragon's lair. The lair itself isn't in the Wilderness, but players are in the Wilderness until they pull the lever. As with all Wilderness levers, if a player is teleblocked, they can't pull the lever. As the lair itself is not considered the Wilderness, players can use any means of teleportation to leave.

label: King Black Dragon/Strategies
title: King Black Dragon/Strategies
lead:
: While the King Black Dragon's lair is not considered to be a part of the Wilderness, you will need to cross a short distance in deep level 42-Wilderness that is commonly patrolled by Player killers. Do not bring any items into the Wilderness you are not willing to lose.

The King Black Dragon, commonly referred to as KBD, is a three-headed dragon located in his lair deep in the Wilderness. The King Black Dragon has a combat level of 276, which makes him one of the strongest dragons in Old School RuneScape. Players should always take an anti-dragon shield as his dragonfire breath is very deadly without protection. The King Black Dragon can also be killed as an alternative for a black dragon Slayer task, except those given by Krystilia.

label: King Bolren
title: King Bolren
lead:
King Bolren is the king of the Tree Gnome Village. He is the younger brother of the village's former king, Bolrie, who abdicated after being deceived by Glouphrie the Untrusted, after which Bolren was elected as the new king.

He plays a large role in the Tree Gnome Village quest, asking for you to recover the orbs of protection to help protect his people, and maybe stop the endless war with General Khazard's army. During the quest, agents of Khazard break into the village and kill his family. He is a possible customer (a hard order) in the Gnome Restaurant minigame and players must speak to him for the Treasure Trail anagram 'GOBLIN KERN'.

label: King Byrne I
title: King Byrne I
lead:
King Byrne I was the king of Great Kourend, ruling from the 47th to 50th decade. Byrne, working as a farmer, one day witnessed a child working on the same field being murdered by a lizardman guard. Outraged, he singlehandedly killed the lizardman, having the whole town as a witness. Urging people to fight back, he started the revolt and within 7 days, the lizardmen were outnumbered and driven beyond the kingdom's grounds to the Kebos Lowlands. During the rebellion, the temple that surrounded the Dark Altar was demolished, further weakening the powers of Xeric and forcing him to exile, travelling west to Mount Quidamortem.

After the successful revolt against Xeric, Byrne was crowned king of Great Kourend on 339 - 47, and ruled for three decades as King Byrne I, with his son King Byrne II ruling for another three decades after his father's.

label: King Byrne II
title: King Byrne II
lead:
King Byrne II was ruler of the Great Kourend during the 50th to 53rd decade. He was the son of the King Byrne I, who is widely known for overthrowing Xeric's reign. He was married to Queen Biyrene I.

King Byrne II died of unknown causes and his wife took over the throne because his only son (King Byrne III) was too young. Once his son came of age, she unwillingly gave up the throne. Had the law of succession made by her late husband never existed, she would have not given up the throne for her son, wishing to finish the work for the kingdom that she had started.

label: King Byrne III
title: King Byrne III
lead:
King Byrne III was ruler of the Great Kourend during the 54th decade. He was the only son of the King Byrne II and Queen Biyrene I.

King Byrne II died of unknown causes and Queen Biyrene I took over the throne, since his only son (King Byrne III) was too young. Once his son came of age, her mother unwillingly gave up the throne. Had the law of succession made by her late husband never existed, she would have not given up the throne for her son, wishing to finish the work for this kingdom that she had started.

label: King Claudius
title: King Claudius
lead:
King Claudius was once a ruler of Varrock, the capital city of the kingdom of Misthalin. Although the time of his rule is unknown, it is believed he lived some time in the Fourth Age. He does not appear in-game, but is mentioned in issue 4 of Postbag from the Hedge.

According to Duke Horacio of Lumbridge, King Claudius granted his (Duke Horacio's) ancestor Polonius the title of duke in exchange for his service as a in the service of Misthalin. Polonius would later go on to establish Lumbridge Castle in the place of a wooden fort that had previously served as a lone defensive structure. His position of duke was later passed on through the generations.

label: King Danthalas
title: King Danthalas
lead:
King Danthalas was the husband of Queen Rashiliyia and the father of Bervirius. He is only mentioned in the Shilo Village quest.
Very little is known about him, although he is known to have lived during the Third Age and presumably ruled a kingdom consisting of some part of Karamja.

label: King Hosidius V
title: King Hosidius V
lead:
King Hosidius V was the last king before Lord Rickard Shayzien, who later became King Shayzien VII and then Xeric, took rule. He reigned for the duration of the 28th - 33rd decade.

King Hosidius V is known for greatly expanding the Shayzien Army at the recommendation of Lord Rickard Shayzien with the addition of three new regiments: the Elder Warriors, the Twisted Archers, and the Kodai Mages. These regiments each served directly under the command of a General, and each General reported directly to Lord Shayzien.

label: King Kharedst I
title: King Kharedst I
lead:
King Kharedst I was ruler of Great Kourend during the 123rd to 126th decade, coming into power after the War of the Five Houses ended.

He is likely to have been the person referred to as 'King Kharedst the Builder', based on a letter addressed to Jonathan published in the Postbag from the Hedge. In his response, Jonathan mentions a census conducted by King Kharedst the Builder, containing "countless records of mothers without sons or husbands", which in his estimation provides "fascinating insight into life before and after the War of the Five Houses". The conclusion that could be drawn from this document is that King Kharedst the Builder came to power immediately following the War of the Five Houses, meaning he would have been the first of his line, King Kharedst I. As such, he would have been the one to have built the Kourend Castle, amongst other constructions.

label: King Kharedst II
title: King Kharedst II
lead:
King Kharedst II was ruler of Great Kourend during the 126th to 130th decade.

King Kharedst II, along with other rulers of the Great Kourend, is mentioned in Timeline.

label: King Kharedst III
title: King Kharedst III
lead:
King Kharedst III was the ruler of Great Kourend during the 132nd to 135th decade. The war with Varlamore presumably had ended sometime before or during his reign, and in the hope of repairing the relationship between Kourend and Varlamore, which had been destroyed after the war, the King ordered an envoy be sent to Varlamore to transport the Royal Accord of Twill to be displayed in the Grand Museum of Civitas illa Fortis. However, the Accord became lost at sea, and remained so until it was recovered by Artur Hosidius in the 141st decade.

King Kharedst III, along with other rulers of the Great Kourend, is mentioned in Timeline.

label: King Kharedst IV
title: King Kharedst IV
lead:
King Kharedst IV was the last king of Great Kourend, before the Kourend Council overtook the position as rulers of the kingdom.

Approximately 31 years ago, King Kharedst IV's wife died giving birth to Rose, his only daughter. Some time during her childhood, he gave her a memoir for her to record their outings, so that he can reminisce the times they've spent together. During these outings, they would occasionally dress down to experience the life of the people of Great Kourend. Rose and her father also often wrote riddles for each other as well.

label: King Lathas
title: King Lathas
lead: King Lathas Ardignas is the king of East Ardougne, the capital of Kandarin. As the sons of King Ulthas, he and his younger brother Tyras are responsible for the division of the city between West and East. Lathas rules the eastern part of the city, although the existence of the Ardougne City Council leaves the extent of his power uncertain. He and his brother are the great-grandsons of the first King of Kandarin, who founded the kingdom after the Great Battle, leading the Ardignas bloodline to rise to power.

label: King Marhuitz
title: King Marhuitz
lead: King Marhuitz Tullus, sometimes referred to as the Old Wolf, was a legendary Varlamorian hero and the first king of Fortis. His reign marked the beginning of the Tullus dynasty.

label: King Maximus
title: King Maximus
lead:
King Maximus Tullus was a former king of Varlamore, and a member of the Tullus dynasty. Statues of him can be found in the Grand Museum of Civitas illa Fortis, as well as in various locations around the city.

He is best known for having ordered the construction of the Fortis Colosseum, which replaced a temple dedicated to Ralos that had been used to sacrifice criminals.

label: King Narnode Shareen
title: King Narnode Shareen
lead:
King Narnode Shareen is the king of the Tree Gnome Stronghold, part of the Gnome Empire. He is found on the ground floor of the Grand Tree of Tree Gnome Stronghold and features in the following quests: The Grand Tree, The Eyes of Glouphrie, Monkey Madness I and its sequel, Monkey Madness II.

King Narnode is known to have an affection toward humans, but his high regard for the race can often be tainted and contorted through lies, as he once had the player temporarily imprisoned under false accusations.

label: King Narras
title: King Narras
lead:
'Mad' King Narras Ardignas was the second king of Kandarin. He died some years ago, before the rule of King Ulthas. He is the earliest known named king in the Ardignas bloodline.

Narras is said to have been insane, and invented the game of Hangman to encourage literacy amongst his subjects. His idea of hangman, however, involved hanging actual people in the gallows. While one person guessed the word, the one in the gallows would come increasingly closer to death. If the word was not guessed in time, the victim would be hanged and killed. His gallows can still be found in front of the Civic Office of West Ardougne today.

label: King of the Skill
title: King of the Skill
lead:
King of the Skill was a temporary game mode where players competed to gain the most experience in 24 hours of game play. From 1 November 2017 until 30 November, any account with membership would be able to log into dedicated game servers and compete with other players to gain the most experience in a skill, or the highest total level.

Prizes were awarded to the top 10 total level winners, and prizes were awarded to the top 5 skill winners for each skill. Dedicated hiscores were set up to track the competition.

label: King Rada
title: King Rada
lead:
King Rada may refer to:

*King Rada I
*King Rada II
*King Rada III

label: King Rada I
title: King Rada I
lead:
, founder of Great Kourend.]]
King Rada I was the first king and founder of Great Kourend, after he successfully united the five cities of Arceuus, Hosidius, Lovakengj, Piscarilius, and Shayzien during 10th BA (1,510 years ago). He was succeeded on 9th BA by King Rada II.

A statue of King Rada I can be found in the Kourend Castle courtyard.

label: King Rada II
title: King Rada II
lead: King Rada II was the second king of Great Kourend and successor of King Rada I. He ruled Great Kourend from 9th BA to 7th BA.

label: King Rada III
title: King Rada III
lead:
King Rada III was the third king of Great Kourend. He ruled Great Kourend for one decade until the Council of Elders overthrew him in the 6th BA during the Rebellion of the Five Houses.

The Tower of Magic was constructed during his reign. At some point during his reign, King Rada commanded Matthias Vorseth to complete a census of skilled peoples, animals and estates of the lords of the settlement of Kourend.

label: King Raddallin
title: King Raddallin
lead: King Raddallin was the founder and first king of Asgarnia, which was created after he unified many of the smaller tribes and settlements in the area.

label: King Roald
title: King Roald
lead: King Roald Remanis III is the current ruler of the prosperous kingdom of Misthalin. His residence is within Varrock Palace, where the Varrock Palace Secret Guard work to keep him safe. He is located in the south-east side of the Palace on the ground floor. He is notable for being one of the least controversial kings, as he is a very straightforward, stable ruler. He has a wife, Ellamaria, who rules alongside as queen.

label: King Roald I
title: King Roald I
lead: King Roald I was a former king of Misthalin, and the first king in the Roald line. He is the grandfather of Misthalin's current king, King Roald III. Beyond the fact he existed, nothing else is known about him.

label: King Roald II
title: King Roald II
lead: King Roald II was the former king of Misthalin. King Roald II is known to have ruled in at least year 143 of the Fifth Age, and was the present king's father. It was he who made the proclamation stating that whoever returned the Shield of Arrav would receive 1,200 coins (then a large amount of money).

label: King Scorpion
title: King Scorpion
lead: King Scorpions are aggressive monsters found in the Dwarven Mine, the Lava Maze, in the Wilderness, and some areas on Crandor. They typically wander around the mineable rocks. They stop being aggressive at level 65 outside Wilderness.

label: King Shayzien III
title: King Shayzien III
lead:
King Shayzien III was the king responsible for abolishing the royal accord of twill by seizing control of Great Kourend with the military under his command. He reigned for the duration of the 13th - 15th decade.

King Shayzien III is known for writing the Royal Charter into law, which officially abolished the royal accord of twill and therefore the right of succession, forming the State of Kourend that serves the monarchy. Giving the head of state (the monarch) authority over revenue, mobilisation of armies, and territory within the kingdom of Great Kourend.

label: King Shayzien III's Coup d'État
title: King Shayzien III's Coup d'État
lead: King Shayzien III's coup d'état was a military seizure of power carried out by Grand Lord Shayzien III during the 13th decade of Kourend's timeline. With the help of the Shayzien Army, he took control of the kingdom in order to prevent his authority being passed down to the next house in line. Following the coup d'état, Grand Lord Shayzien III annulled the Royal Accord of Twill by signing into law the Royal Charter, granting him power over the kingdom of Great Kourend in perpetuity, and crowned himself as King Shayzien III.

label: King Shayzien VII
title: King Shayzien VII
lead:
King Shayzien VII, previously Lord Rickard Shazyien, ruled Great Kourend from the 33rd to 37th decade. He wrote a journal that plays a role in the A Kingdom Divided quest. His reign was defined by violence.

Before he was king, he was the ruler of Shayzien. Under the rule of King Shayzien V, he recommended in the Armed Forces Report that the king invest greatly in expanding the Shayzien Army with three new regiments: the Elder Warriors, the Twisted Archers, and the Kodai Mages. These regiments would report directly to a general, and each general would report directly to Lord Rickard Shayzien.

label: King Tyras
title: King Tyras
lead: King Tyras Ardignas is the king of West Ardougne, the son of King Ulthas and the younger brother of King Lathas. He is assassinated by the player during the quest Regicide after the player is deceived by King Lathas and Lord Iorwerth.

label: King Ulthas
title: King Ulthas
lead:
King Ulthas Ardignas was the third king of Kandarin and the heir of Mad King Narras. He was the father of King Lathas and King Tyras.

When King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table arrived to Gielinor from Britain in 132 V, they found that he required a castle or fortress to call his own. One such castle was found east of Seers' Village, but at the time it was owned by Lord Sinclair and his children, who were all very young at the time. King Ulthas and Lord Sinclair decided that King Arthur's need of the castle was greater than the Sinclair family's, and so Lord Sinclair and his family left the castle and moved to a mansion he built to the north (much to his children's displeasure). King Arthur claimed the castle and renamed it to Camelot.

label: King Vallance
title: King Vallance
lead: King Vallance is the official ruler of Asgarnia, father of Crown Prince Anlaf and great uncle of Princess Miazrqa. However, he has not been seen for many years; as such, Sir Amik Varze is currently the de-facto ruler.

label: king worm
title: king worm
lead:
King worms are used in gnome cooking to make worm crunchies, worm holes, and worm battas. They can be eaten to heal 2 Hitpoints. When eaten, the message You eat the king worm. It's a bit chewy. is displayed. It is a possible item chosen randomly from a list in the Fairytale I - Growing Pains and Forgettable Tale... quests, to enchant the Secateurs, and trade for the Rowdy dwarf's kelda seed.

When talking to a gnome woman, they occasionally give king worms.

label: kingdom
title: kingdom
lead:
Various kingdoms, city-states and other polities exist throughout Gielinor, generally inhabited and ruled predominantly by one race.

Many of these polities are monarchies ruled by a king or other monarch, while others have a governing structure such as a council or republic. Some civilisations have unspecified forms of government, and not all domains have clearly defined borders.

label: Kingdom (music track)
title: Kingdom (music track)
lead:
Kingdom is a music track that is unlocked in Burthorpe. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track and Principality.

In Classic music mode, this track plays on the west side of Burthorpe outside the Warriors' Guild and on the path to Death Plateau.

label: Kinshra
title: Kinshra
lead: The Kinshra, often referred to as the Black Knights, are a Zamorakian military order based primarily in and around northern Asgarnia, founded in the early Fifth Age. The Kinshra were official defenders of the Kingdom of Asgarnia for roughly 155 years, although their presence within the nation was, and continues to be, a constant point of political tension. The group is currently led by Lord Daquarius Rennard.

label: Kitchen Drawers
title: Kitchen Drawers
lead: A pair of Kitchen Drawers are found on the middle level of the Troll Stronghold. They're located next to My Arm and are able to be opened and searched for a storeroom key used during the Eadgar's Ruse quest.

label: Kitchen table (interface item)
title: Kitchen table (interface item)
lead:
The Kitchen table is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Kitchen table.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Kitchen weaponry
title: Kitchen weaponry
lead: Kitchen weaponry are melee weapons that can be bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest. To buy and wield more advanced kitchen weapons, the player must complete the Recipe for Disaster subquests. All the weapons have the same or almost the same stats as the metal melee weapons. There are no kitchen weapons that have stats equivalent to any of the Dragon weapons.

label: Kite shield (interface item)
title: Kite shield (interface item)
lead:
The Kite shield is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Kite shield (Construction).

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: kiteshield
title: kiteshield
lead:
Kiteshields are shields worn in the shield slot. They are normally used as a melee protection and provide good defence against all melee attack types. They can be smithed from all types of metals except for black and white.

Kiteshields have slightly higher melee and ranged defence bonuses than square shields, but they are also more expensive. Kiteshields also provide a negative Ranged attack bonus and a higher Magic attack penalty than square shields, and as such kiteshields are generally used only for melee combat.

label: kitten
title: kitten
lead:
Kittens are young pet cats that can follow the player. In order to obtain a pet kitten, a player must complete the Gertrude's Cat quest, after which Gertrude will give them a kitten as part of the reward. The first kitten is free, and each kitten after that is 100 coins, but players cannot own more than one kitten at a time. If a fully grown cat is put into the player-owned house Menagerie, another kitten can be obtained from Gertrude. The kitten itself cannot be stored in the Menagerie. If players have an activated ring of charos(a), they are able to charm Gertrude into allowing them to choose a specific colour kitten. Otherwise, players will be given a kitten of a random colour.

Kittens appear as either the player's follower or as an item in the inventory. To change the kitten from an item to a follower, drop the kitten from your inventory. Once it is following you, selecting "Pick-up" with right click will return the kitten back to the inventory.

label: kitten (Gertrude's Cat)
title: kitten (Gertrude's Cat)
lead:
A Kitten is the offspring of Fluffs that appears during the Gertrude's Cat quest. It was separated from its mother within the Lumber Yard, and must be retrieved from a crate to obtain it as an item, which must then be taken to Fluffs. If the item is instead dropped, the kitten will appear on the ground and run back to a crate.

If players speak to Fluffs after Icthlarin's Little Helper with a catspeak amulet, she will thank them for finding her kitten, and admits she has a difficult time keeping track of them.

label: Klank
title: Klank
lead:
Klank is part of a group of dwarves trapped in the Underground Pass. Although he originally came seeking ore, he has become trapped by the evils of the pass, created by Iban.

Klank gives the player a free pair of his specialist gauntlets during the Underground Pass quest. If lost, the gauntlets must be re-bought for 5,000 coins if the player requires another pair. They are used to search the half-soulless' cages for a dove without being bitten.

label: Klank's gauntlets
title: Klank's gauntlets
lead: Klank's gauntlets are a pair of gauntlets obtained during the Underground Pass quest to prevent the half-soulless from biting the player when searching their cages for Iban's dove. If lost, they can be recovered during and after the quest from Klank for coins. Klank's gauntlets have the same stats as steel gauntlets.

label: Klarense
title: Klarense
lead:
Klarense is a sailor involved in the Dragon Slayer I quest and he is found on the second most southern dock of Port Sarim. He sells players his boat, the Lady Lumbridge, for 2,000 coins, which is needed to sail to Crandor.

Players can only buy the Lady Lumbridge during Dragon Slayer I. If players ask him before embarking on the quest, they cannot board to fix the Lady Lumbridge. He will also tell players that "The ship is not ready yet and Port Sarim's workers are slow so there's no telling how long the ship will take to fix."

label: Knife
title: Knife
lead:
A knife is a multi-functional tool used for a large variety of tasks, primarily used for fletching logs in the Fletching skill and cutting food in the Cooking skill. It sees secondary usage in the Crafting skill. Additionally, it can be used to cut through webs and setup Hunter traps.

They are sold in many general stores, at Trader Stan's Trading Post on Karamja, or the Ardougne Spice Stall. A knife can also be found by searching a sack between two webs in front of the lever to the Mage Arena bank, if the player does not have a knife in their inventory.

label: Knight
title: Knight
lead:
A large variety of Knights exist in Old School RuneScape.

*Basilisk knights, Slayer creatures found in Jormungand's Prison.
*Black knights, monsters found mainly in the Black Knights' Fortress.
*Dancing knights, dancing on the tabletop in the Party Room.
*Knights of Ardougne, found in the East Ardougne marketplace and can be pickpocketed at level 55 Thieving.
*Knights of Avarrocka, knights from the Enakhra's Lament quest.
*Knights of the Round Table, King Arthur's knights fought after completion of King's Ransom.
*Knights of Saradomin, found inside the God Wars Dungeon in the main area and in Saradomin's Encampment.
*Knights of Varlamore, found in Civitas illa Fortis and can be pickpocketed at level 55 Thieving.
*Revenant knight, a type of revenant that inhabits the Revenant Caves.
*Sir Gerry, a dying knight laying by the entrance to the God Wars Dungeon.
*Temple Knights, an elite section of White Knights headed by Sir Tiffy Cashien.
*Void Knights, an order of knights loyal to the god Guthix who oversee the Pest Control minigame.
*White knights, found at the White Knights' Castle in Falador.

label: Knight (Falador Party Room)
title: Knight (Falador Party Room)
lead:
The dancing knights are a fun extra feature of the Falador Party Room, available for the price of 500 coins. They can be summoned to dance on the tabletop and sing by using the lever on the wall near the treasure chest.

The knights sing a short song in parody of a similar scene in . If the player attempts to talk with one of the knights, they are told "He is too busy dancing to talk!"

label: Knight of Ardougne
title: Knight of Ardougne
lead:
The Knights of Ardougne are found in the East Ardougne market place. One is also found in the courtyard of the East Ardougne Castle. Most are found attempting to chase away thieves. They will protect all stalls from the silk stall and up by attacking players that they observe stealing from them. After completion of the Song of the Elves, knights of Ardougne can be found patrolling the streets of West Ardougne as well.

Knights of Ardougne can be pickpocketed at level 55 Thieving, giving the player a coin pouch worth 50 coins and 84.3 Thieving experience. The gloves of silence or the medium Ardougne Diary increase success rate by 5% and 10%, respectively. Failing to pickpocket will result in being hit for 3 points of damage. They are a good source of Thieving experience with a theoretical maximum of 3,000 pickpockets per hour for a total of 252,900 experience per hour.

label: Knight of Ardougne (disambiguation)
title: Knight of Ardougne (disambiguation)
lead: Knight of Ardougne may refer to:

label: Knight of Ardougne (unused)
title: Knight of Ardougne (unused)
lead:
The Knight of Ardougne is an unused monster that was added to the game files in the RuneScape 2 beta. Presumably, it was supposed to be a variant of the Knight of Ardougne that would be found in East Ardougne marketplace. Like the regular Knight, players had the option to either fight or pickpocket it.

It was most likely scrapped very early in development, as both the jaw model and the animations are broken. If given a jaw with a beard, the beard colour changes to match the purple of their armour.

label: Knight of Varlamore (disambiguation)
title: Knight of Varlamore (disambiguation)
lead:
Knight of Varlamore may refer to:
* Knight of Varlamore, the common knights around Civitas illa Fortis
* Knight of Varlamore (Kourend Castle), Astra, a Knight of Varlamore visiting Kourend Castle, who later travels to the Forthos Dungeon
* Knight of Varlamore (Children of the Sun), six knights that are a part of the delegation visiting Varrock during the quest Children of the Sun, and visited during Twilight's Promise
* Knight of Varlamore (Twilight's Promise), Mezan, one of the six knights of the delegation and the knight fought during the quest Twilight's Promise

label: Knightly
title: Knightly
lead: Knightly is a music track that is unlocked in the centre of Ardougne. It can also be heard in the Ardougne city prison during Song of the Elves.

label: Kodai
title: Kodai
lead:
Kodai may refer to:

*Kodai wand
*Kodai insignia
*Kodai potion
*Kodai (+)
*Kodai (-)

label: Koftik
title: Koftik
lead:
Koftik is a human that serves as a guide through the Underground Pass during the quest. He teaches players how to make fire arrows to enter the pass and also appears throughout the dungeon. During the quest, he will give the player some food at most of his locations in the dungeon because "it is a dangerous area". However if you've recently claimed some food from him, you will have to wait for some time for more.

Throughout the quest, he slowly loses his mind to Iban's influence. Once Iban is slain at the end of the quest, he regains his sanity. After starting the Regicide quest, he can also be found in the Well of Voyage in the Underground Pass. At this location, he will give the player a small amount of food as a one-time offering, and a broken Iban's staff as a repeatable offering.

label: Kolodion
title: Kolodion
lead:
Kolodion is the shape-shifting master of the Mage Arena. He is fought to gain entrance to the arena, where players fight for their god of choice.

When a player fights him during the Mage Arena I miniquest, he first starts out as a man, then transforms into an Ogre, a giant ice blue spider, a large ghost, and finally a black demon.

label: Konar quo Maten/Strategies
title: Konar quo Maten/Strategies
lead: All of Konar's tasks must be completed at the specific location she requests.

label: Koriff
title: Koriff
lead:
, a piece of armour that once belonged to Koriff.]]
Koriff the Crowd Pleaser was the former hostess of the Duel Arena. Part of the Calamity Coven, she, along with Saika and Maoma, played a part in the staining the reputation of the once glorious Duel Arena, turning it into an immensely corrupt place where they used their positions to accumulate vast amounts of ill-gotten wealth.

As the hostess of the arena, she used her grace and charm to whip up excitement amongst the crowd, causing them to bet higher and riskier, so that she and her accomplices could increase their profits. She would even often bet against certain competitors and secretly kill them off with her sniping skills to gain a profit. In addition, she'd pamper rich visitors and provided them with the best seats and service, all while collaborating with hired thieves to pick their pockets.

label: Kortan
title: Kortan
lead: Kortan, along with Aemad, runs Aemad's Adventuring Supplies. in East Ardougne. The store acts as a General store, but it sells some items not found in other stores such as papyrus and cooked meat. It does not sell some common items found in nearly all other general stores, such as bowls.

label: Kourend Chronicles
title: Kourend Chronicles
lead: The Kourend Chronicles are a compilation of stories relating to the first six quests of the Great Kourend quest series. The stories, which were released weekly in anticipation of the release of A Kingdom Divided, take place sometime before or after the player's intervention in their respective quests.

label: Kourend Council
title: Kourend Council
lead:
The Kourend Council was previously the ruling authority of the kingdom of Great Kourend. The Council was made up of four councillors, with one of the councillors holding the position of head councillor, rotating every year. Every four years, there was an election held for the people of Great Kourend to decide who the councillors should be.

While the five Houses of Great Kourend have their own leader who rules over each city, they must enforce and obey the laws set out by the Kourend Council, but can otherwise rule as they see fit.

label: Kourend Favour
title: Kourend Favour
lead:
interface.]]
Kourend Favour, also simply called Favour, was a members-only system in Great Kourend that allowed players to gain reputation with the five houses ruling the kingdom. Earning favour would unlock many useful privileges, such as access to the Arceuus spellbook with 60% Arceuus favour and access to the Hosidius kitchen ranges with 100% Hosidius favour.

There were a wide range of activities a player could do to earn favour. Activities that reward favour were marked on the minimap with the purple star icon. More activites would become available once the player earned enough favour with the corresponding house.

label: Kraka
title: Kraka
lead: Kraka is a level 91 troll found on Death Plateau. Like the rest of the "big, bad" trolls in the area, such as Stick, Pee Hat, and Rock, he drops a rune warhammer or granite shield, and as such is commonly hunted by ironmen looking to upgrade their armour.

label: Kraken (disambiguation)
title: Kraken (disambiguation)
lead:
Kraken may refer to:

* Kraken, the boss
** Kraken tentacle
** Pet kraken
* Cave kraken, slayer monster
* Kraken Cove, the location
* Kraken display (Old School Museum), scenery

label: Kraken (Sailing)
title: Kraken (Sailing)
lead: Kraken (or sea krakens) are a type of Sailing monsters that can be fought at sea. There are several species of kraken that are found throughout the oceans. All krakens can drop inky paint, although higher-levelled krakens are more likely to do so. Armoured and Vampyre can drop dragon metal sheets, dragon keel parts (in both normal and large) varieties and bottled storms, used for creating a greater teleport focus. Veiled kraken can also drop the dragon cannon barrel.

label: Kraken/Strategies
title: Kraken/Strategies
lead:
The Kraken is a Slayer boss and can therefore only be killed while on a Slayer task to kill it, or (cave) kraken. The Kraken is located in the Kraken Cove.

It is recommended to use the Magic attack style to fight the Kraken, as Ranged deals 1/7th of its normal damage and it is immune to Melee, due to the fact that it cannot be reached by Melee attacks. As there are no complex mechanics, the Kraken is a popular boss (therefore it may be hard to find an empty world). Players can alternatively create an instance for coins, which lasts until the player leaves or logs out.

label: Kree'arra/Strategies
title: Kree'arra/Strategies
lead:
This is a guide to defeating Kree'arra, the Armadyl-aligned general in the God Wars Dungeon.

As Kree'arra is airborne, regular melee attacks will not work; instead, Ranged or Magic must be used to fight him. Halberds and salamanders are the only melee options, but due to Kree'arra's extremely high melee defence, this is not generally recommended unless using the soulflame horn in small teams.

label: Kronos plant (interface item)
title: Kronos plant (interface item)
lead:
The Kronos plant is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide representing the Kronos plant.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Krystilia/Strategies
title: Krystilia/Strategies
lead:
Although other Slayer master tasks may be completed in both Wilderness and mainland locations, all of Krystilia's tasks must be done in the Wilderness. That means players should only take gear they are willing to lose.

: Assess and mitigate risks, and do not ever take any items you cannot afford to lose!

label: kudos
title: kudos
lead:
Kudos is given to players who contribute to the Varrock Museum. Several rewards are unlocked once the player has achieved enough kudos.

Members can earn a total of 243 kudos from activities through the museum, while free-to-players can only earn the five kudos from handing in [[#Ancient relics|ancient relics]]. Players can see a list of activities and check their current Kudos by right-clicking the information booth on the .

label: Kurask (interface item)
title: Kurask (interface item)
lead:
The Kurask is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Kurask

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Kwuarm
title: Kwuarm
lead:
Kwuarm is a medium level herb requiring 54 Herblore to clean. It can be grown from kwuarm seeds at a herb patch at level 56 Farming and is used in the making of weapon poison and the super strength potion. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a kwuarm potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, the herb was originally native to Kourend, with the name being given to it by dwarves, meaning warm death. The name is due to the plant's poisonous sap which is said to cause a burning fever when ingested. Since its discovery, it has often been used as a main ingredient in poison for various pests.

label: Kwuarm potion (unf)
title: Kwuarm potion (unf)
lead: A kwuarm potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a kwuarm on a vial of water, requiring 55 Herblore. Using a limpwurt root on a kwuarm potion (unf) with 55 Herblore yields a super strength(3) and 125 Herblore experience. Using a dragon scale dust on a kwuarm potion (unf) with 60 Herblore yields weapon poison and 137.5 Herblore experience.

label: Kyatt hunter gear
title: Kyatt hunter gear
lead:
Kyatt hunter gear is a set of hunter gear made at the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock or Pellem's Fur Store in the Hunter Guild, with either tattered or normal kyatt furs if a player has Hunter level 52. The gear also requires 52 Hunter to equip.

Individual pieces reduce damage received from Hunter creatures by 20%, giving a total of 60% reduced damage while the full set is worn. Contrary to popular belief, these do not improve catch rates of any hunter creatures.

label: Ladder
title: Ladder
lead: Ladders are used to go up and down to the next or previous level of the Old School RuneScape game. This is a very common piece of scenery found throughout Gielinor. They come in many varieties: ghostly (such as the one at the entrance to Damis' Lair), broken, and regular (commonly found throughout Gielinor). Users cannot ascend or descend 'broken' ladders.

label: Ladder (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course)
title: Ladder (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course)
lead: The ladder is an Agility obstacle found within the Barbarian Outpost Agility Course. Passing the obstacle requires 35 Agility although no experience is awarded.

label: Ladder (Shadow Dungeon)
title: Ladder (Shadow Dungeon)
lead:
Ladders serve as the entrance and exit of the Shadow Dungeon.

The entrance ladder can be found east of Baxtorian Falls, inside a fenced area. The ladder only appears when a ring of visibility or shadows is worn. When the rings are not worn, the ladder will be replaced by a tile of plain grass.

label: Lady Arceuus
title: Lady Arceuus
lead:
Lady Arceuus is the wife of Lord Trobin Arceuus and mother of Asteros Arceuus. She was terminally ill with an unknown disease, which led her husband to seek out the Tasakaal in order to find a cure. The Tasakaal revealed to him how the essence of a mortal could be transferred to an immortal vessel with the power of the Dark Altar. Lord Arceuus would use that knowledge to save his wife - and subsequently he shared the secret with the other citizens of the Arceuus. This eventually led to the event known as the Ascent of Arceuus, where many Citizens of Arceuus adopted their immortal forms.

Despite being the main reason the historical Ascent of Arceuus took place, she cannot be found in-game.

label: Lady Iorwerth
title: Lady Iorwerth
lead:
Lady Iorwerth was the former leader of the Iorwerth Clan through at least some part of the Third Age and most of the Fourth Age. She was the mother of Lord Iorwerth, and one of the leaders of Prifddinas. At some point during the Fourth Age, her son broke one of the nine seals in the Grand Library learning about the existence of a Fragment of Seren sealed away within the Temple of Light. Not knowing the true identity and nature of the fragment, who he misinterpreted as the elven goddess herself, her son became obsessed with finding and freeing it.
When he went to inform Lady Iorwerth of his finding, she brushed him off, but willing to do anything to bring Seren back, Lord Iorwerth killed her remorselessly and assumed her leadership over the Iorwerth Clan and eventually the rest of Prifddinas.

label: Lady Ithell (Fourth Age)
title: Lady Ithell (Fourth Age)
lead:
Lady Ithell was the previous leader of the Ithell Clan and the most accomplished elven architect of her time. Like most of the other elders, she was captured by Lord Iorwerth but liberated by King Baxtorian's army during the Siege of Prifddinas, after which she helped revert the city to its seed form.

She then designed and founded Lletya with the young Arianwyn, calling it her greatest work. Likely aware of her eventual death from chronic illness, she left parts of her soul in the designs so that her eventual successor could inherit her memories to end the civil war. Indeed, she was succeeded by Kelyn Ithell, who gained her memories by seeing a statue built after Lady Ithell's design.

label: Lady Keli
title: Lady Keli
lead:
Lady Keli is a bandit leader and the main antagonist in the Prince Ali Rescue quest. She is found in the jail area (usually inside the jail proper but sometimes within the jail's compound) in Draynor Village.

Lady Keli kidnapped Prince Ali and had plotted to ransom for the prince's release. Keli is vain and arrogant - she likes showing off and being praised, and claims to have killed three men before she was six. The player exploits these traits to outwit her - tricking her into showing the key to Prince Ali's cell, which allows the player to get a clay imprint and make a bronze copy of the key. The player incapacitates her head guard, Joe, before tying Keli up with a rope, locking her in a closet, and freeing Prince Ali.

label: Lady Lumbridge
title: Lady Lumbridge
lead:
The Lady Lumbridge is a ship named after the town of Lumbridge, and is involved in the Dragon Slayer I quest. She is originally of Crandorian design, according to Klarense, but is damaged from "years of wear and tear".

Players purchase her from Klarense in Port Sarim for 2,000 coins in order to get to Crandor. However, they need 90 steel nails, 3 planks, and a hammer to fix Lady Lumbridge before setting off.

label: Lady of the Waves
title: Lady of the Waves
lead:
The Lady of the Waves is a small vessel docked south of Cairn Isle, a small island on the south-western coast of Karamja. She is owned by Captain Shanks, and plays a small role in the One Small Favour quest.

The Lady of the Waves will take players to either Port Sarim or Port Khazard, provided they have a ship ticket, which can be bought on site for a price which is randomised every time you talk to him and can be between 20 and 50 coins. Players should note that it is a one way trip and you cannot use the boat to get back to Cairn Isle.

label: Lady Servil
title: Lady Servil
lead:
Lady Servil is a minor noble of Kandarin, the mother of Sammy Servil and wife of Justin Servil. All three are characters in the Fight Arena quest, in which the player must rescue both Justin and Sammy from the clutches of General Khazard, a maniacal Mahjarrat who delights in fights between his creatures and unfortunate slave fighters.

Lady Servil is located just outside the north-east corner of the hedge-maze surrounding the Tree Gnome Village, and is spoken to in order to begin the quest. You may also need to talk to her about a clue scroll, and some coordinate clues lead to the general area she is in.

label: Lag
title: Lag
lead:
Lag is the delay (also called 'latency') between a player input action and the moment this input is processed and displayed to the player. This delay is always present due to the restraints of data processing and transfer speed, but the term 'lag' is typically used to describe a noticable delay that impedes a smooth gaming experience. The amount of lag depends on several factors, such as server load, the player's internet connection, and the performance of their gaming device. Testing how long it takes for an action to be sent to the game server and back is called pinging. The response time of a 'ping' is often denoted in miliseconds. While moderate lag does often not directly cause a player to fully disconnect from the server, severe lag and sudden disconnections can sometimes be caused by the same underlying issues. Lag is typically not caused by problems within the power of Jagex, except in the event of server lag occurring.

When a player is participating in dangerous activities, lag can be a common cause of death, especially when it occurs suddenly. Lag can be especially dangerous to hardcore ironmen. Players experiencing unstable connections or high levels of lag should avoid partaking in activities such as player killing, boss hunting or fighting other powerful monsters.

label: Laheeb
title: Laheeb
lead:
Laheeb is a bandit from the Kharidian Desert Bandit Camp who stole the gilded cross from Rasolo, a wandering merchant. The cross holds great sentimental value to Rasolo, and thus, during Desert Treasure I, the player is tasked with stealing it back. In exchange for the safe return of the Gilded cross, the player receives the ring of visibility.

The stolen cross is locked in a secure chest found within Laheeb's tent, which the player may attempt to pick using a lockpick. In order to successfully pick the lock, the player must succeed three times in a row.

label: Lamistard
title: Lamistard
lead:
Lamistard is a Zamorakian Mahjarrat mentioned by the golem during Desert Treasure II.

He was a tribune in the Zarosian Empire, but allied with Zamorak in the God Wars.

label: lamp
title: lamp
lead:
The lamp is a reward obtained from several random events or by opening an Intricate Pouch that differs from those awarded by quests. While these lamps cannot be traded or banked, rubbing one gives the option of adding experience to any skill a player chooses. The amount given is ten times their skill level of choice (e.g. a skill at level 21 would give 210 experience).

Lamps are converted to if lost on death in the Wilderness.

lead:

label: lamp oil
title: lamp oil
lead:
Lamp oil is obtained by distilling swamp tar, using a lamp oil still. They are located either in the Chemist's House in Rimmington (the small still, inside the house), or at Miltog's Lamps in Dorgesh-Kaan.

Note: As there is no "lamp oil" item, you need to bring the empty oil lamp, empty oil lantern, sapphire lantern, or bullseye lantern (empty) to hold the oil in. The oil will stay inside the lamp oil still until you use the item in your inventory on the still. You will also need to bring swamp tar (one tar per lamp) in order to make it into lamp oil.

label: Landlubber
title: Landlubber
lead:
Landlubber is a music track that is unlocked in Brimhaven, including on the island accessible by fairy ring code . In this area, the music player will shuffle between this track, High Seas and Jolly R.

In Classic mode, the track only plays in the jungle west of Brimhaven, at the South Brimhaven mine.
