label: lantadyme
title: lantadyme
lead:
Lantadyme is a high level herb requiring a Herblore level of 67 to clean. It is obtained by cleaning grimy lantadyme which can be grown from a lantadyme seed with a Farming level of 73.

Lantadymes are used to make anti-fire potions (with ground blue dragon scales) and magic potions (with potato cactus). To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a lantadyme potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

label: Lantadyme potion (unf)
title: Lantadyme potion (unf)
lead: A lantadyme potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a lantadyme on a vial of water, requiring 69 Herblore. Using dragon scale dust on a lantadyme potion (unf) with 69 Herblore yields an antifire potion (3) and 157.5 Herblore experience. Using a potato cactus on a lantadyme potion (unf) with 76 herblore yields a magic potion (3) and 172.5 Herblore experience.

title: lantern harpooning
lead:
Lantern harpooning is a Fishing activity released with Sailing, requiring at least 47 Sailing and 52 Fishing. Players can use any harpoon (barehanded fishing does not work) and any lit lantern to catch squids at specific fishing spots. These spots are located at The Onyx Crest, Laguna Aurorae, Wintumber Island and Buccaneers' Haven, which require certain Sailing levels to access. An equipable harpoon and lantern may be used to save inventory space.

Players with 52 Fishing can catch swordtip squid, while players with 69 Fishing can catch jumbo squid as well.

label: Larina Hallow
title: Larina Hallow
lead:
Larina Hallow was the daughter of the Icyene Queen Efaritay and her husband the human King Ascertes. She was killed by her father after he was turned into the vampyre Vanstrom Klause by Lord Drakan as part of his scheme of conquering Hallowvale.

During Sins of the Father, Vanescula Drakan reveals to Safalaan, that Larina was his sister and that she was killed in the conquest of Hallowvale, and that she was buried in the mausoleum at the Icyene Graveyard intended for the whole royal family of Hallowvale. During the quest's climax Vanstrom Klause reveals that he killed her without remorse, now being a vampyre removing all attachment to his former life.

label: Laris Gontamue
title: Laris Gontamue
lead: Laris Gontamue was one of the founding members of the Elders of Avarrocka. Romeo and Lilith Gontamue are his descendants, Romeo being adopted into the Gontamue family.

label: Larupia hunter gear
title: Larupia hunter gear
lead:
Larupia hunter gear is a set of hunter gear made at the Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock or Pellem's Fur Store in the Hunter Guild, with tattered or perfect larupia furs, and requires 28 Hunter to wear.

When the full set is worn, players will take 20% less damage from Hunter creatures. Contrary to popular belief, these do not improve catch rates of any hunter creatures. All three pieces of larupia gear count as warm clothing at Wintertodt.

label: Lassar
title: Lassar
lead: Lassar was a Zarosian fortress built on what is now known as Ice Mountain. Nothing remains of the fortress; it is assumed to have been destroyed during the God Wars. The fortress was rebuilt into what is now known as Ruins of Camdozaal; beneath it lies a largely intact Lassar Undercity spared from destruction because of its isolation from Lassar.

label: Last Man Standing Beta
title: Last Man Standing Beta
lead:
The Last Man Standing beta world was initially exclusive to 200 players, where they were selected by Jagex Moderators from an application form given in a newspost in the beginning of July. The next week, it became available to all members, and then free players the day after.

Upon logging in, players appeared in the Last Man Standing lobby, with their coffers already stored with 10,000,000 coins to begin the minigame. Players in normal worlds would still be able to see the lobby and Lisa, but are unable to go inside.

label: Last Man Standing: Beta
title: Last Man Standing: Beta
lead:
The Last Man Standing: Beta is a rework of the minigame, changing from looting objects around the island to having a pre-set inventory and equipment, removing the heavy luck factor in obtaining equipment to be victorious. The beta worlds are available to members, being hosted on worlds 401, 405, 407, 409 and 412.

However, due to technical issues, the live version of Last Man Standing is disabled, making worlds 317, 326, 393 and 425 normal worlds. If players attempted to join a live game, a chatbox message will state that a beta is currently live and ask that players join games there instead to test the features.

label: Lava

lead: Lava may refer to the following:

label: Lava battlestaff
title: Lava battlestaff
lead:
A lava battlestaff is a lava elemental staff which provides unlimited amounts of earth and fire runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. It requires 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield.

The mystic lava staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses. It is obtained by taking the lava battlestaff and to Thormac. (Reduced to or with completion of the hard and elite Kandarin diaries respectively.)

label: Lava Dragon Isle
title: Lava Dragon Isle
lead: The Lava Dragon Isle is a members-only section of the Wilderness which stretches from level 36 to level 42. It is a Multicombat area, and the only place where lava dragons spawn.

label: Lava dragon/Strategies
title: Lava dragon/Strategies
lead: Lava dragons reside on Lava Dragon Isle in the Wilderness (between level 36 and 42 Wilderness) and have low Magic resistance, making spells as low as Water Bolt sufficient enough to kill them due to their Elemental weakness to Water. Despite the dangers involved, willing players can travel there and safespot them in hopes of the highly elusive draconic visage.

label: lava eel
title: lava eel
lead: Lava eel is a type of untradeable fish that restores 11 Hitpoints when eaten. During Heroes' Quest, guild master Achietties will ask players to obtain a cooked lava eel to prove that they are worthy of membership to the Heroes' Guild. It can be obtained by cooking raw lava eel on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 53 Cooking and granting 30 experience when successful. There is no chance of burning a lava eel.

label: Lava Maze
title: Lava Maze
lead:
The Lava Maze is a maze located deep in the Wilderness, around level 40-45. In the entrance and partway through the maze, there are spiderwebs that must be cut with a slash weapon or a knife. Should players somehow lose their slash weapon or knife while inside the maze, there are a couple of knife item spawns.

An Agility shortcut (stepping stone) on the north side of the maze allows you to go to the centre of the maze with 82 Agility.

label: Lava Maze Dungeon
title: Lava Maze Dungeon
lead:
The Lava Maze Dungeon is a dungeon beneath the Lava Maze in high level Wilderness. The dungeon is entirely single-way combat and has two ladder entrances.

The dungeon's western entrance is west of the Lava Maze, level 42 Wilderness in a metal fenced area containing lesser demons. This entrance leads to a small area containing only poison spiders and the lever to enter the King Black Dragon's lair. This part of the dungeon covers level 42 to 43 Wilderness.

label: Lava Maze Dungeon mine
title: Lava Maze Dungeon mine
lead:
The Lava Maze Dungeon mine is a small mining site found in the deep Wilderness. To reach the mine, players must travel to the centre of the Lava Maze, where the Lava Maze Dungeon's eastern entrance can be found.

Once players enter the eastern entrance, they will be in the dungeon's western side. A single runite rock can be found here. However, the mine is extremely dangerous as several greater demons wander the dungeon, and two black dragons can also be found nearby. The dragons can easily be trapped behind the rock, but players will likely be attacked and poisoned by the poison spiders wandering near the rock. With some manoeuvring, however, the spiders can be trapped behind stalagmites. As well as this, due to being located in the Wilderness, players may attack and kill each other here.

label: Lava Maze runite mine
title: Lava Maze runite mine
lead:
Located north-west of the Lava Maze in level 46 Wilderness, the Lava Maze Runite Mine is the only mining site in free-to-play worlds with runite ore to be mined. Therefore, the runite ore is rarely left undepleted, as rune miners often time the spawns and wait for the ore to respawn in anticipation. The mine is located north of both the Bandit Camp Mine and the Lava Maze in the Wilderness. There are two rocks here which contain runite ore. Although the area around the rune rocks is crawling with aggressive deadly red spiders, players will rarely be attacked by the spiders when standing next to the runite. If you are attacked by a spider, run to the other side of the rock. World switching is useful here to fill the inventory with ore, as it takes 12 minutes for the runite to respawn.

Player killers are often found around this mine, as foes cannot teleport until they reach a Wilderness Obelisk, the Mage Arena, or level 20-30 Wilderness. To complement this, it is easy to attack and kill unsuspecting players who are looking for runite ore to mine as they often forego armour in order to reduce weight and item loss upon death. To reduce the risk of being killed while mining, it is recommended that players bring a few pieces of high-healing food, such as sharks.

label: Lava trough
title: Lava trough
lead: The Lava trough is found in the elemental workshop near the fire elementals. During the Elemental Workshop I quest, players must take lava from the trough using a stone bowl and then use it to light the nearby furnace.

label: Law
title: Law
lead:

*Armadyl, a god associated with law and justice.

label: Law Altar
title: Law Altar
lead:
The Law Altar is a runic altar upon which law runes are crafted from pure essence, providing 9.5 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Level 54 Runecraft and completion of the quest Troll Stronghold is required to craft law runes. The altar is believed to have been built upon the very spot where Saradomin first set foot upon Gielinor in the Second Age.

Players may create a law tiara here by using either a law talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 47.5 Runecraft experience. A catalytic tiara can also be created here by using a catalytic talisman and gold tiara, granting 42.5 Runecraft experience.

label: Law rune
title: Law rune
lead: The law rune is a rune used in all teleportation and telekinesis spells, as well as in many of the supportive and utility spells on the Lunar Spellbook. For non-members, the main source of law runes is from monster drops, as most monsters that drop runes may occasionally drop law runes. For members, they may be purchased in the Mage Arena Rune Shop or in the Wizards' Guild, requiring 66 Magic and completion of The Hand in the Sand. They can also be purchased from Ali Morrisane after partial completion of the Rogue Trader miniquest (after completing The Feud quest), from the magic store on Ape Atoll after obtaining the greegree as part of the Monkey Madness I quest, or from the magic store in Prifdinnas after completing Song of the Elves. Guardians of the Rift offers an efficient and affordable way of acquiring law runes.

label: Law talisman
title: Law talisman
lead:
The law talisman is a talisman used to access the Law Altar located on Entrana for the purpose of runecraft. It can also be combined with a silver tiara by using the tiara on the Law Altar with the talisman in your inventory, resulting in a law tiara. Once inside the altar a player can make law runes. This requires 54 Runecraft.

The law talisman is a reward for completing the Troll Stronghold quest, and can be acquired again from Dunstan in Burthorpe for 1000 coins each if lost or if you want to have spare talismans. Dunstan will not sell you another law talisman if there are already five in your inventory or bank.

label: Leafy (attribute)
title: Leafy (attribute)
lead:
The leafy attribute is assigned to monsters that are immune to all but leaf-bladed weapons.

Note that damage from other weapons is still calculated for the purposes of special effects, even though it causes no damage. For example, a player may still use the special attacks of the Toxic blowpipe and Saradomin godsword normally, despite the lack of damage.

label: leafy palm tree
title: leafy palm tree
lead:
Leafy Palm Trees are found only in the Kharazi Jungle. They are spaced sporadically around the jungle but have a fair concentration around the water pool, which is near teak trees marked by the western tree symbol on the map. There is also one near the totem pole in the west of the jungle.

Leafy palm trees cannot be cut, but shaking one causes a palm leaf to drop from it. There is a cool-down period of about 35 seconds before another leaf can be obtained from the same tree. To save a small amount of time on the Karamja Diary, you can shake a leafy palm tree, then drop and pick up the leaf five times.

and more!

League trophies are untradeable cosmetic rewards obtained for placing in specific league point brackets at the end of Leagues. They can be reclaimed for free by speaking to the Leagues Assistant (previously the Leagues Tutor), or from a league trophy case in a player-owned house. Trophies can be stored in the trophy case, or displayed on one of the pedestals in a house.

Trophies can be equipped and right-clicked to perform a unique trophy emote. The adamant, rune, and dragon trophies are two-handed items, and the others are equipped in the shield slot.

label: Leagues
title: Leagues
lead:
Leagues are a seasonal variant of Old School RuneScape revolving around completing various tasks on time-limited servers with additional rules such as area restrictions, trade restrictions and boosted experience rates. Additionally, completing League tasks unlocks relics that further alter the game experience.

Similar to Deadman Mode, every player in Leagues starts without stats or items, and progress in Old School RuneScape is not affected. Each League runs about once a year for eight weeks, and progress made within a League does not carry over to the next League, with the exception of pets, additional bank slots, league-to-league rewards, and league points for purchasing those rewards (but not in-game points for relics).

label: Lean
title: Lean
lead:
Lean is one of four Mime emote unlocked as a Random event reward. Via the loop option, the player character will lean on the air continuously until they interact with the overworld or perform another emote.

Upon completing a Mime event, players are returned to their previous location in game, with a new mime emote unlocked. Players cannot choose which of the four emotes unlock since this is random.

label: Leather
title: Leather
lead:
Leather, or soft leather, is obtained from tanning a cowhide. Leather can be used with a needle and thread to be crafted into leather gloves, leather boots, leather cowl, leather vambraces, leather body, a coif or leather chaps, granting Crafting experience. On every fifth piece of leather used, one thread will be consumed, effectively necessitating a 1/5 ratio of thread needed per leather when creating armour.

A single piece of leather can be found on top of a table in the Shayzien Encampment. You must use telekinetic grab to pick it up.

label: leather armour
title: leather armour
lead: Leather armour is the lowest quality ranged armour. There are no requirements to wear it. All of the pieces can be made using the Crafting skill from leather.

label: Leather body
title: Leather body
lead: Leather body is a part of leather armour and is the weakest ranged torso in the game. It requires 1 Ranged to equip. By using steel studs on a leather body, members can turn them into a studded body at level 41 Crafting.

label: leather boots
title: leather boots
lead: Leather boots is a part of leather armour worn on the foot slot that offer slight bonuses to defence. They can also be found while big net fishing.

label: Leather chaps
title: Leather chaps
lead: Leather chaps is a part of leather armour that is worn in the legs slot, most commonly by low-level rangers. Low-levelled player mages also often wear these chaps, since they give a slight defence bonuses without a magic attack penalty.

label: Leather cowl
title: Leather cowl
lead: Leather cowls are leather armour worn on the head, most commonly by low-levelled rangers.

label: Leather gloves
title: Leather gloves
lead: Leather gloves are basic gloves worn in the hands slot, offering slight defensive bonuses. Making them requires 1 Crafting, 1 leather, 1 thread, and a needle, yielding 13.8 Crafting experience.

label: leather shield
title: leather shield
lead:
Leather shields are a class of shields that are oriented toward rangers. They can be made by using various types of Wooden shields with certain types of leather, while adding metal nails to complete the shield. Players can speak to the shield master in the Ranging Guild to receive a leather shields flyer, which details the materials needed to create each leather shield. Blessed dragonhide shields have the same bonuses as a Black d'hide shield with an additional +1 prayer bonus, and can be acquired from hard Treasure Trails.

As they are made solely for rangers, these shields confer high penalties for players attacking with melee or magic whilst having these shields equipped, while giving moderate resistance to magic attacks and a fairly low resistance for melee and ranged attacks.

label: Leather vambraces
title: Leather vambraces
lead:
Leather vambraces are leather armour worn on the hands. With no requirements to equip, they are most commonly used by low-level rangers, and often mages (as there is no magic penalty). Overall they are generally a superior alternative to leather gloves with a notable exception of the crush defence, and could be considered the best "gloves" for free-to-play users who lack 40 Ranged to equip green dragonhide vambraces, as well as the best-in-slot mage gloves due to their lack of negative penalties.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make spiky vambraces, requiring a Crafting level of 32.

label: Leatherworker
title: Leatherworker
lead:
The Leatherworker is a Tanner and a member of the Ranging Guild. Found on the north-eastern side of the guild, she can cure and tan hides into leather. Her shop is marked with the tanning icon ( ).

Unlike other tanners, she does not have a specific Option to access the tanning interface. It is instead accessed through a dialogue option when talking to her.

Leechfin fishing is pitched as a high-intensity method of training Fishing, with experience rates maxing out in the 120k-130k exp/hr range. The leechfin sandwich was a high-level food item proposed as part of the skilling-focused rewards of the upcoming quest The Blood Moon Rises. It would have been created from leechfin, a new fish caught in the rivers of Vampyrium.

lead: The Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items is a store located on the of Legends' Guild, owned by the Guildmaster's brother, Siegfried Erkle. The shop is the only source of the Cape of legends and Mithril seeds (except the quest reward from Waterfall Quest).

label: Legends' Guard
title: Legends' Guard
lead:
Legends' Guards are unattackable guards outside the Legends' Guild. They wear what appears to be blurite armour and carry an iron spear.

The two guards will greet you when you go through the gate. Their message varies based on your status in the Legends' Quest: during the quest they say "I hope the quest is going well [sir/madam]", while after the quest they say "Attention! Legends' guild member approaching!".

label: Legends' Guild
title: Legends' Guild
lead:
The Legends' Guild is the second most exclusive of the quest-based guilds in Old School RuneScape (with the Myths' Guild being the first). It is located to the north-east of East Ardougne, east of Hemenster and the south of Seers' Village. To enter the grounds of the Legends' Guild, players must have started the Legends' Quest. However, to enter the actual building, players must have completed the entire quest. Radimus Erkle is the grand vizier of the guild, and he is also the start point of the Legends' Quest.

A number of NPCs are implied to be members of the guild, by the fact they themselves wear a cape of legends.

label: Legends' Guild bank
title: Legends' Guild bank
lead: The Legends' Guild bank is a bank found on the top floor of the Legends' Guild. Players must have completed Legends' Quest to enter.

label: Legends' Guild mine
title: Legends' Guild mine
lead:
The Legends' Guild mining site, also called the East Ardougne Mine, is located just south-west of the Legends' Guild and east of Ardougne's east entrance. Both places have a bank that can used for depositing ores. This mine is one of many where three iron rocks can be mined without moving, thus ideal for power-mining. It can be accessed using Fairy ring code and then walking south and slightly west.

This site contains many coal rocks, and some players may find it more useful than the Mining Guild as it is less crowded and is closer to a bank. Players can bank their ores at Ardougne, the Legends' Guild (requires completion of the Legends' Quest), or Zanaris (requires completion of Lost City and partial completion of Fairytale II - Cure a Queen), which can be accessed by the fairy ring near the Legends' Guild.

label: Legends' Quest
title: Legends' Quest
lead:
Legends' Quest is a quest in which the player is sent by Guildmaster Radimus Erkle to explore and map the Kharazi Jungle on the southern part of Karamja, establish relations with the natives and obtain a gift from them.

Legends' Quest was the 50th quest to be released, and the last quest to be released before the launch of the RuneScape 2 beta. It was the first quest to be rated Master.

label: Legion
title: Legion
lead: Legion is a music track that is unlocked at Barbarian Outpost. It can also be heard underneath the Barbarian Agility Course and the lobby of Barbarian Assault. Prior to tracks removal from Wilderness Bandit Camp in 2021, this track was accessible to free-to-play players.

label: lemon
title: lemon
lead:
A lemon is a food item that heals 2 hitpoints when eaten. It is generally used as an ingredient in gnome cooking, in cocktails such as the fruit blast, pineapple punch, the wizard blizzard, and the blurberry special. Players can use a knife to cut the lemon into lemon chunks or lemon slices, which are also used in making cocktails.

Lemons cannot be produced through the Farming skill. However, they can be used to make regular compost.

label: lemon chunks
title: lemon chunks
lead:
Lemon chunks are used in gnome cooking. One can obtain them by using a knife on a lemon and choosing the option to dice the lemon.

Lemon chunks are used as an ingredient in a Blurberry special. It is used in the second step of preparing the drink, and must be in the inventory along with orange chunks, equa leaves and a sliced lime to be able to pour a mixed special into a cocktail glass.

label: Lemon slices
title: Lemon slices
lead:
Lemon slices are used in gnome cooking. Players can obtain them by using a knife on a lemon.

Lemon slices are used as an ingredient in a fruit blast. It is used in the second step of preparing the drink, and must be in the inventory to be able to pour a mixed blast into a cocktail glass.

label: Lens mould
title: Lens mould
lead:
The lens mould is a quest item in the Observatory Quest. It is obtained by searching a stove in a locked kitchen in the Observatory Dungeon. The kitchen is accessed by killing the goblin guard nearby and then using the goblin kitchen key on the gate.

The mould must be given to the Observatory professor along with a piece of molten glass to make a new observatory lens for the telescope. He will be unable to make the lens and will return the mould and glass so the player can make it.

label: Leprechaun
title: Leprechaun
lead:
Leprechauns are a race of small, humanoid creatures. They are quite similar to gnomes and are commonly encountered in farming, especially the tool leprechauns. They have an affinity with nature and live in wood- and farmlands among trees and flora.

They appear to have the same connections as s do in mythology in real life; the Woodcutting Leprechaun appears in a patch of four-leaf clovers along with the Ends of Rainbows that grant the player "leprechaun's luck" when stepped in, and the tool leprechauns located Underwater near Fossil Island weighs itself down with a Pot of Gold.

label: Lesser Demon
title: Lesser Demon
lead:
Lesser demons are the second weakest standard demon, above the imp. They are sometimes killed by Free-to-play players, as they are one of the strongest monsters on those servers and can drop the desirable rune med helm. Lesser demons have a somewhat low Defence, which can make them a good source of combat experience. They are susceptible to the effects of demonbane weapons.

The Chasm of Fire is one of the best locations for slaying lesser demons. The fairy ring ( ) is very close, and a Dwarf Multicannon can be used to speed up the task; players can also safespot in this location. Although combat experience per hour can be above average, lesser demons' sparse drops make them a below average Slayer task.

label: Lesser demon (Melzar's Maze)
title: Lesser demon (Melzar's Maze)
lead:
A Lesser demon is found in the basement of Melzar's Maze, past Melzar the Mad. It must be killed to obtain the green key, which can unlock the green door and complete the maze.

According to Melzar's notes, Melzar summoned and subdued the demon to channel its magic to help perform necromancy to bring back the Crandorian refugees (including his wife) that were slain by Elvarg. However, as Melzar's sanity dwindled due to the numerous repeated failures to resurrect his fellow countrymen, the demon continued to encourage him, which led to Melzar becoming completely insane and obsessed with cabbages.

label: Level 1 certificate
title: Level 1 certificate
lead:
The level 1 certificate is a quest item used during The Dig Site. Players may obtain one after completing the first archaeology exam. The certificate allows players to dig at level 1 sites in the Digsite.

After completing the quest, players may bring the certificate to the Varrock Museum curator who will take it for safekeeping. This is not required to claim the reward from giving in the Level 3 certificate. You will not get the certificate back.

label: Lever
title: Lever
lead:
A lever is a piece of interactive scenery that is used in Old School RuneScape to activate something. This may be a method of transportation—for example, the Ardougne/Edgeville teleport lever. Players can usually pull a lever simply by left-clicking on it (see Game controls).

The "lever" which most players are referring to when mentioning it in game is the Ardougne teleport lever, a common way to get in and out of Deep Wilderness quickly and relatively safely. There is a similar lever located in the mausoleum just south of the Edgeville bank that also leads to the Deserted Keep. There is another lever in the Deserted Keep that can teleport players back out of the Wilderness.

label: Lever (Ardougne)
title: Lever (Ardougne)
lead: The Ardougne teleport lever is located in the west section of East Ardougne, just north of the gate separating the two cities. Along with the Edgeville teleport lever, this is the lever that transports players to the lever located in deep Wilderness in the Deserted Keep when pulled. Doing this is a requirement for the Easy Ardougne Diary. When pulled, the messages You pull the lever... and ... and teleport into the Wilderness. will be displayed.

label: Lever (Deserted Keep)
title: Lever (Deserted Keep)
lead:
The lever, also known as the wilderness lever, can be found in the Deserted Keep, located within the deep Wilderness. The lever can be pulled to teleport to the lever in East Ardougne, and after completion of the easy Wilderness Diary, can also be used to teleport near the lever in Edgeville. Players can set the default left-click teleport option by using the swap-options option on the lever, or in the settings menu.

When pulled, the messages You pull the lever... and ... and teleport out of the Wilderness. will be displayed.

label: Lever (Elemental Workshop I)
title: Lever (Elemental Workshop I)
lead: Levers can be found on the first floor of the Elemental Workshop, operating various machinery in parts of the workshop. A lever in the water room can be pulled to turn the waterwheel once the water controls have been operated. A lever in the air room is used to start the bellows once they have been repaired.

label: Lever (Family Crest)
title: Lever (Family Crest)
lead: Levers can be found at three locations within Witchaven Dungeon. During the Family Crest quest, players must pull the levers in a set sequence. Doing so unlocks a door that leads to room where the player can mine 'perfect' gold ore. Once the door is unlocked, it does not require the lever puzzle to be solved again.

label: Lever (King Black Dragon Lair)
title: Lever (King Black Dragon Lair)
lead:
A lever can be found on the southern wall of the King Black Dragon Lair. Players can pull the lever to exit the lair and teleport to the Lava Maze Dungeon.

: Using the lever to exit the lair will teleport the player to level 42 Wilderness. It is recommended to use an alternative teleportation method to exit the lair if returning to the Lava Maze Dungeon is not necessary.

label: Lever (Lava Maze Dungeon)
title: Lever (Lava Maze Dungeon)
lead:
A lever can be found in the Lava Maze Dungeon, accessible by climbing down the ladder on the west side of the Lava Maze. Players can pull the lever to teleport to the King Black Dragon Lair. However, if a player is teleblocked, they cannot teleport via the lever. Additionally, players have the option to open a private instance of the lair for 50,000 coins; payment for the instance can be deducted directly from their bank. The 'commune' option on the lever allows players to see the number of other players currently within the lair.

: While the lair itself is not in the Wilderness, players are in the Wilderness until they pull the lever.

label: Lever (Temple of Ikov)
title: Lever (Temple of Ikov)
lead:
The lever is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. It is found in the eastern room in the Temple of Ikov after crossing the bridge which requires the player's weight to be below 0 kg (using boots of lightness or other weight-reducing clothing) to successfully cross. It is used to operate a broken lever which opens a door leading further into the temple.

After the quest, the item is still obtainable, but has no further use beyond the quest.

label: Lever (Watchtower)
title: Lever (Watchtower)
lead: Lever is an interactive scenery object that can be found on the of the Watchtower located north-east of Yanille. Players must pull the lever during the Watchtower quest once all the power crystals have been obtained and are in their correct places in order to power the magic shield protecting Yanille from the Ogres.

label: Lever bracket
title: Lever bracket
lead:
The Lever bracket is a broken lever located in the Temple of Ikov, on the south-west wall from the leader near the entrance. The lever has to be repaired first, by using the lever piece on the bracket. The lever can then be pulled.

Warning: If you place the lever but do not pull it and then leave the area, the lever will not be there when you return. You will have to cross the bridge again to collect it.

label: Lieutenant Strongaxe
title: Lieutenant Strongaxe
lead:
Lieutenant Strongaxe was the Dorgeshuun leader that led the Dorgeshuun deeper beneath the ground following the death of General Bloodfist.

Strongaxe, Bloodfist's second-in-command, led the Dorgeshuun further beneath the surface away from the reach of Bandos or any other gods. This was the first time that a goblin tribe wasn't under Bandos' rule since before he discovered the goblin race on Yu'biusk.

label: life leech
title: life leech
lead:
Life leech is a utility effect that can turn a percentage of damage dealt into Hitpoints restoration. Life leech can occur actively through some special attacks or more passively through chance on hit effects. This effect is often sought by advanced players to increase the margin of error during harder content, or increase sustainability on longer outings. Some powerful monsters possess methods to leech health from players in return.

Not all sources of life leech are equal and each method may have unique limitations. For example onyx bolts (e) cannot trigger when facing undead monsters and the Saradomin godsword can restore health when fighting some enemies which are completely immune to the sword's damage like a kurask.

label: Light Ranged weapons
title: Light Ranged weapons
lead:
Light Ranged weapons are a category of equipment typically categorised by faster hitting attacks, such as darts and knives. The most widely used light ranged weapon is by far the Toxic blowpipe.

Notable NPCs that have negative defence against light ranged weapons include Aviansies and lizardmen.

label: Light sources

Light sources are used to illuminate dark caves and dungeons. Some of these areas are inaccessible or very dangerous without a light source.

Most light sources are items that require certain Firemaking levels to be lit. However, there are also certain equipable and stationary light sources.

In Classic mode, the track plays at an area around Goblin Village and in the south-west slope of Ice Mountain. Playing at the latter is presumably unintentional due to Alone playing there before 2021.

One of the lines of products in this brand is the Lightomatic Deluxe, from which the owners of the lighthouse in the Fremennik Province have purchased and installed the Lightomatic Deluxe 500. During the Horror from the Deep quest, the player repairs the lighthouse's equipment by following instructions from the company's manual.

label: Lilith Gontamue
title: Lilith Gontamue
lead: Lilith Gontamue was a former Varrockian noble belonging to the Gontamue family, descending from the Elders of Avarrocka. She was the last blood descendant of Laris Gontamue within the family. She married into the Fitzharmon family.

label: lime
title: lime
lead:
A lime is a members-only green fruit used in Gnome Cuisine, most often used in Gnome cooking. It can be diced with a knife into lime chunks, or sliced with a knife into lime slices. These both heal 2 Hitpoints each.

Unlike most other fruits, it cannot be grown using the Farming skill. Instead, they must be bought from Hudo's groceries and Heckel Funch in the Grand Tree. It is also available from the market seller in Pollnivneach, gotten as drop from gnomes throughout Tree Gnome Stronghold or it can be stolen at the fruit stall in Hosidius or in the Kourend Castle courtyard.

label: Lime slices

lead:
Limpwurt roots are a Herblore secondary ingredient that can be grown through the Farming skill at level 26 with limpwurt seeds. 15 limpwurt roots are used to protect growing teak trees.

They are useful in free-to-play to make strength potions (or super strength for members). The Apothecary in Varrock will exchange them for four-dose antipoison, energy potions, and strength potions. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.

label: Line of sight
title: Line of sight
lead:
__NOTOC__
Line of sight is a game mechanic that determines whether a direct, unobstructed path exists between two points or entities. It is a fundamental requirement for most interactions, including combat, skilling, and NPC detection. Players and NPCs become visible if they are within 15 tiles of the tile an observing player is standing on.

A target is considered to be outside the line of sight if the path is blocked by scenery (such as a wall or a tree), another character, or if the target is around a corner.

label: Line-of-Sight Beta
title: Line-of-Sight Beta
lead:
For the last 15 years, the way the algorithm calculated line-of-sight was not symmetrical, meaning that a player might be able to range/mage their target without the target having line-of-sight to range/mage back. The reason for making these changes is to have more accurate and fairer PvP and PvM challenges.

In June 2009, RuneScape released an update that changed the way line-of-sight was calculated in order to make it symmetrical. As we all know Old School was released based on a 2007 version of the game, and as such, we still have a non-symmetrical algorithm. We plan to implement the updated line-of-sight algorithm in Old School and as a result, we have opened up the beta worlds to allow you to test it .

label: Linked account
title: Linked account
lead: A Linked Account is a third party account or provider which is connected, or 'linked', to a user's Jagex account. Having a third party account linked will allow a user to access Jagex's games and services (such as Old School RuneScape, and the RuneScape website) using the login credentials of the third party. It is possible to link multiple third party accounts to a Jagex account, allowing for multiple methods of logging in (e.g. using a Gmail account to log into Old School RuneScape mobile).

label: List of highest maximum hits
title: List of highest maximum hits
lead:
This list includes the highest theoretical maximum hits currently achievable using legitimite means for each combat style.

For the purpose of this list, only single attacks against single targets are included, even where the weapon includes multiple combined hitsplats. It is assumed the player has maximum stats, is wearing equipment with the highest possible strength in each equipment slot (unless otherwise specified) and is killing the target monster while on a Slayer task wherever relevant.

label: List of keys
title: List of keys
lead:
There are many keys in Old School RuneScape, which usually take the form of bitted keys. The most common purpose for these items is to unlock means to progress in a quest, or to be consumed for access to rewards after being acquired in an activity.

Many keys are very similar in appearance, but their examine text contains an indication of their origin. In addition, a number of them can be stored on the steel key ring, as to save bank space for keys that the player may have to re-use.

label: List of spells
title: List of spells
lead: This is a complete list of spells in the game, including magic from the Ancient, Lunar, and Arceuus spellbooks. Casting a combat spell grants the spell's base experience plus 2 Magic and 1.33 Hitpoints experience for each point of damage the spell caused; "splashing" the spell (casting the spell but failing) grants only its base Magic experience and no Hitpoints experience.

label: Lit candle (unobtainable item)
title: Lit candle (unobtainable item)
lead:
A lit candle is an unobtainable version of the Lit candle. Candles were previously tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. However, they were made untradeable due to an unfixable bug where trading a lit candle in a dark area would not update the lighting for either player. Any player who had a noted Lit candle was given this now discontinued item. Originally, the item was identical to the real lit candle, except being stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

title: Lizardman shaman/Strategies
lead: Lizardman shamans are popular monsters hunted by players for their renowned dragon warhammer drop, which has a useful special attack for high level PvM encounters. This guide will give a few tips and some setups to help out with your kills.

lead: The Lizardmen are a race of reptilian humanoids native to Great Kourend.

label: lobster
title: lobster
lead:
Lobster is a type of fish that restores 12 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw lobster on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 40 Cooking and granting 120 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt lobster. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 74.

When eaten, the message You eat the lobster. is displayed.

label: Lobster pot
title: Lobster pot
lead:
Lobster pots are items that can be bought from major fishing shops for 20 coins each and are used to fish lobsters from cage/harpoon fishing spots with 40 Fishing, which are a common healing food that restores 12 Hitpoints. A lobster pot spawn is found within the Fishing Guild.

They are also used in dark crab fishing. Dark crab fishing spots are only in the Wilderness and require level 85 fishing,

label: Local Gnome
title: Local Gnome
lead: Local gnomes are gnomes found around King Bolren in the Tree Gnome Village. Unlike other gnomes, they can not be attacked.

label: Locating crystal
title: Locating crystal
lead:
The locating crystal is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching the dolmen in the Tomb of Bervirius. It is used to locate the tomb of Rashiliyia. In order for it to function the player is required to have at least 10 prayer points. After the quest is finished, it no longer functions but can be sold to Yanni Salika in Shilo Village for 500 coins.

If the player tries to drop the crystal, it will break and may damage the player for 1-10 Hitpoints. In case a player has less than 15 points of health however, dropping a locating crystal will inflict an amount of damage equal to half their Hitpoints instead.

label: Locating crystal (unobtainable item)
title: Locating crystal (unobtainable item)
lead: The locating crystal is an unobtainable item that appears during the Shilo Village quest. When the player obtains the Locating crystal, they can use it to locate the tomb of Rashiliyia. A different coloured version of the crystal will appear in the chatbox, depending on how close the player is to the tomb. The actual recoloured crystals, however, cannot be obtained by the player.

lead: Locked Gates are cosmetic scenery found in Seers' Village, south-east to the Bank, as well as the Ogresses' Bank Vault at Corsair Cove Dungeon.

label: Locked Ogre chest
title: Locked Ogre chest
lead: The Locked Ogre chest is located in Rantz's cave and is unlocked during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. The chest is closed and weighted shut with a large rock. During the quest, the player has to unlock the chest to obtain ogre bellows.

label: Lockpick
title: Lockpick
lead:
A lockpick is an item used with the Thieving skill that can be used on certain locked objects. While some objects require a lockpick to be unlocked, certain objects are instead only made easier to open.

Lockpicks can be obtained by pickpocketing bandits (with 53 Thieving) and rogues (31 Thieving), or as drops from young implings and scavenger beasts. They can also be purchased from Martin Thwait, though this requires level 50 Thieving and Agility, or level 99 Thieving.

label: Locks
title: Locks
lead: Locks are a potential reward from unlocking chests in the Shades of Mort'ton minigame. They are brought to Dampe along with a broken coffin to create their corresponding wearable coffins.

label: Log balance (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course)
title: Log balance (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course)
lead: The log balance is an Agility obstacle found within the Barbarian Outpost Agility Course. Passing the obstacle requires 35 Agility and will award 13.7 Agility experience.

label: Log balance (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
title: Log balance (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
lead:
The log balance is an Agility obstacle found within the Brimhaven Agility Arena. Failing to cross will cause the player to fall and take damage; they will need to go up a nearby climbing rope to get back onto the course.

The amount of damage dealt by the fall is based on the player's current health, according to the formula below.

label: Log balance (Coal Trucks)
title: Log balance (Coal Trucks)
lead: The log balance is an Agility shortcut found near the coal trucks west of Seers' Village. Crossing requires 20 Agility and will grant 8.5 Agility experience. Crossing the log is an easy task for the Kandarin diary.

label: Log balance (Gnome Stronghold Agility Course)
title: Log balance (Gnome Stronghold Agility Course)
lead: The log balance is an Agility obstacle found within the Gnome Stronghold Agility Course. An Agility level of one is required to pass the obstacle, which will then grant the player 10 Agility experience. It is not possible to fail this obstacle.

label: Log balance (Wilderness Agility Course)
title: Log balance (Wilderness Agility Course)
lead:
The log balance is an Agility obstacle found within the Wilderness Agility Course. Passing the obstacle grants 20 Agility experience, and failing it causes the player to fall into the dungeon below and take damage based on their current health, according to the expression below.

\left\lfloor\text{Hitpoints}\times\frac{3}{20}\right\rfloor + 1

label: Log pile
title: Log pile
lead: Log piles are examinable scenery.

label: Log raft (Waterfall Dungeon)
title: Log raft (Waterfall Dungeon)
lead: Log raft is a small raft found above the Baxtorian Falls behind Almera's house. It is involved in the Waterfall Quest, during which it must be boarded in order to access the Waterfall Dungeon. Boarding the raft will bring the player to a small island to the south near a broken log raft and prints the message "You board the small raft and push off down stream..." followed by "...you crash into a small island.".

label: Logout button
title: Logout button
lead:
The Logout tab is used to end a session of Old School RuneScape, safely removing the player from the world.

Depending on the configured layout, the tab is accessed via a button on either the bottom-right, top-left, or top-right corner. The button resembles a small door or an X, depending on the layout. Once the logout tab is open, the player must click the red button reading "Click here to logout".

label: Logs
title: Logs
lead:
Logs, also called normal logs, are obtained from cutting regular, evergreen, jungle, dying and dead trees, and uncommonly from infected roots. Players can burn these logs using the Firemaking skill. Cutting the logs gives 25 Woodcutting experience, and burning them gives 40 Firemaking experience. These logs have no requirement to be cut or burnt.

Members training Construction can bring logs to a sawmill to make planks at a cost of 100 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes.

label: Logs (bronze axe)
title: Logs (bronze axe)
lead: Logs with a bronze axe on them can be found at various popular Woodcutting locations across Gielinor. Players can take the axe from the logs to obtain it, provided they do not currently have one equipped or in their inventory, or any other item with the "Axe" attack type, such as the zombie axe. Multiple axes can be obtained through the use of drop tricking. The bronze axe respawns on the logs after 30 seconds.

label: Logs (Tutorial Island)
title: Logs (Tutorial Island)
lead:
Logs are a unique variant of logs that can only be obtained on Tutorial Island. They are obtained by cutting down a Tutorial Island tree. The Survival Expert teaches the player how to cut down the trees using a bronze axe; they must obtain some logs and burn them in order to 
proceed to the next part of the tutorial.

A second variant of the logs can be obtained from the alternate Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.

label: Lollk
title: Lollk
lead: Lollk is a young dwarf, son of Gilob. He is in the Goblin Cave south-east of the Fishing Guild, north of East Ardougne. He is involved in the Dwarf Cannon quest. To find him, take the centre path when first entering the cave, and head to the north-western most room of the cave. He will be in one of the crates in the north-eastern part of this room.

label: Long branched tree
title: Long branched tree
lead:
Long branched trees are found at the Ogre island west of Yanille, and on the western shore of Brimhaven.

Near Yanille, one long branched tree supports the ropeswing from the ogre island back to the mainland. Another tree has a branch that a rope can be used on to swing across to the island, although the rope is lost in the process.

label: Long Way Home
title: Long Way Home
lead:
Long Way Home is a music track that can be unlocked outside Falador city walls, at the Falador Farm, Crafting Guild, and the Dark Wizards' Tower. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Miles Away and Nightfall.

In Classic mode, the track plays in Rimmington.

label: Longbow
title: Longbow
lead:
The basic longbow is a bow made from regular logs. It can be equipped at any Ranged level and can fire arrows up to iron. It has a longer range than its shortbow counterpart, but fires at a slower speed.

A longbow can be made at level 10 Fletching by using a knife on some logs to create a longbow (u), granting 10 experience, and then using a bowstring on the unstrung bow, granting another 10 experience.

label: Longbow (u)
title: Longbow (u)
lead: A longbow (u) is made using a knife with logs, requiring 10 Fletching and yielding 10 Fletching experience. Stringing a longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a longbow, also requiring 10 Fletching and yielding an additional 10 Fletching experience.

label: longbow (weapon)
title: longbow (weapon)
lead: Longbows can fire arrows at targets from a further distance than shortbows can, but they fire at a slower rate. They have exactly the same stats as the shortbow, but cost more due to their greater attack range of 10. They are not used often due to their slow speed, but are sometimes used to snipe enemies from a far distance. It is commonly used by archers who need to snipe their enemies (e.g. sniping a lesser demon while camping behind a barricade far away) and can hit up to ten squares away.

label: longsword
title: longsword
lead:
Longswords are medium-speed slashing weapons used in melee combat. While they have a slower attack speed than scimitars, longswords are able to hit higher in a single attack. Many players prefer them to two-handed swords both because a shield can be equipped with a longsword, and because longswords have a faster attack speed. Scimitars, however, have been proven to deal more damage over the course of fights due to having higher attack speeds than longswords. Like all slashing weapons, longswords are good against cloth and leather armour.

The katana is two-handed, unlike other longswords which are one-handed.

label: loop half of key
title: loop half of key
lead:
The loop half of key is an item dropped by any monster that has access to the gem drop table or the rare drop table. It is also a reward from various random events, the gnome restaurant, from Managing Miscellania, caskets, looting magpie implings, and unlocking the crystal chest in Taverley. It can also be found in the Barrows chest as a separate item if the player has 100% rewards potential.

The loop half of a key is used with a tooth half of key to make a crystal key, which is used to unlock the crystal chest, which contains a dragonstone and an assortment of other items.

label: Loose Mud
title: Loose Mud
lead: Loose Mud is located under Gnocci the Cook's hut and in the south-east prison cell of the Underground Pass. It plays a role in the Underground Pass quest where players can either use a spade on it or dig near it, but Loose Mud itself has no right-click interact options.

title: Loose Railing (Combat Training Camp)
lead: Loose Railing can be found within the Combat Training Camp. Players can squeeze-through the railing to enter and exit the ogre enclosure. This is particularly useful to collect drops and spent ammunition.

label: Loose Railing (McGrubor's Wood)
title: Loose Railing (McGrubor's Wood)
lead: The loose railing is a piece of scenery used to enter McGrubor's Wood. The railing and the nearby fairy ring (code ) are the only ways to enter the wood, as the player is prevented from opening the front gates by the Forester.
