label: Lord Arceuus I
title: Lord Arceuus I
lead: Lord Arceuus I was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 5th decade. He is responsible for ordering the creation of the Arceuus Library to preserve the history of Great Kourend.

label: Lord Arceuus II
title: Lord Arceuus II
lead: Lord Arceuus II was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 10th decade.

label: Lord Bourath Arceuus
title: Lord Bourath Arceuus
lead: Lord Bourath Arceuus was the leader of the Arceuus House at the time of the signing of the royal accord of twill and advised it's creation.

label: Lord Dalton Piscarilius
title: Lord Dalton Piscarilius
lead:
Lord Dalton Piscarilius was the leader of Piscarilius until his death during a fishing trip. His only daughter, Lady Shauna Piscarilius, succeeded him as leader of Piscarilius.

Lady Shauna describes him as a man only interested in his own wealth, ignorant of the struggles of his own people.

label: Lord Daquarius
title: Lord Daquarius
lead:
Lord Daquarius Rennard is the current lord of the Kinshra, also known as the Black Knights. Daquarius is held in high regard by ally and enemy alike, and is generally seen as a fair and noble leader.

He was unanimously elected Lord of the Kinshra after the death of his predecessor Lord Shadwell, becoming the youngest to ever gain leadership. Since then, he has been involved in many Kinshra affairs, several of which involved attempts to conquer Falador.

label: Lord Ethrain Hosidius I
title: Lord Ethrain Hosidius I
lead:
Lord Ethrain Hosidius I was the first Grand Lord of Great Kourend after the signing of the Royal Accord of Twill, succeeding the Council of Elders and reigning for the 1st decade.

During the Council of Elder's reign, a famine struck Great Kourend. Five years into the famine, Lord Hosidius met with the lords of the other four families, coming to an agreement that half the land of each would be granted to Hosidius in order to grow more crops to extricate the kingdom from famine. The next day he would send a letter to the Council of Elders pleading for this request to be granted. The council granted his request, and the famine ended sometime after.

label: Lord Handelmort
title: Lord Handelmort
lead:
Lord Francis Kurt Handelmort is the wealthiest man in Ardougne and plays a background role in the Tribal Totem quest.

Although unseen in-game, he possesses great wealth, which is evident from his booby-trapped two-story mansion coupled with aggressive guard dogs, as well as a butler and gardener in his service.

label: Lord Hosidius
title: Lord Hosidius
lead:
Lord Hosidius may refer to:

*Lord Kandur Hosidius, Lord of Hosidius before A Kingdom Divided
*Pandur Hosidius, Lord of Hosidius after A Kingdom Divided
*Lord Ethrain Hosidius I
*Lord Hosidius II
*Lord Hosidius III

label: Lord Hosidius II
title: Lord Hosidius II
lead: Lord Hosidius II was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 6th decade.

label: Lord Hosidius III
title: Lord Hosidius III
lead: Lord Hosidius III was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 11th decade.

label: Lord Lovakengj
title: Lord Lovakengj
lead:
Lord Lovakengj may refer to:
*Lord Solange Lovakengj
*Lord Lovakengj I
*Lord Lovakengj II
*Lord Lovakengj III

label: Lord Lovakengj I
title: Lord Lovakengj I
lead: Lord Lovakengj I was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 2nd decade.

label: Lord Lovakengj II
title: Lord Lovakengj II
lead: Lord Lovakengj II was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 7th decade.

label: Lord Lovakengj III
title: Lord Lovakengj III
lead: Lord Lovakengj III was the last Grand Lord of Great Kourend, reigning for the duration of the 12th decade. He was also the last to follow the Royal Accord of Twill, as King Shayzien III breached the accord, seizing control of Kourend with the military under his command.

label: Lord of the Kinshra
title: Lord of the Kinshra
lead:
Lord of the Kinshra is a title granted to the leader of the Kinshra, a Zamorakian knightly order based around Asgarnia. Kinshra lords are, in theory, elected by the order, although in the past some have risen to power through tolerated violence.

The first Kinshra lords were likely those that established the order near the end of the Fourth Age, prior to the founding of Asgarnia. After helping King Raddallin and the White Knights to establish Asgarnia and its capital, Falador, Kinshra lords held considerable political weight within the nation.

label: Lord Piscarilius
title: Lord Piscarilius
lead:
Lord Piscarilius may refer to:
*Lord Dalton Piscarilius
*Lord Ret Piscarilius
*Lord Piscarilius I
*Lord Piscarilius II

label: Lord Piscarilius I
title: Lord Piscarilius I
lead: Lord Piscarilius I was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 4th decade.

label: Lord Piscarilius II
title: Lord Piscarilius II
lead: Lord Piscarilius II was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 9th decade.

label: Lord Ret Piscarilius
title: Lord Ret Piscarilius
lead: Lord Ret Piscarilius was the leader of the Piscarilius House at the time of the signing of the royal accord of twill and advised it's creation.

label: Lord Rologray
title: Lord Rologray
lead: Lord Rologray, 12th Lord of the North Coast, is the former owner and one of the former occupants of Fenkenstrain's Castle. Not much is known about him, apart from his final resting place, the Mausoleum.

label: Lord Rolomere
title: Lord Rolomere
lead: Lord Rolomere, 14th Lord of the North Coast, is the former owner and one of the former occupants of Fenkenstrain's Castle, before Lord Rologarth. Not much is known about him, apart from him being the son of Lord Rolovanne and that his final resting place is the Mausoleum.

label: Lord Rolovanne
title: Lord Rolovanne
lead: Lord Rolovanne, 13th Lord of the North Coast, is the former owner and one of the former occupants of Fenkenstrain's Castle, before Lord Rolomere. Not much is known about him, apart from him being the son of Lord Rologray and his final resting place, the Mausoleum.

label: Lord Seabry Shayzien
title: Lord Seabry Shayzien
lead: Lord Seabry Shayzien was the leader of the Shayzien House at the time of the signing of the royal accord of twill and advised its creation.

label: Lord Shadwell
title: Lord Shadwell
lead: Lord Shadwell was a former Lord of the Kinshra who died during the Edgeville Incident. According to the Temple Knights, he was an extreme Zamorakian fanatic.

label: Lord Shayzien
title: Lord Shayzien
lead:
Lord Shayzien may refer to:
*Lord Shiro Shayzien, the current leader of Shayzien
*Lord Seabry Shayzien
*Lord Shayzien I
*Lord Shayzien II

label: Lord Shayzien I
title: Lord Shayzien I
lead: Lord Shayzien I was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 3rd decade.

label: Lord Shayzien II
title: Lord Shayzien II
lead: Lord Shayzien II was the Grand Lord of Great Kourend for the duration of the 8th decade.

label: Lord Sinclair
title: Lord Sinclair
lead:
Lord Sinclair was a wealthy noble of Kandarin. He was a good friend of King Ulthas and did many good works for the people of the kingdom. Lord Sinclair and his children lived in a large castle to the east of Seers' Village. His children were spoiled by his wealth and considered themselves even more important than the king.

In the year 132 of the Fifth Age, King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table came to Gielinor from another world. Once there, they realised they were in need of a castle. King Ulthas, the king of Kandarin at the time, met with Lord Sinclair and discussed King Arthur's plight. Sinclair decided that he would give his castle to King Arthur, and King Ulthas built the Sinclairs a large mansion in the north, near the southern border of the Fremennik Province, where they could relocate. King Arthur, meanwhile, renamed the castle to Camelot.

label: Lord Solange Lovakengj
title: Lord Solange Lovakengj
lead: Lord Solange Lovakengj was the leader of the Lovakengj House at the time of the signing of the royal accord of twill and advised its creation.

label: Lordship of the North Coast
title: Lordship of the North Coast
lead: The Lordship of the North Coast was a small independent fief on Morytania's northern coastline founded by Misthalanian humans, presumably at some point in the Fourth Age. These founders may have been part of the settlers from Misthalin who arrived in Morytania in 1777, and decided to set up an independent kingdom where they could worship their chosen god in peace. It was ruled by a line of hereditary Lords, the last of which was Lord Rologarth, who was betrayed by Dr Fenkenstrain at an undetermined time.

label: Lores and Histories
title: Lores and Histories
lead:
Lores and Histories is a compilation of tomes kept by Reldo, the Royal Librarian of Varrock. The lores are all restored tomes that tell the story of Gielinor's past, whether it be through folklore or the diary of an adventurer.

Some of these are verified to accurately express histories of RuneScape, while others are mythologies related to true people and events in which the accuracy is not guaranteed. The Lores and Histories formerly also included the Tales from the Tavern but these were removed some time prior to 2 April 2007 and replaced by the Postbag from the Hedge and other player-submitted writings.

label: Losanium
title: Losanium
lead:
Losanium is the term that refers to the religion of the Kingdom of Varlamore. It encompasses both the worship of Ralos and Ranul though the term itself is uncommonly used due to the rarity of individuals who equally dedicate themselves to both. Losanium is the most common religion across Varlamore, and worship of other gods is hardly seen.

The religion originated with the Talkasti people, one of two groups that eventually came together to form the modern kingdom of Varlamore (along with the Pericans). The Talkasti first worshipped Ralos and Ranul in secret within Kourend, before migrating to Varlamore in order to practice their religion more freely. Eventually, the Pericans began to practice Losanium as well.

label: Lost
title: Lost
lead:
Lost may refer to:

; Quests:
*Lost City
*The Lost Tribe

label: Lost casket
title: Lost casket
lead:
Lost caskets are a type of ocean encounter. There is one lost casket for each tier of treasure trails. When retrieving a lost casket, the loot table of the respective clue tier is rolled one time. The message You find some treasure! displays, and a small amount of Sailing experience is awarded.

They require the same Sailing levels as the clue turtles in order to retrieve. If you do not have the required Sailing level, you will see the message "You're not sure what to do with those goods. You should ask the Captain for help."

label: Lost City
title: Lost City
lead: Lost City is a quest about the fairy land Zanaris. A group of adventurers have set up camp in Lumbridge Swamp, claiming to be searching for the mystical lost city. You must find the truth of this claim, and gain entrance to the moon of Gielinor, Zanaris.

label: Lost crate
title: Lost crate
lead:
Lost crates or lost shipments are ocean encounters found in the water while sailing. The Pandemonium quest must be completed before crates will appear in the ocean. Opening a crate awards an item and a small amount of Sailing experience.

There are multiple tiers of crates with increasingly valuable loot. Each crate has a chance to spawn after reaching a minimum Sailing level; for example, at level 5, only wooden crates can spawn, but all tiers can spawn at level 99.

label: Lost Lover
title: Lost Lover
lead: Lost Lover is an unnamed miniquest not shown in the quest list. It is started by talking to either Fabia or Xilo in the Tlati Rainforest. There are no rewards for completing the miniquest.

label: Lost schematics
title: Lost schematics
lead:
Lost schematics are unique items that unlock recipes for high-level shipbuilding parts, for use in the Sailing skill. There are a total of 11 schematics, 10 of which have lockboxes that contain them, and 10 corresponding small keys that unlock them. The other one is given by Ava after the completion of Animal Magnetism and Pandemonium quests.

Each lockbox gives a lockbox direction which gives a clue to the whereabouts of its key. Keys can be obtained by digging with a spade at the correct location to obtain them.

label: Louie Legs
title: Louie Legs
lead: Louie Legs is a shopkeeper who owns Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar located in the south-eastern corner of Al Kharid. Louie sells platelegs from bronze to adamant in his shop. If you bring him one acorn and one set of bones, he will give you the corrupted platelegs and skirt.

label: Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar.
title: Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar.
lead: Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar is a shop in Al Kharid which sells various platelegs. It is run by Louie Legs.

label: Louisa
title: Louisa
lead: Louisa is the cook to the Sinclair family. She is a witness during King's Ransom.

label: Lovakengj Minecart Network
title: Lovakengj Minecart Network
lead:
The Lovakengj Minecart Network is a rapid transit system serving Great Kourend and some parts of the Kebos Lowlands, offering transportation to ten destinations across Great Kourend and two to the Kebos Lowlands (Farming Guild and Mount Quidamortem)

The travel services offered by the minecarts cost 20 coins per ride. Upon completion of The Forsaken Tower, the fee is waived and players can ride the carts for free permanently.

label: Lovakengj/Historical
title: Lovakengj/Historical
lead:
Earning favour with Lovakengj requires you to assist in the collecting of resources for blast mining and the creation of armour. Blast mining will allow players to get ores at an accelerated rate, but only if they choose to invest their time with Lovakengj.

To progress in the Architectural Alliance miniquest, players must gain 100% Lovakengj favour and speak to Lovada, who is found in the building just outside the blast mine.
__notoc__

label: Love story
title: Love story
lead:
Love story may refer to:

; Quests
*A Tail of Two Cats
*Romeo & Juliet
*Troll Romance

label: Low Level Alchemy
title: Low Level Alchemy
lead:
Low Level Alchemy (also known as low alch or LA) is a utility spell available in the standard spellbook. It requires level 21 Magic to cast, and grants 31 Magic experience per cast.

Casting Low Level Alchemy on an item in the player's inventory will convert that item into a number of coins equal to 40% of the item's value (not the item's Grand Exchange price).

label: Low Life
title: Low Life
lead:
Low Life is a status effect that takes effect when the player has less than 40% of their Hitpoints remaining. Currently, this only applied to the Masori armour prior to its rework, but was available to playtest during the ToA Weapons Beta and Nex Weapons Beta. While Low Life is active, the set would have increased ranged accuracy and Ranged Strength, and would remain so long as the player stayed under 40% of their health.

The Masori amulet, which was only available during the aforementioned betas and later scrapped, would damage players 15% of their health every three ticks (1.8 seconds) until they were under 40% of their health, where the Low Life effect can take effect.

label: Low wall
title: Low wall
lead:
Low wall may refer to:

* Low wall (Agility Pyramid), Agility obstacle found within the Agility Pyramid
* Low wall (Brimhaven Agility Arena), Agility obstacle found within the Brimhaven Agility Arena
* Low wall (Temple of Light), obstacle found within the Temple of Light

label: Low wall (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
title: Low wall (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
lead: The low wall is an Agility obstacle found within the Brimhaven Agility Arena. It is possible to fail this obstacle at very low Agility levels, although no damage is dealt as the player stumbles back to the starting square.

label: Low-defence pure
title: Low-defence pure
lead: Low-defence pure is a type of PvP build that resemble the usual 1 defence build but sacrifices combat levels by gaining defence for certain unlocks.

label: Low-level plant (interface item)
title: Low-level plant (interface item)
lead:
The Low-level plant is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Plant.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Lowe
title: Lowe
lead:
Lowe is the owner of Lowe's Archery Emporium, found in Varrock just east of the general store. He sells ranging equipment including bronze through adamant arrows, bronze bolts, crossbows, and a variety of shortbows and longbows. The higher level equipment there is, the less there will usually be in stock, since it is higher in demand.

On Deadman Mode worlds, he additionally sells Dorgeshuun crossbows, bone bolts, and bone bolt packs.

label: Lowe's Archery Emporium
title: Lowe's Archery Emporium
lead:
Lowe's Archery Emporium is located near central Varrock just east of the main square. This store is operated by Lowe.

Ironman players who intend on buying arrows here should note that the shop very frequently experiences a shortage of arrows, due to other players purchasing them in large amounts. In Deadman mode it also sells bone bolts, and Dorgeshuun crossbow.

label: Lozar
title: Lozar
lead:
Lozar was one of three wizard survivors of the Crandor Island tragedy - the others being Thalzar and Melzar. Each of them took a piece of a map of Crandor to prevent anyone from journeying to the perilous island that was burned down by Elvarg, the Dragon of Crandor. In the year 169, however, Lozar was killed by goblins, who looted her possessions.

It is confirmed during the Dragon Slayer I quest that Wormbrain, an imprisoned goblin, was in fact a member of the raiding party who killed Lozar. To get her map piece from Wormbrain, you need to do one of two things. Either beat him up and use Telekinetic Grab on the map when he's defeated, or pay him a hefty sum of 10,000 gold pieces.

label: Lozar's house
title: Lozar's house
lead:
Lozar's house, also known as the Goblin house, is a small house in Lumbridge found across the river from The Sheared Ram and south of the Groats' farm.

Recently goblins raided the house, killing Lozar, the house's previous inhabitant . The dead trees surrounding the house, the charred bones inside, and the colour of the ground outside the house suggest that the goblins set the place on fire. The goblins have since taken up residence in the house.

label: Lucien
title: Lucien
lead:
Lucien is a Mahjarrat and a powerful mage and necromancer. He sided with Zamorak in his rebellion against Zaros.

Speaking with Lucien starts the Temple of Ikov quest, and he gives you the pendant of lucien needed in the quest. During the quest, the player is tasked with stealing the Staff of Armadyl from the Temple of Ikov. However, the player is later given the choice to side with the Guardians of Armadyl or continuing aiding Lucien.

label: Lucinda Raispher
title: Lucinda Raispher
lead: Lucinda Raispher was a former Varrockian belonging to the Raispher family, descending from the Elders of Avarrocka. She was the last blood descendant of Dathero Raispher within the family. She married into the Fitzharmon family.

label: Luck
title: Luck
lead: Luck may refer to:

label: Lucky Win (Death Plateau)
title: Lucky Win (Death Plateau)
lead:
Lucky Win (Death Plateau) is a Jingle that plays when:
* Winning a dice gamble with Harold during Death Plateau.
* Leveling up Sailing during the 2014 April Fools event.

label: Lucy
title: Lucy
lead:
Lucy is a barmaid and employee of the Falador Party Room, a large venue in the north-eastern part of Falador. When spoken to, she will serve the player beer.

Like all employees of the Party Room, she wears a red partyhat.

label: Luke's Reef
title: Luke's Reef
lead:
Luke's Reef is a large coral reef in the Eastern Ocean. Luke's Reef is unexplored, but is apparently composed mainly of a very spiky species of coral.

The reef is entirely submerged beneath the water, and is apparently low enough that even a large ship can pass over it without damage; this can be seen in that the zombie pirate ship The Inebriated passed over it without any negative side effects.

label: Lullaby
title: Lullaby
lead:
Lullaby is a music track that is unlocked on the path to Rellekka and in the Digsite. In the Digsite area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track and Venture.

In Classic mode, the area around the Digsite where it can be unlocked is reduced to just the northern half of the Digsite. This track will also play on the path to Rellekka in Classic mode.

label: Lumber order
title: Lumber order
lead:
The lumber order is a quest item that is part of The Grand Tree quest.

It is an order from Glough, who intends to build up a gnome army to wipe out humans. Players obtain it from a foreman in the Karamja ship yard, either by talking to him or killing him.

label: Lumber Yard
title: Lumber Yard
lead:
The Lumber Yard is a location north-east of Varrock. It is only accessible to members. Its main feature is the Sawmill operator, who is located in a small room along the yard's south-west wall. He is involved in the Construction skill: he can turn logs into planks for a fee, and he also sells bolts of cloth, three kinds of nails, and saws.

Players can get here the quickest by using the Lumberyard teleport scroll. They can also take the balloon transport system or teleport to the Earth Altar with the ring of the elements to end up right below the Lumber Yard. Alternatively, they can use the digsite pendant to get close by, or simply walk from Varrock.

label: Lumberjack (disambiguation)
title: Lumberjack (disambiguation)
lead:
Lumberjack may refer to:

* Lumberjack outfit, including:
** Lumberjack boots
** Lumberjack top
** Lumberjack hat
** Lumberjack legs
* Lumberjack (Raging Echoes League), a relic from Raging Echoes League
* Lumberjack, a relic from Grid Master
* Lumberjack Leif from Managing Miscellania

label: lumberjack outfit
title: lumberjack outfit
lead:
The lumberjack outfit is an experience-boosting clothing set that grants additional experience when worn whilst Woodcutting. Equipping any piece of the outfit requires 44 Woodcutting.

Each piece equipped increases Woodcutting experience by 0.2–0.8% depending on the piece; wearing the complete set grants an additional set bonus of 0.5%, resulting in a total of 2.5% for the entire set. This stacks with the bonus 10% experience when cutting maples from the Kandarin Diary medium reward, as well as the bonus 10% experience when using a felling axe with Forester's rations in the player's Forestry kit. Pieces of the Forestry outfit will act as lumberjack pieces to obtain the set bonus.

label: Lumbridge
title: Lumbridge
lead:
Lumbridge is a large town where players begin their Old School RuneScape journey. New players are sent here from Tutorial Island to further learn the game from various tutors across the town. Lumbridge gets its name from the bridge that crosses the River Lum.

After a player's death, Lumbridge is the player's default respawn point, although players can change their respawn location to other locations. The main point of interest of Lumbridge is the Lumbridge Castle, where players can start several quests and access its bank at the top floor.

label: Lumbridge cabbage patch
title: Lumbridge cabbage patch
lead: The Lumbridge Cabbage Patch was a small fenced area directly north of Lumbridge which contained cabbages. It was replaced by a pasture containing cows with the release of permanent free-to-play on 19 February 2015 to accommodate for the influx of new free-to-play players.

label: Lumbridge Castle
title: Lumbridge Castle
lead:
Lumbridge Castle is a large castle located in Lumbridge and home of Duke Horacio. The courtyard enclosed by the outer walls features two decorative fountains and two statues, one of an ancient king and one of an ancient hero. A short flight of three steps joins this to the castle's front entrance. Another entrance is behind the castle.

The Lumbridge Home Teleport and Lumbridge Teleport spells take players to the courtyard of the castle.

label: Lumbridge Church
title: Lumbridge Church
lead:
The Lumbridge church, referred to in-game as the Church of Holy Saradomin by Father Aereck, is the official church of Lumbridge. The church is the starting place for the Restless Ghost quest, and also contains the Prayer tutor. There's a playable organ behind the altar.

According to Father Aereck, the church was built over 230 years ago.

label: Lumbridge cow field
title: Lumbridge cow field
lead:
The Lumbridge cow field is a field containing level 2 cows and cow calves. Located in the north-east of Lumbridge, the field is managed by Gillie Groats, and is part of the larger Groats' farm. Also present are dairy cows, which can be milked if you have a bucket in your inventory. This is a good place to train either Magic or Ranged at a low combat level due to the fact that you can safely kill them from the other side of the fence, and run in to loot between kills. There are 2 cow fields in Lumbridge: north of the windmill and east of the town.

This field is a very popular training spot for low levels of both free players and members because of the 100% cowhide drop, as well as raw beef and bones to train Cooking and Prayer with respectively. It is also an extremely good place to train Prayer and Cooking as bones and beef are often left in the rush to collect cow hides. This is also the closest cow field to a bank as well as a Tanner in Al Kharid, which also makes it crowded.

label: Lumbridge Eagles
title: Lumbridge Eagles
lead: The Lumbridge Eagles are a football team favoured by Saradomin, according to Zamorak in the God letters.

label: Lumbridge General Store
title: Lumbridge General Store
lead:
The Lumbridge General Store is the general store located north of the Lumbridge Castle in Lumbridge. When new players arrive in Old School RuneScape, they start in Lumbridge and tend to have a look around, and thus the store is a popular place for new players.

Players can spectate teams attempting the Theatre of Blood raid by speaking to Abigaila upstairs.

label: Lumbridge Graveyard
title: Lumbridge Graveyard
lead:
The Lumbridge Graveyard is located in the south-eastern portion of Lumbridge behind the Lumbridge Church. The graveyard contains various gravestones as well as a mausoleum housing the coffin of the restless ghost. During the The Restless Ghost quest, players must speak with the restless ghost inside the mausoleum. The graveyard also features Nigel and Count Check, as well as an entrance to Death's Office.

A yew tree is located in the north-eastern corner of the graveyard.

label: Lumbridge mine
title: Lumbridge mine
lead:
Lumbridge mine may refer to:

*East Lumbridge Swamp mine, the mine south-east of Lumbridge
*West Lumbridge Swamp mine, the mine south-west of Lumbridge
*Dorgesh-Kaan mine, the cave goblin mine underneath Lumbridge

label: Lumbridge pasture
title: Lumbridge pasture
lead: The Lumbridge pasture is a large cow field in Lumbridge, north of Fred's farm and bordering the River Lum. Players can find a dairy cow, cow calves, cows, and a level 7 farmer. The only way to enter the pasture is through a gate on the southern side.

label: Lumbridge pond
title: Lumbridge pond
lead: The Lumbridge pond is a small body of water found amongst the farms of Lumbridge and Draynor. The pond features two ducks and two ducklings, all of whom are attackable, as well as two more ducks outside of the pond that can only be examined.

label: Lumbridge Swamp
title: Lumbridge Swamp
lead:
The Lumbridge Swamp is located south of Lumbridge and is east of Draynor Village. It can be accessed via a small gateway at the back of the graveyard behind Lumbridge Church. You can also access it via an entry south-east of Draynor Village, or you can swing across an Agility shortcut from Al Kharid. Zandar Horfyre will also teleport the player here, away from the Dark Wizards' Tower, if they refuse to leave when going through his dialogue. It is also possible to get to the Lumbridge swamp by using a ring of the elements to teleport to the water altar, or alternatively by travelling to the altar through the Abyss and exiting the portal.

There are several fishing spots on the east end of the swamps that are ideal for novice anglers. There are two mining sites in the swamps.

label: Lumbridge Teleport
title: Lumbridge Teleport
lead:
Lumbridge Teleport teleports the caster to Lumbridge. Unlike the free Lumbridge Home Teleport spell, this is fast and cannot be interrupted by combat, though like most other teleports, it is unusable above level 20 Wilderness or when the player is teleblocked. Players returning to Lumbridge may save runes by using the free teleport instead, if they are not in danger.

Casting this spell is a requirement for the medium Lumbridge & Draynor diary.

label: lump of crystal
title: lump of crystal
lead:
The lump of crystal is a quest item used during the Legends' Quest. It is obtained by defeating Ranalph Devere in the Viyeldi caves beneath the Kharazi Jungle. When combined with the chunk of crystal and the hunk of crystal (obtained by defeating the other two warriors) at the furnace, they form the heart crystal required to unlock a door that leads further into the caves.

It is not possible to obtain the heart fragments after completing the quest; killing the knights again does not provide the player with the fragments. However, duplicate parts of the crystal can be obtained during the quest by utilising the drop trick. If the player does this, they are able to create another (albeit useless) heart crystal after completing the quest.

label: Lunar
title: Lunar
lead:
Lunar can refer to:

*Lunar Isle, an island located in the northern sea
*Lunar spells, a magic spellbook of mostly non-combat spells
*Lunar Diplomacy, a quest which takes place on Lunar Isle
*Lunar equipment, armour made during Lunar Diplomacy
*Stalagmites (Lunar Isle), also known as Lunar rock, an ore-containing rock only found on Lunar Isle which is used during Lunar Diplomacy
*Lunar ore, a material mined from lunar rocks
*Lunar bar, the refined form of lunar ore
*Lunar chest, the chest looted after killing the Moons of Peril

label: Lunar alphabet
title: Lunar alphabet
lead:
The Lunar alphabet is an alphabet consisting of 26 letters used on Zanaris and Lunar Isle, each of which is equivelant to a letter of the . It does not appear to be in common use, as most of the residents of Zanaris do not recognise it, comparing its letters to doodles or Rorschach ink-blots. Those who do recognise the alphabet are only familiar with it from its use on the rune temple sign outside the mysterious ruins leading to the Cosmic Altar.

During Fairytale II - Cure a Queen, Fairy Nuff writes a hidden message to the player in this alphabet on the back of her certificate after her house is ransacked by the Fairy Godfather. Players can decode it by comparing the message on the sign outside the cosmic altar, which reads "COSMIC RUNE ALTAR".

label: Lunar altar (interface item)
title: Lunar altar (interface item)
lead:
The Lunar altar is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Lunar altar.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Lunar equipment
title: Lunar equipment
lead:
Lunar equipment is the ceremonial attire of the Moon Clan, is made by players during the Lunar Diplomacy quest, and may be kept afterwards. All armour and jewellery pieces of the set require 65 Magic and 40 Defence to wear, and the staff requires 65 Magic to wield. After completion of the quest, the pieces of Lunar equipment may be bought from the Oneiromancer on Lunar Isle. Players may not make the items themselves after the quest is complete; they must buy the items if they lose them.

While Lunar armour has lesser magic bonuses compared to other magical armour of a similar level, it is marginally more defensive compared to other magic armours that usually have few to no melee defences. Because of this, it can be considered a crude hybrid between melee armour and magic armour. However, ranged attacks may still cripple the wearer due to the armour's virtually nonexistent ranged defence.

label: Lunar globe (interface item)
title: Lunar globe (interface item)
lead:
The Lunar globe is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Lunar globe.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Lunar spellbook
title: Lunar spellbook
lead:
The Lunar spellbook is a spellbook that players can access upon completion of the quest Lunar Diplomacy, associated with the magicks of the Moon Clan. Making extensive use of astral runes, the spellbook is primarily oriented towards utility spells and combat-support spells, reducing or eliminating the need for certain items and equipment to carry out certain tasks. A larger set of spells is accessible to players who have completed the quest Dream Mentor and two additional spells are available for completing the Hard Fremennik Diary.

The spells in this spellbook use all rune types except wrath.

label: Lunchbox
title: Lunchbox
lead:
Lunchboxes were items intended to release with the Tower of Life quest, presumably as a reward from the post-quest Creature Creation minigame. They were removed before release, with satchels and the tea flask being the rewards from Creature Creation instead. Despite this, models for the lunchboxes were left in the game files.

Like satchels, lunchboxes would have been equipable in the shield slot, and would likely have had the same ability to store food inside, as the code used to implement the satchels refer to lunchboxes in their variable prefixes.

label: Lundail
title: Lundail
lead:
Lundail sells runes in his store Lundail's Arena-side Rune Shop in the Mage Arena bank, beneath the Mage Arena in a safe area of the Wilderness. He sells air, water, fire, earth, body, mind, nature, chaos, law, cosmic, and death runes.

After completing the easy Wilderness Diary, players can claim-runes from him to receive one type of catalytic rune, selected randomly from the seven kinds he sells. The number of runes increases according to the tier of Wilderness Diary completed:

label: Lundail's Arena-side Rune Shop.
title: Lundail's Arena-side Rune Shop.
lead:
Lundail's Arena-side Rune Shop, owned by Lundail, is located in the Mage Arena bank dungeon. To enter the dungeon, players must traverse the deep Wilderness and pull the teleportation lever. Although this Mage Arena is located in the Wilderness, this area is a safe zone. Be sure to bring a knife or slash weapon in order to slash the webs blocking the lever.

The store sells different kinds of runes. This is a good place to restock runes if you run out when playing the Mage Arena minigame. This store is very popular for ironman accounts as this shop is one of the few Magic shops that sells law runes and cosmic runes, and the only one accessible with no requirements. The other stores are Magic Guild Store (Runes and Staves), Baba Yaga's Magic Shop, and Ali Morrisane's Catalytic Rune Shop.

label: Lunderwin
title: Lunderwin
lead:
Lunderwin is a fairy found near Irksol, who buys cabbages (both the normal and Draynor Manor variant) from the player for 100 coins each. The cabbages cannot be noted. This is not a recommended way for players to make money as it will come at a low profit due to the entrance fee of one diamond to enter the marketplace.

If a player took one diamond and 27 cabbages they could enter the marketplace and sell all of the cabbages to Lunderwin for a profit of .

label: Luthas
title: Luthas
lead:
Luthas is the banana plantation owner on Karamja who plays a small role in the Pirate's Treasure quest. He can be found in his living quarters next to the plantation.

Luthas will pay 30 coins to players that fill a crate with 10 bananas. The trip back to Port Sarim costs 30 coins, so if a player is out of money they can fill up a crate. During the Pirate's Treasure quest, players must put a bottle of Karamjan rum in the banana crate to be shipped over to mainland. Luthas carries a monkey on his back all the time.

label: Lvl-1 Enchant
title: Lvl-1 Enchant
lead:
Lvl-1 Enchant is a utility spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 7 Magic to cast and granting 17.5 experience. The spell enchants sapphire and opal items, primarily jewellery.

This spell can be transferred to a magic tablet by bringing the required runes and a piece of soft clay to a lectern in the study of a player-owned house, granting the same experience as casting the spell.

label: Lvl-2 Enchant
title: Lvl-2 Enchant
lead:
Lvl-2 Enchant is a utility spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 27 Magic to cast. The spell enchants emerald and jade items, primarily jewellery, granting 37 Magic experience when doing so.

This spell can be transferred to a magic tablet by bringing the required runes and a piece of soft clay to a lectern in the study of a player-owned house, granting the same experience as casting the spell.

label: Lvl-3 Enchant
title: Lvl-3 Enchant
lead:
Lvl-3 Enchant is a utility spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 49 Magic to cast. The spell enchants ruby and red topaz items, primarily jewellery, granting 59 Magic experience when doing so.

This spell can be transferred to a magic tablet by bringing the required runes and a piece of soft clay to a lectern in the study of a player-owned house, granting 44.3 Magic experience.

label: Lvl-4 Enchant
title: Lvl-4 Enchant
lead:
Lvl-4 Enchant is a utility spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 57 Magic to cast. The spell enchants diamond jewellery, granting 67 Magic experience when doing so.

This spell can be transferred to a magic tablet by bringing the required runes and a piece of soft clay to a lectern in the study of a player-owned house, granting the same experience as casting the spell.

label: Lvl-5 Enchant
title: Lvl-5 Enchant
lead:
Lvl-5 Enchant is a utility spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 68 Magic to cast. The spell enchants dragonstone jewellery, granting 78 Magic experience when doing so.

This spell can be transferred to a magic tablet by bringing the required runes and a piece of soft clay to a lectern in the study of a player-owned house, granting 58.5 Magic experience.

label: Macarthur Fortune Holding
title: Macarthur Fortune Holding
lead:
Macarthur Fortune Holding LLC is a US-based global asset management firm founded by a group of investment professionals. The company has worked together with management teams and entrepreneurs in the video game, cloud computing, artificial intelligence robotics industries to create long-term sustainable growth. Macarthur Fortune's investments span the full range of opportunities including venture capital, private equity, merger and acquisition and public companies.

It was announced on April 28th 2020 that Macarthur Fortune Holding's private managed fund, Platinum Fortune LP, had acquired a 100% stake in Jagex for $530 million USD from Fukong Interactive Entertainment. Platinum Fortune LP has a focus on the global video game market, and targets global video game companies and designs strategies to help them grow user base and revenue.

label: Mace
title: Mace
lead:
Maces are melee weapons, and one of the few weapons types which have Crush for a primary attack type. Some maces also have a controlled attack style, giving equal experience to Attack, Strength, and Defence.

Maces are special in that most provide a Prayer bonus, a trait rarely found in other melee weapons and entirely absent from the other metal weapons.

label: Mace shops
title: Mace shops
lead: Mace shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Mace merchants sell maces. There are 3 dedicated mace shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Machete
title: Machete
lead:
The machete is an item used in the Woodcutting skill. It can be obtained from the mainland Karamja general store and Shilo Village general store or by trading with another player. It can also be found by looking in Radimus Erkle's cupboard in the Legends' Guild; however, after the quest is complete you may no longer search the cupboard for a machete and are given the message "You don't think Radimus Erkle would be very pleased if he caught you rifling through his possessions".

The machete can be used as a weapon but is primarily used to cut Jungle during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame. It has no requirements to wield though cutting Light, Medium, and Dense jungle requires 10, 20, and 35 Woodcutting to harvest respectively. A machete is also required to gain access to Kharazi Jungle if the player doesn't have access to the level 79 agility shortcut to the south-east of Shilo Village.

label: Machete (weapon)
title: Machete (weapon)
lead:
Machetes are melee slash weapons similar to scimitars with the attack speed of longswords. They are mostly used to cut jungle in the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame, and to enter the Kharazi Jungle.

The normal machete is sold at both the Karamja general store and the Shilo Village general store. The opal, jade, and red topaz machetes are sold at Gabooty's Tai Bwo Wannai Cooperative for trading sticks or can be obtained by exchanging 3 of their respective gems, 1 gout tuber, and trading sticks with Safta Doc.

label: Machine (disambiguation)
title: Machine (disambiguation)
lead:
Machine may refer to:

* Machine (Land of the Goblins)
* Machine (Meiyerditch Laboratories)
* Machine (Varrock Museum)
* Machine (Watchtower)
* Machinery
* Machine panel
* Oaknock's Machine
* Drilling machine
* Strange machine
* Wire machine
* Barbarian Assault Machines:
** Attacker item machine
** Defender item machine
** Healer item machine

label: Machine (Watchtower)
title: Machine (Watchtower)
lead: A machine is scenery that can be found inside the Watchtower building. It is used during the Watchtower quest to activate the shield generator.

label: Mackerel
title: Mackerel
lead: Mackerel is a type of fish that restores 6 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw mackerel on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 10 Cooking and granting 60 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Mackerel is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 45, or 41 when using the Lumbridge range.

label: Mad Eadgar
title: Mad Eadgar
lead: Mad Eadgar is a music track that is unlocked in Eadgar's cave on top of Trollheim.

label: Mad skavid
title: Mad skavid
lead:
The Mad skavid is a Skavid that has become deranged, either through being worked too hard by his Ogre masters or through some torture, and is found in a cave in the heart of Gu'Tanoth.

During the Watchtower quest, the player must speak to the Skavid in his native language, at which point he will say "Hehe! So you speak a little Skavid, eh? I'll give you a prize for that!" and give the player one of the crystals needed to power the Watchtower and complete the quest.

label: Mage Arena
title: Mage Arena
lead:
The Mage Arena is a members-only combat area located deep in the Wilderness. Inside the arena are battle mages affiliated with the gods, which must be fought to unlock the god spells. 
The arena is involved in the miniquest Mage Arena I.

label: Mage Arena (music track)
title: Mage Arena (music track)
lead:
Mage Arena is a music track that is unlocked at the Mage Arena and its bank.

Prior to an update on 28 April 2021, the track was also unlocked in an area outside the Mage Arena.

label: Mage Arena bank
title: Mage Arena bank
lead:
The Mage Arena bank, also known as the mage bank or wildy bank, is a bank located deep within the Wilderness underneath a crumbling building north of the Mage Arena.

In addition to offering a safe area for banking, the bank room connects to a secondary cave through the sparkling pool, where players can acquire god capes and staves. Players do not need to complete Mage Arena I to access this area.

label: Mage Arena I
title: Mage Arena I
lead: Mage Arena I is a miniquest in which the player tests their mettle with a shapeshifting wizard. Players with level 60 Magic may begin the miniquest by speaking to Kolodion in the Mage Arena.

label: Mage Arena Staffs.
title: Mage Arena Staffs.
lead: Mage Arena Staffs is a store found in the Wilderness Mage Arena, owned by the chamber guardian. It can only be accessed after completion of the Mage Arena I miniquest by entering the Sparkling pool, and sells the three god staves for 80,000 coins.

label: Mage Training Arena/Alchemist's Playground
title: Mage Training Arena/Alchemist's Playground
lead: In the Alchemist's Playground, six cupboards are searched for items on which players cast low or high level alchemy to convert into coins. The coins are then deposited into the Coin Collector. For each coins deposited, the player will be rewarded with 1 Pizazz point and coins, as well as 2 Magic experience per coin deposited.

label: Mage Training Arena/Creature Graveyard
title: Mage Training Arena/Creature Graveyard
lead:
In the Creature Graveyard, players must collect 4 different types of bones from bone piles around the room, and use the Bones to Bananas or Bones to Peaches spells to turn them into bananas or peaches respectively. The fruits must then be deposited in the slots along the walls of the room to gain Pizazz points.

The bone piles cycle through 4 bone types, giving four of one type before advancing to the next. The bone types are worth 1, 2, 3 or 4 fruit per bone, respectively; a key showing these values can be seen in the interface in the bottom-right of the screen.

label: Mage Training Arena/Enchanting Chamber
title: Mage Training Arena/Enchanting Chamber
lead: In the Enchanting Chamber, players must use enchantment spells to enchant various shapes and/or dragonstones into orbs for Pizazz points.

label: Mage Training Arena/Telekinetic Theatre
title: Mage Training Arena/Telekinetic Theatre
lead:
The Telekinetic Theatre is one of the four minigames in the Mage Training Arena. It involves casting Telekinetic Grab to move the stone Maze Guardian statue to the exit square in a maze to restore the guardian back to life. The entrance to this minigame can be found at the southern portal, in front of the blue floor mat, of the Mage Training Arena. Entering the room requires level 33 Magic.

There are 10 possible mazes, each taking between seven and ten casts to complete. Each completed maze rewards 2 Telekinetic Pizazz points and 250 Magic experience, with an additional bonus of 8 Pizazz points, 1,000 experience, 10 law runes, and 100% run energy for every fifth maze completed (the player's streak is not reset upon leaving the arena). Therefore, averaged over the long term, each maze rewards 3.6 Pizazz points, 450 experience and 2 law runes, not counting any experience gained or runes expended from casting Telekinetic Grab.

label: Magenta crystal
title: Magenta crystal
lead:
Magenta crystal may refer to:

*Magenta crystal (Mourning's End Part II)
*Magenta crystal (Song of the Elves)
*Magenta crystal (Watchtower)
*Magenta Crystal (Tale of the Righteous)

label: Magenta door
title: Magenta door
lead: The magenta door in the basement of Melzar's Maze is opened with the magenta key dropped by Melzar the Mad during Dragon Slayer I.

label: Mages
title: Mages
lead:
Mages may refer to:
*Players who use the Magic combat class

label: Maggot King
title: Maggot King
lead: The Maggot King is a future boss that will release alongside the quest The Blood Moon Rises. The fight will be instanced, and will be somewhere between Phosani's Nightmare and the Inferno in difficulty. Rewards from the Maggot King include the crimson kisten, a crush-based special attack weapon, and the alpha venator tooth, which can be etched by the player with 84 Crafting and combined with a necklace of anguish to create the necklace of rupture.

label: Magic
title: Magic
lead:
Magic is a skill which allows players to cast different kinds of spells for various purposes, and forms one of the three combat classes in Old School RuneScape. There are broadly three categories of spells: combat spells used in combat, teleportation spells enabling efficient travel across the world of Gielinor, and utility spells which assist the player in non-combat settings. Players gain access to a wider variety of spells as they level up the skill.

As a combat class, Magic behaves slightly differently to Melee and Ranged. While Strength and Ranged levels influence a player's damage output in the respective combat styles, a player's Magic level generally does not affect the damage done by spells. Instead, having a higher Magic level increases both a player's accuracy when casting combat spells as well as a player's defence against magical attacks.

label: Magic axe
title: Magic axe
lead:
Magic axes are monsters that resemble translucent iron battleaxes.

The axes in the magic axe hut can be given as a wilderness Slayer assignment by Krystilia. Players require 23 Thieving for magic axes to be assigned as a task.

label: Magic axe hut
title: Magic axe hut
lead:
The magic axe hut is a small hut located in the north of the Wilderness at level 54 Wilderness. A lockpick and level 23 Thieving are required to unlock either of the doors to the hut. It is infested with aggressive magic axes and also contains three chests which may be searched for traps, then looted.

Looting a chest grants 8 thieving experience and 10 coins.

label: Magic book
title: Magic book
lead:
Magic book may refer to:
*Book of arcane knowledge, a reward from participating in the Arceuus Library.
*Mage's book, a reward from the Mage Training Arena minigame.
*Book of darkness, a God book that provides a Magic attack bonus.

label: Magic bow
title: Magic bow
lead:
Magic bow may refer to:
*Magic comp bow
*Magic longbow or unstrung counterpart
*Magic shortbow or unstrung counterpart

label: Magic cage
title: Magic cage
lead:
Magic cage may refer to:

*Lesser magic cage
*Greater magic cage

label: Magic carpet
title: Magic carpet
lead:
The magic carpet is a transportation method in the Kharidian Desert where magical rugs are used to safely traverse the desert. The magic carpet system is operated by Rug Merchants.

There are two major hubs from which the carpets travel - Shantay Pass and South Pollnivneach. Carpets can travel in both directions between destinations, but other carpet destinations will only travel to one of these two hubs.

label: Magic chest (interface item)
title: Magic chest (interface item)
lead:
The Magic chest is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Magic chest.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Magic damage
title: Magic damage
lead:
gives a 15% boost to magic damage.]]
Magic Damage is an equipment statistic that functions as a damage multiplier that increases the maximum magic hit and therefore the damage dealt by a player to a target. The effects of most equipped items can be seen at the bottom of the stats window (labelled Magic damage: +x%). Both players and non-player characters can utilize magic damage, although when casting Monster Examine on an attackable NPC, their magic damage is instead labelled as "Magic str bonus".

Temporarily boosting Magic increases magical attack accuracy, making it more likely to successfully hit a target. Except for Magic Dart, increasing the Magic level does not increase the damage of spellbook combat spells. It does, however, increase damage for Magic Dart, salamanders, powered staves (such as trident of the seas/swamp, Thammaron's/Accursed sceptre, Sanguinesti staff, and Tumeken's Shadow), and Magic special attacks.

label: Magic Dance
title: Magic Dance
lead:
Magic Dance is a music track that is unlocked in east Yanille.

It is a slow and peaceful track. This track has a very similar chord progression to Sea Shanty.

label: Magic door
title: Magic door
lead:
The magic door is a special door found within the Entrana Dungeon. It is the only exit from the dungeon aside from teleportation as once the player enters the dungeon from Entrana, they are unable to return as it is one-way.

Opening it transports the player to level 32 Wilderness, between the entrance to Vet'ion's Rest and the south Escape Caves entrance. This entire area is a multicombat area, meaning that players can potentially be attacked by several others if unfortunate. There is no warning prompt upon interacting with the door, and players are recommended to use other forms of teleportation rather than using this door.

label: magic door (Thalzar's room)
title: magic door (Thalzar's room)
lead:
The magic door in the Dwarven mine is used in the Dragon Slayer I quest. Thalzar built the door and made it difficult to open in order to prevent anyone from awakening Elvarg. To open the door, players first have to solve a riddle by the oracle.

After solving the riddle and obtaining the correct items, these items have to be used on the door. When all correct items are placed in the door, players can open it. The door remains unlocked after the items have been used for the first time, allowing players to re-enter without having to get more.

label: Magic egg (disambiguation)
title: Magic egg (disambiguation)
lead:
Magic egg may refer to:
*Magic egg, an item from the 2013 Easter event
*The Magic Egg, an object in the 2020 Easter event
*Magic egg ball, an item from the 2020 Easter event

label: Magic gold feather
title: Magic gold feather
lead:
The magic gold feather is a quest item used in the Holy Grail quest given to the player by King Arthur to help find Sir Percival.

Blowing on the feather will cause the feather to point either north, east, south, or west until the player reaches Goblin Village. Once the quest is completed, the feather has no use and can be safely dropped.

label: Magic guild door
title: Magic guild door
lead: The Magic guild doors allow access to the Wizards' Guild in Yanille. If the player has less than level 66 Magic, Wizard Distentor will deny them access.

label: Magic Guild Store
title: Magic Guild Store
lead:
Magic Guild Store may refer to:

*Magic Guild Store (Runes and Staves)
*Magic Guild Store (Mystic Robes)

label: Magic Guild Store (Runes and Staves)
title: Magic Guild Store (Runes and Staves)
lead:
The Magic Guild Store is located on the of the Wizards' Guild in Yanille. One must have a Magic level of 66 to enter the guild. The store is owned by the Wizard Akutha. The store sells all runes except cosmic, astral, wrath, and combination runes.

Due to the high amount sold by this store, restocking takes a long time.

label: Magic Instructor
title: Magic Instructor
lead:
The Magic instructor, whose real name is Terrova, is the last instructor new players meet on Tutorial Island. He teaches players about Magic and how to cast spells, and provided them with 5 air runes and 5 mind runes.

The Magic instructor is found in the building at the end of the dirt road on Tutorial Island. He has a large cage with chickens in it for players to train with the runes he provides to them (you could only use ranged or magic attacks on the chickens because the cage is only made of walls and a metal fence, which doesn't have a gate).

label: Magic Level Up!
title: Magic Level Up!
lead: Magic Level Up! is a Jingle for leveling Magic.

label: Magic Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Magic Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Magic Level Up! (Unlocks) is a jingle for levelling Magic.

label: magic logs
title: magic logs
lead:
Magic logs are logs that can be acquired using the Woodcutting skill from magic trees. Cutting magic trees requires a Woodcutting level of 75 or higher and yields 250 Woodcutting experience per log cut. Due to the slow speed at which magic trees are cut at this level, it is advised that players wait until they have a Woodcutting level of at least 85 before chopping magic trees. Players can expect to gain up to 130 magic logs per hour using a dragon axe.

Magic logs can be fletched into unstrung magic shortbows with a Fletching level of 80, granting 83.3 Fletching experience, or into unstrung magic longbows with a Fletching level of 85, granting 91.5 Fletching experience.

label: Magic longbow
title: Magic longbow
lead:
The magic longbow is a longbow fletched from magic logs. It requires a Ranged level of 50 to wield and can fire arrows up to amethyst.

Players can make a magic longbow with a Fletching level of 85 by cutting an unstrung magic longbow from magic logs, granting 91.5 Fletching experience, and then stringing unstrung magic longbow with a bow string, granting a further 91.5 experience.

label: Magic longbow (u)
title: Magic longbow (u)
lead: A magic longbow (u) is made using a knife with magic logs, requiring 85 Fletching and yielding 91.5 Fletching experience. Stringing a magic longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a magic longbow, also requiring 85 Fletching and yielding an additional 91.5 Fletching experience.

label: Magic ogre potion
title: Magic ogre potion
lead:
The magic ogre potion is a quest item in the Watchtower quest. It is used to kill ogre shamans in the Ogre Enclave below Gu'Tanoth.

It is made by adding to a vial of water a guam leaf, jangerberries, and ground bat bones, in that order, and then bringing the resulting potion to the Watchtower Wizard to enchant. Making the potion requires 14 Herblore. This item will disappear when dropped. Before dropping the item, it will ask for confirmation, stating: "This item will likely break if you put it down here, and you will have to go looking for another."

label: Magic Portal
title: Magic Portal
lead:
Magic Portal may refer to the following portals in Wizards' Guild before being renamed in an update in 2025:

* Dark Wizards' Tower Portal
* Sorcerer's Tower Portal
* Wizards' Tower Portal

label: Magic potion
title: Magic potion
lead:
Magic potions are made by mixing lantadyme and then potato cactus in a vial of water, giving 172.5 Herblore experience. It requires level 76 Herblore to make.

Using a magic potion temporarily raises the player's Magic level by 4.

label: Magic pure (free-to-play)
title: Magic pure (free-to-play)
lead:
A magic pure or mage pure is a type of low level free-to-play combat pure account that focuses on training Magic. This build is one of the most common ones in the low level combat brackets for multicombat, as early on combat spells allow to outdamage most other combat styles on top of their considerable attack range.

While other free-to-play combat pures that rely on melee or ranged attacks typically gain Hitpoints experience while training their combat skills with standard methods, Magic can be reliably trained without gaining any Hitpoints experience in the free-to-play worlds. Because of that, magic pures tend to have low Hitpoints levels and a considerably high damage output in the lower combat level brackets. However, due to the low attack speed of combat spells and the lack of magic max hits progression past 59 Magic level, these pures are rarely used on higher combat levels for typical 1-vs-1 combat.

label: Magic scroll
title: Magic scroll
lead:
Magic scroll may refer to:

* A magic scroll
* Ardougne teleport scroll
* Target teleport scroll
* Magic shortbow scroll
* Spell scroll
* Scroll
* Teleport scrolls

label: Magic shield (disambiguation)
title: Magic shield (disambiguation)
lead: Magic shield may refer to:

label: Magic shops
title: Magic shops
lead: Magic shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. They are usually represented by a icon. Magic shops all sell runes, and some sell staves and other items related to Magic. There are 15 total magic shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Magic shortbow
title: Magic shortbow
lead:
The Magic shortbow is a bow that requires level 50 Ranged in order to use and can fire arrows up to amethyst. It is one of the few shortbows in the game with a Special attack. The bow has an attack range of 7, with longrange increasing attack range by 2.

To make this bow, players must use a magic shortbow (u) on a bow string. This requires 80 Fletching, and grants 83 experience. They can also be received from hard clue scrolls, or as a rare drop from spiritual rangers.

label: Magic shortbow (u)
title: Magic shortbow (u)
lead: A magic shortbow (u) is made using a knife with magic logs, requiring level 80 Fletching and yielding 83.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a magic shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a magic shortbow, also requiring 80 Fletching and yielding an additional 83.3 Fletching experience.

label: Magic staff
title: Magic staff
lead:
A magic staff is a magic weapon providing standard magical bonuses and the autocast option when equipped. It is an improvement over the basic staff, with over double the magical bonuses and higher melee bonuses. Due to not possessing any elemental features, it is a very unpopular weapon of choice.

The staff can most easily be purchased from Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock, dropped by various enemies, or obtained as a reward from the Shades of Mort'ton minigame.

label: magic tablet
title: magic tablet
lead: Magic tablets are stackable, single-use magic spells that are cached in soft clay for future use. Using a magic tablet activates the spell and consumes the tablet. While making a magic tablet for a spell requires the same Magic level (and active spellbook) as casting the spell outright, using one has no level requirements.

label: Magic tank (free-to-play)
title: Magic tank (free-to-play)
lead:
A magic tank is a type of free-to-play combat pure account that focuses on training Defence and Magic.

While largely unsuccessful in typical arranged 1-vs-1 combat due to the low speed and damage output of magic, these accounts are valuable in multicombat areas where they can deal considerable damage to armoured opponents with their combat spells and support their clans. Thanks to their defensive capabilities and access to utility spells, magic tanks can perform tasks like scouting or hopping, and support their team with utility spells such as Snare or Tele Block.

label: Magic tree
title: Magic tree
lead: A magic tree is a rare type of tree that requires 75 Woodcutting to chop down, granting 250 Woodcutting experience per set of magic logs received. The chop rate of magic logs is noticeably slower than that of yew trees. Thus, there is a low supply for the logs due to how long it takes to chop them. They are mainly cut by players looking to gain an income through a very low intensity method, rather than gaining experience due to their slow experience rate. Magic trees are unique among trees as the only tree with an area sound.

label: Magic tree (interface item)
title: Magic tree (interface item)
lead:
The Magic tree is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the magic tree.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: magic wardrobe
title: magic wardrobe
lead:
Magic wardrobe may refer to:
*Magic wardrobe space, Construction hotspot in the Costume Room for storing magic armour sets.
**Oak magic wardrobe, stores up to 7 magic armour sets.

label: Magic weapons
title: Magic weapons
lead: Magic is an attack type that is used primarily by weapons like staves and wands. In contrast to most melee weapons, magic weapons can be used to deal damage to non-adjacent opponents. Magic weapons are associated with the Magic combat skill. They can be divided into items that can autocast combat spells from specific spellbooks, and weapons with built-in spells that are typically charged with runes and various tokens.

label: Magic whistle
title: Magic whistle
lead:
The magic whistle is a quest item in the Holy Grail quest which is originally obtained in the southern room on the top floor of Draynor Manor. This spawn can only be seen and picked up while the player has a holy table napkin in their inventory. In this spawn location, there are two whistles, one for the player and one which must be given to Sir Percival.

Blowing the magic whistle while standing in the location where all of the mysterious statues point, under the tower north-west of Brimhaven, allows players to access the Fisher Realm. Blowing the magic whistle in the Fisher Realm returns the player to Karamja. Attempting to blow the whistle anywhere else will display the following message: The whistle makes no noise. It will not work in this location.

label: Magnus Rimor
title: Magnus Rimor
lead:
Magnus Rimor was Phileas Rimor's ancestor and a captain in the Shayzien Army. He led a reportedly failed expedition to Mount Quidamortem that was ordered by King Shayzien VII over 1,000 years ago. However, the expedition was actually a success, but the expedition team was imprisoned and/or killed to cover it up.

In the story , it is revealed that Magnus was imprisoned in the Tower of Magic and guarded by the lizardman Eek C'ho. He eventually opens up to Eek, who gets him a journal to write in. After a few months, Magnus asks Eek to get the warnings he wrote in the journal outside to the rest of Kourend, because "they have to know". However the Yo'kal ahk, otherwise known as Xamphur, took the journal from Eek, thanking them for getting Magnus to talk. Magnus is presumably killed after this.

label: Mahjarrat
title: Mahjarrat
lead:
The Mahjarrat (pronounced MAH-jer-att) are a very powerful, warlike, and long-lived race from the realm of Freneskae. The Mahjarrat have powerful innate magical powers, some of them delving into necromancy or manipulating the Shadow Realm, and all of them capable of shapeshifting and sensing the presence of another member of their race.

Although not immortal, Mahjarrat age slowly. In their usual form, they take the appearance of skeletal humanoids with gems embedded into their foreheads. They are primarily followers of the gods Zamorak or Zaros and often reference "going North." Additionally, General Khazard and his men make reference to a 'ritual' amongst the Mahjarrat performed 'in the place of half light and ice' when the planets are aligned, which may be related.

label: main account
title: main account
lead:
The term main usually refers to a player's account that is situated on the main game mode.

This term is usually used by players who have multiple accounts, most commonly referred to as "alts" (short for alternates). These accounts are usually disposable and in essence, they are technically 'pures', as they are created and trained for multiple purpose(s), such as money making and typically, only a specific set of skill(s) are focused on and trained for any gain to the player (usually monetary). It can also be particularly used to distinguish against one's Ironman Mode account(s).

label: Main account (free-to-play)
title: Main account (free-to-play)
lead:
Main accounts (or mains) are the primary player accounts with no skill or quest restrictions. They typically train all free-to-play skills, which allows them to achieve the highest combat and total levels among all build types. Mains can achieve up to 126 combat level.

In the context of account builds and player-versus-player activities, high level accounts—typically with evenly distributed combat skills—are referred to as mains. As opposed to the combat pures, main accounts train skills such as Attack, Defence, and Prayer past the point of unlocking the best available items and boosts without any restrictions. As these accounts tend to be on the defensive side, their lack of specialisation on PvP and lack of focus on damage output leaves them less successful on lower combat levels where they have to complete with optimised accounts such as the one-defence pures or rune pures. However, they are the most common high level build since specialised accounts tend to max out their non-restricted combat skills long before reaching the final combat level brackets. Maxed mains are a particularly common build for PvP combat activities.

label: Main Menu
title: Main Menu
lead: The Main Menu is the initial login screen on the game client. Once the client has been loaded (either by being launched locally or through the Old School RuneScape website if you still have the legacy Java Client installed), the main menu will appear. You can login to the game from the main menu or create a new account. You can also toggle the music straight from the main menu as well as switch between worlds.

label: Main Menu/Login screens
title: Main Menu/Login screens
lead:
The appearance of the main menu, for the most part remains the same throughout the year. They are usually changed to commemorate major content releases, as well as during Halloween and Christmas events.

This page serves as a gallery to display past appearances and elements of the main menu.

label: makeover
title: makeover
lead:
A makeover is a feature that allows players to change their character's appearance chosen during the tutorial. Their appearance can be changed after the tutorial, free of charge, in several places.

Appearance features that can be customised include hair, facial hair, body type, pronouns, torso, sleeves, bottoms, shoes, and wristwear. All features can be changed by visiting any of the non-player characters that grant access to the makeover interface and clicking the button on the top left.

label: Makeover Mage
title: Makeover Mage
lead:
The Makeover Mage, also known as Pete or Peta depending on whether they are currently male or female, is a wizard who possesses the magical knowledge to change the player's body type, skin colour or pronouns, completely free of charge. Approximately every 10 seconds, they will switch genders.

They obtained their powers from an amulet they obtained after killing a nest of gazulibirds.

label: Male slave
title: Male slave
lead:
Male slaves can be found working the mines at the Desert Mining Camp. One particular slave, the one who isn't mining, is involved in The Tourist Trap quest and provides information on the deeper parts of the camp. The player initially helps him by breaking his chains, then he trades them his robes for desert robes and becomes an escaping slave.

The generic male slaves (along with female slaves) complain a lot about being there and about their work. They can be spoken to, but no dialogue pops up, they will exclaim and the player will get thrown in jail if done enough times. After completion of The Tourist Trap, it's no longer possible to get thrown in the jail and the slaves can be talked to freely.

label: Malumac
title: Malumac
lead: Malumac was a Zamorakian warrior under Skotizo's command. After the battle of Carrallanger they went to claim an artefact hidden in a temple deep within the Kharazi Jungle. Skotizo however betrayed them and although Malumac initially escaped, he was mortally wounded by a trap in his panic. His skeleton and journal can be found in a dead end within the cave.

label: Malvern
title: Malvern
lead: Malvern is a Hill giant mentioned in the 11th Postbag from the Hedge. He is among the hill giants located south-west of the Tree Gnome Stronghold. He explains that hill giants are called as such because they look like hills, not because they live on them.

label: Mam
title: Mam
lead: Mam is the son of Dad the troll, mentioned in the 27th Postbag from the Hedge. According to Dad, the family's fathers were all named "Dad", who were famous for "toothy troll babies". However, he chose to name his son "Mam" after his defeat at the player's hands caused him to reflect on the "toxic masculinity" present in troll culture that encourages fights.

label: Mammal
title: Mammal
lead: Mammal may refer to animals or creatures that would belong or would likely belong to the real-life vertebrate animal class of , but in Old School RuneScape it is specifically used to describe a category of aquatic monsters encountered in Gielinor's oceans through the Sailing skill. They can be engaged through ship combat.

label: Mammoth (unused NPC)
title: Mammoth (unused NPC)
lead:
Mammoths were an unused monster first added to the RuneScape 2 beta. A Behind the Scenes article from March 2004 promised that one of the upcoming updates would be "A large 'frozen lands' area including penguins, mammoths, polar bears and more." Presumably, they would have been found alongside penguins and the Yeti. For unknown reasons, the mammoths were ultimately never added.

They later appeared at an exhibit in Prifddinas during Old School RuneScape's first anniversary, and updated mammoths were added to the Wilderness with the Wilderness Rejuvenation update of 13 March 2014. Eventually, the original mammoths were deleted from the game cache in 2017.

label: Man
title: Man
lead:
Men are generic NPC civilians of Gielinor. They can be found in most large cities and towns, especially those in Misthalin, such as Lumbridge, Falador, and Varrock. While less common, they can also be found in remote areas such as the Wilderness.

Men can be pickpocketed by members at level 1 Thieving, yielding 8 experience points and 3 coins. They often drop low-level herbs when killed on members-only servers.

label: Man (Canifis bridge)
title: Man (Canifis bridge)
lead:
A man could be found at the flooded bridge to the north-east of Canifis when the area was first released in June 2004. When spoken to, he told players that the bridge and the swamps to the east were flooded, preventing access to eastern Morytania. When the Haunted Woods were released in October, the swamp water receded, and the man was removed. Mazchna took his spot on the bridge when Slayer was released in January 2005.

He was deleted from the game cache and overwritten by Prissy Scilla with the release of the Tree Gnome Stronghold tree patch on 6 November 2006. As such he has never existed in any form in Old School RuneScape.

label: Man (Canifis)
title: Man (Canifis)
lead:
Men were formerly the citizens of Canifis. If players were not wielding a wolfbane dagger when attacking them, they would turn into wolfmen.

In 2007, werewolves were graphically updated. The men were replaced by new named citizens, while the Wolfmen were replaced by werewolves. As a result, they have never been present in Old School RuneScape.

label: Man (level 4)
title: Man (level 4)
lead:
Men are citizens of West Ardougne. They are similar to men found throughout Gielinor, but can only be attacked and talked to, and not pickpocketed. Their appearance is slightly different, in keeping with the theme of West Ardougne supposedly being afflicted with a plague, and their dialogue is slightly different, reflecting their plight under Mourner rule.

They are found near the civilians, children, and women, as well as other non-attackable men.

label: Man (West Ardougne)

lead: Men of West Ardougne are citizens who can be found among other civilians and women who live West Ardougne. Their appearance and dialogue reflect the poor living conditions in the city. These men in particular only have a Talk-to option, compared to attackable men also found in West Ardougne.

label: Managing Miscellania
title: Managing Miscellania
lead:
Managing Miscellania is a repeatable reward/activity unlocked with the completion of the Throne of Miscellania quest. The activity involves assigning the citizens of the island of Miscellania (and additionally Etceteria after the completion of Royal Trouble) to collect a mixture of different resources available on the island/s. Resources may be collected as often as once per day, which results in the resources being deposited directly in the player's bank (meaning ultimate ironmen cannot gain resources from this activity).

The number of resources collected depends on both the player's popularity with the citizens as well as their daily wage, which is taken daily as a percentage of the coins the player has invested in the Miscellania coffers.

label: Maniacal monkey/Strategies
title: Maniacal monkey/Strategies
lead: Killing Maniacal monkeys offers some of the highest experience rates in the game for training Magic (using Ancient Magicks burst/barrage spells) and Ranged (with Chinchompas). Their extremely low Defence and high spawn density allow for consistently high damage across multiple targets. Unlocked after completing Monkey Madness II, this method is both efficient and low-effort, thanks to frequent 1-dose Prayer potion drops. With Protect from Melee active, it becomes a semi-AFK training method comparable to the Nightmare Zone, but with significantly faster experience gains.

label: Manta ray
title: Manta ray
lead:
The manta ray is a type of food that restores 22 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw manta ray on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 91 Cooking and granting 216.3 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt manta ray. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. It will only stop burning entirely when the Cooking cape is worn.

The manta ray is the second highest instant-health single consumption food, behind the marlin, alongside the dark crab, bluefin, anglerfish, and tuna potato. It is recommended to check the prices before using manta rays as a primary source of healing, as they are often more expensive than the other fish that heal the same amount.

Maoma the Corrupt Captain was the captain of the Emir's guard. Part of the Calamity Coven, she, along with Saika and Koriff, played a part in the staining the reputation of the once glorious Duel Arena, turning it into an immensely corrupt place where they used their positions to accumulate vast amounts of ill-gotten wealth.

As the captain of the Emir's guard, she was assigned to oversee the fights at the Arena, ensuring that order was upheld. In reality, she abused her authority by taking bribes and rigged fights so that the Coven would get rich at the people's expense.
