label: map part
title: map part
lead:
Map parts are the three parts of the Crandor map that must be made during the Dragon Slayer I quest to access the island. When the player has all the map parts in their inventory, they can use any two pieces on each other and the three will fuse to form the Crandor map.

* Melzar's map part is in Melzar's Maze, located south of the Crafting Guild, and requires the maze key to enter. To acquire the key, several monsters must be fought throughout the maze, from zombie rats to Melzar the Mad and a Lesser demon. The lesser demon drops the last key of the maze which opens the locked door of the room of a chest that contains the map part.

label: Map part (Lozar)
title: Map part (Lozar)
lead:
Lozar's Crandor Map part is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. This map part is either dropped by Wormbrain, arrested in the Port Sarim jail, after killing him and obtaining the part with telekinetic grab or paying him 10,000 coins.

When all three map parts are in the inventory, using any two pieces on each other will combine all three into the Crandor map, which is given to Ned.

label: Map part (Melzar)
title: Map part (Melzar)
lead:
Melzar's Crandor Map part is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. This map part is found in a chest in Melzar's Maze south of the Crafting Guild. The maze key is required to enter the building, while coloured keys dropped by monsters allow passage through the maze.

When all three map parts are in the inventory, using any two pieces on each other will combine all three into the Crandor map, which is given to Ned.

label: Map part (Thalzar)
title: Map part (Thalzar)
lead:
Thalzar's Crandor Map part is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. This map part is found in a chest sealed behind a magic door in the Dwarven Mines under the foothills of Ice Mountain. This door and room is located east of Drogo's Mining Emporium. To open the door to this room, a lobster pot, silk, an unfired bowl, and a wizard's mind bomb must be used on the door to open it.

When all three map parts are in the inventory, using any two pieces on each other will combine all three into the Crandor map, which is given to Ned.

label: Maple logs
title: Maple logs
lead:
Maple logs are received from cutting maple trees requiring a Woodcutting level of 45 and yield 100 Woodcutting experience (110 with Kandarin Medium Diary) per log. Maple logs can be burned with a Firemaking level of 45, giving 135 experience per log. Maple logs can also be fletched into different items: arrow shafts, maple shortbow (u), maple longbow (u), maple stock and maple shield.

Because of their low price and the moderate experience they provide, maple logs are commonly used for training Firemaking.

label: Maple longbow
title: Maple longbow
lead:
A maple longbow is created by attaching a bow string to a maple longbow (u) with at least level 55 Fletching. Fletching from a maple log yields a total of 116.5 experience (58.3 for fletching and 58.2 for stringing). The bow can use arrows up to adamant.

The maple longbow differs from the shortbow only in terms of speed and range, they share the same Ranged bonus. However, the shortbow is usually preferred over the longbow due to its faster attack speed. It can also be a reward for the Observatory Quest.

label: Maple longbow (u)
title: Maple longbow (u)
lead: A maple longbow (u) is made using a knife with maple logs, requiring 55 Fletching and yielding 58.3 Fletching experience. Stringing a maple longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a maple longbow, also requiring 55 Fletching and yielding an additional 58.2 Fletching experience.

label: Maple shortbow
title: Maple shortbow
lead:
A maple shortbow is a two-handed Ranged weapon that can be created with the Fletching skill at level 50 by using a bow string on a maple shortbow (u), granting 50 experience. A Ranged level of 30 is required to wield it. The bow can use arrows up to adamant. However, this bow isn't powerful enough for the use of broad arrows.

It is notable for being the best bow that free-to-play players can use.

label: Maple shortbow (u)
title: Maple shortbow (u)
lead: A maple shortbow (u) is made using a knife with maple logs, requiring 50 Fletching and yielding 50 Fletching experience. Stringing a maple shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a maple shortbow, also requiring 50 Fletching and yielding an additional 50 Fletching experience.

label: maple tree
title: maple tree
lead: A maple tree is an amber-coloured tree that requires level 45 Woodcutting to cut, granting 100 Woodcutting experience for each set of maple logs received. Maple trees have moderately high cut difficulty and maple logs only have moderate value, making cutting maple trees unfavourable for money making. Maple trees can be cut as an AFK Woodcutting training method for F2P players. Completion of the Medium Kandarin Diary give players 10% additional experience when cutting Maple trees in Seers' Village, granting 110 Woodcutting experience per log received.

label: March 2007 audio rework
title: March 2007 audio rework
lead:
The March 2007 audio rework was a major rework of RuneScape 2's music player that was released on 6 March 2007. As part of this rework, all of the game's existing songs at the time were updated with new recording technology.

When the Music player was first released on 15 March 2004, the game's songs sounded significantly different than they do today. The music player was dependent on the soundcard which meant that an individual music track could sound completely different depending on what computer they were using. To address this, the music player was completely reworked in early 2007 - from March 2007 onwards, songs were created using a bank of instruments built into the game itself so that all music tracks sounded the same regardless of what machine the game was being played on. All existing songs (456 listed and 17 unlisted at the time of the update) were updated to better reflect the new music player's sound. Old School RuneScape uses the music system derived from the audio rework.

label: March 2025 Sailing Alpha
title: March 2025 Sailing Alpha
lead:
The March 2025 Sailing Alpha was a preview of the Sailing skill, available to all members running from 20 March to 26 March 2025. The alpha build allowed players to play-test the early stages of the skill, focusing on initial levels and progression. The skill was not fully implemented, and Sailing levels were capped at 30 during the alpha.

Upon logging into a Sailing alpha world, players were required to complete an in-game CAPTCHA to verify they are using supported clients. For more information, click here.

label: Marimbo
title: Marimbo
lead:
Marimbo (Jagex pronunciation: mah-RIM-bo) is the patron goddess of monkeys. According to the 2021 Birthday event, 'all monkeys send their thoughts and prayers to Marimbo'.

The village of Marim on Ape Atoll is named after her. Apart from this, very little is known about Marimbo. Her altar can be found in the centre of Marim and in the east temple. Although she has an established clergy on the atoll, she does not appear to be worshipped anywhere else.

label: Marionette
title: Marionette
lead:
Marionettes are items obtainable during Christmas events and come in three different colours.

Before the 2013 Christmas event, it could only be obtained from picking one up from various spawn points around the world during 12 - 19 August 2013. When picked up by a player, it would immediately spawn in another random location.

label: Marisa
title: Marisa
lead:
Marisa is a vampyre and one of the possible senders of a message to the player if they successfully complete the Theatre of Blood. Marisa finds the player's attempts laughable and offers them supplies to make their agony last longer.

They are only mentioned in the message, and cannot be found anywhere in-game.

label: Marked wall
title: Marked wall
lead:
The marked wall can be found in the Shaman Caves during the Legends' Quest. Interacting with it will give the riddle

:"Place five stones of magical power - but place them wrong, and your fate will sour. First is the spirit of man or beast (Soul rune), second the place where fools tread least (Mind rune). Third is the soil where plants do grow (Earth rune) - and four and five are the rules you must know (two Law runes). Solve this riddle, and overcome your ignorance; arranged correct, it should make sense."

label: Marrentill
title: Marrentill
lead:
Marrentill is the second lowest level herb. It can be cleaned at level 5 Herblore, giving 3.8 experience. It is used for making antipoison, marrentill tar and Guthix rest potions. Marrentill is also used to light incense burners, in player-owned houses, to boost Prayer experience when sacrificing bones (usually dragon bones).

Marrentill is rarely used for Herblore purposes. Guthix rests and marrentill tar have limited uses and demand among players, and antipoison requires unicorn horn dust as a secondary ingredient, which is costly, due to its use in superantipoison potions. As well as this, antipoison potions can be easily obtained from Jiminua's Jungle Store, further decreasing the demand. If you want to create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a marrentill potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

label: Marrentill potion (unf)
title: Marrentill potion (unf)
lead: A marrentill potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a marrentill on a vial of water, requiring 5 Herblore. Using a unicorn horn dust on a marrentill potion (unf) with 5 Herblore yields an antipoison(3) and 37.5 Herblore experience. In the Bone Voyage quest, a marrentill potion (unf) and 2 vodka are given to the Apothecary for a potion of sealegs.

label: Marshy jungle vine
title: Marshy jungle vine
lead:
Marshy jungle vine is a plant found in Karamja. Searching ripe vines is the only way players can obtain grimy snake weed (and subsequently its clean version), which is needed for some quests like Jungle Potion and Legends' Quest. Snake weed is also an ingredient in making Sanfew serum. The vines can only be searched after regrowing every 60 seconds.

The fastest way to access the vines is by running west from fairy ring . Twenty vines can be found growing near the coast, just north of the Horned graahk hunter area.

label: Martha Rehnison
title: Martha Rehnison
lead: Martha Rehnison lives in the Rehnison household in north-eastern West Ardougne. She is the wife of Ted Rehnison. She has two children, Billy and Milli. Her family sells cooking apples and are known friends of Elena.

label: Marv Halen

lead: Mask may refer to any of the following:

label: Masori armour
title: Masori armour
lead:
Masori armour is a set of ranged armour requiring level 80 Ranged and 30 Defence to equip. The armour belonged to the Masori clan, who were powerful ranged weapon-wielders active around the time of the Kharidian–Zarosian War and were known for defending people from bandits who sought to take advantage of the wartime chaos. Their armour can only be obtained as rare drops from the Tombs of Amascut.

It is the best ranged armour in the game, surpassing Armadyl armour in terms of ranged attack bonuses and does not provide a penalty to melee accuracy like Armadyl armour does. The Masori armour can also be upgraded into a fortified variant with Armadyl plates, increasing the Defence level required to equip it to 80, offering increased defensive bonuses and a +1 prayer bonus. This fortified version provides the highest magic defence bonus of all armour in the game, surpassing other Ranged armour sets such as Karil's or Armadyl. Fortifying the armour requires level 90 Crafting.

label: Mast and sails
title: Mast and sails
lead:
The mast and sails are a combined core boat part used in shipbuilding to make boats for Sailing. While sailing, they can be trimmed every 30 seconds for a short speed boost and some Sailing experience, depending on the tier of the equipment.

Higher-tier equipment make the ship accelerate more quickly, along with providing storm resistance; partial resistance allows navigation of The Storm Tempor without taking passive boat damage, while full resistance additionally negates damage dealt by lightning clouds in that area.

label: Master
title: Master
lead: Master may refer to:

label: Master Chef
title: Master Chef
lead:
Lev the Master Chef is the third non-player character players meet in Old School RuneScape. He lives on Tutorial Island. He teaches new players how to cook more sophisticated food and how the Music Player works.

Until the point in the tutorial when new players meet the master chef, the only thing they would have cooked are shrimps on a log fire. He teaches new players how to bake bread by combining a flour with water to make bread dough, and then baking it on a range.

label: Master Crafter
title: Master Crafter
lead:
The Master Crafter is one of the non-player characters who can be found south-west of Falador inside the Crafting Guild. He teaches many advanced crafters how to use the facilities within the guild, such as the mines, the potter's wheels, and the pottery ovens.

The eldest Master Crafter is the master of Crafting, and wears the Crafting cape. This crafter sells the Crafting cape to members with level 99 in Crafting for 99,000 coins.

label: Master fisher
title: Master fisher
lead:
The Master fisher is the head of the Fishing Guild and can be found by the guild's entrance building.

As the head of the guild, the master fisher watches the entrance to the guild to make sure that only players with at least level 68 in Fishing are allowed to enter. If a player with less than level 68 talks to him, he says: Hello, I'm afraid only the top fishers are allowed to use our premier fishing facilities.

label: Matthias Vorseth
title: Matthias Vorseth
lead: Matthias Vorseth is the author of Rada's census, a book found in the Arceuus Library. Matthias created the census by the command of King Rada III sometime between 6th BA and 5th BA, documenting all skilled peoples, animals and estates of the Lords of the settlement of Kourend.

label: Mature ale
title: Mature ale
lead: Mature ales are members-only, stronger versions of regular ale. They provide stronger skill boosts, larger deboosts, and heal more than the regular versions. These are only obtainable through brewing, where there is a chance that a batch of ale matures during the brewing process. Leaving an ale in the fermenting vat after it has fully set will not turn it mature. The chance of brewing a mature ale increases from 5% to 64% by adding the stuff to the vat after adding in barley malt. The stuff cannot be used to make mature cider, the player must rely on the 5% chance. It is purchasable from Honest Jimmy for 50 pieces of eight, a reward from the Trouble Brewing minigame.

label: Maul
title: Maul
lead:
"Maul" is a word used to refer to certain two-handed blunt weapons. Similar to the one-handed warhammer, they can deal large amounts of damage. There are only a few of them, as they are not one of the standard groups of metal weapons.

Mauls are very popular in PvP due to their level requirements and high damage output, making them ideal for pure builds. They are one of the few weapon types where Strength is a notable requirement.

label: Mauritys Guile
title: Mauritys Guile
lead:
Mauritys Guile is a resident of Meiyerditch and Myreque member referenced in the Darkness of Hallowvale quest. During the quest, a servant in Castle Drakan known as Sarius Guile refers the player to Mauritys' former home, where a message can be found.

Mauritys was forced to work in the blood labs beneath Meiyerditch and narrowly escaped the laboratory's destruction by the vyrewatch. He was later pursued by the vyrewatch, but managed to hide a message within the fireplace of his home. The message is directed at the Myreque, specifically its leader, Safalaan Hallow.

label: Mausoleum (music track)
title: Mausoleum (music track)
lead: Mausoleum is a music track unlocked underneath Paterdomus.

label: Maximum damage cap
title: Maximum damage cap
lead:
A maximum damage cap is the maximum amount of hitpoints of damage that can be inflicted on a monster in a single hit. Maximum damage caps may be active for the entire encounter, or only during specific parts of it.

The global maximum damage cap is 200, which is used as a failsafe against unintended mechanics that may come about as a result of introducing new pieces of equipment.

label: maximum hit
title: maximum hit
lead:
A Maximum hit is the highest possible damage that can be done in one attack.

Under certain circumstances, a maximum hit can always be dealt as a successful hit.

label: Maximum magic hit
title: Maximum magic hit
lead:
Maximum magic hit is the maximum damage a player can deal in a single magic attack. It is affected by player's Magic level, equipment and other special bonuses.

In most cases, the Tumeken's shadow provides the highest maximum magic hit possible. The exceptions to this are the Volatile nightmare staff's special attack, the Accursed sceptre's special attack while in the wilderness, the Accursed sceptre's against Revenants in the wilderness while wearing an Amulet of avarice and having Forinthry Surge, and barrage spells when hitting up to nine targets.

label: maximum melee hit
title: maximum melee hit
lead:
Maximum melee hit is the maximum damage a player can deal in a melee combat. It is affected by player's Strength, equipment and other bonuses such as prayer, passive effects, enemy weaknesses, or potions.

All damage players can deal is capped at 200 to soften the impact of potential exploits.

label: Maximum ranged hit
title: Maximum ranged hit
lead: Maximum ranged hit is a term used to describe the highest amount of damage rangers can inflict. Currently the maximum ranged hit is 110 in PvM. In PvP, the max hit is ~79 with dragonstone dragon bolts (e) and max ranged damage gear.

label: Mayor
title: Mayor
lead:
Mayor may refer to:

* The mayor of Catherby
* Mayor Hobb, the mayor of Witchaven
* Ali the Mayor, the mayor of Pollnivneach
* Awusah the Mayor, the mayor of Nardah

label: Maze
title: Maze
lead:
The maze is a random event initiated randomly by the appearance of the Mysterious Old Man, who offers the player a chance to complete a maze. It is favourable to complete over most other random events because the rewards it gives tend to be much more valuable than those given by other events despite taking longer to complete.

The maze itself is a large square area full of "walls" made of floating cubes. The goal is to navigate through the maze to the centre and touch the rotating shrine found there; once the player does so, they will be teleported back to where they spoke to the Mysterious Old Man and will receive a reward. Run energy doesn't deplete at all in the maze.

label: Maze Centre
title: Maze Centre
lead: Maze Centre is a Jingle that plays when completing the Maze random event. It is based upon Time Out.

label: Maze key
title: Maze key
lead:
The Maze key is a quest item used only in Dragon Slayer I. It is obtained from the Guildmaster in the Champions' Guild when the player has returned to him after speaking to Oziach.

It is used to open the front door of Melzar's Maze.

label: McGrubor's Wood
title: McGrubor's Wood
lead:
McGrubor's Wood is a wooded, fenced-in area north of Hemenster and west of Seers' Village, used primarily for quests. There are two ways in and out: a loose section of the northern railing, and a fairy ring with code .

The loose section of the railing is immediately to the north-east of the small building that borders the fence, and is shown on the map in red, similarly to how a door is portrayed.

label: Meat pie
title: Meat pie
lead:
Meat pie is a type of pie that restores 12 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 6. A pie dish will remain after both bites are consumed. It can be obtained by baking an uncooked meat pie on a cooking range, requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 110 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Meat pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 54, or 49 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Meat pie is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild. Three meat pies are given to the player when starting Nature Spirit.

label: Meat pizza
title: Meat pizza
lead:
Meat pizza is a type of pizza that restores 16 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 8. It can be obtained by using cooked meat or cooked chicken on a plain pizza, requiring 45 Cooking and granting 26 experience.

When the first bite is eaten, the message You eat half of the meat pizza.is displayed. The second bite gives the message You eat the remaining meat pizza..

label: Meat pouch

Meat pouch may refer to:
* Small meat pouch, which can store up to 14 pieces of meat from hunter creatures
* Large meat pouch, which can store up to 28 pieces of meat from hunter creatures

label: Medical gown

lead:
The medical gown is a quest item used in Biohazard and A Tail of Two Cats. It is found in the cupboard of Nurse Sarah's house, south-west of the west Ardougne church.

While it is equipped, the player is allowed to enter the Mourners' Headquarters in the north-east corner of West Ardougne after poisoning the stew in the back yard with a rotten apple. This item may also be used as part of a medical disguise in A Tail of Two Cats.

In Classic mode, this track plays east of Varrock and the hint referred to "near the Varrock East guarded area".

*Medium fossilised ribs
*Medium fossilised pelvis
*Medium fossilised skull
*Unidentified medium fossil

Medium Fossil Display may refer to:

* The Lava Monster medium fossil display

label: Medium helmet
title: Medium helmet
lead: A Medium helmet is armour worn in the headwear slot. Although full helmets are stronger than medium helmets, players training magic and ranging would have no trouble seeing through a medium helmet, giving them better accuracy whilst still having good defences against melee and ranged. Notably, they do not have a negative range accuracy bonus like full helmets.

label: Medium hidey hole (interface item)
title: Medium hidey hole (interface item)
lead:
The Medium hidey hole is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the STASH.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Medium map (interface item)
title: Medium map (interface item)
lead:
The Medium map is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Medium map.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Medium statue (interface item)
title: Medium statue (interface item)
lead:
The Medium statue is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Medium statue.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Medium storage unit (interface item)
title: Medium storage unit (interface item)
lead:
The medium storage unit is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the medium storage unit.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: medium-level build
title: medium-level build
lead: A medium-level build or med is an account build with similar power to a maxed main, but with a significantly lower combat level. This allows meds to attack lower level builds such as berserkers or one-defence pures in low-to-moderate wilderness and exercise significant gear and stat advantages over them. Meds will typically have 60-82 Attack and 70-80 Defence, depending on their desired equipment and combat level. This is combined with high offensive stats and 77 Prayer for Piety, Rigour, and Augury.

label: Megan
title: Megan
lead: Megan is an employee of the Falador Party Room and can be found on the . She will dance with the player upon request or serve beer. Like Party Pete and the other barmaids in the Party Room, she wears a red partyhat.

label: Megarare
title: Megarare
lead:
Megarare may refer to:

*The rarest unique drops from the three raids, colloquially called "megarares"
**Twisted bow from Chambers of Xeric
***Kodai insignia and elder maul are sometimes included in the term
**Scythe of vitur from Theatre of Blood
**Tumeken's shadow from Tombs of Amascut
*Raids megarare voucher, an item previously obtainable during the Raging Echoes League and Grid Master that could be used to redeem a twisted bow, scythe of Vitur, or Tumeken's shadow
*The mega-rare drop table, part of the rare drop table
*The mega-rare drop tables that can be accessed through hard, elite and master tier Treasure Trails rewards: see Reward casket

label: Mehkmets
title: Mehkmets
lead: The Mehkmets are a people from Al Kharid who practise the cutting of tongues. They are referenced only by Saradomin in the first god letter, when he explains the concept of mutes and bans.

label: Meilyr Clan
title: Meilyr Clan
lead: The Meilyr Clan is one of the eight elven clans who were originally brought to Gielinor from Tarddiad by Guthix and Seren in the early First Age. They are a clan of explorers, scientists and chefs. They are located north-east of the Tower of Voices in Prifddinas, off the northern path.

label: Mel Achy
title: Mel Achy
lead:
Mel Achy is an unknown traveller who, while journeying in the far east, learned of a highly explosive and sticky mixture known as fire oil. They recorded the recipe in the Big book of bangs, which includes the ingredients quicklime, sulphur, and naphtha.

At some point, Lord Iorwerth came to possess Mel Achy's book. As he didn't have the troops available to take on King Tyras's forces directly, Lord Iorwerth suggested that the adventurer create a bomb to assassinate Tyras, using the knowledge found in the book.

label: Melee
title: Melee
lead:
The term melee is used to describe the Attack, Strength and Defence skills. Melee is one of the three combat classes in Old School RuneScape. It involves using swords, daggers, and other weapons to damage opponents, as well as wearing heavy armour made from various metals.

Old School RuneScape generally follows the combat triangle, which means that melee-users tend to be strong against rangers but weak to mages. Melee's inability to attack from a distance means that a player may have a hard time fighting a ranger or mage, as they can make use of safespots. However, melee armour has a high resistance to ranged attacks, making warriors effective against rangers.

label: Melee potion
title: Melee potion
lead: Melee potion may refer to:

label: Melee pure (free-to-play)
title: Melee pure (free-to-play)
lead: A melee pure is a type of free-to-play combat pure account that focuses on training melee combat skills such as Attack and Strength. Along with ranged-melee hybrids, melee pures are one of the most common free-to-play account builds on the 1-vs-1 player-versus-player combat scene.

label: Mellow
title: Mellow
lead: Mellow is a music track that is unlocked at the Fishing Guild.

label: Melzar the Mad
title: Melzar the Mad
lead:
Melzar the Mad is one of the three wizards, along with Thalzar and Lozar, who escaped from Crandor when the dragon Elvarg destroyed it, and is the only one of them that is still alive. He has since lost his sanity, leading to his nickname, and has secluded himself and his piece of the map to Crandor in his maze north-west of Rimmington. He is fought during the Dragon Slayer I quest.

In combat, Melzar can kick, punch, cast Fire Strike or a Curse spell, or cast a spell that produces a cabbage in a random spot in the room. (Note that the cabbages CAN be used for food.)

label: Melzar's Maze
title: Melzar's Maze
lead:
Melzar's Maze is a large, three-story building with a basement located north-west of Rimmington. It is the home of Melzar the Mad and contains Melzar's map part required for the Dragon Slayer I quest. To enter the building, players must obtain the Maze key from the Guildmaster of the Champions' Guild during the quest. The building was built by Melzar atop the remains of the Crandorian refugee camp that was destroyed by Elvarg.

Once inside the building, players must go through mazes on each floor and in the basement. However, to proceed to the next floor, players must kill the creature that is holding the key to one of the many doors on the floor. Only one door leads players to the next floor; the rest will send them back to the previous floor.

label: Melzar's notes
title: Melzar's notes
lead: Melzar's Notes are a collection of notes that contain all sorts of information on Melzar's life and experiments. In them, Melzar wrote about his efforts to use necromancy to bring back the Crandorian refugees (including his wife) who were slain by Elvarg.

label: Members
title: Members
lead: Members' worlds or member only worlds are worlds that give players access to the full version of Old School RuneScape.

label: Members object
title: Members object
lead:
Members object was the term given on a free-to-play world to any item that could only be used on a members' world. The item would return to normal if you switched to a members' world again.

Members objects could not be traded in free-to-play worlds. If already equipped, they would remain equipped on the free world, but if removed they could not be put back on. All members objects had the same examine text: "Login to a members' server to use this object."

label: Memoriam crystal
title: Memoriam crystal
lead: Memoriam crystals are items found in Prifddinas which can be used to view the memories of Seren. To view the memories, the player must turn the crystals in to the memoriam device found upstairs in the Tower of Voices. There are four crystals that can be found in each location which contribute to memories.

label: Menaphite clothing
title: Menaphite clothing
lead:
Menaphite clothing consists of two sets of members-only clothing that is commonly seen throughout the Kharidian Desert.

All pieces individually delay the desert heat effect:
*Menaphite purple hat - 12 additional seconds
*Menaphite purple top - 12 additional seconds
*Menaphite purple robe - 12 additional seconds
*Menaphite purple kilt - 12 additional seconds
*Menaphite red hat - 12 additional seconds
*Menaphite red top - 12 additional seconds
*Menaphite red robe - 12 additional seconds
*Menaphite red kilt - 12 additional seconds

label: Menaphite Pantheon
title: Menaphite Pantheon
lead:
.]]
The Menaphite Pantheon is the name given to an octet of deities who ruled the Kharidian Lands. It consists of Tumeken, god of light, his wife Elidinis, goddess of fertility, their children Icthlarin, god of the Underworld, and Amascut, goddess of rebirth, as well as four demi-gods: Apmeken, goddess of companionship, Crondis, goddess of resourcefulness, Het, god of health, and Scabaras, god of wisdom and isolation.

The Menaphite Pantheon acted as spiritual guides rather than leaders, Tumeken himself having appointed a mortal pharaoh to act as leader of their people.

label: Menaphites
title: Menaphites
lead: The Menaphites are a group of people that once inhabited the entire Kharidian Desert. They have lived in the desert for thousands of years and are amongst the oldest surviving factions of humans in Gielinor.

label: Mercenary
title: Mercenary
lead: Mercenaries are guards hired by Captain Siad, the head of the Desert Mining Camp, to guard it. The four of them are led by a Mercenary Captain and their duty is to protect said captain and the entrance to the camp. They will attack the player if they are wielding a weapon or wearing armour outside the Desert Mining Camp. After completion of The Tourist Trap, they are no longer aggressive outside the camp regardless if the player wears any armour or weapons. However, if the player stands inside the camp right next to the gate, they can call out the player and attempt to attack them, but will fail due to the gate being in the way,

label: Mercenary Captain
title: Mercenary Captain
lead:
The Mercenary Captain is the captain of the mercenaries outside the Desert Mining Camp, and was hired to guard the entrance of it to prevent unauthorised people from going in. The Mercenary Captain plays a role in the quest The Tourist Trap, in which he is portrayed as a hot-headed and angry individual, and must be provoked to the point of outrage so that he initiates combat with the player himself, rather than having his mercenaries do his dirty work for him.

Once killed, the captain 'drops' the Metal key, which is automatically added to the player's inventory with the message "The mercenary captain drops a metal key on the floor. You quickly grab the key and add it to your inventory." appearing in the chatbox.

label: Merchant (disambiguation)
title: Merchant (disambiguation)
lead:
Merchant may refer to:

*Merchanting

label: merchanting
title: merchanting
lead:
Merchanting or merching, is the act of purchasing an item at a low price and then selling that item at a higher price to generate profit. It is a popular method used by wealthy players to make money.

With the addition of the Grand Exchange, it is no longer simple for merchants to act as an intermediary between players who seek to easily sell and players who seek to easily buy — the Grand Exchange replaced this. Modern merchants, however, have found ways to work with and around the Grand Exchange to make money, including long-term investments, time-based arbitrage, price manipulation, "market value" to "street value" arbitrage, and item conversion.

label: merfolk
title: merfolk
lead:
Mermaids, also known as Merfolk, are an aquatic humanoid race that frequent the oceans of Gielinor. They have the upper body of a human and the lower body of a fish. A group of mermaids can be found living in the underwater area off the coast of Fossil Island. A merfolk skeleton can be assembled from fossils discovered across Fossil Island, suggesting that merfolk have lived in the area for long enough that their remains have been able to fossilize. Other mermaids can also be found all across the oceans, helping people research the depths of the ocean in exchange for answering their questions about the surface.

Merfolk are elusive beings and little is known about them. They shed pearls, known as Mermaid tears, when they cry, and their hair is strong enough to make fishing nets. Whether or not they are connected to Sirens, who mainly inhabit the Wushanko Isles, is unknown.

label: Merlin
title: Merlin
lead:
Merlin can be found on the of Camelot castle in his workshop, accessed via stairs in the entry room. Note that his (yellow) minimap icon does not show up until you are in his workshop. If the player has not completed the Merlin's Crystal quest, he will be imprisoned within a block-shaped crystal on the top floor of the south-east tower.

After successful completion of the Camelot training room, a player can speak to Merlin in order to change spawning point to Camelot instead of Falador or Lumbridge.

label: Merlin's Crystal
title: Merlin's Crystal
lead: Merlin's Crystal is the first quest in the Camelot quest series, and involves the player rescuing the wizard Merlin from a crystal.

label: Mermaid (disambiguation)
title: Mermaid (disambiguation)
lead: Mermaid may refer to:

label: Mermaid guide
title: Mermaid guide
lead: Mermaid guides are friendly mermaids that help the player chart the depths of the seas.

label: Mermaid storage unit
title: Mermaid storage unit
lead:
.]]

The mermaid storage unit was a location in a vast ocean south of Great Kourend. It is unknown what was here, aside from the assumption that mermaids inhabited these waters.

label: Merodach
title: Merodach
lead:
Merodach was an unreleased group boss developed around mid-2013, just months after the release of Old School RuneScape. The boss, a , was intended to be the Old School RuneScape equivalent of from RuneScape 3, having both combat and skilling aspects, as well as some sort of rage mechanic.

Merodach was developed out of Mod Reach's desire to create his own boss after having QA tested other bosses, as well as to have a place to put the white dragon equipment that he had created prior. He also wanted to create something that was more advanced than the typical "click and wait" that most bosses at the time were. However, the boss was not designed with the guarantee it would be added to the game, instead being more to test the limits of what can be done for future boss encounters.

label: Mervilla
title: Mervilla
lead:
Mervilla is a vampyre and one of the possible senders of a message to the player if they successfully complete the Theatre of Blood. Mervilla is not interested in the Theatre, but thinks her husband Amblor is, and thus she provides the player with supplies to keep her husband busy, so she can read her book in peace.

They are only mentioned in the message, and cannot be found anywhere in-game.

label: Message
title: Message
lead:
Message may refer to one of the following:

* Iorwerth's message, an item given to the player near the end of Regicide
* King's message, used to start the Regicide quest
* Message (Beneath Cursed Sands), an item given to the player after starting Beneath Cursed Sands
* Maisa's message, obtained from a messenger
* Message (fireplace), an item in Darkness of Hallowvale
* Message (Vertida), a message from Vertida Sefalatis to Veliaf Hurtz, also used in Darkness of Hallowvale
* Message (Theatre of Blood), a message received from chests in the Theatre of Blood
* Message (Romeo & Juliet), an item used in Romeo & Juliet
* Old man's message, an item that may be given by the Wise Old Man
* Pirate message, used in Pirate's Treasure
* Sealed message, a letter from Safalaan Hallow to Veliaf Hurtz, used in Darkness of Hallowvale

label: Message (Romeo & Juliet)
title: Message (Romeo & Juliet)
lead:
The Message is a quest item used only in Romeo & Juliet. It is obtained from Juliet after talking to her for the first time.

The player must deliver the letter to Romeo to progress the quest. It is possible to get another message and complete the quest by drop tricking. Only one copy of the message is taken when the player gives it to Romeo.

label: Messenger (disambiguation)
title: Messenger (disambiguation)
lead:
Messenger may refer to one of the following:
* Messengers, who delivered Maisa's message and Varlamore invitation to the player as announcements of new updates
* Guardian of Armadyl (messenger), who delivers an Armadyl communiqué to the player
* King's Messenger, who delivers the King's message to the player
* Messenger (The Frozen Door), who delivers an important letter to the player

label: Metal
title: Metal
lead:
In Old School RuneScape, metals are elements that are malleable, hard, and conduct magic in most cases (though metals such as elemental metal do not follow this rule). They are typically found in the weapons, armour, and equipment players use, but also in monsters as well.

Old School Runescape contains standard armour and weapons made out of most metals. Many of them can be made using the smithing skill, but a lot of them can only be bought or found elsewhere. The following is a list of standard weapons and armour:

label: Metal boots
title: Metal boots
lead:
Metal boots are a subtype of boots and pieces of gear in Old School RuneScape that are worn in the feet slot. They notably provide good defensive bonuses but are predominantly used for their strength bonus. Despite most of them being made out of the same metal used in Smithing, they cannot be made through the skill.

Almost all metal boots are obtained via defeating Slayer creatures, a boss, or doing Treasure Trails with the outliers being White boots and Dragonstone boots; which can be obtained through white knight rankings and opening the elven crystal chest.

label: Metal dragons/Strategies
title: Metal dragons/Strategies
lead:
Bronze, Iron, and Steel Metal dragons can be killed with all three combat styles.

As with chromatic dragons, metal dragons are weak to stab attacks and heavy ranged attacks. Unlike chromatic dragons, metal dragons are weak to Earth spells. Slayer masters can assign metal dragons, though many players tend to skip them, especially at lower levels where they do not have good gear, as metal dragons have higher Defence levels compared to their chromatic counterparts. If the player does not have any dragonbane weaponry, they are highly advised to use a magic setup, as they have a slightly lower Magic level compared to Defence, and they suffer 50% more damage and an extra 50% magic accuracy from earth spells.

label: Metal key
title: Metal key
lead:
The metal key is gained during and after the Tourist Trap quest. During the quest, it is first obtained by killing the Mercenary Captain in order to gain access to the main gate of the Desert Mining Camp.

This key can be placed on the steel key ring.

label: Metamorphosis
title: Metamorphosis
lead:
Metamorphosis is a feature available to some pets which can alter their appearance. This option can be unlocked by default, with consumable or one-time items, or after completing certain criteria depending on the pet.

Pets such as Kalphite princess do not require any items to metamorph, while the pet Beaver colour variants require specific logs every time you want to change its appearance AFTER unlocking the ability to do so with a funky shaped log. These visual appearances are visible to other players and are retained as long as the pet is in your possession, in the bank, or in a menagerie in your player-owned house, but can be temporarily reverted if the pet is lost on death.

label: Mezpah Arkan
title: Mezpah Arkan
lead:
Mezpah Arkan was the first ruler of the Arkan Dynasty, taking the place of Imafore Tullus roughly 100 years ago. His descendants have held the throne ever since, including the current Sun Queen, Zyanyi Arkan, and her son Prince Itzla. The Arkan family name originates from the Talkasti nomads, one of two groups who came together to form the modern Kingdom of Varlamore, along with the Pericans.

One of his acts as emperor was a decree that all statues of Imafore must be beheaded, but not removed, to remain as symbols of his betrayal. This law remains in effect in modern-day Fortis.

label: Mibbiwocket
title: Mibbiwocket
lead:
Mibbiwocket is a giant tortoise, one of many that are used by gnomes in battle. He is the oldest known tortoise and is at least 300 years old. He is currently cared for by the gnomish royal family. Mibbiwocket was presented to King Healthorg the Great, shortly after his birth, by the famous gnome explorer Admiral Bake sometime in the Fourth Age. He makes an appearance in Hazelmere's tale during The Eyes of Glouphrie, as part of Healthorg and tortoise.

Mibbiwocket is the correct answer to the Natural history quiz question: "What is the name of the oldest tortoise ever recorded?"

label: Mid-level plant (interface item)
title: Mid-level plant (interface item)
lead:
The Mid-level plant is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Thistle.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Midsummer event
title: Midsummer event
lead:
Midsummer events were annual holiday events that typically occurred towards the end of June.

Midsummer events were scrapped from 2018 onwards due to lack of available development time; as a result, rewards that were first available from Midsummer events were added to Diango's Toy Store.

label: Miles
title: Miles
lead: Miles is the brother of Giles and Niles. Like his brothers, he may appear to initiate the Certer random event, in which he will ask players to identify an item, such as a fish, with three possible choices of what the object is. If the player correctly identifies the item, Miles will give the player a reward of either coins, a gem (uncut, up to diamond), a cosmic talisman, a half key, a spinach roll, or a kebab.

label: Miles Away
title: Miles Away
lead:
Miles Away is a music track that can be unlocked outside Falador city walls, at the Falador Farm, Crafting Guild, and the Dark Wizards' Tower. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Long Way Home and Nightfall. It can also be unlocked in the Fisher Realm after partial completion of Holy Grail quest.

In Classic mode outside the Fisher Realm, the track plays at the Crafting Guild.

label: Mill
title: Mill
lead:
Mill may refer to:

*Windmill, any one of several buildings used to grind grain to make flour
*Sawmill, a building just north-east of Varrock where players can obtain planks

label: Mill (scenery)
title: Mill (scenery)
lead: Mills are animated scenery found on the middle floor of some windmills. Mills grind wheat into flour when the player interacts with the hopper controls.

label: Mill Lane Mill
title: Mill Lane Mill
lead:
Mill Lane Mill is a windmill on the road from Lumbridge to Draynor Village, just south of the Champions' Guild across the River Lum. Inside is Millie Miller who teaches the player how to make flour, for help during the Cook's Assistant quest.

On the of the mill is a flour bin where up to 30 pots worth of flour is collected after being milled, ready to be put in an empty pot. On the are millstones, which automatically grind grain into flour before sending it to the flour bin below. The has a hopper which is where grain is added. Hopper controls nearby must be operated to start the process for each grain in the hopper, sending it down to the millstones, then to the collection flour bin.

label: Milli Rehnison
title: Milli Rehnison
lead:
Milli Rehnison is a girl found upstairs of the Rehnison house in north-eastern West Ardougne. She is the daughter of Ted Rehnison and Martha Rehnison. She has a brother named Billy.

Players must speak to her for information on Elena during the Plague City quest.

label: millstones
title: millstones
lead: Millstones are animated scenery found on the middle floor of most windmills. Canonically, the millstones are there in order to grind wheat into flour. However, the player is not required to directly interact with millstones, other than noticing they exist on their way to the top floor, where there is a hopper.

label: mime
title: mime
lead: The Mime is an NPC that plays a role in the Mime random event. The player has to copy his movements to complete the event. He appears to be wearing the mime clothing with a beret mask.

label: Mime (Random Event)
title: Mime (Random Event)
lead:
The Mime is a random event in which the Mysterious Old Man appears and offers to teleport players to the mime artist's stage. The player must copy the mime's actions to complete the event. The mime will perform one of 8 emotes (Think, Laugh, Cry, Dance, Climb Rope, Lean, Glass Box, and Glass Wall) that the player will need to copy. If the player gets it right, they will Cheer, and if wrong, they will Cry. If the player takes too long to make a decision, then the mime will perform another emote for the player to guess.

Once the player has completed the event, they will be returned to the place they were before and will be rewarded with either one or two pieces of the mime outfit or one of the four mime emotes. If the player already has all of these, they will be rewarded with an experience lamp instead.

label: Mime boots
title: Mime boots
lead: Mime boots are an item gained from the Mime random event and are part of the mime outfit. They give no bonuses apart from their cosmetic appeal.

label: Mime gloves
title: Mime gloves
lead: Mime gloves are an item gained from the Mime random event and are part of the mime outfit. They give no bonuses apart from their cosmetic appeal.

label: Mime legs
title: Mime legs
lead: Mime legs is an item gained from the Mime random event and is part of the mime outfit. It gives no bonuses apart from its cosmetic appeal.

label: Mime mask
title: Mime mask
lead:
Mime mask is a head item gained from the Mime random event and is part of the mime outfit. It gives no bonuses apart from its cosmetic appeal.

It can be sewn with a black beret to make a beret mask by talking to Patchy, along with 500 coins. Doing so requires the completion of Cabin Fever and a book o' piracy. Once the mask has been sewn to a beret, completion of the Mime random event will once again reward players with a mime mask.

label: mime outfit
title: mime outfit
lead:
The mime outfit is given out when players complete the Mime random event. In the event, players have to repeat the mime's actions in order to return to where they originally were. The mime in the event is wearing a Beret mask, which is a combination of the mask and a beret. Members can obtain this item by talking to Patchy on Mos Le'Harmless whilst holding a mime mask and a Black beret from a Treasure Trail. Patchy will then sew these items together for 500 coins. This is only available to members.

The mime items are cosmetic and have no stat bonuses.

label: Mime top
title: Mime top
lead: Mime top is a reward from the Mime random event and is part of the mime outfit. It gives no bonuses apart from its cosmetic appeal.

label: Mind
title: Mind
lead: Mind may refer to:

label: Mind Altar
title: Mind Altar
lead:
The Mind Altar is a runic altar upon which mind runes are crafted from rune essence or pure essence, providing 5.5 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Level 2 Runecraft is required to craft mind runes.

Players may create a mind tiara here by using either a mind talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 27.5 Runecraft experience. A catalytic tiara can also be created here by using a catalytic talisman and gold tiara, granting 60 Runecraft experience.

label: Mind rune
title: Mind rune
lead:
The mind rune is used for the strike spells including Wind Strike, Water Strike, Earth Strike, and Fire Strike, as well as the Magic Dart spell.

Mind runes are craftable at level 2 Runecraft. Crafting mind runes provides 5.5 Runecraft experience per rune or pure essence used. Using mind cores in place of essences will yield an increased amount of mind runes. Members can also use Warped extracts to increase the quantity of crafted mind runes by 250 per pure essence, requiring partial completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire and access to the Scar essence mine.

label: Mind talisman
title: Mind talisman
lead:
The mind talisman is a talisman used to access the Mind Altar located between Ice Mountain and Goblin Village. It can be combined with a tiara to make a mind tiara for 27.5 Runecraft experience at the Mind Altar by using the tiara on the altar. This makes the talisman disappear, but the tiara can be used in just the same way and can be worn.

One is required to create a mind tiara for the Easy Falador Diary.

label: Mindslayers
title: Mindslayers
lead:
The Mindslayers are a race of intelligent, tree-like humanoids, located in the realm of Zanaris. Very few members of this race appear in-game.

The only mindslayers to appear in-game have taken on the job of the Gatekeepers of Zanaris, guarding the entrances to the Zanaris Market and the Shady Grove, the lair of Tanglefoot and Baby tanglefootii. In-game, they are merely referred to as gatekeepers.

label: Mine cart
title: Mine cart
lead:
.]]
A mine cart or minecart is a large rolling bucket used for transporting items, players, and NPCs.

Mine cart may refer to:

label: Mine Cart (Desert Mining Camp)
title: Mine Cart (Desert Mining Camp)
lead:
The Mine Cart is a scenery object found at the Desert Mining Camp Underground during and after the Tourist Trap quest, used to rescue Ana. Players can use it as a means of transportation by clicking the Search option.

When riding the cart, it temporarily occupies the feet slot, seemingly making your boots disappear. They will reappear at the end of the ride.

label: Mine cart (Dwarven Mine)
title: Mine cart (Dwarven Mine)
lead: Mine carts are decorative scenery found within the Dwarven Mine. The carts can be searched, resulting in the player finding nothing within them.

label: mine cart driver
title: mine cart driver
lead: The Mine cart driver is in the Desert Mining Camp, near the camel cart. He plays a role in The Tourist Trap quest. The player will ride his mine cart with Ana in a barrel in order to save her from the mines. The player will have to compliment him in order to not get caught with Ana.

label: Minecart network
title: Minecart network
lead:
Minecart network may refer to:

*Keldagrim minecart system
*Lovakengj Minecart Network

label: Miner
title: Miner
lead:
Miner may refer to

*Mining
*Cave goblin miner

Mines are areas where ores for Mining can be found. These may be above ground or underground and are scattered around Gielinor. Some of these locations are accessible only after certain quests are complete and some are members-only.

label: Minigames
title: Minigames
lead:
Minigames are small games in which players (or a team of players) set out to complete a certain objective. These games usually allow players to gain experience and/or items. They are identified with a red star icon on the world map. Minigames can be repeated, unlike quests or miniquests which can only be completed once. There are four free-to-play minigames, which are all notably PvP minigames: Emir's Arena, Clan Wars, Castle Wars, and Last Man Standing.

Players can teleport to minigames using the Minigame Teleport spell on any spellbook provided they meet the requirement for the selected minigame. This teleport has a 20 minute cooldown and cannot be cast from PvP worlds, the Wilderness, or Emir's Arena.

label: Minimap
title: Minimap
lead:
The Minimap (also called mini-map in Old School RuneScape documentation) is the area of the game interface in the upper-right of the screen. It shows a bird's eye view of the player's surrounding area, with the player at the centre.

The minimap appears as an approximately circular area with a 19 square-length radius (see below). White lines represent walls, fences, etc., although a red marker indicates a door or other penetrable features. Coloured dots act as markers to identify nearby items, players, monsters and NPCs (see below). Certain buildings and features (such as water sources) are marked by icons. Quest start points are also shown on the minimap.

label: Mining
title: Mining
lead: Mining is a skill that allows players to obtain ores and gems from rocks. The higher a player's Mining level is the more likely they are to successfully extract ore. With ores, a player can then either smelt bars and make equipment using the Smithing skill or sell them for profit. Mining areas are identified with a regular pickaxe icon, and mining shops are identified with a gold pickaxe icon on the minimap and world map.

label: Mining enhancers
title: Mining enhancers
lead: Mining enhancers are items that aid the player in Mining. Their benefits range from invisible mining boosts, to giving a chance to mining an extra ore from a rock. The effects of mining enhancers stack with each other when worn.

label: Mining gloves (disambiguation)
title: Mining gloves (disambiguation)
lead:
Mining gloves may refer to:

*Mining gloves
*Superior mining gloves
*Expert mining gloves

label: Mining Guild
title: Mining Guild
lead:
The Mining Guild, located in and beneath Falador, is a guild for expert miners available to players with at least 60 Mining (can be boosted). The mine is accessible from either the Mining Guild's above-ground complex in the south-east of the city, or through the gate at the southern end of the Dwarven Mine. Both of these entrances are guarded by dwarves who will answer questions about the guild and stop players without the requirements from entering the guild. The guildmaster, Gadrin, also sells the Mining cape to those who have achieved level 99 Mining.

This mine is one of many where three iron rocks can be mined without moving, thus ideal for power-mining.

label: Mining Instructor
title: Mining Instructor
lead: The Mining instructor on Tutorial Island (named Dezzick) is the fifth NPC that a beginning player meets in Old School RuneScape. He informs players about Mining and Smithing skills by teaching them how to make bronze items.

label: Mining Level Up!
title: Mining Level Up!
lead: Mining Level Up! is a jingle for levelling Mining.

label: Mining Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Mining Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Mining Level Up! (Unlocks) is a jingle for levelling Mining.

label: mining shops
title: mining shops
lead: Mining shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Mining shops sell items used in the Mining skill. There are twelve Mining shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Mining/Experience table
title: Mining/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Mining in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Mining level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: Miniquests
title: Miniquests
lead:
Miniquests 
Miniquests are groups of objectives that, unlike quests, have no icon on the world map and offer no quest points upon completion. There will also be no indication of starting nor completing a miniquest, other than what is written in the corresponding Quest List journal entry. There are a total of 19 miniquests, which are all members-only.

title: Miracle Dance

label: mirror
title: mirror
lead: A mirror is used in the Nature Spirit quest to prove to Filliman Tarlock that he is dead. It can be found under the washing bowl on a bench near the entrance to the Nature Grotto south of the Mort Myre Swamp. It is also obtainable after the quest, but it serves no purpose.

label: Miscellaneous key
title: Miscellaneous key
lead: Miscellaneous key is a quest item obtained during the Heroes' Quest from Grip. It is used to access the windowed room in Scarface Pete's mansion in Brimhaven. From here a second player can kill Grip using a Ranged attack, and the first player, the one doing the quest, is then able to retrieve Grips' key from the body. This is one of the keys that cannot be held on a steel key ring.

label: Missable content
title: Missable content
lead:
Missable content is a community-given term for in-game content (items, unlocks, dialogue) that can become permanently inaccessible on an account after a certain point, often without any prior indication that this will be the case.

While the Old School RuneScape developers generally try to avoid creating missable content, for example by giving the players the items from previous holidays upon completion of a holiday event, or through various game updates which have made certain items re-obtainable after being discovered to be missable, many pieces of missable content still remain.

label: Mission report
title: Mission report
lead:
Mission reports are three different items, all used in the Cold War quest. They are:
*Mission report (Ardougne), given to the player by a Penguin in Ardougne Zoo after greeting him.
*Mission report (Lumbridge), given to the player by the penguins dressed as a sheep after giving them the secret phrase.
*Mission report (Fake), given to the player by Noodle after trading him swamp tar and 5 feathers.

label: Misthalin
title: Misthalin
lead: Misthalin ( ) is a major kingdom within Gielinor and is currently ruled by King Roald III and Queen Ellamaria. Misthalin is the most powerful human nation and by far the oldest, having existed prominently since the late Fourth Age, and its capital, Varrock, having existed in some form since soon after the end of the God Wars. It is divided in half by the River Lum, and its eastern border with Morytania is the River Salve.

lead:

label: Misthalin–Morytania War
title: Misthalin–Morytania War
lead:
The Misthalin–Morytania War was a conflict between the vampyres of Morytania and the Varrockian army. After taking over all of Hallowvale in the Third Age, Lord Drakan wanted to expand his borders, so he crossed the River Salve and waged war on the Kingdom of Misthalin.

At first, the human kingdom could not stop Lord Drakan's forces, and Lord Drakan made steady progress towards Varrock. Fearing defeat, a group of Seven Priestly Warriors banded together and, with a blessing from Saradomin, inspired the Misthalin defenders to push back Lord Drakan's army.

label: mithril
title: mithril
lead:
Mithril may refer to:
*Mithril bar, the Smithing material
*Mithril dragons, the third strongest tier of the six metallic dragons
*Mithril equipment, the equipable pieces of gear
*Mithril ore, the product of Mining a mithril rock
*Mithril rocks, the rock the player obtains mithril ore from
*Mithril seeds, the seed that grows flowers

label: Mithril 2h sword
title: Mithril 2h sword
lead:
The mithril 2h sword is a two-handed sword made of mithril. As with all mithril weaponry, it requires 20 Attack to wield.

At level 64 Smithing, players can make one from three mithril bars, granting 150 Smithing experience. Players can also purchase one from a few shops, including Gaius' Two Handed Shop in Taverley and Gulluck and Sons in the Grand Tree.

label: Mithril arrow
title: Mithril arrow
lead:
Mithril arrows are arrows made of mithril, are stackable, and can be used with any standard bow of willow or stronger. Stronger than steel arrows, mithril arrows can be made at level 45 Fletching by using mithril arrowtips on headless arrows. Doing so grants 112.5 experience for every batch of 15 arrows made. As with most arrows, they can be poisoned.

Mithril arrows can be purchased from Lowe's Archery Emporium in Varrock, or Brian's Archery Supplies in Rimmington.

label: Mithril arrowtips
title: Mithril arrowtips
lead:
Mithril arrowtips are made with a mithril bar requiring 55 Smithing, yielding 50 Smithing experience and 15 mithril arrowtips. They are made into mithril arrows when used with headless arrows, requiring 45 Fletching, yielding 112.5 experience per 15 arrows.

They are purchased for coins at the ranging shops: Hickton's Archery Emporium in Catherby, Dargaud's Bow and Arrows in the Ranging Guild, Gulluck and Sons on the of the Grand Tree, and Void Knight Archery Store at the Void Knights' Outpost. They are purchased for coins at the Armoury in the Combat Training Camp.

label: Mithril axe
title: Mithril axe
lead:
A mithril axe is an axe stronger than the black axe, and weaker than the adamant axe. Like all mithril weapons, it requires level 20 Attack to wield. It can be used in combat or in Woodcutting to cut trees. To cut a tree with this axe, a player must have 21 Woodcutting.

The success rate for chopping a log is approximately 250% that of the Bronze axe, or 11% better than a Black axe.

label: Mithril axe head
title: Mithril axe head
lead:
The mithril axe head is an unobtainable item that was originally used in the axe handle random event. The axe head would become detached from the player's mithril axe while Woodcutting. To fix their axe, players had to collect the axe head off the ground and reattach it to the axe handle.

A similar event used to happen to players while Mining, but with a pickaxe head and pickaxe handle.

label: Mithril bar
title: Mithril bar
lead:
A Mithril bar is a bar of refined mithril ore. It can be created through the Smithing skill by using a mithril ore and 4 pieces of coal on a furnace, granting 30 experience. The Superheat Item spell can also be used to make mithril bars. Both ways of creating mithril bars require level 50 Smithing. It can also be created in the Blast Furnace, which can be considerably cheaper as it halves the amount of coal needed.

A mithril bar can be smithed on an anvil by using the Smithing skill to create mithril weapons and armour, granting 50 Smithing experience per bar used. A list of mithril items that can be smithed from mithril bars and the Smithing levels required can be found at Smithing tables.

label: Mithril battleaxe
title: Mithril battleaxe
lead:
A mithril battleaxe is a battleaxe made from 3 mithril bars, requiring 60 Smithing, yielding 150 Smithing experience. 20 Attack is required to wield it. It is stronger than the black battleaxe, but weaker than the adamant battleaxe.

Players can purchase it from Brian's Battleaxe Bazaar in Port Sarim, Bob's Brilliant Axes in Lumbridge, or Gulluck and Sons in the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

label: Mithril chainbody
title: Mithril chainbody
lead:
The Mithril chainbody is a chainbody made out of mithril. As with all mithril armour, it requires 20 Defence to wear.

Like all chainbodies, it provides better Crush defence than a platebody made of the same material, at the cost of lower Stab and Slash defence.

label: Mithril claws
title: Mithril claws
lead:
Mithril claws are a two-handed melee weapon that are member's only. To wield them the player must have at least level 20 Attack.

Mithril claws can be created by using 2 mithril bars on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory after completing the Death Plateau quest. This requires level 63 in Smithing, and grants the player 100 Smithing experience.

label: mithril dagger
title: mithril dagger
lead: The mithril dagger is a dagger made out of mithril. Mithril daggers can be smithed from a single mithril bar at level 50 Smithing. Each mithril dagger created grants 50 experience. Mithril daggers are the fifth strongest daggers, the next strongest being the adamant dagger. Like all mithril weapons, mithril daggers require 20 Attack to wield. As with most daggers, this weapon can be poisoned. Players can purchase this dagger from the Varrock Swordshop.

label: Mithril dart
title: Mithril dart
lead:
Mithril darts are Ranged throwing weapons made from mithril that are only available to members. Mithril darts require level 20 Ranged to wield. They can be obtained by either using the Smithing and Fletching skills or trading with another player. Mithril darts can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Mithril darts are one of the most cost effective Ranged training weapons for lower level players, as they have an extremely quick rate of fire and cost very little compared to similar training methods like throwing knives or arrows. They can be bought in large numbers from the Grand Exchange, costing less than half of what similar tier ranged ammunition costs.

label: Mithril dart tip
title: Mithril dart tip
lead:
A mithril dart tip is a dart tip made with the Smithing skill. Players can smith this item when using a mithril bar on an anvil with a hammer in the inventory and 54 Smithing. Each bar makes 10 mithril dart tips and yields 50 experience. They can be fletched into mithril darts at level 52 Fletching when used with feathers, granting 112 Fletching experience per 10 darts made.

To smith darts, the Tourist Trap must be started and progressed to the point where the player returns to the Bedabin Camp with the weapon plans.

label: Mithril dragon/Strategies
title: Mithril dragon/Strategies
lead: At level 304, mithril dragons are the third strongest tier of metal dragons. They attack from all sides of the Combat triangle in addition to utilising extra long-ranged dragonfire. Players seeking to kill these powerful dragons will need to tank at least one combat style, or two when fighting within Melee distance.

label: Mithril equipment
title: Mithril equipment
lead: Mithril equipment are items made from mithril metal. Mithril equipment is stronger than black equipment, but weaker than adamant equipment. All mithril items are coloured with a dark shade of blue. Mithril armour requires 20 Defence to equip, and mithril weapons require 20 Attack. They are notably popular due to being lighter than equipment made of other conventional metals, while still providing a fair amount of bonuses.

label: Mithril fire arrow
title: Mithril fire arrow
lead:
Mithril fire arrows are mithril arrows wrapped in an oily cloth, which are then lit by using them on a tinderbox. They, along with any other fire arrow, are primarily used to pierce the rope in the Underground Pass to lower the bridge so that a player may walk across.

They have the same Ranged Strength as regular mithril arrows.

label: Mithril full helm
title: Mithril full helm
lead: The mithril full helm is the fourth best full helmet. It requires 20 Defence to equip. It offers better defensive stats than its med helm counterpart, at the cost of having lower magic and ranged attack, and greater weight. One can be made by a player with level 57 Smithing at any anvil with a hammer and 2 mithril bars.

label: Mithril gold-trimmed armour
title: Mithril gold-trimmed armour
lead: Mithril gold-trimmed armour is a possible reward from medium Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to Mithril armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Mithril javelin
title: Mithril javelin
lead:
The mithril javelin is a type of member's only Ranged ammunition used by the light and heavy ballistas. As with most javelins, they can be poisoned.

They can be fletched by attaching mithril javelin tips to javelin shafts at level 47 Fletching, granting 120 experience per 15 javelins made. They can also be obtained by buying them from the Ranging Guild, the Void Knight Archery Store or from Oobapohk's Javelin Store after Monkey Madness II.

label: Mithril kiteshield
title: Mithril kiteshield
lead: The mithril kiteshield is the third best smithable kiteshield, requiring 20 Defence to wield. A player with 62 Smithing can make the shield by using three mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 150 Smithing experience.

label: Mithril knife
title: Mithril knife
lead:
The mithril knife is a throwing knife that requires a Ranged level of 20 to wield. It is stronger than a black knife but weaker than an adamant knife. To create mithril knives, the player must have at least 57 Smithing. Each mithril bar will create 5 mithril knives and give the player 50 Smithing experience. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with a shield or god book for protection.

Throwing knives are among the fastest weapons in the game (along with darts), and are commonly used for PKing or training Ranged.

label: Mithril longsword
title: Mithril longsword
lead: The mithril longsword is a longsword that is stronger than the black longsword/White longsword, but weaker than the adamant longsword. Like all other mithril weapons, it requires an Attack level of 20 to wield. Players can make a mithril longsword with a Smithing level of 56 using two mithril bars, granting 100 experience. Players can purchase this longsword from the Varrock Swordshop.

label: Mithril mace
title: Mithril mace
lead:
The mithril mace is a mace made of mithril. Like all mithril weapons, it requires 20 Attack to wield, and is exclusively used in melee combat.

Players can make a mithril mace with the Smithing skill at level 52 by using a mithril bar on an anvil with a hammer in their inventory, giving the player 50 Smithing experience.

label: Mithril med helm
title: Mithril med helm
lead: The mithril med helm is a medium helmet made of mithril. This helm requires 20 Defence to wear. It provides more protection than its bronze, iron and steel counterparts. It can be made at level 53 Smithing using a mithril bar.

label: mithril ore
title: mithril ore
lead:
Mithril ore can be mined at level 55 Mining providing 80 Mining experience. After mithril rocks are mined, it will take two minutes until it reappears. Mithril ore is used with four coal to smelt mithril bars. Smelting a mithril bar gives 30 Smithing experience.

Wearing either superior mining gloves or expert mining gloves while mining a mithril rock makes the rock not deplete upon mining mithril, allowing you to mine one or two additional ore, respectively, before depleting.

label: Mithril pick head
title: Mithril pick head
lead:
A mithril pick head was obtained as part of a discontinued random event, in which the mithril pickaxe head flew off the handle while the player was mining. To fix it, the player had to collect it off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

If players were not paying attention when this occurred, the head would disappear from the ground or be picked up by another player, requiring them to purchase another.

label: Mithril pickaxe
title: Mithril pickaxe
lead:
The mithril pickaxe is a pickaxe that is weaker than the adamant pickaxe. It requires an Attack level of 20 to wield, and a Mining level of 21 to mine with. It mines on a 5-tick cycle, 1-tick faster than the steel pickaxe and the same speed as the black pickaxe.

It is also one of the lightest pickaxes in the game (although heavier than the black pickaxe), making it ideal for activities such as training Runecraft via the Abyss.

label: Mithril platebody
title: Mithril platebody
lead:
The mithril platebody is an armour used in melee with stat bonuses between steel and adamant (not including the black and white platebodies). It requires 20 Defence to equip and provides greater protection than a mithril chainbody. Like all platebodies, however, it gives a crippling negative bonus to the user's Ranged and Magic stats.

Players with level 68 Smithing can make one by using 5 mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 250 Smithing experience. Alternatively, they can be bought from a handful of armour shops.

label: Mithril platelegs
title: Mithril platelegs
lead: Mithril platelegs are the third best free-to-play platelegs. They require level 20 Defence to equip. A player with 66 Smithing can make it by using three mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 150 Smithing experience. Mithril platelegs offer similar stats to a mithril plateskirt but weigh more.

label: Mithril plateskirt
title: Mithril plateskirt
lead: Mithril plateskirts give the fifth best stat bonuses of all plateskirts. This piece of armour can be made with Level 66 Smithing by using 3 mithril bars on an anvil, therefore granting the player with 150 smithing experience. At least 20 Defence is required to wear it. Mithril plateskirts have similar stats to mithril platelegs but weigh less.

label: mithril rocks
title: mithril rocks
lead:
Mithril rocks are a rock that can be mined through the Mining skill to obtain mithril ore in various places throughout Gielinor. Mithril rocks can be mined with a Mining level of 55 or higher, granting 80 Mining experience and one mithril ore.

Hobgoblin Mine in level 30-35 Wilderness contains the greatest amount of mithril rocks. It also has several adamantite rocks, but like all Wilderness locations, player killers are always on the prowl, so take necessary precautions, and never bring anything you can't afford losing.

label: Mithril scimitar
title: Mithril scimitar
lead: The Mithril scimitar is a scimitar stronger than the black scimitar. Like all mithril weapons, it requires 20 Attack to wield. It can only be used in combat. Players can make a mithril scimitar with the Smithing skill at level 55 using 2 mithril bars, giving 100 experience.

label: Mithril seeds
title: Mithril seeds
lead:
Mithril seeds are a magical type of seed that can be planted almost anywhere to grow some flowers in the ground, and are purchasable from the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items.

Upon planting the seeds, the player will move one adjacent square west if possible; if there's an obstacle preventing movement to the west, the flowers will attempt to move the player to the east first, then south, then north. Once the flower is grown, players are then given the option to pick them, producing one of nine different colours of flowers.

title: Mithril shield

Mithril shield may refer to:

*Mithril kiteshield

label: Mithril spear
title: Mithril spear
lead: The mithril spear is a two-handed melee weapon made from mithril requiring 20 Attack to wield. Mithril spears are a members-only weapon. It can be bought from the Mount Karuulm Weapon Shop or Fortis Blacksmith, or obtained as a drop from monsters. Using the Smithing skill, players can create mithril spears on one of the barbarian anvils in either Otto's Grotto or Barbarian Village. However, players must have begun Barbarian Smithing training to be able to smith these spears. Like most spears, the mithril spear can be poisoned.

label: Mithril sq shield
title: Mithril sq shield
lead:
A mithril square shield is the fourth strongest square shield. Players with level 58 Smithing can make the shield by using two mithril bars on an anvil while carrying a hammer, granting 100 Smithing experience.

This shield can be bought from Raum Urda-Stein on Jatizso. This shield provides less defence than the mithril kiteshield, but is much lighter. As with all pieces of mithril armour, it requires 20 Defence to wield.

label: Mithril sword
title: Mithril sword
lead:
The Mithril sword is a sword stronger than the black sword. It requires 20 Attack to wield.

Players can make this sword at level 54 Smithing by using one mithril bar and a hammer on an anvil, granting 50 experience. It can also be purchased from the Varrock Swordshop.

label: Mithril thrownaxe
title: Mithril thrownaxe
lead: The mithril thrownaxe is a Ranged throwing weapon. To wield a mithril throwing axe the player must have at least 20 Ranged. They can be obtained either by buying from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or trading with another player. The mithril throwing axe can be wielded with a shield or prayer book for protection.

label: Mithril trimmed armour
title: Mithril trimmed armour
lead: Mithril trimmed armour is a possible reward from medium Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to Mithril armour. The armour pieces cannot be made via the Smithing skill.

label: Mithril trophy
title: Mithril trophy

label: Mithril warhammer
title: Mithril warhammer
lead:
The mithril warhammer is a warhammer stronger than the black warhammer, being made out of mithril. It may be used as an effective way of killing monsters weak to crush, such as earth warriors. Unlike other mithril weapons, it requires level 20 in Strength to wield.

Players can make a mithril warhammer with the Smithing skill at level 59 using 3 mithril bars, giving the player 150 Smithing experience. Members can purchase this warhammer from Skulgrimen's Battle Gear in Rellekka, and Vigr's Warhammers in Keldagrim.

label: Mixed chemicals
title: Mixed chemicals
lead: Mixed chemicals are used in the The Dig Site to create the chemical compound. It is made by combining nitroglycerin with ammonium nitrate, granting 2 Herblore experience. The chemicals can then be combined with ground charcoal, granting 2.5 Herblore experience, to make step 2 of the compound. Finally, it can be combined with an arcenia root to make the chemical compound, granting 3 Herblore experience. Due to the nitroglycerin, dropping the mixed chemicals will cause an explosion that destroy the item and deals a significant amount of damage to the player. The chemicals deal 45 damage after step 1, or 55 damage after the addition of ground charcoal in step 2, but the damage is not lethal.
