label: Mixed flowers
title: Mixed flowers
lead:
Mixed flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds. They can also be purchased from the Flower Girl in Miscellania.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

label: Mixed hide armour
title: Mixed hide armour
lead:
Mixed hide armour is a set of ranged armour obtained either through Crafting with Mixed hide bases or by having Pellem in the Hunter Guild make them. Pellem will create your desired piece of armour when provided the required furs and 20,000gp per piece. The only exception on price is for the boots at 17,500gp. Players need 46 Hunter to access Pellem's hide-making services.

Requiring level 60 Ranged and 50 Defence, the armour set boasts some melee strength bonuses that complement the hunter's spear. The legs have no Defence level requirement, similar to dragonhide armour. The set's low cost and relatively high stats make it a popular low-risk choice for activities in the Wilderness.

label: Mizzarch

label: Mod Reach
title: Mod Reach
lead:
Mod Reach is a former Content Developer at Jagex. He was one of the primary architects and internal campaigners for Old School RuneScape, alongside Mod Ash & Mod Nexus. Mod Reach was also the Bug Abuse Lead Curator for the studio, a position previously and infamously held by Mod Chrisso, and was responsible for overseeing Jagex's response to minor and major exploits found within both RuneScape and Old School RuneScape.

Mod Reach has stated that he campaigned internally for a "2006 nostalgia version of RuneScape" soon after joining Jagex in 2010 before colleagues dismissed his suggestions and joked he should "go back to the rants forum", a reference to a largely unmoderated section of the RuneScape Forums where trolls would often frequent. He has also stated he was often seen as a controversial figure, due to his stance on speaking openly and honestly about his thoughts and feelings towards Old School RuneScape and management at Jagex who he believed were frequently "undermining the efforts and hard work of the Old School RuneScape team" by limiting their access to internal resources and curbing visibility of Old School RuneScape at RuneFest by "electing staff from RuneScape 3 to hand out Golden Gnome Awards to those who competed in challenges specific to Old School RuneScape".

label: Molten glass
title: Molten glass
lead:
Molten glass is used in the Crafting and Construction skills, as well as some quests, to form glass items. It is created through the Crafting skill by using a bucket of sand and soda ash on a furnace, granting 20 Crafting experience. This only requires level 1 Crafting. Alternatively, players can use the Lunar spell Superglass Make, which combines all buckets of sand and all seaweed or soda ash in the player's inventory into molten glass, granting 10 Crafting experience per pair of items.

Molten glass is used in some quests such as Observatory Quest, Horror from the Deep, Wanted!, Desert Treasure I, Another Slice of H.A.M. and The Fremennik Exiles. Although molten glass cannot be bought in any shop, buckets of sand and soda ash are available from the charter ship shops. This is especially useful for ironmen, who could buy both items and then smelt them in a furnace. For larger amounts, giant seaweed and sandstone are efficient sources of the materials required; as a result, making and blowing glass is a common method of training Crafting.

label: Money making guide/Creating eternal glories
title: Money making guide/Creating eternal glories
lead:
To efficiently charge glories to try and create an eternal glory, first buy or create a large amount of uncharged amulets of glory, then prepare gear and inventory to begin. Wield the Wilderness sword 4, an uncharged amulet of glory, and possibly some black dragonhide armour, then fill your inventory with 28 uncharged amulets of glory. Use the Wilderness sword's teleport option to go directly to the Fountain of Rune (preferably without being seen, as the teleport has a unique animation that a PKer could follow you with), use one of the glories on it, then run out of the peninsula and north towards the level 50 Wilderness obelisk, near the Rogues' Castle. Ensure your selected teleport is to somewhere below level 30 Wilderness, such as Ferox Enclave. Immediately after teleporting with the obelisk, use your equipped amulet of glory to teleport to Edgeville to bank, storing all 28 charged amulets of glory and getting new uncharged ones.

Without the elite Wilderness Diary completed, the closest teleport to the Fountain of Rune is an Annakarl teleport tablet, costing per trip and taking 1 less glory to the fountain, making each trip worth . Returning to the bank will take longer without at least the hard Wilderness Diary completed to direct the obelisk, needing to either repeatedly teleport with the obelisk or simply run south to level 30 Wilderness.

label: Money making guide/Killing The Nightmare
title: Money making guide/Killing The Nightmare
lead:
5-man is a very common group size for killing the Nightmare; however, smaller group sizes are possible and will achieve similar profit. Although the kills per hour will be lower, the chance of an individual party member receiving a drop is greater.
All profit from The Nightmare comes from the unique drops, whereby the staff, mace and armour table has a ~1/85 chance to roll per kill, and the orb table a 1/320 chance per kill. When either of these tables are rolled, a random party member is chosen to receive the drop, weighted by the total damage dealt by each party member.

The chance of receiving a drop from either of these tables per kill is 1%, or 0.75% excluding the Nightmare Staff

lead: It is worth noting that you can minimize the cost of the pineapple rings by buying whole pineapples and cutting them into rings yourself. This reduces the cost down to approximately 92,500GP if buying from the G.E. and 3,125GP if buying from the charter ship traders(the closest one to a bank is Port Khazard). You would need to purchase 625 pineapples in order to make 2,500 pineapple pizzas, as each pineapple gives you 4 rings. This requires a knife. To make the process of cutting them into rings as efficient as possible; as well as to avoid losing any of the rings; set your banks custom quantity to 6 and only do that many at a time. While being more cost effective, this method is far more time consuming and click intensive.

label: Money making guide/Mining gemstones
title: Money making guide/Mining gemstones
lead:
If a player has obtained the gem bag from the Motherlode Mine they can use it to save inventory space by storing standard uncut gems. This can be combined with fletching uncut opal and uncut jade into bolt tips, leaving the remaining 24 inventory spaces to be filled with uncut red topaz, maximising profit in the above ground mine. In the underground section where it is possible to mine continuously, using a gem bag should increase experience and profit by roughly 2% through time saved between inventory deposits without tick manipulation.

Players who have completed the Medium Karamja Diary gain access to the underground portion of the gem mine, which has an additional 48 gem rocks, and a Bank Deposit Chest. With tick manipulation at high efficiency, mining in the underground section of the mine at 99 Mining can yield 105,000-115,000 Mining experience and up to 1,650 gems per hour, totaling up to profit.

label: Money making guide/Temple Trekking
title: Money making guide/Temple Trekking
lead:
Escort hard companions along Route One. The aim is to complete runs as quickly as possible to maximize the number of nail beast encounters, so use the evade-encounter left-click option to skip any other combat encounters. Repeat this back and forth between Paterdomus and Burgh de Rott.

Use reward tokens on bow strings, giving a minimum of 100 bow strings per run. Alternatively, use the tokens on XP tomes for early progression of Agility, Firemaking, Fishing, Mining, Slayer, Thieving, and Woodcutting while still earning profit from the nail beast nails. Assuming 35 successful easy treks per hour, this would net a player roughly 40,000 XP across the seven possible skills (5,700 XP per skill per hour on average) on top of the XP gained during combat.

lead:
Most of the profit from Theatre (nearly 90%) comes from the raid's unique drops. The chance of a unique being received is 10.99% for a deathless raid regardless of group size, and is decreased for every death and per skipped room (which is 0 for nearly all raids). Upon receiving a unique drop, it is given to one of the players in the raid at random (with the MVP having a higher chance). The weighting for unique drops is:

label: monk
title: monk
lead:
Monks are worshippers of Saradomin who live in monasteries, churches, and on the island of Entrana. Monks will heal the player 2 + 20% of their Hitpoints if the player talks to them and asks them to do so, unless on a PvP world. Monks at the Ardougne Monastery do not provide this option.

Monks will occasionally heal themselves 2 Hitpoints at random intervals in combat. They are useful for training on at lower combat levels, as players can talk to another monk and request healing. Because monks can survive small amounts of damage, it's possible for a defence pure to train on the same monk indefinitely.

label: Monk (Lost City)
title: Monk (Lost City)
lead: The Monk is part of a band of adventurers searching for Zanaris. The Monk and his three companions, an archer, a wizard, and a warrior, can be found in the north-west part of the Lumbridge Swamp, near the Draynor bank. He is a part of the Lost City quest.

label: Monk of Entrana
title: Monk of Entrana
lead:
Monks of Entrana are NPCs that must be talked to in order to sail back and forth between Port Sarim and Entrana, as long as the player has no weapons or armour.

They will allow you to carry magic secateurs, as they do not count them as a weapon. They cannot be talked to on a non-member account.

label: Monk of Zamorak
title: Monk of Zamorak
lead:
Monks of Zamorak are evil clerics that follow Zamorak, god of chaos. They are found in several locations, including the Asgarnian Chaos Temple, Taverley Dungeon, Paterdomus Temple, Battlefield mine and Deep Wilderness Dungeon. A level 17 monk of Zamorak is in a cage under the stairs on the of Varrock Palace. He is often used in free-to-play servers to train magic using the Curse spell.

Despite them being feared, they are extremely useful for Ranged training as they are weak towards Ranged and there are many safespots. The Chaos Temple is also a useful spot because there is an altar located in the temple for Prayer. The monks in Paterdomus Temple provide less experience than regular monsters, providing players with only a quarter of the usual experience gained from dealing damage.

label: Monk's Friend
title: Monk's Friend
lead: Monk's Friend is a short novice quest in which the monks of the Ardougne Monastery ask you to do them a couple of favours, allowing them to throw a party without any setbacks.

label: monk's robe
title: monk's robe
lead: Monk's robe is a part of Monk's robes and is found lying on the table upstairs in the Edgeville Monastery, which requires a Prayer level of at least 31 to enter. The monk's robe bottom provides a +5 Prayer bonus while having no requirements to wear.

label: Monk's robe top
title: Monk's robe top
lead: Monk's robe top is a part of Monk's robes and can be found lying on the table upstairs in the Edgeville Monastery, which requires a Prayer level of 31 to enter. The monk's robe top is useful in that it provides a +6 Prayer bonus while having no requirements to wear.

label: monk's robes
title: monk's robes
lead: Monk's robes are a set of robes (top & bottom) made to honour Saradomin that are found on the of the Edgeville Monastery north-east of Falador and just slightly north-west of the Barbarian Village between Ice Mountain and Edgeville. Each piece can be worn independently of one another. Monk's robes reduce the Prayer point cost of any Prayers the wearer has activated by means of a Prayer bonus. The robes are worn by monks, and are popular with player and monster killers due to their high Prayer bonus and low cost of acquisition. Monk's robes are particularly popular with free-to-play players and combat pures as they have no quest or level requirements and are free to players who have at least level 31 Prayer, required to access the Monastery.

label: Monkey
title: Monkey
lead:
Monkeys are an animal species native to certain islands on Gielinor, namely Karamja, Mos Le'Harmless, and Ape Atoll, although they can also be found in the Ardougne Zoo.

In Old School RuneScape, 'monkey' is used to refer to any primate and is often used interchangeably with 'ape'.

label: Monkey (disambiguation)
title: Monkey (disambiguation)
lead:
Monkey can mean any of the following:

* Monkey, the species.

label: Monkey (monster)
title: Monkey (monster)
lead:
Monkeys are small, level 3 monsters that may be found in a variety of locations. They are not ideal for training combat, as they have a low amount of hitpoints and have few useful drops. However, monkey bones do give slightly more Prayer experience than regular bones.

During the Tai Bwo Wannai Trio quest, all monkeys located on Karamja cannot be damaged by Melee attacks (with the exception of using a halberd to attack from beyond the monkey's melee range) as the player will be unable to touch them, rendering Magic and Ranged as the only ways to kill them. This only occurs during the quest; before and after the quest they can be damaged by all attacks. It is not possible to kill them using rings of recoil as they do not attack back during the quest.

label: Monkey bar (disambiguation)
title: Monkey bar (disambiguation)
lead: Monkey bars may refer to:

label: Monkey bars (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
title: Monkey bars (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
lead: The Monkey bars are an Agility obstacle found within the Brimhaven Agility Arena. Failing to cross will cause the player to fall and take damage; they will need to go up a nearby climbing rope to get back onto the course.

label: Monkey bones (disambiguation)
title: Monkey bones (disambiguation)
lead:
Monkey bones may refer to:

*Monkey bones
*Small zombie monkey bones

*Gorilla bones
*Bearded gorilla bones
*Small ninja monkey bones
*Medium ninja monkey bones
*Bones (Ape Atoll), bones of a skeletal gorilla

label: Monkey language
title: Monkey language
lead: Gielinor's monkey population possesses an advanced language that is unintelligible to most other races. By wearing a monkeyspeak amulet (or completing Monkey Madness II), it is possible to understand the monkey language as English. Otherwise, it appears as unintelligible babble, depending on the type of monkey.

label: Monkey Madness I/Plot
title: Monkey Madness I/Plot
lead: This is a plot summary of the events of Monkey Madness I.

label: Monkeybars (Edgeville Dungeon)
title: Monkeybars (Edgeville Dungeon)
lead:
The monkeybars is an Agility shortcut found within the Edgeville Dungeon. An Agility level of 15 is required to traverse these monkey bars. This obstacle allows access to the part of the Edgeville dungeon that contains earth warriors, the area is mostly used by people doing Earth warriors as their Wilderness Slayer task. Some people use the monkey bars as a low-intensity way to train Agility, as with the right camera placement it is possible to keep the mouse cursor in one spot and continuously click. This obstacle can not be failed. Players can gain up to 13,000 experience per hour.

Be aware that the monkey bars are located in the Wilderness, and as such the player may be attacked by other players while using them.

label: Monkeybars (Yanille Agility Dungeon)
title: Monkeybars (Yanille Agility Dungeon)
lead:
Monkeybars are an Agility shortcut located inside the Yanille Agility Dungeon. An Agility level of 57 is required to use the shortcut. It provides access to the Chaos druids deeper in the dungeon, as well as a lockpick respawn down the nearby stairs. There's a chance of failing this shortcut and falling into a lower level crawling with poisonous spiders.

Clicking the Monkeybars without moving the camera is an Idle training method and can gain you up to 13,333xp per hour.

label: monster
title: monster
lead:
Monster is the official term for an attackable character or being that is not player-controlled. A monster can range from a not-so-harmful Rat to the extremely strong Chaos Elemental. Monsters are often fought by players for training, entertainment, and loot. Killing monsters is one of the most popular activities in Old School RuneScape. Nearly all monsters drop remains.

While some monsters will never begin a fight with a player, many high level creatures are aggressive, potentially causing unwanted death. If a player has over double the combat level of the monster, the monster will be docile, and will only attack when provoked. However, in areas such as the Wilderness, most monsters are indefinitely aggressive. As a rule of thumb, "humanoids" are not aggressive towards players except in some cases when the humanoid's nature or occupation has malign or criminal connotations (i.e. Black Knight, Zombie, Mugger). Most cities are also safe from aggressive monsters, though the perimeter or surroundings may not be as secure.

label: Monster attribute
title: Monster attribute
lead:
Monster attributes are characteristics of monsters that cause certain strengths, vulnerabilities, or effects in combat.

Attributes that cause vulnerabilities does not necessarily mean that the damage boosting weapons will be the best weapon to use. Players should consider the monsters defensive stats as well as their own stats and equipment to determine the best combat style to use.

label: Monster killing
title: Monster killing
lead: Monster killing, also known as player vs monster (PvM) or player vs environment (PvE), is the aspect of killing monsters for the purposes of gaining experience, obtaining drops, or as part of a quest or minigame. PvM is contrasted with player killing (PvP) in the sense that monsters are entities controlled by the game itself.

label: Monster maximum hit
title: Monster maximum hit
lead:
The maximum hit of a monster is the highest amount of damage that a monster will inflict for a given attack style. If a player is hit by this monster, the player will receive damage up to and including this amount. The amount of damage done is not affected by a player's Defence level. Players can reduce the max hit by either making use of mechanics in a boss fight, or with passives such as those from justiciar armour, dinh's bulwark and the elysian spirit shield.

The Lunar spell "Monster Examine" may be used to identify the max melee hit of a monster. If a monster doesn't use melee attacks, and only attacks with ranged or magic (such as dark wizards), then it will display the monster's max hit with the attack style it uses. Monsters with more than one attack style (ex. melee and magic), may have two different maximum hit levels, one for each attack style. This information is useful for players that can protect from a certain style of attack with prayer.

label: Monsters with abnormal projectiles
title: Monsters with abnormal projectiles
lead: In most cases, to successfully use protection prayers against monsters with projectile attacks, the prayer must be active before the attack happens. This is a list of monsters whose behaviour deviates from this norm.

label: Monument
title: Monument
lead:
The Monuments plays a role in the Priest of Peril quest, located under Paterdomus. Using the golden key on the southern monument containing the key will give the player the iron key, which is used to free Drezel from his prison.

Furthermore, for souvenir purposes only, golden variants of common tools can be obtained by swamping them with their respective monument. This can only be done once during the quest ; specifically, before using the blessed water on the coffin! Attempting to use normal tools again on the already swapped monuments during this part of the quest will output a dialogue box, "You have already taken the Golden ".

label: Moody
title: Moody
lead:
Moody is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness and also plays in the Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, it plays east of Ferox Enclave as well as at Deserted Keep in Deep Wilderness.

label: Moon Clan
title: Moon Clan
lead: The Moon Clan are a tribe of magical Humans residing on Lunar Isle and led by the Oneiromancer, a powerful wizard. The Clan is believed to be named after the crescent-shaped image of Lunar Isle, and may have derived their powerful magicks from the mystical nature of the island. The Moon Clan has been in a bitter war for centuries with the Fremenniks in Rellekka. During the Lunar Diplomacy quest, the player discovers more about the Moon Clan and helps end the conflict between the Moon Clan and the Fremennik.

label: Moon equipment
title: Moon equipment
lead: Moon equipment refers to a number of sets of combat equipment found in the Lunar Chest inside the Moons of Peril activity. There are three sets of Moon equipment: all three can be used by warriors, but one each is for melee/ranged and melee/magic hybrids. Each set has four pieces: a two-handed weapon, a helmet, a torso piece, and legwear. When all four pieces for a particular Nagua are equipped, a special set effect is granted, which is different for each set. Moon sets cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

title: Moonclan robes
lead:
Moonclan Robes are sold on Lunar Isle in the clothing store (run by Rimae Sirsalis, found south of the bank) during and after the Lunar Diplomacy quest.
For this robe set, you can either wear a Moonclan hat or a Moonclan helm, both in the headwear slot. The combined cost of all 7 pieces is 6,000 coins. None of them are tradeable.

This robe set can be stored in the magic wardrobe in a player's costume room.

label: moonlight mead
title: moonlight mead
lead:
Moonlight mead is a type of ale that restores 4 Hitpoints. It can be obtained through brewing at level 44 Cooking, granting 380 experience. It is brewed using 2 buckets of water, 2 barley malt, 4 mushrooms, and a pot of ale yeast. The stronger, mature version of the ale is the moonlight mead(m).

It can be bought for 5 coins from Roavar in the Hair of the Dog tavern, located in Canifis.

title: Moonlight moth (interface item)
lead:
The Moonlight moth icon is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the moonlight moth.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Moons of Peril/Strategies
title: Moons of Peril/Strategies
lead:
This page shows various strategies which may help you in Neypotzli, where you fight the Moons of Peril. This includes navigating the prison, gathering resources, and information on the bosses themselves, but does not include other monsters within that are not part of the fight, such as the Sulphur Nagua and Moonlight Cockatrice.

If the player dies while in Neypotzli their grave will appear at the antechamber.

label: Mooring point
title: Mooring point
lead:
Mooring points, also called docking points, are facilities where players can board or disembark their boats or other players' boats. Clicking the gangplank at a port or the mooring point at an island to disembark sets the location the player will teleport to if they escape or capsize their boat, similarly to a buoy. The docks at Port Sarim and The Pandemonium can be used at level 1 Sailing, but other mooring points require higher Sailing levels and/or quest requirements to use.

When disembarking at a port that has a bank deposit box, the first crewmate in the crew registry will be available on the dock to bank the contents of the ship's cargo hold. This function is not available on any island, even if it has a bank. When disembarking at the destination of a courier task, crewmates will automatically withdraw as many cargo crates as they can hold to bring them to the ledger table.

label: Morgan
title: Morgan
lead:
Morgan is a worried citizen you talk with to start the Vampyre Slayer quest. He can be found in his house north of Ned's house in Draynor Village.

Garlic can be found in his house upstairs.

label: Morgan Le Faye
title: Morgan Le Faye
lead: Lady Morgan Le Faye is King Arthur's nemesis, and owner of Keep Le Faye. Her son is Sir Mordred. She is involved with Merlin's Crystal and King's Ransom, as she turns King Arthur into stone and works with the Sinclairs and the Black Knights. She has many magical powers, including some that surpass even Merlin's ability, as she was capable of imprisoning him within a crystal.

title: Morrigan's equipment
lead: Morrigan's equipment is a part of the Ancient Warriors' equipment. Three versions of this equipment set exist: two can be earned by participating in the Bounty Hunter minigame, and can only be used within Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings, while the third set is exclusive to Deadman Mode.

label: Morris
title: Morris
lead: Morris is a resident of Hemenster. He acts as a gatekeeper for the Fishing Contest, only allowing those who have a fishing pass onto the contest grounds.

label: Mort myre fungus
title: Mort myre fungus
lead:
Mort myre fungi can be obtained in Mort Myre Swamp. It can be used to add 1 charge to a Druid pouch or used in the Herblore skill to make super energy potions.

It is obtained by casting Bloom with a Druidic spell (given to the player by Filliman Tarlock during the Nature Spirit quest), or blessed silver sickle (created during the same quest), or any of: Emerald sickle (b), Enchanted emerald sickle (b), Ruby sickle (b), Enchanted ruby sickle (b), Blisterwood sickle, Ivandis flail, or Blisterwood flail near rotting logs. Each cast of Bloom will drain 1-6 Prayer points from the player and may cause two mort myre fungus to spawn on each surrounding rotting log. Prayer drain is completely random and unaffected by the player's Prayer level or how many items are actually made. Alternatively, they can be obtained as a [[#Dropping monsters|drop]] from certain monsters or by chopping sulliuscep mushrooms.

label: Mort myre pear
title: Mort myre pear
lead:
A Mort myre pear is obtained during or after the Nature Spirit quest. It appears when the Bloom spell is cast, using a silver sickle(b) near certain small bushes in the Mort Myre Swamp. Each pear can be used to add 3 charges to a druid pouch for use as protection from Ghasts. However, they are not common, and it is generally easier to find Mort myre fungi or Mort myre stems.

It is a possible item requirement in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.

label: Mort myre stem
title: Mort myre stem
lead:
Mort myre stems can be obtained by operating a silver sickle (b) near rotting branches on the ground in Mort Myre Swamp. Each stem can be used to add 2 charges to a druid pouch for use as protection from ghasts.

It is a possible item requirement in Fairytale I - Growing Pains.

label: Mort Myre Swamp
title: Mort Myre Swamp
lead: The Mort Myre swamp, also known simply as Mort Myre and once a forest known as Humblethorn, is a swampland in western Morytania. Players first unlock the gate to the swampland by starting Nature Spirit, but the swamp can also be accessed by Barrows or Mort'ton teleport scrolls. Much of the swamp is plagued by ghasts, which attack players and rot food, aswell as a swamp decay effect, hitting the player periodically. Both can be avoided by building a Fire of Dehumidification after completion of Making Friends with My Arm.

label: Mortarium
title: Mortarium
lead:
Mortarium is an individual who accompanied Ohn, and several other men, in Tirannwn. He has a son, Onan, who still lives in Zul-Andra today.

According to Ohn's diary, they were being tracked down by clans of the elves, and have escaped to the Poison Waste, and attempted to fish for sacred eels with Onan.

label: Morytania
title: Morytania
lead:
Morytania (pronounced ) is a members-only area in the easternmost part of Gielinor. Players must complete the Priest in Peril quest to enter. Often described as a land of evil, the land is filled with many aggressive creatures such as vampyres, werewolves, ghasts, and the undead. It is currently ruled by Lord Drakan.

Prior to the God Wars, Morytania was marked by fertile land and thriving cities, and was occupied by Saradominists and Zarosians. In the Third Age, the vampyre Lord Lowerniel Vergidiyad Drakan betrayed the Zarosians in the name of Zamorak, ousting the Saradominists and turning the land to a swamp in the process. Lord Drakan then erected a wall around the former Saradominist capital of Hallowvale, turning it into a dense concentration camp and committing genocide against the Icyene race.

label: Morytania (music track)
title: Morytania (music track)
lead:
Morytania is a music track that is unlocked in the northern parts of Morytania, outside the Mort Myre Swamp and the Haunted Woods.

In Classic mode, the track only plays in the area directly around the Paterdomus, including in the part that is not part of Morytania itself.

label: Morytania Campaign
title: Morytania Campaign
lead:
The Morytania campaign was an event in the late Third Age in the vampyre-controlled region of Morytania. Six brothers (now known as the Barrows Brothers) named Ahrim, Dharok, Verac, Karil, Guthan and Torag, led a crusade consisting of several thousand Saradominist forces. The aim of the campaign was to reverse the damage done by Lord Drakan, who had conquered the then Saradominist city Hallowvale.

After Hallowvale had fallen to Drakan's continued raids, the Saradominists west of Morytania formed an army of the strongest warriors they could muster, including six young and promising brothers who had been provided power, weapons and armour by the Zarosian Mahjarrat Sliske.

label: Morytania legs
title: Morytania legs
lead:
Morytania legs are a reward for completing the Morytania Diary. There are four types, depending on which part of the diary the player has completed. Those are:

*Morytania legs 1, from the easy tasks set
*Morytania legs 2, from the medium tasks set
*Morytania legs 3, from the hard tasks set
*Morytania legs 4, from the elite tasks set

label: Mosol Rei
title: Mosol Rei
lead: Mosol Rei is a warrior and inhabitant of Shilo Village, and involved in the Shilo Village quest. After completion of the quest, he offers a way into the village past the Undead ones.

label: Mosquito
title: Mosquito
lead:
Mosquito may refer to:

*Giant mosquito, a monster found on Mos Le'Harmless.
*Large mosquito, a monster encountered during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame.
*Mosquito swarm, a monster encountered during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame.
*Proboscis, a 100% drop from a mosquito swarm and a rare drop from a giant mosquito.
*Swarm, a discontinued random event.

label: Moss Giant Island
title: Moss Giant Island
lead:
Moss Giant Island is a small island located west of Brimhaven, accessed by using a rope swing (Rope not needed) requiring 10 Agility. There are five moss giants on the island. Players can use safespots when fighting them.

There are two slice of cake spawns, which have a respawn time of 45 seconds. Players with 40+ Defence do not need to bring much food because of this resource. Lower-level players should, however, be cautious of the Poison Scorpions near the island.

label: moss giant
title: moss giant
lead:
Moss giants are large giants, found in areas that are tied to nature. Moss giants are very commonly trained on, since their Defence level is rather low in comparison to other monsters of the same combat level, and they are vulnerable to Fire spells.

They can drop the mossy key, which is required to access the moss giant boss Bryophyta's lair for the first time, and loot her chest thereafter.

label: mossy rock
title: mossy rock
lead: Mossy rocks are found in the north-west corner of the Kharazi Jungle. Any of the rocks can be searched in order to enter the Shaman Caves and deeper Viyeldi caves, requiring an Agility level of 50.

label: Mother of Seren
title: Mother of Seren
lead:
The mother of Seren is an ancient and mysterious deity who created Seren and her brother.

Over time, Seren's brother began to resent her possessiveness and left, while Seren remained devoted to her. In grief, she dreamt new beings into existence, beginning with some that were intelligent but only imitations of Seren and her brother, and eventually creating some that were purely instinctual. The act of creating these beings weakened her. Seren was able to convince some of the creations to sacrifice their energy to return it to her mother, but this only slowed her decline. When it became clear there was nothing more Seren could do, she left her mother as well.

label: Motherland
title: Motherland

title: mould
lead:
Moulds can be used to form a distinct object from a metal bar, such as a holy symbol out of a silver bar. Moulds are most often used for crafting, though the ammo mould is used in conjunction with Smithing.

Most of the moulds can be bought from crafting shops. In free-to-play one may be found in Al Kharid and the other one in Rimmington. The ammo mould can be bought from Nulodion in the west building at the dwarven mines (after Dwarf Cannon).

label: Mountain Dwarf (historical)
title: Mountain Dwarf (historical)
lead:
The Mountain Dwarf was a former character who could previously be found guarding the entrance to the White Wolf Tunnel. Players spoke to him in order to start the Fishing Contest quest. He later appeared in his own subquest during Recipe for Disaster.

In 2006, the Fishing Contest quest was reworked, and the Mountain Dwarf was replaced by two new characters named Austri and Vestri. As a result, he has never normally been present in Old School RuneScape, but remains in Recipe for Disaster.

label: Mountain goat
title: Mountain goat
lead:
Mountain goats are animals that can be in the mountains around Troll Country, specifically the top of Trollheim; south of Mount Quidamortem; the cliff overlooking Death Plateau; around the ice troll settlement of Weiss; and inside a cage in the troll kitchen, ready to be cooked (although Burntmeat the troll cook prefers to cook humans if he gets the chance).

Eadgar, through a dialogue option, will turn them into goat stew if the player gives him some logs for his fire. This heals 20 Hitpoints.

label: Mountain troll
title: Mountain troll
lead:
Mountain trolls are aggressive creatures which can be found patrolling various mountainous areas. They are commonly killed as part of an assigned Slayer task of "trolls".

Trolls regenerate health twice as quickly as other monsters, but are still vulnerable to poison. They usually use crush weapons, which, combined with their relatively high Strength, can hit rather hard. However, they attack slowly and are quite inaccurate, so it's not strictly necessary to use protection prayers for players that have high Defence. A good strategy for conserving supplies is to use Bones to Peaches on the big bones that they drop; this will almost always cover any damage they manage to deal. Bringing a staff of fire (or similar item) and nature runes is recommended in order to alchemise their frequent low-level armour and weapon drops.

label: mourner gear
title: mourner gear
lead:
Mourner gear is worn by mourners. It is first obtained during Mourning's End Part I, and is also required during the subsequent quests Mourning's End Part II and Song of the Elves. Wearing the full set allows the player to enter the door under the mourner headquarters in West Ardougne to access dark beasts and the east entrance of the Temple of Light. Players can alternatively use the Slayer ring's Dark Beasts teleport to get there. The set is no longer required to enter after completing the first section of Song of the Elves.

The full set can be stored in an armour case in the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: Mourner Headquarters
title: Mourner Headquarters
lead:
The Mourner Headquarters, also known as the Mourner HQ, is the headquarters for the Mourners, who are secretly the Death Guard of Prifddinas and members of the Iorwerth Clan. It is located in the north-eastern part of West Ardougne and plays a major role throughout the elf quest line.

During the Elven Civil War, the headquarters serves as a base of military and strategic operations for the Iorwerth Clan. After completion of Song of the Elves, the building is taken over by the paladins and knights of Ardougne, and the Iorwerth warriors relocate to the Iorwerth Dungeon.

label: Mouse (Witch's House)
title: Mouse (Witch's House)
lead:
The mouse plays a minor role in the Witch's House quest as part of the security system in Nora T. Hagg's house. The mouse must be lured out of its hole with a piece of cheese, then given a magnet in order to open the door from the house to the garden.

This convoluted security system was installed by Professor Oddenstein, and is described in the witch's diary.

label: Mouse hole (scenery)
title: Mouse hole (scenery)
lead: The mouse hole is a piece of scenery found in the witch's house north of Taverley. During the Witch's House quest, the hole is the home of a large mouse that the player lures out with cheese to unlock a door. In and after Grim Tales, the hole serves as the entrance to the mouse hole dungeon, where Miazrqa's pendant can be found. A (seemingly) large mouse hole also serves as the exit out of the dungeon.

label: Mouse keys
title: Mouse keys
lead:
Mouse keys are an accessibility feature of many operating systems that allows the numeric keypad to take on some of the functions of a pointing device. They can be useful when playing Old School RuneScape because (for example) the "5" key can be used as a mouse-click, which can reduce strain on the player's hand when performing click-intensive playing, and it is possible to use mouse keys on some operating systems to jump the cursor a set distance, which can be used to reach options on drop-down menus.

Since January 2017, Jagex's stance is that "players may only use their operating system's official default mouse keys program, unless it is to remap a key to any other button. If we find evidence of you using other forms of mouse keys in game, we will take action against your account. If you're using your system's default mouse keys, you're playing within the rules." This means that other popular programs such as AutoHotkey are not allowed unless to merely remap keys.

label: muddy chest
title: muddy chest
lead:
The muddy chest is a locked chest located in the centre of Lava Maze. It can only be opened with a muddy key, consuming one key each time the chest is opened. A slash weapon is necessary to cut through the web that allows access to the maze centre (Aranea boots may also be used), or 82 Agility to use the stepping stone shortcut north of the fenced area.

Opening the chest is a task in the Medium Wilderness Diary.

label: Muddy key
title: Muddy key
lead:
The muddy key is a key that can be used to open the muddy chest in the centre of the Lava Maze in the Wilderness. You will need a knife or sword to access it. It can be obtained as a drop from chaos dwarves (in both the Wilderness and Taverley Dungeon), and the crazy archaeologist.

Using a muddy key to open the muddy chest is a medium Wilderness Diary task.

label: mugger
title: mugger
lead:
Muggers are weak human non-player characters that have a combat level of 6. Because of their low combat level, they are generally more of a nuisance, but they can still be a threat for brand-new players.

Muggers are aggressive, which means that they attack players who are two times the mugger's combat level or less. Thus, muggers are aggressive against players who have a combat level between 3 and 12.

label: Multi-hit weapons
title: Multi-hit weapons
lead:
Multi-hit weapons (also called double-hitting weapons and twin weapons ) are weapons that hit an enemy multiple times in one attack. Some weapons attack multiple times on the same game tick while others attack multiple times on consecutive game ticks.

Multi-hit weapons are useful when fighting NPCs with negative flat armour, such as the Blue Moon, as the flat damage increase gets applied to each hitsplat separately. They can also be useful for delivering killing blows in PvP.

label: Multicannon parts for sale
title: Multicannon parts for sale
lead:
Multicannon parts for sale is a store located in the dwarven industrial area of Ice Mountain, owned by Nulodion. It sells dwarf multicannon parts, ammo moulds, and the instruction manual. The Dwarf Cannon quest must be completed to access the store.

It is cheaper to buy the cannon parts through Nulodion's dialogue, as he will sell a full set of four parts together for 750,000 coins, whereas buying them individually would cost a total of 802,500 coins.

label: multicombat area
title: multicombat area
lead:
A multicombat area, also known as a Multiway Combat area is an area of the Old School RuneScape world where a player or monster can be attacked by more than one player or monster at a time.

Multicombat areas are identified upon entering by two crossed swords ( ) which appear in the bottom right-hand corner of the interface or under the mini world map. Anywhere else is a Single-way combat area, also known as a single-combat area, with an exception for the Revenant Caves, Wilderness Agility Course and lesser Wilderness bosses, which are Singles-plus combat ( ).

label: Mummy (historical)
title: Mummy (historical)
lead:
Mummies were an unused monster first added to the RuneScape 2 beta. A Behind the Scenes article from March 2004 promised that one of the upcoming updates would be "A pyramid quest in the desert full of traps, treasure and mummys ." Presumably, the mummies were created as part of this planned update.

Though this idea was used for a planned update in 2004, development was halted after the intern was dismissed. The mummies were deleted from the game files with the release of Slayer. Ultimately, new mummies were released with Desert Treasure I in April 2005, who had a similar appearance.

label: Murky water
title: Murky water
lead:
The murky water is a quest item used only in Priest in Peril. It can only be made during the quest by using a bucket on the well in the Paterdomus mausoleum to obtain water from the River Salve.

It is used to make blessed water by speaking to Drezel.

label: Murphy
title: Murphy
lead:
Murphy is a sailor who is located at Port Khazard. To reach him quickly, use the Minigame teleport to Fishing Trawler. Players must speak to him during the Freeing Pirate Pete subquest of Recipe for Disaster, in order to obtain a diving apparatus to go diving. He runs the Fishing Trawler minigame and also gives players a sextant which is 1 of 3 items that the observatory professor tells you is needed to solve a coordinate in a Treasure Trail.

In order to go diving to the Mogre Camp, the player must weigh less than 28 kg. This is required for an elite clue step.

label: music
title: music
lead:
|275x275px]]

Music in Old School RuneScape is comprised largely of in-game tracks tied to specific locations or quests. These compositions draw inspiration from a wide variety of musical genres, and can be unlocked for playback using the in-game Music Player. A counter at the bottom of the Music Player screen tracks how many pieces of music have been unlocked and how many are yet to be unlocked.

label: Music Player
title: Music Player
lead:
The Music Player tab displays what music track is playing at the moment. Music tracks are unlocked as you play the game, exploring new places and content.

Players can choose between Area Mode, playing a selection of songs for the current area the player is in; Shuffle Mode, playing songs randomly; or Single Mode, playing a chosen song on loop indefinitley. When in Shuffle Mode clicking the Skip Track button will stop playback and start a new randomly chosen song.

label: Music/Free-to-play

*Purchasing from the Wizards' Guild store (blue mystic robes).
*Catching Dragon implings.
*Opening the Brimstone chest (dusk mystic robes).
*Buying from another player.

Slayer monsters that originate from the Slayer Tower drop dark mystic pieces, while slayer monsters that originate from Fremennik Slayer Dungeon drop light mystic pieces, with few exceptions.

label: mystic staff
title: mystic staff
lead:
Mystic staves are combined melee and magical weapons which can be used in combat, requiring level 40 Attack and Magic to wield. They are primarily used for casting combat spells, having +2 more Magic Attack bonuses compared to battlestaves, although they also have Melee Attack bonuses.

To create a mystic staff, the Scorpion Catcher quest must be completed. After this you can then take a battlestaff to Thormac and pay him 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries).

label: mystic water staff
title: mystic water staff
lead:
The mystic water staff is an elemental staff requiring 40 Attack and 40 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created after the completion of the quest Scorpion Catcher by taking a water battlestaff and to Thormac. After completion of the Hard Kandarin Diary and Elite Kandarin Diary, Thormac will only require or respectively.

label: Mystical wall chart
title: Mystical wall chart
lead:
Mystical wall charts were wall decorations that could be found in various locations throughout Gielinor. They depict a pentagram.

They were removed from the game in a hidden update in January 2006 and replaced with Demonic symbols. Presumably this was due to Jagex wishing to avoid controversy, because of the pentagram's associations with Satanism.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: MyYearInOSRS
title: MyYearInOSRS
lead:
#MyYearInOSRS is a yearly promotional email campaign that gives you a summary of your progress over the year.

The 2025 summaries will be sent as batches: Friday 19 December 2025, Tuesday 23 December 2025, and a third batch in January after the team is back from break 
. ? (edit) Please add information about previous years

label: nagua
title: nagua
lead:
A nagua is a type of spirit summoned through a type of magic called naguanil. Nagua generally appear as floating entities with four arms and tentacle-like appendages in place of legs, though their individual appearances vary.

In combat, nagua make use of flat armour, which influences the damage dealt from a player's individual hits. Additionally, most nagua tend to make use of multi-hitting attacks; lesser nagua make two hits per attack and the Moons of Peril make three hits per attack.

label: Nagua boss
title: Nagua boss
lead:

* The Moons of Peril, a trio of nagua consisting of:
** Blood Moon
** Blue Moon
** Eclipse Moon

label: naguanil
title: naguanil
lead:
Naguanil is a type of magic practiced by the Old Ones and used to summon nagua for various purposes 
. It is involved in the Perilous Moons quest, as the player uses infused water and earth talismans to detect the source of naguanil and find Eyatlalli. Additionally, Eyatlalli explains that naguanil is involved in the ritual that sealed the Moons of Peril into their prison.

Knowledge of naguanil is rare in present-day Gielinor, although some individuals have familiarity with it, including Nahta, who runs the magic shop in Cam Torum and the Blacksmith of Cam Torum.

label: Nails
title: Nails
lead:
Nails are metal items used in a variety of quests and for various skill applications. They can be created through Smithing on an anvil except Dragon nails which can be produced at the Dragon forge, with each bar creating 15 nails. Steel nails are the only type of nail available to free-to-play players.

Nails are commonly used for Construction and Sailing, particularly for building low-level furniture and Facilities on boats. Though most pieces of higher-tier furniture do not require nails to construct, there are some exceptions like STASH units and the bridges within the Hallowed Sepulchre. While using nails in Construction, there's a chance of bending them depending on what metal the nails are made of and the player's Construction level, with the chances lowering with better nails and higher Construction level. If multiple types of nails are carried at the same time, the higher tier ones are used first.

label: Narogoshuun
title: Narogoshuun
lead:
The Narogoshuun are a goblin tribe found while doing the Land of the Goblins quest, who wear orange goblin mail. Like the other tribes found in the temple, they were called upon by the god Bandos to fight in his name during the God Wars.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Goblins of the West". Hopespear, a prophet, is a notable Narogoshuun.

label: Natural
title: Natural
lead:
Natural is a music track that is unlocked on the island of the the Nature Grotto in Mort Myre Swamp. It can also be heard on the island in the River Salve, or during Temple Trekking in combat events with one escape route.

In Classic mode, the track plays in a large area around the Nature Grotto, as well as on a small part of the shore of the Digsite.

label: Natural history quiz
title: Natural history quiz
lead:
The natural history quiz is the basement section of the Varrock Museum miniquest. It consists of 14 creature displays in which the player must answer 3 questions correctly in order to earn 2 kudos each for a total of 28.

Each of the rooms has a Natural historian who will give a lecture about each creature for which the quiz is based on.

label: Nature Altar
title: Nature Altar
lead:
The Nature Altar is a runic altar upon which nature runes are crafted from pure essence, providing 9 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Level 44 Runecraft is required to craft nature runes.

Players may create a nature tiara here by using either a nature talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 45 Runecraft experience. A catalytic tiara can also be created here by using a catalytic talisman and gold tiara, granting 42.5 Runecraft experience.

label: Nature Grotto
title: Nature Grotto
lead:
Nature Grotto is a small cave located deep within the Mort Myre Swamp. It is located north-west of the village of Mor'ton and directly east of the Exam Centre, though of course across the river. You may pray at the altar of nature in the cave, earning you 2 extra Prayer points until spending them.

The Nature Grotto first appears in the quest Nature Spirit, of which it is a vital part of the quest. Jumping across the broken bridge will bring you to the cave entrance – a black hole in the mound – and Filliman Tarlock.

label: Nature rune
title: Nature rune
lead:
Nature runes are runes used for transmutation spells such as Low and High Alchemy and Superheat Item. They are also used for the spells Bind, Snare, and Entangle, and several spells on the Lunar and Arceuus spellbooks. They can be purchased from many magic shops.

Nature runes can be crafted from pure essence by members with level 44 Runecraft at the Nature Altar, granting 9 experience per pure essence used. Players with 91 Runecraft will always craft two nature runes per essence.

label: Nature Spirit
title: Nature Spirit
lead: Nature Spirit is a quest that takes place deep in the Mort Myre Swamp. The nature spirit Filliman Tarlock needs help restoring the Nature Grotto, his home, to its previous glory.

label: Nature talisman
title: Nature talisman
lead:
The nature talisman is a talisman used to gain access to the Nature Altar, located north of Shilo Village on the island of Karamja, where players can craft nature runes. The talisman can also be combined with a tiara at the Nature Altar by having both the nature talisman and tiara in your inventory, and using the tiara on the altar. This action grants the player 45 Runecraft experience; some players choose to do this in order to save an extra inventory space and make quicker trips when crafting nature runes, as the Nature Altar may be accessed simply by left-clicking on it while the player is wearing the nature tiara.

A good way to obtain the talisman is to kill abyssal leeches in the abyss after completing the Enter the Abyss miniquest. Keep in mind that the abyss is very dangerous and you may find yourself quickly overwhelmed without proper armour and food. Always bring a teleport in case you need a quick escape. The nature talisman is also a part of the rare drop table, therefore any monster with access to the rare drop table has a chance of either dropping this talisman or a chaos talisman (with a couple of exceptions being able to drop both, such as fire giants and abyssal demons).

Naval shirt is a cosmetic reward from the Trouble Brewing minigame. It can be purchased from Honest Jimmy's House of Stuff for 1000 Pieces of eight. It cannot be resold to the shop.

Naval shirts can be stored in the Player-owned house Costume room along with a Tricorn hat and Navy slacks of the same colour. They come in 7 different colours.

Naval slacks can be stored in the Player-owned house Costume room along with a Tricorn hat and Naval shirt of the same colour. They come in 7 different colours.

label: Nazastarool
title: Nazastarool
lead:
Nazastarool is an undead encountered during the Shilo Village quest after searching a dolmen in Rashiliyia's Tomb. He has three forms; the first being a level 91 Zombie, second a 68 Skeleton and finally a 93 Ghost. All three forms have to be fought during the quest. A very easy way to kill him is to either range or use magic on him, as he can get stuck behind obstacles. All three forms may also be safespotted with a Halberd.

When defeated, he curses the player and disappears.

label: necklace
title: necklace
lead:
A Necklace is a type of equipment item worn in the neckwear slot. Necklaces are the second item type that players can make with a gem with the skill Crafting.
To enchant a necklace (with gem on it), you need runes to cast the appropriate enchant spell. Only members can enchant necklaces. Necklaces can be created using a necklace mould, a gold bar and gems can be used via the Crafting skill.

label: Necklace mould
title: Necklace mould
lead: A necklace mould allows a player to make necklaces through the Crafting skill out of gold bars and possibly gems by using them on a furnace. It can be bought at various crafting shops, and an unlimited amount can also be taken from a tool store 4 in a player-owned house.

label: Necklace of rupture
title: Necklace of rupture
lead: The necklace of rupture is an upgraded variant of the necklace of anguish requiring 90 Hitpoints to wear. It is intended to be made by combining the necklace of anguish with an etched alpha venator tooth, with an untradeable non-etched alpha venator tooth being a drop from the Maggot King.

label: Necromancer
title: Necromancer
lead: The Necromancer is found on the of the Necromancer Tower just south of East Ardougne. He will attack with his fists, curse spells, and by summoning Summoned Zombies to aid him. He has a long respawn time.

label: Necromancer (disambiguation)
title: Necromancer (disambiguation)

label: necromancy
title: necromancy
lead:
.]]
Necromancy is a branch of Magic involving communing and resurrecting the dead. Necromancy is considered a very dark and abhorred art and practising it is considered a dangerous activity as numerous individuals have turned insane while attempting to raise the dead. Necromancers are usually followers of Zamorak, as the practice of necromancy is considered "evil" by most societies; however, a handful of non-Zamorakian necromancers have been accepted within society at various times.

The animation of undead such as skeletons and zombies are the usual fare for necromancers, and have often been used as disposable troops, as seen during the God Wars. Although on the surface appearing similar to Summoning, necromancy and summoning have nothing to do with each other. According to Irwin Feaselbaum, necromancers are capable of bringing themselves back from the dead.

label: Ned
title: Ned
lead:
Captain Ned is an old sailor who lives in a small house in eastern Draynor Village. He plays a part in the Dragon Slayer I and Prince Ali Rescue quests. Players can bring him 15 coins or four balls of wool to make a rope. Alternatively, he sells rope (for 18 coins) at his store, Ned's Handmade Rope (100% Wool).

After The Fremennik Isles, players who buy rope from him will notice that his rope seems funny, and Ned will confess that he actually gets the ropes from Neitiznot by trading balls of wool and doesn't actually make them himself. He will give the player another rope for free in exchange for them keeping quiet about it. He will also rename his store to Ned's Handmade Rope (100% Wool - not yak, honest!) in an attempt to cover up his past deceit.

label: Ned (historical)
title: Ned (historical)
lead:
Ned was a character who could previously be encounted during Dragon Slayer I. He could be found on the Lady Lumbridge after the ship was repaired, and on Crandor where the ship had crashed.

During Dragon Slayer I, Ned from Draynor Village is recruited to help sail the player to Crandor. Due to game limitations in 2001, a second version of Ned had to be created specifically for use during Dragon Slayer. He has a different appearance to the Draynor Village Ned, as he was not graphically updated alongside the other in 2005.

label: needle
title: needle
lead:
A Needle is an item used along with thread to create armour out of leather and dragon leather through the Crafting skill. It can be bought in crafting stores, such as Dommik's Crafting Store. in Al Kharid. They can also be bought from Moon Clan Fine Clothes on Lunar Isle, the Canifis General Store and Fancy Clothes Store in Varrock (Members). After completion of Death on the Isle, a Costume needle can be used for crafting without needing thread.

Needles can also be found from digging in the Digsite. They can also be found with a 10% probability by searching haystacks or hay bales - this is a reference to the idiom "finding a needle in a haystack", meaning something that is almost impossible to find because it is hidden among so many other things. When your character finds one this way, they will remark on how rare an occurrence it is.

label: Neilan Redmark
title: Neilan Redmark
lead:
Neilan Redmark was an inexperienced necromancer who came to Great Kourend from the mainlands. He felt snubbed by the people of Arceuus and stole a book on necromancy from the Arceuus Library to try and conjure up something to impress them. He fled westward to a cave in the Kebos Lowlands, where he started practicing necromancy on dead rats. Believing that he needed to work on something bigger, he recovered a rotten bear corpse in the Kebos Swamp and brought it to a cave by the shore. He resurrected the corpse as a headless beast, which abruptly killed him.

During Getting Ahead the player tracks down Neilan's headless beast and kills it in the cave, where the remains of Neilan Redmark can be found alongside his journal.

label: NPC IDs
title: NPC IDs
lead:
A non-player character, or NPC, is a character not controlled by a player.

Each unique NPC model has an in-game ID associated with it which can be used by tools such as plugins or the online interactive world map. For example, the boss Zulrah has three different forms which are each a different colour, and each form has a separate unique ID.

label: Neitiznot (person)
title: Neitiznot (person)
lead:
Neitiznot was the founder of Neitiznot, a Fremennik island. He was one of the youngest sons of an unnamed king, and the brother of Jatizso, Jatizso's namesake and founder; they were both exiled by their father due to their feuds, which are still manifested in the feuds between native islanders.

Mawnis Burowgar, ruler and Burgher of Neitiznot, is descended from him.

label: Nelta
title: Nelta
lead:
Nelta is a position that exists in the Varlamorian religion of Losanium, referring to those who act in the service of their respective god. It is roughly equivalent to a standard "priest" within the Church of Saradomin. Neltas exist in both the Church of Ralos and the Sect of Ranul, and are the lowest ranking position in each hierarchy, below teoki and the Teokan.

Several Neltas of Ralos can be found at various shrines to Ralos across Varlamore, including the Teomat.

lead:
Nettles are plants that can be picked to obtain nettles. Though nettle plants can be found in nonmembers regions, nettles can only be picked on members worlds.

Players must wear gloves in order to pick nettles. If no gloves are worn, no nettles will be obtained and the player will be dealt up to 2 Hitpoints of damage. Although the resulting hitsplat is green, similar to poison, the player will not be poisoned. After picking nettles, they disappear and will respawn after a few seconds.

label: New player guide
title: New player guide
lead:
The new player guide is intended to help both new and returning players. The guide covers a wide range of topics including; skills, money making, and some early-game content in Old School RuneScape.

Important:
* RuneScape login credentials will work on Old School RuneScape, however previous account progress is not carried over.
* Account progression is not shared between Old School RuneScape and RuneScape.
* Membership status is shared between Old School RuneScape and RuneScape.
* Account progression is not tied to a specific world/server. 
* Players can play Old School RuneScape on PC or phone, and account progression is shared as long as the same login details are entered.
* A specific account can only be logged into one location at a time, whether PC and phone, or Old School RuneScape and RuneScape. In order to play the other game or at a different location, the first needs to be logged out.
** Separate accounts, on the other hand, can log into multiple locations or games at the same time, even on the same computer.

It will possess a special attack made to specialise as a consistent finisher on opponents, and will be able to attack high-tier Vampyres.

label: Newbie Melody

label: Newcomer map
title: Newcomer map
lead:
A Newcomer map is a map sold at many general stores for one coin. It is also sold by Rasolo and Trader crewmembers for 2 coins.

The map helps new players of the game find their way around Gielinor. The map does not give clear directions, but shows a general view of eastern Asgarnia and western Misthalin, being the main Free-to-play area of the game. The map will also display the rough location of the player with a blinking X on the map. This item is not particularly useful anymore due to the world map interface serving a similar purpose.

label: Nex/Strategies
title: Nex/Strategies
lead:
Nex, the Zarosian general of the Ancient Prison, is one of the most powerful bosses in Old School RuneScape. It is strongly recommended that players fight her with a team, as it is extremely difficult and unfeasible to solo Nex.

Worlds 332, 481, 505, and 523 are the official worlds for killing Nex in a free-for-all group. Players may also utilise in-game chat-channels to find groups to kill Nex with.

label: Nezikchened
title: Nezikchened
lead:
Nezikchened is a level 187 black demon that has to be defeated three different times during the Legends' Quest. He is also among the strongest demons in the game. At the start of each fight he drains the player's prayer points. Like all demons, he is also vulnerable to the effects of demonbane weapons. He has a very peculiar habit of calling the player 'Vacu.' According to Gujuo, 'Vacu' was the name for shamans who could summon powerful and wise spirits, but were enslaved by the spirits for asking too much of them.

Despite being a black demon, he is not considered one for the purpose of a Slayer task. He can be fought in the Nightmare Zone after the quest is complete.

label: Niles

Like his brothers, he may appear to initiate the Certer random event, in which he will ask players to identify an item, such as a fish, with three possible choices of what the object is. If the player correctly identifies the item, Niles will give the player a reward of either coins, a gem (uncut, up to diamond), a cosmic talisman, a half key, a spinach roll, or a kebab.

label: Nitroglycerin
title: Nitroglycerin
lead:
Nitroglycerin is a vial of chemicals used in The Dig Site quest which, when combined with ammonium nitrate, ground charcoal and an arcenia root, create a chemical compound. Unidentified liquid may be obtained by using an empty vial on the barrel with a skull & crossbones symbol, to the west of the tent south of the Digsite, before being brought to Terry Balando for identification. After Terry has identified the liquid, all vials in your inventory will be converted to Nitroglycerin. If the barrel has not previously been opened, a trowel may be used on it in order to do so.

When dropped, a vial of unidentified liquid does 25 damage to the player and causes them to say . This damage is increased to 35 if dropping a vial of nitroglycerin and the message is changed to However, neither can kill the player in the event that the player's Hitpoints are already 25 or below (35 or below for nitroglycerin). Followers are a broad class of NPCs that follow the player in a variety of situations. Pets are the most common type of follower, but other types of follower NPCs use the same underlying system. Much like pets, these non-pet followers have a corresponding item that will spawn the follower NPC when dropped from the player's Inventory.

The item forms of these followers are generally not obtainable through normal gameplay, and exist within the game code as a failsafe measure in case the follower behaviour is interrupted somehow.

label: Non-player character
title: Non-player character
lead:
.]]
A non-player character, or NPC, is a character not controlled by a player. As such, NPCs are computer-controlled characters with pre-defined functions, paths, and methods to enhance players' immersion to the game. Players can usually talk to NPCs, but they are not attackable; if they are attackable, they are considered monsters. They include store owners, quest contacts, bankers and civilians. NPCs can give out quests, sell items, restrict access to certain areas and perform other vital duties. Many have no useful function, but provide atmosphere or interesting conversation. Some can talk in public, but this will not appear in the chat list. NPCs have a yellow colour on the minimap and in context menus.

If a space is occupied by a player or an NPC, another player may walk through them without their path being blocked (with some exception, such as various monkey guards on Ape Atoll), but most NPCs cannot walk onto or over a space occupied by a player or another NPC. Additionally, if a player blocks an NPC from moving for too long, the NPC will reset to its respawn location.

label: Nonexistence
title: Nonexistence
lead:
The term you have searched for does not exist in Old School RuneScape. It may have never existed, or was added to RuneScape after the August 2007 Archive of RuneScape, which Old School RuneScape was based on, and has not been backported or otherwise reimplemented into the game.

If you are searching for a future update, please look for it at upcoming updates or create an article about it, supplying definite sources and citations.

label: Noob
title: Noob
lead:
Noob, Newb, and Newbie are terms used amongst RuneScape players as well as much of the gaming community in general. "Noob" and its alternatives are used to refer to a new player or newcomer who is generally incompetent or has a low Combat or skill level.

Over the years noob has been seen as a common insult, as it was popular to use as players could not be reported for using it unless it was done to such a degree that it constituted spamming, which would have to be sufficient "to render the chat window useless".

label: Nora T. Hagg
title: Nora T. Hagg
lead:
Nora T. Hagg is a witch who lives in a house located in Taverley. She is the central figure in the Witch's House quest, during which the player must retrieve the boy's lost ball from her garden.

She has a pet experiment that she hides in her shed, along with other experiments of hers that live in the sewers beneath her house.

label: North
title: North
lead:
North is an absolute direction, found by referring to the minimap. The name "North" can also refer to several areas in Gielinor:

* The Northern Tundras, a snowy area in northern Arceuus
* The Northern Ocean, a vast, open body of water containing various islands
* The North, a mostly-inaccessible area of great importance to the Mahjarrat

label: North Brimhaven mine
title: North Brimhaven mine
lead:
The North Brimhaven mine (also known as the horseshoe mine or Karamja north-western mine) is located on the peninsula north-west of Brimhaven. The mine has ten gold rocks from which players may mine gold ore as well as a single gold ore spawn. The mine is in a members-only area. It is worth noting that there are several Poison Scorpions in the area (they will automatically attack you unless you are combat level 41 or higher).

Players may get to this area quickly from the Fisher Realm by blowing a magic whistle and then walking a few steps south.

label: North Crandor mine
title: North Crandor mine
lead: North Crandor mine is a mining site scattered across the northern area of Crandor. Access to this mine is obtained by traversing the tunnel entered from the Karamja Volcano, or as a one-time deal, through a ship from the Dragon Slayer I quest. The closest bank to these mines are in Draynor Village for free players and in Mor Ul Rek for members. Beware of the lesser demons lurking around the dungeon entrance.

label: Noterazzo
title: Noterazzo
lead: Noterazzo is the owner of the Bandit Duty Free, he is located in the Wilderness Bandit Camp. He purportedly gives players the best deals they will find. When asked why, he says it is due to the heavy taxes on general stores in Asgarnia and Misthalin and because of that it is hard for them to run an effective business, while he claims that the taxmen do not visit him. This is reflected in his buying prices, which at empty stock are the same as High Level Alchemy value, a trait shared with Martin Thwait's Lost and Found.

label: Nothing
title: Nothing
lead:
Nothing, also known as an empty roll, is a possible drop that can be found on many monsters in Old School RuneScape. This is associated mainly with low-level to medium-level monster drop tables and the rare drop table/gem drop table. Equipping a ring of wealth will remove all empty rolls from the rare drop table and gem drop table, increasing the likelihood of obtaining a more valuable drop.

In the case where a monster rolls their drop table more than once, for example the Alchemical Hydra, the empty roll affects only one roll at a time.

label: Null
title: Null
lead:
In the context of computing, null is a value in various programming languages that indicates something is unset, undefined, or invalid. Null exists as a value in both Java and RuneScript, and can occasionally be seen in game by players in certain atypical situations.

The string Null may be visible in interfaces when the config data for an entity is unable to load. For example, opening the Choose Option menu on an item may incorrectly display the name of the item as Null for a brief duration until the data has fully loaded, after which the correct name of the item will be visible.

label: Nulodion
title: Nulodion
lead:
Nulodion is the official Dwarf Cannon engineer and Weapons Development Chief of the Dwarven Black Guard. During the Dwarf Cannon quest, he gives the player an ammo mould and Nulodion's notes to bring back to Captain Lawgof. Nulodion's Multicannon parts for sale is the only place that sells the parts of the dwarf multicannon (once the player has completed the Dwarf Cannon quest). The store also sells the cannon instruction manual, and ammo moulds to make your own cannonballs. Ammo moulds are used in the Between a Rock... quest.

If your cannon decays or you log out while your cannon is set up you can talk to him, selecting the dialogue option "I've lost my cannon" will allow you to retrieve it free of charge. If you had Shattered cannon ornament kits attached to your cannon, they will also be retrieved.

label: Nulodion's notes
title: Nulodion's notes
lead:
Nulodion's notes are a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. It is obtained from Nulodion after speaking to Captain Lawgof after repairing his broken dwarf multicannon.

It is given to Captain Lawgof alongside Ammo mould to complete the quest.

label: Nurmof
title: Nurmof
lead:
Nurmof is the owner of Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop, where he sells bronze through rune pickaxes. He resides in the back of the Dwarven Mines, near the Keldagrim train cart and dwarven gang members.

Nurmof can also repair broken dragon pickaxes for a fee of . This is useful for ironmen accounts who don't yet have one, but is not always worth it for players wishing to sell the pickaxe on the Grand Exchange. At current prices, repairing a broken dragon pickaxe and then selling it on the Grand Exchange will bring the player a profit of .

label: Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop.
title: Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop.
lead:
Nurmof's Pickaxe Shop is located in the north-west cul-de-sac of the Dwarven Mine, accessed through the alley with the anvil, south-west from the north entrance. Alternatively, a disk of returning can be used anywhere within the mine to teleport players south west of the cul-de-sac entrance.

Nurmof stocks all pickaxes from bronze up to normal rune, except for black.

label: Nurse Sarah
title: Nurse Sarah
lead:
Nurse Sarah is a nurse running the medical clinic in West Ardougne, and she's the only medical professional in the city. She is involved in the Biohazard quest, where the player acquires the medical gown needed to access the mourners' hideout in the cupboard in the northern part of her house.

She may also be involved in Song of the Elves, where the player, disguised as a mourner, claims that all medical practitioners must undergo more training to deal with the "plague", which increases the public's hostility towards King Lathas.

label: Nutcracker outfit
title: Nutcracker outfit
lead:
The nutcracker outfit is a holiday reward received from completing a Christmas event from 2022 onwards. The costume gives no bonus to any stats. Each piece of the outfit has a "Change-style" option that switches between the festive and sweet variants.

If lost or destroyed, the costume can be reclaimed from Diango in Draynor Village. In addition, all of the costume items may be stored in the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: nylocas
title: nylocas
lead:
The nylocas are a race of arachnids originating from Vampyrium. Many of them can be encountered in the Theatre of Blood.

According to Arachnids of vampyrium, the nylocas do not typically grow any larger than an adult human, and often group together in small colonies. While weak individually, they could overwhelm an opponent with numbers. When the Stranger from Afar led the vampyres from Vampyrium to Gielinor, Verzik Vitur brought many of her domesticated nylocas along.

label: Oak logs
title: Oak logs
lead:
Oak logs are logs obtained from cutting oak trees at level 15 Woodcutting and give 37.5 experience points each. Players can burn these logs using the Firemaking skill at level 15 for 60 experience each. Members can also fletch these logs.

Members training Construction can bring oak logs to a sawmill to make oak planks at a cost of 250 coins each. Alternatively, the Lunar spell Plank Make can allow players to convert them to planks at a lower cost, but at the expense of runes. The use of oak planks in Construction increased the price of oak logs.

label: Oak longbow

lead:

It can be made at level 25 Fletching by using a knife on oak logs to cut them into an oak longbow (u), granting 25 experience, and then using a bowstring on the unstrung bow, granting another 25 experience. It requires level 5 Ranged to wield and can fire arrows up to and including steel.

It has identical stats to the oak shortbow, but fires at a slower speed.

* Wilderness obelisk, a teleportation device for moving around the Wilderness
* Fountain of Rune, a source of infinite spell usage in the Wilderness
* Obelisk (Construction), the player-owned house version of the Wilderness obelisk
* Obelisk (Necropolis), used to unlock the teleport to Jaltevas via the Pharaoh's sceptre
* Magical Obelisk in Hallowed Sepulchre
* Grouping Obelisk used to form raid parties in the Tombs of Amascut
* Obelisk in the Wardens' fight in the Tombs of Amascut
* Obelisk (Proudspire), found at the top of The Proudspire

label: Obelisk (interface item)
title: Obelisk (interface item)
lead:
The Obelisk is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the obelisk.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Obelisk of Air
title: Obelisk of Air

label: Obelisk of Earth
title: Obelisk of Earth
lead:
The Obelisk of Earth (aka Earth Obelisk) is used to cast the Charge Earth Orb spell at level 60 Magic. The spell is cast on the obelisk in order to charge an Unpowered orb into an Earth orb. The Obelisk is located in the Wilderness area of Edgeville Dungeon, south of the Black demons in the area where Chronozon is found. In order to avoid taking damage from Chronozon while casting the spell, stand on the south side of the obelisk.

When using this obelisk it is recommended to have a method of curing poison in your bank as the poison spiders can poison you even if you have Protect from Melee prayer on. If you are low combat level and afraid that the poison may kill you, you can bring a method of curing poison with you at the price of having fewer orbs in your inventory. Alternatively, an Antipoison potion that grants immunity can be sipped at the bank right before you head to the obelisk as well. For instance, an Antidote++ dose will grant 12 minutes of immunity, which is roughly 3-4 trips.

label: Obelisk of Fire
title: Obelisk of Fire
lead: The Obelisk of Fire (referred to as fire obelisk in the standard spellbook) is used to cast the Charge Fire Orb spell; the spell must be cast on the obelisk, not on an orb. It is used for enchanting an unpowered orb into a fire orb, requiring level 63 Magic, granting 73 Magic experience. The obelisk is located at the end of Taverley Dungeon, west of the black dragons.

label: Obelisk of Water
title: Obelisk of Water
lead:
