The Obelisk of Water (referred to as water obelisk in the standard spellbook) is used to cast the Charge Water Orb spell; the spell must be cast on the obelisk, not on an orb. It is used for enchanting an unpowered orb into a water orb, requiring level 56 Magic, granting 66 Magic experience. The obelisk is located on the island across from the shore of Catherby, reached by climbing a ladder at the end of Taverley Dungeon by the black dragons.

label: Object IDs
title: Object IDs
lead: Each unique object in the game (typically called scenery) has an in-game ID associated with it which can be used by tools such as plugins or the online interactive world map.

label: Obli
title: Obli
lead: Obli runs Obli's General Store in Shilo Village. His shop does not have the normal stock of a general store, but rather has the same items available for purchase as Jiminua's Jungle Store in Tai Bwo Wannai. The price of items in the store change if the player wears Karamja gloves.

label: Obli's General Store.
title: Obli's General Store.
lead:
Obli's General Store is a general store run by Obli in Shilo Village on Karamja. This general store has the largest stock of general stores with items varying from Machetes to Candles, and Charcoal to Spades.

Unlike other general stores on the island of Karamja, Obli offers better prices with Karamja Gloves 1 instead of needing Karamja Gloves 3.

label: Observatory
title: Observatory
lead: The Observatory is a complex mostly used during the Observatory Quest. It consists of four parts. The area was overrun by goblins, who have damaged the telescope, and players must fix it during the quest. The original bridge to the Observatory has been destroyed, so you must go underground at the ruined buildings and through the Observatory Dungeon to get to it. Alternatively, players who have completed the Observatory Quest can use the grapple shortcut with 23 Agility, 24 Ranged, and 28 Strength. It should be noted that players who use this shortcut forfeit their mith grapple, but in doing so create a permanent shortcut.

label: Observatory Dungeon
title: Observatory Dungeon
lead: The Observatory Dungeon leads from the Goblin settlement found north-east of the Observatory, to the Observatory. The dungeon is a giant maze, infested with low-levelled goblins and a few high-levelled goblin guards.

label: Observatory Quest
title: Observatory Quest
lead: The Observatory Quest is a quest where you must help the professor of the observatory repair the structure and restore it to its former glory.

label: OSBuddy
title: OSBuddy
lead:
OSBuddy (formerly RSBuddy) was a third-party client for Old School RuneScape. As of June 2022, the website for the client is no longer available, and was officially discontinued in 2023. Instead, the URL now displays a page warning players of fake OSBuddy clients, and a link to the official Jagex Launcher:

It was one of three non-Jagex clients on the Approved Client List that players are permitted to use, along with RuneLite and HDOS, until it was taken off the list in November of 2023.

label: Observatory assistant
title: Observatory assistant
lead:
Patrick, the Observatory assistant, can be found in the reception building just north of the Observatory.

He and Professor Gronigen do not get along, but Patrick meekly follows along with the Professor's demands. If you talk to Patrick after completing the Observatory Quest, he will thank you and hand you a Jug of wine. Additionally, he will tell you Scorpius would be proud, at which your character is confused. He tells you to look at a book or "Check out old graveyards" referring to where you can find Scorpius.

label: Observatory lens
title: Observatory lens
lead: The observatory lens is a quest item made and used during the Observatory Quest. During the quest, a lens mould and a piece of molten glass must be given to the professor in the Observatory. The professor will then attempt to craft the lens but be unable to do so. He will then return the mould and glass to the player and request it be crafted. Once made, the lens should be given to the professor so that the telescope can be repaired.

label: Observatory professor
title: Observatory professor
lead: Professor Mambo-duna-roona Gronigen (labelled as Observatory professor) is a scholar found in the Observatory reception (north of Castle Wars). He is the main NPC for the Observatory Quest. After the quest, he is found in the observatory itself. He and his assistant often bicker. In Recipe for Disaster, he is referred to as Professor Gronigen during the short quiz for the Enchanted egg and also in the update in which Observatory Quest was released.

label: Obsidian
title: Obsidian
lead:
Obsidian may refer to:

*Obsidian armour
*Obsidian equipment
*Onyx jewellery (sometimes called obsidian jewellery).
*Tokkul, a currency made from obsidian.

label: obsidian armour
title: obsidian armour
lead:
Obsidian armour is melee armour, which can be purchased from TzHaar-Hur-Zal's Equipment Store in the inner area of Mor Ul Rek or TzHaar-Hur-Tel's Equipment Store in the outer area of the city; however, TzHaar-Hur-Tel only sells the cape and shield. Alternatively, players can obtain this armour from killing TzHaar-Kets that reside in the city. The helmet, platebody, and platelegs are uncommon due to the fact that only the level 221 TzHaar-Ket, which require the completion of the Fight Caves activity to access, drop them.

Equipping the armour requires 60 Defence; however, the cape does not have any Defence requirement. When the platebody, platelegs, and helmet are equipped together, all obsidian weaponry will be given a 10% boost in melee accuracy and melee strength. Note that this set bonus stacks with the 20% damage boost offered by the berserker necklace when wielding obsidian weaponry.

label: Obsidian decorative bench (interface item)
title: Obsidian decorative bench (interface item)
lead:
The Obsidian decorative bench is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Obsidian decorative bench.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Obsidian equipment
title: Obsidian equipment
lead:
Obsidian equipment is equipment made from obsidian, often used by the TzHaar. They are weapons and other pieces that can be obtained by exchanging Tokkul or as rare drops from TzHaar creatures.

The obsidian helmet, platebody and platelegs are uncommon due to the fact that only the higher level TzHaar-Ket, which require the completion of the Fight Caves activity to reach, drop them.

label: Obsidian fence (interface item)
title: Obsidian fence (interface item)
lead:
The Obsidian fence is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Obsidian fence.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Obsidian mauler
title: Obsidian mauler
lead: An obsidian mauler is a type of pure build. The name derives from the build's iconic weapon: the Tzhaar-ket-om, which is most commonly referred to as 'obby maul'. The main objective of the build is to train Strength to extremely high levels (often level 99) whilst restricting all other Combat stats to maintain a low Combat level. Obbies typically remain at a low Attack level (often level 1), naturally having low Ranged and Magic levels. Obby maulers unlock access to the tzhaar-ket-om at just 60 Strength allowing obbies to hit high amounts of damage in comparison to other pures in their combat level bracket. As of 21 April 2021, all warhammers including Dragon warhammer now require Strength to wield instead of Attack, making this account build massively more powerful than ever before for both non-members and members Player killing.

label: Obstacle net
title: Obstacle net
lead: Obstacle net may refer to:

label: Obstacle net (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course)
title: Obstacle net (Barbarian Outpost Agility Course)
lead: The obstacle net is an Agility obstacle found within the Barbarian Outpost Agility Course. Passing the obstacle requires 35 Agility and will award 8.2 Agility experience.

label: Obstacle net (Gnome Stronghold Agility Course)
title: Obstacle net (Gnome Stronghold Agility Course)
lead: The Obstacle net is an Agility obstacle found within the Gnome Stronghold Agility Course. An Agility level of one is required to pass the obstacle, which will then grant the player 10 Agility experience. It is not possible to fail this obstacle.

label: Obstacle pipe
title: Obstacle pipe
lead: Obstacle pipe may refer to:

label: Obstacle pipe (Barbarian Outpost)
title: Obstacle pipe (Barbarian Outpost)
lead:
The Obstacle pipe is an Agility shortcut that connects the Barbarian Outpost to the agility course. Passing through the pipe awards the player 10 Agility experience.

Clicking the pipe without moving the camera is an Idle training method and can gain you up to 10,000xp per hour.

label: Obstacle pipe (Gnome Stronghold Agility Course)
title: Obstacle pipe (Gnome Stronghold Agility Course)
lead: The obstacle pipe is the final Agility obstacle on the Gnome Stronghold Agility Course. It requires 1 Agility to pass which grants 10 Agility experience. It is not possible to fail this obstacle.

label: Obstacle pipe (Wilderness Agility Course)
title: Obstacle pipe (Wilderness Agility Course)
lead: The obstacle pipe is an Agility obstacle found within the Wilderness Agility Course. An Agility level of 49 is required to pass the obstacle, which will then grant the player 12.5 Agility experience.

label: Obstacle pipe (Yanille Agility Dungeon)
title: Obstacle pipe (Yanille Agility Dungeon)
lead: An obstacle pipe is an Agility shortcut. It is the second obstacle in the Yanille Agility Dungeon, and traversing it leads to a group of skeletons. Failing the pipe obstacle will cause the player to take damage, and become stuck for a short time.

label: Occult altar (interface item)
title: Occult altar (interface item)
lead:
The Occult altar is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Occult altar.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Occupation of Paterdomus
title: Occupation of Paterdomus
lead:
The Occupation of Paterdomus is a conflict occurring in year 169 of the Fifth Age. The conflict occurred after attacking Monks of Zamorak stormed the Saradominist temple of Paterdomus, which lies on the border of Misthalin and Morytania, in a narrow mountain-pass called Silvarea.

The Zamorakians broke into the temple and imprisoned Drezel, the resident Saradominist priest, in the upper levels of the building, next to a coffin containing a vampyre that the Zamorakians had brought. It is unknown if the two Saradominist priests, Ulizius and Hiylik Myna, were present at the time of the attack.

label: ocean
title: ocean
lead:
Oceans are the largest bodies of water on the world of Gielinor.
[[File:OCEANS_(2).png|thumb|right|The seas of Gielinor are divided into nine oceans. For a large image [ click here].]]

label: Ocean depth
title: Ocean depth
lead:
Ocean depth is a scrapped mechanic that referred to the height of a water body's surface, relative to the seabed.

The different depths were visually shown in-game and on the world map with the water colour, with the deepest waters being a dark shade of blue and shallower waters being increasingly lighter shades.

label: ocean encounters
title: ocean encounters
lead:
Ocean encounters are a variety of events that appear at random to interact with players while they are Sailing. It is not necessary to actually be moving for an encounter to spawn; simply turning in place is able to spawn one. Ocean encounters are 4% more common while aboard a ship that has a keg filled with kraken ink stout.

A sound effect (id 10969) is played when an event spawns in the player's vicinity.

label: Ocga
title: Ocga
lead: Ocga is an attackable citizen of Burthorpe with many dialogues when spoken to, often welcoming the player. He may also speak about the Burthorpe Imperial Guard, White Knights, and Trolls, who unfortunately took his baby son.

label: Odd batta
title: Odd batta
lead:
An odd batta was previously obtained during Gnome cooking. If a player added incorrect ingredients to a Half baked batta, they would receive this item.

As the cooking process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added via the reworked interface, which eliminated the possibility of any mistakes by the player. As a result, the odd batta was discontinued.

label: Odd cocktail
title: Odd cocktail
lead: An odd cocktail was the result of a player error when making a gnome cocktail. An update in 2006 eliminated this with an improved cocktail interface; as a result, it has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape. The odd cocktail healed some health, increased Strength, but reduced Attack, making it similar to certain beers.

label: Odd crunchies
title: Odd crunchies
lead:
Odd crunchies were previously obtained during Gnome cooking. If a player added incorrect ingredients to a Half baked crunchy, they would receive this item.

As the cooking process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added via the reworked interface, which eliminated the possibility of any mistakes by the player. As a result, the odd crunchies were discontinued.

label: Odd gnomebowl
title: Odd gnomebowl
lead:
An odd gnomebowl was previously obtained during Gnome cooking. If a player added incorrect ingredients to a Half baked bowl, they would receive this item.

As the cooking process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, all ingredients are automatically added via the reworked interface, which eliminated the possibility of any mistakes by the player. As a result, the odd gnomebowl was discontinued.

label: Odd looking wall
title: Odd looking wall
lead: The Odd looking wall is the entrance to the Elemental Workshop dungeon. You need a battered key to open it, which can be found in the battered book that starts the elemental workshop quest series.

label: Odd looking wall (Edgeville Dungeon)
title: Odd looking wall (Edgeville Dungeon)
lead:
The odd looking wall is a piece of interactive scenery found in the Edgeville Dungeon, north west of the Edgeville entrance.

Pushing the wall gives access to a room containing some coin spawns, two giant rats level 3 and 6, as well as some chests, crates and barrels.

label: Odd markings (Underground Pass)
title: Odd markings (Underground Pass)
lead: The odd markings are a trap found within the Underground Pass dungeon. Players must first search the odd markings to disarm the trap before safely passing through it. It is possible to fail disarming the trap, accidentally triggering it, which can damage 3 to 14 Hitpoints. Passing through the trap without disarming first will damage the player based on a percentage of their current health.

label: Offering spells
title: Offering spells
lead: Offering spells are a category of utility spells in the Arceuus spellbook. Requiring completion of A Kingdom Divided to use, these spells convert up to three sets of remains to prayer points, granting three times the normal experience of burying or scattering remains.

label: Offerings (disambiguation)
title: Offerings (disambiguation)
lead:
Offerings may refer to:

label: Og
title: Og
lead: Og is an ogre encountered during the Watchtower quest. During the quest he sends you to get his gold that the ogre chieftain Toban took from him. Surprisingly, Og seems to be one of the few ogres that can speak the common language rather fluently. He can be located north-west of Yanille within debris remains along with other ogres. After the quest, he cannot be spoken to.

label: ogre
title: ogre
lead:
Ogres are a monster found throughout Gielinor, most notably the ogre city of Gu'Tanoth.

The best place to kill ogres for Slayer is directly west of Yanille, near where Og is situated and the small island, although the location may be crowded with cannon users that can make training there inhospitable; if that's the case, it is possible to kill the ogres camping in the ruins immediately to the north, behind a line of trees, as those are not affected by the cannon.

label: Ogre (race)
title: Ogre (race)
lead:
Ogres are a race found throughout Gielinor. They are known for their brute strength and considered to be dim. During the God Wars, ogres were followers of Bandos.

Ogres can be found in several regions:
* Mainly in Kandarin
* Asgarnia, in the God Wars Dungeon
* Tirannwn, in the Underground Pass
* In the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon

label: ogre arrow
title: ogre arrow
lead:
Ogre arrows are used for hunting large game birds such as Chompy birds and Jubbly birds. These arrows can only be fired from ogre bows or composite ogre bows. Ogre arrows are required in Big Chompy Bird Hunting and the Freeing Skrach Uglogwee sub-quest of Recipe for Disaster.

They can be created through the Fletching skill at level 5, by using wolfbone arrowtips on flighted ogre arrows. 6 arrows can be made at a time with 1.0 Fletching experience granted per arrow made.

label: Ogre arrow shaft
title: Ogre arrow shaft
lead: Ogre arrow shafts are components used in making ogre arrows and brutal arrows. They require level 5 Fletching and starting the quest Big Chompy Bird Hunting to make. They are made by cutting an Achey tree and using a knife on the Achey tree logs. The amount of shafts given is random; between two and six will be made. 1.6 Fletching experience is gained per shaft made. Adding 4 feathers to each shaft makes flighted ogre arrows.

label: Ogre bellows
title: Ogre bellows
lead:
Ogre bellows are obtained by "unlocking" the Locked Ogre chest (i.e. pushing a boulder off from on top of it) in the north-west part of the cave near Rantz (not on worldmap) in eastern Feldip Hills where the ogre Rantz and his son and daughter live, directly north from the quest start icon where Big Chompy Bird Hunting is started (fairy ring code is nearby). Multiple ogre bellows can be taken from Rantz's chest.

This item is also needed for obtaining various Chompy bird hats, a section of the quest Recipe for Disaster, Mourning's End Part I and the western provinces diary.

label: Ogre bench
title: Ogre bench
lead: Five Ogre benches are located in Rantz's cave, which is inhabitted by Rantz's children, Bugs and Fycie. The cave is part of the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest.

label: Ogre bow
title: Ogre bow
lead:
The ogre bow is a weapon requiring 30 Ranged to wield. Along with the comp ogre bow, it is used to kill chompies. The bow cannot be fletched, and it can fire ogre arrows as well as brutal arrows up to mithril brutals.

The ogre bow is obtained from Rantz during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. If the bow is lost, another can be purchased from him for an amount which changes each time, but is in the range of 500-550 coins. The bow is also required for Freeing Skrach Uglogwee in the Recipe for Disaster quest.

label: Ogre chieftain
title: Ogre chieftain
lead:
Ogre chieftains are ogres that can be found in the Feldip Hills and inside the Ogre Enclave. Players can kill ogre chieftains towards an ogre Slayer task.

Due to their lacklustre drops and being more difficult to kill compared to standard ogres, players usually avoid killing them.

label: Ogre Enclave
title: Ogre Enclave
lead:
The Ogre Enclave, located south-west of Yanille and accessed via the cave in the market of Gu'Tanoth, is one of several locations containing Blue dragons, and is visited during the Watchtower Quest.

In the centre of the cave is the Rock of Dalgroth, which you can mine during the Watchtower Quest for the grey crystal.

label: Ogre guard
title: Ogre guard
lead:
Ogre guards can be found all over Gu'Tanoth. To gain access to the ogre city, you must present the Ogre relic to a guard.

In the city, the Ogre Guards will ask you to bring them something like a gold bar or, from the market (a rock cake). If you haven't got it the second time you meet them, they punch you down the hill and you will lose a varied amount of Hitpoints.

label: Ogre merchant
title: Ogre merchant
lead: Grud, named Ogre merchant in game, is an inhabitant of the ogre city of Gu'Tanoth. He owns Grud's Herblore Stall in Gu'Tanoth, which sells various Herblore items. The Watchtower quest is required to get to him.

label: Ogre relic
title: Ogre relic
lead:
An ogre relic is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. During the quest, it is given as a gift to the ogre guards, who stand at the gates of Gu'Tanoth. In return, they grant the player permanent access to the city. It should also be noted from a lore point of view that upon gifting the relic to the guards, they recognise it as a statue of the ogre warrior, Dalgroth.

The player can make the ogre relic by giving the three individual pieces to the Watchtower Wizard and having him combine them, each of which is obtained by performing tasks for ogres who live in and around Gu'Tanoth. Attempting to use the pieces on each other in order to combine the pieces will only result with the game message, "The pieces look like they would fit together, but you can't work out how to do it. Maybe someone with more experience of ogres could help."

label: Ogre spit-roast
title: Ogre spit-roast
lead: Two ogre spit-roasts are located in Feldip Hills where most ogres live. There is one at the entrance of Jiggig and another north of Rantz. Ogre spit-roasts can be used to cook raw chompy, raw jubbly or raw chicken. Any other types of food cannot be cooked on the spit-roast, simply giving Nothing interesting happens.. The "Cook-X" interface is not available when cooking here, so the individual birds need to be used on the spit-roast manually. They are the only place where raw jubbly can be cooked for the Recipe for Disaster subquest, Freeing Skrach Uglogwee.

label: Ogre tooth
title: Ogre tooth
lead:
The ogre tooth is obtained from the corpse of Gorad when he is killed by the player during the Watchtower quest.

The player must then bring the tooth to Grew, as proof that his request for Gorad's death was fulfilled.

label: Ogre trader
title: Ogre trader
lead:
Ogre traders are traders located in Gu'Tanoth. There are 3 ogre traders which can be found in Gu'Tanoth, the ogre city south-west of Yanille.

The only ogre traders that will trade with the players are Dal, the general store owner, and Grud, the ogre merchant. The other two traders will not trade with the player, saying things like "Trade with me? Who do you think you are?" and will attack the player.

label: Ogre trader (Dal)
title: Ogre trader (Dal)
lead: Dal, named Ogre trader in game, is one of three ogre traders within Gu'Tanoth. He is one of two ogre traders that do not attack if asked to trade by humans, the other being Grud. He sells basic supplies seen in most general stores.

label: Ogress
title: Ogress
lead:
Ogresses are female ogres. It may refer to one of the following:

*Chief Tess, leader of the ogresses
*Ogress Shaman, an inhabitant of the Corsair Cove Dungeon
*Ogress Warrior, an inhabitant of the Corsair Cove Dungeon

label: Oh Dear!
title: Oh Dear!
lead: Oh Dear! is a Jingle that plays during the Ceril side of Hazeel Cult, when the player returns the Carnillean armour to Ceril Carnillean and a fake "quest complete" interface appears.

label: Ohn
title: Ohn
lead: Ohn was an individual who accompanied Mortarium and his son, Onan, and several other men, in Tirannwn.

label: Oil
title: Oil
lead:
Oil may refer to:

*Lamp oil
*Blamish oil
*Sacred oil
*Olive oil
*Oil can
*Oil lamp
*Oil lantern
*Oil lantern frame
*Oily fishing rod
*Anchovy oil

label: Oil can
title: Oil can
lead:
The oil can is a quest item used only in Ernest the Chicken. It is found in the basement of Draynor Manor at the end of a maze puzzle.

It is one of three items needed to repair Professor Oddenstein's machine along with a pressure gauge and a rubber tube, so he can turn Ernest back into a human. Duplicates can be obtained after the quest, but it serves no further use.

label: Oily cloth
title: Oily cloth
lead:
Oily cloth can be obtained by searching the abandoned equipment next to the fire in the Underground Pass.

It is used to wrap around any standard arrows, which, in turn, can then be lit on fire to become fire arrows. This is only necessary during the Underground Pass quest, however, all types of fire arrows can be made with the oily cloth and used outside the quest, although they do not give extra benefits.

label: Oily fishing rod
title: Oily fishing rod
lead:
The oily fishing rod is a unique fishing rod made during the Heroes' Quest by using blamish oil with a normal fishing rod. However, players do not need to have started the quest to make this item. An oily fishing rod can be used with fishing bait to catch raw lava eels and infernal eels, which is required during the Heroes' Quest itself, as well as the Hard Wilderness Diary.

The equipable version of the fishing rod, the oily pearl fishing rod, can be made by using blamish oil on the pearl fishing rod (bought with molch pearls from Alry the Angler).

label: Olaf
title: Olaf
lead:
Olaf is the first name of two NPCs, namely:
*Olaf Hradson, found north-east of Rellekka and is the starting point for Olaf's Quest
*Olaf the Bard, found in Rellekka and is involved in The Fremennik Trials

label: Old
title: Old
lead:
Old may refer to:

* Ancient
* Old School RuneScape, the game this Wiki is about.

label: Old Bookshelf
title: Old Bookshelf
lead:
Old Bookshelf may refer to:

* Broken Old Bookshelf
* Old Bookshelf (Desert Mining Camp)
* Old Bookshelf (Recruitment Drive)
* Old Bookshelf (Seers' Village)
* Old Bookshelf (Wise Old Man)

label: Old boot
title: Old boot
lead: An old boot is an untradeable, useless item. It cannot be worn, nor can it be used with another old boot or any other item.

label: Old journal
title: Old journal
lead:
The old journal, or The Journal of Randas, is found during the Underground Pass quest near the first well. It is written by the adventurer Randas and tells of the creation of the Orbs of Light that the player has to destroy to get farther inside.

After finding the book, it can be found on the shelves in the player's house. It can also be found on one of the bookshelves in the Grand Library after Song of the Elves.

label: Old Man (disambiguation)
title: Old Man (disambiguation)
lead: Old Man may refer to:

label: Old man (Discovery of the Runes)
title: Old man (Discovery of the Runes)
lead:
, depicted in ]]
The old man was a wizard from Misthalin and the son of a smith of high standing. Near the end of his life, he told his in exchange for ale.

He was born in a time before runes, back when man struggled to survive, before they held an alliance with the dwarves. When he was young, his father told him a tale about a mage from the north that had visited his shop to buy basic tools such as hammers and chisels. The old man, eager for knowledge, snuck out in the middle of the night to find the man, to learn of magicks.

label: Old notes
title: Old notes
lead:
Old notes may refer to one of the following items:

* Old notes (Dragon Slayer II), notes written by Zorgoth on his experiments on dragons found during Dragon Slayer II
* Old notes (A Taste of Hope), notes in Serafina's home that you must obtain for Safalaan during A Taste of Hope.

label: Old Ones
title: Old Ones
lead:
.]]
The Old Ones are an ancient race of humanoids who once inhabited modern-day Varlamore and the Kebos Lowlands. They were a fairly advanced race, having their own language, were capable of drawing intricate illustrations on wood carvings, and possessed knowledge of runes (including how to craft them ) and herblore. Additionally, they were able to build large structures such as Neypotzli and Tapoyauik, and practiced a type of nature magic known as naguanil, part of which involves summoning spirits known as nagua.

Ruins of the Old Ones are plentiful within the kingdom, reaching as far north as the Kebos Swamp, and their architectural style appears to have been adopted by the lizardmen. Additionally, some of their beliefs have been incorporated into the religion of Varlamore, such as Ximoua, which refers to an endless cycle of destruction and rebirth of the world; the Twilight Emissaries believe that the Old Ones were "willingly" wiped out by the last cycle of Ximoua.

label: Old robe

Old robe is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest and it can be found after the quest's completion. The player can find it by searching the bushes surrounding the Watchtower outside the north wall of Yanille.

This item serves no purpose and is most likely there as a red herring. It cannot be worn.

label: Old School RuneScape
title: Old School RuneScape
lead:
Old School RuneScape is Jagex's official term for a previous version of the RuneScape game that was introduced from the August 2007 Archive of RuneScape, a backup of the RuneScape source code as it had been on 10 August 2007. It is also commonly referred to as OSRS or 2007scape.

This version of the game was announced in a on , which was followed by the opening of a poll to determine community interest on 2013. The poll, which ended 2013, decided, among other things, whether an additional membership fee would be charged for access to the game.

label: Old tooth
title: Old tooth
lead: An old tooth can be found while digging at the digsite using a trowel, obtained from the Varrock Museum or an Examiner, on the digging area west of the animal skull or panning in the panning area with a panning tray. When shown to Terry Balando, he says "Oh, an old tooth. It looks like it has come from a mighty being. Pity there are no tooth fairies around here!" There are currently no uses for the old tooth. Omart is an NPC encountered during the Biohazard quest. He helps you to cross the wall between West and East Ardougne. He can be found on the south end of the wall.

In the Song of the Elves, he is part of the Resistance and he and Kilron suggest riling up citizens by announcing that all doctors and nurses have to retrain.

label: one-defence pure
title: one-defence pure
lead:
A one-defence pure is a combat pure that sacrifices training Defence to focus on maximising damage output at a lower combat level. One-defence pures are usually created for player-killing as high offensive combat stats typically provide greater leverage against low- to medium-tier armour. The levels of these accounts vary, although many are within the 50 to 90 combat level range.

One-defence pures are formidable in short fights as they rely on killing their opponent quickly but are disadvantaged in sustained fights due to taking damage more consistently. This also makes training combat skills slightly more dangerous as monsters will do more damage over time.

label: One-defence pure (free-to-play)
title: One-defence pure (free-to-play)
lead: One-defence pure is an umbrella term for combat pures that do not train the Defence skill in order to maximise the damage output or utility on any given combat level. In particular, unlike their pay-to-play counterparts, free-to-play one-defence pures often train skills such as Attack or Prayer up to different, typically lower thresholds that might be otherwise suboptimal in members-only activities.

label: One-Eyed Hector
title: One-Eyed Hector
lead:
One-Eyed Hector was a pirate captain, being rather successful and wealthy. He had a room at the Blue Moon Inn in Varrock and a casket of treasure buried in Falador Park.

In 168 of the Fifth Age, his ship was boarded by agents from the Customs and Excise Office and he was killed along with most of his crew. Amongst the escapees was Redbeard Frank, who took Hector's treasure chest key with him. A year later, he trades it to an adventurer for Karamjan rum, thus relinquishing Hector's treasure.

label: onion
title: onion
lead:
Onions are a food item that can be picked from fields around Gielinor or grown through the Farming skill at level 5 with onion seeds. They heal 1 hitpoint when eaten. When eaten, the message You eat the onion. is displayed. If eaten at full health, a message will appear saying, It's always sad to see a grown [man/woman/person] cry.. If eaten below full health, the message It makes your eyes water, but it does heal some health. is displayed instead. When picking onions from fields, members may randomly receive 1 onion seed.

They are used in the following recipes:
* Mushroom potato
* Ugthanki kebab
* Vegetable batta, veg ball, worm hole (Gnome cooking)
* Garden pie (temporarily boosts Farming level by 3)

Onions picked up in a field will respawn after 50 ticks (30 seconds). Unlike onions picked from a Farming allotment, picking onions from fields provides no experience.

title: Onion & tomato
lead: Onion & tomato is a type of food that restores 3 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by using chopped onion with a tomato or using chopped tomato with an onion. Creating Onion & tomato is one of multiple steps needed to create the ugthanki kebab which requires level 58 Cooking and restores 19 Hitpoints.

label: oomlie bird
title: oomlie bird
lead:
Oomlie birds are found within the Kharazi Jungle. Like tormented warriors, these enormous version of chickens are not aggressive (however using the bullroarer near them will cause them to attack you with the message "A nearby Oomlie bird takes a dislike to the sound you are making" appearing in your chatbox). They can be killed for their oomlie meat, the main ingredient of oomlie wraps. To create one, the player needs the raw oomlie and a palm leaf found in the surroundings by shaking leafy palm trees.

The Legends' Quest needs to be started in order to kill this monster. However, it can be ranged and then the Telekinetic Grab spell can be used to get the meat before starting Legends Quest.

label: Opal
title: Opal
lead:
Opals are semi-precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut opals with a chisel, yielding 15 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the opal, resulting in a crushed gem and 3.8 experience.

Opals are the lowest level gemstone.

label: Opal bolt tips
title: Opal bolt tips
lead:
Opal bolt tips are created by using a chisel on a cut opal with 11 Fletching, yielding 1.5 Fletching experience and 12 opal bolt tips.

They are made into opal bolts when used with bronze bolts, requiring 11 Fletching, yielding 16 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. They can also be made into opal dragon bolts, requiring 84 Fletching, yielding 16 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. Both of these can then be enchanted into opal bolts (e) and opal dragon bolts (e) respectively.

label: Opal bolts
title: Opal bolts
lead:
Opal bolts are bronze bolts tipped with opal bolt tips. Opal bolts can be created through the Fletching skill for players of level 11 or above. Use a chisel on a cut opal to make 12 opal bolt tips. Attaching opal bolt tips also requires a Fletching level of 11, and for each opal bolt tip attached to a bronze bolt, a player is granted 1.6 Fletching experience. Once the opal bolt tips have been attached, the bronze bolts become opal bolts.

Opal bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Opal) by a player with level 4 Magic. The spell enchants 10 opal bolts at a time, and once they are enchanted they become enchanted opal bolts and gain a special ability.

label: Operation: Phoenix
title: Operation: Phoenix
lead:

Operation: Phoenix is the name given to what is claimed to have been an organised attack by Zamorakian wizards against the first Wizards' Tower. The operation supposedly took place in the year 70 of the Fifth Age, and ultimately resulted in the complete destruction of the tower and the loss of many magical secrets. The event, though referenced frequently throughout Gielinor's history and dialogue, has been referred to by name only once, in a Temple Knight commorb dossier obtained during the Wanted! quest.

Details regarding the incident itself are few. Prior to the attack, Zamorakians had worked in the Wizards' Tower itself. The Zamorakians supposedly tried to claim the discoveries of the Wizards' Tower in the name of Zamorak. However, they failed and burned the Wizards' Tower to the ground in retaliation. Many of the secrets of magic and runecrafting were lost as a result, including the incantation needed to teleport to the Rune Essence Mine.

label: Optimal quest guide
title: Optimal quest guide
lead: The optimal quest guide lists Old School RuneScape quests in an order that allows new Members to progress in a way that minimises the amount of skill training to completion of all the quests. This guide does not show the most efficient quest order. It does not take into consideration unlockable content, such as fairy rings or dragon equipment, that provide numerous benefits to the player's game progression. For that, it is recommended that players complete the quests in the notable quest unlocks section as soon as possible.

label: Optimal quest guide/Free-to-play
title: Optimal quest guide/Free-to-play
lead:
As few free-to-play quests have skill requirements, quests in this guide can mostly be grouped together by region.

This list does not recommend specific combat level requirements, and experienced players should be able to do all quests except for Dragon Slayer I without training skills in between doing the quests. This requires knowledge of how to safe spot Count Draynor, however, so inexperienced players may wish to train combat stats before taking on this quest.

label: Optimal quest guide/Free-to-play/Ironman
title: Optimal quest guide/Free-to-play/Ironman
lead:
Unlike the standard optimal quest guide, this optimal free-to-play Ironman quest guide focuses mostly on optimizing the progress through many different quests at once, instead of optimizing for quest experience rewards. Because many free-to-play quests can be completed more efficiently by combining their progress, most of these quests are grouped together by region. When following this guide, make sure to look at the Additional info column for not just the current quest in progress, but also at the next one or two quests, in order to more optimally prepare for the next quests.

The Additional info column will list which other quests need to be progressed during the completion of this quest, for optimal quest progress. This list does not recommend specific combat level requirements, and experienced players should be able to do all quests except for Dragon Slayer I without training skills in between doing the quests. This requires knowledge of how to safe spot Count Draynor, however, some inexperienced players may need to train combat stats before taking on this boss.

label: Oracle
title: Oracle
lead:
The Oracle is a strange woman who lives atop Ice Mountain. She is an important figure in the Dragon Slayer I quest, as she provides a clue as to how to access one of the map pieces. Occasionally, she will be visited by Postie Pete. One of the Wise Old Man's tasks involves taking a message to her.

To reach the Oracle, use the Ice Mountain pathway just below Edgeville Monastery.

label: orange
title: orange
lead: An orange is a fruit that can be grown as part of the Farming skill. Oranges are used in several gnome cooking recipes, and can be used with a knife to create orange slices or orange chunks. You can give a basket of oranges to a farmer as payment to protect a maple tree (farming). It heals 2 hitpoints regardless of the state the orange is in (whole, sliced or chunks). Oranges can be added to a compost bin to make regular compost. 3 spawns are present on an inaccessible island populated by pygmy hippos east of Kastori, the northernmost spawn can be Telegrabbed from the western coast of the Avium Savannah.

label: Orange cape
title: Orange cape
lead: An orange cape is made by using orange dye on another coloured cape.

label: orange chunks
title: orange chunks
lead:
Orange chunks are used in gnome cooking. You can obtain them by using a knife on an orange and selecting the "Dice" option.

Orange chunks are used when making a fruit batta. They are added to a half baked batta along with 4 equa leaves, 1 lime chunks and 1 pineapple chunks to create an unfinished batta (fruit).

label: Orange door
title: Orange door
lead: The Orange doors are located on the of Melzar's Maze. They must be opened during Dragon Slayer I, using an orange key obtained from killing the nearby Ghost with a hood, and no cape.

label: orange dye
title: orange dye
lead: Orange dye is a dye made by combining red dye and yellow dye. Its main use is in the quest Goblin Diplomacy, when the player must use the dye on goblin mail. This item can also be bought from the Lletya Seamstress for 6 coins. In order to access the shop, one must have at least started the Mourning's End Part I quest. Players can also obtain red and yellow dye from Aggie in Draynor Village provided she is given the ingredients needed and 5 coins per bottle of dye. Players can then combine the red and yellow dye to make orange dye.

label: Orange flowers
title: Orange flowers
lead:
Orange flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

label: Orange goblin mail
title: Orange goblin mail
lead:
Orange goblin mail is made by using orange dye on a goblin mail. Like all goblins mail, it is too small for players to normally wear as armour.

It is used during the Goblin Diplomacy quest, along with a blue and un-dyed goblin mail with Generals Bentnoze and Wartface fighting over what colour they prefer.

label: orange slices
title: orange slices
lead:
Orange slices are a food item that players can obtain by using a knife on an orange. Eating orange slices will heal 2 hitpoints. Orange slices are needed in the Goblin part of Recipe for Disaster.

Orange slices are used in gnome cooking as an ingredient in a pineapple punch cocktail. They are used in the final step of creating the drink, and must be in the inventory along with 1 lime chunks and 1 pineapple chunks to pour a mixed punch into a cocktail glass.

label: Orb of light
title: Orb of light
lead:
An orb of light, also known as a Sphere of Light, is a magical orb used in Underground Pass quest. The player destroys four of these orbs in the furnace found in the dungeon in order to progress into the next part (note: one cannot destroy the orbs in another furnace outside the underground pass). Destroying an orb yields the message, You feel a cold shudder run down your spine as the light of the orb fades.

According to the old journal, they were placed in the Underground Pass by the warrior, Randas, in a failed attempt to ward off the darkness prior to the player's involvement.

label: Orb of light (scenery)
title: Orb of light (scenery)
lead:
Orb of light is scenery found in the Underground Pass that is used to provide item spawns of four orbs of light during the quest. The orb has the appearance of a regular item, including the colour of the name and red dot on the minimap. After an orb has been destroyed by using it on the furnace, the spawn will no longer be visible.

When Underground Pass was first added to RuneScape 2 in 2004, the northern three orb spawns used actual item spawns. The southernmost spawn instead used this scenery object to handle the special behaviour with the log trap that must be disarmed, with an invisible dead orb item spawn placed at the same position to make a red dot appear on the minimap. After a bug was discovered in 2017 that caused the dead orb to be picked up , the dead orb was removed and the red dot was changed to instead be a map icon on the orb of light scenery. With the release of Song of the Elves in 2019, the northern three orb spawns were also replaced with the scenery object and are no longer visible after destroying the orbs.

label: Orb of protection
title: Orb of protection
lead:
The orb of protection is a quest item that the player must recover during the Tree Gnome Village. At the start of the quest the orb has been stolen by Khazard troops and this one is currently being held in the Khazard stronghold north-east of the Tree Gnome Village.

To recover this orb the player must break a hole in the stronghold's defences using a nearby ballista, climb in and either kill the Khazard commander or loot the chest upstairs.

label: Orbs of protection
title: Orbs of protection
lead:
The orbs of protection are a quest item that players must recover during the Tree Gnome Village quest. They are stolen by a Khazard warlord during the quest and the player must find and defeat him in order to reclaim the orbs.

Once the orbs have been recovered the player must return them to King Bolren in the centre of the Tree Gnome Village maze.

label: Orchid
title: Orchid
lead: Orchids are flowers that have white petals with pale pink labella and are found throughout some southern regions of Gielinor. Orchids are ubiquitous on Ape Atoll and also found commonly in the northern region of the Kharidian Desert and near Corsair Cove, south of Feldip Hills.

label: Order of Wizards
title: Order of Wizards
lead:
The Order of Wizards is a Saradominist organisation specialising in magic and runecraft, headquartered in the Wizards' Tower. Archmage Sedridor, the chief of research at the Tower, currently leads the Order.

The Order of Wizards was founded at the start of the Fifth Age, following the rediscovery of runecrafting. Initially, the Order was welcoming of all researching wizards, regardless of their religion or race, though it has been claimed that Zamorakian wizards were barred from certain research topics.

Orikalkum, known to adventurers by the name dragon, is a strong, red metal. While not being an ore that is minable or smeltable (although reforgable and repairable) by the player, dragon equipment is still considered as the next level up from rune and thus is included in the metals category. Dragon items typically require level 60 in their respective combat stats to equip.

The dragonkin are the original creators of Orikalkum armour and weaponry, which is nicknamed by adventurers as dragon equipment.

label: Ornament Kit
title: Ornament Kit
lead:
Ornament kits are items that are used on certain items to change their appearance. This also makes the item untradeable, unless the ornament kit is removed.

Some are obtainable by completing beginner, hard, elite or master tier Treasure Trails, but unlike most unique Treasure Trail items, these kits and some of the ornamented items are not storable at a Player-owned house. Note 1 in the table below indicates storable items.

label: Ornamental armour
title: Ornamental armour
lead:
Ornamental armour refers to a number of armour pieces that are possible rewards from Treasure Trails. All ornamental armours offer the same bonuses and penalties as their standard counterparts (with a couple of minor exceptions in the rune armour variants), although they tend to cost more due to their comparatively higher rarity. Ornamental armour is often worn as a status symbol instead of for practical purposes, especially in free-to-play.

Players cannot trim armour. The only way to obtain ornamental armour is through a Treasure Trail or by trading with another player.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Orrery (disambiguation)
title: Orrery (disambiguation)
lead:
Orrery may refer to:

* Orrery, found in the reception building north of the Observatory
* Small orrery, an ornament built in a Study of a player-owned house at level 86 Construction
* Large orrery, an ornament built in a Study of a player-owned house at level 95 Construction

label: Osman
title: Osman
lead:
Osman is the spymaster of Al Kharid and can be found just outside the palace. He plays a significant role in the quests Prince Ali Rescue and Contact!. He also makes an appearance in the first cutscene in the Recipe for Disaster quest. He is very skilled at espionage and subterfuge and politically very astute. Additionally, Osman has shown himself capable of holding his own in combat against dangerous creatures, armed with a scimitar.

Replacement Keris daggers can be bought from him for 20,000 coins after finishing Contact!, if the one initially picked up at the end of the quest be lost. If the dagger was never claimed during the quest in the first place, Osman will supply it free of charge. He also rewards players with Thieving experience in exchange for Sq'irk juice, which players can obtain in the Sorceress's Garden minigame. In order to start the minigame, one is required to first speak to Osman about it.

label: Othainian
title: Othainian
lead:
Othainian is a demon encountered during the Underground Pass quest. When killed, it drops the amulet of othanian, which is needed to obtain Iban's shadow. Protect from Melee should be used during this part of the quest to save hitpoints for coping with its attacks.

It is possible to use the small bridges connecting the platforms as a safespot to attack using Ranged, Magic, or with a halberd. In the quest, the player must also kill the other demons, Holthion and Doomion.

label: Otherworldly being
title: Otherworldly being
lead:
Otherworldly beings are unusual Zanarian monsters. They are commonly assigned as Slayer tasks by Vannaka. They are found south of the bank in Zanaris and can be safespotted by standing next to the flower pond and attacking the ones on the other side, however they move around quite a lot and players may find them difficult to safespot. An alternate and more consistent safespotting method is standing on the north or south of the pond and corner trapping the mobs on the pond corners.

More specifically, five of the six otherworldly beings have a wander radius which permits safespotting without having them retreat as long as the player stands right next to the pond. One of these five will retreat if attacked horizontally across the pond, and another will retreat when attacked vertically. The other three will not retreat as long as you stay next to the pond.

label: Otherworldly theme (interface item)
title: Otherworldly theme (interface item)
lead:
The Otherworldly theme is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Otherworldly theme.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Otrava
title: Otrava
lead:
Otrava was a member of the Sisterhood, a healer, and one of Phosani's closest companions. When the kingdom of Hallowvale fell to Lord Drakan's forces in the Third Age, Otrava, along with Phosani and Insela, swore allegiance to Zamorak and the vampyres and handed over their remaining squadrons to the invaders. Otrava followed Phosani in founding the town that would later be known as Slepe in east Morytania.

Using old texts from Senntisten, Otrava uncovered the secrets of blood magic and blood healing, which she had witnessed the Zamorakians use. She started experimenting with potions with blood and came up with the battlemage and bastion potion, which she documented in a book. There were two other potions that she had been working on, but cancelled the development of; one, the 'totality potion', for being too dangerous, and the other, the 'vigour potion', for missing ingredients.

label: Ourania
title: Ourania
lead:
Ourania may refer to:
*Locations
**Ourania Cave
**Ourania Altar
**Ourania Hunter area
*Spells
**Ourania teleport

label: ourg
title: ourg
lead:
The ourgs are a near-extinct race of gigantic ogre-like creatures, one of the most powerful races in service to the god Bandos. They were believed to be extinct, until the God Wars Dungeon thawed out. There, in the Bandos Stronghold, resides General Graardor, the last living ourg. The undead ourg Slash Bash is fought during Zogre Flesh Eaters.

Players have a chance to find ourg bones when looting ogre coffins.

label: Outpost (disambiguation)
title: Outpost (disambiguation)
lead:
Outpost may also refer to:
* Barbarian Outpost, home of barbarians in Kandarin, north of Baxtorian Falls, contains the Barbarian Outpost Agility Course and Barbarian Assault
* Outpost, a building north-west of East Ardougne where Jorral lives
* Shayziens' Wall, also known as the Shayzien Outpost, is a wall west of Shayzien near the Lizardman Settlement
* Void Knights' Outpost, home to the Void Knights and Pest Control minigame

label: Overhanging rock
title: Overhanging rock
lead: Overhanging rocks are along the Baxtorian Falls near the start of the River Dougne.

label: Overheads
title: Overheads
lead:
Overheads is a term that describes prayers that display over a character's head when in use. Overhead prayers are commonly used in a plethora of PvM and PvP-related activities. Players usually use the term "overhead" to refer specifically to protection prayers, especially in bossing and quests, as Retribution and Smite are mainly relegated to PvP usage.

Only one of these prayers may be active at a time. Activating another overhead prayer will cause the previously-active overhead to be turned off.

label: Overload

lead:
Overload may refer to:

* Overload (Chambers of Xeric)
* Overload (+)
* Blighted overload

label: Overture
title: Overture
lead: Overture is a music track that is unlocked in Seers' Village.

label: Oyster
title: Oyster
lead: An oyster has a chance to contain an oyster pearl or be an empty oyster. They can sometimes be obtained by fishing with a big fishing net (requires 16 Fishing), by drift net fishing, or through panning at the Digsite. They can also be obtained as a drop from various monsters. The pearls found from an oyster can be made into pearl bolt tips at level 41 Fletching by using a chisel on them.

label: Oyster pearl
title: Oyster pearl
lead:
An oyster pearl is a small, round, milky-coloured semi-precious gem obtained by opening oysters. They can also be collected by fishing with a big fishing net, participating in the Fishing Trawler minigame, panning in the river at the Digsite, sorting large salvage, or by killing various monsters.

Players with 41 Fletching can use a chisel on this item to gain 6 pearl bolt tips, which can be attached to iron bolts or dragon bolts to make pearl bolts or pearl dragon bolts.

label: Oyster pearls
title: Oyster pearls
lead: Oyster pearls are a reward from the Sea Slug quest. They can also be dropped by some monsters or obtained through shipwreck salvaging. Players with 41 Fletching can use a chisel on this item to gain 24 pearl bolt tips, which can be attached to iron bolts or dragon bolts to make pearl bolts or pearl dragon bolts.

label: Oziach
title: Oziach
lead:
Oziach is a master smith with ties to the Champions' Guild. He lives just north-west of Edgeville and, during Dragon Slayer I, informs applicants to the Guild where the three map parts to Crandor can be found. Afterwards, he sells rune platebodies, green dragonhide bodies and anti-dragon shields from his shop.

Oziach appears to wear a bulkier version of the rune platebody with alternate colouring. Along with the Hero, he is the only other NPC wearing alternatively coloured Rune armour.

label: Oziach (shop)
title: Oziach (shop)
lead: Oziach is an armour shop located in Edgeville, just south of the Wilderness ditch. The completion of the Dragon Slayer I quest is required to access the shop. Oziach sells rune platebodies, green d'hide bodies, and anti-dragon shields.

label: P boots
title: P boots
lead:
P Boots can refer to multiple sets of boots, including but not limited to:

* Pegasian boots
* Pirate boots
* Primordial boots
* Prospector boots
* Pyromancer boots

label: Paddewwa
title: Paddewwa
lead: Paddewwa was once a fortress of the Zarosian Empire. It was destroyed by Saradomin's forces following the Betrayal of Zaros.

label: Pado's robes
title: Pado's robes
lead:
Pado's robes were a armour set, proposed alongside the Warding skill. They were a set of degradable mage robes that would have required level 30 Magic, Defence, and Prayer to wear. In order to ward the robes, players had to learn to do so via Brother Jered in the Edgeville Monastery, this would require level 30 Warding, along with holy silk and silver bars.

The set had the following passive effects when all pieces are worn.
*The total prayer bonus increases from +8 to +20.
*Will of Saradomin - 10% increased damage against the following Zamorakian followers: Chaos druid, Elder Chaos druid, Monk of Zamorak, Lesser demon, Greater demon, Black demon, Vampyre, Werewolf, Chaos dwarf, Dark wizard, Solus Dellagar, Dessous, Damis, Fareed, Kamil, K'ril Tsutsaroth, Balfrug Kreeyath, Tstanon Karlak, Zakl'n Gritch
*Players cannot cast Flames of Zamorak whilst wearing the robes.

label: Page (Kharedst's memoirs)
title: Page (Kharedst's memoirs)
lead:
Pages that were torn from Kharedst's memoirs are obtained as rewards from quests around Great Kourend. Except for the secret page, adding one to Kharedst's memoirs or to the Book of the dead unlocks a teleport location, adds 20 teleport charges to the book, and increases the book's maximum charges by 20. Each page also unlocks an entry that can be read in the book, and unique dialogue encountered when using the book on a specific NPC.

If the pages are lost before putting them in the book, they can be freely reclaimed from the respective lords of each Kourend house.

label: Painting (scenery)
title: Painting (scenery)
lead: Paintings are found in many locations, they serve no purpose other than aesthetics.

label: Palace
title: Palace
lead:
Palace may refer to any of the following:

*Varrock Palace, a building in Varrock (marked as "Palace" on the world map)
*Keldagrim Palace, a large building in Keldagrim that is the headquarters of the Consortium
*Al Kharid Palace, a building in Al Kharid and the residence of The Emir

label: paladin
title: paladin
lead:
Paladins are found in East Ardougne, wandering near the castle and market. Upon completion of the Song of the Elves, paladins will patrol the streets of West Ardougne as well. They are from Ardougne's Holy Order of Paladins, and wear the symbol of Saradomin. Three unique paladin variants – Sir Carl, Sir Harry, and Sir Jerro – are found in the Underground Pass, all of whom must be killed during the quest in order to obtain their badges.

Players can pickpocket paladins at level 70 Thieving to gain 131.8 experience, 80 coins and 2 chaos runes.

label: Paladin (disambiguation)
title: Paladin (disambiguation)
lead: Paladin may refer to:

label: Paladin's badge
title: Paladin's badge
lead:
Paladin's badge may refer to:

*Paladin's badge (Sir Carl), the green badge.
*Paladin's badge (Sir Harry), the red badge.
*Paladin's badge (Sir Jerro), the blue badge.

label: Paladin's badge (Sir Carl)
title: Paladin's badge (Sir Carl)
lead: Paladin's badge is a green coloured coat of arms held by Sir Carl in the dungeon west of West Ardougne. During the Underground Pass quest the player must kill the three paladins, Sir Carl, Sir Harry and Sir Jerro, in order to obtain their badges and then throw the badges and a unicorn horn down a well in order to progress to the next part of the dungeon.

label: Paladin's badge (Sir Harry)
title: Paladin's badge (Sir Harry)
lead: Paladin's badge is a red coloured coat of arms held by Sir Harry in the dungeon west of West Ardougne. During the Underground Pass quest the player must kill the three paladins, Sir Carl, Sir Harry and Sir Jerro, in order to obtain their badges and then throw the badges and a unicorn horn down a well in order to progress to the next part of the dungeon.

label: Paladin's badge (Sir Jerro)
title: Paladin's badge (Sir Jerro)
lead: Paladin's badge is a blue coloured coat of arms held by Sir Jerro in the dungeon west of West Ardougne. During the Underground Pass quest the player must kill the three paladins, Sir Carl, Sir Harry and Sir Jerro, in order to obtain their badges and then throw the badges and a unicorn horn down a well in order to progress to the next part of the dungeon.

label: Palingrad
title: Palingrad
lead: Palingrad is a penguin city within the Motherland. The Pescallion has declared that until research on the southern species was complete and a plan was developed, the Killer Gentoo Penguins operatives could not return to Palingrad.

label: Palkeera
title: Palkeera
lead:
Palkeera was a Zamorakian Mahjarrat mentioned by the golem during Desert Treasure II and in some notes written by her fellow Mahjarrat, Zemouregal.

She was a pontifex in the Zarosian Empire, but allied with Zamorak in the God Wars. She was also the mother of General Khazard.

label: Palm leaf
title: Palm leaf
lead:
Palm leaves may be obtained by 'shaking' the leafy palm trees located around the small pool of water in the middle of the Kharazi Jungle or on Remote Island. This is a primary ingredient in the oomlie wrap made for the Karamja Hard Diary, as they protect the delicate meat of the oomlie bird from burning. This item is also used during Troubled Tortugans to craft makeshift bandages.

There is a hard Karamja Diary task to collect five palm leaves, though one can drop and pick up the same leaf multiple times to complete the task.

label: Palm leaf (unobtainable item)
title: Palm leaf (unobtainable item)
lead:
A Palm leaf is an unobtainable version of the Palm leaf. Palm leaves could previously be traded and turned into bank notes; however, they were made untradeable in 2007 due to frequent use in scams. Any player who had a noted palm leaf was given this now discontinued item. It is identical to the real leaf, except it is stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

label: Palm tree (Ardrigal)
title: Palm tree (Ardrigal)
lead:
Palm tree is a scenery object found growing north-east of Tai Bwo Wannai near the harpie bug swarms. The palm tree is searchable in order to obtain a grimy ardrigal. The ardrigal has uses during Jungle Potion and Legends' Quest.

After picking, the palm tree is searchable again after 60 seconds.

label: Palm tree (Shilo Village)
title: Palm tree (Shilo Village)
lead: Palm trees are scenery objects that can be found north-west of the Ship Yard on Karamja. Players must search a tree during the Shilo Village quest in order for a set of doors used to enter Rashiliyia's Tomb to appear.

label: Panning guide
title: Panning guide
lead: The Panning guide can be found in the south-east section of the Digsite, near the River Salve. He helps teach players how to pan for gold nuggets during The Dig Site quest.

label: Panning point
title: Panning point
lead:
A Panning point is a location found at the Digsite where players can pan for nuggets, uncut opal, uncut jade, oysters or coins. It also plays a role in The Dig Site quest, where the panning point is used to find a special cup in the river for one of the students.

Panning at these points will fill the panning tray with mud, which must then be inspected to obtain the item rewards.

label: Panning tray
title: Panning tray
lead:
The panning tray is a quest item used during The Dig Site quest to retrieve a special cup. One spawns in the tent near the south-eastern short of the Digsite east of Varrock.

To use it, the panning guide must be bribed with a cup of tea. This can be done before the quest is started.

label: Panning tray (unobtainable item)
title: Panning tray (unobtainable item)
lead:
The panning tray is an unobtainable item that is used during The Dig Site. In the quest, the player is required to use the panning tray to retrieve a special cup. There is a chance of finding gold nuggets when searching the panning tray, causing this item to appear in the chatbox. The actual panning tray full of gold cannot be obtained by the player however.

In RuneScape Classic, the item could be obtained after searching the muddy panning tray. It is unknown what happened to these items on the transition to RuneScape 2.

label: Papyrus
title: Papyrus
lead:
Papyrus is an item used in building various furniture in a player-owned house. Additionally, after completing Enlightened Journey, using a ball of wool and unlit candle on a papyrus results in an origami balloon.

Papyrus is notably required for the following quests:
*Darkness of Hallowvale (given during quest)
*Three for Enlightened Journey
*At least three for Legends' Quest to map the Kharazi Jungle
*One for The Golem quest to write him a new program
*Zogre Flesh Eaters (given during quest)
*Shilo Village
*While Guthix Sleeps

label: Papyrus (unobtainable item)
title: Papyrus (unobtainable item)
lead:
Used papyrus is an unobtainable item that was released during the RuneScape 2 beta. It is a version of papyrus that has been used to write something using charcoal. Presumably, it was intended to be used during Shilo Village, which had been slightly reworked during the transition to RuneScape 2. However, for unknown reasons the used papyrus was never added to the game.

If the player loses the Bervirius notes at any point during the quest, they must recreate them using both Papyrus and Charcoal. It is possible therefore that the used papyrus would have either been a product of this action, or merely appear as a chatbox message similar to the Locating crystal.

label: Parade
title: Parade
lead:
Parade is a music track that is unlocked at Silvarea and the Paterdomus Temple.

In Classic mode, it unlocks in a more limited area around the Silvarea Limestone Mine.

label: Paramaya Inn
title: Paramaya Inn
lead:
The Paramaya Inn is an inn in Shilo Village. It is run by Kaleb Paramaya, who used to give players a reward for completing the medium Karamja Diary. Pirate Jackie the Fruit is now solely responsible for that task.

Players can purchase wine for one coin and beer for two coins. Also if players want to, they can purchase a Paramaya ticket for 35 coins and rent a room for the night. On the top floor (the area requiring a Paramaya ticket to enter) are only some beds and cabinets. The Inn was useful during RuneScape Classic, as beds were necessary for players to rest on to restore their Fatigue; however, as fatigue is not present in Old School RuneScape, this area is useless during normal gameplay.

label: Paramaya ticket
title: Paramaya ticket
lead:
A paramaya ticket is a ticket that allows a player to spend the night in the dormitory of the Paramaya Inn. It looks identical to an Archery ticket. Gaining access to the dormitory is a purely aesthetic feature which has no function, as players cannot actually sleep in the beds there.

One ticket may be purchased from Kaleb Paramaya for 35 coins or a pack of five can be bought for 175 coins. This item was made untradeable in an update on 22 January 2007 because of its use in scams.

label: Paramaya ticket (unobtainable item)
title: Paramaya ticket (unobtainable item)
lead:
A Paramaya ticket is an unobtainable version of the Paramaya ticket. Tickets could previously be traded and turned into bank notes; however, they were made untradeable in 2007 due to frequent use in scams. Any player who had a noted Paramaya ticket was given this now discontinued item. It is identical to the real ticket, except it is stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

Parchment may refer to:

*Parchment (Olaf's Quest) - The reward from Olaf's Quest
*Parchment (Contact!) - Obtained during the quest Contact!
*Trouver parchment - Reward from Last Man Standing

Parrot may refer to:

*Drunk parrot, obtained by feeding one of the zoo parrots alco-chunks

*The Shrimp and Parrot, a restaurant in Brimhaven
