title: Parrot (Sailing)
lead: Parrot is an NPC in the Sailing alpha.

label: Part summer pie
title: Part summer pie
lead:
Part summer pie may refer to:
* Part summer pie (strawberry)
* Part summer pie (watermelon)

label: Partisan
title: Partisan
lead:
Partisans are a category of one-handed melee weapons with combat stats balanced between stab and crush, and with no access to a slash attack style. Due to their one-handed nature, partisans may be wielded in conjunction with a shield or defender to provide additional bonuses.

There are currently 5 partisans in game, 4 of which are upgraded versions of the keris partisan (obtained as a reward from the quest Beneath Cursed Sands) using jewels rewarded from the Tombs of Amascut.

label: Party
title: Party
lead:
Party may refer to:

*Party (emote), the emote unlocked after completing a birthday event
*House party, a party held in a player-owned house
*Partyhat
*Drop party, a party involving items dropped on the ground for others to pick up
*Falador Party Room, a designated area for drop parties
*Party balloon, balloons dropped in the Falador Party Room
*Party Pete, the NPC who runs the Falador Party Room

label: Party Balloon
title: Party Balloon
lead:
Party balloons are interactable decorations most commonly found in the Falador Party Room and Clan Halls. A player can choose to burst a balloon that is on the ground, doing so has a chance of an item from the nearby chest dropping to the ground. A balloon will remain on the ground for 2 minutes before despawning.

In the case of the Falador Party Room, balloons will begin to fall evenly across the room after a player pulls the lever next to the chest, and opts to pay 1000 coins to start a Balloon Bonanza. A similar process exists for the Clan Hall by pulling the lever present in that location.

label: Party Pete
title: Party Pete
lead:
Party Pete is the founder and owner of the Falador Party Room, and the first offspring of the Pete Family. He features in several events, the most notable being the 2017 Birthday event.

Talking to him reveals more information about the Party Room. Additionally, you can purchase Party Pete's Bumper Book of Games. He is one of the few non-player characters to adorn a partyhat.

label: Partyhat
title: Partyhat
lead:
Partyhats, commonly abbreviated as phats (pronounced pee-hat), can be obtained in the form of two partyhat sets from participating in a Christmas event. Alternatively, players can pull christmas crackers and choose to receive any tradeable partyhat.

Before the 2013 Christmas event, they were made available in Old School RuneScape on 4 July 2013, requiring players would search the different spawn locations across Gielinor and/or attend the Grab-a-hat community streams with Mod Mat K between 4 July 2013 and 14 July 2013.

label: Passageway
title: Passageway
lead:
Passageway may refer to:
* Passageway (Rogues' Den)
* Passageway (Tarn's Lair)

label: passive effect
title: passive effect
lead: Many items and equipment sets have passive effects or set effects, which trigger on their own when equipped. These effects confer a wide variety of benefits, both combat and non-combat. In the case of a passive effect that applies to an equipment set, all items of that set must generally be equipped for the set to activate.

label: Password
title: Password
lead: A Password is a set of characters which is used to gain access to an account. It is recommended to change your password every 1 to 3 months to ensure that your account stays secure. Never tell anyone the password of your account as it will compromise the security of your account. Jagex Moderators will never ask for your password. Anyone that attempts to ask for your password should immediately be reported for scamming. There is a system that prevents any IP address from accessing any Old School RuneScape account if five or more incorrect passwords are tried in succession. This is to prevent would-be hijackers from gaining unauthorised access to your account.

label: Paste
title: Paste
lead:
Paste is a quest item used in Prince Ali Rescue to disguise Prince Ali so he can escape from Lady Keli's prison.

Aggie can make it from ashes, redberries, flour, and water for free.

label: Paste (disambiguation)
title: Paste (disambiguation)
lead:
Paste may refer to any of the following:

* Paste, a quest item used in Prince Ali Rescue
* Raw swamp paste, used to make Swamp paste
* Swamp paste, used in various activities
* Anchovy paste, used to make Anchovy oil
* Karambwan paste, used to posion spears & Hastae
* Karambwanji paste, used to make different types of Pasty jogre bones
* Tchiki nut paste, used to make Raw stuffed snake for the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster
* Moonlight grub paste, used to make Moonlight potions
* Mox paste, used in Mixology
* Aga paste, used in Mixology
* Lye paste, used in Mixology

label: pastry dough
title: pastry dough
lead:
Pastry dough is used to make pies. It is made from a pot of flour and either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water. It can then be used on a pie dish to make a pie shell. The pie shell is then used with the filling, which varies according to which pie is to be made.

Pastry dough can also be made as a source of money. By buying or making one pot of flour, and one bucket of water or jug of water, then mixing the ingredients together, selling the dough will give profit.

label: Patch Notes
title: Patch Notes
lead: Patch Notes were updates documenting game changes such minor gameplay element changes and correcting graphical issues.

label: Paterdomus Temple
title: Paterdomus Temple
lead: The Paterdomus Temple is the temple marking Misthalin's eastern border. It acts as the gateway into Morytania, and is located in eastern Silvarea, along the River Salve. The priest Drezel is the owner of the temple, although Monks of Zamorak have taken it over during Priest in Peril quest, trying to take down the Salve's magical barrier.

label: Pathfinding
title: Pathfinding
lead: Pathfinding is the process of calculating which path of game squares (after this point referred to as 'tile') a player or NPC should move to get to its desired destination. This process happens whenever a player or NPC attempts to walk, run, or interact with a different player, different NPC, or an object in the world.

label: Paul Gower
title: Paul Gower
lead:
Paul Gower is the co-founder of Jagex, along with Ian and Andrew Gower. In addition, he helped develop and program RuneScape since 1999 when he helped create an early version of the game. The Sunday Times Rich List 2007 ranked Paul and his brother Andrew Gower as the 654th richest entrepreneurs in the UK, worth £196 million. They were awarded the Industry Legend prize at the 2010 Develop Awards.

He developed many of the quests in RuneScape, and thus was a key figure in shaping the story of the game. Paul has also created Karamja, leather crafting, and the Cooks' Guild.

label: Paw
title: Paw
lead:
Paw may refer to:

* Bunny paws, an Easter holiday item
* Kruk's paw, an item obtained from killing Kruk during Monkey Madness II to create a Kruk monkey greegree
* Monkey paw, a quest item used in the Rag and Bone Man I quest
** Polished monkey paw, a quest item made by boiling a monkey paw in a pot of vinegar

label: Pay-to-play Cooking training
title: Pay-to-play Cooking training
lead: This guide aims to assist players in training Cooking by using the most effective methods available. The Grand Exchange prices of items will fluctuate, so check the prices before buying and selling supplies in large quantities.

label: Pay-to-play Crafting training
title: Pay-to-play Crafting training
lead: Crafting training methods usually cost money and require a lot of capital to buy the supplies needed. Prices of materials will fluctuate, so check the Grand Exchange prices before buying and selling them in large quantities.

label: Pay-to-play Firemaking training
title: Pay-to-play Firemaking training
lead: This article gives tips about training the Firemaking skill.

label: Pay-to-play Fishing training
title: Pay-to-play Fishing training
lead: This guide outlines the best methods for training the Fishing skill.

label: Pay-to-play Hitpoints training
title: Pay-to-play Hitpoints training
lead: Unlike most skills, Hitpoints is rarely leveled on its own, as most methods of training combat skills (Attack, Strength, Defence, Ranged, and Magic) also give Hitpoints experience. However, there are a few methods for training Hitpoints specifically.

label: Pay-to-play Magic training
title: Pay-to-play Magic training
lead:
Magic can be trained passively while training other skills. The passive training methods can be tedious or expensive before High Level Alchemy becomes available, so consider low-effort or cheaper alternatives to get through the early levels.

At higher levels, Magic can be trained much faster through casting multi-target burst or barrage spells on Ancient Magicks. An efficient way to do this is on Slayer tasks, as certain Slayer monsters (such as dust devils and Greater Nechryael) can be bursted or barraged for fast Slayer experience.

label: Pay-to-play melee training
title: Pay-to-play melee training
lead:
This article provides information about effective ways to train Attack, Strength, Defence, and Hitpoints through melee combat.

This guide is organised into sections based on skill levels. For example, if the section header is Levels 20 to 30, you should begin training at the area with an Attack and Strength level of at least 20. Defence is also preferred to be at that level but is not always required. The solution to lower Defence is to bring more food or use food that heals more.

label: Pay-to-play Mining training
title: Pay-to-play Mining training
lead: This article provides an overview of strategies used to train the Mining skill.

label: Pay-to-play Prayer training
title: Pay-to-play Prayer training
lead:
Despite the high cost to Train Prayer effectively, it is a very important skill due to what it provides in combat utility.

Many quests recommend 43 Prayer, so that all 3 protection prayers are available for use. Important skill milestones include Level 50 for completing all quests, Level 77 for unlocking all prayers and Level 85 for completing all Achievement Diaries. A higher Prayer level also allows the player to restore more prayer points per dose of prayer potion/super restore/sanfew serum.

label: Pay-to-play Ranged training
title: Pay-to-play Ranged training
lead: This article provides an overview of strategies used to train the Ranged skill.

label: Pay-to-play Runecraft training
title: Pay-to-play Runecraft training
lead: This guide describes the most effective methods to train the Runecraft skill.

label: Pay-to-play Smithing training
title: Pay-to-play Smithing training
lead: This article gives tips about training Smithing.

label: Pay-to-play Woodcutting training
title: Pay-to-play Woodcutting training
lead:
This guide outlines the best methods for training the Woodcutting skill. The profit from Woodcutting is low compared to other money-making methods and the profitable methods offer very slow experience per hour. Some players may find it more beneficial to perform the fastest experience methods and use the saved time to make money from other activities.

For maximum theoretical experience rates for certain Woodcutting training methods, see this page.

label: Pearl
title: Pearl
lead:
Pearl may refer to:

*Molch pearl
*Oyster pearl
*Pearl Danio
*Abyssal pearls

label: Pearl bolt tips
title: Pearl bolt tips
lead:
Pearl bolt tips are created by using a chisel on an oyster pearl or oyster pearls with 41 Fletching, yielding 3.2 Fletching experience both, but 6 and 24 pearl bolt tips respectively.

They are made into pearl bolts when used with iron bolts, requiring 41 Fletching, yielding 32 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. They can also be made into pearl dragon bolts, requiring 84 Fletching, yielding 32 Fletching experience per 10 bolts. Both of these can then be enchanted into pearl bolts (e) and pearl dragon bolts (e) respectively.

label: Pearl bolts
title: Pearl bolts
lead:
Pearl bolts are iron bolts tipped with pearl bolt tips. Pearl bolts can be created through the Fletching skill by attaching pearl bolt tips to iron bolts. Attaching pearl bolt tips requires 41 Fletching. Once the pearl bolt tips have been attached, the iron bolts become pearl bolts.

Pearl bolts can be enchanted through the spell Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Pearl) with level 24 Magic. The spell enchants 10 bolts at a time. Once they are enchanted they become enchanted pearl bolts and gain a special ability.

label: Pearl rod (disambiguation)
title: Pearl rod (disambiguation)
lead:
Pearl rod may refer to:

* Pearl fishing rod
* Pearl barbarian rod
* Pearl fly fishing rod
* Oily pearl fishing rod

label: Peasant
title: Peasant
lead: Peasants are men that serve The Fisher King who rules the Fisher Realm and guards the Holy Grail. They can not be attacked.

label: Pee Hat
title: Pee Hat
lead: Pee Hat is a level 91 troll found on Death Plateau. Like the rest of the "big, bad" trolls in the area, such as Stick, Kraka, and Rock, he drops a rune warhammer or granite shield, and as such is commonly hunted by ironmen looking to upgrade their armour.

label: Pegasian
title: Pegasian
lead:
Pegasian may refer to the following:

*Pegasian crystal
*Pegasian boots

label: Peksa
title: Peksa
lead: Peksa is a barbarian who owns the Helmet Shop in the Barbarian Village. Players can purchase a variety of helmet from him. He also plays a small part in the Scorpion Catcher quest where he hid a scorpion in his brother Ivor's room.

label: Pelican
title: Pelican
lead: Pelicans are non-interactive birds that are found alongside cormorants. They are found on Fossil Island and south of the Isle of Serpents.

label: Penance
title: Penance
lead: Penance are a race only found within and fought through the minigame Barbarian Assault. They are a strange bunch of creatures, and can only be killed by certain strategies. They are lead by the deadly Penance Queen, also only fought during the minigame. All Penance have one eye, and are able to communicate and coordinate with each other through telepathy. Penance creatures all start out as Queen spawn, and receive communication from the Penance Queen who determines what type of Penance creature they should grow into. If a Queen spawn receives no communication from the Penance Queen, it turns into a Queen itself.

label: Penance (attribute)
title: Penance (attribute)
lead: The penance attribute is assigned to monsters that receive extra damage in Barbarian Assault from players in the attacker role.

label: Penance armour
title: Penance armour
lead:
Penance armour is level 40 armour (or 45 Defence with the hats) that can be bought using points earned in the Barbarian Assault minigame. There are four roles: Attacker, Defender, Collector and Healer. A Penance hat, torso, skirt and gloves require points in each role in order to be bought. The hat, torso, and skirt also require the Penance Queen to have been killed in the 10th wave.

A full set costs 1,275 Honour points, in all four roles, thus a total of 5,100 points (all roles added together).

label: Penance hat
title: Penance hat
lead:
Penance hat may refer to:

*Fighter hat
*Healer hat
*Ranger hat
*Runner hat

label: Penda
title: Penda
lead: Penda is a citizen in Burthorpe, a bar patron and hangs out more at The Toad and Chicken than his own house.

label: Pendant (disambiguation)
title: Pendant (disambiguation)
lead:
Pendant may refer to:

* Armadyl pendant, an item obtained from a Guardian of Armadyl
* Crystal pendant, an item obtained during the Regicide quest
* Digsite pendant, a teleportation item
** Mounted digsite pendant, a piece of furniture

* Pendant of ates, a teleportation item
* Pendant of lucien, an item obtained during the Temple of Ikov quest
* Stolen pendant, an item obtained whilst stealing artefacts

label: Pendant of lucien
title: Pendant of lucien
lead:
The pendant of lucien is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. Lucien gives the player the pendant immediately after starting the quest. Equipping it allows access to the northern dungeon door in the Temple of Ikov dungeon because it is imbued with Lucien's courage.

If lost it can be reobtained by:
* Talking to Lucien in the Flying Horse Inn in Ardougne north of the Ardougne Castle.
* Talking to Lucien in his house east of Edgeville, once he has moved there and only if you sided with him.
* Pickpocketing Movario.

label: Penguin
title: Penguin
lead:
Penguins (Spheniscidae callidus) are a race of flightless aquatic birds found in Gielinor, specifically in the north, the Penguin 'Motherland', and other islands. Penguins are one of Andrew Gower's favourite animals , revered in a manner similar to Bob the Jagex Cat, and have therefore been included in many aspects of RuneScape. A notable item honouring penguins includes the penguin mask, which is obtainable from medium clues in Treasure Trails. Penguins originate from the Motherland, its capital being Palingrad.

While some penguins, such as those found on an island near Miscellania (accessible via fairy ring code ), are apparently benign and unintelligent, presumably not part of The Pescallion's organisation, the penguins found on the Iceberg have organised themselves into a cunning and militant organisation known as the Killer Gentoo Penguins, or KGP, led by The Pescallion. One of his sons, Pescaling Pax, rules the Iceberg. Their goal is to destroy all humans and take over Gielinor. They are incredibly adept at technology, and they have created advanced infrastructures and a number of disguises like the "Thing" found in Fred the Farmer's sheep pen.

label: Penguin (monster)
title: Penguin (monster)
lead: Penguins are low-levelled monsters found on Here Be Penguins, only accessible by using the fairy ring, and also inside an exhibit in the Ardougne Zoo. They have no drops apart from bones, and are therefore rarely killed.

label: Perfected armour
title: Perfected armour
lead:
Perfected armour may refer to:

*Perfected crystal equipment
*Perfected corrupted equipment

label: perfected corrupted equipment
title: perfected corrupted equipment
lead:
Perfected corrupted equipment is a set of armour and weapons created within The Corrupted Gauntlet. It is the highest tier of the corrupted sets, one tier higher than attuned corrupted equipment. Its crystal counterpart is the perfected crystal equipment.

Creating the full armour set from scratch requires 540 crystal shards and 13 each of linum tirinum, crystal ore and phren bark. Upgrading from the attuned armour set requires 240 crystal shards and 6 each of linum tirinum, crystal ore and phren bark.

label: Perfected crystal equipment
title: Perfected crystal equipment
lead:
Perfected crystal equipment is a set of armour and weapons created and only used within The Gauntlet. It is the highest tier of the crystal sets, one tier higher than attuned crystal equipment. Its corrupted counterpart is the perfected corrupted equipment.

Creating the full armour set from scratch requires 540 crystal shards and 13 each of linum tirinum, crystal ore and phren bark. Upgrading from the attuned armour set requires 240 crystal shards and 6 each of linum tirinum, crystal ore and phren bark.

label: Perican
title: Perican
lead:
The Pericans were a group of refugees who fled Great Kourend through the Custodia Mountains in order to escape from Xeric. The Pericans would unite with the Talkasti to found what would become present day Varlamore.

The Pericans arrived in the region after the Talkasti, with Civitas illa Fortis as their first major settlement. The River Varla was an early boundary between Perican and Talkasti territory.

label: Perseriya
title: Perseriya
lead:
Perseriya was a siren who served the Zarosian Empire under the rank of Praefectus Classis, the Admiral of the Fleet. At some point during the Third Age, after the Betrayal of Zaros, Perseriya was tasked with transporting the Elder Horn, known by its codename "Imperium", to the far east. This was not without difficulty; one legionary would interact with the artefact, resulting in another legionary causing a massacre. The Admiral would order both soldiers executed. While a strict disciplinarian, the Admiral was fair, inviting the crew to celebrate in her ancestral home following success of the mission.

However, the artefact sent east was in fact a fake; the delivery of the artefact eastwards was a cover operation, with the real one kept inside Perseriya's private cabin. The Elder Horn would later be transported and sealed within the Ancient Vault after returning from the far east, where the means to open it would be entrusted to the Whisperer, Duke Sucellus, Vardorvis, and Perseriya herself. Following the success of her missions, Zarosian intelligence would discover the location of the Stone of Jas, known by its codename "Primus", which was stolen by Saradomin sometime after the Betrayal of Zaros. The Stone, known as the Eye of Saradomin by his followers, was hidden within the Temple of the Eye, found beneath the ocean south of Hallowvale.

label: Pest Control/Strategies
title: Pest Control/Strategies
lead:
Pest Control is a cooperative minigame set on the Void Knights' Outpost, where players work together to protect the Void Knight and destroy four enemy portals. The objective is simple: defeat the pests, destroy the portals, and keep the Void Knight alive.

The game features various types of pests, each with unique abilities and behaviours. Players must manage their roles, whether attacking the portals, defending the Void Knight, or preventing pests from healing the portals.

label: Pestle and mortar
title: Pestle and mortar
lead:
The pestle and mortar is a tool used to crush items for use in Herblore and many quests, as well as the Sorceress's Garden minigame.
It can be bought from Herbalists and certain general stores. If used to auto-crush items, it will do so every three game ticks.

label: pet
title: pet
lead:
housing many pets.]]
A pet is a non-combat NPC loyal to a player that is generally obtained from monster drops and skilling. Most pets are very rare drops from certain bosses or skilling activities and do not serve a purpose other than aesthetics. The player is able to interact with most pets, but they may only have one pet following them at a time. Pets are limited to a walking pace (except for Nexling and Babi); if they become stuck and/or too far away from the player they follow, they will teleport close to the player and continue. They can also be called to the player's side using the "Call follower" button under the Worn Equipment tab. There are currently 68 available pets in Old School RuneScape.

Pets may be stored in the bank or inventory and will follow the player when dropped. Players can store up to 68 pets in the menagerie of a player-owned house (with the highest-level pet house). Restrictions on bringing pets into minigames and boss encounters vary by activity; for example, pets are prohibited in Barbarian Assault but are allowed in Guardians of the Rift.

label: Pet list (interface item)
title: Pet list (interface item)
lead:
The Pet list is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Pet list.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Pete (disambiguation)
title: Pete (disambiguation)
lead:
Pete may refer to:

* Pete, a canoe instructor on the River Dougne
* Makeover Mage, whose name is Pete when in male form
* 'Picarron' Pete, a pirate aboard the Lady Zay
* ScarFace Pete, a man from the Heroes' Quest
* Solus Dellagar, a dangerous criminal nicknamed Stealthy Pete

label: Pete's candlestick
title: Pete's candlestick
lead: Pete's candlestick is a quest item used in Heroes' Quest. The player must work collaboratively with another player to kill Grip in order to obtain his keyring and can then use this to access a treasure room that contains the candlesticks. However, players cannot complete the quest if they trade someone else's candlestick, they must obtain their own.

label: Pew
title: Pew
lead: Pews are seating located in the Entrana church and Paterdomus Temple. They feature a symbol of Saradomin on either side.

label: Phantom
title: Phantom
lead:
Phantom may refer to:

* Phantom Muspah
* Phantom Hand, summoned by Xamphur
* The phantom that appears in the final phase of the Wardens' boss fight
* Tombs of Amascut's demi-bosses phantoms:
** Akkha's Phantom
** Ba-Ba's Phantom
** Kephri's Phantom
** Zebak's Phantom

label: Phantom Muspah/Strategies
title: Phantom Muspah/Strategies
lead: After completion of Secrets of the North, the Strange Creature can be fought again in the form of a Phantom Muspah (aka, "Muspah"). This time, it is stronger.

label: Phearthee Levalsyx
title: Phearthee Levalsyx
lead: Phearthee Levalsyx, according to the Varrock Census, is the name of the mugger in south-west Varrock.

label: Pheasant costume
title: Pheasant costume
lead:
The pheasant costume is created by using a needle and thread (or a costume needle) on pheasant tail feathers, which are a possible reward as part of the Pheasant Control Forestry event. There are four pieces of the outfit in total.
It takes 60 pheasant tail feathers to obtain the full costume. The costume is cosmetic only.

label: Philipe Carnillean
title: Philipe Carnillean
lead: Philipe Carnillean is the son of Sir Ceril Carnillean and Henryeta Carnillean, and the heir of the Carnillean family, featured in the Hazeel Cult quest.

label: Philop
title: Philop
lead:
Philop Fairweather is one of Gertrude's four children. He can be found with his brother Kanel inside Gertrude's house. The two older children, Wilough and Shilop, are found in Varrock Square. He appears to be playing with his red dragon toy.

Although the player may attempt to talk to him, there is no dialogue other than a message in the chat stating that the boy is busy playing.

label: Philophaire
title: Philophaire
lead: Philophaire is the writer of the book Ideology of Darkness. In the book they tell a story about a teaching a student of theirs about a philosophical perspective on light and darkness, indicating that they are or were a teacher of sorts. In The Ascent, a story from the Kourend Chronicles written by Mori, Philophaire is mentioned, as Mori recalls a line from their work 'Philosophy of Darkness'. This might be an alternative title of the same book, or another book that does not exist in-game currently. Little other information about them is known.

label: Phoenix crossbow
title: Phoenix crossbow
lead:
The Phoenix crossbow is a quest item, although it can be traded. It has the same stats as a regular Crossbow except for attack range, but weighs significantly less. It can be obtained and is used in the quest Shield of Arrav. The Phoenix crossbow has no requirements to wield, and can only fire bronze bolts. It can also be used with a mith grapple for agility shortcuts.

The Phoenix crossbow is not often used, as the Bronze crossbow requires the same Ranged level to equip, but gives a Ranged accuracy of +18, whilst the Phoenix crossbow only gives +6. However, the Phoenix crossbow is essentially free, and since Bronze crossbows and above are members-only items, the Phoenix crossbow is the second-best crossbow available to free-to-play players. While the Phoenix crossbow is lighter than and has the same +6 range bonus as the standard Crossbow, the Phoenix crossbow has a maximum range of 7 tiles, whereas the standard Crossbow has a range of 10 tiles.

label: Phoenix Gang
title: Phoenix Gang
lead:
The Phoenix Gang is a gang at war with the Black Arm Gang. Their base is situated in the south-east of Varrock, between the city's southern entrance and the altar of Zamorak to the east. The gang operates under a front known as the VTAM Corporation, , which stands for Varrock Thieves and Muggers.

According to their leader, Straven, the Black Arm Gang is a splinter group of the Phoenix Gang that mutinied. During the process, the Shield of Arrav was broken in two. Only the left half remains with the gang.

label: Phoenix Gang Hideout
title: Phoenix Gang Hideout
lead:
Located in the south-eastern alleys of Varrock, the Phoenix Gang Hideout is a meeting place for the notorious gang members of the Phoenix Gang.

The Phoenix Gang Hideout is known to the people of Varrock as the headquarters of the VTAM Corporation, an alias used by the Phoenix Gang to hide their identity. During the Shield of Arrav quest, the Phoenix Gang Hideout is accessible to members of the gang. Upon joining the gang, players are given a key to the weapons store room, which is next door to the hideout. If the player kills the weaponsmaster, they can steal a Phoenix crossbow. This crossbow can only use bolts up to bronze. The store room also contains a spawn of grapes which respawn roughly every 43 seconds if taken.

label: Phosani
title: Phosani
lead:
Phosani was a former Saradominist Justiciar, known as the Justiciar of the Wolf. Known by her knights as the White Wolf, in part because of her bright silver hair, she was described as the most loyal and fiercest of Saradomin's followers, and the bastion against all evil.

She was stationed in Hallowvale when the Zamorakian vampyre Lowerniel Drakan and his army attacked it during the Third Age. The kingdom of Hallowvale fell as Queen Efaritay was forced to surrender after the capture of her human husband, King Ascertes. Despite her loyalty to Saradomin, Phosani felt abandoned by Saradomin following this crushing defeat, and she, along with her closest companions, Insela and Otrava, decided to desert Saradomin and swore allegiance to Zamorak and Lowerniel Drakan. Phosani and her companions went before him, and the former offered her remaining troops as blood tithes and thralls for the vampyres. The sacrifices were accepted by the Drakans, and Phosani and her companions became part of the new regime in the Sanguinesti region.

label: Phosani's Nightmare/Strategies
title: Phosani's Nightmare/Strategies
lead:
Phosani's Nightmare is a solo boss located in the Sisterhood Sanctuary, a dungeon beneath Slepe in Morytania. It is the stronger version of the Nightmare.

Players can initiate the fight by entering the Pool of Nightmares which is located north of The Nightmare's arena on a raised area. As a solo instanced fight, players do not need to hop worlds.

label: Phyrrys
title: Phyrrys
lead: Phyrrys was the apprentice of the legendary astronomer Scorpius in the Fourth Age, mentioned in the 21st Postbag from the Hedge. Following Scorpius's death, Phyrrys began work on the Calendar of Gielinor. Phyrrys was unable to make his calendar account for 40 days of the year. Many years after his death, an astronomer discovered the remains of his journal, and solved this problem by adding the 40 days in between Septober and Novtumber. This month was named the Ire of Phyrrys in honour of his work.

label: Physical boundary
title: Physical boundary
lead:
A physical boundary is something in the area which does not allow a player to pass through it. Some examples of physical boundaries are:

*Walls
*Fences
*Locked doors or gates
*Rocks
*Prison bars
*Trees
*Plants
*Barrels
*Crates
*Signposts
*Ladders
*Hedges

label: piano
title: piano
lead: Pianos are scenery objects found in various locations throughout Gielinor. Players cannot interact with most pianos, but they can examine them. Piano stools are often found nearby.

label: PJ timer
title: PJ timer
lead:
The PJ timer (Pile jumping timer) is a grace period in single-way combat areas during which a player cannot be attacked by another opponent or aggressive monsters since the last time they were attacked. The timer ensures that fights cannot be interrupted as long as both participants exchange attacks. The name of this term refers to PJing, a common abbreviation of player jacking or pile jumping, which is used to describe rushing or interrupting fights in PvP combat.

Additionally, players cannot log out for 16 ticks after being attacked in both PvP and PvM combat, regardless of whether they are under the effect of the PJ timer.

label: PJ Timer Beta
title: PJ Timer Beta
lead:
To test out changes to the PJ timer, the beta worlds were once again briefly opened for players. Changes included being that the timer is now active in all single way and singles plus areas and also NPCs respecting the grace period.

Upon logging in, players were provided with PvP gear and max stats inside the Ferox Enclave as with previous beta periods.

label: PM
title: PM
lead:
PM or Pm may refer to:

*Private Message, private exchange of messages facilitated by the game
*Player Moderator, players who given special privileges along with accompanying responsibilities by Jagex
*Pirates' Hideout mine, commonly known as the Pirate Mine
*Phantom Muspah, a solo boss that can be fought after completion of the quest Secrets of the North.
*Perilous Moons, a quest in Varlamore which unlocks the Moons of Peril.
*Neypotzli, the dungeon unlocked during Perilous Moons.

label: Piano (disambiguation)
title: Piano (disambiguation)
lead:
Piano may refer to:
* Piano, a scenery object found in various locations
* Piano (Clan Hall)
* Piano (Hosidius)
* Piano (KGP Headquarters)
* Piano (Misthalin Mystery)
* Piano (Seers' Village)
* Piano (Witch's House)

label: Piano stool
title: Piano stool
lead: Piano stools are scenery objects found throughout Gielinor and always located next to a piano. Regular piano stools appear next to both the regular grand and upright pianos, while the ornate stools appear next to grand pianos with pedals and the Clan Hall piano. Players cannot interact with piano stools, but they can examine them.

label: Pick (disambiguation)
title: Pick (disambiguation)
lead:
Pick may refer to:

*Pickaxes
*Picking something up after it has been dropped.

label: pickaxe
title: pickaxe
lead:
Pickaxes, often abbreviated to picks, are tools used to mine any type of ore or otherwise mineable items, and some types of blockages in Gielinor. Pickaxes can either be held in the inventory or wielded; but, to wield a pickaxe, the wielder's Attack level must be high enough. Wielding the pickaxe provides extra space in the inventory. This is useful when mining for a profit, as one extra ore can be held.

Pickaxes are also a category of melee weapon with its own set of combat options, using stab and crush attack styles.

label: pickaxe handle
title: pickaxe handle
lead:
A pickaxe handle was the handle of a pickaxe. When players were mining, a random event may have caused the pickaxe head to fly off. Players had to pick it up and attach it back onto the handle. A similar thing used to happen to players while woodcutting, only with an axe head and axe handle.

After random events were voted to be reworked in late 2014, they were subsequently removed from the game with the next update.

label: pickaxe head
title: pickaxe head
lead:
A Pickaxe head may fly off the handle of a player's pickaxe due to a random event which may occur while a player is mining. To fix it, collect it off the ground and reattach it to the handle.

title: Picket fence (interface item)

The Picket fence is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Picket fence.

label: Picnic bench
title: Picnic bench
lead: Various Picnic benches can be found scattered across Gielinor. They're purely decorational, and trying to use an item on a picnic bench will result in a game message in the chatbox saying "The table appears to be in use."

label: Picture
title: Picture
lead:
The picture is a quest item used only in Plague City. It is found in Edmond and Arlena's house in the north-west of East Ardougne.

It is shown to Jethick, who will direct the player to the Rehnison house in West Ardougne.

label: Picture (disambiguation)
title: Picture (disambiguation)

Picture may refer to several drawings and portraits:

**Signed portrait, signed by the Dragon Inn Bartender acknowledging that he did, in fact, see Sithik Ints

label: pie
title: pie
lead:
A pie is a type of food that players can make with the Cooking skill. It takes two bites to eat, leaving an empty pie dish which can be reused.

In order to make a pie, players must use flour and water to make pastry dough, and then add it to a pie dish to get a pie shell. Then, various fillings may be added to create a raw pie. A list of fillings can be found in the recipe book, or in the chart below. Finally, players can use a range to bake the pie. Players with level 65 Magic and who have completed Lunar Diplomacy can use the spell Bake Pie instead, which cooks pies with a 100% success rate.

label: Pie dish
title: Pie dish
lead:
A pie dish is used in Cooking to bake pies. Players must add a pastry dough (a pot of flour and either a jug of water, a bucket of water, or a bowl of water combined) to the pie dish to form a pie shell. It then can be filled by the filling of choice. Afterwards, the pie can then be baked in an oven. Players can create this in a pottery oven.

Despite unfired pie dishes requiring 7 Crafting to make, turning an unfired pie dish into a pie dish has no Crafting requirement and can be done at level 1.

label: Pie shell
title: Pie shell
lead:
A pie shell is used to make various kinds of pie. It is made by using a pastry dough on a pie dish. Players can fill a pie shell with any of several fillings to make a raw pie which must be cooked on a range.

Possible fillings include: redberries for redberry pie, cooked meat or cooked chicken for meat pie, or cooking apple for an apple pie and many more. Members have access to a wider variety of fillings from mud pies to summer pies.

label: Piece of railing
title: Piece of railing
lead:
A piece of railing is a quest item in the Underground Pass quest. It is obtained by searching a cage that contains a unicorn. The railing is used to lever a rock off of a ledge so that it crashes down and breaks the cage open, killing the unicorn in the process. The player can then search the broken cage to obtain a withered unicorn horn.

It can be safely dropped after obtaining the horn, as it serves no other purpose during the quest.

label: Pierre
title: Pierre
lead: Pierre is the Sinclair dog handler. He is called as a witness during the King's Ransom quest. When he is called up, players should ask him about the poison bought for the disappearance.

label: Pigeon cage
title: Pigeon cage
lead:
A pigeon cage is a quest item used in Biohazard and One Small Favour. It can be found in the garden behind Jerico's house, immediately south of the northern bank in East Ardougne.

In Biohazard, it is used to distract the mourner guards on the watchtower with bird seed. In One Small Favour, five of them are turned into chicken cages by using a steel bar.

label: Pike
title: Pike
lead: Pike is a type of fish that restores 8 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw pike on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 20 Cooking and granting 80 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt pike. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Pike is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 54, or 49 when using the Lumbridge range.

label: Pile jumping
title: Pile jumping
lead:
Pile jumping means attacking a player who has just killed someone else in a player-killing area. In other words, it's attempting to kill an already weakened opponent who may be busy looking at their loot from a previous kill. Pile jumping can be considered as dishonourable since the player being jumped may have been able to easily take out their jumper if they were ready.

The abbreviaton PJing can also mean player jumping or player jacking, which is attacking a player whose opponent is not dead yet.

label: Pile of rocks
title: Pile of rocks
lead:
Pile of rocks are found in the Underground Pass when the player fails the rope swing. Failing the rope swing will bring the player to a large area where the player must follow the path to reach the pile of rocks to exit the area.

A second pile of rocks were added alongside a very small cavern with the release of Song of the Elves. It is not currently known how to access this cavern, or what happens when the rocks are climbed.

label: Pile of rubble (Yanille Agility Dungeon)
title: Pile of rubble (Yanille Agility Dungeon)
lead: The pile of rubble is an Agility shortcut in the Yanille Agility Dungeon. It provides access to an area with 4 chaos druids and Salarin the twisted.

label: Pillar
title: Pillar
lead:
Pillar may refer to:

*Pillar (Hallowed Sepulchre)
*Pillar (Corsair Cove Dungeon)
*Pillars in the Brimhaven Agility Arena
*Pillars in the Inferno
*Pillars of Zanash
*Weathervane pillar
*Pillar (Revenant Caves)
*Structural pillar
*Pillar (Runic altar)
*Pillar (The Garden of Death)
*Pillar (Dream World)
*Ruined Pillar
:* Ruined Pillar (Blood Altar), a variant found only at the true Blood Altar
:* Ruined Pillar (unused), a variant found only in the game cache
*Pillars in the Theatre of Blood's nylocas room
*Supporting Pillar
*Ancient Pillar
*Ancient Pillar (Desert Treasure II)
*Pillar frag used to grow an pillar coral plant
*Pillar coral harvested from an pillar coral plant
*Pillar coral plant

label: Pillar (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
title: Pillar (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
lead:
The pillar is an Agility obstacle found within the Brimhaven Agility Arena. Failing to cross will cause the player to fall and take damage; they will need to go up a nearby climbing rope to get back onto the course.

The amount of damage dealt by the fall is based on the player's current health, according to the formula below:

label: Pillar (Runic altar)
title: Pillar (Runic altar)
lead: Pillars can be found at the Runic altars as part of the temples surrounding the altars. They are also found in the Eastern Ruins in the Wilderness. They are non-interactive.

label: Pillars of Zanash
title: Pillars of Zanash
lead:
The Pillars of Zanash are a shrine to Saradomin found in the vicinity of East Ardougne and Witchaven. The pillars, known to be made of marble, are mentioned by name only in the Tourist's Guide to Ardougne. The book can be found in the real-estate agency within the city, though it incorrectly states they are found west of Ardougne.

According to Brother Maledict, the shrine is over 150 years old, and predates the founding of Witchaven. When the village came into being, the shrine was abandoned and has fallen into disrepair. In addition, Mayor Hobb (while possessed by sea slugs) says that the shrine is "ancient beyond knowledge" and that its history "should not be overlooked."

label: Pincers
title: Pincers
lead:
The Pincers are a group of islands located within the Wushanko Isles. The islands have a relatively warm climate, and like the rest of the Wushanko Isles , the islands are inhabited mainly by sirens.

The following characters are known to be from this region:
*Shura, a siren who is specifically from the island of Ashihama
*The Nightmare, an otherworldy horror who feeds on the life force of sleeping people is from Ashihama

label: pineapple
title: pineapple
lead:
A pineapple is a fruit that can be found growing just south of Brimhaven or on a player grown Pineapple plant. Additionally, they may be purchased from Trader Crewmembers operating Trader Stan's Trading Post, Funch's Shop from Heckel Funch, or from Hudo Glenfad in the Grand Tree Groceries store.

found south of Brimhaven.]]
Pineapples provide an easy way to make supercompost by putting it into a compost bin, as they are relatively cheap and easy to obtain. It can be sliced or diced with a knife. Slicing the pineapple will yield 4 pineapple rings, each healing 2 Hitpoints. Dicing the pineapple yields one pineapple chunks, an ingredient used in gnome cooking, which also heals 2 Hitpoints when consumed. When slicing the pineapple into pineapple rings if you don't have enough space in your inventory, the rings will drop to the ground instead.

label: Pineapple chunks
title: Pineapple chunks
lead:
Pineapple chunks are a food item that heals 2 hitpoints when consumed. Players can make pineapple chunks by using a knife on a pineapple or a tenti pineapple by choosing "Dice".

The main use for pineapple chunks is as an ingredient in other foods; for example, members can use them to make a pineapple pizza with level 65 Cooking.

label: Pineapple pizza
title: Pineapple pizza
lead:
Pineapple pizza is a type of pizza that restores 22 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 11. It can be obtained by using pineapple chunks or pineapple rings on a cooked plain pizza, requiring 65 Cooking and granting 45 experience. It is recommended to cut the pineapple into rings, as this yields four rings for use on multiple pizzas, compared to the single chunk if dicing it. Pineapple pizza is one of the highest healing foods in the game and are also a type of fast food.

100 noted pineapple pizzas can be given to Yama to initiate a fight that is identical to the aether catalyst, oathplate shard, and diabolic worm acquisition contract fights, as a way to practice these fights in exchange for standard loot rolls.

label: Pineapple Plant (wild)
title: Pineapple Plant (wild)
lead:
Pineapple Plants are wild plants found on Karamja and Ape Atoll. The wild pineapple plants found near Brimhaven can grow up to five pineapples at a time, while the variants found on Ape Atoll will only ever grow one pineapple at a time. Picking wild pineapples will not give any Farming experience. Unlike the pineapple plants found in farming patches, picking pineapples from the wild Pineapple Plants will only take a single game tick, meaning that these can be picked much faster. Once picked, the plant takes 5 minutes to regrow.

found south of Brimhaven.]]
The fact the Ape Atoll plants only grow up to one pineapple at a time should be taken into account when running laps on the Ape Atoll Agility Course. Very close to the course's end, a single plant can be found, which can be used to help recover some health from running laps on the course. Once the pineapple regrows on this plant, it is beneficial to pick it as soon as conveniently possible, due to no further food growing there until it is picked again. Picking this pineapple should be enough health restoration to sustain players with mid to high Agility levels indefinitely, provided they bring a knife to cut the pineapples up into pineapple rings. For lower levels, however, this single pineapple may not be sufficient to sustain them.

label: Pineapple punch
title: Pineapple punch
lead:
Pineapple punch is a drink that can be made at level 8 Cooking, granting 70 experience points. It heals 9 hitpoints. To mix a pineapple punch, a player needs a lemon, 2 oranges, 3 pineapples, a lime, a cocktail shaker, a knife, and a cocktail glass.

To make it: 
# Use the "mix-cocktail" option on the shaker, and select pineapple punch.
# Use the knife on the remaining pineapple and select "dice".
# Use the knife on the lime and select "dice".
# Use the knife on the orange and select "slice."
# Use the cocktail shaker on the glass or select "pour mixed punch" on the cocktail shaker.

label: Pineapple ring
title: Pineapple ring
lead:
Pineapple rings are a members-only Cooking ingredient that are used on plain pizzas to create pineapple pizzas.

Pineapple rings are obtained by using a knife on a pineapple or a tenti pineapple and choosing the "slice" option. 4 pineapple rings are obtained for each pineapple that is sliced. If the "dice" option is chosen, the player will receive Pineapple chunks instead.

label: Ping (Server)
title: Ping (Server)
lead: Ping is the time it takes for a player's computer to send a request to the server, and for the server to respond, usually measured in milliseconds. If the server has many players or is farther away, the Ping will be higher. If the server has fewer players or is closer, the Ping will be lower. The higher the Ping, the longer the server takes to respond.

label: Pink
title: Pink
lead: Pink may refer to:

label: Pink boots
title: Pink boots
lead: Pink boots can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the of the Grand Tree. Their stats are identical to Leather boots.

label: Pink hat
title: Pink hat
lead: A pink hat is a piece of headwear that can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store Fine Fashions, located to the north-east on the of the Grand Tree. The hats are a slight upgrade from wizard hats, offering one more Magic attack and defence.

label: Pink robe bottoms
title: Pink robe bottoms
lead: Pink robe bottoms can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions. You can find Rometti on the of the Grand Tree, in the north-eastern area.

label: Pink robe top
title: Pink robe top
lead: A pink robe top can be purchased at the Tree Gnome Stronghold from Rometti at his store, Fine Fashions, located north-east on the of the Grand Tree.

label: Pink skirt
title: Pink skirt
lead:
A pink skirt is one of several skirts available to free players. It is used in the quest Prince Ali Rescue as part of the disguise Prince Ali wears in order to impersonate Lady Keli and escape from prison. The rowdy dwarf may ask for this item in the quest Forgettable Tale... in return for a Kelda seed.

It can be stored in the STASH unit outside the southern entrance to the Grand Exchange together with a pink robe top and a body tiara.

label: Pipe
title: Pipe
lead: Pipe may refer to:

label: Pipe (Plague City)
title: Pipe (Plague City)
lead:
A pipe can be found in the western section of the Ardougne Sewers. During the Plague City quest, players must climb up the pipe in order to gain access to West Ardougne. Access to the pipe is initially blocked by a grill, which players must remove by first by attaching a rope to the grill, followed by asking Edmond for assistance in pulling it off.

Players must have a gas mask equipped before being allowed to climb up the pipe.

label: Pipe (Underground Pass)
title: Pipe (Underground Pass)
lead: The pipe is a one-way Agility shortcut in the Underground Pass that requires 1 Agility and rewards 3 Agility experience. It allows the player to return to the previous section of the Underground pass before the grid and rope jump from the furnace area. A second, two-way pipe connects the spike walkway area to the unicorn room and also rewards 3 Agility experience.

label: Pirate
title: Pirate
lead:
Pirates are non-player characters that can be found in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon and the Pirates' Hideout at level 55 Wilderness or around Brimhaven, Port Piscarilius, in the Port Sarim jail, and around the Pirates' Cove at level 23. They are also fought during Cabin Fever.

The pirates at Brimhaven, the Pirates' Cove, and Port Piscarilius can also be spoken to, although they will only respond with short phrases consisting of seemingly nonsensical pirate slang. Unlike the pirates found on Mos Le'Harmless, carrying a book o' piracy does not change their dialogue in any way.

label: Pirate (disambiguation)
title: Pirate (disambiguation)
lead:
Pirate may refer to:
* Pirate, the standard monster found in the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, Brimhaven, Port Piscarilius, and other locations
* Pirate (Thieving), pickpocketable pirates that can be found on The Onyx Crest, Laguna Aurorae, and Buccaneers' Haven

* Pirate (Mos Le'Harmless), friendly pirates found on Mos Le'Harmless
* Pirate (Catacombs of Kourend), a friendly pirate found near the deviant spectres in the Catacombs of Kourend
* Pirate (Great Sound), seen sailing on a ship in the Great Sound with Captain Cotus
* Pirate (Rock Island Prison), seen on a ship circling Rock Island Prison

label: Pirate bandana
title: Pirate bandana
lead: Pirate bandanas are headwear that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank. A Book o' piracy is required to make purchases.

label: Pirate chest
title: Pirate chest
lead:
Pirate chest may refer to:

*Rusty chest
*Tarnished chest
*Reinforced chest
*Zombie Pirate's Locker

label: Pirate clothing
title: Pirate clothing
lead:
Pirate clothing is worn by players who want to look like pirates and includes:
*Pirate boots
*Pirate leggings
*Stripy pirate shirt
*Pirate bandana

Pirate clothing can be purchased from Mike on Mos Le'Harmless.

label: Pirate Guard
title: Pirate Guard
lead:
Pirate guards are posted just west of the Brimhaven Agility Arena, and are also found in Scarface Pete's mansion. Pirate guards resemble the old Varrock town guards, but with black equipment instead of bronze equipment.
You can speak to Pirate guards, but they do not provide you with any useful information.

Pirate guards do not drop anything when killed apart from bones.

label: Pirate Jackie the Fruit
title: Pirate Jackie the Fruit
lead:
Pirate Jackie the Fruit can be found at the Brimhaven Agility Arena entrance. She runs the Agility Arena Store, exchanging the tickets and vouchers obtained in the arena for various rewards, consisting of valuable herbs, amylase packs, Agility experience, and the expensive pirate's hook. The amount of Agility experience received can be increased by 10% by wearing Karamja gloves 2 or higher. Players can also use graceful outfit pieces that have been recoloured blue on her to revert them to their default colouring, although this does not refund any tickets.

She also awards players the Karamja gloves for completing easy, medium, hard and elite Karamja Diary tasks. After the completion of the elite diary she lets the player switch whether bars from the metal dragons in Brimhaven Dungeon drop noted or not.

label: Pirate leggings
title: Pirate leggings
lead: Pirate leggings are legwear that can be purchased from Dodgy Mike's Second-hand Clothing on Mos Le'Harmless, south-east of the bank.

label: Pirate map
title: Pirate map
lead:
Pirate map is a decorative piece of scenery that can be found in various locations across Gielinor. Players cannot interact with the pirate map, but they can examine it.

Three pirate maps are in the Wise Old Man's house in Draynor, one on the bottom floor and two on the top floor. One map is located on the western wall of the Dead Man's Chest in Brimhaven. Two can also be found in the Pirates' Hideout in the Wilderness. Lastly, one pirate map is on the wall of Amelia's house in Shayzien.

label: Pirate message
title: Pirate message
lead:
The Pirate message is a quest item used only in Pirate's Treasure. It is found in a locked chest, that is unlocked with a key, on the of the Blue Moon Inn.

The message informs the player of the buried treasure's location somewhere in Falador Park. It is kept upon quest completion, but has no use.

label: Pirate's hat
title: Pirate's hat
lead: A Pirate's hat is a possible reward from completing hard Treasure Trails. Players who have completed Cabin Fever can pay Patchy to attach a pirate's hat to an eye patch to create a hat eyepatch.

label: Pirate's hook
title: Pirate's hook
lead:
The pirate's hook is a reward from the Brimhaven Agility Arena that occupies the glove slot. It can be purchased from Pirate Jackie the Fruit for 800 Brimhaven vouchers.

Without the completion of the elite Karamja diary, it takes a minimum of 800 minutes (or 13 hours 20 minutes) to earn enough tickets for this item, assuming no dispensers are missed. Players with the diary completed have a 10% chance to gain double tickets, which lowers the time to 728 minutes (12 hours 8 minutes).

label: Pirate's Treasure
title: Pirate's Treasure
lead: Pirate's Treasure is a quest in which you help the pirate Redbeard Frank obtain some Karamjan rum in return for the location of the treasure of One-Eyed Hector, his old captain.

label: Pirates' Hideout
title: Pirates' Hideout
lead:
The Pirates' Hideout is a building located in deep Wilderness. A lockpick and 39 Thieving are required to pick the door lock, gaining entry.

Many aggressive pirates are located here. There are also 4 Thieving chests that have to be searched for traps before the player can loot them, and half of a redberry pie (5 hitpoints healing) spawns in the hideout. This is a single-way combat area.

label: Pirates' Hideout mine
title: Pirates' Hideout mine
lead: The Pirates' Hideout mine, or Pirates' Mine, is a mining site located east of the Pirates' Hideout in the deep Wilderness. Player killing in the Wilderness greatly increases the risk of mining at this site along with all Wilderness mines, so mining at this site can be very dangerous. There are also a number of giant bats around this mine. The closest bank is in the Mage Arena; however, players will need a sharp object (like a knife) to cut through the webs blocking its entrance.

label: Pisc banner
title: Pisc banner
lead:
Pisc banner may refer to:

*Piscarilius banner, a tradeable reward from medium Treasure Trails representing the House of Piscarilius in Great Kourend
*Western banner, an untradeable reward from the Western Provinces Diary which offers a teleport to Piscatoris Fishing Colony

label: Piscarilius (disambiguation)
title: Piscarilius (disambiguation)
lead:
Piscarilius may refer to:

*Port Piscarilius

label: Pit
title: Pit
lead: Pit may refer to:

label: Pit Scorpion
title: Pit Scorpion
lead: Pit scorpions are scorpions found in the dungeon of the Legends' Guild and Ardougne Zoo.

label: Pitta bread
title: Pitta bread
lead:
Pitta bread are a type of food used to make Ugthanki kebabs, and can be obtained by baking pitta dough on a cooking range, requiring level 58 Cooking and granting 40 experience when successful. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 37 on ranges. However, since the Cooking requirement is level 58, it can never be burned.

Players can make pitta dough with level 58 Cooking by combining a pot of flour with a jug or bucket of water. They can then use the cooked pitta bread with kebab mix to complete an ugthanki kebab.

label: Pitta dough
title: Pitta dough
lead:
Pitta dough is created by mixing a pot of flour with either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water. It can be cooked on a range (not a fire) to make pitta bread.

Unlike many cooking recipes, this item cannot be burned, even though the burnt version exists. This is because players can no longer burn it by the time they have the level required to cook it.

label: Pixie
title: Pixie
lead:
, a pixie]]
Pixies are a type of fairy , known to be hardworking but overly excitable, which causes them to gather static magic around them and release it in a burst of magical energy. They featured most prominently in the 2013 Halloween event, 2014 Christmas event, and 2017 Christmas event, as they were hired by Diango from the Fairy Godfather to help create toys for Christmas. The pixies, during these events, could be found in a large toy workshop beneath Draynor Village.

It was suggested in the 2013 Halloween event that pixies may explode when worked up. This is likely literal, based on them releasing magical bursts when overexcited. This could be seen in the 2014 Christmas event, as the pixies would occasionally release an explosion and fall to the ground before getting back up.

label: pizza
title: pizza
lead:
Pizza is a type of food that players can make with the Cooking skill. A plain pizza requires 35 Cooking, and is made by using tomato on a pizza base, then adding cheese to the incomplete pizza, and then cooking the uncooked pizza on a range. The plain pizza can then be enhanced by adding different toppings to create different types of pizza that restore more Hitpoints.

All pizzas are two-bite foods, meaning a full pizza will turn into a 1/2 pizza upon consumption. Two halves can be combined back into a full pizza by using the same type of half together.

label: pizza base
title: pizza base
lead: A pizza base is an ingredient used to make pizza. It can be made by using either a bucket of water, bowl of water, or jug of water with a pot of flour. With a Cooking level of 35 it can be used with a tomato and cheese to make an uncooked pizza, which can then be cooked. Tomato must be added first, then cheese to make an uncooked pizza. Pizza bases can also be purchased from Tony's Pizza Bases in the Bandit Camp.

label: Place of worship
title: Place of worship
lead: Places of worship refer to standing sites or buildings dedicated to worship. Most of these places also contain an altar; players can pray at an altar to replenish their Prayer points.

label: Plague City
title: Plague City
lead: Plague City is the first quest of the Elf quest series. The quest investigates a plague that has affected West Ardougne.

label: Plague jacket
title: Plague jacket
lead:
The plague jacket is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder. It and the plague trousers are obtained from Doctor Orbon by purchasing it from him for 100 coins. It cannot be obtained again after completing the quest.

It must be worn when prodding the sick-looking sheep into the pen. It forms half of the plague suit set, the other half being the plague trousers.

label: plague sample
title: plague sample
lead:
The plague sample is a quest item used only in Biohazard. It is obtained from Elena after returning her distillator to her.

It is given to Guidor in south-east Varrock, alongside liquid honey, sulphuric broline, ethenea, and touch paper.

label: Plague suit
title: Plague suit
lead:
The plague suit is a set of items bought from Doctor Orbon for 100 coins during the Sheep Herder quest. The set protects the player from the plagued sheep. This set can only be reclaimed during the quest, not after.

The set consists of the following equipment:
* Plague jacket 
* Plague trousers

label: Plague trousers
title: Plague trousers
lead:
The plague trousers is a quest item used only in Sheep Herder. It and the plague jacket are obtained from Doctor Orbon by purchasing it from him for 100 coins. It cannot be obtained again after completing the quest.

It must be worn when prodding the sick-looking sheep into the pen. It forms half of the plague suit set, the other half being the plague jacket. It appears visually identical to the Mourner trousers.

label: plain pizza
title: plain pizza
lead:
Plain pizza is a type of pizza that restores 14 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 7. It can be obtained by baking an uncooked pizza on a cooking range, requiring level 35 Cooking and granting 143 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pizza. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases, and it will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 68.

Toppings can be added to the plain pizza in order to create meat pizza (meat or chicken), anchovy pizza (anchovies), or pineapple pizza (chunks or ring).

label: Plank
title: Plank
lead: A plank is a common Construction item and is used in several quests. Made from normal logs, it is the lowest-level type of plank. Each plank used while training Construction yields 29 experience. They are also used to repair fishing cranes, which yields Crafting and Construction experience equal to 4 times the player's current level.

label: Plank (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
title: Plank (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
lead:
The plank is an Agility obstacle found within the Brimhaven Agility Arena. Failing to choose the correct plank, the smooth one, will cause the player to fall and take damage; they will need to go up a nearby climbing rope to get back onto the course. Players with 99 Agility will be able to successfully cross any of the 3 planks, however, choosing a broken plank takes 1 extra tick to cross.

The amount of damage dealt by the fall is based on the player's current health, according to the formula below.

label: Plank (disambiguation)
title: Plank (disambiguation)
lead:
Plank is a common Construction item and is used in several quests.

Plank may also refer to:

label: planks
title: planks
lead:
Planks are items that members use primarily in the Construction skill to make furniture for their houses, along with components for their boats. They are also used in some quests and for repairing fishing cranes, which gives Crafting and Construction experience equal to 4 times the player's current level.

Planks come in seven different varieties, namely normal, oak, teak, mahogany, camphor, ironwood, and rosewood. Planks from other wood types, such as yew or maple, do not exist.

label: Plant (Dwarven Mine)
title: Plant (Dwarven Mine)
lead: Plants can be found growing on the floor surrounding the chest that holds Thalzar's map part used in the Dragon Slayer I quest. Players cannot interact with the plant, only examine them.

label: Plant fossil
title: Plant fossil
lead:
Plant fossil may refer to:

*Fossilised roots
*Fossilised stump
*Fossilised branch
*Fossilised leaf
*Fossilised mushroom

label: Plant Fossil Display
title: Plant Fossil Display
lead:
Plant Fossil Display may refer to:
* The Petrified Mushtree plant fossil display
* The Petrified Large Mushroom plant fossil display
* The Petrified Spine Plant plant fossil display
* The Petrified Pitcher plant fossil display
* The Skroom plant fossil display

label: Plaque
title: Plaque
lead: Plaques are common scenery found on walls. The plaque has no text visible on it and examining it does not provide any additional information. Plaques are purely decorative and have no other interaction options.

label: Plaque (disambiguation)
title: Plaque (disambiguation)
lead:
Plaque may refer to:

* Plaque, a commonly found scenery object
* Plaque (Ancient Vault), encountered during Desert Treasure II
* Plaque (Varrock Museum)
* Plaque (Burthorpe Games Room)
* Plaque (In Aid of the Myreque)
* Plaque (Phoenix Gang)
* Plaque (Varrock Palace), an unused plaque

label: Plaque (Varrock Palace)
title: Plaque (Varrock Palace)
lead:
A plaque could previously be found in Varrock Palace next to the cage containing the imprisoned Monk of Zamorak. Players had the option to read the plaque, which would give the message "Witness the fate of those who serve Zamorak the master of evil..."

With the graphical update of Varrock in 2007, the plaque was removed. As a result, it has never been present in Old School RuneScape.

label: platebody
title: platebody
lead:
A platebody is a type of armour worn mainly by warriors. Among melee attack types, platebody provides good defence against the slash attack type but is more vulnerable to the crush attack type.

Most platebodies give players penalties towards magic and ranged attacks and penalties towards magic defence. However, platebodies have very good defence against ranged as well as melee attacks.

label: Platebody shops
title: Platebody shops
lead: Platebody shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Platebody shops sell platebodies. There are 6 dedicated platebody shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: platelegs
title: platelegs
lead:
Platelegs are a type of armour worn mainly by warriors in the leg slot. Among melee attack types, platelegs provides good defence against the slash attack type but is more vulnerable to the crush attack type. Platelegs gives a player penalties towards ranged attacks and penalties towards magic defence. However, platelegs have very good defence against ranged attacks.

Platelegs are made with the Smithing skill or purchased at the plate legs shop identified by the icon on the map. One such location is Louie's Armoured Legs Bazaar in Al Kharid. Horvik's Armour Shop offers iron platelegs.

label: Platelegs shops
title: Platelegs shops
lead: Platelegs shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor which primarily sell platelegs. The stores are represented by an icon.

label: Plateskirt
title: Plateskirt
lead:

Among melee attack types, plateskirts provide good defence against the slash attack type but are more vulnerable to the crush attack type. Plateskirts give a player penalties towards ranged attacks and penalties towards magic defence. However, plateskirts have very good defence against ranged attacks.

Standard plateskirts can be made with the Smithing skill (with the exception of the black,
white and dragon plateskirts) or purchased at the plateskirt shop identified by the icon on the map.

label: player character
title: player character
lead: The Player, also known as the Adventurer, is the avatar of someone playing Old School RuneScape. The Player is a human, may be either body type and may be freely customised. Their adventuring career begins in the year 169 of the Fifth Age on Tutorial Island, and thereafter involves a number of quests until they become a well-known hero.

label: Player identification number
title: Player identification number
lead:
A player identification number (often referred to as PID) is a unique identification number for player. Upon logging in, a PID is assigned which will randomise every 100 to 150 game ticks, 60 to 90 seconds, for each player. On Bounty Hunter, PvP, and tournament worlds, PID randomises every 40 to 60 game ticks, 24 to 36 seconds, per player.

The engine uses this to deal with two players doing something at the same time, the lower PID will have priority in processing the action. This could be dealing damage to a monster, dealing damage to a player, picking up an item, almost any action. This is done to make combat and many other aspects of the game more consistent.

label: Player killing
title: Player killing
lead:
Player killing (commonly known as PKing, player vs. player, or PvP), is the act of two or more players partaking in combat against each other. Player killing differs from other forms of combat in that players do not fight against monsters whose actions are defined by RuneScape's game engine. There are various places throughout Old School RuneScape that players can participate in PvP activities, such as Castle Wars, Soul Wars, Bounty Hunter, and the TzHaar Fight Pit. On every world, the Wilderness is a PVP-enabled zone, allowing players in a similar combat bracket to fight with each other.

Players can also participate in player killing in dedicated "PvP worlds", worlds where players can attack other players in most places around Gielinor except for designated safe areas and banks. World 392 is permanently designated as a PvP world, with other PvP worlds being made active/inactive on a rotating schedule. The currently-active PvP worlds can always be found on the world list.

label: Player killing/Mechanics
title: Player killing/Mechanics
lead: A player killing mechanic, or PvP mechanic, is a term that can be used to describe any mechanic used in player versus player combat.

label: Player Moderator
title: Player Moderator
lead:
Player Moderators (colloquially PMods or just mods) are Old School RuneScape players chosen specifically by Jagex staff due to their commitment to the in-game community. They are ambassadors of the game and help to maintain an enjoyable in-game environment. They were introduced to the original game on 14 June 2004 , and since then the team has grown to 2,364 player moderators as of 30 December 2019.

Other types of moderators include Forum Moderators and Jagex Moderators. Player Moderators hold their status on both games: Old School RuneScape and . Back when and RuneScape Classic existed, Player Moderators held their status there as well.

label: player spoof
title: player spoof
lead: A player spoof is an NPC designed to resemble an Old School RuneScape player. Typically they are fictional, but some of the NPCs are modeled and named after real players, such as for contributing player-designed content.

label: player-owned house
title: player-owned house
lead:
A player-owned house (often shortened to POH) is the focus of the Construction skill. It can be bought from an estate agent for , or received for free upon completion of the miniquest Daddy's Home. Players' houses are located in Rimmington by default but can be moved to one of 8 different cities for a fee by talking to an estate agent, if the required (unboostable) Construction level is met. Players can enter the house through house portals, labelled on the world map as . For a list of pros and cons on different locations consult the house portal page.

Additionally, owning a house is required for the following:
* Ability to use an experience lamp on the Construction skill
* Ability to gain Construction experience from repairing Wintertodt braziers, Tempoross totem poles, and Tempoross masts

label: Player-owned houses glitch
title: Player-owned houses glitch
lead:
The player-owned houses glitch was a glitch that occurred on 9 December 2020.

After the 2020 Christmas Event update, various player-owned house furniture had disappeared for many players. This was hotfixed less than an hour after the update.

label: Players' Gallery
title: Players' Gallery
lead:
The Players' Gallery (originally called the Postbag Gallery) was a place on the RuneScape website showing fanart sent in by players. It originally launched in October 2006, after being announced in issue 10 of Postbag from the Hedge.

In 2009, Jagex deleted all of the galleries except for 24 of the "best" artwork, put in three "Best of" galleries (Galleries 1-3), and ignored requests for the old pictures to be made available again. On 12 August 2016, all mentions of the players' gallery were completely removed from the website. Any previous links to them redirect to the Customer Support section.

label: Poison
title: Poison
lead:
Poison is a status effect that players and monsters suffer when they are attacked by a poisonous weapon. Many NPCs are able to inflict poison naturally, whilst players can use weapons laced with weapon poison (or smoke spells from the Ancient Magicks) to inflict poison. However, not all monsters can be inflicted with poison; a full list of monsters susceptible to poison can be found here, whilst a list of monsters immune to poison can be found here.

Monsters that can inflict poison may do so regardless of whether or not they inflict any damage, even if protection prayers are used. Player inflicted poison does need to deal damage to apply.

label: Poison (item)
title: Poison (item)
lead:
Poison is an item used during the Ernest the Chicken and Hazeel Cult quests. It can be found as a spawn inside Draynor Manor, or purchased from Rasolo near the Baxtorian Falls or Jossik in the Lighthouse.

It is used to poison the fish food and the piranhas found in the fountain on the grounds of Draynor Manor during the Ernest the Chicken quest. Finally, it is used to poison the Carnillean household's food in Hazeel Cult. You can try to use the poison obtained from the Hazeel Cult to poison the sheep in Sheep Herder, but a message will appear saying: "The sheep isn't going to drink the poison from the bottle. Perhaps you should try feeding it something else more appropriate."

label: Poison chalice
title: Poison chalice
lead: A poison chalice is a cocktail obtained for free from Stankers, a dwarven miner near the Coal Trucks west of Seers' Village. Drinking a poison chalice applies a random effect, and leaves behind an empty cocktail glass. Drinking the poison chalice cannot lower your Hitpoints past 4.

label: Poison Salesman
title: Poison Salesman
lead: The Poison Salesman is a non-player character who can be found near the bar in Seers' Village, and is involved in The Fremennik Trials and Murder Mystery quests.

label: Poison Scorpion
title: Poison Scorpion
lead:
Poison Scorpions are found in the Taverley Dungeon and Brimhaven. They are poisonous, and their poison starts at 3 Hitpoints per hit. As such, a form of antipoison is recommended when fighting them.

They are considered a scorpion for the purpose of a Slayer task.

label: Poison spider
title: Poison spider
lead:
Poison spiders are monsters that can be found in many locations, including the Wilderness. They are aggressive and attack with Melee, being fairly accurate and able to inflict a poison that starts at a 6. Contrary to popular belief, Protect from Melee does not prevent them from causing poison.

The level 31 variant may be encountered during the Observatory Quest when searching chests for the goblin kitchen key. These spiders will immediately poison the player similar to cave slime, where simply being in combat with them will inflict poison.

label: Poisoned dagger (unobtainable item)
title: Poisoned dagger (unobtainable item)
lead:
The Poisoned dagger is an unobtainable item that was added during the RuneScape 2 beta. It uses the default untextured model for poisoned daggers. Its purpose is unknown; however, it may have been created in order to test poisoned daggers in RuneScape 2, or as part of an interface.

With the release of Weapon poison(+) and Weapon poison(++), extra strong and super strong poison variants of the dagger were added too.

label: Poisoned dart(p)
title: Poisoned dart(p)
lead:
The Poisoned dart(p) is an unobtainable item that was added during the RuneScape 2 beta. Its purpose is unknown; however, it may have been created in order to test poisoned darts in RuneScape 2, or as part of an interface.

The item briefly appeared in the search interface of the trading post. Aside from this, it has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

label: Poisoned fish food
title: Poisoned fish food
lead:
Poisoned fish food is a quest item used in Ernest the Chicken, and in Crack the Clue III. It is made by using poison with fish food (both found in Draynor Manor).

Poisoned fish food is used to kill the piranhas in the fountain in order to retrieve the pressure gauge.

label: Polar camouflage gear
title: Polar camouflage gear
lead:
Polar camouflage gear is a set of members-only hunter gear made at the Fancy Dress Shop in Varrock or Pellem's Fur Store in the Hunter Guild with polar kebbit fur. Contrary to popular belief, these do not improve catch rates of any hunter creatures.

To make a polar camo top and legs, bring 4 polar kebbit furs (2 for the top and 2 for the legs) and 40 coins to the Fancy Dress Shop or Pellem's Fur Store. Polar kebbit furs are obtained by hunting polar kebbits in the Rellekka Hunter area, requiring at least level 1 Hunter to trap, or they may be bought from other players. The set may be stored in a costume room's armour case. When worn, the top reduces weight by 3 kg, and the legs by 2kg.

Despite the existence of the mutually exclusive banners weapon category, there are several banners (ex. the Arceuus banner) in the polestaff category. These are listed below.

label: Polls
title: Polls
lead:
Polls are in-game in which players are asked to express their preferences for certain changes within Old School RuneScape. Only members with a total level of 300 or above and with a minimum total play-time of 25 hours can participate, though specific polls or questions may have additional requirements.

When a poll is live, players who log in and have not cast their votes will receive a message in the chatbox stating colour=#7f00ff Poll booths will also have a small raised flag to indicate that the player has not yet voted, and the Account Management Community tab will indicate that a poll is active, letting players vote from the tab. Town Criers in various cities also remind players to vote via overhead text.
