label: Port Khazard
title: Port Khazard
lead: Port Khazard is a port located south of Ardougne and north of Yanille. It is one of the most convenient Sailing ports, as it offers a bank chest, shipwright, and an anvil within close proximity of the gangplank, which can be used from level 30 Sailing. Apart from that, it offers charter ships to other locations, the Fishing Trawler minigame, and other minor facilities.

label: Port Khazard mine
title: Port Khazard mine
lead:
Port Khazard mine is a mining site found in Port Khazard. The mine actually consists of two smaller areas, which occupy the northern and southern parts of the port, but the proximity and small sizes of the two has generally led to them being considered as part of the same site.

The northern portion of the mine possesses one mithril rock and two tin rocks, as well as two exhausted rocks which never contain any ore, while the southern one has one mithril and two copper rocks. A deposit box can be found near the Fishing Trawler minigame, which makes it an ideal spot for players in need of tin and copper. The port also houses an anvil that can be used in conjunction with the Superheat Item spell in order to smith mined ore. The area's charter ships can also be used to reach various other ports.

label: Port Piscarilius/Historical
title: Port Piscarilius/Historical
lead:
Earning Piscarilius favour can be done by assisting with repairing the fishing cranes, taking fish to the market, hunting grubs on the beach and stealing artefacts from houses.

To progress in the Architectural Alliance miniquest, players must gain 100% Piscarilius favour and speak to Piliar, who is found in the building directly north-west of the general store.
__notoc__

label: Port Sarim
title: Port Sarim
lead: Port Sarim is a small port in south-eastern Asgarnia. The port connects to a number of other ports, including Entrana, Karamja, Crandor, Great Kourend, Corsair Cove, and the Void Knights' Outpost, as well as even more destinations via charter ship.

label: Port Sarim jail
title: Port Sarim jail
lead: The Port Sarim jail is a top security prison located in Port Sarim, commonly referred to as the worst jail in Gielinor. Players can get sent to the jail by Shantay should they declare themselves an outlaw and refuse to pay his fine of five coins twice, although they can escape quite easily by picking the lock on the door or teleporting out. Picking the lock to get out awards 4 Thieving experience on members' worlds, while not providing any experience on free-to-play worlds.

label: Port wizard
title: Port wizard
lead:
Port wizards appear when a player requests a shipwright move their boat from another port or retrieve a capsized boat. Currently there are four port wizards in the game cache, although only three appear in-game:

* Port Wizard Perrie
* Port Wizard Peter
* Port Wizard Petra
* Port Wizard Paulie (does not appear in-game)

label: portal
title: portal
lead: A portal is a form of transportation that enables players to teleport between two places. Unlike ordinary teleports, portals can only be used at a fixed location and they can be used an unlimited number of times.

label: Portal (Rune essence mine)
title: Portal (Rune essence mine)
lead:
Portals are found in the Rune essence mine and can be used to exit the area. Travelling through the portal will teleport the player back to the NPC that was used to enter the mine: one of Aubury, Wizard Sedridor, Wizard Distentor, Wizard Cromperty, or Brimstail.

There are seven variants of the portal, with varying colours and interaction options. Upon teleporting to the mine, a random variant is selected and the four portals in the mine will be replaced with that variant. The small variations are likely intended to counteract bots that rely on specific colours or option text.

label: Portal (Runecrafting)
title: Portal (Runecrafting)
lead: Runecrafting portals are portals found within various runic altars which allows one-way transportation to its corresponding mysterious ruins in the overworld. Apart from teleports, the portals are the only exit from the altar.

label: Postbag from the Hedge
title: Postbag from the Hedge
lead:
Postbag from the Hedge are a collection of letters to, and responses from, RuneScape non-player characters, including some who may not exist in the playable game. They are often replied to in a humorous fashion, although some replies (especially those from the Chaos Elemental) hint at possible future updates. The letters are delivered by Postie Pete. Postbag from the Hedge replaced the old letters from the gods of RuneScape, as the gods have "neither the time nor the inclination to speak with mere mortals".

Starting with postbag 11, some issues included a section known as Wise old tips, where the Wise Old Man provided insight to the readers. Other issues included sections from various other personalities such as the Chaos Elemental or Evil Dave.

label: Pot
title: Pot
lead:
A pot is an item that can be used to hold a variety of liquids or powdery substances, such as flour. It is one of the most common items, so players will often simply drop them and buy new ones when needed, as they are very inexpensive.

Players can find them on various counters and tables through Gielinor, including the ground-floor kitchen in Lumbridge Castle. Alternatively, they can be made by forming soft clay on a potter's wheel, then firing the resulting unfired pot in a pottery oven.

label: Pot (Bamboo)
title: Pot (Bamboo)
lead: Pots are scenery objects made of bamboo found mostly in the tropical regions of Gielinor. Players cannot interact with these pots, but they can examine them. A special bamboo pot can be found in the Ape Atoll bank. This pot becomes a Bank Deposit Pot after completion of Monkey Madness II.

label: pot of cream
title: pot of cream
lead:
A pot of cream can be made by using a bucket of milk on a dairy churn at 21 Cooking. It provides 18 Cooking experience. They can also be purchased from the Culinaromancer's Chest in the Lumbridge Castle cellar, after you're at a certain point in the Recipe for Disaster quest as well as from Hudo or Heckel Funch at the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

Pots of cream can be further churned into a pat of butter. When eaten, the pot of cream heals 1 hitpoint.

label: Pot of flour
title: Pot of flour
lead:
A pot of flour is a Cooking ingredient used to produce several types of dough when combined with water.

Using an empty pot on a barrel of flour is a faster alternative to having to get grain and use a windmill. One barrel is in the kitchen of Sinclair Mansion after starting the Murder Mystery quest and another barrel is located on the of Gordon and Mary's farm.

label: Pot of flour (Tutorial Island)
title: Pot of flour (Tutorial Island)
lead:
The Pot of flour is a unique variant of the pot of flour that can only be obtained on Tutorial Island. Lev the Master Chef gives the player the pot of flour and a bucket of water, and teaches them how to combine the two to make bread dough. Players must bake the bread in order to proceed with the tutorial.

The pot of flour was not available in the alternative Tutorial Island experienced by some players in 2020, as the Master Chef was replaced with the Master Navigator.

label: Pot of tea
title: Pot of tea
lead:
A Pot of tea is an item used to make a cup of tea in the kitchen of a player-owned house allowing the player to temporarily boost Construction by up to 3 levels. Players can obtain this item by using a hot kettle with a teapot with leaves. When made, a pot of tea has four doses. Players must use the pot of tea on a clay cup, porcelain, or trimmed porcelain cups producing a cup of tea to make the tea drinkable. Complete directions on how to make tea can be found here.

Note: If a player leaves the house in any way, then this item will disappear from their inventory.

label: Potato
title: Potato
lead:
Raw potatoes are a food item that can be picked from fields around Gielinor or grown through the Farming skill at level 1 with potato seeds. They heal 1 hitpoint when eaten raw. When picking potatoes from fields, members may randomly receive 1 potato seed.

They are used in the following recipes:
* Baked potato (must be cooked on a range, not a fire)

label: Pothole Dungeon
title: Pothole Dungeon
lead:
The Pothole Dungeon (also known as the Jogre Dungeon) is located on Karamja, south of Brimhaven and north-east of Tai Bwo Wannai. Level 53 Jogres live here. This is the only place where rogue's purse herbs grow, and they can be found by searching the Fungus covered Cavern walls.

There are multiple harpie bug swarms at the start of the beach, which may be aggressive depending on combat level. Search the pile of rocks near the end of the beach, and you will be asked if you want to climb down into the dungeon.

label: Potion storage
title: Potion storage
lead:
The potion storage is an unlock purchased from the Mixology Rewards shop with 7,750 mox resin, 6,300 aga resin, and 8,950 lye resin, which are earned from participating in the Mastering Mixology minigame. Upon purchase, a message in the chatbox will state You have unlocked potion storage within the bank!

Purchasing the potion storage feature unlocks an interface in the player's bank to store potions to avoid taking up bank space. This includes unfinished potions, barbarian mixes, divine potions, and empty vials. When adding a potion, the storage will remember the dosage of the first potion stored, and withdraw potions with the same dosage until every dose is taken out. The potion image in the interface will display the total number of doses currently selected next to the potion's name. Alternatively, right click the potion image to set the desired dosage. Both options will automatically decant the potion to the desired dose without needing empty vials. Players can save up to 8 favourites, which are sorted alphabetically.

label: Potion storage glitch
title: Potion storage glitch
lead:
The potion storage glitch was a major glitch that occurred before an emergency server maintenance response was initiated on 1 October 2024. This glitch involved the use of the chugging barrel (formally named the pre-pot device) and the potion storage, both unlocked as rewards in the Mastering Mixology minigame. By moving all but one potion from storage into the bank, and then withdrawing potions while both the potion storage and chugging barrel interfaces were open, it was possible to duplicate potions into the barrel at the cost of making the amount in storage negative.

Jagex implemented a 15-minute timer before the servers were offline so that players could move to a safe area. During this 15-minute timer, there were item restrictions where players could not trade in the Grand Exchange, in any shops, and players could not pick up/drop any items on the ground. This means non-tradeable items disappeared when players were participating in minigames during this 15-minute timer. To resolve this issue with lost items, this prompted a server rollback that occurred approximately five minutes before the 15-minute timer was complete. This rollback was completed at 09:45 UTC on 1 October 2024 and only restored gameplay before the 15-minute timer (before the servers were momentarily offline).

label: potions
title: potions
lead:
Potions are consumable items that have a variety of different effects and bonuses. Players are able to make most of them at various levels with the Herblore skill using herbs and other ingredients.

Most potions act as a temporary skill boost, but some have other effects, like curing poison or providing dragonfire protection. A player must add a secondary ingredient to the unfinished potion, finishing the potion completely. A newly finished vial of potion contains three (3) doses of the potion. Some higher-level potions require a vial of coconut milk or blood to be used instead of water.

label: Potter's Wheel
title: Potter's Wheel
lead:
A Potter's Wheel is used to mould soft clay, obtainable by mixing water and clay, into other objects. With the relevant Crafting level, the player can make unfired versions of clay items, gaining Crafting experience. The player sits down, operates the pedals with their feet and uses their hands to shape the malleable clay. The unfired items produced in this way can then be further refined by placement in a pottery oven.

Free-to-play players can make unfired bowls, pie dishes, and pots while members can also create cups, pot lids, and plant pots.

label: pottery oven
title: pottery oven
lead:
A pottery oven (also known as a kiln) is used in crafting clay items that have been moulded from soft clay on a potter's wheel or with a mould. Unfired versions of clay items can be placed inside a pottery oven to harden them, producing a usable clay item and granting Crafting experience. Unlike shaping the soft clay, firing it has no Crafting level requirement.

The player places the unfired clay item in the oven, waits for a few seconds, then removes the fired clay object. There is, however, a small chance that the unfired items may break in the pottery oven. The chance of cracking a piece of pottery decreases with higher Crafting levels, resulting in a guaranteed success rate at level 14 Crafting for all types of earthenware.

title: powered staff
lead:
Powered staves are a category of magic weapons that possess a built-in magic spell that can be used regardless of the spellbook the player is using. The built-in spells give no base experience and grants the player 2 Magic experience per damage dealt.

They are typically charged with runes or coins to automatically cast magic projectiles. Unlike other Magic weapons, they cannot be used to autocast spells. In addition, they have an attack speed of 4, faster than other magic weapons, which have an attack speed of 5. The Tumeken's shadow, however, has an attack speed of 5 and the Eye of ayak has an attack speed of 3.

Bones can be buried, offered to gilded altars with incense burners, offered to the altar in the Chaos Temple, converted into Ectofuntus, converted to Blessed bone shards and offered at the Libation bowl, or have Sinister Offering cast on them. Demonic ashes can be scattered or converted into experience with Demonic Offering. Players can also kill monsters that were reanimated with reanimation spells, or cremate shade remains to unlock chests. These chests can drop pieces of the zealot's robes, a skilling outfit which gives a 1.25% chance per piece to save most remains when used.

label: Prayer points
title: Prayer points
lead:
Prayer points are a measure of the player's ability to use prayers and are measured in whole-point increments. A player's maximum, unboosted number of prayer points is equal to their Prayer level. Prayer points can be restored a number of ways, including praying at an altar, using a rejuvenation pool (or better) in a player-owned house, or drinking a dose of a prayer potion.

The player's current prayer points are displayed on the game's skills tab and are displayed by the minimap if the Data orb option is toggled on. The number of prayer points the player has remaining is an indication of how long a player can use prayers before having to restore them. The player can left-click on the prayer orb to begin using quick prayers, or the player can right-click on the prayer orb to set up their desired quick prayers.

label: Prayer potion
title: Prayer potion
lead:
A Prayer potion is a potion made by using snape grass on a ranarr potion (unf), requiring 38 Herblore, yielding a Prayer potion(3) and 87.5 Herblore experience. A dose of Prayer potion restores Prayer points equal to 7 + 25% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. If a Prayer cape, Max cape or ring of the gods (i) is equipped or a Prayer cape, Max cape or holy wrench is in the player's inventory, the restore increases to 7 + 27% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. It provides less Prayer point restoration than a super restore potion by 1 point per dose.

Prayer potions are always in high demand due to use of Prayers during combat and a need to restore points without travelling to an altar.

label: Prices
title: Prices
lead:
Prices are commonly accepted values for items which are determined by either a set number or supply and demand. Old School RuneScape is an interesting and challenging game, due in no small part to the complexity of its economy.

There are several ways and places in which players can buy, sell and barter goods. Where governed by the game itself, prices will be predictable, or even fixed. At the opposite extreme, when players are directly interacting, the prices will be less predictable, and sometimes even irrational.

Lady Keli's plan is to hold him for ransom, but this is to be foiled by the player.

Prince Ali has a dark skin tone and wears a top similar to Lady Keli when captive in the jail area. label: Prince Ali (disguised)
title: Prince Ali (disguised)
lead: During Prince Ali Rescue, Prince Ali escapes from jail by lightening his skin using paste, donning a wig, and wearing a pink skirt in order to make himself resemble Lady Keli. Due to a change in the quest released alongside Beneath Cursed Sands, the skin paste is instead used to cover a black eye rather than to lighten his skin, while the rest now happens off-screen, so the NPC is no longer used.

label: Prince Ali Rescue
title: Prince Ali Rescue
lead: Prince Ali Rescue is a free-to-play quest, and one of the first released. It's notable for allowing entry through the Al Kharid/Lumbridge gate without the fee of 10 coins. It also introduces characters who are a part of the Kharidian quest series.

label: Prince Anlaf
title: Prince Anlaf
lead:
Crown Prince Anlaf is the current ruler of Burthorpe, a small human settlement in northern Asgarnia that is currently engaged in a bloody war with the trolls. Anlaf is the son of King Vallance, the ruler of Asgarnia and an important figure within the White Knights of Falador. He is known to be a lover of puzzles and games.

Political unrest within Asgarnia has recently driven Prince Anlaf to drop from the public eye. Concerned with the possibility of assassination or capture, Anlaf has for some time governed Burthorpe behind closed doors.

title: Princess
lead: Princess may refer to:

label: Principality
title: Principality
lead:
Principality is a music track that is unlocked in Burthorpe, including on Mac's island. In this area, the music track shuffles between playing this track and Kingdom.

In Classic music mode, this track plays on the east side of Burthorpe.

label: Prison door (Desert Mining Camp)
title: Prison door (Desert Mining Camp)
lead: The prison door in the Desert Mining Camp can be opened with the cell door key. Without it the bars in the window of the jail cell must be bent to escape.

label: Prison Door (Fight Arena)
title: Prison Door (Fight Arena)
lead: There are several prison doors located within the Fight Arena prison. These are the cells where the player is locked in during the Fight Arena quest.

label: Prison Door (Sammy Servil's cell)
title: Prison Door (Sammy Servil's cell)
lead: The prison door to Sammy Servil's cell is located inside of the prison in the Fight Arena. During the Fight Arena quest, the cell door is unlocked with the Khazard cell keys, which are obtained after getting a guard drunk.

label: Prison door (Shantay Pass)
title: Prison door (Shantay Pass)
lead:
The prison door is for the Shantay Pass jail. Players are freely allowed to enter and leave jail cell, however when talking to Shantay and asking "What is this place?" followed by "I am definitely an outlaw, prepare to die!", they are thrown into the jail cell with the door locked. Shantay will immediately ask the player to pay the fine, or if cancelled, attempting to open the door will cause him to ask. The fine of five coins must be paid to Shantay before he will unlock the door.

If the fine is not paid by refusing to pay it twice, Shantay to send the player to Port Sarim jail. Teleporting out is also an option. In either case, returning to the prison door in Shantay Pass and attempting to open it will cause Shantay to say "You should be in Jail! Well, no doubt the authorities in Port Sarim know what they're doing. But if you get into any more trouble, you'll be stuck back in jail."

label: Prison key
title: Prison key
lead:
Prison key may refer to:

*Prison key (Prison Pete)
*Prison key (Troll Stronghold)

label: Prison key (Troll Stronghold)
title: Prison key (Troll Stronghold)
lead:
The prison key is a quest item used only during Troll Stronghold. It opens the door to the troll prison and is a drop from both the level 113 Troll generals in Troll Stronghold. Players must kill a general to get the key.

As Troll generals may hit high (up to 38 hitpoints), it is recommended to use a safespot or protect from melee when trying to kill one for the key. Once the key is dropped, players may enter the locked door to continue the quest.

label: Profane waters
title: Profane waters
lead: Profane waters are a sailing hazard found surrounding the Cursed Archipelago in the Eastern Ocean. Attempting to traverse these waters will significantly slow the player's boat and continuously deal 5 damage to both the player's hitpoints and their boat, as well as drain the player's prayer points by 5. Once prayer drops to 0, the damage dealt to players increases to 7, though the boat damage remains at 5. It will also give the chatbox message No boat can withstand these profane waters! and prevent the usage of any prayers. Currently, there is no way to mitigate the effects of profane waters.

label: Professor Answith
title: Professor Answith
lead: Professor Answith is the author of the book Treachery of Royalty. As the book is written mostly about past events, it is possible that Professor Answith is or was a historian. Nothing else is known about them.

label: Professor Oddenstein
title: Professor Oddenstein
lead:
Professor Oddenstein is a mad scientist who lives on the top floor of Draynor Manor. He is a central character of the Ernest the Chicken quest, and minder of the Interdimensional rift for the Killerwatt plane. Ava works as his assistant.

As a mad scientist, he is responsible for creating various things:
*The strange machine, which has transformed Ernest into a chicken.
**Although it is currently a transmutation machine, Oddenstein claims that at various points it used to be a time travel machine, a dramatic lightning generator, and a "thing for generating monsters".
**Aggie, the witch who lives in Draynor Village, says that the machine was turning people into flying fish a few years ago.
*The portal machine, which has created an interdimensional rift to the Killerwatt plane.
*The Phantasmic Destabiliser Mark 500, used to get rid of ghosts, and later retrofitted into the Easter blaster.
*The security system in Nora T. Hagg's basement.

label: Project Rebalance
title: Project Rebalance
lead:
Project Rebalance is a long-term, multi-update project that rebalanced and reworked multiple older game systems for both combat and skilling, including many features that have been unchanged since before 2007.

Project Rebalance was first announced as a project in Game Jam IV led by Mods Arcane, Halo, Husky, and Kieren. At the time, the project had a smaller scope, mainly around "making under-utilised content a little less obsolete" and "making early-game content a little bit more intuitive." Afterwards, the project expanded to include concerns about "power-creep" and high-level reward space.

label: Project Rebalance Beta
title: Project Rebalance Beta
lead:
As part of Project Rebalance, players were able to test the proposed changes to various NPC defence stats, including adding elemental weaknesses and splitting ranged defence into three styles - Light, Standard, and Heavy - akin to melee's Stab, Slash, and Crush.

Unlike other betas before it, players can import their account's game data via the Gameplay section of the Settings interface, and then logging out and manually switching to a beta world via the Main Menu. Upon logging in, the player's last saved state is imported, and a boss helper tool is inserted into the inventory.

label: Project Zanaris
title: Project Zanaris
lead:
Project Zanaris was the name given to the development of community servers for Old School RuneScape. The project was announced at Summer Summit 2024, and later paused indefinitely with a post on 3 June 2025.

The community server system was described as a way for players to rent separate servers from Jagex. These servers could then be customised by the players to "create a brand-new gameplay experience". Proposed server customisations included restrictions on who could join, damage changes, region restrictions, and access to Leagues content.

label: Pronouns
title: Pronouns
lead:
Pronouns are a group of words used in natural English speech as a substitute abbreviation for a that has usually already been referenced. In Old School RuneScape, there are three "Pronouns" settings available that change how the game refers to the player. In order of appearance in the settings drop-down menu, they are: He/him, She/her, and They/them.

A player's chosen pronouns do not affect their in-game abilities in any way, nor does the choice change or restrict the player's available Body type. Pronouns are chosen during initial character creation on Tutorial Island, but the choice can be changed later at any time, as often as desired, and at no cost. It is either set through the settings menu (Wrench icon > All Settings > Gameplay > Pronouns) or by speaking to the Makeover Mage.

label: Proselyte armour
title: Proselyte armour
lead:
Proselyte armour can be obtained after completing The Slug Menace quest by purchasing it from Sir Tiffy Cashien in Falador Park. The quest is a requirement for wearing the set, along with Defence level of 30 and Prayer level of 20. It has the same stats as its Adamant armour counterpart, except for the Prayer bonus and lower weight.

Proselyte armour is commonly used for completing Slayer tasks that players employ Protection Prayers to complete. This armour saves a lot of food and banking as Prayer potions are used alongside its high Prayer bonus to protect the player from damage longer than armour with an average amount of Prayer bonus, given that the player's Prayer level is high enough to use combat Protection Prayers.

label: Prospector kit
title: Prospector kit
lead:
The prospector kit is an experience-boosting set, purchasable from Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop in the Motherlode Mine for a total of 180 golden nuggets, which are obtained occasionally when cleaning pay-dirt, or from Petrified Pete's Ore Shop near the Volcanic Mine for a total of 120,000 volcanic mine reward points. Pieces purchased from Petrified Pete cannot be sold back to Prospector Percy for golden nuggets; attempting to do so will yield the message "You can't sell this item back to Percy as you did not buy it from this shop".

The full set, when worn, grants +2.5% bonus Mining experience. Players who have completed the elite Varrock Diary may wear Varrock armour 4 in place of the jacket.

label: Prospector kit (golden)
title: Prospector kit (golden)
lead:
The golden prospector kit is an experience-boosting clothing set that grants 2.5% additional Mining experience when worn while mining. The golden prospector kit is a cosmetic variant of the prospector kit and therefore provides the same benefits as the normal prospector kit, and each piece will act as a normal piece for the purpose of obtaining the set bonus.

This set can be stored in the armour case space of a costume room in a player-owned house. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

label: Protect
title: Protect
lead:
Protect may refer to:

*Dragonfire protection, protection against dragonfire
*Equipment
**God protection, equipment that makes monsters following a respective god unaggressive towards you in the God Wars Dungeon and Wilderness God Wars Dungeon
**Slayer equipment, specific equipment that protects you from negative effects or to finish off a monster at low health
**Tier-5 Shayzien armour, the full set that protects you from the poison attacks of lizardman shamans
**Warm clothes, warm or winter-themed equipment that reduces damage taken from the Wintertodt
**Yak-hide armour, mainly used in the Fremennik Isles quest to mitigate the attacks of Ice Trolls
*Heat protection, protection against desert heat
*Orbs of protection, a quest item used during Tree Gnome Village
*Protection prayers, prayers that grant immunity from Magic, Ranged or Melee attacks dependent on the respective prayer
**Protect Item, a prayer that lets you keep one extra item upon dying
*Farming patch disease protection
**See seeds for a specific list of protection by seed

label: Protect from Magic
title: Protect from Magic
lead:
Protect from Magic is a protection prayer unlocked at level 37 Prayer that places a diagonal Magic spell bolt graphic above the player's head. Protect from Magic grants players 100% resistance to almost all NPC magic attacks, and 40% resistance to magic attacks dealt by players. With a prayer bonus of 0, It depletes prayer at a rate of 1 point per 3 seconds (or 5 game ticks).

If the player has this prayer active when they were hit by Tele Block, its potency is reduced by 50% making it last two minutes and thirty seconds compared to five whole minutes; but the chance of Tele Block splashing is unaffected.

label: Protect from Melee
title: Protect from Melee
lead:
Protect from Melee is an overhead Melee protection prayer accessible to players with a Prayer level of at least 43. The prayer allows the player to resist 100% of the incoming melee damage dealt by monsters and 40% of melee damage by other players. It depletes prayer at a rate of 1 point per 3 seconds (or 5 game ticks).

Tougher monsters, mainly PvM or certain quest bosses, are able to hit through this prayer or deal reduced damage (for example, Kruk from Monkey Madness II).

label: Protect from Missiles
title: Protect from Missiles
lead:
Protect from Missiles is an overhead Ranged protection prayer unlocked at level 40 Prayer. It offers players 100% resistance to most NPC ranged attacks, and 40% resistance to player-dealt ranged attacks. It depletes prayer at a rate of 1 point per 3 seconds (or 5 game ticks).

Certain NPCs may still ignore or partially bypass Protect from Missiles, such as Scions spawned during the Abyssal Sire fight, which will deal reduced damage with the prayer active.

label: Protect Item
title: Protect Item
lead:
Protect Item is a prayer unlocked at level 25 Prayer. If the player is skulled, it will allow the player to keep one item upon death, in most other situations it will allow four.

It cannot be used in high-risk worlds. Though Ultimate Ironmen can activate this prayer, they will not benefit from it.

label: protection prayers
title: protection prayers
lead:
Protection Prayers are often used to refer to the three "Protect from x" Prayers that could nullify or mitigate damage from incoming attacks of the respective combat style or discipline from monsters or players. These are available in both free-to-play and pay-to-play.

Only one protection prayer can be activated at a time; activating a different protection Prayer will deactivate the current one. Protection Prayers only provide a 40% damage reduction in PVP. Protection prayers block all damage in most circumstances against NPCs, though some bosses (typically high-levelled) have attacks that can deal partial or full damage through them.

label: Prototype dart
title: Prototype dart
lead:
The prototype dart is a quest item made during the Tourist Trap quest. It is made by smithing a prototype dart tip on an experimental anvil that is not visible on the Minimap. 10 Fletching experience is given after attaching the feather.

Should the player have a spare (via the drop trick) and speak to Al Shabim (after the quest section is complete or after completing the quest), he will confiscate the item and exclaim: Where did you get this from Effendi! I'll have to confiscate this for your own safety!

label: Prototype dart tip
title: Prototype dart tip
lead: A prototype dart tip is a quest item used in Tourist Trap. It can be made by using a bronze bar on an experimental anvil in the Bedabin Camp. If used on a feather, it will create a prototype dart.

label: Pukkamay
title: Pukkamay
lead:
Pukkamay was a gnome chef of the late Fourth Age. While he is deceased, his culinary achievements continue to affect gnome culture significantly even today.

He is most famous for his invention of crunchies, a popular gnomish dish not unlike the humans' . Although his creation of crunchies was an accident, he soon realised the potential in the crunchy and opened a highly successful business. Pukkamay further shook the gnome world when he invented toad crunchies, the first gnome dish to utilise swamp toads as an ingredient. When his invention was unveiled, some thought he had gone insane; however, the idea soon caught on, and today toad is used in many gnome dishes.

title: Pump and drain (interface item)

The Pump and drain is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Pump and drain.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

The Pump and tub is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Pump and tub.

label: Pumpkin
title: Pumpkin
lead:
Pumpkins are the first holiday food rare and second holiday rare to be dropped, the first being the scythe. Pumpkins can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

If you plan to sell your pumpkin, it is recommended that you put it in note form to avoid accidentally eating it.

label: Pungent pot
title: Pungent pot
lead:
The pungent pot is a quest item found at the murder scene during the Murder Mystery quest. It is later used as evidence during the murder investigation.

Using the pot on a barrel of flour will result in a message stating You probably shouldn't use evidence from a crime scene to keep flour in...

label: Pure

Pure may refer to:
*Combat pure, a player who works primarily on raising certain combat skills high
*Skill pure, a player that develops non-combat skills while keeping combat skills low
*Pure essence, a rune essence that can be crafted into any type of rune
*Purepker895, a NPC player spoof seen in the Draynor Bank Robbery

title: Purple
lead:
Purple may refer to:

*Zaros, a god associated with the colour purple.

label: Purple boots
title: Purple boots
lead:
Purple boots can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The boots come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. They give the same stats as leather boots.

Unlike leather boots, these cannot be crafted. Because of their stats, they are mostly worn for cosmetic purposes.

label: Purple cape
title: Purple cape
lead: A purple cape is made by using purple dye on another coloured cape.

label: purple dye
title: purple dye
lead:
Purple dye is a dye made by combining blue dye and red dye, both of which may be made by Aggie in Draynor Village. It is used for colouring capes, granting 2.5 Crafting experience in the process, and for dying orange slices during Recipe for Disaster.

It respawns to the north of the Clock Tower, near the spirit tree, south of East Ardougne, as well as on a table on the top floor of the church in Hosidius. It can also be bought at Lletya Seamstress in Lletya. Players must have at least started the Mourning's End Part I quest to access this shop.

label: Purple flowers
title: Purple flowers
lead:
Purple flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

label: Purple gloves
title: Purple gloves
lead:
Purple gloves can be purchased in Canifis from Barker at his store, Barker's Haberdashery, and are also dropped by Crawling Hands. The gloves come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. These gloves are often worn to match certain armour sets, such as gold-trimmed and god armour sets.

Their defence bonus is equal to that of leather gloves.

label: Purple hat
title: Purple hat
lead: Purple hats can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The hats come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Purple naval set
title: Purple naval set
lead: The Purple naval set is a set of clothing that can be bought from Honest Jimmy. The set consists of a Purple tricorn hat, Purple naval shirt, and Purple navy slacks.

label: Purple partyhat
title: Purple partyhat
lead:
Purple partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July) as part of a rare item drop.

label: Purple robe bottoms
title: Purple robe bottoms
lead: Purple robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Purple robe top
title: Purple robe top
lead: Purple robe tops can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe tops come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Puzzle box
title: Puzzle box
lead:
Puzzle boxes can be obtained by doing hard, elite, and master Treasure Trails. Before you are able to continue with your clue scroll, you will have to complete the puzzle.

A puzzle box is always scrambled 101 times before being handed to the player, by randomly sliding a piece into the empty position starting from the solved state.

label: PvP world
title: PvP world
lead: PvP worlds (also known as Player-versus-Player worlds) are a type of themed servers that allow players to engage in combat almost everywhere. On these worlds, players may attack each other within all locations outside of safe zones, which include banks and respawn areas.

label: Pyromancer outfit
title: Pyromancer outfit
lead:
The pyromancer outfit is an experience-boosting set that grants bonus Firemaking experience when worn. It provides a small boost to experience received when training Firemaking - a total of 2.5% when the full set is equipped. Although warm gloves match the appearance of the pyromancer outfit, they do not count towards the set bonus. However, they do count as a piece of warm clothing when subduing the Wintertodt.

The pyromancer outfit does not currently boost the experience gained from cremating shade remains on a Funeral Pyre as part of the Shades of Mort'ton minigame, nor does it affect gains from fixing Dorgesh-Kaan lamps (including the bonus xp for repairing 50).

label: Q&A livestreams
title: Q&A livestreams
lead:
Q&A livestreams are productions hosted by Jagex in the Old School RuneScape Discord server, Twitch, and/or YouTube, in which Jagex Moderators discuss various topics relating to the game, usually chosen by the community. After the streams conclude, they are often uploaded to YouTube, sometimes unlisted.

The broadcasts have historically aired on a roughly weekly basis, featuring a selection of JMods sitting on a couch or appearing on a video call. They typically centre around interactions with the audience, often by way of developers answering questions about upcoming content, and round-table discussions amongst the JMods present. They also sometimes deviate from the standard format, featuring artists drawing players' suggestions, interviews, presentations, or tech demos.

label: Quartz

lead:

* Amethyst, the product of mining an amethyst rock, also referred to as quartz during development

* Shadow quartz, an item from The Whisperer used to upgrade the ancient sceptre

label: Queen
title: Queen
lead:
Queen may refer to:
*Queen Efaritay, the legendary Icyene queen of Hallowvale.
*Queen Ellamaria, wife of King Roald.
*Fairy Queen, the ruler of Zanaris and the fairies, who is involved in the Fairy Tale quest series.
*Queen Glarial, a legendary elven queen married to the powerful king Baxtorian until her death and has a grandson named Islwyn.
*Ice Queen, resides under White Wolf Mountain and drops the ice gloves used in several quests, notably Heroes' Quest, Recipe for Disaster, and Desert Treasure I.
*Kalphite Queen, a boss monster in the Kalphite Lair.
*Penance Queen, the boss monster of the Barbarian Assault minigame.
*Sea Slug Queen, the main antagonist in the Sea Slug quest series.
*Sea Troll Queen, a quest boss monster who attacked the Piscatoris Fishing Colony along with her Sea Trolls during Swan Song.
*Queen Sigrid, the queen of the island of Etceteria.
*The Queen of Thieves, a quest and NPC named eponymously as the alias of Lady Shauna Piscarilius.
*Queen Zyanyi Arkan, the queen of Varlamore.
* Branda the Fire Queen, the fire giant boss.

label: Queen Biyrene I
title: Queen Biyrene I
lead:
Queen Biyrene I ruled the Kingdom of Great Kourend from the 53rd to 54th decade. Her rule was cut short by King Byrne III, who came of age during her reign.

She was the wife of King Byrne II and had two children, a daughter later known as Queen Biyrene II, and a son later known as King Byrne III. After the death of King Byrne II she married Lord Piscarilius.

label: Queen Biyrene II
title: Queen Biyrene II
lead:
Queen Biyrene II was ruler of Great Kourend during the 57th to 58th decade. Born during her mother's reign in the 53rd decade, her father was Lord Piscarilius, who at the time was responsible for Kourend's spy network as Lord of Intelligence.

Queen Biyrene II, along with other rulers of the Great Kourend, is mentioned in Timeline.

label: Queen Efaritay
title: Queen Efaritay
lead:
.]]
Queen Efaritay Hallow was the legendary Icyene queen who founded and ruled the kingdom of Hallowvale with her human husband Ascertes from their palace during the Third Age. With Ascertes, she had two half-human, half-icyenic children; a daughter, Larina, and a son, Safalaan. After 820 years of peace, a Zamorakian army led by the vampyre Lord Drakan invaded Hallowland. Ranis Drakan managed to capture Ascertes, which forced Queen Efaritay to surrender immediately. It is unknown what happened to Queen Efaritay after her capture.

In Sins of the Father, the icyenic Graveyard located south-east of Efaritay's former palace, now known as Ver Sinhaza, is visited. There, it is revealed by Vanescula Drakan that she is not buried in her family's tomb, suggesting that she could still be alive to this day. It is also revealed that Safalaan Hallow is her son.

label: Quest (music track)

label: Quest Complete 1
title: Quest Complete 1

label: Quest Complete 2

label: Quest Complete 3
title: Quest Complete 3

label: Quest Difficulties
title: Quest Difficulties
lead:
Quest difficulties are official measures of the level of strenuousness in a quest. The different levels are in order from least difficult to most difficult as follows: 
*Novice
*Intermediate
*Experienced
*Master
*Grandmaster

There is an additional official level:
*Special

label: quest experience rewards
title: quest experience rewards
lead:
This page contains a list of quests which gives experience in a specific skill; each skill has its own section displaying the experience given in ascending order.

There are also quests that let you choose between different skills, see here.

label: Quest experience rewards (F2P)

label: Quest Guide
title: Quest Guide
lead: The Quest Guide is the fourth non-player character whom players meet in Old School RuneScape. He gives players information about quests and the quest journal. He also explains the differences between free quests and members quests. He is only found on Tutorial Island, and can never be encountered again. During his lecture, he makes references to the quests Imp Catcher and Dragon Slayer I.

label: Quest item rewards
title: Quest item rewards
lead: This page is a list of the possible item rewards obtained upon completing quests.

label: quest items
title: quest items
lead:
Quest items are generally items used, made, or obtained only during quests. These include:
*Items that are used only in the quest, but not anywhere else, like the red cog from the Clock Tower
*Rewards from quests, like Iban's staff from the Underground Pass
*Unofficial rewards, like the blurite sword from The Knight's Sword
*Items that may be kept after the quest is complete, but only have a use during the quest, like the Burnt diary from the Royal Trouble quest
*Items that may be kept and used after the quest is complete, like the dramen staff from the Lost City

Quest items do not include:
*Common items, even though they are required for quests, which can be obtained and used without starting or completing any quests, like buckets and crushed gems
*Items not used during quests, like the security book
*Common food, such as karambwan, or minigame-related food, such as Premade blurb' sp.
*Items that are unlocked by quests, but must be purchased, like dragon longswords and rune platebodies, or can only be obtained after the quest, but are not a direct reward for the quest, such as unique Temple Trekking items.

label: Quest List
title: Quest List

label: Quest points
title: Quest points
lead:
Quest points, often abbreviated as QP, are part of the reward players get after they complete quests. They are considered a completion measure of quests in Old School RuneScape.

The amount of points awarded depends on the quest, ranging from 1 to 6 points. As a special case, Recipe for Disaster awards a total of 10 QP, as each of its sub-quests awards one point each.

label: Quest rewards (disambiguation)

label: Quest Speedrunning
title: Quest Speedrunning
lead:
Quest Speedrunning is a members-only game mode released on 12 October 2022. The game mode takes place on separate worlds and gives players a different save profile, similarly to Leagues. From there, players are able to choose a quest that they want to speedrun and will be given the relevant levels and items to start them.

The game mode was originally scheduled for release on 28 September, but it was pushed back to review player feedback from the Quest Speedrunning beta and updating the game engine to accommodate the launch.

label: Rabid Jack
title: Rabid Jack
lead:
Captain Rabid Jack is the single most feared pirate of the Eastern Ocean. Very little is known about him as almost no people dare to speak of the infamous Rabid Jack, but he apparently terrorised the Eastern Ocean and its islands such as Mos Le'Harmless. He has, however, not been seen for years, and currently appears to reside somewhere near a temple in the Eastern Ocean (likely the Cursed Archipelago) where he practises necromancy, resurrecting zombie pirates to expand his crew and plotting his return. It is suggested that this hideout is located beneath the sea.

Rabid Jack is responsible for sending Captain Donnie and his crew to invade Braindeath Island to plunder the island's production of Braindeath 'rum' and kill all the brewers. He also sent the undead Surgeon General Mi-Gor to invade Harmony Island and to conduct experiments on the residing monks to find a way to enhance his zombies by giving them un-rotting brains. In sending his lackeys, Jack appears to be trying to conceal his own involvement in these events. The player managed to thwart both plots during the Rum Deal and The Great Brain Robbery quests.

They are only mentioned in the message, and cannot be found anywhere in-game.

label: Radiant oathplate armour
title: Radiant oathplate armour
lead:
Radiant oathplate armour is a cosmetic upgrade of regular oathplate armour that can be created by using the purifying sigil and 2,500 aether runes on each piece of armour. The sigil is made by combining five separate pieces obtained from Yama after completing five specific contracts – a bottom, top, left, right, and middle.

The sigil has unlimited uses, though converting a piece of oathplate armour into its radiant variant requires an additional 2,500 aether runes.

label: Radimus Erkle
title: Radimus Erkle
lead:
Radimus Erkle is the Grand Vizier of the Legends' Guild and is in charge of admissions into the guild. He is also the brother of Siegfried Erkle, who owns the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items.

He will send players off to complete the Legends' Quest as proof that they are worthy enough to enter the guild. After the quest, dark daggers can be freely reclaimed from him.

label: Radimus notes
title: Radimus notes
lead:
Radimus notes is a quest item given to the player by Radimus Erkle during the Legends' Quest and is needed to enter the Kharazi Jungle. The notes consist of an incomplete map of the Kharazi Jungle, which Radimus wants to have fully charted. The player must take the notes to the western, central and eastern parts of the jungle, and use the notes at each location with 3 papyrus and a piece of charcoal in their inventory. If you lose the notes at any time during the quest then you can talk to Radimus Erkle and pay 30 coins to get them back, though regardless of any previous progress they will be incomplete.

Once the map is completed, the player should give the notes to a Jungle Forester in exchange for a bullroarer. The Jungle Forester will copy them and return them so you can turn them in to Radimus at the end of the quest.

label: Raft
title: Raft
lead:
A raft is a tiny boat that can be purchased from a shipwright for . One is provided to the player as part of the Pandemonium quest.

Rafts consist of a wood base, helm, and mast and sails, which provide hitpoints, speed, defence, and resistance stats, which can be upgraded with better materials. Flags and an eternal brazier can also be built on a raft. Additionally, rafts have one facility hotspot which can be used to build certain facilities; however, the selection of buildable facilities is limited, and as such is generally reserved for a cargo hold.

label: Raging Echoes League
title: Raging Echoes League
lead:
The Raging Echoes League was the fifth League in Old School RuneScape. The League was announced during the Summer Summit 2024 and began on 27 November 2024, lasting 8 weeks, ending on 22 January 2025.

The League carried forward the region-locking mechanic of Trailblazer League and Trailblazer Reloaded League with the additional option of Varlamore, and new content such as Echo Bosses.

label: Raging Echoes League/Areas
title: Raging Echoes League/Areas
lead:
In the Raging Echoes League, players are locked to certain areas within Gielinor. All players will begin the league restricted to Misthalin and unlock Karamja for free during the tutorial. Up to three other areas can be unlocked after completing 90, 200, and 400 League tasks.

Travel options from region to region are restricted by magical barriers unless players have access to the appropriate areas. Death's office, the Player Owned House, Random Events and the Essence mine will be accessible from all areas. Usage of transportation methods such as Charter Ships, Fairy Rings, Customs Officers, gnome gliders, etc. will require the destination area be unlocked before they can be used.

label: Raging Echoes League/Areas/Asgarnia/Summary
title: Raging Echoes League/Areas/Asgarnia/Summary
lead: The Asgarnia area covers the entire Kingdom of Asgarnia along with the island of Entrana, the Pest Control islands, and Troll Country. Instances of areas in Asgarnia and underground areas with an entrance in Asgarnia will also be included. Access to Catherby from White Wolf Mountain will be restricted and prevented through the use of magical barriers.

label: Raging Echoes League/Areas/Fremennik Province/Summary
title: Raging Echoes League/Areas/Fremennik Province/Summary
lead: The Fremennik Province area covers the entire Fremennik Province (including the Fremennik Isles) along with Lunar Isle and Weiss. Instances of areas in the Fremennik Province and underground areas with an entrance in the Fremennik Province will also be included. Access to Kandarin via the bridge south of Rellekka will be blocked by magical barriers.

label: Raging Echoes League/Areas/Kandarin/Summary
title: Raging Echoes League/Areas/Kandarin/Summary
lead: The Kandarin area covers the entire Kingdom of Kandarin along with the Feldip Hills, Ape Atoll and Crash Island. Instances of areas in Kandarin and underground areas with an entrance in Kandarin will also be included (with the exception of Taverley Dungeon and the Underground Pass). Access to Nightmare Zone is restricted. To obtain Nightmare Zone points speak to Dominic Onion and purchase them for 1 GP each.

label: Raging Echoes League/Areas/Karamja/Summary
title: Raging Echoes League/Areas/Karamja/Summary
lead: The Karamja area covers the entire island of Karamja along with the island of Crandor and the Realm of the Fisher King. Instances of areas in Karamja and underground areas with an entrance in Karamja will also be included.

title: Raging Echoes League/Boosted drops
lead: Items from certain sources are given a boosted drop rate in Raging Echoes League. All players receive a 2x drop rate multiplier after unlocking their first relic, this is further boosted to 5x upon reaching the fourth tier of relics.

label: Raging Echoes League/Combat Masteries
title: Raging Echoes League/Combat Masteries
lead:
Combat masteries are a new system to Raging Echoes League that offer boosts to combat. Masteries are a separate progression system to relics, offering players new choices and permanent decisions to further increase power.

The Combat Masteries are split into three styles: Melee, Ranged, and Magic, each with 6 Masteries. Each Combat Mastery in a style requires the previous tier of that style to be unlocked. The first time the player reaches a tier of Combat Mastery in any style will also enable an additional passive bonus that applies to all styles of combat.

id: page:raging echoes league/echo bosses and echo equipment
label: Raging Echoes League/Echo bosses and echo equipment
title: Raging Echoes League/Echo bosses and echo equipment
lead: Echo bosses are a new system to Raging Echoes League that grant players the opportunity to fight challenging variants of existing bosses, targeting difficulty levels more suited to the power level that players attain during leagues. Each unlockable area contains an echo boss that drop echo equipment. An area's echo equipment is designed to supplement the area's shortfalls for attainable items and can rival other areas' best-in-slot equipment.

label: Raging Echoes League/Guide
title: Raging Echoes League/Guide
lead: Raging Echoes League presents unique decisions and challenges unlike most content in Old School RuneScape. Since players are restricted to just 5 of the 11 available areas, sacrifices will have to be made when it comes to training skills and making money. This guide aims to provide information about the league mechanics, different training methods, and money making guides based on the constraints within the league.

label: Raging Echoes League/Guide/Skills
title: Raging Echoes League/Guide/Skills
lead:
All skills available in the main game are available in the Raging Echoes League. Skills can be trained similarly to that of regular ironman accounts, depending on what combination of areas are unlocked. Players begin with level 3 Herblore, and 5 Runecraft.

Experience rates are multiplied by 5x the usual rate. By unlocking relic tiers, this multiplier can be increased further.

label: Raging Echoes League/Relics
title: Raging Echoes League/Relics
lead:
Relics are powerful buffs which are unlocked with League Points. Relics offer bonuses that boost actions related to gathering, processing, teleportation, and combat. Upon completing the league tutorial, players are presented with the choice of their first relic between three. Additional relics can be unlocked as players reach certain point thresholds and unlock new tiers.

Once players choose a Relic of a tier, they will be permanently unlocked, but cannot change their relic selection for that tier.

label: Raging Echoes League/Tasks
title: Raging Echoes League/Tasks
lead:
This page contains a list of all the tasks in the Raging Echoes League. Completing tasks during the league allows players to earn league points and unlock relics that buff their character and areas containing new bosses and tasks. Tasks span five difficulty levels: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite, and Master. Completing a task requires its respective area to be unlocked, unless otherwise stated.

Some general tasks have region requirements. Not all general tasks are completable depending on region selection.

label: Rahul Vohra
title: Rahul Vohra
lead:
Rahul Vohra interned at Jagex during the summer of 2004. He developed the quests Monkey Madness I and Tai Bwo Wannai Trio.

Mod Ash has described Rahul's code as "remarkably hard to follow," not due to technical failures, but due to Rahul's background in object-oriented programming. RuneScript, the scripting language used by Jagex, is designed to be easy for those with little programming background; it does not use an object-oriented approach, and triggers different scripts, rather than different files. Because Rahul's coding is based on OOP, and calls multiple different files at once, the development team has found it difficult to modify the code, resulting in some long-lasting differences between Ape Atoll mechanics and other parts of the game.

title: Railing
lead:
A railing is a quest item used only in Dwarf Cannon. In the quest, six railings are obtained from Captain Lawgof and used to replace six bent railings in the fence surrounding the Coal Trucks. A hammer is also needed to repair the fence.

There is a chance to fail when repairing sections of the fence, and the player may receive small amounts of damage which will deal 1-2 Hitpoints. The player will also receive a message saying either You cut your hand on the rusty old railing., You strain your back trying to handle the railings., or You accidentally crush your hand in the railing.

label: Raiments of the Eye
title: Raiments of the Eye
lead:
The Raiments of the Eye are a set of robes that grant additional runes when worn while Runecrafting. The robes are a reward from Guardians of the Rift. Each piece of the outfit grants a 10% bonus, and an additional 20% bonus is provided when wearing the full set for a maximum bonus of 60%. Bonus runes do not provide additional experience. The hat, robe top, and robe bottoms can also be recoloured with abyssal dyes that are obtained as a rare reward from the Rewards Guardian.

Pieces of the outfit are purchased from the Guardians of the Rift reward shop for a total of 1,350 abyssal pearls. At an average of 2.14 pearls per search, this equates to roughly 180 games of Guardians of the Rift, and 630 searches, to obtain the full set.

label: Ralos
title: Ralos
lead:
Ralos is the god of the sun within the religion of Losanium and the brother of Ranul, the god of the moon. Ralos is commonly worshipped by the people of Kingdom of Varlamore. Little is known about Ralos; he is said to have been born from a giant burst of light before the world began.

Originally, criminals were sacrificed to Ralos at a temple on the Fortis Cliffs, but when King Maximus took the throne, he ordered the temple be destroyed and replaced with the Fortis Colosseum. Though outright human sacrifice is no longer practiced, the Colosseum still serves a religious purpose in that every bit of blood spilled in the arena is considered an offering to the god; it is believed that Ralos' power will fade without continued offerings.

label: Ralvash
title: Ralvash
lead:
Ralvash is a Zamorakian Mahjarrat mentioned by the golem during Desert Treasure II.

He was a tribune in the Zarosian Empire, but allied with Zamorak in the God Wars. Little else is known about him.

label: Raminme Altrodor
title: Raminme Altrodor
lead: Raminme Altrodor was a resident of Varrock in the Year 160 of the Fifth Age mentioned in the Varrock Census. According to the Varrock Census, he was a chef.

label: Ramone Ravitz
title: Ramone Ravitz
lead: Ramone Ravitz was one of the founding members of the Elders of Avarrocka. He has two known descendents, Horvik and Shauna Ravitz.

label: Ranael
title: Ranael
lead: Ranael is a shopkeeper who runs a shop in Al Kharid that sells plateskirts in her shop, Ranael's Super Skirt Store, located in south-eastern Al Kharid.

label: Ranael's Super Skirt Store.
title: Ranael's Super Skirt Store.
lead: Ranael's Super Skirt Store is located in south-eastern Al Kharid. It sells plateskirts up to adamant. It is run by Ranael.

label: Ranalph Devere
title: Ranalph Devere
lead: Ranalph Devere is one of the three long-dead warriors alongside San Tojalon and Irvig Senay that are required to be killed to collect a piece of the heart crystal for the Legends' Quest. He is hostile until you kill him to obtain the lump of crystal, but you can still attack him afterwards and he will fight back. He attacks with melee.

label: Ranarr potion (unf)
title: Ranarr potion (unf)
lead: A ranarr potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a ranarr weed on a vial of water, requiring 30 Herblore. Using white berries on a ranarr potion (unf) with 30 Herblore yields a defence potion(3) and 75 Herblore experience. Using a snape grass on a ranarr potion (unf) with 38 Herblore yields a prayer potion(3) and 87.5 Herblore experience. In the Eadgar's Ruse quest, using ground thistle on a ranarr potion (unf) yields a troll potion and 77.5 Herblore experience.

label: Ranarr weed
title: Ranarr weed
lead:
Ranarr weed, commonly referred to simply as ranarr, is a herb that can be cleaned at level 25 Herblore. The herb can be grown by players with level 32 in Farming by planting ranarr seeds in herb patches. It's also an uncommon drop from various monsters. Despite being one of the lowest-level herbs available, ranarr is one of the most valuable herbs in the game, due to its role in making prayer potions.

Ranarr is one of three herbs with "weed" in its title, alongside snake weed and dwarf weed. According to Gielinor's Flora, the plant's name comes from the word "rana," meaning "eye-catching" in an ancient Kharidian language, and is considered a weed due to how fast it grows.

label: Randas
title: Randas
lead:
Randas is a hero known to have travelled through the Underground Pass, placing the orbs of light to protect travellers, boosting faith and courage as detailed in his journal. His records feature prominently in the Underground Pass quest.

According to the , Randas travelled to the Underground Pass to fulfil his desire of becoming a great and mighty warrior. As such, he was susceptible to Zamorak's corruption. Due to this corruption, he performed an ancient ritual that altered his spirit forever, turning him into a soulless. It is said that he remains in the Pass in this state even today. While several sources corroborate Zamorak as the source of corruption in the pass, it is also likely that Iban is responsible, whose voices and practices coincide with the descriptions of Randas's fate.

label: random events
title: random events
lead:
Random events, anti-macro events, or simply randoms refers to a variety of NPCs and their associated areas that appear throughout Gielinor to interact with players. They will appear either to provide an item to a player or to ask the player to play a short minigame to earn a prize. When random events appear, they specify one player with whom they will interact, and only that player will be able to interact with them, besides basic dismissive dialogue. If the player does not wish to interact with the random event, they can right-click and dismiss the event, or just ignore the event, which disappears after a minute.

Not all random events are allowed everywhere in the game. For example, any random event that takes players into a separate instance will never appear in the Wilderness (as it could allow a fleeing player to escape and remain there until it is safe). Random events will also not appear in most banks, boss areas, and minigames; if a random event NPC is following the player into a disallowed area, it will despawn and not return, except for Count Check, Dr Jekyll, and the Genie.

label: range
title: range
lead:
A range is used to cook food through the Cooking skill. Except for special cases, any food that can be cooked on a fire can be cooked on a range. To cook food, simply 'use' it on the range. Ranges are marked on a player's map by the icon. Clay ovens and ovens also serve the same function as a range.

Cooking on a range reduces the burn chance for certain foods. The range in Lumbridge Castle (referred to as the "Cook-o-matic 100"), which requires completion of Cook's Assistant to use, has an even lower burn rate for certain foods. Lastly, the clay ovens in the Hosidius Kitchen give the best reduction in burn rates, provided the player has completed the easy Kourend & Kebos Diary.

label: Range (Carnillean Mansion)
title: Range (Carnillean Mansion)
lead:
A range is found in the basement of the Carnillean Mansion near Claus the chef. The range cannot be used to cook food, as the player will be stopped by Claus. The range can otherwise be inspected to observe a pot of soup bubbling.

During Hazeel Cult, if the player is aligned with the Cult of Hazeel a bottle of poison is used on the range to kill the dog Scruffy.

label: Ranged
title: Ranged
lead:
Ranged is one of the three combat classes in Old School RuneScape. It involves using bows, crossbows, blowpipes, and thrown weapons to damage opponents from a distance, and Ranged armour can mostly be made from animal hides. Players who specialise in this skill are known as rangers or archers.

The combat triangle dictates that rangers are strong against mages but weak against melee fighters.

label: Ranged Level Up!
title: Ranged Level Up!
lead: Ranged Level Up! is a jingle for levelling Ranged.

label: Ranged Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Ranged Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Ranged Level Up! (Unlocks) is a jingle for levelling Ranged.

label: Ranged magic
title: Ranged magic
lead: Ranged magic (also known as ranged-based magic) attacks are projectiles that are less likely to hit players wearing armour with high Ranged defence bonuses, but are fully protected against by the Protect from Magic prayer instead of Protect from Missiles.

label: ranged melee
title: ranged melee
lead: Ranged melee (also known as ranged-based melee) attacks are attacks which roll for accuracy against your ranged defensive bonuses but are fully protected against by the Protect from Melee prayer instead of the Protect from Missiles prayer.

label: Ranged pure (free-to-play)
title: Ranged pure (free-to-play)
lead:
A ranged pure is a type of free-to-play combat pure account that focuses on training Ranged.

In the free-to-play worlds there are no ranged knockout weapons such as the ballistae or high tier crossbows. Because of that, ranged pures are considered ineffective in typical arranged 1-vs-1 player-versus-player combat, and are pretty rare in general. However, they do find some use in multicombat areas due to their high damage output.

label: Ranged shield
title: Ranged shield
lead: Ranged shield may refer to:

label: Ranged Strength
title: Ranged Strength
lead:
Ranged Strength is one of the Equipment Stats, primarily found on ammunition. It helps determine how much damage a Ranged attack will do, whilst the Ranged attack bonus determines how likely an attack will be to hit. Although Ranged Strength is usually found on ammunition, darts, knives, and chinchompas are examples of projectiles which provide their own Ranged Strength bonus and are equipped in the weapon slot.

Weapons which provide a Ranged Strength bonus include the toxic blowpipe, which uses darts as ammunition, the crystal bow, which generates its own ammunition, and the venator bow, which uses arrows as ammunition. Various items in other equipment slots, such as the necklace of anguish and Ava's assembler, also provide a Ranged Strength bonus.

label: Ranged weapons
title: Ranged weapons
lead: Ranged is an attack type that is used primarily by weapons like bows, crossbows, and thrown weapons. In contrast to most melee weapons, ranged weapons can be used to deal damage to non-adjacent opponents up to a maximum range of 10 squares, depending on the weapon type. Ranged weapons are associated with the Ranged combat skill and, similar to melee weapons, have three distinct types of damage: standard, heavy, and light. Some monsters are weaker to certain damage types than others. For example, most dragons are weaker to heavy ranged damage than other types. The type of damage a weapon inflicts usually depends on its ammunition.

label: Ranged-magic hybrid (free-to-play)
title: Ranged-magic hybrid (free-to-play)
lead:
A ranged-magic hybrid is a type of low level free-to-play combat pure account that focuses on Magic and Ranged combat styles.

Since melee attacks can be underwhelming in terms of damage early on and lack the extra range of the other combat styles, this build is often followed by pures in low level clans trained to fight in multicombat areas. These pures also tend to have relatively low Hitpoints levels, since Magic and Ranged can be reliably trained without getting Hitpoints experience, and melee combat skills can be neglected without an effect on the damage output.

label: Ranged-melee hybrid (free-to-play)
title: Ranged-melee hybrid (free-to-play)
lead: A ranged-melee hybrid is a type of free-to-play combat pure account that combines Ranged and melee combat styles. It is one of the most common free-to-play combat pure builds on the 1-vs-1 player-versus-player combat scene.

lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Ranged in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Ranged level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: Ranger boots
title: Ranger boots
lead:
Ranger boots are a rare reward received from the completion of medium Treasure Trails. It is part of the ranger kit, and requires 40 Ranged to wear; it can also be stored in a treasure chest. Ranger boots are the third best Ranged footwear in terms of ranged attack bonus.

The drop rate of ranger boots is 1/1,133 per slot. With each medium clue reward, a player will receive 3-5 slots of items; this makes the effective drop rate ~1/283.6 per casket. The ranger boots are the most valuable drop from medium clues.

label: ranger kit
title: ranger kit
lead: The ranger kit is a possible reward from various levels of Treasure Trails.

label: Ranging Guild
title: Ranging Guild
lead: The Ranging Guild is an encampment located between Seers' Village and East Ardougne. Level 40 Ranged is required to enter, though this can be boosted. Inside, there are several shops, a minigame, and a training area.

label: Ranging Guild Doorman
title: Ranging Guild Doorman
lead: The Ranging Guild Doorman is a man who stands outside the entrance to the Ranging Guild. He makes sure that no-one can enter the guild unless they have at least level 40 Ranging. He looks identical to the guards found throughout the Ranging Guild.

label: Ranging Guild Ticket Exchange
title: Ranging Guild Ticket Exchange
lead:
The Ranging Guild Ticket Exchange is an archery shop in the Ranging Guild that sells Ranged equipment in exchange for Archery tickets.

You buy the whole quantity of items for the indicated price. That is, for example, you buy 30 Barb bolttips at once for 140 Archery tickets.

label: Ranging pedestals (interface item)
title: Ranging pedestals (interface item)
lead:
The Ranging pedestals is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Ranging pedestals.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: ranging potion
title: ranging potion
lead:
A ranging potion is a potion made by using a wine of Zamorak on a dwarf weed potion (unf), requiring 72 Herblore, yielding a ranging potion(3) and 162.5 Herblore experience. A dose of ranging potion provides a temporary skill boost to Ranged equal to 4 + 10% of the player's current Ranged level, rounded down, and will wear off at a rate of 1 level every 60 seconds (90 with preserve).

Crystal dust may be added to ranging potion, 1 dust per dose of potion, to make a divine ranging potion, requiring 74 Herblore.

label: Rank
title: Rank
lead:
Rank may refer to:
*White Knight ranks
*Rank Titles for Clans
*A rank in a Chat-channel
*Hiscores

label: Rantuki Tribe
title: Rantuki Tribe
lead:
The Rantuki Tribe is one of many elusive and nomadic tribes native to the tropical island of Karamja, found in the central Ardent Ocean. The Rantuki are mostly jungle-dwellers, living primarily in the isolated jungles of the island's southern regions, remaining out of sight.

The Rantuki have managed to remain hidden for decades without problems, and a member of the tribe, Kangai Mau, only recently revealed the tribe's existence as he needed help to reclaim a totem stolen by the East Ardougne noble Lord Kurt Francis Handelmort. This event plays a central role, as does Kangai Mau, in the Tribal Totem quest.

label: Rantz
title: Rantz
lead: Rantz is an ogre who lives in a cave in the eastern part of Feldip Hills with his children, Fycie and Bugs. He is located at the only quest start icon in that area, and is first encountered during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. After the quest, players can kill chompies to claim Rantz's feather hats.

label: Rantz's cave
title: Rantz's cave
lead:
Rantz's cave is a cave in which Rantz and his children Fycie and Bugs live. It's located in the eastern part of the Feldip Hills, north-east of the fairy ring (code ). The cave is featured in the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest.

The Locked Ogre chest can be found inside the cave, which players can open and search for ogre bellows.

label: Ranul
title: Ranul
lead:
Ranul is the god of the moon within the religion of Losanium. Ranul is much less popular than his brother Ralos in Varlamore, but has a small group of dedicated followers. Little is known about Ranul; he is said to have been born from the darkness of the night.

Followers of Ranul believe that after life begins, the only other significant event is death, believing it should be embraced and respected, shaping the lives of themselves and those around them. Ranul has an essential role in guiding those who pass away to the Gates of Mictl, or the afterlife. Thus, those who serve him in the Sect of Ranul have many responsibilities relating to funerary processes.

label: Rapid Heal
title: Rapid Heal
lead:
Rapid Heal is a prayer unlocked at level 22 Prayer. Rapid Heal doubles the natural regeneration rate of the player's Hitpoints to 1 Hitpoint per 30 seconds instead of the natural rate of 1 Hitpoint per minute. This does not stack with the Hitpoints cape perk, but does stack with the regen bracelet to regenerate 2 Hitpoints per 30 seconds.

Activating or deactivating Rapid Heal resets the countdown timer natural health regeneration to 30 seconds or 60 seconds, respectively. This effect can be useful in places such as Nightmare Zone, to prevent health regeneration, or to reset the timer for overhealing (such as with anglerfish) to prevent Hitpoints from decreasing.

label: Rapid Restore
title: Rapid Restore
lead:
Rapid Restore is a prayer unlocked at level 19 Prayer that doubles the restore rate of all reduced stats except for Hitpoints and Prayer.

The prayer will restore reduced stats every 60 seconds starting from the moment it is activated. Its timer is completely independent from the normal timer used to restore reduced stats. Rapid Restore can be useful for restoring stats that are reduced by a small amount, such as the Attack penalty after drinking beer. For quickly restoring heavily reduced stats, restore potions or super restores may be a more effective choice.

label: Rapids
title: Rapids
lead:
Rapids are fast and turbulent circular vortices of water found while Sailing. There are several kinds of rapids, and as the rapids increase in intensity, the tier of helm required to use them increases. Having too low tier of a helm will result in your boat taking damage, whilst having the required tier or higher will result in your boat getting a speed boost.

Your boat's rapid resistance can be found from stats panel in the sailing options represented as a number.

label: Rare creature part
title: Rare creature part
lead:
A rare creature part is an item collected while investigating Hunters' Rumours for the Hunter Guild. Once obtained, they must be handed back to the player's relevant Guild Hunter to finish off the rumour. The rare creature part will only drop for the Hunter creature that the player currently has an active rumour for. Having a rare part in your inventory prevents you from obtaining another, even if it is a different type of rare part. However, if you are hunting for your next rumour (with an extra rare part in your inventory) your successful hunts will still count toward the "pity threshold", i.e. once the threshold is hit, you will receive the rare part as long as you destroy the rare part from your previous rumour. This means that hunting while in possession of an excess rare part isn't a complete waste, although it is still not ideal.

A "pity threshold" exists for them in which the player is guaranteed to receive a "pity drop" after hunting a set amount of creatures; this threshold is slightly lower if wearing the full Guild hunter outfit. Additionally, if the player's inventory is full, the rare creature part will be dropped on the ground; however, if the part is received as a pity drop, it will be destroyed. As such, it is recommended to always have 1 free inventory space while doing rumours to avoid accidentally losing parts obtained as a pity drop.

label: rare drop table
title: rare drop table
lead:
The rare drop table or RDT is a drop table that is accessed by medium-level and high-level monsters. The rare drop table drops some rune items and other items of moderate value, and also has access to the gem drop table as a sub-table. The rare drop table also has a chance at rolling the mega-rare drop table.

The mega-rare drop table contains mostly empty drops, but also the rune spear, dragon spear and shield left half. The player does NOT need to have Legends' Quest completed to access the mega-rare drop table via the rare drop table, however it IS required to access it via the gem drop table.
