label: Rashiliyia
title: Rashiliyia
lead:
Queen Rashiliyia, wife of King Danthalas, mother of Bervirius, is the ghost who sent the undead ones to Shilo Village. 
Rashiliyia was a powerful sorceress and queen of an unknown kingdom on Karamja during the Third Age. Rashiliyia was in love with Zadimus, a high priest of Zamorak, who resided in the magnificent temple of Ah Za Rhoon. When Zadimus rejected her, she tortured and hanged him before collapsing the entire temple.

After her son Bervirius was killed in battle, she swore fealty to Zamorak, the god of chaos, if he would return her son to her. Zamorak returned her son as an undead, who terrorised her and her husband and apparently went on a rampage, killing several guards, before being killed by fire.

label: Rashiliyia corpse
title: Rashiliyia corpse
lead: The rashiliyia corpse is a quest item used in the Shilo Village quest. It is obtained near the end of the quest by defeating the three forms of Nazastarool in the tomb of Rashiliyia. The corpse must then be placed upon the dolmen within the Tomb of Bervirius, located underneath Cairn Isle, to complete the quest.

label: Rashiliyia's Tomb
title: Rashiliyia's Tomb
lead: Rashiliyia's Tomb is the final burial ground for the zombie queen, Rashiliyia. The tomb is visited during the Shilo Village quest, where it was taken over by Nazastarool. After the quest, the dungeon is filled with undead ones. If you are inside without wearing Beads of the Dead, Rashiliyia will appear, briefly attack, and summon two level 68 and one level 73 undead ones.

label: Rat
title: Rat
lead:
Rats are small animals commonly found throughout Gielinor, mostly in cities, sewers, and dungeons. They respawn rapidly, and are not marked on the minimap.

Although most rats have no drops, the rats in the Stronghold of Security have a 100% chance to drop bones when killed by the player.

label: Rat (attribute)
title: Rat (attribute)
lead: The rat attribute is assigned to monsters that can be attacked by rat bone weapons.

label: Rat bone weapons
title: Rat bone weapons
lead: Rat bone weapons, known colloquially as "ratbane" weapons, are a class of weapons that have an affinity for monsters with the rat attribute. They are primarily used for killing Scurrius, but also brine rats, giant rats, zombie rats and other rats. Rat bone weapons are not effective against most monsters, and can only deal damage to rats. Each weapon is made from scurrius' spine, dropped by Scurrius.

label: rat poison
title: rat poison
lead:
Rat poison is a quest item used in Clock Tower and Ratcatchers.

In the Clock Tower quest, players can pick up the rat poison spawn in the basement of the Clock Tower before retrieving the white cog. It is used on the rats' feeding trough to poison them, killing them, thus opening the western door to pick up the white cog.

label: Rat's tail
title: Rat's tail
lead:
A Rat's tail is a quest item used in the Witch's Potion quest. It can be obtained by killing any standard rat after the player has begun Witch's Potion. The item has a 100% chance to drop once you begin the quest.

Brian's Archery Supplies, a store that sells Ranged supplies, has a couple of rats which are very convenient for the player, since the store is located near Hetty the Witch's house.

* Forester's ration, an item used in Woodcutting as part of Forestry

*The Ratpit bar under Varrock

Raurgs are an extinct race of creatures in the service of Bandos that were likely wiped out during the cataclysmic God Wars. Their remains, Raurg bones, can be found in the coffins at Jiggig.

The appearance and nature of Raurgs is largely unknown, they are however suspected to be similar to ogres, orks, fayrgs and ourgs.

label: Raw anchovies
title: Raw anchovies
lead: Raw anchovies are a fish that require a Fishing level of at least 15 to be caught. Doing so requires a small fishing net, and grants 40 Fishing experience. This makes anchovies a useful source of Fishing experience for players looking to train Fishing from level 15 to 20. Raw anchovies can be bought from Charley in Mos Le'Harmless for 16 coins.

label: Raw bass
title: Raw bass
lead:
A raw bass can be caught by players with a Fishing level of 46 or higher using a big fishing net at a fishing spot, this cannot be boosted. Doing so yields 100 Fishing experience per bass caught. They can be cooked into bass with a Cooking level of 43.

It is also possible for players to catch a big bass which can be stuffed by the taxidermist in Canifis and subsequently displayed in the Skill Hall of one's player-owned house.

label: Raw batta
title: Raw batta
lead:
A raw batta is created by adding gianne dough to a batta tin. It can be cooked on a range to create a half baked batta.

Unlike other items requiring a range, raw batta cannot be cooked using Mor Ul Rek sulphur vents.

label: Raw bear meat
title: Raw bear meat
lead:
Raw bear meat can be obtained by killing any bear (except Callisto or Artio), or by purchasing it from Rufus in Canifis. It is dipped in the Cauldron of Thunder during the Druidic Ritual quest. It can be cooked at level 1 Cooking, granting 30 Cooking experience if successful. After successfully cooking it, it will simply be cooked meat, burning it will result in burnt meat (burning can be achieved at any level by cooking it twice). The raw bear meat can also be made into sinew at level 1 Cooking by using it on a range.

Bears can be found throughout Gielinor, mainly in woodland areas such as near Castle Wars, south of Yanille and in a cage in Varrock castle. To get to this a player must go through the Varrock Sewers. A single black bear can be found south of the South-east Varrock mining site, along with two unicorns. Another good place to kill bears is north-east of Ardougne, near the Legends' Guild.

label: Raw beef
title: Raw beef
lead: Raw beef is an uncooked food. Raw beef is one of the requirements of the Druidic Ritual quest. Players require only level 1 Cooking to cook raw beef. It gives 30 Cooking experience when cooked. When cooked, the raw beef may become cooked meat or burnt meat. Players can buy it from Rufus' Meat Emporium in Canifis and from Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim. Raw beef is always dropped from cows. Members can convert raw beef into sinew by using it on a range and choosing the "Make sinew" option.

label: Raw chicken
title: Raw chicken
lead:
A Raw chicken is an uncooked food item dropped by chickens or roosters. They are also sold at Rufus' Meat Emporium in Canifis and Wydin's Food Store in Port Sarim.

There is also a crate in Wydin's shop in Port Sarim that provides unlimited raw chicken. A white apron is required to enter the room which contains the crate.

label: Raw chompy
title: Raw chompy
lead:
A raw chompy is obtained by killing a chompy bird. It can be cooked on an iron spit or at the ogre spit-roast near Rantz's cave, to make cooked chompy. Failure to cook it properly will result in a ruined chompy. Raw chompy is one of the three main ingredients in a wild pie.

The ability to hunt chompies is unlocked during the Big Chompy Bird Hunting quest. They are also used in the quest Recipe for Disaster during the portion where Skrach Uglogwee needs to be freed.

label: Raw cod
title: Raw cod
lead:
Raw cod is a fish that can be caught with a big fishing net at any fishing spot. It requires a Fishing level of 23 to catch and grants 45 fishing experience per catch. It can be cooked into cod with level 18 Cooking. The most common spot to fish cod is Catherby.

Raw cod is used for the Freeing Pirate Pete section of the Recipe for Disaster quest. It is also used for the Cold War quest, but it can be substituted with the use of the activated Ring of Charos.

label: Raw crunchies
title: Raw crunchies
lead:
Raw crunchies are obtained by using gianne dough on a crunchy tray. They can be used on a range to make half baked crunchies.

Unlike other items requiring a range, raw crunchies cannot be cooked using Mor Ul Rek sulphur vents.

label: raw giant carp
title: raw giant carp
lead:
A raw giant carp is a quest item used only in Fishing Contest. It requires Level 10 Fishing and is caught with a fishing rod and red vine worms after stuffing the pipe with a garlic.

It is given to Bonzo in order to win the Fishing trophy.

label: Raw gnomebowl
title: Raw gnomebowl
lead:
Raw gnomebowls are the base of gnomebowl cooking and are obtained by using gianne dough on a gnomebowl mould. They can be used on a range to make half baked bowls.

Unlike other items requiring a range, raw gnomebowls cannot be cooked using Mor Ul Rek sulphur vents.

label: Raw Herring
title: Raw Herring
lead:
Raw herring is an item that is obtained through the Fishing skill by using a fishing rod with fishing bait on a net/bait fishing spot using the bait option. Herrings can only be caught in fishing spots by the sea. Catching a raw herring grants 30 Fishing experience. It can be cooked into herring with a Cooking level of 5, granting 50 Cooking experience.

This fish can be caught at level 10 Fishing and cooked at level 5 Cooking.

label: Raw lava eel
title: Raw lava eel
lead:
Raw lava eels require level 53 Fishing to catch, and a Cooking level of 53 to cook. Raw lava eels may be caught using an oily fishing rod and bait in the lava rivers found in Taverley Dungeon, the Wilderness Lava Maze, or the Charred Dungeon (level 60 Sailing).

Players who wish to reside in Taverley Dungeon for extensive periods of time can bring equipment (logs, tinderbox, oily fishing rod and bait) to fish and cook the lava eels to produce food for combat. This is especially true for players on a Slayer task for black demons or blue dragons.

label: Raw lobster
title: Raw lobster
lead:
A raw lobster is a type of crustacean which can be caught at level 40 Fishing with a lobster pot, resulting in 90 Fishing experience. It can be cooked into lobster at level 40 Cooking, yielding 120 Cooking experience. Starting at level 74 Cooking, raw lobsters will no longer burn; wearing cooking gauntlets reduces this threshold to 64 Cooking instead.

Raw lobster is also used in Creature Creation together with a raw jubbly to make a jubster.

label: Raw mackerel
title: Raw mackerel
lead: Raw mackerel is a fish that can be caught with a big fishing net at any big net fishing spot. It requires a Fishing level of 16 to catch and can be cooked into mackerel with level 10 Cooking. The most common spot to fish mackerel is Catherby. There's a possibility that 10 raw mackerel will be required for a part in the quest In Aid of the Myreque.

label: Raw manta ray
title: Raw manta ray
lead:
Raw manta ray are fish that can be obtained with level 81 Fishing. They can be caught while playing the Fishing Trawler, from the Tempoross Reward pool, or while drift net fishing at Fossil Island with 90 Fishing, which cannot be boosted. They are also a possible reward from a bowl of fish bought from Mairin's Market. They can be cooked into manta rays with 91 Cooking, giving 216.3 experience.

Wearing the Cooking cape while cooking manta rays will prevent players from burning them.

label: Raw meat
title: Raw meat
lead:
Raw meat is an uncooked food item. Specifically, the term may refer to any of the following:
*Raw bear meat, a drop from bears that becomes cooked meat when used on a range or fire
*Raw beast meat, received from hunting kebbits
*Raw beef, a drop from cows that becomes cooked meat when used on a range or fire
*Raw bird meat, received from hunting birds
*Raw boar meat, a drop from boars that becomes cooked meat when used on a range or fire
*Raw chicken, a drop from chickens that becomes cooked chicken when used on a range or fire
*Raw jubbly, a drop from jubbly birds that becomes cooked jubbly and can only be cooked on an ogre spit-roast
*Raw oomlie, a drop from oomlie birds that must be cooked with a palm leaf to produce an oomlie wrap
*Raw rabbit, a drop from rabbits that becomes cooked rabbit when used on a range or fire
*Raw rat meat, a drop from giant rats that becomes cooked meat when used on a range or fire
*Raw snail, a drop from snails. There are 3 different types
**Fat snail
**Lean snail
**Thin snail
*Raw yak meat, a drop from yaks that becomes cooked meat when used on a range or fire

label: Raw oomlie
title: Raw oomlie
lead:
Raw oomlie may be obtained by killing the oomlie birds found in the depths of the Kharazi Jungle, south of Shilo Village. To get into the Kharazi Jungle, the player must have started Legends' Quest. At 50 Cooking, it can be wrapped in a palm leaf to get a wrapped oomlie, which can then be cooked to get a cooked oomlie wrap.

Wrapping it in a palm leaf is required to cook it; the raw oomlie cannot be cooked on its own. Attempting to do so will always fail (even with a cooking cape), resulting in a burnt oomlie, with the message You cook the Oomlie Meat on the fire..., and after the player burns it, "The meat is far too delicate to cook like this. Perhaps you should wrap it up to protect it from the heat."

label: Raw pie
title: Raw pie
lead:
Raw pie may refer to:

*Uncooked berry pie
*Uncooked meat pie
*Raw mud pie
*Uncooked apple pie
*Raw garden pie
*Raw fish pie
*Uncooked botanical pie
*Uncooked mushroom pie
*Uncooked dragonfruit pie

*Raw wild pie
*Raw summer pie

label: Raw pike
title: Raw pike
lead:
Raw pike are fish that can be caught with a Fishing level of 25, granting 60 fishing experience per catch. They can be cooked into pike with a Cooking level of 20. Successfully cooking a raw pike gives 80 Cooking experience. Raw pike are caught through bait fishing, which requires a fishing rod and bait.

The fish are caught with the bait option at lure/bait fishing spots found in rivers. While fishing there, a roll is made every 5 ticks (3 seconds) to catch a pike, although there is a 1/5 chance the interval is increased by 1 tick to 6 ticks (3.6 seconds) instead with the casting animation happening twice, one tick apart.

label: Raw rat meat
title: Raw rat meat
lead:
Raw rat meat is usually obtained by killing a giant rat. It can be cooked on a range or on a fire. It requires level 1 Cooking to be turned into Cooked meat, granting 30 Cooking experience if successful. It is one of the four raw meats needed in the Druidic Ritual quest. It can be used as bait when trapping sabre-toothed kebbits. Raw rat meat can be bought from Rufus in Canifis. Unlike raw beef, raw boar meat, and raw bear meat, raw rat meat cannot be turned into sinew.

If looking for a giant rat to kill, level 3 giant rats are common in Lumbridge Swamp and always drop raw rat meat. The level 6 giant rat in Lumbridge Swamp, the giant rat near the mine south-east of Varrock and the giant rats in the Stronghold of Security rarely drop rat meat.

label: Raw salmon
title: Raw salmon
lead: Raw salmon are fish that can be caught with a Fishing level of 30, granting 70 Fishing experience per catch. It can be cooked into salmon with a Cooking level of 25. Players will stop burning salmon unaided at a Cooking level of 58 or 55 when using the Lumbridge Castle range. Successfully cooking a salmon yields 90 Cooking experience. Raw salmon are caught through fly fishing, which requires a Fishing level of 30, a fly fishing rod, and feathers. The fish are caught with the lure option at Lure/Bait fishing spots found in rivers. Fly fishing trout and salmon is a very common way for players to train Fishing quickly.

label: Raw sardine
title: Raw sardine
lead:
Raw sardines are fish that require a Fishing level of 5 to catch by using a normal fishing rod on a bait fishing spot, by the sea. Fishing bait is required in the inventory, one being used for each catch, which yields 20 Fishing experience. Raw sardines may be cooked at level 1 Cooking to produce cooked sardines.

In the quest Gertrude's Cat, players have to rub a sardine with doogle leaves to feed Gertrude's lost cat. This creates a seasoned sardine.

label: Raw sea turtle
title: Raw sea turtle
lead:
Raw sea turtle are fish that can be obtained with level 79 Fishing. They can be caught while playing the Fishing Trawler minigame, from the Tempoross Reward pool, or while drift net fishing at Fossil Island with 80 Fishing, which cannot be boosted. They are also a possible reward from a bowl of fish bought from Mairin's Market. They can be cooked into sea turtles with 82 Cooking, giving 211.3 experience.

With level 99 Cooking, about 23% of sea turtles will be burnt. Wearing the Cooking cape while cooking sea turtles will prevent players from burning them.

label: raw shark
title: raw shark
lead:
Raw sharks can be fished with a harpoon with level 76 Fishing. They require level 80 Cooking to cook into sharks and heal 20 Hitpoints each. Raw sharks can be caught at many net/harpoon fishing spots with locations including the Fishing Guild, Catherby, Burgh de Rott, Rellekka, Iorwerth Camp, East of Hosidius, Jatizso, Isle of Souls, Gwenith, and Salvager Overlook. Raw sharks can also be caught without using a harpoon at level 96 Fishing and 76 Strength by starting the second part of barbarian fishing with Otto Godblessed. The rate at which they are caught can be increased with the use of shark lure, but doing so will reduce the experience gained.

A single raw shark can also be bought at Rufus' Meat Emporium in Canifis for 221 coins. 25 raw sharks can be bought at Frankie's Fishing Emporium starting at 170 coins.

label: Raw shrimps
title: Raw shrimps
lead: Raw shrimps can be caught at 1 Fishing with a small fishing net at a net fishing spot, granting 10 experience per catch. They can be cooked into shrimps at level 1 Cooking, granting 30 Cooking experience when successful. Raw shrimps can be used as a source of food for a growing kitten.

label: Raw shrimps (Tutorial Island)
title: Raw shrimps (Tutorial Island)
lead:
Raw shrimps are a unique variant of raw shrimps that can only be obtained on Tutorial Island. They are obtained by fishing at a Tutorial Island fishing spot. The Survival Expert teaches the player how to fish for shrimp using a small fishing net; they must catch and cook some shrimp in order to proceed to the next part of the tutorial.

A second variant of the raw shrimps could be obtained from the alternate Tutorial Island available to some players in 2020.

label: Raw swamp paste
title: Raw swamp paste
lead:
Raw swamp paste can be made by mixing flour with swamp tar. Raw swamp paste can be cooked on a fire (not a range) to create swamp paste, giving 2 Cooking experience. It is possible to burn the paste, resulting in the player discarding the burnt tar.

Swamp tar can be found in Lumbridge Swamp and in Mort Myre Swamp.

label: Raw swordfish
title: Raw swordfish
lead:
A raw swordfish is a type of fish that players can catch at level 50 Fishing with a harpoon at cage and harpoon fishing spots, and can be cooked at level 45 Cooking. It also can be obtained at level 60 fishing while drift net fishing which cannot be boosted.

Catching a swordfish grants 100 Fishing experience. Fishing for swordfish takes longer than lobsters because Tuna is caught along with it. Free players fishing on Karamja generally drop their tuna (often cooking it first for the experience), but the members-only fishing spots in Catherby, Port Piscarilius, Jatizso, and the Fishing Guild are close enough to banks that it is actually faster for players to bank the raw tuna than to drop it, additionally, the Fishing Guild gives an invisible +7 fishing boost. Cooking Swordfish will grant 140 experience.

label: Raw trout
title: Raw trout
lead:
Raw trout are fish that can be caught by luring Lure/Bait fishing spots with a Fishing level of 20, granting 50 Fishing experience per catch. It can be cooked into trout with a Cooking level of 15. Players will stop burning trout at level 49 if using a range, or 50 if using a fire. Successfully cooking a raw trout gives 70 Cooking experience.

Raw trout are caught through fly fishing, which requires a fly fishing rod and feathers. This method can also net salmon at the appropriate Fishing level. The fish are caught with the lure option at Lure/Bait fishing spots found in rivers.

label: Raw tuna
title: Raw tuna
lead:
Raw tuna is a type of fish, obtained by harpoon fishing at a cage/harpoon fishing spot. Raw tuna require 35 Fishing to catch and award the player 80 experience when caught. They can be sold, or cooked with a Cooking level of 30 to produce tuna, granting 100 experience in Cooking and will no longer be burned after level 63. The cooked version is often used by mid-levelled players when training combat.

Raw tuna can also be bought from Flosi Dalksson in Jatizso or thieved from the Fish stalls in The Warrens, Rellekka, Miscellania, and Etceteria, requiring a Thieving level of 42.

label: Raw ugthanki meat
title: Raw ugthanki meat
lead: Raw ugthanki meat can be obtained by killing an ugthanki. It can be cooked at level 1 Cooking, granting 40 Cooking experience if successful. After successfully cooking it, it will be ugthanki meat. Burning it will result in burnt meat. The raw ugthanki meat cannot be made into sinew, and cannot be cooked twice to create burnt meat.

label: Real life
title: Real life
lead:
Real life is a fantasy, sporadically referenced by various inhabitants spread across Gielinor. The official position of the RuneScape Council remains that rumours of a 'real life' are a dangerous and nihilistic distraction meant to lead adventurers astray from contributing to the overall experience gain of productive society.

As such, it is the duty of every conscientious adventurer to swiftly report such references to 'real life' and to chastise any peers suspected of engaging in 'real life' activities. A non-exhaustive list of such rumours is given below:

label: Real world trading
title: Real world trading
lead:
Real-world trading (RWT), also called real-world item trading (RWIT), is the act of exchanging anything outside of RuneScape, such as real-world money, for RuneScape items or services, such as gold, items, or skill levels, Jagex accounts, or vice versa. In addition, performing out-of-game services like using a Twitch channel or Discord server to advertise other Twitch channels or Discord servers in exchange for gold/real-world money is also categorised as RWT.

This is a rule-breaking activity that violates RuneScape s Terms and Conditions and is subject to severe consequences; players who conduct RWT risk being temporarily or permanently banned without warning, and in the case of buying in-game items, illegitimately obtained goods may be confiscated.

label: Realms
title: Realms
lead:
Realms in Old School RuneScape are separate dimensions scattered about in different planes. Many of Gielinor's inhabitants have arrived in Gielinor through the World Gate during the First Age and Second Age from other realms.

Below is a list of realms in which either are accessible or are known by players:
*Abyssal Space
*Cosmic Plane
*Dream World
*Enchanted Valley
*Fisher Realm
*Freneskae
*Gorak Plane
*Infernal Dimensions
*Killerwatt Plane
*Puro-Puro
*ScapeRune
*Shadow Realm
*Tarddiad
*Vampyrium
*Yu'biusk
*Zanaris

label: Reanimation spells
title: Reanimation spells
lead:
Reanimation spells are a category of spells in the Arceuus spellbook. These spells reanimate certain creatures whose heads still contain their souls. Killing reanimated creatures will grant differing amounts of Prayer experience, depending on the reanimated creature. A majority of reanimated creatures will have a maximum of 35 Hitpoints.

If players are on a Slayer task for the appropriate reanimated creature (such as a reanimated abyssal), they will also receive 35 Slayer experience for killing the reanimated creatures. Similarly, if reanimating a Slayer creature, players must have the appropriate Slayer level in order to claim the Prayer experience. However, certain reanimated creatures (demons, giants, horrors, and dragons) will not grant Slayer experience, due to the fact that multiple types of task monsters can drop the same head.

label: Rebellion of the Five Houses
title: Rebellion of the Five Houses
lead: The Rebellion of the Five Houses was a successful and mostly bloodless insurrection against the reign of King Rada III which took place in the 6th decade BA (Before the Accord) of Kourend's timeline, orchestrated by the Lords of all five cities of Great Kourend. Directly following the uprising, they established the Council of Elders, which jointly ruled Kourend for a few decades before the transition to a rotating monarchy with the signing of the Royal Accord of Twill. The events of the Rebellion of the Five Houses are narrated in the Extract from Eathram and Rada.

label: recess

lead:
The recess is a scenery object found in the Viyeldi Caves during and after the Legends' Quest. It is located to the right of the shimmering field which connects with the area containing 3 lesser demons.

If the heart crystal is used on it, it will turn into the Filled Recess, and the shimmering field can be passed through.

label: Recruiter
title: Recruiter
lead:
The Recruiter is found in the city square of West Ardougne. He tries to recruit the citizens of West Ardougne into King Tyras's army. Due to Tyras being unpopular and hated among the people of West Ardougne, his job has been a really tough one as he is pelted with tomatoes whenever he mentions Tyras. Apparently, the Recruiter is not aware of the death of King Tyras, which occurs during Regicide.

After the events of the Ardougne Revolution and Song of the Elves, he can no longer be found anywhere.

label: red bead
title: red bead
lead:
The red bead is a bead used in Imp Catcher quest. It is a drop from Imps and is returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with Black bead, White bead and Yellow bead to finish the quest.

The bead can also be used to bait traps when hunting imps.

label: Red boots
title: Red boots
lead:
Red boots can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The boots come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. They give the same stats as leather boots.

Unlike leather boots, these cannot be crafted. Because of their stats, they are mostly worn for cosmetic purposes.

label: Red cape
title: Red cape
lead: A red cape can be made by using red dye on another coloured cape, or purchased from Thessalia's Fine Clothes in Varrock or Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis.

label: Red chinchompa (interface item)
title: Red chinchompa (interface item)
lead:
The Red chinchompa is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the Red chinchompa

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Red cog
title: Red cog
lead:
The red cog is a quest item used only in Clock Tower. It is found in a room with three ogres in the Clock Tower's basement.

It is used to repair the northern red clock spindle on the .

label: Red crystal
title: Red crystal
lead:
Red crystal may refer to:

*Red crystal (Mourning's End Part II)
*Red crystal (Song of the Elves)

label: Red d'hide body
title: Red d'hide body
lead:
A red d'hide body is red dragonhide armour equipped in the body slot, requiring 60 Ranged and 40 Defence.

Although the Dragon Slayer I quest must be completed to equip the green d'hide body, it is not required to equip the blue d'hide body, red d'hide body, or black d'hide body.

label: Red d'hide chaps
title: Red d'hide chaps
lead:
Red d'hide chaps are a piece of the red dragonhide armour set, and require level 60 Ranged to wear. Similarly to other dragonhide chaps, they have no Defence level requirement.

A player with 75 Crafting can make them using 2 red dragon leather and 1 thread with a needle, granting 156 experience.

label: Red d'hide gold-trimmed armour
title: Red d'hide gold-trimmed armour
lead: Red d'hide gold-trimmed armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as Red d'hide armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from hard Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: Red d'hide trimmed armour
title: Red d'hide trimmed armour
lead: Red d'hide trimmed armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as red d'hide armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from hard Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: Red d'hide vambraces
title: Red d'hide vambraces
lead:
Red d'hide vambraces are a piece of red dragonhide armour worn in the hand slot that requires a Ranged level of 60 to equip.

Kebbit claws can be used on these vambraces to make red spiky vambraces, requiring a Crafting level of 73.

label: Red decorative armour
title: Red decorative armour
lead:
Red decorative equipment is a reward from the Castle Wars minigame. The armour set requires 5 Defence to equip and the sword requires 5 Attack to wield.

To purchase all pieces of the Red Decorative Armour set, it would cost 44 Castle wars tickets. These calculations are excluding time waiting between each game.

label: Red door
title: Red door
lead: The Red doors are located on of Melzar's Maze. They must be opened during Dragon Slayer I, using a red key obtained from killing the nearby Zombie rat with a long tail.

label: red dragon
title: red dragon
lead:
Red dragons are second-to-most powerful of the adult chromatic dragons. As with all adult dragons, an anti-dragon shield and/or antifire potion is essential when fighting them to mitigate damage from their dragonfire. The red dragonhides and dragon bones that they drop are worth substantial amounts of money.

The ability to be assigned red dragons can be purchased for 50 Slayer reward points. Once unlocked, they can be disabled, but players must spend another 50 points to unlock them again. Killing brutal red dragons in the Catacombs of Kourend will also count toward a red dragon task. One Red Dragon is fought during Dragon Slayer II.

label: Red dragon leather
title: Red dragon leather
lead: Red dragon leather is used in the Crafting skill to make red dragonhide armour. It can be created by giving a red dragonhide and 20 coins to a tanner. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, Forthos Dungeon, Crafting Guild, Kebos Lowlands, and Auburnvale. The last two tanners require the completion of Getting Ahead and children of the Sun, respectively. Alternatively, red dragon leather can be made using the Tan Leather spell. Crafting any piece of red dragonhide armour will grant the player 78 experience per hide.

label: Red dragonhide
title: Red dragonhide
lead:
Red dragonhide (also called Red d'hide by tanners) is a 100% drop from red dragons when they die. The hide can be tanned to become red dragon leather by paying a tanner or by using the Tan Leather lunar spell. A tanner will charge 20 coins for each hide, or 45 in Canifis. Tanners can be found in Al Kharid, the Ranging Guild, Canifis, Forthos Dungeon, and the Crafting Guild.

Players can then make red dragonhide armour from red dragon leather via the Crafting skill if they have a high enough level.

label: Red dragonhide armour
title: Red dragonhide armour
lead: Red dragonhide armour is a type of Ranged armour. All of the pieces require 60 Ranged to wear, and the body and shield require 40 Defence to equip. All of the pieces can be made through the Crafting skill from 8 pieces of red dragon leather.

label: red dye
title: red dye
lead:
Red dye is a dye created by taking 3 redberries to Aggie in Draynor Village along with 5 coins or Ali the dyer in Pollnivneach along with 25 coins. It can also be bought in Lletya from Oronwen for 6 coins. It can also be found in the Sisterhood Sanctuary in Slepe, as well as in the farmhouse featured in Getting Ahead, south of the Farming Guild, located in the shelves next to the stairs in the house.

Red dye can be combined with yellow dye to make orange dye, or with blue dye to make purple dye. It can be used to dye normal capes red. Red dye is used in Enlightened Journey, Getting Ahead, Song of the Elves, and Goblin Diplomacy if making orange dye. It is also a possible required item for Ghosts Ahoy because the colour needed is random.

label: Red flowers
title: Red flowers
lead:
Red flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

label: Red gloves
title: Red gloves
lead:
Red gloves can be purchased in Canifis from Barker at his store, Barker's Haberdashery, and are also dropped by Crawling Hands. The gloves come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. These gloves are often worn to match certain armour sets, such as gold-trimmed and god armour sets.

Their defence bonus is equal to that of leather gloves.

label: Red halloween mask
title: Red halloween mask
lead:
The Red halloween mask is a tradeable cosmetic item. Red halloween masks can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year. This also rewards the player with all other holiday items associated with Halloween.

After the playerbase was polled, it was decided that all tradeable rares will be distributed during their corresponding holiday events thus making them seasonal rares and not completely rare, this to prevent them from being worth hundreds of millions of coins again, like in RuneScape 3.

label: Red hat
title: Red hat
lead: Red hats can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The hats come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Red headband
title: Red headband
lead: The red headband is a members only item worn on the head. There are no requirements to wear it and it does not offer any combat bonuses.

label: Red naval set
title: Red naval set
lead: The Red naval set is a set of clothing that can be bought from Honest Jimmy. The set consists of a Red tricorn hat, Red naval shirt, and Red navy slacks.

label: Red partyhat
title: Red partyhat
lead:
Red partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July) as part of a rare item drop.

label: Red Reef Trading Company
title: Red Reef Trading Company
lead:
The Red Reef Trading Company are the antagonists of the Tortugan quest series. Their headquarters, Red Rock is located in the Red Reef sea. Little is currently known about them, but their primary focus appears to be harvesting a type of red coral, processing it into a red material, and exporting it.

At the end of Troubled Tortugans, one of their ships appears to be seen fleeing the scene of the Shellbane gryphon attack on the Tortugan eggs located on The Little Pearl.

label: Red robe bottoms
title: Red robe bottoms
lead: Red robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Red robe top
title: Red robe top
lead: Red robe tops can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe tops come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Red Sheep
title: Red Sheep
lead:
Red Sheep are sick sheep found near the East Ardougne north bank that must be prodded with the cattleprod to the sheep pen and fed the poisoned sheep feed during the Sheep Herder quest. Its wool is slightly reddish. Once killed, it drops the sheep bones (1).

After Mourning's End Part I, the sheep are of a darker red as a result of the player dyeing them with a Fixed device loaded with a Red toad. Once dyed, they can no longer be prodded or interacted with in any way. Players only need to dye one, and all the sheep of the same colour turn more saturated. This is how players can tell they haven't missed the sheep during the quest.

label: Red spiders' eggs
title: Red spiders' eggs
lead:
Red spiders' eggs are a Herblore ingredient that members can use to make one of three different potions. Those with level 22 Herblore can combine them with a harralander potion (unf) (made by adding harralander to a vial of water) to make a restore potion and gain 62.5 experience points. Those with level 63 Herblore can combine the eggs with a snapdragon potion (unf) (made by adding snapdragon to a vial of water) to make a super restore potion and gain 142.5 experience. Those with level 73 herblore can combine the eggs with coconut milk and a cactus spine to make weapon poison(+) and gain 190 experience.

All players can give red spiders' eggs along with a limpwurt root and 5 coins to the apothecary in Varrock, and he will give them a 4-dose strength potion in return.

label: Red topaz
title: Red topaz
lead:
Red topaz is a semi-precious gem used mainly in Crafting. It can be cut from uncut red topaz with a chisel at level 16 Crafting, yielding 25 experience. There is a chance to unsuccessfully cut the red topaz, resulting in a crushed gem and 6.3 experience.

3 red topaz can be given to Safta Doc alongside a gout tuber and 1,200 trading sticks in exchange for a red topaz machete.

label: Red vine worm
title: Red vine worm
lead:
The red vine worm is used in the Fishing Contest quest to catch the giant carp that wins the contest. They also may be needed to make a pair of magic secateurs in the quest A Fairy Tale I - Growing Pains, and can be possible a clue for finding Solus Dellagar in the quest Wanted!.

They are obtained by digging with spade near the red vines that can be found in McGrubor's Wood. The fairy ring code can be used to quickly reach the vines.

label: Red-X
title: Red-X
lead:
Red-X is a method by which players are able to prevent movement of monsters while standing underneath them. Clicking to interact with an object, such as clicking on a dropped item, an NPC, or a piece of scenery or object with an interaction, creates a Red "X" on screen which causes different NPC behaviour than clicking elsewhere in the game world. If a player is standing underneath a monster while in combat with them (have recently attacked said monster) and their most recent interaction with the game was a Red-X action, then the monster in question will not attempt to pathfind to the player.

The method allows players to preserve supplies against bosses that can only attack players in melee distance, such as General Graardor, K'ril Tsutsaroth, and Ba-Ba. It can also be used in the Fight Caves or the Inferno under certain niche situations to enable clearing with lower stats than would otherwise be possible.

label: Redbeard Frank
title: Redbeard Frank
lead: Redbeard Frank is a pirate featured in Pirate's Treasure. During the quest, players must smuggle Karamjan rum onto the mainland for Frank, who has offered them access to Hector's old treasure in exchange. Players must smuggle the illegal drink in on a banana shipment from Luthas's plantation in Musa Point, Karamja.

label: Redberries
title: Redberries
lead:
Redberries can be harvested from a bush patch after planting redberry seeds or picked from wild redberry bushes. They are used in Cooking to make redberry pies or to create dyes.

Redberries themselves cannot be eaten, despite being used in Cooking. Adding them to a compost bin makes regular compost.

label: Redberry pie
title: Redberry pie
lead:
Redberry pies are a type of pie that restores 10 Hitpoints in total, 2 bites each healing for 5. A pie dish will remain after both bites. It can be obtained by baking an uncooked berry pie on a cooking range, requiring level 10 Cooking and granting 78 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Redberry pie is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 45, or 42 when using the Lumbridge range. Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

A redberry pie is required in the quests The Knight's Sword, The Giant Dwarf, and Prying Times and is a possible task from Romily Weaklax in the Cooks' Guild.

label: registered email
title: registered email
lead: An account's Registered Email, also known as its Contact Email, is how Jagex will contact users about account management issues such as password resets, authenticator removal, and account recovery. This is not to be mistaken with the account's login email, which is only used to log into Jagex's services such as in-game, and on the Official RuneScape Forums. While the login email and registered email can be the same, it is strongly encouraged to keep them different for an extra layer of security.

label: Regular cape

label: Relic part 1
title: Relic part 1
lead:
The relic part 1 is a quest item that appears in the Watchtower quest. When combined with Relic part 2 and Relic part 3 it forms an Ogre relic which can be used to access the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth.

To obtain Relic part 1 the player must retrieve a bar of gold that Toban stole from Og.

label: Renegade knight

lead: Renegade knights are knights devoted to serving the evil sorceress Morgan Le Faye. They imprisoned the Knights of the Round Table and Merlin during King's Ransom. They can be accessed by taking the crate behind the candle shop in Catherby after the quest Merlin's Crystal.

label: Rentos

label: Repair kits
title: Repair kits
lead:
Repair kits are used to repair boats if they take damage from any source. They can be used while aboard a boat, including while at the Shipyard. Crewmates may also repair the ship using the repair kits stored in the ship's cargo hold. They provide an increased heal of their deckhandiness level − 1, which is added to the repair kit’s base healing. Commanding a crewmate to repair the ship does not give the player any attack delay.

Players can use the Construction skill to create repair kits. Depending on the tier of kit, they can be made 2–3 at a time using 5 swamp paste, 1–2 of the appropriate tier of plank, and 5–10 of the appropriate tier of nails. Wooden repair kits can be crafted without a hammer or saw by using the items on each other from the inventory; the rest can only be crafted from a Shipwrights' Workbench, and thus require a hammer and saw.

label: Repaired leak
title: Repaired leak
lead: Repaired leaks are found all the way along the sides of the hull of the Fishing Trawler. When the hole leaks, a swamp paste can be used on the hole to repair it, so that it is again a repaired leak.

label: Restless ghost
title: Restless ghost
lead: The restless ghost is the ghost main character of The Restless Ghost quest. Talking to him requires a ghostspeak amulet obtained from Father Urhney, who lives in a shack on the other side of the Lumbridge Swamp. He will say that a warlock stole his skull from the coffin. The ghost's skull is on an altar in the basement of the Wizards' Tower. Upon returning his skull to coffin, he will thank the player and disappear into the River Lum. Should the player see the ghost after that, he will not be interested in talking.

label: Restore potion
title: Restore potion
lead:
A restore potion is a potion made by using red spiders' eggs on a harralander potion (unf), requiring 22 Herblore, yielding a restore potion(3) and 62.5 Herblore experience. A dose of restore potion restores levels of temporarily reduced stats in Attack, Strength, Defence, Ranged, and Magic equal to 10 + 30% of the related maximum level, rounded down, for each skill. It does not restore Prayer points or any other skill that is not listed like a super restore. Restore potions will not boost any skill above its base level, even if the listed restore is greater than the current reduction.

After partial completion of the In Aid of the Myreque quest, garlic can be added to a restore potion(3), requiring 22 Herblore, yielding a Guthix balance (unf) and 25 Herblore experience.

label: Resurrection spells
title: Resurrection spells
lead:
Resurrection spells are a category of spells in the Arceuus spellbook. Casting these spells requires having the book of the dead equipped or in the player's inventory (which is obtained upon completion of A Kingdom Divided), and they cost prayer points in addition to runes.

Each spell summons a thrall that attacks the same target that the player is attacking for a certain amount of time ( 0.6 * MagicLevel seconds). Players can only summon one thrall at a time which cannot attack other players. Thralls have an attack speed of 4 (attacking every 2.4 seconds), cannot be damaged, and ignore accuracy checks when attacking.

label: retaliation
title: retaliation
lead: Retaliation refers to the behaviours of players and various monsters in Old School RuneScape when attacked by players or other monsters.

label: retreat
title: retreat
lead: Retreat or retreating, is a tactic that some monsters implement when their Hitpoints falls below a certain level, at which point they try to run away. This behaviour makes safespotting less than ideal for these monsters. Most monsters will also retreat if you walk out of their roaming area and attack them with a long-ranged weapon, even if they otherwise wouldn't retreat at a certain amount of health.

label: Revenants
title: Revenants
lead:
Revenants are the ghostly versions of creatures slain during the God Wars found in the Revenant Caves within the Wilderness in levels 19 to 40. They are capable of hitting high and accurately for their combat levels, although most of the damage can be mitigated with a charged bracelet of ethereum. As the Revenant Caves location is members-only, all revenants are members-only creatures.

Revenants have a fairly generous drop table, but as they are in the Wilderness, the player is always at risk of getting killed by other players. Due to the revenants' lucrativeness, player killers are common. The caves they inhabit are singles-plus combat, where PvP situations take priority over PvM: a player in combat with a revenant can be attacked by another player.

label: Revenants/Strategies
title: Revenants/Strategies
lead:
Revenants are monsters that can be found in the Revenant Caves, which are located in singles-plus combat Wilderness. They have generous drop tables, consisting of valuable rewards, and are found within level 17-40 Wilderness in the Revenant Caves.

: The entire area counts as the Wilderness. Players will be able to attack you here and the area is a rather popular one to do so.

The player can possess unlimited amounts of reward caskets up to the stack limit. Players are eligible to receive more clue scrolls regardless of how many reward caskets are in the player's possession. In other words, caskets don't count towards the scroll box capacity.

label: Rift guardian (combatant)
title: Rift guardian (combatant)
lead: Rift guardians is a collective term used to describe the creatable NPCs inside the Guardians of the Rift minigame. With a chisel and a weak, medium, strong or overcharged cell a player may create a Rift guardian by clicking either the catalytic or elemental essence piles inside the minigame, to produce either a catalytic or an elemental guardian respectively, whether the resulting guardian is weak, medium, strong or overcharged depends on the type of cell consumed. Once created, guardians will walk toward the barriers in front of the great guardian to attack abyssal creatures.

label: Right eye patch
title: Right eye patch
lead:
A right eye patch is an item commonly worn by pirates, and can be obtained as a drop from them. An eye patch can be bought from the Fancy Dress Shop or Trader Stan's Trading Post. When equipped, the eye patch takes place in the head slot, which means players may not wear a helmet or any other headgear at the same time.

Players who have completed Cabin Fever can pay Patchy 500 coins to sew together an eye patch and pirate bandana to create a bandana eyepatch. Players can also bring Patchy an eye patch and pirate's hat, to create a hat eyepatch, or a big pirate hat and eye patch to create a pirate hat & patch. It is also possible to ask Patchy to combine this item with a left eye patch to create a double eye patch. A book o' piracy is not required.

label: Righteousness
title: Righteousness

label: Rimmington
title: Rimmington
lead: Rimmington is a small village in south-west Asgarnia. In addition to playing a role in several quests, the village is popular for its player-owned house portal, which players use to train Prayer by un-noting bones with Phials and then using them on a gilded altar.

label: Rimmington church
title: Rimmington church
lead:
The Rimmington church, often called the Port Sarim church due to its proximity to the Port Sarim jail, is a church visited by the residents of Rimmington. There is a small graveyard attached to the church.

The church is very small, with one altar and four pews. It isn't known who runs the church; it appears completely abandoned, but there are lit candles inside. Father Urhney may be partially responsible for the church, as he keeps the key to the church's crypt.

label: Rimmington General Store
title: Rimmington General Store
lead: The Rimmington General Store is a general store in Rimmington. It is run by the shop keeper and his assistant. The shop is most notable for being the location of Phials, who is often used in conjunction with the nearby POH portal for fast Construction and Prayer training.

label: Rimmington mine
title: Rimmington mine
lead:
The Rimmington mine is located north-east of Rimmington, west of Port Sarim and south-west of Falador. The mine is a huge pit about as large as the town of Rimmington itself. Its major advantage is that it has no aggressive monsters. The mine contains 2 tin rocks, 5 copper rocks, 6 iron rocks, 2 clay rocks, and 2 gold rocks.

Many non-members use the gold rocks here, as they are the best way to mine gold ore until access to the Crafting Guild is acquired. Many members also use the clay rocks in this mine as a quick way to train Construction, by having their player-owned houses just down the road in Rimmington. This makes it a good way to get soft clay for furniture, as there is a well in Rimmington. Players can bank their ore in Falador or at the bank deposit box in Port Sarim.

label: Rimor
title: Rimor
lead:
Rimor may refer to one of the following:

*Captain Rimor, a high ranking Shayzien officer
*Phileas Rimor, a retired Shayzien soldier
*Magnus Rimor, ancestor of Phileas and Shayzien captain
*Vesta Rimor, a Shayzien lieutenant
*Paidi Rimor , a Shayzien captain

label: ring
title: ring
lead: A ring is a piece of jewellery worn in the ring slot of the Worn Equipment tab.

label: Ring mould
title: Ring mould
lead: A ring mould allows a player to make rings through the Crafting skill out of gold bars and possibly gems by using them on a furnace. It can be bought at various crafting shops, and an unlimited amount can also be taken from a tool store 4 in a player-owned house.

label: Ring of dueling
title: Ring of dueling
lead:
The ring of dueling is a teleportation ring that may be made by casting Lvl-2 Enchant on an emerald ring, granting 37 Magic experience. A full ring of dueling will provide 8 teleports before it crumbles away into nothing.

When teleporting using the ring, the message You rub the ring... will be displayed, followed by a message with the number of charges remaining, ex. Your ring of dueling has four uses left. If using the last charge on the ring, the message Your ring of dueling crumbles to dust. will be displayed instead.

label: Ring of forging
title: Ring of forging
lead:
A ring of forging gives smelting iron ore a 100% success rate of creating an iron bar while it is worn. It can be made by casting Lvl-3 Enchant on a ruby ring, or by paying 250 coins with a ruby ring to Murky Matt in the south-east quadrant of the Grand Exchange.

A newly-enchanted ring has 140 charges. Each time the player smelts an iron ore while wearing the ring, one charge is consumed; after all charges are consumed, the ring crumbles to dust. If the player auto-smelts more iron ores than the number of remaining charges, the smelting will stop once the ring crumbles. The number of charges is specific to the player, not the ring, so swapping, dropping, or alching rings before 140 charges are used will not reset the number of smelts the player has left before a ring breaks. Players can right-click a ring of forging to either "check" how many charges remain in it or "break" it and reset the next one they use to its maximum charges.

label: Ring of life
title: Ring of life
lead:
The ring of life is a diamond ring that has been enchanted with Lvl-4 Enchant. While worn, if the wearer is attacked and has 10% or less of their Hitpoints remaining, the ring automatically teleports the wearer to their respawn point. The ring crumbles to dust after one use. A Defence cape can be worn for the same effect, which does not destroy itself on activation. An Escape crystal can be configured to provide the same effect and more.

The ring does not guarantee total safety, as a player wearing one will still die if they are hit from above 10% of their maximum Hitpoints to zero (for example, being hit 15 while at 15 hitpoints), and it will not cure poison. Self-inflicted damage, such as guzzling a dwarven rock cake or using a locator orb, can also activate the effect. If it is worn along with a phoenix necklace, the necklace effect will trigger first. In PvP, the Tele Block spell will prevent a player's ring of life from activating.

label: Ring of recoil
title: Ring of recoil
lead:
A ring of recoil is created by using Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire ring. When worn, 10% + 1 of the damage received by the player (rounded down) is dealt to the attacker - the attacking entity must cause damage before the recoil effect takes place. This effect applies to both players and NPCs. The ring of recoil is capable of dealing up to 40 hitpoints of damage before shattering.

To see the remaining damage the ring can deal, the player can check it, while equipped, in the Worn Equipment interface. The amount of damage left is kept track of for each player, not each ring; thus, a newly-equipped ring will have the same number of charges remaining as any other ring the player wears. If the player wishes to obtain a ring with 40 charges remaining, the player must use any ring of recoil completely until it shatters, or use the right-click "Break" option on a ring while in the inventory.

label: Ring of wealth
title: Ring of wealth
lead:
The ring of wealth is a dragonstone ring that has been enchanted by the Lvl-5 Enchant spell. Like other enchanted dragonstone jewellery, it can be charged to provide teleports. Unlike the other pieces, the ring can only be charged by the Fountain of Rune. Wearing this ring (whether charged or not) while killing monsters will automatically pick up coins, Tokkul, or numulites dropped by monsters. This effect can be toggled off in the right-click menu when held in the inventory. When worn it also removes the chance to receive a "nothing" drop when accessing the rare drop table and gem drop table. See [[#Rare drop enhancement|below]] for more information about this feature.

The price difference between a fully charged ring and an uncharged ring is , so each charge costs about .

label: Ring slot table
title: Ring slot table
lead: Click a column header icon to sort the table by that column. Use SHIFT click to sort by multiple columns.

label: Ripper Demon
title: Ripper Demon
lead:
Ripper demons are a particularly nasty kind of demon. They are former humans or humanoids taken over by a parasitic demonic force which warps their bodies, making their skin appear as if they are wrapped in bloody bandages, and giving them long, razor-sharp claws, which are their namesake. They feed on meat and pain, and therefore tear their enemies and prey mercilessly apart in a gruesome manner, torturing them before devouring them, as this "adds flavour" to their meat.

During the Second Age, they were in the service of Zaros, although their murderous nature and instincts meant they needed to have keepers to keep them under control. After Zaros' fall at the hands of Zamorak, a loyal Zarosian named Corveth led a pack of ripper demons to hunt down the Dragon rider Ablenkian, whom she had deemed a traitor to Zaros, after slaying his dragon mount, Hekala, although Ablenkian was one of the Dragon riders who had remained loyal. Ripper demons haven't been documented since then, and it is unknown if there are any still remaining on Gielinor or elsewhere.

label: Rise of the Red Axe
title: Rise of the Red Axe
lead: The Rise of the Red Axe is a series of quests centring around The Red Axe's devious plans to take over Keldagrim.

label: Rising Sun Inn
title: Rising Sun Inn
lead:
The Rising Sun Inn can be found on the west end of Falador, across from the bank. The bar is run by three barmaids: Kaylee, Emily, and Tina. All three barmaids will sell any player a wizard's mind bomb, dwarven stout, or Asgarnian ale. This bar does not sell ordinary beer. It does, however, offer the unusual service of buying back (noted or unnoted) empty beer glasses for 2 coins each.

This bar is also a stop on the miniquest, Alfred Grimhand's Barcrawl, and is involved in the quests Below Ice Mountain and Recipe for Disaster. It is also the place where many players obtain a wizard's mind bomb for the Dragon Slayer I quest. On the top floor of the bar you can find Tina and a drunken man, who has some mildly amusing dialogue.

label: Ritchard Haring
title: Ritchard Haring
lead: Ritchard Haring was a citizen of Varrock in the year 160. According to the Varrock Census, Haring was a dietician. He does not appear in-game.

label: Ritual of Rejuvenation
title: Ritual of Rejuvenation
lead: The Ritual of Rejuvenation (also referred to as the Ritual of the Mahjarrat ) is a mysterious Mahjarrat ceremony referenced across multiple quests. It is implied that the next Ritual of Rejuvenation will be a central part of a future quest, as the celestial alignment once again approaches and tensions among the remaining Mahjarrat rise.

label: river
title: river
lead: Rivers are geographical features in Gielinor that flow water from one place to another. They serve many purposes, including transportation via canoes, and a variety of fly fishing spots. Rivers are often the borders between different regions of Gielinor, and play vital roles in some quests. There are sometimes Agility shortcuts like stepping stones and log balances that can be used to cross the rivers.

label: River (Waterfall Dungeon)
title: River (Waterfall Dungeon)
lead:
River is scenery found at the Baxtorian Falls and forms a small portion of the River Dougne. It can be accessed by boarding the log raft behind Almera's house. The river has an option to "swim", which will cause the player to attempt to swim to the small island further down the river. However, this will always fail and the player will be washed away. Instead, the proper way to reach the next island is to use a rope on the rock downstream.

Attempting to swim in the river will print the message "You swim out into the water..." followed by "...but the current is too strong, washing you downstream.". The player will wash up on the shore some distance to the south.

label: River Dougne
title: River Dougne
lead:
The River Dougne ( ) is the longest river in Gielinor.

The river begins at the Baxtorian Falls and runs south-east through Kandarin. It passes through Ardougne, turning west to pass through Castle Wars before draining into the Shrouded Ocean east of the Poison Waste.

label: River Lum
title: River Lum
lead: The River Lum is a river flowing through mostly Misthalin and the Wilderness, moving north-to-south. It is the second longest river in Gielinor. Its source is in the Wilderness. It runs as an underground stream until it briefly emerges at the Ferox Enclave, before it reemerges just north of the Wilderness border. It filters through the Lum Lagoon and Lumbridge Basin into the Ardent Ocean on the Misthalin-Kharidian border. The town of Lumbridge is named after the river.

label: river Salve
title: river Salve
lead: The River Salve is a river marking the border between Misthalin and Morytania. The river was blessed by the seven priestly warriors at the end of the Misthalin - Morytania War during the Fourth Age. Some legends claim it was blessed by Saradomin himself, making it a holy barrier between the two kingdoms which, according to legend, will not allow any evil from Morytania to cross its banks. Through unknown means, the blessing was bypassed by several werewolves during the Darkness of Hallowvale quest.

label: River troll (random event)
title: River troll (random event)
lead:
River trolls were a random event that used to appear when attempting to fish. On appearance, it would say . As with similar guardian random events, the river troll's combat level and stats scaled with the player's combat level, as well as only being attackable by the targeted player.

They were removed from the game with the random event update in 2014. Similar River trolls can now be found in the Enchanted Valley.

label: Riverside
title: Riverside
lead: Riverside is a music track that is unlocked to the west of Tyras Camp.

label: Roachey
title: Roachey
lead: Roachey is the Fishing Guild Shop owner. He sells some types of fish and fishing gear. The guild requires 68 Fishing to enter.

label: Roavar
title: Roavar
lead:
Roavar is a werewolf who owns the Hair of the Dog tavern in Canifis, the Village's tavern and community centre. In the bar they sell moonlight mead and pickled brain, the latter being an item needed during the Creature of Fenkenstrain quest.

If you talk with him, you will have the option to either buy a drink, hear a story, or hear some gossip about various things. You can ask him about Canifis, about Morytania, about some of the shopkeepers, or about Paterdomus. From this you can discover many things, such as the average age of werewolves (Roavar is over 400 and he is not considered an "old" werewolf), and that werewolves like serving Lord Drakan, unlike much of the populace. If you right-click him, then select Trade, he takes 5 coins from you and gives you moonlight mead, an alcoholic beverage.

label: Rob law
title: Rob law
lead: Rob Law (also known as Rab or Moderator, not to be confused with Mod Erator) was one of the few people who helped develop RuneScape before its public release in 2001. Starting as one of four alpha testers, he playtested updates made to the game beginning in February 2000. In October 2000 he started writing RuneScript himself and developed four quests for the game. He worked closely with Andrew Gower as an in game moderator, listed in the credits of the 2001 RuneScape Beta for additional quest design and also part of the 2002 Jagex Team as Freelance staff for Quest design.

label: Robes
title: Robes
lead: There are many different types of robes in Old School RuneScape. Many of them are members-only. Most also give a prayer bonus.

label: Robes of darkness
title: Robes of darkness
lead:
Robes of darkness are a set of magic robes. To wear these robes the player must have at least 20 Defence and 40 Magic. To obtain robes of darkness the player can either complete a master Treasure Trail or buy them from another player.

The pieces have the same stats as the corresponding mystic counterparts. The robes are aligned with Zaros, allowing the wearer protection while in the Ancient Prison located in the God Wars Dungeon.

label: Robes of Ruin
title: Robes of Ruin
lead:
The Robes of Ruin is a reward received from completing the Crack the Clue III event. Like the Crack the Clue II event, this set is available to free-to-play players.

The set consists of the following:

label: Robin hood hat
title: Robin hood hat
lead:
The Robin hood hat is an item worn in headgear slot, requiring level 40 Ranged. It is part of the ranger kit, and can be obtained as a reward from hard Treasure Trails. This item provides the fifth best-in-slot Ranged attack bonus for headgear, at +8.

The Robin hood hat has the highest Ranged attack bonus for headgear that has no Defence requirement, making it popular among 1 Defence pures.

label: Rock
title: Rock
lead: Rock or rocks may refer to any of the following:

label: Rock (elemental)
title: Rock (elemental)
lead:
Rocks are received when killing earth elementals, mining rocks in the Feldip Hills, smashing boulders in the Shaman Caves, or picked up from the ground after failing some of the first traps in the Underground Pass and dropping into a pit. The tool leprechaun by the Troll Stronghold herb patch also sells them.

Rocks are mainly used in the quest Recipe for Disaster when freeing Skrach Uglogwee, where they are used for jubbly hunting. It can be also used to turn an ore-attuned rock golem pet back into its original state.

label: Rock (limestone)
title: Rock (limestone)
lead:
Rocks are items created when a chisel is used on a piece of limestone in an attempt to craft a limestone brick unsuccessfully. 12 Crafting is required to do so, but there is a chance to fail. Failing to craft a limestone brick yields 1.5 experience. Players stop failing at level 40 Crafting.

Rocks can also sometimes be found inside barrels in the Shaman Caves.

label: Rock (The Tourist Trap)
title: Rock (The Tourist Trap)
lead: Rocks are items that can be mined only from Rocks during the Tourist Trap quest yielding 1 mining exp. If caught by the guards while in the Desert Mining Camp mine, players will be sent to the jail, where they have to mine 15 rocks to leave. Upon completing the quest, players will no longer be sent to the jail mine.

label: Rock (Troll)
title: Rock (Troll)
lead:
Rock is the strongest troll on Death Plateau. He possesses a higher max hit and attacks 2 ticks faster than Stick, who spawns next to him.

Since he only attacks with melee, Protect from Melee is recommended, as he can hit up to 30 without it. Like the other named trolls on the plateau, such as Stick, Pee Hat, and Kraka, he may drop a Rune warhammer or Granite shield.

label: rock (volencia moss)
title: rock (volencia moss)
lead:
The rocks are a scenery object found within the Karamja Jungle mine located north of Shilo Village. Players can search the rocks to find a grimy volencia moss, which is primarily used during the Jungle Potion quest. Players may also require a volencia moss as one of the random items requested by Malignius Mortifer during the Fairytale I - Growing Pains quest.

After being searched, the rock becomes searchable again after 60 seconds.

label: Rock (Waterfall Dungeon)
title: Rock (Waterfall Dungeon)
lead:
A rock is located on a small island above the Baxtorian Falls. The rock is used to safely swim down the River Dougne in order to reach the Waterfall Dungeon during the Waterfall Quest.

In order to reach the dungeon, the player must use a rope on the rock. There is an option to "swim to" the rock, but this will always fail and the player will be swept down the river and wash up downstream.

label: Rock cake
title: Rock cake
lead:
A rock cake is a strange ogre delicacy. It is a cake made of stone. Players cannot buy rock cakes from the ogres. Instead, they are stolen from the market stall in the ogre town of Gu'Tanoth. Stealing a rock cake requires a Thieving level of 15 and yields 6.5 Thieving experience.

Rock cakes cannot be gained until the relevant part of the Watchtower quest. A rock cake is required as a bribe in order to access the central parts of the Gu'Tanoth, which is necessary during the Watchtower quest. The player must give a rock cake to an ogre guard in order to be allowed to climb over a rampart that blocks the way to a rope bridge.

label: Rock golem (monster)
title: Rock golem (monster)
lead:
Rock golems can be found in the Enchanted Valley, accessible only by use of the fairy ring . They appear when the player attempts to mine a rock, and will use a ranged attack; Protect from Missiles will negate all damage.

Before the random event update in 2014, the rock golem used to appear randomly when Mining. Upon appearing, it would say . As with similar guardian random events, the rock golem's combat level and stats scaled with the player's combat level, as well as only being attackable by the targeted player.

label: Rock of Dalgroth
title: Rock of Dalgroth
lead:
The mysterious Rock of Dalgroth stands in the middle of the Ogre Enclave. It is named after the ogre warrior Dalgroth. Here players can mine the fourth crystal needed in the Watchtower quest. The enclave is filled with high levelled blue dragons, greater demons, and ogres, so players must be cautious while inside.

In the quest, players must bring a pickaxe and a potion used to kill the ogre shamans, in order to mine the rock. The rock can also be prospected to check for ore, however all that appears on screen is "The rock contains a crystal!" (before completing the Watchtower quest) or "The rock has a gap in which the crystal used to sit." (after the Watchtower quest). After the quest has been completed, the rock no longer serves any purpose.

label: Rock pick
title: Rock pick
lead: A rock pick is needed to dig for items in the Level 2 Digs in the Digsite and to clean finds at the Varrock Museum. They can be found at the Exam Centre in a cupboard on the northern wall of the same room with Terry Balando or on the tool rack on the southern wall of the roped-off archaeology area in the museum. The rock pick cannot be equipped nor can it be used as a pickaxe for Mining.

label: Rock sample
title: Rock sample
lead:
Rock samples were items originally obtained during The Dig Site. Players were required to find three rock samples and give them to the Students, who in return would provide the correct answers to the Digsite exam.

* The first sample could be obtained by pickpocketing Digsite workmen
* The second sample could be found while panning
* The third sample could be found searching some bushes

label: Rock Skin
title: Rock Skin
lead:
Rock Skin is a prayer unlocked at level 10 Prayer. Rock Skin increases the player's Defence by 10%.

Like all other stat-affecting prayers, it cannot be used in conjunction with another prayer that increases the player's Defence level, such as Steel Skin, with the notable exceptions of Deadeye and Mystic Vigour which allow for simultaneous use.

label: rock-shell armour
title: rock-shell armour
lead:
Rock-shell armour (also known as Rockshell armour) is Fremennik armour for warriors that can only be made by going to Waterbirth Island or the Catacombs of Kourend, or bought. Additionally, parts of this armour can be dropped by Dagannoth Rex. This set of armour cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

Excluding the gloves and boots, the armour shares the same bonuses as rune equipment with slightly higher ranged attack bonus, requiring a Defence level of 40 to wear as well. While wearing the full set of armour (boots and gloves are not needed), the title of "Rockcrusher" is added to the Fremennik name of the player when being addressed by other Fremennik. Since this armour can only be worn after completing The Fremennik Trials quest, players are advised not to buy it unless they have completed the quest, or plan to do so soon.

label: Rockery
title: Rockery
lead: Rockery is scenery found in Falador Park and near Edmond's house in East Ardougne. It has no interaction options and is purely decorative.

label: Rocking chair (interface item)
title: Rocking chair (interface item)
lead:
The Rocking chair is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Rocking chair.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Rocking chair (scenery)
title: Rocking chair (scenery)
lead:
Rocking chairs are common decorative scenery found in many locations across Gielinor. The rocking chair's design is very similar to the common chair but with two curved bands affixed to the bottom, enabling would-be occupants to rock back and forth. Rocking chairs on Fred's farm and in the Farming Guild have solid backs, but the rest do not.

Some rocking chairs are purely decorative and cannot be examined; none can be interacted with.

label: Rocking Out
title: Rocking Out
lead:

Rocking Out is a quest originally released in RuneScape 2 on 11 June 2008, ten months after the August 2007 archive from which Old School RuneScape was created. Assets from were backported into Old School RuneScape and exist in the June 2025 Sailing Beta cache but the content was not accessible.

label: Rockpile
title: Rockpile
lead: A Rockpile can be found at the start of the cages and the obstacle maze portion of the Underground Pass quest, or the second part of the Underground Pass dungeon. It can be used to return to the previous section of the dungeon.

label: Rocks (adamantite, gas)
title: Rocks (adamantite, gas)
lead:
Adamantite rocks with a gas cloud would occasionally appear as part of the former exploding rock random event. Attempting to mine the rock would cause an explosion, turning the player's pickaxe into a broken pickaxe and dealing a small amount of damage. The broken pickaxe could no longer be used to mine and would have to be repaired by Nurmof in the Dwarven Mine, Bob in Lumbridge, or Brian in Port Sarim.

The exploding rocks were removed on 11 September 2014 as part of the optional randoms update, after it was no longer considered a useful feature for preventing bots. The numerous graphical variants correspond to the historical adamantite rocks that existed until the 21 January 2016 rework that changed all rocks to use the original mining rock model.

label: Rocks (adamantite, historical)
title: Rocks (adamantite, historical)
lead: Adamantite rocks were graphical variants of regular adamantite rocks for Mining that were formerly used across many mining sites. The graphical variants were removed in a 2016 update after a poll passed to revert the appearance of all rocks to how they originally appeared between 2003 and early 2007.

label: Rocks (Climbing boots)
title: Rocks (Climbing boots)
lead:
The rocks are Agility shortcut in the area north of Death Plateau and on Trollheim, requiring 15 Agility to use. They allow players to reach the troll arena from the Death Plateau, as well as being part of the series of shortcuts available on Trollheim. Failing this shortcut deals 1-3 damage.

They can only be used after starting Troll Stronghold. The westernmost and southernmost rocks require climbing boots to be worn when attempting to pass them, when going in the direction towards Troll Stronghold. When going down the mountains (i.e. heading outside of troll country), no climbing boots need to be worn. The other locations of these rocks do not require climbing boots to be worn.

The graphical variants were removed in a 2016 update after a poll passed to revert the appearance of all rocks to how they originally appeared between 2003 and early 2007.

label: Rocks (Death Plateau)
title: Rocks (Death Plateau)
lead: The rocks are an obstacle allowing players to reach the Death Plateau without being attacked by Thrower Trolls. Climbing these rocks in either direction requires climbing boots to be worn.

label: Rocks (gem, gas)
title: Rocks (gem, gas)
lead:
Gem rocks with a gas cloud would occasionally appear as part of the former exploding rock random event. Attempting to mine the rock would cause an explosion, turning the player's pickaxe into a broken pickaxe and dealing a small amount of damage. The broken pickaxe could no longer be used to mine and would have to be repaired by Nurmof in the Dwarven Mine, Bob in Lumbridge, or Brian in Port Sarim.

The exploding rocks were removed on 11 September 2014 as part of the optional randoms update, after it was no longer considered a useful feature for preventing bots. The numerous graphical variants correspond to the historical gem rocks that existed until the 21 January 2016 rework that changed all rocks to use the original mining rock model.

title: Rocky Ledge
lead:
Rocky ledges and rocks are found on the elevated part at the entrance of the Viyeldi caves. They must be climbed over to proceed further into the caves. Depending on their Agility level, the player can fail to cross the obstacle unharmed, leading to one of the following outcomes:
#The fall is avoided by grabbing a handhold at the last second, incurring a small amount of damage and draining Agility by some levels.

##All damage is avoided, owing to one's Agility.
##A light amount of damage is taken, equal to around 10% of the player's Hitpoints.
##A major amount of damage is taken, equal to 50% of one's Hitpoints, or up to 49 points of damage at level 99.
