label: Sails (windmill)
title: Sails (windmill)
lead: Sails are animated scenery found on the top floor of most windmills. Canonically, they harness wind energy to power millstones in order to grind flour.

label: salamander
title: salamander
lead:
Salamanders are unique and versatile two-handed weapons that facilitate the training of all combat styles, namely the Ranged, Magic and Strength skills.

Salamanders may be obtained through net trapping and must be fuelled using a variety of herb-tars made with the Herblore skill. The black salamander is commonly used by players with a low budget to kill the Barrows brothers or to safespot Lava dragons. Due to their ability to output multiple types of damage, salamanders also have a niche use in PvP against bot accounts which use auto-prayer macros. They are also able to attack diagonally over some obstacles and corners similar to most ranged or magic attacks, which allows it to be used in melee safespotting without having to flinch or use a halberd. Salamanders can also be used to flinch an enemy by while dealing magic or ranged damage such as the Kalphite Queen's second phase, because spells and other ranged weapons have a delay that makes flinching unsafe.

label: Salarin the twisted
title: Salarin the twisted
lead:
Salarin the twisted is a chaos druid found at the end of the Yanille Agility Dungeon. Reaching his cave requires level 67 Agility; this can be boosted from as low as 62 with a summer pie. Additionally, players will need to bring a blade to cut the webs near the dungeon entrance.

Salarin is one of the two NPCs that drop the sinister key on death, alongside the Chaos Fanatic. This key opens the Sinister chest, located nearby, which rewards the player with a guaranteed noted drop of nine grimy herbs (see below), including a torstol. The key is dropped at a rate of 7.8%, making him a common target for low-level ironmen who can't yet grow the herbs.

label: Salmon
title: Salmon
lead:
Salmon is a type of fish that restores 9 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw salmon on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 25 Cooking and granting 90 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt fish. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Salmon is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 58, or 55 when using the Lumbridge range.

Salmon is one of the fish required by Caleb during the quest Family Crest.

label: Salt
title: Salt
lead:
Salts are minerals able to be mined by players after completion of the Making Friends with My Arm quest. Salts can be found in the salt mine beneath Weiss. There are three types of salts: Te salt, Efh salt, and Urt salt. Within the salt mine players can mine all three types of salt with level 72 Mining.

Basalt can also be mined within the salt mine with level 72 Mining. Basalt can be used with salt to create stony basalt and icy basalt, which can teleport the player to the Troll Stronghold and Weiss, respectively.

label: salvage
title: salvage
lead:
Salvage is acquired by using a salvaging hook on shipwrecks, and in some cases from monster drops. It can be stored in a boat's cargo hold and sorted at salvaging stations to receive various useful drops.

Using a salvaging hook to retrieve salvage gives small amounts of Sailing XP, and sorting salvage at a salvaging station gives about half that amount.

label: salvaging hook
title: salvaging hook
lead:
A salvaging hook is a type of facility that can be installed on player-owned boats. They can be used to salvage shipwrecks, providing Sailing experience and salvage that can be placed in the ship's cargo hold. In general, increasing the tier of hook increases the chance of success when salvaging, but higher tiers require higher Sailing and Construction levels to build and higher deckhandiness requirements for crewmates to use the hooks.

Crewmates with the appropriate Deckhandiness level can be assigned to operate the salvaging hook, as long as the player has the required Sailing level. As such, players who used temporary boosts to build it must maintain the Sailing boost when a crewmate or themselves are using it.

label: Salve
title: Salve
lead:
Salve may refer to any of the following:
*River Salve, marks the border between Misthalin and Morytania
**Salve Graveyard is bordered to the west by the river, with Canifis a short way to the east. 
***Salve Graveyard Teleport, provides quick access to the Salve Graveyard, and is popular for its nearby Fairy rings
***Salve Graveyard Portal, provides quick access to the Salve Graveyard from a Player-owned house
*Salve shard, a crystal cut from deep inside the Haunted Mine
*Salve amulet, provides a boost in combat while attacking undead monsters
**Salve amulet (e), provides a boost in combat while attacking undead monsters
**Salve amulet(i), provides a boost in combat while attacking undead monsters
**Salve amulet(ei), provides a boost in combat while attacking undead monsters
*Shipwreck salvaging, a low-intensity gathering activity in Sailing

label: Salve Graveyard
title: Salve Graveyard
lead: The Salve Graveyard is located east of the River Salve and north of Mort Myre Swamp. The graveyard contains six dead trees, various gravestones, and a number of ghouls. Players can use the Salve Graveyard Teleport spell or fairy ring code to quickly reach the graveyard.

label: Salve Island
title: Salve Island
lead:
An island could originally be found in the middle of the River Salve. It was added with the release of The Dig Site in 2003. It was possibly added as a placeholder to ensure there was terrain on the other side of the river, as otherwise the player would have appeared to be panning for gold in the ocean.

With the release of RuneScape 2, the island was expanded to the east.

label: Sam (disambiguation)
title: Sam (disambiguation)

*Sam, a customer at the Arceuus Library
*Sam (merchant), sells team capes
*Sam (barmaid), found at the entrance to the Burthorpe Games Room

label: Samael Leynes
title: Samael Leynes
lead:
, depicted in ]]
Samael Leynes is the author of Conversations with a Mage, a book that containing Samael's interview with an elderly wizard who had lived prior to the discovery of runes.

Samael does not appear in-game, and is only mentioned in of his book in Lores and Histories.

label: Sammy Servil
title: Sammy Servil
lead: Sammy Servil is the only son of Lady Servil and Justin Servil, two minor nobles of Kandarin. During the Fight Arena quest, he is kidnapped by the forces of General Khazard and imprisoned in the Fight Arena; the player must rescue him during the quest by fighting in the arena.

label: Samurai armour
title: Samurai armour
lead:
Samurai armour can be obtained as a master clue scroll reward from Treasure Trails.

Equipping the samurai outfit requires level 35 in Defence. It has bonuses comparable to adamant armour, but with positive magic defence and reduced weight.

label: San Tojalon
title: San Tojalon
lead: San Tojalon is one of the three long-dead warriors alongside Irvig Senay and Ranalph Devere that are required to be killed to collect a piece of the heart crystal for the Legends' Quest. He is hostile until you kill him to obtain the chunk of crystal, but you can still attack him afterwards and he will fight back. He attacks with melee.

label: Sand (pile)
title: Sand (pile)
lead:
Sand is a piece of interactable scenery. Players are able to fill up buckets with the sand, making buckets of sand. Due to the distance from the bank, collecting buckets of sand from sand piles is inefficient and not suggested over using available sand pits. Using the sand's "Look" option will give the player a message telling them how large the pile is, such as This looks like a large pile of sand.

Buckets cannot be filled with sand on free-to-play worlds.

label: Sand pit
title: Sand pit
lead:
Sand pits are mostly used in glassblowing to train Crafting. Sand pits are located in Entrana, Yanille, Rellekka, Dorgesh-Kaan, Prifddinas, Zanaris, Sunset Coast, and The Great Conch.

Molten glass that can be blown with Glassblowing pipe is made by using Soda ash and a bucket of sand with a Furnace. Buckets of sand can be obtained simply by using an empty bucket on a sand pit. Soda ash can be obtained by burning Seaweed on a Range or a fire.

label: Sandwich lady outfit
title: Sandwich lady outfit
lead: The sandwich lady outfit is the outfit of the sandwich lady, a random event that supplies you with food if you select the right one. It is a rare reward from beginner clue scroll treasure trails, and the outfit is purely cosmetic with no bonuses.

label: Sanfew
title: Sanfew
lead: Sanfew is the leader of the druids and resides in Taverley, on the of Jatix's Herblore Shop. He plays a part in several quests, including Druidic Ritual, Eadgar's Ruse, and One Small Favour. He is also the inventor of the Sanfew serum.

label: Sanguine
title: Sanguine
lead: Sanguine may refer to:

label: Sanguine torva armour
title: Sanguine torva armour
lead:
Sanguine torva armour is a cosmetic upgrade of regular torva armour that can be created by using the ancient blood ornament kit and 20,000 blood runes on each piece of armour. The ornament kit is awarded after the player defeats the awakened versions of Vardorvis, The Leviathan, The Whisperer and Duke Sucellus at least once.

The kit has unlimited uses, though converting a piece of torva armour into its sanguine variant requires an additional 20,000 blood runes.

label: Sanity
title: Sanity
lead:
Sanity is a game mechanic occurring at the Shadow Realm from the Lassar Undercity. The sanity will lower as long as the player prolongs in the Shadow Realm or by getting hit from the Lost Soul and The Whisperer attacks, indicated by a hitsplat ( ). When the sanity meter depletes to 0, the player will receive the message The darkness of the Shadow Realm begins to consume your mind! and will begin to take damage every 2 ticks; this starts at 5 damage, and doubles afterwards; 10 damage at 4 ticks, 20 at 6, 40 at 8, 80 at 10. The sixth occurrence of damage will instantly kill the player, as it would deal 160 damage.

The sanity loss can either be prevented by standing next to the shadow blocker or mitigated by using the revitalising idol. During the The Whisperer battle, sanity is restored when outside the Shadow Realm (in normal mode), killing the cyan Lost Souls during her souls mechanic and successfully stopping her shadow seeds mechanic.

label: Santa hat
title: Santa hat
lead: Santa hats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

label: Santa outfit
title: Santa outfit
lead:
The Santa outfit is a holiday reward received from completing a Christmas event from 2014 onwards. The costume gives no bonus to any stats. Its appearance changes depending on the player's body type.

If lost or destroyed, the outfit can be reclaimed from Diango in Draynor Village. In addition, all of the costume items may be stored in the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: Sap
title: Sap
lead:
Sap may refer to:

*Bucket of sap
*Saplings
*Super attack potion

label: sapling
title: sapling
lead:
A sapling is a tree seedling that has grown sufficiently to be planted in a tree patch. Players must have the appropriate Farming level to plant the sapling in a tree patch, which can be aided by temporary boosts. Players may apply compost, supercompost, or ultracompost to a tree patch before planting the sapling.

Despite not being farming produce, Tool leprechauns will note saplings. Players should be careful when planting saplings as otherwise they will have to visit a bank to unnote them.

label: Sapphire
title: Sapphire
lead: Sapphires are precious gems used mainly in Crafting. They can be cut from uncut sapphires with a chisel at level 20 Crafting, yielding 50 experience.

label: Sapphire amulet
title: Sapphire amulet
lead:
A sapphire amulet can be created with 24 Crafting by using a gold bar on a furnace while also carrying a cut sapphire and an amulet mould. This will grant 65 Crafting experience and create a sapphire amulet (u), which may not be worn. A ball of wool must be used on the unstrung amulet to complete it, which gives 4 Crafting experience.

Sapphire amulets provide no bonuses, but casting Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire amulet will turn it into an amulet of magic.

label: Sapphire amulet (u)
title: Sapphire amulet (u)
lead: A sapphire amulet (u) can be created with level 24 Crafting by using a gold bar on a furnace while also carrying a cut sapphire and an amulet mould. This will grant 65 Crafting experience. A ball of wool can be used on the unstrung amulet to create a strung sapphire amulet, which can then be enchanted at level 7 Magic using the Lvl-1 Enchant spell to create an amulet of magic.

label: Sapphire glacialis (interface item)
title: Sapphire glacialis (interface item)
lead: The sapphire glacialias is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the Sapphire glacialias. The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Sapphire necklace
title: Sapphire necklace
lead:
The sapphire necklace is made by using a gold bar, a sapphire and a necklace mould on a furnace. This requires a Crafting level of 22 and gives 55 experience when made.

Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim buys at a higher price than High Alchemy, if he has no sapphire necklaces for sale. He will buy the first for 735 coins, compared with the High Alchemy value of 630 coins. However, his price decreases in relation to the amount he has in stock, going below High Alchemy value when his stock goes above five.

label: Sapphire ring
title: Sapphire ring
lead:
The sapphire ring is made by using a gold bar on a furnace while having a sapphire and a ring mould in one's inventory. Making it requires a Crafting level of 20, and gives 40 experience.

Grum's Gold Exchange in Port Sarim buys at better price than High Alchemy, depending on his current stock. If he has no sapphire rings for sale, he buys the first for 630 coins.

label: Saradomin
title: Saradomin
lead: Saradomin (Jagex pronunciation: sa-ra-DOME-in) is the god of order and wisdom and one of the three major gods in Gielinor, alongside Zamorak and Guthix. Little is known about his past, but he has a great many followers; there are far more churches dedicated to Saradomin than any other god.

label: Saradomin armour
title: Saradomin armour
lead:
The Saradomin armour set is a set of melee armour affiliated to the god Saradomin. Pieces of the armour provide identical attack and defence stats as rune armour, except for the kiteshield's ranged attack bonus being -2 (rather than -3), as well as each item having a +1 prayer bonus. Therefore, they require 40 Defence to be worn.

Each piece of the Saradomin armour set can be obtained by completing hard Treasure Trails, and cannot be made
via the Smithing skill.

label: Saradomin blessed dragonhide armour
title: Saradomin blessed dragonhide armour
lead:
The Saradomin blessed d'hide armour is a set of Ranged armour said to be blessed by Saradomin. Every piece requires 70 Ranged and 40 Defence, except for the blessed chaps and blessed bracers, which do not have the Defence requirement. Blessed dragonhide has better defensive stats and the same offensive stats as the corresponding black dragonhide armour with an additional +1 Prayer bonus. Unlike normal dragonhide armour, a coif and boots are also available. Each piece of armour may be obtained as a reward from hard Treasure Trails.

Wearing any piece of Saradomin blessed d'hide armour will make the Saradomin followers unaggressive within the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon.

label: Saradomin cape
title: Saradomin cape
lead:
The Saradomin cape is a reward from Mage Arena I miniquest. To receive the cape, the player must defeat Kolodion in his four guises, then speak to him, step through the nearby sparkling pool, and finally pray at the Statue of Saradomin. Upon praying at the statue, the Saradomin cape will appear next to the player and can be picked up.

The Saradomin cape and the Saradomin staff are required to benefit from the Charge spell, which enables the player to hit up to 50% more damage with the Saradomin Strike spell.

label: Saradomin cloak (disambiguation)
title: Saradomin cloak (disambiguation)
lead:
Saradomin cloak may refer to the following:

* Saradomin cloak - Part of the Saradomin vestment set
* Castlewars cloak (Saradomin) - Bought from Lanthus at the Castle Wars minigame for 10 Castle wars tickets
* Saradomin cloak (Castle Wars) - Worn in the Castle Wars minigame to indicate a player's team

label: Saradomin full helm
title: Saradomin full helm
lead:
The Saradomin full helm is a decorated rune full helm that is affiliated with the god Saradomin. Sharing the same stats as the rune full helm with a +1 prayer bonus, the Saradomin full helm also looks visually similar. Its appearance differs in that the helm features an ornamental white trim around the symbol of Saradomin. The full helm requires 40 Defence to wear and cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Players can obtain a Saradomin full helm as a reward from completing hard Treasure Trails.

Wearing any piece of this armour set will cause followers of Saradomin to become unaggressive upon entering the God Wars Dungeon.

label: Saradomin kiteshield
title: Saradomin kiteshield
lead:
The Saradomin kiteshield is a decorated rune kiteshield that is affiliated with the god Saradomin. Sharing the same stats as the rune kiteshield except for the ranged attack bonus and prayer bonus, the Saradomin kiteshield also looks visually similar. Its appearance differs in that the shield features an ornamental white trim.

The shield requires 40 Defence to wear and cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

label: Saradomin page
title: Saradomin page
lead: Saradomin pages are rewards from Treasure Trails. If a player has all four they can use them to make a Holy book.

label: Saradomin platebody
title: Saradomin platebody
lead:
The Saradomin platebody is a trimmed Rune platebody fashioned to praise Saradomin. It has the same stats as the Rune platebody but provides protection from followers of Saradomin in the God Wars Dungeons as well as a +1 prayer bonus. It requires 40 Defence and the completion of the Dragon Slayer I quest to wear.

It can only be obtained as a reward from hard Treasure Trails, and cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

label: Saradomin platelegs
title: Saradomin platelegs
lead:
The Saradomin platelegs are a decorated version of rune platelegs that are affiliated with the god Saradomin. Sharing the same stats as rune platelegs (with the addition of a +1 prayer bonus), the Saradomin platelegs also look visually similar. Their appearance differs in that they feature an ornamental white trim around the symbol of Saradomin. The platelegs require 40 Defence to wear and cannot be made using the Smithing skill. Players can obtain Saradomin platelegs as a reward from completing hard Treasure Trails.

These platelegs are a constituent of the Saradomin armour set which consists of the following items: Saradomin full helm, Saradomin platebody, Saradomin platelegs or Saradomin plateskirt, and Saradomin kiteshield—all of which are decorative versions of their respective rune armour counterparts. Wearing any piece of this armour set causes followers of Saradomin to become unaggressive to the player.

label: Saradomin shield
title: Saradomin shield
lead:
Saradomin shield may refer to:

*Saradomin d'hide shield
*Saradomin kiteshield
*Steel kiteshield (Saradomin)
*Adamant kiteshield (Saradomin)
*Rune kiteshield (Saradomin)

label: Saradomin staff
title: Saradomin staff
lead:
The Saradomin staff is a god staff that can only be obtained by finishing the Mage Arena minigame. Like the other God staves, this staff requires level 60 Magic to acquire and therefore wield. To get it, the player must defeat Kolodion the mage in all of his forms. Afterwards, they will have to pick a god to worship to receive a cape and the staff corresponding to that god. If the player has already chosen another god, the staff can be purchased from the Chamber Guardian for 80,000 coins.

The staff allows wielders to cast the Saradomin Strike spell, which must be cast 100 times inside the Mage Arena minigame to gain the ability to use it outside of the arena. The spell can deal a maximum of 20 damage. Saradomin Strike lowers the target's Prayer level by one point on each successful cast.

label: Saradomin Strike
title: Saradomin Strike
lead:
Saradomin Strike is a combat spell in the standard spellbook, requiring 60 Magic and the completion of Mage Arena I to cast. In addition, players must also be wielding a Saradomin staff or staff of light; only the staff of light is able to autocast the spell.

Initially, the spell can only be cast within the Mage Arena against the battle mages. Upon casting the spell 100 times (regardless of whether it was a successful hit or not), the spell becomes usable outside the arena.

label: Saradomin symbol (interface item)
title: Saradomin symbol (interface item)
lead:
The Saradomin symbol is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Saradomin symbol.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Saradomin vestment set
title: Saradomin vestment set
lead: The Saradomin vestment set is a members item set of Prayer armour aligned with Saradomin. It is only obtainable by completing easy, medium, and hard Treasure Trails.

label: Saragorgak
title: Saragorgak
lead:
The Saragorgak are a goblin tribe found while doing the Land of the Goblins quest, who wear white goblin mail. Unlike the other tribes found in the temple, they were sold to Saradomin and fought in his name during the God Wars. Despite their subservience to Saradomin in the God Wars, they appear to be worshippers of Bandos in the modern day.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Footsoldiers of Holy Wrath".

label: Sarah (disambiguation)
title: Sarah (disambiguation)
lead:
Sarah may refer to any of the following NPCs:

*Sarah, owner of a Farming shop north of Port Sarim
*Nurse Sarah, an NPC found in West Ardougne
*Sarah, found in Port Piscarilius
*Sarah, an NPC encountered during the Temple Trekking campsite event
*Sarah, a ghost encountered in Port Phasmatys during the Dragon Slayer II quest
*Sarah, a Varrock resident and Mahogany Homes contract
*Saradomin, the god of order, commonly abbreviated as 'Sara'

label: Saranthium
title: Saranthium
lead: Saranthium was a city established somewhere around the 37th and 38th century of the Third Age, that sat upon the ruins of Senntisten, the capital of the Zarosian Empire. It was built by Saradominists for the sole purpose of covering up the remains of Senntisten.

label: Sarcophagus
title: Sarcophagus
lead: A Sarcophagus is . It can mean any of the following in the game:

label: Sardine
title: Sardine
lead: Sardine is a type of fish that restores 4 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw sardine on a fire or cooking range, granting 40 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt sardine. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Sardine is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 38, or 34 when using the Lumbridge range.

label: Sargrita
title: Sargrita
lead:
Sargrita is a vampyre and one of the possible senders of a message to the player if they successfully complete the Theatre of Blood. Sargrita believes that, if anyone would ever beat the Theatre, it would be the player, but still believes that no human can overcome the challenge.

They are only mentioned in the message, and cannot be found anywhere in-game.

label: Sarl Dunegun
title: Sarl Dunegun
lead:
Sarl Dunegun was one of the Seven priestly warriors who died fighting the Morytanian hordes at Silvarea. He came from what is now Edgeville.

He is described in The Sleeping Seven as "A pious yet brutal man. When wielding his mace he led many fighters on skirmishes to keep the evil from spreading and outflanking the group."

label: Satchel
title: Satchel
lead:
Satchel can refer to:
* The satchels dropped by monsters from Creature Creation, which can hold a cake, banana, and triangle sandwich. These satchels are equipped in the shield slot, give no combat bonuses, and enhance the beckon emote.

** (dropped by Jubster)
** (dropped by Unicow)
** (dropped by Frogeel)
** (dropped by Spidine)
** (dropped by Newtroost)

* , used during Monkey Madness II to sabotage the airship construction platform.
* , used during Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire to defend from the Strangled.

label: Sawmill coupon
title: Sawmill coupon
lead:
Sawmill coupon may refer to:
* Sawmill coupon (wood plank), used to cover the cost of making planks at a Sawmill
* Sawmill coupon (oak plank), used to cover the cost of making oak planks at a Sawmill
* Sawmill voucher, a Forestry reward that doubles the amount of planks per log from a Sawmill

label: Sbott
title: Sbott
lead: Sbott is the werewolf tanner on the northern side of Canifis. His shop is marked with the tanning icon ( ). His tannery is more expensive than average, charging a bit more than double what most other tanners charge to tan a hide. However his shop is very close to the fairy ring in Canifis as well as a bank, so some players find the convenience to be worth the few coins extra cost.

label: Scabarites
title: Scabarites
lead:
Scabarites refer to any of the minions of Scabaras, the scarab-headed Menaphite god of wisdom and isolation. They are fairly strong monsters that can hit rather hard. As they generally share the same dungeon area and have various combat styles, it can be fairly difficult to fight them, even with protection prayers. To receive them as a Slayer assignment, players must have done most of the Contact! quest.

"Minions of Scabaras" are assigned as Slayer tasks only by Nieve and in fairly low numbers (between 30 and 60 when unextended). Scarab swarms are not recommended as they are accurate, hit hard, and are a random spawn chance. However, all scabarites are susceptible to the effects of the keris and keris partisan.

label: Scaffold
title: Scaffold
lead: Scaffolds are bits of decorative scenery, usually found at remote locations or construction sites.

label: Scale
title: Scale
lead: Scale may refer to one of the following:

lead:
minigame, an example of scale theory. Locations depicted in the minigame cannot be visited by the player outside of it, but canonically exist in-universe. This is because Morytania is much larger than it appears to be while playing the game.]]

Scale theory is a term used by Jagex and players to describe the apparent contradiction between the size of Gielinor in-game and its actual canonical size as confirmed by official lore.

label: Scams
title: Scams
lead:
Scamming is the act of stealing money, items or accounts from another player through deception or trickery. Rule 2 of the Old School RuneScape Code of Conduct prohibits the act of scamming which is punishable by a mute or ban if reported.

This page is not a comprehensive list of every scam or lure to ever exist; instead, it acts as a general overview of what to look out for.

label: Scape Cave
title: Scape Cave
lead: Scape Cave is a music track that is unlocked on the cave on Tutorial Island, making it the second track heard by all new players. It can also be heard in Varrock Sewers and parts of Edgeville Dungeon, the basement of the Woodcutting Guild, and Pandemonium Cave.

label: Scape Original
title: Scape Original
lead:
Scape Original is a music track from the early days of RuneScape 2. It was the first login screen music track before being replaced with Scape Main. It is now unlocked automatically by all players upon their first login. It was also the track that played in the Realm of Memories during the 20th and 25th Anniversary events.

This music track is considered to be the "theme song" of RuneScape. Many of RuneScape s other songs make references to it, including Scape Main.

label: Scape Sad
title: Scape Sad
lead:
Scape Sad is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness or during the ending cutscene of Dragon Slayer II. It also plays in Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, the track plays at the Fountain of Rune and at the Demonic Ruins in the Wilderness.

label: Scape Soft
title: Scape Soft
lead:
Scape Soft is a music track that is unlocked in the north-east of Asgarnia, around Ice Mountain or the Monastery or east of Falador. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track and Lightness.

In Classic mode, the track plays in a smaller area just north of Falador.

label: Scape Wild
title: Scape Wild
lead:
Scape Wild is a music track that is unlocked in the Wilderness and also plays in Wilderness Agility Course Dungeon.

In Classic mode, the track plays north of the Chaos Temple, and north of Lava Dragon Isle.

label: Scarab (disambiguation)
title: Scarab (disambiguation)
lead: Scarab may refer to:

label: Scared skavid
title: Scared skavid
lead: The Scared skavids can be found in various places throughout the Skavid caves all around Gu'Tanoth and the Feldip Hills, which the player must go to during the Watchtower quest in order to retrieve one of the Watchtower crystals. In order to get them to cooperate, players must speak with the Scared Skavids in their native language.

label: Scarface Pete
title: Scarface Pete
lead: Scarface Pete is a pirate from the Heroes' Quest, from whom players must steal a candlestick for the Phoenix Gang and Black Arm Gang.

label: Scavenger
title: Scavenger
lead:
Scavengers are a race found exclusively in the Chambers of Xeric. They closely resemble skavids, but are bigger and have slightly different faces.

Currently, the only scavengers in the game are the scavenger beasts and the corrupted scavenger found in the Chambers of Xeric.

label: Scavvo
title: Scavvo
lead: Scavvo runs Scavvo's Rune Store on the of the Champions' Guild. He can be found on the south side of the room. Players can purchase rune plateskirts, rune platelegs, rune maces, rune chainbodies, rune longswords, rune swords, green d'hide vambraces, green d'hide chaps, and coifs from him. Unlike Oziach, Scavvo does not sell the rune platebody or the green d'hide body.

label: Scavvo's Rune Store.
title: Scavvo's Rune Store.
lead:
Scavvo's Rune Store is located on the of the Champions' Guild and operated by Scavvo. This means players will need to acquire 32 quest points before they can access his shop.

The shop is noteworthy because it is the only place for free-to-play players to acquire green dragonhide armour apart from other players. It is also one of the few shops in the game to stock rune armour.

label: scenery
title: scenery
lead:
Scenery refers to the various decorative and natural objects found around the game world such as trees, rocks and plants. Most types of scenery can be examined, and even interacted with in some cases. For example, trees can be cut, ranges and fires can be used to cook raw food, and storage units can be searched.

Some larger scenery will block a player's path (for example, trees and bushes), while others have no colliders and can be walked over (for example, ferns). The scenery you can walk over will prevent you from lighting a tinderbox. Some types of scenery will block the path, but will allow for attacks with projectiles. Many enemies can be 'tricked' by exploiting their pathing and these types of scenery, this is also referred to as safespotting.

label: Sceptre
title: Sceptre
lead:
Sceptre may refer to one of the following:
* Ancient sceptre, an upgraded version of the ancient staff
** Smoke ancient sceptre, the variant upgraded with Smoke quartz
** Shadow ancient sceptre, the variant upgraded with Shadow quartz
** Blood ancient sceptre, the variant upgraded with Blood quartz
** Ice ancient sceptre, the variant upgraded with Ice quartz
* Crystal sceptre, an item used in The Gauntlet
** Corrupted sceptre, the corrupted equivalent
* Lithic sceptre, dropped from the Echo Grotesque Guardians in the Demonic Pacts League.
* Pharaoh's sceptre, found in the Pyramid Plunder minigame whilst looting chests and sarcophagi
* Skull sceptre or skull sceptre (i), available to players constructed from four untradeable pieces dropped by monsters in the Stronghold of Security
** Runed sceptre, the bottom part of the Skull sceptre
* Royal sceptre, a reward from elite Treasure Trails
* Thammaron's sceptre, a magic weapon once owned by Thammaron
** Thammaron's sceptre (a), the autocasting variant
** Accursed sceptre, the upgraded variant
** Accursed sceptre (a), the upgraded, autocasting variant
* Warped sceptre, a powered staff dropped by Warped creatures

Alternatively, it might be a misspelling of the following:
* Aberrant spectre, a Slayer monster
** Abhorrent spectre, the superior version of the aberrant spectre
** Deviant spectre, a stronger version of the aberrant spectre
** Repugnant spectre, the superior version of the deviant spectre

label: scimitar
title: scimitar
lead:
Scimitars are a type of slash weapon that can also be used as a stab weapon, although less effectively. They can deal slightly higher hits than swords, but less than longswords.

Scimitars have exactly the same attack speed as daggers and claws, but provide a higher attack bonus than daggers and yield lower defence bonuses than claws. The combination of high attack and swing speed give the scimitar its large popularity in melee training.

label: Scimitar shops
title: Scimitar shops
lead: Scimitar shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. There are 3 dedicated scimitar shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Scorched earth
title: Scorched earth
lead:
Scorched earth is a scenery object found within and just south of Tai Bwo Wannai. Players can search the scorched earth to find a grimy sito foil, which is primarily used during the Jungle Potion quest.

After being searched, the earth becomes searchable again after 60 seconds.

label: Scoreboard
title: Scoreboard
lead:
A scoreboard shows points and statistics related to competitive activities such as minigames. The term may colloquially refer to a scenery object, an interface, or any entity that performs this function, even if they do not resemble a board. The following scoreboards can be found:

* Colosseum scoreboard
* Scoreboard (Castle Wars)
* Scoreboard (Duel Arena), the legacy scoreboard of the Duel Arena
* Scoreboard (Emir's Arena), the currently useable scoreboard at the Duel Arena
* Scoreboard (Last Man Standing)
* Scoreboard (Soul Wars)
* Scoreboard (TzHaar-Ket-Rak)
* Score board (Pest Control)

label: Scoreboard (Duel Arena)
title: Scoreboard (Duel Arena)
lead: There are two Scoreboards around the Duel Arena. These scoreboards show the last 50 fights that have been fought in the arena.

label: STASH
title: STASH
lead:
STASH (short for "Store Things And Stuff Here") are storage units for emote clue items, saving bank space and time for players who frequent Treasure Trails. While beginner-tier clues can be done in free-to-play, only members can make use of these units as they require use of the Construction skill.

There are a total of constructible STASH units throughout Gielinor. All these locations are initially labelled as "inconspicuous bushes/crates/holes/rocks" and, once built, become usable STASH units. Players can see which units they've already constructed and filled via a S.t.a.s.h chart in the study of a player-owned house, or by reading the noticeboard within Watson's house.

label: Scorpia/Strategies
title: Scorpia/Strategies
lead:
Scorpia is a powerful Wilderness boss capable of poisoning her opponents starting at 20 damage as well as hitting up to 16 with melee. Her lair, located beneath the Scorpion Pit, is filled with many Scorpia's offspring, which use accurate ranged attacks with a max hit of 2 and inflict poison starting at 6 damage.

Once Scorpia reaches 99 health or lower, she will summon two Scorpia's guardians which will continually heal Scorpia when within 3 tiles of her until they are killed or despawned. The guardians will not respawn if killed, and will despawn if they are too far away to heal Scorpia for 15 seconds.

label: Scorpion
title: Scorpion
lead:
Scorpions are monsters historically iconic for inhabiting free-to-play areas, but have been increasingly more widespread in modern updates. They can be dangerous to low level players training Mining.

Scorpions are a relatively weak variety of monster, with the strongest being located in the Stronghold of Security (level 59).

label: Scorpion cage
title: Scorpion cage
lead:
The scorpion cage is an item obtained from Thormac at the beginning of Scorpion Catcher. This item is used in the quest to capture the scorpions which are obtainable from: Taverley Dungeon, Barbarian Outpost and Edgeville Monastery. According to Thormac, these scorpions are rare. If you lose the cage, you can get another by talking to Thormac again. After losing the cage, you will need to recapture any previously caught scorpions.

It's possible to get this item from Thormac without starting Scorpion Catcher. It's also possible to obtain duplicates by having a full backpack when Thormac attempts to give the player a cage. However, the cage serves no purpose outside the quest.

label: Scorpion Catcher
title: Scorpion Catcher
lead: Scorpion Catcher is a quest in which Thormac, a wizard in the Sorcerer's Tower, has lost three of his scorpions. He tasks you with finding them for him.

label: Scorpion Pit
title: Scorpion Pit
lead:
The Scorpion Pit is a valley in the northern portion of the Wilderness extending from level 53 to 55. The surface of the pit is infested with many level 14 Scorpions. With the Wilderness Rejuvenation update, multiple cave entrances (3 in the north and south) can now be interacted with, which takes the player into an underground cavern which contains Scorpia and her offspring.

On the valley itself, there are several headless arrow and bone spawns, along with many level 14 Scorpions. The Scorpion Pit (both inside and outside), along with the surrounding area is multi-combat, and is a hotspot for PKers who come to kill Scorpia hunters. Players should take caution around the pit as the Chaos Elemental can also wander into the Scorpion Pit, dealing high damage to lower-levelled players.

label: Scout
title: Scout
lead:
Scout may refer to:

*The scouts of General Khazard in The General's Shadow miniquest
**Scout (Falador)
**Scout (Tai Bwo Wannai)
**Scout (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
**Scout (Shantay Pass)
*Scout (2013 Goblin Invasion), part of the third stage of the event
*Scout (Ghorrock Dungeon), found after completion of Secrets of the North quest
*Scout, an alternate account used to survey the Wilderness for player killers or potential victims

label: Scrawled note
title: Scrawled note
lead: The scrawled note is an item obtained while searching the crate in Viyeldi caves during Legends' Quest. It cannot be reobtained after completing the quest.

label: Screen
title: Screen
lead: Two screens can be found in southernmost tent of the desert Bandit Camp and one in Falador, upstairs of Cassie's Shield Shop. Players cannot interact with the screens but are able to examine them.

label: Screenshots
title: Screenshots
lead:
From 4 August 2004 (Website Overhaul) until 1 July 2008 (New Website and Much More...), the RuneScape website prominently featured a selection of gameplay screenshots. These were all updated periodically as the game interface changed.

This page is a gallery of all preserved official screenshots from that section of the website. A small number are only known to be preserved as thumbnails, and some are currently considered lost.

label: Scribe
title: Scribe
lead:
Scribe may refer to:
*Goblin scribe, a cave goblin scribe found in Dorgesh-Kaan
*Guild Scribe Verity, a scribe for the Hunter Guild
*Santa's scribe, an NPC encountered during the 2022 Christmas event

label: Scroll
title: Scroll
lead: Scroll may refer to:

label: Scroll box
title: Scroll box
lead:
Scroll boxes are a stackable variant of clue scrolls, in which opening them will give players a clue scroll of the same tier. However, they do not share the one hour despawn timer that clue scrolls have, instead possessing the normal despawn timer of three minutes. If a clue scroll is already in the player's inventory or bank, players will receive the message, The clue box refuses to open - you already have a clue.

Upon completion of X Marks the Spot, scroll boxes are obtained in place of clue scrolls, and are stackable up to a certain limit depending on the number of clue completions; this cap, which includes scrolls and scroll boxes, starts at 2 for each clue tier, and can be increased to a maximum of 5 by opening the following scroll cases:
* Minor scroll case - increases the stack limit of scroll boxes by 1 for a specific tier.
* Major scroll case - increases the stack limit of scroll boxes by 1 for a specific tier (for a total of +2 with the minor case).
* Mimic scroll case - rewarded upon defeating the Mimic, and increases the stack limit of scroll boxes by 1 for all tiers.

label: Scrumpled note
title: Scrumpled note
lead: The scrumpled note is an item obtained while searching the bed in the Shaman Caves during Legends' Quest. It cannot be reobtained after completing the quest.

label: Scrumpled paper
title: Scrumpled paper
lead:
A scrumpled paper is a recipe for Ugthanki kebabs that is dropped by Shantay (found in the Shantay Pass) when a player talks to him. To get one quickly, players can spam the "Talk-to" option until one is dropped.

When one is dropped on the ground, the message Something drops out of Shantay's pocket onto the floor. It looks like a piece of paper. is given.

label: Scrying pool (interface item)
title: Scrying pool (interface item)
lead:
The Scrying pool is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Scrying pool.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Scurrius/Strategies
title: Scurrius/Strategies
lead:
Within the Varrock Sewers, players can fight Scurrius, the Rat King. Players can make their way east from the sewer entrance just east of the Varrock Palace courtyard, then climbing through the broken bars. Players can right-click the bars to choose whether to enter the public area or create an instance, which is free.

The public area contains a much stronger Scurrius (having 1,000 more health and slightly higher combat stats), though it has a more generous experience multiplier. The private version of Scurrius is faster to kill, but is weaker and gives a lower multiplier.

label: Scuttle
title: Scuttle
lead: Scuttles are non-interactable scenery found across Morytania. Despite their examine text, they cannot be used for any sort of storage.

label: Scythe (Halloween event)
title: Scythe (Halloween event)
lead:
The scythe is an untradeable event reward. It can be obtained by completing one of the Halloween holiday events that occur once per year.

The scythe is not particularly powerful, as it is intended to be a decorative weapon. It has very low bonuses and a slow attack speed. Notably, it has several unique attack animations.

label: Scythe (weapon)
title: Scythe (weapon)
lead: Scythes are a category of melee weapons that use a set of combat options containing slash and crush attack styles. They have the same attack speed as battleaxes.

label: Sea
title: Sea
lead:
Sea may refer to:

Seas can be charted for sailing experience and rewards. For the purposes of charting, there are 70 seas in total; many seas make up an ocean.

label: sea charting
title: sea charting
lead:
displaying some sea charting tasks for the Port of Sarim.]]

Sea charting is a Sailing activity in which players perform tasks around the sea to receive one-time rewards of experience and items. The Captain's log contains records of completed charting tasks and hints for where to find incomplete ones. These tasks vary from simple exploration to puzzles and even data collection, many of which require specific tools to complete.

label: Sea charting/By oceans
title: Sea charting/By oceans
lead:
, from a crate in the Hosidian Sea of the Western Ocean.]]
This page displays all experience rewards from completely charting seas and oceans. Tasks are also grouped by ocean, and seas can be manually marked as finished at the bottom of this page.

label: Sea charting/Current
title: Sea charting/Current
lead:
can be used.]]
Current is a type of sea charting task that involves tracking sea currents using the current duck. As the duck is acquired as a reward from the Current Affairs quest, these tasks have a minimum requirement of at least 22 Sailing. To complete these tasks, set the current duck down in the water at a spot where the water has some distinct ripples and follow it to the end. The duck will drift along in the currents before eventually coming to a stop where you can then retrieve it and complete the task. Note that you do not need to escort the duck, you can go to the end location directly. The duck will only despawn a few minutes after it has arrived at its end location.

label: Sea charting/Weather
title: Sea charting/Weather
lead:
Weather is a type of sea charting task requiring at least level 57 Sailing that involves assisting Meaty Aura Logist in various locations by measuring weather patterns using the portable weather station. Despite being a sea charting activity, some weather data must be gathered on land. Once speaking with Meaty Aura Logist, she will give you a portable weather station specific to that particular location. Then you must use it to get a reading at the location where there is no wind, before returning to Meaty Aura Logist to turn in the Data filled portable weather station and complete the task.

Boosts may be used to hit the 57 Sailing requirement. Boosting is only required when starting and when getting a reading, handing in the data filled station to Meaty does not require a boost.

label: Sea Shanty
title: Sea Shanty
lead:
Sea Shanty is a music track that unlocks around Musa Point and Karamja Volcano. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track and Jungle Island.

In Classic mode, the track plays at Musa Point and its docks.

label: Sea Shanty 2
title: Sea Shanty 2
lead:
Sea Shanty 2 is a music track that is unlocked in Port Sarim. It can also be unlocked by going to the docks west of Prifddinas or on Tempoross Cove after defeating Tempoross.

The track has become arguably one of the most iconic tracks in Old School RuneScape; Ian Taylor, the track's composer, would later comment on its fame in an interview in late 2018:

Without Telekinetic Grab, it will merely damage the player for 3 hitpoints, causing them to exclaim "Ouch!" If dropped, players can only pick it up again using another Telekinetic Grab spell.

label: Sea slug (race)
title: Sea slug (race)
lead: Sea slugs (Opisthobranchia alucinor) are a race of slug-like creatures which are able to control the minds of humans by latching on to them. They are ruled by the Mother Mallum.

label: Sea Slug Conflicts
title: Sea Slug Conflicts
lead:
The Sea Slug Conflicts is an ongoing conflict around the fishing village of Witchaven. The conflict essentially began at some point during the Fourth Age, when the Temple Knights fought against the Sea Slug Queen Mother Mallum, who was a malevolent slug-like entity producing tiny sea slugs capable of taking over the minds and bodies of other creatures.

The majority of the Sea Slug Conflicts took place when Mother Mallum first emerged from the sea. She used her forces to corrupt and control the important political figures of the world. Eventually, she was sealed within an underground cave network by the Temple Knights. However, the Temple Knights have since forgotten the process used to imprison Mother Mallum.

title: Sea turtle

It can be obtained by cooking raw sea turtle on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 82 Cooking and granting 211.3 experience when successful. Sea turtles never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape.

Players without the cooking cape are encouraged to cook sea turtles on the clay oven within the Hosidius Kitchen, as this provides the player the best chances to successfully cook them.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. It can be used with a filled fishbowl to catch a fish in the Catherby aquarium, or be cooked on a range or fire to create soda ash. Seaweed may also be used in place of soda ash in the superglass make Lunar spell, skipping the need to convert it to soda ash. Seaweed can be used for normal compost.

label: Second Age
title: Second Age
lead:
The Second Age is the period following the First Age. It is also the 'Golden Age' of Zaros and the Zarosian Empire, until he was betrayed by Zamorak. This age approximately began when Guthix disappeared and descended deep beneath the earth, and is estimated to have been about 2,000 years long.

Numerous other gods began setting foot on Gielinor; Tumeken, Elidinis, Zaros, Saradomin, Armadyl and Bandos are known to have arrived during the Second Age, bringing with them new races to the world, gathering new followers and claiming territory.

title: Seeker arrows
lead:
]]
Seeker arrows are an upgraded type of arrow that have +20 more accuracy and an increased minimum hit, compared to their regular counterparts. They will be released with The Blood Moon Rises quest, and will be created by adding bloodwood sap to arrows to upgrade them, or by adding the sap to logs or arrow shafts before fletching them into arrows.

The exact way the mechanic would function was clarified in Update:Blood Moon Rises Rewards, as follows:

The Seers' Village bank, sometimes known simply as Seers bank, is a bank in Seers' Village.

The bank has an upper level, which contains a locked section with chests, crates, and some statues. The Seers' Village Agility Course starts on top of the bank, by climbing the south-eastern wall on the outside of the building. Players on the top floor can see other players who are starting a lap of the Agility course while they do the climbing animation.

It is also the end of the Seers' Village Agility Course.

label: Senntisten
title: Senntisten
lead:
Senntisten was the capital city of the Zarosian Empire, which existed during the Second and Third Age. According to archaeologists, it was home to a massive temple complex, and occupied roughly the area east of modern-day Varrock and parts of Silvarea, making it one of the largest known cities in Gielinor's history.

The city continued to act as the capital after the fall of Zaros at the hands of his general Zamorak, surviving throughout most of the God Wars until it was eventually conquered by Zamorakian forces. Under Zamorakian occupation, the city was destroyed, and was later conquered by Saradominists. They built the city Saranthium where the Zarosian capital once stood.

She inspired the elves to build their city, Prifddinas, the way they did so they could communicate, protect themselves, and prosper. label: Server blackout
title: Server blackout
lead:
A server blackout is the unexpected crash of a server, typically resulting in all players being logged out for an extended period of time. Blackouts usually affect most, if not all, game servers and may affect other RuneScape facilities, such as the main website.

Blackouts are generally caused by a technical failure on the part of Jagex. Players who suffer from blackouts can only wait until the problem is fixed by Jagex. In some cases, a rollback is necessary. A rollback is an operation that returns server databases to their previous state from before the blackout occurred. On rare occasions where a rollback is performed, any changes that occurred between the crash and the previous state are lost. This includes gained experience, trade transactions, quest progress, etc. Rollbacks typically revert the servers to the state they were in anywhere from 15 minutes to one hour prior.

label: Server crash glitch
title: Server crash glitch
lead:
The server crash glitch or the 'W501 Glitch is a major glitch that was revealed on 26-27 November 2019.

On 26 November 2019, an Old School RuneScape content creator disclosed information about a glitch which allowed players to duplicate items including coins by abusing server save states and crashes. When a server crashes, players are reverted to their save state from either 15 minutes ago, or their last logout. This could be manipulated by trading coins with another player for example, logging out on the account which now has the coins, and then forcing a server crash within a 15 minute period. As the original player's save state reverts, their coins are returned (that they originally traded), but the second player keeps the traded coins. A similar glitch occurred on RuneScape seven months after the Old School RuneScape glitch was uncovered.

label: Settings
title: Settings
lead:
Settings is the screen that lets players change various settings, such as the brightness of the game client, whether or not chat effects display, whether to accept aid or not, the volume of the music and sound effects, and much more.

While the settings tab allows players to quickly change their Control, Audio, and Display settings, players can change or toggle additional settings via the main settings interface, accessed by clicking the "All Settings" button at the bottom of the tab.

label: Seven Priestly Warriors
title: Seven Priestly Warriors
lead:
The Seven Priestly Warriors is a term widely applied to Ivandis Seergaze, Iriandul Caistlyn, Sarl Dunegun, Derygull Templeton, Erysail the Pious, Friar Twiblick, and Essiandar Gar, Temple Knights that defended Misthalin and Asgarnia from invading Morytanian forces during the Misthalin - Morytania War, in roughly 1200 of the Fourth Age. They fought at Silvarea, upon which the Paterdomus was constructed after their death in battle. Of them, only Ivandis Seergaze of Lumbridge survived the direct conflict with Lord Drakan's forces, although he himself died during a later venture into the region.

The warriors also blessed the River Salve during the final battle of the Misthalin - Morytania War, creating a barrier to prevent Morytanian invasion in the future. This blessing has held, although there have been several instances of crossing through various methods. The warriors remain some of humanity's most universally celebrated historical figures, although they are most frequently referenced in Misthalinian lore and history.

title: Sewer valve
lead:
Sewer valves are water-controlling devices found just south of Ardougne. They are used in the Hazeel Cult quest. There are 5 sewer valves total. Each has a "turn-right" and "turn-left" option.

Just east of the Clock Tower is a dungeon entrance. Inside there is a raft. When boarded, this raft goes to different places based on the positions of all 5 sewer valves.

Sewers are artificial, dungeon-like, underground tunnel networks through which waste is disposed of. In Old School RuneScape, sewers are usually areas beneath large cities where monsters can be found. Sewers may refer to:

*Ardougne Sewers, a small sewage network running beneath East and West Ardougne
*Draynor Sewers, sewers beneath Draynor Village
*Varrock Sewers, a large sewage network beneath Varrock, and by far the largest of the sewers
*Sewer valves, interactive scenery found south of East Ardougne
*The Warrens, a sewer located beneath Port Piscarilius

label: sextant
title: sextant
lead:
A sextant is an item used for solving coordinate clues whilst on a Treasure Trail. It does not need to be brought with the player if the exact coordinate is known beforehand.

A chart can be obtained by first talking to the Observatory professor (who may be at the Observatory or the nearby Observatory reception building to the north-east, depending upon whether the player has completed the Observatory Quest), then, speaking to Murphy in Port Khazard, who will give you a sextant. Murphy is found on the dock near the trawler for the Fishing Trawler. Brother Kojo in the Clock Tower can then give the player a watch.

The shades in the Stronghold of Security are found next to the ladder leading to the fourth floor, while the ones in the Catacombs of Kourend are found in the northernmost area of Reeking Cove, south from the steel dragons. Shades in the Catacombs of Kourend are next to the Twisted Banshee and Deviant spectre and you will have to pass them to get to the shades, so ensure you have suitable protection, for example a Slayer helmet, otherwise it is easy to die to the banshee or spectres special attacks.

label: Shadow Realm
title: Shadow Realm
lead:
The Shadow Realm is a realm that is, in some sense, a hidden part of Gielinor rather than a separate dimension. It forms an invisible layer of reality seemingly spanning the entire world. Objects and people that are inside the Shadow Realm are normally not visible to people outside of it, although it is still possible to see them using a ring of visibility or a ring of shadows. Some beings, such as certain Gods and Mahjarrat, are also able to see things hiding in the Shadow Realm, seemingly without any external aid. Dark beasts also have a natural connection to the shadows, giving them a greater connection to the Shadow Realm.

Objects from the Shadow Realm are featured in several quests and miniquests such as the entrance to the Shadow Dungeon in Desert Treasure I, the ghostly robes in the Curse of the Empty Lord, and the shadow sword in The General's Shadow. In addition, the player is able to be present in the Shadow Realm by being targeted to guide the maze during the fight with Sotetseg in the Theatre of Blood, and while possessing the blackstone fragment and entering the puddles in Lassar Undercity during and after Desert Treasure II. Entering the Shadow Realm is also a prominent mechanic in the fight with The Whisperer.

label: Shadow spells
title: Shadow spells
lead:
Shadow spells are one of four types of Ancient Magicks combat spells. In addition to dealing damage, they have a chance to lower the target's Attack level if it has not already been drained. If cast using the shadow ancient sceptre, they will also lower the target's Strength and Defence levels if they have not already been drained. The level drain effect is also capable of lowering up to nine targets in a 3x3 grid around its primary target, just like the other additional effects of ancient magicks, on multi-target damaging Magic spells (burst and barrage).

Shadow spells may refer to:

label: Shadow spider
title: Shadow spider
lead:
Shadow spiders are one of few monsters that are hidden on the player's minimap. If a player initiates combat, it will drain the player's Prayer points by half of the current amount, rounded up. If a player is in combat with them over a long period, they will continue to drain the player's Prayer at regular intervals. Wearing a spectral spirit shield reduces the Prayer drain by half.

They can never take away a player's last prayer point.

label: Shadow warrior
title: Shadow warrior
lead: Shadow warriors are one of few monsters that are hidden on the player's minimap. They are not considered undead, so the salve amulet has no effect on them. Shadow warriors appear to be wielding battleaxes, but they attack at the same speed as scimitars. After completion of Legends' Quest, Shadow warriors are a possible Slayer task from Chaeldar and Vannaka.

label: Shaman

lead: Shaman may refer to:

label: Shaman Caves
title: Shaman Caves
lead:
The Shaman Caves are the upper floor of a cave system located in the Kharazi Jungle in southern Karamja. They play a large role in Legends' Quest, which must be started in order to access the caves. The entrance to the cave is in the north-western part of the Kharazi Jungle and is accessed by squeezing into the mossy rock, which requires 50 Agility.

The first room of the caves has a fire wall containing Ungadulu, a shaman possessed by the black demon Nezikchened. Ungadulu later helps the player reach the deeper sections of the cave, including the deeper Viyeldi caves accessed via a winch at the end of the dungeon. There is a shortcut on the western wall near the entrance that bypasses a majority of the cave, requiring 96 Agility.

label: Shaman robe
title: Shaman robe
lead: The shaman robe is an item that can be found during or after the Watchtower Quest on the ground inside the Ogre Enclave. The robe cannot be worn. It only serves for the purpose of retrieving the cyan crystal if during the quest the player has lost it. The crystal can be found by searching the robe. After doing so, it has no other use and it can be safely dropped.

label: Shaman's tome
title: Shaman's tome
lead:
Shaman's tome can be found in the Shaman Caves during the Legends' Quest. It can be obtained by searching the desk inside the octogram of Fire walls. It doesn't give much useful information, more just the mental state of the shaman inside the flaming octagon and a mention of the fact he's actually being controlled by a demon.

After finding the book, another copy can be found on the shelves in your house.

label: Shamanism
title: Shamanism
lead:
Shamanism was proposed to players as a new skill in March 2023 in a blog alongside two other potential skills, Sailing and Taming. It would allow players to use gathered materials in rituals to create powerful items, along with the ability to access the Spirit Realm, which would likely be similar to .

The skill concept came in second place in a poll, and as such has been currently shelved for potential future use due to outstanding player support.

label: Shamus
title: Shamus
lead:
Shamus is a leprechaun whom the player is required to talk to during the Lost City quest. He lives in a tree in Lumbridge Swamp, which the player must chop in order to get him to appear. When spoken to, he tells the player where to find Zanaris and how to enter.

The tree he lives in is located due west from the adventurers that start the player on the Lost City quest. The player can find it easily, because its left-click option is "Chop Tree" instead of "Chop down Tree".

label: Shantay
title: Shantay
lead:
Shantay is a merchant who runs the Shantay Pass. He owns the Shantay Pass Shop, and sells Shantay passes. Shantay also provides some information about desert survival, as the effects of the desert heat starts taking its toll south of Shantay Pass, which can be useful for new players going into the desert.

If a player declares being an outlaw, Shantay will call upon his guards to have the player arrested and demands the player pay a fine of 5 coins. If the player pays, they will be released. If the player refuses twice, Shantay will then transport the player to be locked in Port Sarim "High-security" jail.

label: Shantay disclaimer
title: Shantay disclaimer
lead: The Shantay disclaimer was an item that was given to players passing through the Shantay Pass, saying that no responsibility is taken if the player dies in the desert. By retaining one, players were able to skip a long-winded dialogue explaining the dangers of entering the desert. This system was replaced with the Doomsayer in July 2007, and the shantay disclaimers were removed. As a result, they have never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

label: Shantay Guard
title: Shantay Guard
lead: Shantay Guards can be found guarding the Shantay Pass in southern Al Kharid. There are 3 attackable level 22 guards, and one who manages who passes through the gate. The attackable guards only drop bones, and are not often fought.

label: Shantay Pass
title: Shantay Pass
lead: The Shantay Pass is a small area that separates Al Kharid from the Kharidian Desert. Players will need to have 5 coins to buy a pass from Shantay, or have completed the elite Desert Diary, if they wish to enter the desert.

label: Shantay pass (item)
title: Shantay pass (item)
lead:
The Shantay pass is an item used to exit Al Kharid through the southern gate at the Shantay Pass. Players can buy one for 5 coins from Shantay, who stands near the gate. One pass is required for each entrance into The Kharidian Desert from Al Kharid or the Ruins of Unkah, but is not required for passage vice versa.

After completing the Elite Desert Diary, players no longer need to buy a pass and can enter the desert free of charge.

label: Shantay pass (scenery)
title: Shantay pass (scenery)
lead: Shantay passes can be found at Shantay Pass as well as the Ruins of Unkah. In both locations, the scenery acts as a gateway to the rest of the Kharidian Desert, where its desert heat will quickly drain a player's health unless they have a source of water on them. These gateways require a shantay pass to cross, which can be bought from Shantay or his guards at the Ruins of Unkah.

label: Shantay Pass Shop
title: Shantay Pass Shop
lead:
The Shantay Pass Shop is a shop owned by Shantay in the Shantay Pass. It sells items players might need in the Kharidian Desert, such as waterskins, knives, and desert clothing.

The shop can also be accessed from the Ruins of Unkah by trading the Shantay guards there. The stock is shared between Shantay and the two Shantay guards.

label: Sharhai
title: Sharhai
lead: The Sharhai is a legendary sea monster only mentioned by Bosun Zarah, Elder Raley, and the Sharhai's purse. Very little is known about it, as it does not appear in-game, but it is supposedly a fearsome monster that sailors have not managed to take down yet. The Sharhai's purse Sea charting object suggests the Sharhai is a shark-like creature, as it resembles a ; such casings are sometimes called mermaid's purses. Additionally, the "hai" part of the name resembles the word for shark in various Germanic languages. Taken more literally, the Sharhai's purse may imply that the Sharhai is greedy, as the examine text mentions its "little treasures".

label: Shark
title: Shark
lead:
Shark is a type of fish that restores 20 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw shark on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 80 Cooking and granting 210 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt shark. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. It will only stop burning entirely if the player is wearing a Cooking cape, or using Cooking gauntlets at level 94 (84 if elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is completed while cooking at the Hosidius kitchen).

When eaten, the message You eat the shark. is displayed.

label: Shattered Relic Hunter (T1)
title: Shattered Relic Hunter (T1)
lead:
The Shattered Relic Hunter (T1) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing the Shattered Relics League. It can be purchased for 1,000 League points from the Leagues Reward Shop. It consists of a hood, top, trousers, and boots.

The set can be stored in an armour case in a player-owned house. It can also be displayed by using it on furniture built in the League hall's outfit stand space.

label: Shattered Relic Hunter (T2)
title: Shattered Relic Hunter (T2)
lead:
The Shattered Relic Hunter (T2) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing the Shattered Relics League. It can be purchased for 3,000 League points from the Leagues Reward Shop. It consists of a hood, top, trousers, and boots.

The set can be stored in an armour case in a player-owned house. It can also be displayed by using it on furniture built in the League hall's outfit stand space.

label: Shattered Relic Hunter (T3)
title: Shattered Relic Hunter (T3)
lead:
The Shattered Relic Hunter (T3) is a cosmetic set of clothing representing the Shattered Relics League. It can be purchased for 15,000 League points from the Leagues Reward Shop. It consists of a hood, top, trousers, and boots.

Purchasing the tier 3 outfit from the Leagues Reward Shop comes with a Shattered cane. Wearing the tier 3 outfit is required to perform the Shattered cane's emotes.

label: Shattered Relics League
title: Shattered Relics League
lead: The Shattered Relics League was the third league in Old School RuneScape. Originally set to release on 3 November 2021, the launch was delayed to 19 January 2022, and the league ended on 16 March 2022. It was announced on 3 February 2022 in a Modcast Q&A that it would be extended by two weeks, originally ending on 2 March 2022. The theme was set around collection and adventure and it was the first league to expand upon the lore of the game mode, with the introduction of The Sage.

label: Shattered Relics League/Boosted Drops
title: Shattered Relics League/Boosted Drops
lead:
As fragment slots are unlocked, passive bonuses will activate. Specific items will received boosted drop rates. Rates begin at 1x, increase to 2x when the 4th fragment slot is unlocked, and 3x when the 6th slot is unlocked. The following lists contain the drops that benefit from the boosted rates. Items are organised by which region they can be obtained.

Note: All unique drops from Revenants are also boosted. Notable drops from revenants include: Amulet of Avarice, ancient crystal, Craw's bow, dragon platelegs, Thammaron's sceptre, and Viggora's chainmace.

label: Shattered Relics League/Fragments
title: Shattered Relics League/Fragments
lead: Fragments are the result of The Sage shattering relics into fragments and scattering them across Gielinor. Fragments are weaker in isolation, compared to relics of previous leagues but they can be combined to form very powerful set effects. Players are limited to a set amount of active fragments at a time, up to a maximum of seven, but they can be exchanged while inside a bank, near a bank chest, or near The Sage.

label: Shattered Relics League/Guide
title: Shattered Relics League/Guide
lead: Shattered Relics League presents unique decisions and challenges unlike most content in Old School RuneScape and previous leagues. Since players are restricted to the skills and bosses they have unlocked, there are many strategic options. This guide provides information about the league mechanics, different training methods, and money making guides based on the constraints within the league.

label: Shattered Relics League glitch
title: Shattered Relics League glitch
lead:
The Shattered Relics League glitch was a major glitch that occurred on 19 January 2022. With the release of Shattered Relics League, there were problems with player profiles. Some players lost their Ironman Mode status upon logging back into the main game after logging into a Shattered Relics League world, and some players had their main game items and stats transferred over to their Shattered Relics League profile.

Jagex turned the game offline around an hour after the update to perform a rollback. The rollback only affected main game profiles and not Shattered Relics.

label: Shauna Ravitz
title: Shauna Ravitz
lead: Shauna Ravitz was a former Varrockian belonging to the Ravitz family, descending from the Elders of Avarrocka. She was the last blood descendant of Ramone Ravitz within the family. She married into the Fitzharmon family.

label: Shayzien armour
title: Shayzien armour
lead:
Shayzien armour is armour requiring 20 Defence to wear. Each tier grants slightly higher protection against the green acidic attack of Lizardman shamans. In order to obtain Shayzien armour, players must compete in the Shayzien Combat Ring within Shayzien, or create it by Smithing lovakite bars (11 bars for a full set). The collection log slots are filled regardless of how the armour is obtained. There are 5 different tiers of Shayzien armour:

*Shayzien armour (tier 1)
*Shayzien armour (tier 2)
*Shayzien armour (tier 3)
*Shayzien armour (tier 4)
*Shayzien armour (tier 5)
Shayzien armour can be stored in the armour case of a costume room. Ultimate Ironmen will be unable to retrieve individual pieces until the full set is stored.

label: Shayzien armour (tier 1)
title: Shayzien armour (tier 1)
lead:
Shayzien armour (1) is a set of armour that requires 20 Defence to wear. It is dropped by the tier 1 soldier at the Combat Ring in Shayzien. Players must defeat the soldier 5 times in order to receive all the pieces. The set pieces have melee defence values similar to bronze armour, but have much lower magic and ranged attack penalties.

Alternatively, players can smith a tier 1 Shayzien armour set with lovakite bars, requiring a Smithing level of 53 for a full set.

label: Shayzien armour (tier 2)
title: Shayzien armour (tier 2)
lead:
Shayzien armour (2) is a set of armour that requires 20 Defence to wear. It is dropped by the tier 2 soldier at the Combat Ring in Shayzien. Players must defeat the soldier 5 times in order to receive all the pieces.

Alternatively, players can smith a tier 2 Shayzien armour set with lovakite bars, requiring a Smithing level of 63 for a full set.

label: Shayzien armour (tier 3)
title: Shayzien armour (tier 3)
lead:
Shayzien armour (3) is a set of armour that requires 20 Defence to wear. It is dropped by the tier 3 soldier at the Combat Ring in Shayzien. Players must defeat the soldier 5 times in order to receive all the pieces.

Alternatively, players can smith a tier 3 Shayzien armour set with lovakite bars, requiring a Smithing level of 73 for a full set.

label: Shayzien armour (tier 4)
title: Shayzien armour (tier 4)
lead:
Shayzien armour (4) is a set of armour that requires 20 Defence to wear. It is dropped by the tier 4 soldier at the Combat Ring in Shayzien. Players must defeat the soldier 5 times in order to receive all the pieces. In terms of melee defensive values, these pieces are comparable to a steel armour, while having much lower ranged and magic attack penalties.

Alternatively, players can smith a tier 4 Shayzien armour set with lovakite bars, requiring a Smithing level of 83 for a full set.

label: Shayzien armour (tier 5)
title: Shayzien armour (tier 5)
lead:
Shayzien armour (5) is a set of armour that requires 20 Defence to wear. It is dropped by the tier 5 soldier at the Combat Ring in Shayzien. Players must defeat the soldier 5 times in order to receive all the pieces. In terms of melee defensive values, these pieces are comparable to a steel armour, while having much lower magic attack penalties and a sizable ranged attack bonus comparable to wearing a set of green d'hide armour.

Alternatively, players can smith a tier 5 Shayzien armour set with lovakite bars, requiring a Smithing level of 93 (and 11 lovakite bars) for a full set.

label: Shayzien Army
title: Shayzien Army
lead:
.]]
The Shayzien Army is the military force of the city of Shayzien. It consists of six regiments, with Lord Shiro Shayzien, the leader of the Shayzien House, being the commander-in-chief of the Shayzien Army. Though other cities, excluding Arceuus, have some form of militia, the Shayzien Army is the largest military force in Great Kourend.

Despite the size of the Shayzien Army and their importance to the defence of Great Kourend, there are two areas in particular in which they are lacking: defence against magical arts and a naval force. The naval force is meant to be lead by the Piscarilius House, but the current head, Lady Shauna Piscarilius, has no interest in forming the Kourend Navy. Despite this, there is pushback from the rest of the kingdom for Lord Shayzien to form a Shayzien Navy due to concerns over Shayzien having too much military power.

label: Shayzien supply armour
title: Shayzien supply armour
lead:
Shayzien supply armour was the non-equipable version of Shayzien armour. Unlike Shayzien armour, Shayzien supply armour could be smithed, but was not useable/equipable by players.

The crate for the armour had to be collected by searching the drawers in any of the armourer's buildings, and was found in noted form. Players would need to exchange this banknote for a crate, then 'pack' the crate in order to hand in armour sets in bulk for experience and/or Lovakengj favour.

label: Shayzien/Historical
title: Shayzien/Historical
lead:
Players can gain favour with Shayzien by assisting them in various activities in the Shayzien Encampment. Earning Shayzien favour will allow players to fight lizardmen, tackle organised crime in the kingdom to help keep order, and earn tiers 1-5 Shayzien armour through the Combat Ring as the player earns more favour.

To progress in the Architectural Alliance miniquest, players must gain 100% Shayzien favour and speak to Shayda, who is found south of the Shayzien Administration building in the centre of Shayzien.
__notoc__

label: Shears
title: Shears
lead:
Shears can be bought in almost any general store for 1 gp. They are required to shear wool from sheep, and are needed for the Sheep Shearer quest if you choose to gather the wool yourself. They are also needed for the quest A Tail of Two Cats.

They can be picked up off of the table in Fred the Farmer's house for the quest Sheep Shearer. It can also be found in Hosidius, in the building just north of the estate agent.

*The shed near Edgeville that is unlocked with the Brass key to get into the Edgeville Dungeon.

label: Shed (Lumbridge Swamp)
title: Shed (Lumbridge Swamp)
lead:
The Lumbridge Swamp shed is a seemingly inconspicuous storage shed located at the heart of the swamp, east of the mysterious runes for the water altar. Entering the shed can only be done on members worlds, and entering without wielding either a Dramen staff or Lunar staff will simply allow the player to enter the building. However, while wielding either of the staves, the player will be teleported to the entry fairy ring of Zanaris.

There are frogs, big frogs, and giant frogs as well as giant rats that spawn outside the shed.

Herding the sheep can prove challenging, since they are not very cooperative.

label: Shield (weapon)
title: Shield (weapon)
lead:
Shields are normally a piece of equipment used to defend. However, certain shields can be used to attack or wielded in the weapon slot.

Most of the shields that can be used to attack are wielded in the shield slot and use a chargeable special attack to deal damage. The only shield that can be wielded in the weapon slot is Dinh's bulwark.

*Shield right half

label: shield left half
title: shield left half
lead:
The shield left half is an item that can be joined with the right half to create the dragon square shield with level 60 Smithing. Joining the right half with the left half nets 75 Smithing experience. The other half of the shield is sold by Siegfried Erkle in the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items for 750,000 coins.

This item is a rare drop from the rare drop table. Wearing a ring of wealth will increase the chances of receiving one from the rare drop table. Goraks fought in the Gorak Plane are likely droppers of the shield left half, with a drop rate of 1/243.75 (with a ring of wealth equipped) if Fairytale II - Cure a Queen and Legends' Quest have been completed.

label: Shield of Arrav
title: Shield of Arrav
lead: Shield of Arrav is a quest where the shield of the famous Arrav of Avarrocka has been stolen by organised crime syndicates in Varrock.
