The slayer dungeon referenced in the in-game Agility skill guide's level 62 shortcuts is the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon.

label: Slayer equipment
title: Slayer equipment
lead: Slayer equipment refers to various tools and weapons used when fighting Slayer monsters. When slaying monsters, it is often required to use a specific piece of equipment to protect oneself from negative effects or to finish off a monster at low health. All Slayer masters run a Slayer Equipment shop, selling the same items at the same price.

label: Slayer guardians
title: Slayer guardians
lead: Slayer guardians are non-player characters who guard and operate certain Slayer task-only areas, preventing players from slaying monsters whilst not on an assigned Slayer task. The guardians are largely made up of members of Nieve's family, but also include a number of other non-relatives.

label: Slayer key
title: Slayer key
lead:
Slayer key may refer to:

*Brimstone key, dropped from slayer monsters assigned by Konar quo Maten. Used to unlock the Brimstone chest.
*Brittle key, a one-time drop from Gargoyles while on a slayer task. Used to unlock the rooftop of the Slayer Tower to fight the Grotesque Guardians.
*Larran's key, dropped from slayer monsters in the wilderness assigned by Krystillia. Used to unlock Larran's big or small chest.

label: Slayer Master
title: Slayer Master
lead:
Slayer Masters are NPCs who serve as guides to the Slayer skill and assign tasks to players requiring them to kill specific monsters a certain number of times. Each Slayer Master has a different combat level requirement for players to be assigned tasks from them. Slayer Masters with higher combat level requirements will generally assign longer tasks with more difficult monsters. Players receive Slayer reward points upon completing tasks with bonus points being awarded at regular intervals (except for tasks from Turael and Spria). These points can be redeemed for a variety of different rewards, unlocks, and upgrades which enhance a player's Slayer experience.

All Slayer Masters sell Slayer equipment at an equipment shop. These items are helpful and sometimes essential to specific Slayer tasks. They also provide rewards in exchange for Slayer points.

label: Slayer monsters
title: Slayer monsters
lead:
A Slayer monster is a monster that can only be killed with the required Slayer level. Special equipment may be needed to kill them, which is usually purchasable from any Slayer Master. Some monsters can only be killed when on an assignment.

Some monsters have alternatives that can be killed and count toward a particular task, see Slayer task.

label: Slayer store
title: Slayer store
lead:
Slayer store may refer to:

*Slayer Equipment, the shops run by Slayer masters which stock various tools and weapons for use against Slayer monsters.
*Slayer Rewards, the reward system that awards points after every completed Slayer assignment, from every Slayer master except Turael.

label: Slayer task
title: Slayer task
lead:
A Slayer assignment is given by a Slayer master. Killing the assigned monsters grants players Slayer experience.

For some monsters, players may also be able to access more exclusive locations when assigned them as a task. These monsters can only be killed as part of a slayer assignment; attempting to kill them without the required task will prevent the player from doing so.

label: Slayer task tips
title: Slayer task tips
lead:
Slayer task tips are given by each Slayer Master if players ask them for tips after being assigned a task. They are meant to help the player know the ins and outs of their assigned slayer creature, although some serve as flavour text and are not practical tips.

Players can ask for tips by either contacting a Slayer Master through an enchanted gem or a Slayer ring.

label: Slayer task/Aberrant spectres
title: Slayer task/Aberrant spectres
lead:
Aberrant spectres can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 60 Slayer and level 65 combat by various Slayer masters. They are popular among most players for their common herb and herb seed drops, which includes higher-level herbs such as ranarr and dwarf weed.

A nose peg or Slayer helmet is required when fighting aberrant spectres, as they emit noxious fumes that will severely damage the player without proper protection. The salve amulet(ei) gives a bonus against their undead attribute, however the Slayer helmet bonus and the amulet bonus do not stack.

label: Slayer task/Ankous
title: Slayer task/Ankous
lead:
Ankous can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 40 combat by various Slayer masters. As their only attack is melee, Protect from Melee can be used to negate all incoming damage.

Ankous are a fairly fast task and have generous drop rates for death and blood runes.

label: Slayer task/Aquanites
title: Slayer task/Aquanites
lead:
Aquanites are Slayer monsters found in the Ynysdail Cavern beneath Ynysdail. They require level 78 Slayer to fight, and accessing Ynysdail itself requires 73 Sailing and a boat equipped with an adamant keel or better.

Aquanites can be killed normally; however, to receive them as a Slayer task, players must first unlock them for 80 Slayer reward points. They may be assigned by both Nieve and Duradel, and a task extension is available for 100 points.
Aquanites can drop the unique Aquanite tendon, used to make the Aquanite hopper.

label: Slayer task/Araxytes
title: Slayer task/Araxytes
lead:
Araxytes are a potential slayer assignment exclusively from Nieve/Steve and Duradel/Kuradal after completion of Priest in Peril. Turael/Aya and Spria can also assign them, albeit indirectly as a spiders task. They require 92 Slayer in order to be harmed. They are found exclusively in the Morytania Spider Cave.

Araxytes attack with melee, and are also able to inflict venom starting at 6 damage, therefore, it is recommended to bring venom immunity to all encounters, preferably extended anti-venom+ for long trips. They are fairly far from a bank, though a spider cave teleport will bring players to the entrance of the cave.

label: Slayer task/Aviansie
title: Slayer task/Aviansie
lead:
Aviansie can be assigned as a slayer task provided that players have access to the God Wars Dungeon (requiring completion of Death Plateau) and has unlocked Watch the birdie slayer perk for 80 Slayer reward points.

Aviansie can be found in the normal and Wilderness God Wars Dungeon; as followers of Armadyl, Armadylean God-aligned items are required to make them tolerant. Aviansie have an increased sense of danger and will attack players if they are attacked, even if they're in combat with another monster. Their flying height means that they can only be harmed with ranged and magic, although salamanders and halberds are an exception as a direct target.

label: Slayer task/Bandits
title: Slayer task/Bandits
lead:
Bandit can be assigned as a slayer task. It does not have a required combat level to be assigned by Krystilia. Bandits are most commonly found in Bandit Camp (Wilderness).

Along with Bandits and Guard Bandit, Speedy Keith, Donny the lad, and Black Heather can be killed to satisfy the task.

label: Slayer task/Banshees
title: Slayer task/Banshees
lead:
Banshees can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 15 Slayer and level 20 combat by various Slayer masters. They are found in the Slayer Tower and the Catacombs of Kourend. Players must wear earmuffs or a Slayer helm when fighting banshees. Lower levelled players who do not have access to a Slayer helm can wear a salve amulet. Note that the bonuses from the salve amulet do not stack with those from the Slayer helmet.

Banshees are primarily known for their common drops of pure essence, which is helpful for ironmen for runecrafting.

label: Slayer task/Basilisks
title: Slayer task/Basilisks
lead:
Basilisks can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 40 Slayer, level 40 combat, and level 20 Defence by medium-level Slayer Masters. In order for higher-levelled masters to assign them, the player must pay 80 points for the Basilocked perk.

When fighting any basilisk, the player must bring a mirror shield or V's shield, or the basilisk's gaze will deal immense damage and massively drain the player's stats.

label: Slayer task/Bats
title: Slayer task/Bats
lead: Bats can be assigned as a Slayer task from Turael, Spria and Mazchna. They have a requirement of level 5 combat to be assigned and are generally meant as tasks for beginners. There are a variety of bats, but the most commonly killed are regular bats and giant bats. Bats only drop bat bones or nothing at all, meaning there is little reason to slay higher-level bats.

label: Slayer task/Bears
title: Slayer task/Bears
lead:
Bears can be assigned as a slayer task at level 13 combat by various low-level Slayer masters. Bears can be found in various locations throughout Gielinor.

Black bears, bear cubs, grizzly bears, grizzly bear cubs, reanimated bears, and Callisto can all be killed to satisfy the task. Angry bears (found in Tolna's rift), the Headless Beast (fought during the quest Getting Ahead), and the Crystalline and Corrupted Bear (fought in the Gauntlet and the Corrupted Gauntlet respectively) do not count towards the task.

label: Slayer task/Birds
title: Slayer task/Birds
lead:
Birds can be assigned as a Slayer task from Turael or Spria. They have no requirements to be assigned and are generally meant as tasks for beginners. There are a wide variety of birds, but the most commonly killed are chickens, seagulls and ducks, which are low-level, rarely deal damage and easy to access. Chickens drop bones, raw chicken and feathers, but most other birds only drop bones or nothing at all, meaning there is little reason to slay higher-level birds.

Birds introduced with the Sailing skill do not reward Slayer experience and thus do not count towards task completion.

label: Slayer task/Black demons
title: Slayer task/Black demons
lead:
Black demons can be assigned as a Slayer task at 80 combat level by various Slayer masters. They can be found in a variety of dungeons around Gielinor. Black demons can be easily killed using safespots when attacking with Ranged or Magic, or by using melee with the Protect from Melee prayer. They are weak to demonbane weapons, as well as water spells.

For lower-levelled players, black demon tasks can be very daunting, as their high stats requires safespotting, which will significantly lower kill rates. Higher-levelled players will not have this problem, but the demons have a near non-existent drop table which makes killing them generally not worth the time or experience.

label: Slayer task/Black dragons
title: Slayer task/Black dragons
lead:
Black dragons can be assigned as a slayer task at level 80 combat by various Slayer masters after partial completion of Dragon Slayer I.

Black dragons are the rarest of chromatic dragons. As with all other chromatic dragons, they use melee and short-ranged dragonfire. When killing the standard variant of Black dragons, its recommended to use Protect from Melee and basic dragonfire protection (such as an anti-dragon shield and extended antifire potion), as the dragons are quite accurate and hit relatively hard.

label: Slayer task/Bloodveld
title: Slayer task/Bloodveld
lead:
Bloodvelds are a type of demon that use their long tongues to attack their victims. Being a Slayer monster, bloodvelds require a Slayer level of 50 to be damaged by players. As a demon, it is affected by demonbane weapons. An ash sanctifier may be brought to receive Prayer experience. Bloodvelds are popular among many players for their high Hitpoints and low Defence, thus making them good sources of experience.

Bloodvelds are one of few monsters that attack with magic-based melee, meaning that despite it using melee attacks against the player, it is the player's magic defence (rather than their melee defence) that is used to determine the accuracy of the bloodveld's attack. As such, it is recommended for players killing bloodvelds to equip armour with decent magic defence, such as dragonhide or blood moon armour, as they are relatively accurate in combat. Players using Prayer should still pray Protect from Melee instead of magic to nullify damage.

label: Slayer task/Blue dragons
title: Slayer task/Blue dragons
lead:
Blue dragons can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 65 combat by mid- and high-level Slayer masters after starting Dragon Slayer I. They can be found in various caves across Gielinor, with most of them having some requirement to access, such as completion of quests, a dusty key, or level 70 Agility.

Blue dragons attack using melee, as well as dragonfire, for which some form of dragonfire protection should be considered. Additionally, brutal blue dragons can also attack with magic. Due to their large size, blue dragons can usually be safespotted with ranged, magic, or halberd-like weapons. Like all dragons, they are also susceptible to dragonbane weapons.

label: Slayer task/Cave horrors
title: Slayer task/Cave horrors
lead:
Cave horrors can be assigned as a slayer task starting at level 85 combat by Chaeldar, Nieve, and Duradel. Cave horrors are found exclusively in the Mos Le'Harmless Cave, requiring completion of Cabin Fever.

You must wear a witchwood icon to fight cave horrors at melee distance, otherwise they will use a special attack which always deals damage equal to 10% of the player's base Hitpoints level, rounded down (e.g. 9 damage at 96). This can be completely mitigated by using Protect from Melee, or using a safespot.

label: Slayer task/Cave krakens
title: Slayer task/Cave krakens
lead:
Cave kraken can be assigned from level 87 Slayer. They are exclusively found within Kraken Cove.

Cave krakens have low value drops and are generally only killed for their uncharged trident which has a 1/200 drop rate. They take reduced damage from ranged attacks, and cannot be reached with Melee, so must be fought with Magic, such as with earth spells due to their elemental weakness. Damage can be protected against with Protect from Magic.

label: Slayer task/Crabs
title: Slayer task/Crabs
lead:
Crabs can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters. They have no requirements to be assigned and are found in many areas across Gielinor. Crabs are often used as popular monsters for combat training, due to their low offence and high hitpoints. King Sand Crabs and Giant Rock Crabs are the exceptions, having much higher combat stats, and are only advisable to kill for a Slayer task if seeking specific drops from them (such as pieces of rock-shell armour).

As most crabs deal relatively little damage, no particular gear is required for them. Accounts with lower combat levels may need to wear armour or bring food, but at higher levels, neither are necessary. All crabs use the crush attack style, so if wearing armour, armour with the highest crush defence is advised. For example, a chainbody will offer more crush defence than a platebody.

label: Slayer task/Custodian stalker
title: Slayer task/Custodian stalker
lead:
Custodian stalkers can be assigned as a Slayer task starting at level 54 by Chaeldar and Nieve, and can be found in the Stalker Den after the completion of the Shadows of Custodia quest. There are multicombat areas where cannons can be placed in the south-western side of the dungeon, and single-combat caverns in the south-eastern and northern parts.

The stalkers all drop broken antlers, which are used to create atlatl dart tips for creating atlatl darts outside of subduing the Moons of Peril. The mature and elder variants are also able to drop the antler guard, a powerful off-hand item boasting offensive stats in all styles, with no defence requirement to wield. These tougher variants require a higher Slayer level to fight however, of level 67 and 76 respectively.

label: Slayer task/Dagannoths
title: Slayer task/Dagannoths
lead:
Dagannoths are a slayer task assigned by the advanced Slayer masters. Requiring completion of Horror from the Deep to be assigned, Dagannoths are known for their high slayer experience rates and easy task completions. For players who are seeking a more difficult challenge, the Dagannoth Kings are a viable alternative for players of moderate to experienced combat ability.

The weaker variant of Dagannoths can be found within the Lighthouse basement, Jormungand's Prison, and the Catacombs of Kourend. In the first two locations, a dwarf cannon can be used very effectively as the area is multicombat. For players who wish to maximise AFK time without relying on prayer, the lighthouse is a good choice. Otherwise, it is best to kill them in the prison or catacombs, as these two locations only house melee-using dagannoth.

label: Slayer task/Dark beast
title: Slayer task/Dark beast
lead:
Dark beasts can be killed with Melee, Magic or Ranged. Melee is the most effective against them and should be used in conjunction with high prayer bonus armour, such as Proselyte armour, for Protect from Melee. To maximize profit, players should bring a herb sack and a gem bag so that they can loot all herbs and gems they receive.

Dark beasts are good point-gaining tasks as they are not assigned in large numbers; even the extension doesn't give as much as other monsters, though this is balanced by their large health pool.

label: Slayer task/Dogs
title: Slayer task/Dogs
lead:
Dogs can be assigned as a Slayer task from Turael, Spria and Mazchna at level 15 combat. A wide variety of dogs can be found across Gielinor. Most dogs, except those in Brimhaven Dungeon, are aggressive and they all attack with melee. Dogs have no noteworthy drops beside bones and ensouled dog heads.

File:Guard Dog (Hosidius) safespot.png|A safespot for the guard dogs in Hosidius.

label: Slayer task/Dragons
title: Slayer task/Dragons
lead: A dragons Slayer task may refer to:

label: Slayer task/Drake
title: Slayer task/Drake
lead:
Drakes are high level Slayer monsters found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. They can drop their claws and teeth, which are used to upgrade the boots of stone and holy sandals into boots of brimstone and devout boots, respectively. These items are five times more common when killed on a Slayer task.

Drakes use both ranged and ranged melee, so melee armour is recommended against their attacks. Additionally, they will launch a fireball at the player's position, which deals 6-8 damage per hit for four hits if dragonfire protection is not used. It functions the same as chromatic dragonfire, although it can also be avoided by stepping away from the target tile.

label: Slayer task/Dust devils
title: Slayer task/Dust devils
lead:
Dust devils can be assigned as a slayer task by various medium and high-levelled Slayer Masters upon reaching 65 Slayer and 70 combat. In order to obtain these as a Slayer task, the player must have started Desert Treasure I.

Dust devils are an incredibly popular task amongst most slayers, as they have a superior, the choke devil, and are often found in multicombat areas which allows for chinning and burst/barraging. They have relatively decent drops which usually covers the cost of supplies.

label: Slayer task/Dwarves
title: Slayer task/Dwarves
lead:
Dwarves are a Slayer task assigned by Turael and Spria. They lack valuable drops, and give only between 10 and 61 Slayer experience.

Along with standard dwarves, Black Guards, dwarf gang members, chaos dwarves, and Black Guard Berserkers can also be killed for dwarf tasks.

label: Slayer task/Earth warriors
title: Slayer task/Earth warriors
lead: Earth warriors are a type of humanoid earth elemental found in a dirt-lined chamber in the Edgeville Dungeon. This area is in the Wilderness so it is advised to come prepared for player killers.

label: Slayer task/Elves
title: Slayer task/Elves
lead:
Elves can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 70 combat by various Slayer masters after completion of Regicide. Elves either use ranged or melee, depending on their weapon; wielding either a crystal bow or a crystal halberd, of which the latter has an attack range of 2 tiles.

Until the player has access to Lletya, the only place for them to kill elves is the Iorwerth Camp. Reaching the camp can be very tedious without using an Iorwerth camp teleport, and players intending to use a dwarf multicannon are discouraged from doing so as the camp is impeded by tents, barrels, and crates. Players may prefer reanimating elves using the Arceuus spellbook spell Adept Reanimation at the Dark Altar, the ensouled heads being purchasable through the Grand Exchange, and gaining 754 Prayer experience per kill but gaining less Slayer and combat experience.

label: Slayer task/Fire giants
title: Slayer task/Fire giants
lead:
Fire giants can be assigned as a slayer task at level 65 combat by various Slayer masters. They are the strongest generic giants for their category and are mostly known for their rune scimitar drops.

Fire giants can be found in an array of locations, most of which allow for the use of a dwarf multicannon. The lone exception is the Catacombs of Kourend, which does not allow a cannon but is a multicombat area.

label: Slayer task/Fossil Island wyverns
title: Slayer task/Fossil Island wyverns
lead:
Fossil Island Wyverns are a Slayer monster requiring 66 Slayer to kill. A combat level of 60, as well as the completion of the quests Elemental Workshop and Bone Voyage, is required for them to be assigned as a slayer task.

Similarly to their skeletal cousins, Fossil Island Wyverns use both melee and an icy breath. The icy breath requires the use of an elemental shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, or ancient wyvern shield in order to take reduced damage from the breath; the latter also provides immunity from being frozen. Protect from Magic can also be used but only provides half the damage reduction of the prior protections. Antifire potions of any type and the anti-dragon shield do not work to mitigate icy breath.

label: Slayer task/Gargoyles
title: Slayer task/Gargoyles
lead:
Gargoyles can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters at level 75 Slayer, level 80 combat, and with completion of the Priest in Peril quest. They are only found in the Slayer Tower, either on the top floor or in the basement. The gargoyles in the basement of the Slayer Tower can only be killed while on a Slayer task, as Raulyn will stop the player if they attempt to fight them off-task. Gargoyles have a Superior slayer monster variant, the level 349 marble gargoyle. Unlike regular gargoyles, the marble gargoyle also utilises ranged attacks. It also has a special attack, launching a white-red orb that deals heavy damage and entraps the player if not dodged; this attack has a 1x1 AoE.

Gargoyles are weak to both magic and crush attacks, but melee is commonly used due to the lack of safespots, less defence against their attacks and expenses for casting spells. They have -2 flat armour, so weapons such as Dual macuahuitl are recommended to make use of the extra damage. Even then, they are still easily fought with most standard weapons one might have available.

label: Slayer task/Ghosts
title: Slayer task/Ghosts
lead:
Ghosts can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 13 combat by Turael, Spria, and Mazchna. Ghosts spawn in various locations throughout Gielinor.

Only regular ghosts, forgotten souls, tortured souls, death wings and Revenants can be killed to satisfy the task. Spectres, ghasts, banshees and shades will not count towards the task.

label: Slayer task/Goblins
title: Slayer task/Goblins
lead: Goblins can be assigned as a slayer task, with no Slayer level requirement by Turael (or Spria after A Porcine of Interest). Sergeant Strongstack, Sergeant Grimspike, and Sergeant Steelwill count, and are susceptible to the bonus from Slayer Helmet/Black Mask.

label: Slayer task/Greater demons
title: Slayer task/Greater demons
lead:
Greater demons can be assigned by Krystilia, Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve/Steve, and Duradel/Kuradal. Despite their "greater" status, they possess a somewhat lackluster drop table, with their two most valuable drops being the rune full helm and the hard clue scroll. There are many different types of greater demons residing around Gielinor; however, with the exception of the Wilderness Slayer Cave, all have the same drop table.

When not killing greater demons as part of Konar or Krystilia's tasks, players have many spots to choose from. The most common spots are the Chasm of Fire and Catacombs of Kourend. The Chasm of Fire is a cannonable area in a small space, allowing for plenty of AFK and fast kill times, along with contracts for challenging a stronger version of Yama. Catering to the increased drop rates will require more banking and less AFK time, however. The Catacombs of Kourend has access to the ancient shard and dark totem piece drops. It is also a Multicombat area, allowing for players to AFK until the aggression timer expires, which can be easily reset.

label: Slayer task/Green dragons
title: Slayer task/Green dragons
lead:
Green dragons can be assigned as a slayer task at level 52 combat by Krystilia after partial completion of Dragon Slayer I. As Krystilia is the only Slayer master to assign green dragons, they must be fought in the Wilderness, and other variants outside the Wilderness do not count. They attack with melee and dragonfire, thus some protection against it should be considered. Due to their large size, they are usually able to be safespotted with ranged or halberd-like weapons. As dragons, they are also weak to dragonbane weapons.

A majority of dragons are above the level 20 line, thus a level 30 teleport such as an amulet of glory or royal seed pod is recommended for escaping player killers. A small cluster of three dragons can be found below level 20 Wilderness just west of the Dark Warriors' Fortress, making it ideal for killing with good attention, as the use of a teleport tab is enough to escape any hostile players. The dragons near the Lava Maze are above level 30 Wilderness, and thus it is not recommended to kill them there.

label: Slayer task/Gryphons
title: Slayer task/Gryphons
lead:
Gryphons can be assigned as a slayer task by Vannaka and Chaeldar after completion of the Troubled Tortugans quest. Additionally, both Nieve and Duradel may assign gryphons after the perk Wings Spread has been purchased.

Gryphons are found exclusively on The Great Conch. There are three lairs for gryphons; a western cavern, an eastern cavern (Slayer task only) and a lair in the centre of the island which leads to the Shellbane gryphon. Both the eastern and western caverns have a southern room that is multi-combat and cannon-able.

label: Slayer task/Hellhounds
title: Slayer task/Hellhounds
lead:
Hellhounds can be assigned as a slayer task at 75 combat level by various Slayer masters. They can be found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The task is very straightforward as regular hellhounds only attack with their fairly accurate melee bites; it is recommended to either safespot them or keep Protect from Melee on at all times. Hellhounds are primarily known for their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls, at a rate of 1/64, or 1/32 if killing in the Wilderness with a imbued ring of wealth. They also drop ensouled hellhound heads and the smouldering stone.

Outside of the Wilderness, hellhounds are primarily killed in the Stronghold Slayer Cave for general slayer, as there are four rooms of three or four hellhounds in each one, and a dwarf multicannon can be set up in their caves. They may also be killed in the Catacombs of Kourend for ancient shards and dark totem pieces. The catacombs do not allow for a cannon, but is a Multicombat area and allows for relative AFK training, especially with a Venator Bow. Once the aggression timer expires, the player can simply run south and up the vine to the Giants' Den to reset aggression.

label: Slayer task/Hill giants
title: Slayer task/Hill giants
lead:
Hill giants can be assigned as a slayer task from Mazchna and Vannaka at level 25 combat. Hill giants can be found many places both above and under ground. They all attack with melee. They always drop big bones and their drop table includes runes, herbs, limpwurt roots and the giant key, which is required to access the hill giant boss Obor. Cyclopes also count as hill giants for tasks.

File:Hill Giant (Edgeville Dungeon) safespot.png|A safespot for the hill giants in Edgeville Dungeon.
File:Hill Giant (Giant Pit) safespot.png|Hill giant safespot in the Giant Pit.

label: Slayer task/Hobgoblins
title: Slayer task/Hobgoblins
lead: Hobgoblins can be assigned as a slayer task, with no Slayer level requirement, other than having a Combat Level of 20.

label: Slayer task/Hydras
title: Slayer task/Hydras
lead:
Hydras can be assigned as a slayer task at level 95 Slayer. This is a task exclusive to Konar quo Maten; no other Slayer master can assign hydras.

Despite the hydra task having a weight of 10, Konar has a large array of slayer tasks, so any player seeking a hydra task must either be willing to complete her general tasks or have plenty of slayer points to skip undesirable tasks. Players who wish to have the highest chance of being assigned this task should block metal dragons, wyrms, drakes, abyssal demons, cave krakens, and black demons, as not only can these tasks take a while (even with a cannon) but also have competitive weighting to hydras (15/10/10/9/9/9) respectively, while hydras have a weight of 10. Six block slots will require 300 quest points and players should prioritise the higher weight tasks if they cannot unlock all slots. A seventh slot is unlocked with completion of the Elite Lumbridge Diary. If this slot is unlocked, the player should block fire giants, who also have a weight of 9 and have less ideal spots compared to bloodveld.

label: Slayer task/Ice giants
title: Slayer task/Ice giants
lead:
Ice giants can be assigned as a Slayer task at 50 combat by Vannaka and Krystilia. They are the second strongest generic giants for their category, only slightly stronger than their mossy counterparts, with very slight defensive bonuses and having a 100% weakness to fire spells.

Ice giant tasks are generally not completed by players not training via Wilderness Slayer, as they have very unimpressive drops and many of them are far from a bank.

label: Slayer task/Jellies
title: Slayer task/Jellies
lead:
Jellies can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 52 Slayer and level 57 combat by various medium-level Slayer masters. They are found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon. They are popular to kill similarly to hellhounds due to their high drop rate of hard clue scrolls. While fairly weak, jellies have an unusually high Defence level compared to other similar monsters around their level.

It is not recommended to kill normal jellies in most circumstances as they have a fairly poor drop table and are very far from a bank.

label: Slayer task/Kalphites
title: Slayer task/Kalphites
lead:
Kalphites can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 15 combat by all Slayer masters, with the exception of Wilderness Slayer master Krystilia. Kalphites come in a wide variety of levels, which is why they are possible tasks from all Slayer masters. They can be found in the Kalphite Lair in the north-west Kharidian Desert, as well as in a Slayer task-exclusive area, the Kalphite Cave, just east of Shantay Pass.

Kalphites comes in four varieties: workers, soldiers, and guardians, as well as the boss monster the Kalphite Queen. With the exception of the Queen, all Kalphites use melee attacks. Additionally the soldiers and guardians can induce poison starting at 4 and 6 Hitpoints damage respectively. This poison bypasses protection prayers. Protect from Melee and some type of poison immunity will completely negate damage from the workers, soldiers and guardians.

label: Slayer task/Kurasks
title: Slayer task/Kurasks
lead:
Kurasks can be assigned as a Slayer task by various medium- and high-levelled Slayer masters upon reaching 70 Slayer and 65 combat level.

Kurasks are most commonly found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon, but they can also be found in the Iorwerth Dungeon and Kurask Lair. They attack with somewhat inaccurate crush attacks that can hit up to 11. They are weakest to stab, ranged, and magic attacks.

label: Slayer task/Lesser demon
title: Slayer task/Lesser demon
lead:
Lesser demons can be assigned by Krystilia, Chaeldar, and Vannaka. They are combat level 82, 87, and 94 and all have the same drop table, with the exception of the Wilderness Slayer Cave.

When not killing lesser demons as part of a Krystilia task, players have many spots to choose from to kill lesser demons.

label: Slayer task/Lesser Nagua
title: Slayer task/Lesser Nagua
lead:
Lesser Nagua are a potential Slayer assignment rarely assigned by Konar quo Maten or Chaeldar after completion of Perilous Moons.

Players have three options when assigned Lesser Nagua, depending on their quest completion:
*Players who have completed Perilous Moons can be assigned to kill Nagua at Neypotzli, where Sulphur Nagua can be found.
*Players who have completed The Heart of Darkness can be assigned to kill Nagua at the Ruins of Tapoyauik, where Frost Nagua and Amoxliatl can be found.
*Players who have completed The Final Dawn can also be assigned to kill Nagua at the Crypt of Tonali, where Earthen Nagua can be found.

label: Slayer task/Lizardmen
title: Slayer task/Lizardmen
lead:
Lizardman can be assigned as a Slayer task after being unlocked at a cost of 75 Slayer reward points via the Reptile got ripped ability.

Normal lizardmen come in three forms; a plain level 53 and 62 variant, and the level 75 lizardman brute. These are simple enemies and have a weak poison that starts at 3 damage. They have very few lucrative drops, so these variants are primarily killed for the sake of speeding through a task with a cannon, often at the Lizardman Canyon due to it being a multicombat area.

label: Slayer task/Lizards
title: Slayer task/Lizards
lead: Lizards are unlocked as a Slayer task after Slayer level 22. With a Slayer level of 44, players may kill sulphur lizards or grimy lizards instead.

label: Slayer task/Metal dragons
title: Slayer task/Metal dragons
lead:
Metal dragons can be assigned by high-levelled slayer masters as a potential task.

Players have many options for killing these dragons:

label: Slayer task/Monkeys
title: Slayer task/Monkeys
lead:
Monkeys can be assigned as a slayer task by Turael and Spria. There is no combat or slayer requirement needed to be assigned monkeys. Monkeys are commonly found in tropical areas throughout Gielinor.

Regular monkeys are most commonly killed to complete this task. However, there are high level alternatives locked behind Monkey Madness I and Monkey Madness II, namely Monkey Archers, Monkey Guards, Monkey Zombies, Tortured gorillas, Demonic gorillas, and Maniacal monkeys.

label: Slayer task/Moss giants
title: Slayer task/Moss giants
lead:
Moss giants can be assigned as a Slayer task from Slayer Masters Vannaka, starting from level 40 combat, and Krystilia, at any combat level. Bryophyta can be slain in their stead.

Moss giants are located across Gielinor and most of these locations have safespots. Moss giants have zero defence against every attack style and are 50% weak to fire damage. Their most notable drops are the mossy key (required to loot Bryophyta's chest) and their somewhat valuable seed drop table. The mossy key drop rate is improved to 1/75 while slaying moss giants on task.

label: Slayer task/Nechryael
title: Slayer task/Nechryael
lead:
Nechryael are a type of demon that can be assigned as a slayer task at level 80 Slayer and 85 combat by various Slayer masters. They are notable for their frequent drops of herbs, seeds, and alchable items, making them an extremely good slayer task.

Nechryael attack with melee, and can periodically summon up to two death spawns to assist them in battle. These death spawns are fairly inaccurate with a max hit of 2, but as they attack with typeless melee, Protect from Melee has no effect on them. Uniquely, they are able to attack you in single-combat areas regardless of if you are already in combat. It is recommended to bring food if using Melee or to have runes to cast blood spells if using Magic to kill nechryaels. It is also possible to leave the area and return to lose aggression, but this is impractical in most situations.

label: Slayer task/Ogres
title: Slayer task/Ogres
lead:
Ogres can be assigned as a slayer task at level 40 combat by Vannaka. Ogres are most commonly found in Kandarin.

Along with ogres and Ogress Warriors and Shamans, Mogres, Zogres, and Skogres can be killed to satisfy the task. Jogres do not count towards the task.

label: Slayer task/Pirate
title: Slayer task/Pirate
lead:
Pirates can be assigned as a Slayer task from Krystilia.

Pirates can be found at level 55 Wilderness in the Pirates' Hideout. A lockpick is required to enter. They are combat level 26 and have a very minimal droptable. They are located in single-way combat.

label: Slayer task/Pyrefiends
title: Slayer task/Pyrefiends
lead:
Pyrefiends can be assigned as a Slayer task at level 30 Slayer and level 25 combat.

Pyrefiends attack with magic-based melee, meaning armour that provides magic defence should be worn or Protect from Melee should be used with Prayer equipment, alternatively Prayer flick.

label: Slayer task/Rats
title: Slayer task/Rats
lead: Rats can be assigned as a slayer task from Turael and Spria. They have no requirements to be assigned. There are a wide variety of rats that can count toward the task, but the most commonly killed are rats and giant rats, which are low-level, rarely deal damage, and practically ubiquitous. Scurrius can be fought for greater xp and profit, although his minions will also decrement the task, reducing how many times the boss can be fought on task. Brine rats are accessible during Olaf's Quest, and drop medium clues and the elusive brine sabre. Hell-rat behemoths can be accessed after Freeing Evil Dave, and drop full spice shakers for spicy stews. Crypt rat and giant crypt rat variations require completion of Priest in Peril for access to Morytania and may be slain by players for the higher Slayer experience reward or for changing their reward potential inside the Barrows minigame. It is recommended to use Rat bone weapons as it has greatly increased effectiveness against rats.

label: Slayer task/Red dragons
title: Slayer task/Red dragons
lead:
Red dragons can be assigned as a Slayer task after unlocking Seeing red for 50 Slayer reward points and requiring partial completion of Dragon Slayer I to receive the Anti-dragon shield.

Adult and brutal variants use melee and dragonfire, so sufficient dragonfire protection is needed to avoid taking heavy damage. Alternatively, using Protect from Magic will suffice.

label: Slayer task/Scabarites
title: Slayer task/Scabarites
lead:
Scabarites refers to any of the minions of Scabaras. They are fairly strong monsters that can hit rather hard. To receive them as a Slayer assignment, players must have completed most of the Contact! quest.

When given Scabarites as a Slayer task, only small scarabs, scarab swarms, locust riders, and scarab mages will count, along with the Giant Scarab in Nightmare Zone.

label: Slayer task/Scorpions
title: Slayer task/Scorpions
lead:
Scorpions can be assigned as a slayer task at level 7 combat by various low end Slayer masters and are generally meant as tasks for beginners. Scorpions attack with melee and a few certain varieties are capable of poisoning. Interestingly various fightable lobsters also counts as scorpions.
Scorpions have very limited drop tables, usually only dropping ensouled scorpion heads and beginner clue scrolls.

Players can also kill Scorpia as part of a scorpion task; however, she is located in extremely deep (50+) Wilderness in a multicombat area, and freezes are required in order to kill the boss efficiently. It is a very popular player killing spot, so players should not bring items they are unwilling to lose.

label: Slayer task/Sea snakes
title: Slayer task/Sea snakes
lead:
Sea snakes can be assigned as a slayer task by Vannaka at level 40 Slayer and level 50 combat after the completion of Royal Trouble. They are found in the Miscellania and Etceteria Dungeon, which can be entered during and after the quest. They attack with melee and are poisonous so antipoisons of any variety are strongly recommended. Both variants share the same drop table, although the hatchling drop regular bones whereas the young drop big bones (and by extension long and curved bones).

Dwarven multicannons can be used in the dungeon, although it is in single combat.

label: Slayer task/Shades
title: Slayer task/Shades
lead: Shades can be assigned as a slayer task, with no Slayer level requirement by Mazchna and Vannaka. Level 159 Shades may be found in Stronghold of Security and level 140 Shades may be found in Catacombs of Kourend. The Loar Shades in Mort'ton count for a slayer task as well, and are typically preferred as they are much faster to kill. They are susceptible to the Salve Amulet and Crumble Undead (however, their 40% weakness to wind spells means that Wind Bolt will do more damage than Crumble Undead for the same cost of a chaos rune, providing the player has 35 Magic or more). It is worth noting that combat experience gained while fighting the shades in the Stronghold of Security is drastically reduced; the player will gain 1 experience for 10 damage dealt.

label: Slayer task/Skeletons
title: Slayer task/Skeletons
lead:
Skeletons are undead monsters that can be assigned as tasks at combat level 15 by various low-level Slayer masters. They are often found in cemeteries and dungeons. A good strategy to kill them is to use melee with a weapon with crush bonuses (such as a Viggora's chainmace) and a salve amulet or salve amulet (e), due to their low crush defence.

Another strategy to kill them would be with magic. Many skeletons have an elemental weakness to earth spells, making those a very effective option.

label: Slayer task/Smoke devils
title: Slayer task/Smoke devils
lead:
Smoke devils can be assigned as a slayer task at level 93 Slayer and level 85 combat by high-end Slayer masters. They are only found in the Smoke Devil Dungeon south of Castle Wars and can only be fought if on a task. They attack with magical ranged. As with dust devils, players must wear a facemask or slayer helm when fighting smoke devils, or their attacks will always deal moderate damage that also drains stats.

Players may choose between killing smoke devils or their boss variant, the thermonuclear smoke devil.

label: Slayer task/Spiders
title: Slayer task/Spiders
lead:
Spiders can be assigned as a Slayer task by Turael, Spria, and Krystilia. They can be found in numerous places across Gielinor.

Most spiders generally use melee, but a few stronger ones will also use Ranged and/or Magic alongside them. Low-levelled spiders are generally weak to all forms of combat, though higher-levelled spiders are weaker to crush.

label: Slayer task/Spiritual creatures
title: Slayer task/Spiritual creatures
lead:
Spiritual creatures are a potential slayer assignment given by medium and high-levelled Slayer Masters after completion of Death Plateau, a combat level of 80 and either 60 Strength or Agility with a minimum Slayer level of 63 in order to be assigned them.

There are three types of spiritual creatures players can kill as part of a task: spiritual rangers, the weakest at 63 Slayer, warriors at 68 Slayer, and mages, the only NPCs that drop dragon boots, at 83 Slayer.

label: Slayer task/Suqah
title: Slayer task/Suqah
lead:
Suqah can be a good Slayer task, due to the relatively high amount of experience per hour that can be gained from killing them with the help of a dwarf multicannon. However, the use of a dwarf multicannon and toxic blowpipe will also result in a loss of coins due to their lack of valuable drops.

If using the northern area on Lunar Isle, players should pray Protect from Magic and wear armour with high Melee defence, as these Suqah attack with both a melee attack and a magic attack.

label: Slayer task/Trolls
title: Slayer task/Trolls
lead:
Trolls can be assigned as a Slayer task at 60 combat level by various Slayer masters. Trolls are, for the most part, found in the Fremennik Province and north of Burthorpe.

Trolls fought in quests all count towards the Slayer task, with the exception of sea trolls. The bosses can be fought again in the Nightmare Zone.

label: Slayer task/Turoth
title: Slayer task/Turoth
lead:
Turoth can be assigned as a Slayer task from Vannaka, Nieve/Steve, Chaeldar, or Konar quo Maten, requiring 55 Slayer and 60 combat. They are melee based, and as such Protect from Melee will negate all of their damage. They are only found in the Fremennik Slayer Dungeon.

Turoth can only be damaged with leaf-bladed weapons, broad arrows and bolts, or the Magic Dart spell. Attacking with any other weapons or spells will always deal 0 damage.

label: Slayer task/TzHaar
title: Slayer task/TzHaar
lead:
TzHaar are an ancient race dwelling underneath the Karamja Volcano in Mor Ul Rek that can be assigned as a Slayer task if the player has unlocked the perk Hot Stuff for 100 slayer points.

TzHaar come in four varieties: the artisans TzHaar-Hur, the sages TzHaar-Mej, hunters TzHaar-Xil, and guards TzHaar-Kets. Killing any of these while wearing a charged Ring of wealth increases their chances of dropping gems (and Onyx bolt tips for level 221 TzHaar-Kets).

label: Slayer task/Vampyres
title: Slayer task/Vampyres
lead:
Vampyres can be assigned as a Slayer task by various Slayer masters once the player has completed Priest in Peril and achieved at least level 35 combat. Mostly confined to the Morytania region, access to different variants of vampyres is usually tied to progression within the Myreque questline.

Prior to the Actual Vampyre Slayer unlock, vampyre tasks can only be assigned by Slayer masters Mazchna and Vannaka and only 10 to 20 assigned at a time.

label: Slayer task/Warped creatures
title: Slayer task/Warped creatures
lead:
Warped creatures can be assigned as a slayer task starting at level 56 Slayer by Chaeldar, Konar, Nieve, and Duradel, and will only be assigned if the player has unlocked them with the Warped Reality slayer point reward. Warped creatures are found exclusively in the Poison Waste Dungeon, requiring completion of The Path of Glouphrie.

Players must have the crystal chime in their inventory to fight them, otherwise they will be invulnerable.

label: Slayer task/Waterfiends
title: Slayer task/Waterfiends
lead:
Waterfiends can be assigned as a slayer task at 75 combat level by two Slayer masters, Konar quo Maten and Duradel. Waterfiends can only be assigned as a slayer task after being granted access to the Ancient Cavern. They are found in the Ancient Cavern, Kraken Cove, and Iorwerth Dungeon. Iorwerth Dungeon is only accessible after completing Song of the Elves.

Waterfiends attack with Magic and magical Ranged so protection Prayers cannot be used to negate all of their damage. However, both types of attacks roll against the player's Magic Defence, so armour with Magic Defence bonuses, such as Dragonhide Armour or Karil's armour, is most helpful when fighting them. A saturated or imbued heart can also help slightly increase magic defence. Protect from Missiles will be the most helpful if they are dealing too much damage.

label: Slayer task/Wolves
title: Slayer task/Wolves
lead:
Wolves can be assigned as a slayer task at 20 combat level by Turael and Mazchna. They can be found in a variety of locations around Gielinor. The task is very straightforward as regular Wolves only attack with their fairly accurate melee bites; it is recommended to either safespot them or keep Protect from Melee on at all times.

One fast way to complete a wolves Slayer task is with a Dwarf multicannon in the Stronghold of Security, as it has a large amount of wolves.

label: Slayer task/Wyrms
title: Slayer task/Wyrms
lead:
Wyrms are draconic creatures in the lower level of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon in Mount Karuulm, requiring 62 Slayer to kill. Boots of stone, boots of brimstone, or granite boots must be worn to protect against the extreme heat of the dungeon floor unless the elite Kourend & Kebos Diary has been completed.

Attacking outside of direct melee range will cause wyrms to only attack with Magic, so Protect from Magic will negate all of their damage. Wyrms have a flat armour value of 1, but this is not a big concern with their low stats.

label: Slayer task/Zombies
title: Slayer task/Zombies
lead:
Zombies can be assigned as a slayer task at level 10 combat by various Slayer masters. Zombies are most often found in places that depict death, such as graveyards.

Monkey Zombies, Undead chickens, Undead cows, Undead Druids, Undead ones, Vorkath, Zogres, and Zombie rats can all be killed to satisfy the task. The zombies found in Tarn's Lair do not count towards the task, nor does the Zombies Champion.

label: Slayer task/Zygomites
title: Slayer task/Zygomites
lead:
Zygomites can be assigned to level 60 combat and level 57 slayer by Chaeldar, Konar quo Maten, Nieve, and Duradel. Zygomites cannot be killed unless a fungicide spray has been used to deliver the final blow.

Zygomites can be safespotted by trapping them and moving out of their attack range. For instance, in Zanaris near the Cosmic Altar, players may trap them using a pillar and standing back near the mysterious ruins.

label: Slayer training
title: Slayer training
lead:
.]]
Slayer is a skill that allows players to kill monsters that may otherwise be immune to damage. Players must visit a Slayer Master, who will assign them a task to kill certain monsters. Slayer experience is roughly equal to a slain monster's Hitpoints and is awarded each time the player kills an assigned monster.

This guide focuses on the fastest ways to train Slayer. While there are no real requirements to begin Slayer training, it is strongly recommended to have fairly high combat stats and to have completed many quests. This enables the ability to block more undesired Slayer assignments (known as "block slots," which are applied using the "[[#Cancelling and blocking tasks|block task]]" option, and have quest point requirements). High combat stats increase damage output considerably and allow the player to use the best equipment available. Having a higher combat level also gives access to better Slayer Masters, as the low-level Slayer Masters have worse task lists and give fewer Slayer reward points than the higher-level ones. Alternatively, players may choose to train combat stats while in the process of training Slayer.

label: sloop
title: sloop
lead:
A sloop is a medium-sized boat that can be purchased at level 50 Sailing from a shipwright for coins. The sloop supports a maximum of 5 NPC crew members and 10 players.

Compared to smaller boats, sloops have more facility hotspots and crew slots but cannot fit into all the waterways a skiff or a raft can. A sloop is useful for port tasks, shipwreck salvaging, ship combat, and deep sea trawling, but less useful for exploration and Barracuda Trials.

label: Small fishing net
title: Small fishing net
lead: A small fishing net is used to catch fish such as shrimps, anchovies, karambwanji, minnows, and monkfish. Nets can be purchased from various fishing shops for 5 coins. It can also be obtained for free from either the Fishing tutor south of Lumbridge near the coast east of the swamp, or from the Spirit Angler at the Ruins of Unkah.
