title: Small Table
lead: A small wooden table. Found in Slayer Tower.

label: Smashed cage
title: Smashed cage
lead: The Smashed cage is the result of the player rolling a large boulder downhill onto the Unicorn and the cage trapping it in the Underground Pass during the Underground Pass quest, it can be searched for a Unicorn horn. The horn is required to proceed further in the quest, and the only way to obtain it is through killing the unicorn by smashing the cage with the boulder.

label: Smashed chair
title: Smashed chair
lead: Smashed chairs are found in various locations in many different colours. They serve no purpose other than aesthetics.

label: Smashed glass
title: Smashed glass
lead: Smashed glass is a useless item found in several places. Three of them can be found in the southernmost house in Mort'ton. Fighting with holy water results in smashed glass appearing on the ground. Finally, it appears after a Mourner throws a potion that reduces a player's combat stats. It is similar to broken glass but it can be traded to other players and can not be used to light a torch.

label: Smashed table
title: Smashed table
lead:
A smashed table is found in Ah Za Rhoon during the Shilo Village quest. The player can look at it, which produces the dialogue "This table might be useful with some adjustment." and attempting to craft it offers the player three options: a ladder, a crude raft and a pole vault.

Only a raft can be successfully crafted, granting 5 Crafting experience. The resulting raft can be boarded in order to escape Ah Za Rhoon. Alternatively, players may walk south and exit through the waterfall, or simply teleport out.

label: Smith (disambiguation)
title: Smith (disambiguation)
lead:
Smith may also refer to:
*Smith is a pirate smith at Mos Le'Harmless.
*Smithing, a skill that players can use to smith weapons and armour out of metal bars - players who do so may be referred to as a "smith".
*Ali the Smith, a blacksmith found in Al Kharid.
*Asgarnia Smith, an NPC that starts the Desert Treasure I quest.
*Assistant Le Smith, a gnome that operates the balloon transport system.
*Orlando Smith, an NPC found in the basement of the Varrock Museum.

label: Smithing
title: Smithing
lead: Smithing is a production skill through which players create a wide variety of metal items from ore and metal bars. It is the companion skill of Mining, which generates raw materials used in Smithing. Ores acquired from Mining are smelted into metal bars at furnaces, and then hammered into items at anvils. Many smithable items are useful in combat, quests, and the training of a number of other skills such as Crafting and Fletching.

label: Smithing (interface item)
title: Smithing (interface item)
lead:
The Smithing is an interface item that can be seen in the Smithing skill guide representing the Smithing.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Smithing catalyst (Blast Furnace)
title: Smithing catalyst (Blast Furnace)
lead:
Smithing catalyst is an entity presumably visible at the Blast Furnace after smithing catalyst is deposited on the conveyor belt, before it goes into the melting pot.

It is unconfirmed if this can be observed in game.

label: Smithing gauntlets
title: Smithing gauntlets
lead:
Smithing gauntlets might refer to:
*Goldsmith gauntlets, a reward from the Family Crest quest which increase experience from making gold bars
*Smiths gloves, a piece of the smiths' uniform set which gives a 20% chance of speeding up anvil Smithing actions by 1 tick
*Smiths gloves (i), a combination of the above item and ice gloves

label: Smithing Level Up!
title: Smithing Level Up!
lead: Smithing Level Up! is a jingle for levelling Smithing.

label: Smithing Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Smithing Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Smithing Level Up! (Unlocks) is a jingle for levelling Smithing.

label: Smithing/Experience table
title: Smithing/Experience table
lead: This table shows all possible experience sources for Smithing in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Smithing level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

label: Smiths' Uniform
title: Smiths' Uniform
lead:
The Smiths' Uniform is the skilling outfit for Smithing. The complete outfit costs Foundry Reputation at the Giants' Foundry Reward Shop. Individual items can be resold to the shop for 80% of their purchase price by using them on Kovac.

Each piece gives a 20% chance to speed up Smithing actions performed at an anvil by 1 tick (from 5 to 4), up to a 100% chance with the full set. Each piece also gives a 20% chance to give increased progress on preforms in the Giants' Foundry, with the whole outfit giving a 100% chance. The bonus is 5% increased progress per action for the trip hammer, and 10% for the grindstone and polishing wheel.

label: Smoke
title: Smoke
lead:
__NOTOC__
Smoke may refer to:

label: Smoke (game mechanic)
title: Smoke (game mechanic)
lead:
Smoke is a game mechanic occurring in the Smoke Dungeon as well as the Smoke Devil Dungeon. It causes the player to take 10 damage every 12 seconds (20 ticks), though this cannot reduce the player's Hitpoints below 1.

Wearing a gas mask, facemask, Slayer helmet or Slayer helmet (i) will prevent the smoke from damaging the player.

label: Smoke devil/Strategies
title: Smoke devil/Strategies
lead: Smoke devils are a slayer monster requiring level 93 Slayer in addition to an active slayer task to kill. When using Ice Barrage and a cannon, smoke devils can provide Slayer experience rates of up to 180,000 per hour, depending on the player's efficiency; however, a rate of 120,000 is more realistic. Valuable common drops like the rune chainbody as well as fire and air battlestaves generally compensate the rune and cannonball costs, and the rarer occult necklace drops can provide a net profit.

label: Smoke spells
title: Smoke spells
lead:
Smoke spells are one of four types of Ancient Magicks combat spells and the only type of spells that can inflict poison on their targets. They are the weakest of the Ancient Magicks, but can be used to provide passive damage on longer fights through poison damage.

Smoke spells have a 1/8 chance to poison on a successful hit. When using the multi-target spells, poison can be inflicted on up to nine targets in a 3x3 grid around the targeted enemy. Poison severity for the lower-level spells (Smoke Rush and Smoke Burst) is 10, while poison severity for the higher-level spells (Smoke Blitz and Smoke Barrage) is 20. Poison severity decreases once and inflicts \lfloor \frac{Severity + 4}{5} \rfloor poison damage every 30 ticks (18 seconds). All variants of the ancient sceptre increase poison severity by 10%.

label: Smouldering
title: Smouldering
lead:
Smouldering may refer to:

* Smouldering stone, an item used to upgrade the dragon axe, dragon harpoon, and dragon pickaxe into the infernal axe, infernal harpoon, and infernal pickaxe
* Smouldering pot, an item used in the Ratcatchers quest
* Healing items dropped by tormented demons:
** Smouldering pile of flesh, which restores hitpoints
** Smouldering gland, which restores Prayer points
** Smouldering heart, which boosts combat stats

label: Snaarldor
title: Snaarldor
lead:
Snaarldor was a high-ranking ourg general during the God Wars who led a small army of Bandosian troops over the River Salve into Viggora's Folly. His exploits are detailed in the lore book, The living statues.

In an attempt to gain more recruits, Snaarldor attempted to bring two statues, Dawn and Dusk, to life. Once he had thought he gained their allegiance, he gave a speech detailing their instructions. These instructions included directives to fight against the forces of Zamorak. He had a Dorgeshuun assistant who he often berated, even though the assistant knew that Viggora's Folly was constructed with Zamorakian magic. The two gargoyles began attacking Snaarldor; Snaarldor soon engaged in a mid-air brawl with one of the statues, chopping one of its wings clean off as he fell into the swamp below, though he survived the fall. Upon recovering, he immediately ordered his remaining forces to retreat; though his fate is unknown, it is likely he perished in another battle during the God Wars.

label: snail
title: snail
lead:
A snail (Achatina acidia) is an attackable monster found within Mort Myre Swamp.

Snail may also refer to:

label: Snail meat
title: Snail meat
lead:
Snail meat may refer to:

;Raw snails
*Thin snail
*Lean snail
*Fat snail

label: Snake
title: Snake
lead: Snakes (Serpentes Fellis) are serpentine monsters primarily found on Karamja. Unlike bush snakes, these snakes do not inflict poison.

label: Snake (disambiguation)
title: Snake (disambiguation)
lead:
__NOTOC__
Snake may refer to:

label: Snake weed
title: Snake weed
lead:
Snake weed is a herb found by searching a marshy jungle vine, twenty of which can be found south-west of Tai Bwo Wannai, on the coast of western Karamja. It is also dropped in grimy form by jogres and tribesmen. It can be used as a secondary ingredient in Herblore to make relicym's balm or Sanfew serum. It is not possible to store it in a reagent pouch.

Snake weed is first encountered during the Jungle Potion quest, but is also used during Zogre Flesh Eaters as well as Legends' Quest; therefore it may be wise to take extras during Jungle Potion.

label: Snakeskin armour
title: Snakeskin armour
lead: Snakeskin armour is a set of ranged armour requiring 30 Ranged and 30 Defence to wear. All of the pieces can be made through the Crafting skill from tanned snakeskins. It takes a total of 46 snakeskins and 53 Crafting to make a full set, or 48 snakeskins and 56 Crafting when including the shield. The full set (excluding the shield) can be stored in an armour case inside the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: Snakeweed mixture
title: Snakeweed mixture
lead:
A snakeweed mixture is an unfinished potion made via the Herblore skill. Players make it by using a snake weed on a vial of water.

Using a rogue's purse herb on it will make a Relicym's balm.

label: snapdragon
title: snapdragon
lead:
Snapdragon is a herb which can be cleaned at level 59 Herblore. It may be grown from a snapdragon seed with a Farming level of 62, granting 98.5 Farming experience for every snapdragon grown. Once planted, the herb takes 80 minutes to fully grow.

Snapdragons are used to make super restore potions and sanfew serums with a Herblore level of 63 and a Herblore level of 65 respectively. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a snapdragon potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

label: Snapdragon potion (unf)
title: Snapdragon potion (unf)
lead: A snapdragon potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a snapdragon on a vial of water, requiring 63 Herblore. Using red spiders' eggs on a snapdragon potion (unf) with 63 Herblore yields a super restore(3) and 142.5 Herblore experience.

label: Snape grass
title: Snape grass
lead:
Snape grass is a Herblore secondary ingredient that can be grown through the Farming skill at level 61 with snape grass seeds. 8 snape grass are needed to protect growing potato cactus.

It is used to make prayer potions and fishing potions. It is also used when making the hangover cure quest item. When placed in a compost bin, snape grass will create supercompost.

label: Snare
title: Snare
lead:
Snare is a level 50 Magic spell. Casting Snare on an opponent will prevent it from moving for 16 ticks (9.6 seconds). When used on a player and the snare is about to wear off, the snared player will receive this message in their chatbox: The holding effect is beginning to fade. Players can increase the binding duration by equipping swampbark armour; the helm, body, and legs will increase the duration by 2 ticks (1.2 seconds) each, up to a maximum of 22 ticks (13.2 seconds).

Snare gives 61 Magic experience if it successfully hits the target, or 60 experience if it splashes.

label: Snelm
title: Snelm
lead: Snelm is a portmanteau of the words "snail" and "helm". Players can create a snelm through the Crafting skill at level 15, by using a chisel on the shell of any snail found in Mort Myre swamp or near the Haunted Woods. There are a variety of colours for both round and pointed snelms, and they give considerable protection against the snails of Morytania.

label: Snip Snip
title: Snip Snip
lead: Snip Snip is a crab who lives underwater in the Mogre Camp, first mentioned in Postbag from the Hedge. He writes a poem which laments how his Uncle Joe (a rock crab) was killed for experience by an adventurer. In it, he also asks that his kind not be killed, lest they live in the sea forever.

label: Sniping
title: Sniping
lead:
Sniping is the act of targeting and seizing an item or items for oneself by beating out the opposition. In other words, to snipe is to target and gain a desirable item by outbidding, such as in the Grand Exchange, or by beating another player to it.

When Jagex releases names, it is common practice for players to snipe names. Name sniping on multiple accounts has led to all offenders and their accounts being banned especially if real-world trading or employing the use of bots.

label: Snow imp costume
title: Snow imp costume
lead:
The Snow imp costume is a holiday reward received from completing a Christmas event from 2017 onwards. The costume gives no bonus to any stats. If the costume was lost during the 2017 Christmas event, it may be reclaimed by speaking to Iffie in the Varrock clothes shop.

If lost or destroyed after the event, the outfit can be reclaimed from Diango in Draynor Village. In addition, all of the costume items may be stored in the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: Snowman (disambiguation)
title: Snowman (disambiguation)
lead:
Snowman may refer to:
* Snowman, a historical snowman formerly found in Falador Park
* Snowman (2021 Christmas event)
* Snowman (2022 Christmas event)
* Snowman (2023 Christmas event)
* Snowman (2024 Christmas event)

label: Snowy knight (interface item)
title: Snowy knight (interface item)
lead:
The Snowy knight is an interface item that can be seen in the Hunter skill guide representing the Snowy knight.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Socks
title: Socks
lead:
Socks may refer to one of the following:
* Ankou socks, a rare reward from master Treasure Trails
* Socks of ruin, an item obtained as part of Crack the Clue III
* Smelly sock, an item obtained from rummaging through the spooky cauldron

label: Soda ash
title: Soda ash
lead:
Soda ash is made into Molten glass to make glass items in Crafting. Soda ash is made using seaweed, giant seaweed, swamp weed, or edible seaweed on a range, oven, or fire. Smelting it with a bucket of sand in a furnace or the Lunar spell Superglass Make produces molten glass.

It can be purchased from Trader Stan's Trading Post at charter ships for coins; the closest one to a bank is in Port Khazard. Another option close to a bank is the Corsair Cove shop, which is about 10 tiles farther from a bank but may be more likely to have soda ash in stock.

label: Sofa (disambiguation)
title: Sofa (disambiguation)
lead:
Sofas may refer to:

* Sofa
* Sofa (Anti-Santa)
* Sofa (Darkmeyer)
* Sofa (2014 Halloween event)

label: Soft cheese
title: Soft cheese
lead:
The soft cheese is an item only available to Jagex Moderators. It has two right-click options affecting the game's graphics:

*Activate - turns on anti-aliasing, causing edges to smooth. 
*Deactivate - turns off anti-aliasing, causing edges to turn back to normal.

label: soft clay
title: soft clay
lead:
Soft clay is used to create items in the Crafting and Construction skills and to make magic tablets. It can be created by using a container of water such as a vial of water, jug of water, or bucket of water on clay, by using the Humidify spell, or by mining clay rocks whilst wearing a bracelet of clay. It is used on a potter's wheel to craft various Crafting items.

The only place to mine soft clay directly is in the Trahaearn mine, where soft clay rocks can be found. In addition, wearing a bracelet of clay in this mine can yield 2 soft clays per action, whereas mining clay rocks elsewhere yields only a single soft clay per action.

label: Soil
title: Soil
lead: Soil can be found throughout the digsite area, and plays an important role in The Dig Site quest. Depending on the type of digs in the area, players can use their trowel or rock pick, along with a specimen brush and specimen jar in their inventory, to dig up several items. Soil can also be found on Fossil Island in the Museum Camp.

label: Sojourn
title: Sojourn
lead:
Sojourn is a music track unlocked around Trollheim and the entrance to the Troll Stronghold. It can also be unlocked without having completed any quests, using Classic mode on the eastern side of the Mountain Camp.

During the fight with the Giant Roc, Roc and Roll plays on the plateau with My Arm instead.

label: Soldier
title: Soldier
lead:
Soldier may refer to:
* Kalphite Soldiers found in the Kalphite Lair
* Sergeant Damien and his random event
* Soldier found injured at the Death Plateau
* Soldiers of the Yanille army
* Soldiers of the Burthorpe Imperial Guard
* Toy soldiers made in a player-owned house workshop
* Vespine soldiers, offspring of Vespula

label: Soldier (Burthorpe, sitting)
title: Soldier (Burthorpe, sitting)
lead: Three soldiers are sitting in front of a campfire in Burthorpe eating a drumstick, in the midst of the camp where other members of the Burthorpe Imperial Guard are training. Although the player can attempt to speak to them, doing so will only print the game message: The soldier is busy eating.

label: Soldier (Death Plateau)
title: Soldier (Death Plateau)
lead:
The wounded soldier is located south of the Death Plateau, troll territory, and he is featured prominently in the Death Plateau quest. He was hit by thrower trolls and is unable to head back to Burthorpe, warning players not to head on further. He is the brother of Harold.

After seeing him, players can head south-west on the winding mountain path to reach Tenzing's hut. If proceeding north, however, it is strongly advised to activate Protect from Missiles to negate the thrower trolls' bombardment of Ranged attacks.

label: Soldier (Lizardman kill count)
title: Soldier (Lizardman kill count)
lead: The soldier is a member of the Shayzien Army found resting near the entrance to the Lizardman Canyon. He can be asked for the kill counts of both Lizardmen and Lizardman shamans inside the canyon, as well as the number of players currently present in either side of it.

label: Soldier (Yanille)
title: Soldier (Yanille)
lead:
Soldiers are similar to Guards except they are higher level and are found only in Yanille. They are under the command of Colonel Radick.

They appear to be wearing a Steel med helm, a Steel chainbody, Leather gloves and Leather boots. They also wield a Steel longsword as a weapon.

label: Solomon Lamescus
title: Solomon Lamescus
lead: Solomon Lamescus is a vampyre noble partially responsible for managing the Sanguinesti region. A prominent member of House Drakan, Solomon appeared in the 19th Postbag from the Hedge on behalf of Lord Lowerniel Vergidiyad Drakan. He appears to be rather civil, and without intense cruelty (at least by vampyre standards), as he writes in a professional, albeit biased, manner.

id: page:song of the elves/warped library guide
label: Song of the Elves/Warped Library guide
title: Song of the Elves/Warped Library guide
lead: Talk to Lord Ieuan Amlodd to be transported into the Grand Library. If you log out inside, you will be kicked out but your progress will be saved.

id: page:song of the elves/warped library quick guide
label: Song of the Elves/Warped Library quick guide
title: Song of the Elves/Warped Library quick guide
lead:
Note: It is recommended to charge your teleport crystals now if you're running low, since the area becomes instanced later on and you cannot do this until much later.

Talk to Lord Ieuan Amlodd to be transported into the Grand Library.

label: Sorcerer's Tower
title: Sorcerer's Tower
lead:
The Sorcerer's Tower is a four-story tower south of Seers' Village. It is the residence of Thormac the sorcerer.

At the Sorcerer's Tower, players may begin the Scorpion Catcher quest by talking to Thormac, the completion of which allows the player to pay Thormac 40,000 coins to enchant any elemental battlestaff into a mystic staff.

label: Sorcerer's Tower Portal
title: Sorcerer's Tower Portal
lead: The Sorcerer's Tower portal is one of the three teleportation portals found on the top floor of the Wizards' Guild. Located on the western wall of the guild, entering the portal will teleport the player to Sorcerer's Tower, south of Seers' Village.

label: Sorceress's Garden/Autumn
title: Sorceress's Garden/Autumn
lead: The Autumn Garden is available starting at level 45 Thieving. It is located south of the teleport spawn point.

label: Sorceress's Garden/Spring
title: Sorceress's Garden/Spring
lead: The Spring Garden is available starting at Level 25 Thieving. It is located east of the teleport spawn point.

label: Sorceress's Garden/Summer
title: Sorceress's Garden/Summer
lead: The Summer Garden is available starting at level 65 Thieving. It is located north of the teleport spawn point.

label: Sorceress's Garden/Winter
title: Sorceress's Garden/Winter
lead: The Winter Garden is available for all levels of Thieving. It is located west of the teleport spawn point.

label: Soul
title: Soul
lead:
__NOTOC__
Soul may refer to:

label: Soul rune
title: Soul rune
lead: Soul runes are one of the runes used to cast spells in the Magic skill. It is used for the strongest curse spells, the teleport-other spells, Enchant Crossbow Bolt (Dragonstone), Blood Barrage, the shadow spells, and most Reanimation spells. Soul runes are also used in charging Tumeken's shadow, the soul bearer, and Kharedst's memoirs, as well as creating Elidinis' ward (f).

label: Soul Split
title: Soul Split
lead:
Soul Split is an overhead prayer currently used by two bosses: Nex and the Phantom Muspah. It is not useable by players.

Nex, when using Soul Split, will heal a small percentage of her health for every successful hit she inflicts on up to three players. She will use this as soon as her fifth phase, the Zaros phase, begins.

label: Soul Stone
title: Soul Stone
lead:
The Soul Stone is a mysterious artefact that was fought over by Armadylean and Bandosian forces on the Isle of Souls during the God Wars. The stone was eventually claimed by Bandos, who evidently used it to destroy not only the Armadyleans but his own army as well. This resulted in some of those slain becoming ancient ghosts, unable to move on to the next world. The current location of the stone is unknown.

The artefact is only directly mentioned by name via a message carved into the wall of the basement of the Crumbling Tower.

label: Soul Wars Beta
title: Soul Wars Beta
lead:
Players who linked their Old School RuneScape and Amazon Prime Gaming accounts were able to playtest Soul Wars before the full release. Free-to-play players were also able to playtest the minigame despite it being members only.

This was announced in the Gielinor Gazette for December 2020.

label: Soul Wars cape
title: Soul Wars cape
lead:
Soul Wars cape may refer to:

* 
*

label: Soulbark armour
title: Soulbark armour
lead: Soulbark armour was a set of improved bloodbark armour, proposed alongside the Warding skill. They were a set of mage robes that would have required level 70 Magic and Defence to wear. In order to ward the set, players required level 80 Warding, along with moonfly silk and soulbark. While bloodbark armour was later approved as an addition to Shades of Mort'ton, soulbark armour has not been added elsewhere.

label: Soulless
title: Soulless
lead:
Soulless are soulless humans found within the Underground Pass. They are aggressive and retreat at low health, and they do not drop anything besides bones.

The Soulless are humans who have entered the Underground Pass and fell under the control of Iban. Those who resist are locked in cages, being subjected to Iban's voice until they deteriorate to become the half-soulless. They are seen as still visibly human, rocking back and forth with extremely pale skin. From here, they deteriorate further into Soulless.

label: Sound effects
title: Sound effects
lead:
Sound effects are short pieces of audio used throughout the game.

Unlike music tracks and jingles, these are not files being played through the soundbank, and thus several can be played at the same time. Sound effects can only be a maximum of 10 seconds and thus they are commonly played together and in sequence to create a lot of the sounds ingame.

label: Soundbank
title: Soundbank
lead:
The soundbank is a bank of instruments that the game uses to play Music, since 6 March 2007, the game has used its own soundbank, no longer depending on the systems sound capabilities and letting jagex give the game a distinct sound.

This soundbank also allows new instruments to be added to the game, as featured in The Fat Lady Sings and Boss Moosic. These are commonly backported from instruments added to the soundbank in rs2. In addition to instruments, sound effects can be played, as seen on Nora's Broken Record (Grim Tales).

label: Soundscape
title: Soundscape
lead:
Soundscape is a music track that is unlocked at the areas directly north west and west of Yanille, including the Castle Wars Lobby.

If music area type is set to Classic, it unlocks at the Feldip Hills glider area. It is one of the few tracks that plays has no overlap in unlock area between Classic and Modern mode.

label: Soundtrack
title: Soundtrack
lead: Soundtracks or Albums are releases of Old School RuneScape music

label: Soup (disambiguation)
title: Soup (disambiguation)
lead:
Soup may refer to:
* Soup, the Sailing pet
* Green gloop soup, a Dorgeshuun delicacy
* Rock soup, made during The Fremennik Trials
* Stew
** Incomplete stew
** Uncooked stew
** Burnt stew
* Spicy stew
* Curry
** Uncooked curry
** Burnt curry

label: South Brimhaven mine
title: South Brimhaven mine
lead:
The South Brimhaven mine (also known as the Brimhaven Dungeon mine) is located south-west of Brimhaven by the entrance to Brimhaven Dungeon. The mine contains 6 gold rocks. Due to its large distance from a bank and few gold rocks, it is not recommended for any use, even if you have your house in Brimhaven. The mine is not easy to reach, and far from any banks. The low amount of rocks makes it an inefficient place to train mining or obtain gold ore, especially compared to the North Brimhaven mine with 10 gold rocks and a gold ore spawn closeby.

The mine is also a possible crash site for a shooting star.

label: South Crandor mine
title: South Crandor mine
lead: The South Crandor mine consists of two mining spots very close to one another on the southern portion of the island of Crandor. Access to this mine is obtained by traversing the tunnel entered from the Karamja Volcano, or as a one-time deal, through a ship from the Dragon Slayer I quest. The closest bank to these mines are in Draynor Village for free players and in Mor Ul Rek for members.

label: South Falador Farm
title: South Falador Farm
lead:
The South Falador Farm is a large farm between Falador and Port Sarim. Found in the north-eastern edge of the farm, there is a herb patch, a flower patch, and two allotment patches that can be used to train Farming. A tool leprechaun and compost bin are located nearby, and Elstan will watch over your crops for you if you pay him. Players that have completed the Medium Falador Diary will receive 10% more Farming experience from these patches.

In the farm building, Sarah runs a Farming shop that stocks various farming items, such as sacks and baskets. The building also has a loom, which can be used to created certain items using Crafting.

label: South Varrock farm
title: South Varrock farm
lead: The South Varrock farm is a large farm in Lumbridge, north of Groats' farm and outside the walls of Varrock. The farm features a wheat field, sheep, rams, and a master farmer. The farm can be quickly reached by travelling to the Champions' Guild canoe station.

label: South Wilderness mine
title: South Wilderness mine
lead:
The south Wilderness mine is a small mine located in level 6 Wilderness, near the Air Obelisk hill. It is rarely used, if ever, although visited quite often for the Mage of Zamorak is stationed nearby the mine and can teleport players to the Abyss. It is, however, quite close to the banks at Edgeville and the Grand Exchange.

It contains three coal rocks and two iron rocks, and so can be useful for Superheat Item smithers. The downside is the mine is filled with several aggressive level 22 and 25 Skeletons, which also patrol around the River Lum, meaning you will constantly be attacked when mining. PKers can also attack you here, but because the level of the Wilderness is so low here, the skeletons are usually a greater threat than the PKers.

label: South-east Ardougne mine
title: South-east Ardougne mine
lead:
The South-east Ardougne mine, also referred to as Monastery Mine or South Ardougne Mine, can be found south of East Ardougne and east of the Clock Tower near the Kandarin Monastery. It contains four coal rocks and thirteen iron rocks, which form a channel leading to the monastery door and a ring around the entrance to the Ardougne Sewers. There are nine light coloured rocks which do not have ores; five between the door and coal rocks and four between the coal and iron rocks.

The mine can be useful for mining the resources for steel bars, as there is a furnace in East Ardougne along with the North Ardougne Bank nearby.

label: South-east Varrock mine
title: South-east Varrock mine
lead:
The south-east Varrock mine (also called East Varrock Mine) is a good low to medium level mine located outside the south-east corner of the city wall. The mine contains no resident monsters, which makes it suitable for newer players or players with a low Combat level, with iron and the raw materials for bronze. However, there is a level 6 Giant rat slightly to the north of the mine, which is aggressive to players level 12 Combat or lower.

It is also arguably one of the closest free-to-play mines in relation to a bank (along with the Dwarven Mine), making it popular for miners who wish to bank the iron ore that they obtain. The nearest bank is Varrock east bank, which is accessed via going north by the city wall and taking the east entrance. Players walking to the east bank should make sure to walk to the bank with a full inventory, to conserve run energy, and then run on the way back. Although Varrock west bank and the Grand Exchange are only slightly further, the east bank should be used, and the Varrock Teleport can be used for a faster trip if money isn't an issue. However, competition for iron ore here makes it hard for low levelled players to get iron ore.

label: South-west Varrock mine
title: South-west Varrock mine
lead:
The South-west Varrock mine (also called West Varrock Mine) is a low-medium level mine located outside the south-western corner of Varrock. The mine contains 8 tin rocks, 3 iron rocks, 3 silver rocks, and 3 clay rocks, along with some other rocks that have no ores.

Due to its close proximity to Varrock west bank and the Grand Exchange, this mine is suitable for mining large amounts of iron, clay or other ores. However, as this is one of the few silver mining sites on free-to-play, it is often crowded with higher-level miners.

label: South-west Wilderness mine
title: South-west Wilderness mine
lead:
The south-west Wilderness mine is located in level 9 Wilderness, just north-west of Edgeville, north of the Black Knights' Fortress, and south of the Dark Warriors' Fortress. This Mining site is a very rich coal mine since it contains over 30 coal rocks, which is sizeable in comparison to the Mining Guild, but players have to rely on running to safety or teleporting if attacked by player killers. This mine is recommended when the Mining Guild or other coal sites are crowded, or for players with a high Combat level.

*The skeletons are aggressive to players of all levels. They stop being aggressive after around 10 minutes.
*If players want to avoid additional monster encounters, they should travel north/south along the edge of the Black Knights' Fortress.
*The closest bank is in Edgeville.
*Because of the large amount of coal present here, this place is excellent for players wishing to use Superheat Item to smelt ores into bars.

label: Space
title: Space
lead:
Space may refer to:

*Bank space, the number of spaces remaining in a player's bank
*Game square, a unit of length
*Inventory space, the number of spaces a player has left
*Storage, any interactive content a player utilises to store items, such as accounts (known as mules), banks, bags, pouches, etc.
*Unknown, inaccessible blank areas on the borders of Gielinor
*Birdhouse space, location for placing a birdhouse on Fossil Island

label: spade
title: spade
lead:
A spade is a multi-functional tool used for a variety of activities. One of its major uses is in the Farming skill, though it also comes in handy for many quests and Treasure Trails. A spade is also needed to enter the Barrows crypts and the Mole Hole.

Spades are sold in farming shops and many general stores, and an infinite supply can be added to the player-owned house by making a tool store 2. They can also be obtained from a rogue kit, or taken from scenery objects found in various places. Finally, players can ask Konoo at the saltpetre mine in Hosidius for a spare spade.

label: Sparkling pool
title: Sparkling pool
lead: The Sparkling pools connect the Mage Arena bank area to the cave that contains the Statue of Saradomin, Statue of Guthix, and the Statue of Zamorak. The Chamber guardian and his shop, Mage Arena Staffs, are also found in this cave. The sparkling pools can only be used after completion of the Mage Arena I miniquest, at which point Kolodion will tell the player to travel through the pool and choose their god.

label: Spawn (disambiguation)
title: Spawn (disambiguation)
lead: Spawn may refer to:

label: Spawning
title: Spawning
lead: In Old School RuneScape, spawning is the in-game creation of an entity, for instance a player character, non-player character (NPC), or an item. Respawning is the recreation of a player, NPC, monster, resource, or item after its death, destruction, or use. On the other hand, despawning is the instantaneous destruction or removal of a resource, such as fishing spots, or a monster, such as a gangster.

label: spear
title: spear
lead:
Spears are two-handed stabbing weapons used in melee combat. They belong to the Spear weapon category, along with hastae and a few other weapons. They are not to be confused with halberds, which have a longer attack range (as one may expect from a spear) and overall function differently.

They are obtained from either monster drops, purchasing from players, or smithing on the special anvil south of the Barbarian Outpost or Barbarian Village. Most spears can be poisoned with normal weapon poisons or karambwan paste.

label: Spear (disambiguation)
title: Spear (disambiguation)
lead:

**Spears, a category of weapons including Spears, Hastae, and a few others.

label: Spear wall
title: Spear wall
lead: Spear walls are bits of decorative scenery that can be found across Gielinor.

label: Special attacks
title: Special attacks
lead:
Special attacks, also commonly referred to as specs or specials, are unique abilities offered by various weapons. Unlike passive effects, the player must choose to activate the special attack by clicking on the special attack bar or special attack orb, found under the Combat Options interface or the minimap respectively. Doing so will consume energy.

Special attacks offer a variety of benefits, including temporary boosts in stats, restoration of health or prayer, and extra damage or accuracy. If a weapon has a special attack, hovering over the special attack bar, or spec bar, will show the player a tooltip with a weapon's unique special attack name and description.

label: Special patches
title: Special patches
lead:
Many varieties of unique farming patches exist across Gielinor, used exclusively for growing very specific plants. Most often, only a single type of seed can be planted in these patches; though some, such as the Anima patch, have a few seeds available.

The mechanics of each specific patch may also be different than similar patches more familiar to the player. For example the celastrus tree, while having celastrus bark to harvest, has a variable yield and doesn't regenerate, making it unlike regular or fruit trees.

label: Special tree sapling
title: Special tree sapling
lead:
Special tree sapling may refer to:

*Spirit sapling
*Celastrus sapling
*Redwood sapling
*Hardwood tree saplings
**Teak sapling
**Mahogany sapling

label: Special tree seedling
title: Special tree seedling
lead:
Special tree seedling refer to tree seeds that have specialized patches not commonly shared with other tree , fruit tree, or hardwood tree seedlings.

Some examples include
*Calquat seedling
*Spirit seedling
*Celastrus seedling
*Redwood seedling

label: Specimen brush
title: Specimen brush
lead:
Specimen brush is an item used in the Digsite. It is needed in The Dig Site quest and to dig in level 3 sites. It can be obtained by pickpocketing a Digsite workman. You can also take it from the tool rack in the Varrock Museum. It cannot be withdrawn as a bank note.

It is also given to the player during the quest Another Slice of H.A.M.

label: Specimen jar
title: Specimen jar
lead:
A specimen jar is an item that is obtainable during The Dig Site quest, used to dig in the level 3 digs. Specimen jars can be obtained by searchingsacks in the Digsite, or by searching the cupboard on the south wall in the west room in the Exam Centre.

In addition to being used for level 3 digs, specimen jars can also be used to dig in specimen trays for charcoal (also used during The Dig Site) and other loot.

label: Specimen tray
title: Specimen tray
lead: A specimen tray is a pile found in the Digsite, which contains a collection of items found in the nearby excavation. It can be searched to obtain several items, most notably charcoal, which is used in The Dig Site quest. The player must have a specimen jar on them or a digsite workman will stop them from searching the tray.

label: Spectator (Fight Arena)
title: Spectator (Fight Arena)
lead: Spectators are non-player characters found at the Fight Arena south of East Ardougne. They have come to watch General Khazard's slaves and creatures fight to the death in the arena.

title: Spectral
lead:

*Spectral spirit shield
*Spectral potion
*Spectral (attribute)

label: Spectral (attribute)
title: Spectral (attribute)
lead: The spectral attribute is given to monsters who give Prayer XP when killed by players with the Ectoplasmator. Most spectral creatures also classify as undead, and are therefore weak to the effects of the salve amulet and its upgraded variants, however, this does not apply to all spectral creatures.

title: Speedy

label: Speedy Gnome
title: Speedy Gnome
lead:
Speedy Gnome was a scrapped random event mentioned in a Behind the Scenes article in August 2005. It was to be released alongside several other random events such as the Sandwich lady. In the event, the player would have been kidnapped and forced to race against Sebastian Gno, the "fastest gnome in the world", in an agility course modelled to look like an Olympic stadium with obstacles.

However, Sebastian Gno was not added to RuneScape along with the rest of the random events named, because the course was the same every time and was therefore not an effective anti-bot feature. The random event was scrapped, despite having completed graphics and testing.

label: Speedy Keith
title: Speedy Keith
lead: Speedy Keith is one of the three leaders of the Wilderness Bandit Camp. Like the other two leaders, Black Heather and Donny the lad, he is not aggressive. Attempting to talk to Speedy Keith yields the message: "Speedy Keith is not interested in talking".

label: spell scroll
title: spell scroll
lead: Spell scroll is a scroll that you receive as a reward from the quest, Watchtower. When read, the player learns the Watchtower Teleport (requires level 58 Magic). If a player loses the scroll before use, they can speak to the Watchtower Wizard. The player may learn the spell even without the requirement of level 58 Magic to use it. The drop trick may be performed to obtain multiple scrolls, allowing the player to 'learn' this spell multiple times.

label: Spellbook
title: Spellbook
lead:
A spellbook is a list of magic spells available for casting to a player. There are currently four spellbooks: the standard spellbook, the Ancient Magicks spellbook, the Lunar spellbook and the Arceuus spellbook. Ancient Magicks and the Lunar spellbook require a quest to be completed in order to unlock them. A player may only cast spells from their current spellbook, and if they wish to use spells from another spellbook, they must change to that spellbook.

It is possible to switch between spellbooks by visiting altars associated with those spellbooks, with the standard spellbook being accessible at the Ancient Pyramid altar, Astral Altar, and Tyss near the Dark Altar. It is often most efficient to utilize player-owned house altars.

label: Sphere
title: Sphere
lead:
Sphere may refer to:

*A globe.

label: Spice
title: Spice
lead:
Spice is an item used in Cooking. It can be bought from the Culinaromancer's Chest after completing the beginning portion of Recipe for Disaster or from spice stalls in Ardougne, Civitas illa Fortis, and Prifddinas. It can also be stolen from those stalls with level 65 Thieving or looted from a Gourmet impling or Baby impling.

You need spice in the goblin sub-quest of Recipe for Disaster, as well as for the Desert Treasure I quest.

title: Spice rack (interface item)

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Spice seller
title: Spice seller
lead: The spice seller runs the spice stall in the south-west corner of the Ardougne Marketplace in East Ardougne. He guards his spice stall while continually circling it in the south-west corner of the market square, near the fur stall and the silk stall. If he sees a player trying to steal from his stall, he'll stop them. He cannot be talked to or traded with for six minutes after a player has stolen from the spice stall.

label: Spice shops
title: Spice shops
lead: Spice shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. Spice shops sell spice and gnome spice. There are 4 dedicated spice shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Spice stall
title: Spice stall
lead:
The spice stall is a stall that can be found in multiple locations across Gielinor. Players can steal from this stall with a Thieving level of 65. If players are successful, they will steal spice. Items that can be seen on the spice stall, other than the spice which can be stolen, are a knife and a limpwurt root, as well as some unknown twigs, leaves, and a scroll.

There is also a spice stall in Sophanem that cannot be stolen from; it instead has "Search" option that yields the message "Nothing interesting happens." when searched.

label: Spice stall (disambiguation)
title: Spice stall (disambiguation)

* Prifddinas Spice Stall, a shop in Prifddinas

label: Spice stall (unused)
title: Spice stall (unused)
lead: Spice stall is an unused variant of spice stalls that may have been intended for use in free-to-play areas. The stall has no interaction options, but is otherwise identical to the standard stalls.

label: Spicy crunchies
title: Spicy crunchies
lead:
Spicy crunchies are a food that players consume in one bite, healing 7 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade s'y crunch are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 85 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make spicy crunchies via gnome cooking with 12 Cooking, yielding 102 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Spicy toad's legs
title: Spicy toad's legs
lead:
Spicy toad's legs was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Toad batta. It could be made by adding Gnome spice to Toad's legs. Equa leaves was then added to these in order to create Seasoned legs, an ingredient in the Toad batta.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the toad's legs, equa leaves and gnome spice are all automatically added at once to create a Half made crunchy. If the player attempts to add Gnome spice to toad's legs, nothing happens.

label: Spicy worm
title: Spicy worm
lead:
A Spicy worm was previously obtained during Gnome cooking when making a Worm batta. It could be made by adding Gnome spice to a King worm. This was then added to a Half baked batta alongside Cheese, then cooked to make an Unfinished batta.

As this process was unnecessarily intricate, it was altered with the Gnome Restaurant rework in 2006. Now, the king worm and gnome spice are all automatically added at once to create a Half made batta. If the player attempts to add gnome spice to a king worm, nothing happens.

label: Spider
title: Spider
lead:
Spiders are found all over Gielinor, but most notably in the Stronghold of Security, where a stronger variant can be found in large numbers. Spiders are usually considered a nuisance and rarely drop items, and are generally only killed to quickly complete a spider Slayer task.

Similar to rats, spiders do not appear on the minimap.

note: Spiked boots cannot be used in place of climbing boots for climbing over rocks in the mountain path.

label: Spinach roll
title: Spinach roll
lead:
Spinach roll is a food item that restores 2 hitpoints when eaten. It is received as a reward from random events such as the Mysterious Old Man and Rick Turpentine, or looted from opening a Crystal chest, Christmas cracker or Barrel.

During Demon Slayer, Traiborn will give players a spinach roll if they choose chat options When eaten, the messages You eat the spinach roll. and It tastes a bit weird, but it fills you up. are displayed.

label: Spindel/Strategies
title: Spindel/Strategies
lead:
: Spindel resides in level 29 Wilderness. You may be attacked by other players at any time during the fight. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose. Items like the dragon defender are permanently lost if not protected beyond level 20 Wilderness.

Spindel is a level 302 spider boss that is found in the Web Chasm. The fight with her is nearly identical to Venenatis, although with reduced stats and in a singles-plus combat area. Completion of the hard Wilderness diary is required to fight Spindel.

label: Spined armour
title: Spined armour
lead:
Spined armour is Fremennik armour for rangers that can only be made by going to Waterbirth Island. It requires 40 Defence and Ranged to wear. Most of the set can only be worn after the completion of The Fremennik Trials. Parts of this armour can be dropped by Dagannoth Supreme. While wearing the full set (boots and gloves not needed), the title of "Spinewielder" is added to your Fremennik name.

Spined armour may be placed in the Armour case in the Costume room of a player-owned house, so players may own it without the armour taking up bank space.

label: Spinning blades

lead:
Spinning blades may refer to:

* The spinning blades found within the Rogues' Den

label: Spinning blades (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
title: Spinning blades (Brimhaven Agility Arena)
lead:
The spinning blades are an Agility obstacle found within the Brimhaven Agility Arena. Failing to dodge the obstacle will cause the player to take damage, and display the message You were hit by the spinning blades!.

The amount of damage is based on the player's current health, according to the formula below.

label: spinning wheel
title: spinning wheel
lead:
A spinning wheel is a device used with the Crafting skill to spin fibers into strings. Spinning wheels are marked on the map by this symbol: .
The following table shows what fibers can be spun into what strings using a spinning wheel:

The closest spinning wheel to a bank is in the Crafting Guild, but the bank requires the hard Falador Diary or 99 Crafting to use, and the spinning wheel is a floor above the bank so requires two extra clicks per trip.

label: Spirit
title: Spirit
lead: Spirit may refer to:

label: Spirit (music track)
title: Spirit (music track)
lead:
Spirit is a music track that can be unlocked inside Varrock city walls, excluding the Grand Exchange. It also plays in the Phoenix Gang Hideout and in the basement of the Blue Moon Inn. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Adventure, Garden, and Medieval.

In Classic mode, this track plays in western Varrock.

label: Spirit angler's outfit
title: Spirit angler's outfit
lead:
The spirit angler's outfit is a cosmetic variant of the angler's outfit that grants 2.5% additional experience when worn while training the Fishing skill. Wearing the complete set also acts as a rope for tethering to totem poles and masts while battling Tempoross.

Showing the outfit to Kylie Minnow is suitable to gain access to the minnows in the Fishing Guild, but does not need to be equipped. Pieces of the spirit angler's outfit can be equipped alongside pieces of the angler's outfit for the purpose of receiving the extra 0.5% set XP bonus.

label: Spirit of Adventure
title: Spirit of Adventure
lead: Spirit of Adventure is an unnamed miniquest not shown in the quest list. It is started by talking to a ghost by the name of Bernina by the Auburn Valley coast. The miniquest explains the lore behind Bernina and Bernard. There are no rewards for completing the miniquest. It was released on 23 July 2025 as part of Varlamore: The Final Dawn update.

label: Spirit of Scorpius
title: Spirit of Scorpius
lead:
The Spirit of Scorpius is a Zamorakian ghost. After completion of Observatory Quest, he will give the player an unholy mould and bless unholy symbols. He is found south-west of Ardougne by the Grave of Scorpius, due north of the Observatory. An unholy mould must be claimed from him before he will bless any unholy symbols. He will not give the player an unholy mould if there is one already in their inventory.

Scorpius is close to both the red salamander hunting area and the Ourania Cave.

label: Spirit of Zadimus
title: Spirit of Zadimus
lead:
The Spirit of Zadimus is a ghost who appears during the Shilo Village quest, when you bury the Zadimus corpse at the Tribal Statue in Tai Bwo Wannai. In the following conversation, he gives you a bone shard.

According to Trufitus, Zadimus was a high priest of Zamorak. Zadimus was loved by Rashiliyia, however he did not love her back and was later tortured and killed by her. His corpse was found hanging in the gallows in the Temple of Ah Za Rhoon, which he built.

label: Spirit shields
title: Spirit shields
lead:
Spirit shields are a range of members shields known for their prayer bonus. There are five types of spirit shields, with the stronger ones being upgraded versions of the base shield. Both the base shield and the items for upgrading are obtained as rare drops from the Corporeal Beast.

Holy elixir can be added to a spirit shield to upgrade it to a blessed spirit shield; spirit sigils can then be attached to the blessed spirit shield to upgrade it further. Attached sigils cannot be removed, with the exception of the arcane sigil; Abbot Langley can extract it from the arcane spirit shield, returning the sigil but destroying the blessed spirit shield in the processes.

label: Spirit tree
title: Spirit tree
lead: Spirit trees are a gnomish method of transportation. Completion of the Tree Gnome Village quest is required for access to the network. Additional completion of The Grand Tree is required to travel from the spirit tree at the Tree Gnome Stronghold, but is not required to travel to it. All other trees can be used to travel directly from one tree to another tree.

label: Spirit tree (interface item)
title: Spirit tree (interface item)
lead:
The spirit tree is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the spirit tree.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Spirit tree & fairy ring (interface item)
title: Spirit tree & fairy ring (interface item)
lead:
The spirit tree & fairy ring is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the spirit tree & fairy ring.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Spirit tree dummy (interface item)
title: Spirit tree dummy (interface item)
lead:
The spirit tree dummy is an interface item that can be seen in the Farming skill guide representing the spirit tree.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Spirit tree patch
title: Spirit tree patch
lead:
Spirit tree patches are a type of farming patch where players can grow their own spirit tree from a spirit sapling, created with a spirit seed. Spirit seeds are a rare and untradeable drop.

Spirit trees grow in about 58 hours and 40 minutes. Growing a spirit tree yields 19,501.3 Farming experience, which is the sum of planting (199.5 experience) and checking its health (19,301.8 experience). They cannot be cut down, but may be cleared with a spade.

label: Spiritual creature
title: Spiritual creature
lead:
Spiritual creatures are Slayer monsters found in the God Wars Dungeon and Wilderness God Wars Dungeon. There are 3 types of spiritual creature, each requiring a different Slayer level to kill:

*Spiritual ranger, requiring 63 Slayer
*Spiritual warrior, requiring 68 Slayer
*Spiritual mage, requiring 83 Slayer

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

The Spiritual Ranger is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Spiritual Ranger

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

The Spiritual Warrior is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Spiritual Warrior

label: Spit roast
title: Spit roast
lead:
Spit roast can mean any of the following:
* Ogre spit-roast
* Spit roast (Rellekka)
* Iron spit

label: Spitting
title: Spitting
lead:
Spitting may refer to one of the following:
* Spitting Scarab, a monster encountered in the Tombs of Amascut
* Spitting Wyvern, a slayer monster found in the Wyvern Cave

label: splashing
title: splashing
lead:
Splashing is the act of purposely wearing items with bonuses that total -64 Magic attack bonus or lower (e.g. full plate armour with d'hide vambraces, or full plate armour and a cursed goblin staff), and attacking a weak opponent that cannot be interacted with by other players (such as any NPC that can be pickpocketed, or rats, which can be killed by cats). Simply bring enough runes, and turn auto cast and Auto Retaliate on.

Prior to a hidden update implemented on 10 September 2015, a player could go away-from-keyboard (AFK) until the game forced the player to log out after six hours provided the player kept their computer on and had a reliable internet connection. After an update, splashing is still possible, but after twenty minutes the player will stop auto-retaliating, making it impossible to splash for hours as in the past.

label: Splashing/Guide
title: Splashing/Guide
lead:
This article details how to splash. Splashing is the act of training magic by casting combat spells against an enemy while having too low magic accuracy to be able to actually hit. Although no damage is dealt, each Magic combat spell will still give the player a constant base amount of experience.

Despite the enemy remaining alive indefinitely, after 20 minutes the player will stop auto-retaliating. As a consequence, timely interaction with the game is needed to not be logged out due to inactivity.

label: Splendour
title: Splendour
lead:
Splendour is a music track that is unlocked in Taverley. In this area, the track shuffles between playing this track and Horizon.

In Classic music mode, this track plays at an area between Taverley and Burthorpe where the Heroes' Guild is located or at the Chaos Temple.

label: splitbark armour
title: splitbark armour
lead:
Splitbark armour is a set of members-only magic armour that requires 40 Magic and 40 Defence to wear. Each piece is made from Fine cloth (from Shades of Mort'ton) and Bark (from woodcutting Hollow Trees). The full set requires 11 Fine cloth and Bark. If the player does not have the required crafting level, they can bring the materials along with some coins to Wizard Jalarast at the Wizards' Tower. The armour can also be obtained from implings and the Chaos Fanatic, or by trading with other players.

Splitbark armour is often used for its rare combination of providing a sizeable magical attack bonus while still maintaining defensive bonuses to both melee and magic defence. The melee defensive bonuses offered by splitbark are similar to those of black armour. While this is useful, especially for up-close combat against enemies by which there is no "safespot", many players with the same required Magic level of 40, and especially a lower required Defence level of 20, would likely favour the mystic robes set for farcasting and safespotting, due to a considerably higher magic attack and defence bonus, though no melee defence is offered by Mystic.

label: spookier outfit
title: spookier outfit
lead:
The spookier outfit is a holiday reward received by using any costume piece from the spooky outfit on the swampy sink outside the Lumbridge Swamp tool shed, or on the Ectofuntus (while the Ghostspeak amulet is not equipped) outside Port Phasmatys. The costume gives no bonus to any stats.

If lost or destroyed, the outfit can be reclaimed from Diango in Draynor Village or the Toy box in the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: Spooky
title: Spooky
lead:
Spooky is a music track that is unlocked at Draynor Manor or during the Gravedigger random event. It could also be unlocked during the 2021 Halloween event.

Although it is presumably not supposed to do so, Spooky is replaced with Scape Soft and Lightness in Modern mode after playing once within Draynor Manor fenced area.

label: Spooky Jungle
title: Spooky Jungle
lead:
Spooky Jungle is a music track that is unlocked in the Kharazi Jungle, in Rashiliyia's Tomb and the Tomb of Bervirius, and during cutscenes in Tai Bwo Wannai Trio when Tamayu fights The Shaikahan . It also plays in the Nightmare Zone when facing Nazastarool in Practice or Endurance mode.

In Classic mode, it does not play in the Tomb of Bervirius, and in the Kharazi Jungle it only plays in the westernmost area.

label: Spooky outfit
title: Spooky outfit
lead:
The spooky outfit is a holiday reward received from completing a Halloween event from 2019 onwards. The costume gives no bonus to any stats. The pieces of the spooky outfit can be used on the swampy sink or the Ectofuntus to unlock the spookier outfit.

If lost or destroyed, the outfit can be reclaimed from Diango in Draynor Village. In addition, all of the costume items may be stored in the costume room of a player-owned house.

label: Spooky picture
title: Spooky picture
lead:
Spooky pictures are pictures that appear to depict a red dragon. These pictures are found prominently throughout Melzar's Maze as well as inside Draynor Manor. There is also one located in the Misthalin Manor. They cannot be built within a player-owned house or interacted with in any way.

Upon loading a scene with a spooky picture in it, the picture will move in a specific way:
* 3 of the paintings in Draynor Manor and the one in Misthalin Manor will spin.
* The rest of the paintings and the ones in Melzar's Maze will look around the room.

label: Spotlight
title: Spotlight
lead: Two spotlights can be found in the mime random event. They turn on whenever the player or the mime performs an action.

label: Spring garden (interface item)
title: Spring garden (interface item)
lead:
The Spring garden is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving skill guide representing the spring garden.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: sq'irk
title: sq'irk
lead:
Sq'irk is a fruit obtained during the Sorceress's Garden minigame. It can be crushed into a beer glass using a pestle and mortar to make sq'irkjuice. Five are required for a winter drink, four for a spring drink, three for an autumn drink, and two for a summer drink. These drinks may be used to temporarily boost the player's Thieving level and energy, or may be traded to Osman in Al Kharid for Thieving experience.

Note: Picking sq'irks does not give Thieving experience, it gives Farming experience. You have to make sq'irkjuice and give it to Osman to get Thieving experience. Despite this, Tangleroot is not obtainable during this minigame. Instead there is a small chance that Rocky will be rewarded while picking a fruit in the Sorceress's Garden.

label: Sq'irkjuice
title: Sq'irkjuice
lead:
Sq'irkjuice is made from sq'irk fruit, which are obtained by picking them one at a time within the Sorceress's Garden minigame. The juice is made by using a pestle and mortar with a sq'irk fruit while the required amount of fruit, as well as an empty beer glass, are in the inventory. The resulting juice can then be traded to Osman (or Selim after Beneath Cursed Sands) for Thieving experience.

When drunk, sq'irkjuice will temporarily boost a player's Thieving level. There are 4 types of sq'irkjuice: winter, spring, autumn, and summer. Winter sq'irks are the easiest to obtain, although 5 of them are needed to make one glass, with each glass rewarding just 350 experience. Spring sq'irks reward significantly more at a total of 1350 experience each, but 4 fruits are needed for a glass. Autumn sq'irks are the second most rewarding, and only 3 are needed to make a glass which rewards 2350 experience. Finally, summer sq'irks are the most sought after by Osman/Selim, and just 2 are needed to fill a glass; they are the most rewarding, granting 3000 experience each.

label: square shield
title: square shield
lead:
A square shield or sq shield is a type of metal shield with a rectangular shape. They are normally used as a melee protection and provide good defence against all melee attack types. They can be smithed from all types of metals except for black and white.

Compared to kiteshields, square shields provide less overall defence, weigh slightly less, take fewer bars to make, do not provide negative Magic defence, and have no negative Ranged attack bonus. This makes them somewhat useful for rangers and mages.

label: Stab weapons
title: Stab weapons
lead: Stab weapons are weapons that deal stab-based damage. These weapons are more likely to deal damage to monsters with low stab defence.

label: Stackable items
title: Stackable items
lead: Stackable items are items which only take up one space in a player's inventory. When multiple stackable items are carried in the inventory, a number is shown on the item's picture to indicate the quantity of items in the stack. Stackable items do not weigh anything, and cannot be withdrawn as a bank note. Stackable items include coins, runes, arrows, seeds, bank notes, purple sweets and other items such as feathers, arrow shafts, nails, bolt tips, skewer sticks, woad leaves, and proboscises. Also, swamp tar and anything made from swamp tar, such as swamp paste or guam tar, is always stackable. Most items appear to be stackable in a player's bank to preserve bank space.

label: Staff
title: Staff
lead:
A staff is a cheap magic weapon which provides modest magical bonuses and the autocast option when equipped. Due to not possessing any elemental features and offering poor combat stats, it is only useful as a very cheap option for autocasting.

The staff can most easily be purchased from Zaff's staff shop in Varrock. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players or dropped by various enemies.

label: Staff (disambiguation)
title: Staff (disambiguation)

label: Staff of air
title: Staff of air
lead:
A staff of air is the basic air elemental staff. It provides unlimited amounts of air runes as well as the autocast option when equipped. All elemental staves offer the same Magic bonuses and only differ by the type of rune they supply and their Melee stats.

The staff can be purchased from various shops across Gielinor, including Zaff's Superior Staffs! in Varrock. It can also be bought on the Grand Exchange, obtained through other players, dropped by various enemies, or obtained as a reward from beginner and easy clue caskets.

label: Staff of armadyl
title: Staff of armadyl
lead:
The Staff of Armadyl is a quest item in the Temple of Ikov quest. If allied with Lucien, the staff of Armadyl is stolen from a table within the Temple of Ikov dungeon after killing a Guardian of Armadyl and brought to Lucien to complete the quest. If allied with the guardians, the player will receive an Armadyl pendant to equip and prove they are no longer allies of Lucien, then go and kill him.

Multiple copies of the staff cannot be obtained. The staff also cannot be telekinetically grabbed. If the staff is dropped and then the quest is completed, attempting to pick up the staff will yield the message: "You have completed the quest of the Temple of Ikov."

title: Staff shops
lead: Staff shops are a type of store throughout Gielinor. The stores are represented by a icon. There are 4 staff shops in Old School RuneScape.

label: Stagnant
title: Stagnant
lead:
Stagnant is a music track that is unlocked in the Mort Myre Swamp.

It can later be heard while Temple Trekking, during the River puzzle or in combat events with no escape routes. The track also plays during Sins of the Father, when escorting Ivan Strom past the River puzzle and In Aid of the Myreque during the meeting between Gadderanks and Vanstrom Klause. In the Mort Myre Swamp area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track, Dead Quiet and Waterlogged.

The Stained glass is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Stained glass.

label: Staircase
title: Staircase
lead:
Staircases are found in buildings or houses with two or more stories. They may also be found leading downwards into dungeons. A staircase may simply be a row of steps, or it may be in the more ornate form of a spiral staircase. All staircases are climbed at the same speed (as they have no animation for climbing them) so the size differences are purely aesthetic.

When a player right-clicks a staircase they will usually be given three options based on whether they lead up as well as down: 'Climb', 'Climb-Up' and 'Climb-Down.' If a player chooses the climb-up or climb-down option their character will do just that, either progressing to the next floor or digressing to the floor below. If a player selects the 'Climb' option, or merely left-clicks the staircase, a message will appear. The message will ask the player to choose whether they wish to climb up or down the staircase.

label: Stairs (Count Draynor)

lead: These stairs lead to the crypt of Count Draynor Drakan in the Draynor Manor. During the Vampire Slayer quest the player must use these stairs to enter the crypt and slay Count Draynor.

label: Stairs (Dwarven Tunnel)
title: Stairs (Dwarven Tunnel)
lead: These stairs serve as entrances and exits to the White Wolf Tunnel. The stairs down into the tunnel are guarded by Austri and Vestri. To be allowed into the tunnel, players must win the local Fishing Contest at Hemenster.

label: Stairs (Tribal Totem)
title: Stairs (Tribal Totem)
lead: Stairs are a scenery object found in the western room on the of Handelmort Mansion in East Ardougne. Before climbing the stairs, players must first investigate them for traps, requiring level 21 Thieving. If players attempt to climb the stairs without first disabling the trap, a trapdoor will open dropping the player to the Ardougne Sewers below. During the Tribal Totem quest, players must use these stairs in order to reach the chest on the floor above in order to obtain the totem.

label: Stake
title: Stake
lead:
The stake is a quest item used in the Vampyre Slayer quest. This item is obtained by talking to Dr Harlow at the Blue Moon Inn in Varrock. The player must use the stake, along with a hammer, to kill Count Draynor.

Duplicates can be obtained with the drop trick and offering another beer to Dr Harlow. All duplicates must be dropped before killing Count Draynor, if the player wishes to keep them after the quest. Any duplicates that are not dropped will be destroyed.

label: Stalactite (Taverley Dungeon)

They should not be confused with the similarly named Stalagmites, which are scenery on the floor of the Taverley Dungeon. A helpful for remembering the difference is that stalactites hold tightly to the ceiling, while stalagmites might reach the ceiling some day.

label: stall
title: stall
lead: A stall is a stand that NPCs use to display their product. The majority of stalls can be stolen from with appropriate level in Thieving. Items sold include: silk, fur, scimitars, fish, vegetables, etc. Most types of stalls can be found in Ardougne; however, there is also a selection in Rellekka, Miscellania, Sophanem, Keldagrim, Draynor, Varrock, Great Kourend and Prifddinas. Stealing from a stall may alert a nearby guard who will attack until they die, you unsuccessfully pickpocket them, or the area is left. To prevent guards/merchants from noticing you, thieve with the stall between your character and the NPC. Stall owners will not talk to players if they have stolen from their stall within the last 20 minutes (in-game time). It's not needed for the stalls found on Ape Atoll.

label: standard spellbook
title: standard spellbook
lead:
The standard spellbook is a group of Magic spells available to all players, being unlocked by default upon character creation. Standard spells make use of all runes except Astral. Staves are also required to cast some of the spells, including Iban's staff, slayer's staff or staff of the dead, Saradomin staff or staff of light, Zamorak staff, and Guthix staff or void knight mace.

Magic spells are divided into three distinct types: Combat, Utility, and Teleport spells.

label: Stanford
title: Stanford
lead:
Stanford is the gardener of the Sinclair Mansion. He had an affair with Anna Sinclair, the daughter of his employer Lord Sinclair, but when the relationship ended, she tried to have him fired by destroying the flowers in the garden. When Lord Sinclair was murdered, he was convinced Anna was the killer.

When Anna was arrested and put on trial, he was called as a witness, where he claimed she didn't use her poison for her chore but couldn't provide any concrete evidence that she was the killer.

label: Stankers
title: Stankers

label: stat restoration

lead:
Stat restoration is the process of returning the player's skills back to their normal levels. Temporary skill drain can occur from the environments, like the Ice Path, negative effects of boosts, using certain items, when attacked by other players in PvP, or from monsters.

Death is a special stat restore that resets all temporary skill boosts as well.

label: Statue of Glarial

label: Statue of Guthix
title: Statue of Guthix
lead: The Statue of Guthix can be found in the Mage Arena cave after completing the Mage Arena I miniquest, alongside the Statue of Saradomin and Statue of Zamorak. They can be accessed by travelling through the Sparkling pool in the bank area, near Kolodion. Praying at the Statue of Guthix will not recharge your prayer points, and instead will drop a Guthix cape on the floor. After claiming their first cape, players can talk to the Chamber guardian to claim a free staff of the god cape of their choice.

label: Statue of Saradomin

They can be accessed by travelling through the Sparkling pool in the bank area, near Kolodion. Praying at the Statue of Saradomin will not recharge your prayer points, and instead will drop a Saradomin cape on the floor. label: Statue steps
title: Statue steps
lead:
Statue steps are an unused scenery object that were added in the RuneScape 2 beta. Originally, they could be found in Falador, and were a plinth upon which the statue of Saradomin stood. However, they were removed from Falador quite early on and have not been seen since. It is unknown when exactly they were removed, but it was definitely between 13 and 21 December 2004.

The statue steps cannot be found anywhere else, and as a result have never been present in Old School RuneScape.

label: Status effect
title: Status effect
lead:
A negative status effect is a condition that impairs the player. Contrary to buffs and with the exception of being skulled or stunned, these status effects could sap the player's health, stats or both. Below is a list of status effects.

Status effects can stack with each other; e.g a player can be diseased, envenomed and poisoned at the same time.

label: Staves
title: Staves
lead:
Staves generally are Magic weapons that have the ability to autocast spells. Elemental staves are unlimited sources of certain runes depending on the element of the staff, and are popular because they save coins otherwise spent on runes.

Staves tend to give Magic attack bonuses as well as mediocre melee attack bonuses. Battlestaves are upgraded versions of normal staves with slightly better Magic and melee bonuses. Mystic staves are enchanted versions of battlestaves with further improved magic and melee bonuses.
