label: Tarddiad
title: Tarddiad
lead:
Tarddiad (pronounced tar-THEE-add) is the original homeworld of the elves. Long before the First Age on Gielinor, it was discovered by the goddess Seren. She was enamoured by the elves and stayed with them, teaching them the art of crystal singing. Seren also granted the elves longevity, but at the cost of bonding the elves to her. To break this bond, Seren convinced the elves to come to Gielinor after having been told of its power by Guthix. Eight of the nine elven clans came with her. The Cywir Clan decided to stay behind. It is currently unknown if they survived after being separated from Seren for so long.

Players currently cannot visit the planet.

label: Target (Ranging Guild)
title: Target (Ranging Guild)
lead:
Targets can be found in the eastern corner of the Ranging Guild, which play the central role in the guild's shooting range minigame. To shoot at the target, players must provide their own bow, but bronze arrows are provided by the judge. Players who lose any of the provided 10 arrows may buy more arrows for 100 coins, regardless of the amount of arrows they happen to be missing.

Shooting at these targets can only be done after paying the Competition Judge 200 coins to partake in the minigame, after which you will receive 10 bronze arrows to shoot at the target. 1 Ranged experience is rewarded for every 2 points obtained. At the end of the game, one archery ticket is rewarded for every 10 points obtained in the game. It is also possible to miss the target, which will reward no points and grants no experience.

label: Tarrlo Remanis
title: Tarrlo Remanis
lead: Tarrlo Remanis was one of the founding members of the Elders of Avarrocka. His descendants eventually took over Avarrocka as monarchs. His furthest known descendant is King Roald.

label: Tarromin
title: Tarromin
lead:
Tarromin is the third lowest level herb. It can be cleaned at level 11 Herblore, and it is used for making strength potions, serum 207, shrink-me-quick and tarromin tar. It can be grown with the Farming skill with a level of 19, by planting a tarromin seed in a herb patch. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a tarromin potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

According to the book Gielinor's flora - herbs, tarromin are native to tropical regions and it is believed to be one of the earliest cultivated plants of Gielinor.

label: Tarromin potion (unf)
title: Tarromin potion (unf)
lead: A tarromin potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a tarromin on a vial of water, requiring 12 Herblore. Using a limpwurt root on a tarromin potion (unf) with 12 Herblore yields a Strength potion(3) and 50 Herblore experience. In the Shades of Mort'ton quest, after reading the diary of Herbi Flax, using ashes on a tarromin potion (unf) with 15 Herblore yields a Serum 207 (3) and 50 Herblore experience. In the Grim Tales quest, using shrunk ogleroot on a tarromin potion (unf) with 52 Herblore yields a Shrink-me-quick and 6 Herblore experience.

label: Tasakaal
title: Tasakaal
lead:
The Tasakaal are a race of golem-like creatures that inhabit Mount Karuulm, a sulphurous volcano found within the Kebos Lowlands.

Currently, there are only three Tasakaal that players can find: Kaal-Mej-San, Kaal-Ket-Jor, and Kaal-Xil-Dar.

label: Taverley
title: Taverley
lead: Taverley is a small Guthixian village found north-west of Falador inhabited primarily by druids. The village has no bank, but it is a starting point for several quests, and houses the Taverley Dungeon. The village is often the first place that members visit outside of free-to-play.

label: Taverley Dungeon
title: Taverley Dungeon
lead: The Taverley Dungeon is one of the largest dungeons in Old School RuneScape. There are many monsters, ranging from low to high combat levels, getting stronger as players venture deeper into the dungeon. These include poisonous monsters, so bringing antipoison potions is advised if travelling through the parts of the dungeon that contain them. Taverley Dungeon is entirely single combat (although cannons can still attack multiple targets if the player is not in direct combat).

label: Tea seller
title: Tea seller
lead:
The tea seller runs a tea stall in Varrock south-east of the east bank. Stealing from his stall will make him yell "You're the one who keeps stealing from me! Guards, Guards!", although no-one will ever come to him. If players touch the tea sitting on the table in front of him, he will yell, "Hey! Put that back! Those are for display only!" Furthermore, using Telekinetic Grab on the cup will prevent the spell and result in him saying the same thing.

Level 5 Thieving is required to steal from a tea stall. Like all stalls, if you talk to him again, he will shout rather pointlessly. The tea he sells is sold for coins.

label: Tea stall
title: Tea stall
lead:
Tea stall is a stall located in south-eastern Varrock and Kourend Castle. In Varrock the shop is owned by the tea seller as part of Ye olde Tea Shoppe. The player can steal from it with a Thieving level of 5, granting 16 experience.

There is a cup of tea on the bench nearby, but it cannot be taken because it is apparently just for display.

title: Teal boots
lead:
Teal boots can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The boots come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. They give the same stats as leather boots.

Unlike leather boots, these cannot be crafted. Because of their stats, they are mostly worn for cosmetic purposes.

label: Teal gloves
title: Teal gloves
lead:
Teal gloves can be purchased in Canifis from Barker at his store, Barker's Haberdashery, and are also dropped by Crawling Hands. The gloves come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. These gloves are often worn to match certain armour sets, such as gold-trimmed and god armour sets.

Their defence bonus is equal to that of leather gloves.

label: Teal hat
title: Teal hat
lead: Teal hats can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The hats come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Teal robe bottoms
title: Teal robe bottoms
lead: Teal robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Teal robe top
title: Teal robe top
lead: Teal robe tops can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe tops come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Team cape
title: Team cape
lead:
Team capes (also known as Wilderness capes) are purchased for 50 coins from various Cape merchants. Alternatively, three (Team cape i, Team cape x, and Team cape zero) are obtainable only through the completion of a Clue scroll (easy) or via the Grand Exchange.

Another player with the same team cape equipped will show up on the minimap as a blue dot rather than white, and the left-click "Attack" option will be moved to a right-click, as if the other player is of higher level than the player. These capes are primarily used as a precaution between adventuring friends and player killers in a group or clan.

label: Tear
title: Tear
lead: Tear may refer to:

label: Tears of Guthix (disambiguation)
title: Tears of Guthix (disambiguation)
lead:
Tears of Guthix may refer to:
* Tears of Guthix, the quest.
* Tears of Guthix (minigame), the weekly minigame.
* Tears of Guthix (music track), the music track.
* The Chasm of Tears, an area south of Lumbridge Swamp Caves.

label: Technical difficulties
title: Technical difficulties
lead:
Technical difficulties may refer to:

* Lag
* Server blackout

label: Technical plans
title: Technical plans
lead:
The technical plans are a quest item from The Tourist Trap quest. You bring these plans for a weapon to the Bedabin nomads and use their experimental anvil to make it. After you've shown the prototype to Al Shabim, he takes the plans from you.

The first option on this item is "Read", if you read it, this comes up: The plans look very technical! But you can see that this item will require a bronze bar and at least 10 feathers. Upon completing the quest, it will instead read: Some technical looking plans.

label: Technical updates
title: Technical updates
lead: Technical updates are updates which generally deal with improvements to servers, or maintenance. The Old School RuneScape development team have typically favour website updates in most cases, however on occasion use this category.

label: Tecuani
title: Tecuani
lead: Tecuani is one of the seven teoki of Ranul responsible for maintaining the seven holy sites across Varlamore. He was responsible for overseeing the temple of Tal Teok along side his counterpart, Jatziri, Teoki of Ralos. However, he ended up abandoning his role and joining the Twilight Emissaries cult. According to Jatziri, a replacement will be chosen after Tecuani is killed for being a traitor.

label: Ted Rehnison
title: Ted Rehnison
lead: Ted Rehnison is a man who lives in the Rehnison household, located in north-eastern West Ardougne. He is the husband of Martha Rehnison. He has two children, Billy and Milli. His family sells cooking apples and are known friends of Elena.

label: Tele group
title: Tele group
lead:
Tele Group may refer to any of the following group teleportation spells available with the Lunar Spellbook:

label: Telekinetic Grab
title: Telekinetic Grab
lead:
Telekinetic Grab (also known as telegrab) is a utility spell available in the standard spellbook. It requires level 33 Magic to cast, and grants 43 Magic experience per cast.

The spell can be used to pick up an item (or a pile of a stackable item) up to 10 tiles away, including over or through obstacles such as fences, gates, and rivers. It is useful when picking up item spawns that are guarded by dangerous monsters, such as the wine of Zamorak in the Chaos Temple, and is also sometimes required for quests in order to pick up items that are guarded by NPCs or otherwise unreachable. For repeated casting, it is recommended to have a staff of air equipped to negate the need for air runes, and to have a way of restoring Magic level if grabbing wine of Zamorak outside of the Deep Wilderness Dungeon.

title: Teleother

Teleother may refer to:

label: Teleport focus (interface item)
title: Teleport focus (interface item)
lead:
The Teleport focus is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Teleport focus.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Teleport scrolls
title: Teleport scrolls
lead: Teleport scrolls are items offering a one-time teleport to a certain location, and are consumed upon use. There are many different scrolls for varying teleport locations. Up to 1,000 of each type can be stored inside the master scroll book.

label: Teleport sphere
title: Teleport sphere
lead: Teleport spheres, also referred to as Moving-over-distance spheres, are a unique method of teleportation devised and produced by Dorgeshuun professor Oldak in his lab in Dorgesh-Kaan. Dorgesh-kaan spheres can be purchased after Death to the Dorgeshuun, Goblin village spheres can be purchased after Another Slice of H.A.M., and Plain of mud spheres can be purchased after Land of the Goblins. Each teleport sphere costs 2 law runes and 1 molten glass, which must be brought to Oldak and exchanged for the sphere of choice; the items may be noted though the runes may not be in a rune pouch.

label: Teleport to house (redirected)
title: Teleport to house (redirected)
lead:
The Teleport to house (redirected) tablet is an item obtainable by using a scroll of redirection on an ordinary Teleport to house tablet. The player is then able to choose the house portal they want to redirect it towards, as well as Trollheim. Multiple tablets can be redirected at once if the player has multiple tablets and scrolls.

A redirected house tablet can be reverted back into its original form, but you will not receive your scroll back. However, unused scrolls can be refunded without any loss of points.

label: Teleport trap (interface item)
title: Teleport trap (interface item)
lead:
The Teleport trap is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Teleport trap.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Teleportation spells
title: Teleportation spells
lead:
Teleportation spells are spells that instantly transport players to a predetermined location. As teleportation spells save lots of time when travelling around the world, they are widely used among all players. Many of these teleportations can be linked to a portal or portal nexus in a POH, where players will have unlimited access to the spells' destinations, and can also be made into a magic tablet, which can be used to teleport to the respective destination without runes.

Note that using a teleport spell is not possible above level 20 Wilderness, nor in any of the combat based minigames such as Castle Wars and Pest Control. Teleportation is possible in "non-Wilderness" parts, though, like in the Mage Arena bank.

label: Telescope
title: Telescope
lead: Telescope may refer to:

label: Telescope (Observatory reception)
title: Telescope (Observatory reception)
lead: A telescope can be found next to the Observatory assistant at the Observatory reception. Players cannot interact with it, but they can examine it.

label: Telescope (Observatory)
title: Telescope (Observatory)
lead: The Observatory telescope is repaired and used during Observatory Quest.

label: Temple
title: Temple
lead:
Temple can refer to:

*Paterdomus, also known as the Temple of Saradomin, which is labelled "Temple" on the world map
*The Flamtaer temple, which plays a role in the Shades of Mort'ton quest and subsequent minigame
*Temple of Ikov, a members-only quest
**Temple of Ikov (dungeon), a dungeon in Hemenster
*The Temple of Light from Mourning's End Part II; the Death Altar is on the western bottom floor
*Temple Trekking, a minigame
*Temple Knights of Saradomin from the Recruitment Drive and Wanted! quests
*Temple of Marimbo on Ape Atoll
*Goblin Temple in the Goblin Cave
*Temple of the Eye, a quest unlocking the Guardians of the Rift minigame
**Temple of the Eye (location), where the minigame takes place
*Temple (music track)
*Temple of Ralos located in Civitas illa Fortis
*Iban's temple, a small temple in the Underground Pass.

label: Temple door (Iban's Temple)
title: Temple door (Iban's Temple)
lead: The Temple door is the entrance to Iban's Temple, where Iban is fought during the Underground Pass quest. In order to fight Iban, players have to wear zamorak monk robes and carry the Doll of iban.

label: Temple Guardian
title: Temple Guardian
lead:
The Temple Guardian (also known as Spots) is a dog-like monster that dwells in the entrance of the underground passageway to Canifis.

Players are required to kill the Temple Guardian in the Priest in Peril quest. Attempting to attack the monster outside of the quest will result in the message You have no reason to attack a helpless dog!

label: Temple Knight Armour
title: Temple Knight Armour
lead:
Temple Knight armour may refer to the following:

* Initiate armour
** Initiate sallet
** Initiate hauberk
** Initiate cuisse
** Initiate harness m

label: Temple Knights
title: Temple Knights
lead:
The Temple Knights are an elite section of the White Knights, dedicated to defeating any threat to Falador. To join, the applicant must be at least a White Knight. Sir Tiffy Cashien is head of recruitment. Players must complete the Recruitment Drive quest in order to join the Temple Knights.

It is reasonable to assume that they have been established for an extremely long time, as Juna the snake has heard of them, despite being in the Chasm of Tears since the end of the Third Age.

label: Temple of Ikov
title: Temple of Ikov
lead: Temple of Ikov is a quest featuring Lucien, a Mahjarrat. The quest revolves around the infiltration of the Temple of Ikov in order to steal a powerful artefact known as the Staff of Armadyl.

label: Temple of Ikov (dungeon)
title: Temple of Ikov (dungeon)
lead:
The Temple of Ikov is a dungeon underneath Hemenster. The main entrance to the dungeon is located south of the Ranging Guild and secondary entrance inside the house in McGrubor's Wood requires a shiny key.

There are no requirements to access the dungeon, however players that have not completed the Temple of Ikov quest will need to wear a pendant of lucien to pass through the gates north-west of the southern entrance.

label: Temple of Ralos
title: Temple of Ralos
lead:
Temple of Ralos may refer to:

* Temple (Civitas illa Fortis)
* Ortus temple
* Outer Fortis temple
* Stonecutter Outpost temple
* The Teomat

label: Temporary event
title: Temporary event
lead: Temporary events are special limited-time activities that do not directly impact regular gameplay, though sometimes events reward participants with cosmetic items, membership, or commemorative scenery placed permanently in the game.

label: temporary skill boost
title: temporary skill boost
lead: Skill boosts increase a player's level in one or more skills. They usually come from consuming foods or potions, but they can also come from: executing special attacks, equipping certain weapons, or standing in a specific area. Boosts are useful for increasing skilling success or performing actions above their current level.

label: Temporary skill boost/Sailing
title: Temporary skill boost/Sailing
lead:
Players can boost the Sailing skill in order to be able to recruit higher-level crewmates (providing other requirements are met, if any exist), as well as build higher-tier facilities and core boat parts.

If boosting to build a higher rank facility, such as a higher level cannon or salvaging hook, the boost must be maintained in order for the player or crewmates to keep using it. Core boat parts and cargo holds can still be used below the required level, however.

label: Temporary skill boost/Slayer
title: Temporary skill boost/Slayer
lead: Players can boost the Slayer skill in order to be able to kill higher-level Slayer monsters. If the player's Slayer skill drops below the threshold to kill a monster while fighting it, the player will stop attacking the monster and will be told they need higher Slayer in order to attack it. Boosts do not allow players to acquire tasks that require a Slayer level above their base unboosted level.

label: Temporary skill drain
title: Temporary skill drain
lead:
A temporary skill drain is an effect caused by items, monsters, weapon and ammunition special attacks or passive abilities, or interactions with scenery or the environment, which temporarily lowers a player's level in one or more skills. This can be counter-acted with temporary skill boosts or stat restoration.

Skill drains on players can prevent them from performing specific actions if their level is underneath the requirement, particularly when attempting skilling activities. For example, a player grinding Musca mushrooms would get 6 musca powder at 80 and higher Herblore; however, if this was drained to 62, the player would get 4 powder per action. Likewise, if a player had 85 Mining but was drained 5 levels to 80, they would not be able to mine runite rocks until the stat is restored.

label: tendrils
title: tendrils
lead: Tendrils are that are found as scenery on several places across Gielinor, most notably the Tar Swamp, Pit of Pestilence and the Abyss.

label: Tendrils (Green)
title: Tendrils (Green)
lead:
Green Tendrils are pieces of scenery that can be found in several places among Gielinor:
* In the Pit of Pestilence.
* Near Vespula in the Chambers of Xeric. (No Dripping tendrils, only Tendrils and Stinking tendrils)
* In the Abyssal Nexus.

Players cannot interact with them, but they can be examined.

label: Tent door (Bedabin Camp)
title: Tent door (Bedabin Camp)
lead: A tent door is located at the entrance to the north tent in the Bedabin Camp. It is being guarded by the Bedabin Nomad Guard, who will only allow players to use it during The Tourist Trap quest. Behind the door is an experimental anvil, which is used to smith prototype dart tips.

label: Tentacle
title: Tentacle
lead:
Tentacle may refer to:

*Abyssal tentacle, weapon created by combining an abyssal whip with a kraken tentacle
*Enormous Tentacle, part of the Kraken's body
*Kraken tentacle, item obtained as a drop from cave krakens and the Kraken
*Ten-tacles, an elite Kraken combat achievement
*Tentacle (Abyssal Sire), monster that is controlled by the Abyssal Sire
*Tentacle (Shadow Realm), found within the Shadow Realm in the Lassar Undercity
*Tentacle (Temple Trekking), monster fought during the Temple Trekking minigame
*Tentacle (The Whisperer), used by the Whisperer in its standard attack
*Tentacle pool, pool that can be built in the oubliette in a player-owned house
*Pygmy kraken tentacle, item obtained as a drop from Pygmy krakens
*Spined kraken tentacle, item obtained as a drop from Spined krakens
*Armoured kraken tentacle, item obtained as a drop from Armoured krakens
*Vampyre kraken tentacle, item obtained as a drop from Vampyre krakens

label: Tentacle pool (interface item)
title: Tentacle pool (interface item)
lead:
The Tentacle pool is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Tentacle pool.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Tenti pineapple
title: Tenti pineapple
lead:
The Tenti pineapple is a quest item used in The Tourist Trap quest. It is received from the Bedabin Camp bandits to bribe the guards to let the player pass into the slave mining dungeon. Like ordinary pineapples, it has an 'Eat' option, but cannot be consumed whole, and it is possible to use a knife on it, giving the option to cut it into pineapple rings or pineapple chunks. It can also be placed in a compost bin to create supercompost. If it is lost, it can be re-obtained from Al Shabim until The Tourist Trap is completed.

Also known as the 'Bedabin ambrosia' (according to the Bedabin nomads) it is a special pineapple that according to Al Shabim is grown in a secret location in order to prevent thieves from raiding them.

label: Tenzing
title: Tenzing
lead:
Tenzing is a living in the house just west of Burthorpe. The player needs to go through his house to take the secret path past Death Plateau on the way to Trollheim.

He is involved in the Death Plateau and Troll Romance quests. He sells climbing boots for 12 coins each.

label: Teokan
title: Teokan
lead:
Teokan is a position that exists in the Varlamorean religion of Losanium, referring to a high priest. The two major gods, Ralos and Ranul, each have their own Teokan.

The current Teokan of Ralos is Servius, responsible for leading the Church of Ralos; the current Teokan of Ranul is Metzli, responsible for leading the Sect of Ranul. The Teokan also is responsible for appointing teoki of their respective god.

label: Teoki
title: Teoki
lead: Teoki is a position that exists in the Varlamorian religion of Losanium, referring to a number of senior priests appointed by the Teokan of their respective god. Seven teoki exist in both the Church of Ralos and the Sect of Ranul, and they are tasked with maintaining holy sites across Varlamore.

label: Terror dog (interface item)
title: Terror dog (interface item)
lead:
The Terror dog is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Terror dog

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Terrorbird
title: Terrorbird
lead:
Terrorbirds (Aves Terror) are animals used by the gnomes as mounts. They are found on the west side of the Tree Gnome Stronghold. They are also involved in the Rag and Bone Man II quest, where the ones that don't have any gnomes mounted upon them will drop a special bone needed for the quest.

Killing a Terrorbird is a requirement for the Easy Western Provinces Diary.

label: Terry Balando
title: Terry Balando
lead:
Terrance Balando, known by his nickname Terry, is an archaeological expert at the Digsite who is interested in the historical value of items which might be found there. Players can use items on him and he will tell them if there is any archaeological significance to the item. Players who bring him 3 gold nuggets will also receive 1 gold ore in return.

He is involved in the Desert Treasure I quest, where he translates a set of etchings near the beginning of the quest. If players speak to him while wielding an ancient staff, he will say it is incredible and will comment on the Zarosian symbol.

label: Thalzar
title: Thalzar
lead:
Thalzar was one of a trio of wizards to escape Crandor after Elvarg laid waste to the island. He, Lozar and Melzar (of whom Melzar is the last survivor, later to be killed by the adventurer) each took a piece of the Crandor map, in the hope of preventing others from journeying there. It is assumed Thalzar died peacefully - his third of the map is found in a sealed room in the Dwarven Mine, and the Oracle is now charged with ensuring only those strong enough to defeat Elvarg are given access to Thalzar's map piece.

During the Dragon Slayer I quest, players will encounter an engraving from Thalzar on the lid of the chest containing one of the map pieces. It makes brief mention of the events on Crandor and asks the player to reconsider taking the map piece within.

label: Thammaron
title: Thammaron
lead:
Thammaron was an Avernic demon. He was the chief lieutenant to Zamorak and a major ally of his who helped him to overthrow Zaros. During the God Wars, Thammaron and his mighty army attacked Uzer and destroyed it, but not before being mortally wounded by the elite guard of clay golems in the process. After the battle, Thammaron retreated to his own plane, where he later died of his injuries.

Thammaron once had a sceptre, which is now a possible drop from revenants. It was lost during the Battle of Uzer and claimed by a warrior who later died and became a revenant. It gives a significant boost in Magic accuracy and damage when fighting monsters in the Wilderness.

label: Thammaron's robes
title: Thammaron's robes
lead:
Thammaron's robes were a armour set, proposed alongside the Warding skill. They were a set of degradable mage robes that would have required level 60 Magic to wear. In order to ward the robes, players required level 70 Warding, along with occult and mystic silk.

The set had the passive effect Thammaron's Fury when the entire set was worn, the effect applies an additional 50% magic accuracy and 12.5% magic damage when attacking any
non-player character in the Wilderness. While the effect would stack with Thammaron's sceptre, the sceptre would not count towards activating Thammaron's Fury.

label: Thanksgiving event
title: Thanksgiving event
lead: Thanksgiving events were annual holiday events that occurred towards the end of November.

label: Thatch spar
title: Thatch spar
lead:
Thatch spar may refer to:

*Thatch spar light, from light jungle
*Thatch spar med, from medium jungle
*Thatch spar dense, from dense jungle

label: Thaumaturge armour
title: Thaumaturge armour
lead:
Thaumaturge armour was a armour set, proposed alongside the Warding skill. They were a degradable mage set that would have required level 40 Magic to wear. In order to ward the set, players required level 50 Warding, along with occult and dark silk.

The set had the passive effect Spellwarp when the entire set was worn, the effect decreased the attack speed of combat spells from the standard spellbook from 5 to 4 (3 seconds to 2.4 seconds). As the thaumaturge warper was equipped in the shield slot, a tome of fire could not be equipped to benefit from the Spellwarp effect.

label: The Adventurous
title: The Adventurous
lead:
The Adventurous is Bill Teach's ship. He will sail players between Port Phasmatys and Mos Le'Harmless after the Cabin Fever quest. It can be found in both ports' docks.

During Cabin Fever, the player replaces Bill's crew to help fend off an enemy attack. The Adventurous is damaged by cannon fire from Bill's rival captain's ship but she is repaired and survives the battle.

label: The Black Bug
title: The Black Bug
lead:
rebuilt for the Black Bug.]]
The Black Bug is a dwarven mining company presumably based in Keldagrim. The director of the company may be chosen to have their head replace the head of the statue of King Alvis during The Giant Dwarf quest.

Unlike the eight main Consortium mining companies, the Black Bug do not physically appear in the game, as the company is merely an error handler chosen when the game is unable to determine which company director the player chose to replace the head of the giant dwarf statue. This can be accomplished by choosing to skip the consortium meeting cutscene at the end of the quest, which causes the value telling the game which statue head to use to never be set. As a result, the statue will remain headless permanently, and text regarding it will refer to the Black Bug.

label: The Butcher (vampyre)
title: The Butcher (vampyre)
lead:
The Butcher is an erratic vampyre who created the Pestilent Bloat, an undead monstrosity made from dead body parts of various creatures, for Verzik Vitur. While his main goal in making the Bloat was to please Verzik in hopes of receiving a reward, his notes also suggest that he feared a punishment from her if he did not succeed.

When he reported to Verzik Vitur's chambers to show her his creature, he found her chamber empty except for her Nylocas; he then became fearful that he had witnessed something he was not meant to see.

label: The Carlyle Group
title: The Carlyle Group
lead:
The Carlyle Group is a global investment firm. They had their IPO on NASDAQ in May of 2012. In 2020, it was the world's second largest private equity firm by capital raised over the previous five years. By 2025, its rank has fallen to sixth largest by the same metric.

In January 2021, the Carlyle Group acquired Jagex from Macarthur Fortune Holding.

label: The Desert
title: The Desert
lead:
The Desert is a music track unlocked in members parts of Kharidian Desert. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing this track, Arabian 3, Desert Heat, Desert Voyage, Egypt, Scarab, Sphinx, and Sunburn.

In Classic mode, the track plays in or east of the Bedabin Camp.

label: The Desert Trout
title: The Desert Trout
lead:
The Desert Trout was the ship of Taiman and his crew from Al Kharid. It was a fishing boat and sailed out from Al Kharid every fortnight to fish. However not long ago, the ship was attacked near Karamja by Tempoross, an ancient sea spirit. The ship was sunk by the powerful storm Tempoross whipped up. Taiman and his crew all survived and washed ashore near Al Kharid, where they reported the event to Chancellor Hassan, who called upon help from more fishers to fight against Tempoross, thus forming the Spirit Anglers.

The crew of The Desert Trout consisted of four members: Taiman the skipper, Koanee the navigator, Timallus the chef, and Lauretta the crewmember.

label: The Diary of Randas
title: The Diary of Randas
lead: The Diary of Randas is a book by Randas that can only be read during the Underground Pass quest by talking to Koftik at the bridge at the beginning of the Underground Pass. It does not exist as an item in-game, though a copy can be obtained in the Grand Library in Prifddinas.

label: The Dig Site
title: The Dig Site
lead: The Dig Site is a quest where you must pass an archaeology exam for the Varrock Museum to be able to excavate the site where the city of Saranthium previously stood, but you discover something else...

label: The Emir's Arena
title: The Emir's Arena
lead: The Emir's Arena is a music track that is unlocked in or around the Emir's Arena.

label: The Fisher King
title: The Fisher King
lead:
The Fisher King ruled the Fisher Realm and protected the Holy Grail. During the quest he and his land have a connected sickness. This is cured only when Sir Percival, his son, arrives to take the crown from his father's sick head. At the end of the quest, it is speculated he dies.

During the quest, the Fisher King appears to be wearing a white chainbody, though it has a shoulder pad and a sleeve on the left arm. He is also wearing white platelegs, leather gloves, and wielding a staff.

label: The Forgotten Cemetery
title: The Forgotten Cemetery
lead:
The Forgotten Cemetery is a minor area in the Wilderness at around level 30. It contains ankous, ghosts, skeletons, zombies, and a man. The cemetery is visited by those wishing to complete the Wilderness Diary, as a medium task requires the player to kill an ankou in the Wilderness and is the one of the two locations where they can be found.

The Agility shortcut (level 60) just north-west of the cemetery is a one-way shortcut from the God Wars Dungeon into the Wilderness.

label: The Forgotten Four
title: The Forgotten Four
lead:
The Forgotten Four is a term used to refer to four important figures in the Zarosian Empire who feature prominently in Desert Treasure II. These figures are:
* The Whisperer
* Carnifex Maximus Vardorvis
* Praefectus Classis Perseriya
* Duke Sucellus of the Sixth Legion

Within PvM context, the term instead refers to the bosses that are fought during and after the quest (i.e. the Leviathan in place of Perseriya).

label: The Fractured Archive
title: The Fractured Archive
lead:
The Fractured Archive is an upcoming raid first announced during the Winter Summit 2026, scheduled to release in late 2026. Described as the "toughest raid yet", the raid will be a combat-focused "bossing experience" with minimal skilling or puzzle elements in a manner similar to that of the Theatre of Blood. . It will be the fourth raid released in Old School RuneScape.

Teams of up to 8 players can enter the raid, with the difficulty planned to scale from 2-8 players, meaning it would be possible to solo the raid, but would be more difficult. Upon release, team wipes will reset the raid fully, but in the weeks following its release, this is planned to change to a system similar to Tombs of Amascut, where raiders have infinite retries with reduced rewards and fewer resources.

label: The Gauntlet/Strategies
title: The Gauntlet/Strategies
lead: This page shows various strategies and in-depth mechanics of The Gauntlet and The Corrupted Gauntlet.

label: The Grand Tree
title: The Grand Tree
lead: The Grand Tree is a gnome quest centred on protecting the Grand Tree from dying upon the gnome race.

label: The Great Battle
title: The Great Battle
lead:
The Great Battle was a conflict fought in the Year 98 of the Fifth Age.

The battle occurred at the Outpost north of Ardougne, between a small number of Zamorakian and Saradominist forces. The Zamorakians, amongst whom former Ardougnese citizens such as Drozal, had terrorised Ardougne for some time, their attacks causing the "Dreaded Years of Tragedy".

id: page:the hand in the sand/quick guide
label: The Hand in the Sand/Quick guide
title: The Hand in the Sand/Quick guide

label: The History of the Outpost
title: The History of the Outpost
lead: The History of the Outpost is a book that can be found in the bookcase at the Outpost after completion of Making History. It can not be removed from the bookcase. The book details the 140 year history of the Outpost.

label: The Hueycoatl/Strategies
title: The Hueycoatl/Strategies
lead:
The Hueycoatl is a group boss located atop the Darkfrost in Varlamore, requiring only completion of Children of the Sun and having spoken to Taala at the base camp to fight. Players can enter the public area via the chain to fight the Hueycoatl with up to 20 players at once, or create a private instance at the meeting flag next to the bank buffalo. Creating a private group/solo instance costs 50,000 coins (25,000 if the player is eligible to claim the hard Combat Achievement rewards).

If the player dies while fighting the Hueycoatl, their grave will appear at the base camp.

label: The Hutnuts
title: The Hutnuts
lead: The Hutnuts are a non-official development team at Jagex. The current lineup consists of Mod Ed, Mod Nin, and Mod Lenny. The group made their debut with the release of the Scrambled! quest.

label: The Journal of Owen Clearstone
title: The Journal of Owen Clearstone
lead: The Journal of Owen Clearstone is a compilation of stories that released on the Old School RuneScape website during the lead-up to the release of the Sailing skill. The stories are stylized as entries in a journal, and are focused around a man named Owen Clearstone taking up sailing to search for his father, Graham Clearstone, who has gone missing after taking a risky job escorting a special cargo.

label: The Kendal (God)
title: The Kendal (God)
lead:
The Kendal is a god of the mountain from the Mountain Tribe's legends.

During the Mountain Daughter quest, a man impersonates the Kendal because the Mountain Tribe are scared of their gods and magic, and he desires to be left alone. He also kills Asleif, the chieftain's daughter.

label: The Knight's Sword
title: The Knight's Sword
lead: The Knight's Sword is a free-to-play intermediate quest in which the White Knight Squire Asrol needs help making Sir Vyvin a new ceremonial sword.

label: The Lady of the Lake
title: The Lady of the Lake
lead:
The Lady of the Lake is a powerful sorceress and guardian and bestower of Excalibur. She is located on a peninsula in the lake south-east of Taverley. She plays a minor role in the Merlin's Crystal quest by giving the player Excalibur after the player passes her test.

If you lose your Excalibur, you can visit her and pay 500 coins for another one.

label: The Leviathan/Strategies
title: The Leviathan/Strategies
lead:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of the Leviathan. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by climbing the handholds with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted.

If the player dies while fighting the Leviathan, their grave will appear in the Scar by the rowboat. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

label: The Long Hall
title: The Long Hall
lead: The Long Hall is a tavern located in the northern part of Barbarian Village. Many Barbarians are found inside. It may be dangerous to attack more than one Barbarian, especially since one or two use Ranged weapons. It has a cooked meat spawn. There are also two non-stop fires at the end of the hall, useful for cooking fish caught in the river to the east. If players take an empty beer glass and use it on a barrel of beer, they will be attacked by barbarians that are close to the player.

label: The Mimic/Strategies
title: The Mimic/Strategies
lead: Upon completion of an elite or master clue scroll, the casket received has a chance of turning out to be a mimic chest. Mimic caskets can only be obtained from an elite or master reward casket after asking the strange casket to enable the chance to obtain a mimic casket (which is disabled by default). If players have not talked to the strange casket when they receive their first elite or master reward casket, they may choose whenever both casket types can roll for a mimic or not.

label: The Myreque
title: The Myreque
lead: The Myreque (Jagex pronunciation: ) is a resistance group trying to liberate Morytania from the grasp of Lord Drakan and his vampyres.

label: The Mysterious Adventurer
title: The Mysterious Adventurer
lead:
The Mysterious Adventurer is a book which can be read from Jorral's bookcase in the Outpost, after finishing the Making History quest. It describes an adventurer - which happens to be you - and lists selected achievements which refer to various quests.

The book cannot be taken from the bookcase.

id: page:the nightmare of ashihama: rewards beta
label: The Nightmare of Ashihama: Rewards Beta
title: The Nightmare of Ashihama: Rewards Beta
lead:
against the Fragment of Seren.]]

In preparation for the Nightmare of Ashihama boss, players were able to log in to an unrestricted world to test various rewards to be polled for the boss, including:
*Inquisitor's armour
**Inquisitor's great helm
**Inquisitor's hauberk
**Inquisitor's plateskirt
*Inquisitor's mace
*Nightmare staff
**Eldritch nightmare staff
**Harmonised nightmare staff
**Volatile nightmare staff
*Siren's tome

label: The Nightmare/Strategies
title: The Nightmare/Strategies
lead: The Nightmare is a group boss located in the Sisterhood Sanctuary, a dungeon beneath Slepe in Morytania.

label: The North
title: The North
lead:
The North is a frozen region of snow and ice where the city of Ghorrock once stood, along with its surrounding lands.

The area is often referred to by the Mahjarrat, expressing plans to “go North” or “meet again in the North” since an old shrine at the center of the area serves as the site of their rejuvenation ritual.

label: The Orange Flame
title: The Orange Flame
lead:
The Orange Flame is an unreleased dwarven mining company established primarily in the bustling city of Keldagrim, the capital of the Dwarven Realm. The Orange Flame was intended to replace The Red Axe in the Consortium following their departure, after the events of The Giant Dwarf.

The Orange Flame was never released, but its logo among other assets with the company's orange colour was added, intended to be used in the unreleased minigame Keldagrim Trading.

label: The Other 50% Reef
title: The Other 50% Reef
lead:
The Other 50% Reef is a coral reef in the Eastern Ocean. It earns its name from 50% Luke, a pirate that lost half of his body to the reef.

The reef is close to Luke's Reef, a similar reef that Luke discovered when he fell overboard on his captain's ship, The Inebriated. Like Luke's Reef, The Other 50% Reef consists almost entirely of a species of extremely spiky coral. However, it is considerably taller, nearly reaching a ship's hull.

label: The Pescallion
title: The Pescallion
lead:
The Pescallion is the leader of the Killer Gentoo Penguins. He has a number of sons, one of which is the head of research and development at the KGP Headquarters, Pescaling Pax. While his son, Pescaling Pax, seems to be mostly in charge of the penguins at the Iceberg, The Pescallion still has a somewhat active role, as a KGP spy mentions that the Pescallion sent him on a mission to Ardougne Zoo during the Cold War quest.

The Pescallion's location is unknown, but presumably Palingrad or another city in the Motherland. He is also notable for having found the Iceberg.

label: The Red Reef
title: The Red Reef
lead:
The Red Reef is an upcoming quest, scheduled for release in Summer 2026. It will be the second quest in the Tortugan quest series, following up on the events of Troubled Tortugans. It involves helping Floopa overcome her injury while investigating the dealings of the Red Reef Trading Company, a potential new threat to the Tortugan way of life. Completion of the quest will unlock access to the Sacred Grove. Partial completion of the quest is required to access the Red Rock.

Part of the quest will involve travelling underwater in a diving bell and repairing some broken coral dredgers that the company uses to collect coral from the seafloor.

label: The Rehnison household
title: The Rehnison household
lead:
The Rehnison household is a house in the northern part of West Ardougne. It is inhabited by Ted Rehnison, his wife Martha Rehnison, and their two children Billy and Milli.

Its basement, accessed by searching the eastern bed, acts as a shelter for the Ardougne Resistance during the Song of the Elves quest.

label: The Restless Ghost
title: The Restless Ghost
lead: The Restless Ghost is one of the six quests released with the launch of RuneScape Classic. In it, the player helps the priest of the Lumbridge church get rid of the ghost that haunts the Lumbridge graveyard.

id: page:the ribbiting tale of a lily pad labour dispute/quick guide
label: The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute/Quick guide
title: The Ribbiting Tale of a Lily Pad Labour Dispute/Quick guide

label: The Sage (disambiguation)
title: The Sage (disambiguation)
lead:
The Sage may refer to:
* The Sage from the Shattered Relics League
* The Sage from the Trailblazer Reloaded League
* The Sage from the Raging Echoes League
* The Sage from the Grid Master community event
* The Sage from the Demonic Pacts League

label: The Shadow
title: The Shadow
lead:
The Shadow is a music track that is unlocked on Crandor. Since 2021, it requires partial completion of Dragon Slayer I to unlock.

In Classic mode, there is a very small region on the west of Crandor that is accessible to Members only, which plays Fruits de Mer.

label: The Shrimp and Parrot
title: The Shrimp and Parrot
lead: The Shrimp and Parrot is a restaurant in Brimhaven. It is run by Alfonse the waiter. During the Heroes' Quest, it is revealed that the restaurant is actually a hideout for the Phoenix Gang, set up as part of a scheme to steal Scarface Pete's candlesticks.

label: The Sisterhood
title: The Sisterhood
lead:
The Sisterhood is an ancient Zamorakian order dating back to the Saradominist kingdom of Hallowvale in the Second Age. Originally an order of Saradominist healers (whose name is not known), they converted to Zamorak after seeing Phosani, the Justiciar of the Wolf, turn away from Saradomin's teachings. Those who refused to abandon his teachings were either killed or given to the vampyres as blood tithes.

After the order was "enlightened", the order became known as the Sisterhood, with Phosani as its leader (who they refer to as 'Mother'), and founded the town Slepe in eastern Morytania. Soon after, they began expanding underground, constructing a large sanctuary beneath the town, where they were free to perform their rites and offerings in relative peace.

label: The Strangler
title: The Strangler
lead: The Strangler is a parasitic organism that has infected a forest in Zeah, now known as The Stranglewood.

label: The Times of Lathas
title: The Times of Lathas
lead:
The Times of Lathas is a book found in Jorral's bookcase inside the Outpost north of West Ardougne after finishing the Making History quest. The book cannot be taken from the bookcase. While the book can be interacted with, its contents are only referred to rather than being available to read. The book contains information about the kings from the family of Ardignas and their line of succession.

The book states that here have been five kings since the Ardignas family came into power 68 years ago, and that the current king is King Lathas (or King Thoros if Song of the Elves has been completed). This information puts the creation of the book between the years 168 and 169 of the Fifth Age. The book's author is unknown.

label: The Toad and Chicken
title: The Toad and Chicken
lead:
The Toad and Chicken is a bar and an inn found in Burthorpe, north of Taverley. It caters primarily to the soldiers and citizens of Burthorpe. Wizard's mind bomb, Dwarven stout and Asgarnian ale are all purchasable from Tostig for two coins each. Players can also find a trapdoor leading to the Rogues' Den behind the bar on the . Players can also pickup an Asgarnian ale and an empty beer glass on the bar counter.

Players doing the Death Plateau quest can find Harold in the last room on the of the inn. On the , players can help Bernald, in the garden, during the Garden of Tranquillity quest by curing his grape vines.

label: The Tourist Trap
title: The Tourist Trap
lead: The Tourist Trap is an intermediate quest set in the Kharidian Desert. The quest involves an undercover rescue operation into a slave camp to save an Al Kharidian woman's daughter.

label: The Tower
title: The Tower
lead: The Tower is a music track that is unlocked in East Ardougne. It can also be heard in Ardougne's western sewers. In Classic mode, it also unlocks in the basement of the Chaos Druid Tower.

label: The Whisperer/Strategies
title: The Whisperer/Strategies
lead:
After the completion of Desert Treasure II - The Fallen Empire, players can fight a stronger variant of the Whisperer than the one fought during the quest. An even stronger awakened variant can be fought by disturbing the Odd Figure with an awakener's orb in the player's inventory and selecting "Yes" when prompted in a fresh instance - having obtained an orb in the instance will not cause the prompt to appear.

If the player dies while fighting the Whisperer, their grave will appear in the Ruins of Camdozaal, by the rope leading to the Lassar Undercity. Players will have their reclamation fee reduced by 75% until they have five kills, after which the standard death cost will apply.

label: Theatre of Blood Rewards Testing
title: Theatre of Blood Rewards Testing
lead:
Duration: 8 March - 17 March 2018
 against Glough.]]

In preparation of the Theatre of Blood, players were able to log in to an unrestricted world to test various rewards to be polled for the raid, including:

label: Theatre of Blood/Entry Mode
title: Theatre of Blood/Entry Mode
lead:
In Entry Mode, the player is given an unlimited amount of deaths to try to finish the raid. Hardcore ironmen will lose their status on the first death.

Players will get 80% less loot in Entry Mode compared to Normal Mode. Additionally, Entry Mode does not grant uniques or a chance at the pet. Each death takes away from the loot available at the end of the raid.

label: Theatre of Blood/Hard Mode
title: Theatre of Blood/Hard Mode
lead:
Theatre of Blood's Hard Mode is a Theatre of Blood raid with increased difficulty released on 3 June 2021. Similarly to Challenge Mode Chambers of Xeric, the enemies have more health, though their combat stats are usually the same or lower, and the bosses' mechanics are modified.

To attempt a hard mode raid, all participants must have at least one normal mode completion. However, it is not recommended to attempt hard mode until the player is experienced with the tactics required in normal mode, as they are more or less the same as in hard mode.

label: Theatre of Blood/Records
title: Theatre of Blood/Records
lead: This list contains historical documentation of Theatre of Blood records. Only records from Jagex's official Theatre of Blood records page prior to its decommissioning are listed here.

label: Theatre of Blood/Strategies
title: Theatre of Blood/Strategies
lead:
The Theatre of Blood is a raid located in Ver Sinhaza. It is the second raid released to date.

Unlike in Tombs of Amascut, players are not allowed to teleport out of the Theatre of Blood - the only way to escape in the middle of a fight is through an escape crystal, sold by the Mysterious Stranger outside the raid for each. Players who die during the raid will be placed in purgatory. If the room is successfully cleared by the remaining players, those who have died will be reunited with the rest of their team. If the entire team dies, the raid will end and team members will have to reclaim their items from the chest for . Dying elsewhere without claiming items from the chest will result in them being lost for good.

label: Theatre of Blood/Strategies/Nylocas
title: Theatre of Blood/Strategies/Nylocas
lead:
The Nylocas encountered in the Theatre of Blood have consistent spawning and aggression patterns that many players can use to recognize the highest priority targets.

Below a chart of each wave of Nylocas encountered. The only variable to the waves are how often the waves spawn. Before wave 20, the cap is 12 nylocas; afterwards, the cap is doubled to 24.

label: Theme
title: Theme
lead: Theme is a music track that is unlocked at the Coal Trucks, or in the Waterfall Dungeon.

label: Theoretical experience rates
title: Theoretical experience rates
lead: This page outlines the theoretical experience rates for certain skill training methods.

label: Thermonuclear smoke devil/Strategies
title: Thermonuclear smoke devil/Strategies
lead: The thermonuclear smoke devil is a boss variant of the regular smoke devils, requiring 93 Slayer to kill. Similarly to Kraken, despite its high requirements, the boss fight is mechanically simple and kills are quite quick, reaching 60–100 kills per hour depending on gear and strategies used.

label: Thessalia
title: Thessalia
lead: Thessalia Nitter runs Thessalia's Fine Clothes, a makeover shop in Varrock. Items of clothing can be bought from her, or a player can get a makeover to change their appearance underneath their worn items free of charge. She also exchanges frog tokens for a royal frog costume, a frog mask, or an experience lamp. She will also return bunny ears and scythes to a player if they have lost them.

label: Thessalia's Fine Clothes.
title: Thessalia's Fine Clothes.
lead: Thessalia's Fine Clothes is located in central Varrock square. In addition to selling clothes, Thessalia will offer to give a player a "total clothing-makeover". This allows the player to change the default shirt or trousers they chose when creating their character. Browsing the store is a requirement for the Easy Varrock Diary. An old woman named Iffie sits against the northern wall of the store.

label: Thessalia's Makeovers
title: Thessalia's Makeovers
lead:
Thessalia's Makeovers was a shop in Varrock that could change a player's default clothing free of charge. The makeover was run by Thessalia, who also owns another clothing shop in the same building. Players could not customise shoes here — they must have instead gone to Yrsa's Shoe Store. There was no fee attached to the service, neither for the tops or for the legwear, allowing players to customise their default outfit as often as they like.

To get a makeover, talk to Thessalia and ask for one, or right-click her and choose "Makeover". Equipment can be worn while getting a makeover, but a player will not be able to see the changes afterwards until they remove anything in the torso or leg slots.

label: Thick Skin
title: Thick Skin
lead:
Thick Skin is a Prayer that the player starts with upon creating their character. Thick Skin increases the player's Defence by 5%.

Like all other stat-affecting prayers, it cannot be used in conjunction with another prayer that increases the player's Defence level, such as Rock Skin, with the notable exceptions of Deadeye and Mystic Vigour which allow for simultaneous use.

label: Thief
title: Thief
lead: A thief is a criminal found in various places around Gielinor, and can be a challenge for new or low level players. They can be either male or female. One of their characteristics is that they will stop attacking and retreat when at low health.

label: thieves' armband
title: thieves' armband
lead:
A thieves' armband is one of the three items required by Achietties during Heroes' Quest. To obtain it for the quest, you must speak to your gang leader (Black Arm Gang, Katrine; Phoenix Gang, Straven). You will also need a partner from the other gang.

Firstly, both of you must go to the Black Arm Gang's hideout Brimhaven. The Black Arm gang member should be wearing full Black armour (Black full helmet, Black platebody, Black platelegs). Then, the Black Arm gang member is to retrieve an ID to enter the building, but you must get two candlesticks from Scarface Pete first. (Note: You need to give one to your Phoenix gang partner.) Then, you must retrieve a Miscellaneous key, in order for your partner to range the level 22 Grip, who drops the key required for the armband. Both of you must bring your candlestick back to your gang leaders for reward, that is: Straven for the Phoenix gang member, and Katrine for the Black Arm gang member.

label: Thieving
title: Thieving
lead: Thieving is a members-only skill which allows players to obtain coins and items by stealing from market stalls, chests, or by pickpocketing non-player characters. This skill also allows players to unlock doors and disarm traps.

label: Thieving Level Up!
title: Thieving Level Up!
lead: Thieving Level Up! is a Jingle for leveling Thieving.

label: Thieving Level Up! (Unlocks)
title: Thieving Level Up! (Unlocks)
lead: Thieving Level Up! (Unlocks) is a jingle for levelling Thieving.

label: Thieving training
title: Thieving training
lead:
This is a guide for training the Thieving skill.

For maximum theoretical experience rates for certain Thieving training methods, see this page.

label: Thieving/Experience table
title: Thieving/Experience table
lead:
This table shows all possible experience sources for Thieving in the game, as well as all interactions that require a Thieving level. It also lists the items involved in the interactions, as well as other skills involved in processing the item.

While some of these entries may be listed as Free-to-play, the only thieving-related action that may be done on Free-to-play worlds is unlocking the Port Sarim jail door, which grants no Thieving experience on those worlds. NPCs cannot be pickpocketed when not on a Members server.

label: Think
title: Think
lead:
Think is the fifth listed emote. Upon use the player scratches their head.

This emote is already unlocked upon making an account.

label: Third Age
title: Third Age
lead:
The Third Age, also known as The God Wars, is one of the five ages of Gielinor, between the Second and Fourth Age. 
The Third Age lasted around 4,000 years and officially began when Zamorak, having recently ascended to godhood, began a massive war. These God Wars would last throughout the entire Third Age, and their end was marked by the establishment of the Edicts of Guthix. The God Wars led to millions of deaths, the destruction of dozens of major settlements and cities, the near complete eradication of all references to Zaros, and the extinction of several races.

The God Wars and concurring conflicts are by far the most notable events that happened during the Third Age, although others did occur. For example, the Void Knights were established during the Third Age and the dwarves founded Keldagrim (albeit as a result of them fleeing from the war).

label: Third Age minions
title: Third Age minions
lead:
Third Age minions may refer to:

*Third Age Warrior
*Third Age Mage
*Third Age Ranger

label: Thistle
title: Thistle
lead: Thistles are a common decorative scenery found across Gielinor, with notable concentrations near Lumbridge, the Fight Arena, and Hosidius. They are purely decorative and have no particular function. A similar-looking thistle can be constructed in the garden of a player-owned house.

label: Thistle (disambiguation)
title: Thistle (disambiguation)
lead:
Thistle can refer to:
* Thistle, a common decorative scenery.
* Thistle (Construction), a decoration that can be built in the garden of a player-owned house
* Troll thistle, an item used in Eadgar's Ruse to make the troll potion
** Dried thistle, made by drying the troll thistle on a fire
** Ground thistle, made by crushing a dried thistle with a pestle and mortar
** Thistle (Trollheim), the appearance of the troll thistle on the ground atop Trollheim

label: Thormac
title: Thormac
lead:
Thormac is a sorcerer who can be found at the top of his home; the Sorcerer's Tower, found south of Seers' Village. Players must speak to him to begin the Scorpion Catcher quest.

After completing the quest, he can perform a service for players which will enchant a battlestaff into a mystic staff. This service costs 40,000 coins. The price is reduced to 30,000 coins if the player has completed the Hard Kandarin Diary, or 20,000 if the player has completed the Elite Kandarin Diary.

label: Thorny hedge (interface item)
title: Thorny hedge (interface item)
lead:
The Thorny hedge is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Thorny hedge.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Thorobshuun
title: Thorobshuun
lead:
The Thorobshuun are a goblin tribe that live in Goblin Village and wear red goblin mail. In the Goblin Diplomacy quest, players make peace between the Garagorshuun and the Thorobshuun.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "Goblins of the Hills".

label: Thrall
title: Thrall
lead: Thralls are undead beings which can be summoned to attack enemies.

label: Thrantax the Mighty
title: Thrantax the Mighty
lead:
Thrantax the Mighty is a ghost that players must bring under their control during the Merlin's Crystal quest. This can be done by using the magic words found under the chaos altar.

If the player uses the wrong words, Thrantax will attack them. The player may attempt to fight him or run away. Either way, he will despawn shortly.

label: thread
title: thread
lead:
Thread is used along with a needle to make armour out of leather, dragon leather and cured yak-hide. Each thread spool has 5 uses before it is consumed. A "use" means an action performed, not number of leathers used (e.g. making vambraces, which use 1 hide each, consumes thread at the same rate as making chaps, which use 2 hides each).

After completion of Death on the Isle, a Costume needle can be used for crafting without needing thread.

label: Three headed dragon of Jarn
title: Three headed dragon of Jarn
lead:
The three headed dragon of Jarn, was a dragon defeated by Arrav in the Fourth Age.

It is unknown whether Jarn refers to a location, a person, or some other title.

label: Three wise monkeys
title: Three wise monkeys
lead:
The three wise monkeys - Mizaru, Kikazaru, and Iwazaru - are three monkeys who reside in the Temple of Marimbo. They interact with the player as one entity and help you during the Freeing King Awowogei subquest of Recipe for Disaster. When first asked about it by the player, they say that each of them was cursed by King Awowogei to lose one sense, to try to prevent them from revealing his favourite dish. They say he had intended for them each to lose all their senses, but the magician who cursed them had only enough ingredients for one spell.

Mizaru is blind, Kikazaru is deaf and Iwazaru is mute, but they overcome their disabilities by co-operating with each other and communicating via sign language.

label: Throne
title: Throne
lead: Throne may refer to:

label: Throne (Construction)
title: Throne (Construction)
lead:
Thrones are furniture which can be built on the throne hotspots in the Throne Room of a player-owned house. Thrones are built in matching pairs. Despite their lack of any particularly useful functions, thrones are often built as a show of wealth and Construction expertise, especially the Demonic throne.

Anybody can sit on a throne, despite thrones having the examine description "Sit here and rule all you survey."

label: Throne (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
title: Throne (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
lead: A throne can be found on the of the Grand Tree, located within the Tree Gnome Stronghold. This kingly seat is for the royal behind of King Narnode Shareen.

label: Thrower Troll
title: Thrower Troll
lead:
A Thrower Troll is a troll that attacks with ranged. They are relatively annoying monsters that throw rocks at passing adventurers, regardless of being engaged in combat or not. They are rarely ever on their own, preferring to be together in groups. Unlike most other monsters, the thrower troll's attacks are always successful hits. As they are found in multi-way areas, being attacked by three or more thrower trolls at once can be deadly.

Equipping a Neitiznot shield will reduce their maximum hit to 2.

label: Thrower troll (Trollheim)
title: Thrower troll (Trollheim)
lead:
A thrower troll is a troll that attacks with ranged. They are aggressive monsters that throw rocks at passing adventurers, regardless of being engaged in combat or not. They are rarely ever on their own, preferring to be together in groups. Unlike most other monsters, the thrower troll's attacks are always successful hits. As they are found in multi-way areas, being attacked by three or more thrower trolls at once can be deadly.

Equipping a Neitiznot shield will reduce their maximum hit to 2.

label: throwing axe
title: throwing axe
lead:
Throwing axes are a type of members ranged throwing weapon that target a monster's light ranged defence. They must either be bought from the Tribal Weapons store at the Ranging Guild or from another player, as they cannot be made using the Smithing skill. They can be wielded with shields and prayer books for protection.

In terms of both damage and ranged attack accuracy, throwing axes are stronger than throwing knives, but slower. Unlike other throwing weapons, throwing axes cannot be poisoned.

label: throwing knife
title: throwing knife
lead:
Throwing knives are a type of members ranged throwing weapon that target a monster's light ranged defence. They can be poisoned and can be wielded with shields or god books for protection.

Throwing knives can be created via the Smithing skill, with the exception of black and dragon knives. Each bar will produce 5 throwing knives of the corresponding metal.

label: Throwing rope
title: Throwing rope
lead: The throwing rope is an animation item used in the Underground Pass. It is temporarily wielded by the player during the animation when tying a rope to the rope swing. Aside from this, the item cannot be obtained.

label: Thug
title: Thug
lead:
Thugs are level 10 aggressive monsters who are found exclusively in the Wilderness. A group of them can be found in low level Wilderness, north of the Grand Exchange, and another group can be found at the beginning of the Wilderness section of the Edgeville Dungeon.

They are rarely killed, except by players trying to obtain a looting bag who kill them due to their low hitpoints, as well as their locations being out of the way from the more heavily trafficked sections of the Wilderness.

label: Thurgo
title: Thurgo
lead:
Thurgo, the supposed last of the Imcando dwarf race, is found outside the Asgarnian Ice Dungeon, south of Port Sarim, and just north of Mudskipper Point. You can use the fairy ring code and run north to reach him. He is a master of Smithing and players who have achieved level 99 in Smithing can purchase the Smithing cape from him for 99,000 coins. Additionally, he is one of the main characters encountered during the The Knight's Sword quest.

Using the book Imcandoria's fall on him will reveal hidden dialogue in which he asks the player that they bring him along should they plan an expedition to the Isle of Garmr mentioned in the book. After the player talks to Ramarno upon completing the Below Ice Mountain quest, Thurgo can be informed of the discovery of another living Imcando dwarf. He is taken aback by the revelation and has yet to meet Ramarno because he "wouldn't know what to say".

label: Tiara (disambiguation)
title: Tiara (disambiguation)
lead:
Tiara may refer to

*Tiara
*Gold tiara
*Tiara mould
*A special tiara
*Fancy tiara
*Circlet of water

label: Tick eating
title: Tick eating
lead:
Tick-eating is the act of eating a piece of food between the time a monster's attack calculates its damage and when it hits the player.

Almost all monster attacks are capped to the player's current hp when the damage is first calculated. If a player stays at low hp when a monster first attacks, they can artificially lower the monster's maximum possible damage to their current hp. By healing after the attack calculates its damage but before the damage is actually applied, players can guarantee that they will survive the next attack even if the monster's (uncapped) maximum hit would have been sufficient to kill them.

label: tick manipulation
title: tick manipulation
lead:
Tick manipulation is a method in which players are able to use the tick system to their advantage in activities such as combat and skilling.

The RuneScape game engine runs on a unit of time colloquially referred to as "ticks", with each tick lasting 0.6 seconds (this amount of time can vary by hundredths or thousandths of a second due to things like server lag or the number of players on a world). By performing certain actions in the right order and at the right times, players can reduce the amount of ticks required for certain other actions to occur. Due to the click-intensive nature of some tick manipulation methods, many players shy away from using these methods in favour of more conventional methods.

label: Ticket
title: Ticket
lead: Ticket may refer to one of the following:

label: Ticket Dispenser
title: Ticket Dispenser
lead:
The ticket dispenser is found inside the Brimhaven Agility Arena where it will distribute Agility arena tickets and Brimhaven vouchers to players that tag the correct dispenser in time. There is no Agility level required to touch either this version of the dispenser, or the version that shoots darts, to claim a ticket. Tagging the marked dispenser awards 30 Agility experience for every 10 Agility levels (including Agility boosts or drains), maxing out at 300 if boosting to level 100 Agility, and will display the message You have received an Agility Arena Ticket and Brimhaven Voucher!.

Attempting to touch a marked pillar after having touched it and claimed experience already will not award additional experience or tickets, and will display the message You can only get one ticket at a time, wait till the arrow moves again..

label: Ticket Dispenser (darts)
title: Ticket Dispenser (darts)
lead:
The ticket dispensers with darts are Ticket Dispensers found inside the Brimhaven Agility Arena where it will distribute Agility arena tickets and Brimhaven vouchers to players that tag the correct dispenser in time, and are also an obstacle within the arena. Tagging the marked dispenser awards Agility experience scaled to the player's Agility level, and will display the message You have received an Agility Arena Ticket and Brimhaven Voucher!.

Attempting to touch a marked pillar after having touched it and claimed experience already will not award additional experience or tickets, and will display the message You can only get one ticket at a time, wait till the arrow moves again..

label: Ticket Merchant
title: Ticket Merchant
lead:
Ticket Merchants are members of the Ranging Guild who run the Ranging Guild Ticket Exchange. The shop deals exclusively in archery tickets which can be earned in the guild's target shooting minigame. As they are in the guild's western corner, they require level 40 Ranged to access.

You buy the whole quantity of items for the indicated price. That is, for example, you buy 30 Barb bolttips at once for 140 Archery tickets.

label: Tile
title: Tile
lead:
A tile is a formerly useless item that can be found in certain places in the Wilderness. Some tiles spawn in the Graveyard of Shadows and the western ruins.

Prior to the release of the Construction skill in 2006, many players speculated that tiles would be used in player-owned houses; however, they were never given a purpose when the skill was released. The tile remained a useless item until the robe bottom of ruin was discovered during the Crack the Clue III event, as a tile is required to obtain this reward.

lead: Time Out is a music track that is unlocked at the Maze Random event. It also plays at the end of Death on the Isle, when the player confronts Naiatli during the play.

lead: Tin bath is scenery that can be found in several places throughout Zeah, including Piscarilius and Varlamore.

label: Tin ore
title: Tin ore
lead: Tin ore can be mined at level 1 Mining providing 17.5 Mining experience. After mining tin rocks, it will take 2.4 seconds until it reappears. Tin ore is used with copper ore to smelt bronze bars. Smelting a bronze bar gives 6.2 Smithing experience.

label: Tin rocks
title: Tin rocks
lead:
Tin rocks contains tin ore mined upon with a pickaxe. It can be mined with any level Mining. Mining 14 tin ore and 14 copper ore (wielding the pickaxe as a weapon to free the 28th inventory space) and smelting them to bronze bars is a slow but effective way to raise Mining and Smithing.

For members, players can power level the Mining skill with tin ore in the Port Khazard mine and amass ore. This is because of two fast respawning tin rocks that are very close to a bank deposit box. These two tin rocks are the closest mining rocks to a fast bank source, which surpasses the West Falador mine and level 5 Agility shortcut.

label: Tinderbox
title: Tinderbox
lead:
The tinderbox is used primarily for lighting fires by clicking 'use' on the tinderbox, then clicking a log. A tinderbox can be bought in most general stores. It is also used to light and relight candles and lanterns, so any player venturing into a dark area such as the Lumbridge Caves should bring one in case their light source goes out.

When used on logs that the player has the Firemaking level to light, the messages You attempt to light the logs. and The fire catches and the logs begin to burn. are displayed. If the player does not have the Firemaking level, a variation of the message will display You need a Firemaking level of X to burn X logs.

label: Tithe Farm/Strategies
title: Tithe Farm/Strategies
lead:
This article is a guide to Tithe Farm. Always remember to include a spade, a seed dibber (or completed Bare-handed planting), and enough filled watering cans in your inventory.

If you are new to the minigame, it might be worthwhile to try a few rounds with fewer plants (for example, 8 per run) until you have gotten some practice.

label: Titles
title: Titles
lead: Titles refer to a list of in-game titles awarded to player often through quests and their dialogue. There is no official designation for this mechanic and as such how it is referred to may vary. Titles may include memberships of different orders and organisations or ranks within these. Frequently these have no direct advantageous effect for the player however when unlocked they often come bundled with another rewards which may be beneficial to the player. Similarly, some of these titles are ranks within their organisations and progression may unlock other content.

label: Toad (disambiguation)
title: Toad (disambiguation)
lead: Toad (not to be confused with Frog) may refer to any of the following:

label: toad batta
title: toad batta
lead:
A toad batta is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 12 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade toad battas are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 120 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a toad batta via gnome cooking with 26 Cooking, yielding 152 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Toad crunchies
title: Toad crunchies
lead:
Toad crunchies are a food that players consume in one bite, healing 8 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade t'd crunch are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 85 coins, with 3 in stock. They are also dropped by tortoises.

Members can make toad crunchies via gnome cooking with 10 Cooking, yielding 100 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Toad's legs
title: Toad's legs
lead:
Toad's legs are a food used in Cooking and Herblore. They are made by pulling the legs off of swamp toads found in the swamp of Tree Gnome Stronghold or lake south of Taverley, and from pickpocketing gnomes, requiring 75 Thieving. They heal for 3 Hitpoints. Adding them to a toadflax potion (unf) makes an Agility potion (3), requiring 34 Herblore, and yielding 80 Herblore experience. Toad's legs are main ingredients of the gnome cooking foods: Tangled toad's legs, toad batta and toad crunchies.

Toad's legs can be used as a fast food, a subtype of food that incurs non-standard attack or eating delays when consumed. Toad's legs may be consumed after other foods with almost no delay; this does not work if the toad's legs are eaten first, and does not work when eating two toad's legs in a row. This technique (commonly referred to as combo eating) can be further enhanced by drinking a dose of Saradomin brew after your alternative food item, and before your toad's legs (food>brew>toad's legs).

label: Toadflax
title: Toadflax
lead:
Toadflax is a low level herb, requiring level 30 Herblore to clean. It can be acquired from Random events or grown with a Farming level of 38, by planting toadflax seeds in herb patches. It can also be acquired by trading in 3 vouchers from the Brimhaven Agility Arena or as a reward from Temple Trekking. It is used to make agility potions and most commonly, Saradomin brews. To create a potion, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a toadflax potion (unf), and then add the secondary ingredient.

Using Toadflax in the coconut milk based Antidote+ potion is often considered a waste, as Antidote++ is vastly preferred by PvM'ers, whereas the Antidote+ is not usually in demand. However, Antidote+ can be a viable and cheaper option in certain situations, such as fending off poison while training Ranged or Magic at the Skeletal Monkeys on Ape Atoll. Ironmen may also prefer to create Antidote+ until they reach a high enough level to create its more potent counterpart.

label: Toadflax potion (unf)
title: Toadflax potion (unf)
lead:
A toadflax potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a toadflax on a vial of water, requiring 34 Herblore. Using toad's legs on a toadflax potion (unf) with 34 Herblore yields an agility potion (3) and 80 Herblore experience. Using a crushed nest on a toadflax potion (unf) with 81 Herblore yields a saradomin brew (3) and 180 Herblore experience.

One is used in the Land of the Goblins quest.

label: Toban
title: Toban
lead:
Toban is one of the chieftains of an ogre tribe in the Feldip Hills. His tribe lives on an island east of the ogre city.

Toban enjoys chewing on dragon bones and gives players the Relic part 3 in exchange for a set of them. Players also have to recover a bar of gold that Toban stole from his nemesis, Og, during the same quest in order to get another part of the Ogre relic.

label: Toban's gold
title: Toban's gold

lead:
