label: Tomb (Iban)
title: Tomb (Iban)
lead:
A tomb belonging to Iban can be found in the lowest level of the Underground Pass, beneath Iban's lair. During the Underground Pass quest, players must set the tomb alight using some dwarf brew and a tinderbox on it, in order to obtain Iban's ashes which are used on the doll of iban.

Searching the tomb before setting it on fire will cause the player to take 10 damage.

label: tomb dolmen (Rashiliyia's Tomb)
title: tomb dolmen (Rashiliyia's Tomb)
lead:
A tomb dolmen can be found within the Rashiliyia's Tomb, located in a room behind a set of tomb doors adorned with skeletons. Players must search the dolmen during the Shilo Village quest in order to spawn Nazastarool.

The dolmen is typically used by players as a safespot whilst killing Nazrastool.

label: Tomb dolmen (Tomb of Bervirius)
title: Tomb dolmen (Tomb of Bervirius)
lead: A tomb dolmen can be found within the Tomb of Bervirius. Players must search the tomb during the Shilo Village quest in order to receive a sword pommel, a locating crystal, and Bervirius notes.

label: Tomb doors
title: Tomb doors
lead: Tomb doors are scenery objects found within Rashiliyia's Tomb. Players must pass through the doors during the Shilo Village quest to reach the dolmen used to spawn Nazastarool. In order to open the doors, players must first use three bones on the doors to complete the skeletons. Subsequent openings do not require bones.

label: Tomb of Bervirius
title: Tomb of Bervirius
lead: The Tomb of Bervirius (referred to as Cairn Island Dungeon in the world map) is a burial ground visited during the Shilo Village quest. The player finds the sword pommel, locating crystal and Bervirius notes on the dolmen inside. To get to the tomb, head to Cairn Isle, and cross the bridge. Climb down the well stacked rocks to the north, and enter the cave from there.

In preparation for the Tombs of Amascut raid, players were able to log in to an unrestricted world to test various rewards to be polled for the boss, including:

label: Tombs of Amascut/Strategies
title: Tombs of Amascut/Strategies
lead:
The Tombs of Amascut is a raid located within the Jaltevas Pyramid in the necropolis. The raid makes use of the invocation system, allowing players to customise the difficulty of the raid by choosing to enable various invocations that act as difficulty modifiers to the raid.

The raid is composed of four paths, with each comprising a challenge section followed by a boss. These can be taken on in any order the player(s) chooses, although the order in which they are fought can slightly change clear times.

label: Tony's Pizza Bases

lead:
Tony's Pizza Bases is a shop owned by Fat Tony that sells pizza bases for 4 coins each stocking them 30 at a time. The shop is located in the Wilderness Bandit Camp. Players should be careful as the shop is in the Wilderness and they risk getting attacked by PKers and Bandits.

There is also a cheese and tomato spawn, as well as giant rats that can be killed for meat and fishing spots for anchovies, making the shop an excellent place to make various pizzas. There are also everlasting fires outside, which allows the player to cook their rat meat.

label: Tools (gardening)
title: Tools (gardening)
lead: Tools are decorative scenery found in various locations around Gielinor. A variant of the scenery exists in which a player is given an option take a spade or a rake, provided they do not currently have one in their inventory. If a player already has one of the tools in their inventory, the other tool will be automatically taken. The takeable variant can be found in the small shed located within Lumbridge Swamp, and within the Farming shop in Prifddinas. Despite being visible, free-to-play players are not able to open the shed door and can not reach the tools.

lead:

It is also a reward from various random events, the gnome restaurant, from Managing Miscellania, caskets, looting magpie implings, and unlocking the crystal chest in Taverley. It can also be found in the Barrows chest as a separate item if the player has 100% rewards potential.

The tooth half of a key is used with a loop half of key to make a crystal key, which is used to unlock the crystal chest, which contains a dragonstone and an assortment of other items.

Torag's set requires 70 Defence to wear the armour and 70 Attack and 70 Strength to wield the weapon.

label: Torch

lead:
An unlit torch may be used with a tinderbox or used on a fire or range to get a lit torch. It is useful for dark tunnels and smoking Hunter traps once lit. 39 Hunter is required to smoke traps. Smoking traps increases the chance of catching a creature by 2% (additive).

Unlit torches are dropped by many cave dwelling creatures including the level 49 and level 76-78 Catablepons, and Cave slimes. They can also sometimes be found inside barrels in the Shaman Caves.

label: Torch (unobtainable item)
title: Torch (unobtainable item)
lead:
A Torch is an unobtainable version of the Lit torch. Torches were previously tradeable and could be turned into banknotes. However, they were made untradeable due to an unfixable bug where trading a lit torch in a dark area would not update the lighting for either player. Any player who had a noted lit torch was given this now discontinued item. Originally, the item was identical to the real lit torch, except being stackable.

As this change occurred prior to August 2007, the item has never been obtainable in Old School RuneScape.

They drop the tormented synapse, which is used to create powerful demonbane weaponry, and the burning claw, which can be combined in a pair to make burning claws.

label: Torstol
title: Torstol
lead:
Torstol is the highest level herb, which requires level 75 Herblore to clean and yields 15 experience. Torstol can be grown in herb patches at level 85 Farming with a torstol seed.

Obtaining torstol herbs may be difficult as they are only rarely dropped by monsters. They can be obtained by Farming, looting nature implings, or rarely as drops from Zulrah and the Kalphite Queen. They can also be obtained in their grimy form from the Sinister chest, Skotizo, Cerberus, and the Chambers of Xeric. To create a Zamorak brew, you need to add the cleaned herb to a vial of water to create a torstol potion (unf), and then add jangerberries.

label: Torstol potion (unf)
title: Torstol potion (unf)
lead: A torstol potion (unf) is an unfinished potion made by using a torstol on a vial of water, requiring 78 Herblore. Using jangerberries on a torstol potion (unf) with 78 Herblore yields a Zamorak brew(3) and 175 Herblore experience. Using a super attack, super strength, and super defence on a torstol potion (unf) with 90 Herblore yields a super combat potion(4) and 150 Herblore experience. Using an anti-venom(4) on a torstol potion (unf) with 94 Herblore yields an anti-venom+(4) and 125 Herblore experience. Using a demonic tallow on a torstol potion (unf) with 81 Herblore yields a surge potion(3) and 185 Herblore experience.

label: Tortugan
title: Tortugan
lead: Tortugans are a race of turtle-like people who live on the Great Conch.

label: Torture Rack
title: Torture Rack
lead:
Torture racks or simply Racks are scenery found throughout Gielinor. They do not serve any in-game purpose, although they are presumably meant to be used by NPCs for torture.

The rack found in the Troll Stronghold can be used to hide a drunk parrot during the events of Eadgar's Ruse.

label: Torva (character)
title: Torva (character)
lead: Torva was a powerful Zarosian warrior who served directly under Nex. Little else is currently known about him, but his armour can be obtained in a damaged state as a possible drop from Nex.

label: Torva armour
title: Torva armour
lead:
Torva armour is a set of equipment named after the Zarosian warrior Torva requiring level 80 Defence to equip. The individual armour pieces are obtainable only as rewards from Nex.

The pieces of armour are dropped in a broken state, and must be repaired using Bandosian components made by breaking down Bandos chestplates and tassets. Breaking down the components can only be performed at the Ancient Forge within the God Wars Dungeon's Ancient Prison.

label: Tostig
title: Tostig
lead: Tostig is the bartender at The Toad and Chicken pub in Burthorpe. He stocks 12 Asgarnian ale, 12 wizard's mind bomb, and 12 dwarven stout at 2 coins each.

label: Total level
title: Total level
lead:
Total level is the sum of the levels of all of a player's skills. The current maximum for members is 2,376, while the maximum for free players is 1,494 or 1,485, depending on whether members' skills (each having one level) are counted – hiscores and the total level counter include them, while free-to-play total level locked worlds do not. Total level is a common way for players to compare their stats.

The opening page on the HiScores ranks players by their total level, then by experience. Other than when new skills have been recently released, the top ranked players in the HiScores are generally listed in order of experience rather than rank. The number one player won't have a higher level than the number two player, but certainly more experience.

label: Totem
title: Totem
lead:
The totem is a holy relic of the Rantuki Tribe. It is a quest item used only in Tribal Totem. Lord Handelmort of Ardougne had stolen it from the Rantuki Tribe and the player is asked by Kangai Mau, a member of the tribe, to retrieve it.

The player can acquire multiple totems in the quest by using the drop trick.

When looked at, the totem pole will turn either restored or corrupted depending on whether it has been replaced or not.

label: Totem Pole (Legends' Guild)
title: Totem Pole (Legends' Guild)

The totem pole can be found in the main hall of the Legends' Guild. It is the scenery version of the gilded totem, which the player receives as a reward during the quest. It can be used to recharge skills necklaces and combat bracelets after the player has completed the Legends' Quest.

Unlike the Fountain of Rune, which charges skills necklaces and combat bracelets with 6 use charges, the totem pole only charges jewellery with 4 uses.

label: Touch paper

It is given to Guidor in south-east Varrock, alongside plague sample, liquid honey, sulphuric broline, and ethenea.

The centre is visited during the Waterfall Quest, and the Book on Baxtorian can be found upstairs in a bookcase. Gerald can be found near the river just south of the centre.

label: Tower Archer

Tower archers are located on top of the archer tower in the Ranging Guild. They are aggressive to players of all levels. The archers have an attack range of 11, and players must have an attack range of at least 9 to be able to hit them with Ranged or Magic attacks.

When the archers attack, sometimes an arrow appears underneath where the player is standing. The level 19, 34, 49, and 64 archers drop iron, steel, mithril, and adamant arrows, respectively.

label: Tracker gnome 1
title: Tracker gnome 1
lead: The First tracker gnome, known in game as Tracker gnome 1 is a member of the Gnome royal army, sent to obtain the co-ordinates of the Khazard forces headquarters in the Battlefield south of West Ardougne. This tracker can be found behind the largest building of the Khazard stronghold (just across the River Dougne from the Battlefield itself).

label: Tracker gnome 2
title: Tracker gnome 2
lead: The Second tracker gnome, known in game as Tracker gnome 2, is a member of the Gnome royal army, sent to obtain the co-ordinates of the Khazard forces headquarters in the Battlefield south of West Ardougne. He can be found in the building to the north of the Battlefield, where he has been captured, beaten and imprisoned by Khazard's army.

label: Tracker gnome 3
title: Tracker gnome 3
lead: The Third tracker gnome, known in game as Tracker gnome 3 is a member of the Gnome royal army, sent to obtain the co-ordinates of the Khazard forces headquarters on the Battlefield south of West Ardougne. The Third gnome can be found in the south-western corner of the Khazard stronghold, amongst the battle. He is encountered in the Tree Gnome Village quest to get part of the coordinates of the battlefield so the gnomes can fire the ballista. This tracker, however, has been driven mad by the constant and unrelenting fighting, and now only speaks in riddles and frightened gibberish.

label: Tracking
title: Tracking
lead:
Tracking is a Hunter technique that is used to catch several kebbits and herbiboars. With this technique, the player inspects scenery objects in the creature's habitat to uncover a creature's tracks. These tracks will eventually lead the player towards the hiding creature. When the hiding creature is found, right-click 'Attack' while wielding a noose wand to receive loot and experience. Each player follows a unique track and does not compete with other players to get kebbits.

Catching a kebbit gives the player bones, raw beast meat, and kebbit fur. The hides obtained from kebbit tracking can be used to make camouflage costumes. All camouflage outfits can be put in the armour case in the costume room.

label: Trading
title: Trading
lead: Trading is the exchange of gold and items between players. Trading is one of Old School RuneScape's oldest features and while not essential to game play, it plays a large part in the community and is utilised by nearly every player except for Ironmen who cannot trade with other players.

label: Trading post
title: Trading post
lead:
The Trading post was a trading system released on 10 December 2014 for players to sell almost every tradeable item, or search for item offers by other players. Players got six spaces in which they may have posted offers. Sellers were required to advertise their offers on the trading post in order for buyers to be able to view their offers. This trading system resembled a real-life auction house. The trading post was accessible from any bank.

Players were able to assemble certain item sets to save space. They behaved like ordinary items except that they could not be worn or used until they are disassembled. Only the trading post was able to be used to assemble and disassemble sets, and this could be done an unlimited number of times for free. Right-clicking a set and selecting "Drop" did not disassemble it. Players could right-click the trading post and select the "Item sets" option to exchange item sets.

label: Trahaearn Clan
title: Trahaearn Clan
lead: The Trahaearn Clan is one of the eight elven clans who were originally brought to Gielinor from Tarddiad by Guthix and Seren in the early First Age. They are skilled in metalwork, being blacksmiths and miners. They are located south-east of the Tower of Voices in Prifddinas, off the southern path.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)
title: Trailblazer League (2020)
lead:
The Trailblazer League was the second league in Old School RuneScape, which began on 28 October 2020 (12:30PM GMT) and lasted until 6 January 2021. Development for the league began in mid-June of 2020.

A rerun of the league called the Trailblazer Reloaded League started on 15 November 2023 and ended on 10 January 2024, featuring Great Kourend and Kebos Lowlands as a new region.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas
lead:
In the Trailblazer League, players are locked to certain areas within Gielinor. All players will begin the league restricted to Misthalin and unlock Karamja for free during the tutorial. Up to three other areas can be unlocked after completing 60, 140, and 300 League tasks.

Death's office, the Player Owned House, Random Events and the Essence mine will be accessible from all areas. Slayer assignments will also only take place in unlocked areas. Usage of transportation methods such as Charter Ships, Fairy Rings, Customs Officers, Gnome Gliders, etc. will require the destination area be unlocked before they can be used.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Asgarnia
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Asgarnia
lead:
The Asgarnia Area covers the entire Kingdom of Asgarnia along with the island of Entrana, the Pest Control islands, and Troll Country (excluding Weiss). Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in the area are also included.

Access to Catherby from White Wolf Mountain will be restricted and prevented through the use of magical barriers.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Kandarin
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Kandarin
lead:
The Kandarin Area covers the entire Kingdom of Kandarin along with the Feldip Hills, Ape Atoll, and Crash Island. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in the area are also included, with the exception of Taverley Dungeon and the Underground Pass.

Access to the Nightmare Zone is restricted. To obtain Nightmare Zone points speak to Dominic Onion and purchase them for 1 coin each.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Karamja
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Karamja
lead: The Karamja Area covers the entire island of Karamja along with the island of Crandor and the Realm of the Fisher King. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in Karamja are also included. When purchasing a Player Owned House from an Estate Agent your house will be placed in Brimhaven so that Construction can be trained from level 1.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Kharidian Desert
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Kharidian Desert
lead: The Kharidian Desert Area covers the entirety of the Kharidian Desert. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in the area are also included. Access to Misthalin north of Al-Kharid and south of Varrock is restricted and prevented through the use of magical barriers.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Misthalin
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Misthalin
lead: The Misthalin Area covers the Kingdom of Misthalin as well as Fossil Island, Zanaris, and some Realms accessible by Fairy Rings (Abyssal Area, Abyssal Nexus, Cosmic Entity's Plane, Enchanted Valley, Gorak Plane). The Abyss is not included within Misthalin despite the Leagues interface stating otherwise. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in Misthalin are also included. Magical barriers prevent access to Al-Kharid, Port Sarim, and the western exit of Barbarian Village.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Morytania
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Morytania
lead: The Morytania Area covers the entirety of Morytania along with the island of Mos Le'Harmless, Braindeath Island, Dragontooth Island, and Harmony Island. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in the area are also included.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/The Fremennik Provinces
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/The Fremennik Provinces
lead: The Fremennik Provinces Area covers the entire Fremennik Province including the Fremennik islands, Lunar Isle, and Weiss. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in the area are also included. Magical barriers prevent access to Kandarin via the bridge south of Rellekka.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Tirannwn
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Tirannwn
lead: The Tirannwn Area covers the entirety of Tirannwn along with the Temple of Light and the Underground Pass. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in the area are also included.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Wilderness
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Wilderness
lead:
The Wilderness Area covers the entirety of the Wilderness. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in the area are also included. Last Man Standing will not be accessible.

During Trailblazer League, deaths will behave differently in the Wilderness:
*PvP deaths will be treated like a PvM death with your lost items moving to a gravestone, the gravestone will then move to your respawn location
*PvM deaths will be unaffected

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Wilderness/NotableDrops
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Areas/Wilderness/NotableDrops
lead: * All unique drops from Revenants are also boosted by the passive relic. Notable drops from revenants include: Amulet of Avarice, ancient crystal, Craw's bow, dragon platelegs, Thammaron's sceptre, and Viggora's chainmace.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Guide
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Guide
lead: Trailblazer League presents unique decisions and challenges unlike most content in Old School RuneScape. Since players are restricted to just 5 of the 9 available areas, sacrifices will have to be made when it comes to training skills and making money. This guide aims to provide information about the league mechanics, different training methods, and money making guides based on the constraints within the league.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Guide/Money Making
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Guide/Money Making
lead:
Coins are useful for many things within Trailblazer League such as: 
* Imbuing equipment at the Nightmare Zone, 1 gp is worth 1 imbue point
* Buying runes and ammunition from shops
* Making planks and buying other construction materials from sawmills
* Tanning hides with a Tanner
* Purchasing expensive equipment such as a dragon scimitar from Daga's Scimitar Smithy

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Guide/Skills
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Guide/Skills
lead:
All skills available in the main game are available in the Trailblazer League. Skills in Trailblazer League can be trained very similarly to that of regular ironman accounts, depending on what combination of areas are chosen as unlocks. Players will begin with level 3 Herblore, 5 Runecraft, and level 10 Agility to enable herblore training, runecraft training, and the use of the Draynor Village rooftop agility course.

Experience received for training any skill will be multiplied by 5x the usual rate. By unlocking relic tiers 2, 4, and 6, this multiplier can be increased to 8x, 12x, and 16x, respectively.

label: Trailblazer League (2020)/Relics
title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Relics
lead:
Relics are powerful buffs that are unlocked with League Points. Upon completing the tutorial, players are presented with three Relics to choose from without the need for points. There are six tiers of relics in total, as well as an additional passive buff automatically unlocked at each tier. Each tier corresponds to a different aspect of the game: skilling, teleportation, combat, and utility.

Once players choose a Relic of a tier, they will be permanently unlocked, but cannot change their Relic selection for that tier.

title: Trailblazer League (2020)/Tasks
lead:
This page contains a list of all of the tasks in the Trailblazer League. Completing tasks during the league allows players to earn league points and unlock relics that buff their character. Tasks span five difficulty levels - Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite, and Master.

Tasks per region are as follows:

title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Areas/Morytania/Summary
lead:
The Morytania area covers the entirety of Morytania along with the island of Mos Le'Harmless, Braindeath Island, Dragontooth Island, and Harmony Island.

Instances of areas in Morytania and underground areas with an entrance in Morytania will also be included.

label: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Areas/Tirannwn/Summary
title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Areas/Tirannwn/Summary
lead:
The Tirannwn area covers the entirety of Tirannwn along with the Temple of Light and the Underground Pass.

Instances of areas in Tirannwn and underground areas with an entrance in Tirannwn will also be included.

label: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Areas/Wilderness/Summary
title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Areas/Wilderness/Summary
lead:
The Wilderness Area covers the entirety of the Wilderness. Underground areas and instanced areas with an entrance in the area are also included. Last Man Standing and Bounty Hunter will not be accessible.

During Trailblazer League, deaths will behave differently in the Wilderness:
* PvP deaths will be treated like a PvM death with your lost items moving to a gravestone, the gravestone will then move to your respawn location
* PvM deaths will be unaffected
* Loot keys are disabled on League Worlds

label: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Boosted drops
title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Boosted drops
lead: Items from certain sources are given a boosted drop rate in Trailblazer Reloaded League. The drop rate multiplier increases as more relics are unlocked: the items listed below become 2x as common when the starting tier 1 relic is chosen; then become 3x as common when unlocking a tier 4 relic; proceeding to 4x as common at tier 6; and finally 5x as common at tier 8.

label: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Guide
title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Guide
lead: Trailblazer Reloaded League presents unique decisions and challenges unlike most content in Old School RuneScape. Since players are restricted to just 5 of the 10 available areas, sacrifices will have to be made when it comes to training skills and making money. This guide aims to provide information about the league mechanics, different training methods, and money making guides based on the constraints within the league.

label: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Guide/Quests
title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Guide/Quests
lead: This page is for Trailblazer Reloaded League. Click here if you are looking for Raging Echoes League.

label: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Guide/Skills
title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Guide/Skills
lead:
All skills available in the main game are available in the Trailblazer Reloaded League. Skills can be trained similarly to that of regular ironman accounts, depending on what combination of areas are unlocked. Players begin with level 3 Herblore, 5 Runecraft, and level 10 Agility to enable herblore training, runecraft training, and the use of the Draynor Village rooftop agility course.

Experience rates are multiplied by 5x the usual rate. By unlocking relic tiers, this multiplier can be increased further.

label: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Relics
title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Relics
lead:
Relics are powerful buffs that are unlocked with League Points. Upon completing the tutorial, players are presented with three Relics to choose from without the need for points. There are eight tiers of relics in total, as well as an additional passive buff automatically unlocked at each tier.

Once players choose a Relic of a tier, they will be permanently unlocked, but cannot change their Relic selection for that tier.

title: Trailblazer Reloaded League/Tasks
lead:
This page contains a list of all the tasks in the Trailblazer Reloaded League. Completing tasks during the league allows players to earn league points and unlock relics that buff their character and areas containing new bosses and tasks. Tasks span five difficulty levels: Easy, Medium, Hard, Elite, and Master. Completing a task requires its respective area to be unlocked, unless otherwise stated.

Tasks per region are as follows:

label: Traitorous Ali
title: Traitorous Ali
lead:
Traitorous Ali is a man from Pollnivneach. He was a member of the Menaphites but apparently betrayed them, gaining his nickname. He used to visit The Asp & Snake Bar.

During The Feud, the player must poison the drink he left in the bar. After the quest, when the player has turned against the bandits and Menaphites to help the town, the bartender can be informed about the poison and will give the player a free beer.

label: Tramp
title: Tramp
lead:
The tramp is a poor, penniless human who can be found in south-east Varrock. Upon speaking to him, he will ask the player for money, giving the player options to donate money to him (one coin) or to refuse, resulting in the tramp shouting phrases such as "I hate [player name]!" and "Don't ask [player name] for anything - he's/she's/they're stingy!" This also happens when you don't have any money and explain this to him.

Varrock is also home to Charlie the Tramp, a quest NPC who begins the Shield of Arrav quest by informing the player of the Black Arm Gang. He also asks the player for money, though does not shout anything out when a player refuses to give him money.

label: Translation book
title: Translation book
lead:
The Translation book, or Gnome-English Translation Dictionary, is a book written by Anita. It is obtained during The Grand Tree quest to help players translate what Hazelmere, who only speaks in the Gnomic tongue, is telling them. It is also used to help solve a puzzle later in the quest. During The Eyes of Glouphrie however, players don't need the book to talk to Hazelmere, as he will use magic to communicate with the player instead.

After completing the quest, players can reclaim the book from their bookcase in their player-owned house under the name 'Gnome Translation Dictionary'.

label: Travel cart
title: Travel cart
lead:
The travel cart is a scenery object that is part of the Shilo Village cart system. The carts are run by, and can be found near, Hajedy in Brimhaven, and Vigroy in Shilo Village. Players can utilise the carts to quickly travel to the alternate cart within the system. Boarding the cart will incur a varying fee between 10 to 200 coins, based on the amount of coins the player is carrying. Alternatively, a flat fare can be paid for 200 coins which will skip the dialogue with the cart operators.

The cart system is free to use after a player has completed the Karamja Elite Diary.

label: Trawling net
title: Trawling net
lead:
A trawling net is a type of facility that can be installed on player-owned skiffs and sloops. They can be used for deep sea trawling at shoals, providing Sailing and Fishing experience and fish that can be placed in the ship's cargo hold. Better trawling nets will allow players to catch higher quantities of fish per successful action, as well as being able to catch certain shoals that swim to deeper depths. All nets fish at the same speed of 4 ticks, although with tick manipulation this can be every 2 ticks.

A maximum of 250 fish can be stored in a net, regardless of type, before it is full; the "Collect-from" option will allow players to place their catch in the inventory or cargo hold. Additionally, having two trawling nets on a boat does not provide additional capacity, and emptying one will empty both.

label: Treasure Trails/Guide/Challenge scrolls
title: Treasure Trails/Guide/Challenge scrolls
lead:
Challenge scrolls are logical problems posed to the player by an NPC. They appear in medium, hard and elite clues in Treasure Trails and have two steps to it: first, the player has to find the right NPC to speak to (when they get a cryptic or anagram clue), and then they have to solve the riddle, to advance along their trail.

To complete the scroll, view the question on the scroll, then speak to the NPC which gave it to provide the answer. When the correct answer is provided, the challenge is complete, and the player will receive either the next clue, or the reward.

title: Treasure Trails/Guide/Emote clues/Items
lead: The following is a list of all the items, organised by level, that are needed for emote clues. The items in a list are alphabetically organised. For items that require multiple items, the quantity is given, so that you know exactly how many items you are going to need for each clue type; this is useful for stocking up items when making STASH units. When no quantity is given to an item it means it only needs one item for that clue level by default. Note that one item in the list of one level of a clue, can also appear in the list of another level of a clue. Don't forget this when stocking up on items!

label: Treasure Trails/Guide/Light boxes
title: Treasure Trails/Guide/Light boxes
lead:
Light boxes are a puzzle players will occasionally need to solve for a master Treasure Trail. Light boxes contain a 5x5 grid of lights and 8 switches to turn them on and off. The goal of the puzzle is to light all the lights.

If destroyed, or otherwise lost, the puzzle will have to be solved again from the beginning.

label: Treasure Trails/Guide/Puzzle boxes
title: Treasure Trails/Guide/Puzzle boxes
lead:
__NOTOC__

Occasionally, players will need to solve puzzle boxes for a hard, elite or master clue in a Treasure Trail. Puzzle boxes contain a scrambled image that players must work to unscramble by clicking on tiles to move them to an empty space. Once the puzzle box is completed, players will need to talk to the NPC who gave the puzzle box to receive the next clue or the reward.

label: tree
title: tree
lead:
Trees are the most common scenery found almost everywhere around Gielinor, and can be chopped down to provide logs and 25 Woodcutting experience.

The most common varieties of regular trees in Gielinor are a double canopy tree with round leaves, and a single canopy with a pointy tip. The single canopy and pine varieties can be used with a knife to fill a bucket of sap from an empty bucket; the double canopy variants do not provide sap. The trees can also be distinguished by their examine text and the icon that appears on the minimap, with the double canopy tree showing a round tree icon ( ), the single canopy variety showing a pointy-tipped icon ( ), and the pine variant showing a pine ( ).

label: Tree (Agility, unused)
title: Tree (Agility, unused)
lead: Tree is an unused scenery object that may have been intended for use in Rooftop Agility Courses. The tree has the same interaction options and examine text as the tree in the Pollnivneach Rooftop Course, but has slightly different dimensions. Similar to other agility obstacles, the tree object does not have a visible model, and would instead have been used as a region near the tree that would be clicked to jump over the obstacle.

label: Tree (burnt)
title: Tree (burnt)
lead: Trees are decorative scenery objects found at various burnt and volcanic regions of Gielinor. Unlike other burnt trees, they have no interaction options and are purely decorative.

label: Tree (Crandor)
title: Tree (Crandor)
lead:
Trees are scenery found on Crandor that have been burnt by Elvarg the dragon. Crandor trees are purely decorative and have no interaction options.

The first variant of this tree can also be found outside the Wintertodt boss area in the Northern Tundras of Great Kourend. The examine text still indicates that a dragon damaged the tree, which is likely an oversight and not indicative of dragons in this region.

label: Tree (Crash Site)
title: Tree (Crash Site)
lead: Trees are scenery located around the entrance to the Crash Site Dungeon accessed during Monkey Madness II. The trees have no interaction options and are purely decorative. They appear to be fallen over and burned as a result of Glough's airship crashing to the ground during the quest.

label: Tree (dead, unused)
title: Tree (dead, unused)
lead: Dead trees are unused scenery objects that have the appearance of burnt tropical trees. They may have been intended for use on Mos Le'Harmless, based on the proximity in the cache to other scenery objects. The trees have no interaction options and would be purely decorative.

label: Tree (disambiguation)
title: Tree (disambiguation)
lead:
Trees are scenery objects found all across the realm of Gielinor.

Tree may refer to:

label: Tree (Drill Demon)
title: Tree (Drill Demon)
lead:
Trees are scenery found in the Drill Demon random event training area. The trees are similar in appearance to regular trees but cannot be chopped down to obtain logs. The trees are located outside the area with the training maps, making them inaccessible to the player. They have no interaction options and are purely decorative.

The first variant of the tree is repurposed for use in Last Man Standing in the deserted island map.

label: Tree (Farming Guild)
title: Tree (Farming Guild)
lead: Trees are decorative scenery found in the Farming Guild. There are 3 tall variants that have slightly different dimensions, and a fourth variant that appears closer to a regular tree. The first variant can also be found on the island in Lake Molch used for aerial fishing.

label: Tree (Ferox Enclave)
title: Tree (Ferox Enclave)
lead: Trees are decorative scenery found around the Ferox Enclave in the Wilderness. The trees are purely decorative and cannot be chopped down to obtain logs. They have no interaction options.

label: Tree (Glough's house)
title: Tree (Glough's house)
lead:
Trees are interactive scenery used to climb up and down in Glough's house in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. During Monkey Madness II, the branch used to climb down will also have an option to investigate, which provides a handkerchief needed to progress in the quest. The branch used to climb to the top floor will not have a climb option until talking to Anita during the quest.

A separate tree branch is used to climb up to the main floor of Glough's house.

label: Tree (interface item)
title: Tree (interface item)
lead:
The Tree is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Tree (Construction).

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Tree (Isle of Souls, scenery)
title: Tree (Isle of Souls, scenery)
lead:
Trees are decorative scenery found on the Isle of Souls in the Soul Wars lobby near Nomad and Zimberfizz. They appear identical to the regular trees on the Isle of Souls, but cannot be chopped down to obtain logs. The trees have no interaction options and are purely decorative.

One specific variant of the tree in the northern area of the lobby is replaced by a table of supplies when logged into a tournament world. On regular worlds, the tree is indistinguishable from the other scenery.

label: Tree (Lletya)
title: Tree (Lletya)
lead: Trees are scenery that can be found outside the entrance to Lletya. Two trees block the path, which can be passed after entering Lletya for the first time during Mourning's End Part I. Clicking pass on the trees will cause them to open upwards and the player will walk through.

label: Tree (Lost City)
title: Tree (Lost City)
lead: Tree is a unique variant of regular trees that is involved in Lost City. The tree is located north-west of Lumbridge Swamp and can be identified by having the option "Chop" instead of "Chop down" like regular trees. Attempting to chop the tree will cause the leprechaun Shamus to appear, who will tell the player how to access Zanaris.

label: Tree (Morytania)
title: Tree (Morytania)
lead:
Trees are scenery found throughout Morytania. They have no interaction options and are purely decorative.

The first 4 variants are distributed in the north and east parts of Morytania from Canifis to Slepe. They were also repurposed for use in Zul-Andra and the Ghastly Swamp in Clan Wars.

label: Tree (Poison Waste)
title: Tree (Poison Waste)
lead:
Trees are scenery objects found in the Poison Waste. They are located in the middle of the swampy area between the islands, making them inaccessible to the player. The trees have no interactions and are purely decorative.

The trees have the same appearance of other scenery trees in Tirannwn, but darkened by the poison in the swamp, similar to the colours of swampy dead trees.

label: Tree (rope bridge)
title: Tree (rope bridge)
lead: Trees are climbable scenery found in The Hollows in Morytania. The two trees support a rope bridge that must be repaired during In Search of the Myreque in order to reach Curpile Fyod and the Myreque Hideout for the first time. Repairing the bridge requires three planks and 225 steel nails.

label: Tree (spooky)
title: Tree (spooky)
lead: Trees are decorative scenery found throughout north-eastern Morytania between Canifis and Slepe. The trees have varying heights, made up of either 0, 1, or 2 trunk portions between the stump and crown of the tree. Each portion of the tree is placed on a progressively higher plane, which causes the trunks and crowns to be hidden when roofs are disabled. The trees have no interaction options and are purely decorative.

label: Tree (Tirannwn, scenery)
title: Tree (Tirannwn, scenery)
lead:
Trees are decorative scenery found throughout the forrests of Tirannwn. Unlike other Tirannwn trees, they are not able to be chopped down and have no interaction options.

There are 9 tree variants with different appearances, but all have the same name and examine info.

label: Tree (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
title: Tree (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
lead: The tree in Tree Gnome Stronghold is used during The Grand Tree quest to climb into Glough's watch tower and put the twigs on the pillars. Climbing the tree requires 25 Agility.

label: Tree (tropical, unused)
title: Tree (tropical, unused)
lead: Trees are unused scenery objects that may have been intended for use in tropical areas. The tree is identical to other tropical and jungle trees. It has no interaction options and would be purely decorative if used.

label: Tree (tropical)
title: Tree (tropical)
lead:
Tropical trees are decorative scenery found throughout most tropical areas in Gielinor. Unlike other jungle trees, they are not able to be chopped down and have no interaction options.

The trees can be found in large numbers across Karamja, the Feldip Hunter area, and Mos Le'Harmless, but are also located intermittently in the Kharidian Desert, Fossil Island, Ape Atoll, Mount Quidamortem, and other coastal and riparian areas.

label: Tree (Tutorial Island 2)
title: Tree (Tutorial Island 2)
lead:
Trees are scenery encountered during the alternate Tutorial Island that was accessible to some new accounts during 2020. They are similar to the regular Tutorial Island trees, but each design has a variant with a chop option and a variant with no chop option.

The trees could only be chopped during the appropriate part of the tutorial. Doing so provided the player with logs.

label: Tree (Tutorial Island)
title: Tree (Tutorial Island)
lead:
Trees are a type of scenery found on Tutorial Island, which can be chopped down to obtain logs. The types of tree found here have a darker bark than other trees found across most of Gielinor. There are three varieties of regular trees on Tutorial Island: a double canopy tree with round leaves, and a single canopy with a pointy tip, and a dead tree.

Trees can only be cut during the Woodcutting section of the tutorial. Attempting to chop down a tree before this will print the message You cannot cut down this tree yet. You must progress further in the tutorial. After the first gate is passed, further attempts to chop down trees will print the message Perhaps you've done enough woodcutting now. Only the double-canopy variant is found before the gate, so the single canopy and dead variants are impossible to chop down.

label: Tree (unhealthy, unused)
title: Tree (unhealthy, unused)
lead: Unhealthy trees are unused scenery objects that have the appearance of leafless dead trees. The models are similar in appearance to some scenery trees in Tirannwn as well as trees in the Wilderness. The trees are completely unused, but have no interaction options and would be purely decorative.

label: Tree (vines)
title: Tree (vines)
lead:
A tree with hanging vines is an unused scenery object. It has an appearance similar to the ropeswing in Brimhaven, but with two hanging vines instead of a single rope. This bears a very strong resemblance to the ropeswing's original appearance in RuneScape Classic.

The tree may have been intended as the original model of the ropeswing or as a different agility shortcut. The tree has no interaction options, which could instead indicate that the tree was intended to just be decorative scenery in a jungle region.

label: Tree (Wilderness, burnt)
title: Tree (Wilderness, burnt)
lead: Trees are burnt variants of trees found throughout the Wilderness. The burnt trees are found besides various instances of lava in the Wilderness, including the Lava Maze, the Chaos Temple, and the Deserted Keep. The trees cannot be chopped down and are purely decorative.

label: Tree (Wilderness, snow)
title: Tree (Wilderness, snow)
lead: Trees are snowy variants of trees found in the Wilderness. The snowy variant found in the Frozen Waste Plateau, as well as the snowy regions of Great Kourend near the Wintertodt. The snowy trees cannot be chopped down and are purely decorative.

label: Tree (Wilderness)
title: Tree (Wilderness)
lead:
Trees are scenery found in the Wilderness that cannot be chopped down like regular trees. The trees have no interaction options and are purely decorative. There are 24 variants of the trees, which have increasingly darker colours at deeper levels of the Wilderness. This matches the overall aesthetic of the Wilderness becoming increasingly more burnt and desolate at deeper levels.

There are 6 tiers of trees, each with 4 variant models. The trees in each tier are distributed across the entire width of the Wilderness, in bands approximately 10 Wilderness levels deep.

label: Tree (young)
title: Tree (young)
lead:
Young trees are a variant of regular trees that have slightly orange bark. They can be chopped at level 1 Woodcutting to obtain regular logs. After the tree is chopped down, it will be replaced by a tree stump for a few seconds before respawning.

The first variant of the young tree is found around the Ratcatchers Mansion and in the unicorn pen at the Ardougne Zoo, while the second variety is only found in the zoo.

label: Tree branch (Gnome Stronghold Agility Course)
title: Tree branch (Gnome Stronghold Agility Course)
lead: The Tree branch is an Agility obstacle found within the Gnome Stronghold Agility Course. An Agility level of one is required to pass the obstacle, which will then grant the player 6.5 Agility experience. It is not possible to fail this obstacle.

label: Tree Gnome Stronghold
title: Tree Gnome Stronghold
lead: The Tree Gnome Stronghold, sometimes shortened to Gnome Stronghold, also called Ta Quir Priw in Gnomish, is one of the largest cities in Gielinor and is populated solely by gnomes. Its most notable features are the Grand Tree, the Gnome Stronghold agility course, the Gnome Ball field and the Stronghold Slayer Cave. As the largest gnome settlement it is considered the capital of the Gnome Empire.

label: Tree Gnome Village
title: Tree Gnome Village
lead: Tree Gnome Village is the first quest in the Gnome quest series and focuses on the war between General Khazard's army and the Tree Gnomes. During the quest, you need to aid the gnomes by retrieving stolen orbs.

label: Tree Gnome Village (location)
title: Tree Gnome Village (location)
lead: The Tree Gnome Village is the home of the gnomes. It is primarily a giant hedge maze, at the centre of which lies a village. To enter the village, follow the Gnome Maze and then squeeze through the loose railing. If you talk to Elkoy, he will take you through the maze saving a bit of time.

label: Tree Gnome Village Dungeon
title: Tree Gnome Village Dungeon
lead:
The Tree Gnome Village Dungeon is found beneath the Tree Gnome Village. Its surface entrance is in the maze just south of the main village area.

The dungeon features in Waterfall Quest, where players visit it to obtain glarial's pebble from Golrie. To reach Golrie, a key must first be obtained from the eastern room, which is inhabited by zombies and giant bats. The key is found in the large crate in the south-east corner that is coloured differently from the rest of the crates. The key can then be used in the western room full of hobgoblins to unlock the door Golrie is imprisoned behind.

label: tree patch
title: tree patch
lead:
Tree patches are farming patches used by players to grow their own personal trees. There are a total of 7 tree patches currently. Much like other trees, these can be chopped using the Woodcutting skill to obtain logs. The necessary tree seeds to grow them must be obtained from bird nests or other sources. Planted trees do not require watering.

First, an empty plant pot may be used on any empty farming patch with a gardening trowel to fill the plant pot with soil. Plant one tree seed on the pot with the gardening trowel and water it with a watering can. After a few minutes, the seedling will grow into a sapling which can then be planted in a cleared tree patch; players must have a spade in their inventory when planting and removing the stump of a tree.

label: Tree roots (disambiguation)
title: Tree roots (disambiguation)
lead:
Tree roots may refer to:

* Tree roots, the sea charting object.
*Tree roots from digging up planted trees:
**Oak roots, obtained from clearing an oak farming tree.
**Willow roots, obtained from clearing a willow farming tree.
**Maple roots, obtained from clearing a maple farming tree.
**Yew roots, obtained from clearing a yew farming tree.
**Magic roots, obtained from clearing a magic farming tree.
**Unobtainable spirit roots.
*Sprouting Roots, found within the Wintertodt's prison.
*Tree roots (Forestry), chop growing Tree roots for anima-infused bark and other rewards.
*Infected roots, found in the Ruins of Mokhaiotl.

label: Tree roots (Farming)
title: Tree roots (Farming)
lead: Tree roots are roots that have been dug up from a tree patch by a player after growing and then chopping down the related tree. The number of roots obtained when digging up a tree depends on the player's Farming level. A temporary skill boosting item like a garden pie may be used when digging up the tree to increase the number of roots given. In order to receive the extra roots through a temporary skill boost, the boost must be active when digging the stump not checking the health or chopping the tree.

label: Tree sapling
title: Tree sapling
lead:
Tree saplings are any sapling that may be planted in a tree patch through the Farming skill. When fully grown, they can be cut down using the Woodcutting skill. Their roots may be used for other purposes afterwards.

It is common to cut down and uproot lower-levelled trees, but keep the stub and let the tree re-grow for higher ones.

label: Tree seedling
title: Tree seedling
lead:
Tree seedling may refer to:

*Oak seedling
*Willow seedling
*Maple seedling
*Yew seedling
*Magic seedling

label: tree spirit
title: tree spirit
lead:

Tree spirits are monsters which can be found in the Enchanted Valley using the fairy ring code when attempting to cut down a tree (an axe is required). They commonly drop nature rune, rune and adamant axes and various seeds. However, they give reduced experience and as such are mainly a source of early game resources. The tree spirit's combat level varies depending on that of the player's, a minimum of 14, and up to a maximum of level 159.

label: Tree spirit (disambiguation)
title: Tree spirit (disambiguation)
lead: Tree spirit may refer to:

label: Tree spirit (Lost City)
title: Tree spirit (Lost City)
lead:
The Dramen Tree Spirit only appears in Entrana Dungeon when doing the Lost City quest. Players have to fight it with limited armour and weapons, as it only appears on Entrana.

During the quest, it is also considered a ghost for the purposes of a Slayer task. It can be fought in the Nightmare Zone after the quest is complete, but will not count towards a ghost task.

label: Tree Spirits
title: Tree Spirits
lead: Tree Spirits is a music track that is unlocked west of the entrance to the Tree Gnome Stronghold.

label: Tree stump
title: Tree stump
lead:
A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a tree after a short amount of time (35.4 - 58.8 seconds). The tree stump has no interaction options.

The basic variety of tree stump is shared by multiple kinds of trees, including:
* Double and single canopy regular trees
* One variety of jungle tree
* The third variant of evergreen
* Double and single canopy trees found in Pest Control
* Double canopy trees found on Tutorial Island
* Regular trees found on The Node

label: Tree stump (Ape Atoll)
title: Tree stump (Ape Atoll)
lead: Tree stumps are decorate scenery found in Ape Atoll and Crash Island. The stumps do not respawn into trees and are purely decorative. Tree stumps have no interactions.

label: Tree stump (Burgh de Rott)
title: Tree stump (Burgh de Rott)
lead: Tree stumps are scenery objects found in Burgh de Rott that do not respawn into trees. The stumps can be found in the town as well as scattered around the woods to the east. The tree stumps have no interaction options and are purely decorative.

label: Tree stump (Crandor)
title: Tree stump (Crandor)
lead:
Tree stump is a scenery object found on Crandor near the dungeon entrance. The tree stump appears burnt, and does not respawn into a tree. The tree stump has no interaction options and is purely decorative.

The tree stump is visually identical to one of the unused tree stumps likely intended to be used in the burnt portions of the Wilderness, and has the same examine text.

label: Tree stump (dead, old)
title: Tree stump (dead, old)
lead: A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when an old dead tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a dead tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

label: Tree stump (dead, snowy)
title: Tree stump (dead, snowy)
lead: A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a snowy dead tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a dead tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

label: Tree stump (dead, swampy)
title: Tree stump (dead, swampy)
lead: A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a swampy dead tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a dead tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

label: Tree stump (dead, weathered)
title: Tree stump (dead, weathered)
lead:
A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a weathered dead tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a dead tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

Strangely, the weathered dead tree stump variant is used when cutting down a maple tree in Miscellania. When a maple tree is cut down anywhere else, a maple tree stump is used instead.

label: Tree stump (dead)
title: Tree stump (dead)
lead:
A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a dead tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a dead tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

There is a different variant of tree stump for each type of dead tree. Strangely, the dark variant dead tree stump is also used when chopping down burnt dead trees, as well as the light variant jungle tree in the dense Kharazi Jungle.

label: Tree Stump (Enchanted Valley)
title: Tree Stump (Enchanted Valley)
lead:
Tree stumps are scenery found in the Enchanted Valley near the trees. Since chopping a tree causes a tree spirit to spawn, the trees can never be chopped down to produce a stump. Instead the stumps are purely decorative and have no interaction options.

The same tree stump can be found at the goblin settlement near the Observatory.

label: Tree stump (Evergreen tree)
title: Tree stump (Evergreen tree)
lead:
A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when an evergreen tree has been chopped down. The stump will respawn into a tree after a short amount of time, and has no interaction options before regrowing.

This stump variant is shared by the first, second, and fourth variant of evergreen, as well as all three variants of snow covered trees.

label: Tree stump (jungle)
title: Tree stump (jungle)
lead:
A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when the dark variant of jungle tree in the dense Kharazi Jungle has been chopped down. After the jungle tree is chopped down, the player will automatically walk across the stump. The stump can otherwise not be walked across, and further movement requires chopping another jungle tree.

A stump will respawn into a jungle tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

label: Tree Stump (magic)
title: Tree Stump (magic)
lead: A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a magic tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a magic tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

label: Tree Stump (maple)
title: Tree Stump (maple)
lead: A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a maple tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a tree after a short amount of time (35.4 seconds). The tree stump has no interaction options.

label: Tree stump (oak)
title: Tree stump (oak)
lead:
A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when an oak tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a tree after a short amount of time (8.4 seconds). The tree stump has no interaction options.

The regular oak stump is also shared by the variant oak trees found on The Node.

label: Tree stump (Prifddinas)
title: Tree stump (Prifddinas)
lead:
A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a tree has been chopped down outside Prifddinas. A stump will respawn into a tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

The two variants of trees have different sized stumps, corresponding to the size of the tree that was chopped down.

label: Tree stump (Rellekka)
title: Tree stump (Rellekka)
lead: Tree stumps are scenery found in the Fremennik Province surrounding Rellekka. There are two varieties of tree stumps around the city: a common smaller variety with 146 instances, and a larger variety found in only 2 locations. The stumps are purely decorative and do not respawn into trees. They have no interaction options.

label: Tree stump (scenery)
title: Tree stump (scenery)
lead:
Tree stumps are scenery objects that can be found in many places around Gielinor. Unlike standard tree stumps, these do not respawn into trees and are purely decorative.

The first variant is very common and can be found in most of mainland Gielinor, including Misthalin, Kandarin, and the Wilderness, as well as the Fisher Realm.

label: Tree stump (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
title: Tree stump (Tree Gnome Stronghold)
lead: Tree stump is a scenery object found north of the Tree Gnome Stronghold outside the entrance to the Crash Site Cavern. The tree stump does not respawn into a regular tree. The stump is purely decorative and has no interaction options.

label: Tree stump (unused)
title: Tree stump (unused)
lead: Tree stumps are unused scenery that appear similar to regular tree stumps. Like regular tree stumps, they have no interaction options. The unused stump varieties may have been intended to be placed as the result of chopping down a tree or dead tree, but were never assigned to appear for any tree that is possible to chop down.

label: Tree stump (Wilderness)
title: Tree stump (Wilderness)
lead:
Tree stumps are decorative scenery found throughout the Wilderness that do not respawn into trees. There are 5 tree stump variants in the wilderness, with each variant used at progressively deeper levels of wilderness with a darker appearance to match the scenery. The 5 variants appear respectively at Wilderness levels 3-8, 9-16, 17-24, 25-33, and 34-40.

The first variant, located in the Wilderness approximately between levels 3-8, can also be found in the Kebos Lowlands between the Shayziens' Wall and Lizardman Settlement.

label: Tree Stump (willow)
title: Tree Stump (willow)
lead:
A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a willow tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a tree after a short amount of time (8.4 seconds). The tree stump has no interaction options.

The multi-canopy variants of willow trees all share a single type of stump, while the single-canopy willow has a separate stump model.

label: Tree stump (yew)
title: Tree stump (yew)
lead: A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a yew tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a yew after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

label: Tree stump (young)
title: Tree stump (young)
lead: A tree stump is a type of scenery left on the ground when a young tree has been chopped down. A stump will respawn into a tree after a short amount of time. The tree stump has no interaction options.

label: Tree stumps
title: Tree stumps
lead: Tree stumps are a type of scenery that can be found after chopping down trees. There are many varieties of tree stumps depending on the type of tree that was chopped down. Additionally, several variants of tree stumps are used as decorative scenery and never respawn into choppable trees.

label: trees
title: trees
lead: Trees are a part of the natural scenery of Old School RuneScape. Trees can be found all across the realm of Gielinor, but especially in forested kingdoms, such as in the tropical jungles of Karamja and the temperate forests of Asgarnia and Misthalin.

label: trellis
title: trellis
lead: The trellis is a wall obstacle on the north wall of the Watchtower building that acts as the ladder up to the Watchtower quest starting point. Level 18 Agility is required to climb the trellis. Doing so will grant the player 31 experience in Agility. It is not possible to climb down the trellis.

label: Tremble
title: Tremble
lead: Tremble is a music track that is unlocked on the Death Plateau.

label: Trevallyn
title: Trevallyn
lead:
Trevallyn is a vampyre and one of the possible senders of a message to the player if they successfully complete the Theatre of Blood. Trevallyn has bet on the player's progress in the Theatre and thus provides supplies for them to get them to win his bet.

They are only mentioned in the message, and cannot be found anywhere in-game.

label: Trevick Ramlock
title: Trevick Ramlock
lead: Trevick Ramlock was a resident of Varrock during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. According to the Varrock Census of that year, he was a banker. He may be related to Idonea Ramlock.

label: Tribal
title: Tribal
lead:
Tribal is a music track that is unlocked in the Karamjan Jungle. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track, Jungly 1, Jungly 2, Jungly 3, Jungle Troubles, Reggae, Reggae 2 and Tribal 2.

In Classic mode, the track is unlocked south-east of Tai Bwo Wannai Village, at the entrance to the Nature Altar.

label: Tribal 2
title: Tribal 2
lead:
Tribal 2 is a music track that is unlocked in the Karamjan Jungle. In this area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track, Jungly 1, Jungly 2, Jungly 3, Jungle Troubles, Reggae, Reggae 2 and Tribal.

In Classic mode, the track is unlocked at the gnome glider on Karamja, and east of Shilo Village.

label: Tribal Background
title: Tribal Background
lead:
Tribal Background is a music track that is unlocked in Tai Bwo Wannai, including the area north of the fenced part of the village.

In an update in 2022, the track got extended to include the area north of Tai Bwo Wannai. After 2024, the Modern mode got an update changing the track's unlock area, whereas Classic mode still plays the track in the area north of Tai Bwo Wannai, as well as in the Pothole Dungeon.

label: Tribal mask
title: Tribal mask
lead:
Tribal masks (also known as broodoo masks) are a members-only set of masks worn in the headwear slot. They provide no bonuses.

Tribal masks come in three different colours:

label: Tribal top
title: Tribal top
lead:
Tribal tops are shirts that can be purchased with 360 trading sticks from Gabooty's Tai Bwo Wannai Cooperative.

If players are wearing Karamja gloves 1 or better, the price is reduced to 300 trading sticks per top.

label: Tribal Totem
title: Tribal Totem
lead: Tribal Totem is a quest that involves the retrieval of an artefact sacred to the Rantuki tribe of Karamja, which has been taken from them by the nobleman Lord Handelmort.

label: Tribal Totem/Quick guide
title: Tribal Totem/Quick guide
lead: __TOC__

label: Tribal Weapon Salesman
title: Tribal Weapon Salesman
lead: The Tribal Weapon Salesman is a shop keeper in the Ranging Guild. His shop is called Authentic Throwing Weapons, which sells javelins and throwing axes of all types, up to rune.

label: Tribesman
title: Tribesman
lead:
Tribesmen are warriors that inhabit the jungles of Karamja. They can be found in various areas around Karamja, notably near Brimhaven around a cauldron and in the Tai Bwo Wannai village. They may also be encountered during the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame when players attempt to cut the jungle bushes. Though their attacks have a fairly low max hit, any successful hit from them will inflict a potent poison, dealing 11 poison damage per hit. As a result, players are advised to bring a form of antipoison when travelling through their areas.

They are not aggressive towards players with a Combat level of 65 or higher, eliminating the need to counteract their poison.

label: Tricorn hat
title: Tricorn hat
lead:
Tricorn hat is a cosmetic head-slot reward from the Trouble Brewing minigame. It can be purchased from Honest Jimmy's House of Stuff for 500 Pieces of eight. It cannot be resold to the shop.

Tricorn hats can be stored in the Player-owned house Costume room along with a Naval shirt and Navy slacks of the same colour. They come in 7 different colours.

label: Trident
title: Trident
lead:
Trident may refer to:

* 
* , and its enhanced version.
* , and its enhanced version.

label: Trimmed monk's robes
title: Trimmed monk's robes
lead: Trimmed monk's robes are possible rewards from beginner Treasure Trails. The set has identical stats to monk's robes.

label: Trimmed studded leather armour
title: Trimmed studded leather armour
lead: Trimmed studded leather armour is a set of Ranged armour that has identical bonuses as Studded leather armour. Pieces of the armour can be obtained as rewards from easy Treasure Trails. The set consists of only body and chaps.

label: Trimmed wizard robes
title: Trimmed wizard robes
lead:
Trimmed wizard robes may refer to:

* Black trimmed wizard robes
** Black wizard hat (t)
** Black wizard robe (t)
** Black skirt (t)
* Blue trimmed wizard robes
** Blue wizard hat (t)
** Blue wizard robe (t)
** Blue skirt (t)

label: Trindine
title: Trindine
lead:
Trindine was a Zarosian Mahjarrat mentioned by the golem during Desert Treasure II.

She is currently believed to be deceased, as the location she was dispatched to, Kharid-et, was abandoned and she never returned.

label: Trinity
title: Trinity
lead: Trinity is a music track that is unlocked inside of the Legends' Guild, as well as a small corner just south of Keep Le Faye. It can also be heard in the Legends' Guild dungeon.

label: Trinket (disambiguation)
title: Trinket (disambiguation)
lead:
Trinket may refer to:
* Crystal trinket, a reward for completing Mourning's End Part II
* Trinkets in Deadman Mode, Deadman: Apocalypse, and Deadman: Armageddon:
** Trinket of advanced weaponry (seasonal Deadman Mode only)
** Trinket of fairies
** Trinket of undead
** Trinket of vengeance
** Trinket of avarice
** Trinket of fortuity
** Trinket dust (permanent Deadman Mode only)

label: Trista Donaldson
title: Trista Donaldson
lead: Trista Donaldson was a resident of Varrock during the Year 160 of the Fifth Age. According to the Varrock Census of that year, she was a banker.

label: Trobert
title: Trobert
lead: Trobert is a Black Arm Gang contact players must meet during the Heroes' Quest. He can be found in the building south of the Brimhaven Agility Arena.

label: Trojan cow
title: Trojan cow
lead: The Trojan cow is a project embarked upon by Fred the Farmer and is his excuse for needing all of the wool given to him by players who complete the Sheep Shearer quest. The only reference to the Trojan cow is in the 8th Postbag from the Hedge.

label: troll
title: troll
lead:
Trolls are one of the more unique, though not very intelligent, races of Gielinor. Whilst the main population exists within the mountainous region known as Troll Country, the race is quite widespread, populations being known to stretch as far as Piscatoris, Neitiznot, and Weiss.

Trolls are named after whatever they first attempted to eat, so it is not uncommon for trolls to have strange names. Their weapons are rather crude, but are effective in combat. They often wield clubs, axes, and rocks for throwing, though a few may use other weapons, such as scimitars.

label: Troll (historical)
title: Troll (historical)
lead:
The Troll was a former character that appeared in RuneScape 2. It is arguably the most obscure character to have existed since the transition to RuneScape 2, with very little information and no screenshots of the monster surviving.

At least one troll could be found in the Clock Tower Dungeon, locked in one of the jail cells. It had the appearance of a much thinner version of the River troll.

label: Troll (interface item)
title: Troll (interface item)
lead:
The Troll is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Troll (Construction).

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Troll arena
title: Troll arena
lead:
The Troll arena is a combat arena used by trolls in the Troll Country.

The arena is on one route to Trollheim and the Troll Stronghold. Players can enter the area during and after the Troll Stronghold quest. The player fights trolls in the arena is in two quests: Troll Stronghold, against Dad, and Troll Romance, against Arrg.

label: Troll boss
title: Troll boss
lead:
Troll boss may refer to:

*Arrg, fought at the end of Troll Romance
*Dad, fought in the Troll Stronghold quest
*Ice Troll King, leader of the ice trolls and fought at the end of The Fremennik Isles
*Kob, fought during Monkey Madness II
*Troll generals, encountered on the top floor of the Troll Stronghold

label: Troll Country
title: Troll Country
lead: The Troll Country is a region in north Gielinor. It is a mountainous kingdom controlled mainly by trolls.

label: Troll General
title: Troll General
lead:
Troll generals are huge and powerful trolls that live in the Troll Stronghold, on the top floor.

Troll generals can be very advantageous to kill as a higher-level choice when assigned trolls, as they have a reasonably high drop rate of law and nature runes, as well as high alch drops such as steel platebodies, adamant axes, rune warhammers, and granite shields.

label: troll kitchen
title: troll kitchen
lead:
The troll kitchen is a kitchen located on the middle floor of the Troll Stronghold.

In the middle of the room lies a gigantic cooking pot used by the trolls to prepare their meals, to the north of the room is a caged pen where goats are kept for cooking, the Strongholds prison is used to store humans, the more valued meat by trolls. On the east side of the room there are drawers which contain a hidden key for the Goutweed storeroom.

label: Troll spectator
title: Troll spectator
lead: Troll spectators are trolls found in the Troll arena, where fights with Dad and Arrg take place. They watch instead of fight, just as the name suggests. They may be battled though, and are exactly the same as mountain trolls. They are non-aggressive, but if the player kills Dad, they will immediately attempt to attack the player.

label: Troll Stew
title: Troll Stew
lead: Troll stews can be seen inside cooking pots in the cave during Making Friends with My Arm and in the Troll Stronghold kitchen.

label: Troll Stronghold
title: Troll Stronghold
lead: Troll Stronghold is a quest about gaining access to the Troll Stronghold beneath Mount Trollheim in order to rescue Godric, a soldier from Burthorpe. It is the second quest in the Troll Series.

label: Troll Stronghold (location)
title: Troll Stronghold (location)
lead:
The Troll Stronghold is a stronghold inhabited by mountain trolls in the Troll Country. Notable trolls found inside include Burntmeat, My Arm, Ug and Kob from various quests involving trolls.

The stronghold itself is carved into the side of the mountain that the Mountain Camp is situated on top of.

label: Trollheim
title: Trollheim
lead: Trollheim is a mountain in Old School RuneScape. It is located directly to the east of the entrance to the Troll Stronghold.

label: Trophy
title: Trophy
lead:
Trophy may refer to:

* Fishing trophy, obtained as a reward for winning the fishing competition during the Fishing Contest quest.

label: Trophy head
title: Trophy head
lead:
Trophy heads are Slayer monster drops that can be used to recolour equipment, sacrificed to the Dark Altar, or they can be stuffed at the Taxidermist and mounted in the Head trophy space of a player-owned house.

label: Trout
title: Trout
lead:
Trout is a type of fish that restores 7 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be obtained by cooking raw trout on a fire or cooking range, requiring level 15 Cooking and granting 70 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in a burnt trout. The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Trout is one of a number of foods with a reduced burn rate while using the Lumbridge Castle range with Cook's Assistant completed. It will stop burning entirely at Cooking level 49, or 45 when using the Lumbridge range.

Trout is used as an ingredient in fish pie which requires Cooking level 47 to make. 10 Trout are required during the Death Plateau quest.

label: Trufitus
title: Trufitus
lead:
Trufitus Shakaya is the shaman of Tai Bwo Wannai Village. He wishes to "commune with the gods", possibly the Karamjan gods, and needs herbs to do so. During Jungle Potion, the player gathers these herbs for him. During Shilo Village, the adventurer brings to him scrolls and other artefacts to have them examined and be given advice on what to do next. He is in the eastern-most house north of Tai Bwo Wannai Village. He appears to be wearing beads of the dead. He seems to be an influential figure on Karamja.

After completion of the Shilo Village quest, players can speak to Trufitus to remove the prompt when entering Shilo Village.

Tumeken (Jagex pronunciation: TOO-meh-ken), sometimes referred to in Menaphite texts as the God of the Sun, is the god of light, who shaped the Kharidian Desert, and is the husband of Elidinis, with whom he created Icthlarin and Amascut using their divine essence. In this capacity, he is the main god worshipped by the desert's inhabitants.

Despite being considered the head of the Menaphite Pantheon, precious little is known about Tumeken. He is known to have created the four lesser deities (correctly called his avatars) of the pantheon: Apmeken, Crondis, Het and Scabaras, which, according to the Book of Light and Day, were made from four dreams Tumeken had over the course of four days. Together the eight deities led the Kharidian empire in what is today known as the Kharidian Desert. The pharaohs that have ruled Menaphos and the desert in the gods' stead are known as the Sons of Tumeken and are buried in the Jalsavrah Pyramid.

label: Tutorial Island

lead:
Tutorial Island is the starting place for every new Old School RuneScape player character. It is located in the Kingdom of Misthalin, and is connected to The Node just to the south. The island is also the starting location for the Learning the Ropes quest, which all players must complete before they can leave the island.

If players get stuck during the tutorial, the required next action will be hinted at from the controls guide in the top left corner of the game client screen after a short amount of time has passed. The controls guide will also inform them to follow the instructions in the chat box.

label: Twilight Emissaries
title: Twilight Emissaries
lead:
The Twilight Emissaries are a religious cult obsessed with the end of the world. Though their beliefs are not part of the official religion of Losanium, they are driven by an unapproved interpretation of the concept of Ximoua, which they call "Tsak Tauli" or "the Final Dawn". Their belief is not simply that the world will end, but that they must actively work to bring about this end themselves. 
They are involved with Twilight's Promise. Metzli gives the player information about their beliefs. Then, several cultists launch an attack on the Teomat, wounding Servius. Additionally, during this quest it is heavily implied that they were responsible for the attempt on Servius's life during Children of the Sun, and that their current plans centre around his death.

During The Heart of Darkness, the player and Prince Itzla join the Emissaries while undercover in order to find hard evidence implicating them for the assassination attempt on Servius. During their initiation ceremony, it is revealed that Metzli is the current Augur, or leader, of the Emissaries. Additionally, Metzli claims that Ennius and Furia Tullus are the human reincarnations of Ralos and Ranul, respectively. When the player and Itzla descend into the Ruins of Tapoyauik, where Metzli went to seek information about enacting Tsak Tauli, they find the frost nagua Amoxliatl. Metzli, Ennius, and Furia soon follow them, with the former teleporting Itzla to an unknown location.

The robes do not provide any bonuses for the player. They cannot be unequipped when inside the temple.

label: Twisted bow glitch
title: Twisted bow glitch
lead:
The twisted bow glitch was a major glitch that occurred on 28 February 2019. After an update, a twisted bow item spawn was found directly east of the cactus patch outside the Farming Guild. Players could pick it up and it had a respawn time of 60 seconds. This was hotfixed 32 minutes after the update. The item spawn was not removed, but attempting to pick it up would result in the bow being deleted. Another hotfix 53 minutes after the update launched added four tree stumps around the spawn to make the bow unreachable even via Telekinetic Grab.

The cause of the glitch was soon discovered to be that while mapping the flower behind the Hespori cave entrance, a twisted bow spawn was also accidentally mapped on the other side of the guild wall. The twisted bow spawn had been added by a senior artist assisting the new artist mapping the flower as an example of how to use the map editor tool, with the senior artist erasing all but one of the twisted bow spawns. The tester did not notice the twisted bow spawn when checking if the flower worked properly, though the spawn was likely out of the minimap's range when standing next to the flower.

label: Twisted Tales
title: Twisted Tales
lead:
Twisted Tales is a series of quests taking place within Great Kourend and the Kebos Lowlands. These short, standalone quests are intended to add additional worldbuilding, life, and character to the continent, as the only quests that existed prior to the Twisted Tales series focused on the five Houses of Great Kourend as part of the Great Kourend quest series.

The quest series was created by Mod Ed in response to player criticism of a lack of quests within the continent in comparison to the mainland, where there were many standalone quests such as Imp Catcher, Clock Tower, and A Soul's Bane. Twisted Tales aims to bring such quests to the continent to make them feel as if they were part of it since the very beginning.
