label: Username
title: Username
lead:
An account's Username, also known as its Login, is the name or email which uniquely identifies the player's account within Jagex's systems. Players must choose a login as part of the process for creating an account, and they currently cannot change it at any time afterwards. Accounts that were created before November 2010 will have a login name that is the first ever character name the account had (the original username upon account creation). Any account created after November 2010 will use a login email. The login email may be different than the registered email.

A username can only be used to access one account.

label: Utility spells
title: Utility spells
lead: Utility spells are a type of magic spell typically used by players outside of combat or teleporting, such as enchanting items or reanimating ensouled heads. Ancient Magicks are the only spellbook that does not have utility spells, as it is a combat-oriented spellbook.

label: Valaine
title: Valaine
lead:
Valaine is the owner of Valaine's Shop of Champions on the of the Champions' Guild.

She runs a general store, allowing players to sell anything to her. She sells blue capes, black full helms, black platelegs, and adamant platebodies. It is not recommended to sell items to her as she is far away from a bank.

label: Valaine's Shop of Champions.

Although the shop stocks armour, it functions similarly to a general store in that any tradeable item can be sold to the shop.

label: Vambraces
title: Vambraces
lead:
:For all items and their stats worn in this slot, see this table
Vambraces are Ranged armour worn in the gloves slot. They offer a small range and defence bonus. Dragonhide and leather vambraces can be spiked with kebbit claws which increases the Strength bonus.

Dragonhide vambraces only require a certain Ranged level, depending on the type of dragonhide. This means combat pure players can take advantage of their bonuses.

label: Vampyre
title: Vampyre
lead:
Vampyres are a bat-like humanoid race, originating from Vampyrium. They were brought to Gielinor by the Stranger from Afar, who taught them the concepts of civilised culture. Prior to the Stranger's arrival, vampyres were organised into small hunter-tribes. Their main competitors were the Yarasa, who were also fierce bat-like humanoids and often warred with the vampyres. All the Yarasa, with the exception of Xarpus, the Yarasa King, were driven to extinction when the vampyre tribes united together.

Prior to the God Wars, vampyres were brought to live in the Zarosian Empire. Some vampyres held important roles in the empire, such as Vardorvis who was Carnifex Maximus or chief executioner. Following the collapse of the Zarosian Empire, the vampyric race played a major role in helping Zamorak wage the God Wars.

label: Vampyre (attribute)
title: Vampyre (attribute)
lead: The vampyre attribute is assigned to vampyres and modifies the type of damage they can receive. There are three different vampyre types.

label: Vampyre Houses
title: Vampyre Houses
lead:
The eight vampyre houses form the aristocracy of the Sanguinesti region. Their history can be traced back to Vampyrium, where the current houses were formed as a result of a civil war. Previously having a tribal culture, the vampyres were introduced to the concept of civilised society by Zaros. This drastic change of society divided the vampyres which threw the tribes into a civil war. Eight tribes emerged victorious which eventually reformed into the current houses.

On Vampyrium, each house had their personal preference in blood taste and hunting methods. Before the vampyre migration to Gielinor, the burgeoning House Drakan managed to increase in power and eventually subjugate the other houses to become the most powerful house on Vampyrium.

label: Vampyre Slayer
title: Vampyre Slayer
lead: Vampyre Slayer is a free-to-play quest that takes place in Draynor Village. The player is asked to slay the terrifying vampyre count Draynor terrorising the village that lives in a large mansion just north of Draynor, with the help of an experienced vampyre slayer.

label: VPSG code
title: VPSG code
lead:
VPSG code is a coded language consisting of 26 letters, each of which is equivalent to a letter of the . Described as a "strange language" by the player character, it is in fact heavily warped letters of the alphabet. It appears to be used exclusively by the Varrock Palace Secret Guard (VPSG), though it appears those outside of the organisation can decipher it, such as Surok Magis.

During What Lies Below, Rat Burgiss, an agent of the VPSG, writes a coded letter addressed to Surok Magis in VPSG code. The beacon ring, provided by Zaff, another agent, also contains inscriptions in VPSG code.

label: Vampyric name
title: Vampyric name
lead:
Vampyric names are given to the player by Vanescula Drakan during Sins of the Father quest. The name and identity are given to the player to allow them to pose around Darkmeyer as an upcoming vampyre noble. This will be used by vampyres to refer to them in Darkmeyer.

Currently, the player's Vampyric name cannot be changed after it has been given.

label: Vampyrium
title: Vampyrium
lead: Vampyrium is the home world of vampyres, yarasa, and the nylocas. It is described by Lord Drakan to have blood-red skies and forests of darkwood. In a future update, scheduled for release in summer 2026, the quest The Blood Moon Rises will unlock access to Vampyrium. Vampyrium is planned to be slightly larger than the Stranglewood in size.

label: Vannaka
title: Vannaka
lead:
Vannaka is a highly accomplished fighter who serves as the Combat Instructor on Tutorial Island and a Slayer master in Edgeville Dungeon. He claims to be the greatest swordsman alive, which is suggested by his combat level of 146 and his ability to carry both a steel two-handed sword and dragon square shield at the same time, a trait unattainable by players. According to the 14th Postbag from the Hedge, his Strength level is 112.

During the tutorial, he dismisses the player character's attempts at making idle conversation, and proceeds to teach them how Melee and Ranged combat work. He tasks the player with slaying a giant rat in close combat. Afterwards, he instructs the player to kill a second rat from outside of the enclosure using ranged attacks, a strategy colloquially known as safespotting.

In the first round, two groups of four animals were put against each other, with the capybara and the toucan winning their respective categories. label: Varmen
title: Varmen
lead:
Varmen was an archaeologist responsible for the discovery of Uzer, an ancient ruined city that once dominated the Kharidian Desert. He was employed by the Varrock Museum and apparently wanted to excavate Uzer but due to the giant project at the Digsite being closer to the museum, he was not able to get funding for it. Elissa was his wife, and refers to him as her late husband, which points out his death, but, however, the circumstances surrounding his death are unknown.

Varmen never appears in-game, although his notes regarding the Ruins of Uzer and the Rock golem can be found at the Digsite Exam Centre.

label: Varrock
title: Varrock
lead:
Varrock (Jagex pronunciation: ) is the capital of the kingdom of Misthalin. It is one of the largest cities in Old School RuneScape, and the largest city available to free players. In addition to being popular due to its proximity to the Wilderness, the city hosts the massive Grand Exchange, through which players can trade any item they wish, and features in many of the quests throughout the game.

Varrock can be entered from all sides, and each entrance has non-aggressive level 21 guards surrounding it. The city is safe for all players, although care should be taken when coming from Lumbridge through the south entrance, as there are aggressive level 7 and 20 dark wizards.

label: Varrock armour

* the Varrock east bank, a hub for players in east Varrock
* the Grand Exchange, a massive trading hub
* the chest in the Cooks' Guild

label: Varrock chapel
title: Varrock chapel
lead:
The Varrock chapel is a four-story building found in the north-east part of Varrock, which represents the Varrock branch of the Church of Saradomin. It's implied that the church is falling apart; the church's priest, Father Lawrence, is an alcoholic, and his room on the is a mess. Elsie on the second floor describes the church as draughty; furthermore, the two church-goers Martina Scorsby and Jeremy Clerksin are asleep in the pews.

Like most churches, there is an altar inside which will restore Prayer points to full when prayed at. There is also a yew tree just outside the church.

label: Varrock east bank
title: Varrock east bank
lead:
The Varrock east bank, also known as Varrock east or the East Varrock bank, is a popular bank found south of the Varrock Museum.

The bank was once a very popular place to buy and sell items from other players before the introduction of the Grand Exchange. Some of the more common items that were sold here were rune essence and player killing goods such as food, lower levelled weapons and armour, runes, and potions.

label: Varrock General Store
title: Varrock General Store
lead:
The Varrock General Store is one of the most popular stores in the game. Located in the centre of Varrock, it is a general store that is fairly typical of other such similar stores found in the game.

This store used to be a major player trading centre, acting as a sort of flea market for players looking for bargains and other players simply wanting to unload surplus goods that they may have on hand. Due to its central location of a busy player centre for both F2P and member worlds, its proximity to two banks, and its general reputation as a centre of commerce, it served as a major point of player to player commerce for many years. Frequently players would also advertise requests for player to player trades to either buy or sell items without even using the store, but merely being there because of the large numbers of people that would often be there looking for bargains. On some worlds the trading would spill out onto the centre plaza, you would see players requesting trades spilling beyond even both banks in Varrock.

label: Varrock mine
title: Varrock mine

label: Varrock Museum
title: Varrock Museum
lead:
The Varrock Museum is dedicated to the history of Gielinor. It is located east of Varrock Palace, just south of the city's church.

Several activities can be found within this museum that award experience as well as kudos, which unlock a variety of rewards. For instance, players with at least 100 kudos will be able to start the Bone Voyage quest, which grants access to Fossil Island.

label: Varrock Palace
title: Varrock Palace
lead:
Varrock Palace is the official residence of the ruler of Misthalin as well as the nation's primary diplomatic and military centre. Located in central Varrock, it is the largest building in the city.

Since the Fourth Age, Varrock Palace has been a hub of economic, political, and social development within Misthalin. The palace currently houses King Roald III and his wife, Queen Ellamaria. As their full-time residence, it is equipped with kitchens, barracks, dining areas, a church, a large garden, troop housing areas, and other facilities.

label: Varrock Palace Library
title: Varrock Palace Library
lead:
The Varrock Palace Library is a moderately sized library found on the ground floor of the Varrock Palace on the north side and is overseen by Reldo. The player will frequently visit the library to consult with Reldo or pick out texts and documents on several topics relevant to various quests they engage in. Surok Magis will also be stationed here until the completion of What Lies Below.

Beside the table in the north-east alcove of the room is the Varrock Census that lists the citizens of Varrock and their profession.

label: Varrock Sewers
title: Varrock Sewers
lead:
The Varrock Sewers are a network of tunnels under the city of Varrock. It is a fairly large multi-combat underground area filled with low to mid-level monsters and is one of the largest dungeons in free-to-play.

A knife, slashing weapon or sharp-object (e.g. scimitar) is required to access certain parts of the sewer to cut a spider web (note: a throwing knife will not work).

label: Varrock Square
title: Varrock Square
lead:
Varrock Square is a square found directly south of Varrock Palace. It contains a large fountain with four statues on each side; the square's signature landmarks. Players teleporting to Varrock appear here, unless you have completed the medium Varrock Diary and changed your teleport to south of the Grand Exchange.

Varrock Square is one of the city's largest business centres, and as such hosts a number of shops and open-air stalls. Full stores such as the Varrock General Store, Thessalia's Fine Clothes, and Zaff's Superior Staves surround the square. Baraek's fur stall and Benny's newsstand, from which players can buy Varrock Herald newspapers, can be found in the north-east corner of the square while Eliza runs the Speedrunning Reward Shop in the south-east. Nevet runs the Events Reward Shop from a stall in the north-west corner of the square.

label: Varrock Swordshop
title: Varrock Swordshop
lead: The Varrock Swordshop is a shop in southern Varrock run by a Shop keeper. The shop can be found opposite the Blue Moon Inn. The shop sells daggers, swords, and longswords, all of which range from bronze to adamant. A list of all prices in the shop is located below. Players use the shop as a speedy way to purchase lower-level weapons, though this shop does not see much business as many players consider scimitars to be a better weapon choice.

label: Varrock Teleport
title: Varrock Teleport
lead:
Varrock Teleport is a teleport spell in the standard spellbook which teleports the player to Varrock's town square, near the fountain. This spell may be transferred to a piece of soft clay at a lectern in the Study of a player-owned house, creating a teleport tablet. The same runes are required, as well as the Magic level needed to cast the spell, and the Magic experience is gained at the time the tablet is created.

Casting this spell is a requirement for completing the Medium Varrock Diary. Completing it allows players to switch the location of the teleport to the Grand Exchange by right-clicking the spell and changing the destination. Changing the default location using the right-click Configure option will also change the default teleport when using the Varrock Portal.

label: Varrock west bank
title: Varrock west bank
lead:
The Varrock west bank, also known as Varrock west, West Varrock bank, or historically the Bank of Varrock, is a popular bank found just south of the Grand Exchange. Beyond its proximity to many shops, the bank also offers close access to a nearby anvil. There is a Deadman chest in the bank.

The Varrock west bank was the first bank in RuneScape. On release, it could only store coins. Prior to the Grand Exchange, the bank was also a common market location, similar to Falador Park. Today, the bank is the most popular free-to-play bank, and rares and Halloween items are still traded here in some worlds.

Although this item can be found at the Digsite, Terry Balando doesn't have any dialogue when showing it to him.

label: Veg ball
title: Veg ball
lead:
A vegetable ball is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 12 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade veg balls are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 150 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a vegetable ball via gnome cooking with 35 Cooking, yielding 175 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

Premade veg battas are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 120 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a vegetable batta via gnome cooking with 30 Cooking, yielding 156 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Velrak the explorer
title: Velrak the explorer
lead:
Velrak the explorer plays a small role in the Heroes' Quest and Scorpion Catcher quests as he is the one who gives the player a dusty key (assuming that players are not fishing for lava eels in the Lava Maze during Heroes' Quest and do not have access to the Legends' Guild to buy a dusty key during Scorpion Catcher). He can be found in the Black Knights' Base in Taverley Dungeon in a prison cell.

To obtain the dusty key, the Jailer outside of the cell must be killed. The Jailer will then drop a Jail key, which is used to unlock Velrak's cell. When Velrak is asked if there are any good places to explore, he will provide the dusty key. When giving the player a dusty key, the message states that he "reaches somewhere mysterious". This may be a reference to the mystery of players having invisible backpacks.

label: Venenatis/Strategies
title: Venenatis/Strategies
lead:
: Venenatis resides in a multi-way area in moderately high-level Wilderness. You may be attacked at any time during the fight, and this is always a possibility in any deep wilderness multicombat area. Do not bring any items that you are not willing to lose. Items like the Dragon defender are permanently lost if not protected beyond level 20 Wilderness.

Venenatis is a level 464 spider boss that is found in the Silk Chasm. Spindel is the level 302 lesser variant of Venenatis found in the Web Chasm, but otherwise her mechanics are identical. Completion of the medium Wilderness Diary is required to fight Venenatis.

label: Venom
title: Venom
lead:
Venom is a stronger form of poison that players and monsters suffer after they are successfully envenomed. When a target is envenomed, a number appears with a dark green hitsplat ( ) instead of a bright green one ( which indicates poison), indicating the amount of damage the venom has dealt.

Zulrah and its snakelings, Vorkath, Araxxor and its araxytes, Doom of Mokhaiotl's acid blood, cursed baboons, manticores (when the Mantimayhem tier 2 or 3 handicap is active), and spiders in the Ungael laboratory are the only monsters able to inflict venom. Players are able to inflict venom upon their enemies by using certain weaponry.

label: Verac the Defiled's equipment
title: Verac the Defiled's equipment
lead:
Verac the Defiled's equipment is obtainable from the Barrows minigame. Completing the Barrows minigame does not guarantee players will get a Barrows item. The set requires 70 Defence to wear the armour and 70 Attack to wield the weapon. Verac's set is the only set of Barrows equipment to give a Prayer bonus with each piece. Verac's set is still useful for players who wish to combine Melee and Prayer. The Brassard does, however, give lower defensive bonuses than other Barrows platebodies; its bonuses are roughly on par with a Rune platebody.

Along with Dharok's set and Guthan's set, Verac's is one of the more popular Barrows Equipment. Apart from the usual Defence and Attack bonuses that Barrows sets confer, the Verac's set also provides moderate Prayer bonuses at the price of a marginally lower Ranged Defence bonus. In addition, it also does not penalise Magic defence.

label: Veronica
title: Veronica
lead: Veronica is the fiancée of Ernest. They came upon Draynor Manor, and Ernest went in to ask for directions, as they were a little lost. However, he hadn't emerged after an hour, and she began to worry. She doesn't consider him to be particularly brave. She is found outside the Manor, north of Draynor Village and starts the Ernest the Chicken quest.

It can also be purchased from the Nightmare Zone using 145 reward points. You may buy them in packs of 100, called a water-filled vial pack, which starts at 201 coins.

label: Villager clothing

Tribal outfits come in blue, brown, pink and yellow colours. A full tribal outfit costs 1200 trading sticks normally, but with Karamja gloves 1 or higher, each set only costs 1000 trading sticks. Each tribal outfit can be stored in the magic wardrobe.

Wearing the outfits will increase the trading sticks received (and Tai Bwo Favour reduced) when speaking to villagers in the Tai Bwo Wannai Cleanup minigame.

label: Vitruvius
title: Vitruvius
lead:
Vitruvius was an artisan and metallurgist during the early Fifth Age. After the discovery of elemental ore, he authored many books on the subject of metallurgy and applying magic to metal-work, most of which have since become scattered across the lands and few remain in good condition.

Vitruvius is best known for creating the Elemental Workshop, as well as the creation of the elemental, mind elemental, and possibly more elemental equipment. It is said that the magicians of the time feared the threat posed by the greater and more powerful weapons that were being created with the elemental metal, and so they closed down Vitruvius's workshop and attempted to destroy all knowledge of the manufacturing processes.

label: Viyeldi
title: Viyeldi
lead:
Viyeldi is a spirit encountered during the Legends' Quest, when Nezikchened - disguised as Echned Zekin - asks you to kill him. When you first enter the Viyeldi caves, he pretends to be a blue hat on the ground until picked up. Upon beginning a conversation with him, he informs you of a different path you could take in the quest. You can choose to carry out Nezikchened's request, and kill Viyeldi using the Dark dagger that Echned Zekin gives you at the source of the holy water spring, or you could listen to him, and kill the warriors for the fragments of the Heart crystal to progress.

Killing Viyeldi, while quicker, results in a more difficult final fight, as you will have to defeat the three warriors San Tojalon, Irvig Senay, and Ranalph Devere alongside Nezikchened in the fight. You can avoid this if you listen to Viyeldi and give the dagger to Ungadulu instead, and kill the warriors. Ungadulu will also give you a Holy force card to use against Nezikchened and weaken him in the next two fights.

label: Viyeldi caves
title: Viyeldi caves
lead:
The Viyeldi caves, named after their resident spirit Viyeldi, are the lower floor of a cave system located in the Kharazi Jungle in southern Karamja. They play a major role in Legends' Quest, of which partial completion is required for access to the caves.

The Viyeldi caves may be visited after the quest for the purpose of a master cryptic step. Additionally, barrels in the room just above the caves (containing the winch used to enter) can be smashed for a chance at random treasure, such as noted cooked sharks.

label: Vladirog
title: Vladirog
lead:
Vladirog is a vampyre and one of the possible senders of a message to the player if they successfully complete the Theatre of Blood. Vladirog is spectating the Theatre with his wife, they both want to see some more antics before the player dies and therefore sends them supplies to keep them alive a little longer.

They are only mentioned in the message, and cannot be found anywhere in-game.

label: vodka

lead: Vodka is a clear spirit that can be obtained from Heckel Funch in the Gnome Stronghold, The Asp & Snake Bar at Pollnivneach, Jossik in the Lighthouse, Atlazora's Rest in Outer Fortis, or The Flaming Arrow in Civitas illa Fortis. There is also a chance of receiving a bottle during the King's Ransom quest.

label: Voice in your head
title: Voice in your head
lead:
The voice in your head is the voice that helps guide a player. It is written to in the 16th Postbag from the Hedge. The voice, while not heard in game, is known to be charming and educated, and speaks with a comforting accent. The voice is so eloquent such that some believe it to be a gift to mankind from the gods themselves. The voice often prevents players from performing actions that serve no purpose.

It is a joking reference to examine texts and other messages that appear in the chatbox, such as Nothing interesting happens.

label: Void Knight equipment
title: Void Knight equipment
lead:
Void Knight equipment, often referred to as the void set, void armour, or simply just void, is a set of armour which can be purchased from the Void Knights with the commendation points earned from Pest Control. To buy or equip any of the items (besides the seal), a player must have 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, along with 22 Prayer.

Void Knight armour contributes Defence bonuses to all stats equally (including Magic and Ranged) without lowering any attack bonuses. Wearing a complete set offers various combat bonuses which make the armour a popular choice for players using multiple attack styles.

label: Volcanic eruption
title: Volcanic eruption
lead:
Volcanic eruptions are an effect found around the low-level Wilderness Chaos Temple, the Blighted Volcano, and the Fossil Island Volcano. The lava in these locations regularly shoots out balls of fire at random intervals, which will first shoot up to a certain height, and then crash down onto square within 8 tiles of the source of the fire ball.

The fire balls in these eruptions can only land on walkable tiles, but this may include tiles that are inaccessible (e.g. walkable tiles on an inaccessible island in the lava). They will deal one hitpoint of damage to all players standing in a 3x3 square, centred around the impact location of the fire ball. Due to being area-of-effect damage, this is typeless damage and therefore cannot by avoided by using protection prayers. The damage is also lethal.

label: Volencia moss
title: Volencia moss
lead:
Volencia moss is a herb which requires level 3 Herblore to clean, yielding 2.5 experience. It is used in the Jungle Potion quest as the fourth herb that the player brings Trufitus. Players can make volencia moss by cleaning the grimy volencia moss obtained by searching the grey rocks at the Karamja Jungle mine, north of Shilo Village. In order to be able to collect the herb, the player must first have started the Jungle Potion quest.

Volencia moss is one of the items that Malignius Mortifer may ask the player to give to the Nature Spirit during the quest Fairytale I - Growing Pains.

label: Voodoo Cult
title: Voodoo Cult
lead: Voodoo Cult is a music track that is unlocked at the lower level of Ah Za Rhoon. It can later be heard during Legends' Quest in the Viyeldi caves. It also plays in the Nightmare Zone when facing Nezikchened in Practice or Endurance mode.

label: Vorkath/Strategies
title: Vorkath/Strategies
lead:
After completion of Dragon Slayer II, Vorkath can be fought again. This time, it is stronger.

To get to Vorkath, talk to Torfinn, located in Rellekka on the 3rd dock to the right. This brings you to Ungael, at the entrance of Vorkath.

label: Voyage

lead: Voyage is a music track that is unlocked at the top of Baxtorian Falls.

label: Vulnerability
title: Vulnerability
lead: Vulnerability is a level 66 Magic spell within the standard spellbook. When cast on an opponent, their Defence level is reduced by 10% (or 15% if the tome of water is also equipped). The spell gives 76 Magic experience per cast and requires 1 Soul, 5 Earth, and 5 Water runes to be cast. The spell can only be cast if their stats haven't already been lowered, meaning you cannot stack stat reduction with multiple spells in a row.

label: Vyre
title: Vyre
lead:
Vyres are citizens of Darkmeyer that can be talked to as well as pickpocketed from with level 82 Thieving. A successful pickpocket yields coins or other items and 306.9 Thieving experience.

Although the rogue equipment can be used to double the rewards from pickpocketing, nearby Vyrewatch Sentinels are hostile to anyone not wearing a full set of vyre noble clothing and the bank cannot be used without it. Players may opt to only wear the rogue gloves and rogue mask as they occupy different equipment slots or use the full rogue equipment set when there are no sentinels near; for the latter strategy, there are many vyres who can be trapped in their houses. Noctillion Lugosi can be trapped inside the bank. Vallessia von Pitt can be trapped in a house with Jug of wine spawn while also being relatively close to a bank chest.

label: Vyre noble blazer

*Vyre noble blazer (purple)

label: vyre noble clothing
title: vyre noble clothing
lead:
Vyre noble clothing are a set of clothing that is required to be worn to access the bank and shops within Darkmeyer. It is scented with the blood of a vampyre noble to help blend in with the vampyres, which makes Vyrewatch Sentinels unaggressive and NPCs less hostile towards the player. Each piece of vyre noble clothing also adds 35% to the chance of not being noticed by one of the vyrewatch patrolling Meiyerditch, meaning the player will never be arrested by them while wearing a full set of three.

A vyre noble top, legs, and shoes are created during the quest Sins of the Father. Should players lose this disguise, they can reclaim a set from the chest underneath the trapdoor in Old Man Ral's house.

label: Vyrewatch outfit
title: Vyrewatch outfit
lead:
The Vyrewatch outfit is a set of clothing resembling that of the Vyrewatch, who patrol the city of Meiyerditch in Morytania. A player who wears it is less likely to be caught by the patrolling Vyrewatch to pay a blood tithe (or alternatively get sent to the mines if the player has made enough progress in the Darkness of Hallowvale quest). The outfit can be bought from Trader Sven in the south of Meiyerditch.

Each piece of the vyrewatch outfit will add 20% to the chance of being ignored by a patrolling vyrewatch, up to a total of 60% while wearing all three pieces.

label: Vyrewatch Sentinel/Strategies
title: Vyrewatch Sentinel/Strategies
lead: Vyrewatch Sentinels can be found in Darkmeyer, the capital city of Morytania located in the Sanguinesti region, north of Meiyerditch.

label: Wahisietel
title: Wahisietel
lead: Wahisietel is a Zarosian Mahjarrat mentioned in Tullia's letter, in which Tullia mentions that Wahisietel travelled to Ghorrock to inform its citizens that the Zarosian capital of Senntisten had fallen. He is also mentioned in Zemouregal's Mahjarrat notes, and he has an entry in the ancient golem's database.

label: Walk here
title: Walk here
lead:
The "Walk here" option is available to players as an alternate means of moving about the game world. By right clicking, a player will see a list of options that are available at that present time. If 'Walk here' is selected, the player will move to the position the cursor was in when the option was selected. If two mouse buttons are selected, left clicking a position makes player walk there, as they would right clicking and selecting.

If the player does not want to click on the game, they can click on the minimap, which uses up less clicking overall, and moves the character farther per click than the 'Walk here' option.

label: Wall
title: Wall
lead: Wall may refer to:

label: Wall (Carnillean Mansion bedroom)
title: Wall (Carnillean Mansion bedroom)
lead:
A fake wall located on the of the Carnillean Mansion hides access to a secret room. The wall is first encountered if the player is aligned with the cult during Hazeel Cult, during which the player must visit the secret room to unlock a chest and steal the Hazeel scroll. The wall is later used during Secrets of the North while investigating the death of Ceril Carnillean, where it is apparent that the wall is damaged and the intruder entered the secret room.

After the quest, the secret room can still be accessed using the push-against option on the wall.

label: Wall (Crandor and Karamja Dungeon)
title: Wall (Crandor and Karamja Dungeon)
lead:
The wall is interactive scenery in the Crandor and Karamja Dungeon, north of the deadly red spiders. It cannot be opened until Dragon Slayer I is partially completed after sailing to Crandor and then opening the wall from the northern side to Karamja, unlocking the wall permanently from both sides.

The wall will automatically unlock itself after completing Dragon Slayer I, even if the player did not open the wall from the Crandor side during the quest.

label: Wall Pipe
title: Wall Pipe
lead:
The Wall Pipes are located on the southern wall of one of the houses in Hemenster, and are used in the Fishing Contest quest. During the quest, the player must put a garlic in one of the pipes, to make the Sinister Stranger move to another location, making the best fishing spot available for the player to use.

Interestingly, these pipes can be interacted with from larger distances than most objects. From right beside the pipes, or 1 square away from the pipes, players will walk towards the pipe and a chat message of the player saying "Ewww - it's a smelly sewage pipe." is shown. When interacted from 2 squares away, a chat message "I can't reach that.' is given in the chat box. Searching the pipe from 3 or more squares away, but within 8 or fewer squares away, the chat box will instead read "Nothing interesting was found.". Searching it from any further distance from the pipe will cause the player to walk to within 8 spaces of the pipe before giving the latter message. This behaviour occurs both when searching the pipes, or using items on the pipes.

label: Wallpapers
title: Wallpapers
lead:
Wallpapers (also known as backgrounds) were found on the "Downloads" section of the RuneScape website between approximately 2004 and 2013, alongside the official client and the world map. They were made from official artwork, and could be downloaded at several resolutions. They would sometimes first appear in Postbag from the Hedge before or alongside being released as wallpapers.

Wallpapers based on Old School RuneScape are currently released on the official Flickr account.

label: Walter Fairweather
title: Walter Fairweather
lead:
Walter Fairweather is the husband of Gertrude Fairweather and father of Wilough, Shilop, Kanel, and Philop Fairweather. Walter is a resident of Varrock, the capital city of Misthalin, but has not visited it for the last year.

Walter is mentioned in the Varrock Census of the Year 160, Fifth Age, as being a travelling merchant, explaining his long absence from the city.

label: Wampum belt
title: Wampum belt
lead: A wampum belt is a quest item used in the Shilo Village quest. It is given to the player at the start of the quest by Mosol Rei outside the east entrance to Shilo Village. The player gives the belt to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village in order to find out more about the curse placed on Shilo Village.

label: Wand
title: Wand
lead:
Wands are Magic weapons that have the ability to autocast spells. Unlike most other Magic weapons, they have no Melee bonuses. They also do not provide an unlimited source of any type of runes (with the exception of the Kodai wand). Wands give higher Magic bonuses than other Magic weapons, but are significantly more difficult or expensive to obtain.

Standard wands are rewards from the Mage Training Arena minigame. Each wand can be obtained from the Rewards Guardian in exchange for pizazz points and requires a different Magic level to wield.

label: Wander
title: Wander
lead:
Wander is a music track that is unlocked around Draynor Village. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Start and Unknown Land.

In Classic mode, the track plays at the Falador Farm.

label: Wander radius
title: Wander radius
lead:
wander range.]]
The wander radius of a non-player character refers to the maximum number of game tiles it can walk from its spawn point. In general conversation, the term is typically used to describe an NPC's overall wander area, alongside the terms wander range, wander distance, and roam range.

With some exceptions, monsters have an invisible square drawn around their spawn point, in which they will randomly wander. Due to the nature of RuneScape's tiles, drawing an odd-numbered square of tiles around a monster results in an equal number of tiles from the centre of the square to any of the tiles along its perimeter; as such, the wander radius refers to this distance from the spawn to the edge, and the range refers to the area of the square itself.

label: War of the Five Houses
title: War of the Five Houses
lead:
The War of the Five Houses was a civil war in Great Kourend near the end of the Fourth Age in the 121st - 123rd decade of Kourend's timeline. Despite the name, Arceuus never participated in the war.

During the 120th decade, King Agata IV was overthrown by the leaders of the five Houses, presumably due to his mismanagement of the kingdom that left it ravaged by famine. With no one next in line to the throne, an alliance between the Lovakengj and Piscarilius House formed to murder Lord Shayzien, which was short lived as the two houses began to fight one another. Meanwhile, the Hosidius House began to mobilise their forces, and Lord Trobin Arceuus has begun to reinforce the defences of Arceuus, not wishing to participate in the civil war.

label: War ship
title: War ship
lead:
The war ship is an untradeable holiday item obtained during birthday events. It cannot be equipped, nor be interacted with in the inventory.

It was originally found in Glough's house in RuneScape Classic, where it could be picked up by players but did not have a use. The item was discontinued in 2004 with the transition to RuneScape 2, making it extremely rare, although worthless as it could not be traded.

label: Warding
title: Warding
lead:
Warding was a skill that allows players to create magical robes and armour, as well as other magical items by using fabrics and vis. Warding was first announced at RuneFest 2018 and developed over the course of 2019, but ultimately failed to reach enough support in the polls and was never added to the game.

label: Wardrobe (skeleton, cobweb)
title: Wardrobe (skeleton, cobweb)
lead:
Wardrobes are interactive pieces of scenery that can be predominantly found in spooky places such as the Draynor Manor, the Slayer Tower, or the abodes of witches and necromancers.

The wardrobe features two large doors with a line of faded golden veneer painted around the edges, crowned by a decorative piece of carved panelling, with a cobweb attached to its top-right corner.

label: Warhammer
title: Warhammer
lead:
Warhammers are a type of slow but powerful one-handed melee weapon that employ the Crush style of attack. Notably, warhammers require sufficient Strength levels to wield instead of Attack, which can be leveraged by players that choose not to train Attack.

One of the drawbacks of warhammers is their trade-off of higher damage for a lower attack speed. Because of this, most players choose to use scimitars since they hit faster.

label: Warhammer (unobtainable item)
title: Warhammer (unobtainable item)
lead:
The warhammer is an unobtainable item released alongside RuneScape 2. Although it is classified internally as a weapon, it lacks a wield option and does not have any equip animations defined.

It was presumably a leftover from development, created in order to test the implementation of the new warhammers in RuneScape 2.

label: Warning sign (Mort'ton)
title: Warning sign (Mort'ton)
lead: Warning signs are scenery that can be found at the north-west entrance to Mort'ton at the either end of the bridge.

label: Warped Terrorbird (interface item)
title: Warped Terrorbird (interface item)
lead:
The Warped Terrorbird is an interface item that can be seen in the Slayer skill guide representing the Warped Terrorbird

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Warrant
title: Warrant
lead:
The warrant is a quest item used only in Plague City. It is obtained from Bravek after giving him a hangover cure and telling him about the kidnapping.

The warrant is used to distract the mourner guard by the entrance to the plague house in the south-east corner of West Ardougne, granting the player access to search for Elena.

label: Warrior
title: Warrior
lead:
__NOTOC__
Warrior may refer to:

label: Warrior (Lost City)
title: Warrior (Lost City)
lead:
The Warrior in Lumbridge Swamp is part of a band of adventurers who are looking for the lost city of Zanaris. The rest of his group will not say anything about its mission, but the Warrior, being the dimmest, reveals the mission. The Warrior does not have a good reputation with his team after that.

The warrior and his three companions, an archer, a monk, and a wizard, can be found in the north-west part of the swamp.

label: Warrior (Thieving)
title: Warrior (Thieving)
lead:
Warriors are human soldiers in the employ of certain cities of Gielinor. They can be found patrolling the streets of East Ardougne, but also maintain a presence in the north-western wing of the Varrock Palace, as well as the outer walls of the Ardougne Castle. A group of four warriors can also be encountered on the outskirts of the city, in a camp just north-west of the castle.

In terms of level and stats, warriors are very similar to guards, yet their lack of drops means they are rarely fought. However, warriors are an infrequently used alternative to thieving from stalls at lower levels. They may be pickpocketed at level 25 Thieving, giving 18 coins and 26 Thieving experience, while hitting the player for 2 damage if they are caught in the act. Warriors that keep watch over the Ardougne Market are quite convenient to rob, as any damage they may deal in retaliation can be redressed by stealing from the Ardougne Baker's Stall instead.

label: Washing bowl
title: Washing bowl
lead: A washing bowl can be found on a bench in Filliman Tarlock's Nature Grotto, south of the Mort Myre Swamp. Hidden underneath it is a mirror required for the Nature Spirit quest. The bowl respawns almost instantly and serves no purpose in the quest after revealing the mirror.

label: Watch
title: Watch
lead:
A watch is an item for solving coordinate clues whilst on Treasure Trails. A chart can be obtained by first talking to the Observatory professor (who may be at the Observatory or the nearby Observatory reception building to the north-west, depending upon whether the player has completed the Observatory Quest). After talking to him, you have to receive the sextant from Murphy at Port Khazard in order for Brother Kojo to give you a watch at the Clock Tower.

Although not required for coordinate clues, a watch can be used with a sextant and a chart in the inventory to find the coordinates.

label: Watchman
title: Watchman
lead: Watchmen are guards located on the middle floor of the Watchtower on the north-western end of Yanille. They can be attacked and pickpocketed at level 65 Thieving. Thieving from them yields 60 coins and bread along with 137.5 experience. The route outside of walls requires going west from Nightmare Zone. From inside the walls, walk north and follow the northern wall and use the underwall tunnel, requiring 16 Agility, or climbing rocks, requiring 5 Agility, then walk west to the Watchtower. On the north side of the building, climb the trellis, requiring 18 Agility, to the middle floor of the Watchtower.

label: Watchman (random event)
title: Watchman (random event)
lead:
The watchman was a random event that appeared during Thieving, similar to other guardian events such as the rock golem. His level differed depending on the player's combat level. The Watchman would say "(Player's Name), you are under arrest!" before attacking. He was removed in a hidden update in August 2006 due to players' complaints about being killed too quickly when pickpocketing at a low hitpoint level and wearing no armour. As a result, he has never been present in Old School RuneScape.

Eventually, references to him were removed from the Knowledge Base between 2 November and 5 November 2006.

label: Watchtower
title: Watchtower
lead: Watchtower is a quest about the conflict between Yanille and the ogres of Gu'Tanoth. It involves the restoration of the city's Watchtower so that it may defend itself against an ogre attack.

label: Watchtower (building)
title: Watchtower (building)
lead: The Watchtower is a fortified defensive structure situated on the northern wall of Yanille. Its primary purpose is to defend the city from the ogres that inhabit the nearby Feldip Hills. After completion of its eponymous quest, it can be accessed directly by casting Watchtower Teleport.

label: Watchtower Teleport
title: Watchtower Teleport
lead:
Watchtower Teleport teleports the player to the top floor of the Watchtower, just north of Yanille. Unlocking the spell requires completion of the Watchtower quest to read the spell scroll given as a reward by the Watchtower Wizard.

Casting this spell is a requirement for completing the hard Ardougne Diary. Completing the hard Ardougne Diary grants the ability to teleport to the centre of Yanille by right-clicking the Watchtower teleport icon in the standard spellbook.

label: Watchtower Wizard
title: Watchtower Wizard
lead:
The Watchtower Wizard is the wizard who built a strange crystal-run machine defending Yanille from the nearby ogres. This wizard initiates the Watchtower Quest.

Should any duplicated or leftover quest items be used on him, he will confiscate the item.

label: water
title: water
lead:
Water can be found in many locations, in the forms of sinks, water pumps, and wells. A water source is indicated on the map by the symbol. It is used in a number of skills, including Cooking, Crafting, Construction, Herblore, and Farming.

Water may also be obtained from objects not marked with a water drop symbol, like the water barrel.

label: Water (disambiguation)
title: Water (disambiguation)
lead:
Water may refer to:

*Water, a liquid.

label: Water Altar
title: Water Altar
lead:
The Water Altar is a runic altar upon which water runes are crafted from rune essence or pure essence, providing 6 Runecraft experience per essence imbued. Level 5 Runecraft is required to craft water runes.

Players may create a water tiara here by using either a water talisman or a tiara on the altar whilst having both in their inventory, granting 30 Runecraft experience. An elemental tiara can also be created here by using an elemental talisman and gold tiara, granting 40 Runecraft experience.

label: Water battlestaff
title: Water battlestaff
lead:
The water battlestaff is an elemental staff requiring 30 Attack and 30 Magic to wield. In addition to increased Melee and Magic Attack bonuses, the staff provides unlimited amounts of water runes as well as the autocast option when equipped.

This staff can be created at level 54 Crafting by combining a water orb and battlestaff. It can also be upgraded to a mystic water staff by paying Thormac 40,000 coins to upgrade it (less with the completion of certain Kandarin Diaries). The mystic water staff is an even stronger alternative, providing better melee and magic stat bonuses.

label: Water Blast
title: Water Blast
lead:
Water Blast is a water-based blast spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 47 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

It is the strongest water spell available to free-to-play players.

label: Water Bolt
title: Water Bolt
lead: Water Bolt is a water-based bolt spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 23 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

label: water controls
title: water controls
lead: Two water controls are used in the Elemental Workshop I quest to let the water wheel spin. Players can turn them, making the flow indicators green.

label: water elemental
title: water elemental
lead:
Water elementals inhabit the area accessed during the Elemental Workshop I and Elemental Workshop II below Seers' Village. This monster can be helpful in training Herblore as it always drops a vial of water upon defeat, as well as an array of grimy herbs. It can be accessed during and after the quest.

Killing one is a requirement for an Easy Kandarin Diary task.

label: Water orb
title: Water orb
lead:
A water orb is a glass orb that has been charged at the Obelisk of Water by using the Charge Water Orb spell, requiring 56 Magic, on the obelisk. The spell requires an unpowered orb, 30 water runes, and 3 cosmic runes, yielding 66 Magic experience.

The Water Obelisk is located on the island across from the shore of Catherby, getting there by climbing a ladder at the end of Taverley Dungeon by the black dragons. Accessing this section of the dungeon requires the dusty key or 70 agility.

label: Water Pool
title: Water Pool
lead:
The Water Pool containing pure water is located in the Kharazi Jungle, and is used to fill the gold bowl during the Legends' Quest. Filling the bowl requires the player to use a hollow reed on the pool, as the rocks makes it impossible to fill the bowl normally.

Using the look option on the pool results in the message: "A pretty babbling spring. The water bubbles with a strange effervescence." Using the investigate option on the pool results in the message: "The water's hard to reach with all these rocks around. There's a narrow gap, but you'll struggle to fit a container through it."

label: Water rune
title: Water rune
lead:
Water runes are one of the four elemental runes. They are used to cast water-based combat spells in the standard spellbook, as well as many spells found in other spellbooks. The Confuse, Weaken, and Curse spells, often regarded as an inexpensive source of Magic experience, require water runes in conjunction with body and earth runes to cast. Some items, such as a staff of water, provide infinite water runes while equipped.

Water runes or packs can be bought from Magic shops, such as Aubury's Rune Shop in Varrock. Non-ironman players can also purchase them from the Nightmare Zone using 25 reward points.

label: Water spells
title: Water spells
lead: Water spells may refer to:

label: Water Strike
title: Water Strike
lead: Water Strike is a water-based strike spell in the standard spellbook, available starting at level 5 Magic. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

label: Water talisman
title: Water talisman
lead: A water talisman is a type of talisman that lets the player use the Water Altar. Use the talisman on the altar to get inside allowing one to create water runes at the altar. It is also used to make a water tiara if you have a tiara and a water talisman and use them on the altar, granting 30 Runecraft experience. If you are a member, it can be used to runecraft mist runes at the Air Altar, steam runes at the Fire Altar, or mud runes at the Earth Altar. The water talisman is consumed in the process.

label: Water Wave
title: Water Wave
lead:
Water Wave is a water-based wave spell in the standard spellbook, requiring level 65 Magic to cast. As an offensive combat spell it can only be cast on attackable NPCs, or other players in a PvP situation.

It is the second-strongest water spell in the game, with the strongest being Water Surge.

label: Water wheel (disambiguation)
title: Water wheel (disambiguation)
lead:
Water wheel may refer to:

* Water wheel (Elemental Workshop)
** Water wheel (frame)
* Water wheel (Lumbridge)
* Water wheel (Motherlode Mine)
* Waterwheel (Giants' Foundry)

label: Water wheel (Elemental Workshop)
title: Water wheel (Elemental Workshop)
lead: The Water wheel is found in the elemental workshop near the water elementals. During the Elemental Workshop I quest, players should make it turn by operating the nearby water controls.

label: Water wheel (frame)
title: Water wheel (frame)
lead: Water wheels are located on the north side of the Elemental Workshop near the water elementals.

label: Waterfall (disambiguation)
title: Waterfall (disambiguation)
lead:
Waterfall may refer to:

*Waterfall Quest, an intermediate quest
*Baxtorian Falls, the primary location of the Waterfall Quest
*Lacerta Falls, a waterfall at the south-eastern end of the Kebos Lowlands
*Waterfall (music track), unlocked near the Baxtorian Falls
*Waterfall (Tombs of Amascut), a scenery object
*Waterfall (Giants' Foundry), an object used in the Giants' Foundry minigame

label: Waterfall (music track)
title: Waterfall (music track)
lead: Waterfall is a music track that is unlocked south of the Baxtorian Falls. It can also be heard in Glarial's Tomb. It also plays in the Nightmare Zone when facing the Moss Guardian in Practice or Endurance mode.

label: Waterfall Dungeon
title: Waterfall Dungeon
lead: The Waterfall Dungeon is a set of connected caverns underneath the Baxtorian Falls. The dungeon can be accessed during and after the completion of the Waterfall Quest, and is an important destination in the quest.

label: Waterfall Quest
title: Waterfall Quest
lead: Waterfall Quest is an intermediate quest about a legendary treasure hidden somewhere in the Baxtorian Falls. The waterfall holds the history of the great elven King Baxtorian and his wife Glarial.

label: Waterfall rocks
title: Waterfall rocks
lead:
Waterfall rocks are a set of wet rocks found in the first cavern in Ah Za Rhoon, which the player enters during the Shilo Village quest. They play no role in the quest itself, but can be used to leave the cavern.

Choosing to "look-at" them reveals a precarious pathway, which leads through the waterfall ahead. Searching the rocks will give players the option to follow this path, taking them just east of the stepping stones shortcut found south of the temple.

label: Waterlily
title: Waterlily
lead: Waterlilies are non-interactive scenery that can be found in bodies of water across Gielinor.

label: Waterlogged
title: Waterlogged
lead:
Waterlogged is a music track that is unlocked in the Mort Myre Swamp.

It can later be heard while Temple Trekking, during the Bridge puzzle and the battle with the creature on the boat trip. The track also plays during Sins of the Father, when escorting Ivan Strom past the Bridge puzzle. In the Mort Myre Swamp area, the music player will shuffle between playing this track, Dead Quiet and Stagnant.

label: Waterpump
title: Waterpump
lead:
Waterpump may refer to:

* Water pump (amenity) - a water pump built with the Construction skill at level 17 for use on Sailing islands
* Waterpump (Falador)
* Waterpump (Morytania)
* Water pump (Tempoross Cove)
* Water Pump (The Gauntlet)
* Water Pump (Trouble Brewing)
* Water pump (Varlamore)

label: Waterpump (Falador)
title: Waterpump (Falador)
lead: A Waterpump is a water source found by the entrance of the Hairdresser in Falador. Using it to fill an empty bucket is a requirement for the easy Falador diary.

label: Waterpump (Morytania)
title: Waterpump (Morytania)
lead: A Waterpump is a water source found east of Fenkenstrain's Castle and outside an abandoned village west of the Barrows in Morytania.

label: Waterskin
title: Waterskin
lead:
A waterskin carries up to four servings of water, and provides protection against the desert heat effect in the Kharidian Desert. The amount of water will be noted by the waterskins name in parenthesis e.g. "Waterskin (4)" is a waterskin that is holding the maximum amount of water.

These can be bought from Shantay, in the Shantay Pass, south of Al Kharid. There are several ways to refill waterskins. In the table below, different methods of refilling are given, along with the amount of water doses are refilled by that method. Note that it is possible to decant water into other containers, for example using a vial of water on an empty bucket. Doing this before refilling the waterskin will quadruple the amount of water refilled in the skin.

label: Wave
title: Wave
lead:
Wave is the sixth listed emote. Upon use, the player waves their left hand. This gesture is often used as a greeting and farewell, but can also be used to catch one's attention.

This emote is already unlocked upon making an account.

label: Wave (disambiguation)
title: Wave (disambiguation)
lead:
Wave may refer to:

* Wave emote
* Wave spells
**Wind Wave
**Water Wave
**Earth Wave
**Fire Wave

label: Wave spells
title: Wave spells
lead: Wave spells are the second strongest elemental group of magic combat spells in the standard spellbook. Elemental staves can be used to cover the costs of these spells. These are members only spells. Like all combat spells, each damage point caused by these spells yields 2 Magic experience and 1.33 Hitpoints experience.

label: Wayne
title: Wayne
lead:
Wayne is the owner of the chainmail specialty shop, Wayne's Chains. He may be found in his shop, located in southern Falador. Wayne's Chains sells all chainmail up to adamant. Despite his cheap prices, his shop is normally deserted.

During the 2021 Christmas event, it is revealed he has been trying to obtain sets of goblin mail in order to complete Goblin Diplomacy and become an adventurer, eventually hoping to join the Legends' Guild.

label: Wayne's Chains! - Chainmail specialist.
title: Wayne's Chains! - Chainmail specialist.
lead: Wayne's Chains is a shop owned by Wayne located in southern Falador. It is the only shop that specialises exclusively in chainbodies.

label: Waystone
title: Waystone
lead:
Waystone may refer to:

* Mokhaiotl waystone, a teleport to the Ruins of Mokhaiotl
* Waystones in Leagues:
** Waystone (Shattered Relics League)
** Waystone (Trailblazer Reloaded League)
** Waystone (Raging Echoes League)
** Waystone (Demonic Pacts League)

label: weaken
title: weaken
lead:
Weaken is a level 11 Magic spell. When cast on an opponent, their Strength is reduced by 5%. The spell gives experience whether it hits or misses, making it a popular way to gain experience cheaply. The spell can only be cast if the targets stats haven't already been lowered, meaning you can not stack stat reduction with multiple spells in a row.

The spell grants 21 Magic experience and requires three water, two earth, and one body runes to be cast.

label: Wealthy citizen (interface item)
title: Wealthy citizen (interface item)
lead:
The Wealthy citizen is an interface item that can be seen in the Thieving and Pickpocketing subsections of the Thieving skill guide. The item represents the Wealthy citizen.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Weapon poison
title: Weapon poison
lead:
Weapon poison is a potion made by using dragon scale dust on a kwuarm potion (unf), requiring 60 Herblore, yielding a weapon poison and 137.5 Herblore experience. It can be applied to all metal arrows (including amethyst), normal metal bolts, javelins, darts, and throwing knives, most daggers, spears and hastae as well. Weapon poison can be removed from a weapon with a cleaning cloth.

A single vial of weapon poison can poison only 5 arrows, bolts, darts, or throwing knives. This makes poisoning a substantial amount of ammo quite costly.

label: Weapon poison (disambiguation)
title: Weapon poison (disambiguation)
lead:
Weapon poison may refer to:

* Weapon poison salesman

label: Weapon poison (unobtainable item)
title: Weapon poison (unobtainable item)
lead:
Weapon poison is an unobtainable item that was intended to be released with the Ranging Guild, but for unknown reasons was cut before launch. Most likely, it would have been sold by the Weapon poison salesman, who was also not released. Since Weapon poison was relatively difficult to obtain at the time, it is possible the developers feared making it available in a store would cause the item to become too common.

It is referred to in the game files as "Display poison". This suggests that, similar to the Tea seller, the Weapon poison salesman would have owned a stall, and yelled at any player who attempted to take the display poison.

label: Weapon poison salesman
title: Weapon poison salesman
lead:
The Weapon poison salesman is an unreleased NPC who would have been located in the Ranging Guild. His name suggests that he would have sold Weapon poison to the player, that could be used on darts, throwing knives, and the new javelins.

An unobtainable item called "Display poison" exists, that aside from the different colour is identical to the real weapon poison. This suggests that, similar to the Tea seller, the Weapon poison salesman would have owned a stall, and yelled at any player who attempted to take the display poison.

label: Weapon shop
title: Weapon shop
lead:
Weapon shop may refer to:

*Axe shops
*Sword shops
*Scimitar shops
*Magic shops
*Archery shops
*Crossbow shops

label: weapon slot
title: weapon slot
lead:
Weapon slot may refer to:
* One-handed slot table
** One-handed slot table (F2P)
* Two-handed slot table
** Two-handed slot table (F2P)

label: Weapon store key
title: Weapon store key
lead:
The Weapon store key is an item used during the Shield of Arrav quest to access the Phoenix Gang's weapon storage room. In order to obtain it, you must either be in or have a partner in the Phoenix Gang who can get the key.

This item was previously named just "Key" until the Varrock update, when it was renamed to "Weapon store key", possibly to avoid confusion with other keys.

label: weapons
title: weapons
lead: Weapons are worn equipment in the weapon slot used to deal damage in combat. One-handed weapons can be used with a shield in the shield slot (or another item such as a defender) and two-handed weapons prevent the use of the shield slot. Stackable weapons are all equipped at the same time. Some equipment used in other skills such as axes, pickaxes, the Imcando hammer, pearl fishing rods from Alry the Angler's Angling Accessories, and Amy's saw from Mahogany Homes are also equipable.

label: Weapons rack (interface item)
title: Weapons rack (interface item)
lead:
The Weapons rack is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Weapons rack.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Weapons/Categories
title: Weapons/Categories
lead: This is a list of weapons grouped by their category, which is found in game at the bottom of the Combat Options tab. All weapons within a category use the same set of combat options. (The one exception to this is the 3rd age longsword, which uses the combat options of a 2h sword despite being one-handed and categorised as a slash sword.)

label: Weaponsmaster
title: Weaponsmaster
lead:
The Weaponsmaster is a member of the Phoenix Gang and plays a role during the Shield of Arrav quest. He is located upstairs in the southern alley of Varrock (south-west of Aubury's Rune Shop).

Players who are trying to get into the Black Arm Gang will have to kill him to be able to pick up the two required Phoenix crossbows. He will also attack members of the Black Arm Gang if they try to talk to him.

label: Weather vane (disambiguation)
title: Weather vane (disambiguation)
lead:
Weather vane may refer to:

*Seers weathervane, an object used during One Small Favour
*Weather vane, the scenery object

label: Website updates
title: Website updates
lead: Website updates are updates which generally affect the main website but may also include content reveals and poll information.

label: weight
title: weight
lead:
Weight is a property of items which is primarily related to run energy depletion. A player's weight is calculated as the sum of all items' weight that are equipped and held in the inventory. Having a higher weight will cause run energy to deplete faster, so it is generally recommended to minimise weight during activities that require running.

Players can see the total weight of the items they have equipped or are carrying in their inventory on the Equipment Stats screen, measured in kilograms. Items can weigh fractions of a kilogram, but the Equipment Stats screen will round down to the nearest whole kilogram. For example, a rune platebody weighs 9.979 kg but is displayed as 9 kg, and equipped boots of lightness weigh -4.535 kg but display as -4 kg.

label: weight-reducing clothing
title: weight-reducing clothing
lead:
Weight-reducing clothing is clothing that players can wear that will reduce their weight.

If a player wore the pieces of armour that offered the maximum weight reduction (Graceful hood, Graceful top, Graceful legs, Boots of lightness, Penance gloves, and Spottier cape), that player would achieve the lowest possible weight of –27.5 kilograms.

label: Weird Old Man
title: Weird Old Man
lead: The Weird Old Man is an insane man who can be found outside the northern entrance to the Kalphite Lair.

label: Welcome Screen
title: Welcome Screen
lead:
The Welcome Screen is the interface that is shown after logging in. It displays a welcome message, the time since you last logged in, several informational tiles about your account and about recent updates, and a button to start playing the game. (Note: you can’t access your inbox on mobile)

The welcome screen will not appear if the player logs in to a dangerous area, such as the wilderness, or if the player is creating a new account.

label: Welcome Screen/Message of the week
title: Welcome Screen/Message of the week
lead:
The Message of the week is the banner and 2 models that are consistently at the bottom of the Welcome Screen. Since the release of Old School RuneScape, there have been over 650 messages of the week.

The banner displays the message of the week, chosen by Jagex , the message of the week will summarise the major changes in the most recent update, often with a humorous twist. Visually, the banner is fielded by two chosen models, sometimes animated, relevant to the message of the week.

label: Welcome Screen/Message of the week/2025
title: Welcome Screen/Message of the week/2025
lead: This is a gallery of all unique messages of the week that appeared in 2025. The images may vary in quality due to different sources, some may lack all or some of the animation frames that would've existed at the time. Message of the weeks that reuse the previous updates animations are shown without them.

label: Welcome Screen/Message of the week/2026
title: Welcome Screen/Message of the week/2026
lead: This is a gallery of all unique messages of the week that appeared in 2025. The images may vary in quality due to different sources, some may lack all or some of the animation frames that would've existed at the time. Message of the weeks that reuse the previous updates animations are shown without them.

label: Welcome Screen/Message of the week/Other
title: Welcome Screen/Message of the week/Other
lead: This is a gallery of all unique messages of the week that appear on specific worlds or under certain conditions. The images may vary in quality due to different sources, some may lack all or some of the animation frames that would've existed at the time.

label: Welcome Screen/Message of the week/Transcript
title: Welcome Screen/Message of the week/Transcript
lead: Transcripts of the messages of the week found on the Old School RuneScape welcome screen.

label: well
title: well
lead: A well is a common object found throughout Gielinor, and is used as a source of obtaining water by using an empty bucket or cup on them. They are marked on the map with a icon, although other sources of water share the same icon.

label: Well (disambiguation)
title: Well (disambiguation)
lead:
A well is a piece of scenery, usually where one can obtain water with a bucket.

Several special wells, not used for gathering water, exist across Gielinor:
* Vyre well
* Well (Paterdomus)
* Smokey well
* Several wells in the Underground Pass: 
** Flames of Zamorak (well)
** Well of Voyage
* Well of Goodwill (discontinued)

label: Well (Paladin badges)
title: Well (Paladin badges)
lead:
A well is located deep within the Underground Pass, where the player sacrifices three Paladin's badges and a unicorn horn to the well for access to the final chamber of the dungeon in the Underground Pass quest.

After the completion of the quest, Iban's staff or upgraded version can be recharged for free when used on the well, instead of paying the Dark Mage in West Ardougne.

label: Well (Paterdomus)
title: Well (Paterdomus)
lead:
A well found in the dungeon under Paterdomus Temple is used in a number of Morytania quests such as Priest in Peril and In Aid of the Myreque. In Priest in Peril you first obtain Murky water from the well for Drezel to bless in order to free him. Later in the quest you will give Drezel either Rune essence or Pure essence in order for him to bless the well and return the holiness of Saradomin to the river Salve.

In the In Aid of the Myreque quest you make the Rod of ivandis and it needs to be blessed by dipping it into the river Salve via the well. In order to do this players MUST HAVE a rope in their inventory.

label: Well of Voyage
title: Well of Voyage
lead:
The Well of Voyage (also known as the Well of the Damned up until starting Regicide) is a well that allows transport between Tirannwn and Kandarin, located in the Underground Pass in Iban's Temple. The player uses the Well of Voyage during Underground Pass to destroy Iban by throwing a doll combined with his blood, shadow, ashes and the crushed bones of a dead dove into it.

It was constructed by the elves in the Second Age as a means of expanding their land, but it was captured and corrupted recently by Iban. King Lathas has his wizards work on repairing the well after completing Underground Pass, and the well becomes usable by the player upon starting Regicide.

label: Well stacked rocks
title: Well stacked rocks
lead: Well stacked rocks are found on Cairn Isle in Karamja. Players can search them to enter the Tomb of Bervirius during the Shilo Village quest.

label: West Ardougne
title: West Ardougne
lead: West Ardougne is the western part of the capital city of Ardougne. Which has been quarantined due to a mysterious plague. It is only available to players who have partially completed the Plague City quest.

label: West Ardougne Cat Appreciation Society
title: West Ardougne Cat Appreciation Society
lead: The West Ardougne Cat Appreciation Society is an organisation in West Ardougne centred around cats. According to Siv Illian, the West Ardougnese citizens use cats to keep the mouse and rat population under control in order to prevent the spreading of the plague, for which they are very thankful. The society is planning on opening a 'community-led cat café' to the public at some point.

label: West Ardougne church
title: West Ardougne church
lead: The West Ardougne church is a Saradominist church in the city of West Ardougne. It is only available to players who have partially completed the Plague City quest.

label: West Ardougne clinic
title: West Ardougne clinic
lead: The West Ardougne clinic is a small clinic run by Nurse Sarah in the city of West Ardougne. It is only available to players who have partially completed the Plague City quest. Players visit the clinic during the elf questline.

label: West Ardougne General Store
title: West Ardougne General Store
lead:
The West Ardougne General Store is run by Chadwell in West Ardougne. It is where most of the city's populace get their food from.

The store sells items that all other general stores sell with the addition of food. The store is convenient for players who wish to go through the Underground Pass, as it carries nearly everything that they will need - a bow, arrows, and two ropes. The only two things the shop is lacking for this are a plank and a spade.

label: West Falador mine
title: West Falador mine
lead:
The West Falador mine is located west of Falador and south of Taverley. The mine features two copper, six tin, three iron, and two coal rocks.

Players needing to bank their ores may walk south-east to a crumbled wall on the borders of Falador, climb over it, and walk a very short distance to the Falador west bank. Players need to have at least level 5 Agility to pass over the crumbled wall. An alternative banking method is heading south of the mine to the gate near the Makeover Mage, and going east and then north to Falador. Either way, this makes the mining site very convenient for players.

label: West Lumbridge Swamp mine
title: West Lumbridge Swamp mine
lead: The West Lumbridge Swamp mine, also known as Lumbridge Swamp (South) West Mine or South-west Lumbridge Swamp Mine, is a mine that may be found in the south-west area of the Lumbridge Swamp. The closest bank from this mine is the Draynor Village bank; walking/running there takes about 1 minute and 10 seconds. Alternatively, a ring of the elements can be used to reach the mine quickly by teleporting to the water altar.

label: Western banner
title: Western banner
lead:
The Western banner is a reward from completing the Western Provinces Diary. There are four depending on which tier of the diary is completed:

*Western banner 1, from the easy tasks
*Western banner 2, from the medium tasks
*Western banner 3, from the hard tasks
*Western banner 4, from the elite tasks

label: Wg
title: Wg
lead:
Wg may refer to:
* Warriors' Guild
* Woodcutting Guild
* Weird gloop

label: wheat
title: wheat
lead:
Fields of wheat can be picked to obtain grain, which can then be milled into flour.

Crop circles may appear inside of a wheat fields.

label: Wheat (Hosidius)
title: Wheat (Hosidius)
lead: Decorative wheat can be found across Hosidius across coastal regions and near the Hosidius Kitchen. Unlike wheat planted in crop fields, the decorative wheat cannot be picked to obtain grain. Hosidius wheat has a unique minimap icon that can help distinguish it from the pickable wheat found in fields.

label: Whetstone (interface item)
title: Whetstone (interface item)
lead:
The Whetstone is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Whetstone.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: While Guthix Sleeps/Historical
title: While Guthix Sleeps/Historical
lead: While Guthix Sleeps was originally released in RuneScape on 26 November 2008, more than a year after the August 2007 archive of RuneScape that Old School was built off of. Multiple changes exist between the original and backported versions.

label: Whip
title: Whip
lead:
Whips are one-handed Melee slash weapons with the same attack speed as daggers and scimitars, but with higher slash and Strength bonuses. They can only use the slash attack style.

The abyssal whip and its variants require an Attack level of 70 to wield, while the abyssal tentacle requires an Attack level of 75.

label: Whip (disambiguation)
title: Whip (disambiguation)
lead: Whip may refer to:

label: Whip mix
title: Whip mix
lead:
Whip mix may refer to:

*Frozen whip mix
*Volcanic whip mix

label: Whirlpool
title: Whirlpool
lead:
Whirlpool may refer to:

* Whirlpool (random event)
* Whirlpool (Baxtorian Falls)
* The kraken's whirlpools

label: Whirlpool (random event)
title: Whirlpool (random event)
lead:
The whirlpool is a discontinued random event. While fishing, there was a chance of the players' fishing spot becoming a whirlpool. If the player continued to fish in the same spot, they would lose their fishing equipment. Like most random events, its purpose was to prevent macroing.

Attempting to fish with Barbarian Fishing caused a dialogue box to come up saying "I'm not putting my hands in there."

label: Whisky
title: Whisky
lead:
Whisky is an alcoholic beverage that heals 5 hitpoints and temporarily increases Strength by 5% + 1 and decreases Attack by 2% + 3. It is also used as an ingredient to make the gnome drink choc saturday. It, along with the other gnome drinks, is often used at player parties or other events.

There are several ways to obtain whisky: it can be bought from Heckel Funch at the of the Grand Tree, from The Asp & Snake Bar in Pollnivneach, from Jossik at the of the Lighthouse, from Atlazora's Rest in Outer Fortis, or from The Flaming Arrow in Civitas illa Fortis. It can also obtained for free by searching Grip's cupboard (while Grip and the guards are dead) in Scarface's mansion from the Heroes' Quest.

label: Whistle
title: Whistle
lead:
Whistle may refer to:

*

*
