lead:
Workshop is a music track that can be unlocked inside Falador city walls. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Arrival and Fanfare.

In Classic mode, the track plays in eastern Falador.

label: World
title: World
lead:
.]]
A world is an instance of Old School RuneScape that can be joined in order to play the game. These are sometimes referred to as servers (though multiple worlds can be hosted on the same physical server), or shortened to W (e.g. "Hop to W301"). Each members world allows 2000 players to be connected at once while free-to-play worlds have a limit of 1400 players at once.

label: World 347 glitch
title: World 347 glitch
lead:
The World 347 glitch was a glitch that occurred on 24 April 2018. Jagex were taking USA servers offline that were scheduled for maintenance; World 345, the standard Deadman Mode world, was transferred to world 347, however Deadman Mode mechanics were prematurely applied by not forcing players to logout on world 347. Jagex estimated that the glitch lasted for less than two minutes.

This resulted in some players dying to other players and losing their items on the main server, and many accounts experience game-breaking effects, such as the permanent loss of experience. A player who had previously achieved 99 Herblore died during the glitch; their base Herblore level was lowered and they still possessed the skillcape, unable to wear it. Players who killed other players and received bank keys during the glitch who logged out and back into the main server held the bank keys, unable to use them. When players attempted to log out or teleport in combat, they were subject to the Deadman Mode delay. Players also received five times as much experience during the glitch which was added to their main server accounts.

label: World border
title: World border
lead:
With the addition of the Sailing skill, players are able to sail their boat towards the borders of the known world map of Gielinor. As far as visible, nothing lies beyond these borders except noticeably darker seas.

Should the player reach a world border, the message The seas here are dangerous. You cannot sail any further this way. will be shown in chat, repeating every three seconds (five ticks) while the player stays near the border. After the message is displayed four times, the screen will violently start to shake and a sound can be heard.

label: World entity
title: World entity
lead: A world entity is a portion of the map that is projected onto another location, typically the ocean. Named entities are denoted by pink text in the right-click Choose Option menu. Players and NPCs can move relative to a world entity and interact with items and objects placed inside it, while the entity itself is free to rotate and move across the map. Currently, the only examples of world entities are boats belonging to players and NPCs, and trawling shoals.

label: World Gate
title: World Gate
lead:
The World Gate is a location rarely spoken of in Gielinor. It is said to have been lost at some point after the elves used it to come from their homeworld of Tarddiad to Gielinor.

When Guthix and Seren shaped the world during the First Age, it is believed that they also created a gateway through which the many worlds, or universes, could commune. Its only known users are the elves and humans, who arrived in Gielinor during the First Age. The gate is thought to have been sealed soon after their arrival; whether by Guthix or another is unknown. Since then, none have been able to access Gielinor directly through the world gate. Instead, beings from other worlds have found alternative methods of entering, usually through unstable portals, fairy rings or other means of teleportation.

label: World map
title: World map
lead:
[[File:Old School RuneScape world map.png|thumb|450px|The Old School RuneScape world map. [ Full resolution image].]]

The world map interface is a large, scrolling map of the entire surface of Gielinor, including its oceans. On the map are the names of cities, towns, islands, kingdoms, mountains, caves, dungeons, rivers, lakes, oceans, seas and countless other geographic features as well as information icons for specific locations, buildings, and quest starting points. The map also shows features such as terrain types, features of the oceans, structures and buildings, and many other features that can be found in the world.

label: World map/History
title: World map/History
lead: The following is an archive of official world maps released by Jagex on their website and prior to that, the web client. For maps before Old School RuneScape, see the page on the RuneScape Wiki.

label: World switching
title: World switching
lead:
World switching, also known as world hopping, is the act of switching to a different server. The most common reason for doing so is to find a server where there are currently no other players in a given area, allowing the world hopper to freely harvest the resources there without competition.

World switching can be very important in merchanting as prices often vary between worlds. This is noticeable in the Fishing shop in Port Sarim, particularly with the prices of lobster and swordfish. Another type of merchanting is called vial hopping. It consists of buying out the stock of Herblore potion vials in a particular shop then switching worlds and repeating the process.

label: Worm
title: Worm
lead:
Worm may refer to:

* Wyrm - the Slayer monsters found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon
* Worms - one of the foods used in Barbarian Assault to lure Penance Runners onto runner traps
* King worms - an ingredient used in gnome cooking
* Cave worms - bait obtained and used within the Chambers of Xeric
* Sandworms - bait used to catch raw anglerfish at Port Piscarilius
* Diabolic worms - bait used to catch raw anglerfish at an increased rate
* Red vine worm - a quest item used in Fishing Contest to catch the raw giant carp
* Worm (unobtainable item) - an interface item seen when talking to a gnome child

label: Worm (unobtainable item)
title: Worm (unobtainable item)
lead: A Worm is an unobtainable item seen when conversing with a Gnome child. When talking to a gnome child, they have a chance of offering you a snack, which displays a picture of this item in the chatbox. Although the "Worm" item is shown, King worms are obtained instead.

label: Worm batta
title: Worm batta
lead:
A worm batta is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 12 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade w'm battas are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 120 coins, with 3 in stock. They are also dropped by tortoises.

Members can make a worm batta via gnome cooking with 27 Cooking, yielding 154 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Worm crunchies
title: Worm crunchies
lead:
Worm crunchies are a food that players consume in one bite, healing 8 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade w'm crun' are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 85 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make worm crunchies via gnome cooking with 14 Cooking, yielding 104 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Worm hole
title: Worm hole
lead:
A worm hole is a food that players consume in one bite, healing 12 hitpoints. Players may need to make one as part of Training part I for the Gnome Restaurant minigame. Premade worm holes are sold by gnome waiters in the north-west corner of the of the Grand Tree for 150 coins, with 3 in stock.

Members can make a worm hole via gnome cooking with 30 Cooking, yielding 170 experience. Like all gnome foods, they stop burning at Cooking level 38.

label: Wormbrain
title: Wormbrain
lead: Wormbrain is a goblin in Port Sarim jail that the player must barter with, paying coins, or attack for Lozar's map part of the Crandor map during the Dragon Slayer I quest. Lowering his Hitpoints to 0 causes him to say, "Ow!", and drop the map part, which Telekinetic Grab must be used on to acquire.

label: Worn Equipment
title: Worn Equipment
lead: The Worn Equipment tab, also called the equipped tab, the worn items screen, or the equipped inventory, shows all the equipment that the player is wearing or wielding. The equipped inventory is divided into 11 slots for each area of the body that some piece of equipment can be worn on. Since the 11 slots can each be equipped with an item which then no longer appears in the backpack inventory, a player can effectively carry 39 items with them at once. The slots and what they can be equipped with are listed below.

label: Woven top
title: Woven top
lead:
Woven tops are sold in Keldagrim at Vermundi's Clothes Stall (brown) and Agmundi Quality Clothes (yellow and blue). They can also be bought at the Miscellanian Clothes Shop in Miscellania, although this requires partial completion of Royal Trouble. They are purely for decoration.

The clothes are specifically made for dwarves but Agmundi does sell the clothes to the few humans who come past her shop in Keldagrim. The woven tops are made by Agmundi's sister, Vermundi.

label: Wrapped oomlie
title: Wrapped oomlie
lead:
Wrapped oomlies are uncooked food made from the raw oomlie and a palm leaf. If cooked, it creates a cooked oomlie wrap.

Wrapped oomlies can be cooked with a Cooking level of 50 or higher, granting 30 Cooking experience.

label: Wrath (disambiguation)
title: Wrath (disambiguation)
lead: Wrath may refer to:

label: Wrathmaw
title: Wrathmaw
lead:
Wrathmaw was a proposed PVP world boss announced at the Summer Summit 2024. It was originally part of a Game Jam project by Mod Soffan.

A poll was released during the Summer Summit regarding Wrathmaw. If passed, the rewards would have been discussed on a further date.

label: Wrought iron key
title: Wrought iron key
lead:
The Wrought iron key is a reward from the Tourist Trap quest. It opens a door deep inside the Desert mining camp and allows passage to a special mining area inside. If you lose it, it can be replaced by searching one of the tables in the building located inside the Desert Mining Camp.

This key allows access to the north-western most tunnel (after riding the cart underground) that has several higher rocks for mining including adamantite ore and mithril ore bearing rocks.

label: Wushanko Isles
title: Wushanko Isles
lead: The Wushanko Isles (also known as the Eastern Lands) are an archipelago in the far east of Gielinor, across the Eastern Ocean from Morytania and the Kharidian Desert. They are currently inaccessible.

label: Wydin
title: Wydin
lead:
Wydin is the owner of Food Store in Port Sarim. He sells a variety of fresh food. Wydin also plays a small part in the Pirate's Treasure quest; players must retrieve smuggled rum from a crate in his storeroom. To enter the storeroom players must be both an employee of Wydin's store, and wearing a white apron. There is an apron located in the storeroom, but it cannot be telegrabbed as there is a solid wall in the way. However, there is also an apron hanging in the nearby Gerrant's Fishy Business directly north.

It is suggested that Wydin lives in the store, as there is a bed on the , above the .

label: Wyrmscraig
title: Wyrmscraig
lead: Wyrmscraig is an upcoming island located in the south-western sea of Gielinor. Designed as part of the Sailing skill expansion, it was the winning entry of the "Sailing Player-Designed Island" competition held in early 2026. The island is characterised by its unique basalt column geography and its ties to the Icyene race.

label: Wyson the gardener
title: Wyson the gardener
lead:
Wyson the gardener is a gardener in the Falador Park. You can buy woad leaves from him, which you can give to Aggie in Draynor Village to make blue dye.

Wyson will send players off to kill the Giant Mole underneath the park. He will take players' mole skins and mole claws in exchange for bird nests which may contain seeds or jewellery, with a higher chance of containing high-level allotment and herb seeds than other nests. Players will receive nest boxes when exchanging noted mole parts.

label: Wyvern
title: Wyvern
lead: Wyvern may refer to:

label: Xazyd Wier
title: Xazyd Wier
lead:
Xazyd Wier was a Zarosian warlock, who resided somewhere around Kharyrll in the early Third Age. He managed to flee, when Kharyrll was overrun by Zamorakians. Wier fled into the forests to the south and managed to find shelter by a hollow tree near the ruins of Flamtaer. He however found himself stuck in the tree, and whilst stuck he began to have mysterious dreams and visions of both past and future events. Whilst dreaming he saw Otrava, a Zamorakian healer and potioneer, who apparently received much inspiration from Wier in his tree form. He also saw the vampyres' invasion of Hallowvale, fighting against the icyene. It is also hinted that he saw both the six Barrows brothers crusading into Morytania, and the Seven Priestly Warriors fighting against the vampyric forces during the Fourth Age.

Eventually Wier was able to escape the hollow tree, and he wrote down his dreams and visions in the Tree wizards' journal. It is however unknown what happened to Wier, with his journal being found in the Shade Catacombs not far away from the tree he was stuck in.

label: Xeric
title: Xeric
lead:
, depicting an ancient Xerician priest. The examine text implies that it is possibly a statue of Xeric himself.]]

Xeric, formerly known as King Shayzien VII, is a powerful mage who once ruled Great Kourend nearly 1,030 years ago. He was responsible for the Age of Strife and is the creator of the lizardmen, who honour him as a great king. In the present day, he is Veos' Client, having possessed the treasure hunter Veos' body when Veos put on the amulet found inside the ancient casket dug up during the X Marks the Spot quest.

label: Xeric's (disambiguation)
title: Xeric's (disambiguation)
lead: Xeric's may refer to:

label: Xeric's cape
title: Xeric's cape
lead:
Xeric's capes or Xerician capes are a set of capes received by completing certain amounts of the Chambers of Xeric:
* – 100 raids
* – 500 raids
* – 1000 raids
* – 1500 raids
* – 2000 raids

label: Xerician (attribute)
title: Xerician (attribute)
lead: Xerician is an attribute assigned to monsters that reside within the Chambers of Xeric.

label: Xerician robes
title: Xerician robes
lead:
Xerician robes (known as Xerician armour in game) is a set of magic robes obtainable by crafting Xerician fabric, which are dropped by lizardmen. 12 fabrics and level 22 in Crafting are required to craft a full set, in addition to a needle and thread or a costume needle.

In order to equip Xerician robes, players require a Magic level of 20 and a Defence level of 10. Due to their low price and comparatively high Magic bonuses, Xerician robes are often used in Wilderness Player killing.

label: Xerna
title: Xerna
lead:
Xerna, the Mother of Wisdom was a legendary hero in Varlamorian history. Currently, not much else is known about her, except that she married Quoatlos. Her diadem was recently stolen from the Grand Museum, though an adventurer helped track it down and brought it back safely.

Two statues of Xerna are found at the Church of Ralos location south of the Stonecutter Outpost. Another statue of Xerna is found outside this church at the south-east corner of the continent, facing south-east.

label: Ximoua
title: Ximoua
lead: The Ximoua is the continuous cycle of destruction and rebirth of the world in the Losanium religion. The cycle ends with an eclipse that would destroy the world, leaving only ash and embers, from which a new world will be born. In Losanium it is believed that when the eclipse occurs Ralos and Ranul will come together at the centre of the world, known as Mokhaiotl, and unite all life as one, restarting the cycle. This knowledge is seen as a gift, passed down from the Old Ones. However, the Twilight Emissaries interpret this knowledge differently, they do not believe in Ximoua (destruction and rebirth) they believe in Tsak Tauli (Final Dawn). They only believe the world will end and that it is their duty to make that happen.

label: Yak-hide armour
title: Yak-hide armour
lead:
Yak-hide armour is a type of members only armour requiring 20 Defence to wear. It can be crafted from tanned yak hide or bought from other players. 3 Tanned yak hide are required to craft a full set.

The raw materials are dropped by yaks on the Fremennik Isles. Once a yak hide has been obtained, the player can take it to Thakkrad Sigmundson, who will tan them for a price. Three hides are required for the full set.

label: Yama/Strategies
title: Yama/Strategies
lead:
After the completion of A Kingdom Divided, players can fight Yama once they speak to him in person. In order to challenge Yama, players must first speak to the Voice of Yama at the bottom of the Chasm of Fire to reach Yama's Domain, then agree to sign a contract to face him in an inhibited form.

Yama can be fought solo or with another player. His stats are not affected by group size, but some mechanics can be made easier and the fight will progress much faster with another player.

label: Yanille
title: Yanille
lead: Yanille (pronounced "ya-NEEL") is a members-only city south of Ardougne, known for hosting Wizards' Guild. Due to the threat of ogres from nearby Gu'Tanoth, the city is surrounded by tall walls, and is heavily patrolled by guards.

label: Yanille Agility Dungeon
title: Yanille Agility Dungeon
lead:
The Yanille Agility Dungeon (also known as Yanille Dungeon) is the dungeon under the town of Yanille. Part of the dungeon can be entered by players with any Agility level, while other parts have minimum Agility requirements.

The experience rewards for using this dungeon are not as good as most other Agility courses, so players rarely come here to train Agility. Instead, players use it to train combat skills using the monsters there and gather their drops. Players training Herblore also use the dungeon, since many monsters here sometimes drop high-level herbs. Torstol, a fairly rare herb, can be obtained here.

label: Yanille bank
title: Yanille bank
lead: The Yanille bank is the only bank in the city of Yanille. There is a Deadman chest in the bank.

label: Yanille Chain
title: Yanille Chain
lead:
The Yanille Chain is a series of islands to the east of Yanille where Hazelmere the gnome lives. His house is on the southern end of the easternmost island in this small chain. The gnome can be found on the top floor of his house.

There are several Jungle spiders that reside in the small chain.

label: Yanni Salika
title: Yanni Salika
lead:
Yanni Salika owns the antique store in Shilo Village, and is also the starting point for the One Small Favour quest. He is located north of the river. Yanni will buy many non-tradeable items that are made or gathered during quests, but are of no use after the quest has been completed.

After the completion of Shilo Village, he will buy the Tattered scroll, Crumpled scroll, Bervirius notes, Bone key, Stone-plaque, Locating crystal, and Beads of the dead. After the completion of Zogre Flesh Eaters, he will buy the Black prism.

label: Yarasa
title: Yarasa
lead:
, the last of the Yarasa.]]
The Yarasa are a species of bat-like creatures native to Vampyrium. Visually impaired but with heightened senses of smell and sound, they were powerful predators competing with the vampyres for food. When the god Zaros arrived on Vampyrium, he taught the vampyres of society and culture. The establishment, understanding and unity of a society along with their superior numbers allowed the vampyres to kill the Yarasa with ease. While some managed to escape the initial slaughter, they too were eventually killed by the vampyres.

The only survivor of the race was Xarpus, also known as the Yarasa King, who was the most powerful and dangerous of his kind. Xarpus roamed the forests for millenia until he was caught by Lowerniel Drakan, who had returned to Vampyrium. Drakan captured Xarpus and brought him to Gielinor, where he handed him over to Verzik Vitur to be used as a beast in the Theatre of Blood.

label: Yard
title: Yard
lead:
Yard may refer to:

*Bone Yard
*Lumber Yard
*Ship Yard

label: Ye olde Tea Shoppe.
title: Ye olde Tea Shoppe.
lead:
Ye olde Tea Shoppe is a Tea stall located in south-eastern Varrock, next to the city wall. The shop is owned by the tea seller. The player can either buy tea from the shop or steal it with a Thieving level of 5, granting 16 experience. It takes roughly four seconds for the stall to reset and one second to steal. Without the need to empty one's inventory, one could gain up to 11,520 Thieving experience per hour, but as it takes about 20 seconds to run to bank and return, the maximum experience per hour is around 10,000.

There is a cup of tea on the bench nearby, but it cannot be taken because it is apparently just for display.

label: Years
title: Years
lead: Years may refer to:

label: Yellow
title: Yellow
lead:
Yellow may refer to:

*Gold, a yellow-orange colour.
*Yellow armour

label: Yellow armour
title: Yellow armour
lead:
Yellow armour may refer to:

* Gilded equipment
* Gold-trimmed armour
* Gold mystic set
* Yellow robes

label: Yellow bead
title: Yellow bead
lead:
The Yellow bead is a bead used in the Imp Catcher quest. It is returned to Wizard Mizgog in the Wizards' Tower along with a black bead, a white bead and a red bead to finish the quest. It can be obtained by killing imps.

The bead can also be used to bait traps when hunting imps.

label: Yellow boots
title: Yellow boots
lead:
Yellow boots can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The boots come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. They give the same stats as leather boots.

Unlike leather boots, these cannot be crafted. Because of their stats, they are mostly worn for cosmetic purposes.

label: Yellow cape
title: Yellow cape
lead: A yellow cape can be made by using yellow dye on another coloured cape and can be purchased from Barkers' Haberdashery in Canifis, Fancy Clothes Store in the Varrock, or Shayzien Styles in Shayzien.

label: Yellow crystal
title: Yellow crystal
lead:
Yellow crystal may refer to:

*Yellow crystal (Mourning's End Part II)
*Yellow crystal (Song of the Elves)
*Yellow crystal (Watchtower)

label: Yellow door
title: Yellow door
lead: The Yellow doors are located on the of Melzar's Maze. They must be opened during Dragon Slayer I, using a yellow key obtained from killing the nearby Skeleton with a round shield.

label: Yellow dye
title: Yellow dye
lead: Yellow dye is a dye that can be created by taking 2 onions and 5 coins to Aggie in Draynor Village, or 2 onions and 25 coins if taken to Ali the dyer in Pollnivneach. It can also be bought in Lletya from Oronwen for 6 coins. It can also be found in the farmhouse featured in Getting Ahead, south of the Farming Guild, located in the shelves next to the stairs in the house. Yellow dye can be combined with red dye to create orange dye, and with blue dye to create green dye. It can be used to dye normal capes yellow.

label: Yellow flowers
title: Yellow flowers
lead:
Yellow flowers are a type of flower that can be harvested after planting mithril or adamant seeds.

When planting the seeds, players have an option to either pick the flowers (and obtaining a random coloured flower) or leave them planted on the ground. A player only has one chance to pick their flowers; if they refuse to do so, they will not get the option again unless they plant another seed. Flowers that are left on the ground will stay there temporarily for around 5 minutes.

label: Yellow gloves
title: Yellow gloves
lead:
Yellow gloves can be purchased in Canifis from Barker at his store, Barker's Haberdashery, and are also dropped by Crawling Hands. The gloves come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple. These gloves are often worn to match certain armour sets, such as gold-trimmed and god armour sets.

Their defence bonus is equal to that of leather gloves.

label: Yellow hat
title: Yellow hat
lead: Yellow hats can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The hats come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Yellow partyhat
title: Yellow partyhat
lead:
Yellow partyhats are tradeable cosmetic items obtained by completing one of the Christmas holiday events that occur once per year.

Previously, they were obtainable during the 2013 Rare Drops event (from 4 July to 14 July) as part of a rare item drop.

label: Yellow robe bottoms
title: Yellow robe bottoms
lead: Yellow robe bottoms can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe bottoms come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Yellow robe top
title: Yellow robe top
lead: Yellow robe tops can be purchased in Canifis from Barker in his store, Barkers' Haberdashery. The robe tops come in five different colours: grey, red, yellow, teal, and purple.

label: Yellow Sheep
title: Yellow Sheep
lead:
Yellow Sheep are sick sheep found near the East Ardougne north bank that must be prodded with the cattleprod to the sheep pen and fed the poisoned sheep feed during the Sheep Herder quest. Its wool is slightly yellow. Once killed, it drops the sheep bones (4).

After Mourning's End Part I, the sheep are of a darker yellow as a result of the player dyeing them with a Fixed device loaded with a Yellow toad. Once dyed, they can no longer be prodded or interacted with in any way. Luckily, players only need to dye one and all the sheep of the same colour turn dark. This is how players can tell they haven't missed the sheep during the quest.

label: Yes
title: Yes
lead:
Yes is the first listed emote. Upon use the player nods their head up and down.

This emote is already unlocked upon making an account.

label: Yesteryear
title: Yesteryear
lead:
Yesteryear is a music track that is unlocked when the player first arrives in Lumbridge. It can also be heard around the Lumbridge Swamp and farmlands. In this area, the music player will also shuffle between playing Autumn Voyage, Book of Spells, Dream, Flute Salad, and Harmony.

In Classic mode, the track plays in the eastern part of Lumbridge swamp.

label: Yeti
title: Yeti
lead:
The Yeti was a Runescape 2 beta monster that would have been found in the ice lands, as a Behind the Scenes article from March 2004 promised that one of the upcoming updates would be "A large 'frozen lands' area including penguins, mammoths, polar bears and more."

For unknown reasons the Yeti was never released, but its model was reused for King Vargas, who is revealed to have been transformed into a Yeti.

label: Yew (disambiguation)
title: Yew (disambiguation)
lead:
Yew can refer to any of the following:

* Yew tree
** Yew tree (Farming)
* Yew logs
* Yew shortbow
* Yew longbow
* Yew shield
* Yew stock
* Yew seed
* Yew bird house

label: Yew bow
title: Yew bow
lead:
Yew bow may refer to:
*Yew comp bow
*Yew longbow or unstrung counterpart
*Yew shortbow or unstrung counterpart

label: yew logs
title: yew logs
lead:
Yew logs are logs obtained from cutting yew trees, which require at least level 60 Woodcutting for players to cut. They give 175 experience when cut with an axe. Players can burn these logs with the Firemaking skill at level 60, granting 202.5 Firemaking experience.

Yew logs can also be made into bows, stock, and arrow shafts using the Fletching skill. When the log is cut into a yew longbow (u) at level 70, it yields 75 experience. Cutting a yew shortbow (u) at level 65 will give 67.5 experience. Stringing the unstrung bows will give the same experience as for cutting them.

label: yew longbow
title: yew longbow
lead:
The yew longbow is a longbow stronger than the maple longbow that can use arrows up to rune. The yew longbow requires a Ranged level of 40 or higher to wield.

Players can make a yew longbow through the Fletching skill at level 70. First, a player must cut a yew longbow (u) from yew logs, giving 75 Fletching experience. The unstrung bow is then strung with a bow string, for an additional 75 experience for a total of 150 experience a log. It can also be obtained as a very rare drop from a young impling.

label: Yew longbow (u)
title: Yew longbow (u)
lead: A yew longbow (u) is made using a knife with yew logs, requiring 70 Fletching and yielding 75 Fletching experience. Stringing a yew longbow (u) with a bowstring makes a yew longbow, also requiring 70 Fletching and yielding an additional 75 Fletching experience.

label: yew shortbow
title: yew shortbow
lead:
A yew shortbow is a two-handed ranged weapon stronger than the maple shortbow but weaker than the magic shortbow. It can be made with a Fletching level of 65 by using a yew shortbow (u) on some bow string, granting 67.5 experience when made, or 135 total experience when making one from scratch.

Fletching a yew shortbow from yew logs and a bow string will profit while fletching a yew shortbow from a yew shortbow (u) and a bow string will profit .

label: Yew shortbow (u)
title: Yew shortbow (u)
lead: A yew shortbow (u) is made using a knife with yew logs, requiring 65 Fletching and yielding 67.5 Fletching experience. Stringing a yew shortbow (u) with a bowstring makes a yew shortbow, also requiring 65 Fletching and yielding an additional 67.5 Fletching experience.

label: Yew tree
title: Yew tree
lead: A yew tree is a high level lumber tree requiring level 60 Woodcutting to chop, providing 175 experience per set of yew logs received. They are mostly used for Woodcutting to gather yew logs used in Fletching or Firemaking, but also play a role in Farming. Due to the use of yew logs for fletching yew longbows, which are commonly used with the High Alchemy spell, yew logs are extremely popular and constantly in demand. Cutting yew logs is a common moneymaker for free-to-play.

label: Yew tree (interface item)
title: Yew tree (interface item)
lead:
The Yew tree is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Yew tree.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Yohnus
title: Yohnus
lead:
Yohnus owns the blacksmith in Shilo Village. Inside of his blacksmith contains the closest furnace to a bank in the entire game, which requires 20 coins per smelt to use, unless the player has completed the Karamja Elite Diary.

After completion of the Karamja Elite Diary, money can no longer be deposited into his coffer, only withdrawn.

label: Yommi totem
title: Yommi totem
lead:
The yommi totem is a quest item used during the Legends' Quest to replace the evil totem in the centre of the Kharazi Jungle. It may be cut from a yommi tree, grown from yommi tree seeds in the fertile soil just north-west of the pool of pure water.

Players must be quick in producing the yommi totem in order to prevent the tree from rotting. If the tree does rot, players may ask Ungadulu for more seeds to restart the production process.

label: Yommi tree
title: Yommi tree
lead:
The Yommi tree is a tree grown during Legends' Quest in the Kharazi Jungle. It is grown from Yommi tree seeds and then chopped down and carved to create the Yommi totem.

The tree progresses through 3 growth stages. The tree starts out as a baby, then grows to a sapling, and finally an adult. Once grown, it can be felled, then trimmed, and finally carved into a liftable totem. The tree may also die or become rotten if it is not quickly carved and "lifted-up" (picked-up).

label: Yommi tree seeds
title: Yommi tree seeds
lead:
Yommi tree seeds are a quest item used during the Legends' Quest. They are given to the player by Ungadulu after freeing him. The seeds must first be germinated in holy water before they can be grown into a Yommi tree, and to do this the player must perform a number of tasks in an underground dungeon.

It is possible to be unsuccessful when planting the seed, prompting the following message: "You planted the seed incorrectly in the fertile soil". The chance of this happening is dependent on the player's Herblore level. . Once the tree has grown the player can cut a Yommi totem from it. Three seeds are obtained from Ungadulu at a time. If the seeds are lost or planted incorrectly, one can ask Ungadulu for three more. The seeds require level 45 Herblore to plant. The tree grows at an amazing rate, but can be cut only with a rune axe, and must be cut quickly so as to prevent it from getting rotten.

label: Yonrith Lovakengj
title: Yonrith Lovakengj
lead:
Yonrith Lovakengj was a dwarf who lived during the Third Age. He was leader of an army allied with Saradomin and fought against the Zarosians at Lassar during the God Wars. Yonrith fled to the west with his closest allies, but was pursued by the Carnifex Maximus Vardorvis. Vardorvis claimed that he was an enemy of the Empty Lord, but one of his subordinates believed it was due to damaged pride, as Yonrith was somehow able to escape his axe. Vardorvis and his forces set up camp in The Stranglewood, but ended up getting infected by The Strangler after investigating the ritual site. This helped to allow Yonrith and his forces to wipe out their camp, and even beheading Vardorvis himself. Yonrith later went on to found the city of Lovakengj.

Lady Lovakengj, in issue 23 of the Postbag from the Hedge, confirms that Yonrith founded Lovakengj, and also noted that he was a great military commander, though not a great smith.

label: Yorah
title: Yorah
lead: Yorah is a Kualti in-training mentioned only in the story A Kingdom United. While guarding Queen Zyanyi Arkan in the Grand Museum on the day they were to be officially inducted as a member of the Kualti, Yorah spotted a figure wearing a "bone-white cloak", believing it to be a thief intending on stealing one of the Kualti's daggers on display in the museum. Yorah pursued the figure deeper into the museum, eventually cornering it in a room with no other exits. Upon searching the room, Yorah found nothing; they noted the figure's hiding skills were inhuman. They brushed off the figure as being a figment of their imagination and left the museum to attend their initiation ceremony.

label: You Are Dead!
title: You Are Dead!
lead: You Are Dead! is a Jingle that plays when the player dies.

label: You Are Victorious! (Emir's Arena)
title: You Are Victorious! (Emir's Arena)
lead: You Are Victorious! (Emir's Arena) is a Jingle that plays when winning a match in the Emir's Arena.

label: Your Feedback updates
title: Your Feedback updates
lead: Your Feedback updates are updates related to feedback from the Old School RuneScape community, including newsposts and dev blogs.

label: Yurkolgokh
title: Yurkolgokh
lead:
The Yurkolgokh are a goblin tribe found while doing the Land of the Goblins quest, who wear yellow goblin mail. Like the other tribes found in the temple, they were called upon by the god Bandos to fight in his name during the God Wars.

Their name, in the ancient goblin tongue, translates to "The Flatulent".

label: Zadimus corpse
title: Zadimus corpse
lead:
The Zadimus corpse is a quest item that is obtained during the Shilo Village quest by searching an ancient gallows in the temple of Ah Za Rhoon. The corpse must be given to Trufitus in Tai Bwo Wannai village. Afterward, it must be buried next to the Tribal Statue in the middle of Tai Bwo Wannai. The Spirit of Zadimus then appears and gives the player the key to Rashiliyia's tomb.

Though it cannot be dropped, the Zadimus corpse can be lost upon death or alchemised using Magic (albeit for 0 coins). Simply search the gallows again to reclaim it.

label: Zaff
title: Zaff
lead:
Zaff is a salesman who owns Zaff's Superior Staves in the city of Varrock. He is located in his shop just north-west of Varrock centre. His shop is often visited because it is one of the few places that sells battlestaves, the other being Baba Yaga on Lunar Isle. He is also involved in the What Lies Below quest. During the quest, players can summon him by using a beacon ring and Zaff's instructions.

Zaff is secretly a member of the Varrock Palace Secret Guard (likely accounting for his shop's proximity to it), known to Rat Burgiss, and it appears his proficiency at magic is far higher than many would presume, as it was he who possessed the Beacon and used a spell to counter Surok's mind control spell, disabling Surok's teleportation magic and imprisoning him in the library.

label: Zaff's Superior Staffs!
title: Zaff's Superior Staffs!
lead: Zaff's Superior Staffs is a staff shop located near central Varrock, owned by Zaff. It is the main source of battlestaves and of elemental staves for free players.

label: Zahwa
title: Zahwa
lead:
Zahwa is an injured fighter at the Emir's Arena. He has tattered brown clothes and has several injuries, such as cut shins, some sort of eye injury, and outgrown, unkempt hair.

He, along with several other NPCs at the Emir's Arena, serves no distinct purpose other than to represent wounded fighters after participating in several battles.

label: Zamorak
title: Zamorak
lead: Zamorak (Jagex pronunciation: ZAM-or-ack), is the god of chaos, power, and destruction, as well as personal ambitions and change. He is one of the three major gods of Gielinor, alongside Saradomin and Guthix. Originating from the hazardous plane of Freneskae, he climbed through the ranks of the Zarosian Empire to become its highest-ranking general, before ascending into godhood himself after usurping Zaros - a historic event that ended the Second Age and ushered in the God Wars. Throughout the Third Age, he and the other gods that remained battled over Gielinor, until Guthix woke from his slumber and banished the gods with the Edicts of Guthix.

label: Zamorak (disambiguation)
title: Zamorak (disambiguation)
lead:
Zamorak may refer to:
*Zamorak
*Monk of Zamorak
*Mage of Zamorak (Ourania)
*Zamorak crafter
*Zamorak mage
*Zamorak ranger
*Zamorak warrior
*Zamorak wizard

label: Zamorak armour
title: Zamorak armour
lead:
The Zamorak armour set is a set of melee armour affiliated to the god Zamorak. Pieces of the armour provide identical attack and defence stats as Rune armour, except for the kiteshield's ranged attack bonus being -2 (rather than -3), as well as each item having a +1 prayer bonus. Therefore, they require 40 Defence to be worn.

Each piece of the Zamorak armour set can be obtained by completing Hard Treasure Trails, and cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

label: Zamorak blessed dragonhide armour
title: Zamorak blessed dragonhide armour
lead:
The Zamorak blessed d'hide armour is a set of Ranged armour said to be blessed by Zamorak. Every piece requires 70 Ranged and 40 Defence, except for the blessed chaps and blessed bracers, which do not have the Defence requirement. Blessed dragonhide has better defensive stats and the same offensive stats as the corresponding black dragonhide armour with an additional +1 Prayer bonus. Unlike normal dragonhide armour, a coif and boots are also available. Each piece of armour may be obtained as a reward from hard Treasure Trails.

Wearing any piece of Zamorak blessed d'hide armour will make the Zamorak followers unaggressive within the God Wars Dungeon and the Wilderness God Wars Dungeon.

label: Zamorak brew
title: Zamorak brew
lead:
A Zamorak brew is a potion made by using jangerberries on a torstol potion (unf), requiring 78 Herblore, yielding a Zamorak brew(3) and 175 Herblore experience. A dose of Zamorak brew provides a temporary skill boost to Attack equal to 2 + 20% of the player's base Attack level, rounded down, and Strength equal to 2 + 12% of the player's base Strength level, rounded down. It temporarily lowers Defence equal to 2 + 10% of the player's current Defence level, rounded down, and current Hitpoints by 12%, rounded down, though it will not lower a player's Hitpoints below the minimum of 1. Additionally, 10% of the player's current Prayer level is restored as Prayer points. When used in conjunction with a Saradomin brew, Attack and Defence will be boosted, Prayer and Health will be restored (possibly boosted by the brew), Ranged and Magic will be lowered.

Restore potions are frequently used with Zamorak brews to raise lowered Defence. A super strength potion will always boost Strength level higher than a Zamorak brew; however, the Zamorak brew's Attack boost is slightly better than a super attack potion. At levels 85, 86, 90-93, and 95-99, the Zamorak brew will give a boost of 2 levels more than a Super attack potion. You can also use a super strength potion or a dragon battleaxe special attack before you sip a dose to increase your Strength level to the max.

label: Zamorak cape
title: Zamorak cape
lead:
The Zamorak cape is a reward from Mage Arena I miniquest. To receive the cape, the player must defeat Kolodion in his four guises, then speak to him, step through the nearby sparkling pool, and finally pray at the Statue of Zamorak. Upon praying at the statue, the Zamorak cape will appear next to the player and can be picked up.

The Zamorak cape and the Zamorak staff are required to benefit from the Charge spell, which enables the player to hit up to 50% more damage with the Flames of Zamorak spell.

label: Zamorak cloak (disambiguation)
title: Zamorak cloak (disambiguation)
lead:
Zamorak cloak may refer to the following:

* Zamorak cloak - Part of the Zamorak vestment set
* Castlewars cloak (Zamorak) - Bought from Lanthus at the Castle Wars minigame for 10 Castle wars tickets
* Zamorak cloak (Castle Wars) - Worn in the Castle Wars minigame to indicate a player's team

label: Zamorak full helm
title: Zamorak full helm
lead:
Zamorak full helm is a decorated rune full helm that is affiliated with the god Zamorak. Sharing the same stats as the rune full helm except for a prayer bonus, the Zamorak full helm also looks visually similar. Its appearance differs in that the helm features an ornamental red plume instead of the typical purple plume.

The full helm requires 40 Defence to wear and cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

label: Zamorak kiteshield
title: Zamorak kiteshield
lead:
The Zamorak kiteshield is a decorated rune kiteshield that is affiliated with the god Zamorak. Sharing the same stats as the rune kiteshield except for the ranged attack bonus and prayer bonus, the Zamorak kiteshield also looks visually similar. Its appearance differs in that the shield features an ornamental red trim.

The shield requires 40 Defence to wear and cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

label: Zamorak mage (disambiguation)
title: Zamorak mage (disambiguation)
lead:
Zamorak mage may refer to:
*Battle mage
*Mage of Zamorak
*Mage of Zamorak (Ourania)
*Spiritual mage
*Zamorak mage
*Zamorak wizard

label: Zamorak monk bottom
title: Zamorak monk bottom
lead:
The Zamorak monk bottom is part of the Zamorak monk robes set. They are bright red, and like the related Zamorak monk top they are dropped by disciples of Iban and monks of Zamorak.

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the Wilderness due to providing decent Prayer and Magic bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab Wine of Zamorak at the Chaos Temple (Asgarnia) without being attacked.

label: Zamorak monk robes
title: Zamorak monk robes
lead:
Zamorak monk robes are a set of red robes available to free players. They provide Magic offence, Defence, and Prayer bonuses, with no other stat changes. Unlike the wizard robes which offer the best bonuses to Magic attack, and the plain monk's robes worn by Saradominist monks, which offer the best Prayer bonus in free-to-play, the Zamorak monk robes offer a balance between Magic attack and Prayer.

They were released in an update on 28 May 2002. Zamorak monk robes are dropped by disciples of Iban, Necromancer, monks of Zamorak, and Zamorak wizards. They are required to be worn in order to enter Iban's Temple in the quest Underground Pass, as well as the of the Asgarnia Chaos Temple.

label: Zamorak monk top
title: Zamorak monk top
lead:
The Zamorak monk top is part of the Zamorak monk robes set. They are bright red, and like the related Zamorak monk bottom they are dropped by disciples of Iban, necromancers and monks of Zamorak.

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the Wilderness due to providing decent Prayer and Magic bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab Wine of Zamorak at the Chaos Temple (Asgarnia) without being attacked.

label: Zamorak page
title: Zamorak page
lead: Zamorak pages are rewards from Treasure Trails. If a player has all four they can use them to make an Unholy book.

label: Zamorak platebody
title: Zamorak platebody
lead:
The Zamorak platebody is a trimmed rune platebody fashioned to the colours of Zamorak. It has the same stats as a normal rune platebody, but provides protection from followers of Zamorak in the God Wars Dungeons as well as a +1 prayer bonus. It requires 40 Defence and the completion of the Dragon Slayer I quest to wear.

It can only be obtained as a reward from hard Treasure Trails, and cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

label: Zamorak platelegs
title: Zamorak platelegs
lead:
Zamorak platelegs are a trimmed version of rune platelegs which are associated with the god Zamorak. Zamorak platelegs have the same stats as rune platelegs, apart from a Prayer bonus of 1. Like rune platelegs, these platelegs require 40 Defence to wear and cannot be made using the Smithing skill.

Players can obtain Zamorak platelegs as a reward from completing hard Treasure Trails. Wearing Zamorak platelegs in the God Wars Dungeon will cause followers of Zamorak to become unaggressive.

label: Zamorak robes
title: Zamorak robes
lead:
Zamorak robes may refer to:

*Zamorak monk robes
**Zamorak monk top
**Zamorak monk bottom
*Zamorak vestment set
*Elder chaos druid robes, which are visually similar to Zamorak monk robes.

label: Zamorak set
title: Zamorak set
lead:
Zamorak set may refer to:
* Zamorak dragonhide set
* Zamorak armour
** Zamorak armour set (sk)
** Zamorak armour set (lg)

label: Zamorak shield
title: Zamorak shield
lead:
Zamorak shield may refer to:
*Zamorak d'hide shield
*Zamorak kiteshield
*Zamorak heraldic kiteshields
**Adamant kiteshield (Zamorak)
**Rune kiteshield (Zamorak)
**Steel kiteshield (Zamorak)
*Unholy book

label: Zamorak staff
title: Zamorak staff
lead:
The Zamorak staff is a god staff aligned with Zamorak, obtainable after completing Mage Arena I miniquest by defeating Kolodion. Like the other God staves, this staff requires 60 Magic to acquire and wield.

After the miniquest, players pick a god to worship to receive a god cape and the god staff corresponding to that god. If a different god is chosen, the staff can be purchased from the chamber guardian for coins. This staff and corresponding runes are required to cast Flames of Zamorak from the standard spellbook.

label: Zamorak symbol (interface item)
title: Zamorak symbol (interface item)
lead:
The Zamorak symbol is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Zamorak symbol.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Zamorak vestment set
title: Zamorak vestment set
lead: The Zamorak vestment set is a members item set of Prayer armour aligned with Zamorak. It is only obtainable by completing easy, medium, and hard Treasure Trails.

label: Zamorak wizard
title: Zamorak wizard
lead:
Zamorak wizards are hostile followers of Zamorak that appear when doing hard clue coordinates in the Wilderness.

Upon appearing, they will call out , immediately attacking the player with the Flames of Zamorak spell. Unlike their Saradomin wizard counterparts, they attack exclusively with Magic, do not deal poison and all damage can be negated with Protect from Magic. They are also generally weaker, having low Hitpoints and low Defence (except against Magic).

label: Zamorakian Chapel
title: Zamorakian Chapel
lead:
The Zamorakian Chapel, referred to in-game as the evil temple, is a small temple found in the south-east part of Varrock. The temple is run by the Mage of Zamorak, a member of the ZMI who helps other Zamorakians in hiding. In addition to the chaos altar, there is also an altar slab found in the northern section of the temple.

The temple has no official name in-game, but is referred to as "evil temple" in dialogue with Elsie. The name "Zamorakian Chapel" comes from an update post on 15 June 2022.

label: Zanaris
title: Zanaris
lead:
Zanaris, also known as the Lost City, is the home of the fairies and is the moon of Gielinor. Accessed during the Lost City quest, the settlement is notable for bearing several amenities, such as a marketplace to buy a dragon longsword, and the highly useful fairy ring transportation system.

The entrance to Zanaris is located in the shed in Lumbridge Swamp.

label: Zanaris bank
title: Zanaris bank
lead:
The Zanaris bank is a bank in the fairy city of Zanaris, found in the north-west corner of the city. The Zanaris bank was released to members only alongside the bank in Catherby. There are no bank booths; instead, five chests and four bankers inhabit the area.

Interestingly, the two tiles to the east of the deposit box cannot be walked on; players who click on them will have their character take a step to the south immediately after.

label: Zanaris General Store
title: Zanaris General Store
lead:
The Zanaris General Store is run by the fairy shop keeper and her assistant, both denizens of Zanaris.

The fairy shop keeper sells the usual general store items, including Newcomer maps.

label: Zanaris windmill
title: Zanaris windmill
lead:
The Zanaris windmill is a windmill located in Zanaris, east of the bank. The windmill can be used to grind grain into flour. Unlike most wind-powered mills, the Zanaris mill is powered by a cow on an oversized hamster wheel. There is a wheat field located south-east of the windmill.

On the of the mill there is a flour bin into which all the milled flour is poured. On the there is the hopper into which grain is put and the hopper controls which control the flow of the grain from the hopper to the millstones. To mill flour, a player will need grain and an empty pot to collect the flour.

label: Zaros
title: Zaros
lead:
Zaros is the divine aspect of darkness, an ancient and today mostly-forgotten god of Gielinor. During the Second Age, Zaros reigned over a vast empire, which covered at least what is today Misthalin, Asgarnia, the Wilderness (formerly Forinthry), and the northern parts of Morytania. Among his followers were the demons, vampyres, Mahjarrat, dragon riders, and some humans. At the time, Zaros was by a significant margin the most powerful of all of the gods, except for Guthix. The golden age of Zaros came to an end when he was betrayed by one of his generals, the Mahjarrat Zamorak. This event also marked the end of the Second Age and ignited the God Wars.

Zaros is mostly forgotten in today's Gielinor, and almost all knowledge about him has been lost. The few who know about him still fear him immensely, with many refusing to even speak his name out of fear for invoking his power. The handful of Zarosians still in existence are mostly in hiding, with some silently plotting the return of their master.

label: Zarosian Empire
title: Zarosian Empire
lead: The Zarosian Empire was a vast ancient empire that covered the territories of where Misthalin, Asgarnia, the Wilderness, and north-western Morytania now stand. Zaros founded the Empire expeditiously after his arrival on Gielinor. It was the predominant force during the Second Age and the beginning of the Third Age. The fall of the Empire was instigated when Zaros was betrayed by Zamorak, which banished Zaros from Gielinor. The God Wars ensued, in which the Empire was destroyed. Saradomin and Zamorak attempted to remove all traces of the Empire after its fall. Today, only its ruins remain as evidence of its existence. The Empire was ruled by the god Zaros himself, presumably from the capital city of Senntisten which was located east of Varrock where the Digsite can be found today. Recently, archaeological discoveries at the Digsite have ignited interest in Zarosian history and culture.

label: Zartharim
title: Zartharim
lead: Zartharim was a settlement from the Fourth Age and hometown of the hero Aivas. Nothing else is known about it, and it presumably no longer exists or goes by a different name. Zartharim is only named as part of the riddle on the tomb of Camorra.

label: Zaryte
title: Zaryte
lead:
Zaryte may refer to:

* Zaryte bow
* Zaryte crossbow
* Zaryte vambraces (beta)
* The Nihil race

label: Zealot (disambiguation)
title: Zealot (disambiguation)
lead:
Zealot refers to several NPCs and items, as well as a music track:

* Undead Zealot, a monster that have the chance to spawn when players open chests in the Shade Catacombs.
* Zealot, a music track unlocked at the Water Altar.
* Zealot, a follower of Saradomin who starts the quest Haunted Mine.
** Zealot's key, an item found by pickpocketing the Zealot
* Zealot's robes, a set of robes found in the Shade Catacombs that give a chance of saving bones and other remaining while training Prayer.
** Zealot's helm
** Zealot's robe top
** Zealot's robe bottom
** Zealot's boots

label: Zealot (music track)
title: Zealot (music track)
lead: Zealot is a music track that is unlocked at the Water Altar or Anglers' Retreat.

label: Zealot's robes
title: Zealot's robes
lead:
Zealot's robes are an untradeable set of robes obtained from looting gold chests within the Shade Catacombs, which require gold shade keys to open. The robes provide a 1.25% chance per piece to prevent various remains from being consumed whilst training Prayer – totalling 5% with the full set equipped. This bonus stacks multiplicatively with the bone-saving effect of the Chaos Temple altar , yielding a 52.5% chance to not consume a bone at that altar, meaning each bone can effectively be sacrificed on average 2.1 times.

Aside from affecting bones offered on an altar, they also affect burying bones, offering Ensouled heads, offering bonemeal at the Ectofuntus. They may also be used when sacrificing Blessed bone shards at the Libation bowl; this affects individual shards, rather than the set of 100 shards. The set does not save resources when casting Demonic Offering, Sinister Offering , or offering bones at the Sacred Bone Burner .

label: Zek
title: Zek
lead:
Zek may refer to:

*Ket-Zek, a level 360 monster found in the Fight Caves
*Jal-Zek, a level 490 monster found in the Inferno
*Ur-zek, a member of the Dorgeshuun council

label: Zeke
title: Zeke
lead:
Zeke is the owner of Zeke's Superior Scimitars in Al Kharid. He sells scimitars up to mithril.

If asked about dragon scimitars, Zeke will say "A dragon scimitar? A DRAGON scimitar? No way, man! The banana-brained nitwits who make them would never dream of selling any to me. Seriously, you'll be a monkey's uncle before you'll ever hold a dragon scimitar." This is a reference to the Monkey Madness I quest which must be completed to wield a dragon scimitar, and in which the player pretends to be the uncle of a Monkey Child. If the player has completed the quest, they will respond with "Hmmm, funny you should say that...".

label: Zeke's Superior Scimitars.
title: Zeke's Superior Scimitars.
lead: Zeke's Superior Scimitars is located in Al Kharid, just north-east of the bank. It is run by Zeke, and sells scimitars up to mithril.

label: Zembo
title: Zembo
lead: Zembo runs a bar and Karamja Wines, Spirits, and Beers, on Musa Point in Karamja. He is involved in the Pirate's Treasure quest, where he sells the player a bottle of Karamjan rum, which they have to smuggle off the island to Port Sarim.

label: Zen theme (interface item)
title: Zen theme (interface item)
lead:
The Zen theme is an interface item that can be seen in the Construction skill guide representing the Zen theme.

The actual item cannot be obtained by players.

label: Zenesha
title: Zenesha
lead: Zenesha is a platebody seller who resides in East Ardougne. Additionally, she is one of the several NPCs that appear in the Ratcatchers quest as a guest in the mansion.

label: Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop.
title: Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop.
lead:
Zenesha's Plate Mail Body Shop is a shop owned by Zenesha in East Ardougne. As the name suggests, it sells types of platebodies. These platebodies range from bronze to mithril.

This shop can be found in a building on the south-west side of the East Ardougne market square.

label: Zip line
title: Zip line
lead:
Zip line or zipline may refer to:

* Zip line (Al Kharid Rooftop Course), found within the Al Kharid Rooftop Course
* Zipline (Colossal Wyrm Agility Course), found within the Colossal Wyrm Agility Course
* Zip line (Werewolf Agility Course), found within the Werewolf Agility Course
* Zipline (Shayzien Agility Course), found within the Shayzien Advanced Agility Course
* Zip line (Fossil Island), level 74 Agility shortcut found attached to the House on the Hill

label: Zodiac symbols
title: Zodiac symbols
lead: Zodiac symbols are used somewhat rarely as decorative ground‑scatter. They are primarily used in places where magical‑looking incantations are likely to occur, in areas of wizardry and necromancy.

label: zombie
title: zombie
lead:
Zombies are generic monsters found throughout Gielinor, often located in cemeteries, sewers, and dungeons. They count as undead NPCs and are weak to the effects of both the Salve amulet and the Crumble Undead spell.

Most common zombies are low-leveled, hence serving as a decent training method for low-level players. Many locations have distinct zombie [[#Variants|variants]] that have different combat levels, drops, and appearances.

label: Zombie (disambiguation)
title: Zombie (disambiguation)
lead:
Zombie may refer to:
* Zombie, the common monster
* Zombie (Entrana Dungeon)
* Zombie (Kourend)
* Zombie (Melzar's Maze)
* Zombie (Sepulchre of Death)
* Zombie (Shayzien Crypts)
* Zombie (Tarn's Lair)
* Zombie (Temple Trekking)
* Zombie (Wilderness)
* Zombie (Zogre Flesh Eaters)

label: Zombie (Entrana Dungeon)
title: Zombie (Entrana Dungeon)
lead: Zombies can be found in the Entrana Dungeon, near the entrance. While visually similar to generic zombies, the ones in the Entrana Dungeon are the only zombies with a combat level of 25, and have a unique drop table as well.

label: Zombie (Melzar's Maze)
title: Zombie (Melzar's Maze)
lead:
Two zombies can be found in the basement of Melzar's Maze. They must be killed in order to obtain the blue key, which can unlock the blue door to progress through the maze.

According to Melzar's notes, the zombies were created as a result of attempting to grow flesh on the skeletons of Crandorian refugees so their bodies could hold a spirit, but this failed as the flesh immediately decayed.

label: Zombie (Wilderness)
title: Zombie (Wilderness)
lead:
Zombies are monsters found in the Wilderness at the Graveyard of Shadows and the Eastern Ruins. They have combat levels of 18 and 24 and are aggressive to players.

Both level 18 and 24 zombies in the Wilderness share the same drop table.

label: Zombie monkey greegree
title: Zombie monkey greegree
lead:
Zombie monkey greegree may refer to:
* Zombie monkey greegree (small)
* Zombie monkey greegree (big)

label: Zombie outfit
title: Zombie outfit
lead: The zombie outfit is a possible reward from the Gravedigger random event. It consists of the zombie mask, the zombie shirt, the zombie trousers, the zombie boots, and the zombie gloves. The set can be stored in a Costume box in a player-owned house.

label: Zombie pirate (disambiguation)
title: Zombie pirate (disambiguation)
lead:
Zombie pirate may refer to:
* Zombie pirates found at the Chaos Temple in the Wilderness
* Zombie pirate (Braindeath Island), encountered on Braindeath Island during the quest Rum Deal
* Zombie pirate (Harmony Island), encountered on Harmony Island during the quest The Great Brain Robbery
* Zombie pirate (NPC), a lone NPC at the shipwreck at the eastern coast of the Wilderness
* Zombie pirate (Sailing)

label: Zombie rat
title: Zombie rat
lead:
A zombie rat is a monster only found in Melzar's Maze. It comes in two sizes, but both have the same stats. It is quite similar to the giant rat except with a few cuts, gashes, and a washed-out colour. The small zombie rat with a long tail is the only variant that will drop the red key. Players may choose to equip a salve amulet for a combat bonus against this creature.

According to Melzar's notes, zombie rats are the result of Melzar's first experiments with necromancy in his efforts to resurrect the dead Crandorians that were slain by Elvarg.

label: Zombified thrall
title: Zombified thrall
lead:
Zombified thrall may refer to one of the following:

* Lesser zombified thrall
* Superior zombified thrall
* Greater zombified thrall

label: Zoo keeper
title: Zoo keeper
lead: Zoo keepers are employees who work at the Ardougne Zoo. They keep watch over the animals and clean up after them. Players can talk to a zoo keeper named Larry to start the Cold War quest and can also talk to a zoo keeper named Charlie to start the Eagles' Peak quest.

label: Zulrah/Strategies
title: Zulrah/Strategies
lead: Zulrah is a level 725 solo-only snake boss found at a shrine east of Zul-Andra, accessible by boat. Zulrah's shrine can be exited through victory, death, logout/hopping worlds, or teleportation.

label: Zuriel's equipment
title: Zuriel's equipment
lead: Zuriel's equipment is a part of the Ancient Warriors' equipment. Three versions of this equipment set exist: two can be earned by participating in the Bounty Hunter minigame, and can only be used within Daimon's Crater, Castle Wars, Clan Wars, Soul Wars, the TzHaar Fight Pit, and both the player-owned house and Clan Hall combat rings, while the third set is exclusive to Deadman Mode.

label: Zuriel's hood (disambiguation)
title: Zuriel's hood (disambiguation)
lead:
Zuriel's hood may refer to:

* Zuriel's hood (bh), the version earned at Bounty Hunter
** Corrupted zuriel's hood (bh), the corrupted version earned at Bounty Hunter
* Zuriel's hood (Deadman Mode), the version available in Deadman Mode
* Zuriel's hood (beta), the beta version from the Bounty Hunter beta test
** Zuriel's hood (c), the beta corrupted version from the Bounty Hunter beta test
